Description

Reporting to the Director of Spiritual Care and Education for HOSPITAL, the Clinical Pastoral Education (CPE) Resident is responsible for responding to the spiritual needs of patients, their loved ones, and staff of all and no religious and spiritual traditions throughout HOSPITAL. The CPE Resident assesses patients’ needs; provides spiritual, emotional, religious, and existential support in diverse clinical settings; collaborates closely with interdisciplinary teams of staff; and liaises with priests, Eucharistic ministers, and community clergy. The CPE Resident also provides staff support through Take10 visits and other initiatives. The CPE Resident functions as a team member of the Department of Spiritual Care and Education and throughout the Mount Sinai Health System, establishes collaborative relationships with the interdisciplinary care team and other professionals, and actively participates in department initiatives. All CPE Residents share responsibility for overnight and weekend on-call shifts across several hospitals. CPE Residents are expected to actively participate in Mount Sinai’s Association for Clinical Pastoral Education (ACPE) residency training program, which includes completing all written requirements and reading assignments and engaging actively in class with the goal of completing the educational requirements for chaplaincy certification.



Responsibilities

1. Assess the spiritual, emotional, religious, and existential needs of patients and their loved ones and provide appropriate spiritual care interventions.

2. Demonstrate and deepen skills for working with patients in multiple clinical areas including general medical-surgical settings, critical care, Emergency Department, and ambulatory settings.

3. Chart visits in the electronic health record (EHR) in a timely and appropriate manner and complete all other required record keeping and data collection.

4. Collaborate closely on patient care with interdisciplinary teams of staff and develop and maintain professional relationships.

5. Liaise with priests, Eucharistic ministers, volunteers, and other local clergy people to meet patients’ needs.

6. Provide spiritual care to patients and staff in the context of religious holidays and special events.

7. Engage in staff support initiatives, including Take10 visits and activities during Nurses’ Week.

8. Support and train incoming CPE interns, as appropriate and needed.

9. Participate in the overnight, weekend and holiday on-call rotation.

10. Adhere to all MSHS standards, policies, and procedures, including those that create a safe environment of care.

11. Complete all required trainings and in-services.

12. Participate, as appropriate, in the department’s quality improvement activities.

13. Perform other related duties and activities as may be requested by the Director of Spiritual Care and Education.

14. Participate actively in the Clinical Pastoral Education program, including completing all written requirements and reading assignments and engaging actively in class.

15. Adhere to the code of ethics of the Association of Professional Chaplains (APC).



Qualifications

Must have successfully completed at least one unit of CPE at an ACPE-accredited center

ABOUT GREYSTAR


Greystar is a leading, fully integrated global real estate platform offering expertise in property management, investment management, development, and construction services in institutional-quality rental housing. Headquartered in Charleston, South Carolina, Greystar manages and operates over $350 billion of real estate in more than 260 markets globally with offices throughout North America, Europe, South America, and the Asia-Pacific region. Greystar is the largest operator of apartments in the United States, managing over one million units/beds globally. Across its platforms, Greystar has nearly $79 billion of assets under management, including over $34 billion of development assets and over $36.5 billion of regulatory assets under management. Greystar was founded by Bob Faith in 1993 to become a provider of world-class service in the rental residential real estate business. To learn more, visit www.greystar.com.

JOB DESCRIPTION SUMMARY

This role manages the day-to-day operations of an assigned property including managing the team members, daily activities, and resources of the property to achieve established budgeted financial and operational goals, and ensures that the operation of the property complies with Company policies and procedures, Fair Housing, Americans with Disabilities Act, Fair Credit Reporting Act, and other laws and regulations governing multi-family housing operations.

JOB DESCRIPTION

Property Type: Midrise

Stage: Stabilized

Unit Count: 367


  • Provides input into the development of budget(s) for the property by analyzing and evaluating financial statements, reviewing current and projected marketing information, and accessing operational reports that establish historic and predict performance patterns.
  • Meets targeted revenues by setting rent rates, ensuring rent and fees are collected and posted in a timely manner, making financial bank deposits, and preparing and reviewing monthly financial status reports.
  • Approves invoices from vendors, contractors, and service providers for payment by reconciling work performed or products purchased, ensuring validity of certificates of insurance, coding charges to appropriate Chart of Account codes, and managing communication between the vendor/contractor, accounting, and the client/owner as needed.
  • Controls expenditures by staying within the constraints of the approved budget and manages the balance and maintenance of the petty cash fund.
  •  Oversees the lease enforcement process by approving prospective resident applications, discounts and renewal leases, conducts periodic apartment inspections, follows proper notice requirements, evicts residents, and imposes and collects late fees and other charges as allowable and stated in the terms of the lease.
  • Gathers, analyzes, and interprets current market and economic trends that may impact the property and implements short- and long-range marketing and leasing strategies to achieve the property’s occupancy and revenue goals.
  •  Promotes resident satisfaction and retention by responding to complaints, questions, and requests in a timely manner, and taking appropriate action to resolve and address service issues. Ensures the property’s maintenance team members comply with the Company’s standards with respect to responding and completing resident service requests.
  •  Conducts regular property inspections and takes appropriate actions to ensure that the physical aspects of the property, grounds, buildings, and amenities meet established standards for safety, cleanliness, and general appearance and appeal.
  • Supervises property staff by interviewing, hiring, orienting, and training employees, and manages their performance in accordance with Company policies, values, and business practices.
  • Assists in managing the client/owner relationship by meeting with the owners, conducting property tours, providing updates and information about the property’s performance, and responding to owner requests as needed.
  •  Completes various accounting, financial, administrative, and other reports and performs other duties as assigned or as necessary.
  • For California Only: Community Managers working in California are responsible for managing the lease process by utilizing the California specific Lease File Checklist to ensure all lease documents are complete, compliant, and consistently organized.

BASIC KNOWLEDGE & QUALIFICATIONS:

  • Bachelor’s degree from an accredited college or university preferred in Business Management, Real Estate, or related field.
  • 4-6 years minimum of relevant experience that demonstrates the application of property management, sales, marketing, and customer service background sufficient to manage the day-to-day operation of an apartment community, resolve customer complaints and issues, complete financial records, documents, and reports, increase sales revenues, and coordinate the work of a team
  • Ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment.
  • Excellent communication, conflict resolution, and customer service skills.
  • Detail-oriented and self-motivated with the ability to work independently, as a leader, and as a collaborative member of a team.

SPECIALIZED SKILLS:

  • Incumbents must have all licenses and/or certifications as required by State and Local jurisdictions.
  • Incumbents must have valid driver’s license to drive a golf cart on property and must ensure all other on-site staff that has access to drive the golf cart also has a valid driver’s license.
  •  Proficiency in Internet, word processing, spreadsheet, and database management programs in order to complete required reports and employment documents. 
  • Strong proficiency in using property management software (preferably Entrata, Yardi, and/or OneSite).
  •  Management and supervisory skills sufficient to hire, lead, direct, evaluate, and manage subordinate and team members, including maintenance specialists

TRAVEL / PHYSICAL DEMANDS:

  • Team members work in an office environment but also may have frequent exposure to outside elements where temperature, weather, odors, and/or landscape may be unpleasant and/or hazardous. Incumbents must be able to physically access all exterior and interior parts of the property and amenities. 
  •  Incumbents must be able to physically access all exterior and interior parts of the community and amenities.
  • Incumbents must be able to push, pull, lift, carry, or maneuver weights of up to twenty (20) pounds independently and fifty (50) pounds with assistance.
  •  Routine, local travel may be required to make bank deposits, attend training classes and outreach events, or other situations necessary for the accomplishment of some or all of the daily responsibilities of this position.

#LI-JMC1

The salary range for this position is $85,000 - $100,000


Additional Compensation:


Many factors go into determining employee pay within the posted range including business requirements, prior experience, current skills and geographical location.

  • Corporate Positions: In addition to the base salary, this role may be eligible to participate in a quarterly or annual bonus program based on individual and company performance.
  • Onsite Property Positions: In addition to the base salary, this role may be eligible to participate in weekly, monthly, and/or quarterly bonus programs.

Robust Benefits Offered*:

  • Competitive Medical, Dental, Vision, and Disability & Life insurance benefits. Low (free basic) employee Medical costs for employee-only coverage.
  • Generous Paid Time off. All new hires start with 15 days of vacation, 4 personal days, 10 sick days, and 11 paid holidays. Plus your birthday off after 1 year of service! Additional vacation accrued with tenure.

*Benefits offered for full-time employees. For Union and Prevailing Wage roles, compensation and benefits may vary from the listed information above due to Collective Bargaining Agreements and/or local governing authority.

About the role

The Family Pastor leads Christ Covenant's Families department, setting the strategy and vision for how the church disciples children, students, and the parents who shepherd them from birth through graduation. This role directs Covenant Kids and Covenant Students as one connected pathway across every campus, and owns Family Worship as a churchwide rhythm of the Covenant Wheel, equipping parents to be the primary disciple-makers in their homes.


What you'll do

Family Discipleship Strategy & Family Worship

  • Own Family Worship as an emphasis of the Covenant Wheel, championing it churchwide as a regular, intentional rhythm of reading God's Word, praying, and singing together as a family.
  • Set and communicate the strategy and vision for family discipleship at Christ Covenant, from birth through graduation.
  • Develop and maintain Family Worship resources for the congregation that could include devotion guides, reading plans, catechism materials, and worship playlists that connect the home to what is taught on Sunday.
  • Partner with the Discipleship team to equip group leaders to shepherd their members toward Family Worship.
  • Advocate for the family and parent lens in churchwide planning, calendaring, and ministry decisions.
  • Assess the health of family discipleship across the church and adjust strategy as needed.

Covenant Kids & Covenant Students Alignment

  • Direct Covenant Kids and Covenant Students as one connected discipleship pathway, ensuring a child moves from the nursery to graduation without falling through the gaps between ministries.
  • Build the handoff between Kids and Students, including the transition from elementary to middle school, so families experience one ministry rather than two.
  • Align curriculum, teaching calendars, and discipleship emphases across both ministries and with the church's preaching calendar.
  • Oversee the quality and consistency of the Kids and Students experience at every campus, including new campus launches, contextualizing where needed without losing a unified philosophy of ministry.
  • Visit campuses on a regular rotation to evaluate ministry environments, encourage staff and volunteers, and ensure standards are being met.
  • Partner with campus pastors and directors so family ministry is well integrated into the life of each campus.

Parent Equipping, Milestones & Child Dedications

  • Build a parent equipping pathway that supports families at every stage, including new parents, parents of early elementary children, parents entering the student years, and parents launching graduates.
  • Plan and lead parent gatherings, classes, and seminars at each campus, and recruit seasoned parents and elders to teach alongside you.
  • Oversee child dedications churchwide, including parent preparation, scheduling with campus and worship teams, and follow-up with families.
  • Define and shepherd family milestones, working with the Discipleship and Care teams on conversations around salvation, baptism, and the Lord's Supper.
  • Develop a communication rhythm that keeps parents informed and equipped, in partnership with the Communications team.
  • Connect families new to the church into Covenant Kids, Covenant Students, and a group, in partnership with the Assimilation team.

Teaching & Pastoral Care

  • Prepare and deliver teaching in parent and family environments, including parent classes, seminars, and family worship gatherings.
  • Provide pastoral care to families in the church, and partner with the Care Pastor, elders, and Counseling Ministry on complex or sensitive situations involving children and students.
  • Build evangelistic and discipling relationships with parents, children, and students.
  • Participate in the weekly rhythms of pastoral ministry, including staff meetings, membership processes, and shepherding responsibilities as assigned.

Staff Leadership, Budget & Minor Protection

  • Direct the Covenant Kids and Covenant Students staff teams through weekly meetings and personal coaching, reviewing and planning all ministry activities.
  • Lead the recruiting, hiring, onboarding, and performance management of Families department staff and interns.
  • Set and manage the Families department budget, and steward ministry resources, curriculum purchases, and event spending.
  • Oversee the volunteer strategy for Kids and Students across campuses, including recruiting, training, and retention, and manage Planning Center workflows and profiles for the department.
  • Hold the Families department accountable to the church-wide Minor Protection Policy at every campus, including background checks, volunteer vetting, training, ratios, check-in and check-out procedures, and incident reporting.
  • Partner with the Operations and Facilities teams on safe, well-prepared ministry environments at each campus.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

Qualifications

Education & Experience

  • Bachelor's (B.A.) in related field and Master of Divinity (M.Div.) degree preferred
  • At least 5 years of ministry or pastoral experience, with significant experience in children's or student ministry
  • Demonstrated experience leading staff and volunteer teams
  • Experience shepherding and equipping parents, and a personal conviction about the home as the primary place of discipleship
  • Ability to lead ministry across multiple campuses and locations
  • Understanding of and willingness to minister within the church's statement of beliefs
  • Character congruent with the biblical requirements for leaders (1 Tim. 3:1-13; 2 Tim. 2; Titus 1:5-9)
  • Membership at Christ Covenant, or willingness to become a member


Licenses, Registrations, and Certifications

  • Ordination or licensure, or willingness to pursue ordination through Christ Covenant
  • Completion of a background check and the church's Minor Protection Policy training prior to ministry with minors, and annually thereafter

Physical Requirements

  • This is an in-person role based on site, with regular travel between Christ Covenant campuses.
  • Regularly required to sit, stand, walk, talk, and hear, and to use hands to handle or feel objects, tools, or controls.
  • Frequently required to move throughout ministry spaces, including classrooms, hallways, stairs, and outdoor areas, and to sit or kneel on the floor at a child's level.
  • Must be able to lift and carry up to 40 pounds occasionally, such as ministry supplies, curriculum boxes, and event equipment.
  • Must be able to speak clearly and project to groups, with and without amplification, for extended periods.
  • Specific vision abilities required include close vision, distance vision, and the ability to adjust focus, including sustained work on a computer screen.
  • Requires a schedule that includes Sundays, evenings, and occasional overnight travel for camps, retreats, and ministry trips, including outdoor activity in varying weather conditions.
  • Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

God has called InterVarsity to plant and to build witnessing communities of students and faculty who follow Jesus on college and university campuses. Through these groups, we believe ever- increasing numbers of students and faculty from all ethnic groups and areas of the campus will be transformed by the Gospel. We expect to see campuses increasingly become places where people, ideas, and structures flourish to the glory of God. We confidently anticipate that our InterVarsity alumni will become change agents across the country and around the world. We pursue this calling by discerning and actively participating in what God is already doing on campus. This is the essence of being a Campus Staff Minister (CSM).

ESSENTIAL COMMITMENTS/RESPONSIBILITIES 

Spiritual Growth 

You pursue maturity as a disciple of Jesus Christ so that your life and work increasingly reflects a growing love for God, God’s Word, God’s people of every ethnicity and culture, and God’s purposes in the world. To do this, you will: 

  • Pursue a vibrant relationship with the triune God through engagement with Scripture, prayer, and worship, both individually and in community 

  • Develop self-leadership (growing in self-awareness, self-management, relational integrity, and resiliency) 

  • Embrace Scriptural standards for behavior and attitudes 

 

Campus Leadership 

You communicate and model InterVarsity’s vision to see students and faculty transformed, campuses renewed and world changers developed 

  • Create a culture of humble dependence on God and bold expectation in God’s intention to start new witnessing communities throughout the campus and on new campuses 

  • Model – in person and through programs – InterVarsity’s vision and Core Values, including a biblically-defined commitment to engage every ethnic and social group on campus 

  • Lead students and faculty – individually and collectively – through Scripture, prayer, teaching, and discipleship experiences, so that they articulate and align their ministry activities around this vision 

  • Set annual goals through prayer, research and reflection with your teams (students, faculty, and staff) for qualitative and quantitative growth, including conversions and leadership development 

 

You create, develop, align and leverage ministry plans, programs, teams, and structures to close the gap between current reality and the aspirational goals. 

  • Build leadership teams who trust and partner well with you and who demonstrate spiritual vitality, relational health, and mission alignment 

  • Develop and execute plans to achieve annual goals, evaluating and modifying the plan as needed throughout the year 

  • Increase momentum for the vision by aligning programs, structures, conferences and teams around the goals 

  • Mobilize students and faculty to engage their relational networks with the gospel and to start new missional communities 

  • Under the direction of the Area Director, may supervise Ministry Interns and Campus Ministry Interns as delegated 

 

You intentionally gather, invite, and develop diverse groups of students and faculty so that they not only encounter and follow Jesus as Savior and Lord but also advance the mission on campus as participants and leaders. 

  • Create ways for faculty and students to encounter and follow Jesus through Scripture, worship, prayer, mission experiences, conferences, etc. 

  • Equip students and faculty so that they think strategically about campus engagement and so that they proclaim – in word, deed, and power – the good news of Jesus, regularly inviting students and faculty to follow him as Savior and Lord 

  • Disciple students and faculty by equipping them to hear the Word, respond actively, and debrief and interpret the experience so that they grow in Christlikeness, reflect our Core Values, and develop ministry skills 

  • Invite, coach, and equip students and faculty to become increasingly effective participants and leaders, including starting new witnessing communities on campuses 

 

Organizational Collaboration 

You work with a network of other local, area, regional, and national InterVarsity staff and volunteers so that our work reflects Biblical standards of excellence, integrity, and partnership. 

  • Partner with and respond positively to the direction and coaching of your supervisors and national leaders 

  • Contribute to collaborative and productive team meetings and relationships 

  • Affiliate chapters under your care and submit Graduating Student Forms in order to increase our partnership with current students and alumni 

  • Use national ministry resources and tools, as requested, including recruiting and/or participating in local, regional, or national conferences as  

  • Complete reporting, planning and review requirements in a timely way so that you and your supervisors can assess and improve your work as a CSM 

  • Comply with all InterVarsity policies and procedures 

 

Ministry Partnership Development 

You will develop a team of partners – churches and individuals (including alumni and community members) – who will resource the ministry financially, in prayer, or volunteer service that advances the mission. 

  • Raise 100% of the financial budget assigned by your supervisor 

  • Communicate regularly with your ministry partners, nurturing the relationship through visits, phone calls, emails and regular prayer letters 

  • Develop on-going, long-lasting partnership with alumni and volunteers 

  • Comply with all Ministry Partnership Policies 

  • Identify and invest in advocates who will build networks of volunteers and donors on InterVarsity’s behalf 

 

Accomplish all other assigned tasks as appropriate 

 

QUALIFICATIONS (common to all levels of CSM) 

  • Annually affirm InterVarsity’s Statement of Agreement (Doctrinal Basis and Purpose Statement). Abide by InterVarsity’s Code of Conduct. Believe and behave consonantly with InterVarsity’s Human Sexuality Theological Paper. Affirm and behave consonantly with InterVarsity’s “Women in Ministry Statement of Affirmation” 

  • Bachelor’s degree for CSMs assigned to a four-year campus. A minimum of an Associate’s degree for CSMs assigned to a two-year campus or a community college 

  • Strong interpersonal skills (including ability to minister to diverse ethnic communities and faculty) 

  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills 

  • Demonstrated problem solving skills 

  • Familiarity with word processing, presentation, email, and spreadsheet software 

 

WORK ENVIRONMENT/PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS 

The CSM position leads ministry in a college campus environment. A designated office space may or may not be available. The CSM is required to travel to on-campus and off- campus sites as appropriate. Off-campus travel includes, but is not limited to: student ministry conferences, Ministry Partnership Development meetings, and InterVarsity- sponsored training sessions, meetings, and conferences. The CSM is regularly required to communicate with others, and routinely uses standard office equipment such as computers, phones, photocopiers, filing cabinets, etc.

Associate Pastor Position Overview:

We are a multi-generational, multi-ethnic Bible-believing church in the Valley neighborhood of Syracuse. Syracuse Alliance Church exists to magnify Jesus Christ and empower God's people to share the Good News of the gospel. We are seeking a dynamic and strategic leader to serve as our Associate Pastor.

The Assistant Pastor supports the Lead Pastor in shepherding the congregation of Syracuse Alliance Church through pastoral care, discipleship, and ministry oversight. This role provides leadership to key fellowship and Youth ministries, assists with ordinances and church administration, and helps ensure the spiritual health and operational effectiveness of the church. The Assistant Pastor serves with joy, humility, and a heart for people, advancing the mission and vision of Syracuse Alliance Church.

Key Responsibilities:

The responsibilities of this position will be tailored to the unique strengths, skills, and giftings of the man filling the role. Core responsibilities may include, but are not limited to:

  • Share in the preaching and teaching responsibilities as needed, bringing biblical, relevant, and Spirit-led messages.
  • Partner with the Lead Pastor to officiate weddings and funerals, providing pastoral care to families as needed.
  • Lead efforts to connect new attendees to pathways of membership, baptism, service, small groups, and spiritual growth.
  • Create and maintain a Communion schedule, coordinating with the Elders.
  • Collaborate with the Lead Pastor to develop and execute strategic initiatives that align with the church's mission and vision.
  • Represent the church in the community, building relationships and creating opportunities for outreach and service.

Families have been and will continue to be the foundation of our congregation. SAC’s Youth and Family Ministry is one of its key ministries, seeking to reach out to and serve the youth of our local and commuter communities and their families and to provide them all with a true and hospitable church home that is centered on the Word of God as its only source of truth.

  • Participate in pastoral care, counseling, and home visitation to youth and families.
  • Connect and follow up with newcomer families and welcome them to the church fellowship.
  • Create and shepherd a (bi-weekly middle school) Youth Sunday School by guiding, mentoring and discipling the members of the relevant ministry team.
  • Bring creativity, energy, and heart to help students find their place in God’s story and in the mission of SAC.
  • Be a visible and relational presence at student gatherings, retreats, and events to come alongside, invest, and multiply impact.
  • Assess ministry needs and develop programs and activities to meet those needs (e.g., Easter, Christmas, and other holiday outreaches, Vacation Bible School, tutoring programs, and other outreach events).

  • Proven ability to lead leaders and inspire teams toward a shared vision.
  • Strong strategic thinking and organizational skills.
  • Flexibility and adaptability to serve in various capacities as needs arise.
  • Excellent interpersonal and communication skills.
  • A commitment to the church’s mission and values.
  • A degree in ministry, theology, or a related field, or equivalent ministry training.
  • Proven ministry experience.

SUMMARY

The Associate Campus Pastor reports to and serves alongside the Campus Pastor to help lead, shepherd, and equip the Pinelake Oxford campus. As an extension of the Campus Pastor’s office, this role enhances and provides greater span of care and depth in pastoral leadership, team development, and ministry oversight. The core focus is to partner with the campus pastor to ensure the mission, vision, and values of Pinelake Church are carried forward with excellence and faithfulness.

GENERAL RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Learn
    • Pursue a growing relationship with Jesus through consistent time in God’s Word and prayer.
    • Continually grow in your understanding of the Jesus-Centered Life (salvation, identity, life, and authority in Christ).
    • Remain teachable and hungry, seeking feedback, learning from others, and developing both spiritually and professionally.
    • Cultivate awareness of God’s presence in everyday life, listening to the Holy Spirit and responding in obedience.
  • Live
    • Practice and model the rhythms of Be the Church (Grow, Pray, Connect, and Share).
    • Pursue emotional health by engaging in self-awareness, addressing past wounds, and cultivating honest, healthy relationships.
    • Practice healthy rhythms, prioritizing your relationship with Jesus and your family
    • Embody a life of integrity and surrender, allowing your private life with God to shape your work.
  • Lead
    • Take ownership of disciple-making by personally investing in others and helping them move toward a Jesus-Centered Life.
    • Walk others through the Discipleship Pathway (Essentials → JCL → Be the Church), helping them discover and take their next step.
    • Shepherd people, not just programs, by listening for where God is at work in their story and walking with them toward transformation.
    • Equip and release others by developing Servant Leaders and multiplying disciples who Learn from Christ, Live in Christ, and Lead others to Christ.
    • Measure success by life change, spiritual formation, and multiplication—not just attendance or activity.
  • Embrace the Culture
    • Value and embody the staff values, which we call the 7 H’s: Humility, Honor, Honesty, Hunger, Holy Spirit, Health, and Harmony
    • Communicate clearly, honestly, and proactively in a way that builds trust, unity, and momentum.
    • Work in alignment with the church vision and leadership
    • Participate fully in the life of your campus or team, contributing to the unity, health, and shepherding of the faith family.


    SPECIFIC LIST OF DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

    • Help lead, develop, and care for staff and volunteer teams
    • Provide pastoral leadership through presence, prayer, care, and relational connection
    • Support weekend services and key ministry environments
    • Champion a culture of discipleship, teamwork, and servant leadership
    • Step in to lead ministries or initiatives as needed to support campus health and growth
    • NextGen & Discipleship Oversight
      • Provide direct leadership, coaching, and accountability for the Lead College Pastor, Lead Student Pastor, Kids Pastor, Preschool Minister, and (as assigned) the Adult Groups/Discipleship Pastor
      • Champion a unified discipleship pathway across preschool, kids, students, college, and adult groups to ensure alignment and continuity
    • Conduct regular one-on-one meetings with direct reports to provide spiritual care, leadership development, goal alignment, and performance feedback
    • Ensure ministry strategies, calendars, and environments are aligned with Pinelake Church’s mission, vision, values, and campus priorities
    • Support, coach, and equip ministry leaders in volunteer recruitment, leader development, and team health
    • Oversee ministry planning, execution, and evaluation for key seasonal initiatives (camps, retreats, conferences, and milestone events)
    • Collaborate with the Campus Pastor to identify leadership development opportunities and succession planning for NextGen and discipleship ministries
    • Perform other duties as assigned.

    SPECIFIC RESPONSIBILITIES – NEXTGEN, FAMILIES, & DISCIPLESHIP OVERSIGHT

    • Serve as a catalyst and guide in equipping parents to become disciple-makers in their homes. Partner with NextGen families through intentional initiatives and relational engagement to strengthen the family unit and cultivate faithful followers of Jesus who, in turn, make disciples.

    SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES

    • Adult Groups and Connections ministry staff as well as all NextGen ministry staff to include preschool, kids, middle school, high school and college.

    QUALIFICATIONS

    To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily. The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skill and/or ability required. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform essential functions.

    • Proven ministry leadership experience in a local church with comparable context to Pinelake Oxford’s size and culture
    • Deep love for the local church with proven leadership toward building a discipleship culture
    • Passionate about people and energized to see others grow
    • Strong relational and team leadership skills
    • Flexible and dependable to lead and execute key initiatives
    • Focused and aligned with Pinelake Church’s mission, vision, and values
    • Spiritually mature, emotionally healthy, and secure enough to lead from the second chair.

    EDUCATION AND/OR EXPERIENCE

    Bachelor’s degree minimum; Required to be licensed/ordained. Seminary experience is a plus. Eight or more years of related experience and/or training.

    LANGUAGE SKILLS

    The individual must have excellent interpersonal skills, ability to work with a diverse group of people, communicate clearly and effectively on the telephone, e-mail and in person demonstrating tact and diplomacy. Exceptional interpersonal skills are required to develop and maintain strong working relationships with volunteers, co-workers, the public and church members and regular attendees. The individual must have the ability to understand written or oral instructions; read, analyze and interpret complex documents, instructions manuals, policies and procedures is essential.

The individual must have basic mathematical skills, knowledge of bookkeeping and basic accounting, and budget and expense monitoring. The individual must have the ability to read financial information and spreadsheets.

The ability to work effectively and efficiently under stressful conditions to ensure deadlines are met is essential.

Description:

There are nearly 300,000 teenagers of active-duty U.S. military parents who are stationed all over the world. These teens move an average of seven times during their school-aged years. The questions of identity and belonging that all teens face grow even more challenging to answer amid starting over and meeting new friends at each location.

This is where you can be the difference in a military teen’s life! By being in their world, walking alongside them, and creating a community where they experience the truth of God’s love and purpose for them, our staff provide a safe space where teens can develop friendships and connections to experience laughter, build hope, and generate resiliency.

We are currently providing incarnational ministry at many military installations around the world. You will have the opportunity to lead and oversee the overall Young Life Military program, known as Club Beyond, which is ecumenically focused and outreach oriented.

We are currently looking for both full-time and part-time staff throughout the United States, as well as international locations. Colorado Springs, CO, is the headquarters.

Responsibilities:

  • Actively develop healthy relationships with adults, as well as kids, and build vibrant relationships with the local community, the military installation, and the chapel community.
  • Be a role model (incarnational) and assist with developing community outreach to "unchurched" teens, discipleship to Christian teens, and leading and equipping volunteers to do "hands-on" middle and high school Christian youth programs.
  • Work well in an environment that sees (due to high military operational tempo) a high degree of turnover among teens, families, chaplains and volunteers.
  • Be respectful of and embrace a community that is deeply influenced by a military culture.

Club Beyond is a Christ-centered community of leaders with an exclusively military focus. Our methods are incarnational, and our perspective is ecumenical. We leverage strategic partnerships for the greatest results. We value professionalism from our staff and excellence in our stewardship.

post_html:
Campus Staff Minister – Upstate NY (Graduate and Faculty Ministry)

Work Location:

New York

Job Type:

Full time

God has called InterVarsity to plant and to build witnessing communities of students and faculty who follow Jesus on college and university campuses. Through these groups, we believe ever- increasing numbers of students and faculty from all ethnic groups and areas of the campus will be transformed by the Gospel. We expect to see campuses increasingly become places where people, ideas, and structures flourish to the glory of God. We confidently anticipate that our InterVarsity alumni will become change agents across the country and around the world. We pursue this calling by discerning and actively participating in what God is already doing on campus. This is the essence of being a Campus Staff Minister (CSM).

This position is open to both full-time and part-time applicants. The pay range listed is for an employee working 40 hours/week as a Campus Staff Minister. Pay will be prorated for employees who work less than 40 hours/week.


We have positions in the following locations:

  • Syracuse University – graduate students and/or faculty

  • SUNY Buffalo – graduate students

  • SUNY Albany – graduate students

Other schools may be available.

Please submit the GFM Interest Form before completing the full application for a position with Graduate & Faculty Ministries in our online system. We will contact you when we are ready to proceed with the application process.

Volunteers are welcome. Volunteer opportunities range from prayer and hospitality to leading a campus fellowship of graduate students and faculty. Those interested in volunteering will go through an application and interview process, however, volunteer openings are not posted online. For more information, complete the GFM Interest Form or contact your local InterVarsity staff.

ESSENTIAL COMMITMENTS/RESPONSIBILITIES 

Spiritual Growth 

You pursue maturity as a disciple of Jesus Christ so that your life and work increasingly reflects a growing love for God, God’s Word, God’s people of every ethnicity and culture, and God’s purposes in the world. To do this, you will: 

  • Pursue a vibrant relationship with the triune God through engagement with Scripture, prayer, and worship, both individually and in community 

  • Develop self-leadership (growing in self-awareness, self-management, relational integrity, and resiliency) 

  • Embrace Scriptural standards for behavior and attitudes 

 

Campus Leadership 

You communicate and model InterVarsity’s vision to see students and faculty transformed, campuses renewed and world changers developed 

  • Create a culture of humble dependence on God and bold expectation in God’s intention to start new witnessing communities throughout the campus and on new campuses 

  • Model – in person and through programs – InterVarsity’s vision and Core Values, including a biblically-defined commitment to engage every ethnic and social group on campus 

  • Lead students and faculty – individually and collectively – through Scripture, prayer, teaching, and discipleship experiences, so that they articulate and align their ministry activities around this vision 

  • Set annual goals through prayer, research and reflection with your teams (students, faculty, and staff) for qualitative and quantitative growth, including conversions and leadership development 

 

You create, develop, align and leverage ministry plans, programs, teams, and structures to close the gap between current reality and the aspirational goals. 

  • Build leadership teams who trust and partner well with you and who demonstrate spiritual vitality, relational health, and mission alignment 

  • Develop and execute plans to achieve annual goals, evaluating and modifying the plan as needed throughout the year 

  • Increase momentum for the vision by aligning programs, structures, conferences and teams around the goals 

  • Mobilize students and faculty to engage their relational networks with the gospel and to start new missional communities 

  • Under the direction of the Area Director, may supervise Ministry Interns and Campus Ministry Interns as delegated 

 

You intentionally gather, invite, and develop diverse groups of students and faculty so that they not only encounter and follow Jesus as Savior and Lord but also advance the mission on campus as participants and leaders. 

  • Create ways for faculty and students to encounter and follow Jesus through Scripture, worship, prayer, mission experiences, conferences, etc. 

  • Equip students and faculty so that they think strategically about campus engagement and so that they proclaim – in word, deed, and power – the good news of Jesus, regularly inviting students and faculty to follow him as Savior and Lord 

  • Disciple students and faculty by equipping them to hear the Word, respond actively, and debrief and interpret the experience so that they grow in Christlikeness, reflect our Core Values, and develop ministry skills 

  • Invite, coach, and equip students and faculty to become increasingly effective participants and leaders, including starting new witnessing communities on campuses 

 

Organizational Collaboration 

You work with a network of other local, area, regional, and national InterVarsity staff and volunteers so that our work reflects Biblical standards of excellence, integrity, and partnership. 

  • Partner with and respond positively to the direction and coaching of your supervisors and national leaders 

  • Contribute to collaborative and productive team meetings and relationships 

  • Affiliate chapters under your care and submit Graduating Student Forms in order to increase our partnership with current students and alumni 

  • Use national ministry resources and tools, as requested, including recruiting and/or participating in local, regional, or national conferences as  

  • Complete reporting, planning and review requirements in a timely way so that you and your supervisors can assess and improve your work as a CSM 

  • Comply with all InterVarsity policies and procedures 

 

Ministry Partnership Development 

You will develop a team of partners – churches and individuals (including alumni and community members) – who will resource the ministry financially, in prayer, or volunteer service that advances the mission. 

  • Raise 100% of the financial budget assigned by your supervisor 

  • Communicate regularly with your ministry partners, nurturing the relationship through visits, phone calls, emails and regular prayer letters 

  • Develop on-going, long-lasting partnership with alumni and volunteers 

  • Comply with all Ministry Partnership Policies 

  • Identify and invest in advocates who will build networks of volunteers and donors on InterVarsity’s behalf 

 

Accomplish all other assigned tasks as appropriate 

 

QUALIFICATIONS (common to all levels of CSM) 

  • Annually affirm InterVarsity’s Statement of Agreement (Doctrinal Basis and Purpose Statement). Abide by InterVarsity’s Code of Conduct. Believe and behave consonantly with InterVarsity’s Human Sexuality Theological Paper. Affirm and behave consonantly with InterVarsity’s “Women in Ministry Statement of Affirmation” 

  • Bachelor’s degree for CSMs assigned to a four-year campus. A minimum of an Associate’s degree for CSMs assigned to a two-year campus or a community college 

  • Strong interpersonal skills (including ability to minister to diverse ethnic communities and faculty) 

  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills 

  • Demonstrated problem solving skills 

  • Familiarity with word processing, presentation, email, and spreadsheet software 

 

WORK ENVIRONMENT/PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS 

The CSM position leads ministry in a college campus environment. A designated office space may or may not be available. The CSM is required to travel to on-campus and off- campus sites as appropriate. Off-campus travel includes, but is not limited to: student ministry conferences, Ministry Partnership Development meetings, and InterVarsity- sponsored training sessions, meetings, and conferences. The CSM is regularly required to communicate with others, and routinely uses standard office equipment such as computers, phones, photocopiers, filing cabinets, etc. 

Pay Range: $39,288.00 - $52,392.00 per year

Pay: This position is funded through personal fundraising. Accordingly, compensation will vary based on the ability of the individual to secure a donor team to fund the cost of his/her salary. The anticipated salary range for this position on a full-time basis (40 hours/week) is dependent on a variety of factors, including location and cost of living. The actual salary received, including any geographic adjustment to account for location and cost of living, is subject to the individual’s ability to raise funds necessary to cover the full amount of such salary within the range set forth in the job posting details.

Benefits:

We offer a competitive benefits package, including health care and retirement savings with a match. Eligibility is based on employee type and hours worked.  Benefits include the following:

  • 403(b) Retirement Savings Plan

  • 403(b) matching contributions

  • Dental insurance

  • Employee assistance program

  • Employee discounts

  • Flexible work schedule

  • Flexible spending accounts

  • Health insurance

  • Health savings account

  • Life insurance

  • Paid time off

  • Parental leave

  • Professional development assistance

  • Vision insurance

Equal Employment Opportunity: 

 

InterVarsity Christian Fellowship/USA is both an equal opportunity employer and a faith-based religious organization. We conduct hiring without regard to race, color, ancestry, national origin, citizenship, age, sex, marital status, parental status, membership in any labor organization, political ideology, or disability of an otherwise qualified individual. The status of InterVarsity Christian Fellowship/USA as an equal opportunity employer does not prevent the organization from hiring staff based on their religious beliefs so that all staff share the same religious commitment.  Pursuant to the Civil Rights Act of 1964, Section 702 (42 U.S.C. 2000e 1(a)) InterVarsity Christian Fellowship/USA has the right to, and does, hire only candidates who agree with InterVarsity’s Statement of Agreement: Purpose and Doctrinal Basis because InterVarsity believes that each and every staff plays a vital role in advancing InterVarsity’s mission and purposes.

EAST CARBON COMMUNITY CHURCH

BI-VOCATIONAL SENIOR PASTOR

East Carbon Community Church (ECCC) is seeking a Senior Pastor that will help the church creatively reach out to their community and equip the members to make disciples. The successful candidate will be dedicated, community-minded, personable, empathic and forward-thinking leader. The position will be Bi-Vocational role to start with and a monthly stipend will be provided. A retired Pastor or International Worker looking for a part-time position would be an ideal candidate.

THE PEOPLE AND CULTURE

ECCC has 15 official members. Before COVID the church was averaging around 30 people for their Sunday worship service. Most of the church members are blue-collar workers. There are a few professionals and several retired persons as well. The church is welcoming of newcomers, accepting and has a casual family atmosphere.

THE HISTORY

ECCC was started in the 1940’s during an Alliance church planting movement in Utah. The current building was the sold to the church for $1. God provided it in a miraculous way. ECCC is one of only two evangelical churches in East Carbon.

THE COMMUNITY

East Carbon is located in the center of Utah. It is a rural community with a history of Coal Mining. The population within a five-mile radius of the church is 1,785. The aver- age household income is $38,000. The community is approximately 75% white and 25% Hispanic. East Carbon is located at the base of the Bookcliff Mountains and the view is beautiful. Outdoor activities such as hunting, fishing, mountain biking, hiking and ATV riding are abundant. East Carbon has a grocery store, a gas station, two cafes and a medical clinic. It is only 25 miles from Price, UT, which has shopping and medical facilities. It is located 2.5 hours from Salt Lake City and 1.5 hours from Moab and Arches National Park. The housing cost is very low in comparison with other places in Utah.

THE FACILITY

The facility is debt free. It is two stories. On the main level there is a sanctuary that seats 120 people, an office, a small classroom bathroom and lobby. In the basement there is a fellowship hall that seats 60, a kitchen, male/female bathrooms, a storage room and three classrooms. It is located in a very visible location. The church recently put a new roof on the building.

THE MOVEMENT

ECCC is part of the Christian and Missionary Alliance. Potential candidates must be in agreement with the Alliance Statement of Faith and be eligible to be accredited with the C&MA. Accreditation must be completed prior to placement in this role. More information on the Alliance can be found at on the Central Pacific District webpage at www.cpdistrict.org and at our national website at www.cmalliance.org

To be considered for this position, please complete the application to include your testimony, resume and other background information related to the position.

If the district office has reviewed your application and they think you may be a potential match for the position, that the hiring manager will reach out to you for next steps.

This position requires licensing with The Christian & Missionary Alliance. To learn more about The Alliance and requirements for licensing, please visit our website

Please do not contact the church directly.

Company Description

Inland Hills Church has consistently been a church that values innovation in service to our mission. We were among the first in Southern California to commit to being a contemporary, relevant church for unchurched people. Currently, we are leveraging the power of ever-changing technologies and the global reach of the internet to share the love of Jesus as broadly as possible.

Today, thousands of people attend Inland Hills from all over the Inland Empire. The numbers, however, are not what drive the leadership at Inland Hills Church. We long to see lives changed by Jesus. We long to align everything we do and everything we invest in with the goal of people encountering and being transformed by Christ.

Job Description

Overview:

The Creative Arts Pastor will empower IHC's music and production teams to create immersive worship experiences that lead people into a growing relationship with Jesus. You'll oversee staff and volunteers, partner with our leadership team, and play an active role in the life and growth of IHC's ministries.

You have a track record developing staff and volunteers. You have musical and/or technical expertise; you connect easily with different kinds of people; and you find working collaboratively with others energizing.

You're a strategic, proactive, and innovative leader. You thrive in a fast-paced environment, and you truly enjoy solving unexpected problems. You can approach a problem from multiple angles, and you make sure the details don't get overlooked.

Pastorally, you prioritize your relationship with Jesus, and you have a spiritual maturity that enables you to pour into others. You're aware of your spiritual gifts, and using your gifts brings you great joy.

Finally, you're passionate about your own growth: you network with other leaders, you read books and/or listen to podcasts for fresh perspectives, and you're more uncomfortable with the status quo than the prospect of change.

 

Key Responsibilities:

•  Lead. Recruit, train, pastor and develop staff and volunteers serving in worship arts and production ministries. Ensure that team members are equipped for their roles, immersed in IHC culture, and spiritually growing in their relationships with Jesus.  

•  Supervise. Oversee the work of the worship pastor, music, and production teams in supporting them in establishing workflows, protocols, etc. Define and monitor ongoing progress toward departmental milestones. Maintain an awareness of team members’ strengths and growth opportunities. Delegate decision-making authority, as appropriate, while also making critical decisions on behalf of your team leaders, where needed.

•  Communicate. Maintain regular contact with staff and volunteers to encourage, provide essential information, and solicit feedback to ensure issues are identified and addressed on an ongoing basis.

•  Steward ministry resources. Oversee development and execution of annual ministry budgets (worship arts and production-related) consistent with Inland Hills’ mission and vision. Steward facilities, equipment and other resources committed to worship arts; advocate for additional resources, as needed.

•  Innovate and make things better. Develop and implement high-quality, forward-looking solutions within your sphere of responsibilities. Be proactive; be willing to “think outside of the box” to solve problems; consistently contribute your best effort and attitude and inspire others to do the same. 

•  Pastor. Lead others to find life by following Jesus. Model authentic, ongoing personal spiritual growth, and encourage your team to do so as well. Provide care and counsel for the staff and volunteers within your ministry, and across IHC.

•  Demonstrate Inland Hills’ core values. Make it better; work collaboratively; care personally, challenge directly; develop others; choose joy.

Qualifications

  • Strong capabilities in either production or musical worship arts, with the ability to serve/lead alongside staff/volunteers in either a musical or technical context within the Creative Arts team
  • Excellent problem-solving, communication, and collaboration skills, especially in high-pressure situations, with a track record of effective leadership in complex situations
  • Demonstrates spiritual depth, maturity, and leadership (supervision) of staff and volunteers
  • A pastorally-hearted leader with a commitment to ongoing personal growth for the sake of serving Jesus and the local Church ever-more effectively

Additional Information

TO APPLY: Submit your resume, cover letter, and a brief personal intro video at inlandhills.com/careers.

post_html:
The Discipleship Pastor at Peoples Church will provide oversight and direction across our broader discipleship and pastoral care ministries. This pastor will shepherd the congregation through classes, groups, men’s ministry, recovery programs, and our pastoral care rotation, leading as a pastor rather than a program manager. We want people to grow through individual discipleship via Bible reading plans, collaborative discipleship through coaching and training, and group discipleship through Bible studies and classes. The Discipleship Pastor will lead our volunteer teachers and leaders, work alongside dedicated administrative support, and partner closely with our leadership in shepherding the broader life of the congregation.


Key Responsibilities

  • Lead and shape the overall discipleship strategy for Peoples Church, including our framework of individual, collaborative, and group discipleship.
  • Oversee our volunteer teachers for classes, our recovery programs, and our men’s ministry, an area we are eager to invest in more deeply.
  • Direct our pastoral care ministry, including hospital visits, the pastor-on-call rotation, and the deployment of pastoral staff to care for the congregation.
  • Serve as a primary provider and overseer of pastoral counseling, including premarital counseling.
  • Develop and train our teachers and leaders, investing in those who lead classes and groups.
  • Lead and develop administrative support connected to discipleship and pastoral care.
  • Continue building integrated discipleship resources, such as Bible reading plans connected to weekend teaching, that help people take real next steps with Jesus.
  • Remain open to refining, and even overhauling, our current discipleship philosophy as you lead.


Key Qualifications

  • A bachelor’s degree minimum, preferably in biblical studies, theology, or a related field. A master’s degree is a plus.
  • Two to five years of discipleship or comparable experience preferred, or broader pastoral experience that demonstrates the substance this role requires.
  • A self-starter who sets their own goals and a team player willing to work within the wide hallways of our leadership culture.
  • An excellent communicator, both in person and electronically, capable of preaching from the main platform several times a year.
  • Experienced in leading and developing volunteer teams and in working with administrative staff.
  • A thoughtful approach to pastoral counseling, including comfort overseeing or referring premarital counseling.
  • Aligned with our theological convictions.


Why We Love This Opportunity

This is a great opportunity for an experienced pastor who wants real scope and real freedom. Peoples Church will hand the right person a broad portfolio, administrative support, a healthy budget, and the trust to lead it as a pastor rather than an administrator. There is room here to shape the discipleship vision, to teach, to walk with people through life’s hardest moments, and to build something that lasts, all within a church family that will embrace you and a community where you can put down deep roots.


About This Organization

Peoples Church is a church in Fresno, California, and has been a prominent presence in the Central Valley for over 70 years. We average around 3,500 in Sunday morning attendance at our gatherings. We are well known and respected in the community for our focus on serving the city we love, and we are traditionally known as a loving church where people feel at home when they come on campus. Guided by our vision of Helping People See God and Participate in His Redemptive Story, we come alongside our community to show them the hope found in Jesus, shaped by our values of Loving God, Loving Others, Loving Truth, Loving Culture, and Loving Sacrifice. We are a multi-generational and increasingly diverse congregation, and we actively extend a hand into the community through events that meet people where they are. We are a big church that works hard to feel like a small one, where it is easy to get connected and where people are welcomed in and treated like family.


Location

Fresno is a respite from the large cities that typify ideas about California, such as San Francisco and Los Angeles. Fresno County produces agriculture that feeds the world and is home to a tight-knit, diverse community with a rich history and a small-town feel. Sitting in the heart of the Central Valley, Fresno offers an enviable location with easy access to both the mountains and the coast, with Yosemite, Sequoia, and Kings Canyon National Parks practically in the backyard, and both Los Angeles and the Bay Area within easy reach for a weekend trip. It is a place where a pastor and family can put down roots, raise children, and build a life alongside their ministry for the long haul.

Overview:

  • Job Position: Full-time Children's Ministry Director
  • Church Size: 200 - 300
  • Children's Ministry Group Size: 80-100

Education Preferred:

Bachelor's degree in ministry, elementary education, or a related field; however, equivalent ministry or related experience may be considered in lieu of a degree.

Professional Development:

Licensure with The Christian and Missionary Alliance (C&MA) is valued but not required. For candidates interested in pursuing Alliance licensure, support and opportunities for professional development and credentialing are available.

Who We Are:

Community Alliance Church in Detroit Lakes, MN is a multi-generational, Christ­-Centered church that exists to abide and grow in relationship with God, connect with others, and reach our community and world. Located in the land of lakes, Detroit Lakes is a summer tourist hub with lots of fun activities for the entire family including: great live music, art festivals, farmers market, flea market, mountain biking, hiking, fishing, community festivals, musical theater, unique shopping, lots of restaurants, and anything you can think of to do on or around a lake! In winter, it's the home of Polar Fest - a two­-week winter festival, plus plenty of opportunity for downhill and cross-country skiing, snowshoeing, ice fishing and snowmobiling!

Position Description:

The time has come to hire our next Children's Ministry Director. We are a church that highly values reaching, equipping, and empowering future generations. We are looking for a leader who has a genuine love for children and their families, is abiding in a deep relationship with Christ, and out of that relationship is passionate about helping children know, love, and follow Jesus.

Our Current Ministry Rhythms:

  • Wednesday night ministry for children from preschool through 5th grade from 6:30-8:00 p.m. Preschool children participate in Cubbies, while elementary students participate in Sparks (K-2nd grade) and Ignite (3rd-5th grade). Elementary students rotate through large-group teaching, games, and grade­level small groups designed to foster Biblical understanding and relational discipleship.
  • Sunday morning ministry. Preschool children meet in age-appropriate classrooms while elementary students gather for worship and large-group teaching before transitioning into grade-level small groups.
  • Selecting, implementing, and evaluating curriculum that helps children understand God's Word and engage in meaningful discipleship on Sundays and Wednesdays.
  • Recruiting, training, encouraging, and developing volunteer leaders who relationally disciple children and help create a safe, welcoming, and Christ­centered ministry environment.
  • Coordinating nursery ministry schedules and maintaining strong communication with nursery volunteers and parents.
  • Communicating consistently with families through digital platforms to keep parents informed, connected, and equipped for discipleship at home.
  • Leading and coordinating children's ministry events throughout the year, including Winter Camp, Fall Fest, Christmas Program, New Year's Eve Party, Tubing Night, Game Night, Grand Prix, and other opportunities that build community and foster spiritual growth.
  • Providing leadership and coordination for Vacation Bible School, a week-long summer outreach ministry that serves both church and community families.
  • Helping children discover how God has uniquely gifted them to serve others and participate in His mission (Ephesians 2:10).
  • Partnering with parents as the primary spiritual influencers in their children's lives by providing encouragement, resources, and opportunities for family discipleship.
  • Working alongside a staff team that enjoys serving Jesus together. We value Gospel partnership, collaboration, shared mission, and genuine friendship. This includes attending staff meetings, participating in ministry planning, contributing to the overall health and vision of the church, and occasionally sharing a good laugh along the way.
  • Maintaining a growing personal relationship with Jesus Christ and leading from a place of spiritual maturity, humility, and dependence upon Him.

Who Thrives in This Role?

The person who thrives in this role will likely be someone who:

  • Loves Jesus deeply and leads from a vibrant personal walk with Him.
  • Enjoys building relationships with children, parents, and volunteers.
  • Believes some of the most significant spiritual growth in children happens through caring, consistent relationships with trusted adult leaders.
  • Values discipleship more than simply running programs.
  • Is organized enough to lead ministry systems while remaining flexible and relational.
  • Enjoys working as part of a collaborative staff team.
  • Is excited about helping the next generation discover, follow, and serve Jesus.

To be considered for this position, please complete the application to include your testimony, resume and other background information related to the position.

If the district office has reviewed your application and they think you may be a potential match for the position, that the hiring manager will reach out to you for next steps.

This position may require licensing with The Christian & Missionary Alliance. To learn more about The Alliance and requirements for licensing, please visit our website

Please do not contact the church directly.

  • Exercise self-leadership (growing in self-awareness, self-management, relational integrity, and resiliency)
  • Embrace and practice Scriptural standards for behavior and attitudes, including those described in the Code of Conduct

​2. Campus Ministry Leadership

As an Area Director, you inspire, coach and develop campus staff ministers (“ministers”), students, faculty, and ministry partners to increase the number of witnessing communities, as well as the size, health, spiritual maturity, and campus-wide influence of existing witnessing communities by being a:

Visionary Guide:

  • Create a culture of dependence on God to gain vision for establishing and advancing witnessing communities that reach every corner of every campus in your area

Structural Architect:

Missional Developer:

  • Develop ministers professionally so that they are consistently increasing their gifts and skills as ministry leaders

  • Proactively establish and develop healthy relationships across racial, ethnic, national background, and gender barriers with staff, students, faculty, and ministry partners to build effective and diverse communities
  • Build an effective minister team that collaborates well and accomplishes goals

3. Organizational Collaboration

As an Area Director, you are part of a national organization and work in partnership with local, area, divisional, regional, and national InterVarsity ministers and volunteers.

  • Participate in regional leadership as determined by the Regional Director, to set ministry vision and strategies, contribute to accomplishing plans, and provide regional leadership in specific areas
  • Positively and constructively respond to the direction and coaching of line supervisors
  • Build productive ministry partnerships with regional and national collaborative leaders
  • Establish systems, processes and protocols to fulfill regular operational and administrative tasks in a timely manner (reporting, finances, human resources, etc.)
  • Maintain sound financial status of the area through management of budgeting, expense control and ministry partnership development
  • Become familiar with and comply with all InterVarsity policies and procedures

4. Ministry Partnership Development (MPD)

As an Area Director, you will develop a team of partners who will resource the ministry financially, in prayer, or with volunteer service that advances the mission.

  • Develop and maintain a ministry among partners who will fund InterVarsity
  • Ensure ministry budget is fully funded
  • Supervise each minister’s MPD (collaborating with coaches when applicable) and equip staff to build ministry partners
  • Build resource networks with alumni, volunteers, churches, advocacy councils, and major donors, in particular to fund low-network ministers
  • Communicate regularly with ministry partners

5. Accomplish all other assigned tasks as appropriate

QUALIFICATIONS

Description
SUMMARY Under the direction of the Pastor, the Parish Catechetical Leader serves in a consolidated position encompassing two distinct but interconnected roles: Parish Catechetical Leader and Administrative Assistant to the Pastor. As Parish Catechetical Leader, the incumbent is primarily responsible for the overall leadership, development, implementation, administration, and evaluation of the Basilica of St. Paul’s comprehensive catechetical ministry, serving parishioners from Pre-K through adulthood, including lifelong faith formation, sacramental preparation, and the catechumenal process, in accordance with Catholic teaching and diocesan requirements. As Administrative Assistant to the Pastor, the incumbent provides professional and confidential administrative support to the Pastor and coordinates designated pastoral services, including Baptisms, First Holy Communion, Confirmation, weddings, and funerals, as well as related parish communications. These two complementary roles are integrated into a single position, with catechetical leadership serving as the principal responsibility while administrative and pastoral support functions contribute to the effective operation of the parish and the fulfillment of its pastoral mission.
 The Diocese of Orlando's four core values lay the foundation for the work performed by its employees: 1. Authenticity: The conviction that God has called us to reflect our inner life of faith in our daily living. 2. Respect: Affirming each person's God-given dignity and uniqueness. 3. Courage: Inspired by this gift of the Holy Spirit, we proclaim and live the Word of God fearlessly and devotedly. 4. Commitment: Individually and collectively, we are steadfast to the team and its purpose 
 ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES The following duties are representative of the tasks performed in this classification and are not listed in order of importance. The omission of a specific duty does not exclude it from the classification if the work is similar, related, or a logical assignment for this position. Other duties may be required and assigned. Administrative Support to the Pastor • Provides general administrative support to the Pastor, including correspondence, communications, calendaring, travel                            arrangements, and follow-up. • Manages the Pastor's calendar and contacts and maintains the parish master calendar. • Opens and distributes daily mail, determines importance and priority, and routes correspondence for action.  • Prepares documents and reports by collecting information and by transcribing, formatting, editing, and transmitting text, data, and graphics. • Keeps the Pastor and appropriate personnel informed of developments and situations, exercising sound judgment and maintaining confidentiality in all areas of responsibility. • Develops and maintains effective records and information management systems, including a current and accurate filing system. • Coordinates and sets up meetings, conferences, liturgical celebrations, special events, luncheons, and other gatherings as requested by the Pastor. • Attends required meetings and gatherings, takes minutes, and offers assistance as needed.  Catechists, Volunteers, and Collaborative Ministry   • Recruits, orients, forms, schedules, and supports catechists and volunteers; coordinates ongoing catechetical training and appropriate leadership development. • Ensures that personnel and volunteers involved in formation satisfy applicable diocesan Safe Environment, background screening, and catechetical certification requirements. • Provides functional direction, resources, coaching, and program support to the formation team while collaborating across other parish ministries. • Fosters welcoming and culturally responsive relationships with parishioners and families, including effective ministry in English and Spanish. 
 Pastoral Services and Parish Communication • Coordinates pastoral services in support of the Pastor’s office, including Baptisms, First Holy Communion, Confirmation, weddings, and funerals, in close collaboration and ongoing communication with the Director of Liturgy to ensure proper planning, scheduling, and coordination of liturgical celebrations. • Serves as liaison between the parish and its community partners, and between the Pastor's office and parish ministries and groups. • Ensures timely and professional communication with stakeholders throughout the parish community 
 Catechetical Leadership • Develops goals, objectives, and strategies for a comprehensive catechetical program serving parishioners from Pre-K through adulthood, including preparation for the Sacraments of Initiation, Reconciliation, and Marriage. • Develops and implements a coherent, unified curriculum and catechetical plan for the parish in collaboration with the Pastor, parish staff, formation team, advisory committees, and others. • Directs and oversees catechetical programs that support comprehensive, systematic, and lifelong discipleship in the Catholic faith, in accordance with Sacred Scripture, the Catechism of the Catholic Church (CCC), the Directory for Catechesis (2020), the National Directory for Catechesis (NDC), Church law, diocesan guidelines, and parish needs. • Directs the work of the formation team, provides training, resources, and program support, and develops a yearly schedule for all programs with the team. • Recruits and trains catechists and volunteers and ensures they meet diocesan Safe Environment and certification requirements. • Researches, evaluates, and recommends primary and supplemental catechetical resources and materials.  • Evaluates parish formation programs and makes recommendations to the Pastor. • Serves as a resource in catechetics for the formation team, parish staff, Pastor, and parish community. • Promotes catechetical programs, best practices, and milestones through the parish bulletin, weekly update, website, social media, and other channels. • Promotes catechetical programs, best practices, and milestones through the parish bulletin, weekly updates, website, social media, and other communication channels, in close collaboration with the parish Communications Assistant to ensure consistent, accurate, and timely communication. Records, Budget, and Reporting • Maintains all sacramental records, program registrations, evaluations, and related data. • Prepares the annual catechetical budget for review by the Pastor and parish finance council and manages expenditures within approved parameters. • Develops accurate and reliable statistical measures of the parish's catechetical efforts and submits reports to the Pastor, pastoral council, diocese, or others as required.
 Meetings and Professional Development • Attends and participates in parish staff meetings and facilitates formation staff and committee meetings. • Attends diocesan meetings and events related to catechetical ministry or job responsibilities. • Stays current on diocesan policy and on developments in educational and catechetical practice. • Participates in local and regional professional organizations related to catechetics and prioritizes professional development, including keeping credentials current as a parish catechetical leader in the Diocese of Orlando. • Performs other job-related duties as assigned 









Requirements

 QUALIFICATIONS 

To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily. The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skill, and ability required. Reasonable accommodation may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.


 Catholic Faith 

Must be a practicing Catholic with sufficient knowledge and training in theology, liturgy, and ministry in the Roman Catholic tradition. Church employees must conduct themselves in a manner that is consistent with and supportive of the mission and purpose of the Church. Their public behavior must not violate the faith, morals, or laws of the Church or the policies of the diocese. 


Education and Experience: Required 

• Master’s degree in Theology, Pastoral Studies, Religious Education, Catechetics, or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and experience, consistent with the applicable diocesan catechetical leader classification. 

• Experience as an office supervisor or office manager, including experience with technology-based office management and support.

 • Ministry experience in a parish or diocesan position. Related degrees and comparable experience will be considered.

 • Valid driver's license and the ability to travel as required.

  • Must pass diocesan Safe Environment requirements and background screening.

 • Professional proficiency in both English and Spanish Administrative and Professional Skills 

• Strong organizational skills and attention to detail, with the ability to prioritize and manage multiple tasks, deadlines, and frequent interruptions.

 • Excellent writing skills, including the ability to read and analyze correspondence, compose appropriate responses, and present reports and information clearly.

 • Ability to respond effectively to inquiries from internal and external sources. 

• Ability to define problems, collect data, establish facts, and draw sound conclusions.

 • Proficiency in Microsoft Word and PowerPoint, with working knowledge of Excel and Outlook.

 • Initiative, creativity, and sound judgment in anticipating and resolving problems, including under pressure.
