post_html:
Description

A Learning Community

Notre Dame High School, San Jose is the center for women’s leadership in Silicon Valley and has provided an exceptional Catholic college preparatory education for young women since 1851. The school's mission is guided by the teachings of Saint Julie Billiart, the foundress of the Sisters of Notre Dame de Namur, with a strong focus on social justice to create lifelong learners, spiritual seekers, justice advocates and community leaders.  Our mission, summarized by the words of Saint Julie Billiart, is to “teach them what they need to know for life.”

Summary:

The Director of Mission and Ministry ensures the integration, vibrancy, and sustainability of Notre Dame Catholic identity, Hallmarks, and mission. The director leads initiatives and programs that provide for the ongoing formation to mission for students, families, faculty, staff, board and community members. As the school’s spiritual leader in partnership with the Head of school on mission priorities ensure Notre Dame sustains relationships with the Sisters of Notre Dame de Namur, Catholic, diocesan and interfaith networks.

 

Essential Duties and Responsibilities: Essential responsibilities are primarily job duties that all incumbents must be able to perform without assistance or with some reasonable accommodation made by the employer.

 

Administrative Team

Administrative team member responsibilities:

  • Work collaboratively in a shared leadership model.
  • Center the mission, hallmarks, graduation outcomes, women’s leadership, race equity diversity and inclusion (REDI) in all leadership work.
  • Communicate at weekly team meetings area highlights, changes and future needs to ensure accountability and transparency to the team.
  • Provide strong personnel management, supervision and development opportunities for direct reports, notably the Campus Ministry team staff. Ensure annual performance cycle for staff to motivate growth.
  • Manage horizontally with team members (Director of Teaching and Learning, Director of Co-curriculars, and Director of Student Life) and collaborate on cross area initiatives.
  • Shape big picture perspective with the team for communication, solution-finding, and short- and long-term planning purposes.
  • Model professionalism for and with colleagues.Represent the Administration Team in community communications, particularly in response to significant community, local, national, or global events, ensuring that messaging reflects Notre Dame’s mission, Catholic Social Teaching, and the Hallmarks of a Notre Dame de Namur Learning Community.

 

Pastoral Care

Ensures the spiritual leadership of the faith community and pastoral care of community members.

  • Serves as the pastoral leader of the faith community. Such as but not limited to, spiritual wellness and pastoral care offering
  • Responsible for retreat sequence, sacramental life,and grief/crisis response. 
  • Advises the Head of School and Administrative Team on matters of faith, justice, spiritual development, moral and pastoral concerns, as well as strategies for responses to issues.
  • Ensures the implementation of spiritual wellness and pastoral care offerings.
  • Coordinates with the Administrative Team to provide necessary communication, spiritual companionship, coaching, and support resources for employees and various constituents.
  • Partners with network relationships to provide additional faith and justice resources and support services.
  • Creates proactive plans to respond to community crises which include events pertaining to those on our campus, local/national news, and international events that impact our campus community.

 

Formation to Mission and REDI (Race, Equity, Diversity and Inclusion)

Provides vision, leadership and oversight for the comprehensive mission and REDI formation for Notre Dame students, families and employees

Student Formation & Family Engagement

  • Advises on the vision and alignment of an academic religious studies curriculum to Notre Dame and Catholic standards for religious, intellectual, spiritual, and moral formation.
  • Oversees the vision and effective implementation of campus ministry programs for spirituality, service, and justice that serve a Catholic and multifaith community. Programs include community service learning, liturgy and prayer, interfaith dialogue, mentoring, ongoing spiritual development, social justice advocacy, and student leadership.
  • Partners with the Assistant Head of School, Director of Teaching and Learning, the Director of Student Life, and the Director of Co-curricular Programs to ensure mission-aligned student culture, experiences, curriculum, and programs.

Employee Formation

  • The Director of Mission and Ministry plays a role in the hiring process for mission-critical positions and contributes to the development of hiring practices that ensure alignment with the school’s mission, Catholic identity, and Notre Dame Hallmarks.
  • Partners with the Administrative Team to provide mission-aligned professional development and formation for employees.
    • Oversees the orientation and ongoing formation to the mission, charism, and Catholic identity for all employees in individual, cohort, and community settings. These include annual retreats, mission formation days, prayer and reflection, service and justice activities.
    • Provides support and coaching to faculty & staff as necessary to ensure the visibility of the Hallmarks and the Notre Dame Catholic worldview in the learning community.
    • Collaborates with the East-West Province Sponsorship office to plan and offer formation opportunities for employees.

 

Mission-aligned Connection

Cultivates and maintains key stakeholder relationships with mission and ministry network constituents.

  • Collaborates regularly with the Sisters of Notre Dame de Namur, sponsorship staff, and related Notre Dame Network learning communities and ministries for the promotion of global, national, and regional priorities and programs.
  • Serves as a liaison to Notre Dame Network committees
  • Serves as a liaison to the Bishop, the Diocese of San Jose,the pastor of the Cathedral Basilica of St. Joseph,  and the greater Catholic community.
  • Fosters mutual partnerships with spiritual leaders and the multi faith community for Catholic, interfaith and multicultural engagement.
  • Fosters mutual partnerships with social justice leaders and related organizations for social justice, civic, educational, and community service engagement.
  • Supports formation and engagement efforts with parents/guardians, families, board members, and alumni/graduates of Notre Dame San Jose.

 

Supervises: Mission and Ministry Operations Manager, Campus Minister - Service and Justice, Campus Minister - Spirituality; partners with religious studies faculty

Member of:  Administrative Team, Campus Ministry Team, Mission Integration Committee (Board), Notre Dame Network Committees (ie. Hallmarks Committee)



Qualifications

Minimum Qualifications:

  • Bachelor's degree in Educational Leadership, Divinity, Pastoral Ministry, Religious Studies, or Theology
  • 5-7 years of leadership, administrator or personnel management in a school setting.

 

Desired Knowledge and Abilities:

  • Master's or doctorate degree in Educational Leadership, Divinity, Pastoral Ministry, Religious Studies, or Theology
  • 10-15+ years of experience in school ministry, parish, or youth and young adult evangelization
  • Demonstrated experience in pastoral care, mission formation and integration, interfaith coalition-building, community service programming, and cultural competency through a Catholic lens. 
  • Practicing Catholic in good standing

Benefits:
  • Dental insurance
  • Flexible schedule
  • Vision insurance
  • Wellness resources
Hospice Chaplain / Pastoral Counselor

Location: San Antonio
Employment Type: Part-Time / PRN (Flexible Hours)
Agency: Harmony Hospice Care

Compassion. Dignity. Peace.

At Harmony Hospice Care of San Antonio, we believe spiritual support is a vital part of holistic end-of-life care. We are seeking a compassionate and empathetic Hospice Chaplain / Pastoral Counselor to join our interdisciplinary team and provide meaningful emotional and spiritual support to patients and families during their most vulnerable moments.

Job Summary

As a hospice chaplain, you will provide spiritual counseling and emotional support to terminally ill patients and their families in their homes or care facilities. You will conduct spiritual assessments, facilitate community clergy involvement, and participate in interdisciplinary team meetings to ensure the spiritual component of care is integrated into the patient’s plan of care.

Compensation & Schedule

  •  PRN flexible scheduling available 
  •  Mandatory participation in IDT (Interdisciplinary Team) meetings 
  •  IDT meetings compensated at $35 per hour
  •  Patient visits compensated at $55 per PRN / visit per patient
  •  Additional trip fee paid for each patient visit 
Key Responsibilities

  •  Assess and support patients’ and families’ spiritual and emotional needs 
  •  Provide direct counseling and non-denominational spiritual support 
  •  Coordinate with local clergy or religious communities when requested 
  •  Participate in interdisciplinary team (IDT) meetings 
  •  Maintain accurate and timely documentation in the clinical record and plan of care 
  •  Uphold and promote Harmony’s mission and values of compassionate hospice care 
Qualifications

  • Experience: At least 1 year of experience in spiritual counseling or chaplaincy (healthcare or hospice setting preferred)

Why Join Harmony Hospice Care?

  •  Flexible scheduling options 
  •  Opportunities for growth and continuing education 
  •  Meaningful work that truly impacts patients and families 
  •  Locally owned and community-focused hospice agency 
About Us

Harmony Hospice Care is a small, locally rooted hospice agency proudly serving the San Antonio community. We focus on personalized, compassionate care that honors the dignity of every patient and family. As part of our team, you’ll experience connection, meaning, and purpose in your work every day.

Join us in bringing comfort, presence, and peace to those who need it most.

Flexible work from home options available.

Compensation: $55.00 per hour



At Harmony Hospice, compassion, dignity, and community are at the heart of everything we do. We believe every person deserves to be surrounded by love, respect, and understanding—especially during life’s most meaningful moments. Our care philosophy embraces each individual's unique journey. By truly listening to our patients and their families, we create personalized care plans that reflect their values, honor their wishes, and provide comfort every step of the way.

The United City Residency exists to help men and women discern God’s calling and be equipped for long-term faithfulness in ministry. Program Pathways

Residents receive hands-on ministry experience, weekly training, and intentional mentoring from seasoned church leaders, all while serving and leading within the life of United City Church.

We believe God is calling college students into full-time ministry, and this internship offers a meaningful introduction to what life and leadership in the local church can look like.

Application Process

In this application, you will go through a series of phases:

    • Upon provisional acceptance, you will register for support-raising training run by Reliant to start your support-based ministry journey.

Thank you for your interest in the United City Church Residency or Apprenticeship programs!

HISTORY & CURRENT STATUS


Sugar Creek Baptist Church is on a mission "to love and lead all people to life change in Christ." Over the last 45 years, since it was founded in 1975, the church has seen steady growth as they have pursued this mission. Located in Fort Bend County, the most ethnically diverse county in America, Sugar Creek embraces all people and is known for their missions and care efforts in the community. The congregation is made up of people from diverse ethnicities and political views. All in all, over 90 different countries are represented among Sugar Creek's members.


Senior Pastor Mark Hartman has led this church for the last 18 years. Under his leadership, the church has grown from 1600 in average weekly attendance to 5100 across three campuses. In addition, Sugar Creek has a local and thriving prison ministry as a fourth campus.


Everything that Sugar Creek does is expressed by six core values that guide their decision making and planning on a daily basis. These are:


  1. Truth Matters – the Bible is God’s inspired, inerrant and infallible Word, it is truth for all people.
  2. Total Dependence on God – apart from God we can do nothing.
  3. High Expectation – God is worthy of our best, He deserves our greatest commitment.
  4. Eternal Impact – we seek to make a forever difference in people’s lives.
  5. Mutual Respect – all people matter to God, we treat one another with love and respect.
  6. Generational Relevance – every generation matters to God, we communicate the unchanging message of Christ to an ever-changing world.


Sugar Creek, believes that biblical life change occurs as people commit to four key areas of spiritual development. As they worship, connect, serve, and share on a consistent basis, people experience the life change found in following Jesus.


  1. Worship - The gathering of God’s people to respond to God through inspiring music and relevant teaching/preaching of God’s Word. It calls worshippers to engage in Discipleship.
  2. Connect - Smaller groups of God’s people who come together in biblical community to further explain Bible truth for spiritual transformation while equipping believers to care for one another and to serve the body of Christ.
  3. Serve - Servant teams responding to meet ministry needs within the Body of Christ through grace-based giving of time, abilities, and resources according to their spiritual gifts and passions while learning to demonstrate and declare God’s grace with those who may be far from God. 
  4. Share - Individuals, families and teams of believers declaring and demonstrating the story of redemption everywhere with those who may be far from God; practicing a culture of invitation inviting people into the body life of Sugar Creek Baptist Church.


The life change and spiritual maturity a person experiences as he/she engages in the activities listed above become evidenced as they:


  • Commit to God and their family
  • Help others know God
  • Actively practice spiritual disciplines
  • Nurture authentic relationships
  • Give back to God
  • Exercise spiritual gifts in service


Sugar Creek Baptist Church is a Southern Baptist Church affiliated with the Southern Baptist Convention (http://www.sbc.net). It is important to note that every Southern Baptist Church is unique. Each church is individually governed and led by its staff and its members. For more information about Sugar Creek's core beliefs, please visit: https://sugarcreek.net/beliefs/.



WORSHIP & MINISTRY CONTEXT


Excellence in Worship


Corporate worship at Sugar Creek Baptist Church stands as the heartbeat of their ministry across all campuses. Known throughout Houston for both musical excellence and authentic spiritual engagement, their worship experiences feature confident platform leadership that creates space for genuine encounters with God. Their contemporary approach skillfully bridges cultural relevance with timeless truth—weaving modern musical expressions and creative elements while maintaining an unwavering commitment to the gospel message. In this casual, welcoming environment, worship gatherings come alive through the innovative integration of music, creative arts, and cutting-edge technology that inspires and transforms.


The worship experience at Sugar Creek reflects the rich diversity of their community. Depending on which service you attend, you might encounter anything from a full choir and orchestra to a dynamic worship band or a powerful blend of multiple musical expressions—each creating a unique pathway to encounter God.


Sugar Land Campus Experience


The Sugar Land campus offers four distinctive Sunday worship gatherings:


  • 8:00 AM – Traditional Service featuring beloved hymns and classic expressions of worship
  • 9:30 AM – Contemporary Service with modern worship styles for families and all generations
  • 11:00 AM – Contemporary Service offering the same dynamic worship experience with convenient timing
  • 12:35 PM – Spanish Service celebrating cultural diversity while maintaining the same commitment to engaging worship


Regardless of which service you attend, you'll experience transformative worship, life-changing biblical teaching, and meaningful community connections that make Sugar Creek a spiritual home for people from all walks of life.


Cutting-Edge Technology


Sugar Creek embraces technology to enhance both the worship planning process and the Sunday experience. Their teams utilize Planning Center Online for seamless scheduling and rehearsal preparation. Musicians benefit from state-of-the-art in-ear monitor systems that provide crystal-clear audio while improving the overall sound quality throughout the worship space. This also enables the integration of click tracks and backing elements that elevate the musical experience. During services, high-definition video displays present lyrics and compelling visual content that reinforces the worship and teaching moments.



LEADERSHIP & CULTURE


Collaborative Leadership Structure


Sugar Creek operates with a pastor and staff-led governance model that emphasizes servant leadership at every level. The church's deacon body functions as servant leaders rather than policymakers, working alongside committees, the Senior Pastor, and the Executive Staff to provide wise counsel and support. This collaborative approach creates a balanced leadership environment where multiple voices contribute to the church's vision while maintaining clear direction.


Visionary Senior Leadership


Since 2002, Senior Pastor Dr. Mark Hartman has guided Sugar Creek Baptist Church with wisdom and integrity. A theological conservative with exceptional communication skills, Dr. Hartman leads with an authenticity that extends beyond the pulpit into genuine relationships with staff and congregation alike. His leadership philosophy of "high trust, low fear" empowers those around him through consensus-building rather than micromanagement. Staff members consistently describe him as a godly mentor who listens attentively, encourages growth, and instills vision throughout the organization.


Worship Ministry Leadership


Tony Price serves as the Global Worship Pastor, bringing exceptional relational skills to his role. As a consummate team builder, Tony leads through inspiring vision and collaborative decision-making. While deeply creative, he balances artistic expression with strong organizational abilities and meticulous attention to detail—qualities that create both excellence and stability within the worship ministry.


Healthy Staff Culture


The overall staff culture at Sugar Creek has developed into a healthy, relational environment where team members thrive. This high-functioning staff operates within a relaxed atmosphere that combines professional excellence with genuine community. Staff members experience both the support and freedom necessary to develop their ministries effectively while contributing to the church's broader mission.



CHALLENGE & OPPORTUNITY


The worship ministry at Sugar Creek is globally minded. In other words, those in local ministry at all campuses recognize that they are one part of a larger worship ministry. The worship ministry is part of one church in multiple locations with a desire to cultivate worshipers, expand ministry teams at the campus level, and celebrate the church's diversity. At the heart of it, the worship ministry at Sugar Creek Baptist seeks to serve the mission of the church, "to love and lead all people to life change in Christ."


The Worship Leader/Vocal Ministry Associate will report directly to the Global Worship Pastor, Tony Price, and will serve the Sugar Creek campus as one of the primary worship leaders and by providing support for the vocal ministries on this campus. This person will be involved in planning and leading worship in all of the services at the main campus, directing and providing vocal leadership/coaching to all soloists and praise team members, and the choir. While the ability to direct choir(s), conduct vocal auditions, and lead vocal rehearsals would be beneficial, the church has resources available to cover these responsibilities if the candidate doesn't possess these specific skills. This person should be a team player and serve alongside others in the worship ministry to help accomplish overall ministry goals. 


Leadership Development & Career Path


This position offers significant growth potential, with the opportunity to be promoted to Sugar Land Campus Worship Pastor within 3-4 years. Because of this clear advancement path, candidates should demonstrate strong leadership potential beyond musical abilities. We are seeking someone who can grow into a campus-wide leadership role, with the capacity to cast vision, build teams, and develop other worship leaders. The ideal candidate will show initiative in leadership development, strategic thinking, and the ability to shepherd multiple ministry areas effectively.


While it is not absolutely necessary that this person be an instrumentalist, it would be a significant benefit (particularly, skills as a keyboardist). However, it is important that the new leader has strong platform skills with exceptional vocal ability. The candidate should have an understanding of vocal ministry, even if not serving as the primary vocal director. Sugar Creek Baptist has established a high bar of musical excellence, and this person should have the skills necessary to help them maintain this.


This person should be authentic and relational with their teams and with those in the congregation, seeking to engage with people of diverse backgrounds, ages, and stages of life. Not simply a musician, this person should have the heart of a pastor and worshipper who cares for others and invites them into worship. The candidate should be a team player with an observable love for the Lord, who shepherds others with a heart to develop people and see them thrive.


Sugar Creek represents an opportunity for a talented and gifted leader to work in a growing ministry with exceptional support from a great team in a great community!



LOCATION & DEMOGRAPHIC


Sugar Land, just 20 minutes southwest of Houston, offers an ideal blend of suburban comfort with urban amenities. Since 2008, it has been consistently ranked as one of America's safest cities and recognized as one of "America's Best Places to Live" and a "Community of Respect."


The city boasts exceptional diversity. With a population of approximately 108,515, the most prominent groups are Asian (39.0%), White (36.7%), and Hispanic (12.3%) residents. Nearly 60% of adults hold bachelor's degrees or higher, contributing to a highly educated workforce that attracts premium employers.


Education is a standout feature, with public schools ranking in the top 10% of Texas. Math and reading proficiency scores (61% and 70%) significantly exceed state averages. Both Fort Bend ISD and Lamar CISD serve the area with excellent programs.


Recreation and amenities abound, including 50+ miles of trails, Sugar Land Town Square with global dining and shopping, the Fort Bend Children's Discovery Center, Houston Museum of Natural Science at Sugar Land, Constellation Field (home to minor league baseball), and the Smart Financial Center for world-class entertainment.


The city's thoughtfully designed master-planned communities welcome residents from nearby and worldwide, creating an inclusive atmosphere while maintaining suburban tranquility just minutes from all Houston offers.

With its safe neighborhoods, excellent schools, abundant recreation, and strong community, Sugar Land provides an exceptional quality of life for all ages—truly earning its reputation as "The Sweetest City in Texas."

Parish Name: Our Lady of Guadalupe Parish

Our Lady of Guadalupe seeks an individual who exudes excitement for their Catholic faith and has charisma to work with our mostly Latino/a youth population. This youth minister will work closely with a team of volunteers to plan, develop, implement, and evaluate a bilingual program of faith formation to prepare high school age youth for the sacrament of Confirmation. Additionally, this minister will offer activities and programs which attract and support youth in the parish.


Primary Duties and Responsibilities

  • Recruits, develops, and manages a core team to minister to the junior high and high school youth of the parish and who will develop and run the youth ministry program: Youth Group, Laudato Si Group, meetings, retreats, youth choir, socials, field trips, game nights, beach outings, etc.
  • Works collaboratively with the Director of Faith Formation so that the catechetical programs in the Confirmation program are consistent in spirit and content with those of Catechesis Familiar and OCIA, with a goal of establishing a whole life faith formation. This person also works to help with catechetical formation of parents of confirmation students.
  • Advocates and fosters involvement of youth in the life of the parish, including serving on various parish committees, participating in liturgies, giving testimonies at masses, and participating in other parish events.
  • Recruits and trains volunteers needed for programs: assistants, substitutes, team members, facilitators, sponsors. Conducts periodic meetings with this team of volunteers.
  • Collaborates with SDOP and the Jesuits West Province in promoting and supporting youth community organizing. Helps our youth participate in Advocacy Day, Camp Ignite, and the Ignatian Family Teach-in.
  • Plans and coordinates youth masses and the confirmation liturgy, in coordination with the pastoral liturgical team of the parish.
  • Serves as administrator and record-keeper of registration materials, attendance records, and baptismal certificates.
  • Ensures all volunteers have Safe Environment training and background checks. Monitors safety of youth. Makes presentations of Safe Environment programs to youth.
  • Takes responsibility for finances of youth ministries by preparing an annual budget, keeping track of expenditures, sponsoring fundraisers, making deposits and check requests, paying bills, etc., in conformity with diocesan financial practices.
  • Attends parish staff meetings.
  • With input and guidance from the pastor, establishes SMART goals, and through regular one-on-one meetings with pastor, provides updates on progress.
  • Ensures that the parish community is informed of Confirmation and Youth Ministry events, programs, etc., through various channels of communication including parish bulletin, website, and social media.

  • Ability to work in a face-paced and ever-changing environment, responding to pastoral needs as they arise.
  • Performs other duties as required.
Requirements


Background, Education and Experience

  • Must have a dynamic personality and vibrant faith as a practicing Catholic. Must regularly participate in the sacramental life of the Church.
  • Must be familiar with Church documents and teaching related to Catechesis and Evangelization. In particular, must be familiar with and a proponent of the values espoused in Laudato Si, Pope Francis’ encyclical on the environment.
  • Must exercise synodality, that spirit of listening and learning, which is so important in our Church today.
  • Must be fluent in Spanish and English in spoken and written language and be able to relate to Mexican and Latino culture along with a diversity of cultures and groups.
  • Bachelor’s degree or youth ministry certificate and/or experience in the field.
  • Must have strong organizational skills, including time management, delegation, planning, budgeting, and the ability to balance multiple projects at one time.
  • Be highly motivated, a self-starter, creative, and energetic. Ability to network with a variety of persons and groups within and outside of the parish.
  • Proficient in technology, using MS Office products, email, and a variety of technology. Experience in social media and creation of creative marketing materials.

Physical Demands

While performing the duties of this job the employee is regularly required to remain in an office at a computer workstation and access information from a computer and use a telephone. The employee is required to be mobile to, from, and within the office, as well as maneuver throughout the parish facility to attend meetings, briefings, and other work-related events. The employee may be required to conduct trips to, from, and within various city and county-wide locations to attend meetings or events. The employee must occasionally lift and/or move up to 15 pounds. The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.


Please note this position description is not designed to cover or contain a comprehensive listing of activities, duties or responsibilities that are required of the employee for this job. Duties, responsibilities and activities may change at any time with or without notice.

Program Summary

The Ministry Internship Program is offered to qualified male and female candidates who have discerned a call to ministry and who are pursuing a degree from an accredited seminary. The purpose of the program is to help students grow spiritually and clarify their sense of call while worshipping and serving in the local church.


The internship is designed so that students receive a substantial amount of relational and spiritual support from the congregation and its members while also gaining extensive experience in ministry.We anticipate that some Ministry Interns will in the future serve the Church as senior, associate or assistant pastors or as ministry directors, and many will become excellent candidates for future positions at any one of the churches in the growing Resound network.

 

  • Work full time at the local church for a renewable one-year period in supervised ministry in a specific area, such as Community Groups, Pastoral Care, Young Professionals, College Ministry, Youth Ministry, Children’s Ministry, Church Administration, or Mission and Evangelism;
  • Pursue an advanced degree such as a Master of Arts or a Master of Divinity through an accredited seminary;
  • Participate in a series of modules focused on leadership, preaching, mission, pastoral care, cultural dynamics, and church renewal;
  • Receive a monthly stipend and scholarship for seminary.


Application

To apply for the Ministry Internship Program, we invite you to write four essays, with each essay no more than 1,000 words in content. The essays are to be in response to these four prompts/questions:

  • Describe your experience as a follower of Jesus, including the most significant spiritual events and influences in your life.
  • In what ways has God gifted you for ministry, and what ministry experiences have confirmed your sense of call up to this point?
  • Please give some examples of how you have navigated hardships and challenges in your life and ministry to this point.
  • Describe your desire to participate in Resound and your sense of how you must grow and mature to become more effective as a ministry leader.


In addition, please provide:

  • a resume which lists your educational background and work experience
  • an official transcript from college and seminary
  • two letters of reference, preferably one from a professor and one from a church leader.



The application deadline for the Resound internship cohort commencing in September 2026 is May 1st, 2026.

The youth ministry is a disciple-making ministry for youth. The youth leader will develop a ministry to win, build, equip, multiply leaders, and send students to reach others. The youth ministry will be consistent with the beliefs, values, and mission of Florence Alliance Church.

Anticipated Time Commitments

Doing ministry/preparing for ministry: 20 hours per week. (Part-time)

Accountability/Mentoring

The youth leader is accountable to the Governing Board for the duties, goals and mission of the youth ministry. The youth leader will report directly to the pastor as the representative of the Governing Board.
The youth leader will work to maintain a spirit of cooperation with other staff, volunteers, the congregation, and parents of the youth.
The pastor and youth leader will meet regularly for prayer, mutual support, encouragement, and guidance.
In addition, the youth leader will network with other youth leader(s) and/or seek out mentoring by an older youth leader.
The initial agreement is for 6 months. Subsequent agreements will be for one year. Near the end of the agreed upon period, the Sr. Pastor will meet with the Youth Leader to give an evaluation and to receive feed back from the Youth Leader. The Board will then decide whether to extend another offer.
Responsibilities

The first responsibility of any disciplemaker is to maintain a close relationship with the Lord. A deepening knowledge of Christ, prayerful dependence on God, and the infilling of the Holy Spirit are necessary characteristics for the servant-leader.
Relationships are key to effective youth ministry. The youth leader will build healthy relationships with the students as a foundation for the ministry.
The youth leader will also develop a good rapport with the parents of the students. Frequent communication is a key component.
He/she will develop and implement a strategic plan for effective ministry to students.
He/she will develop a ministry team with parents and other volunteers.
Because evangelism is a high value, the youth ministry will reach youth outside our church.
The youth leader will equip students to share their faith and to serve the needs of others. Plan opportunities for service to the community/others.
Develop a small group ministry as the core component of the disciplemaking process.
Occasional preaching opportunities and other pastoral duties may be assigned.
Support

The Board will assign an Elder to be a mentor to the youth leader. This is apart from interaction with the pastor. This is for prayer and spiritual support.
Meet with the Pastor as a staff person for encouragement and accountability as often as is deemed prudent (i.e. every other week).
Assign a committee of interested adults/parents. This committee will meet with the youth leader once-a-month (frequency is negotiable). This group will act as a planning team so the youth leader may bounce ideas off of them and receive feedback, encouragement, and support. This is in addition to the youth ministry team.


Feel free to contact the pastor - leadpastor@florencealliance.org with any questions.

To be considered for this position, please complete the application to include your testimony, resume and other background information related to the position.

If the district office has reviewed your application and they think you may be a potential match for the position, that the hiring manager will reach out to you for next steps.

This position may require licensing with The Christian & Missionary Alliance. To learn more about The Alliance and requirements for licensing, please visit our website

Company Description

The mission of Christ’s Church of the Valley is to win people to Jesus Christ, train believers to become disciples, and send disciples to impact the world. The Students Ministry supports the mission of CCV by shaping students to become Christ-centered difference makers. The Students Pastor will assist pastoring Junior and Senior High students through recruiting, training, and retaining youth coaches, as well as implementing Junior and Senior High school programs and events. The Students Pastor will also assist in growing the campus in all areas numerically such as attendance, coaches, and baptisms. 

Job Description

Essential Job Functions 

  • Execute Junior and Senior High events and programs 
  • Cast the overall CCV & Students Ministry vision with parents and volunteers 
  • Provide pastoral care for families and coaches 
  • Recruit, train, and retain volunteers for all weekend areas and events 
  • Develop and maintain school campus involvement 
  • Following up with first time students 
  • Collect and report accurate weekly attendance according to established standards and deadlines 
  • Work with the team to plan and execute various church-wide events. These may include, but are not limited to: 
    • Kick off events 
    • Easter 
    • Christmas Eve 

Qualifications

Minimum Qualifications 

CHARACTER & CHEMISTRY 

Alignment with our CORE Values & Staff Fundamentals 

  • Commitment to Excellence – We bring our best, every time. Excellence honors God and moves people. 
  • Heart for Evangelism – We will risk it all to reach one more. Jesus’ last command is our priority. 
  • Radical Generosity – We steward all things with open hands. The God who owns it all, gave it all.  
  • Integrity – We commit to zero gap between what we say and do. Jesus modeled integrity in EVERYTHING.

Agreement with our CORE Commitments

  • Must regularly ATTEND WORSHIP with their family 
  • Must be an active participant in a CCV Group and consistently tithe

Fully engaged (or willingness to) in CCV Next Steps:

Education and Experience

Additional Information

All your information will be kept confidential according to EEO guidelines.

General Information

The above statements are intended to describe the general nature and level of work being performed by individuals assigned to this position. They are not intended to be an exhaustive list of all duties, responsibilities, and skills required of employees. CCV Leadership reserves the right to revise the position, its job functions, minimum qualifications and other aspects of the position in any way at any time.

Executive Pastor - Alexandria Covenant Church

Executive Pastor Role Description

PURPOSE:

The Executive Pastor will work directly with the Senior Pastor to provide ministry and staff oversight to all Director and Pastoral staff positions. This person is responsible for implementation of churchwide ministry objectives and the care and development of ministry directors and pastoral staff. The Executive Pastor will serve on the Executive Ministry Team led by the Senior Pastor.

            I.          POSITION TITLE:

                        Executive Pastor

            II.        REQUIREMENTS:

  • Be born-again and living a dedicated Christian life.
  • Possess spiritual gifts, along with the professional and educational background adequate for the position.
  • Possess the ability to implement the vision, mission, and values of ACC under the direction of the Senior Pastor and the Leadership Team of the church.
  • Be licensed or ordained in the Evangelical Covenant Church or other accepted ministry credentials.
  • Ability to work with confidentiality and discretion.
  • Ability to work independently, under pressure, and with multiple people on staff.
  • Excellent verbal and interpersonal skills.
  • Be a member at Alexandria Covenant Church.

  

III.       RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Will provide oversight, care, and development of all Ministry Director and Pastoral Staff positions.
  • Will serve as a member of the Executive Ministry Team.
  • Responsible for the implementation of churchwide ministry objectives.
  • Oversight of local mission ministry in cooperation with Executive Team and Local Mission Team.
  • Oversight of churchwide community engagement.
  • Assist the Senior Pastor in preaching and teaching the Word of God, administering the sacraments, and faithfully carrying out pastoral work as needed.
  • Serve as an advisory member of the Leadership Team. May serve as a voting member of ministry teams and committees, and in such capacity shall strive to establish and accomplish objectives and strategies in conjunction with the mission and purpose of the church.

 

IV.       AUTHORITY:

The Executive Pastor shall have authority to perform duties in accordance with their role description and under the direction of the Senior Pastor.

V.        ACCOUNTABILITY:

The Executive Pastor is accountable to the Senior Pastor.

 

VI.       STANDARDS FOR PERFORMANCE:

  • The Executive Pastor shall conduct themselves at all times in such a manner as set forth in the Word of God for a servant of God.
  • The Executive Pastor will accomplish their duties and responsibilities in a professional manner and should demonstrate, along with the fruit of the Spirit, excellence, integrity, loyalty, and maturity.

 

VII.     EVALUATION:

Yearly, the Executive Pastor will meet with the Senior Pastor for a job performance evaluation.  Goals will be set together for the coming year, the results to be evaluated at the next performance appraisal.

...................

This position requires 15+ years of experience in overseeing church multiple staff teams

...................

Alexandria Covenant Church is seeking a full-time Executive who loves Jesus and is committed to the work and ministry of the gospel.  We are a church of 1000+ regularly attending on Sunday mornings with another 300+ viewing our online services. Our church family is committed to loving Jesus, becoming like Jesus, and sharing Jesus with all people. 

 Our church offers both traditional and contemporary weekly worship services.  All our ministries are bible based, gospel centered, and relationally driven and our largest outreach is children and youth.  In addition, we have 14 global, 5 regional and 13 local missions’ partners.  Alexandria Covenant Church is debt free and operates on a 2 ½+ -million-dollar budget, but we recognize the greatest asset of our church is our people. 

 Alexandria, MN is a lakes community (15,000+ and triples in size in the summer) located in central Minnesota.  We are a summer destination for many people in and outside of Minnesota.  It is often said about Alexandria that it is a great place to come and a hard place to leave.  Our church and our community are unique - we are a larger church family in a relatively small rural setting.  If looking for a great place to live and an amazing church family to experience life with, we may be that place for you!

Associate Director of High School Ministry – Grades 9-12


Department:                        Next Gen Ministry

Direct Supervisor of:           N/A

Tier:                                      Implementation Tier

Work Schedule:                   Sunday - Thursday


Our vision: leading all generations to find and follow Jesus for the flourishing of our city and beyond


PURPOSE OF THIS POSITION

The Next Gen Department seeks to advance and support this vision through proclaiming the Gospel, equipping and resourcing families for life and godliness, and discipling the next generation of believers to be Christ followers.


The Associate Director of High School Ministry will co-lead and support a dynamic and impactful ministry for students in 9th - 12th grade. 


This role prioritizes relational discipleship, engaging programming, transformational trips and events, and collaboration with the Next Gen Team to ensure cohesion and create a thriving ministry environment that meets the unique needs of high school students.


This role requires an outgoing, passionate, creative leader committed to fostering spiritual growth, biblical understanding, and personal development in students during this pivotal stage of their faith journey. The Associate Director of High School Ministry will execute ministry programming, support volunteer leaders, and implement the vision and strategy of High School Ministry to foster a culture where students encounter Christ, grow in their faith, and actively engage in the life of the church. This leader demonstrates consistent relational presence and proactive engagement with students, encouraging them to find and follow Jesus.

The Associate Director of High School Ministry reports to the Pastor of High School Ministry and partners with volunteers, parents, and the broader Next Gen Team to ensure families experience consistent discipleship and community throughout their high school years.

 

DESIRED RESULTS/IMPACT OF THIS POSITION

Relational Discipleship: Students experience consistent relational care and discipleship through meaningful connections with leaders and peers. This is evidenced by:

  • Consistent engagement with Scripture, prayer, worship, and spiritual habits.
  • Growing ability to articulate biblical beliefs, ask thoughtful questions, and model faith in word and deed.
  • Development of healthy, Christ-centered relationships with peers and adult mentors.

Engaging Ministry Environments: Weekly gatherings create welcoming and spiritually formative environments for high school students. This is evidenced by:

  • Programs that are organized, engaging, and developmentally appropriate.
  • Students actively participating in worship, teaching, and small group discussions.
  • New students and guests are welcomed and integrated into the ministry community.

Transformational Events: Retreats, mission trips, service projects, and seasonal events contribute to long-term faith formation. This is evidenced by:

  • Increased student participation in retreats, events, and service opportunities.
  • Service experiences that cultivate compassion, missional awareness, and alignment with church mission partners.
  • Seniors graduate with demonstrated spiritual ownership, consistent spiritual habits, and clarity about next steps in church involvement as they transition into adulthood.

Volunteer Support & Recruitment: Volunteers are equipped, valued, and supported. This is evidenced by:

  • A fully staffed and reliable roster of small group leaders and ministry volunteers.
  • Clear expectations, regular training, and intentional leadership development.
  • A volunteer culture marked by joy, unity, and shared ownership of ministry outcomes.


KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

Relational Ministry & Outreach

  • Cultivate meaningful relationships with students through consistent presence and intentional engagement both inside and outside of the church.
  • Maintain a regular rhythm of student contact work outside of formal programming.
  • Partner with local schools, community organizations, and parachurch ministries to expand ministry reach.

Volunteer-Driven Ministry Development

  • Help recruit, train, and equip volunteers to lead small groups, mentor students, and facilitate events.
  • Provide encouragement, communication, and support for volunteers.
  • Assist with volunteer scheduling and coordination for weekly programming and events.  

Teaching & Programming

  • Assist in planning and executing weekly High School Ministry gatherings with biblically sound and developmentally appropriate teaching.
  • Help create engaging environments that integrate worship, teaching, games, and small group discussion.
  • Support the planning and execution of retreats, trips, and seasonal ministry events.

Ministry Administration & Organization-in partnership with Department Coordinator

  • Assist in maintaining ministry calendars and event planning.
  • Support registration, attendance tracking, and ministry logistics.
  • Help ensure compliance with child protection and safe ministry policies.


EDUCATION, EXPERIENCE, SKILL, ABILITY REQUIREMENTS

  • Spiritual & Theological: A deep love for Jesus, a clear calling to student ministry, and a commitment to ECO theology.·
  • Education: Bachelor’s Degree preferred.
  • Experience: 1-2 years of experience in Children’s or Student Ministry or related field, preferred but not required.
  • Skills: Relational discipleship, effective teaching,
    Microsoft office, relentless pursuit of students
  • Abilities: Frequent lifting under 30 lbs.; ability to maintain composure under pressure.


WORKPLACE EXPECTATIONS

  • Loves Jesus, the people of HP Pres, the city of Dallas and the world
  • Acts as an advocate of the culture and vision of HP Pres
  • Commits to and exhibits our Team Culture Values:
    • Deeply abiding in Jesus
    • We > Me
    • Defiant joy in the trenches of ministry

Contemporary Worship Apprentice

The Contemporary Worship Apprenticeship is a year long, hands on development opportunity for an emerging worship leader who already has experience leading worship and wants to accelerate their growth into a highly capable, well rounded contemporary worship leader. The apprentice will work alongside experienced worship leaders at Highland Park United Methodist Church, receiving intentional coaching and mentorship while gaining practical experience across HPUMC’s contemporary worshiping communities. The apprenticeship develops the apprentice beyond leading songs to understanding and leading the entire worship experience, including worship planning, musical direction, team leadership, production, worship technology, theology of worship, and ministry leadership.

Reports To: Contemporary Worship Leader

Ministrial Exemption: Yes

FLSA Status: No

Campus: Mockingbird, with ministry opportunities across HPUMC worshiping communities

Working Hours: This is a Part Time position that will work an anticipated 8 to 10 hours per week during the school year.

Anticipated Schedule: Schedule will vary based on worship and ministry opportunities and may include Sunday mornings; weekday or evening rehearsals; worship planning and mentorship meetings; religious holidays and special worship services; and occasional ministry events and special projects.

During certain times of the year additional hours may be necessary to meet the demands of the job. All church staff will be asked to support and serve for religious holidays and worship services including Christmas Eve and Easter. Presence on occasional Sundays is also requested to ensure that one has the firsthand understanding of the church culture.

Job Responsibilities and Duties:

Worship Leadership & Planning

• Lead worship vocally and instrumentally in a variety of contemporary worship environments.

• Participate in the planning and preparation of worship services.

• Develop thoughtful song selections, service flow, transitions, and creative worship elements.

• Learn to take a worship opportunity from idea to execution.

• Collaborate with pastors and ministry leaders to support the larger purpose and direction of worship.

• Develop the ability to lead effectively with a full band, smaller team, or as a solo worship leader.

• Assume increasing ownership of complete worship experiences as skills and readiness develop.

Musical & Team Leadership

• Prepare arrangements, charts, tracks, transitions, and other musical resources.

• Develop skills in musical direction and rehearsal leadership.

• Learn to prepare and lead musicians with clarity and confidence.

• Communicate effectively with musicians and volunteers.

• Develop healthy, encouraging, and spiritually meaningful team culture.

• Grow in the ability to recruit, equip, encourage, and develop other worship leaders and musicians.

• Learn how to respond effectively when plans change, musicians become unavailable, or other unexpected challenges arise.

Worship Production & Technology

• Gain hands on experience with ProPresenter and other worship planning and presentation tools.

• Develop a working understanding of audio, lighting, stage setup, presentation, and other production elements.

• Learn how to effectively communicate and collaborate with production staff and volunteers.

• Prepare the technical and production elements necessary for worship.

• Understand how musical, visual, and technical decisions work together to support a cohesive worship experience.

• Develop the ability to troubleshoot common worship and production challenges.

Theology, Spiritual Formation & Ministry Leadership

• Explore the biblical and theological foundations of Christian worship.

• Develop the ability to articulate what worship is, why the Church worships, and the responsibility of the worship leader.

• Learn how theology informs practical decisions about songs, Scripture, prayer, liturgy, creativity, and service planning.

• Grow in spiritual maturity and personal worship.

• Develop pastoral awareness and learn to lead people, not simply music.

• Grow in preparation, organization, communication, collaboration, and other less visible aspects of ministry leadership.

• Receive regular mentorship, coaching, and feedback.

Increasing Leadership Responsibility

• Move from learning and serving alongside experienced leaders into increasing levels of independent leadership.

• As readiness is demonstrated, plan worship, build arrangements, lead rehearsals, coordinate teams, prepare production elements, solve unexpected challenges, and take responsibility for complete worship experiences.

• Develop an understanding not only of how to lead from the platform, but why worship leaders lead, what they are inviting people into, and how to bring a worship experience from idea to execution.

Capstone Project

• Near the conclusion of the apprenticeship, conceive, develop, and lead an original worship focused project or experience.

• Identify an opportunity, develop the vision, build the necessary team and resources, work through theological, creative, technical, and logistical considerations, and bring the idea to life.

• Use the capstone to demonstrate not simply what has been learned, but what the apprentice is now capable of leading.

Other duties as assigned. Changes to job may occur at any time and without notice.

Education and Desired Skills:

• Previous experience leading worship in a church or ministry environment.

• Demonstrated ability as a vocalist and instrumentalist.

• Comfortable leading worship from the platform.

• Desire and potential to develop into an exceptional contemporary worship leader.

• Curiosity about worship beyond its musical elements and a desire to deepen understanding of Christian worship.

• Highly teachable and receptive to coaching, feedback, and mentorship.

• Commitment to preparation, excellence, and reliability.

• Demonstrates humility, creativity, curiosity, and initiative.

• Strong relational and communication skills.

• Ability to work collaboratively with musicians, volunteers, pastors, ministry leaders, and production teams.

• Desire to care for and develop people as well as pursue musical excellence.

• Willingness to learn and serve in a variety of contemporary worship environments.

• Alignment with the mission, theology, and ministry values of Highland Park United Methodist Church.

Candidates are not expected to enter the apprenticeship with experience in every area described above. The ideal candidate brings an existing foundation in worship leadership along with the talent, character, curiosity, and drive to grow quickly through intentional investment and meaningful ministry experience.

Preferred Software Experience:

• ProPresenter

• Planning Center

• Ableton Live or similar playback software

• Creating or editing chord charts and arrangements

• Leading or directing a worship band

• Basic audio and production systems

• Contemporary worship service planning

Physical Demands:

Sitting Standing Walking Seeing Hearing Speaking Fine Motor Skills

Other Qualifications:

Must be a Christian committed to living a life that reflects the Gospel, who feels called to the ministry of the church, and is comfortable working in a United Methodist Church environment. Additionally, employees are expected to follow church policies, lead lives that embody the Gospel, and exhibit an appropriate demeanor both on and off the job.

We’re excited that you are considering joining us at Cypress Church through Reliant! Reliant is a faith-based nonprofit that partners with missional churches and Gospel-centered nonprofits to mobilize support-based missionaries for the Great Commission. Through Reliant, we provide missionaries with the resources, training, and support needed to thrive in their calling, including the critical process of raising financial and prayer support. Here are a couple of quick thoughts to help you through the assessment process:

  5. Reliant Review - Reliant will review all the pieces of your application and create a summary to discuss with your local church.

Note: Once you begin a questionnaire within a stage, you will need to complete that stage fully. You are not able to save within a stage. Please set aside ample time to complete each stage.

Reports to: 

Co-Directors of People Care and Formation

Works closely with:  People Care and Formation Team, Regional Advancement Leaders, HR

Direct Reports:
Young Adult Leader

Position Type: 
Part-Time; Support-Funded

Hours Per Week:
3-5

Location:

Remote work engagement


Position Scope:

This position is responsible for the development and implementation of pastoral services, resources, and support initiatives for missionary families and their children (Missionary Kids (MKs) and Third Culture Kids (TCKs)). The role supports the global responsibilities of People Care and Spiritual Formation within assigned areas of responsibility, with a focus on helping fulfill the mission God has entrusted to Communitas.

This position works collaboratively with the People Care and Formation (PCF) Team to cultivate Communitas’ values and mutual expectations, promoting the health and flourishing of individuals, families, and teams. It provides pastoral care and support to Communitas personnel through coaching, mentoring, care, or processing. 


Principal Duties & Responsibilities:

  • Conduct field visits with staff families and MKs, when possible, to provide developmental support, pastoral care, and encouragement. When direct visits are not feasible, coordinate with trusted and vetted third-party organizations to provide appropriate care and support.
  • Serve as a trusted and approachable resource for staff and families by providing a safe space for processing personal, family, and life-related challenges, while recognizing when additional professional support or referral is needed.
  • Provide opportunities for learning regarding TCKs within Communitas.
  • Collaborate with the People Care and Formation (PCF) Team in developing systems, resources, and policies that promote the holistic well-being of staff, with a particular focus on missionary families and MKs.
  • Participate annually in at least one regional Connect event and/or Leadership Summit.
  • Maintain regular communication with the Co-Director of PCF through monthly check-ins.


Family Pastor System Development Responsibilities:

  • Research current best practices and strategies related to MK and TCK care.
  • Seek input and feedback from Communitas staff and MKs to identify and understand the unique needs of missionary families and children within the Communitas community.
  • Provide vision and strategic planning for MK care within Communitas.
  • Recruit advisors, caregivers, and ministry partners who can contribute to the ongoing care and support of Communitas families and MKs.
  • Advocate for developing healthy self-care systems for MKs and missionary families.
  • Develop sustainable processes and systems that promote ongoing awareness, engagement, and care for MKs while empowering families to build and utilize their own support networks.

We’re excited that you are considering joining us at Awaken Church through Reliant! Reliant is a faith-based nonprofit that partners with missional churches and Gospel-centered nonprofits to mobilize support-based missionaries for the Great Commission. Through Reliant, we provide missionaries with the resources, training, and support needed to thrive in their calling, including the critical process of raising financial and prayer support. Whether you're pursuing a short-term internship, a long-term residency, or a career in ministry, we are here to support and guide you every step of the way.

Here are a couple of quick thoughts to help you through the assessment process:

In this application, you will go through a series of stages:

  1. Application - This is the initial application for Reliant.
  2. Ministry Assessment - This assesses your readiness for your ministry role.
  3. Moral Conduct - This assesses your emotional and character-based readiness for a role in ministry.
  4. Local Interview - In this phase, you will do an interview with your church leadership.
  5. Reliant Review - Reliant will review all the pieces of your application and create a summary to discuss with your local church.
  6. Decision/Discernment - Reliant and your church will come together to make an employment decision.
  7. Provisionally Accepted - If you are accepted onto staff, you will have the opportunity to accept your offer, if desired.
  8. Onboarding - This will include online (and potentially in-person) training and HR paperwork. This is designed to prepare you to become a Reliant employee, as well as ready you to raise financial support.

Note: Once you begin a questionnaire within a stage, you will need to complete that stage fully. You are not able to save within a stage. Please set aside ample time to complete each stage.

When you are ready, click on the "Apply to a Position" button to get started.

The Vietnamese Alliance Fellowship is seeking a bi-vocational pastor for a house church located in a development zone of Erie. General Description:

The individuals in this position are responsible for day-to-day cleaning, setting up and breaking down all

events, opening and/or closing of Church and School facilities. It is the responsibility of the Custodian to

ensure that the facilities are cleaned and sanitized in a condition of operating excellence, cleanliness, and

safety. Whereas, safety, cleanliness, and continued efficiency of operation shall be a major goal at all

times. The successful candidates carry out these functions in a helpful and cheerful manner to all who

enter or contact the Church and School, while meeting the needs of staff, guests, volunteers, and

congregants, and learners.


Essential Job Functions

The custodian is a part-time position reporting to Facilities Coordinator. The custodian will maintain

tasks as listed below as a summary of specific job responsibilities on a daily basis:

• Cleaning of glass doors and windows.

• Vacuuming of all carpeted areas of the Church.

• Cleaning and sanitizing all restrooms.

• Replenishing supplies in restrooms (bath tissue, soap, hand towels).

• Clean floors in kitchen.

• Emptying trash receptacles throughout the building.

• Dusting and wiping walls.

• Sweeping and mopping floors.

• Polishing brass rails.

• Spot cleaning pew cushions and carpets (as necessary).

• Sweep exterior walkways, pick up paper and trash.

• Other related duties as assigned.

• Respond to immediate cleaning requirements during their scheduled work shift.

• Set- up furniture and equipment in meeting spaces for use by ministries.

• Assisting church members with special events, i.e. unloading and loading vehicles.

• Reporting all accidents and injuries.

• Locking and securing the building at the close of hours of operation, to include assuring the

building is clear of guests, locking all windows and entryways, gated parking lots, and initiating

the security system before leaving the building.

• Maintains and monitors inventory of cleaning supplies and notifies Facilities Coordinator so that

orders may be placed.


The above summary of duties represents the major tasks and duties. This is not intended to be an

exhaustive list of all responsibilities. Therefore, this person may perform other related tasks under the

direction of the Campus Support Manager.


Benefits for Part Time Positions:

Cell Phone Stipend $75/month

Requirements

Ongoing Expectations

All Crossroads Church staff and their spouses are required to consider Crossroads Church their

church home.

• Champion Crossroads’ values by engaging in a lifestyle of Christ, Cause, and Community

• Live out Crossroads’ Behavioral Standards in relationships with other staff, congregation and

community.

• Work with each staff member on your team to maintain a balanced work schedule, working with

Crossroads’ HR Team to keep track of vacation days, sick days, days off, make-up days, etc.

• Serve at All-Hands on Deck Holiday and Special Events (e.g. Easter, Christmas, TNT etc.).

• Maintain flexible working schedule as determined by the needs of the ministry.


Education and Experience

• The Custodian must have experience in commercial cleaning and the proper use of cleaning

methods, materials, and equipment.

• Proficiency in reading, speaking, and writing English language.

• Standard cleaning procedures, for chemicals, products, and equipment

• One to three years related experience and/or training or equivalent combination of education and

experience.

• Hazardous material information system

• Ability to read and understand labels and instructions, particularly on the use and application of

cleaning chemicals and products.

• Must show attention to detail and ability to work independently with little supervision

• Problem solving

• Time management


Physical Demands

The custodian position is physically demanding. The custodian must spend the entire time at work

standing, walking, lifting, operating medium weight cleaning equipment such as floor buffers; sweeping

and mopping floors and moving furniture and emptying and carrying trash bags and other disposable

materials to the outside receptacles, climbing stairs and ladders, stooping, crouching kneeling and

pushing. The custodian is required to do a great deal of stretching and bending, often in awkward

positions. The position requires the successful candidate to be able to lift up to 70lbs and to be able to

manipulate chairs, 6 ft tables and other furniture without assistance.

$16.90/hour

post_html:
Campus Staff Minister I – UF/North Florida (Undergraduate Ministry)

Work Location:

Florida

Job Type:

Full time

God has called InterVarsity to plant and to build witnessing communities of students and faculty who follow Jesus on college and university campuses. Through these groups, we believe ever- increasing numbers of students and faculty from all ethnic groups and areas of the campus will be transformed by the Gospel. We expect to see campuses increasingly become places where people, ideas, and structures flourish to the glory of God. We confidently anticipate that our InterVarsity alumni will become change agents across the country and around the world. We pursue this calling by discerning and actively participating in what God is already doing on campus. This is the essence of being a Campus Staff Minister (CSM).

We are looking for a Campus Staff Minister who can gather a thriving community of students in a campus environment full of competing options. Ideally, this CSM will be able to engage UF's diverse student body — across ethnicities and cultures, majors and career tracks, and a wide range of interests and backgrounds — building genuine connection wherever students are.

UF presents its own distinct ministry challenge and opportunity: as a flagship research university with more than 60,000 students in the classic college town of Gainesville, it offers a large and energetic mission field shaped by strong school spirit, packed schedules, and a culture where students often measure their time by labs, internships, and career-building. A CSM here will need to compete not just with other ministries but with a campus rhythm that prizes achievement and involvement, finding ways to invite students into deeper community amid packed academic and extracurricular calendars. UF's student body is also broad and varied, meaning an effective CSM must be able to connect across difference rather than defaulting to a single cultural mode of ministry. And because Gainesville's identity is so tightly bound to the university itself, this role calls for someone who can help students see their faith as central to who they are as Gators, not just one more activity competing for their attention.

ESSENTIAL COMMITMENTS/RESPONSIBILITIES 

Spiritual Growth 

As a Campus Staff Minister, you pursue maturity as a disciple of Jesus Christ so that your life and work increasingly reflect a growing love for God, God’s Word, God’s people of every ethnicity and culture, and God’s purposes in the world. To do this, you will: 

  • Pursue a vibrant relationship with the triune God through engagement with Scripture, prayer, and worship, both individually and in community 

  • Develop self-leadership (growing in self-awareness, self-management, relational integrity, and resiliency)

  • Embrace Scriptural standards for behavior and attitudes 

 

Campus Leadership 

As a Campus Staff Minister, you increase the number of witnessing communities, as well as the size, health, spiritual maturity, and campus-wide influence of existing witnessing communities of students and faculty by being a: 

  • Visionary Guide: 

You communicate and model InterVarsity’s vision to see students and faculty transformed, campuses renewed, and world changers developed 

  • Create a culture of humble dependence on God and bold expectation in God’s intention to start new witnessing communities throughout the campus and on new campuses

  • Model – in person and through programs – InterVarsity’s vision and Core Values, including a biblically-defined commitment to engage every ethnic and social group on campus

  • Lead students and faculty – individually and collectively – through Scripture, prayer, teaching, and discipleship experiences, so that they articulate and align their ministry activities around this vision

  • Set annual goals through prayer, research and reflection with your teams (students, faculty, and staff) for qualitative and quantitative growth, including conversions and leadership development 

  • Structural Architect: 

You create, develop, align, and leverage ministry plans, programs, teams, and structures to close the gap between current reality and the aspirational goals. 

  • Build leadership teams who trust and partner well with you and who demonstrate spiritual vitality, relational health, and mission alignment

  • Develop and execute plans to achieve annual goals, evaluating and modifying the plan as needed throughout the year

  • Increase momentum for the vision by aligning programs, structures, conferences, and teams around the goals

  • Mobilize students and faculty to engage their relational networks with the gospel and to start new missional communities

  • Under the direction of the Area Director, may supervise Ministry Interns and Campus Ministry Interns as delegated 

  • Missional Developer: 

You intentionally gather, invite, and develop diverse groups of students and faculty so that they not only encounter and follow Jesus as Savior and Lord but also advance the mission on campus as participants and leaders. 

  • Create ways for faculty and students to encounter and follow Jesus through Scripture, worship, prayer, mission experiences, conferences, etc.

  • Equip students and faculty so that they think strategically about campus engagement and so that they proclaim – in word, deed, and power – the good news of Jesus, regularly inviting students and faculty to follow him as Savior and Lord

  • Disciple students and faculty by equipping them to hear the Word, respond actively, and debrief and interpret the experience so that they grow in Christlikeness, reflect our Core Values, and develop ministry skills

  • Invite, coach, and equip students and faculty to become increasingly effective participants and leaders, including starting new witnessing communities on campuses 

 

Organizational Collaboration 

As a Campus Staff Minister, you have joined a national mission. Therefore, you work with a network of other local, area, regional, and national InterVarsity staff and volunteers so that our work reflects Biblical standards of excellence, integrity, and partnership. 

  • Partner with and respond positively to the direction and coaching of your supervisors and national leaders

  • Contribute to collaborative and productive team meetings and relationships

  • Affiliate chapters under your care and submit Graduating Student Forms in order to increase our partnership with current students and alumni

  • Use national ministry resources and tools, as requested, including recruiting and/or participating in local, regional, or national conferences as

  • Complete reporting, planning and review requirements in a timely way so that you and your supervisors can assess and improve your work as a CSM

  • Comply with all InterVarsity policies and procedures 

 

Ministry Partnership Development 

As a Campus Staff Minister, you will develop a team of partners – churches and individuals (including alumni and community members) – who will resource the ministry financially, in prayer, or volunteer service that advances the mission. 

  • Raise 100% of the financial budget assigned by your supervisor

  • Communicate regularly with your ministry partners, nurturing the relationship through visits, phone calls, emails and regular prayer letters

  • Develop on-going, long-lasting partnership with alumni and volunteers

  • Comply with all Ministry Partnership Policies

  • Identify and invest in advocates who will build networks of volunteers and donors on InterVarsity’s behalf 

 

Accomplish all other assigned tasks as appropriate 

 

QUALIFICATIONS (common to all levels of CSM) 

  • Annually affirm InterVarsity’s Statement of Agreement (Doctrinal Basis and Purpose Statement). Abide by InterVarsity’s Code of Conduct. Believe and behave consonantly with InterVarsity’s Human Sexuality Theological Paper. Affirm and behave consonantly with InterVarsity’s “Women in Ministry Statement of Affirmation”

  • Bachelor’s degree for CSMs assigned to a four-year campus. A minimum of an Associate’s degree for CSMs assigned to a two-year campus or a community college

  • Strong interpersonal skills (including ability to minister to diverse ethnic communities and faculty)

  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills

  • Demonstrated problem solving skills

  • Familiarity with word processing, presentation, email, and spreadsheet software 

 

WORK ENVIRONMENT/PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS 

The CSM position leads ministry in a college campus environment. A designated office space may or may not be available. The CSM is required to travel to on-campus and off- campus sites as appropriate. Off-campus travel includes, but is not limited to: student ministry conferences, Ministry Partnership Development meetings, and InterVarsity- sponsored training sessions, meetings, and conferences. The CSM is regularly required to communicate with others, and routinely uses standard office equipment such as computers, phones, photocopiers, filing cabinets, etc. 

Pay Range: $40,476.00 - $53,952.00 per year

Pay: This position is funded through personal fundraising. Accordingly, compensation will vary based on the ability of the individual to secure a donor team to fund the cost of his/her salary. The anticipated salary range for this position on a full-time basis (40 hours/week) is dependent on a variety of factors, including location and cost of living. The actual salary received, including any geographic adjustment to account for location and cost of living, is subject to the individual’s ability to raise funds necessary to cover the full amount of such salary within the range set forth in the job posting details.

Benefits:

We offer a competitive benefits package, including health care and retirement savings with a match. Eligibility is based on employee type and hours worked.  Benefits include the following:

  • 403(b) Retirement Savings Plan

  • 403(b) matching contributions

  • Dental insurance

  • Employee assistance program

  • Employee discounts

  • Flexible work schedule

  • Flexible spending accounts

  • Health insurance

  • Health savings account

  • Life insurance

  • Paid time off

  • Parental leave

  • Professional development assistance

  • Vision insurance

Equal Employment Opportunity: 

 

InterVarsity Christian Fellowship/USA is both an equal opportunity employer and a faith-based religious organization. We conduct hiring without regard to race, color, ancestry, national origin, citizenship, age, sex, marital status, parental status, membership in any labor organization, political ideology, or disability of an otherwise qualified individual. The status of InterVarsity Christian Fellowship/USA as an equal opportunity employer does not prevent the organization from hiring staff based on their religious beliefs so that all staff share the same religious commitment.  Pursuant to the Civil Rights Act of 1964, Section 702 (42 U.S.C. 2000e 1(a)) InterVarsity Christian Fellowship/USA has the right to, and does, hire only candidates who agree with InterVarsity’s Statement of Agreement: Purpose and Doctrinal Basis because InterVarsity believes that each and every staff plays a vital role in advancing InterVarsity’s mission and purposes.

While we’re a staff from all different backgrounds and walks of life, our mission is the same - to reach people with the Gospel. We’re grounded in scripture and guided by our values, so check out our website (www.elevationchurch.org) to be sure you’re aligned before you step into the application process with us, particularly paying attention to our Beliefs and our Code.

RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Be a visible leader on the campus, executing the vision of the church and Campus Worship ministry.
  • Assist in the overall leadership of the campus, promoting connection through Worship.
  • Oversee all Worship volunteers, structures, and health.

MUST-HAVES

  • Active participation in a church (we look for a lifestyle of inviting people to church, volunteering, generosity, and prioritizing community)

  • Gifted in leading worship both vocally and presence

NICE-TO-HAVES

  • Ministry training or education
