DAY-TO-DAY

  • We’re a Sunday-Thursday work environment. Monday-Thursday, we’re in the office (8:30AM - 5PM); on Sunday, we’re supporting the weekend worship experience either directly in our roles or by choosing a weekly serving opportunity at one of our Elevation Church campuses.
  • There’s a lot to accomplish each week, so we’re pretty fast-paced. We’re also not afraid to pivot a strategy or project quickly to meet the needs of the weekend - adaptability is a key competence for us.
  • Yes, we work hard. But we’re good at playing hard, too. We’re a creative staff, so there’s no shortage of activities around our offices to have some fun!
  • You can’t help but grow on our staff. You’ll be around some incredible people. Professional development opportunities will be all around you, both in structured and unstructured ways.
  • We expect you to be disciplined in your spiritual practices - be in your Bible, spend time with the Lord in prayer, meditate on and apply the weekly sermon.
  • Bring your full self to every project, conversation, and initiative at hand.

BENEFITS

  • Elevation Church pays 100% of every employee’s medical benefits for full-time staff

  • Dental & Vision benefits

Central Catholic High School is searching for a leader with a contagious deep personal faith and dedication to the Marianist charism who will direct the efforts of evangelization in the school community. This enthusiastic, organized, and self-motivated person is skillful at igniting the fire of faith within our young men and excels at mentoring a team of adult campus ministers.


The Campus Ministry program seeks to nurture and develop the spiritual lives of our students – forming them to live lives filled with faith, hope, and love. We form them to become men of prayer, community, evangelization, and service. Through monthly Masses, daily prayer, retreats, service opportunities, liturgical choir, the sacrament of reconciliation, the LIFE team, and other formational activities, we invite and encourage every student to seek God’s presence in all things and live authentic Christian lives. Our faith community strives to reflect Christ’s care and concern for all people as we draw inspiration from the founder of the Marianist family, Blessed W. Joseph Chaminade. It is one of discipleship and brotherhood, fostering transformative encounters with God.


JOB SUMMARY:

This person oversees the entire programing and personnel of Campus Ministry, which functions as a dimension of a whole Catholic and Marianist education. Campus Ministry works in special collaboration with the Mission Integration Team, the Religion department, the Dean of Students, and the parent club to form a school community that is reflective of the values of the Marianist family.


This person discerns and implements new programming, listening to the needs and gifts of the campus community. All programs designed to integrate faith in the culture of the school community come under the Director’s purview.

This person recruits, mentors, manages, trains, and oversees the entire campus ministry team. As the Marianist charism encourages a model of ministry focused on the richness of diverse gifts, this is collaborative in nature. Ministry is formative for both adults and students. Mentorship provides an experiential and voluntary dimension to religious formation and faith development in the Marianist tradition.


This person recognizes, encourages, and creates ministry programming that presents diverse experiences of Catholic faith to the students. The Director of Campus ministry collaborates and teaches the student body of the breadth of Christ’s mission through a variety of styles of worship, prayer, justice, service, and evangelization.

The Group Leader plays a vital role in bridging camp leadership and frontline staff, overseeing multiple groups of campers and counselors to ensure a safe, structured, and positive camp experience. They support the Camp Director, Program Director, and Office Administrator with daily operations, orientations, and activities while serving as a mentor and trainer for their counselor teams. Group Leaders remain actively engaged in the camp setting, modeling strong leadership and initiative, and may also lead a group of campers directly when needed.

  • Pre-Camp: Group Leaders assist with staff orientation and training, helping prepare counselors for their roles. They review programming and schedules, organize group assignments, and establish expectations for supervision, safety, and camper engagement.

  • During Camp: Group Leaders oversee the daily activities of counselors and their assigned camper groups, providing direction, feedback, and on-the-job training to strengthen staff performance. They ensure safe and smooth transitions between activities, support special programs and field trips, and step in to lead a camper group when necessary. Their presence is hands-on, reinforcing camp culture, energy, and positivity across all groups.

  • Post-Camp: Group Leaders help wrap up weekly programming by reviewing counselor performance, providing feedback to leadership, and assisting with any reporting or administrative close-out tasks. They contribute observations and recommendations to improve staff training and programming for future sessions.

This position requires strong leadership skills, patience, enthusiasm, and adaptability to meet the needs of campers and staff. Group Leaders are key to ensuring that Kidcam delivers on its mission of a safe, fun, and unforgettable summer while developing the next generation of counselor leaders.

post_html:

Description:

There are nearly 300,000 teenagers of active-duty U.S. military parents who are stationed all over the world. These teens move an average of seven times during their school-aged years. The questions of identity and belonging that all teens face grow even more challenging to answer amid starting over and meeting new friends at each location.

This is where you can be the difference in a military teen’s life! By being in their world, walking alongside them, and creating a community where they experience the truth of God’s love and purpose for them, our staff provide a safe space where teens can develop friendships and connections to experience laughter, build hope, and generate resiliency.

We are currently providing incarnational ministry at many military installations around the world. You will have the opportunity to lead and oversee the overall Young Life Military program, known as Club Beyond, which is ecumenically focused and outreach oriented.

We are currently looking for both full-time and part-time staff throughout the United States, as well as international locations. Colorado Springs, CO, is the headquarters.

Responsibilities:

  • Actively develop healthy relationships with adults, as well as kids, and build vibrant relationships with the local community, the military installation, and the chapel community.
  • Be a role model (incarnational) and assist with developing community outreach to "unchurched" teens, discipleship to Christian teens, and leading and equipping volunteers to do "hands-on" middle and high school Christian youth programs.
  • Work well in an environment that sees (due to high military operational tempo) a high degree of turnover among teens, families, chaplains and volunteers.
  • Be respectful of and embrace a community that is deeply influenced by a military culture.
  • In this ministry, you will need to live out the Club Beyond Core Value Statement:

Club Beyond is a Christ-centered community of leaders with an exclusively military focus. Our methods are incarnational, and our perspective is ecumenical. We leverage strategic partnerships for the greatest results. We value professionalism from our staff and excellence in our stewardship.

Qualifications:

  • A deep love for Christ and for lost teens.
  • Competent communicator with youths, parents, and senior military leaders.
  • Teachable heart.
  • Willingness to make a three-year commitment.
  • Minimum of three years' youth ministry experience preferred.
  • College degree preferred.
  • Willingness to raise part of the budget through personal support.
  • Committed to a relational ministry approach.
  • Energetic.
  • Small event planning skills.
  • Strong initiative.
  • Note, this position would require our Staff to live near the community where they would be doing ministry.

Benefits:

  • Full-time salary: Based on experience, responsibility, and fundraising levels.
  • Benefits: Full health coverage (including dental, vision and life insurance).
  • Expense reimbursement (mileage [office and ministry related]).
  • Training and career development is built into the job.

Salary:

The Base Salary range: $45,000 to $60,000 (Salary is based on education and experience). In addition to salary, a Cost of Living Adjustment, dependent on location, is available. The Annual National Funding provided is $16,667.

Location:

Club Beyond works on military installations all over the world. We currently have openings at:

In the USA:

  • Fort Rucker, Alabama

Location: Leesburg, VA · Schedule: Full-time · Practice: Church & Nonprofit

We’re hiring an experienced church and nonprofit attorney who wants to help ministries and mission-driven organizations flourish, at a firm where faith and legal excellence go hand in hand.

Who We Are

The vision of Simms Showers Law is to integrate our faith into the practice of law with excellence, to help people and glorify God. We are a mission-driven firm in the fullest sense. Our shared faith shapes how we treat one another, how we approach our work, and how we understand what it means to serve clients with excellence.

The culture is both intellectually rigorous and genuinely warm. We collaborate closely, invest in one another, and enjoy working together.

The Role

This role serves churches, ministries, and nonprofit organizations at every stage of their life cycle, from formation and tax exemption through governance, policy, and organizational transactions. You will manage your own matters, serve as a primary point of contact for clients and their boards, and take on responsibility that grows with your experience.

Your work will include:

•       Forming churches and nonprofits, including articles of incorporation, bylaws, constitutions, and resolutions

•        Advising clients on federal tax-exempt status, from Form 1023 strategy and organizational classification through reinstatement and ongoing compliance

•       Advising churches and nonprofits on foreign grantmaking and international charitable activities, including OFAC sanctions compliance

•       Advising boards and leadership on governance, leadership structures, membership issues, employment, and organizational decision-making
•       Drafting organizational policies, including child protection, facility use, employment, security, and conflict of interest

•       Drafting and reviewing contracts and agreements related to operations, programs, property, and facilities

•       Handling mergers, affiliations, reorganizations, asset transfers, and dissolutions

•       Handling charitable solicitation registrations across multiple states
•       Researching federal and state law affecting religious and nonprofit organizations and turning it into practical, strategic advice

•       Managing a caseload, monitoring deadlines, and coordinating with paralegals and support staff


You will work alongside experienced partners on complex matters and have a collaborative team behind you, but this role is designed for someone ready to manage matters and client relationships independently.

Compensation & Benefits

We offer a clear path for growth, with compensation that rewards performance over time.

•       $100,000–$200,000+ base salary range, commensurate with experience and qualifications, with the opportunity to transition to a more lucrative hourly and collections-based compensation structure
•       Clear advancement tracks with partnership opportunity

•       Excellent retirement benefits including 401(k) with 4% firm match and annual profit sharing and cash balance plan contributions 

•       Multiple health insurance options with the firm paying 75% of individual premiums for all plans and 60% of qualified dependents. 

Qualifications

We are seeking a lawyer who wants their professional life to reflect their faith and has been looking for a firm where that is possible.

•       2–10 years of experience in church law, nonprofit law, or tax-exempt organization law
•       Active VA Bar license
•       Substantive experience advising on federal tax exemption and exempt-organization compliance, including Form 1023

•       Strong drafting skills across governance documents, policies, and contracts

•       Ability to manage matters independently and communicate clearly with clients, boards, and church leaders

•       For senior candidates: experience supervising junior attorneys or paralegals

Learn More

For additional information, please see our LinkedIn and Mission Statement.
Compensation: $100,000.00 - $200,000.00 per year



 Simms Showers, LLP is a partnership firm between principal attorneys J. Stephen Simms in Baltimore, MD and H. Robert Showers in Leesburg, VA. Together, Simms Showers, LLP represents clients over a wide variety of areas, including criminal defense, church and nonprofit law, personal injury and civil litigation, employment law, marriage defense and family law, estate planning, and more.

Ohio

Full time

An Area Director leads and oversees a ministry team to plant and to grow witnessing communities of students and faculty who follow Jesus on college and university campuses. Through these groups, we believe ever-increasing numbers of students and faculty from all ethnic groups and areas of the campus will be transformed by the gospel. We expect to see campuses increasingly become places where people, ideas, and structures flourish for the common good and to the glory of God. We confidently anticipate that our InterVarsity alumni will be growing disciples and change agents across the country and around the world.

ESSENTIAL COMMITMENTS/RESPONSIBILITIES

1. Spiritual Growth

The Area Ministry Director models spiritual maturity as a disciple of Jesus Christ so that your life and work increasingly reflects a growing love for God, God’s Word, God’s people of every ethnicity and culture, and God’s purposes in the world.

  • Pursue a vibrant relationship with the triune God through engagement with Scripture, prayer, and worship, both individually and in community
  • Exercise self-leadership (growing in self-awareness, self-management, relational integrity, and resiliency)
  • Embrace and practice Scriptural standards for behavior and attitudes, including those described in the Code of Conduct

​2. Campus Ministry Leadership

As an Area Director, you inspire, coach and develop campus staff ministers (“ministers”), students, faculty, and ministry partners to increase the number of witnessing communities, as well as the size, health, spiritual maturity, and campus-wide influence of existing witnessing communities by being a:

Visionary Guide:

  • Create a culture of dependence on God to gain vision for establishing and advancing witnessing communities that reach every corner of every campus in your area
  • Model InterVarsity’s vision and Core Values for supervisees
  • Lead staff, students, and faculty through Scripture, prayer, teaching and discipleship experiences in a way that motivates and shapes their ministry around vision
  • Set appropriate annual goals through prayer, research and reflection with your teams

Structural Architect:

  • Lead your team to develop and implement plans to achieve ministry goals
  • Adapt the plan as needed through rhythms of action, reflection and evaluation
  • Develop, align and leverage programs and structures to move the mission forward

Missional Developer:

  • Recruit a diversity of qualified minister candidates
  • Develop ministers to spiritually grow in Christ in intimacy, like Christ in character, and with Christ in his mission to current and new campuses
  • Develop ministers professionally so that they are consistently increasing their gifts and skills as ministry leaders
  • Supervise ministers, using appropriate leadership style for the individual and situation, to help them accomplish assigned tasks. This will require coaching, assessing, correcting and affirming job-related behaviors
  • Proactively establish and develop healthy relationships across racial, ethnic, national background, and gender barriers with staff, students, faculty, and ministry partners to build effective and diverse communities
  • Build an effective minister team that collaborates well and accomplishes goals

3. Organizational Collaboration

As an Area Director, you are part of a national organization and work in partnership with local, area, divisional, regional, and national InterVarsity ministers and volunteers.

  • Participate in regional leadership as determined by the Regional Director, to set ministry vision and strategies, contribute to accomplishing plans, and provide regional leadership in specific areas
  • Positively and constructively respond to the direction and coaching of line supervisors
  • Build productive ministry partnerships with regional and national collaborative leaders

Its Christian faith-based programs assist alcoholics, drug addicts, the homeless, the elderly, prison inmates, people in crisis, and the unemployed through offerings such as community centers, housing facilities, and rehabilitation centers. Campus Ministry Director - Part Time

Target Start Date - July 1st, 2026

 

As the Charlottesville Area Director, you will provide leadership and direction for a growing ministry serving healthcare students and professionals in the Charlottesville area, including the University of Virginia, Piedmont Community College, and Sentara Martha Jefferson Hospital. This is a part-time ministry role beginning July 1, 2026, focused on cultivating Christ-centered growth, fostering meaningful relationships, and equipping others to live out their faith in healthcare settings. You will play a key role in encouraging spiritual development, building connections across the local healthcare community, and advancing the mission of transforming lives through the Gospel in healthcare. Through discipleship, leadership development, and collaboration, you will help create a thriving and unified ministry that impacts both students and professionals.

 

What You’ll Do

You will disciple healthcare students and professionals through one-on-one and/or small group meetings that center on personal spiritual growth in Christlikeness, and integration of their faith into their profession. Work as doors open with the students, residents, and healthcare professionals within the medical and nursing training areas at the University of Virginia, Piedmont Community College, and Sentara Martha Jefferson Hospital. Identify, disciple, and pray with student and residents in the local chapter to encourage their discipline to God’s means of grace for spiritual maturation (prayer, God’s Word, worship, fellowship with other Christ-followers, pursuit of holiness) despite the tremendous demands on their time as students.  This can be done either individually or in small groups as time allows.

 

You will Identify, train, and disciple student leaders, advisors, and graduate mentors, and meet with them regularly for discipleship, feedback, and planning and scheduling of events. Help student leaders identify their replacements and transition the ministry to new leaders each year. Facilitate the pairing of interested students with same gender mentors both in their schools and in the community. Encourage local students to develop in regional and national leadership roles and to attend CMDA conferences and mission trips.

 

You will engage with leaders of local Christian ministries to identify appropriate opportunities for collaboration in health care related outreach, discipling and education. Reach out to new healthcare professionals in the area, and engage them in support of our student and resident activities. Organize one or more annual dinners for local professionals to come together for fellowship and an inspirational message on relevant topics. You will work to grow a unity of vision and partnership in the Charlottesville area (church leaders, ministry leaders, para-church ministry leaders).

 

You will lead, coordinate and work with the Charlottesville Council on financial development for the CMDA Charlottesville area ministry. The Area Director will participate in the planning and organization of any events the local Council recommends. Send out quarterly newsletters to local healthcare professionals involved in the ministry, all local CMDA members, and former student graduates.

 

You will be expected to attend the national CMDA Staff Connections Conference each year. As the Area Director, you will be a member of and meet, report to, and pray with the Charlottesville area leadership Council at each meeting. You will work within corporate national CMDA structures and ensure that the Charlottesville area chapter is consistent with the vision, mission, and doctrinal statements of CMDA. This will require regular communication with the CMDA Regional Director and work with them on the development of the annual budget and maintain financial records as required by the CMDA national organization.

 

Qualifications

·        Personal relationship with Jesus Christ 

·        Endorsement in writing of CMDA’s Leadership Statement of Faith, Mission, Vision, and Values

·        A minimum of 2 years of leadership in a previous church, faith-based organization, or campus ministry or equivalent

·        Experience in discipling others

·        Leadership skills, Humility, Flexibility

·        Evidence of excellent people (interpersonal) skills

·        Excellent verbal and written communication skills

·        Accountability to leadership (CMDA national, regional, and local council)

 

 

To express interest, please send resume and cover letter detailing your personal faith journey to hr@cmda.org  or visit www.cmda.org/careers to apply.

The International Mission Board is seeking a Senior Church Engagement Strategist to assess, strengthen, and grow relationships with key Southern Baptist churches, ensuring strategic alignment and maximizing partnership effectiveness in support of global missions.


Location: Remote in KY or TN

Compensation: $85,662-100,779k*


The Senior Church Engagement Strategist serves at the forefront of advancing global missions by cultivating strategic partnerships with some of the most engaged Southern Baptist churches across the United States. This high-impact role is responsible for building trusted relationships with pastors, missions leaders, and key church influencers while helping churches deepen their involvement in praying, giving, going, and sending for the fulfillment of the Great Commission.


Beyond managing a portfolio of influential church partners, the Senior Church Engagement Strategist provides leadership across the Church Engagement team by mentoring peers, identifying regional opportunities, informing engagement strategies, and helping coordinate resources that strengthen church partnerships and missionary impact worldwide.  


Responsibilities:

  • Serve as the primary relationship manager for a portfolio of highly engaged Southern Baptist churches.
  • Develop deep, trust-based partnerships with pastors, missions leaders, and church staff.
  • Create customized engagement strategies aligned with each church's missions vision, capacity, and goals.
  • Deliver responsive, proactive, and concierge-level support that strengthens long-term partnership.
  • Inspire churches to increase participation in global missions through prayer, financial support, missionary sending, and field partnerships.
  • Connect church leaders with missionaries, field personnel, and strategic mission opportunities.
  • Facilitate complex partnerships involving multiple churches and ministry stakeholders.
  • Recommend strategic initiatives that increase church participation and impact.
  • Provide insights and recommendations that strengthen regional and national engagement efforts.
  • Mentor and coach Church Engagement Strategists.
  • Share best practices and help strengthen team effectiveness.
  • Support onboarding and development of new team members.
  • May provide direct supervision to Church Engagement Strategists, including performance support and professional development.
  • Collaborate across teams to align resources around strategic church partnerships.
  • Serve as a bridge between churches, missionaries, and internal ministry teams.
  • Communicate mission impact stories and field needs that inspire greater engagement.

Required Qualifications:


  • Bachelor's degree and seminary training (MDiv or MRE) or equivalent missionary experience
  • Minimum of 8 years of progressive experience in ministry, nonprofit leadership, church relations, strategic partnerships, business development, or constituent engagement, with demonstrated impact on organizational growth and mission advancement.
  • Proven ability to cultivate, influence, and steward high-value relationships with executive leaders, key stakeholders, and strategic partners.
  • Exceptional executive communication and presentation skills, with the ability to inspire, influence, and engage diverse audiences.
  • Strong strategic planning, analytical thinking, and problem-solving capabilities, with a track record of identifying opportunities and driving organizational objectives.

  • Ability and willingness to travel extensively, including domestic and international travel, to strengthen partnerships and advance organizational initiatives.
  • Working knowledge of Southern Baptist churches, ministry ecosystems, and church-based missions strategies, with the ability to translate that knowledge into effective engagement approaches.
  • Experience coaching, developing, and mentoring team members, fostering a culture of accountability, collaboration, and growth.
  • Demonstrated success designing and executing scalable engagement, partnership, or growth strategies that expand influence, deepen stakeholder commitment, and advance organizational impact.
  • Needs to be located in KY or TN, will not provide relocation.

One line job description

“The Next Gen Executive Pastor will champion the leadership and spiritual shepherding of the staff and team leading our birth through young adults’ ministries at Cornerstone.”

The Next Gen Executive Pastor will be a member of the Executive Team and will serve in the highest levels of leadership within the church.  They will lead the Children's Ministry Team that is birth through 4th grade and the existing Student Ministry Departments that include 5th/6th grades, Junior High, High School, and College/Young Adults.  The right candidate will already be a thought leader in these spaces, able to take strong teams even further. 

Who we are looking for…

A Strategic Developer – The ideal candidate will be someone who sees the big picture clearly. They will have a deep understanding of the systems and programs it takes to maintain a discipleship pathway for children and students of all ages.

A Ministry Savant – The ideal candidate will be someone who has been doing it at a high level for a long time. They will have spent significant time leading in a context of similar size and scope. The value of experience and a natural God-given leadership gifting cannot be overstated for this role.

A Church Sponge – The ideal candidate will be someone who has their pulse on what’s working in Church today. They will also have a tendency to think outside of the box and not be afraid to approach ministry in a way that will be sure to resonate with the world we live in.

A Decisive Leader – The ideal candidate will be someone who makes decisions in a timely manner that reflects the vision values of the organization. They will design clear courses of action and implement steps with measurable goals that move the team of Pastors, Directors, and staff forward.

A Collaborative Executive – The ideal candidate will be someone who brings immense insight and value to the Executive Leadership team at Cornerstone. They will have the ability to speak into the global ministry integration of the organization at large.

A Leader’s Pastor – The ideal candidate will be someone who is a steady team manager and proven mentor to Pastors and Ministry Directors to all children and student age groups. They will have the ability to pull the most out of their personnel while also creating an environment that builds consensus, symmetry and integration across the team.

Essential duties and responsibilities…

An Executive leader with Cornerstone provides leadership in a number of ways, including…

  • Culture – creating, building, sustaining a culture within their team based on our church and staff values
  • Vision – casting the overall church vision to their team while also creating and casting vision for their division
  • Personnel – a focus on leader development, working to develop the current team for new opportunities while always recruiting high-capacity leaders into the ministry
  • Strategy – helping leaders create strategic pathways for children and students to grow in their faith while setting strategy to grow the ministries to meet the needs of the church
  • Financials – oversees the budgeting process for their teams and stewardship of funds
  • Pastoral Care – the span of care for each team is provided through the Executive

An ideal candidate…

  • has a Bachelors or Master's Degree in Ministry, Biblical Studies or Divinity
  • has 10+ years’ experience in full time ministry, at least 2 years in a church larger than 2000 members.
  • has experience leading both Children's and Student Ministries
  • aligns with the vision, values, and doctrinal statement of Cornerstone
  • is a self-reliant, self-starter, with the ability to innovate
  • generates new ideas, gives direction, and allows others to work the details

Are you ready to lead the next generation at a thriving organization?

Job Posting: Senior Pastor
Church Address: 256 North El Camino Real, San Mateo, CA 94401

Church Expectations:
Peninsula Community Alliance Church (http://www.p-cac.org/) is seeking a Senior Pastor to lead our congregation. The ideal candidate should be devoted to Christ, capable of guiding the church’s growth and development according to God’s will, and demonstrate vision, passion, strong communication skills, and a close walk with God. A clear calling to serve the Lord is essential.

Church History:
Peninsula Community Alliance Church was established in 1996 and relocated to in San Mateo, California in 2005. As part of the Christian and Missionary Alliance, the church has consistently upheld the truths of the Old and New Testaments and revered the teachings of the Lord Jesus Christ.

Currently, the Cantonese congregation averages over 60 attendees, while the Mandarin congregation has over 30 attendees. The church is actively developing an English ministry and expanding children’s and youth programs, with a commitment to serving the Chinese community in the Bay Area, particularly in San Mateo.

Primary Responsibilities and Character Requirements:

  1. Spiritual Vision and Direction
    a) Set the future direction and development of the church’s ministries.
    b) Clearly communicate ministry burdens to church staff and members.
    c) Encourage the church to move in the right direction.
    d) Conduct regular evaluations and improvements during progress.
    e) Participate in church activities and provide appropriate guidance.
  2. Shepherding and Caring for the Congregation
    a) Nurture believers with sound doctrine to foster spiritual growth.
    b) Understand the needs of members through fellowship and communication.
    c) Serve as a role model for the flock, following Christ and making disciples.
    d) Provide training to equip believers and demonstrate strong teaching abilities.
    e) Have a burden for evangelism and leading others to Christ.
  3. Pastoral Qualities and Example
    a) Demonstrate love and kindness.
    b) Be approachable, humble, and skilled in listening and communication.
    c) Lead a devout life, emphasizing prayer and God’s Word.
    d) Exhibit righteousness, integrity, and honesty, aligning with biblical truths.
  4. Functional Requirements
    a) Fluent in Cantonese and Mandarin; proficient in spoken and written English.
    b) Must obtain a Christian and Missionary Alliance license upon appointment.
    c) Hold a degree from an evangelical theological institution and have church ministry experience.

Statement of Faith:

  1. Aligns with all teachings of the Old and New Testaments.
  2. Adheres to the Christian and Missionary Alliance Statement of Faith.
  3. Follows the regulations of the Christian and Missionary Alliance and the bylaws of Peninsula Community Alliance Church

Application Process:
Please carefully consider the above requirements. Briefly explain why you are suitable to take on this role. If you are interested in applying, please email your testimony, resume and other background information related to the position to the PCAC Pastoral Search Committee at: pcac@sbcglobal.net

To be considered for this position, please complete the application to include your testimony, resume and other background information related to the position.

If the district office has reviewed your application and they think you may be a potential match for the position, that the hiring manager will reach out to you for next steps.

This position requires licensing with The Christian & Missionary Alliance. To learn more about The Alliance and requirements for licensing, please visit our website

Please do not contact the church directly.

WORSHIP MINISTRY RESIDENT CANDIDATE

We are seeking an enthusiastic, gifted, and teachable worship leader to join our team as a Worship Ministry Resident in a two-year program. This residency is designed to provide both hands-on ministry experience and theological education, preparing you for long-term leadership in worship ministry—whether in a church plant or a full-time church role. As part of this residency, you will be enrolled in seminary classes through an accredited program, either at the undergraduate or graduate level, depending on your academic background. Our goal is to help you grow not only in skill and leadership but also in biblical and theological depth.

You might be a great fit if:

  • You love Jesus and love helping others encounter Him through worship.
  • You’re excited about learning and trying new things.
  • You value both creativity and spiritual formation.
  • You have some musical or worship-leading experience and want to grow in it.
  • You’re ready to invest two years in preparation for a life of ministry through both classroom learning and real-world experience.

ABOUT OUR WORSHIP MINISTRY

We have a seasoned worship and production staff and a gifted, growing volunteer team. Our culture is built on clarity, consistency, and compelling leadership. We strive to create worship environments that are God-honoring, Spirit-led, and thoughtfully crafted.

As a Worship Ministry Resident, you’ll be mentored by experienced leaders, contribute regularly to planning and leading services, and engage deeply with the daily rhythms of worship ministry. You’ll grow as both a disciple and a leader, equipped for what God may call you to next.


KEYSTONE CHURCH

Classroom Duties
  • Plan and deliver daily activities that support spiritual, social, emotional, and academic development, integrating Bible stories, prayer, and Christian values in age-appropriate ways.

  • Track attendance, developmental milestones, and classroom routines consistently.

Family Engagement

  • Share developmental milestones, learning progress, and spiritual growth updates.

Skills

Through thoughtful organization, excellent communication, and genuine care for people, this position removes obstacles so pastors and ministry leaders can focus on shepherding, discipling, and serving our church family.



Working as part of a collaborative administrative team, this position shares responsibility for supporting every ministry of the church. Whether welcoming a guest, preparing for a funeral, coordinating a baptism, organizing a weekend event, or ensuring the smallest administrative details are handled with excellence, this role reflects the heart of Christ through faithful, behind-the-scenes service. Every phone call answered, every calendar coordinated, every email sent, and every event prepared becomes an opportunity to help people encounter Jesus and experience the love of His Church.



The ideal candidate is highly organized, detail-oriented, spiritually mature, and deeply committed to serving others. They find joy in bringing order to complexity, anticipate needs before they arise, thrive in a collaborative environment, and understand that administration is not simply a profession—it is a ministry. They value excellence, hospitality, humility, and teamwork, recognizing that every act of service, seen or unseen, contributes to advancing the mission of Heights Church.



Key Responsibilities



Ministry Administration & Organizational Support

  • Provide administrative support to assigned pastors, directors, ministry leaders, and church leadership.
  • Coordinate meetings, ministry activities, weddings, memorials, baptisms, and other church functions with excellence, compassion, and attention to detail.
  • Manage calendars, appointments, and scheduling to maximize ministry effectiveness and steward leaders' time wisely.
  • Prepare agendas, meeting materials, research, notes, and follow-up documents.
  • Track assignments, action items, ministry conversations, and follow-up needs to help ministries move forward effectively.
  • Assist with special projects, ministry initiatives, sermon preparation support, and church-wide events including Christmas, Easter, and other key ministry opportunities.
  • Anticipate ministry and administrative needs by exercising sound judgment, initiative, and a servant's heart.
  • Support pastors and ministry leaders in ways that allow them to invest more deeply in people and the mission of the church.



Communication & Guest Relations

  • Serve as a trusted and welcoming point of contact for assigned ministries, pastors, and directors.
  • Respond to ministry-related phone calls, emails, and in-person inquiries with warmth, professionalism, and hospitality.
  • Draft, edit, proofread, and distribute ministry communications, reports, letters, cards, and emails.
  • Act as a communication bridge between church leadership, staff, serve team members, church partners, and guests.
  • Help create an atmosphere where every person who contacts or visits Heights Church feels seen, welcomed, cared for and valued.



Church Operations & Event Coordination

  • Assist in planning, organizing, and executing church-wide events, ministry programs, and special gatherings.
  • Manage room reservations and ministry scheduling through church management systems.
  • Coordinate facility usage, including communication with ministries and outside groups using church facilities.
  • Maintain accurate event calendars and support seamless coordination across multiple ministries.
  • Collaborate with ministry leaders to proactively address logistical and operational needs while maintaining flexibility when priorities shift.



Database, Records & Financial Administration

  • Maintain accurate ministry records, contact information, and church data within Planning Center and other church management systems.
  • Manage registrations, ministry databases, and administrative records with accuracy and consistency.
  • Coordinate travel arrangements, lodging, and itineraries as needed.
  • Process receipts, invoices, and expense reimbursements for submission to the accounting office.
  • Handle confidential information, personnel matters, and ministry records with the highest level of integrity, discretion, and professionalism.



Office Administration

  • Support the daily operations of the church office alongside the administrative team.
  • Assist with front desk responsibilities and office coverage as needed.
  • Maintain office, kitchen, custodial, hospitality, and ministry supplies.
  • Support facility management software and other administrative systems.
  • Help ensure the office, lobby, and shared ministry spaces are welcoming, organized, and reflective of the hospitality of Heights Church.
  • Joyfully perform additional responsibilities and special projects as ministry needs arise.



Qualifications, Skills & Requirements



Experience & Technical Skills

  • Minimum of 1–2 years of administrative experience in a professional office environment required; experience supporting pastors, executive leaders, or ministry teams in a church or nonprofit setting is preferred.
  • Demonstrated proficiency using Microsoft Office Suite (Word, Excel, Outlook, and PowerPoint), with the ability to create professional documents, manage calendars, organize data, and communicate effectively.
  • Experience with Planning Center or comparable church management software is preferred.
  • Strong attention to detail with a consistent record of producing organized, accurate, and high-quality work.
  • Proven ability to organize, prioritize, and manage multiple projects, deadlines, and competing requests while maintaining accuracy and follow-through.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to draft professional correspondence, proofread documents, and communicate with compassion, warmth, discretion, and clarity.
  • Ability to adapt to changing priorities, interruptions, and the fast-paced rhythms of ministry while maintaining a positive, servant-hearted attitude.
  • Demonstrates initiative, adaptability, and the ability to solve problems with wisdom and grace.



Character & Spiritual Qualifications

  • Fully aligns with and supports the Mission, Vision, Values, and Statement of Faith of Heights Church.
  • Demonstrates spiritual maturity, integrity, humility, discretion, and sound judgment.
  • Possesses a servant's heart and a genuine desire to support pastors, ministry leaders, serve team members and the church family.
  • Builds trust through kindness, encouragement, professionalism, and dependability.
  • Thrives in a collaborative team environment while joyfully serving wherever needed.
  • Recognizes that excellence in administration is an act of worship and an important part of caring for our church family and community.



Requirements

  • Ability to work the church's regular office schedule (Monday–Thursday), with occasional remote work as approved by a supervisor.
  • Flexibility to support evening and weekend ministry events, including Christmas, Easter, and other major church gatherings.
  • Ability to maintain confidentiality and steward sensitive information with the utmost care.
  • Ability to work independently while remaining highly collaborative in a dynamic, fast-paced ministry environment.


Physical Demands

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions. 



While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to sit; use hands; and talk or hear. The employee is occasionally required to stand; walk; reach with hands and arms; and stoop, kneel, or crouch. The employee must occasionally lift and/or move up to 20 pounds. 

 

Work Environment 

The work environment characteristics described here are representative of those an employee encounters while performing the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions. The noise level in the work environment is usually low to moderate. May be required to occasionally work holidays, irregular and long hours.

Title of Position: Church Planting Resident (Full-Time)

Location: York, PA

Church: York Alliance Family of Churches

Compensation: Full-time position with benefits

Job Description:

The church planting resident is an 18-24 month position that prepares the candidate to become a church planter with York Alliance/Spring Grove network of churches. As a church planting resident, the candidate will be trained and coached through a developmental program established by the local church. In the residency environment, the candidate will learn and grow in the areas of disciple making, spiritual formation, Community Group ministry, adaptive leadership, emotional health, prayer, preaching/teaching the Gospel, administration and operations, and more through a personalized plan. This plan will be based on the candidate’s current level of knowledge and experience in the areas above.

Key Characteristics:

A Church Planting Resident is expected to be a Gospel-centered, forward-thinking leader who has a clear and affirmed call to church planting. They are to grow as a follower of Jesus through a personal rule of life. They are expected to humbly seek development through healthy personal relationships and a lifestyle of disciple making in their community. They are expected to be creative and collaborative in their learning process as they seek to carry out the call of God on their life to reach new people with the Gospel.

Essential Job Functions:

Develop and execute a personalized development plan based on the Alliance Eastern PA Multipliers Residency and in collaboration with the Pastor of Mission and Multiplication. The candidate will carry out this plan while serving in a local church where you will:

  • Develop a strategy for the new church plant
  • Participate in, and eventually lead, a Community Group
  • Seek to evaluate and strengthen your marriage/family with the help of an older mentor.
  • Execute a missional living plan
  • Grow in spiritual formation through establishing a rule of life
  • Grow in relational disciple making
  • Participate, lead, and multiply ministry teams
  • Practice and develop preaching/teaching skills
  • Learn the administrative and operational systems of the York Alliance/Spring Grove network of churches
  • Connect with the local community through serving
  • Engage in an Alliance global missions partnership
  • Complete recommended readings and specialized training outline in plan
  • Function as a member of the YAC staff participating in team meetings and staff sabbath.
  • Submit to the authority of the C&MA denominational leadership.
  • Establish a Sabbath day and be held accountable to it.
  • Maintain a healthy balance between family life, ministry and other responsibilities.

Requirements:

  • Has a deep and passionate relationship with Jesus.
  • This position requires ordination through the C&MA.
  • Experience with starting ministries in new contexts, communities, and cultures
  • Highly strategic, organized, and entrepreneurial with exceptional communication skills
  • Creativity and a willingness to try new approaches
  • Established skills in team implementation, decision-making, and relationship-building
  • Demonstrate a faithful pursuit of leadership characteristics as listed in 1 Tim 3, Titus 1 and 1 Peter 5.

Church Information

Church Size: Attendance of 400-500 on an average Sunday, including children

Church History: York Alliance was officially incorporated as an Alliance church in 1932. There is a rich history of both local and global missions, with active partnerships around the world. The staff and leadership of York Alliance have been remarkably stable, with only four lead pastors serving over the last 50 years. Over the last several years YAC has developed an increased focus on spiritual formation in addition to the vibrant worship and deeply connected community.

Church Vision: The York Alliance Family of Churches pursues the transformational love of Jesus and seeks to build communities that share this love with all people.

To be considered for this position, please complete the application to include your testimony, resume and other background information related to the position.

If the district office has reviewed your application and they think you may be a potential match for the position, than the hiring manager will reach out to you for next steps.

Please do not contact the church directly.

Lead Pastor Opportunity

Bethel Alliance Church – Bethel, Maine

Bethel Alliance Church is seeking a Lead Pastor to shepherd a Christ-centered congregation that is committed to biblical teaching, authentic community, and reaching the people of western Maine with the gospel.

Bethel Alliance Church is a Christian and Missionary Alliance congregation with 41 members and an average Sunday attendance of approximately 75. Founded in 1969 and affiliated with the C&MA since 1979, the church is known for faithful biblical preaching, contemporary worship, generous care for one another, and a strong commitment to prayer. Active ministries include youth and children's programs, Bible studies, Coffeehouse Conversations, a monthly Community Supper serving approximately 100–150 guests, missions engagement, and a gifted worship team that includes several teenagers.

Primary Responsibilities

  • Preach and teach God's Word faithfully, clearly, and in ways that connect with everyday life.
  • Shepherd the congregation through pastoral care, counseling, visitation, and prayer.
  • Serve alongside the elders, facilitate the Board of Ministries, supervise the part-time administrative assistant, and equip volunteer ministry leaders.
  • Develop emerging leaders as longtime servants transition responsibilities to the next generation.
  • Strengthen evangelism, community partnerships, and youth and children's ministries—particularly with the middle and high school located directly across the street.
  • Model a servant-hearted, empowering leadership style that equips others for ministry.

Qualifications

The ideal candidate will be:

  • A spiritually mature follower of Jesus marked by integrity, humility, compassion, wisdom, and a healthy sense of humor.
  • A gifted communicator with demonstrated effectiveness in biblical preaching, disciple-making, leadership development, and evangelism.
  • Someone who enjoys building relationships across generations and is excited to serve in a close-knit rural community.
  • Ordained (or able to meet Christian & Missionary Alliance licensing and ordination requirements). Five or more years of pastoral ministry experience is preferred.

About Bethel

Nestled in the mountains of western Maine, Bethel is a vibrant New England village that combines small-town charm with exceptional year-round recreation. Surrounded by the lakes, rivers, forests, and peaks of the Mahoosuc region, the community features a walkable downtown, locally owned businesses, Gould Academy, and the Maine Mineral & Gem Museum. Outdoor enthusiasts enjoy world-class skiing at nearby Sunday River, hiking throughout Grafton Notch and the Bethel Community Forest, as well as biking, fishing, paddling, and camping. Portland and Portland International Jetport are approximately 72 miles away, while North Conway, New Hampshire, is just 42 miles away, providing convenient access to shopping, dining, travel, and additional recreation in the White Mountains.

Campus Staff Minister -- Alabama (Undergraduate Ministry)

Work Location:

Alabama

Job Type:

Full time

God has called InterVarsity to plant and to build witnessing communities of students and faculty who follow Jesus on college and university campuses. Through these groups, we believe ever- increasing numbers of students and faculty from all ethnic groups and areas of the campus will be transformed by the Gospel. We expect to see campuses increasingly become places where people, ideas, and structures flourish to the glory of God. We confidently anticipate that our InterVarsity alumni will become change agents across the country and around the world. We pursue this calling by discerning and actively participating in what God is already doing on campus. This is the essence of being a Campus Staff Minister (CSM).

ESSENTIAL COMMITMENTS/RESPONSIBILITIES 

Spiritual Growth 

You pursue maturity as a disciple of Jesus Christ so that your life and work increasingly reflects a growing love for God, God’s Word, God’s people of every ethnicity and culture, and God’s purposes in the world. To do this, you will: 

  • Pursue a vibrant relationship with the triune God through engagement with Scripture, prayer, and worship, both individually and in community 

  • Develop self-leadership (growing in self-awareness, self-management, relational integrity, and resiliency) 

  • Embrace Scriptural standards for behavior and attitudes 

 

Campus Leadership 

You communicate and model InterVarsity’s vision to see students and faculty transformed, campuses renewed and world changers developed 

  • Create a culture of humble dependence on God and bold expectation in God’s intention to start new witnessing communities throughout the campus and on new campuses 

  • Model – in person and through programs – InterVarsity’s vision and Core Values, including a biblically-defined commitment to engage every ethnic and social group on campus 

  • Lead students and faculty – individually and collectively – through Scripture, prayer, teaching, and discipleship experiences, so that they articulate and align their ministry activities around this vision 

  • Set annual goals through prayer, research and reflection with your teams (students, faculty, and staff) for qualitative and quantitative growth, including conversions and leadership development 

 

You create, develop, align and leverage ministry plans, programs, teams, and structures to close the gap between current reality and the aspirational goals. 

  • Build leadership teams who trust and partner well with you and who demonstrate spiritual vitality, relational health, and mission alignment 

  • Develop and execute plans to achieve annual goals, evaluating and modifying the plan as needed throughout the year 

  • Increase momentum for the vision by aligning programs, structures, conferences and teams around the goals 

  • Mobilize students and faculty to engage their relational networks with the gospel and to start new missional communities 

  • Under the direction of the Area Director, may supervise Ministry Interns and Campus Ministry Interns as delegated 

 

You intentionally gather, invite, and develop diverse groups of students and faculty so that they not only encounter and follow Jesus as Savior and Lord but also advance the mission on campus as participants and leaders. 

  • Create ways for faculty and students to encounter and follow Jesus through Scripture, worship, prayer, mission experiences, conferences, etc. 

  • Equip students and faculty so that they think strategically about campus engagement and so that they proclaim – in word, deed, and power – the good news of Jesus, regularly inviting students and faculty to follow him as Savior and Lord 

  • Disciple students and faculty by equipping them to hear the Word, respond actively, and debrief and interpret the experience so that they grow in Christlikeness, reflect our Core Values, and develop ministry skills 

  • Invite, coach, and equip students and faculty to become increasingly effective participants and leaders, including starting new witnessing communities on campuses 

 

Organizational Collaboration 

You work with a network of other local, area, regional, and national InterVarsity staff and volunteers so that our work reflects Biblical standards of excellence, integrity, and partnership. 

  • Partner with and respond positively to the direction and coaching of your supervisors and national leaders 

  • Contribute to collaborative and productive team meetings and relationships 

  • Affiliate chapters under your care and submit Graduating Student Forms in order to increase our partnership with current students and alumni 

  • Use national ministry resources and tools, as requested, including recruiting and/or participating in local, regional, or national conferences as  

  • Complete reporting, planning and review requirements in a timely way so that you and your supervisors can assess and improve your work as a CSM 

  • Comply with all InterVarsity policies and procedures 

 

Ministry Partnership Development 

You will develop a team of partners – churches and individuals (including alumni and community members) – who will resource the ministry financially, in prayer, or volunteer service that advances the mission. 

  • Raise 100% of the financial budget assigned by your supervisor 

  • Communicate regularly with your ministry partners, nurturing the relationship through visits, phone calls, emails and regular prayer letters 

  • Develop on-going, long-lasting partnership with alumni and volunteers 

  • Comply with all Ministry Partnership Policies 

  • Identify and invest in advocates who will build networks of volunteers and donors on InterVarsity’s behalf 

 

Accomplish all other assigned tasks as appropriate 

 

QUALIFICATIONS (common to all levels of CSM) 

  • Annually affirm InterVarsity’s Statement of Agreement (Doctrinal Basis and Purpose Statement). Abide by InterVarsity’s Code of Conduct. Believe and behave consonantly with InterVarsity’s Human Sexuality Theological Paper. Affirm and behave consonantly with InterVarsity’s “Women in Ministry Statement of Affirmation” 

  • Bachelor’s degree for CSMs assigned to a four-year campus. A minimum of an Associate’s degree for CSMs assigned to a two-year campus or a community college 

  • Strong interpersonal skills (including ability to minister to diverse ethnic communities and faculty) 

  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills 

  • Demonstrated problem solving skills 

  • Familiarity with word processing, presentation, email, and spreadsheet software 

 

WORK ENVIRONMENT/PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS 

The CSM position leads ministry in a college campus environment. A designated office space may or may not be available. The CSM is required to travel to on-campus and off- campus sites as appropriate. Off-campus travel includes, but is not limited to: student ministry conferences, Ministry Partnership Development meetings, and InterVarsity- sponsored training sessions, meetings, and conferences. The CSM is regularly required to communicate with others, and routinely uses standard office equipment such as computers, phones, photocopiers, filing cabinets, etc. 

Pay Range: $39,288.00 - $52,392.00 per year

Pay: This position is funded through personal fundraising. Accordingly, compensation will vary based on the ability of the individual to secure a donor team to fund the cost of his/her salary. The anticipated salary range for this position on a full-time basis (40 hours/week) is dependent on a variety of factors, including location and cost of living. The actual salary received, including any geographic adjustment to account for location and cost of living, is subject to the individual’s ability to raise funds necessary to cover the full amount of such salary within the range set forth in the job posting details.

Benefits:

We offer a competitive benefits package, including health care and retirement savings with a match. Eligibility is based on employee type and hours worked.  Benefits include the following:

  • 403(b) Retirement Savings Plan

  • 403(b) matching contributions

  • Dental insurance

  • Employee assistance program

  • Employee discounts

  • Flexible work schedule

  • Flexible spending accounts

  • Health insurance

  • Health savings account

  • Life insurance

  • Paid time off

  • Parental leave

  • Professional development assistance

  • Vision insurance

Equal Employment Opportunity: 

 

InterVarsity Christian Fellowship/USA is both an equal opportunity employer and a faith-based religious organization. We conduct hiring without regard to race, color, ancestry, national origin, citizenship, age, sex, marital status, parental status, membership in any labor organization, political ideology, or disability of an otherwise qualified individual. The status of InterVarsity Christian Fellowship/USA as an equal opportunity employer does not prevent the organization from hiring staff based on their religious beliefs so that all staff share the same religious commitment.  Pursuant to the Civil Rights Act of 1964, Section 702 (42 U.S.C. 2000e 1(a)) InterVarsity Christian Fellowship/USA has the right to, and does, hire only candidates who agree with InterVarsity’s Statement of Agreement: Purpose and Doctrinal Basis because InterVarsity believes that each and every staff plays a vital role in advancing InterVarsity’s mission and purposes.

  • Participates in and provides appropriate leadership in interdisciplinary clinical team activities related to planning and coordinating patient care, including care conferences, team meetings, nursing rounds, palliative care rounds, IDT meetings, and family conferences when appropriate.
  • Provides end of life support, bereavement support as needed.
  • Provides education to patients and hospital personnel/medical staff on Advanced Directives including Power of Attorney for Healthcare and Goals of Care conversations.
  • Develops and leads spiritual care services within the hospital in collaboration with other members of the Spiritual Care Department.
  • Serves as spiritual liaisons between the hospital and community (both religious and secular) with referrals and information with patient/family permission that is compliant with HIPAA regulations.
  • Escalates any concerns or issues following the NM chain of command policies.
  • Offers religious services to hospital personnel/medical staff as appropriate and when requested.
  • Accepts on call for spiritual care coverage, crises and emergencies as assigned including nights, weekends, and holidays. Manager may assign required minimum on-call shifts.
  • Assists in leading CALM/Mindful Moments as assigned or as needed.
  • Attends to cultural and spiritual dynamics that may improve patient treatment and family dynamics.
  • Maintains chapel/sacred spaces and workspaces in a neat fashion while keeping supplies available and stocked.
  • Maintains board certification and/or minimum annual CEU requirements as set by certifying bodies and organization/industry standards.

Minimum Requirements:

Education:

  •  At least one (1) unit of Clinical Pastoral Education (CPE) or in process of completing one (1) unit of CPE within 90 days of hire date

Preferred:

  • Ordination and/or in good standing within one’s faith tradition or certifying organization
  • Four (4) Units of CPE, Board Certification

Additional Information

Northwestern Medicine is an equal opportunity employer (disability, VETS) and does not discriminate in hiring or employment on the basis of age, sex, race, color, religion, national origin, gender identity, veteran status, disability, sexual orientation or any other protected status.

If you are offered a position with us, you will be required to complete an authorization and disclosure form that gives Northwestern Medicine permission to run the background check.  Results are evaluated on a case-by-case basis, and we follow all local, state, and federal laws, including the Illinois Health Care Worker Background Check Act. 

Artificial Intelligence Disclosure

Benefits

Position Title: Catholic Administrative Pastoral Life Coordinator
Position Type: Part Time
Location: Fort Belvoir, VA
Key Responsibilities
  • Assist the Catholic Chaplain and Priest with preparation and coordination of Mass and holy day services
  • Prepare liturgical materials, sacred vessels, and Eucharistic elements for worship services
  • Create and distribute weekly Catholic bulletins and announcements
  • Develop and maintain a monthly Catholic community calendar
  • Maintain Catholic community registration records and attendance reports
  • Collect and prepare sacramental documentation and records in the AMS system
  • Coordinate facility reservations, publicity, and logistics for Catholic community events
  • Attend staff and pastoral meetings required
  • Support quarterly and monthly reports as required
Qualifications
  • Ability to work respectfully within a Catholic pastoral environment
  • Strong organizational, communication, and administrative skills
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, Outlook, PowerPoint)
  • Ability to obtain AMS Catechist Certification.

Ridge Christian (Coweta Campus)

NextGen Minister

Coweta, Oklahoma


Ridge Christian–Coweta is a close-knit, community-centered church seeking a Next Gen Minister to lead and grow its student ministry (6th–12th grade) while providing oversight and support to volunteer leaders in children’s ministry. This role offers a unique opportunity to step into a healthy, relational ministry with strong volunteer engagement and meaningful influence among both churched and unchurched students. The next leader will build on an established foundation while bringing clarity, discipleship depth, and vision for the future. This is an ownership role with room to grow, shape culture, and make a long-term impact.


Why I Love This Opportunity

Ridge Christian–Coweta has that increasingly rare combination of health, humility, and hunger. There’s genuine trust between staff, volunteers, parents, and students — and a shared desire to grow without blowing everything up. I love that this is a remodel (metaphorically), not a rebuild. The ministry is already welcoming, outward-facing, and relational, but it’s craving clearer vision, stronger discipleship pathways, and a leader who can bring structure without losing heart.


This is also a place where a leader can take real ownership. They’re not looking for a program manager or a hype communicator — they’re looking for someone who wants to build, disciple, and stay. For the right leader, this could be both a deeply meaningful role and a place to grow into broader leadership over time. - Brian Aaby (Senior Associate // Slingshot Group)


A great match for this position would be:

  • Teacher: Able to communicate God’s truth clearly and relationally to both churched and unchurched students, helping them understand Scripture and apply it to real life.
  • Biblical & Theological Shaper: Grounds the ministry in Scripture and sound theology, moving students beyond events toward lifelong discipleship.
  • Self Starter: Takes initiative, creates momentum, and moves ministry forward without needing heavy oversight or fully built systems.
  • Visionary: Provides clarity and direction, helping the church articulate where student ministry is headed and why it matters.
  • Delegator: Builds sustainable ministry by recruiting, training, and empowering volunteers rather than carrying everything alone.



About This Organization

Ridge Christian–Coweta began as a satellite campus of a larger suburban church but has grown into a thriving, locally rooted congregation with a strong sense of identity. For more than seven years, Coweta has functioned as a live-preaching campus, steadily growing at a healthy pace while keeping ministry simple and relational. The church averages around 225 in weekend attendance, with approximately 50 students involved across Next Gen ministries.

Ridge Christian is deeply committed to children and students, believing that growth is best celebrated when young families engage through Ridge Kids and Ridge Students. The church is known for its welcoming culture, strong volunteer involvement, and outward focus in the community — particularly in outreach and benevolence toward kids. Life in Coweta moves at a slower pace, offering a safe, family-friendly environment while remaining within easy reach of Tulsa.

The church is elder-led and staff-managed, with a small but collaborative staff team that values trust, autonomy, and shared ownership. Ministry silos are discouraged, and leaders are encouraged to work together while still having freedom to lead within their areas.


Location

“Great for a slow-paced lifestyle… and for kids growing up in a small, loving community.”

Ryan Fankhauser – Campus Pastor


Challenges and Opportunity

  • Clarifying Discipleship Pathways: Ridge Students currently has a strong and welcoming Wednesday-night gathering that attracts both churched and unchurched students, but discipleship beyond that environment is still forming. There is a clear opportunity to define what spiritual growth looks like before and after Wednesday nights, helping students take meaningful next steps toward maturity. The next leader will help shape a more holistic discipleship pathway without losing the relational and invitational heart of the ministry.
  • Leader Development and Expansion: Ridge Christian is rich in willing volunteers who care deeply about students, but many have received little formal training or development. This creates a strong opportunity to establish simple systems for leader coaching, communication, and spiritual growth. A leader who enjoys empowering others will find fertile ground to build a healthy, multiplying volunteer culture.
  • Strong Student Leadership to Build On: The student ministry currently has a particularly strong group of sophomores and juniors, along with solid middle school participation. This provides a rare opportunity for a leader to grow with a cohort of students over the next several years, investing deeply and watching leadership emerge. With intentional discipleship, this group could become a catalytic force for the future of Ridge Students.
  • Vision, Direction, and Creative Momentum: Students and leaders alike are hungry for clearer vision and direction, paired with creativity and fun. While the foundation is healthy, there is room to bring greater intentionality, energy, and polish to gatherings, events, and communication. The right leader will balance structure and creativity—casting vision while keeping student ministry joyful, engaging, and relational.


Leadership

  • The Next Gen Minister reports to the Coweta Campus Preaching Minister (Ryan Fankhauser) and works closely with elders and lay leadership. Ryan has a background in youth ministry and will not be a micromanager, but values collaboration and would love to be a sounding board for the new leaders. 
  • Leadership at Ridge Christian values trust, initiative, and collaboration. The Campus Pastor brings energy, ideas, and deep community knowledge and is eager to empower a leader who can take ownership of Next Gen ministry while remaining aligned with the broader vision of the church.


Key Qualifications

  • A vibrant, growing relationship with Jesus Christ
  • Alignment with Ridge Christian’s theology and mission
  • Ability to teach Scripture clearly and practically
  • Relational leadership style with strong emotional intelligence
  • Comfort leading in a small-staff, high-ownership environment
  • Experience working with students, volunteers, and families
  • Willingness to grow, learn, and lead with humility and confidence

The Kids Minister oversees our Storyline Kids Ministry, leaders, & staff. The Kids Minister will be responsible for helping align Storyline Kids’ ministry (birth- 5th grade) with the overall mission, vision, values, and strategies of the family discipleship team and the church.


Why We Love This Opportunity

I love this role because it gives someone high level leadership opportunities at a growing, thriving church. If someone is wanting to build a great kids ministry at a Gospel-Driven church, serving alongside a growing team, then this is the position for them.

A great match for this position would be:

  • Gospel-Center, Scripture-Driven: Someone who believes in the power of the Gospel and the importance of Scripture on a child’s life and ability to translate it to a child. 
  • Highly Relational: Someone who is warm, leads with humility, doesn’t think they have it all figured out and can relate to parents and kids. 
  • Multiplier of Leaders: Someone who understands that they need to multiply themselves through recruiting, delegating and empowering leaders. 
  • Visionary: Someone who understands and believes the importance of kids ministry and family ministry and is able to transfer that passion and vision to others. 
  • Hungry and Coachable: Someone who is focused on how they can get better, they are curious and they want to grow because they want Storyline kids to be the best it can be.




About This Organization

Storyline Church began as a church plant through the North American Mission Board, launching in February 2015. In 2020, Storyline Church welcomed Dr. JT English as the new Lead Pastor. Under JT’s leadership, we added new staff to our team, saw our church remain unified and hopeful, welcomed hundreds of new people who now call Storyline home, and had new ideas for the next chapter of our story.

In 2024, Storyline embarked on a season called One Sound, where we committed to pray, give, and go in obedience to the Lord to build beyond ourselves and expand our impact in Arvada, invest in the next generation, and plant churches. 

Today, Storyline Church has baptized more than 800 people and regularly gathers over 2,300 in worship and 450 kids on Sundays. More than 1,500 men and women, 200 middle and high school students, and 400 college students connect in Discipleship Spaces throughout the week. And throughout the year, Storyline Members share the gospel in both local missions opportunities and around the world. We are committed to continuing to follow the mission the Lord has given us in the days, months, and years to come. We can’t wait to see how He will continue to lead us.

Location

Arvada is a welcoming, family-friendly community just northwest of Denver, offering the best of both worlds: easy access to the city while still feeling like a connected, suburban community. With the mountains nearby, great parks and trails, and a strong local community, it’s a great place to live, work, and raise a family.



Mission, Vision, and Values

Mission:

  • Live in God’s Story By Knowing Jesus and Loving All People

 

Values:

  • Gospel: The Good News is our hope. We receive God’s grace because of who He is and what He has done. 
  • Scripture: The Bible is for everyone. We teach the Bible as the true story that changes lives. 
  • Discipleship: The good life is in Jesus. We learn to follow and worship Him by taking next steps. 
  • Community: The church is a family. We love one another by using our gifts as we gather, give and serve. 
  • Mission: The good news is for the world. We share Jesus with our neighbors and the nations.


Key Responsibilities


Implement Storyline’s vision of coming alongside families to disciple kids (birth-5th)

  • Execute the scope and sequence for key discipleship outcomes within Storyline Kids
  • Champion Family Discipleship Milestones within Storyline Kids
  • Come alongside the Director of Family Discipleship to develop and implement a strategy to equip parents to become primary disciple makers at home

 

Oversee Storyline Kids

  • Lead Storyline Kids staff team
  • Manage the annual budget for Storyline Kids
  • Maintain excellent and clear communication with parents and families
  • Ensure leaders and families are loved and cared for by maintaining regular contact with them
  • Execute events that provide discipleship and community outreach opportunities throughout the year (Ex. Leader Training, Kids Camp, etc.)
  • Build ministry capacity through the recruitment and training of lay leaders and volunteers to ensure the effective implementation of ministry objectives, goals, and action plans
  • Rotate with the kids team to schedule on weekends

 

Oversee Curriculum within Storyline Kids

  • Work alongside the Director of Family Discipleship to create and implement curriculum in Storyline Kids, including but not limited to:
  • 40 Key Events
  • Alignment series
  • Kids Camp
  • Other discipleship tools

 

First Time Storyline Kids Families

  • Manage First Time Guest Registration and first time guest follow-up, including profile editing

 

Serve on the Family Discipleship Team

  • Attend Storyline staff meetings and staff-related events
  • Attend and give input to team meetings within family discipleship
  • Ensure we are in compliance with all abuse prevention policies



Key Qualifications

  • High capacity and flexibility.
  • Confidence and initiative to anticipate needs within this ministry lane and execute accordingly.
  • Knowledge of developmental and faith stages for preschoolers and children, and the ability to strategically choose and implement appropriate programming for those stages is essential.
  • Experience in a church leading in the spiritual formation area of children, and/or Christian education is preferred.
  • Decisive and proven leader with the ability to encourage, empower, and coach other leaders and teams in the field of education.
  • Organized, strong delegator and follow-through, ability to cast and execute discipleship vision.
  • Ability to develop and organize effective ministry teams made up of staff and volunteer leaders.
  • Ability to create a positive and intentional leadership culture.


For more information, please get in touch with Phil Christian at pchristian@slingshotgroup.org
