  • Lead students and faculty – individually and collectively – through Scripture, prayer, teaching, and discipleship experiences, so that they articulate and align their ministry activities around this vision 

  • Set annual goals through prayer, research and reflection with your teams (students, faculty, and staff) for qualitative and quantitative growth, including conversions and leadership development 

  • Structural Architect: 

You create, develop, align, and leverage ministry plans, programs, teams, and structures to close the gap between current reality and the aspirational goals. 

  • Build leadership teams who trust and partner well with you and who demonstrate spiritual vitality, relational health, and mission alignment 

  • Develop and execute plans to achieve annual goals, evaluating and modifying the plan as needed throughout the year

  • Missional Developer:

Organizational Collaboration

Ministry Partnership Development

  • Raise 100% of the financial budget assigned by your supervisor

Believe and behave consonantly with InterVarsity’s Human Sexuality Theological Paper. Affirm and behave consonantly with InterVarsity’s “Women in Ministry Statement of Affirmation”

WORK ENVIRONMENT/PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS

Join our team to champion a purposeful, fun, safe and engaging discipleship culture for children from birth through sixth grade. Through these groups, we believe ever- increasing numbers of students and faculty from all ethnic groups and areas of the campus will be transformed by the Gospel. We expect to see campuses increasingly become places where people, ideas, and structures flourish to the glory of God. We confidently anticipate that our InterVarsity alumni will become change agents across the country and around the world. LOCATION:

  • University of Oklahoma - Black Campus Ministries
  • Oklahoma State University - General

If you are interested in working at a location that is not listed, fill out the application and indicate where in the relevant question. You are also welcome to input multiple locations and we will take them into consideration. Note that our region of InterVarsity serves the states of Texas, Oklahoma, Arkansas, and Louisiana. If you would like to serve in one of those states, search for it in the search bar to find the openings. During the interview, there will be a greater discussion around location and also the opportunity to go to other places in need of staff.

Spiritual Growth 

You pursue maturity as a disciple of Jesus Christ so that your life and work increasingly reflects a growing love for God, God’s Word, God’s people of every ethnicity and culture, and God’s purposes in the world. To do this, you will: 

  • Pursue a vibrant relationship with the triune God through engagement with Scripture, prayer, and worship, both individually and in community 

  • Develop self-leadership (growing in self-awareness, self-management, relational integrity, and resiliency) 

  • Embrace Scriptural standards for behavior and attitudes 

 

Campus Leadership 

You communicate and model InterVarsity’s vision to see students and faculty transformed, campuses renewed and world changers developed 

  • Create a culture of humble dependence on God and bold expectation in God’s intention to start new witnessing communities throughout the campus and on new campuses 

  • Model – in person and through programs – InterVarsity’s vision and Core Values, including a biblically-defined commitment to engage every ethnic and social group on campus 

  • Lead students and faculty – individually and collectively – through Scripture, prayer, teaching, and discipleship experiences, so that they articulate and align their ministry activities around this vision 

  • Set annual goals through prayer, research and reflection with your teams (students, faculty, and staff) for qualitative and quantitative growth, including conversions and leadership development 

 

You create, develop, align and leverage ministry plans, programs, teams, and structures to close the gap between current reality and the aspirational goals. 

  • Build leadership teams who trust and partner well with you and who demonstrate spiritual vitality, relational health, and mission alignment 

  • Develop and execute plans to achieve annual goals, evaluating and modifying the plan as needed throughout the year 

  • Increase momentum for the vision by aligning programs, structures, conferences and teams around the goals 

  • Mobilize students and faculty to engage their relational networks with the gospel and to start new missional communities 

  • Under the direction of the Area Director, may supervise Ministry Interns and Campus Ministry Interns as delegated 

 

You intentionally gather, invite, and develop diverse groups of students and faculty so that they not only encounter and follow Jesus as Savior and Lord but also advance the mission on campus as participants and leaders.

  • Equip students and faculty so that they think strategically about campus engagement and so that they proclaim – in word, deed, and power – the good news of Jesus, regularly inviting students and faculty to follow him as Savior and Lord 

  • Disciple students and faculty by equipping them to hear the Word, respond actively, and debrief and interpret the experience so that they grow in Christlikeness, reflect our Core Values, and develop ministry skills 

  • Invite, coach, and equip students and faculty to become increasingly effective participants and leaders, including starting new witnessing communities on campuses 

 

Organizational Collaboration 

You work with a network of other local, area, regional, and national InterVarsity staff and volunteers so that our work reflects Biblical standards of excellence, integrity, and partnership. 

  • Partner with and respond positively to the direction and coaching of your supervisors and national leaders 

  • Contribute to collaborative and productive team meetings and relationships 

  • Affiliate chapters under your care and submit Graduating Student Forms in order to increase our partnership with current students and alumni 

  • Use national ministry resources and tools, as requested, including recruiting and/or participating in local, regional, or national conferences as  

  • Complete reporting, planning and review requirements in a timely way so that you and your supervisors can assess and improve your work as a CSM 

  • Comply with all InterVarsity policies and procedures 

 

Ministry Partnership Development 

You will develop a team of partners – churches and individuals (including alumni and community members) – who will resource the ministry financially, in prayer, or volunteer service that advances the mission. 

  • Raise 100% of the financial budget assigned by your supervisor 

  • Communicate regularly with your ministry partners, nurturing the relationship through visits, phone calls, emails and regular prayer letters 

  • Develop on-going, long-lasting partnership with alumni and volunteers 

  • Comply with all Ministry Partnership Policies 

  • Identify and invest in advocates who will build networks of volunteers and donors on InterVarsity’s behalf 

 

Accomplish all other assigned tasks as appropriate

We are looking for an enthusiastic and teachable young leader to help the students of Keystone and our community know and follow Jesus. CURRENT YOUTH MINISTRY


The city of Ankeny is home to over 6,300 middle school and high school students and growing rapidly and the majority of these students remain uninvolved in any gospel ministry. We are passionate about helping these students know and follow Jesus through creating an environment where students belong in authentic community, believe the life-changing power of the gospel, and become who God created them to be. Detailed Job Description


Keystone Statement of Faith

CHILDREN’S AND FAMILY MINISTER

Would you be excited by an opportunity to work with children and families in the heart of the Lower East Side of Manhattan? Our neighborhood is an eclectic mix of Chinese immigrants (speaking Cantonese, Mandarin and Fujianese), Spanish-speaking immigrants and diverse Gen-Z-ers and Millennials.   • Participate in pastoral care, counseling, and home visitation to children and families; and
  • Connect with and follow up on newcomer families and welcome them to church fellowship.

QUALIFICATIONS, TIME COMMITMENT:

  • Growing commitment to the Christian faith, the body of Christ, and God’s work in the world.
  • Assent to the Christian & Missionary Alliance Statement of Faith, including Biblical inerrancy.
  • Have or pursuing MDiv from an accredited seminary (or equivalent bible college degree)
  • Ability to work effectively with children and families, exhibiting creativity, understanding, patience and cultural awareness and flexibility.

  • Full-time position, physical presence at church and in the community.

Description:

This position supports the SAY Detroit Family Clinic

Trinity Health Michigan (THM), is one of the nation's top health care services providers, spanning five counties in Southeastern Michigan. THM represents more than 2,700 physicians and 14,000 nurses and staff, and includes 6 Hospitals, 5 Outpatient Health Centers, 8 Urgent Care Facilities and over 25 Specialty Centers.


The Trinity Health Detroit Ministry is a continuing ministry of Trinity Health. It serves the primary care needs of both uninsured and underinsured individuals throughout the metro Detroit area. All locations strive to eliminate the barriers to accessing health care services. We arrange for specialty care through relationships with specialists and partnerships within Trinity Health. and the larger community.


POSITION PURPOSE


Under physician direction and supervision, prepares patients for office visit, takes vital signs and records in medical record, obtains patient chief complaint, escorts patient to exam room, and prepares patient for physician visit. Assures patients are ready in the exam rooms for physician/mid-level provider arrival. Reviews patient medical record to assure that all needed test results, forms and reports are available to physician/provider. Assists physicians/providers with procedures and processes specimens according to established procedures. Performs in-office testing at direction of physician/provider e.g. EKG's, vision testing, strep tests, urinalysis, suture removals, injections, immunizations, etc. Assists physicians with completion of patient forms as requested by third parties. Arranges patient hospital admissions and test scheduling. Assures that clinical areas and drug sample areas are maintained according to JCAHO and other regulatory agencies. Maintains exam rooms to insure supplies are present and that room and equipment is in working order and in clean condition. May be required to assist with patient phone triage.



ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS AND RESPONSIBILITIES


  • Prepares patient for office visit -obtains patient medical record, assures that necessary reports, forms and test results are available in the record, escort’s patient to exam room. Obtains and documents patient vital signs and chief complaint. Assists patients with gowning as necessary. Assists physician or provider with examinations or procedures. Processes specimens according to established protocols.
  • Completes in-office as directed by physician/provider, e.g. EKG's. injections, immunizations, vision tests, strep cultures, etc. Is able to demonstrate competency in performing these
  • Maintains exam rooms to assure that equipment is in good working condition, supplies are available, room and contents are clean. Assures that room is safe for all ages of patients/visitors, e.g. sharps containers are stored in appropriate fashion.
  • Assists physician/provider with completion of patient forms as requested by third parties, e.g. Workers comp, disability, etc. May be required to assist with copying of records for release of information requests. Assists physician and providers with prescription refill calls and patient call backs.
  • Assists with managed care referral process, pre-authorization, and pre-certification processes. Schedules patient appointments with other physicians or ancillary testing departments at direction of physician. Arranges for inpatient admission to hospital.
  • Assures that clinical work environment meets JCAHO and other regulatory agency requirements. Works in conjunction with MPC Clinical Coordinator, and others to assure compliance. May be requested to assist with the medical record audit process.
  • Documents patient phone calls and advice/treatment given in the patient medical record. Assists physician with keeping problem lists and medication lists up to date. Assists physician with preventive medicine tracking, e.g. mammograms, Halc for diabetics, well-baby and well-child exams, etc.
  • Develops and maintains appropriate patient logs and records, e.g., test ordered, such that tracking is possible to insure that test results are received, reviewed by physician and communication is given to the patient.
  • Assists physician and Office Coordinator in the development and maintenance of procedures that accomplish recall systems for patient testing, e.g. HalC for diabetics, Coumadin logs, etc.
  • Maintains patient confidentiality of information pertinent to patients, physicians, providers, families and visitors. Discusses patient and hospital information only among appropriate personnel in appropriately private places.
  • Evaluates factors related to safety, effectiveness, efficiency, environmental concerns and cost and chooses the option that results in acceptable outcomes.
  • Receives and evaluates incoming telephone calls according to Best Practice Model for MPC and SJMHS customer service standards. Involves physician and or providers as appropriate to assure patient triage protocols are followed.
  • Maintains good rapport and cooperative relationships. Approaches conflict in a constructive manner. H~DS
  • Identify problems, offer solutions and participate in their resolution.
  • Behaves in accordance with the Mission, Vision, and Values of SJMHS
  • Assumes responsibility for performance of job duties in the safest possible manner, to assure personal safety and that of coworkers, and to report all preventable hazards and unsafe practices immediately to management.
  • Knowledgeable of age-specific needs of patients following appropriate guidelines. Interacts with patients and others in a non-judgmental and nondiscriminatory manner that is sensitive to cultural, racial and ethnic diversity.

REQUIRED EDUCATION, EXPERIENCE AND CERTIFICATION/LICENSURE

  •  CMA, RMA, CCMA, or NCMA, certification through an NCCA accredited program approved provider list includes the American Association of Medical Assistants (AAMA), the American Medical Technologists (AMT), the National HealthCareer Association (NHA) or the National Center for Competency Testing (NCCT).  Required;
  • 2 years previous clinical experience or equivalent combination of education and experience preferred.
  • Formal education in medical terminology and anatomy & physiology preferred

REQUIRED SKILLS AND ABILITIES


  • Familiarity with common prescription drugs
  • Ability to demonstrate competency in obtaining accurate vital signs and in the performance of in-office procedures
  • Must participate in and be knowledgeable in mandatory safety education and environment of care, e.g. infection control, universal precautions, medical waste disposal, quality control and proficiency testing for office equipment, proper handling of specimens, electrical safety, sterilization techniques, etc.
  • Experience with managed care plans and the associated requirements of patient referrals

Fellowship Alliance Chapel (FAC) seeks an experienced Senior Pastor to lead our established congregation of 1,200+ in Medford, New Jersey. This role offers the opportunity to build upon 40+ years of ministry while providing strategic leadership through facility stewardship and growth.

Position Overview: The Senior Pastor will provide primary preaching and teaching, lead strategic planning, oversee 20+ staff, and partner closely with the elder board on major organizational initiatives including debt reduction and facility optimization. The ideal candidate values collaborative leadership and thrives in a team-oriented governance environment.

Leadership Structure: The Senior Pastor serves in collaborative partnership with a plurality of elders who provide governance oversight and spiritual guidance. This team-based leadership model emphasizes mutual accountability, shared decision-making, and unified vision casting.

Our church is a member of the Christian and Missionary Alliance with an annual operating budget of ~$4M. FAC stewards multiple buildings on campus plus a lake/summer day camp. FAC is a single-site, multigenerational congregation committed to helping more people live Jesus-centered and missionally engaged lives. A recent campus building project positions us well for continued growth.

Financial Context: FAC maintains strong financial position with recent land acquisitions requiring strategic debt management. The Senior Pastor will collaborate with the Finance Committee and Board of Elders on stewardship initiatives.

SUMMARY OF POSITION


The Director of Student Ministry at MBC Prince William will lead a ministry to middle school and high school students and their families that is centered on Jesus, rooted in Scripture, and focused on helping students take meaningful next steps of faith. We are looking for a leader who is burdened to reach students across Prince Willliam County with the gospel of Jesus Christ, especially students who are unchurched, dechurched, spiritually curious, or disconnected from Christian community.

This leader will give primary attention to reaching, discipling, and sending students as followers of Jesus who live with faith, courage, and purpose in their schools, teams, neighborhoods, and friend groups. The Director of Student Ministry will also inspire, equip, and shepherd a Serve Team of adult leaders to do the work of ministry by helping students feel known, loved, challenged, and sent.


RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Develop and lead a missionary-minded Student Ministry strategy that reaches, disciples, and sends middle school and high school students across Prince William County with the gospel of Jesus Christ.
  • Build a culture where every student is encouraged to reach one person with the hope of the gospel, take next steps as a disciple of Jesus, and live as a witness in their schools, teams, neighborhoods, and friend groups.
  • Recruit, inspire, equip, and shepherd a Serve Team of adult leaders who joyfully do the work of ministry by helping students feel known, loved, challenged, and sent.
  • Faithfully teach God’s Word in Student Ministry environments in a way that is biblically grounded, culturally aware, and compelling for churched, unchurched, dechurched, and spiritually curious students.
  • Disciple and develop student leaders who are growing in Christ, serving the church, and taking personal responsibility for the mission of God in their generation.
  • Partner with parents by providing encouragement, resources, and practical tools that help them disciple their students in the everyday rhythms of life.
  • Create welcoming and intentional environments where students can build meaningful relationships, hear the gospel clearly, ask honest questions, and take next steps toward Jesus.
  • Collaborate with the MBC Student Ministry team to plan and execute church-wide moments such as Winter Camp, Summer Camp, and other strategic events that help students encounter Jesus and grow as disciples.
  • Establish and maintain clear safety, security, and care practices that protect minors and create trustworthy ministry environments for students, parents, and leaders.

 

 

OTHER MINISTRIES / RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Faithfully participate in the life of McLean Bible Church through membership, worship, and ongoing involvement in a Church Group.
  • Serve as a trusted member of the MBC Prince William team by contributing to staff meetings, ministry planning, prayer rhythms, and location-wide initiatives.
  • Provide care and ministry support as needed, including student and family care, visitation, assimilation, follow-up, and other ministry responsibilities assigned by the MBC Prince William Location Pastor.
  • Use personal gifting, leadership, and ministry experience to strengthen the overall health and mission of MBC Prince William.
  • Model a life of spiritual maturity, humility, collaboration, and joyful service among staff, Serve Team members, students, and families.


REQUIREMENTS

  • A passionate disciple of Jesus Christ who continually seeks to abide in Christ and demonstrates the biblical qualifications for spiritual leadership.
  • A proven disciple-maker who has helped others grow as followers of Jesus and is able to equip students and leaders to make disciples.
  • A spiritually mature and emotionally healthy leader who demonstrates humility, wisdom, integrity, and consistency in both personal and public life.
  • A theologically grounded leader who is in agreement with MBC doctrine and teaching.
  • A servant leader who can inspire, equip, and shepherd adult leaders to joyfully do the work of ministry.
  • A missionary-minded leader with a demonstrated burden to reach unchurched, dechurched, and spiritually curious students.
  • An effective implementer who can take vision and build clear ministry rhythms, leader development pathways, and student discipleship environments.
  • A humble learner who continually seeks feedback, evaluates ministry effectiveness, and develops ways to strengthen Student Ministry at MBC Prince William.
  • An effective communicator who can teach Scripture faithfully, communicate clearly with parents and leaders, and connect meaningfully with students.
  • A collaborative team member who works well with others and resolves conflict in a biblical and healthy way.

















#ZR

Do you have a passion for building community within the body of Christ and a strong desire to get adults fully engaged with others to do life together while pushing roots deep into the soil of God’s word? 

Would you like to be an integral part of helping people find hope and healing as they journey with others in a Christ-centered care and recovery ministry?

Are you a strong leader who loves developing, equipping, and deploying volunteer teams, and seeing them use their gifts and abilities to further God’s Kingdom?

Do you have exceptional interpersonal skills, excellent discernment, and a healthy biblical approach to conflict resolution? And would you find great joy in using those gifts to encourage adults in their relationship with Jesus Christ?

 

Our ideal candidate for this people-focused pastoral staff position will be someone who will use the unique gifts mentioned above to sheperd and oversee the adult discipleship ministries at the DeKalb Campus. In collaboration with the one-church adult ministry team and the campus pastor, this person serves as a key contributor to the strategic development of Community Groups, Adult Ministries programs, events, and initiatives for the campus. This role works closely with the campus pastor to provide leadership in pastoral care, connections, and outreach on campus, while helping people connect with the church. The adult ministries pastor plays a crucial role by coming alongside those who are hurting or need care through the church's weekly Care Night support and recovery ministry. We see this person as a vital key in helping people become thriving followers of Jesus Christ, who are fully engaged in the life of Christ Community Church.

In addition to all Teacher responsibilities, the Lead Teacher supports the onboarding, observation, and mentorship of new teachers within their age group, helping to verify skills and foster a culture of excellence and spiritual growth. This position is designed for experienced educators who demonstrate spiritual leadership, strong communication, and a heart for serving others.
 

Classroom & Instructional Leadership

  • Plan and deliver daily activities that support spiritual, social, emotional, and academic development, integrating Bible stories, prayer, and Christian values in age-appropriate ways.
  • Maintain a safe, clean, and age-appropriate learning environment; follow all licensing, NAC, and CACFP requirements.
  • Use varied instructional strategies to meet diverse learning needs.
  • Track attendance, developmental milestones, and classroom routines consistently.

Mentorship & Onboarding

  • Serve as a mentor for new teachers within the assigned age group, providing classroom observation, feedback, and support during onboarding.
  • Assist with skills verification and practical training for new hires, using Lionheart’s New Employee Orientation tools and checklists.
  • Model best practices in classroom management, curriculum implementation, and spiritual integration.
  • Support the development of a positive, collaborative team culture.

Leadership & Professional Development

  • Participate in Lead Teacher orientation/training and ongoing leadership development.
  • Take initiative in identifying and addressing classroom or team needs.
  • Assist Academy Directors and Assistant Directors with special projects, pilot programs, or process improvements as needed.
  • Demonstrate flexibility and a willingness to serve across age groups or support academy-wide initiatives.

Family Engagement

  • Build strong partnerships with families through daily communication, milestone sharing, and spiritual updates.
  • Respond promptly and professionally to family concerns.

Team & Academy Responsibilities

  • Collaborate with co-teachers, floaters, and leadership to ensure smooth classroom operations.
  • Participate in staff meetings, training sessions, and academy events.
  • Assist with housekeeping, laundry, and restocking supplies as needed.

 

  • At least 18 years of age; high school diploma or GED required.
  • Meets all state minimum standards and qualifications for an Early Childhood Lead Teacher; CDA, AA, or BA in Early Childhood Education preferred.
  • Minimum 1 year of experience in a licensed child care facility.
  • Demonstrated spiritual leadership and alignment with Lionheart’s mission and values.
  • Positive peer and family relationships; strong communication skills.
  • Criminal background check.

Competencies

  • Spiritual Alignment: Models a Christ-centered life and integrates faith into daily work.
  • Mentorship & Leadership: Guides, encourages, and supports peers and new hires.
  • Intentional Relationships: Builds trust and collaboration with children, families, and staff.
  • Heart to Serve: Joyfully serves with humility and strength.
  • Tenacity & Adaptability: Perseveres through challenges and responds creatively to change.
  • Effective Communication: Clearly conveys updates, feedback, and biblical principles.

Skills

  • Safety & Compliance: Maintains sight-and-sound supervision, adheres to licensing, NAC, and CACFP requirements, and ensures a safe and clean classroom.
  • Curriculum Implementation: Plans and delivers developmentally appropriate spiritual and academic activities tailored to children’s needs.
  • Family Engagement: Builds trust through daily communication, milestone sharing, and proactive partnership with families.
  • Observation & Documentation: Accurately records attendance, care routines, developmental progress, and CACFP point-of-service counts.
  • Effective Communication: Clearly conveys updates to families, collaborates with co-teachers, and models biblical principles.

Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)

  • Successful onboarding and retention of new teachers.
  • Positive feedback from mentees, families, and team members.
  • Compliance with all state licensing, NAC, CACFP, and safety standards.
  • Accurate and timely completion of documentation.
  • Demonstrated teamwork and alignment with Lionheart’s mission and values.

Description

Job Title: Campus Minister, Discipleship

Ministry/Department: Multisite

Reports to: Campus Pastor

Status: Full-time, exempt

Supervisory Role: No

Objective

The goal of this position is to equip the saints for the work of ministry and the discipleship of The Church of Eleven22® church family. This position will partner with the corresponding Campus Pastor to shepherd the flock.

Key Responsibilities

  • Model spiritual intensity in and assist in the execution of weekend worship gatherings—requests could include stage communication, prayer and anointing and preparing worship spaces
  • Conduct general ministerial responsibilities alongside the Campus Pastor(s) and ministerial staff to shepherd and care for the local congregation; requests will include:
    • Aiding in officiating and executing weddings and Celebrations of Life
    • Devoting time weekly to hospital visitations, ministerial counseling and ministering to those in need
    • Providing the sacraments of baptism and Communion
  • Lead the disciple-making journey of congregants by helping individuals identify their spiritual gifts and equipping the saints with the skills necessary to accomplish the ministry at hand; this includes:
    • Teaching baptism, covenant membership and Growth Track classes
    • Meeting weekly with serve staff to pray, disciple and empower them for ministry
    • Leading serve staff huddles at each service to educate, inform and inspire serve teams
  • Lead the campuses efforts to integrate multiplication efforts across ministry areas; this includes:
    • Leading serve staff teams for multiplication connection and short-term trip send-offs
    • Develop a team of short-term trip leads
    • Encourage, equip and care for campus multiplication staff
    • Connect groups and ministry areas to local ministry and Outreach partners
  • Collaborate with Central Ministries to deliver ministry at the local level through equipping congregants. Key central partners include Disciple Groups Director, Connections Director and Care Director
  • Build, lead and shepherd serve staff teams to accomplish the ministry objectives of welcome, disciple groups and connect
  • Perform other duties as required by Campus Pastor and/or the Associate Campus Pastor

Competencies

  • Model The Church of Eleven22 mission, vision and core values
  • Ability to maintain strict confidentiality
  • Ability to adapt to change
  • Strong proactive communication skills
  • Ability to learn and use new computer software
  • Demonstrated ability to build organizational relationships/partnerships (internal and external)
  • Proven track record of effective leadership, judgment and above-reproach character
  • Demonstrated ability to shepherd and equip staff, serve staff and congregants
  • Excellent written and oral communication skills

Education and Experience

  • Three to five years of ministry leadership experience, including experience managing teams, volunteers and/or ministry areas
  • Bachelor’s degree required

Position Type/Expected Hours of Work

Work Hours Expectations: 40 hours or more

Schedule Expectations: Work hours include all worship gathering times (typically Thursday and Sunday), with weekly rhythms of working in and around the campus office on Mondays, Wednesdays and Thursdays, at the Central Office on Tuesdays and evenings as needed for events, disciple groups and weekly worship services on Thursday evenings and Sundays.

The church has several big events (“All-Skates”) throughout the year to help further the mission of Eleven22. These events are mandatory for all staff to be in attendance and may vary, depending on the vision cast for the current year.

Our entire staff family is called to action, so that we can continue to be a movement for all people to discover and deepen a relationship with Jesus Christ.

Work Environment/physical Demands

This role operates in a dynamic church and campus environment, including offices, worship spaces, classrooms and offsite locations such as hospitals, homes and event venues. The position requires a flexible schedule, including evenings and weekends and involves periods of standing, walking, lifting items up to 25 pounds and active participation in worship gatherings, classes, pastoral care and ministry events. Occasional travel between campus and central ministry locations is expected.

Ministerial Exception

The ministerial exception furthers the purposes of the Free Exercise and Establishment Clauses of the First Amendment by barring legal claims against church bodies by staff members who perform religious functions. All church pastors are subject to the exception, but a formal ministerial credential is not required. While there is no rigid formula to determine other church staff members that qualify, various factors are considered to determine which staff members are subject to the ministerial exception (please see handbook).

Staff members who qualify under the ministerial exception are not covered by federal and state employment and anti-discrimination laws. Please see the Human Resources Ministry team if you have questions on whether you are subject to the ministerial exception.

Code of Conduct

  1. We live authenticity
  2. We are gospel-centered and mission-focused
  3. We are family
  4. We are lifelong learners
  5. We aim for excellence in the experience with zero excess
  6. We choose to trust
  7. We pray 1st and decide 2nd
  8. We glorify God by honoring others
  9. Our team unites under clear vision
  10. We walk in humble confidence

EEO Statement

The Church of Eleven22 provides equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants for employment and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any type without regard to race, color, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status or any other characteristic protected by federal, state or local laws. The Church of Eleven22 reserves the right to discriminate on the basis of religion to the full extent permitted by law.

Title: Lead Pastor (Full-Time)

Church: Moosic Alliance Community Church

Location: Moosic, PA

About the Community
Moosic is a close-knit suburban community in northeast Pennsylvania’s Lackawanna County, between Scranton and Wilkes-Barre. It offers small-town character with easy access to city amenities, the Poconos and major routes to NYC and Philadelphia. Moosic is part of the Ridge and Valley province of the Appalachian Mountains.

About the Church
Moosic Alliance Community Church has served this region since 1973. It is debt-free and averages 50–100 in Sunday attendance. The vision of the church is to walk as Jesus walked. Their missions it to point people to Christ, build them up in Christ, and equip them to serve for Christ.

The Opportunity
We’re seeking a lead pastor who will partner with the elders and leaders to develop disciples who make disciples. You’ll build a clear pathway for people to get connected, grow, serve, be cared for, multiply, and reach the community.

Key Responsibilities

  • Preach and teach the Word of God
  • Lead alongside the elders in vision, direction and discipleship strategy
  • Provide pastoral care and shepherding to the congregation
  • Identify, equip and release leaders
  • Lead the church in outreach to the Moosic area

Qualifications

  • Associate’s degree or higher, or at least 30 credit hours in Bible, theology and ministry
  • Preferred: 5+ years of pastoral staff experience (or equivalent ministry experience)
  • Must be willing to pursue licensing and ordination with The Christian and Missionary Alliance

Compensation
Full-time salary, health coverage, parsonage, and additional benefits to be discussed.

The History
In the 1890s, Rev. William T. MacArthur was sent to plant a church in the Pittston area. Using innovative “cell church” methods, the movement spread across northeast Pennsylvania and planted daughter churches in Duryea, Avoca, Glendale and Moosic. More than 40 people from this movement went into full-time ministry, missions, and Christian education. We pray God will do it again.

To be considered for this position, please complete the application to include your testimony, resume and other background information related to the position.

If the district office has reviewed your application and they think you may be a potential match for the position, the hiring manager will reach out to you for next steps.

This position requires licensing with The Christian & Missionary Alliance. To learn more about The Alliance and requirements for licensing, please visit our website

Please do not contact the church directly.

Dover Bible Church is a church located in rural Illinois and is seeking a pastor to join the elder team as a "leader among equals." It is expected that the pastor will demonstrate Holy Spirit-filled servant leadership and continue to grow the gospel footprint of the church and lead in the shepherding of the congregation.

To be considered for this position, please complete the application to include your testimony, resume and other background information related to the position.

Please do not contact the church directly.

Our church... is a non-denominational multi-site church with four St. Louis-area campuses where we gather each weekend to study this ancient story found in Scripture that is still transforming lives today. We believe church should be a place where believers in Jesus and skeptics can stand side-by-side to study truth and ask tough questions. We blend teaching and worship with art and technology to create a service where you can experience the message of Jesus in practical and life-changing ways.

Kids Coordinator......provides leadership and oversight for the Nursery/Twos, PreK or Elementary rooms at the Chesterfield campus, with primary responsibility for weekend execution and the recruitment, development, care, and management of coaches and volunteers. The coordinator works to create an engaging, safe, relational, and spiritually formative environment where kids can grow in their relationship with Jesus and volunteers are equipped and empowered to serve effectively. The ideal candidate is highly relational, flexible, and organized, with a passion for Jesus Christ, The Crossing’s vision, and helping children become fully devoted followers of Christ.

ESSENTIAL JOB RESPONSIBILITIES

Weekend Service Leadership

  • Prepare for and oversee coaches and volunteers during assigned weekend services, ensuring rooms are appropriately staffed, equipped, organized, and ready for ministry.
  • Communicate relevant weekend information and ensure programming is implemented effectively.
  • Empower coaches to lead their teams and provide ongoing support, feedback, and direction.
  • Engage with parents and families, providing encouragement and addressing behavioral or care concerns.
  • Step in and serve wherever needed to ensure an effective weekend ministry experience.

Volunteer Leadership & Development

  • Help build the volunteer team by inviting people to join the team.
  • Identify emerging leaders, invest in their development, and equip/empower them to take on greater responsibility.
  • Provide care and support to volunteers and families during times of crisis as needed.

Ministry Operations & Participation

  • Attend and actively participate in KidsCrossing staff, campus, and other ministry meetings as needed.
  • Participate in special events, team celebrations, baptisms, kid-focused events, and other ministry initiatives.
  • Perform other duties as assigned by the supervisor.

Spiritual Gifts Helpful For This Position

  • Leadership
  • Encouragement
  • Administration
  • Shepherding

Character Traits Needed For This Position

  • Spiritual Maturity
  • Team Player and Team Builder
  • Trustworthy, reliable, teachable, humble, flexible

MUST HAVES FOR ALL STAFF AT THE CROSSING

  • Attend a service at one of The Crossing campuses on a weekly basis
  • Passionate about their relationship with God
  • Baptized after making the thoughtful decision to follow Christ
  • Regard the Bible as God’s final authority in all areas of Christian life and desire to be wholly obedient to it
  • Wholeheartedly affirm The Crossing’s Statement of Faith, including our view on Baptism
  • Live a lifestyle consistent with scriptural principles


Apply today and see why The Crossing may be a great fit for you!

Church of the Holy Spirit seeks a part-time Youth Minister to lead and grow a vibrant Catholic youth ministry for middle and high school students. Working with the Director of Religious Education (DRE) and parish clergy, the Youth Minister will help young people encounter Christ, grow in faith and prayer, and participate actively in the life of the Church. The ideal candidate is a practicing Catholic who is passionate about mentoring young people and helping them develop a lifelong relationship with Christ and His Church.  Schedule: Part-time, approximately 15–20 hours per week, including regular evening programming and occasional weekends, retreats, service projects, and parish events.

Compensation: Hourly, commensurate with experience and qualifications.

Key Responsibilities

  • Plan and lead engaging youth ministry programming, including regular gatherings, social activities, retreats, service projects, and summer trips.
  • Build meaningful relationships with students and foster a welcoming, faith-filled youth community.
  • Encourage participation in Mass, Eucharistic Adoration, Confession, parish events, prayer, and other opportunities for spiritual growth.

  • Passion for working with middle and high school students.
  • Strong interpersonal, organizational, and communication skills.
  • Ability to build positive relationships with youth, families, volunteers, staff, and clergy.
  • Previous experience in Catholic youth ministry, religious education, teaching, or a related field preferred.
  • Availability for evening programs and occasional weekends, retreats, service projects, and parish events.

JOB TITLE:                  Six78 Worship Leader

DEPARTMENT:          Family Ministry

REPORTS TO:             Youth Director

STATUS:                       Hourly non-exempt

HOURS:                        Full-time (40)

LOCATION:               2401 W Cypress Creek Rd. Fort Lauderdale, FL 33309

_____________________________________________________________________

At Calvary Chapel, we are called to make disciples of Jesus Christ by connecting people to God, people to people, and people to outreach. Our vision is to reach our community and change our world. As a staff member, it’s not what we do, it's who we are.

 

Your passion:

You must have a passion to disciple, train, and lead students in a growing relationship with Jesus Christ; to lead students in worship and develop them to lead their peers; to assist the worship ministry, as well as the youth ministry in making disciples. This leader desires to see young men and women not only be leaders, but friends and servants to students around them. The candidate will strive to create an atmosphere where students, as a body of believers, are able to freely worship their God!

 

You are:

  • Convinced a relationship with Jesus changes everything in a person’s life

  • Committed to keeping your family as your first ministry

  • Dedicated in your personal study of God’s Word 

  • Consistently placing a high priority on worship and your personal prayer life

  • An excellent and generous steward of your personal finances

  • Obedient to God to take a Sabbath and make space for soul-keeping

  • Deeply compassionate towards people who are in need or hurting

  • Excited about global missions and local outreach - you want to change the world 

  • A part of a healthy friendship community and accountability circle 

  • Willing to give up personal pleasures and freedoms in order to live a life above reproach and that is aligned with our Leadership Covenant

  • Passionate about discipleship and hanging out with middle and high school students

 

You will:

  • Shepherd, disciple, and develop current youth worship leaders and musicians. (30%)

  • Prepare and practice leading worship in weekly Six78 services. (HSM/campuses if available) (15%)

    • Manage our youth venues (gear, platform, staging, sound).

    • Find, arrange, and chart music for the student worship teams.

  • Shepherd, disciple, develop and be available for counseling and discipleship of current youth as opportunities arise. (5%)

  • Lead, plan and execute youth discipleship opportunities, events and outreaches.  This includes off and on campus opportunities for students to engage in community outside of regular service times.   (10%)

  • Assist in various youth ministry tasks and ministry opportunities as needed(5%)

  • Lead a First Priority Club at a local middle school (5%)

 

You have:

  • Experience and passion for leading worship

  • Musical proficiency in both singing and instrumentation

  • Proficiency in Planning Center and Ableton

  • The ability to teach and train

  • Excellent interpersonal and communication skills for relating effectively with staff members, leadership and the church body

  • Flexibility with good time management skills

It would be incredible if:

Full time (40 hours/week) hourly non-exempt

Campus Staff Minister - NYC

Work Location:

New York

Job Type:

Full time

POSITION SUMMARY

God has called InterVarsity to plant and to build witnessing communities of students and faculty who follow Jesus on college and university campuses. Through these groups, we believe ever- increasing numbers of students and faculty from all ethnic groups and areas of the campus will be transformed by the Gospel. We expect to see campuses increasingly become places where people, ideas, and structures flourish to the glory of God. We confidently anticipate that our InterVarsity alumni will become change agents across the country and around the world. We pursue this calling by discerning and actively participating in what God is already doing on campus. This is the essence of being a Campus Staff Minister (CSM).

ESSENTIAL COMMITMENTS/RESPONSIBILITIES 

Spiritual Growth 

As a Campus Staff Minister, you pursue maturity as a disciple of Jesus Christ so that your life and work increasingly reflect a growing love for God, God’s Word, God’s people of every ethnicity and culture, and God’s purposes in the world. To do this, you will: 

  • Pursue a vibrant relationship with the triune God through engagement with Scripture, prayer, and worship, both individually and in community 

  • Develop self-leadership (growing in self-awareness, self-management, relational integrity, and resiliency) 

  • Embrace Scriptural standards for behavior and attitudes 

 

Campus Leadership 

As a Campus Staff Minister, you increase the number of witnessing communities, as well as the size, health, spiritual maturity, and campus-wide influence of existing witnessing communities of students and faculty by being a: 

  • Visionary Guide: 

You communicate and model InterVarsity’s vision to see students and faculty transformed, campuses renewed, and world changers developed 

  • Create a culture of humble dependence on God and bold expectation in God’s intention to start new witnessing communities throughout the campus and on new campuses 

  • Model – in person and through programs – InterVarsity’s vision and Core Values, including a biblically-defined commitment to engage every ethnic and social group on campus 

  • Lead students and faculty – individually and collectively – through Scripture, prayer, teaching, and discipleship experiences, so that they articulate and align their ministry activities around this vision 

  • Set annual goals through prayer, research and reflection with your teams (students, faculty, and staff) for qualitative and quantitative growth, including conversions and leadership development 

  • Structural Architect: 

You create, develop, align, and leverage ministry plans, programs, teams, and structures to close the gap between current reality and the aspirational goals. 

  • Build leadership teams who trust and partner well with you and who demonstrate spiritual vitality, relational health, and mission alignment 

  • Develop and execute plans to achieve annual goals, evaluating and modifying the plan as needed throughout the year 

  • Increase momentum for the vision by aligning programs, structures, conferences, and teams around the goals 

  • Mobilize students and faculty to engage their relational networks with the gospel and to start new missional communities 

  • Under the direction of the Area Director, may supervise Ministry Interns and Campus Ministry Interns as delegated 

  • Missional Developer: 

You intentionally gather, invite, and develop diverse groups of students and faculty so that they not only encounter and follow Jesus as Savior and Lord but also advance the mission on campus as participants and leaders. 

  • Create ways for faculty and students to encounter and follow Jesus through Scripture, worship, prayer, mission experiences, conferences, etc. 

  • Equip students and faculty so that they think strategically about campus engagement and so that they proclaim – in word, deed, and power – the good news of Jesus, regularly inviting students and faculty to follow him as Savior and Lord 

  • Disciple students and faculty by equipping them to hear the Word, respond actively, and debrief and interpret the experience so that they grow in Christlikeness, reflect our Core Values, and develop ministry skills 

  • Invite, coach, and equip students and faculty to become increasingly effective participants and leaders, including starting new witnessing communities on campuses 

 

Organizational Collaboration 

As a Campus Staff Minister, you have joined a national mission. Therefore, you work with a network of other local, area, regional, and national InterVarsity staff and volunteers so that our work reflects Biblical standards of excellence, integrity, and partnership. 

  • Partner with and respond positively to the direction and coaching of your supervisors and national leaders 

  • Contribute to collaborative and productive team meetings and relationships 

  • Affiliate chapters under your care and submit Graduating Student Forms in order to increase our partnership with current students and alumni 

  • Use national ministry resources and tools, as requested, including recruiting and/or participating in local, regional, or national conferences as  

  • Complete reporting, planning and review requirements in a timely way so that you and your supervisors can assess and improve your work as a CSM 

  • Comply with all InterVarsity policies and procedures 

 

Ministry Partnership Development 

As a Campus Staff Minister, you will develop a team of partners – churches and individuals (including alumni and community members) – who will resource the ministry financially, in prayer, or volunteer service that advances the mission. 

  • Raise 100% of the financial budget assigned by your supervisor 

  • Communicate regularly with your ministry partners, nurturing the relationship through visits, phone calls, emails and regular prayer letters 

  • Develop on-going, long-lasting partnership with alumni and volunteers 

  • Comply with all Ministry Partnership Policies 

  • Identify and invest in advocates who will build networks of volunteers and donors on InterVarsity’s behalf 

 

Accomplish all other assigned tasks as appropriate 

 

QUALIFICATIONS (common to all levels of CSM) 

  • Annually affirm InterVarsity’s Statement of Agreement (Doctrinal Basis and Purpose Statement). Abide by InterVarsity’s Code of Conduct. Believe and behave consonantly with InterVarsity’s Human Sexuality Theological Paper. Affirm and behave consonantly with InterVarsity’s “Women in Ministry Statement of Affirmation” 

  • Bachelor’s degree for CSMs assigned to a four-year campus. A minimum of an Associate’s degree for CSMs assigned to a two-year campus or a community college 

  • Strong interpersonal skills (including ability to minister to diverse ethnic communities and faculty) 

  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills 

  • Demonstrated problem solving skills 

  • Familiarity with word processing, presentation, email, and spreadsheet software 

 

WORK ENVIRONMENT/PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS 

The CSM position leads ministry in a college campus environment. A designated office space may or may not be available. The CSM is required to travel to on-campus and off- campus sites as appropriate. Off-campus travel includes, but is not limited to: student ministry conferences, Ministry Partnership Development meetings, and InterVarsity- sponsored training sessions, meetings, and conferences. The CSM is regularly required to communicate with others, and routinely uses standard office equipment such as computers, phones, photocopiers, filing cabinets, etc. 

Pay Range: $50,772.00 - $67,680.00 per year

Pay: This position is funded through personal fundraising. Accordingly, compensation will vary based on the ability of the individual to secure a donor team to fund the cost of his/her salary. The anticipated salary range for this position on a full-time basis (40 hours/week) is dependent on a variety of factors, including location and cost of living. The actual salary received, including any geographic adjustment to account for location and cost of living, is subject to the individual’s ability to raise funds necessary to cover the full amount of such salary within the range set forth in the job posting details.

Benefits:

We offer a competitive benefits package, including health care and retirement savings with a match. Eligibility is based on employee type and hours worked.  Benefits include the following:

  • 403(b) Retirement Savings Plan

  • 403(b) matching contributions

  • Dental insurance

  • Employee assistance program

  • Employee discounts

  • Flexible work schedule

  • Flexible spending accounts

  • Health insurance

  • Health savings account

  • Life insurance

  • Paid time off

  • Parental leave

  • Professional development assistance

  • Vision insurance

Equal Employment Opportunity: 

 

InterVarsity Christian Fellowship/USA is both an equal opportunity employer and a faith-based religious organization. We conduct hiring without regard to race, color, ancestry, national origin, citizenship, age, sex, marital status, parental status, membership in any labor organization, political ideology, or disability of an otherwise qualified individual. The status of InterVarsity Christian Fellowship/USA as an equal opportunity employer does not prevent the organization from hiring staff based on their religious beliefs so that all staff share the same religious commitment.  Pursuant to the Civil Rights Act of 1964, Section 702 (42 U.S.C. 2000e 1(a)) InterVarsity Christian Fellowship/USA has the right to, and does, hire only candidates who agree with InterVarsity’s Statement of Agreement: Purpose and Doctrinal Basis because InterVarsity believes that each and every staff plays a vital role in advancing InterVarsity’s mission and purposes.

About This Organization

The mission of Sequim Community Church is “responding to God’s love by inviting people to join us as we become more like Jesus.” This is a strong community in a beautiful part of the country. The Worship Director role is an opportunity to not just lead worship, but to build a thriving worship culture in a church that values the presence of God.


Position Description

The Director of Worship is responsible for designing and implementing worship experiences and events that are both biblically significant and culturally relevant. This person shall provide spiritual, artistic, and administrative leadership to the music ministry and all areas of church life and ministry related to worship and the arts.

 

Key Responsibilities:

  • Develop and implement a philosophy of worship and arts ministry, which is consistent with the overall philosophy of ministry of Sequim Community Church.
  • Provide vision and leadership to the Worship, Music & Arts Committee.
  • Recruit, lead, supervise and provide ongoing training and discipleship of both paid and volunteer staff for worship, music & arts.
  • Plan and share leadership of all worship services and special services as deemed appropriate, in consultation with the Lead Pastor.
  • Direct or provide direction for the musical teams at SCC.
  • Select, guide, train, and shepherd members of the SCC Worship, Music & Arts teams.
  • Responsible for the acquisition and maintenance of all musical instruments and other equipment used primarily in worship and arts ministries.
  • Perform or assign administrative duties necessary to the functioning of the worship and arts ministries.
  • Provide opportunities at all age levels for the congregation to grow in the understanding and practice of Christian worship and in the use of the arts in the service of God.

74,000 – 82,000

Company Description

The purpose of the Special Needs Ministry at CCV is to provide an inclusive and supportive environment where individuals with special needs can grow in their understanding of God’s love. The Special Needs Pastor will collaborate with the Kids/Students Ministry to ensure that children, teens, and adults are included to the greatest extent possible. The Special Needs Pastor will assist the ministry efforts of the Kids Ministry by providing excellence in the implementation, development, and execution of Special Needs services on the campus.  

Job Description

Key Responsibilities  

Volunteer Leadership & Development 

  • Identify, recruit, and onboard volunteers with a heart for special needs ministry, ensuring all safety protocols and background checks are completed. 
  • Provide ongoing training, coaching, and spiritual development to equip volunteers for success in inclusive ministry environments. 
  • Foster a culture of encouragement, accountability, and excellence among volunteers through regular communication and appreciation. 

Family Engagement & Support 

  • Build authentic relationships with families through one-on-one interactions, school visits, and community engagement. 
  • Serve as a pastoral resource for families, offering spiritual guidance, emotional support, and practical tools for navigating life with special needs. 
  • Connect new families to the ministry, helping them feel welcomed, understood, and empowered to participate fully. 

Program Oversight & Execution 

  • Lead all aspects of Special Needs Ministry programming across age groups (Kids, Students, Adults), ensuring experiences are inclusive, engaging, and Christ-centered. 
  • Design and implement curriculum and activities that reflect biblical truth while accommodating diverse learning and sensory needs. 
  • Ensure environments are safe, welcoming, and tailored to the unique needs of individuals with disabilities. 

Strategic Collaboration 

  • Partner with the Kids and Students Ministry teams to integrate special needs participants into broader church programming wherever possible. 
  • Collaborate with the Campus Pastor and other ministry leaders to grow attendance and deepen engagement within the special needs community. 
  • Lead and empower the ministry team to meet goals, steward resources, and drive innovation in inclusive ministry practices. 

Event Leadership 

  • Plan and execute key events such as Night to Shine, Dad/Daughter Dinner, Volunteer Appreciation, Easter, Christmas Eve services, Exceptional Stars, Special Needs Camp, and Kids Camp. 
  • Ensure events are inclusive, well-organized, and aligned with CCV’s mission to reach and serve all families. 

Systems & Administration 

  • Utilize the Rock system to manage attendance, check-ins, volunteer scheduling, and communication effectively. 
  • Monitor ministry metrics and goals, making data-informed decisions to improve programming and outreach. 
  • Maintain clear documentation and communication with staff, volunteers, and families. 

Vision & Culture 

  • Uphold and champion the vision and mission of the Special Needs Ministry across all touchpoints. 
  • Inspire and equip volunteers and staff to lead with compassion, excellence, and a heart for inclusion. 
  • Build strong relationships with parents, volunteers, and church leadership to foster unity and shared purpose.

Qualifications

Qualifications  

Character & Chemistry 

  • A deep passion for reaching the lost and discipling the next generation. 
  • Demonstrates personal integrity, humility, and spiritual maturity. 
  • Actively engaged in CCV’s community through worship, giving, and group participation. 
  • Models CCV’s values and mission in personal and professional life. 

Competency 

  • Leadership & Influence: Inspires and mobilizes others toward a shared vision. 
  • Relational Intelligence: Builds trust, communicates effectively, and navigates conflict with grace. 
  • Organizational Skills: Manages time, tasks, and resources with excellence and attention to detail. 
  • Adaptability: Thrives in a fast-paced, evolving ministry environment. 
  • Initiative & Drive: Takes ownership, solves problems, and pursues results with passion. 
  • Technology Proficiency: Familiarity with ministry databases, scheduling tools, and digital communication platforms. 

Education & Experience 

  • Bachelor’s degree in ministry, education, child development, or related field preferred. 
  • Minimum of 2 years of experience leading volunteers or staff in a church or children’s ministry setting. 
  • Experience with large-scale programming and volunteer coordination is a plus. 

Additional Information

All your information will be kept confidential according to EEO guidelines.

General Information

The above statements are intended to describe the general nature and level of work being performed by individuals assigned to this position. They are not intended to be an exhaustive list of all duties, responsibilities, and skills required of employees. CCV Leadership reserves the right to revise the position, its job functions, minimum qualifications and other aspects of the position in any way at any time.

Summary

The Congregation Executive Pastor/Operations Director (CXP/COD) provides primary executive leadership within a local congregation of The Austin Stone Community Church. 

In partnership with the Congregation Pastor (CP), the CXP/COD shares stewardship of the congregation's health and mission. The CXP/COD contributes meaningfully to ministry discernment and gives primary executive leadership to translating agreed ministry direction into aligned & effective plans, people, resources, systems, leadership rhythms and accountability.

The CXP/COD partners and supports CP leadership of Congregational Leadership Community (elders, deacons, staff, and key lay ministry leaders) by helping establish clear roles, rhythms, goals, communication, accountability, and deployment across the community.

As a churchwide executive leader, the CXP/COD helps ensure the contextualized ministry of the congregation is aligned with the doctrine, culture, philosophies, shared ministry commitments, and direction of The Austin Stone while exercising appropriate local agency as one church through local congregations. The CXP/COD reports to the Congregation Pastor.

Essential Responsibilities

Congregational Disciple-Making Leadership

  • Partner with the Congregation Pastor to assess congregational health, clarify ministry priorities, and establish annual plans that help people take wise, practical next steps toward joyful devotion to Jesus by gathering, growing, giving, and going.
  • Give executive leadership to the implementation of agreed congregation plans and churchwide ministry commitments by clarifying ownership, goals, resources, timelines, and accountability and ensuring they are effectively contextualized and coordinated within the congregation.

Congregation Leadership Community

  • Partner with the CP's leadership of the Congregational Leadership Community to establish and sustain clear roles, rhythms, goals, communication, and accountability across elders, deacons, staff, and key lay leaders, increasingly entrusting meaningful ministry responsibility to qualified leaders.
  • Lead the congregational deacon team, supporting the CP and elders’ provision of pastoral oversight and care giving particular leadership to deacon development, integration, deployment, and clear ministry ownership.
  • Lead the congregational staff with the CP, with the CP giving primary leadership to spiritual tone and ministry direction and the CXP/COD giving primary executive leadership to organizational clarity, management, staff rhythms, accountability, performance, development, and effective deployment.
  • Identify, develop, and raise up future church leaders (including elders, deacons, staff, managers, and ministry leaders when applicable) in partnership with the CP and Congregational Leadership Community.
  • When serving as an elder, participate meaningfully on the congregational elder team by contributing executive leadership, organizational perspective, shepherding, and wisdom in support of the CP's leadership as first among equals. 

Congregational Operational Excellence

  • Give primary executive leadership to congregational operations, regularly assessing and aligning people, resources, ministry environments, systems, and workflows with ministry priorities and leading adjustments that improve ministry effectiveness.
  • Ensure clear and healthy staff management by establishing roles, reporting relationships, priorities, expectations, and goals, and ensuring staff receive appropriate feedback, care, development, accountability, and support.
  • Steward the congregation’s budget and financial resources through annual budgeting, forecasting, expense management, financial accountability, and wise allocation of resources in alignment with agreed ministry priorities.
  • Ensure excellent Sunday ministry by coordinating with the CP, Worship Pastor/Leader, and appropriate leaders the people, volunteers, systems, logistics, facilities, and resources necessary for effective Sunday ministry.
  • Ensure clear, timely congregation communication by coordinating local leaders and churchwide communication resources so partners, attenders, leaders, and volunteers receive what they need to participate meaningfully in the life and mission of the congregation.

Churchwide Executive Leadership

  • Contribute as a churchwide executive leader to planning, organizational leadership, resource stewardship, training, and strategic initiatives that strengthen the health and mission of The Austin Stone as a whole.
  • Give primary leadership energy to the local congregation while maintaining meaningful churchwide ownership, collaboration, and executive leadership.
  • Collaborate with congregation executive leaders, Division Leaders, Integrators, and churchwide teams to strengthen alignment, share learning, solve common problems, and improve shared systems, resources, and ministry practices.
  • Represent local congregation realities in churchwide planning by surfacing the people, time, financial, and operational implications of shared priorities to the appropriate Lead Pastor and Division leadership; steward local decisions with a whole-church perspective while faithfully championing agreed churchwide direction and ensuring congregation ministries operate within appropriate policies, financial controls, safety standards, and organizational commitments.
  • Partner effectively with shared-service teams and participate fully in required churchwide rhythms, including Finance, HR, Technology, Facilities, Creative/Communications, ministry Integrators, staff meetings, prayer gatherings, leadership meetings, retreats, and development days, modeling spiritual vitality, unity, humility, ownership, and leadership.

General

  • Serve and lead with the congregation at all required events and activities.

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience required; advanced education in ministry, business, organizational leadership, or a related field beneficial but not required.
  • 7 years of experience leading within vocational ministry, organizational leadership, executive leadership, or a comparable leadership environment, preferred.
  • Demonstrated maturity as a disciple of Jesus and commitment to the mission, doctrine, culture, and ministry philosophy of The Austin Stone. If an elder, must meet the biblical and organizational qualifications for eldership at The Austin Stone.
  • If the employee is eligible and becomes an ordained elder at The Austin Stone, the title of Executive Pastor will be used.
  • Demonstrated experience leading staff and managers, developing leaders, creating organizational clarity, and building healthy, high-functioning teams, strategic planning, organizational execution, budgeting, resource stewardship, and assessment.

Competencies

Spiritual Vitality – A personal relationship with Jesus Christ. Living as a mature disciple on mission in family, church, and community. Demonstrates spiritual maturity, humility, prayerfulness, biblical wisdom, and a pattern of dependence on the Holy Spirit.

Executive Leadership – Demonstrated capacity to take complex ministry realities and create clarity, direction, ownership, and action. Able to discern what matters most, steward competing priorities, make wise decisions, allocate resources, and lead leaders toward meaningful ministry outcomes.

Staff Leadership & Development – Skilled in leading staff and managers through clear expectations, feedback, coaching, accountability, development, and care. Builds healthy teams marked by trust, ownership, collaboration, spiritual maturity, and effective performance.

Strategic Planning & Execution – Ability to partner in discerning ministry direction and then organize people, goals, resources, timelines, and accountability around that direction. Demonstrates consistent follow-through and the capacity to move ministry from idea to sustainable implementation.

Resource Stewardship – Demonstrated capacity to steward budgets, staffing, facilities, technology, time, and other resources wisely and strategically. Able to make allocation decisions based on ministry priorities and the good of the broader church rather than merely local preference.

Organizational Intelligence – Capacity to understand how the local congregation functions within the broader Austin Stone organization and to navigate a complex environment with multiple leaders, teams, systems, and areas of shared ownership. Knows when alignment is required, when collaboration is beneficial, and where contextual leadership is appropriate.

Assessment & Problem Solving – Able to assess ministry and organizational effectiveness using both qualitative and quantitative information, identify underlying problems rather than merely symptoms, and lead appropriate change or course correction.

Shepherding – Demonstrates genuine pastoral care for staff, deacons, leaders, and congregation members. Leads people rather than merely processes and creates environments in which those being led experience clarity, care, encouragement, truth, and meaningful development.

Collaborative Leadership – Demonstrates strong complementary leadership alongside the Congregation Pastor and the ability to lead in concert with elders, deacons, staff, lay leaders, Lead Pastors, and churchwide teams. Integrates multiple perspectives into coherent direction while building unity and shared ownership.

Physical Demands and Work Environment

The physical demands and work environment described here are representative of those an employee encounters while performing the essential functions of this job.  Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

  • Occasional lifting of objects up to 30 pounds.
  • Subject to standing, walking, sitting, bending, reaching, kneeling, pushing and pulling.
  • Manual dexterity and coordination are required over 50% of the work period while operating equipment such as a computer keyboard, mouse, and similar machines.

Disclaimer

The information presented indicates the general nature and level of work expected of employees in this classification. It is not designed to contain, nor to be interpreted as, a comprehensive inventory of all duties, responsibilities, qualifications, and objectives required of employees assigned to this job.

Culture and Character   

Employees of The Austin Stone are expected to become Partners (our term for members) of the church, fully embracing the values, mission, and purpose of our church. Additionally, all employees of The Austin Stone are expected to understand, affirm and adhere to our Affirmation of Faith, Bylaws, Culture Map, and other documents defining the beliefs, culture, and mission of The Austin Stone Community Church.

Employees also possess the character qualifications of biblical leadership in the church. At a minimum, each employee must agree and aspire to maturity in these qualifications, invite the authority of church community and leaders as a means of growth in them, and pursue them humbly and faithfully by the power of the Holy Spirit.

As part of our child safety program, employees in this role will be required to participate in a child safety screening and training process upon hire.

Please read Attributes of Leaders as Employees at The Austin Stone for a greater description of cultural, character, and other aspects of joining our team at The Austin Stone. 

The Austin Stone Community Church is an Equal Opportunity Employer including Women, Minorities, Protected Veterans, and Individuals with Disabilities.
