Campus Staff Minister - Illinois & Indiana (Graduate & Faculty Ministry)

Work Location:

Indiana

Job Type:

Full time

God has called InterVarsity to plant and to build witnessing communities of students and faculty who follow Jesus on college and university campuses. Through these groups, we believe ever- increasing numbers of students and faculty from all ethnic groups and areas of the campus will be transformed by the Gospel. We expect to see campuses increasingly become places where people, ideas, and structures flourish to the glory of God. We confidently anticipate that our InterVarsity alumni will become change agents across the country and around the world. We pursue this calling by discerning and actively participating in what God is already doing on campus. This is the essence of being a Campus Staff Minister (CSM).

Please submit the GFM Interest Form before completing the full application for a position with Graduate & Faculty Ministries in our online system. We will contact you when we are ready to proceed with the application process.​ 



The pay range listed is for an employee working 40 hours/week at CSM level II. Pay will be prorated for employees who work less than 40 hours/week. 

We have positions in the following locations:

Illinois

Illinois State University - Faculty

Southern Illinois University Carbondale - Graduate Students, Faculty

University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign - Graduate Students, International Students Ministry and Professional Schools Ministry

Indiana

Indiana State University - Faculty

Indiana University Bloomington - Graduate Students, Faculty, Professional Schools

Purdue University - Graduate Students, Faculty, Professional Schools

University of Notre Dame - Graduate Students, Faculty Professional schools

ESSENTIAL COMMITMENTS/RESPONSIBILITIES 

Spiritual Growth 

You pursue maturity as a disciple of Jesus Christ so that your life and work increasingly reflects a growing love for God, God’s Word, God’s people of every ethnicity and culture, and God’s purposes in the world. To do this, you will: 

  • Pursue a vibrant relationship with the triune God through engagement with Scripture, prayer, and worship, both individually and in community 

  • Develop self-leadership (growing in self-awareness, self-management, relational integrity, and resiliency) 

  • Embrace Scriptural standards for behavior and attitudes 

 

Campus Leadership 

You communicate and model InterVarsity’s vision to see students and faculty transformed, campuses renewed and world changers developed 

  • Create a culture of humble dependence on God and bold expectation in God’s intention to start new witnessing communities throughout the campus and on new campuses 

  • Model – in person and through programs – InterVarsity’s vision and Core Values, including a biblically-defined commitment to engage every ethnic and social group on campus 

  • Lead students and faculty – individually and collectively – through Scripture, prayer, teaching, and discipleship experiences, so that they articulate and align their ministry activities around this vision 

  • Set annual goals through prayer, research and reflection with your teams (students, faculty, and staff) for qualitative and quantitative growth, including conversions and leadership development 

 

You create, develop, align and leverage ministry plans, programs, teams, and structures to close the gap between current reality and the aspirational goals. 

  • Build leadership teams who trust and partner well with you and who demonstrate spiritual vitality, relational health, and mission alignment 

  • Develop and execute plans to achieve annual goals, evaluating and modifying the plan as needed throughout the year 

  • Increase momentum for the vision by aligning programs, structures, conferences and teams around the goals 

  • Mobilize students and faculty to engage their relational networks with the gospel and to start new missional communities 

  • Under the direction of the Area Director, may supervise Ministry Interns and Campus Ministry Interns as delegated 

 

You intentionally gather, invite, and develop diverse groups of students and faculty so that they not only encounter and follow Jesus as Savior and Lord but also advance the mission on campus as participants and leaders. 

  • Create ways for faculty and students to encounter and follow Jesus through Scripture, worship, prayer, mission experiences, conferences, etc. 

  • Equip students and faculty so that they think strategically about campus engagement and so that they proclaim – in word, deed, and power – the good news of Jesus, regularly inviting students and faculty to follow him as Savior and Lord 

  • Disciple students and faculty by equipping them to hear the Word, respond actively, and debrief and interpret the experience so that they grow in Christlikeness, reflect our Core Values, and develop ministry skills 

  • Invite, coach, and equip students and faculty to become increasingly effective participants and leaders, including starting new witnessing communities on campuses 

 

Organizational Collaboration 

You work with a network of other local, area, regional, and national InterVarsity staff and volunteers so that our work reflects Biblical standards of excellence, integrity, and partnership. 

  • Partner with and respond positively to the direction and coaching of your supervisors and national leaders 

  • Contribute to collaborative and productive team meetings and relationships 

  • Affiliate chapters under your care and submit Graduating Student Forms in order to increase our partnership with current students and alumni 

  • Use national ministry resources and tools, as requested, including recruiting and/or participating in local, regional, or national conferences as  

  • Complete reporting, planning and review requirements in a timely way so that you and your supervisors can assess and improve your work as a CSM 

  • Comply with all InterVarsity policies and procedures 

 

Ministry Partnership Development 

You will develop a team of partners – churches and individuals (including alumni and community members) – who will resource the ministry financially, in prayer, or volunteer service that advances the mission. 

  • Raise 100% of the financial budget assigned by your supervisor 

  • Communicate regularly with your ministry partners, nurturing the relationship through visits, phone calls, emails and regular prayer letters 

  • Develop on-going, long-lasting partnership with alumni and volunteers 

  • Comply with all Ministry Partnership Policies 

  • Identify and invest in advocates who will build networks of volunteers and donors on InterVarsity’s behalf 

 

Accomplish all other assigned tasks as appropriate 

 

QUALIFICATIONS (common to all levels of CSM) 

  • Annually affirm InterVarsity’s Statement of Agreement (Doctrinal Basis and Purpose Statement). Abide by InterVarsity’s Code of Conduct. Believe and behave consonantly with InterVarsity’s Human Sexuality Theological Paper. Affirm and behave consonantly with InterVarsity’s “Women in Ministry Statement of Affirmation” 

  • Bachelor’s degree for CSMs assigned to a four-year campus. A minimum of an Associate’s degree for CSMs assigned to a two-year campus or a community college 

  • Strong interpersonal skills (including ability to minister to diverse ethnic communities and faculty) 

  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills 

  • Demonstrated problem solving skills 

  • Familiarity with word processing, presentation, email, and spreadsheet software 

 

WORK ENVIRONMENT/PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS 

The CSM position leads ministry in a college campus environment. A designated office space may or may not be available. The CSM is required to travel to on-campus and off- campus sites as appropriate. Off-campus travel includes, but is not limited to: student ministry conferences, Ministry Partnership Development meetings, and InterVarsity- sponsored training sessions, meetings, and conferences. The CSM is regularly required to communicate with others, and routinely uses standard office equipment such as computers, phones, photocopiers, filing cabinets, etc. 

Pay Range: $44,016.00 - $58,680.00 per year

Pay: This position is funded through personal fundraising. Accordingly, compensation will vary based on the ability of the individual to secure a donor team to fund the cost of his/her salary. The anticipated salary range for this position on a full-time basis (40 hours/week) is dependent on a variety of factors, including location and cost of living. The actual salary received, including any geographic adjustment to account for location and cost of living, is subject to the individual’s ability to raise funds necessary to cover the full amount of such salary within the range set forth in the job posting details.

Benefits:

We offer a competitive benefits package, including health care and retirement savings with a match. Eligibility is based on employee type and hours worked.  Benefits include the following:

  • 403(b) Retirement Savings Plan

  • 403(b) matching contributions

  • Dental insurance

  • Employee assistance program

  • Employee discounts

  • Flexible work schedule

  • Flexible spending accounts

  • Health insurance

  • Health savings account

  • Life insurance

  • Paid time off

  • Parental leave

  • Professional development assistance

  • Vision insurance

Equal Employment Opportunity: 

 

InterVarsity Christian Fellowship/USA is both an equal opportunity employer and a faith-based religious organization. We conduct hiring without regard to race, color, ancestry, national origin, citizenship, age, sex, marital status, parental status, membership in any labor organization, political ideology, or disability of an otherwise qualified individual. The status of InterVarsity Christian Fellowship/USA as an equal opportunity employer does not prevent the organization from hiring staff based on their religious beliefs so that all staff share the same religious commitment.  Pursuant to the Civil Rights Act of 1964, Section 702 (42 U.S.C. 2000e 1(a)) InterVarsity Christian Fellowship/USA has the right to, and does, hire only candidates who agree with InterVarsity’s Statement of Agreement: Purpose and Doctrinal Basis because InterVarsity believes that each and every staff plays a vital role in advancing InterVarsity’s mission and purposes.

The Children's Pastor at Peoples Church will lead a thriving, momentum-filled ministry of 550–650 children, bringing vision and pastoral care to their families and volunteers. Operating out of a brand new children's building, you will inherit a healthy ministry and a dedicated team of three full-time staff members. They are looking for an entrepreneurial leader who loves developing staff, building volunteer systems at scale, and partnering with parents to help kids see God and participate in His redemptive story.

 

About Peoples Church:

  • 3,500 average weekend attendance.
  • 550–650 kids and roughly 100 volunteers each weekend.
  • This is for a high level leader ready to oversee the staff and volunteers and is given the authority to lead.
  • Brand new children's building.
  • A "wide hallways" theological culture that unites different denominational backgrounds around the Gospel.
  • 5+ years of children's ministry experience in a large church context.
  • Experience managing direct reports and scaling large volunteer teams.
  • A self-starting, entrepreneurial mindset



About This Organization

Peoples Church is a church in Fresno, California, and has been a prominent presence in the Central Valley for over 70 years. We average around 3,500 in Sunday morning attendance across our gatherings. We are well known and respected in the community for our focus on serving the city we love, and we are traditionally known as a loving church where people feel at home when they come on campus. Guided by our vision of Helping People See God and Participate in His Redemptive Story, we come alongside our community to show them the hope found in Jesus, shaped by our values of Loving God, Loving Others, Loving Truth, Loving Culture, and Loving Sacrifice. We are a multi-generational and increasingly diverse congregation, and we actively extend a hand into the community through events that meet people where they are. We are a big church that works hard to feel like a small one, where it is easy to get connected and where people are welcomed in and treated like family.


Location

Fresno is a respite from the large cities that typify ideas about California, such as San Francisco and Los Angeles. Fresno County produces agriculture that feeds the world and is home to a tight-knit, diverse community with a rich history and a small-town feel. Sitting in the heart of the Central Valley, Fresno offers an enviable location with easy access to both the mountains and the coast, with Yosemite, Sequoia, and Kings Canyon National Parks practically in the backyard, and both Los Angeles and the Bay Area within easy reach for a weekend trip. It is a place where a pastor and family can put down roots, raise children, and build a life alongside their ministry for the long haul.


Key Responsibilities

  • Provide overall pastoral and strategic leadership for our Children’s Ministry, serving the children, families, and volunteers who make up one of our most active ministries.
  • Lead and develop our team of three full-time staff, including a full-time admin and two full-time coordinators across preschool, elementary, and pre-team environments.
  • Recruit, train, and retain a strong volunteer team of more than 100 leaders who serve our children each weekend.
  • Lead our weekend gatherings for children, ensuring they are environments where kids see God and take real steps in their faith.
  • Lead the volunteers who lead the children while staying personally engaged and present with kids and families.
  • Build and steward relationships with parents, navigating family conversations and concerns with pastoral care and clear communication.
  • Maintain and strengthen safety, background check, and operational systems that protect children and build trust with families.
  • Promote the Children’s Ministry across our congregation, helping our church family stay connected to what God is doing through this ministry.
  • Steward the Children’s Ministry’s staff, volunteer base, new building, and ministry budget with care and intentionality.



Key Qualifications

  • Three to five years of experience leading children’s ministry 
  • Experience in a large church environment preferred, but demonstrated experience and ministry trajectory will be taken into consideration
  • Demonstrated experience managing direct reports and developing staff and volunteer teams.
  • A self-starter who sets their own goals and a team player willing to work within the wide hallways of our leadership culture.
  • An excellent communicator, both in person and electronically.
  • Comfortable navigating parent relationships, safety and background check processes, and the operational complexity that comes with leading a children’s ministry at scale.



Key Distinctives

A loving church where people feel at home: This is what we are known for in our community, and it shapes everything we do.

Over 70 years in the Central Valley: A prominent, respected church with deep roots and a long legacy of serving our city.

A big church that feels like a small one: You can be as connected as you want to be, and we have built a lot of front doors to make that easy.

Wide theological hallways: Gospel-centered, generous on the secondary issues, and home to people from many backgrounds.

Outward-facing and missions-minded. We actively extend a hand into our community and pour into both our city and the world.

A 40-acre campus with real resources: Including an on-campus K–12 school with a generous tuition discount for staff.

Diverse and multi-generational: Our congregation increasingly reflects the makeup of our region, and we value both the legacy of older generations and the energy of younger ones.

SUMMARY

The Director of Recovery will perform as the spiritual and organizational point person for the Recovery Ministry of Pinelake Church. This person will execute the strategy, values, and vision of the Care & Recovery Team of Pinelake Church within the context of the Recovery Ministry. This person will act as the point person by creating support group content, recruiting lay leaders, organizing and launching groups at each of the Pinelake campuses. This will be achieved through partnering with a Pinelake Staff member at each campus. The Pastor of Recovery will ensure the vitality of community, discipleship, and therapeutic standards are held consistent within Pinelake support groups. This role will serve as a model for Emotional Health in leadership.

GENERAL RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Learn
    • Pursue a growing relationship with Jesus through consistent time in God’s Word and prayer.
    • Continually grow in your understanding of the Jesus-Centered Life (salvation, identity, life, and authority in Christ).
    • Remain teachable and hungry, seeking feedback, learning from others, and developing both spiritually and professionally.
    • Cultivate awareness of God’s presence in everyday life, listening to the Holy Spirit and responding in obedience.
  • Live
    • Practice and model the rhythms of Be the Church (Grow, Pray, Connect, and Share).
    • Pursue emotional health by engaging in self-awareness, addressing past wounds, and cultivating honest, healthy relationships.
    • Practice healthy rhythms, prioritizing your relationship with Jesus and your family
    • Embody a life of integrity and surrender, allowing your private life with God to shape your work.
  • Lead
    • Take ownership of disciple-making by personally investing in others and helping them move toward a Jesus-Centered Life.
    • Walk others through the Discipleship Pathway (Essentials → JCL → Be the Church), helping them discover and take their next step.
    • Shepherd people, not just programs, by listening for where God is at work in their story and walking with them toward transformation.
    • Equip and release others by developing Servant Leaders and multiplying disciples who Learn from Christ, Live in Christ, and Lead others to Christ.
    • Measure success by life change, spiritual formation, and multiplication—not just attendance or activity.
  • Embrace the Culture
    • Value and embody the staff values, which we call the 7 H’s: Humility, Honor, Honesty, Hunger, Holy Spirit, Health, and Harmony
    • Communicate clearly, honestly, and proactively in a way that builds trust, unity, and momentum.
    • Work in alignment with the church vision and leadership
    • Participate fully in the life of your campus or team, contributing to the unity, health, and shepherding of the faith family.


SPECIFIC LIST OF DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

    • Work with the Lead Pastor of Care & Recovery to develop and maintain an effective support group vision and strategy that serves a broad range of individuals in recovery at Pinelake.

    SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES

    QUALIFICATIONS

    To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily. The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skill and/or ability required. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform essential functions.


    EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE REQUIRED

    The minimum requirements for the Pastor of Recovery is a Bachelor’s degree, but an advanced degree is preferred (with a focus in Christian psychology or counseling). Also, Church based ministry experience and support group leadership experience are competitive attributes.

About Le Moyne College:

Le Moyne College, located in Syracuse, N.Y., is an independent college established by the Jesuits in 1946 to provide students with a values-based, comprehensive academic program designed to foster intellectual excellence and preparation for a life of leadership and service. Today, Le Moyne has evolved into a nationally acclaimed college of liberal arts and sciences that draws students from across the U.S. and abroad.

Our Mission:

Le Moyne College is a diverse learning community that strives for academic excellence in the Catholic and Jesuit tradition through its comprehensive programs rooted in the liberal arts and sciences. Its emphasis is on education of the whole person and on the search for meaning and value as integral parts of the intellectual life. Le Moyne College seeks to prepare its members for leadership and service in their personal and professional lives to promote a more just society.

Le Moyne College aims to advance the values of diversity and inclusiveness at the college. To do this, Le Moyne seeks scholars and professionals who bring innovation, creativity, and impact to the campus, and who bring greater depth, breadth, and diversity to our campus community.

Campus Ministry

The Office of Campus Ministry provides opportunities for students, staff, and faculty to grow spiritually, to engage in local, domestic, and international service and social justice opportunities, to make spiritual retreats, reflect on contemporary social issues and to actively practice their faith. Campus Ministry welcomes and serves persons of all religious affiliations and faith traditions.

Position Summary                                                                           

Under the supervision of the Director of The Grace Center for Faith and Community and in collaboration with the Campus Ministry Staff, the Campus Minister for Retreat Ministry and Faith Formation promotes the deepening of an active faith and spiritual life, personal and communal, among the students of Le Moyne College. The primary ministry is to create vibrant programing, robust retreat offerings, individual and communal prayer/discernment opportunities, and community centered activities that help deepen, renew, or begin a personal relationship with God. This work is accomplished through a strong understanding of Ignatian spirituality and the stages of faith formation in young adults. This position requires a person who will creatively and strategically develop new programs/mediums and refine existing programs based on the ongoing assessment of student needs and interests.

This is an 11 month position that works from August through June.
 

Principal Duties and Essential Functions

Job duties specific to this position:

  • Create a compelling vision for and develop a dynamic portfolio of retreats and other experiences which will engage students in various aspects of faith formation and spiritual development. 

  • Implement all aspects of the retreat program and other faith formation opportunities for students based on class year (First Year Student Retreat, Senior Retreat etc.) as well as topic based (Kairos, Busy Student Retreat, Health & Wellness Retreat, Silent Retreat). 

  • Create new retreat and faith formation opportunities for students of all faiths and for those with no religious beliefs. 

  • Promote opportunities to learn about and practice Ignatian Spirituality. 

  • Create and maintain assessment measures for the program. 

  • Recruit, mentor, develop and empower student leaders who support the retreat program.     

  • Reserve and coordinate the use of various retreat facilities and college vans.

  • Coordinate the OCIA & Confirmation program.

  • Work with faith and service-based student organizations.

  • Keep and maintain accurate budget records for all programs.

  • Maintain a respectful environment for a diverse population of students; embrace diversity in the College and greater community, and treat students as individuals.

  • Work collaboratively with the Grace Center team and campus partners

  • Serve, as needed, as a mentor for Campus Ministry's Service opportunities

  • Assist with local service/outreach initiatives.

  • Serve as a Campus Ministry presence at Sunday Mass and attend all special liturgies of the college.

  • Attend and be visible at various religious services on campus, including but not limited to weekly Jumu'ah prayer and Protestant worship.

  • Attending and being visible at various campus events, including but not limited to sporting, musical, lectures, and other social events.

  • Contribute to Mission Integration divisional meetings, webinars and committees

Job expectations for all Le Moyne College employees:

  • Demonstrates and role-models all of Le Moyne’s mission-based competencies (collaboration, communication, diversity, integrity, leadership and service) in every interaction with all community members and external parties.

  • Strengthen digital literacy skills through education and the application of digital technologies in order to effectively engage in information gathering, utilization and data management while promoting a security culture.

  • Supports cura personalis by treating all individuals with dignity, professionalism and kindness.

  • Promotes cura apostolica by aligning professional goals, objectives, and performance with college’s strategic goals.

  • Demonstrates excellent work attendance, reliability and work ethic.

  • Attends and actively participates in required meetings and training sessions.

  • Complies and adheres to all of Le Moyne’s established policies, procedures and codes of conduct at all times, including all health and safety requirements and regulations, to promote desired behavior and build awareness.

  • Must complete all required federal, state, institution and department trainings.

  • Engages in a planned program of professional development. Continually maintains skills and knowledge relative to the position and technology industry including best practice, evolving operational requirements, and industry trends.

  • Performs a variety of related duties as assigned.

Qualifications

  • Master's degree preferred, Bachelor's Degree required in Pastoral Studies, theology or a related field.

  • An understanding of the principles of Ignatian spirituality, the Spiritual Exercises of St. Ignatius, the mission of Jesuit education, and Catholic Social Teaching. Desire to work with a diverse faith community of undergraduate college students.

  • Familiarity with Karios retreat program.

  • Flexibility to work extended and/or off-hours to meet program needs.

  • Ability to relate and collaborate with various groups both within the Le Moyne College community and the larger Syracuse community.

Campus Minister

MINISTRY / LOCATION

Tulane Catholic

EMPLOYMENT STATUS

Full-Time | Exempt

On-Site

EMPLOYER

Archdiocese of New Orleans

REPORTS TO

Director of Tulane Catholic

Position Overview

Tulane Catholic is in a season of renewal. We are intentionally and energetically working to build a vibrant Catholic community for a new generation of Tulane students.

The Campus Minister's work is both relational and organizational. On the relational side, the job is presence and outreach: being at Mass, meals, and events, getting to know students, and following up with those who are new or drifting.

Just as important, the Campus Minister is a facilitator. Because the Director and several members of the leadership team serve Tulane Catholic part-time, the Campus Minister is the steady, full-time presence who holds the day-to-day ministry together. Working closely with the Director, the Ministry Operations Manager, our FOCUS missionaries, and student leaders, the Campus Minister keeps people and plans connected so that retreats, formation, events, and student leadership work together as one ministry. This means coordinating rather than owning every initiative: making sure the right people are talking, the calendar holds together, and nothing falls through the cracks.

We are looking for someone who enjoys college students, works well on a team, has the follow-through to manage details, and wants to invest in students and their leadership over the long term.

Compensation and Benefits

  • Salary: $50,000 to $55,000 annually
  • Full benefits package through the Archdiocese of New Orleans
  • Opportunities for your own spiritual and professional development
  • Full-time, exempt position
  • Some evenings and weekends required during events, retreats, and major ministry activities
  • Occasional overnight travel, including retreats and conferences such as SEEK

Start Date

  • January 2027 preferred, with flexibility to Summer 2027 for the right candidate

Reporting

  • Reports directly to the Director of Tulane Catholic
  • Member of the Ministry Leadership Team
  • Works closely with the Ministry Operations Manager and FOCUS team, coordinating with them rather than supervising them
  • Primary staff point of contact for the Student Leadership Team
  • Supervises the campus ministry intern, if one is hired

Duties and Responsibilities

Student Presence and Hospitality

  • Be consistently present at the student center: at Mass, at meals, at events, and in ordinary moments
  • Seek out and welcome new students, with particular attention to those on the margins of the community
  • Help coordinate Sunday Night Supper and other hospitality moments

Formation and Retreats

  • Plan and lead formation evenings, talks, and retreats throughout the academic year
  • Handle retreat logistics, recruit participants, and follow up with students afterward
  • Help students connect their faith to their daily life at Tulane

Student Leadership Team (SLT)

  • Serve as the primary point of contact and formation resource for the SLT
  • Recruit, form, and empower student leaders to take ownership of ministry activities
  • Facilitate regular SLT meetings and help set the direction of student-led initiatives

Coordination and Facilitation

  • Serve as the main point of coordination between the Director, the FOCUS team, the Ministry Operations Manager, and student leaders
  • Build and maintain a ministry calendar that brings FOCUS Bible studies, events, retreats, and formation into one rhythm
  • Support FOCUS missionaries without directing or supervising them; the Director retains direct oversight
  • Communicate proactively about scheduling, logistics, and student needs

Communications

  • Work with the Ministry Operations Manager on social media and promotion for events and programming
  • Help tell the story of Tulane Catholic to students, alumni, and supporters

Qualifications

  • Practicing Catholic who loves the Church and believes deeply in the mission of Catholic campus ministry
  • Bachelor's degree required; degree in theology, ministry, education, or related field preferred
  • Experience in Catholic campus ministry, preferably with FOCUS, Christ in the City, SPO, or a similar apostolate
  • Strong relational skills: naturally warm, energetic, and at ease with college students
  • Ability to collaborate within a team and communicate proactively
  • Comfortable with basic digital communications and social media
  • Must complete the Archdiocese of New Orleans Safe Environment training and background check before beginning work

You'd Be a Great Fit If You...

  • Are excited about building a ministry and investing in the next generation
  • Enjoy college students and are at ease spending time with them
  • Are a natural facilitator who makes things happen by bringing the right people together
  • Have Enablement and Galvanizing among your Working Genius strengths (from Patrick Lencioni's model): you get energy from supporting others and from rallying people around a shared goal
  • Bring enough Tenacity, the Working Genius of seeing work through to completion, to follow through on the details even when it isn't glamorous
  • Complement a more directive, vision-driven leader by running with the vision and making it relational
  • Are eager to learn, willing to stretch, and joyful in your vocation

Definition of Success

In this role, you are succeeding when:

  • Students who walk in for the first time come back because someone made them feel like they belonged
  • The FOCUS team and the broader ministry calendar are well-coordinated and working in the same direction
  • The Director and the Ministry Leadership Team are kept well informed about students, events, and needs
  • Students, led by a Student Leadership Team growing in confidence and faith, are taking ownership of the community: inviting friends, leading events and small groups, and carrying initiatives forward without staff having to drive them
  • Retreats and formation evenings are happening, are well-attended, and are spiritually fruitful
  • The community has a visible, winsome presence on campus and on social media
  • Students are not just participating in programs but are being formed as disciples and leaders

To Apply

This position is posted through the Archdiocese of New Orleans. Interested candidates should submit the following materials:

  • A cover letter expressing interest in and qualifications for the position
  • A current resume
  • A list of three professional references with contact information; references will only be contacted with the applicant's knowledge

Chinese Alliance Church of Westchester (CACW) is seeking a full time Associate Pastor with a passion to cultivate the life of Christ in our church and community.

A Christian and Missionary Alliance (“CMA”) church located in Port Chester, New York, CACW is a community of believers seeking to love God and others. We are a Chinese- and English-speaking church with two congregations and a combined total of about 120-150 attendees.

Associate Pastor -- Responsibilities

  • Support and work collaboratively with the pastoral staff (Chinese and English congregational pastors), along with church leadership, to help our people and our community to experience and live out the love of Christ.
  • A vital area of focus will be to oversee and nurture our Youth Ministry. This group of 6th to 12th graders is made up not only of Chinese youth, but also a diverse mix of young people, and current attendance ranges from 15 to 20. We are looking for someone who will care as deeply about this important ministry as we do.

Responsibilities in connection with the Youth Ministry will include:

    • Leading and working collaboratively with our highly engaged lay youth leaders to plan, coordinate and lead the weekly Youth Group gatherings as well as other special events such annual youth retreats, triannual CMA national youth conferences, short term missions and other community outreach.
    • Teaching and exemplifying biblical precepts and concepts to these young people in weekly Youth Group gatherings, Youth Sunday School, Bible studies/devotionals and other occasional events.
    • Mentoring and discipling members of the Youth group personally and spiritually.
    • Finding ways to encourage and equip parents in their parenting, hosting occasional youth/parent events, etc.
  • Other responsibilities include:
    • Work with the pastoral staff and governing board to plan, pray, and coordinate various ministries within the church.
    • Preaching (frequency will vary depending on the experience of the individual), support children ministry including the annual Vacation Bible Camp, support church mission or evangelical efforts such as annual mission weekend, annual church picnic.
  • Help with community outreach. As a church in diverse neighborhood, we seek to reach out to our local community in a variety of ways; opportunities for the Associate Pastor include:
    • Assist with the church’s bi-weekly food pantry to the community in Port Chester.
    • Assist with our after school program (currently on hiatus, but which has historically met once a week).
    • Connect and build relationship with the families and youth from our local community.

Qualifications:

  • Passion for God: a born-again Christian who believes in the infallibility of the Bible and is willing to abide by the doctrines and traditions of the Christian and Missionary Alliance denomination. (See our our denomination website).
  • Passion to work with youth and cross-cultural ministry.
  • Youth Ministry experience (preferred).
  • A ministry-focused Masters degree is preferred, but we will consider candidates with a minimum of a bachelor’s degree with a relevant focus, preferably from an accredited seminary, Bible college or equivalent.
  • Readiness to pursue C&MA licensing.
  • Fluency in Spanish would be a plus (in order to support our current neighborhood outreach).

Feel free to check out our website www.cacw.org for more information on our church.

For more information about C&MA, please go to https://cmalliance.org/

To be considered for this position, please complete the application to include your testimony, resume and other background information related to the position.

If the district office has reviewed your application and they think you may be a potential match for the position, that the hiring manager will reach out to you for next steps.

This position requires licensing with The Christian & Missionary Alliance. To learn more about The Alliance and requirements for licensing, please visit our website

Please do not contact the church directly.

Family Ministry Director - Fort Myers Community Church
 

The Role

Fort Myers Community Church is looking for a Family Ministry Director to lead FMCC Kids, from babies through elementary school. We want a person who loves kids, equips parents, and helps the next generation know and love Jesus.

The Director's main focus is spiritual formation in a fun, engaging environment. From there, the ministry reaches beyond our walls into local schools and our community.

Spiritual Formation
The heart of this role is forming children in the gospel. Fun matters, but it serves a greater aim. We want kids to leave FMCC knowing who God is, what Jesus has done, and how to follow Him.

• Gospel-Centered Teaching: Choose and shape curriculum that teaches the whole story of Scripture and points every lesson to Jesus.
• Age-Appropriate Pathway: Build a clear discipleship path from the nursery through fifth grade, so each stage prepares kids for the next.
• Equipping Parents: Partner with parents as the primary disciplers of their children. Give them tools to carry Sunday's truth into the home.
• Building the Team: Recruit, train, and shepherd volunteers who love kids and love Jesus. Keep safety and child protection policies strong and current.

Fun, Engaging Environments
Kids should love coming to church. The Director creates spaces where children feel safe, known, and excited to return.


• Sunday Experience: Lead Sunday environments that are joyful, well organized, and full of energy.
• Welcome and First Impressions: Make check-in simple and welcoming, so first-time families feel at home from the start.
• Special Events: Plan seasonal events and family gatherings that build community and invite guests.

School Impact and Community Involvement
FMCC Kids does not stop at our doors. The Director helps our church serve the schools and neighborhoods where our families live.


• School Impact: Build relationships with local elementary schools, principals, and teachers. Find practical ways to serve them well.
• Community Involvement: Lead outreach that brings families into contact with the church, such as community events and service projects.
• Open Doors: Help families who meet us in the community take their next step into the life of FMCC.

Campus Staff Minister -- Tennessee and Kentucky (Undergraduate Ministry)

Kentucky

Full time

God has called InterVarsity to plant and to build witnessing communities of students and faculty who follow Jesus on college and university campuses. Through these groups, we believe ever- increasing numbers of students and faculty from all ethnic groups and areas of the campus will be transformed by the Gospel. We expect to see campuses increasingly become places where people, ideas, and structures flourish to the glory of God. We confidently anticipate that our InterVarsity alumni will become change agents across the country and around the world. We pursue this calling by discerning and actively participating in what God is already doing on campus. This is the essence of being a Campus Staff Minister (CSM).

ESSENTIAL COMMITMENTS/RESPONSIBILITIES 

Spiritual Growth 

You pursue maturity as a disciple of Jesus Christ so that your life and work increasingly reflects a growing love for God, God’s Word, God’s people of every ethnicity and culture, and God’s purposes in the world. To do this, you will: 

  • Pursue a vibrant relationship with the triune God through engagement with Scripture, prayer, and worship, both individually and in community 

  • Develop self-leadership (growing in self-awareness, self-management, relational integrity, and resiliency) 

  • Embrace Scriptural standards for behavior and attitudes 

 

Campus Leadership 

You communicate and model InterVarsity’s vision to see students and faculty transformed, campuses renewed and world changers developed 

  • Create a culture of humble dependence on God and bold expectation in God’s intention to start new witnessing communities throughout the campus and on new campuses 

  • Model – in person and through programs – InterVarsity’s vision and Core Values, including a biblically-defined commitment to engage every ethnic and social group on campus 

  • Lead students and faculty – individually and collectively – through Scripture, prayer, teaching, and discipleship experiences, so that they articulate and align their ministry activities around this vision 

  • Set annual goals through prayer, research and reflection with your teams (students, faculty, and staff) for qualitative and quantitative growth, including conversions and leadership development 

 

You create, develop, align and leverage ministry plans, programs, teams, and structures to close the gap between current reality and the aspirational goals. 

  • Build leadership teams who trust and partner well with you and who demonstrate spiritual vitality, relational health, and mission alignment 

  • Develop and execute plans to achieve annual goals, evaluating and modifying the plan as needed throughout the year 

  • Increase momentum for the vision by aligning programs, structures, conferences and teams around the goals 

  • Mobilize students and faculty to engage their relational networks with the gospel and to start new missional communities 

  • Under the direction of the Area Director, may supervise Ministry Interns and Campus Ministry Interns as delegated 

 

You intentionally gather, invite, and develop diverse groups of students and faculty so that they not only encounter and follow Jesus as Savior and Lord but also advance the mission on campus as participants and leaders. 

  • Create ways for faculty and students to encounter and follow Jesus through Scripture, worship, prayer, mission experiences, conferences, etc. 

  • Equip students and faculty so that they think strategically about campus engagement and so that they proclaim – in word, deed, and power – the good news of Jesus, regularly inviting students and faculty to follow him as Savior and Lord 

  • Disciple students and faculty by equipping them to hear the Word, respond actively, and debrief and interpret the experience so that they grow in Christlikeness, reflect our Core Values, and develop ministry skills 

  • Invite, coach, and equip students and faculty to become increasingly effective participants and leaders, including starting new witnessing communities on campuses 

 

Organizational Collaboration 

You work with a network of other local, area, regional, and national InterVarsity staff and volunteers so that our work reflects Biblical standards of excellence, integrity, and partnership. 

  • Partner with and respond positively to the direction and coaching of your supervisors and national leaders 

  • Contribute to collaborative and productive team meetings and relationships 

  • Affiliate chapters under your care and submit Graduating Student Forms in order to increase our partnership with current students and alumni 

  • Use national ministry resources and tools, as requested, including recruiting and/or participating in local, regional, or national conferences as  

  • Complete reporting, planning and review requirements in a timely way so that you and your supervisors can assess and improve your work as a CSM 

  • Comply with all InterVarsity policies and procedures 

 

Ministry Partnership Development 

You will develop a team of partners – churches and individuals (including alumni and community members) – who will resource the ministry financially, in prayer, or volunteer service that advances the mission. 

  • Raise 100% of the financial budget assigned by your supervisor 

  • Communicate regularly with your ministry partners, nurturing the relationship through visits, phone calls, emails and regular prayer letters 

  • Develop on-going, long-lasting partnership with alumni and volunteers 

  • Comply with all Ministry Partnership Policies 

  • Identify and invest in advocates who will build networks of volunteers and donors on InterVarsity’s behalf 

 

Accomplish all other assigned tasks as appropriate 

 

QUALIFICATIONS (common to all levels of CSM) 

  • Annually affirm InterVarsity’s Statement of Agreement (Doctrinal Basis and Purpose Statement). Abide by InterVarsity’s Code of Conduct. Believe and behave consonantly with InterVarsity’s Human Sexuality Theological Paper. Affirm and behave consonantly with InterVarsity’s “Women in Ministry Statement of Affirmation” 

  • Bachelor’s degree for CSMs assigned to a four-year campus. A minimum of an Associate’s degree for CSMs assigned to a two-year campus or a community college 

  • Strong interpersonal skills (including ability to minister to diverse ethnic communities and faculty) 

  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills

WORK ENVIRONMENT/PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS

The CSM is required to travel to on-campus and off- campus sites as appropriate. Off-campus travel includes, but is not limited to: student ministry conferences, Ministry Partnership Development meetings, and InterVarsity- sponsored training sessions, meetings, and conferences. Come Plant Where the Gospel Is Needed Most

Come and plant in one of the least-reached states in the country.

New York is filled with communities where the presence of the local church has not kept pace with the population and where thousands of people live with little meaningful engagement with the Gospel.

Research from JD Payne identifies 10 Upstate New York metropolitan areas among the 50 least-reached metro areas in the United States, with 5% or less of the population identifying as evangelical. These communities represent strategic opportunities for new Gospel-centered churches and multiplying movements.

Potential church-planting locations include:

  • Malone — 4.31% evangelical
  • Gloversville — 4.18% evangelical
  • Glens Falls — 4.45% evangelical
  • Hudson — 3.27% evangelical
  • Kingston — 2.63% evangelical

And the need extends into some of New York's largest population centers. Barna's Bible-Minded Cities research found that several major Upstate New York markets ranked among the least Bible-minded in America. In the 2017 study, Albany/Schenectady/Troy ranked #100, Buffalo #96, Rochester #86, and Syracuse #68 out of the nation's 100 largest media markets.

We are looking for a church planter who believes the local church can be a catalyst for Gospel transformation and who is willing to go where the need is greatest.

Here's the exciting part: in some locations, you won't be starting completely from scratch. Existing Alliance churches are ready to multiply and are looking for the right planter to help lead the next chapter.

Overview

As a Church Planter, you will serve as the spiritual, visionary, and multiplication leader of a church planting team in a location determined through our discernment and assessment process.

You will seek the Lord's direction in developing and implementing a vision and strategy for establishing a Gospel-centered, disciple-making, multiplying community that is deeply rooted in its local context. There is oppprtunity to in some locations to partner with existing Alliance churches who are ready to mutiply and just need a planter!

We are looking for a Gospel-rooted, courageous, missional, catalytic, and multiplying leader who meets the biblical qualifications of an elder and has a passion for reaching people who are far from Jesus.

What We're Looking For

We are looking for someone who:

  • Lives on mission — willing to move into and become deeply invested in the community where the church will be planted.
  • Sees what could be — able to recognize Gospel opportunities others may overlook and cast a compelling vision for what God could do.
  • Makes disciples — passionate about developing people who follow Jesus and helping them make disciples of others.
  • Builds teams — able to recruit, inspire, develop, coach, and empower leaders rather than attempting to do ministry alone.
  • Thinks entrepreneurially — comfortable starting from scratch, navigating uncertainty, taking appropriate risks, and creating new pathways for ministry.
  • Builds relationships — able to develop meaningful relationships with people both inside and outside the church.
  • Communicates the Gospel — able to clearly and passionately communicate the Gospel in a variety of environments and contexts.

Preferred Skills & Experience

  • Experience starting ministries in new contexts, communities, or cultures.
  • Previous church planting, church revitalization experience or has demonstrated experience pioneering new ministries or initiatives (including business) from the ground up
  • A track record of making disciples and developing multiplying ministry.
  • Highly strategic, organized, entrepreneurial, and self-motivated.
  • Strong communication and relational skills.
  • Creativity and a willingness to experiment with new approaches to ministry.
  • Ability to build teams and create healthy organizational culture.
  • Willingness to partner with established local Alliance churches.
  • Ability to engage and understand a community before determining what ministry should look like.
  • Experience working across denominational, cultural, socioeconomic, or generational lines.
  • Licensed in the C&MA or willing to go through the process

If God has given you a passion for pioneering, a burden for people far from Jesus, and a vision for what a multiplying church could look like in an unreached community, we'd love to talk with you.

Come plant where the need is great. Come build what doesn't yet exist. Come help bring the Gospel to communities where a multiplying church is desperately needed.

Campus Staff Minister- UNC Pembroke

Work Location:

North Carolina

Job Type:

Full time

God has called InterVarsity to plant and to build witnessing communities of students and faculty who follow Jesus on college and university campuses. Through these groups, we believe ever- increasing numbers of students and faculty from all ethnic groups and areas of the campus will be transformed by the Gospel. We expect to see campuses increasingly become places where people, ideas, and structures flourish to the glory of God. We confidently anticipate that our InterVarsity alumni will become change agents across the country and around the world. We pursue this calling by discerning and actively participating in what God is already doing on campus. This is the essence of being a Campus Staff Minister (CSM).

ESSENTIAL COMMITMENTS/RESPONSIBILITIES 

Spiritual Growth 

As a Campus Staff Minister, you pursue maturity as a disciple of Jesus Christ so that your life and work increasingly reflect a growing love for God, God’s Word, God’s people of every ethnicity and culture, and God’s purposes in the world. To do this, you will: 

  • Pursue a vibrant relationship with the triune God through engagement with Scripture, prayer, and worship, both individually and in community 

  • Develop self-leadership (growing in self-awareness, self-management, relational integrity, and resiliency)

  • Embrace Scriptural standards for behavior and attitudes 

 

Campus Leadership 

As a Campus Staff Minister, you increase the number of witnessing communities, as well as the size, health, spiritual maturity, and campus-wide influence of existing witnessing communities of students and faculty by being a: 

  • Visionary Guide: 

You communicate and model InterVarsity’s vision to see students and faculty transformed, campuses renewed, and world changers developed 

  • Create a culture of humble dependence on God and bold expectation in God’s intention to start new witnessing communities throughout the campus and on new campuses

  • Model – in person and through programs – InterVarsity’s vision and Core Values, including a biblically-defined commitment to engage every ethnic and social group on campus

  • Lead students and faculty – individually and collectively – through Scripture, prayer, teaching, and discipleship experiences, so that they articulate and align their ministry activities around this vision

  • Set annual goals through prayer, research and reflection with your teams (students, faculty, and staff) for qualitative and quantitative growth, including conversions and leadership development 

  • Structural Architect: 

You create, develop, align, and leverage ministry plans, programs, teams, and structures to close the gap between current reality and the aspirational goals. 

  • Build leadership teams who trust and partner well with you and who demonstrate spiritual vitality, relational health, and mission alignment

  • Develop and execute plans to achieve annual goals, evaluating and modifying the plan as needed throughout the year

  • Increase momentum for the vision by aligning programs, structures, conferences, and teams around the goals

  • Mobilize students and faculty to engage their relational networks with the gospel and to start new missional communities

  • Under the direction of the Area Director, may supervise Ministry Interns and Campus Ministry Interns as delegated 

  • Missional Developer: 

You intentionally gather, invite, and develop diverse groups of students and faculty so that they not only encounter and follow Jesus as Savior and Lord but also advance the mission on campus as participants and leaders. 

  • Create ways for faculty and students to encounter and follow Jesus through Scripture, worship, prayer, mission experiences, conferences, etc.

  • Equip students and faculty so that they think strategically about campus engagement and so that they proclaim – in word, deed, and power – the good news of Jesus, regularly inviting students and faculty to follow him as Savior and Lord

  • Disciple students and faculty by equipping them to hear the Word, respond actively, and debrief and interpret the experience so that they grow in Christlikeness, reflect our Core Values, and develop ministry skills

  • Invite, coach, and equip students and faculty to become increasingly effective participants and leaders, including starting new witnessing communities on campuses 

 

Organizational Collaboration 

As a Campus Staff Minister, you have joined a national mission. Therefore, you work with a network of other local, area, regional, and national InterVarsity staff and volunteers so that our work reflects Biblical standards of excellence, integrity, and partnership. 

  • Partner with and respond positively to the direction and coaching of your supervisors and national leaders

  • Contribute to collaborative and productive team meetings and relationships

  • Affiliate chapters under your care and submit Graduating Student Forms in order to increase our partnership with current students and alumni

  • Use national ministry resources and tools, as requested, including recruiting and/or participating in local, regional, or national conferences as

  • Complete reporting, planning and review requirements in a timely way so that you and your supervisors can assess and improve your work as a CSM

  • Comply with all InterVarsity policies and procedures 

 

Ministry Partnership Development 

As a Campus Staff Minister, you will develop a team of partners – churches and individuals (including alumni and community members) – who will resource the ministry financially, in prayer, or volunteer service that advances the mission. 

  • Raise 100% of the financial budget assigned by your supervisor

  • Communicate regularly with your ministry partners, nurturing the relationship through visits, phone calls, emails and regular prayer letters

  • Develop on-going, long-lasting partnership with alumni and volunteers

  • Comply with all Ministry Partnership Policies

  • Identify and invest in advocates who will build networks of volunteers and donors on InterVarsity’s behalf 

 

Accomplish all other assigned tasks as appropriate 

 

QUALIFICATIONS (common to all levels of CSM) 

  • Annually affirm InterVarsity’s Statement of Agreement (Doctrinal Basis and Purpose Statement). Abide by InterVarsity’s Code of Conduct. Believe and behave consonantly with InterVarsity’s Human Sexuality Theological Paper. Affirm and behave consonantly with InterVarsity’s “Women in Ministry Statement of Affirmation”

  • Bachelor’s degree for CSMs assigned to a four-year campus. A minimum of an Associate’s degree for CSMs assigned to a two-year campus or a community college

  • Strong interpersonal skills (including ability to minister to diverse ethnic communities and faculty)

  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills

  • Demonstrated problem solving skills

  • Familiarity with word processing, presentation, email, and spreadsheet software 

 

WORK ENVIRONMENT/PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS 

The CSM position leads ministry in a college campus environment. A designated office space may or may not be available. The CSM is required to travel to on-campus and off- campus sites as appropriate. Off-campus travel includes, but is not limited to: student ministry conferences, Ministry Partnership Development meetings, and InterVarsity- sponsored training sessions, meetings, and conferences. The CSM is regularly required to communicate with others, and routinely uses standard office equipment such as computers, phones, photocopiers, filing cabinets, etc.

Equip the Next Generation. Strengthen Families. Advance the Gospel.

Moody Bible Institute invites applications for a full-time Assistant Professor of Children and Family Ministry to join the Applied Theology and Church Ministries Department at our Chicago campus. We are seeking a dedicated scholar, experienced ministry practitioner, and gifted educator who is passionate about preparing students to serve children, parents, and families through biblically grounded and ministry-focused leadership.

This position offers an exciting opportunity to shape future ministry leaders while contributing to the growth and impact of Moody's Children and Family Ministry program.

The ideal candidate will bring a combination of academic excellence, practical ministry experience, and entrepreneurial initiative to support program development, student engagement, ministry partnerships, and curriculum innovation.

About Us

Moody Bible Institute is a Christ-centered higher education and media ministry dedicated to equipping people with the truth of God's Word. Through trusted biblical teaching, media, and educational resources, Moody reaches audiences around the world with the gospel and seeks to make a lasting Kingdom impact.

The Opportunity

The Assistant Professor of Children and Family Ministry serves as a faculty member within the Undergraduate School and provides academic leadership as Program Head for the Children and Family Ministry major. This role is responsible for teaching, mentoring students, overseeing internships and ministry experiences, and contributing to the strategic development of the program.

The successful candidate will help advance Moody Bible Institute's mission of providing a Bible-centered education that equips students to know Christ and make Him known through effective ministry in churches, organizations, families, and communities around the world.

What You’ll Do

  • Teach undergraduate courses in Children and Family Ministry, including biblical foundations, applied theology, child discipleship, family ministry, and practical ministry leadership.
  • Develop course syllabi, learning outcomes, and assessments that support academic excellence and ministry preparation.
  • Serve as Program Head for the Children and Family Ministry major, providing program leadership, oversight, and strategic direction.
  • Design, coordinate, and oversee internships, service-learning experiences, and community engagement opportunities.
  • Teach in multiple instructional formats, including in-person and online learning environments.
  • Advise and mentor students in their academic, vocational, and spiritual development.
  • Maintain regular office hours and an active campus presence.
  • Collaborate with faculty and institutional leaders to support program growth, ministry partnerships, curriculum development, and scholarly engagement.
  • Participate in faculty meetings, committee responsibilities, and institutional initiatives.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

Qualifications

Required

  • Master's degree in Children's Ministry, Applied Theology, Christian Education, Ministry Leadership, or a related field.
  • Ability to teach across related disciplines, including Applied Theology, Church Ministries, Elementary Education, and related ministry areas.
  • Commitment to transformational learning, student discipleship, and practical ministry preparation.
  • Ability to teach effectively in multiple learning environments, including online instruction.
  • Strong interpersonal, communication, and mentoring skills.
  • Demonstrated spiritual maturity, integrity, passion, and perseverance.
  • Collaborative and team-oriented mindset with an openness to diverse ministry approaches.
  • Commitment to the authority of Scripture and alignment with Moody Bible Institute's mission and doctrinal position.
  • Authorized to work in the United States without sponsorship.

Preferred

  • Earned doctorate in a related discipline.
  • Experience leading children's, family, or next-generation ministry initiatives within church or community settings.
  • Demonstrated success developing, growing, or sustaining academic and ministry programs.
  • College-level teaching experience.

Work Environment

  • Faculty members engage in teaching, mentoring, scholarship, and service within a Christ-centered academic environment.
  • This position includes classroom instruction, academic advising, committee participation, and collaboration with colleagues across the institution.
  • Work is performed in professional office, classroom, and ministry-related settings.
  • Faculty schedules generally occur Monday through Friday, with occasional evening and weekend responsibilities.

Additional Information

  • Candidates must demonstrate alignment with Moody Bible Institute's mission, doctrinal beliefs, and Christian values.
  • Employees are required to affirm Moody's Statement of Faith and adhere to Community Standards.
  • Moody Bible Institute values diversity and seeks team members who engage others in ways that honor its biblical foundation.
  • Moody complies with applicable nondiscrimination laws and, as a religious institution, requires employees to hold beliefs consistent with its Doctrinal Statement and Community Standards.

Why Join Us?

At Moody, education is more than a career. It is a calling to invest in the next generation of Christian leaders. As a faculty member, you will have the opportunity to mentor students, shape future ministry practitioners, and contribute to a Christ-centered learning community committed to biblical truth and ministry excellence.

Join us and help equip students to effectively disciple children, strengthen families, and advance the Gospel through transformational ministry around the world.

Join Our Team at Christ Church!

At Christ Church, every role matters because every person matters. When you serve with our ministry team, you’re not simply filling a position; you’re helping create opportunities for people to grow in their faith, develop their gifts, and experience our mission of “Uniting People to God and People to People.”

We’re looking for a Quest Teens Worship Coordinator who is passionate about worship and developing the next generation. If you love equipping young leaders and helping teens grow in their gifts and faith, we’d love to hear from you.

 

Why You’ll Love Working Here

As the Quest Teens Worship Coordinator, you’ll have the opportunity to invest in the next generation by helping teens grow in their faith, develop their musical gifts, and step into meaningful worship leadership.

This role is relational, creative, and full of impact. You’ll equip volunteer leaders, support teen worship teams, coordinate rehearsals and training, and partner with Quest Teens and Worship Ministry leadership.

Here, your leadership doesn’t just support a worship team — it helps shape future worship leaders.

  • You’ll help teens grow spiritually, musically, and as leaders.
  • You’ll work alongside a collaborative, mission-focused ministry team.
  • You’ll build volunteer teams and training systems that strengthen Quest Teens Worship for the future.

 

What You’ll Do

As the Quest Teens Worship Coordinator, you’ll help strengthen Quest Teens Worship through four key areas:

  • Volunteer Leadership Development: Recruit, equip, and support Worship Team Leads and Serving Team members; assist with vetting and onboarding teen worship team members and adult volunteers; and help build strong volunteer ownership and healthy ministry teams.
  • Worship Training & Development: Help teens grow musically, spiritually, and as worship leaders through rehearsals, auditions, coaching, training, and worship opportunities. Periodically lead worship at teen services and events and coordinate vocal coaches or other training resources as needed.
  • Ministry Coordination & Collaboration: Partner with Quest Teens, Worship Ministry leadership, and volunteer Team Leads to align schedules, priorities, training needs, ministry expectations, and participation and safety guidelines.
  • Administration & Planning: Maintain key participation and training records, support ministry activities and budgets, and provide updates on progress, needs, volunteer development, and ministry involvement. 

Why This Role Matters

The Quest Teens Worship Coordinator helps shape the next generation by creating opportunities for teens to grow in faith, develop their musical gifts, and step into leadership.

Your work strengthens Quest Teens Worship today while helping develop future worship leaders.

 

What We’re Looking For

A worship leader who loves Jesus, connects well with teenagers, and enjoys developing people. You’re relational, organized, encouraging, and comfortable working with both teens and adult volunteers.

You understand that strong worship ministry is about more than music — it’s about helping young people grow in faith, confidence, leadership, and using their gifts to serve others.      

Christ Church seeks a candidate who is a committed follower of Jesus Christ and whose personal values align with our mission, vision, and beliefs. The successful candidate will actively support the ministry of Christ Church and be open to pursuing membership as part of becoming fully engaged in the life of our church family.                                                                                                                            

Minimum Qualifications

  • Experience in worship ministry as a worship leader, musician, vocalist, or coordinator.
  • Experience working with teenagers in a church, ministry, or youth setting.
  • Experience leading or developing volunteers.
  • Strong communication, organization, and teamwork skills.
  • Ability to coordinate rehearsals, schedules, and ministry activities.

Knowledge, Skills, Abilities & Other Characteristics

  • Ability to encourage and develop teen musicians and worship leaders.
  • Strong relationship-building and communication skills.
  • Organized, dependable, and able to manage multiple priorities.
  • Demonstrates integrity, maturity, and sound judgment.
  • Strong team-player mindset — the ultimate goal is the Team wins!
  • Demonstrates a mature relationship with Jesus Christ and alignment with the mission, vision, values, and Statement of Faith of Christ Church.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience with youth or student worship ministry.
  • Experience serving in a large or multi-campus church.
  • Experience developing volunteer worship teams.
  • Familiarity with Planning Center or similar ministry scheduling tools.

 

Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA)

At Christ Church, we believe every team member should have the opportunity to thrive. In accordance with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA), we are committed to providing reasonable accommodations for qualified individuals with disabilities.

If you need an accommodation during the interview process or in connection with this role, please let our Human Resources team know.

 

Equal Employment Opportunity (EEO)

Christ Church is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. We value diversity and welcome individuals to bring their unique gifts and experiences to our mission.

 

Ready to Join the Team?

If you're passionate about worship, developing young leaders, and helping teenagers use their gifts to serve God and others, we'd love to hear from you.

job_name: Youth Ministry Director at Joint Base Elmendorf–Richardson JBER, AK
tag_categories: [eCom, Course Creation, Static Site Builder]
post_html:
*Please note this position would require our Staff to live near the community where they would be doing ministry.
Description:
There are nearly 300,000 teenagers of active-duty U.S. military parents who are stationed all over the world. These teens move an average of seven times during their school-aged years. The questions of identity and belonging that all teens face grow even more challenging to answer amid starting over and meeting new friends at each location.
This is where you can be the difference in a military teen’s life! By being in their world, walking alongside them, and creating a community where they experience the truth of God’s love and purpose for them, our staff provide a safe space where teens can develop friendships and connections to experience laughter, build hope, and generate resiliency.
We are currently providing incarnational ministry at many military installations around the world. You will have the opportunity to lead and oversee the overall Young Life Military program, known as Club Beyond, which is ecumenically focused and outreach oriented.
Responsibilities:
  • Actively develop healthy relationships with adults, as well as kids, and build vibrant relationships with the local community, the military installation, and the chapel community.
  • Be a role model (incarnational) and assist with developing community outreach to "unchurched" teens, discipleship to Christian teens, and leading and equipping volunteers to do "hands-on" middle and high school Christian youth programs.
  • Work well in an environment that sees (due to high military operational tempo) a high degree of turnover among teens, families, chaplains and volunteers.
  • Be respectful of and embrace a community that is deeply influenced by a military culture.
  • In this ministry, you will need to live out the Club Beyond Core Value Statement:
Club Beyond is a Christ-centered community of leaders with an exclusively military focus. Our methods are incarnational, and our perspective is ecumenical. We leverage strategic partnerships for the greatest results. We value professionalism from our staff and excellence in our stewardship.
Qualifications:
  • A deep love for Christ and for lost teens.
  • Competent communicator with youths, parents, and senior military leaders.
  • Teachable heart.
  • Willingness to make a three-year commitment.
  • Minimum of three years' youth ministry experience preferred.
  • College degree preferred.
  • Willingness to raise part of the budget through personal support.
  • Committed to a relational ministry approach.
  • Energetic.
  • Small event planning skills.
  • Strong initiative.
  • Note, this position would require our Staff to live near the community where they would be doing ministry.
Benefits:
  • Full-time salary: Based on experience, responsibility, and fundraising levels.
  • Benefits: Full health coverage (including dental, vision and life insurance).
  • Expense reimbursement (mileage [office and ministry related]).
  • Training and career development is built into the job.
Salary:
The Base Salary range: $45,000 to $60,000 (Salary is based on education and experience). In addition to salary, a Cost of Living Adjustment, dependent on location, is available. The Annual National Funding provided is $16,667.
Location:
Club Beyond works on military installations all over the world. We currently have openings at:
In the USA:
  • Fort Rucker, Alabama
  • Joint Base Elmendorf-Richardson (JBER), Alaska
  • Fort Irwin, California
  • Camp Pendleton, California
  • Travis Air Force Base, California
  • Joint Base Anacostia-Bolling (JBAB), Washington, D.C.
  • Eglin Air Force Base, Florida
  • Fort Benning, Georgia
  • Fort Stewart, Georgia
  • Fort Riley, Kansas
  • Fort Bragg, North Carolina
  • Fort Sill, Oklahoma
  • Fort Jackson, South Carolina
  • Fort Belvoir, Virginia
  • Joint Base Lewis-McChord (JBLM), Washington

Overseas:
  • Geilenkirchen, Germany and various other locations in Germany
  • Naval Base Guam
  • Aviano Air Base, Italy
  • Vicenza, Italy
  • Camp Zama, Japan
  • Yokosuka, Japan
Want to know more about our mission and culture?
Please check out clubbeyond.org to learn how Club Beyond has been changing the lives of military teens for over 40 years!

post_html:
MINISTRY SUMMARY
The Pastor of Congregational Care will serve as a facilitator of care to those who are in crisis, hurt, illness, recovery, bereavement, and in times of celebrations. The Pastor of Congregational Care will help the body of HOPE Church respond in a way that exhibits the Christ-like love and care to further the mission of HOPE Church to encourage people to become fully devoted followers of Jesus Christ.
 
MINISTRY DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES
The following duties are normal for this position. These are not to be construed as exclusive or all-inclusive. Other duties may be required and assigned.
  • Recruit, develop, equip, and encourage all Care team ministries that will assist in serving people who are hurting or needing help under the guidance of Congregational Care (visitation teams, prayer teams for services/events, etc.).
  • Meet with people daily as needs arise here at HOPE.
  • Work closely with the HOPE Cares ministry team to assess congregational needs.
  • Conduct and oversee hospital visitations as needed, discerning when to involve volunteers, staff, and pastoral team.
  • Develop new and innovative ministries that will assist HOPE in developing as a community/congregation that does “One Another” well in the “big” moments of life (crisis, hurt, illness, bereavement, and celebration).
  • Develop and lead New Believers ministry including follow up when someone makes a commitment to Christ, next steps, and providing various studies and classes for new believers.
  • To equip and train team leaders to be able to lead people into a personal relationship with Jesus Christ.
QUALIFICATIONS
  • Ability to work collaboratively, receive direction, and adapt in a dynamic ministry environment.
  • Be able to respond to crisis situations in a calm, gracious, and confident manner.
  • Experience in recruiting and training volunteers
  • Be able to relate to people in a variety of settings, demonstrating excellent interpersonal skills (i.e.  groups, individuals, all ages, etc.)
  • Communicate effectively with staff, church members, people in the community.
  • Possess and utilize leadership skills.
  • Experience in managing a team is preferred.
  • A bachelor’s degree (or advanced degree) in Bible, ministry, or a related field is preferred.
HOPE STAFF TEAM EXPECTATIONS
  • Be devoted to Jesus — Maintain a sincere, growing walk with Christ, His Church, and pursue excellence in His service.
  • Be aligned with HOPE’s beliefs — Support and uphold the doctrine, mission, vision, and values of HOPE Church and the Evangelical Covenant denomination.
  • Live with integrity and ethics — Practice Christ-honoring character, honesty, and self-control in every area of life.
  • Engage in worship rhythm — Participate weekly in worship services and be available for occasional evening gatherings.
  • Be present in meetings — Attend staff and ministry meetings as needed.
  • Work as one team — Build relationships, communicate concerns biblically and promptly, and contribute to a collaborative staff culture.
  • Honor confidentiality — Protect sensitive information and foster trust, integrity, and respect.
  • Model generosity — We anticipate our staff are tithing faithfully to HOPE Church or taking steps to move in that direction as a witness of Kingdom investment (Matthew 6:19–20).
  • Develop leaders and volunteers — Equip and empower volunteers within ministry areas.
  • Communicate and coordinate well — Keep staff and leadership informed so ministry efforts move in unity.
  • Demonstrate professionalism — Maintain a neat appearance, an organized workspace, and communicate clearly with Senior Leadership.
  • Serve beyond your lane — Offer assistance to other ministry areas when appropriate.
  • Protect HOPE’s witness — Represent HOPE Church in ways that guard its reputation, unity, and ministry impact.
  • Understand the consequence of expectations — Failure to consistently meet expectations may result in review and possible dismissal.
  • Exit with honor — If employment concludes, do so in a way that protects the unity and ministry of HOPE Church.
Additionally, all HOPE Staff are required to affirm our “Staff Culture and Values” Commitment.
 
HOPE Church is an Evangelical Covenant Church (ECC) in Grand Forks, ND.

Student Intern - Illinois and Indiana (Graduate and Faculty Ministry)

Work Location:

Indiana
