New Life Christian Alliance - Whittier, CA

Senior Pastor

The Senior Pastor will provide spiritual and organizational leadership to a multi-generational, bilingual congregation and help lead the church toward its vision for spiritual maturity, discipleship, evangelism, leadership development, and community engagement.

About Our Church

New Life Christian Alliance desires to become a thriving, multi-generational congregation with a steady influx of new people who reflect the demographics of the surrounding community. The church seeks to lead people along a pathway toward becoming fully devoted followers of Christ Jesus.

The church envisions becoming a united church family marked by:

  • Biblical faithfulness

  • Spiritual maturity

  • Authentic relationships

  • Evangelism

  • Discipleship

  • Community engagement

  • Multiplication of disciples, leaders, and ministries

  • Potentially planting another church within five years

We are “One Church in two languages.” The English congregation is multi-ethnic and multi-generational, with approximately one-third Chinese, one-third other Asian ethnicities, and one-third other non-Asian ethnicities. The Chinese congregation consists of ethnically Chinese, Mandarin-speaking immigrants and is also multi-generational.

The congregation's strengths include faithfulness, genuine love, service, generosity—particularly toward missions—and a strong biblical foundation. Members care for one another in practical ways, and the healthy relationship between the English and Chinese congregations is viewed as a meaningful expression of unity in Christ.

The church desires continued growth in spiritual depth and biblical maturity, leadership development and member engagement, intentional investment in the next generation, evangelism, and community involvement. There is a desire to see members move from comfort and passive participation toward greater spiritual hunger, ownership, leadership, service, and intentional discipleship.

Position Description

The Senior Pastor will serve as the primary spiritual shepherd and leader of our diverse, bilingual church family, guiding people of all ages as they grow in their relationship with Christ. Through prayer, teaching, encouragement, and collaborative leadership, the pastor will help foster a culture of discipleship, equip believers to serve and lead, reach others with the Gospel, and strengthen the church’s presence and ministry within the broader community.

Key areas of pastoral ministry include:

  • Providing leadership and vision

  • Communicating the Word of God through inspiration, instruction, exhortation, and correction

  • Managing conflict biblically

  • Recruiting and mentoring lay leaders

  • Modeling and mobilizing one-on-one discipleship

  • Mobilizing the congregation for evangelistic outreach

  • Pastoral care, including visitation and counseling

  • Ministering to families

The expected average workload is 45–50 hours per week, including services, meetings, Bible studies, and other ministry responsibilities.

Qualifications

The preferred candidate will:

  • Be godly, confident in Christ, disciplined, and Spirit-filled.

  • Have at least 10 years of ministry experience.

  • Preferably be in his late 40s or early 50s.

  • Hold a Master of Divinity degree.

  • Demonstrate strong leadership and vision.

  • Communicate the Word of God effectively.

  • Be capable of managing conflict biblically.

  • Be committed to discipleship and evangelistic outreach.

  • Have the ability to recruit and mentor lay leaders.

  • Demonstrate pastoral care and a heart for families.

Compensation & Benefits

Between 75k - 95k

To be considered for this position, please complete the application to include your testimony, resume and other background information related to the position.

If the district office has reviewed your application and they think you may be a potential match for the position, that the hiring manager will reach out to you for next steps.

This position requires licensing with The Christian & Missionary Alliance. To learn more about The Alliance and requirements for licensing, please visit our website

Please do not contact the church directly.

The Director of Student Ministry @ MBC Loudoun will lead a ministry to middle school and high school students and their families that is centered on Jesus, rooted in Scripture, and focused on helping students take meaningful next steps of faith. We are looking for a leader who is burdened to reach students across Loudoun County with the gospel of Jesus Christ, especially students who are unchurched, dechurched, spiritually curious, or disconnected from Christian community.


This leader will give primary attention to reaching, discipling, and sending students as followers of Jesus who live with faith, courage, and purpose in their schools, teams, neighborhoods, and friend groups. The Director of Student Ministry will also inspire, equip, and shepherd a Serve Team of adult leaders to do the work of ministry by helping students feel known, loved, challenged, and sent.

OTHER MINISTRIES / RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Model a life of spiritual maturity, humility, collaboration, and joyful service among staff, Serve Team members, students, and families.


REQUIREMENTS

  • A passionate disciple of Jesus Christ who continually seeks to abide in Christ and demonstrates the biblical qualifications for spiritual leadership.
  • A proven disciple-maker who has helped others grow as followers of Jesus and is able to equip students and leaders to make disciples.
  • A spiritually mature and emotionally healthy leader who demonstrates humility, wisdom, integrity, and consistency in both personal and public life.

Bridge City Church Residency

Thank you for your interest in the Bridge City Church Residency! Bridge City Church has a vision of becoming a multi-ethnic, multi-generational church, deeply transforming lives for the flourishing of all people. We long to see Heaven meet earth as we follow the Way of Jesus.

As a pastoral resident, you will work directly with the Lead Pastor as you progress through our residency. You will begin immediately engaging with content and praxis that equips and prepares you for high-level leadership in one of three specific contexts: (1) a Pastoral Ministry Context, (2) a Replanting Context, (3) a Church Planting Context.

In partnership with the Holy Spirit and how God has gifted and wired you, we will help determine over time your next steps internally and/or externally.

About the Residency

The aim of our residency is to raise up high character and high capacity Pastors and Church Planters who can influence God’s people to accomplish God’s mission for God’s glory.

We will accomplish this with our three-prong approach. First is theological training and development. Second is practical ministry experience. Third is a thick relational connection with high level leadership, namely the senior pastor and other residents.

Year 1:

The aim of year one is gaining relational equity with Bridge City’s congregation and growing deeply in character development, and to begin your theological training through an accredited program/university. This year will give a foundation in order to be as successful as possible in development. Strong relationships with the Church, growing in character (earning trust), and beginning to grow in theological depth and breadth. Immediate discipling will begin for the resident and those the resident will walk with.

Year 2:

The aim of year two is beginning to lead in ministry departments and preach and teach on Sunday mornings. Now that relationships have been established, character and trust is growing, and theological depth and breadth, the pulpit will be a place of growth. Residents will learn how to teach and preach in a Christ-centered expository way. Residents will launch and lead disciple groups, and add value to ministry departments as they lead teams and people.

Year 3:

The aim of year three is multiplying your ministry as we seek where your next steps are either internally or beyond Bridge City. We will develop a plan in year three that positions you to boldly and confidently step into what’s next.

Next Steps

Click on "Apply to Position" to show your interest. After an initial screening we will then send you the following phases of the application:

  • Phase 1 - Apply (10-15 minutes questionnaire to collect more detailed employment information)
  • Phase 2 - Ministry Assessment (~60-minute questionnaire covering topics related to being a ministry worker)
    • Once your application has been reviewed and approved, you will be sent an email with a link to complete your Ministry Assessment.
  • Phase 3 - Local Assessment
    • The local supervisor(s) for this position will review your application, potentially reaching out to conduct an interview.

    Upon provisional acceptance, you will register for support-raising training run by Reliant to start your support-based ministry journey.

Description:
There are nearly 300,000 teenagers of active-duty U.S. military parents who are stationed all over the world. These teens move an average of seven times during their school-aged years. The questions of identity and belonging that all teens face grow even more challenging to answer amid starting over and meeting new friends at each location.
This is where you can be the difference in a military teen’s life! By being in their world, walking alongside them, and creating a community where they experience the truth of God’s love and purpose for them, our staff provide a safe space where teens can develop friendships and connections to experience laughter, build hope, and generate resiliency.
We are currently providing incarnational ministry at many military installations around the world. You will have the opportunity to lead and oversee the overall Young Life Military program, known as Club Beyond, which is ecumenically focused and outreach oriented.

Residency | Internship

    Discover Your Calling. Develop Your Gifts. Change the World.
    At Cuyahoga Valley Church, we believe that the next generation of ministry leaders is sitting in our churches and colleges right now—men and women who sense God’s call and are ready to take their next step in following Him into intentional Kingdom impact. That’s why we’ve created a two-year leadership development pathway designed to equip, empower, and send emerging leaders into gospel-centered ministry.

    Year 1: The Internship
    The CVC Ministry Internship is a year of discovery and growth. You’ll gain real-world ministry experience by serving in multiple departments—Kids, Youth, Young Adults, Groups, Counseling, Worship, and more—while learning directly from pastors and leaders who have decades of experience.You’ll develop spiritual disciplines, grow as a leader, and begin to discern where God is calling you to serve. And as part of our partnership with Emmaus Seminary, you’ll receive tuition-free theological training that integrates faith and practice in a dynamic, hands-on environment.

    Year 2: The Residency
    Interns who demonstrate exceptional growth and calling may be invited into the second year—The CVC Ministry Residency. This year is all about focus. You’ll embed deeply within one primary area of ministry, take on greater leadership responsibility, and receive advanced coaching to prepare you for life-long ministry.Whether your future includes serving on one of CVC’s campus launch teams, planting a church, or stepping into a full-time ministry role elsewhere, the Residency is designed to send you out ready to lead with conviction and humility.

    Why CVC?

    • Learn from a team of pastors and ministry leaders who have decades of real-world experience.
    • Receive a tuition-free seminary education through our partnership with Emmaus Seminary.
    • Experience life in a thriving, multiplying, multi-campus church.
    • Experience life in one of the most exciting and growing cities in the Midwest.

    If you’re passionate about Jesus, hungry to grow, and ready to give a year or two to discover God’s call on your life, we’d love to talk with you.

    This is more than a fixed program—it’s a launching pad for a lifetime of ministry impact.


    Next Steps

    Click on "Apply to Position" to show your interest. Following an initial screening, we will send you the rest of the application to move forward.

If the successful candidate has training, experience, and desire, he/she could be asked to teach classical voice. This position instructs on the Cedarville University campus. All requirements for the master's degree must be completed by June 2025 Outstanding studio teaching skills Fluency in the English language Ability to balance the diverse priorities of a voice program within a liberal arts institution Fit with the Christian mission of Cedarville University Candidates must be willing to uphold the University's Doctrinal Statement, Community Covenant, and General Work Place Standards This temporary position is subject to Cedarville University policies, verification of credentials, and other information required by law, including the successful completion of a background check. Cedarville University is an accredited institutional member of the National Association of Schools of Music. Contact Information: For consideration, an employment application must be submitted in our online employment application website, including completion of a doctrinal questionnaire, submission of unofficial transcripts, and a CV. All official inquiries should be directed to Beth Porter, Chair, Department of Music and Worship.

Job Overview
Full-time salary position, 45-50 hours per week. Compensation package based on experience and training. Worship Pastor will be responsible to direct volunteers and lead the congregation in worship, including all technical and creative arts aspects of the church’s worship. Models and understands the core values of Shawnee Alliance and fits well into the vision, mission, direction, culture and purpose of the church.

Responsibilities and Duties

  • Serve as the primary shepherd of the worship team.
  • Select music that leads the congregation into worship going along with the theme of the message.
  • Recruit, mentor and train volunteers as needed to ensure dynamic worship in all Shawnee Alliance services.
  • Schedule and plan worship times that include emphasis and sacraments such as communion, baptism, child dedication and other special services.
  • Lead weekly rehearsal and devotional with volunteer team.
  • Able to preach engaging, Biblically grounded sermons that further the vision of the church and implement worship objectives throughout the church.
  • Provide for the advancement of team member skillsets through training and feedback.
  • Oversee the creation of sermon slides for the teaching pastor.
  • Oversee the production of videos including announcement, testimony, promotional and sermon bumper videos.
  • Purchase and maintain equipment for the Worship and Tech Teams.
  • Communicate with the pastoral staff on a regular basis to discuss worship themes for services.
  • Use resources of worship ministries (technical and musical) to support other ministries/events within the church.
  • Create both long and short-term plans for the worship ministries that fit the vision of Shawnee Alliance.
  • Maintain church music licenses and subscriptions related to worship arts and service production.
  • Create and oversee yearly worship budget to accomplish all of the above.
  • Assist in benevolent meetings and other pastoral care items.
  • Assist the Lead Pastor as requested.

Education/Experience and Skills

  • BA in religion, worship arts or comparable degree
  • Hold or be able to be licensed within the Christian and Missionary Alliance
  • Minimum of five years’ experience in worship leadership or relevant experience
  • Possess a positive attitude in the church environment
  • Lead and manage a team well
  • Work well with minimal supervision
  • Undergo and pass a background check at the church’s expense and on a recurring basis

Computer systems/software programs used:

  • Microsoft Word/Excel/Email
  • Adobe Creative Suite
  • Planning Center Online
  • ProPresenter
  • Other video and editing software as required for service production

Other Requirements and Expectations:

Must align with the doctrinal statement and official positions of the Christian and Missionary Alliance (www.cmalliance.org/statement-of-faith)
Candidate Profile
Shawnee Alliance Church is seeking a worship pastor who excels in shepherding and leading teams, planning and coordinating Sunday morning worship experiences, and who possesses a background in pastoral ministry. While this role includes musical worship leadership, the larger responsibility is the pastoral oversight of the Sunday worship experience including team development, service planning, congregational engagement, and volunteer systems. The ideal candidate will also be able to preach engaging, biblically grounded sermons that further the vision of the church and implement worship objectives throughout the church.

Our Next Worship Pastor
Over the past 30 years our worship pastors have engaged primarily as a pastor who oversees the worship ministries of the church. This is different from a song leader, or worship leader. We believe the ideal candidate will develop leaders within the worship ministry to serve and lead on Sunday morning. Our next worship pastor will be a pastor first.

Reporting Relationship
The pastor reports to and is held accountable by the Lead Pastor.

Why This Role Matters
Shawnee Alliance Church defines the role and purpose of our ministries as much broader than Sunday morning. We have been blessed to extend our influence throughout the community in dynamic ministries, both overseen by the church and through our congregation intentionally deployed in our community. However, Sunday morning is still a critical expression of our faith and mission. Leading others in worship is a sacred responsibility, and one that serves to both further the faith of our congregation and to honor God as we worship Him with all our heart, soul, mind and strength. Our next worship pastor should value:

  • The priesthood of all believers. God has equipped the church with leadership to equip the saints for the work of ministry.
  • Dynamic, Christ-focused worship. Our worship team serves to point our people to Jesus, not to impress with performance.
  • Excellence in all we do. Excellence is first an expression of giving God our best, followed by the result of what God himself creates in and through our worship.

Who This Role is Not For
We want to avoid a bad fit. In that spirit, this role would not be a good fit for:

  • Someone who expects to be at the center of every worship set.
  • Someone uncomfortable with leading change.
  • Someone who avoids difficult conversations or healthy conflict.
  • Someone who would prefer serving as a worship leader rather than a pastor who oversees worship ministry.

Goals and Expectations
First year

  • Establish healthy relationships with the worship team, congregation, and community.
  • Address critical technological and infrastructure needs.
  • Work collaboratively with the Lead Pastor and other teaching pastors to plan, coordinate, and execute Sunday morning worship services.
  • Begin equipping our worship team.

General Responsibilities

  • Oversee the planning, coordination, and execution of Sunday morning worship alongside the Lead Pastor.
  • Oversee all aspects of the Sunday morning worship experience including selecting songs, video elements, announcements, vision casting, and hosting for our contemporary, traditional, and online services.
  • Serve as the primary recruiter, trainer, deployer, discipler, and shepherd for the worship team.
  • Serve alongside the pastoral team in implementing pastoral care for the congregation.
  • Oversee the purchase and maintenance of all equipment needed for worship ministry and audio/visual needs of the church.
  • Support the ministries of the church by coordinating volunteers as needed to assist with audio, visual, and worship.

What Success Looks Like

We will know we found the right worship pastor when:

  • He or she builds strong, trust-based relationships within the worship team, congregation, and community.
  • The Sunday morning worship experience is engaging, participatory, and executed with excellence.
  • New volunteers are discovering their role in ministry, both on stage and behind the scenes.
  • The congregation embraces our hire as a pastor, not simply a song leader.


Theological Alignment
Shawnee Alliance Church is a congregation of the Christian and Missionary Alliance. As such, any pastor of our church should be in agreement with the statement of beliefs and theological position papers available at www.cmalliance.com. Additionally, to be an ideal theological fit the next worship pastor should be aligned in:

  • The priesthood of all believers. God has equipped every one of his children with spiritual gifts to be exercised in worshipful service.
  • The pastor. In accordance with Ephesians 4:11-16, the primary role of the pastor is to equip the saints for the work of ministry.
  • Disciplemaking. The role of the church is to make disciples not simply converts or church attendees.


Cultural Fit
Our church has a culture. We are:

  • Authentic. We expect our pastors to be the same person in the pulpit, on the platform, in staff meeting, and our community.
  • Relational. Our work is in the lives of people. Tasks serve people, not their own ends.
  • Driven. We do not micromanage. Our volunteers and congregation are full of passion and drive; we desire to see the same in our pastors.


Education, Experience and Skills

  • BA in religion, worship arts, or comparable degree
  • 5+ years relevant experience
  • Holds or is able to gain ordination within the Christian and Missionary Alliance
  • Positive attitude in a church environment
  • Ability to lead teams
  • Able to work well with minimal supervision
  • Must undergo and pass a background check at the church’s expense and on a recurring basis
  • Familiarity with Planning Center, Microsoft Office and other relevant software


Personal Characteristics

  • Authentic: We desire our pastor to be the same person on and off the stage.
  • Hard working and self-motivated: Our church is full of men and women who work hard, and we want our worship pastor to share this value.
  • Relatable: Our pastor should be able to relate well to our community and church members.

CrossBridge Alliance is a missions-oriented C&MA church in Wyoming’s largest city, serving a growing tech and military community. We missionally engage by being firmly Planted in Christ, Growing in Him, Bearing Fruit in keeping with the Holy Spirit at work in us, and Planting Seeds through our gospel witness.

2. ROLE SUMMARY

The primary responsibility of the Connections Pastor is to connect people to God, the CrossBridge congregation, and the broader community through discipleship, ministry development, teaching, and partnership. This role is all about building relationships.

  • Full Time + Health Benefits, Cell Phone, & More

3. ESSENTIAL RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Connection Structures: Design and implement effective systems to help people move from first-time guests to actively engaged members, facilitating their spiritual journey and involvement in church life.

5. QUALIFICATIONS & REQUIREMENTS

  • General alignment with the Christian & Missionary Alliance’s Statement of Faith and our mission.

  • Able to develop effective structures to accomplish the task of connecting people with church ministries.

Campus Staff Minister – New England Area (Graduate and Faculty Ministry)

Work Location:

Connecticut

Job Type:

Full time

God has called InterVarsity to plant and to build witnessing communities of students and faculty who follow Jesus on college and university campuses. Through these groups, we believe ever- increasing numbers of students and faculty from all ethnic groups and areas of the campus will be transformed by the Gospel. We expect to see campuses increasingly become places where people, ideas, and structures flourish to the glory of God. We confidently anticipate that our InterVarsity alumni will become change agents across the country and around the world. We pursue this calling by discerning and actively participating in what God is already doing on campus. This is the essence of being a Campus Staff Minister (CSM).

This position is open to both full-time and part-time applicants living in CT, ME, MA, RI, VT, or NH. The pay range listed is for an employee working 40 hours/week as a Campus Staff Minister. Pay will be prorated for employees who work less than 40 hours/week. Increased pay may be available in high cost of living areas as a geographic adjustment.


We have positions in the following locations:

  • Dartmouth University -- graduate students

  • Yale University -- graduate students

  • University of Connecticut (UConn), Storrs -- graduate students and/or faculty

  • University of Massachusetts, Amherst -- graduate students and/or faculty

  • University of Maine -- graduate students and/or faculty

  • University of Rhode Island -- graduate students and/or faculty

  • University of Vermont -- graduate students and/or faculty

Other schools may be available.

Please submit the GFM Interest Form before completing the full application for a position with Graduate & Faculty Ministries in our online system. We will contact you when we are ready to proceed with the application process.​

Volunteers are welcome. Volunteer opportunities range from prayer and hospitality to leading a campus fellowship of graduate students and faculty. Those interested in volunteering will go through an application and interview process, however, volunteer openings are not posted online. For more information, complete the GFM Interest Form.

ESSENTIAL COMMITMENTS/RESPONSIBILITIES 

Spiritual Growth 

You pursue maturity as a disciple of Jesus Christ so that your life and work increasingly reflects a growing love for God, God’s Word, God’s people of every ethnicity and culture, and God’s purposes in the world. To do this, you will: 

  • Pursue a vibrant relationship with the triune God through engagement with Scripture, prayer, and worship, both individually and in community 

  • Develop self-leadership (growing in self-awareness, self-management, relational integrity, and resiliency) 

  • Embrace Scriptural standards for behavior and attitudes 

 

Campus Leadership 

You communicate and model InterVarsity’s vision to see students and faculty transformed, campuses renewed and world changers developed 

  • Create a culture of humble dependence on God and bold expectation in God’s intention to start new witnessing communities throughout the campus and on new campuses 

  • Model – in person and through programs – InterVarsity’s vision and Core Values, including a biblically-defined commitment to engage every ethnic and social group on campus 

  • Lead students and faculty – individually and collectively – through Scripture, prayer, teaching, and discipleship experiences, so that they articulate and align their ministry activities around this vision 

  • Set annual goals through prayer, research and reflection with your teams (students, faculty, and staff) for qualitative and quantitative growth, including conversions and leadership development 

 

You create, develop, align and leverage ministry plans, programs, teams, and structures to close the gap between current reality and the aspirational goals. 

  • Build leadership teams who trust and partner well with you and who demonstrate spiritual vitality, relational health, and mission alignment 

  • Develop and execute plans to achieve annual goals, evaluating and modifying the plan as needed throughout the year 

  • Increase momentum for the vision by aligning programs, structures, conferences and teams around the goals 

  • Mobilize students and faculty to engage their relational networks with the gospel and to start new missional communities 

  • Under the direction of the Area Director, may supervise Ministry Interns and Campus Ministry Interns as delegated 

 

You intentionally gather, invite, and develop diverse groups of students and faculty so that they not only encounter and follow Jesus as Savior and Lord but also advance the mission on campus as participants and leaders. 

  • Create ways for faculty and students to encounter and follow Jesus through Scripture, worship, prayer, mission experiences, conferences, etc. 

  • Equip students and faculty so that they think strategically about campus engagement and so that they proclaim – in word, deed, and power – the good news of Jesus, regularly inviting students and faculty to follow him as Savior and Lord 

  • Disciple students and faculty by equipping them to hear the Word, respond actively, and debrief and interpret the experience so that they grow in Christlikeness, reflect our Core Values, and develop ministry skills 

  • Invite, coach, and equip students and faculty to become increasingly effective participants and leaders, including starting new witnessing communities on campuses 

 

Organizational Collaboration 

You work with a network of other local, area, regional, and national InterVarsity staff and volunteers so that our work reflects Biblical standards of excellence, integrity, and partnership. 

  • Partner with and respond positively to the direction and coaching of your supervisors and national leaders 

  • Contribute to collaborative and productive team meetings and relationships 

  • Affiliate chapters under your care and submit Graduating Student Forms in order to increase our partnership with current students and alumni 

  • Use national ministry resources and tools, as requested, including recruiting and/or participating in local, regional, or national conferences as  

  • Complete reporting, planning and review requirements in a timely way so that you and your supervisors can assess and improve your work as a CSM 

  • Comply with all InterVarsity policies and procedures 

 

Ministry Partnership Development 

You will develop a team of partners – churches and individuals (including alumni and community members) – who will resource the ministry financially, in prayer, or volunteer service that advances the mission. 

  • Raise 100% of the financial budget assigned by your supervisor 

  • Communicate regularly with your ministry partners, nurturing the relationship through visits, phone calls, emails and regular prayer letters 

  • Develop on-going, long-lasting partnership with alumni and volunteers 

  • Comply with all Ministry Partnership Policies 

  • Identify and invest in advocates who will build networks of volunteers and donors on InterVarsity’s behalf 

 

Accomplish all other assigned tasks as appropriate 

 

QUALIFICATIONS (common to all levels of CSM) 

  • Annually affirm InterVarsity’s Statement of Agreement (Doctrinal Basis and Purpose Statement). Abide by InterVarsity’s Code of Conduct. Believe and behave consonantly with InterVarsity’s Human Sexuality Theological Paper. Affirm and behave consonantly with InterVarsity’s “Women in Ministry Statement of Affirmation” 

  • Bachelor’s degree for CSMs assigned to a four-year campus. A minimum of an Associate’s degree for CSMs assigned to a two-year campus or a community college 

  • Strong interpersonal skills (including ability to minister to diverse ethnic communities and faculty) 

  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills 

  • Demonstrated problem solving skills 

  • Familiarity with word processing, presentation, email, and spreadsheet software 

 

WORK ENVIRONMENT/PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS 

The CSM position leads ministry in a college campus environment. A designated office space may or may not be available. The CSM is required to travel to on-campus and off- campus sites as appropriate. Off-campus travel includes, but is not limited to: student ministry conferences, Ministry Partnership Development meetings, and InterVarsity- sponsored training sessions, meetings, and conferences. The CSM is regularly required to communicate with others, and routinely uses standard office equipment such as computers, phones, photocopiers, filing cabinets, etc. 

Pay Range: $44,016.00 - $58,680.00 per year

Pay: This position is funded through personal fundraising. Accordingly, compensation will vary based on the ability of the individual to secure a donor team to fund the cost of his/her salary. The anticipated salary range for this position on a full-time basis (40 hours/week) is dependent on a variety of factors, including location and cost of living. The actual salary received, including any geographic adjustment to account for location and cost of living, is subject to the individual’s ability to raise funds necessary to cover the full amount of such salary within the range set forth in the job posting details.

Benefits:

We offer a competitive benefits package, including health care and retirement savings with a match. Eligibility is based on employee type and hours worked.  Benefits include the following:

  • 403(b) Retirement Savings Plan

  • 403(b) matching contributions

  • Dental insurance

  • Employee assistance program

  • Employee discounts

  • Flexible work schedule

  • Flexible spending accounts

  • Health insurance

  • Health savings account

  • Life insurance

  • Paid time off

  • Parental leave

  • Professional development assistance

  • Vision insurance

Equal Employment Opportunity: 

 

InterVarsity Christian Fellowship/USA is both an equal opportunity employer and a faith-based religious organization. We conduct hiring without regard to race, color, ancestry, national origin, citizenship, age, sex, marital status, parental status, membership in any labor organization, political ideology, or disability of an otherwise qualified individual. The status of InterVarsity Christian Fellowship/USA as an equal opportunity employer does not prevent the organization from hiring staff based on their religious beliefs so that all staff share the same religious commitment.  Pursuant to the Civil Rights Act of 1964, Section 702 (42 U.S.C. 2000e 1(a)) InterVarsity Christian Fellowship/USA has the right to, and does, hire only candidates who agree with InterVarsity’s Statement of Agreement: Purpose and Doctrinal Basis because InterVarsity believes that each and every staff plays a vital role in advancing InterVarsity’s mission and purposes.

job_name: Youth Ministry Director at Hohenfels, U.S. Military Installation, Germany
post_html:
*Please note this position would require our Staff to live near the community where they would be doing ministry.

Description:

There are nearly 300,000 teenagers of active-duty U.S. military parents who are stationed all over the world. These teens move an average of seven times during their school-aged years. The questions of identity and belonging that all teens face grow even more challenging to answer amid starting over and meeting new friends at each location.

This is where you can be the difference in a military teen’s life! By being in their world, walking alongside them, and creating a community where they experience the truth of God’s love and purpose for them, our staff provide a safe space where teens can develop friendships and connections to experience laughter, build hope, and generate resiliency.

We are currently providing incarnational ministry at many military installations around the world. You will have the opportunity to lead and oversee the overall Young Life Military program, known as Club Beyond, which is ecumenically focused and outreach oriented.

We are currently looking for both full-time and part-time staff throughout the United States, as well as international locations. Colorado Springs, CO, is the headquarters.

Responsibilities:

  • Actively develop healthy relationships with adults, as well as kids, and build vibrant relationships with the local community, the military installation, and the chapel community.
  • Be a role model (incarnational) and assist with developing community outreach to "unchurched" teens, discipleship to Christian teens, and leading and equipping volunteers to do "hands-on" middle and high school Christian youth programs.
  • Work well in an environment that sees (due to high military operational tempo) a high degree of turnover among teens, families, chaplains and volunteers.
  • Be respectful of and embrace a community that is deeply influenced by a military culture.
  • In this ministry, you will need to live out the Club Beyond Core Value Statement:

Club Beyond is a Christ-centered community of leaders with an exclusively military focus. Our methods are incarnational, and our perspective is ecumenical. We leverage strategic partnerships for the greatest results. We value professionalism from our staff and excellence in our stewardship.

Qualifications:

  • A deep love for Christ and for lost teens.
  • Competent communicator with youths, parents, and senior military leaders.
  • Teachable heart.
  • Willingness to make a three-year commitment.
  • Minimum of three years' youth ministry experience preferred.
  • College degree preferred.
  • Willingness to raise part of the budget through personal support.
  • Committed to a relational ministry approach.
  • Energetic.
  • Small event planning skills.
  • Strong initiative.
  • Note, this position would require our Staff to live near the community where they would be doing ministry.

Benefits:

  • Full-time salary: Based on experience, responsibility, and fundraising levels.
  • Benefits: Full health coverage (including dental, vision and life insurance).
  • Expense reimbursement (mileage [office and ministry related]).
  • Training and career development is built into the job.

Salary:

The Base Salary range: $45,000 to $60,000 (Salary is based on education and experience). In addition to salary, a Cost of Living Adjustment, dependent on location, is available. The Annual National Funding provided is $16,667.

Location:

Club Beyond works on military installations all over the world. We currently have openings at:

In the USA:

  • Fort Rucker, Alabama
  • Joint Base Elmendorf-Richardson (JBER), Alaska
  • Fort Irwin, California
  • Camp Pendleton, California
  • Travis Air Force Base, California
  • Joint Base Anacostia-Bolling (JBAB), Washington, D.C.
  • Eglin Air Force Base, Florida
  • Fort Benning, Georgia
  • Fort Stewart, Georgia
  • Fort Riley, Kansas
  • Fort Bragg, North Carolina
  • Fort Sill, Oklahoma
  • Fort Jackson, South Carolina
  • Fort Belvoir, Virginia
  • Joint Base Lewis-McChord (JBLM), Washington


Overseas:

  • Geilenkirchen, Germany and various other locations in Germany
  • Naval Base Guam
  • Aviano Air Base, Italy
  • Vicenza, Italy
  • Camp Zama, Japan
  • Yokosuka, Japan
  • Camp Humphreys, South Korea

Contact us through:
Robert Raedeke: RecruitingTeam@clubbeyond.org

Want to know more about our mission and culture?

Please check out clubbeyond.org to learn how Club Beyond has been changing the lives of military teens for over 40 years!

North Coast Church is searching for a Campus Pastor for their Carlsbad, California Campus. The Pastor is responsible for providing spiritual direction and pastoral care to the Carlsbad staff and congregation, as well as overseeing operations. The leader in this role reports to the Executive Pastor/CFO and will be provided freedom and trust, while benefiting from the assistance of a large support team positioned to serve each campus.

North Coast is a grace-filled church where ministry is also fun! Each campus is intentional about knowing God and growing spiritually through practical Bible teaching, contemporary worship, and opportunities for significant and supportive relationships.

Estimated Compensation: $90,000 to $110,000

Overview

Lifeway is seeking a Worship Technical Specialist to serve as a key resource for Lifeway Worship, blending technical expertise with a heart for ministry to support churches and worship teams across the country. In this role, you will manage digital and physical worship assets, provide advanced technical support for LifewayWorship.com, and collaborate with programmers, legal, and ministry leadership on strategic worship initiatives. This is a unique opportunity for someone who understands both the technical and ministry dimensions of worship resource development and wants their work to have lasting impact in the local church. 

 

Why Lifeway? 

 

Lifeway is a place where you can bring your faith and work experience to join in the most important mission in the world: making disciples of Jesus Christ. Whether you’re a creator or storyteller, data guru or problem-solver, or anywhere in between, if you’re passionate about serving the church, we have a place for you. Lifeway has a strong Work from Anywhere (WFA) culture that is deeply focused on our mission and values. While headquartered in Nashville, TN, many of our positions are remote-eligible and have autonomy and flexibility with work hours. We provide equipment and resources to ensure team members have access to a productive and ergonomic workspace. We believe building relationships and community is essential to how we work together, so Lifeway hosts all-team meetings several times per year and provides travel for key team gatherings for remote-based team members. Full-time employees are eligible for enrollment in our comprehensive benefits plans including healthcare, vacation and sick time, holiday pay, care days, 401(k) plan, maternity and parental leave, adoption assistance, mission trip time, and more. If this sounds like a place where you would be excited to serve the kingdom of God, we would love for you to join our team.

 

Learn more about our culture at team.lifeway.com/culture-code 

 

This is a remote position in the U.S. with occasional travel to Nashville for in-person team gatherings. #LI-Remote 

 

 

Responsibilities

  • Lives out Lifeway’s mission and values, showing deep commitment to Kingdom work
  • Limited travel: 2-4 times per year, typically overnight
  • Provide advanced technical support for LifewayWorship.com via phone, chat, and email, resolving escalated issues for customers, church partners, and internal support teams 
  • Serve as the primary liaison for the Lifeway Worship Customer Service Teams channel, assisting Church Sales & Support Specialists with complex or escalated cases 
  • Investigate and resolve technical and product-related customer inquiries, maintaining a support spreadsheet to ensure timely follow-ups and accurate records 
  • Manage all digital and physical worship assets, including archive organization, duplication of physical masters, artwork development for vendor relationships, and custom audio edits for church sound systems 
  • Partner with the Legal team to ensure rights and royalties for worship assets are properly administered 
  • Coordinate shipping, tracking, and fulfillment of vendor orders and sample products in partnership with the Order Research team 
  • Oversee One Source administration for Canon accounts and manage Metro 2 mailing list memberships to maintain database accuracy 
  • Collaborate with programmers on regression testing, bug fixes, and feature support for LifewayWorship.com 
  • Support and lead new Lifeway Worship initiatives in partnership with the Project Team Leader, including content development and ministry partnerships 
  • Continuously evaluate and recommend improvements to technical support systems, digital resource management, and customer service processes 

Qualifications

Education

Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Digital Media, Music, or a related field, required 

Master's degree, not required

Advanced graduate degree (PhD, etc.), not required

 

Skills, Knowledge, & Experiences, required

  • Ability to travel to the Middle Tennessee area 2-4 times annually for team gatherings
  • 3+ years of experience in technical support, digital media, or a related field 
  • Experience in local church music ministry 
  • Experience in web design and development 
  • Technical troubleshooting and web platform support 
  • Digital asset management and organization 
  • Vendor coordination and order fulfillment 
  • Clear written and verbal communication across phone, chat, and email 

Actively involved in an evangelical Christian church

 

Skills, Knowledge, & Experiences, preferred 

  • Familiarity with rights and royalty administration for digital media 
  • Experience with regression testing or software QA processes 
  • Experience with audio editing for worship or church sound systems 
  • Background in content development for digital ministry platforms

job_name: Catechesis of the Good Shepherd/Worship Teacher
post_html:
Part-time
Description

Who We Are: 

At St. Thomas More Preschool, our goal is to offer our students a positive and enjoyable experience that will allow them to grow intellectually, emotionally, socially and spiritually. Our school gives special attention to the developmental stages, skills and needs of each child while encouraging and nurturing his or her God-given abilities. The program has been carefully developed for the enrichment of the whole child and is fully licensed by the State of Texas. 


Ministerial Character:

The Pastor is the visible principle and foundation of unity in the parish of St Thomas More Catholic Church which the Bishop has entrusted to him. He makes Christ’s mission present and enduring in the parish. In order to fulfill his mission, the Pastor employs suitable, chosen collaborators (clerics, religious, or lay people). He shares with them his mission and entrusts various responsibilities to them.

Positions employed at St Thomas More Catholic Church help to extend the ministry of the Pastor in particular ways as outlined in the job description. Therefore, the employee in this position is closely connected to and assists the Pastor in the performance of his ministry and thereby engages in ministry for the Church.

  

Job Responsibilities: 

  • Plan and lead developmentally appropriate Level I Catechesis of the Good Shepherd sessions for preschool children in      accordance with the Catholic faith, CGS principles, and the policies and philosophy of the school.
  • Plan and lead monthly Chapel
  • Support each child’s relationship with God through Scripture, liturgy, prayer, quiet reflection, and hands-on exploration.
  • Respect each child’s individual interests, developmental needs, and pace, allowing time for repetition, independent work, and discovery.
  • Prepare and maintain the atrium as a peaceful, orderly, welcoming space that encourages prayer, concentration, and reverence.
  • Prepare, organize, and care for atrium materials, ensuring they are complete, accessible, and consistent with CGS      presentations.
  • Present Scripture and liturgical materials in a thoughtful, prayerful manner, inviting children to wonder and reflect.
  • Model reverence, patience, kindness, and respect for others and for the materials within the atrium.
  • Guide children in caring for their environment and returning materials to their proper places.
  • Use positive guidance and redirection to support participation and maintain a calm learning environment.
  • Supervise children during atrium sessions and transitions to and from their classrooms.
  • Share responsibility for cleaning, organizing, and maintaining the atrium with assigned assistants.
  • Attend monthly staff meetings and other meetings as requested.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

Hours: Monday & Thursday. Work hours are 9 am to 2 pm. 

Requirements

 What you will need: 

• Passion to influence the lives of pre-school children. 

• Patience in lovingly meeting young learners' spiritual, academic, behavioral, social, and emotional needs. 

• Patience in accepting guidance and assignments from the classroom teacher. 


Minimum Qualifications: 

Education: 

• High school diploma 


Experience: 

• Working with young children is preferred. 


Certifications and Training: 

• Catechesis of the Good Shepard Certified

• Valid Texas driver's license. 

• Compliance with the Diocese of Austin Ethics and Integrity Ministry (EIM) policies throughout the employment period. 


Physical Demands: 

• Required to lift or carry supplies, textbooks equipment, etc. 

• Required to sit, stand, bend, stoop, grab, pull, hear, see, and speak daily. 

• Required to monitor students in various locations, including those with noise, activity, and inclement weather. 


Working Conditions:

• All employees of the Parish are engaged in ministry and closely tied to the Pastor in the exercise of his ministry and obligations to the church. 

• The Parish is an at-will employer.

• All buildings and vehicles owned by the Parish are tobacco free.

• Working in a fast-paced environment with priorities and plans that may change rapidly.

• Working on weekends, evenings, and some holidays may be required.

• Will be exposed to religious ceremonies, conduct, and speech, including Roman Catholic Christian prayer and liturgical celebrations.  

• Will be required to adhere to established dress codes and conduct standards.

Duties: 
  1. Assist with Family Retreats and Getaways. Provide support in recruitment and organizing a team of volunteers to carry out retreat tasks before, during and after Family Retreat
    1. Assist with application processes and communications for families and volunteers.
    2. Provide support with background check process for volunteers.
    3. Actively evaluate program post Family Retreat and plan for changes as needed
    4. Assist with Family Retreat preparation, execution and follow-up
  2. Provide support in promoting, facilitating, and leading Joni and Friends church equipping using Joni and Friends Ministry Relations materials and other training materials, for awareness and education in churches and educational settings at every level
  3. Work with marketing team on content for Joni and Friends USA account and other platforms
  4. Participate in local and international Joni and Friends’ programs as opportunities arise.
  5. Assist with logistics in the wheelchair collection program
  6. Support donor development and participate in fundraising efforts as needed
  7. Assist the Ministry Operations Manager executing events or aspects of events
  8. Represent Ministry in the community. In collaboration with other staff members and volunteers, set up and operate promotional efforts at area conferences and events as available
  9. Other duties and projects as assigned by supervisor to support department and organizational needs
Qualifications: 
  • Must possess a vibrant personal relationship with Jesus Christ and agree with the Joni and Friends statement of faith
  • Desire to serve in a growing and dynamic Christian service ministry
  • Self-starter and team player with strong interpersonal and organizational skills
  • Ability to provide support to multiple projects and multiple volunteer teams
  • Able to interact effectively with leaders throughout the community
  • Experience in camping ministry preferred
  • Strong computer knowledge and proficient in Microsoft Office Suite
  • Passion for people affected by disability and scriptural knowledge related to God’s heart for people who are marginalized
  • Flexible and available to work evenings, weekends and travel
  • Valid driver’s license is required
  • Understanding of Christian ministry and specifically Joni and Friends is desirable
Physical Requirements:

Work is primarily performed in an office setting but also includes offsite environments such as hotels, conference centers, and retreat facilities. Offsite work may involve varying temperatures, lighting, and noise levels, as well as periods of increased activity during event setup and execution. Employees are expected to maintain professionalism, safety awareness, and flexibility while adapting to different environments and schedules.

Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions of the job.
This position involves both sedentary office work and occasional physical activity during and in preparation of onsite and offsite events. The employee must be able to sit for extended periods, operate a computer and other standard office equipment, and communicate effectively in person, over the phone, and through virtual platforms. During events, the role may require standing or walking for extended periods, bending, reaching, carrying materials, and setting up or breaking down event spaces. The employee must be able to lift, carry, push, or pull items such as boxes, signage, or supplies up to 25 pounds.

Compensation: $20.50 - $22.50 per hour. The ideal person will work 20 hours per week, but be available to work up to 40 hours during both Family Retreats (June 11-17 and July 23-29, 2027). 

EMPLOYEE MINISTRY ENGAGEMENT:

Joni and Friends is a Christ-centered community. Therefore, we expect every employee at Joni and Friends to excel in their walk with Christ and in their specific employment role in our Christian community. We purposely create a gospel-centered environment and offer leadership and development training to help employees perform their work with integrity and excellence, serving in our Christian community at Joni and Friends to fulfill our religious ministry: to share the gospel and serve people living with disabilities.

All employees do this, regardless of their specific role, by:

  • Modeling Joni and Friends’ Christian beliefs and practices to advance our gospel mission during working hours and nonworking hours
  • Supporting fellow staff and volunteers at Joni and Friends in following Christ, by praying for each other, sharing Scripture and setting an example of how to live a faithful Christian life
  • Engaging in the lives of people living with disabilities with love, dignity, and in a manner that commends and proclaims the gospel.
  • Participating or leading in prayer and worship during meetings, events, and outreaches
  • Affirming the Joni and Friends Statement of Faith annually and not engaging in any conduct or promoting any religious beliefs inconsistent with such beliefs
  • Upholding and advancing Joni and Friends’ Mission and Vision through a focus on our Values.
  • Actively attending a church that has a statement of faith that does not contradict Joni and Friends’ Statement of Faith

Joni and Friends seeks to glorify God in the way we conduct ourselves, and in the work we do together as a Christian community. Employment at Joni and Friends is not only a job but a ministry and a calling from God.

post_html:
Overview

The Corps Ministries Coordinator supports the Corps Officer in the ministry and program life of the Old Orchard Beach Corps. The position coordinates ministry and discipleship programs for all ages, supports volunteer leaders and teachers, and provides local support for special events and the Seaside Pavilion. The Coordinator also contributes to the spiritual life of the corps through teaching and direct ministry involvement.

Responsibilities

In a typical week, the Coordinator leads corps ministry programs, supports volunteer leaders and teachers, and coordinates logistics for special events and the Seaside Pavilion.

  • Plan, organize, and coordinate corps ministry and discipleship programs for all ages, including youth, music and arts, and character building
  • Provide support, guidance, and resources to corps ministry leaders, including Sunday school teachers and youth and arts leaders
  • Provide spiritual leadership in corps programs, including teaching classes and leading ministry activities
  • Recruit, prepare, and support volunteer leaders, local officers, and teachers
  • Coordinate special events and local logistics for the Seaside Pavilion, including retreats and contact with vendors and service providers
  • Participate in corps ministry planning with the Corps Officer, and attend Sunday worship to support corps ministries

Qualifications

  • High school diploma or equivalent and five years of related experience required; a degree in a related field is preferred
  • Valid driver's license
  • Demonstrated ability to coordinate multiple programs, events, and the people involved in them at the same time
  • Ability to guide, encourage, and support volunteer leaders and teachers of varied ages and backgrounds
  • Salvationist in good standing, with a working knowledge of the beliefs and ministry of The Salvation Army and the faith and experience to offer sound spiritual guidance to program leaders
  • Proficiency with Microsoft 365 applications and ability to communicate clearly and professionally with staff, volunteers, and vendors

 

What We Offer:

  • Paid time off
  • Paid holidays
  • Sick leave
  • Personal days
  • Bereavement leave
  • Medical, dental and vision benefits
  • Short term and long term disability
  • Retirement plan

Benefits may vary based on position classification and eligibility.

 

About Us:

The Salvation Army, an international movement, is an evangelical part of the universal Christian church. Its message is based on the Bible. Its ministry is motivated by the love of God. Its mission is to preach the gospel of Jesus Christ and to meet human needs in His name without discrimination.

The Northern New England Division serves communities across Maine, New Hampshire and Vermont through local corps and programs, supported by Divisional Headquarters in Portland, Maine.

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, sex, national origin, disability or protected veteran status.

The Student Pastor at Peoples Church will lead our Student Ministry, providing vision, pastoral care, and team leadership for one of our most visible ministries to junior high and high school students. This pastor will inherit a healthy ministry with its own standalone building, offices, a cafe, administrative support, and a strong base of students and families, with real runway to grow. The role is both evangelistic and discipleship-focused: we want our students to engage on campus and to grow deep in their faith, led by someone who reaches new students while shepherding them toward maturity in Christ. We are looking for a Student Pastor with the leadership instincts to develop other leaders and the pastoral heart to walk with students and families for the long haul.


Why We Love This Opportunity

Peoples Church gives a student pastor everything they need to actually win: a dedicated building, a real budget, administrative support, and the freedom to lead without someone hovering over their shoulder. There is a healthy, diverse ministry here to build on, deep roots in a community that loves its city, and a church family that will genuinely embrace you. For the right leader who loves students, loves being on campus, and wants to develop leaders, this is a rare combination of resources, trust, and runway.


Key Responsibilities

  • Provide overall pastoral and strategic leadership for our Student Ministry, serving junior high and high school students.
  • Lead and develop the teams that run our junior high, high school, and campus ministries, including investing in the relationship with our volunteer Junior High Pastor and our Associate Student Ministry Leader.
  • Design and lead weekly gatherings, including teaching, worship, and discipleship environments for students.
  • Be an evangelistic, present voice on local campuses, engaging students in their extracurricular activities and deepening partnerships like our work with FCA and local sports teams.
  • Lead our annual student outreach events and partner with area youth pastors on shared efforts.
  • Coordinate with our Missions Pastor on student mission trips, reflecting how central missions is to who we are.
  • Steward the Student Ministry’s staff, volunteer base, building, and budget with care and intentionality.
  • Shepherd a diverse student body, including many students in difficult circumstances, helping them know God and take real steps in their faith.


Key Qualifications

  • A bachelor’s degree, ideally in biblical studies or a related field.
  • Two to five years of student ministry experience preferred, ideally as a lead student pastor or strong second chair.
  • Has led a sizable youth group.
  • A self-starter who sets their own goals and a team player willing to work within the wide hallways of our leadership culture.
  • An excellent communicator, both in person and electronically.
  • Comfortable hitting the ground running and able to stabilize and grow an established ministry.
  • A background in evangelistic, campus-engaged youth ministry is a strong plus.
  • Aligned with our theological convictions.



About This Organization

Peoples Church is a church in Fresno, California, and has been a prominent presence in the Central Valley for over 70 years. We average around 3,500 in Sunday morning attendance at our gatherings.We are well known and respected in the community for our focus on serving the city we love, and we are traditionally known as a loving church where people feel at home when they come on campus. Guided by our vision of Helping People See God and Participate in His Redemptive Story, we come alongside our community to show them the hope found in Jesus, shaped by our values of Loving God, Loving Others, Loving Truth, Loving Culture, and Loving Sacrifice. We are a multi-generational and increasingly diverse congregation, and we actively extend a hand into the community through events that meet people where they are. We are a big church that works hard to feel like a small one, where it is easy to get connected and where people are welcomed in and treated like family.


Location

Fresno is a respite from the large cities that typify ideas about California, such as San Francisco and Los Angeles. Fresno County produces agriculture that feeds the world and is home to a tight-knit, diverse community with a rich history and a small-town feel. Sitting in the heart of the Central Valley, Fresno offers an enviable location with easy access to both the mountains and the coast, with Yosemite, Sequoia, and Kings Canyon National Parks practically in the backyard, and both Los Angeles and the Bay Area within easy reach for a weekend trip. It is a place where a pastor and family can put down roots, raise children, and build a life alongside their ministry for the long haul.
