About Child Evangelism Fellowship of Virginia (CEF of VA)

Child Evangelism Fellowship of Virginia is a statewide Christian nonprofit ministry committed to reaching children with the Gospel through Good News Clubs (GNC), 5‑Day Clubs, Christian Youth in Action® (CYIA), and church‑partnered evangelistic programs. We equip volunteers and churches to disciple children with excellence, accountability, and ministry integrity. Our team operates with a commitment to prayer, Scripture, and compliance with CEF’s national standards as we work to advance the Gospel to the next generation.

Position Title: Local Coordinator / Local Director (Peninsula Chapter) 
Full‑time, Ministry Leadership Role

Position Summary

The Local Director (beginning as Local Coordinator during training) serves as the face of the local chapter and is responsible for developing volunteers, building church partnerships, and leading all ministry operations within the chapter. This role requires a spiritually mature Christian leader with strong relational skills, a passion for evangelizing children, and the ability to mobilize churches and volunteers for ministry.

Key Responsibilities
  • Fulfilling the purpose of Child Evangelism Fellowship in the chapter.
  • Executing and accomplishing the plans and objectives of CEF USA Ministries, the local committee and state board.
  • Overseeing all aspects of the ministry within the local chapter with the assistance of the local committee, volunteers and staff. 
Ministry Leadership

  • Lead (implement, grow, improve) a chapter‑wide prayer strategy and model a ministry grounded in prayer.
  • Promote Good News Clubs, 5‑Day Clubs, and CYIA to expand ministry reach.
  • Recruit, train, equip, and supervise volunteers and staff.
  • Maintain direct ministry contact with children through CEF programs.
  • Build and sustain CYIA ministry, including staff and volunteer recruitment and training of short-term missionaries.
  • Coordinate Kick‑Off, Quick Start, Jump Start, and other training events for CYIA
  • Promote further opportunities to serve-including Short-Term Missions and other CEF ministries. 
  • Participate in CYIA Training School as assigned.
Strategic Leadership

  • Work with the local committee to develop vision and strategic plans for evangelizing and discipling children (within the chapter) with the goal of establishing them with local churches.
  • Recruit people to do the work of the ministry (both paid and volunteer); Mobilize churches as ministry partners and cultivate long‑term relationships.
  • Provide leadership development, training, coaching, and evaluation for staff and volunteers, regularly.
  • Support and encourage local committee participation in training opportunities.
  • Assist the local committee in fundraising efforts to sustain ministry operations.
  • Conduct routine employee appraisals for paid staff.
  • Oversee (and teach as needed) the teacher training program
Administrative Oversight

  • Ensure compliance with all CEF policies, procedures, and governance standards.
  • Maintain adequate, accurate, and timely records, reports, minutes, communications, and donor receipts.
  • Develop and submit annual budgets in collaboration with the local committee to the State Director.
  • Communicate consistently and professionally with the State Director and committee.
  • Attend statewide Local Director meetings and trainings.
  • Perform additional duties as assigned
Software & Technical Skills

  • Intermediate proficiency: MS PowerPoint, email communication.
  • Basic proficiency: MS Publisher, Word, Excel, Adobe Acrobat.
  • Ability to use projectors, Blockrockers, and technology used in Good News Clubs.
  • Ability to use MailChimp for newsletters.
Required Qualifications

  • Demonstrated love for Jesus Christ and commitment to prayer
  • Unquestionable passion for reaching children with the Gospel.
  • Ability to recognize how God moves in our midst as He builds the local work (one person/church at a time)
  • Extensive experience in teaching and evangelizing children biblically.
  • Be a continual learner, love the local church, and understand how to mobilize ministry partners
  • Experience discipling, training, and supervising volunteers or staff
  • Strong relational, organizational, and leadership skills.
  • Ability to identify leaders, cast vision, organize groups, and evaluate ministry programs.
  • Flawless record of behavior toward children and families.
  • Understanding of how to mobilize churches as ministry partners.
  • At least one year of Bible College or Seminary training with solid academic performance.
  • Commitment to CEF’s Statement of Faith and Ministry Compliance Agreement.
Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience in nonprofit ministry leadership.
  • Experience building volunteer‑driven programs.
  • Experience working with committees or boards.
  • Familiarity with CEF programs and curriculum.
Work Environment & Expectations

  • Statewide and local travel required.
  • Evening and weekend ministry activities as needed.
  • Must complete CEF background check and child protection screening.
  • Willing to raise personal ministry support if required by chapter policy.
Religious Hiring Notice

As a religious organization, Child Evangelism Fellowship is permitted and reserves the right to prefer employees or prospective employees on the basis of religion.

Flexible work from home options available.

Compensation: $3,750.00 - $3,921.00 per month



Get Involved

Child Evangelism Fellowship® of Virginia (CEF of VA) is a church‑assist ministry dedicated to evangelizing and teaching children ages 4–14. We serve churches and individuals by equipping them to fulfill the Great Commission—training believers to be ambassadors for Christ who share the Gospel and disciple the next generation.

Across the Commonwealth, CEF of Virginia supports local chapters through proven children’s ministry training, materials, and methods. Our statewide team equips volunteers to lead Good News Clubs®, 5‑Day Clubs®, CYIA®, and evangelistic events that help reach boys and girls with the message of salvation. By strengthening church partnerships and mobilizing ministry teams, we help communities bring the Gospel to children and build lasting spiritual impact.

Job Summary:

The Director of Campus Ministry is responsible for promoting the mission of Alvernia University by creating an environment and space for all campus community members to feel a sense of belonging. The work of educating and engaging the community in examining their beliefs, engaging in inter-religious dialogue, and experiencing the living Catholic Franciscan tradition of Alvernia University are all part of the experience. To this end s/he will focus on: (1) leading a cohesive inclusive campus ministry team producing diverse quality programming to meet the needs of all our students, (2) designing and implementing events that highlight our Franciscan mission and campus ministry pillars, (3) promote the enrichment of the spiritual lives of our students, with a special emphasis on vocation, and (4) promote peace and social justice ideals as articulated by the principles of Catholic social teaching. The director must be a Catholic who is active in her/his faith and is competent working with persons of many cultures, ethnicities, and religious traditions.


Essential Functions:

Mission, Culture & Leadership

  • Model Alvernia’s Franciscan values through compassionate service, ethical leadership, and commitment to fostering a welcoming and respectful community for all.
  • Cultivate a campus culture that prioritizes transparency, accessibility, and proactive communication.
  • Lead a cohesive campus ministry team (both pro staff and student leaders) that produce quality spiritual programming that meets the needs of a diverse student body. This includes training a new student leadership team that encourages growth within the mission and ministry office.

Ministerial Vision:

  • Sees him/herself as a spiritual leader – one who walks humbly with others, who calls them to the fullness of life, who comforts and counsels those in need, and who cultivates an authentic community.
  • Leads and unites campus ministers across campus.
  • Equips, empowers, and integrates student leaders.
  • Models respectful, collaborative, and active support of the University’s Mission and of Catholic and Franciscan higher education through dedicated job performance and exemplary service to the University’s many constituencies.
  • Leads the ministry team as it develops an inclusive ministry program which serves the undergraduate, graduate, faculty, staff and alumni of Alvernia University.
  • Participates and leads yearly professional development (books, conferences, classes) and/or formation experiences (retreats, days of reflection)
  • Participates in the liturgical and prayer life of the university community, in particular Sunday and other Campus Masses.


Interfaith Spiritual Development:

  • With the campus ministry team, design and implement liturgical worship and rituals that highlight the Catholic, Franciscan mission of Alvernia University, especially the Franciscan emphases on peace and social justice, conscious of the “new normal” of ministry. 
  • Promote the enrichment of the spiritual lives of our students on campus with special emphasis on vocational language. This enrichment takes shape through small faith groups, retreat programming, faith based Registered Student Organizations (RSOs), athletics, and Interfaith/Ecumenical communities.
  • Coordinate peace and social justice programs on campus, through on campus programming, grounded in Catholic Social teaching and our Franciscan mission.
  • Oversee annual pilgrimages to Assisi for students, faculty, staff, and University board members.
  • Establish and lead a representative council of faith-based student organizations, facilitating collaboration, communication, and shared initiatives that support the spiritual life of the campus community.


Collaboration and Planning:

  • Lead the planning, coordination, and implementation of the University events such as Mission Day and Baccalaureate Mass.
  • Collaborate with Campus Ministers to foster an inclusive campus environment by coordinating recognition of major faith celebrations and supporting interfaith dialogue and events.
  • Design and oversee student retreat experiences that foster spiritual reflection, deepen faith, and support students’ personal and vocational development.
  • Oversee the planning and implementation of student commissioning services that recognize and bless students as they prepare for student leadership roles, athletics seasons, alternative break trips, and other significant endeavors.
  • Partner with the Director of SEARCH to integrate the history and ongoing legacy of the Bernardine Franciscan Sisters into the SEARCH curriculum and first year student experience.
  • Partner closely with the Holleran Center assisting and supporting community service projects and initiatives. 


Professional Development, Customer Service & Representation:

  • Lead or contribute to internal training and professional development initiatives that enhance compliance, service excellence, communication, and inclusive practices across the organization.
  • Promote a high standard of customer service by modeling responsive, solutions-oriented interactions with students, clients, colleagues, and external partners.
  • Serve as a positive ambassador for the organization by communicating its mission, values, and offerings effectively to internal and external audiences.
  • Represent the university at recruitment and outreach events, including open houses, orientations, and community engagement programs.


Other Responsibilities 

  • Perform additional duties assigned to support departmental and organizational needs.


Qualifications/Education: 

  • Master's degree in an appropriate discipline and five (5) years of relevant experience or equivalent 
  • Commitment to the mission statement, core values, and goals of Alvernia University.
  • Practicing Catholic with knowledge of and respect for the Catholic Faith and the Teachings of the Catholic Church are required.
  • Musical experience for liturgical worship is preferred but not required.
  • Experience in the promotion of peace and social justice.


Employee Benefits:

Join a team that values your well-being! We offer a comprehensive benefits package designed to support you and your family:

    • Robust Health Coverage: Choose from three offered medical plans, plus dental and vision.
    • Financial Security: Enjoy University-paid life/AD&D insurance and long-term disability, with options for short-term disability and supplemental coverage for you and your family (including accident, critical illness, and hospital indemnity plans). Flexible spending accounts are also available.
    • Exceptional Retirement: Start saving immediately with our 403(b) Retirement Plan. You will get 100% immediate vesting, a University gift contribution, and a generous match up to 5% of your deferrals.
    • Time Off & Flexibility: Take advantage of 20 paid holidays each year, including 5 floating holidays, and the possibility of flexible or hybrid work options for many roles.
    • Invest in Your Future: Enjoy tuition remission benefits for yourself and your dependents.
    • On-Campus Wellness: Benefit-eligible employees on our main campus receive free access to our Medical & Counseling Center.
    • Employee Meal Plan: This plan provides convenient, flexible dining options on campus at a reduced cost.

Student Ministry Director – Farmington Hills Campus

Woodside Bible Church is seeking a passionate and relational Student Ministry Director to lead and grow a thriving, Christ-centered student ministry at our Farmington Hills Campus. This role is responsible for creating engaging programming, equipping volunteers, and partnering with families to help students develop a lifelong relationship with Jesus.

The ideal candidate is a visionary and organized leader who loves students, builds strong relationships, and thrives in a collaborative, multi-site environment. This individual will oversee weekly student gatherings, recruit and develop volunteer leaders, and lead impactful events such as retreats, mission trips, and outreach opportunities.

Key Responsibilities Include:

  • Leading weekly student ministry gatherings and teaching biblical truth
  • Recruiting, training, and supporting volunteer leaders
  • Building relationships with students, parents, and campus staff
  • Planning events, trips, and outreach initiatives
  • Partnering with the broader Woodside Students team and campus leadership

Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree required; ministry-related field preferred
  • Experience in Student Ministry and volunteer leadership development
  • Strong communication, leadership, and organizational skills
  • Spiritually mature, humble, and aligned with Woodside’s mission and values

If you have a heart for discipling the next generation and equipping others to do the same, we’d love to hear from you.

This is a part-time (25 hours per week), hourly, non-exempt position, requiring membership and active participation at our Farmington Hills campus.

Job Summary: 

The NextGen Worship Lead (Support) role facilitates worship in Kids, Youth, and Young Adult environments at an assigned campus in partnership with the Campus Worship Pastor. This part-time permanent role cares for campus Next Gen worship teams, trains worship leaders and musicians, plans and schedules worship-related events, and leads worship. With support from the Regional Next Gen Associate Worship Pastor, the Team Lead carries the churchwide Next Gen worship standards into each campus environment. 


Principal Job Responsibilities: 

  • Builds and stewards the NextGen worship Serve Team at the campus: recruiting, training, scheduling, retention, and appreciation 
  • Executes the set lists, Ableton/Playback sessions, and service plans provided by Next Gen Worship rather than creating a separate standard 
  • Develops young worship leaders and musicians at the campus, and mentors students on the team 
  • Runs rehearsals and pre-service preparation for NextGen environments at the campus 
  • Partners with the Campus Worship Pastor and campus NextGen leadership on platform, scheduling, and shared needs 
  • Raises local realities and needs to the Regional NextGen Associate Worship Pastor rather than absorbing them 
  • Supports campus NextGen events, camps, and team nights 
  • Is present and serving at weekend services and churchwide events as the ministry calendar requires 
  • Performs other duties as assigned. 

 

As a member of the Gateway Church team, this position is expected to support, recruit, and develop Serve Team members, and to serve alongside the broader team as ministry and organizational needs arise. 

General Skills & Qualifications: 

  • A clear passion for Jesus and a strong biblical foundation 
  • A heart for students and kids, with the ability to lead worship in their environments 
  • Musical craft and talent, with proficiency as a worship leader on voice and at least one instrument 
  • Demonstrated ability to recruit, train, and retain volunteers 
  • Able to take direction on standards from Central while owning execution locally 
  • Consistently growing in craft, character, and leadership capacity 
  • Professional in punctuality, communication, and appearance 
  • Demonstrated emotional and relational intelligence 
  • Strong time-management skills and the ability to hold several priorities at once 
  • Proficient in Microsoft Office and able to learn and function within new software and systems 

Education/Certification(s): 

  • High school diploma or equivalent, and one or more years of worship leading experience — required 
  • Experience leading kids or student worship — preferred 
  • Prior experience in a multisite church environment — preferred 

General Physical Requirements: 

The physical demands described here represent those that an employee must meet to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. While performing the duties of this position, the employee is regularly required to: 

  • Sit or stand for extended periods of time 
  • Occasionally kneel or crouch 
  • Frequently lift and/or move up to 10 lbs. 
  • Occasionally lift and/or move up to 25 lbs. 
  • Able to lift and move instruments and equipment up to 40 lbs, and available to work weekends and evenings as the ministry calendar requires 

*This description is not all inclusive, and other duties may be assigned as necessary. 

 
Gateway Church does not discriminate in employment opportunities or practices on the basis of race, color, sex, national origin, age, disability, or any other characteristic protected by law as it applies to churches. However, Gateway Church does discriminate on the basis of religion. 

 
Employment Requirement: Must be a member or become a member of Gateway Church upon employment.

Campus Staff Minister (George Washington University)

Work Location:

Maryland

Job Type:

Full time

God has called InterVarsity to plant and to build witnessing communities of students and faculty who follow Jesus on college and university campuses. Through these groups, we believe ever- increasing numbers of students and faculty from all ethnic groups and areas of the campus will be transformed by the Gospel. We expect to see campuses increasingly become places where people, ideas, and structures flourish to the glory of God. We confidently anticipate that our InterVarsity alumni will become change agents across the country and around the world. We pursue this calling by discerning and actively participating in what God is already doing on campus. This is the essence of being a Campus Staff Minister (CSM).

ESSENTIAL COMMITMENTS/RESPONSIBILITIES 

Spiritual Growth 

You pursue maturity as a disciple of Jesus Christ so that your life and work increasingly reflects a growing love for God, God’s Word, God’s people of every ethnicity and culture, and God’s purposes in the world. To do this, you will: 

  • Pursue a vibrant relationship with the triune God through engagement with Scripture, prayer, and worship, both individually and in community 

  • Develop self-leadership (growing in self-awareness, self-management, relational integrity, and resiliency) 

  • Embrace Scriptural standards for behavior and attitudes 

 

Campus Leadership

You communicate and model InterVarsity’s vision to see students and faculty transformed, campuses renewed and world changers developed 

  • Create a culture of humble dependence on God and bold expectation in God’s intention to start new witnessing communities throughout the campus and on new campuses.

  • Model – in person and through programs – InterVarsity’s vision and Core Values, including a biblically-defined commitment to engage every ethnic and social group on campus 

  • Lead students and faculty – individually and collectively – through Scripture, prayer, teaching, and discipleship experiences, so that they articulate and align their ministry activities around this vision 

  • Set annual goals through prayer, research and reflection with your teams (students, faculty, and staff) for qualitative and quantitative growth, including conversions and leadership development 

 

You create, develop, align and leverage ministry plans, programs, teams, and structures to close the gap between current reality and the aspirational goals. 

  • Build leadership teams who trust and partner well with you and who demonstrate spiritual vitality, relational health, and mission alignment 

  • Develop and execute plans to achieve annual goals, evaluating and modifying the plan as needed throughout the year 

  • Increase momentum for the vision by aligning programs, structures, conferences and teams around the goals 

  • Mobilize students and faculty to engage their relational networks with the gospel and to start new missional communities 

  • Under the direction of the Area Director, may supervise Ministry Interns and Campus Ministry Interns as delegated 

 

You intentionally gather, invite, and develop diverse groups of students and faculty so that they not only encounter and follow Jesus as Savior and Lord but also advance the mission on campus as participants and leaders. 

  • Create ways for faculty and students to encounter and follow Jesus through Scripture, worship, prayer, mission experiences, conferences, etc. 

  • Equip students and faculty so that they think strategically about campus engagement and so that they proclaim – in word, deed, and power – the good news of Jesus, regularly inviting students and faculty to follow him as Savior and Lord 

  • Disciple students and faculty by equipping them to hear the Word, respond actively, and debrief and interpret the experience so that they grow in Christlikeness, reflect our Core Values, and develop ministry skills 

  • Invite, coach, and equip students and faculty to become increasingly effective participants and leaders, including starting new witnessing communities on campuses 

 

Organizational Collaboration 

You work with a network of other local, area, regional, and national InterVarsity staff and volunteers so that our work reflects Biblical standards of excellence, integrity, and partnership. 

  • Partner with and respond positively to the direction and coaching of your supervisors and national leaders 

  • Contribute to collaborative and productive team meetings and relationships 

  • Affiliate chapters under your care and submit Graduating Student Forms in order to increase our partnership with current students and alumni 

  • Use national ministry resources and tools, as requested, including recruiting and/or participating in local, regional, or national conferences as  

  • Complete reporting, planning and review requirements in a timely way so that you and your supervisors can assess and improve your work as a CSM 

  • Comply with all InterVarsity policies and procedures 

 

Ministry Partnership Development 

You will develop a team of partners – churches and individuals (including alumni and community members) – who will resource the ministry financially, in prayer, or volunteer service that advances the mission. 

  • Raise 100% of the financial budget assigned by your supervisor 

  • Communicate regularly with your ministry partners, nurturing the relationship through visits, phone calls, emails and regular prayer letters 

  • Develop on-going, long-lasting partnership with alumni and volunteers 

  • Comply with all Ministry Partnership Policies 

  • Identify and invest in advocates who will build networks of volunteers and donors on InterVarsity’s behalf 

 

Accomplish all other assigned tasks as appropriate 

 

QUALIFICATIONS (common to all levels of CSM) 

  • Annually affirm InterVarsity’s Statement of Agreement (Doctrinal Basis and Purpose Statement). Abide by InterVarsity’s Code of Conduct. Believe and behave consonantly with InterVarsity’s Human Sexuality Theological Paper. Affirm and behave consonantly with InterVarsity’s “Women in Ministry Statement of Affirmation” 

  • Bachelor’s degree for CSMs assigned to a four-year campus. A minimum of an Associate’s degree for CSMs assigned to a two-year campus or a community college 

  • Strong interpersonal skills (including ability to minister to diverse ethnic communities and faculty) 

  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills 

  • Demonstrated problem solving skills 

  • Familiarity with word processing, presentation, email, and spreadsheet software 

 

WORK ENVIRONMENT/PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS 

The CSM position leads ministry in a college campus environment. A designated office space may or may not be available. The CSM is required to travel to on-campus and off- campus sites as appropriate. Off-campus travel includes, but is not limited to: student ministry conferences, Ministry Partnership Development meetings, and InterVarsity- sponsored training sessions, meetings, and conferences. The CSM is regularly required to communicate with others, and routinely uses standard office equipment such as computers, phones, photocopiers, filing cabinets, etc. 

Pay Range: $39,288.00 - $52,392.00 per year

Pay: This position is funded through personal fundraising. Accordingly, compensation will vary based on the ability of the individual to secure a donor team to fund the cost of his/her salary. The anticipated salary range for this position on a full-time basis (40 hours/week) is dependent on a variety of factors, including location and cost of living. The actual salary received, including any geographic adjustment to account for location and cost of living, is subject to the individual’s ability to raise funds necessary to cover the full amount of such salary within the range set forth in the job posting details.

Benefits:

We offer a competitive benefits package, including health care and retirement savings with a match. Eligibility is based on employee type and hours worked.  Benefits include the following:

  • 403(b) Retirement Savings Plan

  • 403(b) matching contributions

  • Dental insurance

  • Employee assistance program

  • Employee discounts

  • Flexible work schedule

  • Flexible spending accounts

  • Health insurance

  • Health savings account

  • Life insurance

  • Paid time off

  • Parental leave

  • Professional development assistance

  • Vision insurance

Equal Employment Opportunity: 

 

InterVarsity Christian Fellowship/USA is both an equal opportunity employer and a faith-based religious organization. We conduct hiring without regard to race, color, ancestry, national origin, citizenship, age, sex, marital status, parental status, membership in any labor organization, political ideology, or disability of an otherwise qualified individual. The status of InterVarsity Christian Fellowship/USA as an equal opportunity employer does not prevent the organization from hiring staff based on their religious beliefs so that all staff share the same religious commitment.  Pursuant to the Civil Rights Act of 1964, Section 702 (42 U.S.C. 2000e 1(a)) InterVarsity Christian Fellowship/USA has the right to, and does, hire only candidates who agree with InterVarsity’s Statement of Agreement: Purpose and Doctrinal Basis because InterVarsity believes that each and every staff plays a vital role in advancing InterVarsity’s mission and purposes.

About the Worship Pastor: 

The Worship Pastor is responsible for leading and developing the worship ministry at Bayou City Fellowship’s Cypress Campus. This role provides pastoral, musical, and organizational leadership to create worship environments that are Christ-centered, biblically grounded, culturally relevant, and meaningful.

The Worship Pastor will recruit, develop, disciple, and lead worship staff and volunteers while overseeing the planning and execution of weekly worship services and other campus events. This role partners closely with the Lead Campus Pastor and campus staff to support the mission and vision of Bayou City Fellowship.

The Worship Pastor is expected to model a growing relationship with Jesus, a life of prayer and integrity, biblical faithfulness, humility, and dependence on the Holy Spirit.

Ministry Philosophy

The Worship Pastor is committed to helping Bayou City Fellowship become a people who treasure Jesus above all else. Worship ministry should point people to the gospel, faithfully communicate the truth of Scripture, cultivate prayer and discipleship, and create space for people to respond to God in authentic worship.

The Worship Pastor should lead from a posture of dependence on the Holy Spirit, recognizing that worship ministry is ultimately about making much of Jesus—not building a platform, pursuing trends, or elevating talent.

Guiding Scripture: 2 Timothy 1–4

Key Responsibilities

Worship Leadership

  • Plan and lead weekly worship services, including song selection, service flow, musical arrangements, and worship elements.

  • Lead and oversee weekly rehearsals for worship teams and musicians.

  • Ensure worship is biblically faithful, gospel-centered, and aligned with the vision and culture of Bayou City Fellowship.

  • Lead worship for campus-wide and other ministry events as needed.

  • Partner with the Lead Campus Pastor to develop and implement the campus worship vision.

Team Development & Discipleship

  • Recruit, audition, equip, disciple, and develop worship volunteers and leaders.

  • Identify and develop emerging worship leaders, musicians, and vocalists.

  • Provide pastoral care, encouragement, accountability, and spiritual development for worship staff and volunteers.

  • Establish a healthy culture marked by humility, excellence, teamwork, prayer, and spiritual growth.

  • Help develop a sustainable worship development pathway for the Cypress Campus.

  • Encourage worship team members to actively participate in the broader discipleship life of Bayou City Fellowship.

Production & Operations

  • Provide oversight and direction for the Audio/Visual and production teams supporting worship services.

  • Ensure effective coordination between worship, production, communications, and other ministry teams.

  • Maintain appropriate systems, schedules, resources, and processes for weekly worship ministry.

  • Manage the worship ministry budget and related expenses.

  • Utilize Planning Center, ProPresenter, and other ministry technologies effectively.

Campus & Church-Wide Collaboration

  • Participate in weekly staff meetings, leadership meetings, and church-wide initiatives.

  • Collaborate with other ministry leaders to support worship needs for Kids, Students, Women’s Ministry, Community Groups, and other events.

  • Contribute to the overall life and ministry of the Cypress Campus beyond the worship ministry.

  • Participate in staff development and performance management processes.

  • Perform other duties as assigned by the Lead Campus Pastor.

Personal & Spiritual Qualifications

The ideal candidate will:

  • Demonstrate a clear profession of faith in Jesus Christ and a growing personal relationship with Him.

  • Model spiritual maturity, integrity, humility, and moral character.

  • Demonstrate a commitment to prayer, Scripture, discipleship, and the local church.

  • Be committed to the mission, vision, values, and worship philosophy of Bayou City Fellowship.

  • Lead with a shepherd’s heart and a genuine desire to serve and develop others.

  • Be teachable, collaborative, relational, and emotionally healthy.

  • Demonstrate initiative, strong organizational skills, and attention to detail.

  • Balance musical excellence with authentic, Spirit-dependent worship.

SUMMARY

Provide a welcoming, clean, and distraction free environment for people to meet and hear God at Pinelake Church. This is done through maintaining the facilities and grounds of the campus to a high level of excellence. The Facilities Associate will ensure the work is done to the standards of Pinelake and in accordance with Pinelake’s policies as well as the direction of the Pinelake leadership.

GENERAL RESPONSIBILITIES

Learn

  • Pursue a growing relationship with Jesus through consistent time in God’s Word and prayer
  • Continually grow in your understanding of the Jesus-Centered Life (salvation, identity, life, and authority in Christ).
  • Remain teachable and hungry, seeking feedback, learning from others, and developing both spiritually and professionally.
  • Cultivate awareness of God’s presence in everyday life, listening to the Holy Spirit and responding in obedience.

Live

  • Practice and model the rhythms of Be the Church (Grow, Pray, Connect, and Share).
  • Pursue emotional health by engaging in self-awareness, addressing past wounds, and cultivating honest, healthy relationships.
  • Practice healthy rhythms, prioritizing your relationship with Jesus and your family
  • Embody a life of integrity and surrender, allowing your private life with God to shape your work.

Lead

  • Take ownership of disciple-making by supporting and strengthening environments where people can take their next step toward a Jesus-Centered Life.
  • Leverage your role, systems, and responsibilities to remove barriers and create clarity, helping both staff and the church move forward in the Discipleship Pathway (Essentials → JCL → Be the Church).
  • Contribute to life-change by bringing your skills, organization, and follow-through to your work, knowing that what you build and manage helps others lead and shepherd more effectively.
  • Build people through your influence—encouraging, supporting, and serving teammates and Servant Leaders in ways that help them grow and thrive.
  • Measure success not only by task completion, but by how your work contributes to disciples being formed and multiplied across the church.

Embrace the Culture

  • Value and embody the staff values, which we call the 7 H’s: Humility, Honor, Honesty, Hunger, Holy Spirit, Health, and Harmony
  • Communicate clearly, honestly, and proactively in a way that builds trust, unity, and momentum.
  • Work in alignment with the church vision and leadership
  • Participate fully in the life of your campus or team, contributing to the unity, health, and shepherding of the faith family.

SPECIFIC LIST OF DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Proper setup of rooms as directed by the Regional Facility Manager or as described on Pinelake’s calendar system.
  • Surface prep and application of paint.
  • Completing routine maintenance service requests as assigned, such as replacing light bulbs, repairing doors and locks, ceiling tiles, etc.
  • Moving furniture and equipment.
  • Identify and repair plumbing leaks, including openings clogged lines/drains, replacing washers and other minor parts, etc.
  • Repair walls and woodwork.
  • Pressure-wash walkways and buildings.
  • Complete make-ready process for events.
  • Responsible for the proper use and maintenance of all assigned equipment used for maintenance and/or housekeeping to ensure proper operation, safety of the operator, and participants, accountability, and security of the equipment.
  • As a team member, cooperate with other staff members and follow the leadership of the Senior Associate Pastor, Director of Operations, Director of Facilities, and the Regional Facility Manager.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

QUALIFICATIONS

To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily. The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skill and/or ability required. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform essential functions.

EDUCATION AND/OR EXPERIENCE

Three to five years of related experience and/or training is required.

LANGUAGE SKILLS

The individual must have excellent interpersonal skills, ability to work with a diverse group of people, communicate clearly and effectively on the telephone, e-mail and in person, demonstrating tact and diplomacy. Exceptional interpersonal skills are required to develop and maintain strong working relationships with volunteers, co-workers, the public and church members and regular attendees. The individual must have the ability to understand written or oral instructions; read, analyze and interpret complex documents, instructions manuals, policies and procedures is essential.


COMPUTER AND MATHEMATICAL SKILLS

The individual must have demonstrated skill in the use of Windows/MacOS to complete tasks, including word processing and spreadsheets and the ability to use the internet for information retrieval. The individual must have basic mathematical skills, knowledge of bookkeeping and basic accounting, and budget and expense monitoring. The individual must have the ability to read financial information and spreadsheets.


REASONING ABILITY

Simultaneous conceptualization and planning of multiple tasks, ability to project outcomes using different implementation strategies and ability to apply creative and innovative thinking to problem situations. The ability to work effectively and efficiently under stressful conditions to ensure deadlines are met is essential.


PHYSICAL DEMANDS

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

post_html:
Campus Staff Minister-Purdue University/West Lafayette (Undergraduate Ministry)

Work Location:

Indiana

Job Type:

Full time

God has called InterVarsity to plant and to build witnessing communities of students and faculty who follow Jesus on college and university campuses. Through these groups, we believe ever- increasing numbers of students and faculty from all ethnic groups and areas of the campus will be transformed by the Gospel. We expect to see campuses increasingly become places where people, ideas, and structures flourish to the glory of God. We confidently anticipate that our InterVarsity alumni will become change agents across the country and around the world. We pursue this calling by discerning and actively participating in what God is already doing on campus. This is the essence of being a Campus Staff Minister (CSM).

ESSENTIAL COMMITMENTS/RESPONSIBILITIES 

Spiritual Growth 

You pursue maturity as a disciple of Jesus Christ so that your life and work increasingly reflects a growing love for God, God’s Word, God’s people of every ethnicity and culture, and God’s purposes in the world. To do this, you will: 

  • Pursue a vibrant relationship with the triune God through engagement with Scripture, prayer, and worship, both individually and in community 

  • Develop self-leadership (growing in self-awareness, self-management, relational integrity, and resiliency) 

  • Embrace Scriptural standards for behavior and attitudes 

 

Campus Leadership 

You communicate and model InterVarsity’s vision to see students and faculty transformed, campuses renewed and world changers developed 

  • Create a culture of humble dependence on God and bold expectation in God’s intention to start new witnessing communities throughout the campus and on new campuses 

  • Model – in person and through programs – InterVarsity’s vision and Core Values, including a biblically-defined commitment to engage every ethnic and social group on campus 

  • Lead students and faculty – individually and collectively – through Scripture, prayer, teaching, and discipleship experiences, so that they articulate and align their ministry activities around this vision 

  • Set annual goals through prayer, research and reflection with your teams (students, faculty, and staff) for qualitative and quantitative growth, including conversions and leadership development 

 

You create, develop, align and leverage ministry plans, programs, teams, and structures to close the gap between current reality and the aspirational goals. 

  • Build leadership teams who trust and partner well with you and who demonstrate spiritual vitality, relational health, and mission alignment 

  • Develop and execute plans to achieve annual goals, evaluating and modifying the plan as needed throughout the year 

  • Increase momentum for the vision by aligning programs, structures, conferences and teams around the goals 

  • Mobilize students and faculty to engage their relational networks with the gospel and to start new missional communities 

  • Under the direction of the Area Director, may supervise Ministry Interns and Campus Ministry Interns as delegated 

 

You intentionally gather, invite, and develop diverse groups of students and faculty so that they not only encounter and follow Jesus as Savior and Lord but also advance the mission on campus as participants and leaders. 

  • Create ways for faculty and students to encounter and follow Jesus through Scripture, worship, prayer, mission experiences, conferences, etc. 

  • Equip students and faculty so that they think strategically about campus engagement and so that they proclaim – in word, deed, and power – the good news of Jesus, regularly inviting students and faculty to follow him as Savior and Lord 

  • Disciple students and faculty by equipping them to hear the Word, respond actively, and debrief and interpret the experience so that they grow in Christlikeness, reflect our Core Values, and develop ministry skills 

  • Invite, coach, and equip students and faculty to become increasingly effective participants and leaders, including starting new witnessing communities on campuses 

 

Organizational Collaboration 

You work with a network of other local, area, regional, and national InterVarsity staff and volunteers so that our work reflects Biblical standards of excellence, integrity, and partnership. 

  • Partner with and respond positively to the direction and coaching of your supervisors and national leaders 

  • Contribute to collaborative and productive team meetings and relationships 

  • Affiliate chapters under your care and submit Graduating Student Forms in order to increase our partnership with current students and alumni 

  • Use national ministry resources and tools, as requested, including recruiting and/or participating in local, regional, or national conferences as  

  • Complete reporting, planning and review requirements in a timely way so that you and your supervisors can assess and improve your work as a CSM 

  • Comply with all InterVarsity policies and procedures 

 

Ministry Partnership Development 

You will develop a team of partners – churches and individuals (including alumni and community members) – who will resource the ministry financially, in prayer, or volunteer service that advances the mission. 

  • Raise 100% of the financial budget assigned by your supervisor 

  • Communicate regularly with your ministry partners, nurturing the relationship through visits, phone calls, emails and regular prayer letters 

  • Develop on-going, long-lasting partnership with alumni and volunteers 

  • Comply with all Ministry Partnership Policies 

  • Identify and invest in advocates who will build networks of volunteers and donors on InterVarsity’s behalf 

 

Accomplish all other assigned tasks as appropriate 

 

QUALIFICATIONS (common to all levels of CSM) 

  • Annually affirm InterVarsity’s Statement of Agreement (Doctrinal Basis and Purpose Statement). Abide by InterVarsity’s Code of Conduct. Believe and behave consonantly with InterVarsity’s Human Sexuality Theological Paper. Affirm and behave consonantly with InterVarsity’s “Women in Ministry Statement of Affirmation” 

  • Bachelor’s degree for CSMs assigned to a four-year campus. A minimum of an Associate’s degree for CSMs assigned to a two-year campus or a community college 

  • Strong interpersonal skills (including ability to minister to diverse ethnic communities and faculty) 

  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills 

  • Demonstrated problem solving skills 

  • Familiarity with word processing, presentation, email, and spreadsheet software 

 

WORK ENVIRONMENT/PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS 

The CSM position leads ministry in a college campus environment. A designated office space may or may not be available. The CSM is required to travel to on-campus and off- campus sites as appropriate. Off-campus travel includes, but is not limited to: student ministry conferences, Ministry Partnership Development meetings, and InterVarsity- sponsored training sessions, meetings, and conferences. The CSM is regularly required to communicate with others, and routinely uses standard office equipment such as computers, phones, photocopiers, filing cabinets, etc. 

Pay Range: $40,476.00 - $53,952.00 per year

Pay: This position is funded through personal fundraising. Accordingly, compensation will vary based on the ability of the individual to secure a donor team to fund the cost of his/her salary. The anticipated salary range for this position on a full-time basis (40 hours/week) is dependent on a variety of factors, including location and cost of living. The actual salary received, including any geographic adjustment to account for location and cost of living, is subject to the individual’s ability to raise funds necessary to cover the full amount of such salary within the range set forth in the job posting details.

Benefits:

We offer a competitive benefits package, including health care and retirement savings with a match. Eligibility is based on employee type and hours worked.  Benefits include the following:

  • 403(b) Retirement Savings Plan

  • 403(b) matching contributions

  • Dental insurance

  • Employee assistance program

  • Employee discounts

  • Flexible work schedule

  • Flexible spending accounts

  • Health insurance

  • Health savings account

  • Life insurance

  • Paid time off

  • Parental leave

  • Professional development assistance

  • Vision insurance

Equal Employment Opportunity: 

 

InterVarsity Christian Fellowship/USA is both an equal opportunity employer and a faith-based religious organization. We conduct hiring without regard to race, color, ancestry, national origin, citizenship, age, sex, marital status, parental status, membership in any labor organization, political ideology, or disability of an otherwise qualified individual. The status of InterVarsity Christian Fellowship/USA as an equal opportunity employer does not prevent the organization from hiring staff based on their religious beliefs so that all staff share the same religious commitment.  Pursuant to the Civil Rights Act of 1964, Section 702 (42 U.S.C. 2000e 1(a)) InterVarsity Christian Fellowship/USA has the right to, and does, hire only candidates who agree with InterVarsity’s Statement of Agreement: Purpose and Doctrinal Basis because InterVarsity believes that each and every staff plays a vital role in advancing InterVarsity’s mission and purposes.

Who We Are:

The Met Church is located on the Northwest side of Houston and our mission is to invite people into meaningful relationship with God and each other. We believe making disciples of Jesus happens in the context of relationship and that small group environments are where we grow spiritually in community with other believers. We also live to serve and connect our local community to hope through our variety of mission efforts and care ministries. You will find our Sunday morning worship to be contemporary and energetic with Bible based teaching focused on understanding and applying God’s word as truth in our lives. At The Met, we are asking God to build a thriving community of people who are following Jesus, being changed by Jesus, and committed to the mission of Jesus.

 

About This Role:

The Adult Discipleship Pastor plays a vital role in strategically leading the church’s adult ministry by fostering spiritual growth and equipping individuals to live out the mission of the church through relational discipleship. This role fosters a disciple-making culture, with a focus on developing, equipping, and investing in small group leaders to lead healthy disciple-making cultures within our small groups.

 

A central responsibility is to develop and implement strategies that inspire adults to grow as disciples of Christ who can then disciple others. The Adult Discipleship Pastor will work collaboratively with church staff and volunteers to create and execute strategies aimed to promote personal Spiritual growth and biblical learning that will lead to stronger connections and empower individuals to live on mission within the context of meaningful relationship.


A note on this role:  This position carries spiritual authority to teach and lead within the congregation, including authority over men. In keeping with the elder-affirmed convictions of The Met Church regarding spiritual authority, this pastoral position is open to men only. 


Who You Are: Competencies, Abilities, & Character Qualities

  • You love Jesus and are committed to growing as a disciple by abiding in Christ, living in meaningful relationships with others, and being a disciple-maker (John 15, Acts 2, Matt. 4:19, Matt. 28).
  • You are a visionary leader who clearly casts and champions a compelling vision to align people and initiatives and leading others to execute with purpose, unity, and impact.
  • You are a galvanizing leader who naturally encourages and mobilizes others, building and developing volunteer teams that take ownership of ministry and advance the mission of the church. You gain joy from equipping others to lead.
  • You intentionally invest in others and creatr clear pathways for growth, ownership, and multiplication in discipleship environments.
  • You demonstrate emotional and spiritual maturity, effectively working with and through others while navigating relationships and conflict in healthy, God-honoring ways.
  • You champion and model the core virtues of The Met Church – humility, effectiveness, awe, relationship and truth.


What You Will Do:  Essential Duties & Responsibilities

  • Live out the core virtues and mission of The Met to invite others into meaningful relationship with God and each other.
  • Collaborate with leadership to ensure that The Met’s mission and vision of relational discipleship are effectively promoted and implemented across all aspects of the adult discipleship ministry responsibilities.
  • Develop and track clear, strategic goals and objectives for Small Group Pastors, mentors and leaders, ensuring continuous growth and effectiveness within the adult discipleship ministry.
  • Provide ongoing leadership and oversight to a team of direct reports, fostering an environment where discipleship opportunities are created, and both spiritual and leadership growth are prioritized. Conduct regular one-on-one meetings to discuss ministry responsibilities, guide personal spiritual development, and support leadership growth.
  • Collaborately create a strategy & framework for men’s, women’s, and senior adult ministires that align with the overall adult discipleship vision.
  • Create a strategy and framework for Bible studies/course offerings that are targeted to all levels of spiritual maturity.
  • Foster a relational leadership culture within the small group ministry, emphasizing the importance of invitation, personal spiritual health, training, modeling, delegating, empowering others to lead, and creating opportunities for growth and multiplication.
  • Strategically plan and execute events that create an entry for new people, fostor community and ultimately engage unconnected individuals into small group environments.
  • Monitor and track small group health and attendance and provide a framework for increasing overall group health and assimilation into groups for the church.
  • Partner with Marketing & Communications to create compelling promotional materials that raise awareness for ministry initiatives and events.
  • Accountable for the budgeting and stewardship of resources, monthly spending, and adjusting as necessary to meet financial targets according to the provided ministry allocation.
  • Disciple and develop spiritually mature leaders to support small groups and Bible studies.
  • Provide pastoral care, counseling, and support to individuals and leaders. Serve as part of the pastoral staff to conduct baptisms, communion, weddings, funerals and other pastoral duties as needed.
  • Teaching/preaching is not a requirement of the role, but opportunities may be available to do if desire and spiritual gifting is present.
  • Cultivate a spirit of humility, openness to giving and receiving feedback, and a commitment to continuous improvement of self and your team(s).


Your Qualifications: Education & Experience

  • You are a fully committed follower of Jesus Christ and a member of The Met Church (or willing to transfer membership to The Met).
  • You agree with and act in accordance with The Met’s Statement of Beliefs.
  • Minimum 8 years of ministry leadership in a discipleship focused environment or equivalent experience.
  • 5 year's experience living out the Real Life Discipleship method of disciple-making, have attended a DiscipleShift conference, or equivalent experience at a Relational Discipleship Network church.
  • High school diploma or general education degree (GED) required. A Master of Divinity (MDiv) from an accredited seminary strongly preferred.
  • You have been called by God into full-time ministry and are actively involved in making disciples who go and make other disciples of Jesus Christ.
  • Must be actively investing in others living out the concept of being a disciple-maker.
  • Proficient in the use of Microsoft Office software. Able to quickly learn and adapt to new technology & systems.


Hours and Work Environment:

This is a full-time, salaried position.  A typical work schedule is Sunday through Thursday and may include Friday &/or Saturday to meet the needs of various ministry events. As for all staff members, it’s important to maintain a healthy work/life rhythm and schedules may need to adjust from time to time to support this effort.

 

Light physical activity performing administrative and pastoral work in an indoor office setting.

NYU Langone Hospital—Brooklyn is a full-service teaching hospital and Level I trauma center located in Sunset Park, Brooklyn. The hospital is central to a comprehensive network of affiliated ambulatory and outpatient practices, and serves as NYU Langone Health's anchor for healthcare access, growth, and delivery in the entire borough. At NYU Langone Health, equity and inclusion are fundamental values. We strive to be a place where our exceptionally talented faculty, staff, and students of all identities can thrive. We embrace inclusion and individual skills, ideas, and knowledge.

Learn more about NYU Langone Hospital—Brooklyn, and interact with us on LinkedIn, Glassdoor, Indeed, Facebook, X, YouTube and Instagram.

Position Summary:
We have an exciting opportunity to join our team as a Manager of Pastoral Care, Required Board Certified Chaplain - Brooklyn.

In this role, the successful candidate Responsible for the day-to-day direction and management of Spiritual Care operations, including provision of pastoral/spiritual care services and hospitality services. Manages all aspects of coordinating, scheduling, maintaining, and organizing services in collaboration with relevant departments, while providing operational and administrative support to the Director.

Job Responsibilities:

    To design and execute a systemic, multi-staff model for the provision of pastoral/spiritual care services and education throughout NYU Langone-Brooklyn.
    To commit to continuing education self and staff, centered on continuous development of effective skills in contemporary professional chaplaincy.
    To encourage and support research activities through staff and/or students which assess effectiveness of pastoral/spiritual care services, develop tools for benchmarking productive staffing patterns and  promote continuous quality improvement in pastoral care services.
    To foster a climate of education and coordinate whole-person/spiritual care in-service programming for multidisciplinary staff, clinical students, community clergy, volunteers, and the wider community. To assure that all students in programs of Clinical Pastoral Education, interns, and others learning the art of pastoral/spiritual care function within clear institutional/clinical guidelines and a plan of administrative coordination, accountability and support.
    To monitor and effectively measure clinical outcomes relative to the contributions of pastoral/spiritual care services, through collaboration with multidisciplinary managers and caregivers.
    To serve as the primary organizational and financial manager of the Department of Pastoral Care, accountable for sound stewardship of budget, physical, and human resources.

    Responsible for data analysis compilation and reporting to include annual reports to support organizational goals and initiatives.
    To maintain full compliance with all standards of ethics, performance, certification and accreditation, as established by the Association of Professional Chaplains (APC), National Association of Catholic Chaplains (NACC), Association for Clinical Pastoral Education (ACPE), the Joint Commission for Accreditation of Healthcare Organizations (JCAHO), and all relevant professional associations and accrediting agencies.
    To promote and oversee meaningful, timely, community-oriented worship life throughout the healthcare system, in ways that nurture interfaith respect, understanding and participation.
    To oversee the recruitment, training and supervision of volunteers from diverse religio-cultural communities who can provide bi-lingual, faith-group-specific care to patients, residents, and families.
    To oversee a comprehensive pastoral/spiritual care program for trauma, crisis, and disaster response ministries, servicing the Emergency Department, Critical Care Units, Emergency Management Systems, and wider healthcare system.

    Work closely with the educator to ensure a well-developed Clinical Pastoral Education program is developed according to the Association for Clinical Pastoral Education standards.
    To integrate and strengthen pastoral care services in death, dying and bereavement throughout the system, including organ/tissue donation, follow-up bereavement letters to all families, periodic memorial services, and referral to grief support groups.
    To develop effective/efficient means for the documentation of spiritual care activities and services, through such measures as spiritual assessment, progress entries in medical records, logging on-call activities, etc.

    Provides on-call spiritual care coverage in accordance with departmental policies and organizational standards.
    To develop and implement a comprehensive practice of conducting initial visits and individualized spiritual assessment with as many patients as possible. To establish a means for effective risk screening which identifies individuals whose spiritual/theological anguish/conflicts may compromise treatment, recovery, or whole person health.

    To promote religio-cultural competence and seek to safeguard all patients, residents, families and staff from unwelcome proselytizing or forms of spiritual intrusion. To facilitate the interpretation of diverse faith expressions and cultural/ritual practices as they impact clinical services
    To provide direct pastoral care service and serve as one of the key institutional catalysts/leaders in setting a climate of mission-driven, culturally competent spiritual care through quality relationships with patients, residents, families, staff, volunteers, and students.
 

 

Minimum Qualifications:
To qualify you must have a B.A. and M.Div. degrees (or equivalent masters level degree from accredited seminary/graduate prof. school)
Minimum 4 units of ACPE-accredited Clinical Pastoral Education.
3-5 years full-time experience in healthcare ministry
APC, NACC, NAJC, or ACPE certified;Ecclesiastical endorsement from recognized denomination

Preferred Qualifications:
Masters Degree and recent supervisory experience working in a healthcare environment and knowledge of HCAHPs Patient Satisfaction surveys is preferred. Experience leading professionals in improvement programs. Knowledge of instructional design and health literacy in the healthcare setting.

Qualified candidates must be able to effectively communicate with all levels of the organization.

NYU Langone Hospital—Brooklyn provides its staff with far more than just a place to work. Rather, we are an institution you can be proud of, an institution where you'll feel good about devoting your time and your talents.

At NYU Langone Health, we are committed to supporting our workforce and their loved ones with a comprehensive benefits and wellness package. Our offerings provide a robust support system for any stage of life, whether it's developing your career, starting a family, or saving for retirement. Join us and experience the extensive resources and services designed to enhance your overall quality of life for you and your family.

How to Apply

Interested candidates must complete the following steps to be considered for the Campus Ministry Fellowship Program:

 

1. Submit an Online Application

  • Complete the online application through our applicant portal.
  • Upload your résumé and cover letter.

2. Complete the Campus Ministry Application Packet

  • Download and complete the Campus Ministry Application Packet, which includes:
    • Campus Ministry Fellowship Application Form
    • Campus Ministry Fellowship Essay Prompt
    • Campus Ministry Fellowship Project Proposal
  • Email all three completed documents to jobs@richmonddiocese.org.

3. Arrange for Three Letters of Reference

Request letters addressing your qualifications for the program from each of the following:

  • Current Pastor
  • Lay Minister in the Church (e.g., Campus Minister, Youth Minister, or Director of Religious Education)
  • Professional Reference

Letters must be submitted directly by the individuals providing the references to jobs@richmonddiocese.org.

 

Important: Applications are reviewed in monthly rounds. Submit your application by November 30th to be considered in ourfirst review round. Additional review rounds will occur after the following application deadlines: December31st, January 31st, and February 28th. Applying early is strongly encouraged, as positions may be filled during anyreview round. Any incomplete application packages will not be considered.

 


The Catholic Diocese of Richmond is now accepting applications for its Campus Ministry Fellowship Program for the 2027–2029 cycle.

 

This Program is open to all recent college graduates who want to get direct ministry experience while pursuing a graduate degree. The campus ministry Fellow serves for one to two years on a particular campus ministry. As a Fellow, you will participate as part of a team led by the Local Director of Campus Ministry to further evangelization efforts on Campus. You will serve the campus ministry in numerous ways and at the discretion of the Local Director. When possible, continuing education will be provided in the areas of theology or pastoral ministry. 

 

Over the course of the program the Fellow will grow in knowledge and practice so that you are able to fully serve as a campus minister upon completion of the program.

 

Responsibilities

  • Upon consultation with the Local Director, various responsibilities will be assigned in the areas of Evangelization, Word, Worship, Community, and Service.
  • Respond to the pastoral needs of students as appropriate
  • Provide mentorship and discipleship to foster student leadership development. 
  • Supervise  student programs and activities (including but not limited to music ministry, small groups, retreats, community service projects, alternative break trips)
  • Provide logistical support, as necessary, for activities and events proposed by the student leadership and approved by the Local Director.
  • Collaborate with the Diocesan Office for Evangelization by participating in diocesan events (i.e., Campus Ministry Summit, Annual Spring Retreat, Diocesan Work Camp) and campus ministry staff events (i.e., Winter Meeting and Spring Retreat and Conference).
  • Perform all other duties as assigned.

 

The fellow collaborates  regularly with the Local Director of Campus Ministry, the Diocesan Associate Director of the Office for Evangelization, the Campus Ministry team, and other Diocesan Campus Ministry staff members.


  •      Bachelor’s degree and enrolled in graduate level coursework in the areas of theology or pastoral ministry.
  •      1+ years’ Campus Ministry experience
  •      Strong interpersonal and communication skills, with the ability to build positive relationships with others. 
  •      Ability to work well in a multi-faith and multicultural settings
  •      Ability to maintain confidentiality
  •      Detail-oriented and highly organized
  •      Ability to manage multiple priorities and tasks effectively in both office and event settings.
  •      Practicing Catholic in good standing

This is a full-time (40 hours a week) non-exempt professional ministry position. Night and weekend work is necessary primarily during the academic year. The position requires travel to campus ministers’ meetings and other diocesan events.  Approved travel expenses are reimbursed.

Job Purpose

The Director of Ministry Operations role supports a wide range of responsibilities and plays a key role in ensuring excellence, alignment, and efficiency across all aspects of MBC Arlington’s ministry operations.


Duties and responsibilities (Essential Functions)


The following items describe some of the ways the Location admin will operate:


  1. THE BUILDING/ FACILITY
  • Serve as point of contact for issues related to the building
  • Request work orders to MBC Building Services as needed
  • Communicate with MBC Facilities Staff regarding custodian’s schedule changes or issues
  • Handle incoming mail/deliveries to the building
  • Ensure storage areas are tidy and organized well for ongoing use
  • Handle requests for building usage from members and outside groups


  1. PURCHASING, INVOICES AND EXPENSE REPORTS
  • Order supplies for office as needed
  • Maintain supply of worship supplies: communion cups, snacks, response cards, new people packets, etc.
  • Handle receipts and monthly expense reports 
  • Process reimbursements for church members as needed
  • Ensure timely payment of invoices


  1. OUTWARD FACING COMMUNICATIONS
    • Ensure the website is accurate and up to date with the latest information 
    • Work with Communications Team to request graphics for projects
    • Post on social media accounts, with input from Location Pastor


  1. EVENTS AND CLASSES


  • Utilize the MBC Help Desk to request event and class registrations
  • Purchase or order food and supplies for events/classes
  • Ensure the class and events are set up and cleaned up, with help from Serve Teams


  1. MINISTRY PLATFORM


  • Run reports in MP including registration lists, stats on membership, etc.
  • Input / update records in MP
  • Send group emails through MP (eNews, event participant info, etc.)


  1. CHURCH GROUPS
  • Facilitate a smooth connection to CGs from initial request to first visit
  • Communicate with leaders to maintain accurate rosters, and to see where groups have room to grow
  • Facilitate the coverage of CGs (stories/celebrations) in our communications channels


  1. MEETINGS 
    • Ensuring that staff meetings minutes and agenda are communicated to relevant parties 
    • Ensure that accurate meeting notes are taken and disseminated 
    • Ensure that tasks are communicated to those responsible and that project are managed to completion 


  1. COMMUNITIES
  • Serve as the primary staff contact for a Women’s Community.
  • Serve as an additional staff contact for Men’s Community.
  • Work with staff and Community Team leaders to ensure all our events / gatherings are welcoming for new guests and include a process for guest follow-up
  • Facilitate the coverage of Communities (stories/celebrations) in our communications channels


  1. SERVE TEAMS
    • Keep an accurate list of open serving opportunities
    • Ensure the onboarding process for serve teams is smooth and effective across all teams
    • Facilitate the coverage of serve teams in our communications channels


  1. THE SUNDAY EXPERIENCE 
  • Oversee the Welcome Teams strategy and leadership
  • Ensure the building aesthetic and vibe is positive and welcoming
  • Troubleshoot any issues that affect the Sunday experience
  • Ensure that new guests are contacted in a timely way following their first visit with us
  • Develop a team of Connectors to follow up with a personal touchpoint (email, call, invitation, etc.)
  • Route new guests to other staff as appropriate regarding discipleship/care/etc.


  1.  GENERAL INQUIRIES
  • Serve as the point of contact for general inquiries
  • Be available to receive visitors to the building 
  • Respond to questions that come in via email, website form, or phone calls


Qualifications

  1. Must be a “people person” who enjoys working in a fast-paced team environment. 
  2. Must have demonstrated a gifting for organization and administration.
  3. Must be passionate about details, accuracy, follow-through and excellence.
  4. Must be able to manage and prioritize tasks for optimum efficiency.
  1. Must possess excellent verbal and written communication skills. 
  2. Must be able to work well with others as an encouraging and supportive team member. 
  3. Must be able to be joyful and flexible in the midst of constant change.


Working conditions

  • Full -Time Position
  • This job operates in a professional office environment. This role routinely uses standard office equipment such as computers and phones.


Physical requirements

Must be able to read, speak, and hear. Must be able to effectively communicate both orally and in writing. While performing the duties of this job, the individual is regularly required to sit, talk, hear, walk, bend, kneel, and lift. The individual is required to be able to lift and carry items that can weigh 25 pounds or more for short distances.

Our innovative approach to ministry has been featured on CNN, FOX News, and The Today Show. Read this NPR article to get a feel for our vibrant, ethnically diverse, multigenerational community.

Position Summary:

The Church Engagement Director is responsible for managing their assigned portfolio of church relationships as part of a ministry-wide effort to raise East-West’s level of church partnership engagement. They will take responsibility for supporting and accelerating movement in East-West fields by rallying active participants, including giving, long-term goers, mid-term goers, short-term goers, and pray-ers, to join our mission. They will work collaboratively with the Senior Director of Church Engagement and other team members to develop, define, and implement goals and integrated strategies to best accomplish East-West's vision for church partnership engagement.

In this critical position, the effectiveness is measured by meeting regular church engagement goals, including launching new partnerships and deepening existing church partners' involvement. They will faithfully steward assigned church relationships, help raise the quality of church partnership engagement tools and resources, and tap into a vast network of church and non-profit organization leaders built over four decades. Utilizing innovative, pioneering approaches grounded in sound biblical principles and best practices that fit East-West's culture, they will ensure consistent messaging to effectively represent East-West's vision, mission, values, and Statement of Faith to external church partners.

As an ambassador of faith in Christ and rooted in Biblical principles, this role will actively minister to EW leadership, staff, partners, and the community in a manner that exhibits Christ-character through personal and corporate spiritual disciplines.

This is a fully support-raised role.

Essential Duties & Responsibilities:

  • Capitalize on a large network of church leaders in order to engage with churches around the U.S. in exploration of engagement with East-West through:
    • Personally connecting with and meeting with church leaders.
    • Participating in conference/networking events

  • Serve as a primary field advocate between U.S. Churches and assigned ministry fields. Act as an extension of the field team by building deep relationships with overseas staff to accurately represent their needs, culture, and vision to potential church partners.

  • Utilize teaching, preaching, and training opportunities through leadership seminars, mission education/ seminars and preaching in local churches to introduce potential partners to East-West.

  • Develop new engagement tools and presentations, participate in best-practice collaboration and/or train other interested church partnership practitioners.

  • Lead 2-3 Short-term teams each year

  • Participate in or lead East-West project teams and events that serve the organization.

  • In collaboration with Field Leadership and the Recruitment Department, work to help mobilize long-term and mid-term goers.

  • Advise, advocate for, and support the East-West Internship program

  • Develop and maintain a network of personal support

There are nearly 300,000 teenagers of active-duty U.S. military parents who are stationed all over the world. These teens move an average of seven times during their school-aged years. The questions of identity and belonging that all teens face grow even more challenging to answer amid starting over and meeting new friends at each location.
This is where you can be the difference in a military teen’s life! By being in their world, walking alongside them, and creating a community where they experience the truth of God’s love and purpose for them, our staff provide a safe space where teens can develop friendships and connections to experience laughter, build hope, and generate resiliency.
