Description

 

Position Title: Steward for Pastoral Care Ministries
Reports To: Pastor
Schedule: FTE 1.0 (40 hours per week). Monday–Friday; occasional Saturdays and parish events

Parish Family Description

Through the Partners in the Gospel initiative, the Roman Catholic Archdiocese of Seattle has integrated parishes and resources into groupings of parish families that are now in the process of becoming new canonical parishes.

St. Michael Parish and St. Michael Parish School in Olympia, WA comprise a truly vibrant multicultural Catholic community that serves approximately 2,800 families, representing 7,000 individual mass attendees per weekend and approximately 440 school students enrolled in pre-k through 8th grade. The past decade has witnessed unprecedented growth in parish life engagement, ministry participation, and school enrollment.

Saint Edward Parish in Shelton, WA is a diverse parish, inclusive of many ethnic cultures and bilingual function,serving approximately 1200 families per weekend, which strongly suggests vitality for years to come.

Position Summary

The Steward for Pastoral Care provides leadership, coordination, and oversight ministries of compassion, accompaniment, responsiveness, encouragement (C.A.R.E.), across Saint Michael and Saint Edward Parish family. This position ensures that parishioners and members of the wider community receive support during times of illness, grief, disability, loneliness, hardship, and life transition.

Grounded in the Gospel call to “love one another as I have loved you” (John 13:34), the Steward for Pastoral Care develops ministries that foster dignity, belonging, healing, and connection. The role collaborates with parish staff, clergy, volunteers, community organizations, and ministry leaders to strengthen a culture of care and service within Saint Michael and Saint Edward Parish family and the surrounding community.

Parish Family Responsibilities

Eucharistic Visits to the Homebound 

  • Coordinate, train, and support Eucharistic Visitors who bring Holy Communion, prayer, and pastoral presence to parish family members who are temporarily or permanently homebound. 
  • Provide ongoing formation, communication, and support for Eucharistic Ministers serving in this ministry. 
  • Ensure appropriate pastoral follow-up and communication with clergy regarding sacramental needs. 

Eucharistic Visits to Patients at Providence Saint Peter Hospital

  • Maintain regular communication and collaboration with the Director of Hospital Spiritual Care, hospital chaplains, and Eucharistic Visitors.
  • Coordinate, train, support, and commission Eucharistic Visitors who bring Holy Communion, prayer, and pastoral presence to parishioners who are temporarily or permanently homebound. 
  • Provide ongoing formation, communication, and support for Eucharistic Ministers serving in this ministry. 
  • Ensure appropriate pastoral follow-up and communication with clergy regarding sacramental needs. 

Compassion Ministry

 

  • Supervise, train, regularly communicate and assist volunteers. 
  • Ensure that no Catholic, or loved one of a Catholic, faces the experience of dying alone.
  • Prepare trained, compassionate parishioners who can accompany individuals and families through serious illness, the dying process, death, and the early period of grief
  • Work closely with the pastor, clergy, Eucharistic Ministers to the Homebound, hospice, hospitals, and other appropriate professionals. 
  • Cultivate awareness of accompanying people not simply toward death, but toward Christ.

 

Phone Call Ministry

 

  • Supervise, regularly communicate and assist ministry leader and volunteers to ensure every parishioner feels known, valued, and spiritually supported.
  • Supervise program offering phone calls of acknowledgement, prayer, and connection. 

 

Grief Groups

  • Serve as staff contact and coordinator for all grief ministries and gatherings within parish family.

Working Hands

  • Serve as staff contact to coordinate practical assistance for homebound residents through minor home repairs and maintenance. 
  • Support projects such as building ramps, repairing appliances, yard work, and other household needs.



 

Partnership Organizations

  • Chaplains Association for Public Safety - Thurston County (CAPS-TC) serve as staff point of contact for chaplain first responders.

 

  • Project Rachel Ministry: serve as staff point of contact in supporting women, men, and family members experiencing grief or emotional distress following an abortion by connecting them with confidential Catholic post-abortion healing resources.

Pastoral Care and Community Outreach Commission

  • Collaborate with Steward for Community Outreach to represent the Pastoral Care and Community Outreach Commission in supporting parish decision-making and ministry development. 
  • Work closely with commission members in initiatives such as annual grant distribution to community organizations. 
  • Provide pastoral insight, ministry coordination, and recommendations for pastoral care and outreach priorities. 

 

Saint Michael Parish: Additional Responsibilities 

Support Groups

  • Oversee and support faith-based ministries that provide companionship, healing, and spiritual support for individuals and families experiencing grief, illness, loss, and life challenges.

St. Elizabeth Ann Seton Grief Support

 

Saturday Mornings, 10:00 am – 12:00 pm (late November – late February)

  • Facilitate weekly meetings and structured grief support cycles
  • Coordinate grief support programs for individuals coping with the death of a loved one, illness, or other significant life challenges
  • Provide group and individual support grounded in Catholic faith and compassion

Monday Evenings, 6:00 – 7:30 pm

  • Supervise, support and stay in contact with group leader; occasionally attend meetings
  • Coordinate regular meetings focused on prayer, encouragement, and accompaniment

St. Peregrine Cancer Support Group

 

Thursdays, 6:00 – 7:30 pm (in person and via Zoom)

  • Supervise, support and stay in contact with group leader; occasionally attend meetings
  • Support individuals living with cancer, survivors, caregivers, family members, and friends
  • Coordinate prayer, sharing, and support opportunities through in-person and online gatherings

 

St. Dymphna Dementia and Alzheimer's Support Group

 

Wednesday Mornings, 10:00 – 11:30 am

  • Supervise, support and stay in contact with group leader; occasionally attend meetings
  • Provide support and resources for families and caregivers of individuals experiencing dementia and Alzheimer's disease
  • Coordinate regular meetings focused on education, prayer, encouragement, and accompaniment

St. Catherine of Siena Miscarriage and Infant Loss Ministry

 

  • Provide compassionate one-on-one support for individuals and families grieving miscarriage, stillbirth, or neonatal loss

 

Our Lady of Lourdes Suicide Loss Support Group

 

Cycles scheduled according to need and request

  • Facilitate 8-week support cycles
  • Provide a safe, faith-based environment for individuals grieving the loss of a loved one to suicide
  • Offer accompaniment, prayer, and resources to support healing and hope

One-to-One Grief Support

  • Provided as needed

 

All support ministries are rooted in Catholic faith while welcoming people of all religious backgrounds. These ministries provide compassionate peer support and do not replace professional counseling.

Faith and Light: Inclusion & Fellowship

  • Serve as staff contact to support the Faith and Light community, an international ministry that brings together individuals with disabilities, families, and friends for prayer, fellowship, and celebration. 
  • Promote inclusion, friendship, and meaningful participation in parish life.

Prayer Shawl Group

  • Serve as staff contact to support volunteers who create prayer shawls while praying for those who will receive them. 
  • Coordinate the blessing of shawls by clergy. 
  • Supervise distribution of shawls to individuals experiencing illness, grief, hardship, or celebrating significant life moments. 


Qualifications

 

Core Competencies Required

  • Lead, coordinate, and strengthen ministries of compassion, accompaniment, responsiveness, and encouragement (C.A.R.E.) across both parishes.
  • Recruit, train, support, and coordinate volunteers; develop ministry guidelines, resources, and programs.
  • Provide compassionate pastoral presence to individuals and families experiencing illness, grief, disability, loneliness, hardship, or life transitions, including home, hospital, hospice, and assisted-living visits.
  • Maintain timely communication and appropriate follow-through, connecting individuals with clergy, parish ministries, and community resources as needed.
  • Collaborate with clergy, parish staff, volunteers, and community partners to identify pastoral needs and develop effective responses.
  • Maintain appropriate confidentiality, professional boundaries, and records; evaluate ministry effectiveness and encourage ongoing improvement.
    •  

Qualifications

  • Faith and Spiritual Maturity: A strong, active Catholic faith; a commitment to the mission of the Church; and a desire for continued spiritual and pastoral formation.
  • Pastoral Compassion: Demonstrated empathy, patience, prayerfulness, sound judgment, and the ability to accompany people through difficult and sensitive circumstances with dignity and respect.
  • Leadership and Collaboration: Experience or demonstrated ability in ministry leadership, volunteer coordination, program development, and collaborative relationship-building.
  • Communication and Organization: Strong interpersonal, written, and verbal communication skills; effective time management; and the ability to manage multiple priorities, schedules, and timely follow-through.
  • Pastoral Discernment and Boundaries: Ability to recognize pastoral needs, respond appropriately to urgent situations, maintain confidentiality, and identify when professional, medical, counseling, or social-service referrals are appropriate.
  • Administrative and Technology Skills: Proficiency with standard office applications, email, calendars, spreadsheets, and digital communication tools.
  • Flexibility and Initiative: Ability to work independently, adapt to changing pastoral needs, and provide timely support through visits and other ministry activities.
  • Education and Formation: Relevant pastoral-care experience, ministry training, theological education, or equivalent experience is desirable, along with a commitment to ongoing learning and formation.

 

 

Any offered salary is determined based on internal equity, internal salary ranges, market data, applicant’s skills and prior relevant experience, certain degrees and certifications.

Benefits: Eligible positions receive a comprehensive package of benefits including medical, dental, vision, life, accidental death and disability, long term disability, pension, 403(b), HSA, FSA, and generous sick leave, vacation and holidays.

Company Description

Our Mission: 

At CCV (Christ’s Church of the Valley) it is our Missions to WIN people to Christ, TRAIN believers to become disciples, and SEND disciples to impact the world.  

Our Vision:   

To reach the Valley for Christ 

Position Summary: 

The Operations Pastor is primarily responsible for the physical upkeep of campuses which includes, but not limited to: the organization of the campus, cleaning, maintenance and repairs, campus deliveries and inventory. To do the job effectively, the Operations Pastor will have opportunities and responsibilities to lead and develop involved volunteer teams.   

At CCV, our Operations Department and Pastor will also work closely with the campus team and staff to deliver support, resources, and execute the day-to-day needs of the campus. Responsibilities include the facility usage and upkeep, event set up and tear down, room changes, and physical needs that a campus might have for a specific event, and weekend services.  

Job Description

Essential Job Functions: 

  • Actively participate and Complete OPS training set up through the Facilities team. 
  • Consistently recruit and train a robust volunteer team. Teach, train and coach your volunteers while also being a pastoral presence in their lives and guiding them in their next steps. 
  • Maintain Facility operations through a variety of ways: Vendor relationships, Janitorial responsibilities, Campus Cleaning, HVAC, Air filters, General repairs, Power washing, Building strong team relationships with and supporting other team members and ministries, regularly creating and completing many tasks and check listed items for the overall upkeep of the campus.  
  • Inspect rooms and buildings prior to events and make sure all needs are met including temperature settings, doors and access, room configurations, and last-minute needs and details. 
  • Develop a formalized cleaning plan for each area of the facilities to support three approaches to cleaning:  A quick pass-by before or during events, after-event cleaning, and scheduling routine deep cleans. 
  • Trash management and removal for services and special events. Maintain the appearance of the area and its cleanliness. 
  • Operate, clean, and maintain equipment according to CCV operating procedures; train and oversee volunteers to keep with those standards. 
  • Manage all processes of inventory including product ordering, receiving, storing, and displaying merchandise. 
  • Assist and help maintain relationship with Campus Landscaping company and actively be a conduit between CCV and our Landscapers.   
  • Regular 1:1’s with direct report to ensure all goals and objectives are being met.  
  • Consistent communication with campus direct report and maintaining a healthy relationship with both direct report (hard line) and indirect (dotted line) central team lead.  

Qualifications

Minimum Qualifications 

Character & Chemistry 

  • A passion for reaching the lost 
  • Personal integrity in all areas of life 
  • Must be – or willing to become – a participating member of CCV 
  • Regularly attends worship services with their family 
  • Is an active participant in a group, a transformation group, and tithes consistently  

Competency 

  • Customer Focus – is dedicated to meeting the expectations of internal and external customers. 
  • Interpersonal Skills – relates well to all kinds of personalities while building effective relationships, communicates effectively both interpersonally and corporately. 
  • Self-Development – Committed to improvement, seeks constructive criticism, understands strengths and weaknesses. 
  • Drive for Results- Is action-oriented and takes initiative. Ability to identify and solve problems.  

Preferred Experience & Work Environment 

  • Experience successfully managing/leading a team 
  • Ability to recruit, train, develop and retain volunteers 
  • Excellent communication skills with various personality types 
  • Must be willing to work a flexible schedule including weekends 
  • Ability to lift a minimum of 50 lbs.  

Additional Information

All your information will be kept confidential according to EEO guidelines.

General Information

The above statements are intended to describe the general nature and level of work being performed by individuals assigned to this position. They are not intended to be an exhaustive list of all duties, responsibilities, and skills required of employees. CCV Leadership reserves the right to revise the position, its job functions, minimum qualifications and other aspects of the position in any way at any time.

POSITION TITLE: Special Education TEACHER REPORTS TO: BUILDING PRINCIPAL

 OVER-TIME STATUS: EXEMPT PAY GRADE: 710

JOB SUMMARY:

Performs professional work providing limited direct instruction and computer-assisted services to special needs students, motivates students to develop skills in assigned subject matters; does related work as required. Work is performed under the regular supervision of the Principal. Supervision is exercised over paraprofessionals.

 

ESSENTIAL DUTIES:

  • Facilitate specialized subject matter(s), motivating all students to achieve maximum potential;
  • Assesses and evaluates the needs of assigned students
  • Develops individualized instructional programs and monitors their implementation and deadlines
  • Completes and advises on the use of Functional Behavior Assessment and Behavior Intervention Plans;
  • Create lessons designed to instruct students in area(s) of specialization and subject matter specified by State law and administrative regulations and procedures of Portsmouth Public Schools;
  • Establishes and maintains district and school-wide standards of behavior;
  • Encourages students to think independently, develop and express original ideas;
  • Evaluate students' progress, maintain appropriate records, and prepare progress reports/report cards;
  • Communicates with students, student counselors, teachers/other school staff, and parents/guardians through conferences and other means;
  • Maintains professional competence through professional development, in-service education and self-selected professional books and instructional materials;
  • Supervises and monitors student movement and escorts students throughout the building, maintaining student safety at all times
  • Participates in faculty committees and student activity sponsorship;
  • Performs administrative functions in computer-based applications;
  • Models nondiscriminatory practices in all activities,
  • Performs related tasks as required.

 

JOB SPECIFICATIONS/PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS:

Thorough knowledge of the subject(s); thorough knowledge of education principles, practices, and procedures; thorough knowledge of the principles and methodology of effective teaching; thorough knowledge of school division rules, regulations, and procedures; ability to establish and maintain standards of behavior; ability to deliver articulate oral presentations and written reports; ability to establish and maintain effective working relationships with other staff, students and parents; ability to operate a personal computer.

This is sedentary work requiring the exertion of up to 10 pounds of force occasionally and a negligible amount of force frequently or constantly to move objects, and some light work requiring the exertion of up to 20 pounds of force occasionally, up to 10 pounds of force frequently, and a negligible amount of force constantly to move objects; work requires stooping, kneeling, reaching, standing, walking, pushing, pulling, lifting, and repetitive motions; vocal communication is required for expressing or exchanging ideas by means of the spoken word; hearing is required to perceive information at normal spoken word levels; visual acuity is required for preparing and analyzing data, determining the accuracy and thoroughness of work, and observing general surroundings and activities; the worker is subject to inside and outside environmental conditions. Some teaching specialties (i.e. music, art, physical education, etc.) may require hearing, vision, physical coordination and/or exertion and effort in excess of those listed above.

 

EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE:

Must possess a Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in education or a related field. Must possess or be eligible for a Virginia Collegiate Professional License, Postgraduate Professional License or Provisional License with appropriate endorsement to teach specified subject area. 

Detailed licensure information is available from the Virginia Department of Education online at:

http://www.doe.virginia.gov/teaching/licensure/index.shtml

SPECIAL REQUIREMENTS: 

  • Background Investigation
  • Tuberculin skin test or screening results

APPLICATION PROCEDURE:

All applicants please submit an on-line application along with copies of supporting credentials. Be sure to connect your application to the advertised position.

Description

Summary
 

The Faith Kids Global Pastor will lead the Faith Kids ministry team by providing leadership, vision and direction that creates a life giving atmosphere of vibrant and enticing discipleship and evangelism for the children, parents, and Dream Team for all our campuses.  The Faith Kids Global Pastor is responsible for maintaining excellence across all campuses, and works closely with the Faith Kids Campus Directors in the execution, management and direction of each campus. 

 

This position requires its primary duty be the performance of work requiring advanced knowledge, defined as work which is predominantly intellectual in character and which includes work requiring the consistent exercise of discretion and judgment.

 

Essential Functions
Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

Personal:

  • Maintain the God ordained priorities in your life putting Jesus Christ at the center of everything including your spouse, children, and the ministry
  • Passionate about tithing at least 10% of your income to what God is doing through the vision of Faith Church
  • Invest in and lead a Faith Church connect group
  • Be responsible for developing & multiplying Dream Team 
  • Avoid the appearance of evil, let no hint of immorality exist and con­duct life with the upmost of integrity in all situations
  • Attend services regularly with your entire family
  • Maintain loyalty to the vision and staff of Faith Church and always protect the unity God has given this church
  • Believes and operates in the gifts of the Spirit
  • Wholeheartedly believes in the empowerment of women in Pastoral leadership
  • Fully devoted follower of Christ
  • Person of Godly character and integrity
  • Loves Faith Church and lives our vision and culture
  • In alignment with “What We Believe” and “Leadership Core Values”
  • Attend weekly Staff Meeting
  • Personal social media posts in regards to Church activity must be aligned exclusively with Faith Church

 

 

General:

  • Set yearly series schedule, and coordinating set design and curriculum
  • Oversee implementation of policies and enforce compliance.
  • Endure children’s ministry facility standards at their campus are maintained by visiting  each campus monthly and evaluating staff, dream teamers, check-in/out, and overall experience
  • Analyze effectiveness of programming and adjust as needed.
  • Help develop and maintain all security standards.
  • Track growth for future development.
  • Seek opportunities to connect within local schools and community.
  • Oversee quality of services.
  • Help in development of ministry events including Fall Family Bash, Summer Camp, Christmas Events, Volunteer Grow Nights, etc.
  • Provide oversight for Faith Church Sports programs – basketball, soccer, cheer, etc.
  • Monitor financial stewardship of all kids programs, events and sports programs
  • When necessary, help with new campus launch for Faith Kids department
  • All other duties as assigned.

 

Essential Duties & Responsibilities:

  • Managing the Daily Operations of a Campus
    You will be responsible for keeping up a daily list on Basecamp that includes goals and assignments pertaining to your teams
  • Meetings

You will be responsible for having meeting with your Directors, providing leadership and performance and program feedback.

  • Reporting

You will be responsible for analyze weekly reports from each campus weekly and proving feedback to the directors.

  • Administrative Duties
    Responsibilities include project management, ministry systems and processes.
  • Curriculum Development Implementation
    You will be responsible for assisting in the development of Faith Kids content and execution at all campus on the weekends under the guidance of the Executive Pastor.
  • Kids Follow Up
    Oversee follow up with all children that attend campuses including phone calls, emails, weekend evaluations, birthday cards, etc.
  • Set Execution
    Responsible for overseeing stage tear down and set up for each new series.
  • Faith Kids Worship
    Approve song selection and implementation, keep a weekly practice going, make sure new music is out to the volunteers in advance, etc.
  • “What did you learn today?”
    Responsible for insuring that series cards and Family Connect Devotionals are available for students and families at all weekend services.
  • Connect Group
    You must host or attend an Connect group.
  • What’s in it for Me?
    You will be responsible for ensuring Faith Kids Directors maintain a Rewards System that makes sure that kids bring their Bible, memorize scriptures and more. Keeping the “Bible Bucks” store fully stocked, attractive, promoted and ready to roll!
  • Volunteer Scheduling, Recruiting, Building Teams 
    Lead staff team with strategies for recruiting, scheduling and building the teams.
  • Service Planning through PCO 
    Each service should include the following elements: Worship, Prayer, Creative Element, Game Take Home Sheet, Message
  • Summer Camp
    Planning and execution and implementation of our annual Summer Camp program.
  • Update and Maintain Faith Kids Policy and Procedures 
    Keeping Policy and Procedures up to date is a must! You’ll be entrusted with keeping these readily available for all staff and volunteers.
  • Mascots
    You will be responsible for ensuring mascots are scheduled at each campus weekly.
  • Bounce Houses
    Oversight of a team of people to set them up, keeping them in good working order, and filing permits with the city for usage!
  • Grow Team Nights
    You will be responsible for assisting in the development and execution of our monthly volunteer team nights.
  • Faith Kids SPORTS
    You will also be responsible for the development and execution of our Soccer, Basketball and Cheerleading program.
  • It’s all about the Weekend!
    It will be your responsibility to oversee and make sure that your campus has the Faith Kids culture, vibe and excellent experience! From the planning to the execution you’ll monitor the entire weekend program! Utilize weekly reports to monitor this at campuses you aren’t attending.
  • Check In and Check Out
    Safety first! You’ll be responsible for making sure that Check In and Check Out to Faith Kids is smooth and done in excellence according to Faith Kids policies and procedures.
  • Technical Gear
    You’ll be responsible for ensuring your team maintains an inventory list of Technical Gear and report to the Tech Director when a piece of gear is acting up or you need technical support at your campus.
  • All Hands on Deck!
    The Kids Ministry Team will be asked to jump in and help on different church wide initiatives. You are responsible to have a good attitude and jump in when asked!

 

Competencies

  1. Must have a heart for the Church and be a mature follower of Christ.
  2. Excellent verbal and written communication skills.
  3. Excellent interpersonal and customer service skills.
  4. Solid understanding of current trends in children’s ministry.
  5. Excellent organizational skills and attention to detail.
  6. Experience leading teams or groups
  7. Strong administrative skills
  8. Ability to work independently.
  9. Work well under pressure
  10. Enjoys a fast paced environment

 

Work Environment
This job operates in a professional office environment (routinely uses standard office equipment)

 

Physical Demands
Office time is mostly a sedentary role (stationary at desk and working on a computer); during services and events, must have high energy for multiple hour segments. 

 

Position Type and Expected Hours of Work
The weekly schedule will include 40-45 hours per week and will be the same every week.  In addition to your regular weekly hours you will be asked to participate in events that will occasionally include evening or weekend hours, as there are continual seasons where it will be necessary to exceed these minimum hours (i.e., Christmas, Easter, Strategic Planning, are just some examples and do not encompass all of the extended hours opportunities). These hours can/will fluctuate.

                       

Sunday: Varies based on assigned campus

Monday: 9:00AM – 5:00PM

Tuesday: 9:00AM – 5:00PM (rotation week 11:00AM – 9:00PM)

Wednesday: 9:00AM – 5:00PM

Thursday: 9:00AM – 5:00PM

Friday: Off

Saturday: Off (rotation week 3:00pm – 7:00pm)

 

Travel
Campus to campus local travel and occasional overnight trips will be expected for this position.

 

Required Education and Experience

  1. Level of experience: Intermediate (practical application)
  2. 3+ years of multi-site kids ministry leadership experience
  3. Ministry centered Bachelor’s degree

 

Preferred Education and Experience

  1. Pastoral credentials

 

Other Duties
Please note this job description is not designed to cover or contain a comprehensive listing of activities, duties or responsibilities that are required of the employee for this job. Duties, responsibilities and activities may change at any time with or without notice.

Men's Ministry Program Manager -  Mosaic Virginia
 

Mosaic Virginia is a Christian, pro-life nonprofit helping women and men who find themselves unprepared for pregnancy decisions. We are seeking motivated and dedicated staff and volunteers to join our service team.  We offer hope and help for people to make informed decisions about the sanctity of life, faith in Jesus Christ, and sexual integrity, all in a loving and confidential manner.

The Men's Ministry Program Manager is responsible for the day-to-day leadership, administration, and operation of Mosaic Virginia's Men's Ministry Program. This role ensures the effective implementation of the program's mission, goals, and strategic objectives by overseeing daily operations, participant engagement, and volunteer coordination. This role also fosters a Christ-centered environment that reflects Mosaic Virginia's mission and values, promotes spiritual growth and personal accountability among participants, and cultivates meaningful relationships with churches, community partners, and volunteers in support of the ministry's objectives.

This position offers a flexible schedule of 20-25 hours per week.

Description

The Grove’s Ministry Support team is a vital part of keeping our church running efficiently. The Ministry Support Staff work closely with our Ministry Support Team Leads, Support Ministries Director and the entire Grove team, to ensure that all areas of the church are presentable, set-up, and ready to go for every regular church service as well as any other events that are held at The Grove.  
 

Reports to:         Support Ministries DirectorWorks with:       Staff and Volunteers Works:                Part-time, HourlyHours:                 Various Hours As Needed

                          

SUPPORT ACTIVITIES – 70%

  • Set up and tear down rooms for services, classes, meetings, and special events according to provided diagrams, schedules, and instructions.
  • Arrange tables, chairs, staging, signage, and equipment for indoor and outdoor ministry activities.
  • Ensure spaces are prepared on time and meet quality, safety, and ministry standards.

  • Ensure outdoor gathering spaces and common areas are clean, safe, and ready for use.

For consideration, please include a resume and cover letter.

The Highlights:

The Asst Director for Interfaith Ministry and Chaplain for Jewish Life serves within DePaul's Division of Mission and Ministry (DMM), specifically within the department of Interfaith Ministry. The Asst Director will support the religious and spiritual life of DePaul's Jewish community and the DePaul community at large by developing, implementing, and supporting DePaul-sponsored, student-centered and led opportunities for Jewish and interfaith learning, spiritual and Vincentian formation, leadership development, and service. They will develop strong intra-Jewish relationships and a pluralistic Jewish community within DePaul and with partner organizations in order to provide pastoral care and support to students. The Asst Director/Chaplain plays lead role in the division's interfaith and inter-religious dialogue efforts with students, bringing the wisdom of the Jewish tradition into this important mission-based work. This staff person will also collaborate effectively with members of the DMM Faculty and Staff Engagement team and DePaul's Jewish Faculty and Staff Alliance to build a vibrant Jewish community within the university. The AD will seek to draw support, best practices, and prof dev opportunities from organizations fostering Jewish-Christian and interfaith/interreligious engagement. 

What You'll Do:

1. Jewish Life Ministry - As the DePaul Chaplain for Jewish Life , provides leadership of all facets of Jewish Life Ministry at DePaul: Supervise and mentor student leaders; develop learning and formation opportunities, provide spiritual/pastoral support, initiate community building, and foster/support learning opportunities rooted in the Jewish wisdom and spiritual tradition for students, faculty, and staff; oversee event logistics and promotion; provide leadership in coordinating/facilitating Jewish prayer and worship services (particularly around Jewish holidays/celebrations); mentor students around leading Jewish prayers, programs, service, and events; coordinate/collaborate regularly and effectively with external partners around their events in support of the DePaul Jewish community; provide leadership in planning at least one annual Unity Shabbat among/for DePaul's Jewish partner organizations; ensure external Jewish partners are properly vetted, supported, and adhere to university policies/procedures.  

2. Leadership Interfaith Ministry/Religious Pluralism Initiatives - Serves a key leadership role in cultivating a vibrant religious pluralism at DePaul in collaboration with DMM colleagues. Leads student interfaith initiatives such as Interfaith Scholars, dialogue programs, interfaith immersion experiences, etc. Assists in developing annual curriculum and religious pluralism and dialogue calendar; takes lead in guiding students in planning and implementing religious pluralism events and programs. Actively maintains attention to the personal and professional learning and skills needed to lead and facilitate this work. 

3. Contributes to Mission and Ministry Divisional Goals - As with all DMM staff, this role involves participating in regular divisional and DMM-area meetings and divisional strategic planning sessions as well as staffing DMM institution-wide signature events as appropriate (orientation, Vincentian heritage events, BUILD program interfaith education training for faculty and staff). Participates as a contributing team member and mission leader on cross-functional divisional and university committees and task groups as assigned, offering thoughtful Vincentian and Jewish religious/ethical/wisdom insights where applicable. These duties may include but not be limited to leading a service immersion trip, facilitating Vincentian Heritage Tours, and assisting in the implementation of large scale Divisional events or university committees. 

No direct staff reports. Supervises team of student workers, Jewish Faith in Action Scholars, and Interfaith Scholars and Collaborates with Jewish student religious organization leaders. Manages relationships with relevant external Jewish partners (Hillel, Chabad, JUF, etc.).

Manage assigned annual budget for programs and activities under their purview plus additional High Holidays budget and assigned endowment funds. Consult with manager on budget decisions that fall outside established annual budget parameters. Per university expectations, manages/reports on budget and executes financial transactions in Oracle system.

What You'll Need:

  • Master's degree required. (Preferred: Jewish studies, religious studies, Rabbinical studies, Pluralistic Jewish studies)
  • Requires at least two years of prof. experience in Jewish chaplaincy. Work with young adults in education setting (preferred).
  • Requires an articulate and practical understanding of and commitment to a pluralistic Jewish theology.
  • Requires one year of professional experience working within pluralistic Jewish community.
  • Requires at least one year of experience in developing and leading/guiding Jewish ritual and/or worship.
  • Requires at least one year of experience, study, or work within an interreligious discipline or setting.
  • Training or experience in interfaith dialogue preferred.
  • Requires public/professional speaking experience.
  • Clinical Pastoral Experience (preferred / openness to pursuing at least one quarter of CPE as professional development)
  • Training/certification in interfaith/interreligious leadership, dialogue, community-building, and/or facilitation. 
  • Some formal education in Jewish theology, spirituality, and ethics. 
  • Articulate understanding of fundamental theological beliefs and practices of pluralistic Jewish traditions.
  • Leadership of public prayer, ritual, and worship (particularly related to Jewish and interreligious traditions).
  • Encourages and fosters religious pluralism among interreligious groups and within various faith traditions.
  • Encourages leadership of students in spiritual learning, exploration, and formation through theological reflections based on spiritual, religious, and/or ethical values.
  • Fosters connections between spirituality and social action.
  • Communicates effectively on the integration of faith and justice, encouraging and leading students in spiritual learning, exploration, and formation.
  • Listens attentively, provides pastoral care and guidance, and responds pastorally, particularly around the specific needs and issues of young adults and in moments of crisis.
  • Excellent leadership, professionalism, administration, communication, organization, networking, and collaboration skills.
  • Ability as a writer around pastoral/spiritual issues for public consumption highly preferred. 
  • Some adaptability in work hours expected due to needs of student community and job duties. Will include some evening and weekend work, as well as some short-term travel. 

The anticipated hiring range for this position is: $56,222 to $73,000. 

The salary range provided in this posting reflects what we reasonably expect to pay for this position. Actual compensation offered or earned is dependent on experience, education and other factors including departmental budget.


Perks:

  • Working for a stable and well-known University.
  • Top choice medical, dental, and vision benefits.

  • Tuition waivers for employees and dependents.
  • Generous paid time off, sick time, holidays, floating holidays, and more!

Guided by an ethic of Vincentian personalism and professionalism, DePaul compassionately upholds the dignity of all members of its diverse, multi-faith, and inclusive community. We seek to hire collaborative, open-minded, and dedicated professionals who are committed to advancing our university mission to making education accessible to all, with special attention to including underserved and underrepresented communities. post_html:
Reports to: Director for Evangelization and Missionary Discipleship

Location: Pastoral Ministry Center

Work Schedule: Monday through Friday 8:30 am – 5:00 pm, flexible as needed

Position type: Full-time 

FLSA Status: Exempt


Summary: 

The Associate Directors from the Evangelization and Missionary Discipleship team, play a key role in advancing the Archdiocese of San Antonio’s mission of evangelization and missionary discipleship through a collaborative, pastoral approach that supports parish and diocesan ministry leaders. Each Associate Director will help shape and evaluate pastoral plans, contribute to ongoing formation efforts, and assist in fostering vibrant parish communities of faith across all stages of life. 

The Associate Director of Associate Director of Middle & High School Ministry provides direct support to the Director of Evangelization and Missionary Discipleship, to advance the archdiocesan vision and mission in the areas of middle school and high school ministry & formation, outreach initiatives, and sacramental preparation for adolescent Confirmation. 

This position is active in outreach to parishes and deaneries throughout the Archdiocese with an emphasis on formation for parish leaders. Formation may take place through parish visits, deanery meetings, developing and giving workshops and trainings, and the implementation of archdiocesan guidelines and initiatives related to middle school and high school youth and outreach ministry. 

The fundamental basis of this role is an integration of the New Evangelization and Missionary Discipleship in pastoral de conjunto to serve the multicultural pastoral needs of children, youth, young adults, adults (as couples, and men and women as individuals) and seniors. 


Requirements

Position Responsibilities:

• *Develop new formation and workshops, as needed, based on the vision and guidelines of the Department for Pastoral Ministries.

• *Offer trainings and workshops in Sacramental Preparation, and Faith Formation for parish ministry leaders throughout the Archdiocese.

• *Communicate with parish ministry leaders to develop a sense of supportive presence, offer formation, and help make them aware of training opportunities. 

• Create, contribute and manage content for communications to parish leaders and relevant audiences. This includes collaboration with the appropriate DPM staff for promotional efforts. 

• Assist in maintaining up to date contact information for parish leadership in this area of ministry. 

• *Work with the Director in identifying current resources, models and best practices used their area of specialized ministry. 

• *Promote and implement best practices in specialized area.

• *Develop and maintain local partnerships and relationships with Lay Ecclesial Movements, internal and external Church organizations connected to their specialized area of ministry. 

• *Serve as a resource and guide for pastors and parish ministers for specific parish needs or concerns related to their area of specialized ministry, as well as general practices common to all areas of evangelization and missionary discipleship. 

• *Organize, analyze, and present data related to ministry leaders in these areas. Make recommendations based on available data.

• *Serve as the lead or support the lead and appropriate staff for events and initiatives connected to evangelization and missionary discipleship as assigned by the Director.

• Offer formation to Deacons, Religious, Seminarians & Laity at Mexican American Catholic College as requested.

• *Assist the Director in maintaining and implementing sacramental guidelines and ministry policies by promoting them with parish leaders.

• *Identify pastoral needs of ministry leaders and responding appropriately. This includes the awareness of when ministry leaders need referral for guidance or services with other offices; including situations that need referral beyond the scope of pastoral and ministerial support.    

• *Ensures the mission, vision, values and priorities of the archdiocese is communicated clearly and carried out effectively, efficiently and collaboratively within assigned office.  

• Regularly engage in personal growth, professional development, theological study, prayer, charity and justice work, and spiritual formation.

• Foster a “Pastoral de Conjunto” environment by leading by example, resolving issues, and making sound decisions.

• Adhering to safety training and protocols on a daily basis and taking precautionary measure to ensure the safety and well-being of self, others.   

• Responsible for protecting the confidentiality of any information or material obtained in the service with the organization to include but not limited to client names and information, services rendered to clients, donors names and gifts, internal and external investigations or results of any investigations, and financial information.

• Adherence to the Code of Conduct and the Faith and Moral Policy is mandatory.

• Every employee is required to take a solution-oriented approach in their interactions and undertakings, as well as being a team member that promotes collaboration and commitment to the Mission and Vision of the organization.

• Performs other duties as assigned.

 * Essential Functions - ADA   


Minimum Qualifications: 

• Education

o Bachelor’s Degree in any area of ministry, or related field. 

• Experience

o Minimum of seven (7) years of experience in parish youth ministry development and evaluation

o Experience using key catechetical documents such as Catechism of the Catholic Church, the Directory for Catechesis, Evangelii Gaudium to guide parish ministry.

o Must be a Roman Catholic in good standing with the Church.

• License and Credentials

o Reliable transportation

o Valid driver license

o Valid vehicle insurance

Minimum Knowledge and Skills: 

• A thorough working knowledge of the Catechism of the Catholic Church, the General Directory of Catechesis, the National Directory for Catechesis, Christus Vivit, Renewing the Vision, and current developments in the Church’s theology of the vocation of the laity.

• Bi-lingual in English and Spanish preferred;

• Bi-cultural background to recognize and engage different social realities and challenges is highly preferred.

• Intimate knowledge of the Sacred Scriptures and the capacity to offer formation through the lens of the Word of God.

• Excellence in organizational management, setting and achieving goals and objectives, and managing a budget.

• Past success working with committees and the ability to cultivate existing committee member relationships.

• Strong public relations skills with the ability to engage a wide range of stakeholders that include parishes, groups, other churches, as well as within and beyond the Pastoral Center.

• Excellent written and verbal communication skills; a passionate communicator with excellent interpersonal and multidisciplinary project skills, including: professional tact and courtesy, and ability to express ideas clearly, creatively, and logically, both orally and in writing.

• Passion, idealism, integrity, positive attitude and mission-driven.

• Experience with computer software and thorough proficiency of Microsoft Office Suite.  Other publishing programs preferred.

• Keen sense of missionary spirit and missionary zeal.

• Must be detail oriented, organized, self-motivated, work well independently and on a team; passion, idealism, integrity, positive attitude, mission-driven and self-directed.

• Must have good critical thinking and problem solving skills.


Travel Requirements:

Travel requirements for the position includes up to 50% local and 5% overnight.

Overview

The Ministry Assistant will be an integral part of both the social and spiritual ministries. This includes, but is not limited to, assisting with creating and running youth programming, assisting with clients' needs, assisting with transportation, and ultimately bridging the gap between social services and showing the love of Jesus Christ to every client encountered. This position will represent The Salvation Army, the church, and social service programs in a professional and caring manner. Additionally, this role will provide direct social services on a once-a-week basis in downtown Pittsburgh as an extension of our social services. They will respond to requests for assistance in a timely manner by completing intake paperwork, determining eligibility, and providing referral services.

Responsibilities

ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS:

  • Assist in planning, preparing, setting up, and implementing all corps ministry programs and activities.
  • Assist with Sunday ministry, adult Bible study/Sunday school, youth discipleship, and program outreach.
  • Prepare and conduct corps programs and activities as assigned by the Corps Officers.
  • Assist with recruiting volunteers and participants for corps programming.
  • Work with Corps Officers and community partners to plan, coordinate, and participate in community events.
  • Encourage participation in and assist with divisional functions and activities.
  • Collaborate with Social Services personnel to connect clients with corps programs, worship opportunities, and other available resources.
  • Provide direct social services one day per week at a designated partner site in downtown Pittsburgh, including completing intake paperwork, determining eligibility, and providing referrals.
  • Assist with client services, answer telephone calls, and respond to requests for assistance in a timely and professional manner.
  • Coordinate transportation for program participants and scheduled activities in collaboration with the Envoy in Charge.
  • Safely transport participants in a 12-passenger van as needed, including picking up and dropping off participants.
  • Assist the Social Worker with summer Allegheny Camps, including participant transportation and related activities.
  • Maintain accurate program statistics and prepare reports as requested.
  • Maintain regular office hours to prepare for programs, activities, and administrative responsibilities.
  • Ensure the safety and well-being of participants during all programs, activities, and services.

ADDITIONAL RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Assist with maintaining clean, organized, and orderly program areas, facilities, grounds, and equipment.
  • Ensure Salvation Army-owned or rented property and equipment are secured, maintained, and kept in good condition.
  • Practice responsible stewardship of Salvation Army facilities, equipment, supplies, and grounds.
  • Maintain receipts and follow required accounting procedures for Salvation Army expenses in accordance with established accounting guidelines.
  • Serve on call when appropriate and as needed.
  • Maintain flexibility to work evenings, weekends, and extended hours during seasonal programming and other high-demand periods.
  • Assist with increased holiday programming and seasonal activities during November and December, Easter activities in April, and summer camp programming and transportation during July and August.

Perform other duties as assigned by the Corps Officers

Qualifications

KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS AND ABILITIES:

 

  • All three PA Clearances required upon employment and thereafter upon renewal date: PA Child Abuse History Clearance, Request for Criminal Record, and Fingerprint based federal criminal history.
  • PA Mandated and Permissive Reporting and The Salvation Army’s KeepSAfe training required.

 

 

EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE:

  • Possess basic knowledge of The Salvation Army, its mission, programs, and services.
  • Demonstrate strong written and verbal communication skills.
  • Possess basic administrative and office skills, including proficiency with Microsoft Office applications.
  • Demonstrate effective organizational, interpersonal, and time-management skills.
  • Ability to work independently and collaboratively with staff, volunteers, clients, and community partners.
  • Demonstrate professionalism, compassion, sound judgment, and a commitment to the mission and values of The Salvation Army.
  • Possess a valid driver's license and the ability to safely transport program participants as required.
  • Maintain all three required Pennsylvania clearances upon employment and thereafter according to applicable renewal requirements: Pennsylvania Child Abuse History Clearance, Pennsylvania State Police Criminal Record Check, and FBI fingerprint-based federal criminal history clearance.
  • Complete required Pennsylvania Mandated and Permissive Reporting training and The Salvation Army's KeepSAfe training.

EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE

  • High school diploma or equivalent required.
  • Experience working in a ministry setting preferred.
  • Previous experience working with children and adults in recreational, educational, or community service settings preferred.

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS

  • Ability to lift and carry objects weighing up to 50 pounds.
  • Ability to bend, reach, stand, walk, and perform other physical activities frequently as required by program and facility responsibilities.
  • Ability to assist with program setup, transportation, camp activities, and facility maintenance.
  • Ability to work evenings, weekends, and extended hours during seasonal programming and other periods of increased activity.
  • Ability to safely operate a 12-passenger van and transport participants as assigned.

post_html:
Licensed and/or Pastoral Counselor - Hoboken Grace Counseling Center
 

We are a dedicated Christian-based private practice seeking compassionate and experienced Licensed Professional Counselors (LPC), Licensed Clinical Social Worker (LCSW), Licensed Marriage and Family Therapist (LMFT) or Certified Pastoral/Christian Counselors to join our team on a part-time per diem basis. Our practice provides comprehensive mental health and faith-based counseling services, integrating psychological principles with Christian values to support the holistic well-being of our clients.

 

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Provide individual, couples, group, and family counseling sessions to a diverse client population.
  • Conduct assessments and develop individualized treatment plans that incorporate both clinical and faith-based approaches.
  • Utilize evidence-based therapeutic techniques to address a range of mental health issues, including anxiety, depression, trauma, and relational difficulties.
  • Maintain accurate and timely documentation of client interactions and progress notes in compliance with state regulations and practice policies.
  • Participate in regular supervision and team meetings to discuss case progress and receive feedback.
  • Collaborate with other counselors, healthcare providers, and community resources to ensure comprehensive care for clients.
  • Engage in continuous professional development to stay current with advancements in counseling practices and faith-based interventions.
  • Uphold the ethical standards and guidelines of the counseling profession and the principles of Christian faith in all client interactions.

23rd October, 2026

THE OPPORTUNITY
The Lead Pastor will serve as Landing Place Church’s primary spiritual, visionary and organizational leader. Working collaboratively with the elders, trustees and staff, this leader will clarify direction, align people and ministries, and turn shared vision into priorities, responsibilities and measurable action.

Landing Place does not envision a Lead Pastor who personally calls every play. The preferred model is closer to a head coach: a leader who establishes direction, develops trusted ministry leaders, delegates meaningful authority and creates the systems and accountability that allow the whole team to flourish. The pastor will remain relationally present and pastorally credible while building a culture in which care and ministry multiply through staff, elders, groups and lay leaders. The new pastor should care intentionally for both the congregation and the staff rather than allowing either relationship to become secondary.

CANDIDATE QUALIFICATIONS
• Mature Christian character. A humble, prayerful and Spirit-led leader with demonstrated integrity, emotional health, self-awareness, teachability and appropriate accountability.
• Compelling biblical communicator. An engaging teacher who handles Scripture faithfully and communicates through memorable ideas, personal authenticity, practical application and a clear invitation to respond.
• Proven organizational leadership. Evidence of leading at meaningful complexity and establishing goals, systems, roles and accountability. Experience in a growing or scaling church is strongly preferred.
• Developer and delegator. A track record of recognizing potential, coaching staff and lay leaders, sharing ministry and building teams that can carry responsibility without unnecessary dependence on the Lead Pastor.
• Relational shepherd. A leader who enjoys people, listens carefully, builds trust across generations and remains genuinely present before and after all three services. This leader will have a shepherd’s heart and a systems mindset rather than attempting to provide every act of care personally.
• Conflict-ready collaborator. Someone who can engage tension early, speak truth with grace, hold others accountable and work through disagreement without avoidance, domination or defensiveness.
• Succession maturity. The patience and confidence to follow a deeply loved pastor, honor existing strengths and develop a distinct leadership voice without reacting against the past.
• Community commitment. A willingness to live in the area, develop relationships throughout Adams County and lead a church that sees collaboration, no-fee community service and local presence as central to its calling.
• Education and experience. A bachelor’s degree is expected. Graduate theological or organizational-leadership education is valued, though demonstrated fruit, leadership growth and ministry effectiveness will carry greater weight than credentials alone.

The Associate Host Team Pastor leads and develops the volunteer team that creates an unforgettable guest experience to open hearts to the truth of God's word.
 
At Life.Church, we exist to lead people to become fully devoted followers of Christ. It’s been our mission since 1996 and has guided us every day. Leading people isn’t just an expectation; it’s a necessity.  It’s a cornerstone of our culture. That's why we’re always seeking leaders—leaders like you—to bring your skills to life. We are one church meeting in multiple locations, and we want to help you become the person God made you to be. 
 
The Host Team is a team of volunteers who help Life.Church feel like a welcoming and comfortable place for people. From the parking lot to the auditorium and every step in between, Host Team volunteers help each person know Life.Church is a place they can attend and, even better, where they can belong.
 
As the Associate Host Team Pastor, you will partner with the lead Host Team Pastor to recruit, develop, and coach volunteer leaders (leaders of leaders) who make the Host Team run every weekend. Your role builds and invests in the volunteers who serve alongside you to create a team people can’t wait to be a part of. In this role, you will also pastor guests who are looking for a home here and lead them into next steps, a spiritual community, and a relationship with God that changes their life.

What You'll Do

  • Cast a compelling, inspiring vision for the Host Team through weekly huddles and ongoing coaching.
  • Recruit, develop, and coach volunteer leaders, honing their leadership skills and investing in their personal and spiritual growth.
  • Empower leaders to own the guest and volunteer experience.
  • Provide pastoral care to guests and volunteers, helping people find a home at Life.Church.
  • Build community and connection among the team, discipling volunteers toward spiritual, relational, and missional growth.
  • Set clear expectations and coach the team to consistently deliver hospitality with excellence that inspires others.
  • Onboard new volunteers and guide them from their first serving experience through ongoing development.

Skills Needed to Succeed

  • A passion for the guest experience, customer service, and hospitality.
  • Ability to inspire and coach teams toward a shared vision.
  • Strong relational and communication skills with a diverse range of people.
  • Effective at time management and following through on commitments.
  • Effective management of systems and operations that provide safety and support for guests and volunteers.
  • Self-motivated with the ability to make independent decisions.
  • Drive and flexibility to thrive in a fast-paced and dynamic environment.
  • High School Diploma or GED.
At Life.Church, we are passionate about reaching more people in more communities. We hire new team members to begin their journey at an existing Life.Church location so they can learn the culture and systems of our church from experienced pastors already on the team. Our hope is, as we continue to launch new locations, we can send pastors who are ready to lead on day one because of what they’ve learned at an existing location in preparation.  
 
Check out the list of current locations and the cities we’re exploring or considering for future locations. We’d love to discuss which locations you are interested in.

Benefits We Offer

  • Paid parental leave, including maternity, paternity, and adoption leave.
  • Generous employer-paid leave for the use of vacation, sick time, and other qualifying reasons. 
  • Innovative and comprehensive Medical, Dental, and Vision insurance that provides team members with useful resources and savings to navigate their holistic health. 
  • Life insurance policy provided for all staff members at 2x annual salary at no cost. Additional life insurance coverage is available to purchase. 
  • Short-Term and Long-Term disability is covered at 100% for full-time qualified staff members.
  • Comprehensive wellness and mental health benefits allow staff to proactively invest in their physical and emotional health.
  • Generous 401(k) retirement plan allowing a team member to have up to 12.5% (including employee contribution, employer match, and employer discretionary contribution) contributed into their account in their first year. It doesn’t stop there—the more years on staff, the greater the investment! 
  • $160 annually in development dollars for team members to invest in their professional growth. 
  • Casual dress and work environment.
  • And much more!
 

Our Beliefs, Culture, and Commitment to Diversity

At Life.Church, every staff member, and intern is a minister and is expected to engage in the church's ministry fully. We consider ministry readiness and an individual’s capacity to represent Life.Church’s beliefs as a minister during the selection process for all staff and intern positions. An essential function within every position held by a staff member or intern at Life.Church is to uphold and represent the beliefs of Life.Church. Learn more about what we believe at Life.Church. 
 
While we unite around our mission, we know unity doesn’t mean uniformity. Our calling is too great, and our mission is too important not to be intentional about strengthening our team through diversity. We know that diverse perspectives in race, ethnicity, background, age, and gender are essential to reaching the world for Christ. To learn more about how we strengthen our team through diversity, visit our careers page.

Position Summary

That Neighborhood Church (TNC) seeks a spiritually mature, relationally gifted, and mission-minded Senior Pastor to lead the church into its next season. Building on fifteen years of trusted ministry in North Toledo, the Senior Pastor will provide biblical teaching, pastoral care, organizational leadership, community engagement, and partnership development that strengthen TNC's spiritual health, neighborhood impact, and long-term sustainability.

This is more than a Sunday preaching role. The Senior Pastor is expected to become part of neighborhood life, relate meaningfully across racial, economic, educational, and spiritual backgrounds, develop leaders, cultivate ministry and financial partners, and help people encounter the transforming love of Jesus.

Ministry Context

TNC exists to love God, love people, and prove it through action. The church serves neighborhood residents and families, many facing poverty or instability; participants in the nearby Volunteers of America (VOA) re-entry program; and people from surrounding communities who worship and serve alongside them. TNC also ministers to neighborhood children through an after-school program and weekly Kids Church, often reaching children whose parents do not attend Sunday services.

Core Responsibilities

Spiritual Leadership, Preaching, and Discipleship

  • Serve as the congregation's primary spiritual leader and shepherd, leading through prayer, dependence on the Holy Spirit, and obedience to God's Word.
  • Prepare and deliver Gospel-centered, biblically faithful, practical messages accessible to people from varied backgrounds.
  • Keep reaching people who do not yet know Jesus central to TNC's mission, while building clear pathways for salvation, discipleship, service, and leadership.
  • Equip members to share their faith, disciple others, and use their gifts; oversee baptisms, communion, weddings, funerals, and other pastoral responsibilities.

Pastoral Care and Relational Ministry

  • Provide compassionate pastoral care, spiritual guidance, prayer, and crisis support, especially for people navigating re-entry, addiction recovery, poverty, trauma, grief, family instability, or church hurt.
  • Build trust through consistent presence, patient listening, healthy boundaries, and appropriate referrals to professional or community resources.
  • Cultivate a church culture of grace and truth, dignity and accountability, restoration and hope.

Vision, Staff, and Organizational Leadership

  • Work with church leaders, staff, and ministry leaders to clarify and communicate vision, priorities, measurable goals, and sustainable ministry systems.
  • Honor TNC's history and founding mission while guiding the congregation through transition and necessary change.
  • Work with the Elders, Lead team, and staff to develop a clear vision for the future of TNC.
  • Promote healthy communication, cooperation, unity, financial stewardship, transparency, and accountability.

Children's, Re-entry, and Community Ministries

  • Champion ministry to neighborhood children as central to TNC's mission; support after-school and Kids Church staff, pursue relationships with parents and caregivers, and ensure child-safety practices are followed.
  • Strengthen TNC's relationship with the VOA re-entry program and develop relevant worship, discipleship, mentoring, and pastoral-care opportunities for people rebuilding their lives after incarceration.
  • Maintain a visible, relational presence in the neighborhood and identify practical ways the church can respond to community needs.

Partnership Development and Financial Sustainability

  • Treat partnership development as an ongoing pastoral and organizational responsibility essential to TNC's mission and sustainability.
  • Build, strengthen, and steward relationships with churches, donors, businesses, schools, nonprofits, civic leaders, foundations, ministry partners, and other supporters.
  • Regularly communicate TNC's vision, needs, stories, and measurable impact through personal meetings, church visits, written updates, presentations, and other appropriate channels.
  • Invite partners to pray, serve, give, advocate, and collaborate; develop new sources of financial and in-kind support while faithfully caring for existing relationships.
  • Work with church leadership to develop and oversee a responsible annual budget, encourage biblical generosity, and evaluate partnership and revenue-development goals.

Leadership Character and Qualifications

  • A deep and growing relationship with Jesus Christ and alignment with TNC's statement of faith, mission, values, and ministry approach.
  • Biblical qualifications for pastoral leadership as described in 1 Timothy 3:1-7, Titus 1:5-9, and 1 Peter 5:1-4.
  • Integrity, humility, emotional maturity, relational warmth, courage, strong listening skills, and a servant's willingness to participate in everyday ministry.
  • Several years of pastoral or significant ministry leadership, including clear biblical preaching, staff or team leadership, volunteer development, and mentoring.
  • Demonstrated ability to serve across diverse backgrounds and build trust with people affected by poverty, addiction, incarceration, rejection, trauma, or institutional failure.
  • Experience developing partnerships and financial support through churches, nonprofits, community organizations, businesses, donors, or foundations.
  • Formal theological education through a Bible college, seminary, denominational program, or an equivalent combination of training and ministry experience.
  • Willingness to complete required background checks.

First-Season Priorities

  • Build trust with the congregation, staff, volunteers, neighbors, VOA participants, partners, donors, and supporters.
  • Build a healthy transition relationship with the founding pastor and church leaders; learn TNC's history, culture, strengths, and challenges before making major changes.
  • Create a partnership plan covering communication, outreach, financial goals, and leadership reporting.
  • Help church leaders set a focused, sustainable vision for TNC's next season.

The Opportunity

The next Senior Pastor will inherit a strong foundation, trusted community relationships, established ministries, and a congregation committed to demonstrating the love of Jesus in practical ways. TNC seeks a leader who will honor that foundation, embrace its neighborhood-centered calling, strengthen its people and partnerships, and lead the mission toward a healthy and sustainable future.

To be considered for this position, please complete the application to include your testimony, resume and other background information related to the position.

If the district office has reviewed your application and they think you may be a potential match for the position, that the hiring manager will reach out to you for next steps.

This position requires licensing with The Christian & Missionary Alliance. To learn more about The Alliance and requirements for licensing, please visit our website

Please do not contact the church directly.

Worship Leader - Mt. Vernon Baptist Church
 

WORSHIP LEADER JOB DESCRIPTION

Position Summary

The Worship Leader is responsible for planning, coordinating, and leading contemporary worship services and music ministries of the church, including the Adult Worship Team and Youth Praise Team. This individual plays a vital leadership role in the spiritual life of the church and is expected to demonstrate a clear, God-ordained calling to worship ministry, seeking God’s guidance in all decisions and leadership responsibilities.

Accountability & Relationships

The Worship Leader will be under the direct supervision of the Senior Pastor and Personnel Committee with indirect supervision from the Deacons. The Worship Leader is ultimately responsible to the church body and will be a member of the Vision Team. Scheduled meetings with the Senior Pastor for input, scheduling, feedback, and planning are expected, as well as regular meetings with the Vision Team, Worship Team, and Youth Praise Team to plan and coordinate their assistance in ministry.  

Key Responsibilities

Worship Leadership & Planning

  • Plan and lead Christ-centered contemporary worship services that support the church’s mission and vision

  • Prepare and distribute the weekly order of service to pastors and the bulletin coordinator by Wednesday morning

  • Plan and schedule volunteers for worship services using Planning Center, PraiseCharts, Multitracks/Playback, and ProPresenter

  • Remain current with contemporary worship music and trends, introducing new music regularly (at least one new song every 6–8 weeks)

  • Coordinate the Youth Praise Team to lead Sunday morning worship an average of 1–2 times per quarter

  • Conduct and/or coordinate weekly rehearsals for the Adult Worship Team and Youth Praise Team

  • Distribute music and rehearsal materials at least one week in advance

  • Foster a positive, encouraging, and growth-oriented rehearsal environment

  • Actively recruit and develop volunteers for worship and music ministries

  • Coordinate leadership for VBS music and other seasonal programs

Ministry Collaboration & Outreach

  • Support worship and music needs for church ministries and events, including (but not limited to):

    • Kids Praise

    • Vacation Bible School (VBS)

    • Base Camp

    • Summit Kids

    • Youth events

    • Block parties and outreach events

    • Funerals

    • Weddings

  • Plan and participate in worship-centered outreach events designed to reach the unchurched and strengthen believers

Administration 

  • Promote music and worship ministry activities through church announcements, bulletin, website, social media, and other communication channels

  • Coordinate facility use for worship and music activities through the church calendar

  • Prepare and submit worship and music-related budget information to the Finance Team

  • Prepare a monthly worship calendar including Sunday morning, Wednesday evening, and special services, etc

Technical & Facility Responsibilities

  • Coordinate preparation of lyric and sermon slides using ProPresenter for Sunday morning, Sunday night, and Wednesday night services

  • Be present at the church at least 30 minutes prior to worship services and practices and  remain at least 30 minutes afterward to secure the building

General Expectations

  • The Worship Leader and family will be expected to become active members of the church body and participate in church services, activities, and outreach

  • Once worship plans are approved, the Worship Leader is empowered to implement them with the support of the Worship Team

  • Perform additional duties as needed to support the overall ministry of the church

Time Commitment

  • Expected to devote 40 hours per week on-site to ministry responsibilities

  • Weekly hours may include planning, preparation, rehearsals, meetings, and worship services

  • Workload may vary week to week depending on ministry needs

Compensation & Benefits

  • Weekly salary based on experience

  • Vacation Days: 2 weeks annually

  • Sick Leave: Up to 4 compensated sick days per year
