Job Title

Donor & Ministry Services Coordinator

Location

USA - Florida - Orlando - Wycliffe USA Headquarters

 

Job Description Summary

At Wycliffe Bible Translators, your work is more than just a job. As a Donor & Ministry Services Coordinator, you’ll be responsible for providing personalized care to donors, supporting staff with resource requests and responding to inquiries from those seeking information about Wycliffe and the work of Bible translation. You’ll serve on the frontlines of customer care, providing responsive support by phone and email while maintaining knowledge of Wycliffe’s programs and resources, donation records and processes, the website and supporting databases, and organizational messaging.

Your contributions will play a pivotal role in creating a warm and meaningful experience for donors and others who connect with Wycliffe. Through every interaction, you’ll communicate gratitude and care with warmth and professionalism, offer prayer when appropriate and share the mission and vision of Bible translation with enthusiasm. Working within the Communications department, you’ll help those we serve feel valued, supported and meaningfully connected to Wycliffe and the work of Bible translation.

You’ll partner with Communications leadership and other team members to:
- Support and enhance internal communication across departments, among staff and on behalf of executive leadership
- Serve donors, partners, colleagues and the public through shaping and safeguarding messaging, responding to inquiries and providing resources
- Align external messaging across Wycliffe Bible Translators for unified, cohesive and clear communication

Job Description

Overview of Team

The Communications team at Wycliffe Bible Translators works to ensure that internal and external communication efforts are clear, resonant and accurate, advancing not only the objectives of the organization’s various teams but also the mission of Bible translation as a whole. To this end, the Communications team partners with leaders across Wycliffe regarding messaging, strategy and information, ultimately serving under the leadership of the Chief of Staff and Strategy in the Offices of the President.


Responsibilities

You’ll make an impact as you:

  • Faithfully and regularly pray for the ongoing work of Bible translation and for people from around the world to experience transformation.
  • Act as an organizational representative presenting the global ministry of Wycliffe and encouraging interested individuals, organizations and churches to participate in the work of Bible translation.
  • Serve both internal and external constituents with a warm, solution-oriented and caring approach by phone and email.
  • Process donations and answer inquiries by phone in a shared communications workspace, while handling financial information in compliance with all applicable regulations and industry best practices.
  • Create and manage donor records and track activity in the designated customer relationship management (CRM) system, Salesforce, with accuracy and attention to detail.
  • Connect staff to the correct team or resource at Wycliffe using the provided tools and contact list.
  • Work across various web-based applications and databases to synthesize information and serve constituents.
  • Correctly identify during an active call a constituent’s needs, whether stated or unstated, and determine the appropriate action or best solution.
  • Follow up with constituents as needed to clarify information or confirm resolution.
  • Maintain the team’s knowledge base and stay up to date on organizational news and messaging.
  • Share about Bible translation and the organization with confidence, enthusiasm and accuracy.
  • Adhere to guidelines and restrictions related to providing personnel, project or partner information.
  • Assist donors, staff and others with website inquiries and features, providing on-the-spot training and tips as needed.
  • Monitor multiple email inboxes for messages from the public, donors, partners and staff, answering questions and connecting people with resources while following best practices and brand guidelines for written communications.
  • Call and/or write to new donors to express sincere appreciation.
  • Encourage and pray with constituents over the phone when appropriate.
  • Provide annual giving statements, duplicate receipts and other documentation as requested.
  • Creatively identify where improvements to procedures or services can be made.
  • Participate in training and improvement opportunities, team devotional and prayer times, and corporate events.
  • Perform other duties as assigned by the Customer Care Manager.
  • Other Requirements:
    • Adjust work schedule as needed to accommodate meetings across time zones.
    • Ensure access to a strong, reliable internet and phone connection.
    • Be available to work occasional evenings to support high-volume giving seasons.

Minimum Skill Sets

The requirements listed below represent the knowledge, skills and/or abilities necessary to perform each duty satisfactorily. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the following essential functions:

  • Spiritual Bona Fide Occupational Qualification (BFOQ): Demonstrates desire and ability to support corporate biblical and religious goals and participate in regular work-related spiritual activities without reservation as evidenced by your active participation and willingness to pray with and for others; be a consistent witness for Jesus Christ, maintaining a courteous, Christ-like attitude in all verbal and written, internal and external professional communications.
  • Humility: Works well within a team by demonstrating Christ-like maturity and humility that gives appropriate credit to others where it is due. Willing to take ownership of shortcomings and faults, admit and own mistakes, receive correction or exhortation and remain teachable with a willingness to learn and grow.
  • Serving Others: Works well with people, focusing on solving conflict using biblical principles, listening well to others, using emotional intelligence and developing God-honoring relationships. Accepts feedback and responsibility for own actions and follows through on commitments. Promotes positive people skills and service focus among staff by establishing customer service standards, training staff, monitoring customer satisfaction and maintaining healthy working relationships.
  • Customer Focus: Enthusiastic about providing high-quality customer service. Committed to high-quality work and prompt attention to the delivery of results.
  • Communication: Exceptional verbal and written communication skills with the ability to articulate information clearly, listen closely, request clarification when needed and respond well to questions. Writes clearly and informatively and edits work for spelling and grammar, while adhering to Wycliffe’s brand and messaging guidelines.
  • Problem Solving: Exceptional analytical and problem-solving skills, with accuracy and attention to detail. Demonstrates good judgment with strong decision-making skills.
  • Adaptability: Adapts to changes in the work environment, including working with diverse individuals or groups. Modifies approach or methods to fit the situation. Remains flexible and composed when facing frequent change, delays or unexpected events.
  • Information Management & Confidentiality: Uses appropriate procedures to collect, organize, retrieve, maintain, and disseminate information. Has good judgment about what information is important and what is not, the level of confidentiality, and what should be communicated, how, to whom and when. Handles confidential information responsibly to maintain the trust of internal and external customers. Maintains communications and information confidential as per applicable laws, ethical guidelines and instructions.
  • Relationship Building: Effective at relationship-building with the ability to partner effectively with colleagues within and beyond the department, as well as with global staff. Works comfortably in both mono- or cross-cultural situations, winning cooperation through awareness and sensitivity to people's needs.
  • Results-Driven: Able to work autonomously and make independent decisions. High-energy self-starter, driven to achieve results. Seizes opportunities to enhance organizational performance.
  • Technical Skills:
    • Proficient in programs such as Google Suite Workspace (Mail, Calendar, Sheets, Docs, Drive, Slides, etc.) and video conferencing software such as Zoom.
    • Familiar with WordPress, Workday HCM and Salesforce CRM.

Education & Experience

  • Associate’s degree plus 1- 3 years of experience; or an equivalent combination of education, training and/or experience.
  • Experience in customer service, donor support, data coordination and/or a call center environment preferred.

Spiritual and Personal Commitments

As a religious organization and employer, Wycliffe is permitted to and does make employment decisions on the basis of religion, biblical standards and our religious beliefs. You’ll be asked to:

  • Demonstrate a personal commitment to Jesus Christ, as evidenced by your personal testimony.
  • Identify with and participate in a church and proactively seek to grow your faith in Christ.
  • Establish and maintain a team of prayer partners who will support you in your season of ministry at Wycliffe (minimum 3-5 partners).
  • Actively participate in corporate prayer and devotional times.
  • Maintain an exemplary standard of biblical ethics, behavior and conduct within Wycliffe and in your public and private life outside of Wycliffe.
  • Agree to abide by Wycliffe’s ethics, behavior and conduct standards at all times.
  • Demonstrate Christ-like maturity in all interactions as displayed by good judgment based on biblical values and principles.
  • Actively incorporate your faith in Christ, as well as Wycliffe’s beliefs and core values, in all aspects of your daily work.
  • Guided by your faith in Christ, demonstrate these core competencies in daily work and interactions:
    • Faithful in following Christ. (See John 8:31-32, Prov. 3:5-6.) Follow Christ faithfully, allowing Scripture to guide decisions, and continually grow in relationship with God and His people.
    • Intentional in collaboration with humility. (See 1 Cor. 3:5-9, Col. 3:12.) Collaborate intentionally to accomplish work goals, demonstrating a commitment to cross-departmental, inter-organizational and cross-cultural teamwork.
    • Agile in learning. (See Prov. 1:5, Phil. 1:9-10.) Demonstrate a dedication to personal and professional growth within a culture that values continuous learning, individually and collectively.
    • Excellent in stewardship. (See 1 Cor. 4:2, 1 Peter. 4:10.) Participate in God’s work, stewarding His resources responsibly with urgency and excellence.
    • Proactive in discernment. (See John 5:17, 19; Matt. 6:33.) Seek to discern where and how God is at work. Align our efforts with His purposes.

Benefits

We offer a comprehensive benefits package including:

  • Medical, dental, vision and life insurance options for employees and their eligible dependents.
  • Health Savings Account (HSA) and Flexible Spending Account (FSA).
  • 403b retirement savings account with matching.
  • Paid time off with up to a max of 10 vacation days in the first year of employment (based on hours worked).
  • Paid sick time off up to 8 hours per month (based on hours worked).
  • 10+ paid holidays.
  • Short-term disability pay.

We also offer regular spiritual development, worship, prayer, community gatherings and connection opportunities for all staff in all locations. Detailed information per position is available upon request


Compensation

The hiring pay range for this position is $17.84 - $19.88. The range for this position is based upon and considers Wycliffe's non-profit ministry environment. Actual pay rate may be higher based on various factors suck as qualifications, skills and experience, required training, licensure and/or certifications, budget, and allocation, if applicable.


About Wycliffe Bible Translators

For over 80 years Wycliffe Bible Translators, Inc. has been committed to ensuring that people “from every nation, tribe, people and language” (Revelation 7:9) have access to God’s Word in a language and format they can clearly understand. We believe that accurate, clear and natural translations of the Bible in accessible formats lead to people entering into life-transforming relationships with God.

Wycliffe is a catalyst in the global Bible translation movement, engaging with thousands of partners around the world to collaboratively carry out this work.

Wycliffe’s vision is that people from every language will understand the Bible and be transformed. Our mission is to serve with the global body of Christ to advance Bible translation so people can encounter God through His Word.

Wycliffe is a distinctly Christian community where you can flourish by using your God-given talents and abilities to serve and support the ministry of Bible translation. Your employment with Wycliffe is not merely a vocation; it is responding and making a commitment to actively participate in what He’s doing around the world. Your faith, prayers, skills and experiences are foundational as you contribute to and witness God’s Word impacting people around the world. This is a once-in-eternity opportunity!

We believe the Bible is the inspired Word of God and is completely trustworthy, speaking with supreme authority in all matters of belief and practice. Wycliffe’s beliefs and core values can be found here. An exemplary standard of ethics, behavior and conduct that reflects biblical principles is lived out by all staff. As active partners in fulfilling the Great Commission, Wycliffe staff embrace and adhere to these beliefs and values, which are essential to fulfilling Wycliffe’s Bible translation mission.

Prayer undergirds Bible translation and is foundational to Wycliffe’s work culture. Our work atmosphere provides numerous opportunities, individually and corporately, to actively live out your faith in Jesus Christ as you work heartily as to the Lord.

Come use your God-given gifts and contribute to what God is doing around the world through Bible translation!

Campus Staff Minister - North Dakota (Graduate & Faculty Ministry)

Work Location:

North Dakota

Job Type:

Full time

God has called InterVarsity to plant and to build witnessing communities of students and faculty who follow Jesus on college and university campuses. Through these groups, we believe ever- increasing numbers of students and faculty from all ethnic groups and areas of the campus will be transformed by the Gospel. We expect to see campuses increasingly become places where people, ideas, and structures flourish to the glory of God. We confidently anticipate that our InterVarsity alumni will become change agents across the country and around the world. We pursue this calling by discerning and actively participating in what God is already doing on campus. This is the essence of being a Campus Staff Minister (CSM).

Please submit the GFM Interest Form before completing the full application for a position with Graduate & Faculty Ministries in our online system. We will contact you when we are ready to proceed with the application process.​ 

This position is open to applicants working less than 40 hours/week. If you are interested in part-time work please apply for this position.  Additional pay (as a geographic adjustment) is available in high cost of living areas.

The pay range listed is for an employee working 40 hours/week at CSM level II. Pay will be prorated for employees who work less than 40 hours/week. 

Volunteer opportunities range from prayer and hospitality to leading a campus fellowship of graduate students and faculty. People who are interested in volunteering will go through an application and interview process, however, volunteer openings are not posted at the job opportunities link above. For more information, talk with a local InterVarsity staff or staff director.

We have positions in the following locations:

  • Work with Faculty on Multiple Campuses

  • North Dakota State University - Faculty

  • North Dakota State University - Graduate Students

  • University of North Dakota - Faculty

  • University of North Dakota - Graduate Students

ESSENTIAL COMMITMENTS/RESPONSIBILITIES 

Spiritual Growth 

You pursue maturity as a disciple of Jesus Christ so that your life and work increasingly reflects a growing love for God, God’s Word, God’s people of every ethnicity and culture, and God’s purposes in the world. To do this, you will: 

  • Pursue a vibrant relationship with the triune God through engagement with Scripture, prayer, and worship, both individually and in community 

  • Develop self-leadership (growing in self-awareness, self-management, relational integrity, and resiliency) 

  • Embrace Scriptural standards for behavior and attitudes 

 

Campus Leadership 

You communicate and model InterVarsity’s vision to see students and faculty transformed, campuses renewed and world changers developed 

  • Create a culture of humble dependence on God and bold expectation in God’s intention to start new witnessing communities throughout the campus and on new campuses 

  • Model – in person and through programs – InterVarsity’s vision and Core Values, including a biblically-defined commitment to engage every ethnic and social group on campus 

  • Lead students and faculty – individually and collectively – through Scripture, prayer, teaching, and discipleship experiences, so that they articulate and align their ministry activities around this vision 

  • Set annual goals through prayer, research and reflection with your teams (students, faculty, and staff) for qualitative and quantitative growth, including conversions and leadership development 

 

You create, develop, align and leverage ministry plans, programs, teams, and structures to close the gap between current reality and the aspirational goals. 

  • Build leadership teams who trust and partner well with you and who demonstrate spiritual vitality, relational health, and mission alignment 

  • Develop and execute plans to achieve annual goals, evaluating and modifying the plan as needed throughout the year 

  • Increase momentum for the vision by aligning programs, structures, conferences and teams around the goals 

  • Mobilize students and faculty to engage their relational networks with the gospel and to start new missional communities 

  • Under the direction of the Area Director, may supervise Ministry Interns and Campus Ministry Interns as delegated 

 

You intentionally gather, invite, and develop diverse groups of students and faculty so that they not only encounter and follow Jesus as Savior and Lord but also advance the mission on campus as participants and leaders. 

  • Create ways for faculty and students to encounter and follow Jesus through Scripture, worship, prayer, mission experiences, conferences, etc. 

  • Equip students and faculty so that they think strategically about campus engagement and so that they proclaim – in word, deed, and power – the good news of Jesus, regularly inviting students and faculty to follow him as Savior and Lord 

  • Disciple students and faculty by equipping them to hear the Word, respond actively, and debrief and interpret the experience so that they grow in Christlikeness, reflect our Core Values, and develop ministry skills 

  • Invite, coach, and equip students and faculty to become increasingly effective participants and leaders, including starting new witnessing communities on campuses

Program Outline

A Season of Development for a Lifetime of Ministry

The Two Cities Residency is a purposeful, two-year leadership track designed to provide an open door into vocational ministry. Residents serve as integral members of our staff team, gaining hands-on experience and professional mentorship while leading in one of our core ministry tracks, including College, Missions, Worship Production, Student, Kids, Connections, Creative Communications, and Discipleship and Groups. Our vision is to prepare and launch men and women with holistic clarity about how the Lord has equipped them for ministry, focusing on the key pillars of theology, leadership, and character.

Debt-Free Theological Training

We believe in investing deeply in the leaders of tomorrow, which is why we provide a fully-funded academic pathway for our residents. While serving at Two Cities, you will earn a Master of Arts in Christian Ministry from Southeastern Baptist Theological Seminary (SEBTS) with all tuition costs covered by the church. This mentored program allows you t0 apply your seminary studies in a real-world context alongside your cohort.

Real Responsibility and Kingdom Impact

At Two Cities, you won’t just observe ministry; you will lead ministries and manage teams. Whether you are coordinating local outreach, leading community groups, or owning significant projects, you will leave this residency with a proven track record of success and a world-class degree. As a member of our dynamic staff, you will also be connected to the broader Summit Collaborative, gaining access to a national network of church planters and missionaries. We are looking for individuals hungry to grow and with a heart for the Great Commission who are ready to be shepherded well and deployed for the Kingdom.

Job Description

The average time spent per week will be around 40 hours. We do want to ensure that residents are taking two days off to rest each week.

  • Theological/Personal Development: 5-7 hours per week
  • Staff Meetings and Staff Training: 2-3 hours per week
  • Ministry Track: 20 -25 hours per week
  • Administration & Support Raising: 1 hour per week
  • Sunday Services: 7 hours per week (available to serve different ministries)

Next Steps

Click on "Apply to Position" to show your interest. Following an initial screening, we will send you the rest of the application to move forward.

Castlewood Alliance Church - Pastor Job Description

  • Qualifications
    • The pastor must have a genuine conviction that he has been called by God; and be Spirit-filled and Spirit-guided. He should possess the following characteristics; be above reproach, faithful to his wife, temperate, self-controlled, respectable, hospitable, and sincere, studious, sympathetic.
    • Should possess adequate education acceptable by Alliance standards. Must be licensed and ordained or studying for ordination for the C&MA.
  • Overall Purpose of This Position
    • To have oversight of the church in conjunction with the elders, governing board, and ministry leaders. To lead spiritual development of the congregation and to foster its commitment to Jesus Christ as described in the Word of God; to guide and participate in methods to increase membership; and to guide and support religious, social and administrative activities of the church.
  • Areas of Responsibility
    • Preaching and teaching
      • Preach at regular worship services, and conduct special services as needed. (i.e. funerals, weddings, baptisms, Easter, Christmas, etc.)
      • Have a vital relationship to the youth, acting in conjunction with the youth ministry leaders.
      • Promote or conduct membership awareness classes.
      • Have general oversight of the entire Sunday School program alongside the Christian Education Director, including leadership training and the directing of evangelism - serve as a resource to Sunday School as needed.
      • Act as a resource for standing and special committees of the church; lead committee meetings as appropriate (of which he is a member ex-officio).
    • Visitation and Counseling
      • Provide pastoral care in conjunction with the elders to members and adherents of this church through regular visitation and other special needs, i.e. communion to shut-ins, plan and carry out regular scheduled visitation to ensure coverage of attending and non-attending members; be available for and provide counseling to those needing help.
      • Participate in planning visits with prospective members; and visit these families to acquaint with the church.
      • Conduct pre-marital counseling for those wishing to be married.
    • Other Duties
      • Oversee the nominating Committee for church officers and Sunday School
      • Participate as appropriate in such church-related activities as fellowship dinners, Alliance Men's breakfast, etc.
      • Participate as appropriate in community and professional activities as means of representing the church to the community.
      • Participate in committees, camps, etc as requested by the Alliance.
      • Supervise and direct administrative functions such as those relating to the use and maintenance of the building and property as delegated to the church trustees; publishing church bulletin, correspondence, files, inventories, etc., as assigned to the church secretary.
      • Serve as chairman of Governing Board.
      • Participate in General Council and Annual Prayer Conference.
    • Self-development
      • Being sensitive to the Holy Spirit's leading, set goals for self-development; and engage in study, seminars, and other activities designed to assist in meeting these goals.
      • Use allotted vacation time.
      • Be transparent with elders and church leaders, and use qualified elders to assist in administrative and ministry duties as needed.

Vision for the Future

“See, I am doing a new thing. . . do you not perceive it?” Isaiah 43:19

We believe God has good things in store for Castlewood Alliance! Our vision for the future begins with Him, and His plans for His church. We seek His guidance and pray for His will at Castlewood. It is our heart’s desire to glorify Him in everything we do. We want to continue preaching and teaching the Word of God, because we believe it is the ultimate authority and that it is absolute truth. Through spreading the gospel by the sharing of the Word, we want to see the church continue to grow both spiritually and in number, and welcome more new families into our body of believers.

Our youth ministries are at the heart of Castlewood. We desire to see children come to Jesus at the earliest age they are able to understand their need of Him as their Savior. We love our children and teens, and want to see the youth grow more engaged through our AWANA program and Christ-centered activities, equipping them to stand for Christ in today’s world. We also want to see the parents of the children get plugged in, giving us a better connection with them, so that we can minister to each one and begin to disciple them. A possibility might be to offer discipleship classes for the parents while their children are at AWANA meetings, or having counseling available for those who would be interested in talking with someone.

As our numbers grow, we would like to expand and build onto the church. If the Lord wills, in the future we have plans to build a gymnasium/all-purpose facility that could allow more space and opportunities for ministry, especially considering the growing number of youth that we have in the church. The building could be used for AWANA games, Vacation Bible School, athletic and fitness programs, community outreach programs, youth events, concerts, holiday gatherings, and so many other possibilities. Our hope is to allow more room in the future for other areas that we are quickly outgrowing as well, such as the nursery and the current fellowship hall.

We believe in the power of prayer. “The prayer of a righteous man is powerful and effective.” (James 5:16) We want our human desires to align with God’s will, relying on His active power rather than on our human strength. For this reason, we would like to see Wednesday prayer meetings revived (or restructured) and our prayer chain revamped, to allow for more of our church family to be actively involved in prayer.

We would like to offer more discipleship opportunities outside of the church. One way we may do this would be to encourage mentoring through our men’s and women’s ministries. (Titus 2) We want to live life together in and out of the church building, leading by example in our day to day activities.

We want to connect with those in the community through service projects and ministries. Through more connection, we hope to see more diversity in those who join our congregation, opening our doors to new believers from different ethnicities and backgrounds, and providing an increasingly vibrant reflection of the true body of Christ.

We want to make a positive impact on the community around us, sharing the love of Christ, and spreading the four fold gospel message of Jesus as our Savior, Sanctifier, Healer, and Coming King!

Foundational Values – “Who We Are”

We are a small part of Christ’s bride who seek to know Him more, love Him more, and make Him known. We seek to make much of Christ, His word and His gospel in all we do. We believe this is the only means to save and transform souls.

We seek to love one another fervently and to out-do one another in showing honor. We desire unity in the Spirit under the authority of Scripture. We desire to submit to one another in love as we submit to Christ.

We believe the Holy Spirit uses the ordinary means of grace to nourish, strengthen and reveal all the benefits won by Christ to the saints. Therefore, our gatherings revolve around the ministry of the Word; faithful reading, preaching, prayer, and the sacraments of baptism and the Lord’s supper. We gather to worship Christ and serve Him in obedience.

We are committed to the great commission to make disciples of Christ and see all walking in a manner worthy of the calling to which we were called. We want to equip the saints for the work of ministry and build up the body of Christ into maturity and into the fullness of Christ.

We are committed to drawing out the spiritual gifts in every saint and creating an environment where they can use their gifts for the edification and encouragement of the whole body. We will love, serve, evangelize and bless our community and those we encounter.

We believe that this is all accomplished by the faithful proclamation of the Word, as the Spirit is pleased to move in and through us. Above all, let everything we do be done for the glory of God alone!

Castlewood Alliance Leadership

Some have been given the ministry gift of administration with unique abilities to lead others, as one who “leads, with diligence”. (Romans 12:8) We believe Christian leadership should be exercised by those who are “full of the Holy Spirit and wisdom” (Acts 6:3), who also reflect the qualities required for deacon or elder leadership. Those who have the spiritual gift of leadership will plan for the future and will do so as servant leaders.

At Castlewood, Jesus Christ is our Great Shepherd, and the pastor is the caregiver and protector of the flock. He is the “under shepherd” of the Great Shepherd Himself, the Lord Jesus Christ. (1 Peter 5:1-4) It is his charge and responsibility through the calling of the Holy Spirit upon him, to teach, edify and equip God’s children. We respect the pastor’s headship over all the workings and ministries of the church. His leadership is supported by the elders and the governing board, along with all the individual ministry officers of the church.

We have an elder board consisting of four elders. They support the pastor and our church through the following: meeting for prayer with the pastor before Sunday morning services, leading mid-week prayer meetings, bible studies and Sunday School classes, visiting or calling members of our congregation when in the hospital or shut in at home, serving communion alongside the pastor during worship services, anointing and praying for those in need of healing, helping with baptismal services, serving on the church governing board, handling the distribution of benevolence funds in confidentiality, attending elder board meetings and retreats with the pastor, interviewing new members, filling the pulpit as needed when the pastor is on vacation or unable to preach, and being available for anyone who may need counseling.

Our Church Governing Board (which is an elder majority board) consists of the pastor, the four church elders, the board secretary, the church treasurer, and two board members at large. The pastor holds the position of Head Chairman, and a Vice Chairman is chosen from among the four elders. The board members meet at least once per month to make decisions regarding the ministries, events, building projects, maintenance of the church and parsonage, budget, and spending. Everyone serving on the board must be a member of the church.

We also have a missionary/assistant treasurer, Christian Education Director, three trustees, and six deaconesses.

The ministry positions of the church are: Pianists (2); Organists (2); Head Greeter/Usher; Seaters/Greeters (21); Sound Techs (2); Prayer Coordinator; VBS Director; Men’s Director; Women’s Director; Social Media Specialist; Church Auditors (3)

The positions for church officers are filled by the Nominating Committee which is led by the pastor and consists of two members elected by the Governing Board and two members elected by the congregation each year.

Castlewood Alliance Church Overview

Church Attendance

  • Sunday morning worship services, average between 160-170
  • Sunday school - average between 50-70

Services

  • Sunday school at 9:30am
    • Offered for all ages
  • Sunday morning worship service 10:30am (livestream available weekly online)
  • Wednesday night prayer meeting at 6:00pm (includes a brief devotional led by the pastor or one of the elders, followed by corporate prayer time)

Ministries

  • In addition to our Sunday School classes and Sunday morning worship service, there are several other ministries going on in the church. These include:
    • Children’s Church and Toddler Church - offered during Sunday worship services for ages Pre-K to 2nd grade
    • AWANA on Sunday evenings from September through May
    • Vacation Bible School in the summer (usually in June or July for 4-5 days)
    • Women’s weekly bible study on Tuesday mornings
    • Wednesday night prayer meeting 6pm -7pm
    • Small groups in the summer months (usually meet once a week June-Aug)
    • Men’s and Women’s ministries
      • Different events offered throughout the year, typically once a quarter. Examples: men’s bible study, golf outings, women’s painting classes, cake decorating class, coffee shop bible study on Saturday mornings, movie nights, holiday parties, etc.
    • Music - our Praise & Worship Team leads worship every other Sunday. The worship team incorporates modern hymns, choruses, and songs for a contemporary worship feel. The other Sundays we have a song leader who leads traditional hymns, and also gives a call to worship and a benediction. God has also blessed our congregation with several talented musicians and soloists who occasionally share special music.
    • Nursery available during Sunday morning worship services for 0-3 yrs old.
  • Castlewood continues to see new families attend the church on a regular basis. Some who stay, and some who visit a few times a year. We have a nice range of ages, from those who are seniors or retirement age, to a lot of young families with children, currently in our church.

Castlewood Alliance Church: A Look Back

Castlewood C&MA Church owes its existence to our founders who, over 100 years ago, had the vision of a church in what was then known as Moravia Stop.

The Christian and Missionary Alliance Church of Moravia Stop was established in 1923, having been incorporated on December 6, 1922, and recorded at the courthouse on January 22, 1923. Soon after, on January 15, 1923, the initial ground was donated by James G. Houk, and the original church was built and dedicated on October 28, 1923. (Prior to the building of the church, services had been held in Castlewood Grade School, which was on the site where our current parsonage sits.) Due to the elimination of the trolley line, the area was no longer known as Moravia Stop. The name of the area was changed to Castlewood, and consequently, our church name changed to Castlewood Christian and Missionary Alliance Church in November 1957.

The original church included a bell tower, which housed a bell donated by Mrs. James G. Houk. Some years later the tower was struck by lightning and both the tower, and the bell had to be removed. Chauncey and Ella Mae Forbush had the bell mounted outside the church building in memory of Ella Mae’s mother and father, Mr. and Mrs. Harry Ort, late members of the church. The bell was dedicated July 4, 1976. Our first steeple was placed in 1991 and replaced 20 years later in 2011 due to weather damage over the years.

As attendance increased, a lot was purchased from James G. Houk. The lot adjoining the rear of the original church property was bought in November 1957. An extra wing was added to the church between 1957-1958 and dedicated in November 1958. The basement of the former structure was replaced in the fall of 1972.

A third piece of property was purchased from the estate of Bessie Houk in September 1967. This addition to the church property was the two lots adjacent to the church parking lot on which the Old Hill School (later known as Castlewood Elementary) once stood. These were donated by Chauncey and Ella Mae Forbush in December 1971. The school was torn down in 1972 to make room for a new parsonage building. Former parsonages owned by the church were a two-story home behind the church, one on Hollow Road, and one at 707 Harmony Baptist Road. Our current parsonage is located beside the church at 658 Harmony Baptist Road. The parsonage was completed and dedicated in 1979. The 20-yr mortgage was paid off in only 7 ½ years.

Castlewood went through major renovations beginning in December 2014. The plans for reversing the direction of the sanctuary originated with Rev. Hiram Westover in the 1980’s, but they did not become a reality until Rev. James R. O’Hara teamed up with Architect Carl Petrus and Contractor Mark Summers. The new layout of the sanctuary allowed for more seating for our growing congregation, and the old front entrance was eliminated and bricked on the outside, updating the look of the building. A new stage and baptistry were put in. The main entrance was moved to the back of the building, where a wider foyer, office, and cloak room were installed, as well as a handicap accessible restroom and a new nursery. Many other modifications were made to modernize the look and feel of the church facilities. The mortgage for the renovations was paid off in approximately eight years; significantly sooner than the maturity date of the loan. Since then, several additional upgrades and changes have been made to the building and the grounds as our church family has grown and its needs have evolved throughout the years. As God has led us, we have endeavored to follow. We are always amazed at His provision and faithfulness.

Summary of Building and Property

  • The church was renovated in 2015, not only to provide more seating, but also to flip the sanctuary around so people were not walking into the front door of the sanctuary if they arrived late. A baptismal tank was also added at that time.
  • The church foyer/narthex was expanded recently by removing a dividing wall. A large flatscreen tv for viewing the livestream was installed. The new expanded area now has four swivel rockers, creating a quiet space for nursing mothers to use during services.
  • The church has a ranch style 1-story brick parsonage right next door with 5 bedrooms, 3 bathrooms, and an attached 2 car garage. It has a small private finished basement and recently re-carpeted back porch overlooking a nice piece of property (2+ acres)
  • Property has been well maintained both on the church side and the parsonage side.
  • Some other updates that have been made over the last 5 years or so include: Sunday school rooms painted; new flooring in the nursery; parking lot sealed/resurfaced; parsonage rooms were painted and new flooring put down in the kitchen/bathroom.

The School of Music at Baylor University seeks an engaging and collaborative church musician and educator to join its Church Music faculty as a full-time Assistant Teaching Professor. The successful candidate will contribute to undergraduate and graduate teaching, student mentoring and recruitment, and the School of Music’s ongoing work of preparing skilled and thoughtful musicians for service in churches and other ministry contexts.

About Church Music and the Dunn Center for Christian Music Studies:
Church Music at Baylor brings together rigorous musical study, theological reflection, research, and practical formation for service to the church. Students pursue undergraduate and graduate pathways in Church Music, including master’s and doctoral study and a joint M.Div./M.M. with George W. Truett Theological Seminary. The Dunn Center for Christian Music Studies extends this work through research initiatives, conferences and public programs, visiting artists and scholars, church and professional partnerships, and global Music & Missions opportunities. Faculty and staff work collaboratively to prepare musicians and scholars for thoughtful, creative, and faithful leadership in a wide range of Christian denominations and communities.

About the Baylor School of Music:
At the Baylor School of Music, faith and artistry meet purpose. Our faculty guide exceptional students through a rigorous, musically rich education, where every performance, composition, and collaboration reflects excellence and depth. From captivating performers to musical scholars to contemporary innovators, Baylor shapes versatile artists and educators who thrive creatively and professionally.

What sets the Baylor School of Music apart?

  • A vibrant community of 300 students from across the country and around the globe.
  • Award-winning ensembles that have performed at every major national conference in the United States, and many of the world’s most prestigious venues.
  • Our Emmy-nominated television concert event, A Baylor Christmas, reaches 150,000 households during the holidays.
  • Over 300 live performances annually, giving students real-world experiences that prepare them for professional careers.
  • Global opportunities through study abroad and mission trips—from Kenya to Japan to Brazil.
  • Winners of Semper Pro Musica, our signature student competition, perform at Carnegie Hall.
  • Research opportunities for graduate and undergraduate students.
  • Baylor’s mission to integrate academic excellence and Christian commitment within a caring community.

Joining the Baylor School of Music means becoming part of a legacy that combines rigorous artistry and academic pursuits with a deep sense of purpose. Here, we prepare a new generation of musicians and scholars to lead, serve, and inspire.

Responsibilities:  

  • Teach undergraduate and, as appropriate, graduate courses in Church Music/Worship, with particular attention to practical ministry, vocational formation, and areas aligned with the candidate’s expertise and program needs.
  • Mentor students preparing for professional ministry and church-music vocations, helping them integrate musical excellence, theological reflection, pastoral awareness, and practical leadership.
  • Support internships, field-based learning, ministry placements, or other experiential learning as assigned.
  • Participate actively in recruitment, auditions/admissions activities, student advising, and retention efforts for Church Music programs.
  • Collaborate with Church Music faculty and Dunn Center staff on events, educational programs, outreach, and partnerships with churches and ministry leaders.
  • Maintain active professional and/or creative engagement in church music, worship, ministry, or related fields.
  • Participate in School of Music and University service as appropriate.
  • Engage in significant professional and creative activities and/or research within the discipline and contribute to the intellectual life and mission of Baylor University and the School of Music.

Appointment Date: August 15, 2027

Rank:  Appointment at Assistant Teaching Professor, full-time, non-tenure track, promotion eligible

Salary: Competitive and commensurate with experience

About Baylor University: 
Baylor University is located in Waco, Texas and is the oldest college in the state. It has a diverse student population of 21,000 and is recognized as an R1 institution by the Carnegie Classification. Baylor is also noted on the honor roll of “Great Colleges to Work For” by ModernThink. We offer competitive salaries and benefits, allowing faculty and staff to live in one of the fastest-growing parts of the state. As a Christian university with historic Baptist roots and as reflected in the Notice of Non-Discrimination, Baylor strives to be a place characterized by civility and respect. We believe each student, faculty, staff, and administrator is made in the image of God. Baylor's new strategic plan, Baylor in Deeds, guides the University as it continues to fulfill its mission of educating men and women for worldwide leadership and service by integrating academic excellence and Christian commitment within a caring community.



  • A master’s degree in Church Music, Worship Studies, Sacred Music, Music, Ministry/Theology, or a closely related field.

Overview

The Ministry Assistant will be an integral part of both the social and spiritual ministries. This includes, but is not limited to, assisting with creating and running youth programming, assisting with clients' needs, assisting with transportation, and ultimately bridging the gap between social services and showing the love of Jesus Christ to every client encountered. This position will represent The Salvation Army, the church, and social service programs in a professional and caring manner. Additionally, this role will provide direct social services on a once-a-week basis in downtown Pittsburgh as an extension of our social services. They will respond to requests for assistance in a timely manner by completing intake paperwork, determining eligibility, and providing referral services.

Responsibilities

ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS:

  • Assist in planning, preparing, setting up, and implementing all corps ministry programs and activities.
  • Assist with Sunday ministry, adult Bible study/Sunday school, youth discipleship, and program outreach.
  • Prepare and conduct corps programs and activities as assigned by the Corps Officers.
  • Assist with recruiting volunteers and participants for corps programming.
  • Work with Corps Officers and community partners to plan, coordinate, and participate in community events.
  • Encourage participation in and assist with divisional functions and activities.
  • Collaborate with Social Services personnel to connect clients with corps programs, worship opportunities, and other available resources.
  • Provide direct social services one day per week at a designated partner site in downtown Pittsburgh, including completing intake paperwork, determining eligibility, and providing referrals.
  • Assist with client services, answer telephone calls, and respond to requests for assistance in a timely and professional manner.
  • Coordinate transportation for program participants and scheduled activities in collaboration with the Envoy in Charge.
  • Safely transport participants in a 12-passenger van as needed, including picking up and dropping off participants.
  • Assist the Social Worker with summer Allegheny Camps, including participant transportation and related activities.
  • Maintain accurate program statistics and prepare reports as requested.
  • Maintain regular office hours to prepare for programs, activities, and administrative responsibilities.
  • Ensure the safety and well-being of participants during all programs, activities, and services.

ADDITIONAL RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Assist with maintaining clean, organized, and orderly program areas, facilities, grounds, and equipment.
  • Ensure Salvation Army-owned or rented property and equipment are secured, maintained, and kept in good condition.
  • Practice responsible stewardship of Salvation Army facilities, equipment, supplies, and grounds.
  • Maintain receipts and follow required accounting procedures for Salvation Army expenses in accordance with established accounting guidelines.
  • Serve on call when appropriate and as needed.
  • Maintain flexibility to work evenings, weekends, and extended hours during seasonal programming and other high-demand periods.
  • Assist with increased holiday programming and seasonal activities during November and December, Easter activities in April, and summer camp programming and transportation during July and August.

Perform other duties as assigned by the Corps Officers

Qualifications

KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS AND ABILITIES:

 

  • All three PA Clearances required upon employment and thereafter upon renewal date: PA Child Abuse History Clearance, Request for Criminal Record, and Fingerprint based federal criminal history.
  • PA Mandated and Permissive Reporting and The Salvation Army’s KeepSAfe training required.

 

 

EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE:

  • Possess basic knowledge of The Salvation Army, its mission, programs, and services.
  • Demonstrate strong written and verbal communication skills.
  • Possess basic administrative and office skills, including proficiency with Microsoft Office applications.
  • Demonstrate effective organizational, interpersonal, and time-management skills.
  • Ability to work independently and collaboratively with staff, volunteers, clients, and community partners.
  • Demonstrate professionalism, compassion, sound judgment, and a commitment to the mission and values of The Salvation Army.
  • Possess a valid driver's license and the ability to safely transport program participants as required.
  • Maintain all three required Pennsylvania clearances upon employment and thereafter according to applicable renewal requirements: Pennsylvania Child Abuse History Clearance, Pennsylvania State Police Criminal Record Check, and FBI fingerprint-based federal criminal history clearance.
  • Complete required Pennsylvania Mandated and Permissive Reporting training and The Salvation Army's KeepSAfe training.

EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE

  • High school diploma or equivalent required.
  • Experience working in a ministry setting preferred.
  • Previous experience working with children and adults in recreational, educational, or community service settings preferred.

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS

  • Ability to lift and carry objects weighing up to 50 pounds.
  • Ability to bend, reach, stand, walk, and perform other physical activities frequently as required by program and facility responsibilities.
  • Ability to assist with program setup, transportation, camp activities, and facility maintenance.
  • Ability to work evenings, weekends, and extended hours during seasonal programming and other periods of increased activity.
  • Ability to safely operate a 12-passenger van and transport participants as assigned.

NOTE

Applying is a two step-process. You must follow through listing here, and you must also submit a questionnaire hosted on our website.


Access questionnaire here.


DESCRIPTION

The Pastoral Ministry Resident will engage in a 12-month residency program designed to provide hands-on pastoral leadership experience, spiritual formation, and practical ministry training. This program is ideal for individuals preparing for full-time pastoral ministry and desiring to deepen their understanding of church leadership, preaching, pastoral care, and administration. Residents will work closely with the church leadership team, participate in key ministry activities, and receive ongoing mentorship from experienced pastors.

You will incur no cost as a result of your participation in the program. All of your books and materials will be provided for you. Participants are responsible for funding their own time, room, and board during the program with the time not allocated to the program.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Theological Development:
  • Engage in a structured reading program covering theology, pastoral care, leadership, and church administration.
  • Participate in discussions and reflections on theological concepts, such as the Gospel, the Trinity, and gender roles in the church.
  • Pastoral Leadership and Preaching:
  • Preach and teach in various contexts (e.g., worship services, small groups, outreach events), developing Christ-centered sermons and receiving feedback.
  • Assist in leading worship services, including preparing liturgy, scripture readings, and prayers.
  • Develop and implement strategic plans for church ministry and operations in collaboration with the leadership team.
  • Spiritual Formation and Discipleship:
  • Lead personal and communal prayer initiatives within the church.
  • Create discipleship programs that emphasize spiritual growth and biblical literacy for church members.
  • Mentor and disciple small groups of congregants as part of church ministry.
  • Church Administration and Operations:
  • Participate in church administration tasks, such as event planning, budget management, and operational oversight.
  • Lead specific church projects or initiatives, ensuring they align with the church’s mission and strategic goals.
  • Community Engagement and Outreach:
  • Plan and lead community outreach events that focus on evangelism, discipleship, and relational ministry.
  • Build connections with community members and develop programs that address local needs through a Gospel-centered approach.
  • Pastoral Care and Counseling:
  • Participate in pastoral care activities, including counseling sessions, hospital visits, and congregational care.
  • Assist in developing and implementing pastoral care plans for specific groups within the congregation (e.g., families, youth, elderly).


Disclaimer on Employment Practices

Redeemer is a religious organization and is therefore exempt from certain provisions of the Fair Labor Standards Act (FLSA). This exemption allows churches to make employment decisions based on their religious mission and doctrinal beliefs.


In alignment with our mission to glorify God and advance His kingdom, Redeemer Church reserves the right to employ individuals whose beliefs, lifestyle, and conduct align with the Bible and the church’s doctrinal convictions. Employment decisions may consider the following factors:


  1. Religious Beliefs: Applicants must affirm and adhere to the doctrinal statement of Redeemer Church as part of their commitment to our shared faith.
  2. Moral and Ethical Conduct: All employees are expected to live in a manner consistent with biblical teachings, as interpreted by the leadership of Redeemer Church.
  3. Mission Alignment: Applicants must demonstrate a clear commitment to supporting the church’s mission, values, and goals in their role.


Redeemer Church does not unlawfully discriminate based on race, color, national origin, sex, age, disability, or any other status protected by applicable law. However, as a religious organization, we retain the right to make employment decisions in accordance with our faith and theological convictions, as permitted under federal law.


By applying for a position with Redeemer Church, applicants acknowledge and agree to these expectations as a condition of employment.

_______________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________

Are You Passionate About Empowering People in Their Faith Journey? 
Do you have a heart to build and cultivate a healthy church culture, develop life-changing ministries, and create systems that fuel growth?  If so, Friends Church invites you to support a thriving ministry that's shaping the future of the church and our community. 

_______________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________

About Friends Church 
Friends Church is a vibrant, multi-campus community committed to building a community of authentic Christ-followers, compelled to change our world. Our Tustin campus is the newest of Friends Church 7 campuses.  We're dedicated to creating environments where lives are transformed, purpose is discovered, and the next generation is equipped to lead.
 
_______________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________

Your Mission 
As the Director of Operations and Ministry, you will: 

Execute Vision and Strategy 
  • Partner with the Lead Pastor and leadership team to help the church live out its mission, vision, and values to impact both individuals and communities with the good news of Jesus.
  • Be an active presence in both the church and city of Tustin, fostering meaningful relationships and connections.
Manage Campus Operations 
  • Manage day to day operations of the campus, overseeing projects, systems, budgets, and calendars to ensure smooth and effective ministry.
  • Work closely with the Lead Pastor, staff and volunteers to foster a culture of excellence and collaboration.
Empower Volunteers 
  • Cultivate a culture of joy, warmth, and service that mirrors the love and values of God’s kingdom.
  • Equip and support volunteer leaders and teams to live out their gifts and calling with confidence.
  • Build systems and pathways that attract, equip, and empower volunteers to thrive spiritually as they serve.
Oversee Communications & Events 
  • Direct all campus communications, creatively telling the story of Friends Tustin through various platforms.
  • Contribute to planning and executing events that engage both the church and broader Tustin community.
Guide Groups & Discipleship 
  • Oversee group ministries (Life Groups, Alpha, Rooted, etc.) to create opportunities for people to grow spiritually and experience authentic, supportive relationships.
  • Equip group leaders, create engaging content, and implement systems that ensure a dynamic groups ministry.
_______________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________

What We're Looking For 
  • Spiritual Maturity: A strong personal relationship with Jesus Christ, adherence to Friends Church Statement of Faith, Core Values, and a clear calling with a passion for discipleship.
  • Ministry Experience: 3–5 years ministry experience or equivalent combination of education and experience, with demonstrated success in organization and leadership development.
  • Core Competencies: Activator, executor, designer, change manager, team builder, equipper, detail oriented, interpersonal effectiveness, committed to excellence, collaborative, strategic decisionmaker, winsome in relationships.
  • Strategic Vision: Skills in program development, event planning, budget management, and team leadership, with the ability to set and achieve measurable ministry goals.
  • Educational Foundation: Bachelor's degree in theology, ministry, or related field, with commitment to obtain commissioning through Friends Southwest (FSW).
  • Heart for Friends Church: Active membership at Friends Church with full alignment to our mission, values, and ministry approach, including participation in church-wide initiatives.
_______________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________

Why Join Us? 
At Friends Church, you'll have the incredible opportunity to shape the spiritual formation of young adults during some of the most influential years of their lives. You'll work with a supportive team that values innovation, authentic relationships, and measurable impact. We offer: 
  • Comprehensive Benefits: Retirement plan with employer match, parental leave, professional development allowance, and generous holiday and sick pay.
  • Professional Growth: Opportunities for advancement within a multi-campus church environment, conference attendance, continuing education support, and commissioning assistance through FSW.
  • Collaborative Team: Work alongside passionate staff and volunteers.
  • Pastoral Opportunities: If commissioned, opportunities to perform weddings, baptisms, and funerals, expanding your pastoral ministry experience.
  • Ministry Impact: Lead a ministry with clear goals and metrics for success, including Life Group participation rates and connection to broader church community.
_______________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________

Ready to Shape the Future? 
If you're ready to invest in the Tustin Community and help people to become a community of Christ-followers to discover their calling to change the world, we invite you to apply and join our mission.

Friends Church is committed to building diverse communities that reflect the kingdom of God. We encourage applications from candidates of all backgrounds who share our mission and values.

Description:
There are nearly 300,000 teenagers of active-duty U.S. military parents who are stationed all over the world. These teens move an average of seven times during their school-aged years. The questions of identity and belonging that all teens face grow even more challenging to answer amid starting over and meeting new friends at each location.
This is where you can be the difference in a military teen’s life! By being in their world, walking alongside them, and creating a community where they experience the truth of God’s love and purpose for them, our staff provide a safe space where teens can develop friendships and connections to experience laughter, build hope, and generate resiliency.
We are currently providing incarnational ministry at many military installations around the world. You will have the opportunity to lead and oversee the overall Young Life Military program, known as Club Beyond, which is ecumenically focused and outreach oriented.
Responsibilities:
  • Actively develop healthy relationships with adults, as well as kids, and build vibrant relationships with the local community, the military installation, and the chapel community.
  • Be a role model (incarnational) and assist with developing community outreach to "unchurched" teens, discipleship to Christian teens, and leading and equipping volunteers to do "hands-on" middle and high school Christian youth programs.
  • Work well in an environment that sees (due to high military operational tempo) a high degree of turnover among teens, families, chaplains and volunteers.
  • Be respectful of and embrace a community that is deeply influenced by a military culture.
  • In this ministry, you will need to live out the Club Beyond Core Value Statement:
Club Beyond is a Christ-centered community of leaders with an exclusively military focus. Our methods are incarnational, and our perspective is ecumenical. We leverage strategic partnerships for the greatest results. We value professionalism from our staff and excellence in our stewardship.
Qualifications:
  • A deep love for Christ and for lost teens.
  • Competent communicator with youths, parents, and senior military leaders.
  • Teachable heart.
  • Willingness to make a three-year commitment.
  • Minimum of three years' youth ministry experience preferred.
  • College degree preferred.
  • Willingness to raise part of the budget through personal support.
  • Committed to a relational ministry approach.
  • Energetic.
  • Small event planning skills.
  • Strong initiative.
  • Note, this position would require our Staff to live near the community where they would be doing ministry.
Benefits:

The Base Salary range: $45,000 to $60,000 (Salary is based on education and experience). In addition to salary, a Cost of Living Adjustment, dependent on location, is available. The Annual National Funding provided is $16,667.
Location:

TITLE: Finance Ministry Assistant

REPORTING: Finance Manager

STATUS: Part-Time Volunteer Staff 


POSITION DESCRIPTION

The Finance Ministry Assistant provides essential administrative and operational support to the Finance Manager, helping ensure Crossroads’ financial resources are managed with absolute integrity, accuracy, and compliance. This volunteer staff role focuses on routine financial data processing, administrative upkeep, and cross-campus data tracking to streamline day-to-day accounting workflows.

By executing critical tracking and communication tasks that do not require full financial system access, this role serves as a vital administrative bridge between the finance department, campus pastors, and campus administrators.


CHARACTER 

  • A growing follower of Jesus who views administrative excellence, clear tracking, and stewardship as an essential ministry to the church body.
  • Extremely discreet and trustworthy, maintaining strict, absolute confidentiality regarding all sensitive financial data, giving records, and staff accountabilities.
  • Highly detailed and organized, possessing a natural affinity for accuracy, order, clear note-taking, and systematic record-keeping.
  • A supportive team player who is teachable, works well with others, and enjoys working behind the scenes to help the finance team and campus staff succeed.


RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Support Campus Financial Care & Tracking – Partner with local campus leaders to monitor the health of giving pathways. Help cross-reference transaction histories to highlight canceled, stuck, or unresolved items, ensuring our metrics remain accurate and families are cared for well.
  • Maintain Administrative Data Logs – Support the regular aggregation of campus data, assisting with attendance numbers or detailed metrics required for the weekly quick report.
  • Facilitate Campus Communication – Act as an administrative liaison by capturing accurate notes, action items, and financial follow-ups that need to be raised directly to campus pastors or campus administrators.
  • Execute Limited-Access Administration – Complete essential administrative and clerical workflows that support the overall health of the finance department without requiring full or sensitive financial database access.


SKILLS AND COMPETENCIES

  • Exceptional attention to detail and accuracy when working with numerical tracking and data logs.
  • Strong written communication skills, with an ability to capture, organize, and pass along notes clearly.
  • High professional maturity and an uncompromised commitment to confidentiality.
  • Basic technology proficiency, with a comfort in spreadsheets (Excel/Google Sheets) and a willingness to learn basic church database tracking tools.


DUTIES

  • Collaborate with campus pastors to identify and flag canceled transactions or transactions that appear to be stuck or unresolved.
  • Assist in tracking attendance metrics and processing detailed data entries needed for the weekly quick report.
  • Capture and organize clear follow-up notes and action items to be communicated directly to campus pastors or campus administrators.
  • Perform other basic clerical and administrative tasks that support the finance department without requiring full financial software access.
  • Sort, match, and log weekly ministry receipts and credit card statements.
  • Scan and archive physical financial documents into the church’s secure cloud storage.
  • Assist the Finance Manager in compiling folder sets and logs for scheduled financial audits.
  • Track and organize submitted Ramp Card Expenses and Accounts Payable Reimbursement Forms from campus staff for manager review.


QUALIFICATIONS

  • Education: High school diploma required; basic coursework or experience in business, bookkeeping, or office administration is a plus.
  • Experience: Demonstrated capability in data entry, tracking systems, or general office administration. Prior experience using basic spreadsheets is required; familiarity with church platforms (CCB, PushPay) is helpful but not required.
  • Aptitude: High capacity for administrative task follow-through, clear note-taking, and organizational accuracy.
  • Requirements: Signed confidentiality agreement. Full affirmation of the mission, vision, values, and beliefs of Crossroads.


WORK SCHEDULE

  • Part-time volunteer position.
  • Weekly hours are flexible but must be completed in a consistent, predictable mid-week block mutually agreed upon with the Finance Manager to keep weekly data processing on track.


WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE

  • Proactive Pattern Detection: Transaction anomalies, canceled gifts, or stuck records are caught quickly through consistent communication with campus pastors, preventing ongoing donor experience issues.
  • Accurate & Timely Reports: Attendance tracking and detailed weekly metrics are fully prepared and formatted for the quick report without delay.
  • Clear Multi-Campus Communication: Campus pastors and campus administrators receive highly organized, actionable follow-up notes regarding local financial or data items that need their attention.
  • Frictionless Support Systems: The Finance Assistant functions as a true partner to the Finance Manager, managing essential non-access workflows smoothly so the manager can focus on high-level strategy, policy, and compliance.

Associate Pastor of Worship & Connections

Bethel Baptist Church | Fairbanks, Alaska


Job Summary

Bethel Baptist Church in Fairbanks, Alaska is searching for an Associate Pastor of Worship and Connections — a pastor who leads with both a shepherd's heart and a musician's skill. This is a genuinely hybrid role: roughly half pastoral ministry (preaching rotation, counseling, elder responsibilities, and general care of the congregation) and half worship and connections leadership (weekly service planning, team development, and overseeing the first-impressions ministry that helps guests find their way into community). The person who fills this role won't just be handed a platform, they'll be invited into a long-tenured, deeply relational staff team and trusted to help shape the next chapter of a healthy, missions-minded church. For someone who wants to put down roots in a place that takes both theology and people seriously, this is a rare opportunity.


Why I Love This Opportunity

What stands out most about Bethel is the culture of longevity. The senior pastor has served over two decades, and staff members routinely stay for 10, 15, even 20+ years. That kind of stability is rare, and it tells you something important about the quality of the relationships and the health of the leadership. Add to that a congregation with genuine global vision (20 missionaries supported, nearly 200 kids sponsored in Ethiopia, an annual apologetics conference), debt-free finances with a multi-million dollar building project already largely funded, and a senior pastor who leads by trust rather than micromanagement — this is the kind of place where the right person can genuinely thrive and leave a lasting mark.


A Great Match for This Position Would Be...

• A pastor first, musician second — someone who sees worship leading as one expression of shepherding, not the other way around. This role is genuinely 50/50, and the church needs someone who's comfortable in both lanes.

• Theologically grounded with a careful approach to worship content — Reformed-leaning but not rigidly so, deeply comfortable with modern hymnody (Gettys, CityAlight, etc.), and aligned with the church's thoughtful avoidance of New Apostolic Reformation-adjacent material.

•. Administratively capable — able to organize rotating volunteer teams, run Planning Center confidently, coordinate with tech and production teams, and oversee a connections ministry without getting so artsy they can't keep it organized.

•. Built for Alaska — honest with themselves about what it means to live with darkness, distance, extreme cold, and a cost of living 20–25% above the national average. At the same time, appreciative of the world-class outdoor experiences, natural beauty, independent and friendly people, and the deep community Alaska offers.

•. A humble learner — coachable, self-aware, and genuinely excited about being sharpened by a seasoned senior pastor. Experience matters less than the posture.

•. Wired for long-term investment — someone who wants to send down deep roots, not use this as a stepping stone. The congregation is looking for someone who sees this as a calling, not a career move.


About This Organization

Bethel Baptist Church is a roughly 60-year-old, expository Bible-teaching congregation in Fairbanks, Alaska — three miles from the University of Alaska Fairbanks campus and deeply woven into the fabric of the community. With around 600 in weekly attendance (closer to 1,200 on Easter), the congregation is genuinely multigenerational: about 120 kids in elementary and under, 60–80 junior high and high school students, and 30–40 college students on any given Sunday. Military families, young couples, and growing households are well-represented. Bethel is affiliated with Conservative Baptists Northwest and holds conservative theology without being rigid or cold. The senior pastor describes it as "a little heady" with a relational warmth underneath. The church supports 20 missionaries domestically and internationally, sponsors roughly 180 children in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, and hosts an annual apologetics conference featuring nationally recognized speakers. Financially, the church carries no debt and owns its building, with approximately $3.5 million cash on hand toward a $4 million Stage 1 building expansion already underway. The pastoral staff of four has served together for decades, creating an unusually stable and trust-based environment for a new hire to step into.


Key Responsibilities

Shepherding

•      Participate in the full duties of the pastoral staff, including preaching, counseling, weddings, and funerals.

•      Serve as an elder in all capacities as detailed in the church bylaws.

Leading the Worship Ministry

•      Collaborate with other leaders to carry out the overall vision for corporate worship at Bethel.

•      Plan the weekly service — selecting songs, arrangements, and ordering of the service.

•      Recruit, train, organize, and shepherd the worship team and volunteers.

•      Oversee all areas of production (audio, lighting, service management) to facilitate an experience of worship.

•      Lead worship for special events including Good Friday, Easter, and Christmas Eve.

Overseeing the Connections Ministry

•      Work with the Welcome Coordinator to ensure guests are warmly welcomed and helped in finding a seat and navigating the church.

•      Oversee the connections strategy — helping people move from attending to belonging.

•      Help create and sustain a warm, welcoming atmosphere on Sunday mornings.

Administration

•      Manage selected church budget line items jointly agreed upon with the Business Board.


Key Qualifications

•      Demonstrates a personal relationship with Jesus Christ through worship, prayer, Bible reading, application of the Word, and active evangelism.

•      Meets the qualifications of 1 Timothy 3 and Titus 1; models Christ-likeness in marriage and personal relationships.

•      Agrees with and upholds the church's full doctrinal statement.

•      Holds a Bachelor's degree from an accredited Bible college or equivalent proven ministry experience.

•      Demonstrates musical skill and theological discernment in worship selection and leadership.

•      Has a proven track record in ministry and the ability to shepherd a large congregation.

•      Able to shepherd people from the platform during corporate worship — not just perform.

•      Demonstrates excellent verbal communication skills and a proven ability to build and maintain positive, loyal relationships inside and outside the church.
