post_html:
Power Cross Ministry | Statesville & Salisbury, NC.

What if your next ministry role allowed you to invest your life in developing the next generation of Christian men?
Power Cross is looking for a Director of Discipleship who feels called to pour into young men, develop spiritual leaders, equip coaches, teach God’s Word, and help shape a culture where Jesus is at the center of everything we do.

This isn't simply a position overseeing Bible studies.

It's an opportunity to help raise up future husbands, fathers, leaders, and men of God.

Our mission is simple and ambitious:
Building up young men from generational poverty into spiritual leaders through Jesus with daily discipleship and athletics.

THE OPPORTUNITY:
At Power Cross, discipleship isn't a weekly program—it's who we are.
The Director of Discipleship will help lead the spiritual direction of our ministry and develop a discipleship strategy that reaches young men from elementary school through college, while also equipping our coaches and staff to become stronger disciple-makers.

We're looking for someone who loves Jesus, young people, God's Word, and developing leaders.

This role is ideal for a pastor, youth pastor, discipleship pastor, ministry leader, coach, FCA leader, Young Life leader, Christian educator, missionary, or other ministry professional who feels called to invest deeply in the next generation.

YOU MAY BE A GREAT FIT IF:
You:
  • Have a mature Christian faith and a genuine calling to discipleship ministry.
  • Love teaching Scripture and helping people understand how to live it.
  • Connect naturally with young men.
  • Believe athletics can be an incredible platform for ministry.
  • Enjoy developing leaders—not just leading programs yourself.
  • Can mentor and equip coaches to become disciple-makers.
  • Are relational, energetic, organized, and comfortable leading both small groups and large gatherings.
  • Want your work to have Kingdom impact that extends far beyond a job description.

WHAT YOU'LL GET TO DO:
You'll lead and strengthen the discipleship culture across Power Cross, including developing age-appropriate Bible studies and discipleship resources; teaching and leading Bible studies; mentoring young men and coaches; equipping coaches to disciple their teams; building relationships with families and local churches; supporting young men as they make decisions for Christ; helping lead baptisms, prayer gatherings, and special ministry events; and maintaining a meaningful presence in the everyday life of Power Cross.

Most importantly, you'll help ensure that Biblical teaching, mentorship, and spiritual formation remain woven into everything Power Cross does.

THIS IS MORE THAN A DESK JOB:
  • Power Cross ministry happens where our young men are.
  • That means you'll spend time in Bible studies, on athletic fields and sidelines, with coaches, in conversations with young men, at special events, and throughout our Statesville and Salisbury campuses.
  • If you're looking for a ministry where you can teach the Word and live it alongside the people you're discipling, this could be an incredible fit.

COMPENSATION & SCHEDULE:
  • Starting salary: $60,000 annually.
    Cell phone provided.
    Computer provided.
  • Typical schedule:
    • Monday–Thursday | 11:00 AM–8:30 PM
    • Friday and Saturday responsibilities vary depending on games, events, and ministry needs.

THE PERSON WE'RE PRAYING FOR:
We're not simply looking for someone who can run a discipleship program.
We're praying for a spiritual leader and disciple-maker who wants to invest his gifts in young men and help build something that matters for eternity.

Someone who understands that sometimes discipleship happens during a Bible study—and sometimes it happens on a sideline, in a van, over a meal, after a difficult day, or during a conversation a young man may remember for the rest of his life.

If God has given you a heart for developing young men into strong, Christ-centered leaders, we'd love to talk with you.

SUMMARY

The Lead Student Pastor will lead, shepherd, and guide the spiritual development of the Student Ministry through the Student Ministry Staff and servant leaders. The Lead Student Pastor will serve as the primary leader to bring the Pinelake vision to see Mississippi changed one life story at a time to life in Student Ministry as we learn from Christ, live in Christ and lead others to Christ under the leadership of the Madison NextGen Pastor. The Lead Student Pastor will work to train up leaders and students who actively take the gospel into their schools and homes.

GENERAL RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Learn
    • Pursue a growing relationship with Jesus through consistent time in God’s Word and prayer.
    • Continually grow in your understanding of the Jesus-Centered Life (salvation, identity, life, and authority in Christ).
    • Remain teachable and hungry, seeking feedback, learning from others, and developing both spiritually and professionally.
    • Cultivate awareness of God’s presence in everyday life, listening to the Holy Spirit and responding in obedience.
  • Live
    • Practice and model the rhythms of Be the Church (Grow, Pray, Connect, and Share).
    • Pursue emotional health by engaging in self-awareness, addressing past wounds, and cultivating honest, healthy relationships.
    • Practice healthy rhythms, prioritizing your relationship with Jesus and your family
    • Embody a life of integrity and surrender, allowing your private life with God to shape your work.
  • Lead
    • Take ownership of disciple-making by personally investing in others and helping them move toward a Jesus-Centered Life.
    • Walk others through the Discipleship Pathway (Essentials → JCL → Be the Church), helping them discover and take their next step.
    • Shepherd people, not just programs, by listening for where God is at work in their story and walking with them toward transformation.
    • Equip and release others by developing Servant Leaders and multiplying disciples who Learn from Christ, Live in Christ, and Lead others to Christ.
    • Measure success by life change, spiritual formation, and multiplication—not just attendance or activity.
  • Embrace the Culture
    • Value and embody the staff values, which we call the 7 H’s: Humility, Honor, Honesty, Hunger, Holy Spirit, Health, and Harmony
    • Communicate clearly, honestly, and proactively in a way that builds trust, unity, and momentum.
    • Work in alignment with the church vision and leadership
    • Participate fully in the life of your campus or team, contributing to the unity, health, and shepherding of the faith family.

SPECIFIC LIST OF DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Lead, shepherd, and guide the Student Ministry Staff team as each learns from Christ, lives in Christ, and leads others to Christ.
  • Execute the vision, mission, and direction of the campus and One Church as it relates to the entire Student Ministry.
  • Coordinate, guide, and adapt, in partnership with One Church, all curriculum, events, and worship for Student Ministry.
  • Collaborate with the Student Ministry team to create and implement a strategic plan to develop relationships at area campuses and to schedule a consistent, purposeful Pinelake student ministry presence on campuses.
  • Develop the student ministry staff and servant leaders to engage and equip students to become multiplying disciples who learn from Christ, live in Christ, and lead others to Christ as ministers of the gospel within their schools and homes.
  • Support and establish a strategic plan for the assimilation of students and families into the ministries of the church.
  • Create and lead a vibrant discipleship plan for parents of students, providing regular on-ramps for parenting growth and development.
  • Actively and intentionally participate in all three branches of student ministry through teaching and presence as leadership support.
  • Provide oversight for and leadership to Pinelake’s Our House Promise strategy within Student Ministry
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Supervises exempt and non-exempt personnel.
  • Supervises and coordinates work with servant-leaders.

QUALIFICATIONS

To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily. The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skill and/or ability required. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform essential functions.

EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE REQUIRED

Bachelor’s degree minimum; and five years of ministry related experience and/or training.

LANGUAGE SKILLS

The individual must have excellent interpersonal skills, ability to work with a diverse group of people, communicate clearly and effectively on the telephone, e-mail and in person, demonstrating tact and diplomacy. Exceptional interpersonal skills are required to develop and maintain strong working relationships with volunteers, co-workers, the public and church members and regular attendees. The individual must have the ability to understand written or oral instructions; read, analyze and interpret complex documents, instructions manuals, policies and procedures is essential.

COMPUTER AND MATHEMATICAL SKILLS

The individual must have demonstrated skill in the use of Mac/Windows OS to complete tasks, including word processing and spreadsheets and the ability to use the internet for information retrieval. The individual must have basic mathematical skills, knowledge of bookkeeping and basic accounting, and budget and expense monitoring. The individual must have the ability to read financial information and spreadsheets.

REASONING ABILITY

The ability to simultaneously conceptualize and plan multiple tasks; project outcomes using different implementation strategies; and apply creative and innovative thinking to problem situations is required. The ability to work effectively and efficiently under stressful conditions to ensure deadlines are met is essential.

PHYSICAL DEMANDS

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions. While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to sit and talk or hear. The employee is required to stand, walk, and reach with hands and arms.

Must be able to lift up to 25 lbs.

WORK ENVIRONMENT

The work environment characteristics described here are representative of those an employee encounters while performing the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

The noise level of the work environment is usually moderate.

Our vision is to “lead all generations to find and follow Jesus for the flourishing of our city and beyond”


PURPOSE OF THIS POSITION

The Worship Department seeks to advance and support our vision by providing spiritual leadership, musical direction, and creativity to corporate worship and prayer that is theologically grounded, artistically excellent, pastorally sensitive, fostering congregational participation and spiritual formation.


The Director of Contemporary Worship is responsible for leading, developing, and overseeing the church’s contemporary worship ministry.  They work collaboratively with leadership by equipping and empowering the congregation and worship team, across all generations, to encounter God through the contemporary worship at the church. (Please note we already have in place an outstanding Music Director and team who lead our classical music ministry.)


DESIRED RESULTS/IMPACT OF THIS POSITION

Pinelake Church is a thriving multisite church serving communities across Mississippi through five campuses and a unified One Church strategy. Since its beginnings in 1971, Pinelake has grown steadily under faithful leadership and a deep conviction that the local church is God’s primary vehicle for life transformation. Today, more than 15,000 people gather weekly to worship, study Scripture, and live out the mission of helping people Learn from Christ, Live in Christ, and Lead others to Christ.

With a strong commitment to biblical teaching, discipleship, and community outreach, Pinelake is known for creating environments where people encounter the truth of God’s Word and experience life change. Their vision — to see Mississippi changed one Life Change Story at a time — drives every ministry area, including a robust NextGen ecosystem that invests deeply in kids, students, and families. Across all campuses, the One Church Team provides unified leadership, strategy, and resourcing that enables Pinelake to move collaboratively and consistently toward its mission.


The One Church NextGen Pastor provides strategic, spiritual, and cultural leadership for all NextGen ministries at Pinelake. This includes Kids, Students, Young Adults, and the School of Ministry across all five campuses. This leader champions a unified philosophy of NextGen discipleship, builds systems that scale, coaches campus leaders, and ensures every environment from babies to young adults helps people learn from Christ, live in Christ, and lead others to Christ. They serve as a key voice on the One Church Team, helping Pinelake move in a unified direction while honoring unique campus contexts. Above all, they model the emotional, spiritual, and relational health that is now central to the culture of Pinelake.

This is one of the most exciting NextGen opportunities in the country. Pinelake is spiritually hungry, emotionally healthy, organizationally rebuilding, and positioned for growth. The team is collaborative, humble, and deeply aligned around a shared mission to make disciples across Mississippi. The right leader will get to architect systems, shape culture, build teams, and influence thousands of kids, students, and families for decades to come.


  • A spiritually attuned, emotionally healthy leader who embodies Pinelake’s “7 H’s”: humility, hunger, honesty, harmony, health, honor, and Holy Spirit-dependence.
  • A strategist who can see the big picture, build systems, and coach campus staff toward unified execution.
  • A collaborative leader who loves influencing through relationship rather than authority.
  • A developer who invests deeply in staff, volunteers, and families.
  • A steady presence who leads from authenticity, integrity, and a healthy home life.
  • Someone who thrives in a fast-moving, relational, highly team-oriented culture.


Mission, Vision and Values

Pinelake exists to help people Learn from Christ, Live in Christ, and Lead others to Christ. Our vision is to see Mississippi changed one Life Change Story at a time. Everything we do in NextGen reflects this heartbeat — from teaching Scripture to empowering volunteers to creating consistent environments where kids and students encounter Jesus.


Staff Values

Pinelake staff culture is shaped by the “7 H’s”:

  • Honesty
  • Honor
  • Humility
  • Hunger
  • Holy Spirit Dependence
  • Harmony
  • Health


Staff Culture

Pinelake has undergone a multi-year transformation toward emotional health, spiritual depth, relational honesty, and healthy family rhythms. Leaders are expected to live congruently — not with a polished front stage and a hidden backstage, but with authenticity, integrity, and openness.


The staff thrives through:

  • Collaborative decision-making
  • Honest feedback (“last 10%” conversations)
  • Emotional and spiritual maturity
  • Healthy boundaries and Sabbath rhythms
  • A deep dependence on the Holy Spirit, not just strategy
  • A culture where laughter and joy are essential


Key Responsibilities

  • Provide central leadership and vision for Kids, Students, and Family Ministries across all campuses.
  • Directly supervise the One Church Kids, Students, Young Adults, and School of Ministry leaders.
  • Champion a unified NextGen philosophy of discipleship that aligns with Pinelake’s mission, vision, and values.
  • Coach and develop NextGen staff (Kids Directors, Student Pastors, Preschool teams, etc.) across five campuses.
  • Build systems, processes, and ministry playbooks that scale sustainably while allowing contextual expression.
  • Lead One Church collaboration efforts — strategy, calendar, curriculum, events (e.g., camps, retreats).
  • Ensure theological alignment, cultural embodiment, and healthy ministry leadership across teams.
  • Partner closely with Worship, Communications, Groups, Operations, and Campus Pastors.
  • Model emotional and spiritual health as a non-negotiable for ministry leadership.


Key Qualifications

  • 10+ years leading in Student, Kids, NextGen, or Family Ministry in large-church or multisite environments.
  • Proven ability to lead through influence, not just authority.
  • Strong strategist with experience building scalable ministry systems.
  • Demonstrated history of developing staff and volunteers.
  • Theological alignment with Pinelake’s doctrinal positions (non-cessationist, soft complementarian, non-militant Reformed, Spirit-empowered ministry).
  • Bachelor’s degree required; Master’s preferred.

Ninety percent of a child’s brain development happens before the age of 5, and we’re on a mission to help our youngest learners start strong!   

Join Early Learning Corps as an Early Learning Tutor and you’ll spend your days in a pre-kindergarten classroom to help students build skills and confidence. We’ll train you to deliver proven activities and coach you every step of the way! 

How does it work? Partnering with a teacher, you’ll help enhance learning. Whether talking, reading, writing, singing, or playing with students, you’ll be helping them to build early literacy and math skills.    

With the extra attention and support, you'll make an incredible impact and help ignite a love of learning!

post_html:
Campus Staff Minister - Alabama (Graduate & Faculty Ministry)

Work Location:

Alabama

Job Type:

Full time

God has called InterVarsity to plant and to build witnessing communities of students and faculty who follow Jesus on college and university campuses. Through these groups, we believe ever- increasing numbers of students and faculty from all ethnic groups and areas of the campus will be transformed by the Gospel. We expect to see campuses increasingly become places where people, ideas, and structures flourish to the glory of God. We confidently anticipate that our InterVarsity alumni will become change agents across the country and around the world. We pursue this calling by discerning and actively participating in what God is already doing on campus. This is the essence of being a Campus Staff Minister (CSM).

Please submit the GFM Interest Form before completing the full application for a position with Graduate & Faculty Ministries in our online system. We will contact you when we are ready to proceed with the application process.​ 

This position is open to applicants working less than 40 hours/week. If you are interested in part-time work please apply for this position. 

The pay range listed is for an employee working 40 hours/week at CSM level I. Pay will be prorated for employees who work less than 40 hours/week.

We have positions in the following locations:

  • Auburn University
  • University of Alabama - Tuscaloosa
  • University of Alabama - Birmingham
  • University of Alabama - Huntsville
  • University of South Alabama

Volunteers are welcome. Volunteer opportunities range from prayer and hospitality to leading a campus fellowship of graduate students and faculty. Those interested in volunteering will go through an application and interview process. However, volunteer openings are not posted online. For more information, complete the GFM Interest Form. 

ESSENTIAL COMMITMENTS/RESPONSIBILITIES 

Spiritual Growth 

As a Campus Staff Minister, you pursue maturity as a disciple of Jesus Christ so that your life and work increasingly reflect a growing love for God, God’s Word, God’s people of every ethnicity and culture, and God’s purposes in the world. To do this, you will: 

  • Pursue a vibrant relationship with the triune God through engagement with Scripture, prayer, and worship, both individually and in community

  • Develop self-leadership (growing in self-awareness, self-management, relational integrity, and resiliency) 

  • Embrace Scriptural standards for behavior and attitudes 

 

Campus Leadership 

As a Campus Staff Minister, you increase the number of witnessing communities, as well as the size, health, spiritual maturity, and campus-wide influence of existing witnessing communities of students and faculty by being a: 

  • Visionary Guide: 

You communicate and model InterVarsity’s vision to see students and faculty transformed, campuses renewed, and world changers developed 

  • Create a culture of humble dependence on God and bold expectation in God’s intention to start new witnessing communities throughout the campus and on new campuses 

  • Model – in person and through programs – InterVarsity’s vision and Core Values, including a biblically-defined commitment to engage every ethnic and social group on campus 

  • Lead students and faculty – individually and collectively – through Scripture, prayer, teaching, and discipleship experiences, so that they articulate and align their ministry activities around this vision 

  • Set annual goals through prayer, research and reflection with your teams (students, faculty, and staff) for qualitative and quantitative growth, including conversions and leadership development 

  • Structural Architect: 

You create, develop, align, and leverage ministry plans, programs, teams, and structures to close the gap between current reality and the aspirational goals. 

  • Build leadership teams who trust and partner well with you and who demonstrate spiritual vitality, relational health, and mission alignment 

  • Develop and execute plans to achieve annual goals, evaluating and modifying the plan as needed throughout the year 

  • Increase momentum for the vision by aligning programs, structures, conferences, and teams around the goals 

  • Mobilize students and faculty to engage their relational networks with the gospel and to start new missional communities 

  • Under the direction of the Area Director, may supervise Ministry Interns and Campus Ministry Interns as delegated 

  • Missional Developer: 

You intentionally gather, invite, and develop diverse groups of students and faculty so that they not only encounter and follow Jesus as Savior and Lord but also advance the mission on campus as participants and leaders. 

  • Create ways for faculty and students to encounter and follow Jesus through Scripture, worship, prayer, mission experiences, conferences, etc. 

  • Equip students and faculty so that they think strategically about campus engagement and so that they proclaim – in word, deed, and power – the good news of Jesus, regularly inviting students and faculty to follow him as Savior and Lord 

  • Disciple students and faculty by equipping them to hear the Word, respond actively, and debrief and interpret the experience so that they grow in Christlikeness, reflect our Core Values, and develop ministry skills 

  • Invite, coach, and equip students and faculty to become increasingly effective participants and leaders, including starting new witnessing communities on campuses 

 

Organizational Collaboration 

As a Campus Staff Minister, you have joined a national mission. Therefore, you work with a network of other local, area, regional, and national InterVarsity staff and volunteers so that our work reflects Biblical standards of excellence, integrity, and partnership. 

  • Partner with and respond positively to the direction and coaching of your supervisors and national leaders 

  • Contribute to collaborative and productive team meetings and relationships

Church Pastor - Colonial Village Church

 

This is a full-time position for a visionary spiritual leader to partner, guide and shepherd Colonial Village Church as we reach out to our community to share the Good News of Christ with the vision that God has given us.  This is a solo pastor position.

Colonial Village Church is a small, tight-knit community of faith outside of Niagara Falls, NY.  Formed in 1943, Colonial Village Church has been serving the small community of Colonial Village for over 80 years.  We joined the Evangelical Presbyterian Church in 2015 after we were dismissed from the PCUSA with our property.

When our last pastor moved on to another call in late 2023, our session began the Revitalization process through our Presbytery.  Working with the guidance of our coach, they developed a Vision for our church that we presented to the congregation and are diligently moving forward implementing.  While we are an older congregation, we are actively engaged in ministry opportunities outside of the church with the Niagara Gospel Mission and The Potters Field Ministry (for local at-risk children). We also partner with a Christian Counseling office that is located within the church.  Worship on Sunday mornings is accompanied by active Ladies’ and Men’s bible studies before the service, and a Special Needs accessible Children’s Church during the service.

 

Our Mission Statement:

“We are a Fellowship of God’s people who glorify Christ in Growth, Love and Service to All”

 

The ideal candidate will have a love for God and his Word, skilled in expository preaching and teaching, and a gift for encouraging the congregation to discipleship and evangelism.

 

Responsibilities and expectations include:

Ordained or eligible to be ordained in The Evangelical Presbyterian Church (EPC).  Seminary graduate minimally required

It would be expected that our pastor be an example of the ethical life that we are called to live in Jesus Christ. 

Within the congregation we expect the pastor to work with the various committees of the session and give guidance where needed. We desire that a strong relationship be developed with all church staff. We are looking for an individual who works well with people of all ages and backgrounds.

Our Pastor should be an effective communicator of the written and spoken word. The person would be expected to plan and lead weekly worship along with the assistance of our current worship music leaders and provide sound biblical preaching.

Hospital calls and home communions are a very important aspect of our church life and should be done on an as needed basis. The ability to find ways to interact with the members of the congregation is also an important attribute.

Should also feel comfortable reaching out to the community and working alongside the men and women of the church in evangelism. A current example of such efforts would be helping to expand our relationship and work with Niagara Gospel Mission, located in Niagara Falls, NY.

We desire that our next pastor would encourage and equip the congregation to use their God given gifts for ministry both in the church and in the community. We want to walk together with our pastor as we reach out into our community and do the work that Jesus is calling us to do.

We believe that our pastor should be involved in the work of the Presbytery of the Alleghenies, especially with the EPC churches in the Western New York area. This would include being a part of the Western New York Ministry Network made up of other EPC pastors in our area.

ABOUT WOODDALE CHURCH

Wooddale Church is a multigenerational, Bible-teaching church in Minnesota with campuses in Eden Prairie, Edina and the University of Minnesota. With a mission to honor God by making more disciples for Jesus Christ, Wooddale has a rich history and a future of sharing the gospel locally and globally by planting churches, supporting global partners and serving its local community.

OVERVIEW

The Traditional Worship Pastor provides vision, spiritual leadership, and musical direction for the traditional worship ministry at Wooddale Church’s Eden Prairie campus. This ministry includes shepherding and conducting Woodale’s Choir and Orchestra. This leader cultivates a culture of worship that values excellence, equips people to use their gifts, and leads our congregation to worship God fully. The role partners closely with the Senior Pastor and Executive Pastor of Weekend Experience, serves on the Weekend Experience Team, and collaborates with the Modern Worship Director to cultivate a unified culture of worship.

 RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Provide vision and direction for traditional worship and service planning, partnering with the Executive Pastor of Weekend Experience, Senior Pastor and Modern Worship Director to create Biblical, excellent and God-honoring services. 
  • Prayerfully plan the order of service for the weekly Traditional service at Wooddale Church in alignment with the Executive Pastor of Weekend Experience and the Senior Pastor. 
  • Champion a culture of worship which includes thoughtful preparation, strong musicianship, and intentional leadership that honors God and supports Wooddale’s mission.
  • Shepherd and lead the volunteer choir musically and spiritually. Cultivate a community of worshippers through prayer, care, discipleship and musical development. Recruit and develop singers and volunteer leadership teams. 
  • Build and sustain a broad roster of skilled orchestral musicians through recruitment, intentional relationships, and ongoing development. Lead the orchestra to enrich weekend services and holiday services in God-honoring worship as a community. 
  • Serve on the Weekend Experience Team and partner with the Modern Worship Director and Production team to advance a unified vision for worship and contribute to shared services and shared ministry or all-church endeavors. 
  • Plan and execute with excellence the annual Christmas at Wooddale Concerts featuring the choir, orchestra and special guests to reach our community with the gospel.
  • Steward the Traditional Worship Budget to align resources with ministry priorities and goals. 
  • Prepare, plan and execute biannual choir tour in alignment with the mission and values of Wooddale Church. 
  • Serve as a member of Wooddale’s Pastoral staff including providing pastoral congregational engagement, care, on-call responsibilities, funerals and weddings as requested. 

 QUALIFICATIONS

  • Active and growing faith in Jesus. Demonstrated character and calling to vocational ministry.
  • Subscribe to and affirm the Statement of Faith and Covenant of Wooddale Church.
  • Be a regular participant in public worship at Wooddale Church.
  • Become or remain a member in good standing of Wooddale Church.
  • Proven leadership in traditional worship, including strong choral and orchestral conducting skills, service planning and knowledge of sacred music and hymnody.
  • Specific gifting in congregational worship leadership. 
  • A collaborative leader with excellent relational and communication skills and the ability to develop volunteers and professional musicians.
  • Master’s degree in music, theology, ministry or a related field, Doctoral degree preferred. 

RELATIONSHIPS

  • Reports to: Executive Pastor of Weekend Experience.
  • Serves as a member of: Weekend Experience Team.
  • Supervises: Traditional Administrative Assistant, volunteer leaders and musical contractors.
  • Partners collaboratively with ministry leaders to ensure a unified weekend experience.

WORK ENVIRONMENT/PHYSICAL DEMANDS

  • Ability to sit, stand, and walk for extended periods during the workday, including church services, meetings, and special events.
  • Ability to use coordinated arm, hand, and upper-body movements to direct musical ensembles.
  • Ability to read sheet music, musical scores, and written materials, including for extended periods. 
  • Ability to verbally demonstrate vocal techniques as needed. 
  • Ability to communicate effectively in person, by phone, and through video conferencing with staff, volunteers, and guests.
  • Ability to hear and speak clearly in both quiet office settings and large, crowded environments.
  • Ability to use a computer, keyboard, mouse, and other standard office equipment for prolonged periods.
  • Ability to occasionally lift, carry, push, or pull materials and equipment weighing up to 25 pounds, such as event supplies, signage, or hospitality materials.
  • Ability to bend, stoop, reach, kneel, and climb stairs as necessary to support ministry activities and event setup.
  • Ability to work a flexible schedule, including evenings, weekends, holidays, and extended hours during church services, conferences, and special events.
  • Ability to maintain the stamina and mobility necessary to oversee multiple activities simultaneously in a fast-paced ministry environment.

EXPECTED WORK HOURS & TRAVEL

  • Typical schedule includes weekday hours, Thursday evening choir practices, as well as weekly Sunday morning responsibilities.
  • Evening, weekend, and extended hours as holiday and other events require.
  • Requires the ability to occasionally commute to and work from other campuses as needed.

Job Description

EXECUTIVE PASTOR  - Job Description

Full-Time | Reports to: Senior Pastor


About Bayou City Fellowship

Bayou City Fellowship is a gospel-centered church committed to being radically focused on

Jesus, serving our city and the world, and starting new churches. We are a multi-campus

church located in the Houston area with a heart for prayer, discipleship, community, and

Mission.


Position Summary

The Executive Pastor will help the Senior Pastor manage the operational & organizational

aspects of the church. The role may be summarized as one that strengthens and

implements existing operational practices, establishes new systems, processes and

practices where necessary, and facilitates effective ministry to ensure that our mission is

carried out with excellence and humility. There is also an aspect of the pastoral function

that is inherent in this role and therefore, this role may be viewed as one that provides

operational leadership through a pastoral framework to create a healthy, growing, and

spiritually vibrant church. The Executive Pastor will provide operational leadership for both

tactical and strategic aspects of the ministry. While the Executive Pastor will be expected

to attend all global elder meetings, he will not be a member of the elder board. Our

preference is for the Executive Pastor to be based out of the Spring Branch campus.


Primary Responsibilities

Alignment with Vision & Culture

• Champion Bayou City Fellowship’s mission:

Radically focused on Jesus. Serving our city and the world. Starting new churches.

• Model servant leadership, humility, and faithfulness in all areas of ministry.

• Guard unity and foster a culture of prayer, discipleship and generosity.


Strategic Leadership

• Work with the Senior Pastor to develop church-wide and campus-specific strategic

plans.

• Lead the execution / implementation of strategic plans.

• Identify areas for improvement and implement effective ministry systems, processes

and practices.

• Support the launch of new ministry initiatives, outreach opportunities, and

discipleship pathways.

• Collaborate with the Senior Pastor to identify & track meaningful metrics, evaluate

ministry effectiveness, and plan for future growth.

• Interface with the Elder Board to ensure elder governance & oversight while

enabling sufficient autonomy and creative freedom for pastoral and operational

staff.


Operations & Administration

• Oversee central support teams & functions (Finance, HR, Communications, Facilities,

IT), ensuring that they are effective in supporting ministry

• Manage operations to enable collaboration among campuses and ministries to

accomplish the church’s mission

• Help plan and participate in Leadership Team meeting to ensure that they are

productive

• Help plan and organize monthly all-staff meetings

• Develop/Refine/Improve processes as necessary to ensure stewardship of

resources, reduced complexity and improved simplicity.

• Cultivate a healthy & cohesive team culture of trust, accountability, transparency and

grace.

• Work with the direct-report staff to enable them to focus & flourish to their full

potential, serving with their gifts and capabilities.

• Guide and direct implementation of staff performance reviews and development

plans.


Qualifications

Spiritual

• A mature, growing relationship with Jesus Christ marked by humility, integrity, and a heart

for prayer.

• Commitment to Scripture, servant leadership, and shepherding the local church.

• Alignment with the theological convictions and culture of Bayou City Fellowship.


Professional

• 7+ years of operational leadership in a Christian ministry setting, preferably a

church. Experience with a multi-campus church setting is desirable.

• Proven ability to lead teams, develop leaders, and manage complex systems.

• Strong administrative, organizational, and interpersonal communication skills.

• Ability to balance relational warmth with operational excellence.

• Master’s Degree Preferred

The Christ Center Chinese Alliance Church is located in the town of Davie, Florida, between Fort Lauderdale and Miami. Close to beautiful beaches, resorts, golf courses, museums, and shopping, Davie hosts a fast-growing population. This 25 member congregation is seeking a part-time Lead Pastor, possibly bi-vocational, to provide spiritual leadership and pastoral care. The church desires a leader who will move the church towards greater discipleship and evangelism resulting in spiritual growth and community outreach.

The Christ Center Chinese Alliance Church is a multi-lingual congregation that speaks Cantonese, Mandarin, and English. The ideal candidate must be able to preach in Mandarin, but the ability to communicate in Cantonese and English is a plus. In addition, the candidate must be able to meet licensing and ordination requirements with The Christian & Missionary Alliance.

To inquire about this position, please send your resume to Michelle Hill at office@alliancese.org.

Please do not contact the church directly.

Position Description

Cornerstone Alliance Church (CAC) is currently seeking a candidate who feels called to serve in an Associate Pastor of Worship role that focuses on a deep desire to lead the church into the presence of God through worship. This role will include some pastoral responsibilities such as outreach, shepherding, counseling, teaching, and leading depending on the giftedness, calling, and education of the applicant. As a growing church of approximately 400 attendees, we have lots of service opportunities in an exciting time of expansion. The candidate should be able to express a calling to serve in a medium sized, rural Iowa community of 13,000 people.

This is a full time position. Salary commensurate with experience.

CAC will use the term “pastor” for this position if and when a staff member meets elder qualifications, completes ordination requirements, and is appointed as an elder.

Qualifications for the Position

  • A mature Christian modeling I Timothy 3:1-7 (Elder qualities) and Galatians 5:22-23 (Fruit of the Spirit) character.
  • A passion for ministry and an ability to articulate God’s calling.
  • Proven ability to recruit and lead an adult volunteer staff.
  • Effective in communicating God's Word to a wide range of audiences.
  • Working knowledge of and ability to use technology in necessary areas.
  • Accredited Official Worker of the C&MA.
  • Licensed or willing to be licensed by The Christian and Missionary Alliance. (see https://madcma.org/steps-to-getting-licensed/ for more information)
  • Agreement with The Christian & Missionary Alliance doctrine and mission.
  • Prior ministry experience and education preferred.

Primary Responsibilities

  • Coordinate and lead adult worship teams for Sunday services.
  • Develop, support, and encourage worship team volunteers through training and Bible study.
  • Be willing to be trained by the lead pastor to do wedding services and funerals for congregants.
  • Collaborate and serve with all ministry staff.
  • Coordinate with the Lead Pastor and Elder board in the development of discipleship in the assigned area of responsibility.
  • Participate in Sunday morning responsibilities as assigned.
  • Participate in pulpit supply when requested.
  • Participate in staff meetings and pastoral functions as assigned by the Lead Pastor.
  • Attend and serve at “all-church” events.
  • Attend monthly board meetings.
  • Attend bi-weekly elder meetings once the title of “pastor” has been given.
  • Reports to the Lead Pastor
  • Accountable to Lead Pastor and CAC Elders on all ministry initiatives

Cornerstone Alliance Church Mission

Mission Statement

“Cornerstone Church exists to boldly proclaim the gospel of Jesus Christ, to share His love with others, and to be a beacon of hope in our community for His glory.”

Vision Statement

“Our vision is to be a church fully surrendered to the mission of Jesus, to be and make disciples who are equipped and empowered to push back the darkness with the light and Love of Christ, to train up workers for the harvest fields, and send them out in the power of the Holy Spirit.”

To be considered for this position, please complete the application to include your testimony, resume and other background information related to the position.

This position requires licensing with The Christian & Missionary Alliance. To learn more about The Alliance and requirements for licensing, please visit our website

job_name: Children's Director - The Hills Community Church
post_html:
Children's Director - The Hills Community Church
 
  At The Hills our mission is to lead anyone and everyone into a life-changing relationship with Jesus.  

This position is perfect for someone who is looking for a way to make an impact in the lives of kids and their families! The Hills Kids Director leads a team of 30 volunteers consisting of 7-10 per week who create unforgettable experiences for kids every week at The Hills Community Church. The Hills Kids ministry has fluctuated from 15-30 kids. We've built a strong system that you will lead full of leaders and amazing volunteers who teach, lead, and disciple our kids together. 

Sunday Mornings: the Hills Kids Director will oversee the set up, execution, and tear down of Hills Kids for our portable church environment that happens every Sunday at Double Peak School in San Marcos. 

Wednesday Nights: One of the responsibilities of our new Hills Kids Director is to create a Wednesday night experience for kids to learn scripture and grow in their relationship with Jesus. 

Service Opportunities: the Hills Kids Director helps empower kids and their families to serve at the schools, in the community, and even on mission trips. This has looked like mission trips to Tijuana to an orphanage, taking a team to Brooklyn for a mission trip, serving meals to teachers at our local schools, beach days, park days, and helping with work days at local non-profits.

Hills Kids Camp: Every Summer the entire church comes together to put on the most fun week of the year with Hills Kids Camp! Over 140 people are involved (kids and adults), and the entire church comes alongside the kids director to make this the most amazing experience for kids!

The Hills Kids Director is someone who loves kids, has a gift for connecting with them, and can help train up other leaders to connect, teach, and disciple kids. The ideal candidate is a kid magnet--someone who is always connecting with kids and engaging them. You will also need to be a recruiting machine! If you have a hard time recruiting people to help you with something, this job will be impossible. 

The Hills staff and leadership will be fully available to help, train, and empower the Hills Kids Director in every way. We will help raise the funds to accomplish your ministry goals, we will meet with the Kid's Director regularly and help build up the team of volunteers, and we will help the Kid's Director's dream and vision in order to take our kids ministry to the next level! 

This is a part-time position for 20 hours per week that will pay $21-25 per hour. There will not be medical or retirement benefits at this time, but for the right person we will offer vacation.

Sunday Morning 7:00am-12:30pm
Monday Staff Meeting 1:00-2:30pm
Wednesday Night 6:00-9:00pm
Weekly One on One with Pastor - 1 Hour

Description

The Chancery Office of the Diocese of Jefferson City is hiring an Associate Director of Youth and Young Adult Ministry. This role provides leadership for diocesan outreach, evangelization, and faith formation efforts serving youth and young adults. This role equips and accompanies parish and campus ministry leaders, coordinates diocesan programs and initiatives, and promotes opportunities for youth and young adults to encounter Jesus Christ, grow in their Catholic faith, and become missionary disciples.


Duties and Responsibilities

  • Foster a positive, collaborative, and healthy work environment consistent with the mission and vision of the Bishop.
  • Develop and implement a vision for youth and young adult ministry that advances evangelization, faith formation, and missionary discipleship in alignment with diocesan pastoral priorities.
  • Encourage, equip, and connect parish youth ministers, campus ministers, and young adult ministry leaders through individual accompaniment, mentoring, parish and campus visits, and regular communication.
  • Provide consultation, resources, and support to pastors and parish leaders as they assess and respond to the pastoral needs of youth and young adults.
  • Design, supervise, and implement faith-based programs and initiatives that foster an integral formation and address the needs of youth and young adults, such as retreats, conferences, leadership development opportunities, workshops, service/mission opportunities, and discipleship formation in support of parish efforts. Programs may be offered at the deanery, diocesan, regional, national, and international levels, and currently include NCYC, SEEK, and summer camps.
  • Collaborate with the Director of Safe Environment to ensure diocesan youth ministry programs comply with safe environment policies and to support their consistent implementation in parishes.
  • Collaborate within the department to provide regular leadership training programs, ministry workshops, and retreats for all those in ministry, serving as liaison for those working in youth and young adult faith formation.
  • Support and collaborate with the Office of Hispanic Ministry to engage Hispanic/Latino youth and young adults in a spirit of integration and pastoral de conjunto, as envisioned by the U.S. bishops.

Qualifications

  • Active Catholic in good standing with passion for sharing the Catholic Faith with young people and forming others in this endeavor.
  • Bachelor or Masters Degree in Theology, Pastoral Ministry, Youth Ministry, Religious Education or similar field

post_html:
PURPOSE:
To engage newcomers to Germany with the Gospel, with the purpose of developing diverse, locally-rooted, and globally-connected congregations and members who are equipped to faithfully proclaim and live out the good news of Jesus.

This position will remain open until filled.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES:


ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES include the following:

Local Discipleship and Church Planting Ministry
  1. Discover and develop ways to share the whole Gospel in a manner that is effective, meaningful, and culturally appropriate to the people and place.
  2. Develop trusting relationships with non-believers and help them discern and take the next steps in their faith journey.
  3. Disciple new believers individually and in small group settings to deepen their faith, expand their engagement with Scripture, and increase their ability to share their faith with others.
  4. Identify and nurture emerging leaders, equipping them for formal and informal leadership
  5. Work toward launching a new multicultural congregation in Berlin in which the common language is Basic German (i.e., a mono-multicultural church).
  6. Work in partnership with and within the structure of the Berliner Stadtmission (Berlin City Mission).
  7. Collaborate actively with local and international (Resonate) church planting communities of practice for mutual learning and growth.
Leadership Support and Development
  1. Build long-term relationships with national Christian leaders, churches, and organizations that share a vision for missional living and Gospel outreach to diverse groups, including the poor and marginalized.
  2. Support emerging leaders through prayer, mentoring, and pastoral relationships to foster their emotional and spiritual health in ministry.
  3. Use interactive training methods to equip local leaders and young adults to serve and share the Gospel in their communities.
Service to North America
  1. Participate in support-raising (e.g., prayer, care, and financial support) for Resonate Global Mission’s ministries by developing and maintaining a network of supporting churches and individuals in North America.
  2. Educate the CRCNA and others about the nature of the global church and its mission, encouraging them to develop a deeper passion and involvement in global missions.
  3. Provide the CRCNA with insight and resources for ministry among minority groups living in North America.
  4. Communicate the nature and impact of Resonate Global Mission’s ministries to the CRCNA and others through written communications and preaching/speaking engagements.

SKILLS, KNOWLEDGE & EXPERTISE:


QUALIFICATIONS
  1. Professing membership in a Christian Reformed congregation, or of a church in communion with the CRCNA, and agreement with the doctrine of the church signified by signing a covenant statement.
  2. Demonstrated commitment to Gospel witness and the integral word and deed mission of the church as expressed in Resonate’s foundational documents. Commitment to living out the Resonate postures of prayer, listening, serving, learning, mutual care and accountability, and peacemaking.
  3. Demonstrated affinity and passion for ministering among people of different sociocultural backgrounds, including the poor and marginalized.
  4. Commitment to develop fluency in German.
  5. Demonstrated effective cross-cultural and interreligious awareness and capabilities.
  6. Demonstrated ability to listen well and empower others for Gospel witness and ministry.
  7. Proven capacity to be creative and innovative in complex situations without a predetermined map.
  8. Self-motivated and proven quality administrative and organizational skills.
  9. Ability to travel to and from North America periodically.

EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE
  1. M.Div. or equivalent. Commitment to further theological study as appropriate.
  2. At least three years of practical ministry experience in contexts where crossing racial, ethnic, or other social barriers was necessary.
  3. Previous experience and participation in and/or leadership of new expressions of church preferred.
  4. Training in spiritual formation and a demonstrated commitment to interactive learning are preferred.

PHYSICAL DEMANDS
The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

WORK ENVIRONMENT
The work environment characteristics described here are representative of those an employee encounters while performing the essential functions of this job.

***Position Stages****
The successful candidate for this position will start as a Missionary in Training before fully transitioning to the Career Missionary role.

Stage #1 Missionary in Training:
The purpose of this position is to prepare for international service. In this role, the employee will develop language and cultural skills, ministry expertise, and build a network of relationships for prayer, care, and financial support in North America that will enable future ministry. One can expect to remain in this stage for 6 to 18 months, depending on how quickly the support network comes together and their prior background and experience. Typically, this position is a full-time role. The pay range for this position is based on the US or Canadian domestic pay scale.

Stage #2 Career Missionary:
When the missionary is ready to completely assume the duties in their job description, they transition to the Career Missionary role, which is located in their country of service. This position is full-time. The pay range is based on the US or Canadian international pay scale.

post_html:
Pastor of Student Ministry

Eagan Hills Church is a Spirit-led community that seeks to glorify God by humbly following Jesus and making more disciples. Student Ministry serves students grades 6-12 by creating a welcoming community where they experience belonging, hear the Gospel, grow in their faith, and are equipped to follow Jesus in every area of life. The ministry currently averages approximately 50 students on Wednesday evenings and is committed to building authentic relationships, Biblical-discipleship, and meaningful partnerships with families.

The ministry is in a season of rebuilding and presents an exciting opportunity for a relational leader to strengthen volunteer teams, invest in students and families, and help shape the next chapter of student ministry at Eagan Hills. The Pastor of Student Ministries is a full-time pastoral position that provides vision, leadership, and oversight for this ministry.

To apply, please email a cover letter and resume to office@eaganhills.org

Summary

The Pastor of Student Ministries provides vision, leadership, and pastoral oversight for ministry to students in grades 6-12. This position is responsible for recruiting, training, equipping, and shepherding a team of volunteer leaders who disciple students through authentic relationships, Biblical teaching, and a Christlike example. Working alongside these leaders, the Pastor of Student Ministries cultivates a safe, welcoming, and Christ-centered community where students experience belonging, hear the Gospel, grow in their faith, and are equipped to become lifelong disciples of Jesus.

Responsible To

  • Reports to the Lead Pastor and follows the organizational structure.

Essential Job Functions

Leadership & Programming

  • Provide leadership for all Student Ministry programs (6th - 12th Grade), including weekly youth group, weekly small groups, retreats, mission trips, and other related events and ongoing ministries.
  • Design and develop activities with students that cultivate a fun, safe, and welcoming environment where youth can grow in relationship with others and with Jesus.
  • Select or prepare curriculum for High School & Middle School including a scope and sequence to develop mature student disciples.
  • Prepare for scheduled meetings that include devotions, worship, interactive discussions, and outreach activities.
  • Encourage youth participation in service, serving opportunities, and mission projects.
  • Preach and teach as assigned in rotation for Sunday services.

Volunteer & Family Engagement

  • Recruit, train, equip, schedule and support a team of volunteer leaders to shepherd students and families.
  • Connect with and support parents through effective communication and meaningful participation.
  • Build a true team culture with volunteers to ensure volunteer retention and connection.
  • Pray for youth and their families, and support them through highs and lows, even family crises as they may arise.
  • Promote, model, and uphold standards for healthy ministry practice including physical safety, child safety, integrity, transparency, and Christ-like character.

Administration & Operations

  • Maintain accurate records of youth group members, track attendance, and keep family information current.
  • Maintain Student Ministry spaces in good order.
  • Work in developing and maintaining the annual budget for Student Ministry.
  • Attend weekly staff meetings and regularly scheduled 1:1’s with supervisor.
  • Ensure policies are understood and followed by staff, volunteers, and students.
  • Additional ministry-related duties as assigned.

Requirements

  • Strong and growing Christian testimony with a vibrant personal relationship with Jesus Christ.
  • Proven experience in Student Ministries or a related ministry leadership role.
  • Proven ability to recruit, train, equip, and lead volunteer ministry teams.
  • Demonstrated ability to teach and proclaim Biblical truth in a way that engages students and encourages spiritual growth.
  • Self-starter with excellent organizational, communication, and interpersonal skills.
  • Spirit of perseverance, creativity, flexibility, and enthusiasm.
  • Ability to work in a team-oriented atmosphere.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office and the ability to learn and use additional software. Experience with church management software, Planning Center, is a plus.
  • Bachelor’s degree in Christian ministry, Biblical studies, or a related field preferred.
  • Agreement with Scripture, Eagan Hills Church Statement of Faith and Bylaws, and C&MA doctrine.
  • Is willing and eligible for membership at Eagan Hills Church.
  • Credentialed by the Christian & Missionary Alliance, or willing and eligible to pursue C&MA licensing and/or ordination.

Compensation and Benefits

  • Salary range: $47,000-64,000 annually.
  • Health Care stipend: $6,000 annually
  • 401K Employer match
  • PTO

To apply, please email a cover letter and resume to office@eaganhills.org

Competencies

Work Environment/Physical Demands

Ministerial Exception

The ministerial exception furthers the purposes of the Free Exercise and Establishment Clauses of the First Amendment by barring legal claims against church bodies by staff members who perform religious functions. All church pastors are subject to the exception, but a formal ministerial credential is not required. While there is no rigid formula to determine other church staff members that qualify, various factors are considered to determine which staff members are subject to the ministerial exception (please see handbook).

Staff members who qualify under the ministerial exception are not covered by federal and state employment and anti-discrimination laws. Please see the Human Resources Ministry team if you have questions on whether you are subject to the ministerial exception.

Code of Conduct

  5. We aim for excellence in the experience with zero excess
  6. We choose to trust
  7. We pray 1st and decide 2nd

  9. Our team unites under clear vision
  10. We walk in humble confidence

EEO Statement

The Church of Eleven22 provides equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants for employment and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any type without regard to race, color, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status or any other characteristic protected by federal, state or local laws. The Church of Eleven22 reserves the right to discriminate on the basis of religion to the full extent permitted by law.

General Responsibilities:

  • Coordinate the design of an overall stewardship strategy in accordance with St. Paul’s fundraising goals.
  • Execute the annual stewardship plan with staff, Vestry and volunteers, including donor identification, cultivation, solicitation and recognition.
  • Create a donor culture by taking the lead to engage all staff and vestry members as well as focusing members and volunteers on fundraising goals and activities.
  • Participate in department budgeting and monitor progress against goals, including producing monthly reports and analyses of statistics for purposes of tracking and monitoring results, and improving performance.
  • Direct and expand St. Paul’s Planned Giving initiative, including coordinating prospective planned gift donors, volunteer committee members, and activities related to cultivation and solicitation.
  • Coordinate and manage all online gifts and funds as deemed appropriate with other stewardship efforts, including but not limited to ECW fundraising, Easter Offerings, Summer Enrichment fundraisers, etc.  
  • Partner with the Director of Communications to develop annual and ongoing stewardship communications by mail, email, social media, and newsletters, including donor stories whenever possible in messaging for these communications and on the website.
  • Recruit and manage annual stewardship chairs in conjunction with the Rector.
  • Enlist and manage annual stewardship volunteer committee.
  • Oversee the planning and implementation of stewardship events, including monthly Gratitude Gatherings, Listening Lunches with Rector, Parish Fair, Campaign Closure Celebration, and others as created.
  • Manage and oversee donor database to ensure that gifts are entered correctly, and donor information is current.
  • Track and supervise all special giving at St. Paul’s. This includes, but is not limited to, memorial gifts, Easter Memorials, Christmas Memorials, and matured planned gifts.
  • Coordinate and direct the parish fair in August.
  • Perform other job activities as directed by the Rector.

The qualified candidate will be a data-driven and donor-centered fundraiser who thrives in a highly cross-functional, flexible, and relational culture. Essential experience includes working with volunteer leaders and high-level prospects.

Qualifications

The ideal candidate will have:

  • Understanding of the Winston-Salem community
  • At least three years of proven fundraising experience
  • Knowledge of and appreciation for church and church culture
  • Bachelor's degree in a related field or equivalent
  • Donor database experience preferred with familiarity in ACS being highly desirable
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Word, MS Excel
  • Ability to learn new applications quickly

Crucial knowledge and skills for this role include strong interpersonal and written/verbal communication skills; flexibility as a team player who believes in excellent customer service; the ability to manage multiple projects, to work independently and to take initiative on new projects; a high degree of organization and attention to detail; and discretion in handling confidential information. Strong project management skills are essential. 

Additional Information

St. Paul’s Episcopal Church is working with Capital Development Services (CapDev) to conduct a search for this position. Candidates are required to submit a cover letter and a resume. All materials will be kept confidential. Additional inquiries may be directed to [email protected].
company_description: About St. Paul’s: “A House of Prayer for All People” These words are carved in stone over our front door, and they encapsulate the mission St. Paul’s is trying to live up to every day. We believe that “all” means “all,” and as a result, what you will find here is a really diverse group of people. The congregation at St. Paul’s comes from different upbringings, socio-economic backgrounds, denominational histories, political opinions, ages, ethnicities, identities, and college basketball allegiances. What this makes St. Paul’s is a really big tent. Yet, the thing that unites us in all that diversity is the lordship of Jesus Christ and our common worship. Leading this community is a staff team of talented people who work hard to cultivate a healthy work culture of collaboration, excellence, rest, and joy. We need someone to join us who knows how to be playful and professional, sweats the details, and likes to laugh.

The Salvation Army Mission Statement:

The Salvation Army, an international movement, is an evangelical part of the universal Christian church.  Its message is based on the Bible.  Its ministry is motivated by the love of God.  Its mission is to preach the gospel of Jesus Christ and to meet human needs in His name without discrimination.

Salary Range Starting at: $28,121.60/ annually 

Job Objective:

As the Ministry Discovery Intern, you will observe and participate in the leadership of all aspects of corps ministry ensuring that the Mission of The Salvation Army is effectively carried out.  

What You Will Do:

  • Participate in Worship and Christian education programs (Sunday School, Bible Studies, Corps Cadets, Small Groups etc.,) including planning, leading meetings, preaching, teaching, and supporting others in those roles.
  • Participate in and coordinate, as assigned, the development of corps programming, worship arts, music programs, special programming (VBS, Day Camps, Outreaches), Character Building and Leadership Training for corps members.
  • Represent the Army at community events.
  • Support social services as needed including food pantry, financial assistance, and Pathway of Hope.
  • Assist in coordinating seasonal programs including Christmas Kettles, Angel Tree, Summer Day Camp and other special events.
  • Participate in pastoral and evangelistic ministries including Pastoral Care Council, Corps Council and Youth and Adult Planning Committees.
  • Property upkeep and facility preparation for programming.
  • Participate in corps financial goals by observing budget and support of fundraising efforts and thrift store operations.
  • Other tasks as assigned by leadership

Minimum Qualifications: The requirements listed below are representative of the minimal education, experience, skills, and/or abilities required for this position.

Education: High School Diploma required, Bachelor’s Degree preferred.

Background Checks: Position requires a background check to be completed and all background check results will be reviewed.

Experience: One year membership with The Salvation Army.

Certifications: Must have a valid driver’s license and maintain The Salvation Army Driver’s qualification standard; must complete Safe from Harm training within the first 90 days of employment.  

Skills/Abilities: 

  • Able to speak, write and understand English in a manner sufficient for effective communication with leadership, field personnel, and clientele
  • Computer proficiency with Microsoft products and ability to learn electronic reporting systems

Supervisory Responsibility: None

The physical requirements described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the duties of this job. Reasonable accommodation may be made to enable individuals to perform the essential functions of this job. 

Physical Requirements Include:

  • Good speaking, hearing and vision ability, and excellent manual dexterity
  • Lifting, pulling, and pushing of materials up to 25 pounds
  • May require bending, squatting, walking
  • May require standing for extended periods

Travel: Position will require occasional travel for training and events.

Working Conditions: Work is performed in a office, store, and church environment; Will require some weekend and evening work.

All employees recognize that The Salvation Army is a church and agree that they will do nothing as an employee of The Salvation Army to undermine its religious mission.

The Salvation Army is an equal opportunity employer. Candidates who are back-to-work, US Veterans, people with disabilities, people who have been impacted by the justice system, and/or people without a college degree are encouraged to apply.

This job description should not be interpreted as all inclusive. It is intended to identify the essential functions and requirements of the position. Other job-related responsibilities and tasks may be assigned.  Reasonable accommodation may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential job functions.



Why Work with Us?

If you’re ready for a career doing meaningful work with a discernable impact, keep reading. The Salvation Army’s brand promise is to Do the Most Good® - and it’s our employees that help us get there. At every level and in every discipline, you can have a real impact on your community through the work done inside our walls every day. If you work for us, you will be the hands and feet that enable us to help others.

We are as impassioned about our employees as we are about our mission to preach the Gospel of Jesus Christ and help anyone in need in His name without discrimination. Our work culture reflects this quality, which makes our offices seriously great places to work. Just walk inside our doors and you’ll quickly see that our employees are proud to support programs that make a difference.

In addition to traditional Health, Wellness, RX and PTO benefits, see what our employees told us they most liked about working for the Indiana Division of TSA by responding to our most recent 2023 survey…

  • 91% are proud of their work to help meet the needs of people in their communities
  • 75% find their “Work Stress” manageable
  • 80% find their managers supportive during those times of stress
  • 89% appreciate the flexible work options they have in their position
  • 98% appreciate how they are allowed to use 4 sicks days as “Discretionary”
  • 99% appreciate the 11 paid holidays they receive each year

See what our employees said when asked to rank the best reasons for working at the Indiana Division Salvation Army…

  1. Helping People
  2. Faith Centered Organization
  3. Work Environment/ Co-Workers
  4. Benefits

Overview

Lifeway is seeking a Worship Technical Specialist to serve as a key resource for Lifeway Worship, blending technical expertise with a heart for ministry to support churches and worship teams across the country. In this role, you will manage digital and physical worship assets, provide advanced technical support for LifewayWorship.com, and collaborate with programmers, legal, and ministry leadership on strategic worship initiatives. This is a unique opportunity for someone who understands both the technical and ministry dimensions of worship resource development and wants their work to have lasting impact in the local church. 

 

Why Lifeway? 

 

Lifeway is a place where you can bring your faith and work experience to join in the most important mission in the world: making disciples of Jesus Christ. Whether you’re a creator or storyteller, data guru or problem-solver, or anywhere in between, if you’re passionate about serving the church, we have a place for you. Lifeway has a strong Work from Anywhere (WFA) culture that is deeply focused on our mission and values. While headquartered in Nashville, TN, many of our positions are remote-eligible and have autonomy and flexibility with work hours. We provide equipment and resources to ensure team members have access to a productive and ergonomic workspace. We believe building relationships and community is essential to how we work together, so Lifeway hosts all-team meetings several times per year and provides travel for key team gatherings for remote-based team members. Full-time employees are eligible for enrollment in our comprehensive benefits plans including healthcare, vacation and sick time, holiday pay, care days, 401(k) plan, maternity and parental leave, adoption assistance, mission trip time, and more. If this sounds like a place where you would be excited to serve the kingdom of God, we would love for you to join our team.

 

Learn more about our culture at team.lifeway.com/culture-code 

 

This is a remote position in the U.S. with occasional travel to Nashville for in-person team gatherings. #LI-Remote 

 

 

Responsibilities

  • Lives out Lifeway’s mission and values, showing deep commitment to Kingdom work
  • Limited travel: 2-4 times per year, typically overnight
  • Provide advanced technical support for LifewayWorship.com via phone, chat, and email, resolving escalated issues for customers, church partners, and internal support teams 
  • Serve as the primary liaison for the Lifeway Worship Customer Service Teams channel, assisting Church Sales & Support Specialists with complex or escalated cases 
  • Investigate and resolve technical and product-related customer inquiries, maintaining a support spreadsheet to ensure timely follow-ups and accurate records 
  • Manage all digital and physical worship assets, including archive organization, duplication of physical masters, artwork development for vendor relationships, and custom audio edits for church sound systems 
  • Partner with the Legal team to ensure rights and royalties for worship assets are properly administered 
  • Coordinate shipping, tracking, and fulfillment of vendor orders and sample products in partnership with the Order Research team 
  • Oversee One Source administration for Canon accounts and manage Metro 2 mailing list memberships to maintain database accuracy 
  • Collaborate with programmers on regression testing, bug fixes, and feature support for LifewayWorship.com 
  • Support and lead new Lifeway Worship initiatives in partnership with the Project Team Leader, including content development and ministry partnerships 
  • Continuously evaluate and recommend improvements to technical support systems, digital resource management, and customer service processes 

Qualifications

Education

Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Digital Media, Music, or a related field, required 

Master's degree, not required

Advanced graduate degree (PhD, etc.), not required

 

Skills, Knowledge, & Experiences, required

  • Ability to travel to the Middle Tennessee area 2-4 times annually for team gatherings
  • 3+ years of experience in technical support, digital media, or a related field 
  • Experience in local church music ministry 
  • Experience in web design and development 
  • Technical troubleshooting and web platform support 
  • Digital asset management and organization 
  • Vendor coordination and order fulfillment 
  • Clear written and verbal communication across phone, chat, and email 

Actively involved in an evangelical Christian church

 

Skills, Knowledge, & Experiences, preferred 

  • Familiarity with rights and royalty administration for digital media 
  • Experience with regression testing or software QA processes 
  • Experience with audio editing for worship or church sound systems 
  • Background in content development for digital ministry platforms
