post_html:
Mary, Queen of Peace Catholic Church is looking for an Associate Director of Evangelization,
Engagement, and Adult Formation. This is a full-time position.

The Associate Director of Evangelization, Engagement, and Adult Formation works with the Director
to foster a culture of evangelization and intentional discipleship throughout the parish. This
pastoral team member helps create opportunities for people to encounter Jesus Christ, grow in their
relationship with Him and His Church, and become intentional missionary disciples.
The Associate Director supports and enhances existing evangelization and adult faith formation
initiatives, fosters small-group discipleship, equips lay leaders, and helps parishioners identify
and use their gifts in service to the Church. This individual collaborates with the Pastor,
Director, pastoral team, ministry leaders, and volunteers to further the mission of Mary, Queen of
Peace Catholic Church to foster life-changing encounters with Jesus.
As Associate Director of Evangelization, Engagement, and Adult Formation, the individual's behavior
is required to be consistent with the culture and core values of Mary, Queen of Peace Catholic
Church:

● Fundamentally Relational: As fundamentally relational beings, made in the image of our
relational God, we engage in relationships by being attentive and present to those we serve and
serve alongside.
● Mission Driven: We put the Lamb of God at the forefront of all that we do, aligning ourselves
to the collective mission of fostering life-changing encounters with Jesus.
● Innovatively Excellent: Ensuring quality and excellence, we transcend expectations by thinking
beyond the norm to meet the needs of today.


● Radically Hospitable: We are committed to radical hospitality, to be a place for doubters and
disciples, for people with deep questions and deep convictions; all have a home here with us.

Ministerial Character

The Pastor is the visible principle and foundation of unity in Mary, Queen of Peace Catholic
Church, which the Archbishop has entrusted to him. He makes Christ's mission present and enduring
in the parish. In order to fulfill his mission, the Pastor employs suitable, chosen collaborators
(clerics, religious, or laypeople). He shares with them his mission and entrusts various
responsibilities to them.
Positions employed at Mary, Queen of Peace Catholic Church help to extend the ministry of the
Pastor in particular ways as outlined in the job description. Therefore, the employee in this
position is closely connected to and assists the Pastor in the performance of his ministry and
thereby engages in ministry for the Church.

Job Summary

The Associate Director of Evangelization, Engagement, and Adult Formation assists the Director in
fostering a parish culture of evangelization, discipleship, engagement, and ongoing adult faith
formation. This pastoral team member supports the development, coordination, and enhancement of
initiatives that provide opportunities for parishioners to encounter Jesus Christ, grow as
disciples, build meaningful relationships, and become equipped to share their faith with others.
The Associate Director engages, equips, and empowers lay leaders; supports small groups, retreats,
adult faith formation, and other evangelization initiatives; and helps connect parishioners with
opportunities for formation, community, and service. The Associate Director also assists with the
administrative and logistical needs of Evangelization, Engagement, and Adult Formation programs,
events, and resources.

Essential Duties: (Overarching)

● Support and uphold the teachings of the Catholic Church and the mission of the parish in both
your professional and personal life.
● Act as a witness to Gospel values by modeling the teachings of the Roman Catholic Church.
● Continuously grow in your ministry by participating in professional and personal faith
formation.
● Foster a warm, Christ-centered welcome for all visitors and parishioners, demonstrating our
commitment to Radical Hospitality.
● Build relationships by being attentive and present to those served and those you serve
alongside, practicing our Fundamentally Relational value.


● Collaborate across departments and ministries with humility and openness, maintaining a
mission-first mindset.
● Seek opportunities to improve programs, systems, and processes in a spirit of Innovative
Excellence.
● Recruit, equip, and support volunteers and lay leaders involved in Evangelization, Engagement,
and Adult Formation initiatives.
● Collaborate with the Director of Communications and Media to promote Evangelization,
Engagement, and Adult Formation programs, events, and opportunities.
● Ensure compliance with all Archdiocese of New Orleans policies and procedures, including Safe
Environment protocols.
● Participate in parish staff and diocesan meetings and trainings.
● Maintain a work schedule that maximizes availability and accessibility, including weekend and
evening initiatives.

Essential Duties: (Associate Director of Evangelization)

● Collaborate with the Director, Pastor, clergy, pastoral staff, and lay leaders to strengthen
the parish's efforts to reach active parishioners, inactive Catholics, and the unchurched.
● Support the continued implementation and development of the parish Discipleship Pathway,
helping parishioners encounter Jesus Christ, grow in their knowledge and love of Christ and His
Church, and live as intentional missionary disciples.
● Coordinate and support established evangelization and discipleship initiatives, including
Alpha, ACTS, parish retreats, Summit Nights, kerygmatic presentations, and other formation
opportunities.
● Foster opportunities for small-group discipleship, spiritual mentorship, and ongoing
formation.
● Equip parishioners with the formation, resources, and opportunities needed to share their
faith through witness, word, and action.
● Support lay formation and gift discernment initiatives that help parishioners recognize and
live out their unique role in the mission of the Church.
● Cultivate a parish culture in which evangelization and missionary discipleship are understood
as part of every Catholic's call.

Essential Duties: (Associate Director of Engagement)

● Develop and strengthen pathways that help new and existing parishioners connect with the
parish community and grow in their faith.
● Assist parishioners and visitors in identifying their next step along the parish Discipleship
Pathway.


● Collaborate with clergy, staff, and lay leaders to help parishioners identify their gifts and
connect those gifts with meaningful opportunities to serve.
● Help parishioners move toward fuller participation in the life and mission of the parish
through formation, community, and service.
● Support efforts to welcome, connect, and accompany those who are new to the parish or seeking
greater involvement in parish life.

Essential Duties: (Associate Director of Adult Formation)

● Collaborate with the Director in developing and strengthening adult faith formation
opportunities in accordance with the mission and vision of the parish.
● Coordinate and support adult faith formation programs, Bible studies, small groups, guest
speakers, retreats, and other opportunities for ongoing formation.
● Assist parish staff, groups, and ministries in identifying formation needs and connecting
parishioners with appropriate resources and opportunities.
● Assist with the development and coordination of an annual calendar of adult faith formation
and discipleship opportunities.
● Evaluate adult formation programs and initiatives to identify opportunities for continued
growth and improvement.
● Provide administrative and logistical support for the Christian Initiation of adults and
children over the age of seven as needed, including assistance during Holy Week and presence at the
Holy Saturday rehearsal and Easter Vigil.

Other Duties

● Perform other duties as assigned.

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities

● Knowledge of the structure and basic teachings of the Roman Catholic Church.
● Knowledge of catechesis, evangelization, discipleship, and adult faith formation.
● Skill in communicating effectively with diverse audiences, both orally and in writing.
● Ability to build relationships and work collaboratively with clergy, staff, lay leaders,
volunteers, and parishioners.
● Ability to recruit, equip, support, and coordinate volunteers and lay ministry leaders.
● Ability to organize, prioritize, and carry out multiple tasks while meeting deadlines and
utilizing effective time-management techniques.
● Ability to plan and coordinate programs, events, and formation opportunities.

● Ability to operate word-processing software, spreadsheets, databases, and other technology
necessary to fulfill the responsibilities of the position.
● Ability to exercise good judgment and maintain confidentiality at all times.
● Ability to follow instructions furnished in verbal or written format.

Minimum Qualifications

● Bachelor's degree from an accredited college or university with coursework in theology,
religious education, pastoral ministry, or a related field is preferred.
● Experience in pastoral ministry, evangelization, adult faith formation, or a related area is
preferred.
● Must be a practicing Roman Catholic in good standing with the Church.

Interested applicants should send a cover letter, resume, and at least three references to
kbaker@maryqueenofpeace.org. For questions or additional information, please contact our Director
of Parish Operations and Stewardship, Karen Baker, at (985) 202-0232.

post_html:
Campus Staff Minister, UW-Eau Claire, Undergraduate Ministry

Work Location:

Remote - USA

Job Type:

Full time

God has called InterVarsity to plant and to build witnessing communities of students and faculty who follow Jesus on college and university campuses. Through these groups, we believe ever- increasing numbers of students and faculty from all ethnic groups and areas of the campus will be transformed by the Gospel. We expect to see campuses increasingly become places where people, ideas, and structures flourish to the glory of God. We confidently anticipate that our InterVarsity alumni will become change agents across the country and around the world. We pursue this calling by discerning and actively participating in what God is already doing on campus. This is the essence of being a Campus Staff Minister (CSM).

ESSENTIAL COMMITMENTS/RESPONSIBILITIES 

Spiritual Growth 

As a Campus Staff Minister, you pursue maturity as a disciple of Jesus Christ so that your life and work increasingly reflect a growing love for God, God’s Word, God’s people of every ethnicity and culture, and God’s purposes in the world. To do this, you will: 

  • Pursue a vibrant relationship with the triune God through engagement with Scripture, prayer, and worship, both individually and in community 

  • Develop self-leadership (growing in self-awareness, self-management, relational integrity, and resiliency)

  • Embrace Scriptural standards for behavior and attitudes 

 

Campus Leadership 

As a Campus Staff Minister, you increase the number of witnessing communities, as well as the size, health, spiritual maturity, and campus-wide influence of existing witnessing communities of students and faculty by being a: 

  • Visionary Guide: 

You communicate and model InterVarsity’s vision to see students and faculty transformed, campuses renewed, and world changers developed 

  • Create a culture of humble dependence on God and bold expectation in God’s intention to start new witnessing communities throughout the campus and on new campuses

  • Model – in person and through programs – InterVarsity’s vision and Core Values, including a biblically-defined commitment to engage every ethnic and social group on campus

  • Lead students and faculty – individually and collectively – through Scripture, prayer, teaching, and discipleship experiences, so that they articulate and align their ministry activities around this vision

  • Set annual goals through prayer, research and reflection with your teams (students, faculty, and staff) for qualitative and quantitative growth, including conversions and leadership development 

  • Structural Architect: 

You create, develop, align, and leverage ministry plans, programs, teams, and structures to close the gap between current reality and the aspirational goals. 

  • Build leadership teams who trust and partner well with you and who demonstrate spiritual vitality, relational health, and mission alignment

  • Develop and execute plans to achieve annual goals, evaluating and modifying the plan as needed throughout the year

  • Increase momentum for the vision by aligning programs, structures, conferences, and teams around the goals

  • Mobilize students and faculty to engage their relational networks with the gospel and to start new missional communities

  • Under the direction of the Area Director, may supervise Ministry Interns and Campus Ministry Interns as delegated 

  • Missional Developer: 

You intentionally gather, invite, and develop diverse groups of students and faculty so that they not only encounter and follow Jesus as Savior and Lord but also advance the mission on campus as participants and leaders. 

  • Create ways for faculty and students to encounter and follow Jesus through Scripture, worship, prayer, mission experiences, conferences, etc.

  • Equip students and faculty so that they think strategically about campus engagement and so that they proclaim – in word, deed, and power – the good news of Jesus, regularly inviting students and faculty to follow him as Savior and Lord

  • Disciple students and faculty by equipping them to hear the Word, respond actively, and debrief and interpret the experience so that they grow in Christlikeness, reflect our Core Values, and develop ministry skills

  • Invite, coach, and equip students and faculty to become increasingly effective participants and leaders, including starting new witnessing communities on campuses 

 

Organizational Collaboration 

As a Campus Staff Minister, you have joined a national mission. Therefore, you work with a network of other local, area, regional, and national InterVarsity staff and volunteers so that our work reflects Biblical standards of excellence, integrity, and partnership. 

  • Partner with and respond positively to the direction and coaching of your supervisors and national leaders

  • Contribute to collaborative and productive team meetings and relationships

  • Affiliate chapters under your care and submit Graduating Student Forms in order to increase our partnership with current students and alumni

  • Use national ministry resources and tools, as requested, including recruiting and/or participating in local, regional, or national conferences as

  • Complete reporting, planning and review requirements in a timely way so that you and your supervisors can assess and improve your work as a CSM

  • Comply with all InterVarsity policies and procedures 

 

Ministry Partnership Development 

As a Campus Staff Minister, you will develop a team of partners – churches and individuals (including alumni and community members) – who will resource the ministry financially, in prayer, or volunteer service that advances the mission. 

  • Raise 100% of the financial budget assigned by your supervisor

  • Communicate regularly with your ministry partners, nurturing the relationship through visits, phone calls, emails and regular prayer letters

  • Develop on-going, long-lasting partnership with alumni and volunteers

  • Comply with all Ministry Partnership Policies

  • Identify and invest in advocates who will build networks of volunteers and donors on InterVarsity’s behalf 

 

Accomplish all other assigned tasks as appropriate 

 

QUALIFICATIONS (common to all levels of CSM) 

  • Annually affirm InterVarsity’s Statement of Agreement (Doctrinal Basis and Purpose Statement). Abide by InterVarsity’s Code of Conduct. Believe and behave consonantly with InterVarsity’s Human Sexuality Theological Paper. Affirm and behave consonantly with InterVarsity’s “Women in Ministry Statement of Affirmation”

  • Bachelor’s degree for CSMs assigned to a four-year campus. A minimum of an Associate’s degree for CSMs assigned to a two-year campus or a community college

  • Strong interpersonal skills (including ability to minister to diverse ethnic communities and faculty)

  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills

  • Demonstrated problem solving skills

  • Familiarity with word processing, presentation, email, and spreadsheet software 

 

WORK ENVIRONMENT/PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS 

The CSM position leads ministry in a college campus environment. A designated office space may or may not be available. The CSM is required to travel to on-campus and off- campus sites as appropriate. Off-campus travel includes, but is not limited to: student ministry conferences, Ministry Partnership Development meetings, and InterVarsity- sponsored training sessions, meetings, and conferences. The CSM is regularly required to communicate with others, and routinely uses standard office equipment such as computers, phones, photocopiers, filing cabinets, etc. 

Pay Range: $40,476.00 - $53,952.00 per year

Pay: This position is funded through personal fundraising. Accordingly, compensation will vary based on the ability of the individual to secure a donor team to fund the cost of his/her salary. The anticipated salary range for this position on a full-time basis (40 hours/week) is dependent on a variety of factors, including location and cost of living. The actual salary received, including any geographic adjustment to account for location and cost of living, is subject to the individual’s ability to raise funds necessary to cover the full amount of such salary within the range set forth in the job posting details.

Benefits:

We offer a competitive benefits package, including health care and retirement savings with a match. Eligibility is based on employee type and hours worked.  Benefits include the following:

  • 403(b) Retirement Savings Plan

  • 403(b) matching contributions

  • Dental insurance

  • Employee assistance program

  • Employee discounts

  • Flexible work schedule

  • Flexible spending accounts

  • Health insurance

  • Health savings account

  • Life insurance

  • Paid time off

  • Parental leave

  • Professional development assistance

  • Vision insurance

Equal Employment Opportunity: 

 

InterVarsity Christian Fellowship/USA is both an equal opportunity employer and a faith-based religious organization. We conduct hiring without regard to race, color, ancestry, national origin, citizenship, age, sex, marital status, parental status, membership in any labor organization, political ideology, or disability of an otherwise qualified individual. The status of InterVarsity Christian Fellowship/USA as an equal opportunity employer does not prevent the organization from hiring staff based on their religious beliefs so that all staff share the same religious commitment.  Pursuant to the Civil Rights Act of 1964, Section 702 (42 U.S.C. 2000e 1(a)) InterVarsity Christian Fellowship/USA has the right to, and does, hire only candidates who agree with InterVarsity’s Statement of Agreement: Purpose and Doctrinal Basis because InterVarsity believes that each and every staff plays a vital role in advancing InterVarsity’s mission and purposes.

At Embrace, our mission is simple: We relentlessly reach the next person for Jesus. Sioux Falls is one of the fastest-growing cities in America, and by 2031, we’re praying to see 5% of the city (12,500 people) come to know Him. If you love Jesus, love kids, and love having fun, we’d love for you to join the team!


Responsibilities

  • Coordinate and lead Sunday worship services and Wednesday evening youth worship.
  • Lead rehearsals and worship services for weekends in a way that is engaging and authentic.
  • Recruit, develop, equip, train, and motivate worship team members and leaders, while building a strong team culture through development strategies and fostering personal connections among the team.
  • Provide expertise on music, trends and culture to lead people into meaningful worship.
  • Contribute to the overall strategy of the worship department by leading and co-leading along with and alongside other staff.
  • Engage in weekly staff and team meetings, contributing to the creative planning of worship experiences both on the weekend and throughout other special events (i.e. Night of Worship).

Campus Ministry Intern - Virginia Region (Undergraduate Ministry)

Work Location:

Virginia

Job Type:

Full time

To advance the mission and purpose of InterVarsity, this position will focus on learning and preparing for the full responsibilities of a Campus Staff Minister. The Campus Ministry Associate will be assigned work based on skills determined by the application process. This is a one or two-year position in which the individual receives intensive training and exercises ministerial functions consistent with a Campus Staff Minister.

APPLICATIONS ARE DUE FRIDAY, JAN. 8, 2027.

ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS

Personal Spiritual Duties

  • Be a maturing disciple of Jesus Christ: growing in love for God, God's Word, God's people of every ethnicity and culture, and God’s purposes in the world.
  • Practice daily spiritual disciplines
  • Pursue spiritual relationships and involvement in a worshipping community
  • Continue learning and growth in spiritual understanding, biblical knowledge, ministry experience and skills
  • Experience and live out an ongoing call to ministry service with InterVarsity and its mission

Ministry Leadership

  • Participate and be fully engaged in the ministry team to cast spiritual vision and direction, to contribute to the accomplishment of the team’s plans for spiritual growth and transformation, and to provide area leadership in specific areas
  • Teach students to love, study and apply Scripture to their lives
  • Learn about and to assist in leading in ministry to students and faculty on campus
  • Promote and press forward the Mission on campus (To advance witnessing communities that are bolder, broader, and more ethnically diverse)

    • Learn to guide chapters (or assigned segments of a chapter) in the development of strategic thinking regarding witness to the university
    • Learn to model and assist students and faculty in growing in their love for God's people of every ethnicity and culture
  • Help to develop student and/or faculty ministry leadership teams, based on developing skills

  • Engage positively with the supervision you receive from your staff ministry director

Pastoral Care and Support (assist as assigned and based on skill level)

  • Provide pastoral care and support for student and/or leadership teams and individual students and faculty
  • Provide training, resources and opportunities for students and faculty for their spiritual development
  • Recruit students and/or faculty and providing specific leadership for conferences and projects

Administration

  • Perform the necessary administrative tasks required to fulfill the purpose of InterVarsity and to comply with InterVarsity’s policies and procedures
  • Comply with Risk Management policies
  • Follow the budgeting and expense reporting guidelines
  • Lead students in filing annual chapter affiliation, in coordination with assigned CSM
  • Fulfill area and regional reporting requirements
  • Fulfill national reporting requirements

Ministry Partner Development and Public Relations

  • Serve as an ambassador of InterVarsity to individual ministry partners and churches, through prayer, discussion of ministry efforts, mission, and accomplishments.
  • Carryout the tasks required for effective fund development and to develop strong public relations for the ministry of InterVarsity
  • Maintain expenses within allocated budgets
  • Secure personal financial, prayer support and maintain a ministry among partners who will fund InterVarsity
  • Develop and implement an annual 30-day plan for raising their personal budget
  • Communicate with ministry partners at least four times a year
  • Cultivate and maintain supportive relationships with alumni

QUALIFICATIONS

  • Annually affirm InterVarsity’s Statement of Agreement (Doctrinal Basis and Purpose Statement); abide by InterVarsity’s Code of Conduct; believe and behave consonantly with InterVarsity’s Human Sexuality Theological Paper. Affirm and behave consonantly with InterVarsity’s “Women in Ministry Statement of Affirmation”
  • Exploring calling to InterVarsity and its mission
  • Currently enrolled student with prior leadership experience in an InterVarsity Chapter
  • Currently enrolled student in 3rd or 4th year of undergraduate study with the approval of an Area Director
  • Bachelor’s degree not required, but recommended, for non-enrolled student assigned to four-year campuses; Associate’s degree not required, but recommended, for non-enrolled student assigned to two-year campuses and community colleges
  • Prior experience with InterVarsity or other campus ministry preferred (including as a student)
  • Willing to receive training to become a Campus Staff Minister
  • Ability to contribute to an open and supportive relationship with ministry team members
  • Ministry skills: Prior experience teaching spiritual and biblical principles, planning ministry programs, and spiritually discipling others
  • Excellent oral and written communication skills
  • Demonstrated problem-solving skills.

Pay Range: $36,132.00 - $48,168.00 per year

Pay: This position is funded through personal fundraising. Accordingly, compensation will vary based on the ability of the individual to secure a donor team to fund the cost of his/her salary. The anticipated salary range for this position on a full-time basis (40 hours/week) is dependent on a variety of factors, including location and cost of living. The actual salary received, including any geographic adjustment to account for location and cost of living, is subject to the individual’s ability to raise funds necessary to cover the full amount of such salary within the range set forth in the job posting details.

Benefits:

We offer a competitive benefits package, including health care and retirement savings with a match. Eligibility is based on employee type and hours worked.  Benefits include the following:

  • 403(b) Retirement Savings Plan

  • 403(b) matching contributions

  • Dental insurance

  • Employee assistance program

  • Employee discounts

  • Flexible work schedule

  • Flexible spending accounts

  • Health insurance

  • Health savings account

  • Life insurance

  • Paid time off

  • Parental leave

  • Professional development assistance

  • Vision insurance

Equal Employment Opportunity: 

 

InterVarsity Christian Fellowship/USA is both an equal opportunity employer and a faith-based religious organization. We conduct hiring without regard to race, color, ancestry, national origin, citizenship, age, sex, marital status, parental status, membership in any labor organization, political ideology, or disability of an otherwise qualified individual. The status of InterVarsity Christian Fellowship/USA as an equal opportunity employer does not prevent the organization from hiring staff based on their religious beliefs so that all staff share the same religious commitment.  Pursuant to the Civil Rights Act of 1964, Section 702 (42 U.S.C. 2000e 1(a)) InterVarsity Christian Fellowship/USA has the right to, and does, hire only candidates who agree with InterVarsity’s Statement of Agreement: Purpose and Doctrinal Basis because InterVarsity believes that each and every staff plays a vital role in advancing InterVarsity’s mission and purposes.

The House-of-Worship Armed Security Agent is responsible for ensuring the safety and well-being of all within the religious premises. This role involves regular patrols, managing security checkpoints during high-traffic events, responding to emergencies, and offering assistance to visitors. The agent must exhibit both firm security expertise and a deep sensitivity to the unique environment of a house-of-worship.


POSITION SUMMARY


In the role of a House-of-Worship Armed Security Agent, you are more than just a guardian; you are an integral part of the religious community's fabric, ensuring that the sanctuary remains a haven for all who seek solace and worship. Entrusted with the task of safeguarding the congregation, you will navigate the delicate balance of providing stringent security while respecting the sanctity and serenity of the environment. Drawing from specialized training, you'll meticulously patrol, detect potential risks, and swiftly respond to emergencies, always with a deep reverence for the space and its attendees. This position requires vigilance and a profound understanding of the unique sensitivities associated with religious settings, ensuring that every individual feels protected and at peace.


SCHEDULE

Monday through Friday from 6:00am to 10:00am



Requirements

  • Must be 23 years of age or older.
  • Previous security-related work experience.
  • Working knowledge of basic security techniques.
  • Previous Military, Law Enforcement, and Government Agency experience is an advantage.
  • High school diploma or equivalent (Bachelor's Degree from an accredited University is a plus (not mandatory).
  • Authorized to work in the United States
  • Valid Class D License
  • Valid Class G License
  • Valid Class W License (an advantage).
  • Must be able to pass a criminal/background check and must be able to pass a drug test spontaneously while employed.
  • A minimum of CPR/First Aid/AED for all ages is required.
  • Possess a valid and current driver’s license.
  • Strong command of the English language (Others are an advantage).
  • High Self-Confidence balanced with a reasonable amount of humility, strong leadership, and interpersonal relationship skills, very proactive, and outstanding attention to detail.
  • Comfortable kneeling, carrying, bending, walking, and standing for extended periods.
  • Ability to perform continuous physical exertion as needed.
  • Successfully completed Pulmus7 Basic Training’.

*Required documentation:

  1. Resume
  2. Driver’s License or Government Issued Identification
  3. All Security License(s)
  4. DD214 (If Applicable)
  5. Law Enforcement/Corrections Officer Certification (If Applicable)
  6. Referrals 

*Pulmus7 is an equal-opportunity employer.
* Just relevant candidates will be reached if a position is suitable.



Benefits

  • Competitive Wages
  • Holiday Pay
  • Bi-weekly pay with Direct Deposit
  • Advancement Opportunities (90% of our dispatchers, supervisors, and managers were promoted from within the company)
  • Dedicated security training certification by elite security experts.

Overview

Lifeway is seeking a Remote Outbound Church Sales Specialist. In this role you will be responsible for identifying and pursuing new church opportunities and establishing relationships with existing churches to grow and further support their ministry needs with resources that Lifeway offers. This is an excellent position for someone passionate about our mission and wanting to sharpen their selling skills.  

 

Why Lifeway? 

 

Lifeway is a place where you can bring your faith and work experience to join in the most important mission in the world: making disciples of Jesus Christ. Whether you’re a creator or storyteller, data guru or problem-solver, or anywhere in between, if you’re passionate about serving the church, we have a place for you. Lifeway has a strong Work from Anywhere (WFA) culture that is deeply focused on our mission and values. While headquartered in Nashville, TN, many of our positions are remote-eligible and have autonomy and flexibility with work hours. We provide equipment and resources to ensure team members have access to a productive and ergonomic workspace. We believe building relationships and community is essential to how we work together, so Lifeway hosts all-team meetings several times per year and provides travel for key team gatherings for remote-based team members. Full-time employees are eligible for enrollment in our comprehensive benefits plans including healthcare, vacation and sick time, holiday pay, care days, 401(k) plan, maternity and paternity leave, adoption assistance, mission trip time, and more. If this sounds like a place where you would be excited to serve the kingdom of God, we would love for you to join our team.

 

Learn more about our culture at team.lifeway.com/culture-code 

 

This is a remote position in the U.S. with occasional travel to Nashville for in-person team gatherings. #LI-Remote 

 

Responsibilities

  • Lives out Lifeway’s mission and values, showing deep commitment to Kingdom work
  • Build and grow relationships with church accounts across an assigned territory by initiating outbound sales through phone, email, and video calls
  • Develop comprehensive relationships with each church's ministry stakeholders — including Senior Pastors, Worship Pastors, and Small Groups Pastors — to understand their unique needs and maximize resource reach
  • Pursue and convert new church prospects assigned as leads in Salesforce, working a strategic sales plan to hit conversion goals and acquire new business
  • Create and maintain a territory sales plan designed to meet or exceed monthly and annual revenue targets
  • Recommend the right Lifeway resources, events, and services by using a question-based consultative approach to understand each church's demographics and ministry priorities
  • Stay current on new and upcoming Lifeway releases — in print and digital — through ongoing training and product learning
  • Keep Salesforce records up to date, logging all sales activity in real time and surfacing customer feedback to inform future publishing, marketing, and sales strategies
  • Partner with Customer Success and Outbound Field teams to expand territory reach and improve ministry effectiveness
  • Consistently meet or exceed quarterly sales targets in alignment with overall revenue goals
  • Minimal travel, usually overnight

 

Qualifications

Education

High School Diploma, required

Bachelor's degree, preferred

Masters degree, not required

Advanced graduate degree (PhD, etc.), not required

 

Skills, Knowledge, & Experiences, required

  • Strong written and verbal communication skills.
  • Strong consultative and active listening skills with the ability to tailor solutions to individual customer needs
  • Proficiency navigating multiple software systems simultaneously
  • Strong organizational and multitasking skills
  • Highly coachable and adaptable to feedback, process changes, and new product information
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills
  • 1+ years of direct sales experience with a demonstrated ability to meet or exceed sales goals.


Actively involved in an evangelical Christian church


Skills, Knowledge, & Experiences, preferred

  • Experience with Microsoft Suite, Oracle, and/or Salesforce CRM
  • Previous experience in a church, ministry, or faith-based organization
  • Familiarity with Lifeway resources, Bible study curriculum, or church ministry products
  • Fully bilingual and fluent in Spanish and English (written and oral).

post_html:
Campus Staff Minister - Alaska (Undergraduate Ministry)

Work Location:

Alaska

Job Type:

Full time

Is God calling you to change the university and change the world? Want to serve in ministry outside of the four walls of the church? InterVarsity is looking for visionary leaders to serve one of the most strategic mission fields––the college campus! We want to reach every corner of every campus, and you could be a part of that in ALASKA.

God has called InterVarsity to plant and to build witnessing communities of students and faculty who follow Jesus on college and university campuses. Through these groups, we believe ever- increasing numbers of students and faculty from all ethnic groups and areas of the campus will be transformed by the Gospel. We expect to see campuses increasingly become places where people, ideas, and structures flourish to the glory of God. We confidently anticipate that our InterVarsity alumni will become change agents across the country and around the world. We pursue this calling by discerning and actively participating in what God is already doing on campus. This is the essence of being a Campus Staff Minister (CSM).

**If you are interested in this position, please complete the interest form linked in the job description BEFORE you begin the application process.**

Today, nearly 4,000 Alaska Native students are studying at colleges and universities in Alaska, yet very little is being done to reach and develop them as the Kingdom leaders that Creator is calling them to become. Though often overlooked by the campus community, these students have the potential to be future world changers, and their families and communities are looking to them for leadership and hope. We desire to see Alaska Native graduates return home as spiritually transformed and skilled leaders who will foster deep and lasting change in their communities, to the glory of God. Come build a thriving ministry that is fit for Alaska Native students, where they discover how to follow Jesus—while honoring their culture(s). 

If you are interested in this position, please complete this interest form before you begin the application process.

___________________________________________________________________

ESSENTIAL COMMITMENTS/RESPONSIBILITIES

Spiritual Growth

As a Campus Staff Minister, you pursue maturity as a disciple of Jesus Christ so that your life and work increasingly reflects a growing love for God, God’s Word, God’s people of every ethnicity and culture, and God’s purposes in the world. To do this, you will:

  • Pursue a vibrant relationship with the triune God through engagement with Scripture, prayer, and worship, both individually and in community
  • Develop self-leadership (growing in self-awareness, self-management, relational integrity, and resiliency)
  • Embrace Scriptural standards for behavior and attitudes

2.Campus Leadership

As a Campus Staff Minister, you increase the number of witnessing communities, as well as the size, health, spiritual maturity, and campus-wide influence of existing witnessing communities of students and faculty by being a:

  • Visionary Guide:

You communicate and model InterVarsity’s vision to see students and faculty transformed, campuses renewed and world changers developed

  • Create a culture of humble dependence on God and bold expectation in God’s intention to start new witnessing communities throughout the campus and on new campuses
  • Model – in person and through programs – InterVarsity’s vision and Core Values, including a biblically-defined commitment to engage every ethnic and social group on campus
  • Lead students and faculty – individually and collectively – through Scripture, prayer, teaching, and discipleship experiences, so that they articulate and align their ministry activities around this vision
  • Set annual goals through prayer, research and reflection with your teams (students, faculty, and staff) for qualitative and quantitative growth, including conversions and leadership development
  • Structural Architect:

You create, develop, align and leverage ministry plans, programs, teams, and structures to close the gap between current reality and the aspirational goals.

  • Build leadership teams who trust and partner well with you and who demonstrate spiritual vitality, relational health, and mission alignment
  • Develop and execute plans to achieve annual goals, evaluating and modifying the plan as needed throughout the year
  • Increase momentum for the vision by aligning programs, structures, conferences and teams around the goals
  • Mobilize students and faculty to engage their relational networks with the gospel and to start new missional communities
  • Under the direction of the Area Director, may supervise Ministry Interns and Campus Ministry Interns as delegated
  • Missional Developer:

You intentionally gather, invite, and develop diverse groups of students and faculty so that they not only encounter and follow Jesus as Savior and Lord but also advance the mission on campus as participants and leaders.

  • Create ways for faculty and students to encounter and follow Jesus through Scripture, worship, prayer, mission experiences, conferences, etc.
  • Equip students and faculty so that they think strategically about campus engagement and so that they proclaim – in word, deed, and power – the good news of Jesus, regularly inviting students and faculty to follow him as Savior and Lord
  • Disciple students and faculty by equipping them to hear the Word, respond actively, and debrief and interpret the experience so that they grow in Christlikeness, reflect our Core Values, and develop ministry skills
  • Invite, coach, and equip students and faculty to become increasingly effective participants and leaders, including starting new witnessing communities on campuses

3.Organizational Collaboration

As a Campus Staff Minister, you have joined a national mission. Therefore, you work with a network of other local, area, regional, and national InterVarsity staff and volunteers so that our work reflects Biblical standards of excellence, integrity, and partnership.

  • Partner with and respond positively to the direction and coaching of your supervisors and national leaders
  • Contribute to collaborative and productive team meetings and relationships
  • Affiliate chapters under your care and submit Graduating Student Forms in order to increase our partnership with current students and alumni
  • Use national ministry resources and tools, as requested, including recruiting and/or participating in local, regional, or national conferences as required
  • Complete reporting, planning and review requirements in a timely way so that you and your supervisors can assess and improve your work as a CSM
  • Comply with all InterVarsity policies and procedures

4.Ministry Partnership Development

As a Campus Staff Minister, you will develop a team of partners – churches and individuals (including alumni and community members) – who will resource the ministry financially, in prayer, or volunteer service that advances the mission.

  • Raise 100% of the financial budget assigned by your supervisor
  • Communicate regularly with your ministry partners, nurturing the relationship through visits, phone calls, emails and regular prayer letters
  • Develop on-going, long-lasting partnership with alumni and volunteers
  • Comply with all Ministry Partnership Policies
  • Identify and invest in advocates who will build networks of volunteers and donors on InterVarsity’s behalf

5.Accomplish all other assigned tasks as appropriate

QUALIFICATIONS (common to all levels of CSM)

  • Annually affirm InterVarsity’s Statement of Agreement (Doctrinal Basis and Purpose Statement). Abide by InterVarsity’s Code of Conduct. Believe and behave consonantly with InterVarsity’s Human Sexuality Theological Paper. Affirm and behave consonantly with InterVarsity’s “Women in Ministry Statement of Affirmation”
  • Bachelor’s degree required for CSMs assigned to a four-year campus. A minimum of an Associate’s degree required for CSMs assigned to a two-year campus or a community college
  • Strong interpersonal skills (including ability to minister to diverse ethnic communities and faculty)
  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills
  • Demonstrated problem solving skills
  • Familiarity with word processing, presentation, email, and spreadsheet software

WORK ENVIRONMENT/PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS

The CSM position leads ministry in a college campus environment. A designated office space may or may not be available. The CSM is required to travel to on-campus and off- campus sites as appropriate. Off-campus travel includes, but is not limited to: student ministry conferences, Ministry Partnership Development meetings, and InterVarsity- sponsored training sessions, meetings, and conferences. The CSM is regularly required to communicate with others, and routinely uses standard office equipment such as computers, phones, photocopiers, filing cabinets, etc.

InterVarsity Christian Fellowship/USA

Frame of Reference

All staff members subscribe annually to the Purpose Statement of InterVarsity:

In response to God’s love, grace and truth:

The purpose of InterVarsity Christian Fellowship/USA is

to establish and advance at colleges and universities

witnessing communities of students and faculty

who follow Jesus as Savior and Lord:

growing in love for God,

God’s Word,

God’s people of every ethnicity and culture

and God’s purposes in the world.

This purpose is admittedly more limited than the Great Commission.  As a mission extension of the local church, we have adopted boundaries on our activities based on our call to serve a defined group of God’s people.  Within the context of InterVarsity’s purpose, all of the relationships and tasks that staff members engage in as part of their work for InterVarsity have both eternal and temporal components. 

Values:

    

InterVarsity is committed to developing men and women from diverse cultures, backgrounds, and generations, whom God calls to work with us for both shorter and longer periods of service, as we pursue the call of God in the university world.

Maturing Disciple of Jesus Christ:

Every InterVarsity staff member is to be a maturing disciple of the Lord Jesus Christ, growing in obedience to the Scriptures.  The marks of a long-term love relationship with Christ in the fullness of His Spirit are described in Galatians 5:22: “The fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faithfulness, gentleness and self control.”  In the workplace, this fruit is revealed in healthy working relationships which encourage all staff to accomplish their work and enhance their focus on the spiritual aspects of their work.

Team Work:

Each individual staff person is a vital member of Christ’s body.  This means that we will work with one another in ways that honor and encourage all to grow in Christ while accomplishing His work.  Our community requires that each individual serve as a team member in a collegial and open environment based on values, relationships, and vision as well as structure and position.

InterVarsity staff, both employees and volunteers, commit to serve God and all InterVarsity colleagues, students, and partners, with sensitivity to both the eternal and temporal dimensions of our work.  “Whatever your task, work heartily, as serving the Lord.” (Colossians 3:23a)

Pay Range: $39,288.00 - $52,392.00 per year

Job Title: Youth Pastor/Next Gen

Department: Student Ministry

Status: Full-Time

About Church at the Shores

Church at the Shores is a life-giving church for every generation, helping people take their next step with Jesus. As part of the global family of the Christian and Missionary Alliance, we join with believers around the world to take all of Jesus to all of the world. Since relaunching in 2018, we’ve seen hundreds of lives changed, a thriving multigenerational community formed, and ministries launched locally and globally. In November 2025, we will joyfully celebrate 7 years of ministry together.

More about Church at the Shores: www.churchattheshores.com

About Gulf Shores & Foley

The Gulf Shores and Foley area is one of the fastest-growing regions in Alabama, known for its beautiful beaches, strong sense of community, and family-friendly environment. With a mix of year-round residents, seasonal visitors, and a growing number of young families, the area provides unique opportunities for ministry and outreach. It’s a place where hospitality meets coastal living, making it a wonderful community to call home.

Who Are We Looking For?

You have a deep love for Jesus and a passion for the next generation, believing wholeheartedly in their God-given purpose. You’re a strong leader who thrives on building relationships, casting vision, and creating environments where students can know God, love people, make a difference, and grow deeper with Jesus.

You can communicate God’s Word in a way that connects with students and equips them for real life. You are organized, creative, and capable of building systems and teams that make ministry sustainable and effective. You’re confident in leading others, raising leaders, and mobilizing students to serve.

You’re skilled with technology and social media as tools for ministry, and you’re willing to learn new systems to help connect students and families. Most importantly, you’re committed to the vision of Church at the Shores and want to see students fully integrated into the life of the church.

What Will You Do?

You will lead Shores Students to provide vision, direction, and discipleship that helps middle school, high school, and college students follow Jesus for a lifetime.

Main Tasks & Responsibilities (including, but not limited to):

  • Lead Shores Students by casting a vision, building relationships, and helping them take the next steps with Jesus.
  • Oversee student ministry gatherings, discipleship opportunities, and outreach efforts.
  • Preach and teach Scripture in ways that are clear, relational, and life-giving.
  • Develop a teaching calendar and create content that speaks to the real issues students face.
  • Recruit, equip, and encourage a strong team of leaders. Partner with parents by equipping them to disciple their students at home.
  • Plan and oversee camps, retreats, and special events. Provide pastoral care for students and families as needed (baptisms, hospital visits, etc.).
  • Manage the student ministry budget and steward resources wisely.
  • Communicate consistently with students, parents, and leaders.
  • Foster a culture of prayer, worship, and mission within Shores Students.

What Is Important at Church at the Shores?

  • Attitude: A servant’s heart and a love for people
  • Leadership: Able to inspire and develop others.
  • Team Player: Works closely with pastors and staff to advance the overall vision of the church.
  • Work Ethic: Self-starter who is dependable and flexible.
  • Culture: Fun, relational, encouraging, and life-giving.
  • Character: Loyal, humble, and faithful to God’s call.
  • Commitment: Fully engaged in the vision, values, and membership of Church at the Shores

Interested candidates must be in agreement with the C&MA statement of faith and Alliance polity.

Please complete the application to include your testimony, resume, and other background information related to the position. The district office and search team will review your application to see if you are a potential match for the position and will further contact you concerning the next steps.

Please do not contact the church directly.

Job Description

Our vision is to be the most trusted and best-performing rental housing company in America - one that continues to get better as it grows. And we're looking for people who want to help us do it.

At Vivmark, team members move up and across functions, markets, and disciplines, building lasting careers. The best people want to work here. We hope you're one of them.

Campus Ministry Associate - Louisiana Area (Undergraduate Ministry)

Louisiana

Full time

To advance the mission and purpose of InterVarsity, this position will focus on learning and preparing for the full responsibilities of a Campus Staff Minister. The Campus Ministry Associate will be assigned work based on skills determined by the application process. This is a one or two-year position in which the individual receives intensive training and exercises ministerial functions consistent with a Campus Staff Minister.

Personal Spiritual Duties 

  • Be a maturing disciple of Jesus Christ: growing in love for God, God's Word, God's people of every ethnicity and culture, and God’s purposes in the world 

  • Practice daily spiritual disciplines  

  • Pursue spiritual relationships and involvement in a worshipping community  

  • Continue learning and growth in spiritual understanding, biblical knowledge, ministry experience and skills

Ministry Leadership 

  • Participate and be fully engaged in the ministry team to cast spiritual vision and direction, to contribute to the accomplishment of the team’s plans for spiritual growth and transformation, and to provide area leadership in specific areas

  • Learn about and assist in leading in ministry to students and faculty on campus

Administration

Affirm and behave consonantly with InterVarsity’s “Women in Ministry Statement of Affirmation”

job_name: Pastor of Discipleship and Worship - Grace Church
post_html:
Pastor of Discipleship and Worship - Grace Church
 

Church Overview

  • 25-year-old Evangelical Free Church in the beautiful Driftless Region of SW Wisconsin. 
  • Two Sunday morning services | Average attendance: 240 (~50% children & teens)
  • Gospel-centered, intergenerational family-equipping ministry
  • Shining Christ’s light in a politically and culturally diverse rural community

The senior pastor will continue being involved in most areas, collaborating closely with this role. The position empowers the candidate to serve according to their gifts and passions.

 

Qualifications

Category

 

Requirement

 

Character

Above all, be humble and teachable

 

Faith

Strong, growing personal faith; desire to connect others to God’s grace and truth

 

Alignment

Fulfill Grace Church membership commitments; full agreement with Discipleship Strategy, Constitution, By-laws, and policies

 

Discipleship

Proven experience multiplying disciple-makers, developing leaders, recruiting volunteers, and relating well to people

 

Worship

Skills to lead corporate worship; ability to train/equip worship leaders and teams

 

Biblical

Meet elder qualifications per 1 Timothy 3

 

Background

Able to pass a background check

 

Administration

Solid organizational skills to manage ministries, budgets, and volunteers

 

Communication

Technologically literate with strong communication skills

 

Education

Ministry degree or equivalent

 

Credentialing

EFCA ministry credential (or obtain a license within 3 years, ordination within 5 years)

 

Responsibilities

  • 60–70% Discipleship
  • 30–40% Worship

Discipleship (Primary Focus)

  • Identify and develop people/processes for effective discipleship of all ages per the Discipleship Strategy
  • Serve as a spiritual resource for parents on Biblical household application; equip parents as primary spiritual influencers
  • Support youth & family ministry leaders/volunteers in program administration, development, and volunteer recruitment
  • Provide training, resources, and instruction for youth/family and worship ministry leaders/volunteers
  • Encourage spiritual gift utilization and identify service opportunities within the body
  • Promote intergenerational ministries to reveal God’s work across generations

Worship

  • Lead music in worship services as needed (~1x/month)
  • Train and equip worship leaders and team members

Preaching & Leadership

  • Preach up to 12 times/year (flexible, based on giftedness and development)
  • Serve as ex officio elder in mutual submission to the elder board
  • Collaborate with the senior pastor to shepherd the congregation
  • Participate actively in relevant committees/teams
  • Fulfill responsibilities assigned by the elders and the senior pastor

 

Provisions

 

 

Compensation

Salary + housing allowance commensurate with experience/education

Health

Medical insurance/benefits, retirement, workman’s compensation

Ministry Expense

~$2,500/year

Vacation

4 weeks/year

Sabbatical

Per policy, when appropriate

Relocation

Moving expenses covered

Support

Encouragement from the elders and congregation

 

Note from Lead Pastor

The job description may seem pretty huge. That's why a conversation would be helpful.

 

  • In the discipleship areas, I already do most of these things and will keep doing many as we collaborate together. So part of this job description will be shared by me.
  • Preaching is very flexible. It's in there if the person wants to develop in this area, but it's not absolutely necessary.
  • We will want to have a conversation about our discipleship huddles, which form the foundation of all of our disciple-making efforts. It is the best discipleship tool I have ever experienced.

 

To me, the collaboration piece is HUGE. It will allow us to:

  • Be better together than as individuals.
  • Be united in vision and communication at all times.
  • Free each of us to be empowered and freed up to serve according to our gifts and abilities.

Requested Documents

  1. Resume
  2. Cover letter with doctrinal statement, bio and Audio/video links of sermon/teaching/worship leading (if available) 
One may receive a request to answer other questions.

job_name: Campus Minister for Justice and Solidarity
tag_categories: [IaaS]
post_html:
Description

The Campus Minister for Justice and Solidarity leads student formation and co-curricular learning focused on justice, solidarity, service, and community engagement. This position integrates Catholic social teaching and the spirituality and charism of the Sisters of the Holy Cross into service and justice programming while creating opportunities that welcome and engage students from diverse faith backgrounds.

The Campus Minister oversees the Beyond the Belle and Spes Service Experience programs, including program development, logistics, student recruitment and preparation, reflection and integration, and student leader development. The position supervises student community engagement leaders, Spes Service Experience leaders, and interns involved in justice and advocacy programming.

The Campus Minister collaborates across campus to strengthen experiential learning opportunities and develops and maintains meaningful relationships with local community organizations and ministry partners. This position also provides ongoing mentorship and pastoral care to students and contributes to initiatives that advance the mission of Saint Mary’s College as a Catholic and Holy Cross institution.

Minimum Qualifications
  • Master of Divinity, Theology, Spirituality, or a related field required.
  • Experience in higher education in a student-facing role or experience working in ministry with young adults.
  • Experience planning and leading service opportunities and justice-focused programming.
  • Knowledge of and commitment to Catholic social teaching.
  • Demonstrated ability to develop and execute programs or events from conception through completion.
  • Proficiency with computer applications, including Google Workspace.
  • Commitment to hospitality and welcome and the ability to engage students from diverse faith backgrounds.
  • Excellent written, verbal, public speaking, interpersonal, and social communication skills.
  • Demonstrated ability to build effective relationships and collaborate with students, faculty, staff, community partners, and the Sisters of the Holy Cross.
  • Ability to work independently, manage multiple responsibilities, and collaborate effectively as part of a team.
Preferred Qualifications
  • Experience planning and leading justice immersions or service immersion experiences.
  • Familiarity with the charism and spirituality of the Sisters of the Holy Cross.
  • Experience developing student leadership and formation programs.
  • Experience working with community organizations, nonprofit agencies, or ministry partners.
  • Experience integrating faith formation, justice, service, and experiential learning in a higher education setting.
Job Responsibilities
  • Lead the Beyond the Belle and Spes Service Experience programs, including program development, logistics, recruitment and preparation of student participants and faculty/staff advisors, reflection and integration meetings, and student leader development.
  • Collaborate with the Prikkel Advising, Career, and Experience Center, faculty, and other campus partners to strengthen experiential learning opportunities for students.
  • Help students connect faith, justice, and service through guided preparation and reflection that incorporates Catholic social teaching and the charism of the Sisters of the Holy Cross.
  • Oversee and guide the direction of Holy Cross Justice Circles in collaboration with the Director of the Holy Cross Justice Collaborative.
  • Advise the Catholic Relief Services (CRS) Ambassadors program and maintain communication with the local CRS Coalition.
  • Oversee Federal Work-Study Community Service job placements, hiring, and timecard approval in collaboration with Student Financial Services.
  • Develop and maintain relationships with local organizations, community partners, and ministry organizations.
  • Supervise and mentor student community engagement leaders, Spes Service Experience leaders, and student interns who lead justice and advocacy programming.
  • Provide ongoing mentorship, pastoral support, and guidance to students.
  • Evaluate programs and recommend opportunities for growth, improvement, and increased student engagement.
  • Collaborate with the Center for Faith, Action and Ministry team on strategic planning, student leader formation, special events, and other initiatives that advance the mission of Saint Mary’s College.
  • Contribute to a welcoming and inclusive campus environment by developing programs and opportunities that encourage students of diverse backgrounds and faith traditions to participate in service, justice, and community engagement.
  • Perform other duties and responsibilities as assigned.
Schedule

This is a full-time, 12-month position working approximately 40 hours per week. Due to the nature of student programming, the position requires periodic evening and weekend hours as assigned. The position also requires periodic domestic and/or international travel associated with service immersion experiences.

Eligibility to Work

Applicants must be legally authorized to work in the United States at the time of hire and must not require visa sponsorship from the College, either now or in the future.

Please submit a current resume and cover letter with your application. Your cover letter should highlight your relevant experience, qualifications, and interest in the position.

Life.Church wants to make a lasting difference in your life, in our community, and in the world. Our mission is to lead people to become fully devoted followers of Christ. That's how we’re able to make a difference, and it's the driving force behind everything we do.
 
The Life.Church Media Relations Manager is primarily responsible for sharing the stories of what God is doing through Life.Church, including proactive and reactive media relations. This role will strengthen existing efforts under the leadership of the Sr. Director of Public Relations, identify new opportunities for media coverage, craft thoughtful messaging, and improve our ability to tell stories across the organization.
 
The Public Relations Team is part of the Life.Church Communications Group, which consists of four teams—including Social Media, Communication, and Marketing—who collectively develop strategies for how our ministry meets people where they are and empowers them to become fully devoted followers of Christ. The Communications Group introduces people to Life.Church, connects them to our mission, and helps them take the next steps in their journey toward Christ.
 
This role operationally supports the team's direction, initiatives, and ministry efforts to achieve outcomes that further Life.Church’s mission and reach people for Christ.

Who You Are

  • Your super power is your ability to find the news hook in any situation. 
  • You’re often told that you have a way with words and make people feel comfortable and cared for, even when communicating firm expectations.
  • Energized by challenges, fast-paced environments, and a high level of accountability.
  • Known for staying level-headed and responding with grace and patience when things get difficult.
  • Comfortable thinking on your feet when sensitive or unexpected situations arise, and confident in helping shape the right response.
  • A team player who’s ready to roll up your sleeves and work alongside a team that’s hardwired to work hard.
  • Looking to dedicate your life to something that makes an eternal difference.

What You'll Do

Drive the Strategic Direction of National Press Efforts
  • Contribute strategy ideas for various Life.Church press initiatives.
  • Counsel and resource staff for speaking engagements, research projects, or other community-related requests.
  • Craft thoughtful, consistent messaging on sensitive topics across audiences and channels.
  • Regularly evaluate projects and identify ways to improve future efforts.
 
Lead Press Strategies for Proactive and Reactive Opportunities
  • Draft and distribute press materials that appeal to journalists and align with Life.Church voice.
  • Coordinate press logistics across teams to keep PR campaigns running smoothly.
  • Manage and respond strategically to incoming media requests or external inquiries.
  • Stay informed of local, national, and trade news trends to identify pitch angles and get ahead of any potential reactive efforts.
  • Build and maintain rapport with journalists.
 
Maintain Tools and Resources that Support Media Relations
  • Build and maintain research-based media lists.
  • Champion storytelling across the organization to help inspire people to take the next step in their faith journey.
  • Identify newsworthy stories across teams and ministries.
  • Curate a collection of visual assets for press use.
  • Regularly monitor media coverage, responding accordingly.
  • Develop and update biographies, fact sheets, and other historical Life.Church documents for external use.

Skills Needed to Succeed

  • Excellent verbal, written, and interpersonal communication skills to foster relationships and partnerships.
  • Effective at multitasking and time management to meet strict deadlines while remaining flexible and open to change.
  • Strong writing, editing, and proofing skills.
  • Strong leadership skills and experience in coaching and developing others.
  • Ability to self-motivate, make independent decisions, and problem-solve.
  • Ability to manage conflict and differing opinions while maintaining composure.
  • High School Diploma or GED.
  • Bachelor's Degree in Public Relations, Strategic Communication, or a related field required.
  • 5+ years of related work experience preferred.
  • Demonstrated track record of effective media relations strategies.

Benefits We Offer

  • Paid parental leave, including maternity, paternity, and adoption leave.
  • Generous employer-paid leave for the use of vacation, sick time, and other qualifying reasons. 
  • Innovative and comprehensive Medical, Dental, and Vision insurance that provides team members with useful resources and savings to navigate their holistic health. 
  • Life insurance policy provided for all staff members at 2x annual salary at no cost. Additional life insurance coverage is available to purchase. 
  • Short-Term and Long-Term disability is covered at 100% for full-time qualified staff members.
  • Comprehensive wellness and mental health benefits allow staff to proactively invest in their physical and emotional health.
  • Generous 401(k) retirement plan allowing a team member to have up to 12.5% (including employee contribution, employer match, and employer discretionary contribution) contributed into their account in their first year. It doesn’t stop there—the more years on staff, the greater the investment! 
  • $160 annually in development dollars for team members to invest in their professional growth. 
  • Casual dress and work environment.
  • And much more!
 

Our Beliefs, Culture, and Commitment to Diversity

At Life.Church, every staff member, and intern is a minister and is expected to engage in the church's ministry fully. We consider ministry readiness and an individual’s capacity to represent Life.Church’s beliefs as a minister during the selection process for all staff and intern positions. An essential function within every position held by a staff member or intern at Life.Church is to uphold and represent the beliefs of Life.Church. Learn more about what we believe at Life.Church. 
 
While we unite around our mission, we know unity doesn’t mean uniformity. Our calling is too great, and our mission is too important not to be intentional about strengthening our team through diversity. We know that diverse perspectives in race, ethnicity, background, age, and gender are essential to reaching the world for Christ. To learn more about how we strengthen our team through diversity, visit our careers page. 
 
All data collected in our application process, from resume collection to application questions, is used for recruitment purposes only.

Associate Pastor, Aspire Church San Marco


Date Prepared/Updated: October 22, 2026

Congregation (Horizontal): Aspire Church San Marco

Ministry Function (Vertical): Grow

Reports to:   Senior Pastor


Basic Purpose:

The Associate Pastor leads discipleship and spiritual formation at Aspire Church San Marco and assists the Senior Pastor in coordinating ministry to make disciples of Jesus and to equip those who do. He engages, equips, and empowers staff and lay leaders to build a church of groups, where every member has a primary place of belonging, spiritual formation, and routine member care. He shares in preaching and pastoral ministry, develops future leaders, and equips congregations across the Aspire Family of Churches. San Marco is the first priority and serves as a place to develop ministry approaches that other congregations can adapt to their contexts.

 

Adult Groups and Spiritual Formation

  • Lead Adult Grow ministry, strengthening group health, participation, biblical teaching, spiritual practices, leader development, and multiplication.
  • Recruit, equip, coach, and support group leaders and apprentices. Develop a clear pathway that connects participation in groups with growth in faith, service, leadership, and disciple-making.
  • Strengthen the existing group structure to support future expansion. Develop leaders and explore opportunities for groups beyond the church campus, including apartment communities.
  • Collaborate with the Director of Missions and Mobilization, who works with group Go Leaders to engage members in ministry and missions.


Member Care through Groups and Deacons

  • Develop and lead a care approach that strategically places a Deacon in every group and equips Deacons and group leaders to respond to absences, illness, crises, and spiritual concerns.
  • Provide an intentional group connection and named care responsibility for members unable or unwilling to attend regularly, including homebound members and students away at college.
  • Maintain close pastoral relationships with Deacons and group leaders. Coordinate with the Member Care Coordinator and ensure needs beyond group capacity are referred to the pastoral team with appropriate follow-through.


Next Gen and Family Discipleship

  • Supervise the Next Gen Team Leader through coaching, goal setting, and performance evaluation. The team leader retains day-to-day responsibility for Next Gen and supervision of its individual ministry departments and team members.
  • Work with the Next Gen Team Leader to equip parents as the primary disciple makers in their homes and strengthen continuity between family discipleship, Next Gen, and adult groups.


Ministry Coordination and Planning

  • Serve as the Senior Pastor’s principal ministry lieutenant, assisting with strategic planning, ministry evaluation, coordinated programming, and follow-through at San Marco.
  • On the Senior Pastor’s behalf, convene ministry leaders, require their participation and ministry proposals, and help assemble coordinated plans, including contributions from leaders who do not report to this position.
  • Clarify agreed responsibilities, timelines, and commitments; track progress and bring unresolved conflicts to the Senior Pastor. The Senior Pastor retains primary responsibility for overall San Marco ministry planning and final decisions on competing priorities.


Leadership Development

  • Renew leadership-development efforts by identifying and preparing people to lead groups, ministries, and future congregations.
  • Own the ministry design, recruitment, placement, and coaching of internships and apprenticeships. Coordinate with ministry leaders who provide practical ministry experience and mentoring.
  • Work with the Executive Pastor, who handles employment, budget, and administrative requirements for these initiatives.


Family of Churches and Multiplication

  • Develop effective ministry at San Marco and equip its leaders to share adaptable resources, training, and coaching across the Family. Support local pastors and leaders in applying these resources within their own languages and cultures.
  • Develop groups and leaders that contribute to the broader strategy of planting churches for languages spoken in Duval County Public Schools that do not already have a healthy, Gospel-centered church. Collaborate with the Senior Pastor, Director of Missions and Mobilization, and FOC pastors.
  • Identify groups and leaders showing readiness to become congregations and initiate discernment with the Senior Pastor and Family Council. Decisions to establish a congregation are collaborative.
  • Continue Grow coaching after a congregation launches. Its pastor is supervised by the Host Congregation’s pastor, or directly by the Senior Pastor when the host pastor is unable to provide supervision.


Preaching, Teaching, and Pastoral Ministry

  • Assist the Senior Pastor in the preaching ministry, preaching approximately 14–18 Sundays annually across San Marco and other FOC congregations, as scheduled in consultation with the Senior Pastor and local pastors.
  • Lead Next Steps approximately once a month and teach in groups, leader training, and other settings as needed.
  • Serve as part of the core pastoral team, maintaining a pastoral presence among members, staff, and FOC pastors. Participate in the assigned Pastoral Call rotation and assist with hospital visits, counseling, funerals, weddings, emergencies, and other pastoral needs.


Stewardship and Ministry Support

  • Manage the Grow budget, including personnel, adult groups, and Next Gen ministry, within approved church policies and budget authority. The proposed 2027 Grow budget is $223,838, subject to church approval.
  • Coordinate with the Executive Pastor on personnel matters, shared systems, and expenses beyond the approved church budget. Work with the Member Care and Ministry Support Coordinators, who provide support to this role; no dedicated administrative assistant is currently assigned.


Authority and Working Relationships

The Associate Pastor reports directly to the Senior Pastor. The Executive Pastor provides personnel and operational support and owns organization-wide personnel processes, shared systems, and expenses exceeding the approved church budget. Supervision of assigned staff is exercised in accordance with Aspire’s personnel policies.

 

This role owns Grow leadership and exercises delegated ministry-coordination authority on behalf of the Senior Pastor. That authority allows the Director to convene leaders, request proposals, and follow up on agreed plans; it does not create supervisory authority over leaders outside the assigned reporting structure. The Senior Pastor resolves competing ministry priorities in close partnership with the Associate Pastor, Executive Pastor, and Director of Missions and Mobilization.


The Director of Missions and Mobilization retains leadership of Go, including missions, partnerships, ESL, GoJax, and internal and external mobilization. Worship arts, administration, missions and mobilization, community-center management, and building-project leadership are outside this position’s supervisory scope. These leaders remain essential collaborators in a coordinated discipleship ministry.

 

First Year Priorities and Evaluation

The first year will emphasize the following priorities in order, alongside ongoing preaching, pastoral care, and ministry coordination:


  1. Strengthen existing groups, group leaders, Deacon care, and group multiplication.
  2. Coordinate with Next Gen to strengthen parents as their children’s primary disciple makers.
  3. Renew leadership-development initiatives through a manageable approach to internships and apprenticeships.


The Senior Pastor and Associate Pastor will establish goals using current baselines and available resources. Evaluation will consider 

Adult Grow participation, group health, leader and apprentice development, Deacon coverage, care follow-through, and progress toward multiplication. Increased baptisms and worship attendance at San Marco are shared congregational outcomes to which this role contributes. Evaluation will also consider parent equipping, staff development, Family-wide ministry support, and improved planning and follow-through.

 

Skills and Leadership Expectations

  • A growing love for Jesus; biblical faithfulness; prayerfulness; integrity; humility; and pastoral character above reproach; and faith and practice aligned with Aspire’s Statement of Faith.
  • Ability to develop disciples and leaders, communicate clearly, make timely decisions, manage assigned staff, and follow through on commitments.
  • Effective biblical preaching and teaching; sound pastoral judgment, confidentiality, and compassion in member care.
  • Ability to work across cultures and ministry functions, respect local pastoral leadership, and collaborate with staff and lay leaders.
  • Strategic planning, budget stewardship, organization, and proficiency with Microsoft 365 and church ministry systems.
  • Attend required staff and ministry meetings, participate in church-wide ministry, and carry out other related responsibilities assigned by the Senior Pastor in keeping with this position’s purpose and priorities.


Education and Experience

  • Master of Divinity or comparable education in a related field from an accredited school; ordination to pastoral ministry.
  • At least five years of ministry experience demonstrating effective leadership, sound judgment, and pastoral character.
  • Active membership in a church of like faith and practice and willingness and ability to meet Aspire Church San Marco’s membership requirements.
