Adjunct faculty provide engaging, high-quality instruction using innovative teaching methods, current technology, and relevant industry practices. If you are passionate about ministry, education, and supporting students in their academic and spiritual growth, we encourage you to apply.


Why Work at GCU:

  • Tuition benefits specifically for the adjunct employee
  • 401(k)
  • Employee Perks and Discounts

Course: Ministerial Ethics


This course examines the biblical and theological foundations of Christian ethics along with an analysis of the roles and responsibilities of gospel ministry. Significant attention is given to self-care, personal morality, and character formation as well as ethical concerns unique to ministers as they lead, equip, shepherd, and intercede for God’s people.


What You Will Do:


Responsibilities include equipping students with the required skill set, facilitating classroom discussions, assessing student performance, and preparing students to be successful leaders in their chosen profession. Other main responsibilities include the following:

  • Facilitate weekly main discussion forums to engage students in the online classroom.
  • Adhere to weekly grading requirements, deadlines, and timeframes.
  • Respond to students’ questions and emails within the established timeframes.
  • Provide a positive example to students by supporting the University’s Doctrinal Statement, Ethical Position Statement and Mission of Grand Canyon University.

Qualifications: Please read carefully and ensure you meet qualifications before submitting your application.


Minimum: PhD from an accredited college or university in theology or philosophy or ethics AND At least two years professional experience in ministry or teaching at the postsecondary level.

Description:

There are nearly 300,000 teenagers of active-duty U.S. military parents who are stationed all over the world. These teens move an average of seven times during their school-aged years. The questions of identity and belonging that all teens face grow even more challenging to answer amid starting over and meeting new friends at each location.

This is where you can be the difference in a military teen’s life! By being in their world, walking alongside them, and creating a community where they experience the truth of God’s love and purpose for them, our staff provide a safe space where teens can develop friendships and connections to experience laughter, build hope, and generate resiliency.

We are currently providing incarnational ministry at many military installations around the world. You will have the opportunity to lead and oversee the overall Young Life Military program, known as Club Beyond, which is ecumenically focused and outreach oriented.

We are currently looking for both full-time and part-time staff throughout the United States, as well as international locations. Colorado Springs, CO, is the headquarters.

Responsibilities:

  • Actively develop healthy relationships with adults, as well as kids, and build vibrant relationships with the local community, the military installation, and the chapel community.
  • Be a role model (incarnational) and assist with developing community outreach to "unchurched" teens, discipleship to Christian teens, and leading and equipping volunteers to do "hands-on" middle and high school Christian youth programs.
  • Work well in an environment that sees (due to high military operational tempo) a high degree of turnover among teens, families, chaplains and volunteers.
  • Be respectful of and embrace a community that is deeply influenced by a military culture.
  • In this ministry, you will need to live out the Club Beyond Core Value Statement:

Club Beyond is a Christ-centered community of leaders with an exclusively military focus. Our methods are incarnational, and our perspective is ecumenical. We leverage strategic partnerships for the greatest results. We value professionalism from our staff and excellence in our stewardship.

Qualifications:

  • A deep love for Christ and for lost teens.
  • Competent communicator with youths, parents, and senior military leaders.
  • Teachable heart.
  • Willingness to make a three-year commitment.
  • Minimum of three years' youth ministry experience preferred.
  • College degree preferred.
  • Willingness to raise part of the budget through personal support.
  • Committed to a relational ministry approach.
  • Energetic.
  • Small event planning skills.

  • Note, this position would require our Staff to live near the community where they would be doing ministry.

Job Description:

Overview:

We don’t simply hire employees. We invest in them. When you work at Chatham, we empower you — offering professional development opportunities to help you grow in your career, no matter if you've been here for five months or 15 years. Chatham has worked hard to create a distinct work environment that values people, teamwork, integrity, and client service. You will have immediate opportunities to partner with talented subject matter experts, work on complex projects, and contribute to the value Chatham delivers every day. 

Summary:

As a Covenant Data Specialist on Chatham’s Investment Management team, you will help ensure institutional real estate investors have accurate and consistent covenant information to understand financing obligations, anticipate important requirements, and proactively manage risk across complex debt portfolios. You will review commercial real estate loan agreements and related financing documents to identify and interpret financial, reporting, performance, and other loan covenants, translating complex and varied legal language into Chatham’s established standardized covenant data structure. You will also serve as a key quality-control resource, reviewing covenant data, identifying inconsistencies, and helping the team maintain established data-quality standards.

In this role you will:

  • Review commercial real estate loan agreements, amendments, guaranties, promissory notes, and other financing documents to identify relevant financial, reporting, performance, and other covenants.
  • Interpret covenant provisions, related definitions, calculation requirements, thresholds, testing periods, cure provisions, exceptions, and other terms necessary to understand the full requirement.
  • Translate varied legal language into Chatham’s established standardized covenant data structure and consistently apply defined data conventions across different loans and document structures.
  • Distinguish substantive covenant requirements from supporting language and recognize when provisions are unusual, ambiguous, or require additional interpretation.
  • Perform detailed quality-control reviews of covenant data prepared by others, comparing captured information with underlying loan documentation for accuracy and completeness.
  • Identify errors, inconsistencies, and departures from established data standards and provide clear, actionable feedback.
  • Recognize recurring data-quality issues and identify opportunities to improve procedures, training, standards, and quality controls.
  • Partner with teammates across data, implementation, and advisory functions to resolve questions involving loan terms and covenant interpretation.
  • Share subject-matter knowledge and help reinforce consistent covenant interpretation and data-quality practices across the team.

Your impact:

  • Help provide institutional real estate investors with reliable covenant information they can use to understand financing obligations and proactively manage their debt portfolios.
  • Improve the accuracy and consistency of covenant data by applying established standards and conducting thorough quality-control reviews.
  • Partner across Chatham’s data, implementation, and advisory teams to resolve complex or ambiguous questions involving loan terms and covenant interpretation.
  • Develop expertise in commercial loan documentation and covenant structures, enabling you to identify when interconnected provisions require additional analysis or judgment.
  • Strengthen the team’s data-quality practices by identifying patterns in errors and contributing to improvements in processes, standards, training, and controls.
  • Become a trusted covenant data and quality resource by consistently producing high-quality work, sharing subject-matter expertise, and supporting consistent interpretation across the team.

Contributors to your success:

  • Experience reading and interpreting commercial loan documents or other complex legal or financial agreements.
  • Working knowledge of commercial lending concepts and loan covenants.
  • Strong attention to detail and a demonstrated commitment to data accuracy and completeness.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, including the ability to evaluate information in context and exercise sound judgment when information is unclear, unusual, or does not align with established standards.
  • Ability to interpret varied document language and translate it into a consistent, standardized format.
  • Ability to independently identify discrepancies and determine when unusual or ambiguous provisions require additional review.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to provide clear and constructive feedback.
  • Strong organizational skills and the ability to maintain accuracy while working across a high volume of detailed information.
  • Experience with commercial real estate lending, debt management, loan servicing, covenant monitoring, underwriting, or a related field is preferred.
  • Experience performing quality-control, quality-assurance, or peer-review responsibilities is preferred.
  • Familiarity with financial covenants such as debt service coverage ratio, debt yield, loan-to-value, liquidity, net worth, and other borrower- or property-level requirements is preferred.
  • Experience working with structured financial data or established data standards is preferred.
  • Experience identifying requirements across loan agreements, amendments, guaranties, and other interconnected financing documents is preferred.

For Colorado based candidates, the compensation range for the position is expected to be between $100,000 and $115,000 annually. Total compensation, including base pay, discretionary individual bonus and company bonus, may be higher than the range listed depending on applicant's skills, qualifications, and experience. Benefits include health insurance, life and disability insurance, 401K, EAP, paid holidays, and paid time off.

About Chatham Financial:

Chatham Financial is the leading independent capital markets advisor, delivering an integrated blend of expert advice and powerful technology to help you reduce risk and seize opportunity. With decades of capital markets strategy, execution, monitoring, and performance expertise, we serve as an unwavering advocate for your best interests and your innovation partner. Our technology platform unifies data across assets, debt, and derivatives, giving you unmatched agility, transparency, and insight.

It’s clear ahead.

Our commitment is to carry that light forward in every partnership, every solution, and every market we serve.

We help guide the way—giving clients the insight and momentum to move forward with confidence, no matter what lies ahead.

Program Summary

The Residency Program is offered to qualified male candidates who have graduated from seminary and are seeking ordination as ministers of the gospel. Candidates are selected for the Residency Program based on demonstrated leadership ability and the potential to play a significant role in the work of church renewal as pastors. After successful completion of the Residency Program, many residents become excellent candidates to serve as lead pastors of churches in need of renewal, assistant/associate pastors of larger churches within Resound’s network, or church planters, depending on gifting and opportunity.


Residents:

  • Work full-time at the local church in supervised ministry for a two-year period, with select opportunities to teach, preach, facilitate worship, lead a Community Group, participate in a specific area of ministry, and engage in mission and evangelism;
  • Participate in a series of modules focused on leadership, preaching, mission, pastoral care, cultural dynamics, and church renewal;
  • Receive an annual stipend plus health care benefits.


Application

To apply for the Residency Program, we invite you to write four essays, with each essay no more than 1,000 words in content. The essays are to be in response to these four prompts/questions:

  • Describe your experience as a follower of Jesus, including the most significant spiritual events and influences in your life.
  • In what ways has God gifted you for ministry, and what ministry experiences have confirmed your sense of call up to this point?
  • Please give some examples of how you have navigated hardships and challenges in your life and ministry to this point.
  • Describe your desire to participate in Resound and your sense of how you must grow and mature to become more effective as a ministry leader.


In addition, please provide:

  • a resume which lists your educational background and work experience
  • an official transcript from college and seminary
  • two letters of reference, preferably one from a professor and one from a church leader.


The application deadline for the Resound residency cohort commencing in September 2026 is February 1st, 2026.

Company Description

Calvary Church is a multi-generational church family of people from different backgrounds but unified in our love of Jesus, worshipping together since 1955.  We desire to be a disciple making community of 

broken people, being made new in Jesus, overflowing with gratitude, and poured out for others 

whose mission is to 

bless and transform lives and communities through the Gospel of our Lord, Jesus Christ.

Job Description

Calvary Church is seeking a Worship Leader / Pastor that will work closely with the Lead Pastor in cultivating worship services and worship teams that help lead our church family and our community to see and savor the greatness of God in Jesus Christ, in the power of the Holy Spirit. This type of leadership should come from the overflow of the life of a committed Christ-follower, demonstrated by a humble and courageous spirit. Fostering dynamic, participatory, congregational worship while celebrating the best of the past and the best of the new, is a key priority for our church.  Specific responsibilities include:

  1. Serving as a member of the Staff Leadership Team at Calvary, being an engaged, committed, passionate team member developing worship ministries in alignment with the mission of Calvary to bless and transform lives and communities through the Gospel of our Lord, Jesus Christ.

  2. Building on Calvary’s traditions while developing a vision for where God might be calling our church and our worship teams to grow in new expressions of worship.

  3. Modeling and leading heartfelt worship in an invitational style – through creating worship experiences that draws people in, encourages participation, and invites people into a deeper relationship with Jesus through all the seasons of life from celebration to lamentation.

  4. Planning and preparing for worship services. (Currently there are two identical Sunday morning services).  Designing worship elements and selecting “psalms, hymns and spiritual songs” that engages the congregation and supports the preaching of God’s Word.

  5. Leading rehearsals that serve a dual purpose: (A) preparation for worship services and (B) cultivation of a Christ-centered discipling community of worshippers.

  6. Recruiting, shepherding, teaching, and training volunteer leaders, musicians, vocalists, and artists in the church and outside the church to serve the congregation and the community as a team with skill and humility.

  7. Developing and administering an annual budget for the worship ministry in accordance with the financial policies of the church.

  8. Overseeing and assisting in the planning and implementing of special or seasonal worship events outside of Sunday worship services.

  9. Overseeing the AV/Production team staff and volunteers.

  10. Overseeing and developing other worship staff and worship ministries at Calvary.

  11. Performing other duties as assigned by the Lead Pastor

Qualifications

A qualified applicant would have the following characteristics:

  • A clear testimony of faith in Jesus Christ and a vital, growing personal relationship with Him.

  • A clear calling to sacrificial leadership of Christ’s people and a demonstrable heart for the lost, expressed in a life and reputation consistent with that calling.

  • Gifted in leading participatory congregational worship.

  • Experience as a relational leader with organizational skills.

  • Strong, positive interpersonal chemistry with Calvary’s lead staff coupled with a passion lead and develop God’s people specifically in worship arts.

  • Equipped in sound doctrine and able to teach God’s Word.

  • Highly skilled in at least one instrument (guitar, piano or keyboard preferred) with the ability to read music.  Proficiency in other instruments is a plus.

  • Proficiency in vocal pedagogy, coaching and directing for soloists and ensembles.  Experience in choral direction is a plus.

  • Experience as a producer, including planning, organizing, sourcing, rehearsing and presenting worship events.  Experience in creative arts such as writing songs or scripts is a plus.  Experience in visual design and lighting is a plus.

Additional Information

  • Direct report to the Lead Pastor

  • Full-time, salaried, exempt

  • Salary commensurate with experience

  • Health Insurance for entire family

  • 403(b) retirement program

  • Vacation and holiday days

All your information will be kept confidential according to EEO guidelines.

Area Ministry Director - Texas Gulf Coast Area (Undergraduate Ministry)

Work Location:

Texas

Job Type:

Full time

The Area Director for Texas Gulf Coast area would be responsible for our ministry work in Southeast Texas (starting from College Station, TX).

An Area Director leads and oversees a ministry team to plant and to grow witnessing communities of students and faculty who follow Jesus on college and university campuses. Through these groups, we believe ever-increasing numbers of students and faculty from all ethnic groups and areas of the campus will be transformed by the gospel. We expect to see campuses increasingly become places where people, ideas, and structures flourish for the common good and to the glory of God. We confidently anticipate that our InterVarsity alumni will be growing disciples and change agents across the country and around the world.

ESSENTIAL COMMITMENTS/RESPONSIBILITIES

1. Spiritual Growth

The Area Ministry Director models spiritual maturity as a disciple of Jesus Christ so that your life and work increasingly reflects a growing love for God, God’s Word, God’s people of every ethnicity and culture, and God’s purposes in the world.

  • Pursue a vibrant relationship with the triune God through engagement with Scripture, prayer, and worship, both individually and in community
  • Exercise self-leadership (growing in self-awareness, self-management, relational integrity, and resiliency)
  • Embrace and practice Scriptural standards for behavior and attitudes, including those described in the Code of Conduct

​2. Campus Ministry Leadership

As an Area Director, you inspire, coach and develop campus staff ministers (“ministers”), students, faculty, and ministry partners to increase the number of witnessing communities, as well as the size, health, spiritual maturity, and campus-wide influence of existing witnessing communities by being a:

Visionary Guide:

  • Create a culture of dependence on God to gain vision for establishing and advancing witnessing communities that reach every corner of every campus in your area
  • Model InterVarsity’s vision and Core Values for supervisees
  • Lead staff, students, and faculty through Scripture, prayer, teaching and discipleship experiences in a way that motivates and shapes their ministry around vision
  • Set appropriate annual goals through prayer, research and reflection with your teams

Structural Architect:

  • Lead your team to develop and implement plans to achieve ministry goals
  • Adapt the plan as needed through rhythms of action, reflection and evaluation
  • Develop, align and leverage programs and structures to move the mission forward

Missional Developer:

  • Recruit a diversity of qualified minister candidates
  • Develop ministers to spiritually grow in Christ in intimacy, like Christ in character, and with Christ in his mission to current and new campuses
  • Develop ministers professionally so that they are consistently increasing their gifts and skills as ministry leaders
  • Supervise ministers, using appropriate leadership style for the individual and situation, to help them accomplish assigned tasks. This will require coaching, assessing, correcting and affirming job-related behaviors
  • Proactively establish and develop healthy relationships across racial, ethnic, national background, and gender barriers with staff, students, faculty, and ministry partners to build effective and diverse communities
  • Build an effective minister team that collaborates well and accomplishes goals

3. Organizational Collaboration

As an Area Director, you are part of a national organization and work in partnership with local, area, divisional, regional, and national InterVarsity ministers and volunteers.

  • Participate in regional leadership as determined by the Regional Director, to set ministry vision and strategies, contribute to accomplishing plans, and provide regional leadership in specific areas
  • Positively and constructively respond to the direction and coaching of line supervisors
  • Build productive ministry partnerships with regional and national collaborative leaders
  • Establish systems, processes and protocols to fulfill regular operational and administrative tasks in a timely manner (reporting, finances, human resources, etc.)
  • Maintain sound financial status of the area through management of budgeting, expense control and ministry partnership development
  • Become familiar with and comply with all InterVarsity policies and procedures

4. Ministry Partnership Development (MPD)

As an Area Director, you will develop a team of partners who will resource the ministry financially, in prayer, or with volunteer service that advances the mission.

  • Develop and maintain a ministry among partners who will fund InterVarsity
  • Ensure ministry budget is fully funded
  • Supervise each minister’s MPD (collaborating with coaches when applicable) and equip staff to build ministry partners
  • Build resource networks with alumni, volunteers, churches, advocacy councils, and major donors, in particular to fund low-network ministers
  • Communicate regularly with ministry partners

5. Accomplish all other assigned tasks as appropriate

QUALIFICATIONS

  • Annually affirm InterVarsity’s Statement of Agreement (Doctrinal Basis and Purpose Statement). Abide by InterVarsity’s Code of Conduct
  • Bachelor’s degree required
  • Minimum three years campus ministry or equivalent work experience required
  • Strong ministry skills (including the ability to communicate spiritual vision, teach spiritual and biblical principles, plan ministry programs, and spiritually disciple, coach and mentor)
  • Proven ability to work well with others and the ability to develop a team of campus ministers.
  • Strong interpersonal skills (including ability to minister to diverse ethnic communities and faculty)
  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills
  • Demonstrated problem solving skills
  • Familiarity with word processing, presentation, email, and spreadsheet software

WORK ENVIRONMENT/PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS

The AD position leads ministry in a college campus environment. A designated office space may or may not be available. The AD is required to travel to on-campus and off-campus sites as appropriate. Off-campus travel includes, but is not limited to student ministry conferences, MPD meetings, and InterVarsity-sponsored training sessions, meetings, and conferences. The AD is regularly required to communicate with others, and routinely uses standard office equipment such as computers, phones, etc.

Description:
There are nearly 300,000 teenagers of active-duty U.S. military parents who are stationed all over the world. These teens move an average of seven times during their school-aged years. The questions of identity and belonging that all teens face grow even more challenging to answer amid starting over and meeting new friends at each location.
This is where you can be the difference in a military teen’s life! By being in their world, walking alongside them, and creating a community where they experience the truth of God’s love and purpose for them, our staff provide a safe space where teens can develop friendships and connections to experience laughter, build hope, and generate resiliency.
We are currently providing incarnational ministry at many military installations around the world. You will have the opportunity to lead and oversee the overall Young Life Military program, known as Club Beyond, which is ecumenically focused and outreach oriented.
Responsibilities:
  • Actively develop healthy relationships with adults, as well as kids, and build vibrant relationships with the local community, the military installation, and the chapel community.
  • Be a role model (incarnational) and assist with developing community outreach to "unchurched" teens, discipleship to Christian teens, and leading and equipping volunteers to do "hands-on" middle and high school Christian youth programs.
  • Work well in an environment that sees (due to high military operational tempo) a high degree of turnover among teens, families, chaplains and volunteers.
  • Be respectful of and embrace a community that is deeply influenced by a military culture.
  • In this ministry, you will need to live out the Club Beyond Core Value Statement:
Club Beyond is a Christ-centered community of leaders with an exclusively military focus. Our methods are incarnational, and our perspective is ecumenical. We leverage strategic partnerships for the greatest results. We value professionalism from our staff and excellence in our stewardship.
Qualifications:
  • A deep love for Christ and for lost teens.
  • Competent communicator with youths, parents, and senior military leaders.
  • Teachable heart.
  • Willingness to make a three-year commitment.
  • Minimum of three years' youth ministry experience preferred.
  • College degree preferred.
  • Willingness to raise part of the budget through personal support.
  • Committed to a relational ministry approach.
  • Energetic.
  • Small event planning skills.
  • Strong initiative.
  • Note, this position would require our Staff to live near the community where they would be doing ministry.
Benefits:
  • Full-time salary: Based on experience, responsibility, and fundraising levels.
  • Benefits: Full health coverage (including dental, vision and life insurance).
  • Expense reimbursement (mileage [office and ministry related]).
  • Training and career development is built into the job.
Salary:
The Base Salary range: $45,000 to $60,000 (Salary is based on education and experience). In addition to salary, a Cost of Living Adjustment, dependent on location, is available. The Annual National Funding provided is $16,667.
Location:
Club Beyond works on military installations all over the world. We currently have openings at:
In the USA:
  • Fort Rucker, Alabama
  • Joint Base Elmendorf-Richardson (JBER), Alaska
  • Fort Irwin, California
  • Camp Pendleton, California
  • Travis Air Force Base, California

Overseas:
  • Geilenkirchen, Germany and various other locations in Germany

Reports to: Lead Pastor
Direct Reports: Modern Worship Director, Worship Coordinator, and designated Classic Worship staff/leaders
Status: Full-Time, Salaried, Exempt, Commissioned-Clergy


Position Summary

Emmanuel Faith Community Church is seeking a spiritually mature, visionary, and relational Worship Pastor to lead our church in passionate, Jesus-centered worship across multiple styles and venues.

This is a key senior leadership role in a thriving, inter-generational, and inter-ethnic church of 3,000 in North County, San Diego. We currently host five services each Sunday: three Modern, one Classic, and one Spanish. The Worship Pastor will participate in the planning, leading, and equipping of teams to serve in all venues. This leader will help unify our worship culture across generations, stewarding our heritage while thoughtfully leading us into the future.

This role carries significant influence in shaping the theological, liturgical, and spiritual formation culture of our church. We are looking for a shepherd-leader who loves people more than platforms and is passionate about cultivating environments where people encounter God and are formed as disciples of Jesus.


Key Responsibilities

Worship Leadership and Pastoral Presence

  • Serve as a primary worship leader and pastoral presence in both Classic and Modern worship services.
  • Provide leadership, oversight, and coaching to worship staff and volunteers.
  • Collaborate with the Lead Pastor and other staff to plan the annual preaching and worship calendar.
  • Serve as a key member of the staff by contributing to the overall vision, strategy, and spiritual health of the entire church.
  • Develop and articulate a unifying Philosophy of Worship Ministry that aligns with EFCC’s mission, theology, and values.
  • Pastor the choir, orchestra, musicians, and congregation through Scripture, prayer, worship leadership, and personal presence.

Strategic Oversight of Worship Environments

  • Participate in the planning and oversight of the weekly liturgy, music, and service flow for our Sunday services (three Modern, one Classic, one Spanish), cultivating meaningful congregational participation and shaping the church’s love for Jesus and commitment to discipleship.
  • Provide visionary leadership for Classic and Modern worship ministries and their teams, stewarding EFCC’s heritage while guiding the church into the future and helping the congregation navigate growth and change with clarity and humility.
  • Collaborate in planning and leading special services and events during seasons such as Christmas Concerts during Advent and special services during Holy Week.
  • Participate in and help lead all-staff worship gatherings and special worship events.

Team Development and Shepherding

  • Recruit, train, disciple, and develop worship leaders, musicians, vocalists, and creative team members.
  • Build leadership pipelines that cultivate and multiply future worship leaders and musicians.
  • Invest in the spiritual formation and relational health of the worship ministry team.
  • Foster unity across stylistic preferences and generations, modeling humility and bridge-building.
  • Cultivate a culture of excellence without ego, marked by joy, humility, and shared leadership.

Creative and Technical Collaboration

  • Partner with the Production/Tech Director to ensure high-quality in-person and livestream worship experiences.
  • Lead collaborative planning processes that integrate musicians, production teams, and pastoral leadership.
  • Ensure music selection, arrangements, rehearsals, and transitions are prepared with excellence.

Administrative Leadership

  • Oversee worship ministry budgets, scheduling, communication systems, and planning tools (e.g., Planning Center).
  • Ensure copyright compliance and music licensing.
  • Coordinate with other ministries (Students, Children’s, Special Events, etc.) as needed.

Additional Opportunities

  • If gifting and capacity allow, serve as a contributing member of the preaching team.
Requirements

Qualifications


Spiritual and Personal

  • A deep and growing relationship with Jesus, marked by character, humility, and spiritual maturity.
  • A shepherd’s heart that genuinely loves and cares for staff, volunteers, and the congregation you are leading in worship.
  • Commitment to unity in an inter-generational and inter-ethnic church.
  • Agreement with EFCC’s statement of faith.

Professional and Musical

  • 5+ years of worship leadership experience in a large church context (1,000+ preferred), with the ability to lead multiple weekend services and significant seasons like Advent, Christmas, and Easter with excellence.
  • Strong vocal ability and proficiency on at least one lead instrument.
  • Experience leading both Classic and Modern worship styles.
  • Experience directing ensembles (choirs, bands, orchestras).
  • High emotional intelligence, with proven ability to lead through change and navigate conflict.
  • Strong organizational and communication skills.
  • Familiarity with tools such as Planning Center, Ableton, ProPresenter, MultiTracks, etc.

Training and Experience

  • Formal training in music, worship leadership, or theology (M.A. or M.Div. preferred).
  • Love for and familiarity with both Classic and Modern worship music. 
  • Experience growing and developing worship ministries, including mentoring and multiplying younger worship leaders.

Full-time
Description

Summary of Position

The Campus Pastor leads the campus staff team to accomplish the mission and vision of Mercy Hill Church in their local context. This is primarily accomplished through a significant focus on the weekly gathering, oversight of groups ministry at the campus, and leveraging influence to move campus attendees towards giving and going. Success for this role is defined by growing campus metrics, healthy campus culture in alignment with Mercy Hill DNA, and consistent multiplication of leaders.


DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

1. Excellence in Implementing the Culture of Mercy Hill

• Ensure Weekend Gatherings reflect the core DNA of Mercy Hill by overseeing service flow and addressing any distractions in real-time.

• Be a visible pastoral presence, engaging with attendees, praying with those in need, and building relational connections.

• Model and reinforce the Mercy Hill values during meetings, interactions, and team leadership, acting as the “primary carrier” of church culture.

• Actively seek and act on feedback to maintain a culture of continual improvement in gatherings and team performance.


2. Leadership through Accountability and Development

• Lead, manage, and hold campus staff accountable to Mercy Hill’s Mission, Vision, and Values through weekly Level 10 meetings, quarterly rocks reviews, and 1:1 meetings.

• Conduct annual reviews with a focus on growth, alignment, and goal-setting for each team member.

• Oversee the hiring, development, and, when necessary, releasing of staff, ensuring alignment with Mercy Hill’s leadership expectations.

• Create pathways for staff to grow as leaders and shepherds, equipping them to step into new levels of responsibility or roles.


3. Pastoring People Through the Growth Flywheel

• Regularly evaluate metrics and trends (e.g., attendance, groups, and giving) to make proactive decisions that foster growth and engagement.

• Shepherd groups by equipping elders to lead group leaders effectively, ensuring robust discipleship at every level.

• Ensure prompt, consistent follow-up with attendees, particularly first-time guests and those needing care, to build connections and trust.

• Engage with the local community intentionally, creating opportunities to bring people into the flywheel (e.g., outreach events, service opportunities).


4. Multiplication as the Pathway to Missional Impact

• Raise up leaders in every ministry area through the leadership pipeline, ensuring a continual flow of capable leaders.

• Identify and develop future church leaders, equipping them for roles in church planting, campus leadership, or ministry leadership.

• Inspire and mobilize people toward Mercy Hill’s vision of going and multiplying, whether through new services, campuses, or church plants.

• Actively plan and execute strategies for multiplying services or campuses to grow the movement and reach more people for the gospel.


Miscellaneous Responsibilities This job description is not meant to be an allinclusive statement of every duty and responsibility that will be required of an employee in this position. Therefore, additional duties may be assigned.

Requirements

CHARACTER:

  1. Models the biblical standard of personal conduct and lifestyle that is expected of all Mercy Hill Church covenant members. (Eph. 4:1)
  2. Fully participates in the life of the church as an active covenant member by gathering, grouping, giving, and going. (Acts 2:42)
  3. Submits to and supports the leadership of the church elders. (Heb. 13:17)
  4. Demonstrates integrity in all facets of life. (Psalms 101:2, 119:1; Prov. 10:9)
  5. Glorifies God with the humble use of spiritual gifts. (Rom. 12:3-8)
  6. Pursues an active relationship with God through prayer and the Word. (Rom. 12:12, Col. 4:2)
  7. Demonstrates an eagerness to repent and believe the gospel. (Matthew 3:8; Mark 1:15)
  8. Gives regularly and generously of time, talent, and treasure to Mercy Hill Church. (Prov. 11:24-25; Matthew 6:19-21; Acts 20:35)
  9. Pursues a healthy lifestyle by treating the body as the temple of the Holy Spirit (1 Cor. 6:19-20) and seeks to balance work with rest (Exodus 20:8-11; John 15:5).

CULTURE (Staff Distinctives):


1. Extremely Driven

2. High EQ

3. 100% Aligned

4. Wise


Job Requirements

Physical Requirements:

1. Ability to frequently stand, sit, and/or walk.

2. Ability to bend, climb stairs, and/or lift frequently.

3. Ability to lift 40 to 50 pounds occasionally.

4. Ability to squat occasionally.

5. Ability to communicate frequently with other people.

6. Ability to operate computers frequently in order to complete necessary office work.

7. Ability to frequently comprehend physical and/or digital documents and frequently prepare physical and/or digital documents.


Work Environment

1. May occasionally, work in temperatures above 95 degrees and below 32 degrees.

2. May occasionally walk on slippery or uneven surfaces.

3. Noise level in the environment is occasionally loud.

4. May occasionally work outdoors.

5. May frequently work indoors within office spaces.


Office Hours and Work Schedule

1. This is a full time role (40 hrs/week). Office hours are Sundays during campus services & Monday through Thursday (Thursday night service when applicable and each Friday of the Weekender).

Student Ministry Residency

The Student Ministry Resident supports and enhances the ministry to the Junior High and High School students at each of our six campuses. They work under the leadership of the Campus Pastor and the Student Ministry Pastor.

General Duties and Responsibilities

  • Lead by example in character, passion, commitment to Christ and His Word, and genuine love and care for people.
  • Provide encouragement and support to the rest of the Student Ministry Team.
  • Help create a collaborative and encouraging environment for both the paid staff and the volunteers who support the ministry.
  • Participate in regular staff meetings for the Student Ministry team.
  • Following the lead of the Student Ministry Pastor, understand and share the Ministry’s vision and purpose with others.
  • Assist in developing solid relationships with parents and other interested adults, to encourage them to be involved in the Student Ministry.
  • Help in the recruiting and training of volunteers to help support the ministry.
  • Provide teaching on Wednesday or Sunday mornings as requested.

  • Help provide activities and events geared for Junior High and High School students.

Campus Staff Minister (Community Colleges in Delaware & the Eastern Shore)

Work Location:

Delaware

Job Type:

Full time

God has called InterVarsity to plant and to build witnessing communities of students and faculty who follow Jesus on college and university campuses. Through these groups, we believe ever- increasing numbers of students and faculty from all ethnic groups and areas of the campus will be transformed by the Gospel. We expect to see campuses increasingly become places where people, ideas, and structures flourish to the glory of God. We confidently anticipate that our InterVarsity alumni will become change agents across the country and around the world. We pursue this calling by discerning and actively participating in what God is already doing on campus. This is the essence of being a Campus Staff Minister (CSM).

Seeking full-time candidate, open to part-time hours if needed.

ESSENTIAL COMMITMENTS/RESPONSIBILITIES 

Spiritual Growth 

As a Campus Staff Minister, you pursue maturity as a disciple of Jesus Christ so that your life and work increasingly reflect a growing love for God, God’s Word, God’s people of every ethnicity and culture, and God’s purposes in the world. To do this, you will: 

  • Pursue a vibrant relationship with the triune God through engagement with Scripture, prayer, and worship, both individually and in community 

  • Develop self-leadership (growing in self-awareness, self-management, relational integrity, and resiliency)

  • Embrace Scriptural standards for behavior and attitudes 

 

Campus Leadership 

As a Campus Staff Minister, you increase the number of witnessing communities, as well as the size, health, spiritual maturity, and campus-wide influence of existing witnessing communities of students and faculty by being a: 

  • Visionary Guide: 

You communicate and model InterVarsity’s vision to see students and faculty transformed, campuses renewed, and world changers developed 

  • Create a culture of humble dependence on God and bold expectation in God’s intention to start new witnessing communities throughout the campus and on new campuses

  • Model – in person and through programs – InterVarsity’s vision and Core Values, including a biblically-defined commitment to engage every ethnic and social group on campus

  • Lead students and faculty – individually and collectively – through Scripture, prayer, teaching, and discipleship experiences, so that they articulate and align their ministry activities around this vision

  • Set annual goals through prayer, research and reflection with your teams (students, faculty, and staff) for qualitative and quantitative growth, including conversions and leadership development 

  • Structural Architect: 

You create, develop, align, and leverage ministry plans, programs, teams, and structures to close the gap between current reality and the aspirational goals. 

  • Build leadership teams who trust and partner well with you and who demonstrate spiritual vitality, relational health, and mission alignment

  • Develop and execute plans to achieve annual goals, evaluating and modifying the plan as needed throughout the year

  • Increase momentum for the vision by aligning programs, structures, conferences, and teams around the goals

  • Mobilize students and faculty to engage their relational networks with the gospel and to start new missional communities

  • Under the direction of the Area Director, may supervise Ministry Interns and Campus Ministry Interns as delegated 

  • Missional Developer: 

You intentionally gather, invite, and develop diverse groups of students and faculty so that they not only encounter and follow Jesus as Savior and Lord but also advance the mission on campus as participants and leaders. 

  • Create ways for faculty and students to encounter and follow Jesus through Scripture, worship, prayer, mission experiences, conferences, etc.

  • Equip students and faculty so that they think strategically about campus engagement and so that they proclaim – in word, deed, and power – the good news of Jesus, regularly inviting students and faculty to follow him as Savior and Lord

  • Disciple students and faculty by equipping them to hear the Word, respond actively, and debrief and interpret the experience so that they grow in Christlikeness, reflect our Core Values, and develop ministry skills

  • Invite, coach, and equip students and faculty to become increasingly effective participants and leaders, including starting new witnessing communities on campuses 

 

Organizational Collaboration 

As a Campus Staff Minister, you have joined a national mission. Therefore, you work with a network of other local, area, regional, and national InterVarsity staff and volunteers so that our work reflects Biblical standards of excellence, integrity, and partnership. 

  • Partner with and respond positively to the direction and coaching of your supervisors and national leaders

  • Contribute to collaborative and productive team meetings and relationships

  • Affiliate chapters under your care and submit Graduating Student Forms in order to increase our partnership with current students and alumni

  • Use national ministry resources and tools, as requested, including recruiting and/or participating in local, regional, or national conferences as

  • Complete reporting, planning and review requirements in a timely way so that you and your supervisors can assess and improve your work as a CSM

  • Comply with all InterVarsity policies and procedures 

 

Ministry Partnership Development 

As a Campus Staff Minister, you will develop a team of partners – churches and individuals (including alumni and community members) – who will resource the ministry financially, in prayer, or volunteer service that advances the mission. 

  • Raise 100% of the financial budget assigned by your supervisor

  • Communicate regularly with your ministry partners, nurturing the relationship through visits, phone calls, emails and regular prayer letters

  • Develop on-going, long-lasting partnership with alumni and volunteers

  • Comply with all Ministry Partnership Policies

  • Identify and invest in advocates who will build networks of volunteers and donors on InterVarsity’s behalf 

 

Accomplish all other assigned tasks as appropriate 

 

QUALIFICATIONS (common to all levels of CSM) 

  • Annually affirm InterVarsity’s Statement of Agreement (Doctrinal Basis and Purpose Statement). Abide by InterVarsity’s Code of Conduct. Believe and behave consonantly with InterVarsity’s Human Sexuality Theological Paper. Affirm and behave consonantly with InterVarsity’s “Women in Ministry Statement of Affirmation”

  • Bachelor’s degree for CSMs assigned to a four-year campus. A minimum of an Associate’s degree for CSMs assigned to a two-year campus or a community college

  • Strong interpersonal skills (including ability to minister to diverse ethnic communities and faculty)

  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills

  • Demonstrated problem solving skills

  • Familiarity with word processing, presentation, email, and spreadsheet software 

 

WORK ENVIRONMENT/PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS 

The CSM position leads ministry in a college campus environment. A designated office space may or may not be available. The CSM is required to travel to on-campus and off- campus sites as appropriate. Off-campus travel includes, but is not limited to: student ministry conferences, Ministry Partnership Development meetings, and InterVarsity- sponsored training sessions, meetings, and conferences. The CSM is regularly required to communicate with others, and routinely uses standard office equipment such as computers, phones, photocopiers, filing cabinets, etc. 

Pay Range: $40,476.00 - $53,952.00 per year

Pay: This position is funded through personal fundraising. Accordingly, compensation will vary based on the ability of the individual to secure a donor team to fund the cost of his/her salary. The anticipated salary range for this position on a full-time basis (40 hours/week) is dependent on a variety of factors, including location and cost of living. The actual salary received, including any geographic adjustment to account for location and cost of living, is subject to the individual’s ability to raise funds necessary to cover the full amount of such salary within the range set forth in the job posting details.

Benefits:

We offer a competitive benefits package, including health care and retirement savings with a match. Eligibility is based on employee type and hours worked.  Benefits include the following:

  • 403(b) Retirement Savings Plan

  • 403(b) matching contributions

  • Dental insurance

  • Employee assistance program

  • Employee discounts

  • Flexible work schedule

  • Flexible spending accounts

  • Health insurance

  • Health savings account

  • Life insurance

  • Paid time off

  • Parental leave

  • Professional development assistance

  • Vision insurance

Equal Employment Opportunity: 

 

InterVarsity Christian Fellowship/USA is both an equal opportunity employer and a faith-based religious organization. We conduct hiring without regard to race, color, ancestry, national origin, citizenship, age, sex, marital status, parental status, membership in any labor organization, political ideology, or disability of an otherwise qualified individual. The status of InterVarsity Christian Fellowship/USA as an equal opportunity employer does not prevent the organization from hiring staff based on their religious beliefs so that all staff share the same religious commitment.  Pursuant to the Civil Rights Act of 1964, Section 702 (42 U.S.C. 2000e 1(a)) InterVarsity Christian Fellowship/USA has the right to, and does, hire only candidates who agree with InterVarsity’s Statement of Agreement: Purpose and Doctrinal Basis because InterVarsity believes that each and every staff plays a vital role in advancing InterVarsity’s mission and purposes.

Lake Mead Christian Ministries (LMCM) Minister - LM Kids Program Coordinator

Job Type: Seasonal (9-12 months);  Hourly (15-22 hours per week)

Department: Church at Lake Mead

Reports to: Discipleship Pastor (or LM Kids Leader)

Compensation: $15-$22/hour

Job Summary: The LM Kids Program Coordinator assists the LM Kids Director and oversees the programming for LM Kids/Club 46 at the Church at Lake Mead. 

Required Spiritual Qualities:

  • Acknowledges Christ as Savior and lives life as His devoted disciple
  • Supports the LMCM Mission by making disciples of Jesus Christ through community
  • Demonstrates spiritual flourishing through personal disciplines of prayer, Bible study, and outreach to others
  • Believes the Bible to be the inspired, authoritative Word of God
  • Agrees with and actively supports the LMCM Statement of Faith
  • Shows evidence of the fruit of the Holy Spirit in interactions with people 
  • Has a Christ-centered home
  • Attends and actively participates in the Church at Lake Mead 

Primary Responsibilities for LM Kids:

  • Curriculum
  • Worship Coordination
  • Family Resources
  • Department Inventory
  • Graphics, slides, etc.
  • Support of the LM Kids team
  • Volunteer recruitment, training, and support

Essential Job Functions:

  • Lives as an example of following Christ in all areas of life and is held accountable by the church team
  • Seeks God in prayer and prays on behalf of the families and children in LM Kids
  • With a servant heart, “owns” the primary responsibilities listed above as part of the overall LM Kids ministry 
  • Manages the LM Kids worship experience (toddlers -3rd grade):
    • Loads in one worship song slide per month for the toddler room and the preschool room. 
    • Prepares upcoming song link(s) by the 15th of each month
    • Plans worship songs at least 4-6 weeks before the month the songs begin, including motions being recorded and shared with the K-3 worship team
    • Recruits 2 student helpers willing to serve 1x/month for the 11 am K-3 worship team
    • Recruits, trains, and leads worship leaders.
  • Toddler Curriculum: Creates and/or determines monthly verses, worship songs with motions, and video lessons.
  • Participates in the weekly setup for LM Kids Sunday morning gatherings and weekly tear-down
    • Completes setup on Friday for LM Kids rooms including door signs, gates, toy placement, free play table items, lesson/props, small group activity needs, etc.
  • Prepares, updates, and uploads lesson materials (props, slides, content, etc.) and resource bins.
    • Comes up with 1-2 activities from the curriculum to incorporate in ages preschool-3rd grade
    • Prepares from start to finish, including communication to the classroom lead and helper.
  • Keeps all LM Kids supplies and toys organized. Notify the LM Kids Director if any LM Kids supply needs come up, including purchases of prop items, with 3 weeks' notice
  • Deep cleaning of LM Kids toys/supplies; schedule one day monthly for a volunteer team to deep clean each room’s toys/supplies
  • Special Events: support the LM Kids team in the  administrative/planning needs approaching special events, and work the event from setup to tear down
    • Events could be added, but so far include: Easter Jam, Family Movie Night, Jingle Jamboree, and Quarterly Family Sunday (5th Sunday of the month)
  • Ensures policies and procedures are being followed for LM Kids
  • Provides helpful feedback for LM Kids Director or Discipleship Pastor
  • Meets with church staff members or leaders for spiritual development and discipleship
  • Assists the LM Kids leadership team as needed
  • Additional duties as assigned by the LM Kids Leader

Benefits: 

Ministry Scholarship for LMCA and Lil’ Eagles tuition; Reductions - Minimum of an average of 20 hours of employment weekly, 20% scholarship, additional years 5% until max of 30%. The average hours must be met on an ongoing basis and reviewed during the 60-day introductory period and annually.

VISION: The vision of Sandals Church is to be real with ourselves, God, and others.

THE ROLE: Oversees the on-platform execution of worship for Lake Arrowhead, partnering with the Central Support and Campus/Department leadership teams to deliver a spiritually deep and engaging worship experience at SandalsChurch. Owns the strategy and execution of developing a healthy and skilled team of volunteer musicians, vocalists, and leaders.

SCOPE: Sandals Church Lake Arrowhead

REPORTS TO: Campus Pastor

 

WHAT YOU OWN

Worship Leadership

  • Have an openness and awareness of what God is doing in the moment while leading.
  • Lead worship on the platform at all assigned services.
  • Carry, communicate, and execute the spiritual, pastoral, and musical tone under the vision set by the Campus Pastor.
  • Proactively schedule and develop a full team of musicians, vocalists, band leaders, and worship leaders.
  • Prepare and communicate service flow, vocal and band direction, and leadership moments in partnership with the Production and Sandals Worship Leadership team.
  • Ensure setlists, chord charts, and arrangements are accurate and finalized before rehearsal; make thoughtful updates as needed.
  • Facilitate rehearsals in collaboration with Band and Production leaders.
  • Build, care for, and develop campus worship team members to grow in skill, leadership, and spiritual maturity.
  • Relationally invest in team members, fostering trust and spiritual growth.
  • Facilitate and manage auditions for your campus/department.
  • Equip, empower, and release worship leaders and vocalists with the goal of multiplication and sustainability.
  • Maintain accurate team rosters in Planning Center and CCB.
  • Attend campus engagement meetings in person and other required department meetings.
  • Support cross-ministry efforts that reinforce a unified culture across the church.
  • Serve as the primary point of contact for musicians and production regarding instruments, gear, and playback.
  • Maintain and steward campus instruments and gear; anticipate needs and collaborate on repairs or requests.

 

HOW YOU COLLABORATE

  • Develop a healthy and collaborative partnership with the Campus and Central Support teams to align on worship vision, team culture, service flow, and musical style.
  • Work alongside production and campus staff to ensure worship experiences are spiritually grounded, musically excellent, timely, and technically prepared.

 

EVALUATION: Personal and collective feedback is essential for healthy development. You commit to being receptive to a positive culture of feedback and evaluation, understanding that this is a key component for growth, excellence, and success in your role.

SANDALS STAFF CORE VALUES: As Staff, we are expected to champion and live out the Values, Attributes, and Expectations as defined in the Culture Stack.

 

COMPENSATION INFORMATION:

Pay Range: $20-$23 per hour.

We will provide a pay rate that is within our compensation structure and that fits a candidate’s qualifications and experience for the job. A wage range posted is not a guarantee of a specific wage for a job offer

We conduct hiring without regard to race, ethnicity, national origin, citizenship, age, sex, marital status, membership in any labor organization, political ideology, or disability of an otherwise qualified individual. The status of Sandals Church as an equal opportunity employer does not prevent us from hiring staff based on their religious beliefs so that all employees share the same religious commitment, which is central to our mission.

This position requires its primary duty be the performance of work requiring invention, imagination, originality or talent in a recognized field of artistic or creative endeavor.

Essential Functions
Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

Personal:

  • Passionate about tithing at least 10% of your income to what God is doing through the vision of Faith Church
  • Invest in and lead a Faith Church connect group
  • Be responsible for developing & multiplying Dream Team

Essential Duties & Responsibilities:

  • Lead Campus Rehearsal on Thursday
  • Tuesday Night Service worship leading (on a Rotating Schedule)
  • Leading Worship at Staff Meeting (on a Rotating Schedule)
  • Lead 4 (of 6) Connect Group (minimum 2 must be musically focused)
  • Oversee Auditions & Assimilation Process (STL and FL)

St Anselm Church
Maintenance Worker

Scope of Job:

This position is for an enthusiastic, responsible and dedicated worker that will ensure the
facilities, equipment and parish campus are safe, clean and functional. Must be able to work
independently or with maintenance coworker.

Responsibilities:

Inspections: Conduct regular walkthroughs of buildings and equipment to identify potential
issues or safety hazards.

Preventative Maintenance: Perform routine tasks like replacing filters, cleaning A/C systems
to prevent breakdowns, clean gutters and roof drains.

General Repairs: Handle minor electrical, plumbing, carpentry, and HVAC fixes (e.g., changing
bulbs and ballasts, repairing inoperable plumbing fixtures and repairing locks and pew kneelers).

Custodial: Clean, vacuum, mop and maintain all buildings on campus (excluding Rectory)

Setups: Setup for different ministries and events in all campus buildings (tables, chairs,
weddings, funerals, etc.)

Availability: Work weekday shifts, every other weekend evenings (two (2) hours each evening)
and all special events or emergencies as directed by the Pastor

Applicant Must Provide: Cellphone and basic tools to perform repairs; screwdrivers, wrenches,
drill and bits etc.

Qualifications and Skills

Education: High school diploma or equivalent is standard; technical certificates (HVAC,
plumbing, electrical) are desired but not required.

Experience: Number of years of past work in residential or commercial fields.

Hard Skills: Proficiency with hand and power tools, program timers, ability to read
blueprints/manuals, and basic knowledge of building systems.

Soft Skills: Strong problem-solving, communication, and time-management abilities.

Physical and Environmental Requirements

Manual Labor: Ability to bend, pull, push, lift and move heavy objects (often 50+ lbs),
repetitive work (table and chair setups), climb ladders, walking and standing for long periods.
Operate various mechanical custodial machines.

Conditions: Ability to work in various weather conditions, heights, and occasionally late
nights.

Hours and Benefits

Schedule: Position is Monday thru Friday 9 am to 4:30 pm with every other weekend Saturday 5
pm to 7pm and Sunday 6 pm to 8 pm. (Other scheduled events can alter weekday and weekend times).
Overtime is available with busier times throughout the year.

Perks: Benefits include: Employer contribution health insurance, paid vacation and sick days
off (accumulated hours each pay period), 401k, bonuses at Christmas and Easter.

job_name: Resound Project Ministry Intern - Interest Form
post_html:
The Ministry Internship Program is offered to qualified male and female candidates who have discerned a call to ministry and who are pursuing a degree from an accredited seminary. The purpose of the program is to help students grow spiritually and clarify their sense of call while worshipping and serving in the local church.


The internship is designed so that students receive a substantial amount of relational and spiritual support from the congregation and its members while also gaining extensive experience in ministry. We anticipate that some Ministry Interns will in the future serve the Church as senior, associate or assistant pastors or as ministry directors, and many will become excellent candidates for future positions at any one of the churches in the growing Resound network.


Interns:

  • Work full time at the local church for a renewable one-year period in supervised ministry in a specific area, such as Community Groups, Pastoral Care, Young Professionals, College Ministry, Youth Ministry, Children’s Ministry, Church Administration, or Mission and Evangelism;
  • Pursue an advanced degree such as a Master of Arts or a Master of Divinity through an accredited seminary;
  • Participate in a series of modules focused on leadership, preaching, mission, pastoral care, cultural dynamics, and church renewal;
  • Receive a monthly stipend and scholarship for seminary.


If you have any questions, please email Andrew Smith at asmith@resoundproject.org.

Description

Position Title: Pastoral Associate for Parish Life

 

Position Type

Full Time

 

Description

Our Parish Family:

Through the Partners in the Gospel initiative, the Roman Catholic Archdiocese of Seattle has integrated parishes and resources into groupings of parish families that are now in the process of becoming new canonical parishes. Saint Michael Parish (Olympia) and Saint Edward Parish (Shelton) constitute a dynamic and growth-oriented parish family.  St. Michael Parish and St. Michael Parish School comprises a truly vibrant multicultural Catholic community that serves approximately 2,800 families, representing 7,000 individual mass attendees per weekend and approximately 440 school students enrolled in pre-k through 8th grade. The past decade has witnessed unprecedented growth in parish life engagement, ministry participation, and school enrollment. St Edward Parish is a diverse parish, inclusive of many ethnic cultures including multilingual staff, Mass offerings in Spanish and serving approximately 1200 families per weekend.

 

Position Overview:

 

The Pastoral Associate for Parish Life serves as a senior staff leader responsible for assisting the pastor in advancing the parish mission: “To place God first in all things: proclaim the Gospel of Jesus Christ; and grow in holiness through prayer, sacraments, and service. We Make Disciples.”

 

Ingrained in an intimate relationship with Jesus and his Church, the Pastoral Associate for Parish Life reports directly to the pastor and provides leadership and oversight for the parish's efforts related to mission advancement, vision implementation, values integration, hospitality, communications, outreach, evangelization, discipleship, stewardship, volunteer engagement, parish events, and community development. The position establishes the culture, priorities, and strategic direction of the Office for Parish Life and ensures that all parish life initiatives contribute to the mission and long-term vitality of the parish.

The Pastoral Associate for Parish Life oversees parish engagement, hospitality, communications support, volunteer development, stewardship initiatives, major parish events, outreach efforts, and parish personnel administration. The role is responsible for creating pathways through which parishioners encounter Christ, embrace the parish mission and vision, deepen their discipleship, grow in stewardship, and become active participants in the life and mission of the Church.

Essential Responsibilities

Mission, Vision, and Leadership

  • Promote and advance the parish mission in all parish life initiatives.
  • Collaborate with the Pastor and parish leadership in developing and implementing parish vision and strategic priorities including parish mission, vision, priorities, staffing, and ministry development.
  • Work with the Pastoral Associate for Parish Ministry to align parish life initiatives with faith formation, sacramental preparation, pastoral care, and ministry leadership and to cultivate and implement a common vision of discipleship.
  • Work with the Pastoral Associate for Parish Family Finances regarding budgets, stewardship efforts, and financial accountability.
  • Work with the Pastoral Associate for Parish Family Resources regarding facilities, technology, campus readiness, and operational support.
  • Collaborate with the School Principal on parish-school initiatives, family engagement, communications, and events.
  • Support strategic planning and continuous improvement efforts across parish ministries and operations.
  • Ensure that parish values are consistently reflected in programs, communications, events, and staff culture.
  • Provide leadership that fosters hospitality, accountability, evangelization, discipleship, stewardship, and community engagement.
  • Develop systems and structures that help parishioners grow from initial encounter toward active discipleship and leadership.

Outreach and Evangelization

  • Develop parish outreach strategies that welcome newcomers, inactive Catholics, and those exploring the faith.
  • Coordinate evangelization initiatives that invite individuals into deeper relationship with Jesus Christ and the Church.
  • Ensure that outreach activities align with parish mission, vision, and values.
  • Establish pathways that move individuals from outreach encounters into discipleship, ministry involvement, stewardship, and community life.

Discipleship and Stewardship Development

  • Lead the parish's overall strategy for stewardship of time, talent, and treasure.
  • Coordinate annual stewardship initiatives, parish appeals, recurring giving efforts, volunteer recruitment, and engagement opportunities.
  • Encourage parishioners to recognize and share their gifts in service to the Church and community.
  • Support leadership development among parish volunteers and ministry leaders.
  • Promote a culture of generosity, participation, and responsibility for the mission of the parish.

Community Development and Parish Events

  • Oversee planning, promotion, execution, and evaluation of major parish events.
  • Coordinate parish-wide events including the Parish Picnic, Family Fun Night, Parish Gala, and other community-building initiatives.
  • Develop opportunities that strengthen relationships among parishioners and build a strong sense of belonging.
  • Coordinate volunteers, registrations, hospitality, communications, and event logistics.
  • Facilitate the inculturation of the faith and its authentic expression within the cultural diversity of our parish.

Personnel Administration and Staff Development

  • Provide leadership for parish personnel administration.
  • Coordinate hiring processes, onboarding, orientation, and employee record management.
  • Assist supervisors with employee coaching, development, evaluations, and performance improvement plans.
  • Ensure consistent implementation of parish personnel policies and procedures.
  • Support employee formation, professional development, and organizational health.
  • Maintain confidentiality regarding personnel matters and employee records.
  • Foster a workplace culture rooted in professionalism, collaboration, accountability, and mission alignment.

Administration and Office Leadership

  • Direct the daily operations of the Office for Parish Life.
  • Supervise assigned staff and provide regular coaching, support, evaluation, and professional development.
  • Ensure effective systems for parishioner engagement, hospitality, volunteer management, communications, and event coordination.
  • Maintain organized records and administrative processes supporting parish life initiatives.
  • Develop and implement annual goals, objectives, and performance measures for the Office for Parish Life.
  • Promote collaboration among staff, ministries, volunteers, and parish organizations.

Directly Supervises

  • Parish Life Administrative Assistant
  • Parish Life Receptionist
  • Parish Life Media Coordinator
  • Parish Life Bulletin Publisher
  • Parish Life Events Minister
  • Pastoral Assistant for Outreach
  • Childcare Team

Communications and Parish Engagement

  • Coordinate communications that promote parish mission, vision, values, events, outreach opportunities, stewardship initiatives, and ministry involvement.
  • Oversee bulletin production, media support, event promotion, and communications systems housed within the Office for Parish Life.

The Kids Pastor at Trinity Church will lead a thriving children’s ministry that teaches the Bible with depth, makes Jesus fun, and partners with parents to disciple the next generation. This leader will oversee a ministry that serves kids at every weekend service and midweek, and will build the volunteers, staff, and systems that make it work. As Trinity prepares to move into a facility four times its current size, the Kids Pastor will shape the spaces, teams, and culture that let the ministry serve far more families. If you love shepherding kids and parents, multiplying leaders, and building a ministry where joy and discipleship go together, this is a rare opportunity.


About This Organization

Trinity Church is a fast-growing, Bible-teaching, Spirit-empowered church located in the heart of Scottsdale, Arizona. Founded ten years ago by Pastor Mark Driscoll and family, Trinity has become a home for thousands of young families, new believers, and people seeking a healthy, joyful, deeply biblical church community. With a mission to “open our Bibles to learn, open our lives to love, so that lives and legacies are transformed,” Trinity blends robust Bible preaching with vibrant worship, strong discipleship pathways, and a deeply relational, family-first culture. The church is entering its biggest season yet, acquiring a facility four times its current size, expanding parking dramatically, preparing for midweek programming, and anticipating explosive growth. Kids, students, young adults, and families are at the epicenter of that growth.


Mission, Vision, and Values

Trinity’s mission is simple and powerful:

  • “We open our Bibles to learn. We open our lives to love. So that lives and legacies are transformed.”

Core values expressed throughout the church include:

  • Living Kingdom Down: Word and Spirit; repent and forgive quickly; Holy Spirit-led living.
  • Healthy Person: Emotional, spiritual, marital, and relational health prioritized in every leader.
  • Burden Lifter: Serving, encouraging, and supporting one another’s work and ministry.
  • Heart for the House: No silos; one unified team serving one mission.



Location

“The Phoenix area has everything I could ever ask for raising a young family. It has awesome parks and great neighborhoods and really unique things like the aquarium and train park while also having very low-key and quiet neighborhoods within comfortable driving distance of the church. It’s only two hours from an escape in the mountains, where there is snow at Christmas and an escape from the heat in summer. And I love living in a big city without it feeling as congested as some other major cities like Chicago. My wife and I truly love it here.”

Pastor Carl Steele – Campus Pastor



Key Responsibilities

  • Shepherd and lead Trinity’s kids ministry from nursery through elementary, with a pastor’s heart for every child and family.
  • Recruit, train, and care for a growing volunteer team that serves across every weekend service and midweek, and build layers of leaders beneath you.
  • Lead and develop kids ministry staff, coordinators, interns, and part-time team members.
  • Oversee Bible teaching and curriculum so kids learn Scripture, know Jesus, and understand the gospel at their level.
  • Partner with parents and equip them as the primary disciplers of their kids, in step with Trinity’s marriage and parenting content.
  • Create safe, secure, joyful environments, including check-in, safety systems, and the backyard worship and play experience.
  • Lead kids ministry for major Trinity events such as Spring Training, Easter, Christmas in July, Trinity’s Birthday, and Fall Fest.
  • Design kids spaces and midweek kids programming for the new facility.
  • Collaborate with Student Ministry and Young Adults to strengthen transitions and move toward a unified family ministry.
  • Manage the ministry budget, schedules, and systems, and run the ministry on EOS rhythms.
  • Model a healthy marriage, family life, and walk with Jesus.

﻿


Key Qualifications

  • A clear calling to kids ministry and pastoral shepherding.
  • 3 to 5+ years of vocational kids ministry experience, preferably in a church of 1,000 or more.
  • Proven leadership of adults and volunteers, not just kids.
  • Experience building volunteer pipelines, small-group systems, and multi-layered leadership structures.
  • Proven ability to teach kids the Bible in an engaging, practical way.
  • Strong theological grounding: Reformed-leaning soteriology, openness to the gifts and work of the Holy Spirit, and alignment with Trinity’s complementarian convictions on pastoral leadership.
  • A strong theology of family and discipleship that values the home as primary.
  • Emotional intelligence, humility, teachability, and unity-oriented leadership, including a willingness to submit to spiritual authority.
  • A healthy marriage (or a clear pursuit of marriage and family in the future).
  • A bachelor’s degree is preferred; a master’s is a bonus. Seminary is not required. Character and biblical competency matter most.
  • Ability to thrive in a fast-moving, high-autonomy, high-accountability, growth-heavy environment.




A great match for this position would be:

  • A true pastor with a shepherd’s heart for kids and parents, not a kids speaker or a platform builder.
  • A gifted Bible teacher who brings Scripture to kids in a way that is biblical, Spirit-aware, and practical.
  • A developer of leaders who recruits, trains, and multiplies volunteers and moves from doing the ministry to developing ministers.
  • Someone who thrives in a Word and Spirit theological family: anchored in Scripture and open to the gifts and work of the Holy Spirit.
  • A leader who thinks in systems, not just events, and who wants to build structure, clarity, and follow-through for a ministry that will scale.
  • A spiritually and emotionally healthy pastor with a strong marriage and family life, ideally a parent who understands family life firsthand.
  • A humble, teachable leader who sees Trinity as a long-term calling and a place to plant roots.



Challenges and Opportunities

  • The new facility is four times the size of the current one, so this leader can design kids spaces and midweek programming from the ground up.
  • Trinity expects rapid growth when the new building opens. The Kids Pastor must have the team ready before the doors open.
  • Kids ministry runs a high volume of services every week. This leader will build volunteer depth and leaders of leaders so the ministry does not depend on a few people.
  • Trinity has launched a School of Ministry (3 12-14 week units) preparing staff and volunteers for greater excellence in ministry. The Kids Pastor can build a kids-specific leadership pipeline on top of that foundation.
  • Kids ministry has operated largely on its own. This leader will help connect it with Students and Young Adults, and will help shape the path toward a unified family ministry.
  • Trinity keeps joy and depth together. The Kids Pastor will protect both: kids who have a blast and kids who learn and love the Bible.
