post_html:
Standard of Christian Commitment

The candidate must be a professing Christ follower who possesses a strong commitment to the mission and core values of Southwestern Seminary and Texas Baptist College, possess a clear understanding of Southern Baptist heritage and culture, and agrees to serve in accordance with and not contrary to the current edition of the Baptist Faith and Message.

Southwestern Seminary, an entity of the Southern Baptist Convention, is a confessional institution. While the Seminary serves the larger evangelical Christian community, employees must embrace the values and standards the Seminary represents as it fulfills its mission of shaping Christian leaders within our denominational context.

Since duties of this position require the employee to represent the Seminary to prospective and current students, candidates must abide by the Seminary bylaws, the Employee Handbook, and the current edition of the Baptist Faith and Message as a condition of employment.

Job Description

Southwestern Baptist Theological Seminary invites applications for an open rank faculty position (Assistant, Associate, or Full Professor) in Pastoral Ministries in the School of Theology. The professor prepares God-called men for faithful pastoral ministry by teaching courses in preaching and pastoral theology, supervising doctoral research, and modeling healthy pastoral leadership. As a member of the Southwestern faculty, the professor fulfills the five faculty responsibilities of teaching, scholarship, service, community, and formation in support of the mission of the institution and the churches of the Southern Baptist Convention. Rank and appointment will be commensurate with the candidate's qualifications and experience.

Key Responsibilities

  • Teaches the normal full-time faculty load of fifteen ( 15) hours per year, distributed over the academic year, in courses taught at anytime and by any delivery system offered by the Seminary. 
  • Supplemental teaching beyond the normal load may be available as opportunity exists, in accordance with Seminary policy, up to the maximum annual load of nine (9) hours overload.
  • Directs Church Residency Network initiative providing broad leadership of the
    program at the direction of the Provost and Senior Vice President.
  • Designs courses that combine biblical and theological depth with ministry insight and application, preparing students for effective pastoral leadership.
  • Employs teaching methods that engage students with varied learning preferences and incorporates appropriate pedagogical and technological advances.
  • Challenges students intellectually and spiritually, nurturing critical thinking and robust inquiry while remaining faithful to confessional boundaries and developing students' vocational competency.
  • Maintains consistent scholarly activity, writing for peer-reviewed and church-facing publications, and presentations at academic conferences, which advances theological knowledge, academic discourse, and ministry practice.
  • Supervises doctoral students (as determined by rank) thoughtfully and steadily through their dissertations or projects, with careful attention to their development and formation as emerging scholars and experts in their discipline.
  • Serves on doctoral committees as necessary for the department.
  • Attends all required department, school, and general faculty meetings.
  • Attends other key academic events, including convocation, commencement, preview day, and trustee meetings.
  • Participates actively in campus life, chapel, and seminary events; invests in students' holistic development; and cultivates collegiality with fellow faculty and staff.
  • Supervises Administrative Associate of Church Residencies in their organization of the program and its initiatives.
  • Exercises decision-making responsibility for course design, instruction, evaluation of student work, and doctoral supervision within the scope of this position.
  • Participates in the Southern Baptist Convention annual meeting, if requested.
  • Contributes service at the institutional, denominational, church, and community levels, including active membership and involvement in a church cooperating with the Southern Baptist Convention.
  • Pursues ongoing professional and personal formation, modeling an abiding, fruitful, and disciplined walk with Jesus Christ.
  • Meets regularly and collaboratively with supervisor to discuss performance, suggest job description updates and set mutually beneficial goals.

Qualifications and Skills Required

  • PhD in preaching, pastoral theology or ministry, or a related discipline (required).
  • Fifteen or more years of pastoral experience (required).
  • A record of, or demonstrated potential for, scholarship appropriate to rank, including
    research, publication, and presentation.
  • Deep knowledge of preaching, pastoral theology, and the practice of pastoral ministry .
  • Preferred skills in classroom instruction across delivery systems
  • Strong communication and mentoring abilities.
  • Active membership in a church cooperating with the Southern Baptist Convention and agreement with the Seminary's confessional standards.
  • Successful completion of background check, education verification, work verification and credit check may be required.
  • Ability to provide valid proof of identity and Work Authorization in the U.S.
  • Valid driver's license, successful clearance of Motor Vehicle Report (Driving Record).
  • Drives on behalf of the seminary for travel, events, and denominational meetings (e.g., SBC annual meeting), as needed.

Additional Responsibilities

  • Works in an office environment.
  • Sits for extended periods of time.
  • Uses near-visual acuity in reading written documents and statistical data.
  • Uses keyboard devices and a computer monitor.
  • Utilizes analytical capabilities to gather data, provide support and resolve conflicts.
  • Exchanges information by telephone, computer, in writing and in person.
  • Stands and speaks for extended periods while teaching and preaching.

About Southwestern Baptist Theological Seminary 

Southwestern Baptist Theological Seminary, established in 1908 under the visionary leadership of B.H. Carroll, was born out of the urgent need for trained ministers in America’s rapidly growing Southwest. Initially part of Baylor University, the seminary became an independent institution in Waco before relocating to Fort Worth in 1910. Carroll’s unwavering commitment to orthodoxy, gospel-centered education, and the Great Commission shaped the seminary’s mission. Training God-called men and women for ministry,?Southwestern has an expansive academic program training pastors, missionaries, and ministry leaders in theology, missions, evangelism, music and worship, and education. Today, it stands as a beacon of faithfulness, equipping generations to serve Christ’s church globally.

Description:

There are nearly 300,000 teenagers of active-duty U.S. military parents who are stationed all over the world. These teens move an average of seven times during their school-aged years. The questions of identity and belonging that all teens face grow even more challenging to answer amid starting over and meeting new friends at each location.

This is where you can be the difference in a military teen’s life! By being in their world, walking alongside them, and creating a community where they experience the truth of God’s love and purpose for them, our staff provide a safe space where teens can develop friendships and connections to experience laughter, build hope, and generate resiliency.

We are currently providing incarnational ministry at many military installations around the world. You will have the opportunity to lead and oversee the overall Young Life Military program, known as Club Beyond, which is ecumenically focused and outreach oriented.

We are currently looking for both full-time and part-time staff throughout the United States, as well as international locations. Colorado Springs, CO, is the headquarters.

job_name: Minister for Church Legacy and Renewal
post_html:
People Architects is excited to recruit for a Minister for Church Legacy and Renewal for our direct client. 


The Minister for Church Legacy and Renewal will work with Conferences, Associations and local congregations to equip them for sustainable renewal and bold missional impact.  S/he will a) help stable and growing congregations increase missional impact, b) support closing congregations to preserve their enduring legacies, and c) help faith-based institutions of all kinds to align their real estate and other strategic assets with the mission and values of the United Church of Christ to achieve measurable transformation.  This position will advance the UCC core values of strengthening the church, reshaping the narrative, leadership development, and decolonization. 


ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Assist stable and growing congregations to increase missional impact through new and existing education and training offered by CB&LF, Love of Church and other sources.
  • Continuing the work of the UCC Church Legacy and Closure initiative, work with UCC Conferences, the Council of Conference Ministers (CCM), Associations, congregations and clergy to assist and support closing congregations to preserve their enduring legacies and discern mission-aligned real estate disposition strategies.
  • Coordinate the creation of a comprehensive digital and physical UCC Real Estate and Strategic Assets resource, offering best practices for managing, deploying, and preserving church real estate and other strategic assets in alignment with  mission and values.
  • Champion a “Theology of Mission” collaborating with CB&LF staff to create trainings and narratives that empower local church leaders to view every physical asset as a platform for justice and community renewal.
  • Facilitate access to Love of Church resources, providing healthy congregations with the tools to decolonize their assets and strengthen their community presence.
  • Develop a "Legacy Sustainability Model" to ensure that the financial and missional "DNA" of concluding congregations is preserved.
  • Collaborating with CB&LF/ARC’s Senior Data Analyst, and CARD (Center for Analytics, Research, and Data) document research on closing UCC congregations to discern significant patterns, inform the support and training needed for pastors serving declining congregations, and highlight narratives of hope and strategic transformation.
  • Facilitate the churches wide communication, working with Marketing & Communications; (MarCom), to promote and share legacy and renewal resources Church News and other media outlets.
  • Other duties as assigned.


MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS: To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily.  The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skill, and/or ability required.


  • College degree and other related experience and/or training; demonstrated personal interest in, and commitent to church legacy and renewal from a biblical/theological perspective.
  • Commitment to, and theological understanding of, mission in its broad range of concerns; ability to articulate and witness to one’s faith perspective.
  • Understanding of the polity and structures of the United Church of Christ.
  • Ability to conduct research, identify patterns in organizational renewal, and collaborate with data analysts to produce report, articles, and presentations.
  • Demonstrated excellent communication skills, including the ability to write creatively, and the ability to speak publicly in an articulate and engaging manner.
  • Desire and sensitivity to work in diverse racial, ethnic, cultural, and religious settings with commitment to pluralism in the workplace as well as in one’s understanding of mission.
  • High competency in technology and computer literacy.
  • Strong work ethic exhibiting a sense of urgency in completion of tasks and willingness to work a flexible schedule. 
  • Self-starter with ability to handle multiple tasks and prioritize workload and remain motivated and positive. Well organized and detail-oriented, and exceptional time management.  
  • Flexibility to travel for meetings and consultations with local congregations and Conferences. 
  • Other duties as assigned.


This job description is not intended to be a complete list of all duties and responsibilities required for the position and is subject to review and change at any time in accordance with the needs of the ministry. Since no job description can detail all duties and responsibilities that may be required from time to time in the performance of a position, duties and responsibilities that may be inherent in a position shall also be considered part of the position holder's responsibility.

All staff are encouraged to nurture safety within the work performed on behalf of the NMUCC by being attentive to self-care, education, maintaining appropriate boundaries, and the importance of referring those in need to supportive and helpful resources.

Lead Pastor, Refuge Church - Appleton, WI

Refuge Church is seeking a Lead Pastor who will faithfully shepherd, disciple, and lead our congregation with a deep love for Jesus, His Word, and His people.

We are a growing and intentionally multi-ethnic church in the heart of Appleton, Wisconsin, committed to keeping the gospel central in all we do. We desire a pastor who prioritizes relational ministry, discipleship, prayer, and spiritual care.

Our church family is longing for a shepherd/leader who will know people personally, invest deeply in relationships, and help cultivate a healthy culture of discipleship, unity, and spiritual growth.

About Refuge Church

Refuge Church exists to ignite a movement of multi-ethnic Christ-followers to Reach, Develop and Send the next generations.

Our current average Sunday attendance is approximately 125 people, with a membership of around 65. We recently completed a renovation that doubled our ministry space and positioned us well for future ministry opportunities. https://www.refugeappleton.com/

Our ministries currently include:

  • Sunday worship gatherings
  • Children’s ministry
  • Youth ministry
  • Men’s and women’s ministries
  • Life groups
  • Church planting and Greenhouse Environment Residencies

Refuge has also helped develop and send licensed workers to plant churches and send out international workers with the C&MA.

Our Core Values

Simply the Gospel
We believe that the gospel of Christ is entirely applicable and relevant and therefore at the very center of all we do.

Authentic Relationships
We, in like manner to Christ, look to show the character and priorities of Jesus in relationships even when we fall short.

Intentionally Multi-Ethnic
The gospel transcends culture and context and because of this every tribe and tongue will proclaim the glory of God.

Multiplying Disciples
Every gospel-centered ministry will, at its core, fulfill the call to make disciples of Jesus Christ.

Crazy Generosity
Just as God’s generosity was ludicrous, ours should be equally crazy!

Who We Are Looking For

We are seeking a pastor who:

  • Is a shepherd/leader and discipler.
  • Loves people deeply and engages relationally
  • Prioritizes discipleship and spiritual formation
  • Leads through humility, prayer, and presence
  • Preaches and teaches Scripture faithfully and clearly
  • Builds unity within the church body
  • Values intentional multicultural ministry
  • Equips others for ministry rather than carrying ministry alone
  • Models personal spiritual maturity and dependence on Christ

Primary Responsibilities

Shepherding & Discipleship

  • Provide spiritual care and shepherding for the church body
  • Develop a culture of discipleship and spiritual growth
  • Invest personally in mentoring and developing leaders
  • Help cultivate authentic biblical community

Preaching & Teaching

  • Faithfully preach and teach the Word of God
  • Prepare gospel-centered sermons with practical application
  • Lead the church in biblical truth and spiritual maturity

Prayer & Spiritual Leadership

  • Model a life of prayer and dependence on the Holy Spirit
  • Lead the church spiritually with humility and wisdom
  • Provide pastoral care

Leadership & Vision

  • Serve as a member of the elder team and chairman of the Governing Board
  • Help guide the church toward healthy growth and mission
  • Support and strengthen Refuge’s multi-ethnic mission and identity
  • Equip the congregation to engage the community and make disciples

Desired Qualifications

  • A growing and vibrant relationship with Jesus Christ
  • Alignment with the theology and mission of The Alliance (C&MA)
  • Be fully licensed/ordained as an official worker of the Christian and Missionary Alliance. If not already licensed with the C&MA, be willing to be licensed with the Western Great Lakes District prior to hiring and then pursue ordination.
  • Demonstrate pastoral, shepherding, and discipleship gifting
  • Experience in preaching and teaching Scripture
  • Ability to build relationships across cultures and backgrounds
  • Humility, emotional maturity, and relational wisdom
  • A heart for unity, care, and spiritual formation
  • Formal ministry training and pastoral experience required (Bachelor’s preferred / 5+ years of experience preferred)


About Appleton, Wisconsin
Appleton is a vibrant city in the Fox Valley region of Northeast Wisconsin. The area offers a strong sense of community, excellent schools, outdoor recreation, and a growing and diverse population. Refuge Church is uniquely positioned in the heart of Appleton to engage people from a variety of cultural and socioeconomic backgrounds.

post_html:
ACU is affiliated with the fellowship of the Church of Christ. This position requires the employee to be a professing Christian and to be willing to support the Christian mission of ACU.

‌

Position Type: Full-time faculty appointment, tenure-track eligible (terminal degree or equivalent professional experience required) 

Start Date: Spring 2026

Position Summary

The Department of Music at Abilene Christian University invites applications for a full-time, tenure-track faculty member to serve as the Founding Director of Commercial Music and Worship Arts. This position involves an initial program-building phase, followed by ongoing leadership, teaching, and administrative responsibilities once the program is launched, pending new program accreditation approval. The successful candidate will bring significant professional experience in the music industry and/or worship leadership and will be eager to help shape an innovative program that prepares students for careers in music while advancing ACU’s mission as a Christ-centered academic community. During the development and launch phase, the candidate will serve as Founding Director and then will transition to an ongoing leadership role (e.g., Associate Director or Division Head) as the program matures. A graduate degree is preferred; however, candidates with a bachelor’s degree and a record of distinguished professional achievement may be considered as meeting the equivalent of a terminal degree. The program is scheduled to welcome its first students in Fall 2027.

Responsibilities

Phase I: Program Development

  • Lead faculty and industry discussions to design and implement curriculum in commercial music and worship arts.

  • Oversee facilities renovations, including the design and equipping of teaching, rehearsal, and recording spaces.

  • Guide the purchase and integration of industry-standard equipment and technologies.

  • Collaborate with admissions and marketing to recruit prospective students into the new program.

  • Establish partnerships with industry professionals, churches, and alumni networks to support the program’s launch.

  • During the program development phase, devote full-time effort to launching the program; no teaching responsibilities are assigned during this phase.

Ongoing Program Leadership

  • Direct the Commercial Music and Worship Arts programs, including assessment, student advising, and coordination of internships and industry experiences.

  • Teach a regular faculty load in areas of expertise (e.g., music production, songwriting, commercial performance, music business, music ministry, worship leadership), with a two-course annual reduction in recognition of administrative responsibilities.

  • Maintain active professional engagement in the music industry and/or worship communities.

  • Collaborate with colleagues in music, film, and other disciplines to foster interdisciplinary initiatives.

  • Work closely with colleagues at off-campus, experiential learning sites.

  • Support the mission of ACU through Christ-centered teaching, service, and mentoring of students.

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in music, music industry, worship studies, or a closely related field.

  • Professional experience in the music industry and/or worship leadership.

  • Expertise in one or more areas such as:

    • Music production and recording

    • Songwriting and arranging

    • Live sound and performance technology

    • Music business/entrepreneurship

    • Worship leadership and ministry

    • Commercial performance (instrumental or vocal)

  • Strong communication, leadership, and organizational skills.

  • Commitment to the values of Christian higher education.
     

Preferred Qualifications

  • Graduate degree in music, music industry, worship, or a related field.

  • Demonstrated success in higher education teaching.

  • Experience with curriculum development and program administration.

  • Established industry/professional networks

Application Instructions

Completed applications will include:

  • Letter of interest highlighting qualifications for the position. (Upload to "Resume/Cover Letter" Section)

  • Curriculum vitae. (Upload to "Resume/Cover Letter" Section)

  • Contact information for three professional references. (Either include on CV/Cover Letter, or Upload as a separate document to "Resume/Cover Letter" Section)

  • Links to recent professional work. (performances, productions, recordings, etc.)

  • Statement of teaching philosophy.

  • Statement on the relationship of Christian faith and teaching.

  • Statement of personal faith journey.

  • Academic/professional letter of recommendation.

  • Letter of recommendation from a church leader.

  • Copies of transcripts for academic work (official transcripts required upon hire).
     

Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis until the position is filled.

ACU does not unlawfully discriminate on the basis of race, color, age, sex, disability, genetic information, national or ethnic origin in employment opportunities, in keeping with applicable state and federal law.

ACU is committed to maintaining a safe and secure campus environment and protecting the university's financial and physical assets. Therefore, Abilene Christian University conducts background checks on all candidates for employment in security sensitive positions. As a current employee, it will be determined if you need an additional background check upon your hire.

Personal Spiritual Duties 

  • Be a maturing disciple of Jesus Christ: growing in love for God, God's Word, God's people of every ethnicity and culture, and God’s purposes in the world 

  • Practice daily spiritual disciplines  

  • Pursue spiritual relationships and involvement in a worshipping community  

  • Continue learning and growth in spiritual understanding, biblical knowledge, ministry experience and skills 

  • Experience and live out an ongoing call to ministry service with InterVarsity and its mission 

 

Ministry Leadership 

  • Participate and be fully engaged in the ministry team to cast spiritual vision and direction, to contribute to the accomplishment of the team’s plans for spiritual growth and transformation, and to provide area leadership in specific areas 

  • Teach students to love, study and apply Scripture to their lives  

  • Learn about and assist in leading in ministry to students and faculty on campus 

  • Promote and press forward the Mission on campus Seek opportunities to proclaim and demonstrate the Gospel of Jesus Christ  

  • Learn to guide chapters (or assigned segments of a chapter) in the development of strategic thinking regarding witness to the university  

  • Learn to model and assist students and faculty in growing in their love for God's people of every ethnicity and culture  

  • Help to develop student and/or faculty ministry leadership teams, based on developing skills  

  • Encourage a prayerful lifestyle in students and faculty, especially focusing on those who do not yet follow Jesus as Lord and Savior  

  • Engage positively with the supervision you receive from your staff ministry director 

 

Pastoral Care and Support (assist as assigned and based on skill level) 

  • Provide pastoral care and support for student and/or leadership teams and individual students and faculty 

  • Provide training, resources and opportunities for students and faculty for their spiritual development 

  • Recruit students and/or faculty and providing specific leadership for conferences and projects  

 

 

Administration  

  • Perform the necessary administrative tasks to fulfill the purpose of InterVarsity and to comply with InterVarsity’s policies and procedures 

  • Comply with Risk Management policies  

  • Follow the budgeting and expense reporting guidelines  

  • Lead students in filing annual chapter affiliation, in coordination with assigned Campus Staff Minister 

  • Fulfill area and regional reporting requirements  

  • Fulfill national reporting requirements  

 

Ministry Partner Development and Public Relations 

  • Serve as an ambassador of InterVarsity to individual ministry partners and churches, through prayer, discussion of ministry efforts, mission, and accomplishments. 

  • Carry out the tasks required for effective fund development and to develop strong public relations for the ministry of InterVarsity  

  • Maintain expenses within allocated budgets  

  • Secure personal financial, prayer support and maintain a ministry among partners who will fund InterVarsity 

  • Develop and implement an annual 30-day plan for raising personal budget  

  • Communicate with ministry partners at least four times a year  

  • Cultivate and maintain supportive relationships with alumni  

 

QUALIFICATIONS 

  • Annually affirm InterVarsity’s Statement of Agreement (Doctrinal Basis and Purpose Statement); abide by InterVarsity’s Code of Conduct; believe and behave consonantly with InterVarsity’s Human Sexuality Theological Paper. Affirm and behave consonantly with InterVarsity’s “Women in Ministry Statement of Affirmation” 

  • Exploring calling to InterVarsity and its mission  

  • Bachelor's degree for non-enrolled candidates assigned to four-year campuses; Associate's degree for non-enrolled candidates assigned to two-year campuses 

  • Prior experience with InterVarsity or other campus ministry preferred (including as a student) 

  • Willing to receive training to become a Campus Staff Minister 

  • Ability to contribute to an open and supportive relationship with ministry team members  

  • Ministry skills: Prior experience teaching spiritual and biblical principles, planning ministry programs, and spiritually discipling others 

  • Excellent oral and written communication skills  

  • Demonstrated problem-solving skills  

  • A supervisory decision, with input from the Campus Ministry Associate, is made at the end of the term of service as to whether the individual is suitable for continuing employment with InterVarsity

Pay Range: $17.37 - $23.16 per hour

Pay: This position is funded through personal fundraising. Accordingly, compensation will vary based on the ability of the individual to secure a donor team to fund the cost of his/her salary. The anticipated salary range for this position on a full-time basis (40 hours/week) is dependent on a variety of factors, including location and cost of living. The actual salary received, including any geographic adjustment to account for location and cost of living, is subject to the individual’s ability to raise funds necessary to cover the full amount of such salary within the range set forth in the job posting details.

Benefits:

We offer a competitive benefits package, including health care and retirement savings with a match. Eligibility is based on employee type and hours worked.  Benefits include the following:

  • 403(b) Retirement Savings Plan

  • 403(b) matching contributions

  • Dental insurance

  • Employee assistance program

  • Employee discounts

  • Flexible work schedule

  • Flexible spending accounts

  • Health insurance

  • Health savings account

  • Life insurance

  • Paid time off

  • Parental leave

  • Professional development assistance

  • Vision insurance

Equal Employment Opportunity: 

 

InterVarsity Christian Fellowship/USA is both an equal opportunity employer and a faith-based religious organization. We conduct hiring without regard to race, color, ancestry, national origin, citizenship, age, sex, marital status, parental status, membership in any labor organization, political ideology, or disability of an otherwise qualified individual. The status of InterVarsity Christian Fellowship/USA as an equal opportunity employer does not prevent the organization from hiring staff based on their religious beliefs so that all staff share the same religious commitment.  Pursuant to the Civil Rights Act of 1964, Section 702 (42 U.S.C. 2000e 1(a)) InterVarsity Christian Fellowship/USA has the right to, and does, hire only candidates who agree with InterVarsity’s Statement of Agreement: Purpose and Doctrinal Basis because InterVarsity believes that each and every staff plays a vital role in advancing InterVarsity’s mission and purposes.

post_html:
At Cornerstone Church, we believe creativity is a powerful tool to communicate the message of Jesus in compelling, memorable, and meaningful ways.

We're looking for a Creative Programming Director who is equal parts visionary, builder, and collaborator. Someone who doesn't just dream up great ideas but knows how to bring people together to make those ideas a reality.

This role is for someone who thrives in a fast-paced, highly collaborative environment, loves developing people, and has a passion for creating experiences that make an impact.

Who you are:

A Builder. You love creating something from nothing. You're not waiting for the perfect system or team; you enjoy building both.
An Idea Generator. You're naturally curious, imaginative, and consistently thinking about what could be possible.
A Mobilizer. You know that the best ideas require great people. You can inspire, organize, and empower teams to accomplish more together.
A People Person. You genuinely enjoy working with people, building relationships, and helping others succeed. You value collaboration over personal credit.
Highly Teachable. You're confident enough to contribute and humble enough to learn. You actively seek feedback and are willing to change direction when needed.
Comfortable With Fast-Paced Environments. You can manage multiple projects, navigate changing priorities, and remain solution-oriented under pressure.
A Deep Researcher. You don't settle for the first idea. You ask questions, study references, explore possibilities, and do the work necessary to develop thoughtful, compelling creative concepts.
Someone Who Can Receive Feedback. You understand that creative work is collaborative. You don't take critique personally, and you're willing to refine an idea until it serves the mission.
An Executor. You don't just talk about ideas. You take ownership, solve problems, meet deadlines, and make things happen.

What you will do:

Be the Chief Collaborator
  • Lead creative collaboration across departments, bringing together staff, volunteers, and ministry leaders to develop impactful ideas.
  • Facilitate brainstorming, creative development, and problem-solving sessions.
  • Turn big ideas into clear, actionable plans that teams can execute.
  • Build strong relationships across the organization to move creative projects forward.
Build & Mobilize Teams
  • Recruit, develop, and mobilize volunteer creative teams.
  • Identify people's gifts and empower them to contribute meaningfully to the creative process.
  • Create a culture where people feel valued, challenged, and inspired to bring their best.
  • Coordinate staff, volunteers, and resources to bring creative concepts to life.
Bring Ideas to Life
  • Oversee the ideation, development, and execution of creative elements for weekend worship experiences, conferences, and special events.
  • Collaborate with the preaching team to develop practical illustrations, stage props, and visual elements that strengthen message communication.
  • Lead projects from initial concept and research through design, production, and final execution.
  • Partner with Worship, Production, Video, and other teams to ensure creative elements are executed with excellence.
  • Balance creative ambition with budgets, timelines, and available resources.

Research, Innovate & Improve

  • Research cultural trends, creative experiences, storytelling methods, and innovative approaches to communication.
  • Consistently bring fresh ideas and inspiration to the table.
  • Evaluate creative effectiveness and identify opportunities to improve.
  • Build repeatable systems and processes that make creative execution more efficient and sustainable.

Experiences You Have Had

  • Minimum of 5 years experience serving in a creative programming, leadership or comparable role at a church with an average weekly attendance of 5,000 or more.
  • Proven experience in a similar leadership role, with comparable responsibilities in scope, complexity, and expectations to the Director of Creative Programming role.
  • Demonstrated management experience, including leading staff, developing teams, overseeing volunteers, delegating responsibilities, and holding team members accountable.
  • A portfolio of completed creative projects or live experiences demonstrating personal creative contributions, leadership and successful execution.
  • Is highly organized, self-motivated, and proactive
  • Able to perform job duties with a sense of urgency and meet deadlines consistently

What Success Looks Like

  • Creative ideas consistently move from concept to execution.
  • Staff and volunteers are engaged, equipped, and excited to contribute.
  • Weekend experiences, conferences, and preaching elements are thoughtful, innovative, and executed with excellence.
  • Creative projects are delivered on time and within budget.
  • Strong collaboration exists across ministry departments.
  • Creative processes become more effective, scalable, and repeatable.
  • The Creative Arts team continues to develop a culture of innovation, ownership, and excellence.

We're not simply looking for someone who can come up with great ideas. We're looking for someone who can build the team, develop the idea, and lead the execution.

At Cornerstone, creativity isn't about being impressive. It's about making the message of Jesus impossible to ignore.



Opportunity statement:

Cornerstone’s employment policy is to provide equal employment opportunity for all qualified employees and applicants without regard to race, color, sex, age, or national origin. The Church does however, reserve the right to employ persons who have a Christian background and align with the vision, values, and doctrinal statement of Cornerstone Christian Fellowship.  Each employee must be a member of Cornerstone supporting the vision and values of the church.

Pastor of Youth and Families
Full-Time Position with Benefits; FLSA Exempt
Reports to the Executive Director
July 2026

 

Purpose of Role

 

Reporting to the Executive Director, the primary responsibilities of the Pastor of Youth and Families will be leading families of youth and children. The Pastor of Youth and Families directs all aspects of youth and family ministry, including Bible teaching, discipleship, outreach, parent partnership, and leadership development, with the goal of helping students and families grow in their relationship with Christ and become mature believers. The Pastor of Youth and Families will also serve on the pastoral team and will preach, teach, counsel, and complete various pastoral duties in the church.


Qualifications Required  

  • 7+ years of pastoral ministry experience in the context of the local church
  • Master of Divinity from an accredited theological institution preferred; comparable theological education, training, or experience will be considered. Adheres to the qualifications of Biblical elder outlined in 1 Timothy 3:1-7 and Titus 1:5-9.
  • Exhibits a clear vision for student and family ministry and the ability to communicate that vision, set goals, and develop plans for ministry growth and effectiveness.
  • Strong desire to serve the Lord faithfully both publicly and privately while humbly leading others through Christ-like sacrificial leadership.
  • Strong interpersonal and administrative skills are necessary.
  • Adhere to the EPC confessional standards and theological beliefs.

 

Key Job Responsibilities

 

The Pastor of Youth and Families is responsible for, but not limited to, the following.

 

Leadership / Program Development

  • Lead the strategic planning and development of ongoing events and activities to encourage middle and high school students in a personal and growing relationship with Christ.
  • Identify and develop innovative programming that meets the spiritual, social, and developmental needs of students while aligning with the mission and values of Central.
  • Collaborate with church leadership, pastors, staff, and volunteers to ensure alignment of youth and family ministry plans with the strategic direction and mission of Central.
  • Build and maintain teams of adult volunteers and student leaders for youth ministry to serve in areas of teaching, mentoring, event planning, evangelism, and outreach.
  • Oversee the coordinators of the Children’s Ministry and Youth Ministry, providing vision alignment, collaborative leadership, and pastoral support to ensure unified ministry from birth through high school.
  • Develop programs to create gospel opportunities with non-believers in the community.
  • Recruit, train, and develop volunteers for the youth ministry.

 

Discipleship / Teaching

  • Develop and maintain authentic relationships with students and shepherd them as they have needs, concerns, and struggles.
  • Provide pastoral care, biblical counsel, spiritual guidance, and encouragement to students and families.
  • Implement discipleship opportunities for students, including small group studies, discipleship groups, and mentoring.
  • Equip students with a foundation in biblical truth, doctrine, and Christian living; help them understand how to apply God’s Word to their daily lives.
  • Teach students to relationally share Christ in their schools, social circles, and neighborhoods.
  • Support, encourage, and partner with parents in how to Biblically nurture and disciple their children; equip families as the primary disciples of the next generation.
  • Teach at weekly youth gatherings and seasonal communicants/sacraments classes.

 

Administration

  • Oversee all administrative aspects of youth and family ministry including budget management, event planning, parent and volunteer communication, record-keeping, and evaluation of ministry effectiveness.
  • Ensure all ministry activities and events are conducted in accordance with Central’s policies, procedures, and safety guidelines.
  • Collaborate with church staff and volunteers to coordinate ministry activities and programs.


Benefits


      • Medical, dental, and vision plan
      • 403(b) retirement plan including employer contribution
      • Twenty days of vacation per year plus paid time off for federal holidays


About Central Church and Resound Project


Central Presbyterian Church is a historic, 200-year-old congregation in the heart of New York City that
has experienced significant renewal over the past 20 years and is currently home to a diverse body of
seasoned leaders, many families, and a dynamic body of students, young professionals, and artists.
Central launched Resound Project in 2021 with a vision to strengthen new and existing churches in light
of the changing cultural context so that the gospel of Jesus Christ might resound to the next generation.
Resound Project is constituted as an initiative housed within Central Church and under the oversight of
Central’s officers along with its own President and advisory board, yet it will remain deeply tied to
Central through interlocking board appointments, the fact that Central’s Senior Pastor is the President of
Resound Project, and Central’s role as a leading source of funding for the foreseeable future. The
combined budgets of Central Church and Resound Project range between $4 and $5 Million annually,
with plans to scale both entities over time.


Expectations of Central Church Staff

        • A personal and growing commitment to Jesus as Lord and Savior in reliance upon his grace
        • A commitment to the authority of Scripture and to a lifestyle that befits a follower of Jesus
        • A willingness to work within the framework of the church’s governing structure and procedures
        • A willing heart, teachable spirit, positive attitude, flexible nature, and a sense of humor
        • A team ministry commitment which places the good of the whole over individual goals
        • An ability to work collaboratively with staff and volunteers
        • A focus on maintaining proper priorities and boundaries in one’s personal and family life
        • A dedication to our staff values of excellence, integrity, humility, courage, and creativity
        • A commitment to personally support the work of the church.
        • A passion for excellence for the glory of God

NEXTGEN TEAM LEAD

Hillside Fellowship

Family Ministries  |  Full-Time  |  Exempt


Reports To: Director of Family Ministries

Schedule: Sunday - Thursday, with regular evening and weekend responsibilities

Benefits: As outlined in the Hillside Fellowship Personnel Handbook


ROLE SUMMARY

Hillside Fellowship believes that Jesus Changes Everything! Our mission is that we exist to worship God, by proclaiming Jesus, making disciples, rooted in the Word of God, empowered by the Spirit of God. Discipleship is a byproduct, as we know and make much of Jesus.


The NextGen Team Lead serves under the direction of the Director of Family Ministries to lead the day-to-day ministry of NextGen by implementing the vision and strategy while providing spiritual leadership to middle and high school students, their families, and volunteer leaders. This role helps create environments where students are known, rooted in God’s Word, connected in authentic community, and encouraged to follow Jesus throughout every stage of their faith journey.


As a key member of the Family Ministries team, this role contributes to the health and effectiveness of the ministry by shepherding students, developing leaders, strengthening ministry systems, and cultivating engaging, gospel-centered ministry environments where students and families are encouraged to know Jesus, grow in their faith, and live on mission. This role leads the ministry through a strong volunteer leadership structure while also helping establish the systems and foundation needed for future ministry and staff growth.


KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

NextGen Vision + Ministry Strategy

  • Partner with the Director of Family Ministries to implement the vision, priorities, and strategic direction for NextGen Student Ministries in alignment with Hillside Fellowship’s mission, vision, values, and Family Ministries strategy
  • Lead the day-to-day execution of NextGen Student Ministries initiatives, ensuring consistency, excellence, and alignment across ministry environments
  • Evaluate ministry effectiveness and proactively identify opportunities to strengthen discipleship, student engagement, and volunteer effectiveness
  • Strengthen and refine ministry systems that support healthy, scalable, and sustainable ministry
  • Demonstrate strategic thinking by anticipating ministry needs, identifying challenges, and implementing thoughtful, people-centered solutions


Team + Volunteer Leadership Development

  • Identify, recruit, develop, disciple, and support volunteer leaders who shepherd students with wisdom, consistency, and Christlike character
  • Equip volunteers through training, coaching, encouragement, and ministry resources that strengthen their effectiveness in discipling students
  • Foster a healthy leadership culture marked by humility, ownership, encouragement, accountability, and spiritual maturity
  • Establish clear expectations, healthy ministry rhythms, and consistent communication that equips volunteers to lead confidently
  • Build a sustainable leadership pipeline by identifying and developing emerging adult and student leaders
  • Partner with the Director of Family Ministries to assess staffing needs and, as the ministry develops, help establish a NextGen staff structure that supports healthy and sustainable ministry
  • Provide leadership, development, coaching, and accountability to NextGen staff as positions are established and filled


Student Discipleship + Ministry Leadership

  • Lead the overall discipleship strategy for middle and high school students, helping them grow toward maturity in Christ through biblical teaching, authentic relationships, and intentional spiritual formation
  • Build meaningful relationships with students by maintaining a consistent presence in their lives and creating opportunities for discipleship, encouragement, and spiritual growth
  • Partner with parents by providing encouragement, communication, and resources that support the discipleship of students within the home
  • Lead and contribute to the teaching ministry of NextGen Student Ministries by faithfully communicating God’s Word in ways that are biblically grounded, engaging, and relevant to students
  • Encourage students to discover and use their gifts through serving, leadership development, missions, and active participation in the life of the church
  • Provide spiritual care, prayer, encouragement, and biblical guidance to students and families while partnering with other pastors and ministry leaders as appropriate


Ministry Environments + Engagement

  • Provide leadership for weekly gatherings, small groups, retreats, camps, mission trips, and other NextGen ministry opportunities
  • Ensure ministry environments are safe, welcoming, engaging, and aligned with Hillside Fellowship's mission, vision, and values
  • Ensure all child protection, screening, and safety policies are consistently implemented and maintained throughout NextGen Student Ministries
  • Maintain an active presence in ministry gatherings, serving alongside volunteer leaders and providing support as ministry needs arise
  • Collaborate with the Hillside Kids Team Lead to create intentional transition pathways that help students successfully move from Hillside Kids into NextGen Student Ministries


Financial Stewardship + Ministry Oversight

  • Develop and manage the NextGen Student Ministries budget, stewarding resources wisely and in alignment with ministry priorities
  • Regularly review budget performance, practice good stewardship, and seek guidance as needed to support ministry goals
  • Monitor ministry expenses and resource allocation throughout the year, making adjustments as needed to support effective stewardship and ministry priorities
  • Assess future ministry needs and provide recommendations regarding resources, facilities, and other investments needed to support healthy ministry growth


Collaboration + Churchwide Alignment

  • Partner with the Director of Family Ministries and other ministry leaders to support a unified vision for discipleship across Hillside Fellowship
  • Collaborate with other ministry areas to create intentional opportunities for students and families to engage in the broader life of the church
  • Participate in churchwide planning, leadership development, events, and initiatives that strengthen the mission and culture of Hillside Fellowship


Additional Responsibilities

  • This role may include additional responsibilities as needed to support the mission and leadership of Hillside Fellowship, with the scope of ministry growing and adapting as organizational needs change


QUALIFICATIONS AND REQUIREMENTS

Faith + Character

  • Demonstrates a maturing relationship with Jesus Christ and embodies the culture and values of Hillside Fellowship (Galatians 5:22-23)
  • Must be a member of Hillside Fellowship or willing to pursue membership within six months of hire
  • Demonstrates a commitment to Hillside Fellowship’s mission, vision, and values
  • Demonstrates a passion for discipling students, equipping leaders, and partnering with families
  • Models humility, wisdom, integrity, emotional maturity, and a servant-hearted approach to ministry leadership


Education + Experience

  • Bachelor's degree in ministry, theology, biblical studies, education, or a related field preferred; equivalent ministry training and experience may be considered
  • Minimum of three years of student ministry leadership experience required, including experience leading and developing volunteers
  • Experience teaching God's Word, developing leaders, and shepherding students and families required
  • Experience developing ministry teams and emerging leaders preferred


Skills + Competencies

  • Demonstrates strong leadership, teaching, relational, and communication skills
  • Demonstrates strong organizational and strategic planning skills with careful attention to detail and consistent follow-through
  • Demonstrates the ability to lead through others, delegate appropriately, and develop healthy ministry leaders
  • Exercises emotional maturity, relational wisdom, sound judgment, and discretion when serving students, families, volunteers, and staff
  • Demonstrates initiative, adaptability, and resourcefulness in responding to changing ministry needs
  • Demonstrates proficiency with Microsoft 365, Planning Center, church management systems (ChMS), and other communication and collaboration tools
  • Ability to maintain MinistrySafe certification is required
  • Ability to pass a background check is required

post_html:
Campus Ministry Staff, Philadelphia

In Partnership with Langhorne Presbyterian Church 

Ministering to student at Cairn University


OUR MISSION

Our mission is transforming college students to transform the world. We call college students to serve Jesus Christ with their entire lives by:

1. Sharing the Gospel with students and developing passionate disciples of Jesus Christ.

2. Serving together with the church and inviting students into the lives of local congregations. 

3. Giving students a vision for serving Jesus Christ in their studies, jobs, communities, and families.


OUR VISION

Our vision is to see a generation of college students transformed by the power of Jesus Christ and His Gospel, in partnership with the local church, reaching the world for the glory of God.


OUR VALUES

1. All things belong to God.

2. Jesus changes people’s lives.

3. We love college students.

4. We embrace God’s multiethnic kingdom.

5. Faithfulness is pursued together.

6. We celebrate life. 

OUR MODEL 

At the core of CCO ministry is the understanding that God works through the Church to fulfill His purposes in the world. This means the local church is the proper context for gathering, equipping, and sending students into a life-long Kingdom mission. Our partnership model promotes deep collaboration between the CCO and the local church where vision for ministry, ministry strategy, and ministry design are mutually shared. The CCO places Campus Ministry Staff to help mobilize the church to reach students and develop them as future Christian leaders.


PURPOSE OF POSITION

Catalyze Kingdom transformation at Cairn University by sharing the Gospel, inviting students into the life of the local church, and mobilizing the Christian community and churches to engage ministry on campus. Develop deep collaboration between church/community members and students that promotes strong biblical discipleship, life long commitment to the Church, and the flourishing of Christ’s kingdom in their local context and all areas of life. 


RESPONSIBILITIES

Campus Engagement

  • Create and routinely revise a ministry plan according to the CCO’s Annual Ministry Plan and Campus Playbook.

  • Ensure a consistent and visible presence of the CCO and Langhorne Presbyterian Church (LPC) on campus and in meeting with students through regular participation in Cairn University’s activities. 

  • Collect and maintain student contact information, following up with & inviting students into ministry opportunities.

  • Plan and facilitate gatherings of students on campus throughout the week that include prayer, teaching, evangelism, leadership development, and applying Scripture to life in college and beyond.

  • Invite students regularly to church gatherings, CCO’s Jubilee conference and other transformative opportunities.  

  • Establish a healthy relationship with the university that honors Cairn University guidelines for outside organizations and promotes sustainable campus access for the CCO and Langhorne Presbyterian.

  • Partnership specific duties and responsibilities, including ensuring that Cairn students who would like to attend LPC have transportation and helping LPC create space for Cairn students to fulfil their ministry-for-credit requirements.


Church Integration

  • Effectively and consistently communicate the vision and progress of college ministry within the church. 

  • Connect students into discipleship opportunities and relationships within the church body. 

  • Invite and equip congregants to provide hospitality, mentorship, and discipleship of college students and young adults with the aim of sending them out as leaders in their spheres of influence, including the establishment of a College Ministry Team that is integrated into programs in the church as well as on campus. 

  • Support the overarching goals and efforts of the entire church by being an active part of the staff team and maintaining a servant-leadership mentality in all aspects of ministry. 

  • Maintain intentional pastoral relationships with young adults connected to the church, including high school graduates, local college students, and young adults from the church but studying at campuses elsewhere.

  • Develop and oversee a transition plan, in coordination with church staff and leaders, for graduating high school students to help them move into full adult participation in the church, including the intentional reintegration of returning graduates into the life of the church.

  • Collaborate with ministry leaders to ensure that college students and young adults are not siloed but incorporated in the ordinary life of the church.


Leadership Development

  • Develop and mobilize student leaders to co-labor in the on campus fellowship, evangelism, and Bible studies.

  • Disciple and mobilize leaders among students at Cairn University and Langhorne Presbyterian Church to live out their faith in service and evangelism.

  • Directing and overseeing the recruitment of Cairn students into leadership development pathways, such as the Ocean City Beach Project and the formation of a student intern program.

Ministry Context & Partnership 

  • Steward a positive relationship with Langhorne Presbyterian Church that promotes long-lasting ministry in partnership with CCO.

  • Attend regular Langhorne Presbyterian Church staff meetings.

  •  Participation in the ministry rhythms of LPC as a leader and shepherd of the church and integrating students into the life and rhythm of LPC.

  • Teach LPC classes, lead small groups and Bible studies, lead prayer groups, and assist in worship, from time-to-time, as schedules, duties, and coordination with LPC staff allows.

  • Opportunity to preach at LPC from time-to-time.

  • Participate in the shepherding of LPCers through the shepherding of young adults, college students, and their families.


Other Projects & Duties Assigned

  • Participate in all required CCO Training.

  • Report ministry outcomes through CCO Mid-Year/Year-End Reflections and Annual Campus Stats documents.

  • Pray regularly and frequently for the ministry of the CCO.

  • Exceed 100% of support raising ministry goals.

  • Complete other duties and projects as assigned.


REQUIREMENTS

Education

  • Bachelor's Degree required.

    • Master of Divinity (or equivalent) preferred. Ordained or ordainable in the Evangelical Presbyterian Church preferred. LPC, in conjunction with CCO and the EPC’s Presbytery of the East, would be able and willing to assist in earning a Master of Divinity while on staff.

Experience

  • 1-3 years ministry related experience required

Skill Set 

  • Able to internalize ministry vision and strategy.

  • Collaborates with teams.

  • Manages competing priorities and tasks in a timely manner.

  • Displays initiative, can work independently, and can creatively generate proactive steps with follow through  in line with LPC’s vision and strategy. 

  • Ability to engage a wide range of audiences and age demographics.

Spiritual Health

  • Cultivate growth through regular worship in Langhorne Presbyterian church, prayer, Scripture study, and other spiritual disciplines.

Personal Conduct

  • Displays personal conduct consistent with CCO’s Statement of Faith, Core Values and CCO employee handbook. 

  • Review and adhere to all general expectations of Langhorne Presbyterian Church  staff team members.

  • Alignment with the doctrine, values, and vision of Langhorne Presbyterian Church


Professional Growth

  • Plan and pursue professional development opportunities approved by CCO and Partnership Supervisors.

Work Value

  • Maturity to be a pastoral presence in the lives of college students.

  • Demonstrates a passion for the Gospel, the Church, and college students.

  • Proactive in preparation and timely in response. 

  • Encourages the growth and development of others.

  • Values excellence.

Other Requirements

  • Valid Driver’s License and reliable transportation for travel.

University of St. Thomas

Campus Minister

Campus Ministry

The University of St. Thomas (UST), a private Catholic University committed to the liberal arts and the religious and intellectual tradition of Catholic higher education, located in Houston, Texas, near the vibrant central business district, Texas Medical Center, and museum district, is seeking applicants for a full-time Campus Minister. The position reports directly to the Director of Campus Ministry and is within the Student Affairs organization. This position will actively contribute towards furthering our Student Affairs Board of Trustee charges to strengthen UST's (a) student success efforts and (b) Catholic mission and faith integration efforts. Applicants for this position must be Catholic, and they need to be able to support joyfully, professionally, and publicly the University as it seeks to be faithful to and embody both a robust Catholicism--in its intellectual, doctrinal, moral, and spiritual dimensions.

Position Summary:

The Campus Minister is a ministry position directly involved with student formation in the areas of Catholic outreach and spiritual integration of the campus community. This position develops and implements retreats, service opportunities, and peer ministry initiatives, as well as provides support for students leading these initiatives, acts as a liaison with St. Paul's Outreach (SPO) missionaries, and forms small group leaders and faith-centered living communities known as "households." The Campus Minister has the authority to implement operating practices, carries out major assignments in conducting the operations of the organization, and is involved in planning long-term and short-term organizational objectives. This position reports directly to the Director of Campus Ministry.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities:

  • Provide pastoral care and spiritual guidance to students on an ongoing basis
  • Inspire, form, and equip students, faculty, and staff so that they would grow in holiness, form a deeper relationship with God, and invite others to join them by meeting them where they are, building Christ-centered relationships with them, and forming them into lifelong disciples.
  • Form, equip, and send Peer Ministers to evangelize the UST community with ongoing meetings and one-on-ones, as well as lead them in organizing, planning, and running student outreach events.
  • Plan, guide, and lead retreats, alongside the Retreats Intern, to provide overnight and daily faith experiences for students on and off campus, such as the Fall Retreat, Men's and Women's Retreats, Packing Nothing Retreat, Athlete Retreat, Household Retreat, Leadership Retreats, etc.
  • Guide and supervise Households to be Christ-centered living; plan and lead household-related events.
  • Invite, form, and send small group leaders to lead intentional small groups on campus, and continue to shepherd/mentor them.
  • Mentor student leaders on campus
  • Organize and lead the UST group (students and staff) that will attend the annual SEEK Conference, including coordination of all trip logistics and formation of students.
  • Work collaboratively with faculty, staff, and on-campus groups to engage students in Campus Ministry activities.
  • Work alongside other Campus Ministry staff in planning and executing all student leadership-related activities, such as meetings, retreats, and training.
  • Advise the Campus Ministry team on various aspects of Catholic identity for the
  • Participate in various meetings that help support Campus Ministry goals and
  • Serve as UST representative on Young Adult and Campus Ministry activities with the Archdiocese of Galveston-Houston. May serve as a representative of Campus Ministry, as requested (e.g. Care Team, Spiritual Integration Committee, etc.)
  • Act as liaison between Campus Ministry and Paul's Outreach missionaries, helping to organize formation activities and outreach events with the missionaries.
  • Perform other duties as assigned by the Director of Campus
  • Complete all administrative office work, including maintaining the budget and proper communication with co-workers.

Experience and Education Requirements:

  • Bachelor's degree required; preference will be given to candidates with associated degrees in Theology, Religious Studies, Catechetics, or similar fields of Other areas of study are acceptable with additional years of ministry experience.
  • Preference for a Master's degree in Divinity or Theology from an accredited Catholic institution
  • Must be a practicing Catholic in good standing with the Roman Catholic
  • Minimum 2 years of experience in ministry-related activities that concern the faith development of youth or young adults.
  • Excellent communication skills, both verbal and
  • Fluency in reading, writing, and speaking Spanish is strongly
  • Excellent organization skills and the ability to prioritize projects and
  • Ability to work effectively in collaboration with
  • Possess the enthusiasm, creativity, knowledge, and energy needed to meet the demands of the position.
  • Demonstrate an understanding of the spiritual and pastoral needs of the targeted age group which they intend to serve.
  • Must be reliable and dependable to meet the scheduled work hours, which will include evenings and weekends, as planned.
  • Demonstrate an intermediate level of proficiency in Microsoft Office suite and other graphic design software (e.g., Canva, InDesign, Finale, etc.)

Working Conditions

Position will require work during non-traditional business hours and on Sundays, Holy Days (e.g., Easter, Christmas, etc.), and weekends at specific events such as service projects, retreats, evening programs, student conferences, etc. Physical requirements are those of a normal business office. A valid driver's license is required in order to attend retreats and other events off-campus.

The above statements are intended to describe the general nature of work performed by individuals in this job classification. They are not intended to be construed as an exhaustive list of all responsibilities, duties, and qualifications required of individuals in this job classification. All positions may have miscellaneous job duties assigned on an as-needed basis. Management, at the appropriate level, retains the right to assign and change the duties of any position at any time.

The University of Saint Thomas is committed to the religious, ethical, and intellectual traditions of Catholic higher education. As permitted by law, practicing Catholics who will advance the mission of the school are preferred for this position. However, the University invites all qualified applicants to apply.

post_html:
Children’s Ministry Director - New Covenant Church
 

Kids Ministry Director 
Position Type: Part-time/Full-time 
Reports To: Pastor of family ministries

 

OVERVIEW

We are looking for a Kids Ministry Director to join our church family in a leadership opportunity. This person will be responsible for leading and overseeing the church’s children’s ministry programs, fostering a safe, engaging, and faith-building environment for children pre-k to fifth grade. This role involves biblical teaching, volunteer coordination, program development, and partnership with families to nurture spiritual growth in children.

The Director will need to be enthusiastic about the kid’s experience, continue in what we’ve started and create new processes and efficiencies to serve more programs and children as we grow. There will be a high variety of projects and tasks required; communication and collaboration among multiple 'players' will be vital. This role will be to lead and align programs and people in order to create a standard of strong execution and experiences. 

 

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

1. Program Development & Implementation

- Design, plan, and execute age-appropriate curriculum and activities for children’s Sunday School, mid-week programs, special events, and outreach activities.

- Ensure all programs align with the church’s mission, vision, and doctrinal beliefs.

- Continually evaluate and improve ministry programs to meet the spiritual, emotional, and physical needs of children.

2. Co-Lead Volunteer Leadership & Training

- Recruit, co-train, and equip volunteers to serve effectively in various children’s ministry roles alongside Family Pastor.

- Develop leadership teams of volunteers and provide ongoing support, encouragement, and training alongside Family Pastor

- Maintain volunteer policies, safety procedures, and background checks.

3. Safety, Compliance & Policy

- Ensure the safety and well-being of all children and volunteers during ministry activities.

- Maintain a clean, welcoming, and age-appropriate environment.

- Implement and monitor protocols for emergency procedures and child protection.

4. Family & Church Engagement

- Build strong relationships with families to support their role in spiritual development.

- Communicate regularly with parents regarding upcoming events, curriculum, and children’s spiritual growth.

- Partner with other church ministries and community organizations to promote children’s outreach and involvement.

5. Administration & Budgeting

- Manage the ministry’s budget, supplies, and resources.

- Maintain accurate records of attendance, volunteer schedules, and other relevant data.

- Plan and coordinate special events such as VBS, camps, and holiday programs.

 

QUALIFICATIONS

- Strong personal faith and commitment to the Christian faith and the church’s doctrinal beliefs.

- Previous experience working with children and/or in a children’s ministry setting.

- Leadership and team-building skills.

- Excellent communication and interpersonal skills.

- Organizational skills with the ability to plan and execute programs effectively.

- Ability to recruit, train, and motivate volunteers.

- Background check (required) and child safety certification (may be required or encouraged).

 

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

- Bachelor’s degree in education, youth ministry, or related field…

- or 4 years of experience as lead in children’s ministry or age appropriate private or public classroom.

- Certification in child safety and first aid.

- Experience integrating technology into ministry programs.

 

WORKING CONDITIONS

  • Part-time position [25 hours weekly] may vary based on need/annual events…or full-time based on candidate’s experience and qualifications.
  • Must pass background check and child safety training.
  • This environment is a positive faith-focused atmosphere emphasizing teamwork, communication, and a passion for children’s spiritual growth.

 

SUMMARY

The Kids Director often works with volunteers and coordinating training alongside Pastor of Family Ministries to ensure that the ministry aligns with the church’s overall mission and values.  Here at New Covenant Church, this plays a vital role in nurturing children’s spiritual development and building a strong foundation for their relationship with Christ.

post_html:
Rivers & Rails Campus Staff Minister (Ohio, West Virginia, Western Pennsylvania)

Work Location:

Ohio

Job Type:

Full time

God has called InterVarsity to plant and to build witnessing communities of students and faculty who follow Jesus on college and university campuses. Through these groups, we believe ever- increasing numbers of students and faculty from all ethnic groups and areas of the campus will be transformed by the Gospel. We expect to see campuses increasingly become places where people, ideas, and structures flourish to the glory of God. We confidently anticipate that our InterVarsity alumni will become change agents across the country and around the world. We pursue this calling by discerning and actively participating in what God is already doing on campus. This is the essence of being a Campus Staff Minister (CSM).

ESSENTIAL COMMITMENTS/RESPONSIBILITIES

Spiritual Growth

As a Campus Staff Minister, you pursue maturity as a disciple of Jesus Christ so that your life and work increasingly reflects a growing love for God, God’s Word, God’s people of every ethnicity and culture, and God’s purposes in the world. To do this, you will:

  • Pursue a vibrant relationship with the triune God through engagement with Scripture, prayer, and worship, both individually and in community
  • Develop self-leadership (growing in self-awareness, self-management, relational integrity, and resiliency)
  • Embrace Scriptural standards for behavior and attitudes

2.              Campus Leadership

As a Campus Staff Minister, you increase the number of witnessing communities, as well as the size, health, spiritual maturity, and campus-wide influence of existing witnessing communities of students and faculty by being a:

  • Visionary Guide:

You communicate and model InterVarsity’s vision to see students and faculty transformed, campuses renewed and world changers developed

  • Create a culture of humble dependence on God and bold expectation in God’s intention to start new witnessing communities throughout the campus and on new campuses
  • Model – in person and through programs – InterVarsity’s vision and Core Values, including a biblically-defined commitment to engage every ethnic and social group on campus
  • Lead students and faculty – individually and collectively – through Scripture, prayer, teaching, and discipleship experiences, so that they articulate and align their ministry activities around this vision
  • Set annual goals through prayer, research and reflection with your teams (students, faculty, and staff) for qualitative and quantitative growth, including conversions and leadership development
  • Structural Architect:

You create, develop, align and leverage ministry plans, programs, teams, and structures to close the gap between current reality and the aspirational goals.

  • Build leadership teams who trust and partner well with you and who demonstrate spiritual vitality, relational health, and mission alignment
  • Develop and execute plans to achieve annual goals, evaluating and modifying the plan as needed throughout the year
  • Increase momentum for the vision by aligning programs, structures, conferences and teams around the goals
  • Mobilize students and faculty to engage their relational networks with the gospel and to start new missional communities
  • Under the direction of the Area Director, may supervise Ministry Interns and Campus Ministry Interns as delegated
  • Missional Developer:

You intentionally gather, invite, and develop diverse groups of students and faculty so that they not only encounter andfollow Jesus as Savior and Lord but also advance the mission on campus as participants and leaders.

  • Create ways for faculty and students to encounter and follow Jesus through Scripture, worship, prayer, mission experiences, conferences, etc.
  • Equip students and faculty so that they think strategically about campus engagement and so that they proclaim – in word, deed, and power – the good news of Jesus, regularly inviting students and faculty to follow him as Savior and Lord
  • Disciple students and faculty by equipping them to hear the Word, respond actively, and debrief and interpret the experience so that they grow in Christlikeness, reflect our Core Values, and develop ministry skills
  • Invite, coach, and equip students and faculty to become increasingly effective participants and leaders, including starting new witnessing communities on campuses

3.              Organizational Collaboration

As a Campus Staff Minister, you have joined a national mission. Therefore, you work with a network of other local, area, regional, and national InterVarsity staff and volunteers so that our work reflects Biblical standards of excellence, integrity, and partnership.

  • Partner with and respond positively to the direction and coaching of your supervisors and national leaders
  • Contribute to collaborative and productive team meetings and relationships
  • Affiliate chapters under your care and submit Graduating Student Forms in order to increase our partnership with current students and alumni
  • Use national ministry resources and tools, as requested, including recruiting and/or participating in local, regional, or national conferences as required
  • Complete reporting, planning and review requirements in a timely way so that you and your supervisors can assess and improve your work as a CSM
  • Comply with all InterVarsity policies and procedures

4.              Ministry Partnership Development

As a Campus Staff Minister, you will develop a team of partners – churches and individuals (including alumni and community members) – who will resource the ministry financially, in prayer, or volunteer service that advances the mission.

  • Raise 100% of the financial budget assigned by your supervisor
  • Communicate regularly with your ministry partners, nurturing the relationship through visits, phone calls, emails and regular prayer letters
  • Develop on-going, long-lasting partnership with alumni and volunteers
  • Comply with all Ministry Partnership Policies
  • Identify and invest in advocates who will build networks of volunteers and donors on InterVarsity’s behalf

5.              Accomplish all other assigned tasks as appropriate

The Young Adults Pastor is responsible for providing leadership, direction, and oversight for the young adult ministry (ages 20-30) at Victory Family Church. This role focuses on pastoral teaching, building community through small groups, planning impactful events, and raising up the next generation of volunteer leaders. The Young Adults Pastor will also build key relationships within the community, including collegiate sports teams and local campus ministries, ensuring all efforts align with the broader vision and mission of the church.


A great match for this position would be:

  • Compelling Communicator & Preacher: Able to communicate Scripture clearly, dynamically, and effectively to young adults and a broader church audience.
  • Entrepreneurial Self Starter: Ownership, creates momentum, sees opportunities and builds ministry without constant direction.
  • Team Player: Works well within the larger church, supports the org direction, prioritizes mission over personal preference.
  • Humble & Coachable: Receives feedback well, self awareness, and is willing to adapt and grow.
  • Strategic Systems Builder: Can design, implement, evaluate, and improve ministry systems – (e.g. young adult small groups, leadership development).


About This Organization

Founded in 2013, Victory Family Church has grown into a vibrant, multi-site church with campuses in Norman, Newcastle, Chickasha, and Shawnee. We are deeply committed to our mission—to help those far from Christ know Him, and those who know Him grow in Him. Every Sunday, each location delivers the same message, preached live by local campus pastors. Our culture is marked by a true sense of Family, passion for Jesus and his people, commitment to excellence, and missional clarity.


Location

Norman is a thriving college town that is also a part of the OKC metro area. Norman has approximately 128,026 people and the metro is a little over 1 million. Norman consists of a lot of young families. It has a small-town vibe but is close to a larger city.



﻿Key Responsibilities

  • Provide visionary leadership and organizational oversight for the Young Adults Ministry (ages 20-30 focus). 
  • Preach a minimum of 10 Sundays a year across all campuses and speak at a minimum of 25 Young Adult nights, along with other miscellaneous speaking engagements. 
  • Design, build, and oversee a vibrant small group structure tailored for young adults. 
  • Plan, coordinate, and execute strategic events and key initiatives for the young adult community. 
  • Recruit, train, and raise up volunteer leaders to build healthy, sustainable, maturing ministry teams. 
  • Cultivate and manage strategic outward-facing relationships, potentially playing a role with University of Oklahoma (OU) sports teams and the Fellowship of Christian Athletes (FCA).
