The Children’s Ministry Leader is responsible for leading and overseeing the Children’s Ministry at the Johnson County Campus. This role collaborates with staff, volunteers, parents and children to develop spiritual growth by teaching God’s Word at age-appropriate levels. The Pastor/Ministry Leader equips children to become disciples of Jesus Christ who know they are loved, seen and belong. This position also provides leadership and guidance for all weekend programming at the Johnson County Campus, with a strong emphasis on creating environments where children are actively formed into lifelong disciples of Jesus.


Personal Responsibilities

  • Be committed to grow in the grace and knowledge of our Lord Jesus Christ (2 Peter 3:18; 1 Peter 2:2) by assembling for instruction in God’s Word and engaging in the personal study of God’s Word.
  • Responsibly use the resources at your disposal to foster the mission and vision of Abundant Life (1 Peter 5:1-4).
  • Participate in an Abundant Life group (Acts 2:41-42) as well as the discipleship ministry (Matthew 28:18-20).
  • Live in a way that glorifies God and aligns with the staff core values (1 Timothy 3:1-7, Titus 1:5-9).
  • Be committed to giving to the needs of the saints (2 Corinthians 8:1-7 & 9:12).
  • Become a member of Abundant Life.

Essential Functions and Responsibilities

  • Provide leadership, supervision, and development for the Johnson County Campus Children’s Ministry, serving children from birth through 5th grade.
  • Oversee the overall workflow and daily operations of Children’s Ministry programming.
  • Collaborate with the Campus Pastor to align Children’s Ministry with the mission and ministries of the church.
  • Equip, inspire, recruit, train, and deploy volunteers across all areas of Children’s Ministry.
  • Partner with Central Services to establish and implement best practices for Children’s Ministry at the Johnson County Campus.
  • Work with Campus Pastor in planning and preparing the yearly ministry calendar and strategic Children’s Ministry initiatives.
  • Offer leadership for all mile marker classes and celebrations within the ministry.
  • Ensure that all applicable rooms are appropriately equipped and presentable for ministry activities.
  • Maintain clear communication with parents, providing updates and addressing individual concerns as needed.
  • Work with Children’s Ministry team and Campus Pastor to set the direction and goals of the ministry.
  • Steward the Campus Children’s Ministry budget and assist in annual planning with the Campus Pastor.
  • Lead and oversee weekend programming each Sunday morning, in addition to other children’s events throughout the church calendar.
  • Foster a welcoming, nurturing environment where staff and volunteers are attentive to children’s needs, can pray with them, and disciple them to become more like Jesus.
  • Coordinate communication and care between staff, volunteers, and families; refer families to pastoral care when appropriate.
  • Enforce and maintain all child safety policies and procedures to ensure a secure trustworthy environment for all children participating in ministry activities.
  • Strategically schedule and manage volunteer teams for weekend programming.
  • Plan and lead special events such as Kid’s Week (VBS) and other campus-specific programs as needed.
  • Cultivate a thorough understanding of the Children’s Ministry to offer effective leadership and spiritual guidance.
  • Manage and purchase ministry-related supplies and resources as needed.
  • Practice discretion and confidentiality in the dissemination of information.
  • Participate in Central Services Children’s Ministry meetings to help shape the direction of the ministry.
  • Fulfill additional duties as assigned in alignment with the mission of making disciples and serving families well.

Skills and Qualifications

Success in this role will be achieved by a spiritually mature, highly motivated, and mission-driven leader who is passionate about making disciples of Jesus Christ through Children’s Ministry. This role requires someone who is organized, relational, and able to lead others with clarity, humility, and purpose.

  • A deep personal commitment to Jesus Christ and a calling to disciple children and families through biblical teaching and relational ministry.
  • Proven ability to lead and inspire volunteers in creating environments that foster spiritual growth and lifelong faith in Jesus.
  • Strong communication skills with the ability to connect effectively with children, parents, volunteers and staff.
  • Highly organized.
  • Collaborative team player with the capacity to work closely with others.
  • Working knowledge of Microsoft Office and other administrative tools.

Above all, the candidate must demonstrate a clear heart for children, a love for Jesus and a desire to see the next generation grow as devoted disciples of Jesus.


Employment at AL requires a commitment to honoring the Lord in work and life, as well as the character to uphold the AL Staff Core Values of Synergy, Excellency, Integrity, Tenacity, Humility, and Loyalty. The skills, qualifications, and responsibilities listed here are not intended to be all-inclusive of the abilities needed to perform the job.


Education/Experience

  • A minimum of 2 years’ experience in a leadership role is required.
  • 2 years’ experience in Children’s Ministry is preferred.

Church: Journey Church

Job Title: Youth Pastor

Location: Bozeman, Montana


The Big Idea

The Youth Pastor will be a champion of disciple-making for Jesus Christ by incorporating student-aged ministries within the context of the full church body. The primary purpose of this position is to develop, coordinate, and execute a philosophy of discipleship and shepherding within our church and community, with a specific emphasis on middle school (6th – 8th) and high school students. If you love relational ministry, thrive in a healthy team culture, and want to make a lasting impact in one of the most beautiful places in America, you’ll love what God is doing at Journey! 



Why This Is a Great Opportunity

Located in the stunning city of Bozeman, Montana, Journey Church is a healthy, growing church seeking a high-capacity Youth Pastor to lead a thriving student ministry and shape the next generation of all-in followers of Jesus. With 150+ weekly students, 55 volunteer leaders, and a ministry deeply rooted in relational discipleship, you’ll be stepping into a strong foundation and a culture that values shepherding, teamwork, and authenticity. You’ll join a collaborative staff team that believes ministry is best done together. This role offers the opportunity to build on momentum, strengthen community ties, and lead students and families toward a deeper connection with Christ.



About Journey Church

Mission: Together, we lead people in becoming all-in followers of Jesus.

Journey Church launched in 2005 with a passion to reach the Gallatin Valley for Christ. Today, we are a thriving, staff-led church with over 1,800 weekly attendees, a great team of ministry staff, and a heart to make disciples who Gather, Connect, Serve, and Give.

Our culture is defined by relational leadership, authenticity, and fun. We’re not just building programs, we’re developing people. Journey recently celebrated being recognized by Outreach Magazine as one of the Top 100 Fastest-Growing Churches in America (2025) and continues to see double-digit growth year after year. We believe ministry is best done together, equipping leaders who equip others. Every person who calls Journey home should have a shepherd: someone who knows them, loves them, and helps them take their next spiritual step.



Key Responsibilities

  • Lead and implement a comprehensive strategy for the spiritual formation of students.
  • Recruit, train, and shepherd staff, volunteer leaders, and interns within Student Ministries.
  • Partner with parents to engage them as key influencers in their students’ faith journey.
  • Champion relational shepherding where every student is known, loved, and guided toward next steps of faith.
  • Oversee Sunday night gatherings (6–8 p.m.) that include student-led worship, teaching, and small groups.
  • Grow and further develop off-site small group ministry and leader training.
  • Build bridges with local schools, coaches, and community networks.
  • Manage Student Ministries budget, staff, interns, and resources.
  • Participate in broader church life, staff meetings, and all-church events.
  • Carry out additional pastoral responsibilities as needed.
  • Keep the Council and Staff informed of critical situations and comply with recommended best practices related to child safety. 



Qualifications

  • Mature follower of Jesus Christ with a growing faith and commitment to Journey’s mission and core values.
  • Biblically qualified to serve as a leader in accordance with 1 Timothy 3:1-7, Titus 1:5-9, Peter 5:1-9. 
  • Bachelor’s degree required; Master’s degree or seminary education preferred.
  • Proven leadership experience in student ministry (or similar context).
  • Strong relational intelligence and communication skills.
  • A commitment to lifelong learning. 
  • Self-starter who is trustworthy for a senior leadership position at Journey Church.
  • Ability to lead leaders and equip volunteers for ministry.
  • Ability to communicate clearly and effectively both interpersonally and in public settings.
  • Biblically grounded and aligned with Journey’s theological convictions.
  • Demonstrated humility, teachability, and a collaborative spirit.



Core Competencies

  • Relational Shepherding: Values people over programs; builds authentic, lasting relationships.
  • Leadership Multiplication: Recruits, trains, and empowers others for ministry impact.
  • Cultural Fit: Brings fun, authenticity, and humility to a high-trust team environment.
  • Strategic Thinking: Can design and execute a plan that grows both depth and breadth in Student Ministries.
  • Spiritual Velocity: Leads from personal depth and intimacy with Christ.



Benefits & Compensation

  • Full-time position (40 hours/week, including Sundays and select evenings).
  • Salary range: $55,000–$70,000 (based on experience and education).
  • Full benefits package: medical, dental, vision, long-term disability, and retirement.
  • Generous PTO and paid holidays aligned with Bozeman Public School schedule.
  • Healthy staff culture ranked in the Top 5% of all workplaces nationwide (Best Christian Workplace Survey, 2025).



About Bozeman, Montana

Bozeman is one of the fastest-growing cities in the West, a vibrant community of about 55,000 residents (100,000 in the valley) nestled between mountain ranges and near Yellowstone National Park. With top-rated schools, outdoor recreation, and a thriving university (Montana State University, 18,000+ students), Bozeman offers an unmatched balance of adventure, beauty, and community.

While Bozeman’s cost of living is higher than average, nearby towns like Belgrade and Manhattan provide more affordable housing options, all within a 15-minute drive to Journey’s campus.

Chinese Christian Gospel Church of Naples, FL

Our church is located in Collier County along the southwest coast of Florida. Among a population of

over 400,000, there are approximately 2,000 Chinese residents. Established in 2003, our church currently

has a worship attendance of 30 to 40 people. The congregation includes professionals, small business

owners, and retirees coming primarily from mainland China and Taiwan. We are a loving, mutually

supportive family in Christ. For more information about us, please visit our website at ccgcnaples.org.

We are seeking a pastor capable of ministering in both Mandarin and English. This is a part-time lead

pastor position. The pastor will be led by the Holy Spirit to equip brothers and sisters as Gospel

ambassadors in the community—to lead the congregants in developing family-oriented ministries, and

dedicating themselves to the spread of God’s Good News through witness and community service.

Candidates should possess the following experience and qualifications:

1. Sound Christ-centered faith, meeting the biblical qualifications for an elder.

2. A clear calling from God for pastoral ministry.

3. Eligibility for pastoral credentialing and ordination within the Christian & Missionary Alliance.

4. Innovative ability and experience in planning evangelistic ministries to those who serve in and

frequent Chinese-owned small businesses (e.g., restaurants, spas).

5. Familiarity with the Chinese immigrant experience and North American culture, capable of

communication in English.

The pastor’s ministry responsibilities include, but are not limited to, the following areas:

1. Preaching and Teaching: Regularly preach on Sundays and participate in Christ-centered biblical

teaching.

2. Pastoral Care: Provide spiritual care to the congregation through visitation, fellowship, prayer,

biblical counseling, and foster spiritual growth.

3. Discipleship Training: Lead discipleship training to develop ministry coworkers and evangelists.

4. Missions: Organize and lead the congregation in community evangelism and maintain a clear

missions strategy.

5. Church Development Planning: Lead the church in the formulation of a vision and goals for church

development that align with God’s will, effectuating healthy growth in both spiritual maturity and the

number of congregants.

PROGRAM SUMMARY: JustLead is a youth leadership program of EY implemented through a coalition of neighborhood churches and faith-based organizations serving urban youth. The after-school component for elementary, middle, and high school students includes Bible study, tutoring, homework help, health/fitness/nutrition instruction, field trips, service learning opportunities, and job and college readiness activities.


JOB SUMMARY:

This position will coordinate and implement all aspects of the church-based, JustLead Ministry for middle school and high school age youth.  The JustLead Youth Ministry Coordinator will be responsible for the recruitment of youth and families to participate in the JustLead programs as well as volunteers to help support the ministry initiatives and for achieving assigned program goals.  This role will partner with the church or faith-based organization (FBO) for both the youth and family ministry.


 ESSENTIAL JOB DUTIES:

  • Actively identify, recruit, engage, and support neighborhood youth and families to participate in the ministry.
  • Coordinate and implement, for an assigned age group, afterschool/summer day camps, Wednesday night/Sunday morning and other discipleship initiatives, and relationship-building activities under the direction of the JustLead Ministry Director.
  • Ensure assigned program goals are being met including participation, comprehensive engagement, and youth development outcomes.  Participate in weekday and weekend camps, special events, field trips, home visits, and other student event activities.  Be engaged with the participants’ schools and know other activities and organizations with which a participant may be involved.  These events may require some evening work as needed. 
  • Help connect participants in “transition grades” to the next age-level staff and programming and connect students to calling & career center as needed. 
  • Notify Director and respond to families as requested, should an emergency situation arise.
  • Funnel families into family engagement activities.
  • Must become fully immersed in all aspects of the church as a whole through attendance on Wednesday evening and Sunday morning worship services, special events, i.e., Christmas plays, church celebrations, etc.  Serving actively in the church as a staff team in ways that connect youth to the church through programs and events.
  • Collect fees and maintain program budgets.
  • Review and provide needed data and/or report achieved outcomes and measurements for assigned church/FBO.
  • Recruit, manage, develop, and nurture a team of volunteers, AmeriCorps members, and/or youth workers.
  • Follow all organizational safety standards, including but not limited to behavior and discipline, child ratios, transportation, CPR, and first aid.  Ensure AmeriCorps members and volunteers follow all organizational standards as well.
  • Maintain a current CDL and drive large vehicles/buses.
  • Manage additional projects and tasks as assigned, participate with any assigned groups or committees, and participate in area ministry network and organization events, including working outside normal schedule as needed. .


 QUALIFICATIONS:

  • Dedicated Christian with clear knowledge of the Gospel and a passion for the mission of Emerald Youth Foundation; connected to a church community; possesses a strong reputation for honesty, integrity, and high moral standards. 
  • At least 21 years of age with clear driving record and ability to obtain a CDL along with a willingness to drive 15 passenger vans or buses.
  • Bi-lingual, Spanish Speaking a plus!
  • (Ideally) 2-3 years of experience organizing and implementing youth programs (and/or youth ministry).
  • Ability to effectively communicate.
  • Experience in an urban setting ideal.
  • Ministry or related degree preferred.
  • Excellent organizational skills.
  • Familiarity with Microsoft Office.
  • Supervisor/management experience desired.


It is the policy of Emerald Youth Foundation (EYF) to provide employment opportunities to all people without regard to race, color, sex, age, or national origin.

Internship
Description

  

Wellspring Church is a Gospel-Centered, Multiethnic, Intergenerational Church. We Love Discipleship!

WHO WE ARE

A Gospel-centered, Multiethnic, Intergenerational church. We LOVE Discipleship! Nestled in the heart of the Coachella Valley in Southern California, Wellspring Church started with humble beginnings in 1973. Eight believers launched a church in hopes of becoming an outpost for the gospel of Jesus Christ for the community in the desert. Decades later, that inaugural momentum remains the core of our church’s vision to be a church that is centered upon the gospel of Jesus Christ. We are a multiethnic church that believes that the gospel unites all people for the glory of Christ. We are excited about the gospel exchange that should take place from generation to generation. Our mission is to make disciples and unleash believers in the world to champion the gospel in their everyday lives. Sitting on 42 acres that shares a property line with the famous Indian Wells Tennis Gardens. At one of the busiest intersections in the Valley, Southwest stands poised to minister to the 600,000 residents and an annual 3.5 million tourists that have made our region famous around the world!


OUR FOCUS

Wellspring Church is focused on discipling people to become committed followers of Jesus Christ. We desire all members of Wellspring to be:

  • PLANTED (the call to salvation)
  • ROOTED (the call to foundation)
  • GROWING (the call to maturation)
  • GOING (the call to multiplication)

OUR VALUES

  • We are Faithful - We love Jesus! Our gospel-centered church will be driven by our gospel-centered team. We will aim for faithfulness to Jesus,      Jesus’ Word, and Jesus’ will above all else. (1 JOHN 4)
  • We are Family - Our families are our first ministry, not the church.      Our families will love the church and never feel like they have to compete with the church. So we’ll honor the Sabbath, honor time away from work to invest in our families and encourage our people to do the same. (1      TIMOTHY 3)
  • We are Fun - Laughing, enjoyment, and celebration is gonna be normal here. Our calling is a serious one, but it is not one that is without amazing fun! (ECCLESIASTES 8)
  • We are Free - We are a team on a mission. And you’re free to make that mission happen! We let thoroughbreds run. We’ll give you the play and make sure you’re free to run it. Our team is free to lead. Free to speak.      Free to innovate. Free to fail. All for the purpose of achieving the mission God has given us. (GALATIANS 2)
  • We are Forgiving - Sin is serious and we won’t let it remain in the camp. We will constantly forgive one another because we’ve been forgiven.      When conflict happens, we’ll address it quickly, respond graciously, and move forward by keeping short accounts with each other. (MATTHEW 18)
  • We are Flexible - We embrace change! There are no sacred cows here,      just a sacred goal to make Jesus famous! We’ll be geared to the times but anchored to the rock. (MARK 2)
  • We are Forthright - We want to bear much fruit! And because ministry is hard to measure, we’ll allow iron to sharpen iron to make one another better! So we’re gonna be forthright. Because fearless feedback yields fruit! (PROVERBS 27)

SUMMARY

 

The Resident is a developing ministry leader participating in Wellspring Church’s Pastoral Residency Program—a hands-on training experience designed to equip and prepare future pastors for vocational ministry. Under the mentorship of the Residency

Director and church leadership, residents gain practical ministry experience, spiritual formation, and leadership development while actively serving within Wellspring’s ministries. This position is part of the Wellspring Church Residency Program for the 2027–2028 program year.


KEY RESPONSIBILITIES


As a member of the Residency program, you will work closely with the Residency

Director. Your responsibilities include, but are not limited to:


  • Participate fully in the Residency Program curriculum, including theological training, leadership development, and ministry practicums.
  • Serve within assigned ministry areas (e.g., Discipleship, Family Ministry, Experience, Operations, etc.) as directed by the Residency Director.
  • Engage in weekly mentorship meetings and leadership coaching sessions with the Residency Director or designated ministry leader.
  • Actively participate in staff meetings, team gatherings, and church events as part of the Wellspring staff community.
  • Assist in planning and executing ministry programs, services, and outreach initiatives.
  • Contribute to teaching, leading, and pastoral care opportunities under the supervision of ministry leaders. Demonstrate a posture of learning, humility, and growth in spiritual maturity and ministry competency.
  • Complete assigned readings, projects, and evaluations within established deadlines.
  • Represent Wellspring Church with integrity, character, and alignment to the church’s  mission and values.
  • Perform other duties as assigned in alignment with ministry training goals.
Requirements

   

JOB SCOPE


The Resident is an active participant in the development pipeline of Wellspring Church, gaining practical ministry experience while being equipped for future pastoral leadership. Reporting to the Residency Director, this role blends classroom learning,

hands-on ministry, and spiritual mentorship. The Resident plays a key role in the life of the church while being intentionally trained to serve, lead, and disciple others with Gospel-centered excellence.


 

QUALIFICATIONS


  • Must be aligned with the Mission, Vision, and Leadership model of Wellspring Church.
  • A growing and mature relationship with Jesus Christ with a clear call to ministry.
  • Bachelor’s degree preferred or currently pursuing theological/ministry education.
  • Desire to pursue full-time vocational ministry within a local church context.
  • Teachable, humble, and eager to grow in character, competence, and calling.
  • Strong interpersonal, communication, and organizational skills.
  • Ability to work collaboratively as part of a team and under pastoral supervision.
  • Commitment to maintaining confidentiality and integrity in all ministry interactions.
  • Physical requirements: Constant periods of sitting and repetitive motions. Occasionally able to lift or move up to 20lbs and standing or walking.



What it's Like to Live in Indian Wells, CA: 

Indian Wells is a city in Riverside County, California, in the Coachella Valley. Incorporated in 1967, it lies in between Palm Desert and the resort town of La Quinta. The city hosts the sixth-largest tennis tournament in the world, the Indian Wells Masters tennis tournament, presently known as the BNP Paribas Open. The valley also hosts the Coachella and Stagecoach festivals, drawing a multitude of visitors on an annual basis.

The area is great for exploring the natural beauty of the oasis, whether at a national park, nature preserve, or even a zoo. Another uniquely Greater Palm Springs experience is a visit to a date farm—especially when paired with a date shake, a local favorite. The many museums of Greater Palm Springs offer a look at everything from historic airplanes to contemporary art. You can enjoy recreation options including ice skating, baseball, and swimming. Many Greater Palm Springs restaurants are founded on the concept of family, so you’ll find no shortage of kid-friendly eateries and dining spots in the oasis. Take Las Casuelas Terraza in downtown Palm Springs, for example; the restaurant has been serving family recipes, like Grandma Maria Fajardo's creamy guacamole, for four generations. And if you wander inside Brandini Toffee, a local family-owned sweet shop once featured on Oprah’s O List, you may even find one of the original founders working behind the counter or greeting customers.

Director of Church, Alumni & Ministry Relations (Talbot)

 

Position Summary

The Director of Church, Alumni & Ministry Relations provides strategic leadership for cultivating and strengthening Talbot's relationships with churches, ministry partners, and alumni. This role advances Talbot's mission by developing partnerships that support theological education, leadership development, ministry engagement, and alumni involvement. The Director serves as a primary ambassador for Talbot, expanding its influence, visibility, and connection to the broader Church.


Candidates must be willing to relocate in order to work in residence at Talbot’s campus in La Mirada, CA.



Alignment with Theological Positions

The person who fills this position must personally agree with Biola University’s Articles of Faith and Statement of Biblical Principles and be supportive of the positions contained in Biola’s Eschatology Teaching Position. As such, this person may not speak against or act in a manner inconsistent with these positions during the course of their employment at Biola.

 

Department

Talbot School of Theology

 

Supervisor

Reports directly to the Dean of Talbot School of Theology.

 

Supervision over Others

Administrative Assistant

 

Educational Requirements

  • Bachelor's degree required; ministry-related, theological, communications, or leadership field preferred.

  • Master's degree in theology, ministry, organizational leadership, or related field preferred.


Work Requirements

  • Full-time, exempt position (40 hours per week).

  • Requires regular presence on Biola University's campus in La Mirada, CA.

  • Requires regional and national travel for church visits, conferences, alumni engagement, and ministry partnerships.

  • Occasional evening and weekend responsibilities for events and external engagement activities.


Essential Duties

Church & Ministry Relations

  • Develop and strengthen relationships with churches, denominations, ministry organizations, and ministry leaders.

  • Serve as a primary representative of Talbot to pastors, church leaders, and ministry networks.

  • Cultivate partnerships that support theological education, leadership development, ministry collaboration, and student recruitment.

Alumni Engagement

  • Develop and implement strategies that foster lifelong engagement with Talbot alumni.

  • Create opportunities for alumni involvement through mentoring, networking, recruiting, giving, and ministry partnership.

  • Partner with Advancement to support alumni stewardship and donor engagement initiatives.

Ministry Connections

  • Facilitate connections between churches, ministry organizations, students, and alumni.

  • Support opportunities for internships, ministry placement, leadership development, and vocational engagement.

  • Strengthen pathways between theological education and practical ministry service.

Events & External Engagement

  • Lead key engagement initiatives, including alumni gatherings, church leader events, conferences, and ministry forums.

  • Represent Talbot at churches, conferences, and ministry events.

  • Collaborate with faculty and leadership to develop programs and resources for external audiences.

Strategic Leadership & Collaboration

  • Develop communication and engagement strategies that advance Talbot's mission and theological identity.

  • Utilize CRM and other tools to manage relationships and measure engagement effectiveness.

  • Partner with Admissions, Advancement, Marketing, and faculty to ensure coordinated external engagement efforts.

  • Manage projects, events, and resources with excellence and accountability.

  • Other duties as assigned.


Required Skills and Qualifications

  • Commitment to the mission, theological convictions, and values of Talbot School of Theology and Biola University.

  • Bachelor's degree required; Master's degree in theology, ministry, organizational leadership, or related field strongly preferred.

  • 5–7 years of experience in ministry leadership, church relations, alumni relations, advancement, pastoral ministry, ministry placement, or related external-facing roles.

  • Demonstrated ability to build and sustain meaningful relationships with church leaders, ministry organizations, and alumni networks.

  • Strong understanding of evangelical church contexts, ministry ecosystems, leadership development, and theological education environments.

  • Experience designing and leading engagement strategies, events, partnership initiatives, or ministry connection efforts.

  • Excellent interpersonal, verbal, and written communication skills.

  • Strong interpersonal and relationship-building skills, with the ability to build trust and influence stakeholders.

  • Strong organizational, project management, and relational follow-up skills.

  • Ability to work independently while collaborating across multiple departments and constituencies.

  • Demonstrated ability to exercise wisdom, discretion, and relational sensitivity in diverse ministry contexts.

  • Strong computer proficiency, including Microsoft Office, Google Workspace, and relevant data/reporting tools.

  • Familiarity with CRM systems and relational database tools for engagement tracking and reporting.

  • Ability to analyze engagement effectiveness and adjust strategies accordingly.

  • Collaborative, service-oriented, and highly relational leadership style.

  • Mature Christian faith and active participation in a local church.

  • Commitment to maintaining a lifestyle consistent with sound Christian principles and Biola University standards of conduct.

  • Willingness to travel regionally and nationally, and to work occasional evenings and weekends.

  • Evidence of integrity, humility, adaptability, and a teachable spirit in ministry and professional settings.

Cornerstone Church | Bloomington, IL | Illinois State University

The town is Normal. Yea, you read that right. Illinois State University started as a normal college (a teaching school). The town took on the name and the school continues to develop and send educators all over.

At Cornerstone Church, we are committed to God’s Glory, Ways, and Mission at ISU and beyond. We seek to make disciples of those that come to ISU - for education, business, or the new engineering school - and send them out into the world as missionaries.

We believe working as a resident or staff member in campus ministry is some of the most rewarding work you can do. To disciple the next generation to make disciples for their lives is an exciting task. We want staff and residents to engage and grow in understanding God’s glory (theology), ways (discipleship), and mission (evangelism). These are key parts of the normal Christian life, so why not learn and practice them with us in Normal, Illinois.

Reliant

We’re excited that you are considering joining us at Cornerstone Church through Reliant! Reliant is a faith-based nonprofit that partners with missional churches and Gospel-centered nonprofits to mobilize support-based missionaries for the Great Commission. Through Reliant, we provide missionaries with the resources, training, and support needed to thrive in their calling, including the critical process of raising financial and prayer support. Whether you're pursuing a short-term internship, a long-term residency, or a career in ministry, we are here to support and guide you every step of the way.

Here are a couple of quick thoughts to help you through the assessment process:

In this application, you will go through a series of stages:

  1. Application - This is the initial application for Reliant.
  2. Ministry Assessment - This assesses your readiness for your ministry role.
  3. Moral Conduct - This assesses your emotional and character-based readiness for a role in ministry.
  4. Local Interview - In this phase, you will do an interview with your church leadership.
  5. Reliant Review - Reliant will review all the pieces of your application and create a summary to discuss with your local church.
  6. Decision/Discernment - Reliant and your church will come together to make an employment decision.
  7. Provisionally Accepted - If you are accepted onto staff, you will have the opportunity to accept your offer, if desired.
  8. Onboarding - This will include online (and potentially in-person) training and HR paperwork. This is designed to prepare you to become a Reliant employee, as well as ready you to raise financial support.

Note: Once you begin a questionnaire within a stage, you will need to complete that stage fully. You are not able to save within a stage. Please set aside ample time to complete each stage.

When you are ready, click on the "Apply to Position" button to get started.

Campus Staff Minister - Louisiana (Graduate & Faculty Ministry)

Work Location:

Louisiana

Job Type:

Full time

God has called InterVarsity to plant and to build witnessing communities of students and faculty who follow Jesus on college and university campuses. Through these groups, we believe ever- increasing numbers of students and faculty from all ethnic groups and areas of the campus will be transformed by the Gospel. We expect to see campuses increasingly become places where people, ideas, and structures flourish to the glory of God. We confidently anticipate that our InterVarsity alumni will become change agents across the country and around the world. We pursue this calling by discerning and actively participating in what God is already doing on campus. This is the essence of being a Campus Staff Minister (CSM).

Please submit the GFM Interest Form before completing the full application for a position with Graduate & Faculty Ministries in our online system. We will contact you when we are ready to proceed with the application process.  


This position is open to applicants working less than 40 hours/week. If you are interested in part-time work please apply for this position. 

The pay range listed is for an employee working 40 hours/week at CSM level II. Pay will be prorated for employees who work less than 40 hours/week.


Volunteers are welcome. Volunteer opportunities range from prayer and hospitality to leading a campus fellowship of graduate students and faculty. Those interested in volunteering will go through an application and interview process,however, volunteer openings are not posted online. For more information, complete the GFM Interest Form. 


We are particularly seeking candidates for the following universities:

  • Louisiana State University (LSU)
  • University of Louisiana at Lafayette


ESSENTIAL COMMITMENTS/RESPONSIBILITIES 

Spiritual Growth 

As a Campus Staff Minister, you pursue maturity as a disciple of Jesus Christ so that your life and work increasingly reflect a growing love for God, God’s Word, God’s people of every ethnicity and culture, and God’s purposes in the world. To do this, you will: 

  • Pursue a vibrant relationship with the triune God through engagement with Scripture, prayer, and worship, both individually and in community
  • Develop self-leadership (growing in self-awareness, self-management, relational integrity, and resiliency) 
  • Embrace Scriptural standards for behavior and attitudes 

 

Campus Leadership 

As a Campus Staff Minister, you increase the number of witnessing communities, as well as the size, health, spiritual maturity, and campus-wide influence of existing witnessing communities of students and faculty by being a: 

  • Visionary Guide: 

You communicate and model InterVarsity’s vision to see students and faculty transformed, campuses renewed, and world changers developed 

  • Create a culture of humble dependence on God and bold expectation in God’s intention to start new witnessing communities throughout the campus and on new campuses 
  • Model – in person and through programs – InterVarsity’s vision and Core Values, including a biblically-defined commitment to engage every ethnic and social group on campus 
  • Lead students and faculty – individually and collectively – through Scripture, prayer, teaching, and discipleship experiences, so that they articulate and align their ministry activities around this vision 
  • Set annual goals through prayer, research and reflection with your teams (students, faculty, and staff) for qualitative and quantitative growth, including conversions and leadership development 
  • Structural Architect: 

You create, develop, align, and leverage ministry plans, programs, teams, and structures to close the gap between current reality and the aspirational goals. 

  • Build leadership teams who trust and partner well with you and who demonstrate spiritual vitality, relational health, and mission alignment 
  • Develop and execute plans to achieve annual goals, evaluating and modifying the plan as needed throughout the year 
  • Increase momentum for the vision by aligning programs, structures, conferences, and teams around the goals 
  • Mobilize students and faculty to engage their relational networks with the gospel and to start new missional communities 
  • Under the direction of the Area Director, may supervise Ministry Interns and Campus Ministry Interns as delegated 
  • Missional Developer: 

You intentionally gather, invite, and develop diverse groups of students and faculty so that they not only encounter and follow Jesus as Savior and Lord but also advance the mission on campus as participants and leaders. 

  • Create ways for faculty and students to encounter and follow Jesus through Scripture, worship, prayer, mission experiences, conferences, etc. 
  • Equip students and faculty so that they think strategically about campus engagement and so that they proclaim – in word, deed, and power – the good news of Jesus, regularly inviting students and faculty to follow him as Savior and Lord 
  • Disciple students and faculty by equipping them to hear the Word, respond actively, and debrief and interpret the experience so that they grow in Christlikeness, reflect our Core Values, and develop ministry skills 
  • Invite, coach, and equip students and faculty to become increasingly effective participants and leaders, including starting new witnessing communities on campuses 

 

Organizational Collaboration 

As a Campus Staff Minister, you have joined a national mission. Therefore, you work with a network of other local, area, regional, and national InterVarsity staff and volunteers so that our work reflects Biblical standards of excellence, integrity, and partnership. 

  • Partner with and respond positively to the direction and coaching of your supervisors and national leaders 
  • Contribute to collaborative and productive team meetings and relationships 
  • Affiliate chapters under your care and submit Graduating Student Forms in order to increase our partnership with current students and alumni 
  • Use national ministry resources and tools, as requested, including recruiting and/or participating in local, regional, or national conferences as required 
  • Complete reporting, planning and review requirements in a timely way so that you and your supervisors can assess and improve your work as a CSM 
  • Comply with all InterVarsity policies and procedures 

 

Ministry Partnership Development 

As a Campus Staff Minister, you will develop a team of partners – churches and individuals (including alumni and community members) – who will resource the ministry financially, in prayer, or volunteer service that advances the mission. 

  • Raise 100% of the financial budget assigned by your supervisor 
  • Communicate regularly with your ministry partners, nurturing the relationship through visits, phone calls, emails and regular prayer letters 
  • Develop on-going, long-lasting partnership with alumni and volunteers 
  • Comply with all Ministry Partnership Policies 
  • Identify and invest in advocates who will build networks of volunteers and donors on InterVarsity’s behalf 

 

Accomplish all other assigned tasks as appropriate 

 

QUALIFICATIONS (common to all levels of CSM) 

  • Annually affirm InterVarsity’s Statement of Agreement (Doctrinal Basis and Purpose Statement). Abide by InterVarsity’s Code of Conduct. Believe and behave consonantly with InterVarsity’s Human Sexuality Theological Paper. Affirm and behave consonantly with InterVarsity’s “Women in Ministry Statement of Affirmation” 
  • Bachelor’s degree required for CSMs assigned to a four-year campus. A minimum of an Associate’s degree required for CSMs assigned to a two-year campus or a community college 
  • Strong interpersonal skills (including ability to minister to diverse ethnic communities and faculty) 
  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills 
  • Demonstrated problem solving skills 
  • Familiarity with word processing, presentation, email, and spreadsheet software 

 

WORK ENVIRONMENT/PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS 

The CSM position leads ministry in a college campus environment. A designated office space may or may not be available. The CSM is required to travel to on-campus and off- campus sites as appropriate. Off-campus travel includes, but is not limited to: student ministry conferences, Ministry Partnership Development meetings, and InterVarsity- sponsored training sessions, meetings, and conferences. The CSM is regularly required to communicate with others, and routinely uses standard office equipment such as computers, phones, photocopiers, filing cabinets, etc. 

Pay Range: $45,324.00 - $60,420.00 per year

Pay: This position is funded through personal fundraising. Accordingly, compensation will vary based on the ability of the individual to secure a donor team to fund the cost of his/her salary. The anticipated salary range for this position on a full-time basis (40 hours/week) is dependent on a variety of factors, including location and cost of living. The actual salary received, including any geographic adjustment to account for location and cost of living, is subject to the individual’s ability to raise funds necessary to cover the full amount of such salary within the range set forth in the job posting details.

Benefits:

We offer a competitive benefits package, including health care and retirement savings with a match. Eligibility is based on employee type and hours worked.  Benefits include the following:

  • 403(b) Retirement Savings Plan

  • 403(b) matching contributions

  • Dental insurance

  • Employee assistance program

  • Employee discounts

  • Flexible work schedule

  • Flexible spending accounts

  • Health insurance

  • Health savings account

  • Life insurance

  • Paid time off

  • Parental leave

  • Professional development assistance

  • Vision insurance

Equal Employment Opportunity: 

 

InterVarsity Christian Fellowship/USA is both an equal opportunity employer and a faith-based religious organization. We conduct hiring without regard to race, color, ancestry, national origin, citizenship, age, sex, marital status, parental status, membership in any labor organization, political ideology, or disability of an otherwise qualified individual. The status of InterVarsity Christian Fellowship/USA as an equal opportunity employer does not prevent the organization from hiring staff based on their religious beliefs so that all staff share the same religious commitment.  Pursuant to the Civil Rights Act of 1964, Section 702 (42 U.S.C. 2000e 1(a)) InterVarsity Christian Fellowship/USA has the right to, and does, hire only candidates who agree with InterVarsity’s Statement of Agreement: Purpose and Doctrinal Basis because InterVarsity believes that each and every staff plays a vital role in advancing InterVarsity’s mission and purposes.

job_name: Youth Ministry Director at Wiesbaden, U.S. Military Installation, Germany
post_html:
*Please note this position would require our Staff to live near the community where they would be doing ministry.

Description:

There are nearly 300,000 teenagers of active-duty U.S. military parents who are stationed all over the world. These teens move an average of seven times during their school-aged years. The questions of identity and belonging that all teens face grow even more challenging to answer amid starting over and meeting new friends at each location.

This is where you can be the difference in a military teen’s life! By being in their world, walking alongside them, and creating a community where they experience the truth of God’s love and purpose for them, our staff provide a safe space where teens can develop friendships and connections to experience laughter, build hope, and generate resiliency.

We are currently providing incarnational ministry at many military installations around the world. You will have the opportunity to lead and oversee the overall Young Life Military program, known as Club Beyond, which is ecumenically focused and outreach oriented.

We are currently looking for both full-time and part-time staff throughout the United States, as well as international locations. Colorado Springs, CO, is the headquarters.

Responsibilities:

  • Actively develop healthy relationships with adults, as well as kids, and build vibrant relationships with the local community, the military installation, and the chapel community.

KIDS LEAD
SANDALS CHURCH
ROLE DESCRIPTION

Role Purpose

The Kids Lead role exists to build and lead a strong Real Team who creates a safe, fun, and welcoming environment where kids learn to be real with themselves, God, and others. This role is about leading people, not doing all the work alone.

The Kids Lead role exists to cast vision, lead culture, and build a healthy volunteer team of adults and students who create environments where kids (and parents) become real with themselves, God, and others as they grow closer to Jesus. This role focuses on discipling kids, developing leaders, and partnering with parents to disciple their kids. 

Key Responsibilities

Lead Vision & Culture

  • Cast compelling vision for Sandals Kids that reflects the church’s mission and values.
  • Shape and protect a culture of authenticity, discipleship, passion, and fun.
  • Lead with clarity and consistency so kids and leaders know where the ministry is going.

Lead & Develop Your Real Team

  • Recruit, onboard, and train new volunteers.
  • Build team leads and give away real leadership.
  • Create a culture where volunteers feel valued, supported, and discipled.

Weekend Experience

  • Ensure check-in is warm, fast, and easy.
  • Oversee safe and loving environments for babies through preschoolers.
  • Lead volunteers to run an engaging, high-energy elementary service.
  • Keep all spaces organized, prepared, and clean.
  • Model what it looks like to lead an engaging large group experience including leading games, the bible story, worship and response times for kids. 

Curriculum & Programming

  • Collaborate with central staff to execute curriculum with excellence.
  • Equip volunteers to teach confidently and connect with families.

Partnering with Parents

  • Resource, equip and come alongside parents to be the primary spiritual nurturers of their child’s faith. 
  • Equip volunteers to engage and encourage parent partnership. 
  • Strengthen the relationship between families and Sandals Church.

Campus Collaboration

  • Support campus-wide events, engagement, and discipleship.
  • Serve as a unified part of the campus staff team.
  • Support campus events and midweek needs by mobilizing volunteers.

We’re Looking for Someone Who

  • Loves building teams and empowering others.
  • Is teachable, organized, relational, and energetic.
  • Communicates clearly and works well with people.
  • Adapts quickly, stays positive, and leads through change.
  • Someone who is passionate about seeing kids being discipled and a heart for the next generation.
  • Disciple people through relationships and everyday interactions.

You’re a Great Fit If You

  • Can lead yourself spiritually, mentally and emotionally to become a better leader. 
  • Can give and receive feedback to grow as a leader. 
  • Are a leader of leaders who multiplies yourself through others.
  • Build strong relationships with both kids and adults.
  • Are responsible, agile, and passionate about serving families.

post_html:
Campus Staff Minister - PA/MD/DC/DE (Mid-Atlantic Region, Undergraduate Ministry)

Work Location:

Pennsylvania

Job Type:

Full time

God has called InterVarsity to plant and to build witnessing communities of students and faculty who follow Jesus on college and university campuses. Through these groups, we believe ever- increasing numbers of students and faculty from all ethnic groups and areas of the campus will be transformed by the Gospel. We expect to see campuses increasingly become places where people, ideas, and structures flourish to the glory of God. We confidently anticipate that our InterVarsity alumni will become change agents across the country and around the world. We pursue this calling by discerning and actively participating in what God is already doing on campus. This is the essence of being a Campus Staff Minister (CSM).

InterVarsity Christian Fellowship's Mid-Atlantic Region serves students on over 50 campuses in the District of Columbia, Maryland, Delaware, and the eastern half of Pennsylvania.

To learn more about our work in the Mid-Atlantic, you can access our website here: http://midatlantic.intervarsity.org/

ESSENTIAL COMMITMENTS/RESPONSIBILITIES 

Spiritual Growth 

You pursue maturity as a disciple of Jesus Christ so that your life and work increasingly reflects a growing love for God, God’s Word, God’s people of every ethnicity and culture, and God’s purposes in the world. To do this, you will: 

  • Pursue a vibrant relationship with the triune God through engagement with Scripture, prayer, and worship, both individually and in community 

  • Develop self-leadership (growing in self-awareness, self-management, relational integrity, and resiliency) 

  • Embrace Scriptural standards for behavior and attitudes 

 

Campus Leadership 

You communicate and model InterVarsity’s vision to see students and faculty transformed, campuses renewed and world changers developed 

  • Create a culture of humble dependence on God and bold expectation in God’s intention to start new witnessing communities throughout the campus and on new campuses 

  • Model – in person and through programs – InterVarsity’s vision and Core Values, including a biblically-defined commitment to engage every ethnic and social group on campus 

  • Lead students and faculty – individually and collectively – through Scripture, prayer, teaching, and discipleship experiences, so that they articulate and align their ministry activities around this vision 

  • Set annual goals through prayer, research and reflection with your teams (students, faculty, and staff) for qualitative and quantitative growth, including conversions and leadership development 

 

You create, develop, align and leverage ministry plans, programs, teams, and structures to close the gap between current reality and the aspirational goals. 

  • Build leadership teams who trust and partner well with you and who demonstrate spiritual vitality, relational health, and mission alignment 

  • Develop and execute plans to achieve annual goals, evaluating and modifying the plan as needed throughout the year 

  • Increase momentum for the vision by aligning programs, structures, conferences and teams around the goals 

  • Mobilize students and faculty to engage their relational networks with the gospel and to start new missional communities 

  • Under the direction of the Area Director, may supervise Ministry Interns and Campus Ministry Interns as delegated 

 

You intentionally gather, invite, and develop diverse groups of students and faculty so that they not only encounter and follow Jesus as Savior and Lord but also advance the mission on campus as participants and leaders. 

  • Create ways for faculty and students to encounter and follow Jesus through Scripture, worship, prayer, mission experiences, conferences, etc. 

  • Equip students and faculty so that they think strategically about campus engagement and so that they proclaim – in word, deed, and power – the good news of Jesus, regularly inviting students and faculty to follow him as Savior and Lord 

  • Disciple students and faculty by equipping them to hear the Word, respond actively, and debrief and interpret the experience so that they grow in Christlikeness, reflect our Core Values, and develop ministry skills 

  • Invite, coach, and equip students and faculty to become increasingly effective participants and leaders, including starting new witnessing communities on campuses 

 

Organizational Collaboration 

You work with a network of other local, area, regional, and national InterVarsity staff and volunteers so that our work reflects Biblical standards of excellence, integrity, and partnership. 

  • Partner with and respond positively to the direction and coaching of your supervisors and national leaders 

  • Contribute to collaborative and productive team meetings and relationships 

  • Affiliate chapters under your care and submit Graduating Student Forms in order to increase our partnership with current students and alumni 

  • Use national ministry resources and tools, as requested, including recruiting and/or participating in local, regional, or national conferences as  

  • Complete reporting, planning and review requirements in a timely way so that you and your supervisors can assess and improve your work as a CSM 

  • Comply with all InterVarsity policies and procedures 

 

Ministry Partnership Development 

You will develop a team of partners – churches and individuals (including alumni and community members) – who will resource the ministry financially, in prayer, or volunteer service that advances the mission. 

  • Raise 100% of the financial budget assigned by your supervisor 

  • Communicate regularly with your ministry partners, nurturing the relationship through visits, phone calls, emails and regular prayer letters 

  • Develop on-going, long-lasting partnership with alumni and volunteers 

  • Comply with all Ministry Partnership Policies 

  • Identify and invest in advocates who will build networks of volunteers and donors on InterVarsity’s behalf 

 

Accomplish all other assigned tasks as appropriate 

 

QUALIFICATIONS (common to all levels of CSM) 

  • Annually affirm InterVarsity’s Statement of Agreement (Doctrinal Basis and Purpose Statement). Abide by InterVarsity’s Code of Conduct. Believe and behave consonantly with InterVarsity’s Human Sexuality Theological Paper. Affirm and behave consonantly with InterVarsity’s “Women in Ministry Statement of Affirmation” 

  • Bachelor’s degree for CSMs assigned to a four-year campus. A minimum of an Associate’s degree for CSMs assigned to a two-year campus or a community college 

  • Strong interpersonal skills (including ability to minister to diverse ethnic communities and faculty) 

  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills 

  • Demonstrated problem solving skills 

  • Familiarity with word processing, presentation, email, and spreadsheet software 

 

WORK ENVIRONMENT/PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS 

The CSM position leads ministry in a college campus environment. A designated office space may or may not be available. The CSM is required to travel to on-campus and off- campus sites as appropriate. Off-campus travel includes, but is not limited to: student ministry conferences, Ministry Partnership Development meetings, and InterVarsity- sponsored training sessions, meetings, and conferences. The CSM is regularly required to communicate with others, and routinely uses standard office equipment such as computers, phones, photocopiers, filing cabinets, etc. 

Although this job is posted as a "Full Time" position, we are open to those seeking "Part Time" work as well.

Pay Range: $40,476.00 - $53,952.00 per year

Pay: This position is funded through personal fundraising. Accordingly, compensation will vary based on the ability of the individual to secure a donor team to fund the cost of his/her salary. The anticipated salary range for this position on a full-time basis (40 hours/week) is dependent on a variety of factors, including location and cost of living. The actual salary received, including any geographic adjustment to account for location and cost of living, is subject to the individual’s ability to raise funds necessary to cover the full amount of such salary within the range set forth in the job posting details.

Benefits:

We offer a competitive benefits package, including health care and retirement savings with a match. Eligibility is based on employee type and hours worked.  Benefits include the following:

  • 403(b) Retirement Savings Plan

  • 403(b) matching contributions

  • Dental insurance

  • Employee assistance program

  • Employee discounts

  • Flexible work schedule

  • Flexible spending accounts

  • Health insurance

  • Health savings account

  • Life insurance

  • Paid time off

  • Parental leave

  • Professional development assistance

  • Vision insurance

Equal Employment Opportunity: 

 

InterVarsity Christian Fellowship/USA is both an equal opportunity employer and a faith-based religious organization. We conduct hiring without regard to race, color, ancestry, national origin, citizenship, age, sex, marital status, parental status, membership in any labor organization, political ideology, or disability of an otherwise qualified individual. The status of InterVarsity Christian Fellowship/USA as an equal opportunity employer does not prevent the organization from hiring staff based on their religious beliefs so that all staff share the same religious commitment.  Pursuant to the Civil Rights Act of 1964, Section 702 (42 U.S.C. 2000e 1(a)) InterVarsity Christian Fellowship/USA has the right to, and does, hire only candidates who agree with InterVarsity’s Statement of Agreement: Purpose and Doctrinal Basis because InterVarsity believes that each and every staff plays a vital role in advancing InterVarsity’s mission and purposes.

post_html:
Reports to: East York Campus Pastor 
Direct Consultant: Director of Worship Leaders  
Hours Commitment: Full-time (40-45 hours per week) with regular weekend responsibilities. 
 
Objective: To lead the East York campus to increasing effectiveness at introducing more and more people to Jesus and helping them to fully follow him.

Personal Qualifications:

  • Have a personal relationship with Jesus and demonstrate ongoing spiritual growth through everyday habits and practices. 
  • Support LCBC’s mission to introduce people to Jesus and together fully follow him, along with our ministry philosophy, priorities, and beliefs.
  • Be a leader who is:
    • Focused: Work hard with urgency and intensity
    • Collaborative: Bring others into your work, give and ask for feedback
    • Growth-minded: Plan for growth and be ready for when God wants to move by pursuing personal, spiritual, and professional development
  • Lead the way in LCBC’s values: We run after the one, we pursue excellence, we prioritize relationships, we deploy people for impact, and we are real and relatable.
  • Be an LCBC Partner, or willing to become one within 60 days of employment. Regularly attend and participate at LCBC prior to and/or upon employment.

Primary Responsibilities:

  • Commit to leading worship 46-48 weekends per year. 
  • Carry out the weekend plan on location with excellence, passion, and authenticity. 
  • Recruit, train and pastor a community of musicians and artists, who are gifted, prepared, connected, healthy and growing. 
  • Schedule volunteers with consistency and timeliness using Planning Center Online. 
  • Take initiative to stay up-to-date on all centrally planning elements for weekend gatherings and special events. 
  • Provide weekly communication to volunteers about weekend gathering information and programming details. 
  • Intentionally connect with all volunteers on your team at least 3 times a year (1 of the connections will identify goals for growth). 
  • Assist Worship Department in cultivating a worship culture that is God honoring, engaging, and accessible to those who are far from God, as well as challenging and encouraging to those who are Christ followers. 
  • Contribute creatively to the Worship Department in the following ways, but not limited to: 
    • Song Development and Research 
    • Creative Elements and moments for weekend gatherings 
    • Special gathering elements (Christmas, Easter, Campaign, etc.) 
    • Best practices and team management ideas 
    • Songwriting
  • Attend and contribute to Worship Department meetings and projects which include, but are not limited to:
    • Weekly Worship Department meetings
    • Regional Team meetings
    • Worship Department Bible Study
    • Music Recordings
    • Nights of Worship
    • DEVELUP Program
    • Outdoor Worship Nights 

Required Skills:

  • The Worship Leader’s primary role is to serve the greater vision of LCBC Church (introducing people to Jesus and together fully following him). 
  • Be a team player: participate in staff meetings and location-specific events/initiatives such as Growth Track classes, conferences, outdoor worship nights, etc. 
  • Pastoral ability: participate in pastoral care by serving on the PRT (Pastoral Response Team) rotation, and provide music and programming for weddings and funerals. 
  • Ability to lead and participate in “All-Church” functions and events such as: All Staff Huddles, All Staff Meetings, LCBC U, Capital Campaigns, Conferences, etc. 

Benefits We Offer:

  • Competitive medical, dental and vision coverage
  • Retirement plan contribution and employer match
  • Annual counseling benefit
  • Flexible schedules
  • Generous and immediate paid time-off
  • Casual dress
  • Quarterly professional and spiritual development days
  • Intentional investment in personal and professional development
Evaluation: 
The East York Worship Leader will meet regularly with the East York Campus Pastor for planning, goal-setting, progress updates, and general coaching. A formal Action and Development Plan will be completed and reviewed three times throughout the year.

The Minister of Outreach provides leadership and direction for Cornerstone Baptist Church’s efforts to reach people beyond the church, serve the surrounding community, and help individuals take meaningful steps toward Christ and connection with the church.

Job Description

Protestant Musician Worship Leader

Location: Altus Air Force Base Chapel, Building 301, Altus AFB, Oklahoma
Employment Type: Full-Time

Position Overview

Viakorp Corporation is seeking an experienced and motivated Protestant Worship Leader to provide worship leadership services for the Protestant congregation at Altus Air Force Base Chapel. The selected individual will lead contemporary and blended worship services, coordinate weekly rehearsals, recruit and mentor volunteer musicians, and work closely with the Designated Chaplain to support the chapel's Protestant ministry program.

This position requires a mature Christian leader with excellent musical ability, strong leadership skills, and the ability to foster a welcoming worship environment within a multi-denominational military chapel.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities

  • Lead weekly Protestant worship services through vocal and instrumental music.
  • Conduct weekly rehearsals with the Worship Team.
  • Recruit, organize, and maintain volunteer musicians and vocalists.
  • Coordinate worship themes, song selections, and special music with the Designated Chaplain.
  • Prepare presentation slides and song lyrics for each worship service.
  • Maintain a balanced repertoire of traditional hymns and contemporary worship music.
  • Provide musical leadership for special services including funerals, memorial services, Good Friday, Christmas Eve, and other chapel events as requested.
  • Arrive at least 30 minutes before rehearsals and worship services to prepare equipment and coordinate with chapel staff.
  • Set up and restore the stage, sound equipment, microphones, music stands, and other worship equipment before and after services.
  • Maintain professional conduct while working with military personnel, volunteers, and chapel staff.
  • Ensure chapel facilities and equipment are secured and left in clean, orderly condition following each event.
  • Coordinate qualified substitute worship leaders when unavailable, subject to Chaplain approval.

Minimum Qualifications

Applicants must:

  • Be at least 21 years of age.
  • Have a minimum of three (3) years of experience within the last eight (8) years serving as a Protestant Worship Leader and Musician.
  • Demonstrate the ability to lead worship vocally and instrumentally.
  • Be proficient on at least one lead instrument (guitar, piano, or keyboard).
  • Be able to read musical notation or provide musical charts when performing by ear.
  • Possess knowledge of contemporary, traditional, multicultural, and multi-denominational Protestant worship music.
  • Demonstrate strong vocal harmony and worship leadership skills.
  • Be proficient with Microsoft PowerPoint, Proclaim, or similar worship presentation software.
  • Possess excellent interpersonal, organizational, and communication skills.
  • Maintain active membership or regular attendance at a Protestant church and provide a pastoral endorsement letter.
  • Successfully complete all installation access requirements and any required background investigations.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience leading military chapel worship services.
  • Experience directing volunteer worship teams.
  • Familiarity with chapel audio systems and worship technology.
  • Experience working within diverse Protestant faith traditions.

Church Profile

1. Vision, Mission and Values

Queens Christian Alliance Church (QCAC) is a multi-cultural, multi-generational church located in the heart of Flushing, Queens. Queens is one of the most diverse urban places on earth, giving the church a unique representation of a future church in heaven.

The church describes its mission through four key actions:

* Believe: Following Christ in salvation.

* Belong: Building a supportive community of believers.

* Become: Transforming in Christ by sanctification.

* Bless: Blessing others with the blessings we received. Witnessing in Jerusalem, Judea, Samaria and to the ends of the earth

2. Demographics of Congregation

QCAC consists of three congregations. The English congregation is the main congregation. The demographic of the English is well mixed, but being in Flushing, it leans more Asian. The Spanish and Mandarin congregation consists of immigrants. Across the three congregations, life stages are continuous: young babies, students, young adults, and lower to middle working class families.

3. Staff and Lay Leadership Profile

· Lead pastor (David Smith) English pastor and oversees whole church

· Executive pastor (Julia Wong) works closely with the Lead pastor on English congregation ministries. She works on whole church spiritual issues with the lead pastor

· Spanish congregation pastor (Pastor Edgardo Ghidella)

· Mandarin congregation pastor (Pastor Grace Cui)

· Youth pastor (English language, for teens across all three congregation)

· Governing Board- (6 members both Male and Female) representatives from each congregation whose responsibilities include, administrative, property, and financial aspects.

· Elder Board- (5 members) responsible as spiritual leaders and shepherds for the entire church.

4. Programs and Ministries

English, Spanish and Mandarin services meet each Sunday. In addition other ministries include: Worship Teams, Meet and Greet, Teen Team, Wee Worship, Radiant Youth, Young Adults, Home Groups, Women's Fellowship, Friday Youth Events, Prayer Meetings, ESL (English Second Language classes), and others.

5. Missions- is currently managed by our executive pastor. Yearly we have missionary speakers who serve through the Alliance, come and share what the Lord is doing and how we can walk along with them. There are those who have gone out from our church who are currently serving in the mission fields. We also, as a church, collect offerings given to the mission fields. These funds to the “Missions” account are set in accordance with a predetermined allocation, whether Great Commission, local or outreach.

6. Areas of Opportunity- The church is based in Flushing, Queens. Being in a densely populated region in the heart of Flushing, the opportunities are very great for outreach and evangelism. Flushing Queens is a mix of up to 70% Asians, 20% Hispanic / Latino, 10% White and 4% Black / African American. Flushing has a diverse population and cultural mix made up of 71% foreign-born peoples. In addition Queens is one of the most ethnically diverse urban areas in the world. We have a population of 2.32million, over 138 languages and 100 nations represented in Queens. There is a great opportunity for evangelism, outreach and ministry.

7. Financial Profile- Our operating budget is around $500,000

8. Facility- Our building is located in downtown Flushing. It is a bustling city with many businesses and new developments. It is one train stop away from Flushing Meadows park, Citi Field Stadium, the US Open and many new developments. LaGuardia Airport is a 6 minute drive.

We have fully completed the payment of our mortgage in 2025. The building is 29,700 square feet. As the tax assessor’s market value is $9.6 million, we have been offered $22 million. A few parties rent out certain areas of the building. The church owns a 2 bedroom parsonage in College Point. There are challenges with building maintenance as well as

challenges with code compliance with the City of New York. We have a building team that looks after general maintenance.

9. Church History- QCAC was founded in 1982 by Daniel Ho and 15 teens in College Point, Queens. We moved to Flushing in 1998. Joe Desantis was senior pastor 2008-2011. Peter Pendell was interim senior pastor 2011- 2014. David Smith became our senior pastor (now lead pastor) 2014- present.

Pastor Profile

Queens Christian Alliance Church is seeking a lead pastor for our multicultural church and shepherd of its English-speaking congregation.

In accordance with 1 Timothy 3:1-7, Titus 1:6-9, and 1 Peter 5:1-3, the lead pastor must embody the specific biblical qualifications and character traits outlined for church leadership.

The responsibilities of the lead pastor are:

· Preach in the English congregation

· Shepherd the flock in QCAC

· Growing the church body with discipleship and evangelism

· Lead church staff

· Executive Pastor

· Spanish Pastor

· Mandarin Pastor

· Youth Pastor

· Church administrator

· Building and grounds Maintenance

· Lead Elder board

· Lead Governing board

· Oversee Building Team

Base Cash Salary: $60,000- $70,000

Total Compensation Package Equivalent: $95,000- $115,000, including on site parsonage housing and health insurance

To be considered for this position, please complete the application to include your testimony, resume and other background information related to the position.

If the district office has reviewed your application and they think you may be a potential match for the position, that the hiring manager will reach out to you for next steps.

This position requires licensing with The Christian & Missionary Alliance. To learn more about The Alliance and requirements for licensing, please visit our website

Please do not contact the church directly.

SUMMARY

This position serves on the One Church Worship team and provides leadership and direction for Production Ministry across all Pinelake campuses. The Lead Production Director is responsible for developing a clear and unified philosophy for live production, leading and developing Production staff, and building systems and structures that help our teams thrive.

This role will lead the One Church Production team, work closely with Campus Production Directors, and provide oversight for production across weekend services, One Church events, and other ministry initiatives. The goal is to build a healthy, unified, and multiplying Production Ministry that is marked by discipleship and development culture. Where staff and servant leaders are equipped to lead, campuses are well supported, and everything we do serves the mission and vision of Pinelake.

GENERAL RESPONSIBILITIES

Learn

  • Pursue a growing relationship with Jesus through consistent time in God’s Word and prayer
  • Continually grow in your understanding of the Jesus-Centered Life (salvation, identity, life, and authority in Christ).
  • Remain teachable and hungry, seeking feedback, learning from others, and developing both spiritually and professionally.
  • Cultivate awareness of God’s presence in everyday life, listening to the Holy Spirit and responding in obedience.

Live

  • Practice and model the rhythms of Be the Church (Grow, Pray, Connect, and Share).
  • Pursue emotional health by engaging in self-awareness, addressing past wounds, and cultivating honest, healthy relationships.
  • Practice healthy rhythms, prioritizing your relationship with Jesus and your family
  • Embody a life of integrity and surrender, allowing your private life with God to shape your work.

Lead

  • Take ownership of disciple-making by supporting and strengthening environments where people can take their next step toward a Jesus-Centered Life.
  • Leverage your role, systems, and responsibilities to remove barriers and create clarity, helping both staff and the church move forward in the Discipleship Pathway (Essentials → JCL → Be the Church).
  • Contribute to life-change by bringing your skills, organization, and follow-through to your work, knowing that what you build and manage helps others lead and shepherd more effectively.
  • Build people through your influence—encouraging, supporting, and serving teammates and Servant Leaders in ways that help them grow and thrive.
  • Measure success not only by task completion, but by how your work contributes to disciples being formed and multiplied across the church.

Embrace the Culture

  • Value and embody the staff values, which we call the 7 H’s: Humility, Honor, Honesty, Hunger, Holy Spirit, Health, and Harmony
  • Communicate clearly, honestly, and proactively in a way that builds trust, unity, and momentum.
  • Work in alignment with the church vision and leadership
  • Participate fully in the life of your campus or team, contributing to the unity, health, and shepherding of the faith family.
