Job Title: Creative Arts and Worship Coordinator

FLSA Status: Full Time - Exempt
Reports to: Center Director

Schedule: 40 hours exempt, hours vary depending on program needs, including weekends and on-call hours


Supervises: N/A

Rate of Pay: $55,000-$62,400 annually 

Closing Date: 11/2/2026

Benefits: Standard; Full-Time, Exempt employees are eligible for but not limited to the following:

  • Health, vision, dental, life as well as voluntary life and disability insurance
  • Sick leave benefit – 1 day per month, 12 sick days per year (accrual and availability begins at hire)
  • Vacation benefit – 20 vacation days per year, accrued at the rate of .0769 hours for each hour worked (accrual begins at hire but may not be used until the completion of six months of employment)
  • One floating day off for use (accrued immediately, and again annually, but may not be used until the completion of the initial three-month introductory period of employment)
  • Pension Plan (after one year of continuous service)
  • Voluntary Tax-Deferred Annuity Plan (403(b)plan)

 

Position Summary

The Creative Arts and Worship Coordinator position is a combined ministry role integrating music and creative arts education with worship leadership. This role collaborates with the Christian Education Coordinator to provide group music lessons and creative arts during after-school programs and summer day camps, as well as group and individual instruction to children and youth who express interest in developing their musical skills. This coordinator will also provide group music and creative arts lessons to seniors and adults with special needs and/or disabilities in coordination with community center staff. Additionally, the role assists Corps Officer(s) in planning and leading musical worship for church services on Sundays, ensuring that music supports and enhances the spiritual life of the congregation. The position requires a passion for teaching, strong musical ability, and a commitment to fostering both artistic and spiritual growth within the community.

 

Duties and Responsibilities

Creative Arts Coordinator

  • Develop and lead/facilitate structured group music and creative arts education for youth in the after-school program, including piano/keyboard, guitar, brass, voice, dance, drama, music theory, sheet music reading, and other creative disciplines, adapting instruction to varying skill levels and learning styles.
  • Plan and lead/facilitate a consistent group music and creative arts classes for youth, providing progressive instruction, skill development, and opportunities for performance and participation in Corps ministries including at least one evening offering.
  • Develop and lead/facilitate group creative arts classes for seniors and adults with disabilities and/or special needs including a dedicated evening class for adults with disabilities and/or special needs, adapting instruction to participant abilities and interests.
  • Responsible for one dedicated music and creative arts week during Summer Day Camp.
  • Prepare and chaperone students and participants for recitals, Corps and community performances, and divisional or territorial competitions, coordinating fundraising, travel, additional chaperones, and supervision as needed.
  • Organize concerts and creative arts presentations at the Corps and community locations, including nursing homes, community events, and Sunday worship.
  • Recruit, train, mentor, and coordinate volunteers to expand creative arts programming, support group instruction, and maintain appropriate youth-to-adult ratios and child safety standards.
  • Build positive relationships with participants through teaching, mentorship, and encouragement, creating a welcoming, inclusive, and safe learning environment attentive to the needs of the Whittier community.
  • Steward instruments, creative arts equipment, and related AV resources, maintaining inventories and ensuring equipment is properly cared for and available for instruction and performances.
  • Promote creative arts programs through community outreach, events, and social media, and evaluate program effectiveness through appropriate reporting and ongoing improvement.

 

Worship Coordinator

  • Plan and lead/facilitate Christ-centered worship during Sunday services alongside the worship team through music, prayer, Scripture, and creative elements that support the message and encourage congregational participation.
  • Lead worship vocally and/or instrumentally, including guitar or piano, with consistency and excellence.
  • Incorporate creative elements such as choirs, drama, movement, responsive readings, special music, and other expressions of worship.
  • Recruit, train, mentor, and provide pastoral encouragement to worship team members and volunteers, promoting spiritual growth, teamwork, and ministry excellence.
  • Coordinate worship for special events and seasonal services, including Christmas, Easter, VBS, plays, special music, dances, and other Corps ministry events.
  • Ensure sound, projection, and other AV needs are effectively coordinated for Sunday worship, special services, and performances.
  • Manage worship ministry resources and budget responsibly and actively participate in Sunday and holiday worship at Denver Red Shield, serving in additional worship and ministry settings as needed.

 

Shared Ministry Responsibilities

  • Design and lead programming from an intentionally Christ-centered perspective, incorporating prayer, Scripture, devotions, chapel, discipleship, and other spiritually formative practices.
  • Model a Christ-centered life and encourage participants, volunteers, and congregation members toward spiritual growth and connection with all Corps ministries, including worship, youth group, Bible studies, and other discipleship opportunities.
  • Attend weekly staff meetings, complete required child safety and mandatory reporter training, follow Salvation Army policies and procedures, and support Corps and seasonal ministries, including Angel Tree and Christmas Red Kettles, as needed.

Education/Experience, Skills, Qualities, Requirements

Education/Experience

  • Active commitment to growing in the theology of biblical worship.
  • Bachelor’s degree in music education, performance, worship arts, ministry, or a related field (or equivalent ministry experience).
  • Experience teaching music to children and youth in a school or structured setting.
  • Proven experience leading worship vocally and instrumentally (guitar or piano) in a church or ministry context.
  • Strong vocal and instrumental proficiency, with exceptional musical skills.
  • Demonstrated ability in team building, leadership, and fostering spiritual growth through prayer and discipleship.
  • Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with enthusiasm for working with children and youth.
  • Availability for evenings, weekends, and holidays as required.
  • Commitment to continuous learning and creativity in worship planning and execution.

 

Skills

  • Ability to use a computer, email, and new software programs with basic training.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite.
  • Must be a self-starter and a team player, perform well with minimum supervision.
  • Bilingual English and Spanish, preferred.
  • Current First Aid/CPR/AED certification or ability to obtain within 90 days of employment.

 

Qualities

  • Supportive of The Salvation Army’s mission
  • Able to reflect and model the high standards of our organization.
  • A person of genuine Christian character.
  • A team player willing to support other center coordinators and programs.
  • Ability to participate in conflict resolution, de-escalation practices, and respectful communication.

 

Requirements

  • Driving

Driving is required for this position:

  • The employee must be 21 years old at a minimum (for insurance provision) and possess a valid in-state driver’s license
  • An MVR will be processed every year in accordance with The Salvation Army’s policies
  • Background Check
    • Continued employment will be contingent upon a biennial (every two years) background check that is processed in accordance with The Salvation Army’s policies.
    • In addition, able to obtain and maintain a "Cleared" status in the Colorado Provider Hub. This requires passing a federal/state fingerprint background check and a TRAILS child abuse registry check.
  • Physical
    • Ability to maneuver, to remain in a stationary position, to grasp, push, pull, and reach overhead, to lift 50 pounds, to access and produce information from the computer, to operate a telephone, to understand written information
    • Qualified individuals must be able to perform the essential duties of the position with or without accommodation. A request to modify or adjust these requirements may be made to your supervisor and HR. The Salvation Army would attempt to satisfy requests if the accommodation needed is reasonable and presents no undue hardship.
company_description: Battling to provide social services, The Salvation Army is more than 4 million strong -- including some 3.4 million registered volunteers. Its Christian faith-based programs assist alcoholics, drug addicts, the homeless, the elderly, prison inmates, people in crisis, and the unemployed through offerings such as community centers, housing facilities, and rehabilitation centers. The organization also provides disaster-relief services and operates some 1,400 thrift stores. Overall, it serves about 30 million people a year and provides in excess of 64 million meals. The US organization is a unit of the London-based Salvation Army, which oversees activities in more than 100 countries. US operations began in 1880.

Job Title: Associate Campus Pastor (Dickinson)

Department:
Dickinson Campus 

Reports To:
Dickinson Campus Pastor 

Work Schedule: Full-Time≥


JOB DESCRIPTION

Evangel exists to CONNECT REAL PEOPLE TO A REAL GOD! We are one church in multiple locations including campuses in Bismarck, Dickinson, Online and more to come! The church is about one person, Jesus, but it is composed of many different kinds of people and we are always looking for quality people to join the team.


Position Summary

The Associate Campus Pastor will assist in providing leadership to carry out Evangel’s vision for the Evangel Dickinson Campus alongside the Campus Pastor. This individual will focus on pastoral ministry, discipleship, and connection while assisting in helping people take next steps in their faith journey. This role will provide pastoral care to attenders, facilitate ministry environments, and assist in creating intentional connection points for the Dickinson Campus.


Essential Characteristics

This individual should possess Christ-like character. This individual should be guided by the Holy Spirit, should be a leader of leaders, relationally-driven, team-oriented, and highly self-motivated. This position calls for someone who can organize and motivate teams, has a heart for pastoral ministry and discipleship, and is able to communicate in a way that inspires others to join the vision.


Key Areas of Responsibility and Ownership

  • Provide pastoral presence on Sundays, key weekends, and campus events. Serve as the primary service host alongside the Dickinson Campus Pastor, a secondary speaker throughout the year, and assist in facilitating periodic  ministry moments. (ex. Prayer Services, Next Step Opportunities) 
  • Assist with pastoral counsel, care, and ministry to Dickinson Campus attenders and community (i.e., weddings, funerals, care meetings, pastor-on-call duties, child dedications, baptisms, hospital visits, etc.). Serve as the primary driver of team connection/check-ins.
  • Assist Campus Pastor by coordinating men’s events and Connect Groups for the Dickinson Campus. 
  • Own the follow-up process for new serve team members providing accountability, helping onboard new team members, and facilitating necessary follow-up conversations.
  • Oversee prayer teams by raising up, training, scheduling, and leading Prayer Team members for weekend and special services.
  • Assist in the ideation and implementation of City Reach (outreach events) at the Dickinson Campus, translating opportunities from Bismarck while identifying outreach opportunities unique to Dickinson.
  • Provide availability to assist in overseeing Next Gen ministries on occasion 


Qualifications

  • Thinks strategically about the church as a whole
  • Able to execute overall church vision to campus
  • Able to steward opportunities, resources, talent and budget
  • Able to communicate and collaborate effectively across the organization
  • Ability to manage direct reports effectively
  • Strong verbal and written communication skills to a variety of audiences
  • Professionalism and poise when interacting with external contacts
  • Excellent time management skills
  • Strong people skills
  • Pastoral Degree, certification, or experience
  • Highly skilled in the use of Google Workspace 



Church Values

FAMILY FOCUSED - give high priority to our families and marriages

INSIDE OUT - healthy life overflowing from a healthy heart

BRING OUR BEST - make the most of every opportunity

LIVE TO GIVE - be a contributor not a consumer

FUTURE MINDED - honoring the past while pursuing the future


Staff Values

Glorify God and Honor People

Under Promise and Over Deliver

Title: Campus Pastor
Campus: Mesa
Reports To: Campus Team Executive Pastor
Status: Full-Time 

Position Summary 
Central Christian Church is seeking a relationally driven, influential, and passionate leader who loves Jesus, loves people, and thrives on building healthy teams and vibrant communities. 

The Campus Pastor provides spiritual and organizational leadership for the Mesa campus, creating an environment where people feel welcomed, valued, connected, and inspired to take meaningful next steps in their faith. 

The ideal candidate is an engaging communicator, intentional relationship builder, and developer of leaders who inspires others through encouragement, collaboration, and personal example. This individual combines a shepherd's heart with a leader's mindset—leading with humility and empathy while confidently providing direction, making decisions, holding others accountable, and driving ministry results. 

The Campus Pastor champions Central's mission to lead people to discover and fully own their faith in Jesus while modeling our churchwide values and staff leadership culture. 

Key Responsibilities 
Campus Leadership & Culture 
  • Champion Central's mission, vision, values, and leadership culture across the campus. 
  • Provide visible, approachable, and authentic spiritual leadership for staff, volunteers, and congregants. 
  • Lead campus priorities, establish measurable goals, and take ownership of ministry effectiveness and campus health. 
  • Collaborate with Central Support teams to execute churchwide strategies and continuously improve ministry. 
Staff & Volunteer Leadership 
  • Lead, coach, develop, and pastorally care for campus staff and key volunteer leaders. 
  • Build healthy, collaborative teams characterized by trust, clear expectations, encouragement, and accountability. 
  • Identify and equip emerging leaders, empowering others to take ownership and lead ministry. 
  • Establish consistent team meetings, one-on-ones, performance feedback, and leadership development opportunities. 
Community & Ministry Engagement 
  • Build meaningful relationships with attendees, volunteers, Campus Council members, and community leaders. 
  • Champion engagement in serving and groups, helping people move from weekend attendance into authentic community. 
  • Partner with ministry leaders to strengthen guest experiences, first-time visitor follow-up, and next steps. 
  • Provide pastoral care, prayer, benevolence support, and officiate weddings and funerals as needed. 
Campus Operations & Execution 
  • Oversee excellent execution of weekend services, campus events, and ministry initiatives. 
  • Regularly host weekend services and communicate with warmth, enthusiasm, and clarity. 
  • Ensure campus facilities, processes, and ministry environments reflect a high standard of excellence. 
  • Identify opportunities, solve problems proactively, and ensure consistent follow-through on campus priorities. 
Leadership Competencies 
  • Relational & Influential: Naturally connects with people, builds trust, and inspires others through authentic relationships, empathy, and encouragement. 
  • Collaborative & Humble: Leads with a servant's heart, values others' perspectives, and creates unity around shared goals. 
  • Developer of People: Passionate about coaching, mentoring, and empowering others to grow and lead. 
  • Self-Motivated & Action-Oriented: Recognizes opportunities, takes initiative, and moves ideas into action without waiting for direction. 
  • Engaging Communicator: Communicates vision with clarity, enthusiasm, optimism, and the ability to influence diverse audiences. 
  • Dependable & Results-Driven: Establishes clear priorities, follows through on commitments, and holds themselves and others accountable. 
  • Emotionally Mature & Adaptable: Remains steady through challenges, welcomes feedback, and navigates difficult conversations with compassion and confidence. 
Qualifications & Experience 
  • A growing relationship with Jesus Christ and alignment with Central Christian Church's mission, beliefs, and values. 
  • Bachelor's degree or equivalent experience; three or more years of related ministry experience preferred. 
  • Demonstrated experience leading, coaching, and developing staff or volunteer leaders. 
  • Strong interpersonal, communication, organizational, and decision-making skills. 
  • Ability to translate vision into actionable plans and measurable ministry outcomes. 
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications and the ability to effectively use Rock RMS. 
Personal & Spiritual Expectations 
  • Model biblical integrity and maintain a growing personal relationship with Jesus Christ. 
  • Be an active Owner of Central Christian Church and financially support its vision through tithing. 
  • Uphold Central's staff leadership culture: Jesus First, Same Team, Make It Better, Feedback Matters, Give It Away, and Healthy Hustle. 
  • Demonstrate humility, personal accountability, and a commitment to continued spiritual and leadership growth. 
  • Adhere to and encompass the qualities and characteristics required of Central Christian Church employees, defined by the Employee Handbook
Physical Requirements:  
While performing the duties of this job, the employee is occasionally required to stand, walk, sit; use hands to finger handle, or feel objects, tools or controls; reach with hands and arms; climb stairs; balance; stoop, kneel, crouch or crawl; talk or hear; The employee must occasionally lift, carry, push, and pull objects up to twenty-five pounds. Specific vision abilities required by the job include close vision, distance vision, color vision, peripheral vision, depth perception, and the ability to adjust focus.



At Central, we are blessed to have an extraordinary team of people pursuing our goal of leading people to discover and fully own faith in Jesus. We value each individual and strive to maintain a work environment based on our staff values - Jesus First, Same Team, Make it Better, Give it Away, Feedback Matters, and Healthy Hustle.

About Houston Christian University

At Houston Christian University, our Christian liberal arts, professional, and graduate programs have equipped students to lead, collaborate, and discover out of a deep sense of purpose for more than 60 years. We are driven forward by our central confession, “Jesus Christ is Lord,” and defined by our “Ten Pillars” core convictions. From this foundation we guide students confidently into discerning discovery, preparing them to think biblically, critically, and holistically about how to engage the world. We aspire to care for every student by meeting their academic, spiritual, and social needs with mentorship and support. At HCU, we are cultivating a culture of excellence that will mold a new generation of leaders in their communities, standard-setters in their professions, and fruitful disciples in their churches.

HCU is set in the heart of one of the most diverse and fastest-growing cities in the nation—and our growth and diversity match the dynamism of the city we call home. We continue to break records with our incoming freshmen class sizes, our graduate programs have more than doubled in the past decade, and we are significantly expanding our online programs as well.

Houston Theological Seminary & The School of Christian Thought

The School of Christian Thought at Houston Christian University is growing in size and the number of program offerings. We have embraced distance education while maintaining residential programs. We now have students across the globe pursuing their bachelor’s, master’s, and Doctor of Ministry (DMin) degrees

A central part of the School of Christian Thought is Houston Theological Seminary (HTS), which encompasses all graduate programs in our college. HTS is an evangelical seminary, strongly committed to Christian orthodoxy, with an important Baptist heritage. Our students and faculty represent a variety of Christian traditions and perspectives bound together by our shared commitment to Jesus’ Lordship and affirmation of HCU’s preamble and 10 Pillars. We are supported by the Baptist General Convention of Texas (BGCT). The Doctor of Ministry program is supported by the generous Cole Scholarship fund.

The newest seminary offering is our doctoral program – the DMin – which offers two tracks: New Testament and Faith & Culture. Launched five years ago, the DMin has over 50 doctoral students and an excellent roster of affiliated faculty and project supervisors. As the program continues to grow, additional tracks will be added.

Incoming faculty will join a warm community of scholars with active research projects. Community life in the school centers around our fortnightly research seminar with faculty, students, and guest speakers joining in-person and virtually. We also host weekly prayer gatherings and meals with students.

Position Summary:

We are seeking a full-time faculty member who will lead our Doctor of Ministry program. The faculty member will have leadership and ministry experience, be dedicated to training others for service in ministry, and have expertise and a terminal degree in one of the following areas:

  • Practical Theology
  • Biblical Studies
  • Cultural Apologetics

Job Responsibilities:

  • Provide vision and leadership for the Doctor of Ministry program
  • Promote the doctoral program and effectively recruit new DMin students
  • Oversee the operation of the Doctor of Ministry, including planning for the 1-week intensives each semester and managing supervisory assignments
  • Be a point of contact for prospective students interested in Doctor of Ministry
  • Provide mentorship and advising for current doctoral students
  • Advance the Doctor of Ministry program through church partnerships, adjunct recruitment, and other proactive initiatives
  • Lead program accreditation maintenance and renewal
  • Work with the chair of the Department of Theology
  • In conjunction with the Dean’s office, oversee the DMin budget, including the awarding of the Cole Scholarship.
  • Teach the equivalent of a 4-4 load, with a 2-2 course reduction for administrative duties.

The successful candidate will:

  • Provide excellent teaching to School of Christian Thought students in a variety of delivery formats;
  • Actively integrate the Christian faith in teaching;
  • Actively engage in scholarly work in their related discipline;
  • Participate in various service activities to the School, University, and community; and,
  • Maintain an active Christian faith and church participation.

Qualifications:

  • Candidates should have an earned PhD or DMin in a related field;
  • Professional experience within the candidate’s discipline or in a related field will be an advantage; and
  • Substantial experience in organizational leadership and ministry.
  • Candidates must affirm HCU’s statement of faith encompassed in the university preamble and Ten Pillars. This commitment must be reaffirmed annually.
  • HCU seeks candidates with an active Christian faith who are willing to integrate faith and learning in the classroom. The candidate must be able to document an excellent teaching record and provide evidence of scholarly interests and achievements.

Timeline:

The ideal candidate will be able to take up the role in January of 2027. If a suitable candidate is unavailable for a January start, candidates who can begin on August 1st of 2027 will be considered. Review of applications will begin on September 15th. The position will remain open until filled.

Application Process:

Interested candidates should begin by submitting a letter of interest, which addresses the job requirements and agreement with the university’s faith statements, as well as a CV that includes contact information for three professional references. References will not be contacted without the candidate’s permission. The letter of interest and CV should be emailed to sctdean@hc.edu with the subject line “DMin Director Search.”

Additional Information:

Houston Christian University is an independent, private Christian liberal arts university dedicated to the development of moral character, the enrichment of spiritual lives, and perpetuation of growth in Christian ideals. HCU is accredited by the Southern Association of Colleges and Schools Commission on Colleges (SACSCOC).

Houston Christian University is committed to maintaining a teaching faculty and staff who share an active Christian faith. The Preamble to the By-Laws of the University and the Ten Pillars set forth a statement of belief which each University employee is expected to support and personify as an essential function of their employment at the University. Your submittal of an application for employment indicates your acceptance and affirmation of these statements.

As one of the most diverse universities in the nation, Houston Christian University also strives to build a faculty and staff team that will increasingly provide role models who embody biblical orthodoxy and ethics for our students, whatever their background or life experience.

As with all open positions at the University, a contract or employment offer will only be extended when there is confirmed budget availability for the year in which the qualified candidate’s employment would begin.

**Disclaimer**

Background checks are performed for every new hire. If your application is selected to continue in our hiring process, you will be required to submit a background check form authorizing this screening. If you decline, your application may be denied. By proceeding with the online application, you understand and accept this process.

post_html:
The Coordinator for Native American Ministry works on the implementation of the 2024 USCCB’s Pastoral Framework for Indigenous Ministry: Keeping Christ’s Sacred Promise and serves as a pastoral leader and cultural liaison between both Catholic Dioceses of Oklahoma and Native American communities across the state. This role promotes spiritual growth, cultural understanding, and mutual respect by supporting Native American Catholics in their faith journey and encouraging the integration of Indigenous traditions within the life of the Church.  

The Coordinator provides pastoral care and spiritual support to Native American individuals and communities through active collaboration with parishes, apostolic movements, and diocesan leadership. This role is responsible for planning, organizing, and facilitating culturally relevant liturgies, retreats, and faith formation programs that honor both Catholic teachings and Native traditions.

By fostering meaningful relationships and open dialogue, the Coordinator helps strengthen connections between the Church and Native communities while advancing inclusive ministry efforts. Please include your specific ministry experiences in your cover letter. This position is based out of the Catholic Pastoral Center in Oklahoma City. 

Requirements

Minimum of three (3) years of pastoral ministry experience

Demonstrated knowledge of Native American cultures and traditions

Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications

Ability to be flexible, adaptable, and responsive to community needs

Must be an active, practicing Catholic in good standing

Position Posting: Church Partnerships Manager 
Location: Approved Remote Location 
Type of Role: Full-time OR Part-time; 100% Support-raised  
Date: June 2026 
 
About TEAM: The Evangelical Alliance Mission is a global mission agency that partners with the global church to send disciples that make disciples and establish missional churches to the glory of God. We envision the church transforming our world. 
 
Founded in 1890, TEAM workers serve in a variety of ministry roles including evangelism, church planting, community development, healthcare, education, social justice, missional business, and many other areas of global ministry. TEAM is both an equal opportunity employer and a faith-based religious organization. For this reason, TEAM hires only candidates who wholeheartedly and without reservation agree with and live according to  TEAM’s Statement of Faith. TEAM staff thoroughly embrace the purpose, vision, beliefs, and values of TEAM. 
 
About the Role:  The Church Partnerships Manager leads TEAM’s efforts to cultivate and strengthen strategic relationships with local churches across the United States to advance God’s mission among the nations. This role exists to help churches more fully embrace their calling as sending communities—providing meaningful value, trusted partnership, and clear pathways for global engagement. 
 
This leader will champion a vision that TEAM is built for the Church—serving as a bridge between the local church and the global Church through healthy collaboration, shared mission, and long-term partnership. The Church Partnerships Manager develops strategies to help churches discover, develop, send, and sustain global workers while ensuring TEAM serves churches with relational excellence and missiological integrity. This role works closely with Mobilization, Personnel, Development and Global Ministry teams to ensure a unified and innovative approach to Greater Global Gospel Impact. 
 
Key Responsibilities include but are not limited to: 
This is a ministerial leadership role, and the following ministry-related responsibilities are of paramount importance: 
  • Articulate a compelling biblical theology of mission and the Church’s role in God’s global purposes. 
  • Maintain strong alignment with TEAM’s mission, values, and doctrinal commitments. 
  • Raise 100% of your financial support (salary and benefits) 
Strategy & Leadership 
  • Develop and implement a comprehensive church partnership strategy that strengthens TEAM’s relationships with local churches and positions TEAM as a trusted missions partner. 
  • Create systems and best practices for identifying, cultivating, and sustaining strategic church partnerships. 
  • Lead organizational efforts to strengthen church-centered collaboration and engagement. 
  • Research emerging missiological trends to better serve churches and inform TEAM’s strategy. 
Church Partnerships & Engagement 
  • Build and maintain relationships with pastors, missions leaders, and church leadership teams. 
  • Cultivate partnerships characterized by shared vision, mutual investment, and a commitment to sending and sustaining global workers. 
  • Develop pathways for churches to engage in missions through prayer, sending, disciple-making, leadership development, and global partnerships. 
  • Maintain a strategic portfolio of key church relationships and partnerships. 
Mobilization and Equipping 
  • Represent TEAM at churches, conferences, universities, seminaries, and missions events. 
  • Communicate a compelling biblical vision for God’s global mission and the Church’s role in it. 
  • Equip churches to develop healthy sending cultures and missions strategies. 
  • Speak, teach, and provide resources on missions, sending, missiology, and global partnerships.  
Qualifications of the Role: 
  • Spiritually mature with a growing relationship with Jesus Christ and actively involved in a local church. 
  • Prior pastoral, church staff, missions, or nonprofit leadership with cross-cultural ministry experience is desirable as is fluency in a second language. 
  • Highly relational leader experienced in cultivating high-trust relationships and collaborative partnerships, with knowledge across a broad range of local church contexts and missions philosophies, who loves people and inspires others toward greater mission engagement.  
  • Self-starter with strong organizational leadership, strategic thinking and project management capabilities to execute strategy and accomplish goals independently. 
  • Skilled communicator—both verbally and in writing who is comfortable speaking publicly and facilitating training sessions or workshops. 
  • Bachelor’s degree and theological or ministry training preferred. 
  • Proficient in Microsoft 365 or similar productivity tools and experience with Salesforce or similar CRM systems preferred.

Location/Department: Archdiocese of Los Angeles Catholic Center - Victim Assistance Ministry 

Status: Exempt, Full Time

 

POSITION SUMMARY

The Associate Victims Assistance Coordinator (AVAC) extends the Church's concern and support for those who have been victims of sexual abuse by a priest, deacon, or individual representing the Catholic Church by providing pastoral outreach and other appropriate care. Due to the nature of this ministry and those served by it, in-person presence is required and fluency in English and Spanish (both oral and written) is necessary.

 

ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS

Because all Archdiocesan employees represent the Roman Catholic Church, they are expected to conduct themselves to the goals and mission of the Church in performing their work.

The AVAC has five primary areas of responsibility: 

  • Receiving complaints of sexual abuse and initiating the process to respond to and document such complaints involving any priest, deacon, other employee or representative of the Archdiocese of Los Angeles or its parishes or institutions.
  • Offering pastoral assistance to victims of sexual abuse and managing the ongoing care  offered to victims. 
  • Interfacing with Victims Assistance Coordinator and VAM Case Manager with ongoing communication with the victim, their therapist, and others providing ministry to the victim.
  • Providing clinical consultation and guidance on an as needed basis, in support of ADLA personnel dealing directly with disclosure or reasonable suspicion of abuse, e.g., when persons in parishes and schools report matters of familial or “other” non-church related matters. Supports ADLA personnel with assistance making mandated reports of suspected child abuse, referrals, and resources to support healing.
  • Responds to complaints of sexual abuse to minors, elders or dependent adults by reporting to civil authorities as required by mandated reporting laws, according to the established guidelines outlines in the Process for Responding to Complaints of Sexual Abuse by the Archdiocesan Ministries. Thus, informs the appropriate Archdiocesan official upon receipt of a report and links victims to mental health and pastoral care as needed. 

Additionally, the AVAC will:

  • Operating within a trauma-informed and person-centered approach to provide a safe setting for victim-survivors. Communicates appropriately regarding sensitive information, respecting privacy while facilitating thorough investigation and appropriate reporting to civil authorities. 
  • Supports Spanish-speaking victims by facilitating communication between the victim and Archdiocesan officials or investigators, as needed.
  • Identifies and vets possible service providers and ensures timely communications regarding treatment planning with mental health professionals contracted to provide trauma informed therapy to survivors, according to the ADLA Statement of Policy and Guidelines Concerning Therapeutic Services.
  • Participates in ACC or community forums for the purpose of highlighting VAM’s work and enhancing awareness around sexual abuse.


MINIMUM  QUALIFICATIONS: 

Education and Experience 

Any combination of education and experience likely to provide the required knowledge, skill, and abilities, typically: 

  • Master's Degree or its equivalent in Social Work (LCSW), Counseling (LMFT or LPCC) or Psychologist (Ph.D. or Psy.D), or comparable in related field.
  • Current licensure in California, appropriate to degree.
  • Must be a person of faith and commitment to ministry.

 

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities 

Knowledge of:

  • Fluency in English and Spanish (written and oral)
  • Expertise in trauma informed care
  • Civil laws and regulations.
  • Human behavior and mental health treatment methods, community systems and of resources for mental health care. 

Skills in:

  • General management and administrative functions.
  • Excellent listening skills.
  • Public relations and contact.
  • Report preparation and presentation.
  • Organization and planning with good attention to detail. 

Ability to:

  • Maintain clear thinking and balance under pressure
  • Maintain confidentiality.
  • Strong interpersonal skills and experience working with a team in coordinated efforts.
  • Extend compassion to the suffering and display sensitivity to various situations and needs.
  • Analyze situations and use judgment and resourcefulness.
  • Communicate effectively in written and oral form.
  • Demonstrate sufficient verbal/writing skills in Spanish to communicate clearly with victims whose primary language is Spanish.
  • Multi-task and prioritize within a very fast-paced and demanding work environment. 
  • Work in the evening on rare occasions.
  • Be flexible and adaptable.
  • Develop and maintain effective working relationships and as an equal with psychologists, psychiatrists, and other mental health professionals.
  • Demonstrate sufficient verbal/writing skills in Spanish to communicate with victims whose primary language is primarily Spanish.
  • Occasionally travel within Archdiocese boundaries as needed.

 

Physical and Environmental Requirements:

  • Occasionally lift up to 20 pounds.
  • Sit for sustained periods of time on a daily basis.
  • Perform tasks requiring intermittent bending, stooping and walking.
  • Sustain frequent movement of the fingers, wrists, hand and arms.

WHO WE ARE

 

Crossroads Bible Church, founded over 60 years ago, is located in Bellevue, Washington, 15 minutes across Lake Washington from Seattle. Situated between the foothills of the Cascade mountains and Lake Washington and Puget Sound. The Greater Eastside of Seattle is not only a beautiful area, but it is ethnically diverse and home to the headquarters of Microsoft, Amazon, T-Mobile, REI, and Starbucks.

 

Bellevue is also a largely unchurched population, so it is a calling and privilege of our church to minister in the community. Approximately 1100 people attend in person each Sunday. We are a multi-generational and mulit-cultural church committed to building disciples who bring Jesus to our world.

 

Our Core Values Are:

Biblical Teaching

United Worship

Passionate Prayer

Caring Community

Strategic Outreach

Next Generation Focused

 

POSITION

 

Crossroads Bible Church is seeking a Worship and Technical Arts Director who is passionate about bringing God glory through music.  The Worship and Technical Arts Director is responsible for planning, coordination, and execution of the church’s worship services and help with technical production. This role leads worship and volunteers, coordinates weekly services and special events, and ensures that Crossroads’ worship and production ministries are well-organized, prepared, and carried out with excellence.

 

Key Responsibilities

  • Support the overall quality of the Sunday morning worship service through leading the Worship Department.
  • Regularly lead worship during the Sunday morning services and/or coordinate worship leaders and teams.
  • Recruit, schedule, and train worship team volunteers.

  • Create and maintain schedules for worship teams.
  • Communicate clearly and consistently with volunteers, staff, and service participants.
  • Manage the worship and technical arts budget in collaboration with the supervising pastor.
  • Attend all monthly all-staff meetings

 

Qualifications

  • A committed follower of Jesus who supports the church’s theology, mission, and values.
  • Bachelor’s degree in worship ministry, music, technical arts, or a related field is preferred. Equivalent experience in worship ministry, church production, or a related field may be considered in lieu of formal education.
  • Strong administrative and time management skills.
  • Ability to work collaboratively with pastors, staff, and volunteers.
  • Strong organizational and communication skills.
  • A track record of servant leadership.

 

Positional Relationships

Positional Details

post_html:
Description

Sun River Health provides the highest quality of comprehensive primary, preventative and behavioral health services to all who see it, regardless of insurance status and ability to pay, especially for the underserved and vulnerable. Sun River Health is a Federally Qualified, Non-Profit Health Center serving communities in Suffolk, Rockland, Orange, Dutchess, Ulster, Sullivan, Columbia and Westchester County. 

Sun River Health is currently seeking a part time Primary Care Physician to join our team supporting the Church Avenue site. The Primary Care Physician is responsible for managing a diverse patient panel with multiple co-morbidities in a busy Federally Qualified Health Center. Care is delivered in collaboration with advance practice providers, on-site support staff, with an emphasis on preventative health and quality patient care.

Job Type: Part-Time

Salary Range: $133,415.10 - $151,737.30/ year

Sign On Bonus: **** $5,000 Sign-On Bonus for Eligible External Applicants – Terms and Conditions Apply **** 

Essential duties and responsibilities for a Primary Care Physician:

  • Participate in in planning and developing health care services, treatment of conditions and illnesses within scope.
  • Diagnose and provide treatment plans for patients.
  • Collaborate and supervise advanced provider clinicians.
  • Complete and participate in chart review process.
  • Referral and follow-up of patients when needed.
  • Collaborate with other members of the Health Center in order to maintain high quality standards and achieve client satisfaction.
  • Clinical Supervision: Overseeing the clinical work of students or new providers, ensuring they adhere to best practices and organizational standards.
  • Mentorship and Guidance: Providing mentorship and guidance to students or new providers, helping them develop their clinical skills and professional behavior.
  • Educational Support: Facilitating educational sessions, workshops or seminars to enhance the learning experience of the mentees.
  • Performance Evaluation: Assessing the performance of students or new providers, providing constructive feedback and documenting their progress.
  • Patient Care: Ensuring high-quality patient care is maintained while supervising and mentoring students or new providers.
  • Collaboration: Working closely with academic institutions and other healthcare professionals to coordinate the educational activities and ensure a comprehensive learning experience.

Requirements:

  • Doctorate Degree (MD, DO)
  • Active/Valid license as a MD or DO in New York State, DEA, Board certification
  • Bilingual in English and Spanish (preferred)
  • Experience in HIV care and MAT (Medication Assisted Treatment) preferred
  • Demonstrated ability to work with diverse patient population in community health setting

About Sun River Health

Sun River Health has a rich history of providing quality, affordable health care to communities in need. Founded in the early 1970s by four African American women in Peekskill, New York, the organization was established to address the lack of accessible health services in their community. With the help of a small federal grant, the first Sun River Health site opened its doors in 1975. Over the years, Sun River Health has grown into a comprehensive Federally Qualified Health Center (FQHC) system with over 45 locations, serving more than 250,000 patients across the Hudson Valley, New York City and Long Island. Our exceptional primary care practitioners, specialists and support staff are dedicated to delivering high-quality care to all individuals, regardless of their ability to pay. In December 2018, Sun River Health expanded its reach by merging with Brightpoint Health, an FQHC network offering integrated medical, behavioral and social support services in New York City. This merger allowed us to enhance our services and continue our mission under the unified name of Sun River Health.

Our Culture

At Sun River Health, we believe in fostering a culture of wellness, inclusivity and recognition. Our Workforce Wellness Program promotes staff wellness through ongoing challenges and activities, encouraging participation and rewarding engagement. We celebrate our staff's dedication and person-centered spirit through the Planetree Recognition Awards, which honor innovation, leadership and community spirit. We are committed to creating a supportive and collaborative work environment where all team members can thrive. Our values of respect, integrity and excellence guide our interactions with patients and colleagues alike, ensuring that everyone receives the care and support they deserve.

Professional Development, Education and Loan Assistance Benefit Programs 

Sun River Health is committed in fostering continued growth, education, and professional advancement across its organization. Through a range of development opportunities and loan repayment programs employees are supported at every stage of their careers.

Eligible employees may have the opportunity to participate in federal and state loan repayment or loan forgiveness programs, including those administered by the Health Resources and Services Administration (HRSA) and the National Health Service Corps (NHSC) with support provided throughout the application process.

In addition, Sun River Health offers a Tuition Reimbursement Program for eligible employees that supports job-related coursework completed through accredited institutions, helping employees continue building their skills and advancing their careers. 

Benefits

At Sun River Health, we are committed to building a personal relationship with our team and supporting you in every way we can. We offer competitive compensation and a comprehensive benefits package for you and your family, including:

  • Medical, Dental and Vision Insurance: Comprehensive health coverage to ensure you and your family stay healthy.
  • Life and Disability Coverage: Financial protection for you and your loved ones in case of unforeseen circumstances.

Campus Kids Pastor - Cypress  - Overview

The Kids Ministry Pastor is responsible for providing spiritual leadership, vision, direction, and oversight for the Kids Ministry at Bayou City Fellowship Cypress campus. This individual will lead a ministry that partners with parents to help children develop a lasting foundation of faith, grow in their understanding of God's Word, and build a personal relationship with Jesus Christ.

The Kids Ministry Pastor will create an engaging, safe, and welcoming environment where children are known, loved, discipled, and encouraged to grow in their faith. This role requires a passionate shepherd, intentional leader, and strategic ministry builder who is committed to developing teams, equipping volunteers, partnering with families, and reaching the next generation with the Gospel.

As part of the campus ministry team, the Kids Ministry Pastor will work collaboratively with campus leadership to carry out the overall vision and mission of Bayou City Fellowship.

Primary Responsibilities

1. Spiritual Leadership & Discipleship

  • Provide biblical teaching and spiritual leadership that helps children understand the Gospel and develop a growing relationship with Jesus.

  • Establish a clear discipleship pathway that encourages children to grow in their knowledge of Scripture, faith, and spiritual maturity.

  • Create age-appropriate environments and teaching experiences that communicate biblical truth in engaging and meaningful ways.

  • Lead children toward a personal understanding of salvation, baptism, worship, prayer, and living out their faith.

  • Maintain a consistent focus on the mission of Bayou City Fellowship

2. Ministry Leadership & Oversight

  • Provide vision, leadership, and direction for all Kids Ministry leaders, environments, and programming at the Cypress campus.

  • Lead kids staff in 30/60/90 goal setting and performance management process.

  • Oversee weekly Sunday programming, midweek activities, special events, and seasonal ministry opportunities.

  • Develop and implement ministry strategies that support the spiritual growth and engagement of children from birth through elementary school.

  • Evaluate ministry effectiveness and continually identify opportunities for improvement, innovation, and growth.

  • Ensure ministry environments are organized, engaging, welcoming, and aligned with the overall vision of Bayou City Fellowship.

3. Volunteer Development & Leadership

  • Recruit, equip, train, encourage, and develop a strong team of committed Kids Ministry volunteers.

  • Build a culture of ownership, teamwork, spiritual growth, and meaningful relationships among volunteers.

  • Identify and develop emerging leaders who can take on greater ministry responsibility.

  • Establish clear expectations, communication, and accountability for volunteer teams.

  • Provide consistent encouragement, appreciation, and pastoral care to volunteers and their families.

4. Family Partnership & Pastoral Care

  • Partner with parents as the primary spiritual influencers in their children's lives.

  • Provide resources, encouragement, and practical tools to help families disciple their children at home.

  • Build meaningful relationships with families and create opportunities for connection within the church.

  • Provide pastoral care, prayer, encouragement, and support to children and families during significant seasons of life.

  • Help families take meaningful next steps in their faith and involvement at Bayou City Fellowship.

5. Safety & Ministry Administration

  • Maintain a safe, secure, and well-organized environment for every child entrusted to the ministry.

  • Ensure compliance with all church policies and child protection procedures, including volunteer screening, background checks, check-in/check-out processes, and appropriate classroom supervision.

  • Oversee ministry budgets, supplies, curriculum, scheduling, and resources with responsible stewardship.

  • Maintain effective communication with parents, volunteers, staff, and campus leadership.

  • Ensure classrooms and ministry spaces are prepared, clean, welcoming, and appropriately staffed.

6. Outreach & Special Events

  • Develop opportunities to reach children and families in the surrounding community.

  • Plan and oversee special events such as, outreach initiatives, camps, Vacation Bible School, and other ministry opportunities.

  • Collaborate with other campus ministries to create opportunities for families to connect and engage in the life of the church.

  • Encourage children and families to live out their faith through serving others and sharing the love of Christ.

7. Teamwork & Collaboration

  • Work closely with the Campus Pastor and campus ministry team to advance the overall vision and mission of Bayou City Fellowship.

  • Participate in staff meetings, ministry planning, goal-setting, and performance management initiatives.

  • Collaborate with Kids Ministry leaders across all three campuses to maintain alignment, share resources, and strengthen ministry effectiveness.

  • Demonstrate a team-first attitude and willingness to serve beyond the immediate responsibilities of the Kids Ministry when needed.

Qualifications & Experience

  • Demonstrates a growing and authentic relationship with Jesus Christ and a commitment to biblical leadership.

  • Fully aligned with the doctrine, values, mission, and vision of Bayou City Fellowship.

  • Demonstrates a clear calling and passion for ministry to children and families.

  • Previous experience leading, developing, or overseeing a children's ministry is strongly preferred.

  • Proven ability to recruit, develop, equip, and lead volunteer teams.

  • Strong biblical teaching, communication, organizational, and relational skills.

  • Ability to build trust and meaningful relationships with children, parents, volunteers, and church staff.

  • Demonstrates initiative, sound judgment, humility, flexibility, and a commitment to excellence.

  • Previous Kids Pastor experience required.

  • Bachelor's degree in ministry, theology, education, or a related field preferred.

Personal & Spiritual Characteristics

The ideal candidate will:

  • Have a deep love for Jesus and a genuine passion for helping the next generation know and follow Him.

  • Be a shepherd at heart who values relationships, prayer, and the spiritual well-being of children and families.

  • Lead with humility, integrity, enthusiasm, and a servant's heart.

  • Be a strong communicator who can inspire and equip others to invest in the next generation.

  • Demonstrate a commitment to personal spiritual growth and lifelong discipleship.

  • Be a leader who develops leaders rather than simply managing programs.

  • Have the ability to bring energy, creativity, and intentionality to ministry while maintaining a strong foundation in Scripture.

Reporting Relationship

The Kids Ministry Pastor reports directly to the Campus Pastor and works collaboratively with  Bayou City Fellowship staff.

Position Details

  • Position: Kids Ministry Pastor

  • Department: Kids Ministry

  • Campus:  Bayou City Fellowship Cypress Campus

  • Employment Status: Full-Time

  • Reports To: Campus Pastor

Pastor of Senior Adults and Visitation - Alexandria Covenant Church

ROLE DESCRIPTION

Pastor of Senior Adults and Visitation

PURPOSE:  The Pastor of Senior Adults and Visitation will help senior adults connect in meaningful ways with God, the church, the community, and with one another. This role involves direct oversight of the ministry to seniors and visitation to the church membership.

OBJECTIVES:

  • Oversee the ministry to senior adults.
  • Oversee the visitation of members and regular attendees of the church.

POSITION TITLE: 

Pastor of Senior Adults and Visitation

REQUIREMENTS:

  • Be born-again and living a dedicated Christian life.
  • Possess spiritual gifts, along with the professional and educational background adequate for the position.
  • Be committed to the vision, mission, values, and ministry philosophy of Alexandria Covenant Church.
  • Be licensed or ordained in ministry.
  • Be a member at Alexandria Covenant Church.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Provide oversight of the ministry to senior adults in cooperation with the senior’s ministry team.
  • Develop and oversee a visitation ministry to members and regular attendees of the church.
  • Develop and maintain ministry budgets for specific areas of oversight on an annual basis.
  • Participate in weekly staff meetings.
  • Participate regularly in Sunday worship services through prayer, announcements, dedications, baptisms, and the Lord’s Supper.
  • Preach and teach God’s Word periodically in Sunday morning worship services and other ministry settings.
  • Assist the Senior Pastor in officiating funerals for members and attendees of Alexandria Covenant Church.
  • Provide pastoral care to the congregation through prayer, encouragement, counseling, visitation, and other means necessary.

AUTHORITY:

  • The Pastor of Senior Adults and Visitation will have the authority to perform duties in accordance with the job guidelines and under the direct supervision of the Senior Pastor.

ACCOUNTABILITY:

  • The Pastor of Senior Adults and Visitation will be directly accountable to the Senior Pastor.

STANDARDS FOR PERFORMANCE:

  • The Pastor of Senior Adults and Visitation should conduct themselves at all times in such a manner as set forth in the Word of God for a servant of God.
  • The Pastor of Senior Adults and Visitation will accomplish their duties and responsibilities in a professional manner and should demonstrate, along with the fruit of the Spirit, excellence, integrity, loyalty, and maturity.

EVALUATION:

  • The Pastor of Senior Adults and Visitation will be evaluated annually by the Senior Pastor based on ministry performance in accordance with their role description.

job_name: Youth Ministry Director at Fort Rucker, Alabama
post_html:
*Please note this position would require our Staff to live near the community where they would be doing ministry.

Description:

There are nearly 300,000 teenagers of active-duty U.S. military parents who are stationed all over the world. These teens move an average of seven times during their school-aged years. The questions of identity and belonging that all teens face grow even more challenging to answer amid starting over and meeting new friends at each location.

This is where you can be the difference in a military teen’s life! By being in their world, walking alongside them, and creating a community where they experience the truth of God’s love and purpose for them, our staff provide a safe space where teens can develop friendships and connections to experience laughter, build hope, and generate resiliency.

We are currently providing incarnational ministry at many military installations around the world. You will have the opportunity to lead and oversee the overall Young Life Military program, known as Club Beyond, which is ecumenically focused and outreach oriented.

We are currently looking for both full-time and part-time staff throughout the United States, as well as international locations. Colorado Springs, CO, is the headquarters.

Responsibilities:

  • Actively develop healthy relationships with adults, as well as kids, and build vibrant relationships with the local community, the military installation, and the chapel community.
  • Be a role model (incarnational) and assist with developing community outreach to "unchurched" teens, discipleship to Christian teens, and leading and equipping volunteers to do "hands-on" middle and high school Christian youth programs.
  • Work well in an environment that sees (due to high military operational tempo) a high degree of turnover among teens, families, chaplains and volunteers.
  • Be respectful of and embrace a community that is deeply influenced by a military culture.
  • In this ministry, you will need to live out the Club Beyond Core Value Statement:

Club Beyond is a Christ-centered community of leaders with an exclusively military focus. Our methods are incarnational, and our perspective is ecumenical. We leverage strategic partnerships for the greatest results. We value professionalism from our staff and excellence in our stewardship.

Qualifications:

  • A deep love for Christ and for lost teens.
  • Competent communicator with youths, parents, and senior military leaders.
  • Teachable heart.
  • Willingness to make a three-year commitment.
  • Minimum of three years' youth ministry experience preferred.
  • College degree preferred.
  • Willingness to raise part of the budget through personal support.
  • Committed to a relational ministry approach.
  • Energetic.
  • Small event planning skills.
  • Strong initiative.
  • Note, this position would require our Staff to live near the community where they would be doing ministry.

Benefits:

  • Full-time salary: Based on experience, responsibility, and fundraising levels.
  • Benefits: Full health coverage (including dental, vision and life insurance).
  • Expense reimbursement (mileage [office and ministry related]).
  • Training and career development is built into the job.

Salary:

The Base Salary range: $45,000 to $60,000 (Salary is based on education and experience). In addition to salary, a Cost of Living Adjustment, dependent on location, is available. The Annual National Funding provided is $16,667.

Location:

Club Beyond works on military installations all over the world. We currently have openings at:

In the USA:

  • Fort Rucker, Alabama
  • Joint Base Elmendorf-Richardson (JBER), Alaska
  • Fort Irwin, California
  • Camp Pendleton, California
  • Travis Air Force Base, California
  • Joint Base Anacostia-Bolling (JBAB), Washington, D.C.
  • Eglin Air Force Base, Florida
  • Fort Benning, Georgia
  • Fort Stewart, Georgia
  • Fort Riley, Kansas
  • Fort Sill, Oklahoma
  • Fort Belvoir, Virginia
  • Joint Base Lewis-McChord (JBLM), Washington


Overseas:

  • Geilenkirchen, Germany and various other locations in Germany
  • Naval Base Guam
  • Aviano Air Base, Italy
  • Vicenza, Italy
  • Yokosuka, Japan
  • Camp Humphreys, South Korea

Contact us through:
Robert Raedeke: RecruitingTeam@clubbeyond.org

Want to know more about our mission and culture?

Please check out clubbeyond.org to learn how Club Beyond has been changing the lives of military teens for over 40 years!

SUMMARY

The primary responsibility of the Lead Adult Groups Pastor is to provide spiritual, visionary, team-based, value-driven leadership to mobilize the people of Pinelake Church into Biblical community in a manner consistent with the purpose, vision, core values and major objectives as expressed by the Core Leadership of Pinelake Church.

GENERAL RESPONSIBILITIES

Learn

  • Pursue a growing relationship with Jesus through consistent time in God’s Word and prayer
  • Continually grow in your understanding of the Jesus-Centered Life (salvation, identity, life, and authority in Christ).
  • Remain teachable and hungry, seeking feedback, learning from others, and developing both spiritually and professionally.
  • Cultivate awareness of God’s presence in everyday life, listening to the Holy Spirit and responding in obedience.

Live

  • Practice and model the rhythms of Be the Church (Grow, Pray, Connect, and Share).
  • Pursue emotional health by engaging in self-awareness, addressing past wounds, and cultivating honest, healthy relationships.
  • Practice healthy rhythms, prioritizing your relationship with Jesus and your family
  • Embody a life of integrity and surrender, allowing your private life with God to shape your work.

Lead

  • Take ownership of disciple-making by personally investing in others and helping them move toward a Jesus-Centered Life.
  • Walk others through the Discipleship Pathway (Essentials → JCL → Be the Church), helping them discover and take their next step.
  • Shepherd people, not just programs, by listening for where God is at work in their story and walking with them toward transformation.
  • Equip and release others by developing Servant Leaders and multiplying disciples who Learn from Christ, Live in Christ, and Lead others to Christ.
  • Measure success by life change, spiritual formation, and multiplication—not just attendance or activity.

Embrace the Culture

  • Value and embody the staff values, which we call the 7 H’s: Humility, Honor, Honesty, Hunger, Holy Spirit, Health, and Harmony
  • Communicate clearly, honestly, and proactively in a way that builds trust, unity, and momentum.
  • Work in alignment with the church vision and leadership
  • Participate fully in the life of your campus or team, contributing to the unity, health, and shepherding of the faith family.

SPECIFIC LIST OF DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Works in harmony with the One Church Discipleship Team.
  • Pursue small group leadership contacts weekly for the purposes of shepherding, vision casting, and organizational health.
  • Lead the small group leadership culture by developing and leading a team of directors, coaches, and small group leaders.
  • Recruit potential and new small group leadership for multiplication of groups.
  • Strategically pursue couples and individuals for group connection.
  • Train leaders to lead their groups and disciple individuals within their groups.
  • Help execute groups events including but not limited to: Essentials, Jesus Centered Life, Be the Church, Leader Huddles, Men’s and Women’s Specific opportunities and Equip Classes.
  • Prepares and manages the budget for the Adult Groups ministry under the oversight of the Campus Pastor.
  • Share in Pastoral/Ministerial responsibilities of the Reservoir Campus (ie. Pastor/Minister On-Call Rotation, Funeral assistance, Disaster Relief, etc.)
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

QUALIFICATIONS

To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily. The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skill and/or ability required. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform essential functions.

EDUCATION AND/OR EXPERIENCE

Bachelor’s degree minimum; and four to six years of related experience and/or training.

LANGUAGE SKILLS

The individual must have excellent interpersonal skills, ability to work with a diverse group of people, communicate clearly and effectively on the telephone, e-mail and in person, demonstrating tact and diplomacy. Exceptional interpersonal skills are required to develop and maintain strong working relationships with volunteers, co-workers, the public and church members and regular attendees. The individual must have the ability to understand written or oral instructions; read, analyze and interpret complex documents, instructions manuals, policies and procedures is essential.

COMPUTER AND MATHEMATICAL SKILLS

The individual must have demonstrated skill in the use of Windows/MacOS to complete tasks, including word processing and spreadsheets and the ability to use the internet for information retrieval. The individual must have basic mathematical skills, knowledge of bookkeeping and basic accounting, and budget and expense monitoring. The individual must have the ability to read financial information and spreadsheets.

REASONING ABILITY

The individual must be able to define problems, collect data, establish facts, and draw valid conclusions; respond effectively to the most sensitive inquiries; simultaneous conceptualization and planning of multiple tasks, ability to project outcomes using different implementation strategies and ability to apply creative and innovative thinking to problem situations; and solve practical problems. The ability to work effectively and efficiently under stressful conditions to ensure deadlines are met is essential.

PHYSICAL DEMANDS

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to sit and talk or hear. The employee is required to stand, walk, and reach with hands and arms.

Must be able to lift up to 25 lbs.

WORK ENVIRONMENT

The work environment characteristics described here are representative of those an employee encounters while performing the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

The noise level of the work environment is usually moderate.

Worship Pastor - Friends Church
 

Associate Pastor of Worship

Job Summary

The Associate Pastor of Worship leads the planning, execution, and development of the worship ministry at Friends Church. Reporting to the Executive Pastor of Worship & Creative, this role creates Christ-centered worship experiences that help people encounter God, grow in their faith, and take next steps in discipleship.

This pastor recruits, develops, and shepherds worship and production volunteers, leads worship services, and collaborates across ministries to create engaging, excellent weekend experiences. The Associate Pastor of Worship is responsible for building healthy teams, developing future leaders, and cultivating a culture of authentic worship, spiritual growth, and servant leadership.

 

General Ministry Expectations

  • Maintain a growing personal relationship with Jesus through consistent prayer, Scripture, worship, and spiritual disciplines.
  • Live a life consistent with biblical leadership and the mission, vision, and values of Friends Church.
  • Actively participate in the life of Friends Church through worship, discipleship, and church-wide initiatives.
  • Help people encounter Christ, grow spiritually, and engage in the church's discipleship pathway.
  • Equip and develop volunteers to use their gifts in ministry (Ephesians 4).
  • Shepherd volunteers with humility, integrity, and care (1 Peter 5).
  • Support the leadership and direction of the Executive Pastor of Creative and Weekend Services.
  • Foster unity, collaboration, and a positive staff culture.

 

Key Responsibilities

Weekend Worship Leadership

  • Plan and lead engaging, Christ-centered worship experiences.
  • Lead rehearsals, weekend services, and assigned ministry events.
  • Collaborate with Creative, Production, Communications, and Teaching teams to ensure seamless service execution.
  • Build worship sets, service flows, and rehearsal plans using Planning Center.
  • Contribute creative ideas that enhance worship experiences while supporting the overall vision of Friends Church.

 

Team Development & Shepherding

  • Recruit, train, schedule, and develop worship and production volunteers.
  • Coach worship leaders, musicians, vocalists, and technicians toward musical and spiritual growth.
  • Provide ongoing pastoral care, encouragement, and leadership development.
  • Build a culture of discipleship, ownership, excellence, and servant leadership.
  • Develop clear leadership pathways for volunteers from first involvement to team leadership.

Next Generation Worship

  • Lead worship within Student Ministry as assigned.
  • Recruit and mentor student musicians and production volunteers.
  • Develop future worship leaders and create intentional opportunities for students to serve alongside adult teams.
  • Build a sustainable leadership pipeline for future worship ministry.

 

Ministry Operations

  • Maintain accurate Planning Center schedules, resources, and communications.
  • Steward worship equipment, instruments, and ministry resources.
  • Ensure worship environments are prepared, organized, and ministry-ready.
  • Improve ministry systems, workflows, and volunteer processes for greater effectiveness.
  • Assist with special events, conferences, holidays, and church-wide initiatives.

Success Metrics

Weekend Excellence

      • Worship services are prepared and executed with excellence.
      • Planning Center plans are completed by established deadlines.
      • Weekend execution issues remain minimal and are addressed proactively.
      • Volunteer scheduling maintains at least a 90% fulfillment rate.

Team Development

  • Recruit and onboard 20–30 new worship and production volunteers annually.
  • Provide quarterly coaching and care for volunteers.
  • Develop emerging leaders capable of leading teams and worship experiences independently.

Next Generation

  • Lead Student Ministry worship 2–4 times per month.
  • Recruit and develop 10–20 student volunteers annually.
  • Identify and mentor 3–5 student leaders each year.
  • Transition 2–4 students annually into adult worship or production teams.

Ministry Health

  • Maintain healthy volunteer retention and engagement.
  • Strengthen collaboration across Creative, Production, and Weekend Experience teams.
  • Continuously improve ministry systems, communication, and volunteer experience

Qualifications

  • Growing relationship with Jesus Christ and agreement with the beliefs and values of Friends Church.
  • Demonstrated calling to worship ministry and pastoral leadership.
  • Strong vocal and instrumental proficiency.
  • Experience leading contemporary worship in a church setting.
  • Experience recruiting, leading, and developing volunteer teams.
  • Excellent organizational, communication, and leadership skills.
  • Working knowledge of Planning Center and worship technology.

 

Preferred

  • Bachelor's degree in Worship Ministry, Music, Theology, or related field.
  • Three to five years of worship leadership experience in a growing church.
  • Experience leading multi-generational volunteer teams.
  • Familiarity with production environments and AVL systems.
  • Familiarity with Planning Center

Core Competencies

  • Gets It: Understands the vision of Friends Church and the role worship plays in disciple-making.
  • Wants It: Has a passion for leading people in worship, developing volunteers, and building healthy ministry teams.
  • Capacity: Demonstrates the leadership, relational skills, musical ability, and organizational capacity to lead a growing worship ministry.
  • Spiritual Maturity
  • Humility and Servant Leadership
  • Team Builder
  • Musical Excellence
  • Strong Communicator
  • Organizational Excellence
  • Collaborative
  • Disciple Maker
  • Adaptable and Solution-Oriented
  • Creative Thinker

 

Reports to: Executive Pastor of Worship & Creative

Works Closely With:

  • Weekend Experience Team
  • Production Team
  • Communications Team
  • Student Ministry

  • Champion the vision, culture, and values of Alive Church at your campus
  • Lead healthy, prepared, and spiritually alive weekend experiences, including preaching and teaching
  • Shepherd and care for the congregation through crisis, transition, and life moments
  • Lead, coach, and develop campus staff, Dream Team leaders, and Alive Group leaders
  • Help people move from attending to belonging and serving through Growth Track, Dream Team, and Alive Groups
  • Reach and engage the local community through outreach and Big Serve days
  • Manage the campus budget, track key metrics, and report on campus performance to the Executive Pastor

  • A growing, personal relationship with Jesus and alignment with the beliefs and values of Alive Church

  • Proven experience building teams and developing leaders
  • Demonstrated leadership at increasing levels of responsibility
  • Working knowledge of budgets, systems, and campus operations

  • Completion of the Alive Church Campus Pastor Residency
  • Experience leading a campus, church launch, or expansion
  • Experience serving in a multi-campus church
  • Hands-on experience with guest connection, volunteer team, and small group systems

 
As a staff member of Alive Church, the successful candidate must understand, support, and protect the mission, values, culture, and biblical foundation of Alive Church.

PASTOR OF GUEST EXPERIENCE // EAGLE BROOK CHURCH 

JOB OBJECTIVES

  • Champions the guest experience at assigned campus
  • Focuses on creating engaging experiences and building transformational relationships
  • Builds and leads a team of volunteers to carry out Eagle Brook’s vision for Guest Experience ministries
  • Provides an environment in which volunteers are recruited, onboarded, connected and growing spiritually to own Eagle Brook’s mission
  • Collaborates cross functionally with the central Ministry Development team and peers at other campuses

  • Leads the Guest Experience volunteer team
  • Identifies, equips, inspires and invests in volunteers
  • Develops volunteer leaders, directors and team leads to equip and lead core volunteers
  • Meets with leaders one to one and in groups for spiritual and leadership development
  • Manages volunteer schedules

Preferred Qualifications

WORK ENVIROMENT / PHYSICAL DEMANDS 

  • Regular communicating with others to exchange information
  • Occasional assessing the accuracy, neatness and thoroughness of the work assigned

  • Occasional moving of self in different positions to accomplish tasks in various environments, including tight and confined spaces
  • Occasional moving about to accomplish tasks or moving from one worksite to another
  • Occasional sedentary work that primarily involves sitting/standing
  • Occasional light work that includes adjusting or moving objects up to 20 pounds in all directions
  • Occasional medium work that includes adjusting or moving objects up to 50 pounds in all directions

BENEFITS

Eagle Brook Church’s benefit plan is designed to help you stay healthy, feel secure and maintain work/life balance. Offering a competitive benefits package is just one way we strive to provide our employees with a rewarding workplace. We offer the following benefits to our full-time employees:

  • employer-provided short-term and long-term disability

  • 403b retirement plan with company contribution

  • casual dress and work environment

 

APPLICANTS WITH DISABILITIES 

Eagle Brook Church provides reasonable accommodation for their employees and applicants with disabilities. If you have a disability and need assistance in searching or applying for jobs with Eagle Brook Church, call 651-429-9227 or email staffing@eaglebrookchurch.com and let us know the support you need.
