post_html:
Work Shift

Day

Scheduled Weekly Hours

40

Summary

The Vice President of Mission Integration serves as a strategic advisor to the President & CEO and a member of the Executive Leadership Team. This executive leader is responsible for advancing and integrating Mercy’s Catholic identity, mission, vision, values, and heritage throughout all aspects of healthcare delivery, governance, operations, strategic planning, organizational culture, workforce engagement, and patient experience consistent with The Mercy Touch.

The Vice President provides leadership for mission integration, ethics, spiritual and pastoral care, ministry formation, community benefit, ecclesial relationships, and systemwide efforts that promote an exceptional patient and family experience while ensuring Mercy remains faithful to its identity as a healing ministry of the Catholic Church. The role promotes a culture of compassion, dignity, justice, and stewardship consistent with Catholic healthcare tradition and the Ethical and Religious Directives for Catholic Health Care Services (ERDs). The Vice President is also responsible for community outreach, involvement, and partnerships, including the local Catholic community and the Archdiocese of Dubuque.

Job Description

Essential Responsibilities


Mission and Catholic Identity Leadership

  • Serve as the executive steward of Mercy’s mission, vision, values, heritage, and Catholic identity.
  • Ensure mission integration is embedded in strategic planning and transformation, operations, clinical care, human resources, governance, and organizational decision-making.
  • Collaborate with executive colleagues to ensure mission principles inform policies, practices, operational priorities, and culture.
  • Foster an organizational culture reflecting human dignity, compassion, justice, stewardship, and service to persons who are poor and vulnerable.
  • Guide mission discernment processes related to strategic initiatives, partnerships, affiliations, acquisitions, and organizational change.
  • Promote understanding of Catholic social teaching and its application to healthcare ministry.
  • Develop regular accountability reports for executive team and board members regarding key areas of performance.

 

Ethics Leadership

  • Provide executive leadership and consultation regarding organizational, clinical, and business ethics.
  • Ensure adherence to the Ethical and Religious Directives for Catholic Health Care Services.
  • Serve as executive sponsor and co-chair of the Ethics Committee.
  • Facilitate ethical reflection and values-based decision-making throughout the organization.
  • Collaborate with medical staff, legal counsel, compliance, and operational leaders regarding complex ethical issues.

 

Spiritual Care and Pastoral Ministry

  • Provide strategic leadership and oversight for all Spiritual Care and Pastoral Care services.
  • Ensure the delivery of high-quality spiritual care services to patients, families, caregivers, providers, and volunteers.
  • Promote holistic care that addresses physical, emotional, spiritual, and psychosocial needs.
  • Support sacramental ministry, chaplaincy services, grief support, end-of-life care, well-being initiatives, and programs.
  • Foster interdisciplinary collaboration between pastoral care and clinical care experts and teams.

 

Ministry Formation and Leadership Development

  • Develop and implement a comprehensive ministry formation strategy for leaders, providers, board members, and caregivers.
  • Lead initiatives that deepen understanding of Catholic healthcare, Mercy heritage, and mission.
  • Oversee and deliver orientation programs related to Mercy’s’ mission, values, heritage, Catholic identity, and transformational organizational culture.
  • Facilitate formation experiences that strengthen leadership effectiveness and mission-centered decision-making.

 

Community Benefit and Health Equity

  • Provide executive oversight for community benefit and outreach initiatives.
  • Champion efforts addressing health disparities, social determinants of health, and community well-being.
  • Build strategic partnerships with community organizations, faith communities, and public agencies.
  • Ensure compliance with community benefit reporting requirements and charitable mission obligations. Support advocacy efforts consistent with Catholic social teaching.

Ecclesial and Sponsorship Relationships

  • Serve as primary liaison to diocesan leadership, clergy, religious congregations, sponsors, and Catholic organizations.
  • Cultivate collaborative relationships with bishops, diocesan leaders, and parish communities/pastorates.
  • Represent Mercy at Catholic healthcare and Church-related gatherings.
  • Support sponsorship responsibilities and the preservation of Catholic identity and Mercy’s heritage.

 

Patient Experience and Culture Leadership

  • Ensure mission integration serves as a foundational driver of both organizational culture and the patient experience, reinforcing the organization's commitment to whole-person care, healing, and well-being.
  • Serve as the executive sponsor for Mercy’s patient experience strategy and culture of service excellence.
  • Champion the integration of Mercy’s heritage, mission, values, spiritual care, and person-centered care principles into the patient and family experience.
  • Partner with executive, operational, clinical, nursing, physician leaders, and other experts to ensure patient experience priorities are aligned with organizational strategy and performance goals.
  • Advocate for patient and family perspectives in strategic planning, organizational decision-making, and transformation initiatives.

 

Organizational Culture and Workforce Engagement

  • Promote an organizational culture – grounded in Mercy’s heritage, mission, and values – in which every interaction reflects compassion, dignity, respect, hospitality, and well- being for the whole person.
  • Coordinate celebrations and events supportive of Mercy’s Mission, values, heritage, and evolving culture.
  • Collaborate with Human Resources to integrate mission-centered leadership competencies and performance expectations.
  • Champion diversity, equity, inclusion and belonging, inviting appreciation for different faith traditions, beliefs, and cultures.
  • Lead mission-focused celebrations, rituals, blessings, recognition programs, and heritage events.
  • Support caregiver well-being, resilience, and workplace spirituality initiatives.

 

Leadership Competencies

  • Strategic Thinking
  • Mission-Centered Leadership
  • Ethical Discernment
  • Executive Presence
  • Change Leadership
  • Patient and Family-Centered Leadership
  • Collaborative Partnership
  • Organizational Influence
  • Relationship Building
  • Cultural Humility
  • Communication Excellence
  • Formation and Coaching Skills

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities

  • Advanced knowledge of Catholic theology, spirituality, and healthcare ministry.
  • Thorough understanding of Catholic social teaching and the Ethical and Religious Directives for Catholic Health Care Services.
  • Knowledge of mission integration methodologies and Catholic identity assessment tools.
  • Understanding of healthcare delivery systems, clinical operations, and regulatory environments.
  • Ability to facilitate organizational ethics consultations and complex decision-making.
  • Exceptional communication, presentation, and relationship-building skills.
  • Demonstrated ability to influence executive leadership, boards, physicians, and staff.
  • Strong organizational development and formation expertise.

 

Education

  • Master's degree in Healthcare Mission Leadership, Theology, Divinity, Religious Studies, Spirituality, Ethics, Pastoral Ministry, or related field required.
  • Doctorate (D. Min., Ph.D., Ed.D., or equivalent) in an appropriate discipline preferred.
  • Formal education or certification in ethics, mission leadership, or organizational development preferred.

 

Experience

  • Minimum of seven (7) years of progressive leadership experience in Catholic healthcare, mission integration, spiritual care, ethics, formation, or related ministry leadership required.
  • Demonstrated success leading mission-centered organizational initiatives required.
  • Experience working with executive leadership teams and governing boards required.
  • Executive-level leadership experience in a Catholic health system preferred.
  • Experience overseeing pastoral care and spiritual care departments preferred.
  • Experience with ministry formation, sponsorship, and church relations preferred.

 

Faith Commitment

  • Active, practicing Catholic status in good standing with the Roman Catholic Church required.
  • A deep understanding of and commitment to the healing ministry of the Catholic Church, Catholic healthcare ethics, Catholic social teaching, and the mission-driven values essential to a Catholic healthcare organization required.

 

Certifications and Professional Affiliations

Preferred certifications or active participation in:

  • Catholic Health Association (CHA)
  • National Association of Catholic Chaplains (NACC)
  • Catholic Moral Theology or Healthcare Ethics professional organizations

Physical Requirements

Light: Exert up to 20 lbs. of force occasionally and/or up to 10 lbs. of force frequently

Salary

The Junior High Minister (7th & 8th Grade) leads the vision, strategy, and ministry for 7th and 8th grade students. This leader creates environments where students encounter Jesus, build relationships, and grow in faith; recruits and develops adult leaders; partners with parents; and collaborates with the NextGen Team to help connect people to Jesus.

This role is ideal for someone who loves students, thrives on teams, develops volunteers, and builds relationships inside and outside the church.

Campus Staff Minister – Metro NYC (Graduate & Faculty Ministry)

Work Location:

New York

Job Type:

Full time

God has called InterVarsity to plant and to build witnessing communities of students and faculty who follow Jesus on college and university campuses. Through these groups, we believe ever- increasing numbers of students and faculty from all ethnic groups and areas of the campus will be transformed by the Gospel. We expect to see campuses increasingly become places where people, ideas, and structures flourish to the glory of God. We confidently anticipate that our InterVarsity alumni will become change agents across the country and around the world. We pursue this calling by discerning and actively participating in what God is already doing on campus. This is the essence of being a Campus Staff Minister (CSM).

Please visit https://gfm.intervarsity.org/gfm-interest-form and submit the GFM Interest Form before completing the full application for a position with Graduate & Faculty Ministries in our online system. We will contact you when we are ready to proceed with the application process. ​


We are interested in hiring Campus Staff Ministers for various graduate schools in the Metro NYC area. Whether you are open to any school or feel God leading you to start graduate student and faculty ministry at a specific school, please let us know in the Interest form above.

ESSENTIAL COMMITMENTS/RESPONSIBILITIES 

Spiritual Growth 

You pursue maturity as a disciple of Jesus Christ so that your life and work increasingly reflects a growing love for God, God’s Word, God’s people of every ethnicity and culture, and God’s purposes in the world. To do this, you will: 

  • Pursue a vibrant relationship with the triune God through engagement with Scripture, prayer, and worship, both individually and in community 

  • Develop self-leadership (growing in self-awareness, self-management, relational integrity, and resiliency) 

  • Embrace Scriptural standards for behavior and attitudes 

 

Campus Leadership 

You communicate and model InterVarsity’s vision to see students and faculty transformed, campuses renewed and world changers developed 

  • Create a culture of humble dependence on God and bold expectation in God’s intention to start new witnessing communities throughout the campus and on new campuses 

  • Model – in person and through programs – InterVarsity’s vision and Core Values, including a biblically-defined commitment to engage every ethnic and social group on campus

The Young Adult Coordinator is part of the Family Ministry staff team that engages college‐age and young professional (age 18-26) people inside and outside Spanish River Church. This position will build and nurture a thriving relationship with like‐minded ministries on the FAU and Lynn University campuses to have a synergistic relationship that advances the Kingdom of God through the Gospel.   • Entrepreneurial. Able to cast vision, gather people and build ministry towards goals.
  • Passionate pursuit of Christ that is evident in life and relationships.
  • Humble approach to faith and ministry displaying a teachable spirit.
  • Enjoys working in a team environment, supporting those in parallel ministries and able to submit to authority.
  • Pursues team unity, bears with one another, and biblically handles conflict.
  • Operates with a high level of energy.
  • Enthusiastic about young adults thriving in a relationship with Christ.
  • Is able to engage culture from a Biblical worldview and disciple individuals accordingly.

Leadership and Ministry
  • Oversees the entire Young Adult Ministry by leading the ministry team to conduct every aspect of the Young Adult Night, LifeGroup discipleship, events, conferences, retreats, weekend trips, and mission trips.
  • Plans, coordinates and leads annual on-campus fall conference and annual out-of-town spring retreat.
  • Meets regularly with the Young Adult leadership to plan, coordinate tasks, set goals, implement the meetings and events, and training.
  • Plans the message series schedule for the Young Adult Night and is part of the speaking rotation.
  • Participates in the leadership of the events, including planning, scheduling, purchasing, and any necessary preparation to ensure its success.
  • Develops discipleship relationships with young adults, leading them to engage more deeply with Christ, have a more significant commitment to the church, and lovingly bring the gospel to unbelievers.

  • The Young Adult Coordinator reports to the Pastor of Family Ministries.
  • Meets bi‐weekly with the Pastor of Family Ministries to discuss ministry activities, set goals, evaluate ministry activities, and envision ways to improve and grow the ministry.

Summary

The incumbent serves as a Chaplain Clinical Pastoral Educator (CPE) performing senior-level clinical assignments. The incumbent provides comprehensive religious, spiritual, and pastoral care to all persons that are commensurate with the needs, desires, and voluntary consent of the Veteran, caregiver, or staff. The incumbent addresses the spiritual component of health and wellness in every patient care setting to ensure that pastoral care is fully integrated into all aspects of chaplain services.


Duties

Duties include but are not limited to:

  • Serves as a certified Chaplain (CPE) providing comprehensive, religious ministry services and training to Veteran patients and students according to their specific needs.
  • Carries out an education ministry with the CPE Center, which is highly integrated into VHA's Chaplain program. Provides thorough guidance and advice to Chaplain Service management staff, students, other Chaplains, and stakeholders.
  • Manages the daily operations of the CPE Center and develops and implements program policies and procedures. Serves as a certified educator of record for all CPE students for an assigned designated area. Provides administrative oversight and programmatic resources and monitors educational outcomes.
  • Offers students an opportunity to develop and expand professional caring skills in a clinical setting to address a person's spiritual, emotional, and physical needs; and offers students experience with hands-on spiritual care for hospitalized patients.
  • Maintains records for all educator evaluations, student records, center portfolio, and CPE accreditation requirements, which may include off-site CPE satellite and placement contracts.
  • Seeks approval for allied health trainee positions through the Office of Academic Affiliations (OAA). Conducts recruitment and interviews and selects students for the CPE program.
  • Ensures all documentation is completed for compliance. Develops educational curricula that are measurable, outcome-oriented, and evidence-based and designed to meet board certification competencies.
  • Develops relationships with key staff related to the CPE program, e.g., clinical preceptors, Advisory Group members, and OAA staff.
  • Provides extended and intensive pastoral counseling as an integral part of the treatment program with patients facing complex, ethical, moral, and/or spiritual issues.
  • Monitors the CPE Center's program effectiveness and modification of service pattern, which includes research and leadership of clinical teams. Develops and implements methods to measure the effectiveness of the Chaplain educational program.
  • Uses outcome evaluations to improve educational services and to design education system changes. Seeks best practices, primary research, and research literature that informs the ministry specialty and one's spiritual care practice.
  • Provides leadership, direction, orientation, coaching, in-service training, staff development, and continuing education programs.
  • Serves as a primary senior Chaplain education resource, spiritual advisor, and liaison for the spiritual needs of Veterans patients, students, caregivers, and staff.
  • Serves as a primary senior Chaplain education resource, spiritual advisor, and liaison for the spiritual needs of Veterans patients, students, caregivers, and staff.
  • Serves as a Chaplain senior representative and a fully recognized member of an interdisciplinary treatment team (IDT). Advises and collaborates with other senior members of the treatment team to provide comprehensive healthcare services to Veterans.
  • Engages in group consultative discussions or conferences with treatment professionals to provide senior-level Chaplain related input. Collaborates with IDT on the evaluation and review of VHA's CPE Center program progress.
  • Coordinates with community organizations to provide spiritual care and educational outreach, e.g., interested community organizations, local clubs, church groups, special agencies, business organizations, and other stakeholders to sustain the necessary links with the outside community.
Work Schedule: 8:00am to 4:30pm, Monday thru Friday
Telework: Not Available
Virtual: This is not a virtual position.
Functional Statement #: FS#000000 Chaplain (Clinical Pastoral Educator)
Relocation/Recruitment Incentives: Not Authorized
Permanent Change of Station (PCS): Not Authorized
PCS Appraised Value Offer (AVO): Not Authorized


Requirements

Conditions of employment

  • You must be a U.S. Citizen to apply for this job.
  • Selective Service Registration is required for males born after 12/31/1959.
  • Must be proficient in written and spoken English.
  • Subject to background/security investigation.
  • Selected applicants will be required to complete an online onboarding process. Acceptable form(s) of identification will be required to complete pre-employment requirements (https://www.uscis.gov/i-9-central/form-i-9-acceptable-documents). Effective May 7, 2025, driver's licenses or state-issued dentification cards that are not REAL ID compliant cannot be utilized as an acceptable form of identification for employment.
  • Must pass pre-employment physical examination.
  • Participation in the seasonal influenza vaccination program is a requirement for all Department of Veterans Affairs Health Care Personnel (HCP).
  • Complete all application requirements detailed in the "Required Documents" section of this announcement.
As a condition of employment for accepting this position, you will be required to serve a 1 or 2-year trial period during which we will evaluate your fitness and whether your continued employment advances the public interest. In determining if your employment advances the public interest, we may consider:
  • your performance and conduct;
  • the needs and interests of the agency;
  • whether your continued employment would advance organizational goals of the agency or the Government; and
  • whether your continued employment would advance the efficiency of the Federal service.
Upon completion of your trial period, your employment will be terminated unless you receive certification, in writing, that your continued employment advances the public interest.

Qualifications

Basic Requirements:

  • Citizenship. Be a citizen of the United States (U.S.). Non-citizens may be appointed when it is not possible to recruit qualified citizens according to 38 U.S.C. § 7407(a).
  • English Language Proficiency. Candidates must be proficient in spoken and written English in accordance with 38 U.S.C. § 7403(f).
  • Education. Applicants must possess a Master of Divinity degree or equivalent educational qualifications as evidenced by a graduate-level theological degree from a college, university or theological school accredited by a member of the Council for Higher Education Accreditation (CHEA) or Association of Theological Schools (ATS) and recognized by the U.S. Department of Education. NOTE: For applicants who do not possess a Master of Divinity degree or equivalent educational degree, an approved educational equivalency review from a nationally recognized board certification body for chaplains (see paragraph d) is acceptable.
  • Foreign Education. To be creditable, education completed outside the U.S. must be submitted to a current affiliate agency of the National Association of Credential Evaluation Services (NACES) at https://www.naces.org/members and be deemed at least equivalent to that gained in a conventional U.S. program.
  • CPE Educator. CPE Educators must be certified by an agency whose CPE units of training are recognized by the BCCI ® or a U.S. certifying body that has a reciprocity agreement with BCCI ®. CPE Educators must be certified by the same accrediting body as the CPE training program where the position is being filled for the CPE training program to maintain accreditation.
  • Ecclesiastical Endorsement. In accordance with 38 C.F.R. § 17.655, ecclesiastical endorsement is a condition of employment as a VA chaplain. An individual must possess and maintain a full and active ecclesiastical endorsement to be employed as a VA chaplain. Applicants must have an ecclesiastical endorsement, dated within the past 12 months. Ecclesiastical endorsements must be from the official national endorsing authority of the applicant's/employee's faith group or denomination. Ecclesiastical endorsement is a written official statement, by the official national endorsing body of the faith group or denomination, certifying that the applicant is in good standing with the applicant's faith group or denomination; and stating that the individual is, in the opinion of the endorsing body, qualified to perform the full range of ministry required in the VA pluralistic setting. Loss of endorsement will result in removal from the GS-0060 Chaplain series and may result in termination of employment. The National Chaplain Service maintains a list of approved endorsing organizations that can be found here: National VA Chaplain Service SharePoint.
  • Board Certification. Applicants must be a Board-Certified Chaplain certified by BCCI ® or a U.S. certifying body that has a reciprocity agreement with BCCI ®. Board Certification that requires 4 units of CPE is qualifying. The National Chaplain Service maintains a list of approved certifications found on the National VA Chaplain Service SharePoint.
May qualify based on being covered by the Grandfathering Provision as described in the VA Qualification Standard for this occupation (only applicable to current VHA employees who are in this occupation and meet the criteria).

Grade Determinations: GS-12
  • Specialized Experience. At the GS-12 level, the candidate must have one year of creditable experience equivalent to the next lower grade level, GS-11, that is directly related to the position to be filled. Specialized experience can be described as but not limited to: Providing advance care planning education, information, and counseling for patients and their families. Providing guidance and/or support for patients to express values through processes such as life review, oral history, and end of life preparation and documentation. Supporting the development of staff resiliency by providing emotional and spiritual support and compassionate presence and develops programs for staff development and wellness. Providing education and equipping other healthcare staff and trainees to screen for spiritual and religious needs, and the importance of appropriate referrals to chaplains for complex spiritual distress.
  • Certification. CPE Educators must be certified by an agency whose CPE units of training are recognized by the BCCI ® or a U.S. certifying body that has a reciprocity agreement with BCCI ®. CPE Educators must be certified by the same accrediting body as the CPE training program where the position is being filled for the CPE training program to maintain accreditation.
  • Demonstrated Knowledge, Skills and Abilities. In addition to the experience or education above, the candidate must demonstrate the following KSAs:
    • Ability to independently educate all levels of CPE students and plan, organize, and implement all levels of the CPE program.
    • Skill in adhering to all accreditation standards, processes and practices including, but not limited to, timely and professional submission of all required program reports, center portfolio, fees and dues.
    • Skill in written and verbal communication that are articulate, professional and cohesive.
    • Ability to recruit, interview and select students for the CPE program.
    • Knowledge of professional ethics for certified educators and history of CPE.
    • Ability to apply theoretical understanding for and competence in administering and conducting all levels of CPE programs.
    • Knowledge of emerging trends and research in the area of pastoral education.
    • Knowledge of diverse conceptual frameworks for developing educational curriculum.
Preferred Experience:
  • A certified Clinical Pastoral Educator from VA-approved professional organization and recognized by the Department of Education such as Association of Clinical Pastoral Education (ACPE)
  • Experience in providing educational supervision for Clinical Pastoral Education (CPE) to CPE Level 1 and CPE Level 2 students.
  • Experience in providing educational supervision for students seeking to become CPE Educator.
  • Experience in demonstrating skills in adhering to all CPE accreditation standards, processes and practices including, but not limited to, timely and professional submission of all required program reports, center portfolio, fees and dues.
  • Proficiency in Electronic Health Record (EHR) documentation (particularly Spiritual Assessments/Reassessments) and in teaching Joint Commission documentation standards of timeliness to CPE students.

Position Overview:

Embark on a transformative journey as the Coordinator of Youth Ministry at St. Joseph Catholic Church. We are on a mission to breathe life into our vision of helping people "meet, know, live, and share Jesus.” As the Coordinator of Youth Ministry, you will be responsible for nurturing spiritual growth within our Jr. High School and High School ministries through weekly gathering, events and more. You will foster a firm understanding of the teachings of the Church flowing from and leading to an encounter with Jesus. You will reach students who don’t know Jesus and collaborate with local efforts to bring his love to those on the periphery. With all of this, you’ll be supported by a collaborative team who is reliant on the Holy Spirit to anoint our efforts.


Responsibilities:


1. Youth Ministry Leadership:

  - Innovate and orchestrate dynamic programs and events that resonate with the spiritual and social needs of Middle School and High School students.

  - Cultivate an atmosphere that transcends traditional boundaries, fostering active participation and a genuine sense of community among the youth.

2. Faith Formation:

  - Curate and execute age-appropriate catechetical sessions, formation events, and retreats that go beyond the surface, delving deep into Catholic teachings for the youth.

  -Lead periodic youth trips like our yearly Mission Trip, DCYC, etc.

  - Propel the integration of faith into daily life, providing practical and relatable guidance that sparks lasting connections.

  - Assist Coordinator of Youth Sacramental Formation in forming teens before they receive Sacraments. 

3. Pastoral Care:

  - Forge meaningful relationships with youth and their families, serving as a beacon of pastoral support, guidance, and encouragement.

  - Tackle the unique needs of young individuals head-on, creating a sanctuary for discussions on matters related to faith and the issues they face.

  - Build and maintain a core team to assist in pastoral youth ministry efforts

4. Community Engagement:

- Unite with various ministries and organizations to weave a holistic tapestry of parish life, emphasizing the integral role of family involvement.

  - Spearhead community outreach initiatives that ignite a passion for service and compassion within the youth.

  - Supporting parents of our teens to equip them to be the primary catechists of their households.

5. Other Duties

  - Assist the team and commit to working together beyond the aforementioned roles

  - Support the school’s campus ministers in their efforts to bring their teens to Christ by assisting with retreats & building relationships at school lunches. 

  - Assist at Mass occasionally as needs arise

  - Be a team player


Qualifications:

- A fervent Catholic dedicated to understanding and embodying Catholic teachings.

- Preferred bachelor's degree in Theology, Pastoral Ministry, or a related field.

- Advantageous background in youth ministry or a related pastoral role.

- A maestro of interpersonal and communication skills, capable of translating Jesus' teachings into the language of the youth.

- Excellent grasp of the use of technology in ministry (Canva, Google, Office, Database software)

- Strong organizational and leadership abilities.

- Ability to work collaboratively with diverse groups of individuals.

- Infused with creativity and innovation to craft engaging and relevant youth programs.


Ministerial Character

The Pastor is the visible principle and foundation of unity in the parish of St. Joseph Catholic Church which the Bishop has entrusted to him.  He makes Christ’s mission present and enduring in the parish.  In order to fulfill his mission, the Pastor employs suitable, chosen collaborators (clerics, religious, or lay people).  He shares with them his mission and entrusts various responsibilities to them.

Positions employed at St. Joseph Catholic Church help to extend the ministry of the Pastor in particular ways as outlined in the job description.  Therefore, the employee in this position is closely connected to and assists the Pastor in the performance of his ministry and thereby engages in ministry for the Church.

post_html:
Minister of Administration - Cornerstone Baptist Church
 

The Minister of Administration provides leadership and oversight for the administrative and operational needs of Cornerstone Baptist Church. This position helps ensure the church's facilities, finances, administrative practices, security, and kitchen ministry are managed effectively and responsibly. The Minister of Administration works alongside the Senior Pastor, ministry leaders, staff, and volunteers to provide the operational support needed for the church to carry out its ministry. 

Our church is a thriving church family in Arlington, Texas. The Word of God is priority here because it is the foundation and source of life. Relationships are also an intricate and life-giving part of this church.

Cornerstone Baptist Church was founded by Rev. Wm. Dwight McKissic, Sr. in October of 1983. From the first service with 9 adults and 15 children, God has blessed Cornerstone to grow into a church of over 3,000 with an average attendance of 1,100 plus on any given Sunday. We are greatly honored by your presence and seek to serve you in any way that will spiritually enrich your life.

Cornerstone was formed to corporately and publicly worship, praise, glorify, and give thanks to the Trinity, God the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit; to minister the Word of God to believers; to promote fellowship among the body of Christ; and to promote evangelism at home and abroad. In short, our purpose is to exalt the Savior, evangelize sinners, edify the saints and elevate society.

If interested, please submit a resume.

At Northwestern Medicine, every patient interaction makes a difference in cultivating a positive workplace. This patient-first approach is what sets us apart as a leader in the healthcare industry. As an integral part of our team, you'll have the opportunity to join our quest for better health care, no matter where you work within the Northwestern Medicine system. We pride ourselves on providing competitive benefits: from tuition reimbursement and loan forgiveness to 401(k) matching and lifecycle benefits, our goal is to take care of our employees. Ready to join our quest for better?

Job Description

The Chaplain reflects the mission, vision, and values of NM, adheres to the organization’s Code of Ethics and Corporate Compliance Program, and complies with all relevant policies, procedures, guidelines and all other regulatory and accreditation standards.

A chaplain offers spiritual guidance and pastoral care to patients, families, and hospital staff/medical staff. As representatives of spiritual and/or religious traditions, chaplains use insights and principles of psychology religion, spirituality, and theology.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Delivers a ministry of spiritual care, counseling, consultation, worship, prayer, sacraments, and spiritual/ emotional support services to patients, families, and hospital personnel/medical staff for the optimal holistic care of patients.
  • Identifies and clarifies ethical dilemmas. Findings will be shared with the Ethics Committee Chairs to determine whether an ethics consult is necessary per site policy/procedure.
  • Participates in and provides appropriate leadership in interdisciplinary clinical team activities related to planning and coordinating patient care, including care conferences, team meetings, nursing rounds, palliative care rounds, IDT meetings, and family conferences when appropriate.
  • Provides end of life support, bereavement support as needed.
  • Provides education to patients and hospital personnel/medical staff on Advanced Directives including Power of Attorney for Healthcare and Goals of Care conversations.
  • Develops and leads spiritual care services within the hospital in collaboration with other members of the Spiritual Care Department.
  • Serves as spiritual liaisons between the hospital and community (both religious and secular) with referrals and information with patient/family permission that is compliant with HIPAA regulations.
  • Escalates any concerns or issues following the NM chain of command policies.
  • Offers religious services to hospital personnel/medical staff as appropriate and when requested.
  • Accepts on call for spiritual care coverage, crises and emergencies as assigned including nights, weekends, and holidays. Manager may assign required minimum on-call shifts.
  • Assists in leading CALM/Mindful Moments as assigned or as needed.
  • Attends to cultural and spiritual dynamics that may improve patient treatment and family dynamics.
  • Maintains chapel/sacred spaces and workspaces in a neat fashion while keeping supplies available and stocked.
  • Maintains board certification and/or minimum annual CEU requirements as set by certifying bodies and organization/industry standards.
  • Performs other duties as assigned by the Manager of Spiritual Care

Qualifications

Minimum Requirements:

Education:

  •  Master’s degree in theology, religion, pastoral care, spiritual care, or divinity from an accredited institution or equivalent combination of education and experience

Description

A Clinical Pastoral Care resident or (CPE resident) is a person admitted into and participating in a yearlong Clinical Pastoral Education Program under supervision as developed by Association for Clinical Pastoral Education (ACPE) Inc. The individual provides pastoral care and spiritual support to patients, staff, and families as well as other job functions as assigned.



Responsibilities
  1. CPE resident Education and Function
  • Participates in all aspects of the training program according to ACPE and OLOL standards, which includes entering into meaningful learning and ministry relationships that exhibit professionalism and openness to learning.
  • Works with a variety of faith traditions and assigned institutional populations to ensure spiritual care that meets ethical and professional standards for ministry in the healthcare setting.
  • Performs systematic compiling of pastoral care data for department reports and research.
     

      2.  Chaplaincy Care with Patients and Families

  • The CPE resident develops and implements a plan of care to promote patient well-being and continuity of care and facilitates the expression of the patient's spiritual practices.
  • The CPE resident models and collaborates with the organization and its interdisciplinary team in respecting and providing culturally competent patient-centered care. The CPE resident ministers to all person regardless of faith, race, affiliation, or orientation.
     

      3. Chaplaincy Care for Staff and Organization

  • The CPE resident provides pastoral care to the organization in ways consistent with the organization's values and mission statement. The CPE resident presides at memorial services and other special services.
  • The CPE resident provides timely and sensitive pastoral care to the organization's staff via individual and group interactions. The CPE resident facilitates crisis debriefings, provides pastoral care for unit services and special events.
     

      4. Maintaining Competent Chaplaincy Care

  • The CPE resident assumes responsibility for continued professional development, demonstrates a working and current knowledge of current theory and practice, and integrates such information into practice.
  • The CPE resident practices evidence-based care including ongoing evaluation of new practices and when appropriate, contributes to or conducts research.
  • Demonstrates the ability to teach and educate through articulating and intergrading current research of best practice.


Qualifications

Experience
At least Three months functioning in a spiritual ministry role

Education
Bachelor’s degree, and Graduate degree in theology or related field from an accredited seminary or theological school is preferred.

Training
Completion  of one introductory unit of Clinical Pastoral Education (CPE) through the Association for Clinical Pastoral Education (ACPE) 
and
Commitment to completing the 4 units of Residency CPE.

Skills
Appropriate ecclesial endorsement
Fluent in English. 
Knowledge and skill in dealing with spiritual dynamics of illness, loss, and death. 
Ability to function as a member of an interdisciplinary team. Strong interpersonal, teamwork, and communication skills. 
Commitment to professional growth and development, ecumenical openness to working in a pluralistic setting. 
Computer proficiency

SUMMARY

The Lead Student Pastor at Pinelake Church, Clinton Campus, will lead, shepherd, and guide the spiritual development of High School, Middle School and 56 Ministry students through multiplied servant leader development. Our vision is to see Mississippi changed one life-change story at a time. The Lead Student Pastor will serve as a key leader to bring this vision to life as we learn from Christ, live in Christ and lead others to Christ.

GENERAL RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Learn
    • Pursue a growing relationship with Jesus through consistent time in God’s Word and prayer.
    • Continually grow in your understanding of the Jesus-Centered Life (salvation, identity, life, and authority in Christ).
    • Remain teachable and hungry, seeking feedback, learning from others, and developing both spiritually and professionally.
    • Cultivate awareness of God’s presence in everyday life, listening to the Holy Spirit and responding in obedience.
  • Live
    • Practice and model the rhythms of Be the Church (Grow, Pray, Connect, and Share).
    • Pursue emotional health by engaging in self-awareness, addressing past wounds, and cultivating honest, healthy relationships.
    • Practice healthy rhythms, prioritizing your relationship with Jesus and your family.
    • Embody a life of integrity and surrender, allowing your private life with God to shape your work.
  • Lead
    • Take ownership of disciple-making by personally investing in others and helping them move toward a Jesus-Centered Life.
    • Walk others through the Discipleship Pathway (Essentials → JCL → Be the Church), helping them discover and take their next step.
    • Shepherd people, not just programs, by listening for where God is at work in their story and walking with them toward transformation.
    • Equip and release others by developing Servant Leaders and multiplying disciples who Learn from Christ, Live in Christ, and Lead others to Christ.
    • Measure success by life change, spiritual formation, and multiplication—not just attendance or activity.
  • Embrace the Culture
    • Value and embody the staff values, which we call the 7 H’s: Humility, Honor, Honesty, Hunger, Holy Spirit, Health, and Harmony.
    • Communicate clearly, honestly, and proactively in a way that builds trust, unity, and momentum.
    • Work in alignment with the church vision and leadership.
    • Participate fully in the life of your campus or team, contributing to the unity, health, and shepherding of the faith family.

SPECIFIC LIST OF DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

    • Disciple and lead students toward a growing relationship with Jesus.
    • Recruit, onboard, and develop a team of servant leaders to engage High School, Middle School, and 56 Ministry students and families.
    • Work with student ministry colleagues centrally and across campuses to align with Pinelake’s unified vision for student ministry.
    • Facilitate the planning, oversight, and evaluation of all components of the High School, Middle School and 56 Ministry student gatherings, including serving as the primary communicator.
    • Creatively plan and promote events and opportunities for student engagement and growth, such as retreats and summer camps.
    • Lead the development of student small groups in alignment with Pinelake’s small group strategy of discipleship.
    • In coordination with the Family Pastor, create and lead a vibrant discipleship plan for parents of students, providing regular on-ramps for parenting growth and development.
    • Develop relationships with the administrators and students in area high school and middle school campuses and be present through in-school visits, attending extra-curricular functions, and serving as a resource to the schools.
    • Actively and intentionally connect with area local schools through in-school visits, attending extra-curricular functions, and serving as a resource to the schools.
    • Prepare and manage the budget for all student ministry under the oversight of the Family Pastor.
    • Provide oversight for and leadership to Pinelake’s Our House Promise strategy within Student Ministry.
    • Engage students in local, national, and international missions experiences in collaboration the Missions Team.
    • Be a prayer champion for the families and students of Clinton.
    • Serve as an active part of the Clinton Campus Staff Team under the leadership of the Clinton Campus Pastor.
    • Provide pastoral care to those in need.

Summary

This position is part of Department of War. The incumbent will be responsible for serving as the principal Subject Matter Expert (SME) to the Minister/Chief of Defense (MoD/CHOD) and the Commander, Military and Security Authority (MISA) on all aspects of national-level Security operations. Oversees and approves contractor military security SMEs work concerning development of security infrastructure and Mil. security officer training within the MISA, partners Armed Forces, and Mil. installations.


Duties

This position is located in the Defense Security Cooperation Agency (DSCA), Defense Security Cooperation Service (DSCS).
As a Ministry of Defense Advisor at the GS-0301-15 some of your typical work assignments may include:

  • Ability to select and apply appropriate evaluation and measurement techniques to determine partner nation's progress, measure Institutional Capacity Building (ICB) accomplishments, and align outcomes with Combatant Command (CCMD) theater campaign goals and DoW policy direction.
  • Mastery Knowledge of interpersonal relations, diplomatic tact, and political-military acumen required to establish credibility and exert peer-to-peer influence within complex, multi-national environments.
  • Possess expert knowledge of ICB core processes (strategy and policy, force management, human resources management, acquisition and logistics, resource management, and defense governance) and the focus areas supporting security cooperation.
  • The ability to work independently, with a high degree of initiative and resourcefulness, to develop solutions to complex and sensitive problems that are not subject to treatment by commonly used methods.
  • The incumbent is recognized as an expert in developing and interpreting guidance on Security program planning and evaluation.
  • The incumbent must be highly original and use sound judgment to formulate, evaluate, and ensure implementation of programs and policies pertaining to Ministry of Defense Advisor (MoDA)/ICB issues.


Requirements

Conditions of employment

  • Must be a U.S. citizen
  • Males born after 12-31-59 must be registered for Selective Service http://www.sss.gov
  • Resume and supporting documents (See How To Apply)
  • Suitable for Federal employment, determined by a background investigation. Incumbent must obtain and maintain a Special Sensitive/ Top Secret w/ SCI
  • May be required to successfully complete a probationary period
  • Work Schedule: Full time
  • Overtime: Occasionally
  • Tour of Duty: 36 Months
  • Recruitment Incentives: May be authorized
  • Fair Labor Standards Act (FLSA): Exempt
  • Financial Disclosure: Not Required
  • Telework Eligibility: This position is situationally telework eligible
  • Subject to the 5 year foreign area limitation DODI 1400.25-V1230 72612
  • This position is designated as a Testing Designated Position (TDP) under the civilian Drug-Testing Program.
  • Employee must successfully complete Foreign Affairs Counter Threat (FACT) Training in accordance with Department of State, 13 FAM 301.4-2.
  • Employee is required to obtain an Official passport and Visa as specified in the Department of Defense Foreign Clearance Guide for Qatar.
  • Employee will be subject to pre-employment medical requirements and must meet Foreign Service Medical Clearance requirements
  • The incumbent may be required to work other than norm al hours, which may include evening, weekends, and/or holidays and/or overtime
  • Incumbent may be required to use government provided housing and lodging while overseas
  • Must attain DoD SCW Certification IAW with the NDAA 2017, Title 10 USC, Section 384 and Security Cooperation Certification Program 2.0. requirements.

Qualifications

You may qualify at the GS-15, if you fulfill the following qualifications:

One year of specialized experience equivalent to the GS-14 grade level in the Federal service:

  • Serves as the principal subject matter expert to the Minister/Chief of Defense (MoD/CHOD) and the Commander, Military and Security Authority (MISA) or equivalent on all aspects of national-level Security operations;
  • Advise the Minister/Chief of Defense and MISA Commander or equivalent on national security strategy, threat landscape, and security level postures;
  • Collaborates enterprise-wide security program change management efforts across the national security enterprise to achieve mission assurance;
  • Facilitates planning and readiness for the partners security enterprise, crisis response efforts, incident management, and joint exercises;
  • Coordinates with U.S. federal agencies, DoW to include the military departments, and other U.S. private organizations to implement the partners Military Security Officer training program;
  • Analyzes and evaluates issues regarding development in terms of impact to broader U.S. SC and security assistance goals and objectives. Provides ICB input into long-term DoW ICB planning;
  • Prepares written assessments and reports, coordinating ICB visits and representing DoW as a primary Security point of contact for ICB efforts with MoD counterparts.
All applicants must meet qualifications and eligibility criteria by the closing date of the announcement.

Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community, student, social). Co-Groups and Small Groups

Ministry Execution

  • Support volunteer teams and ministry environments during weekly gatherings.

PROFESSIONAL AND SPIRITUAL EXPECTATIONS

  • Commitment to personal and active participation in the fulfillment of the Great Commission.  
  • Exhibit a lifestyle appropriate to a person in public Christian ministry by conducting life with the utmost integrity in all situations. 
  • Exemplify the humility of Christ and a loving, servants heart in all facets of leadership. 
  • Consistent attendance and participation in the life of the church and the YA ministries. 
  • Demonstrate a personal passion to minister to people within the context of the local church. 
  • Solid interpersonal skills with the ability to communicate effectively with staff and volunteers. 
  • Self-motivated and able to initiate projects, work independently, and troubleshoot. 
  • Possess a high attention to detail. 
  • See this opportunity as a calling from the Lord and not simply another job.

post_html:
Director of Children and Family Ministry - Westminster Presbyterian Church
 

About Westminster Presbyterian Church

Westminster Presbyterian Church is a growing, Christ-centered church family just minutes from  uptown Charlotte, NC. Our vision is to be a church who invites people to life in Christ…lived 
together… for the sake of others. We are committed to making disciples of all generations and cultivating relationships across generational lines within our own church family. We are a 
church family who values the covenant promises of baptism such that Children and Family Ministry is at the heart of who we are together. 

Westminster is a member congregation of the ECO denomination- a Covenant Order of 
Evangelical Presbyterians. 

Position Summary

The Director of Children and Family Ministry will be a creative, relational, and resourceful leader who fosters a culture where children are discipled, families are equipped, and volunteers are encouraged. 
We envision a ministry that cultivates the joy of the Lord and deep connection to the applicant's family in the lives of our children. The Director will lead, develop, and oversee ministry for children (birth through 5th grade) and their families, creating a biblically based, Christ-centered, safe, and engaging environment where children can receive a firm foundation for a growing relationship with God.

Supervision & Collaboration
• Reports to: Senior Pastor
• Partners closely with pastoral staff and key ministry leaders (including youth leadership) to support smooth transitions and aligned discipleship for children and families
• Receives support and feedback through: regular 1:1s, clear annual goals, and periodic ministry review

Key Responsibilities

Primary Priorities (First 6–12 Months)

• Deliver consistent, safe, joyful Sunday programming for children (birth–5th)
• Recruit, train, and care for volunteers so teams are supported and sustainable
• Strengthen parent partnership and clear, timely communication with families
• Improve coordination and transitions between children’s ministry and youth ministry

Ministry Leadership

• Plan, implement, and evaluate children’s ministry programming (Sunday School, Children’s Worship, Vacation Bible School, seasonal events, etc.)
• Select and adapt age-appropriate curriculum that is biblically based, theologically sound, and engaging for children
• Cultivate a welcoming environment that is joyful and grounded in Christ’s love
• Support children with diverse learning and behavioral needs by helping volunteers use wise, calm, and appropriate adaptations

Volunteer Coordination

• Recruit, train, and support adult volunteers for children’s ministry
• Provide spiritual encouragement and practical resources for those serving in the ministry
• Set volunteers up to succeed and build healthy connections with children

Family Engagement

• Partner with parents as the primary spiritual nurturers of their children
• Offer resources, events, and opportunities for families to grow together in faith administration

• Steward children’s ministry spaces, budget, and resources to cultivate a joyful, engaging, vibrant environment
• Ensure all children’s ministry programs comply with church safety and child protection policies

Qualifications

• A mature and growing faith in Christ, with a passion for nurturing the faith of children and families
• Knowledge and love of Scripture as the Word of God
• Commitment to the essential tenets of ECO ECO-CONSTITUTION
• Prior experience leading children’s ministry in a church or Christian ministry setting
• Strong leadership, communication, and organizational skills.
• Proven ability to build warm, meaningful relationships with children, parents, and 
volunteers
• Facility with technology and media for communication and teaching
• Bachelor’s degree 
• Applicants must be legally authorized to work in the United States at the time of hire. 


Employment eligibility will be verified in accordance with applicable laws. WPC will not sponsor employment visas for this position.

How to Apply
If interested in applying for this position, please submit a cover letter, résumé, and three references.

This is a lead children’s ministry role for the Mclean Bible Church Montgomery County Location (MBC MoCo).  Montgomery County is the largest county in Maryland with a population of over one million people.  It’s widely known for its ethnic and cultural diversity, economic affluence, high percentage of adults with postgraduate degrees, as well as being a hub for scientific research and US government offices.  Montgomery County, along with bordering areas, provides a unique opportunity to reach the nations for Christ in a post-Christian context. 

MBC MoCo is a multigenerational church family that includes young adults, families, transient professionals, and long-time residents, representing all kinds of ethnic, social, and cultural backgrounds.  Although we’re diverse in age, we remain steadfast in creating ministry environments that strategically evangelize and disciple the emerging generation.  Kid’s Quest (KQ) is our ministry to infants-5th grade children that aims to encourage and equip children to be disciples of Jesus Christ who makes disciples.  KQ averages about 220+ children in attendance on Sunday mornings and requires our largest volunteer team at MBC MoCo.  

The Children Ministry Director is a full-time position that provides direction and oversight for the entire KQ ministry, which is experiencing rapid growth.  Under the leadership of our pastors, the Children's Ministry Director will take a leading role in creating a discipleship pathway that invests in the spiritual formation of children, and a strategy for equipping parents to fulfill their calling as the primary spiritual leaders of their children.  The Children's Ministry Director is also responsible for managing a team of staff and volunteers who partner with families in our church to teach children how to follow Jesus and lead others to Jesus. 


Duties and responsibilities (Essential Functions)


The following items describe some of the ways this individual will accomplish this task:


1.    Ministry to Children

  • Provide vision, strategy, & development for all Children’s Ministry environments (infants– 5th grade).
  • Oversee the implementation of all curricula for the teaching environments (Nursery, Preschool, Elementary).
  • Create environments, activities and programming for Elementary children (K-5th grade) that will facilitate learning and encourage spiritual growth.
  • Teach large group lessons regularly on Sunday mornings to Elementary children.
  • Maintain a strategy for reaching and assimilating new children and families.
  • Create and maintain a clear communication plan that keeps families informed on ministry updates.
  • Manage the annual budget for children’s ministry and oversee/approve expenses.
  • Develop and maintain a safe, clean, aesthetically pleasing learning environment for all KQ areas.
  • Establish, implement and adhere to MBC’s safety and security policies that protect minors in our care.
  • Plan and oversee special KQ events for children. 
  • Collaborate with KQ staff across MBC locations in the planning and execution of Kid’s Summer Camp.
  • Remain a student of children’s ministry, self-educating through reading and attending conferences for growth.

2.   Ministry to Parents

  • Identify and provide resources that make disciple-making in and through the home natural and easy for KQ families. 
  • Oversee the baptism application process for children at MBC MoCo.
  • Plan and oversee the processes for special ceremonies including 2nd Grade Bible Presentations and Parent Commissioning’s.
  • Provide care for children and families within the church including intercessory prayer, hospital visits and follow-up. 
  • Consult with MBC Pastors and the Director of Classes in creating classes or hosting conferences that equip parents to be the primary spiritual leaders of their children. 

3.    Ministry Collaboration

  • Provide leadership and manage KQ staff member(s). 
  • Provide leadership, direction, training, and appreciation for all Children’s Ministry volunteers.
  • Establish, implement, and hold accountable all KQ staff and volunteers to adhere to MBC’s safety and security policies that protect minors in our care.
  • Lead the Elementary ministry team on Sunday mornings. 
  • Meet regularly with MBC MoCo NextGen ministries staff to discuss overall family ministry strategy and effectiveness.
  • Meet regularly with MBC MoCo staff to discuss overall day-to-day ministry strategy and effectiveness at the MoCo location.  
  • Collaborate with KQ staff across MBC locations to evaluate effectiveness of ministry across locations, share resources and plan KQ Summer Camp.
  • Support Church Group Leaders in cultivating an environment that engages children in the word and prayer within groups ministry. 
  • Collaborate with the Connect & Hospitality ministry team in ensuring the NextGen check-in process for families runs smoothly on Sunday mornings. 
  • Coordinate Childcare for ministry leader meetings or key events at MBC MoCo
  • Assist with any other Location events outside of KQ as required by the Location Pastor (e.g., church picnics, prayer nights and family events)


Qualifications

  • Must be a passionate disciple of Jesus Christ who continually seeks to abide in Christ and demonstrates the biblical requirements for leaders.
  • Must be a proven disciple-maker who, by God’s grace, has made disciples who make disciples. 
  • Must be a spiritually mature leader who demonstrates that maturity in both personal and public life.
  • Must be a servant leader with a demonstrated ability to lead others sacrificially on mission.
  • Must have a minimum of two years of children’s ministry (Direct oversight and leadership of ministry staff - paid or volunteer staff members and/or a large volunteer team of 25+ volunteers – is preferable, but not required). 
  • Must be able to relate to children and their families and have a passion to see families grow in their faith together.
  • Must be able to work flexible hours including weekends and holidays.  
  • Must be able to recruit and develop teams to fulfill the mission of MBC.
  • Must be passionate about serving children and parents. 
  • Must be able to work well with others as an encouraging and supportive team member.
  • Must be an effective communicator. 
  • BA or BS degree desirable.


Working Conditions


  • Full-Time Position: The Children's Ministry Director typically works Sunday through Thursday and may be required to work occasional evenings and Saturdays for special projects, as well as occasional holidays like Christmas and Easter.
  • This job operates in a professional office environment. This role routinely uses standard office equipment such as computers and phones.
  • This position requires up to 0% local travel.


Physical Requirements


Must be able to read, speak, and hear. Must be able to effectively communicate both orally and in writing. While performing the duties of this job, the individual is regularly required to sit, talk, hear, walk, bend, kneel, and lift. 

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job.

Overview

Presbyterian Homes & Services Walnut Ridge is seeking a Campus Pastor to support our community.  The Campus Pastor is responsible for providing spiritual guidance, counsel and comfort to the residents and staff. Sound inter-personal relationships, which are built on Christian values and principles, form the basis of
practice and service.

 

The Presbyter Campus Pastor reports to the Site Leader or Pastoral designee, and may supervise and mentor diaconal pastors.

 

 

ABOUT THIS COMMUNITY

 

Walnut Ridge is a beautiful senior living community located near I-35/80, adjacent to the walking trails and aquatic center in Clive and in close proximity to several restaurants, retail shops and medical facilities.  The campus is comprised of 116 independent living apartments, 44 assisted living apartments, 18 memory care assisted living apartments and a beautiful skilled care center for 60 residents.  The campus also houses an exceptional wellness center and warm water swimming pool that employees are encouraged to enjoy.

 

Address:  1701 Campus Drive, Clive, Iowa

 

As an employee you can take advantage of a variety of amenities such as:

*  Free employee meals

*  Free Wellness Center access (family members welcome)

*  Great walking paths

*  Access to bus route

*  Attractive comprehensive benefit package

Walnut Ridge is located in the Des Moines' western suburb of Clive in close proximity to Urbandale, West Des Moines, and Waukee.

 

 

Responsibilities

  1. Assist in maintaining an environment that achieves high quality care and service for residents (physical, mental, emotional, social and spiritual) and maintain their independence and dignity to the highest degree possible. Establish and maintain effective communication systems with all customers.     
  2. Implement, organize and coordinate the Spiritual Care (Worship, Sacraments, Prayer, Bible Studies, and PHS’ Programs) program to enhance the care and services for residents. In accordance with resident requests and desires, provide for Sunday worship and chapel services throughout the week. Plan, arrange/conduct special events for Christmas, Easter, Thanksgiving, Lent and Advent and other special holiday services. Schedule and arrange services for all major resident denominations using outside clergy as needed. Serve or arrange for the serving of communion. Conduct small Bible studies on a weekly basis. Visit and pray with residents on an individual basis. Document visits. Maintain accurate records and reports on all resident programming and visits. Provide specialized services to the dementia care program residents. Implement PHS’ spiritual care programs Blessing of the Hands, Procession of Honor and others. Support Hospice programs and staff as appropriate.      
  3. Establish and maintain effective working relationships with outside agencies and organizations Promote Presbyterian Homes and its ministry at assorted church functions. Participate with the various community constituencies to achieve mutually beneficial results. Coordinate spiritual services collaboratively with Pastoral Care Director and other professionals inside and outside PHS. Participate in local and conference ministeriums as directed              
  4. Visit residents on a regular basis on campus. Participate in care conferences and family conferences as required. Communicate and document appropriate resident information in resident file, maintaining confidentiality. Conduct funeral and memorial services when requested. Provide pastoral counseling, personal support and guidance to residents and families experiencing life changes, including death of a resident. Provide emergency pastoral care as needed.
  5. Provide bereavement follow-up of families for a one-year period after the death of a resident as appropriate or needed.  Document visits/interactions. Conduct regular memorial services for residents who have passed away. Provide referral services for families and staff. Maintain an ongoing process of support for the staff as needed during times of crisis or following significant deaths. Collaborate with Learning and Development staff to identify and deliver on-going staff and volunteer education regarding care-giving, grieving, the role of faith in health care, spirituality and aging, etc. Act as a liaison between resident/family and “home” church and/or act as the pastor for those residents without a church, regardless of denomination.         
  6. Implement established spiritual care services and policies, procedures and practices.  Use quality management process to meet resident needs. Ensure compliance with regulations and established best practices. Apply the knowledge and skills needed for the position, including technical competence in the field and current knowledge of laws and regulations affecting your position. Maintain current knowledge of community resources available for residents.  Use discretion and independent judgment to compare and evaluate possible courses of action and decision-making. Maintain knowledge of organization and industry policies and practices.   
  7. Evaluate and monitor Diaconal pastors every week meeting quarterly with Senior Director of Pastoral Care Services for the first year after hire, as applicable.
  8. Manage resource allocations in order to achieve or exceed operational goals.  Demonstrate good stewardship of available resources.
  9. Lead and support the integration of Christian Culture in the community; reinforce the Christian heritage and culture through communication and education and support systems; recognize the importance of spiritual matters to PHS employees as well.       

Qualifications

  1. Bachelor’s degree and a Master of Divinity (M.Div.) degree from an accredited theological seminary or equivalent
  2. Three years of experience in a church setting or other pastoral care/chaplaincy ministry preferred. One unit of clinical pastoral education (CPE) is preferred.
  3. Specific requirements:
    1. Demonstrate the ability to make independent decisions.
    2. Ability to tactfully deal with residents, family members, staff, visitors, outside public, and church organizations.
    3. Demonstrate good moral character.
    4. Plan, organize, develop, and implement goals and objectives necessary for delivering pastoral care program dependant on the size, hours allocated and need of the community...
    5. Ecclesiastical endorsement by a recognized religious denomination.
    6. Agreement with the mission statement, vision and values of Presbyterian Homes, espousing an evangelistic pastoral commitment. Demonstrated compatibility with PHS's mission and operating philosophies.
  4. Demonstrated computer proficiency including Microsoft Office and other common computer programs.
  5. Demonstrated ability to read, write, speak and understand the English language to communicate with all customers.

Benefits

Full-time benefits-eligible employment begins at a minimum of 30 hours per week:

  • Health, and dental, including applicable HSA & FSA
  • Employer Contribution to HSA for eligible Health Plans
  • Life insurance (AD&D)
  • Retirement, with eligibility for an employer match
  • Holiday pay and extended sick

 

Full and Part-time benefits-eligible employment working between 20-29 hours per week:

  • Vision insurance
  • Voluntary short-term & long-term disability
  • Accident & hospitalization coverage
  • Education assistance programs

 

All employees:

  • Accrue PTO (Paid time off)
  • Same-day pay
  • Employee assistance program (EAP)
  • College partnership educational discounts
  • Access to Learn to Live Resources

About PHS

8

Presbyterian Homes & Services (PHS), based in St. Paul, Minnesota, is a nonprofit, faith-based organization providing a broad array of high-quality housing choices, care and services options for older adults. Some 8,000 employees serve more than 41,800 older adults through 60 PHS-affiliated senior living communities in Minnesota, Iowa and Wisconsin, and through Optage® home and community services. PHS is also co-owner of Genevive, the largest geriatric primary care practice in Minnesota, providing comprehensive care for more than 15,500 older adults. Established in 1955, PHS has earned the reputation as an innovative leader dedicated to promoting independence, purposeful living and the overall well-being for those they serve. Today, PHS is one of the largest nonprofit providers of senior housing and services in the nation.

 

 

PHS is an EEO/AA employer. All applicants will receive consideration for employment regardless of their race, color, creed, religion, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, disability, age, marital status, or status with regard to public assistance.

Riverview Alliance Church
Associate Pastor of Discipleship

Ministry Profile

Position Summary
The purpose of this position is to facilitate the spiritual growth of men, women and children of
Riverview Alliance Church. Working as a team with the Lead Pastor and Elders, the role of the
Associate Pastor is to coordinate, oversee and provide leadership for outreach, evangelism
and spiritual growth ministries directed towards the younger families, young adults, youth and
children in Oconto Falls and the surrounding area.

Responsibilities
The Associate Pastor of Discipleship carries the following responsibilities:

  • To work as a team with the Lead Pastor and Elders.
  • Outreach and Evangelism: The Associate Pastor will be involved in developing outreach& evangelism ministries that will directly target the young families of Oconto Falls and the surrounding area.
  • Discipleship: The Associate Pastor will develop and oversee discipleship ministries for our children, youth, and young adult and young families. Note: Although this is not a “Youth Pastor” position, the Associate Pastor will oversee and be involved in the youth ministries.
  • Social Media: The Associate Pastor will lead in developing a Social Media presence for

Riverview Alliance Church.

  • Worship: The Associate Pastor will attend and be directly involved in the worship ministries of Riverview Alliance Church.
  • Preaching/Teaching: The Associate Pastor will fill the pulpit of Riverview Alliance Church as necessary and in coordination with the Lead Pastor.
  • Other Ministries:The Associate Pastor may be asked to participate or officiate at weddings; funerals; baptisms and community events.
  • On occasion, the Associate Pastor may also be asked to assist in other ministries within the church.

Qualifications

  • The person called to this ministry must have the qualifications of an Elder, as outlined in 1 Timothy 3.
  • He must be in agreement with the Christian and Missionary Alliance (C&MA) statement of faith.
  • He must be licensed by the C&MA
  • He must be ordained or be willing to begin the ordination process of the C&MA

Characteristics

  • The pastor called to this ministry must have a professed faith in Jesus Christ as Lord and Savior of his life.
  • He must be fully committed to serving the Lord Jesus Christ and living under His Lordship.
  • He must be a student of the Word of God.
  • He must be committed to personal, spiritual transformation and growth.
  • If married, he must lead a godly family.
  • He must be self-motivated.
  • He must have a passion for the lost.
  • He must be able to develop caring relationships with young families and youth.
  • He must be willing to submit to those in authority over him

Accountability

  • The Associate Pastor will be directly accountable to the Lead Pastor
  • He will be expected to give a monthly report to the Governing Board of the Riverview Alliance Church.
  • He will participate and contribute as needed in Elder’s meetings

To be considered for this position, please complete the application to include your testimony, resume and other background information related to the position.

If the district office has reviewed your application and they think you may be a potential match for the position, then the hiring manager will reach out to you for next steps.

This position requires licensing with The Christian & Missionary Alliance. To learn more about The Alliance and requirements for licensing, please visit our website
