Campus Staff Minister – Columbia University (Graduate & Faculty Ministry)

Work Location:

New York

Job Type:

Full time

God has called InterVarsity to plant and to build witnessing communities of students and faculty who follow Jesus on college and university campuses. Through these groups, we believe ever- increasing numbers of students and faculty from all ethnic groups and areas of the campus will be transformed by the Gospel. We expect to see campuses increasingly become places where people, ideas, and structures flourish to the glory of God. We confidently anticipate that our InterVarsity alumni will become change agents across the country and around the world. We pursue this calling by discerning and actively participating in what God is already doing on campus. This is the essence of being a Campus Staff Minister (CSM).

Please complete and submit the GFM Interest Form before completing the full application for a position with Graduate & Faculty Ministries in our online system. We will contact you when we are ready to proceed with the application process. ​


This position is open to candidates interested in part-time or full-time positions serving graduate students and faculty at Columbia University in New York City, NY. A geographic pay adjustment may be available depending on cost of living for location and fundraising capacity.

ESSENTIAL COMMITMENTS/RESPONSIBILITIES 

Spiritual Growth 

You pursue maturity as a disciple of Jesus Christ so that your life and work increasingly reflects a growing love for God, God’s Word, God’s people of every ethnicity and culture, and God’s purposes in the world. To do this, you will: 

  • Pursue a vibrant relationship with the triune God through engagement with Scripture, prayer, and worship, both individually and in community 

  • Develop self-leadership (growing in self-awareness, self-management, relational integrity, and resiliency) 

  • Embrace Scriptural standards for behavior and attitudes 

 

Campus Leadership 

You communicate and model InterVarsity’s vision to see students and faculty transformed, campuses renewed and world changers developed 

  • Create a culture of humble dependence on God and bold expectation in God’s intention to start new witnessing communities throughout the campus and on new campuses 

  • Model – in person and through programs – InterVarsity’s vision and Core Values, including a biblically-defined commitment to engage every ethnic and social group on campus 

  • Lead students and faculty – individually and collectively – through Scripture, prayer, teaching, and discipleship experiences, so that they articulate and align their ministry activities around this vision 

  • Set annual goals through prayer, research and reflection with your teams (students, faculty, and staff) for qualitative and quantitative growth, including conversions and leadership development 

 

You create, develop, align and leverage ministry plans, programs, teams, and structures to close the gap between current reality and the aspirational goals. 

  • Build leadership teams who trust and partner well with you and who demonstrate spiritual vitality, relational health, and mission alignment 

  • Develop and execute plans to achieve annual goals, evaluating and modifying the plan as needed throughout the year 

  • Increase momentum for the vision by aligning programs, structures, conferences and teams around the goals 

  • Mobilize students and faculty to engage their relational networks with the gospel and to start new missional communities 

  • Under the direction of the Area Director, may supervise Ministry Interns and Campus Ministry Interns as delegated 

 

You intentionally gather, invite, and develop diverse groups of students and faculty so that they not only encounter and follow Jesus as Savior and Lord but also advance the mission on campus as participants and leaders. 

  • Create ways for faculty and students to encounter and follow Jesus through Scripture, worship, prayer, mission experiences, conferences, etc. 

  • Equip students and faculty so that they think strategically about campus engagement and so that they proclaim – in word, deed, and power – the good news of Jesus, regularly inviting students and faculty to follow him as Savior and Lord 

  • Disciple students and faculty by equipping them to hear the Word, respond actively, and debrief and interpret the experience so that they grow in Christlikeness, reflect our Core Values, and develop ministry skills 

  • Invite, coach, and equip students and faculty to become increasingly effective participants and leaders, including starting new witnessing communities on campuses 

 

Organizational Collaboration 

You work with a network of other local, area, regional, and national InterVarsity staff and volunteers so that our work reflects Biblical standards of excellence, integrity, and partnership. 

  • Partner with and respond positively to the direction and coaching of your supervisors and national leaders 

  • Contribute to collaborative and productive team meetings and relationships 

  • Affiliate chapters under your care and submit Graduating Student Forms in order to increase our partnership with current students and alumni 

  • Use national ministry resources and tools, as requested, including recruiting and/or participating in local, regional, or national conferences as  

  • Complete reporting, planning and review requirements in a timely way so that you and your supervisors can assess and improve your work as a CSM 

  • Comply with all InterVarsity policies and procedures 

 

Ministry Partnership Development 

You will develop a team of partners – churches and individuals (including alumni and community members) – who will resource the ministry financially, in prayer, or volunteer service that advances the mission. 

  • Raise 100% of the financial budget assigned by your supervisor 

  • Communicate regularly with your ministry partners, nurturing the relationship through visits, phone calls, emails and regular prayer letters 

  • Develop on-going, long-lasting partnership with alumni and volunteers 

  • Comply with all Ministry Partnership Policies 

  • Identify and invest in advocates who will build networks of volunteers and donors on InterVarsity’s behalf 

 

Accomplish all other assigned tasks as appropriate 

 

QUALIFICATIONS (common to all levels of CSM) 

  • Annually affirm InterVarsity’s Statement of Agreement (Doctrinal Basis and Purpose Statement). Abide by InterVarsity’s Code of Conduct. Believe and behave consonantly with InterVarsity’s Human Sexuality Theological Paper. Affirm and behave consonantly with InterVarsity’s “Women in Ministry Statement of Affirmation” 

  • Bachelor’s degree for CSMs assigned to a four-year campus. A minimum of an Associate’s degree for CSMs assigned to a two-year campus or a community college 

  • Strong interpersonal skills (including ability to minister to diverse ethnic communities and faculty) 

  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills 

  • Demonstrated problem solving skills 

  • Familiarity with word processing, presentation, email, and spreadsheet software 

 

WORK ENVIRONMENT/PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS 

The CSM position leads ministry in a college campus environment. A designated office space may or may not be available. The CSM is required to travel to on-campus and off- campus sites as appropriate. Off-campus travel includes, but is not limited to: student ministry conferences, Ministry Partnership Development meetings, and InterVarsity- sponsored training sessions, meetings, and conferences. The CSM is regularly required to communicate with others, and routinely uses standard office equipment such as computers, phones, photocopiers, filing cabinets, etc.

A parsonage, and a congregation that lives in two languages

Hope Lutheran Church is calling a solo pastor to serve a bilingual congregation in Annandale, Virginia, seven miles from Washington, DC. A move-in-ready parsonage is provided, with utilities covered — a real home, available now, in one of the most expensive housing markets in the country.

Hope was organized in 1957. About fifty people worship here each week, in English and in Spanish, and the Spanish service is not an add-on: it grew from one Sunday a month into a weekly service because the congregation kept showing up for it. Members call Hope "the little church that could." It is small, it is genuinely diverse, and it has spent decades working in Annandale rather than talking about it — a founding member of the Annandale Christian Community for Action, twenty years of adult ESL classes, backpacks and food drives with Annandale High School, quilts for Lutheran World Relief, a monthly seniors' luncheon in its thirty-fifth year, and the local relief effort for Puerto Rico after Hurricane Maria.

Where Hope is growing right now is with children. Sunday Bible school keeps adding students, Vacation Bible School runs every summer, and the music program has grown enough that children now take part in worship itself rather than sitting through it.

Hope owns its building and its parsonage, rents out a third building on the property, and has been debt-free since 2018, when the last of the mortgage was paid off.

Who we are in Christ

Hope is a Lutheran congregation, which means we start from grace: God's love comes to us as a gift, not a reward, and it comes to everyone at the same table. We gather every week around Word and Sacrament, and we do it in two languages because the Gospel has never belonged to one. At Pentecost each person heard the good news "in their own language" (Acts 2:6), and that is still the church we are trying to be. We believe the body of Christ is bigger than any one denomination, which is why we welcome the gifts of our full communion partners as our own.

What this pastor will do

  • Preach and preside at worship in both English and Spanish, every week
  • Lead and reshape ministry with Annandale's Hispanic and immigrant community — the heart of Hope's work and where it is growing
  • Help members across four generations grow spiritually, with particular attention to children, teens, and young families
  • Build on a children's ministry that is already growing — Sunday Bible school, Vacation Bible School, and a music program bringing children into worship
  • Represent Hope beyond its own walls — with neighboring congregations, local non-profits, and local and state government. A fifty-person church extends its reach through partnership or it does not extend it at all.
  • Expand Hope's social ministries, and start new ones
  • Build shared community inside the congregation and beyond its doors
  • Develop leaders — the aim is ministries that outlast any one pastor
  • Reinvigorate adult ESL, which ran for two decades and has been waiting for new leadership

What this call requires

  • Ability to preach, teach, lead worship, and provide pastoral care with fluency in both English and Spanish. This is a requirement of the position, not a preference. Hope worships in both languages every week.
  • Cultural competence with the Hispanic community, not Spanish alone. Many of Hope's neighbors are immigrant families under real pressure, and they can tell the difference.
  • Ordination as a Minister of Word and Sacrament in the ELCA or one of its full communion partner churches (preferred), or candidacy with a synod bishop's recommendation — including through TEEM, and including approved candidates awaiting a first call, whose ordination follows the call. Normal preparation is a bachelor's degree and a Master of Divinity, and study still in progress is welcome. Whether preparation is sufficient is the synod's candidacy decision, not ours. Ordained in a partner church? Please read the next section — it is written for you.
  • A willingness to treat a fifty-person congregation like a mission congregation. Hope is asking for growth, and is honest that membership has declined and its givers are aging.

ELCA and full communion partner pastors: preferred

We are looking first for a pastor of the ELCA or of one of the six churches the ELCA is in full communion with:

  • The Episcopal Church
  • Presbyterian Church (U.S.A.)
  • Reformed Church in America
  • United Church of Christ
  • Moravian Church in America (Northern and Southern Provinces)
  • The United Methodist Church

Full communion means our churches recognize one another's ministries and share one table. A minister ordained in any of these churches can serve an ELCA congregation under the full communion agreements (for most partners, the Orderly Exchange of ordained ministers), and the Metro DC Synod office handles the arrangement. If that is you, we would genuinely like to hear from you.

Ordained somewhere else? There is still a path: reception onto the ELCA roster. It takes longer, and the synod office will tell you what it involves in your case. Write to us anyway.

Either way it starts in the same place: contact the Metro DC Synod office, and write to us as well.

What Hope offers the pastor

An office manager and a working Council that carry administration, legal, and financial detail. A cadre of volunteers who show up and need someone to build them into teams. A small church where a pastor does a bit of everything and has room to grow into it. Fertile ground: an engaged Spanish-speaking community already at the door. And virtual worship and study offerings kept from the pandemic years.

Compensation

$75,000–$95,000 per year, depending on experience, plus a move-in-ready parsonage with utilities covered by the congregation. This is defined compensation under the Metro DC Synod's 2026 guidelines, and it does not include the value of the parsonage or its utilities; pension and health coverage (through Portico Benefit Services, the ELCA's benefits ministry, for ELCA clergy) and expense reimbursement are provided in addition.

What the parsonage is worth. The Metro DC Synod's 2026 compensation worksheet values housing in a provided parsonage at roughly $25,000 to $32,000 a year for a call at this level, and the congregation pays its utilities on top of that. In practical terms, this call carries the housing that a comparable salary elsewhere would have to buy in one of the most expensive markets in the country.

Also provided: four weeks of vacation a year, including three Sundays · two weeks of continuing-education time a year, which may accumulate for up to three years · a $3,000 annual allowance for professional expenses, synod meetings, and continuing education, at least $500 of it for continuing education · mileage for church business at the IRS rate, within limits set in the Letter of Call · parental leave of at least six weeks with full salary, housing, and benefits · moving expenses, negotiable

How this call works

Our Ministry Site Profile is approved by the synod bishop and live. Candidates are introduced through the synod. The call committee interviews, the congregation votes by a two-thirds majority, and the Letter of Call is countersigned by the bishop.

If you are rostered, the fastest way to be considered is to ask your synod office to forward your Rostered Minister Profile to the Metro DC Synod.

One piece of process, said plainly: the Letter of Call itself goes to a minister on the ELCA roster of Ministers of Word and Sacrament, or to a candidate our synod bishop recommends for this congregation (ELCA constitution ∗C9.02). That is the constitution we serve under rather than a preference of ours — and it is a question the synod settles, not one we decide here. So if you are not on that roster today, treat it as a starting point rather than a stop sign. Write to us anyway.

A resume and short letter of interest is welcome if you'd like to send one. Links to two recorded sermons — one in English, one in Spanish — are welcome but not required. Please do not send references at this stage.

Interview accommodations are available on request.

Priority review begins Monday, October 26, 2026; open until filled.

Pastor(a) Solo(a), Tiempo Completo — Bilingüe Inglés/Español
Iglesia Luterana Hope · 4604 Ravensworth Rd, Annandale, Virginia 22003
Iglesia Evangélica Luterana en América · Sínodo Metro DC

Una casa pastoral, y una congregación que vive en dos idiomas

La Iglesia Luterana Hope busca llamar a un pastor o una pastora para servir a una congregación bilingüe en Annandale, Virginia, a siete millas de Washington, DC. Se provee una casa pastoral lista para habitar, con los servicios públicos cubiertos — un hogar de verdad, disponible ya, en uno de los mercados de vivienda más caros del país.

Hope se organizó en 1957. Unas cincuenta personas adoran aquí cada semana, en inglés y en español, y el culto en español no es un añadido: pasó de ser un domingo al mes a ser semanal porque la congregación siguió llegando. Sus miembros llaman a Hope "la iglesita que sí pudo." Es pequeña, es realmente diversa, y lleva décadas trabajando en Annandale en vez de hablar de ello — miembro fundador de Annandale Christian Community for Action, veinte años de clases de inglés para adultos, mochilas y colectas de alimentos con la escuela secundaria de Annandale, colchas para Lutheran World Relief, un almuerzo mensual para personas mayores que va por su trigésimo quinto año, y el esfuerzo local de ayuda a Puerto Rico después del huracán María.

Donde Hope está creciendo ahora mismo es con la niñez. La escuela bíblica dominical sigue sumando estudiantes, la Escuela Bíblica de Vacaciones se realiza cada verano, y el programa de música ha crecido lo suficiente como para que los niños ya participen en el culto en vez de solo sentarse a escucharlo.

Hope es dueña de su templo y de su casa pastoral, alquila un tercer edificio en la propiedad, y no tiene deudas desde 2018, cuando terminó de pagar la hipoteca.

Quiénes somos en Cristo

Hope es una congregación luterana, y eso significa que partimos de la gracia: el amor de Dios nos llega como un regalo, no como un premio, y llega a todas las personas en la misma mesa. Nos reunimos cada semana en torno a la Palabra y el Sacramento, y lo hacemos en dos idiomas porque el Evangelio nunca ha pertenecido a uno solo. En Pentecostés cada persona escuchó la buena noticia "en su propia lengua" (Hechos 2:6), y esa sigue siendo la iglesia que queremos ser. Creemos que el cuerpo de Cristo es más grande que cualquier denominación, y por eso recibimos como propios los dones de nuestras iglesias en comunión plena.

Lo que hará esta pastora o este pastor

  • Predicar y presidir el culto en inglés y en español, cada semana
  • Dirigir y renovar el ministerio con la comunidad hispana e inmigrante de Annandale — el corazón del trabajo de Hope y donde está creciendo
  • Acompañar el crecimiento espiritual de cuatro generaciones, con atención particular a la niñez, la juventud y las familias jóvenes
  • Fortalecer un ministerio con la niñez que ya está creciendo — la escuela bíblica dominical, la Escuela Bíblica de Vacaciones, y un programa de música que está integrando a los niños al culto
  • Representar a Hope más allá de sus propias paredes — con congregaciones vecinas, organizaciones sin fines de lucro, y el gobierno local y estatal. Una iglesia de cincuenta personas amplía su alcance mediante alianzas, o no lo amplía.
  • Ampliar los ministerios sociales de Hope, y crear nuevos
  • Construir comunidad dentro de la congregación y más allá de sus puertas
  • Formar líderes — la meta son ministerios que perduren más allá de cualquier pastor
  • Reactivar las clases de inglés para adultos, que funcionaron por dos décadas y esperan nuevo liderazgo

Lo que requiere este llamado

  • Capacidad para predicar, enseñar, dirigir el culto y ofrecer cuidado pastoral con fluidez en inglés y en español. Es un requisito del puesto, no una preferencia. En Hope adoramos en ambos idiomas cada semana.
  • Competencia cultural con la comunidad hispana, no solamente el idioma. Muchos de nuestros vecinos son familias inmigrantes bajo presión real, y saben notar la diferencia.
  • Ordenación como Ministro de Palabra y Sacramento en la ELCA o en una de sus iglesias en comunión plena (preferible), o candidatura con la recomendación de un obispo sinodal — incluida la vía TEEM, e incluidas las personas aprobadas para la ordenación que esperan su primer llamado, cuya ordenación sigue al llamado. La preparación habitual es una licenciatura y una Maestría en Divinidad, y damos la bienvenida a quienes aún están estudiando. Si la preparación es suficiente lo decide el proceso de candidatura del sínodo, no nosotros. ¿Fue ordenado u ordenada en una iglesia en comunión plena? Lea la próxima sección — está escrita para usted.
  • Disposición para tratar a una congregación de cincuenta personas como una congregación misionera. Hope pide crecimiento, y reconoce con franqueza que su membresía ha disminuido y que quienes sostienen la ofrenda van envejeciendo.

Pastores de la ELCA y de sus iglesias en comunión plena: preferibles

Buscamos en primer lugar a un pastor o una pastora de la ELCA o de una de las seis iglesias con las que la ELCA está en comunión plena:

  • La Iglesia Episcopal
  • La Iglesia Presbiteriana (EE. UU.)
  • La Iglesia Reformada en América
  • La Iglesia Unida de Cristo
  • La Iglesia Morava en América (Provincias del Norte y del Sur)
  • La Iglesia Metodista Unida

La comunión plena significa que nuestras iglesias reconocen mutuamente sus ministerios y comparten una misma mesa. Una persona ordenada en cualquiera de estas iglesias puede servir en una congregación de la ELCA conforme a los acuerdos de comunión plena (para la mayoría, el Intercambio Ordenado de ministros), y la oficina del Sínodo Metro DC se encarga del proceso. Si ese es su caso, de verdad nos gustaría saber de usted.

¿Fue ordenado u ordenada en otra tradición? Todavía hay un camino: la recepción en el registro de la ELCA. Toma más tiempo, y la oficina del sínodo puede explicarle lo que implica en su caso. Escríbanos de todos modos.

En ambos casos comienza en el mismo lugar: comuníquese con la oficina del Sínodo Metro DC, y escríbanos a nosotros también.

Lo que Hope ofrece a su pastor(a)

Una gerente de oficina y un Concilio activo que llevan la administración y los asuntos legales y financieros. Un grupo de voluntarios que da la cara y necesita a alguien que los forme en equipos. Una iglesia pequeña donde quien pastorea hace un poco de todo y tiene espacio para crecer en ello. Terreno fértil: una comunidad hispanohablante ya comprometida y a la puerta. Y las opciones virtuales de culto y estudio que se conservaron de los años de la pandemia.

Compensación

$75,000–$95,000 al año, según la experiencia, más una casa pastoral lista para habitar con los servicios públicos cubiertos por la congregación. Corresponde a la compensación definida según las guías 2026 del Sínodo Metro DC y no incluye el valor de la casa pastoral ni de sus servicios; la pensión y la cobertura médica (a través de Portico Benefit Services, el ministerio de beneficios de la ELCA, para el clero de la ELCA) y el reembolso de gastos se proveen adicionalmente.

Cuánto vale la casa pastoral. La hoja de compensación 2026 del Sínodo Metro DC valora la vivienda en una casa pastoral provista en aproximadamente $25,000 a $32,000 al año para un llamado de este nivel, y la congregación paga además los servicios públicos. En la práctica, este llamado incluye la vivienda que un salario comparable tendría que pagar en uno de los mercados más caros del país.

También se provee: cuatro semanas de vacaciones al año, incluidos tres domingos · dos semanas al año para educación continua, acumulables hasta por tres años · una asignación anual de $3,000 para gastos profesionales, reuniones del sínodo y educación continua, de la cual al menos $500 es para educación continua · millaje por asuntos de la iglesia según la tarifa del IRS, dentro de los límites que fije la Carta de Llamado · licencia parental de al menos seis semanas con salario, vivienda y beneficios completos · gastos de mudanza, negociables

Cómo funciona este llamado

Nuestro Perfil del Sitio Ministerial está aprobado por el obispo sinodal y está activo. Las candidaturas se presentan a través del sínodo. El comité de llamado entrevista, la congregación vota por mayoría de dos tercios, y la Carta de Llamado lleva la firma del obispo.

Si usted está en el registro, la vía más rápida es pedir a su oficina sinodal que envíe su Perfil de Ministro al Sínodo Metro DC.

Una nota de proceso, dicha con franqueza: la Carta de Llamado se extiende a una persona inscrita en el registro de Ministros de Palabra y Sacramento de la ELCA, o a quien nuestro obispo sinodal recomiende para esta congregación (constitución de la ELCA ∗C9.02). Es la constitución bajo la cual servimos, no una preferencia nuestra — y es algo que resuelve el sínodo, no nosotros. Así que si hoy usted no está en ese registro, tómelo como un punto de partida y no como una puerta cerrada. Escríbanos de todos modos.

Si desea enviar una breve carta de interés, la leeremos con gusto. Los enlaces a dos sermones grabados — uno en inglés y otro en español — son bienvenidos pero no requeridos. Por favor no envíe referencias en esta etapa.

Ofrecemos adaptaciones para la entrevista a solicitud.

La revisión prioritaria comienza el lunes 26 de octubre de 2026; abierto hasta cubrirse.

Description

Location Worship Director (GT)

Please note that this posting is intended to gather resumes for consideration for a future opportunity. While the position is not currently being filled, we are reviewing submissions to identify individuals we may connect with as the role becomes available.

Location: Georgetown

Reports To: Central Worship Director/Georgetown Location Pastor

 

Summary of Role

The Location Worship Director leads, plans, and coordinates the worship experience and Worship Dream Team at Celebration Church’s Georgetown Location, serving under the direction of the Central Worship Pastor and in alignment with the vision of Celebration Worship.

 

Position Status & Schedule

  • Exempt, Salary
  • Full-Time (40 hours)
  • Sunday through Thursday: may include weekends and evenings
  • Christmas, Easter, Pursuit Weeks (January/August), and Dream Team Appreciation service dates and times are black out days for time off. Major conferences are required workdays for this position. There may be other events that you are required to work outside of your normal schedule, you will be informed in advance of any of these requirements.

 

Essential Functions & Responsibilities

 

Service and Event Coordination

  • Coordinate and manage the execution of worship experiences at the Georgetown location
  • Lead worship vocally at weekend services, events, and conferences as needed
  • Foster a culture of worship that aligns with the church’s mission and values
  • Collaborate with ministry leaders to ensure cohesive worship experiences
  • Maintain central standards, systems, and expectations for services and events
  • Assist with the planning and execution of special worship events and conferences

 

Administration and Oversight

  • Liaise with the Central Worship Pastor to ensure alignment within worship with and church-wide goals
  • Liaise with Georgetown Location Pastor to ensure location-specific goals and needs are met
  • Maintain operational standards for worship at your location
  • Manage worship-related budgets, purchases, and equipment needs for the location

 

Team Development

  • Build and develop dream team members, fostering growth and skill enhancement through relational leadership and our Development Program
  • Manage/operate the Development Program at the Georgetown location
  • Promote a culture of excellence and continuous improvement, implementing the core values of Celebration Church and the Spiritual Standards of Celebration Worship
  • Provide ongoing mentorship for spiritual growth and provide/coordinate pastoral care for Dream Team volunteers

 

Contribute to the overall success of the Celebration Church by performing all other duties as assigned

 

Requirements

  • Mature Christian who calls Celebration Church home and supports the Church’s culture, vision, and values
  • Unwavering commitment to place Christ first in all you do
  • Desire to ensure people are known, loved, and celebrated
  • Continually seeking growth with Christ and encouraging others to do the same
  • Passion for excellence, always looking to improve
  • Deep understanding of the value of being part of a family that is unified for a greater cause
  • Must have completed all steps of Connection Point within 60 days of hire

Competencies

  • Proven worship leadership experience within a church setting
  • Passion for developing leaders and growing a strong, unified worship culture
  • Proficiency in leading worship vocally and instrumentally
  • Team builder able to recruit, train, and mentor musicians and vocalists
  • Excellent leadership, communication, and organizational skills
  • Self-motivated and determined with a strong work ethic 
  • Ability to inspire and lead a diverse team of staff and volunteers, especially in a fast-paced, live creative environment
  • Strong proficiency with Ableton, Planning Center, and other worship technology
  • Proficient in macOS, Microsoft Office Suite, Rock Database, Planning Center Online
  • Willingness to work occasionally outside normal business hours

 

Education & Experience

  • Minimum 3 years Worship experience at a church
  • Minimum 3 years in a Worship environment with high-level leadership responsibilities
  • Leading within a multi-location experience preferred

Work Environment & Physical Demands

  • Must be able to remain in a stationary position 50% of the time.
  • Must be able to occasionally move about inside the office and Church facility.
  • Must be able to position self to maintain supplies and equipment on lower shelves and in closets.
  • Often move supplies and equipment weighing up to 40 pounds
  • Constantly work in an open office environment
  • Ability to work outside in various climates and temperatures 

Other Information

Celebration Church is an equal employment opportunity employer to the extent required by law applicable to religious institutions. This job description is not inclusive and often includes other responsibilities. Duties, responsibilities, and activities may change and/or new ones assigned at any time with or without notice.

post_html:
The Residency Program is offered to qualified male candidates who have graduated from seminary and are seeking ordination as ministers of the gospel. Candidates are selected for the Residency Program based on demonstrated leadership ability and the potential to play a significant role in the work of church renewal as pastors. After successful completion of the Residency Program, many residents become excellent candidates to serve as lead pastors of churches in need of renewal, assistant/associate pastors of larger churches within Resound’s network, or church planters, depending on gifting and opportunity.


Residents:

  • Work full-time at the local church in supervised ministry for a two-year period, with select opportunities to teach, preach, facilitate worship, lead a Community Group, participate in a specific area of ministry, and engage in mission and evangelism;
  • Participate in a series of modules focused on leadership, preaching, mission, pastoral care, cultural dynamics, and church renewal;
  • Receive an annual stipend plus health care benefits.


If you have any questions, please email Andrew Smith at asmith@resoundproject.org.

The role of Campus Pastor is fulfilled by one who has a deep love for the local church and a clear calling to lead the congregation of one of our regional campuses to accomplish the Great Commission and the Great Commandment. This posting is not for a specific, current opening, but instead is for applicants who want to be considered for future campuses and opportunities.

WHAT YOU WILL DO

Maintain and Grow a Healthy Church

  • Evaluate trends and build strategies to improve the health and growth of the campus. This includes reaching the unchurched/dechurched, salvations, baptisms, church membership, spiritual maturity, ministry involvement, mission involvement, small groups, discipleship classes, and all other key areas of church health.
  • For the growth of the congregation, the Campus Pastor (CP) functions as the vision caster for the campus. Each Saddleback campus shares the same macro-vision, core ministry models, signature ministries, branding, doctrine, and video teaching; however, each campus has a responsibility to reach and have a vision for its community.

Shepherd the Flock

  • Care for the congregation by providing counseling, prayer, hospital visits, serving communion, performing baptisms, weddings, and funerals, serving as Minister of the Day, and an all-around pastoral presence at weekend services and special events.
  • Engage relationally by meeting new people, discovering their stories, making connections, and continually looking for ways to guide them into taking the next step in their spiritual journey.

Develop Strong Staff and Volunteer Leaders

  • Build and develop an effective, impactful, and healthy staff team by leading the hiring processes, providing spiritual care, developing their skill sets, and empowering them for their work of ministry.
  • Champion the development of every member to be used by God in ministry. The CP is the primary recruiter and ministry mobilizer. They are the door opener for ministry involvement.

Have an Eye for the Details

  • Responsible for the annual budgeting process, financial oversight, staff budget management, cost control, etc.
  • Responsible for managing timesheet approvals and payroll changes.
  • Responsible for leading the hiring process for all staff positions at their campus.

WHAT YOU HAVE DONE

  • Led a local church or large ministry with multiple components
  • Built healthy and growing ministries
  • Communicated dynamically from the stage
  • Developed leaders in varied ministries
  • Supervised staff at all levels
  • Demonstrated continuous learning through university and seminary courses

WHO YOU ARE

  • Leader - A servant by example. Able to mobilize volunteers and staff. Understands strategy and the spirit in which we execute such strategy at Saddleback. Able to engage with large groups of attendees and members very quickly, relating to each individually while extending care and love.
  • Purpose Driven - Doesn’t just understand Saddleback's Purpose Driven Church model but has our DNA, is a raving fan, and is called to build a PD Church as they lead others to live a life balancing the 5 purposes.
  • Innovator - An ability to contextualize ministry, provide solutions and creatively reach their community. An ability to try new ideas and not give up. Like a church planter, a CP is passionate about going into the unknown and building something out of nothing. Able to take risks and learn from failure.
  • Planner / Implementor - An ability to plan and implement large projects and ministry events. Able to handle details without losing perspective and collaborate with a team to accomplish objectives.
  • Builder - An ability to lead, develop, equip, and empower teams, volunteers, and staff for ministry. Able to see the value in volunteers and multiply volunteers constantly.
  • Implementor - Must be equally comfortable maintaining existing systems and ministries as well as developing/growing new ones.
  • Compelling Communicator – Able to connect one-on-one or in front of thousands, exuding love with relaxed energy. Able to cast vision and inspire the staff and the congregation into action. Assures believers and unbelievers alike that they are welcome and wanted.

WHAT WE OFFER

  • Highly competitive benefits plans. Health plans with employee low deductible medical (EPO and PPO), dental, and vision coverage at no cost to the employee. Family coverage is as low as $250 per month for full health benefits.
  • 403(b)-retirement plan with employer contribution.
  • Generous holiday and paid time off plans including paid week off between Christmas and New Year’s Day.

 

Saddleback Church’s pay philosophy is based on internal and external data for pay equity, along with budgetary considerations for effective stewardship. Pay will be provided at a range of $85,000.00 - $90,000.00 annually. We will provide a pay rate that is within our salary structure and that fits a candidate’s qualifications and experience for the job. A wage range posted is not a guarantee of a specific wage for a job offer.

Saddleback Church is both an equal-opportunity employer and a faith-based religious organization. We conduct hiring without regard to race, ethnicity, national origin, citizenship, age, sex, marital status, membership in any labor organization, political ideology, or disability of an otherwise qualified individual. The status of Saddleback Church as an equal opportunity employer does not prevent us from hiring staff based on their religious beliefs so that all employees share the same religious commitment which is central to our mission.

GENERAL PURPOSE OF POSITION:

The Special Assistant position was created to ensure the GMP/CEO can focus on high-level leadership while the assistant manages critical administrative and governance support of the office. The Special Assistant provides strategic thinking, operational excellence, and trusted relationship with the CEO. Success in this role comes from effectively managing the complexities of the GMP/CEO’s office by using good judgement, independent discretion, and sound decision-making around responsibilities, while communicating effectively with the GMP/CEO and working closely with the Chief of Staff. The assistant serves as a primary point of contact and bridge between the GMP/CEO, staff, Board, and external stakeholders.

ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS AND RESPONSIBILITIES:

Strategic Implementation:

The Special Assistant is responsible for working alongside the GMP in implementing the strategies of the GMP’s office.

  • Maintain full knowledge of the GMP’s goals and priorities.
  • Align daily and long-term goals and priorities with the GMP’s vision for the office and the organization.
  • Identify efficiencies that are needed both technologically and otherwise to ensure that the priorities can be accomplished within deadlines.

 

Special Projects:

  • Oversee special projects, track progress, and ensure deadlines are met.
  • Provide leadership for logistics and support necessary for GMP initiatives, with attention to details, working collaboratively with internal and external partners.
  • Coordinate with the Chief of Staff on special projects and events and act as a project manager to ensure projects and events are completed within the scope and on time.
  • Conduct research on specific policies or topics and prepare concise written reports or oral briefings for the GMP, working collaboratively with internal and external stakeholders.
  • Understand the outcomes established for all projects, key performance indicators, and desired goals established by the GMP, structuring work for their efficient achievement.

 

Communications & Media:

TITLE: Kids Ministry Coordinator

REPORTING: Family Ministries Director

STATUS: Full-time, Exempt



POSITION DESCRIPTION

The Kids Ministry Coordinator leads childhood discipleship and family ministry at the campus level by helping create a space where kids feel known, safe, and excited to learn who Jesus is in a way that sticks. This role focuses on relational volunteer leader development, behind-the-scenes administrative organization, and equipping parents to act as the primary disciplers of their children throughout the week.


Through Sunday leadership and intentional volunteer care, this role ensures weekends run smoothly, leaders feel supported and developed, and families are warmly welcomed into a thriving, mission-aligned discipleship pathway.



CHARACTER 

  • A growing follower of Jesus, who genuinely loves kids and families, displaying a clear commitment to model, lead, and disciple people to take deep (knowing Jesus) and wide steps (serving others) to follow Jesus.
  • Relational and approachable, enjoying connecting with people, building trust, and showing high relational warmth to staff, volunteers, leaders, parents, and congregants. 
  • Organized and dependable, following through on commitments, handling administrative details well, and serving with excellence and integrity. 
  • Comfortable leading volunteers with clarity, encouragement, and care while modeling a healthy, balanced leadership rhythm. 
  • Values-aligned, living out Crossroads' beliefs and values (connect, grow, serve, give, and invite) in everyday life. Leads with love, serves with excellence and integrity, communicates with clarity and grace, empowers others, embraces innovation, demonstrates humility and a hunger to develop, and lives our mission daily.


RESPONSIBILITIES

  1. Reproduce Culture – Embrace and replicate Crossroads’ culture within all kids ministry environments. Hold self and volunteers accountable with attitudes and interactions that reflect our core values.
  2. Cultivate Volunteer Leadership – Recruit, onboard, and schedule volunteers using Crossroads systems and processes. Build relationships with your team by meeting regularly to encourage, support, and celebrate them regularly.  Help volunteers feel confident by equipping them with clear expectations and best practices.  Ensure each classroom is fully staffed and set up for success each weekend, and step in to problem-solve when last-minute needs or gaps arise.
  3. Kids Connection & Caregiver Engagement – Be a warm, relational presence for families, especially those who are new, helping them feel comfortable, confident, and cared for from their first visit on.  Communicate clearly about what kids are learning, execute relational first-time family follow-up, and manage ongoing engagement. Communicate upcoming events and invite the next step opportunities.  Support kids and parents or caregivers in taking meaningful next steps in their faith journey, helping grow the ministry by building trust, strengthening relationships, and inviting others into serving.  Partner intentionally with parents to equip them as the primary spiritual leaders of their children
  4. Execute initiatives and Events –. Partner with the Family Director to plan and execute campus-specific events (child dedications, seasonal events, parent gatherings, volunteer appreciation, etc.). Help bring these moments to life through strong organization, communication, and volunteer coordination to reflect our heart and mission.
  5. Collaboration & Alignment –Work closely with your Campus Team to stay connected to the life of your campus.  Partner with the Family Ministry Director for support, feedback, and ongoing development.  Maintain strict alignment with Crossroads Kids systems, curriculum, safety standards, and volunteer processes, participating in regular check-ins and team rhythms to stay connected and supported. 


SKILLS AND COMPETENCIES

  • Strong leadership development, volunteer management, and team-building capabilities, including a passion for equipping adult and youth volunteers.
  • High emotional intelligence and a deep understanding of childhood spiritual development and family discipleship practices.
  • Excellent organizational skills, database management, and project tracking.
  • Strong communication skills, with the ability to cast vision clearly to groups of parents, volunteers, and kids
  • Technology proficient (e.g., church database systems, check-in kiosks, communication platforms, and collaboration tools).


DUTIES

  • Help create a welcoming, fun, and safe environment where kids love to be.
  • Lead the setup and tear-down of  spaces so everything is ready to go before services begin.
  • Ensure classrooms are clean, stocked, and prepared for both kids and volunteers.
  • Execute the programming and curriculum in a way that feels smooth and engaging.
  • Be the go-to person on Sundays for volunteers, kids, and parents or caregivers of kids.
  • Maintain safety, check-in/ check-out procedures with consistency and care.
  • Follow established guidelines around childcare guidelines, background checks, required trainings, allergies, behavior, health, and incident reporting to create a safe environment for every child.
  • Attend staff meetings, retreats, and conferences as delegated.
  • Provide appropriate care, support, and resource tools to parents and leaders throughout the week.


QUALIFICATIONS

  1. Education: Associate’s or Bachelor’s degree required, preferably in ministry, early childhood education, leadership or a related field.
  2. Experience: Demonstrated ability to lead teams, manage multiple priorities, navigate technology/audio tools, and understand the childhood discipleship process. Proven success in leading technical or relational volunteer environments and executing large-scale family ministry events. 
  3. Gifting: Aptitude for administration, shepherding, and teaching.


WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE

  • Flawless Sunday Execution: Kids spaces are consistently safe, clean, fully stocked, and completely set up before services begin, utilizing check-in and security systems with absolute care.
  • Thriving Volunteer Culture: Volunteers are systematically recruited, scheduled, and onboarded. Team members feel personally known, celebrated, and confident in their roles due to clear communication and robust mid-week support.
  • Equipped & Connected Families: New families feel instantly welcomed and secure. Parents feel fully resourced with clear communication regarding weekly lessons, upcoming events, and practical strategies to act as the primary disciplers at home.
  • Collaborative & Unified Posture: Campus events—like child dedications and seasonal gatherings—are executed with organizational excellence in lockstep with the Family Ministry Director, consistently reflecting the ministry's core standards.


WORK SCHEDULE

  • Full-time, requiring regular weekend and evening availability for services, volunteer trainings, and special ministry events.
  • Office hours will be consistent and mutually coordinated with the Family Ministry Director.

Regent University’s College of Arts & Sciences is seeking a full-time, tenure-track faculty member in Old Testament to teach in the Biblical Studies and Christian Ministry department. This will be a residential position located on the Virginia Beach, Virginia, campus.

The successful applicant will possess a PhD in Old Testament, Bible Exposition, or an equivalent field from a regionally accredited institution. The ideal candidate will specialize in the intertextuality of the Old Testament books, assigning more contextual weight to the greater narrative that binds the thirty-nine books in anticipation of Jesus Christ and the New Testament. The candidate will also possess skill in teaching at the undergraduate level. Ability to teach Biblical Hebrew I and II is also preferred. Candidates will primarily teach 15-week, on-campus courses. However, an ability to teach 8-week online courses via Canvas is expected.

Regent University is one of the nation’s leading academic centers for Christian thought and action, offering over 150 associate, bachelors, masters, and doctoral degrees and enrolling more than 13,000 students worldwide. Regent offers high-quality, in-demand and affordable degree programs while remaining committed to its foundational mission to educate Christian leaders to change the world.

Work Location: Virginia Beach, VA

Salary Range: $65,000-$75,000 annually

Expectations include 1) dedication to Christ-centered teaching and learning; 2) an ability to teach undergraduate-level courses; 3) experience with online instructional technology (i.e., Canvas); 4) facility in oral and written communication; 5) demonstration of academic publishing success (and an agenda for further research and writing); 6) regular participation and engagement in academic societies; 7) eagerness to engage in inter-faculty collegiality in the College of Arts and Sciences; and 8) a willingness to embrace the College and University Identity and Mission statements and subscribe to a statement of Christian faith.

To apply, complete the faculty application and submit a current resume/CV with a cover letter explaining your interest in and qualifications for this position. Official transcripts will be required at time of employment.

Appointment will begin July 1st, 2027. Applications will be accepted until the position is filled.

Regent University does not discriminate in employment in its programs or activities on the basis of race, color, national or ethnic origin, sex, disability, age or veteran status. For full Non-Discrimination Policy click here.

Benefits

Regent offers a wide range of generous benefits including health, life and disability insurance; flexible spending accounts; tuition incentives; fully vested retirement plans; life and disability insurance options, time off, and more. All regular faculty and staff serving at Regent and working a minimum of 30 hours per week will receive an attractive benefits package.

Director of AVL & Technology - Trinity United Presbyterian Church

POSITION DESCRIPTION: Director of AVL & Technology
Trinity United Presbyterian Church – Santa Ana, CA
Full-Time | Approx. 40 hrs/week | Exempt

Accountability:  

Reports directly to the Co-Lead Pastor and works closely with the Director of Worship & Music and Director of Communications to support Trinity’s worship and ministry vision, including worship production, technical planning, communications, and ministry support.

 

SPIRITUAL AND MINISTRY EXPECTATIONS

The person serving in this position is expected to have personally embraced the essential tenets of the Christian faith, including a personal profession of faith in Jesus Christ as Lord and Savior, and to be in agreement with the essential tenets of ECO (Covenant Order of Evangelical Presbyterians).

The Director of AVL & Technology is expected to demonstrate a growing relationship with Christ and a commitment to Trinity's mission, vision, and ministry. This position serves as a ministry leader who uses technical expertise to support worship, discipleship, communication, and the broader life of the church.

BASIC FUNCTION

The Director of AVL & Technology provides leadership, oversight, and technical support for Trinity's worship, production, livestream, and media systems across the church campus.

This position is responsible for maintaining and improving Trinity's technical infrastructure, troubleshooting and resolving technical issues, coordinating technical staff and volunteers, and helping ensure that worship services and ministry events are executed with excellence and reliability.

The Director of AVL & Technology works closely with the Director of Communications, Director of Worship & Music, Contemporary Worship & Arts Coordinator, technical staff, pastors, ministry leaders, volunteers, and the T3 Committee to develop effective, sustainable, and consistent technical systems throughout Trinity.

Technical Systems and Infrastructure

  • Diagnose, troubleshoot, maintain, and repair audio, video, lighting, livestream, networking, and related technical equipment.
  • Identify and troubleshoot the root causes of audio, visual, and livestreaming issues, implementing effective, long-term solutions to ensure reliable performance during worship services, events, and ministry activities.
  • Research, recommend, install, configure, and maintain audio/visual equipment, including sound systems, microphones, mixing consoles, cameras, projectors, displays, lighting, and livestreaming technology.
  • Evaluate and recommend upgrades or replacements for outdated audio/visual equipment, production software, and related systems to maintain quality, reliability, and compatibility.
  • Establish consistent audio/visual equipment standards, system configurations, and operating procedures across the Trinity campus.
  • Develop and maintain documentation, operating procedures, troubleshooting guides, and best practices for audio/visual systems, livestream production, and technical support for worship services and events.

Worship and Sunday Production

  • Provide technical oversight for Sunday morning worship and ministry activities across campus, including the Sanctuary, Fellowship Hall, Well Room, Center, and other spaces as needed.
  • Manage and troubleshoot the Sunday morning livestream, working to ensure consistent quality and reliability.
  • Collaborate with worship and ministry leaders to ensure that technical systems effectively support the goals of each service or event.
  • Assist with the planning and execution of special worship services, concerts, events, and ministry gatherings.

Staff and Team Leadership

  • Coordinate and support part-time technical staff and volunteers.
  • Recruit, develop, train, schedule, and retain technical volunteers, helping build healthy, capable, and sustainable volunteer teams.
  • Develop and maintain schedules for part-time technical staff.
  • Review and approve staff timecards.
  • Provide training, mentoring, and technical guidance to staff and volunteers.
  • Foster a collaborative, accountable, and service-oriented culture among Trinity's technical teams.
  • Interface with other technical staff to coordinate systems, responsibilities, and priorities.
  • Work with the T3 Committee as needed on technical planning, infrastructure, equipment, and projects.

Media and Communications

  • Film and organize B-roll and other video content from worship services and church events for use on Trinity's website, social media, and other communications.
  • Produce and edit videos for worship services, VBS, special events, and other ministry needs.
  • Help develop sustainable systems for capturing, storing, organizing, and distributing media content.

Collaboration and Administration

  • Work closely with the Director of Worship & Music, Director of Communications, Contemporary Worship & Arts Coordinator, pastors, staff, and ministry leaders to support Trinity's overall worship and ministry vision.
  • Oversee budgeting, long-term planning, equipment replacement schedules, and vendor relationships specifically related to audio/visual systems, livestreaming production, and theatrical and architectural lighting for worship services, events, and ministry activities.
  • Communicate audio/visual, livestreaming, and lighting needs, equipment recommendations, system improvements, and technical solutions clearly to staff, ministry leaders, volunteers, and outside vendors.
  • Prioritize audio/visual, livestreaming, and lighting projects while responding promptly and effectively to urgent technical issues to ensure uninterrupted worship services, livestream broadcasts, and church events.
  • Attend staff, ministry, and technical meetings as required.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

Schedule and Physical Requirements

  • Sunday attendance is required. The position also requires flexibility to work evenings, weekends, holidays, and special events as ministry and production needs require.
  • The role requires the ability to work in active production environments and to safely handle, move, and set up technical equipment as needed.

KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, AND ABILITIES

Knowledge of:

  • Audio, video, lighting, livestream, and production systems.
  • Digital audio, video, and media production workflows
  • Computer hardware, software, networking, and related technology.
  • Worship production and church technology systems.
  • Technical troubleshooting, system integration, and root-cause analysis.
  • Production workflows, technical standards, and industry best practices.
  • Current and emerging production technologies relevant to worship, media, communications, and live production.
  • Media and production software and platforms used by Trinity, including ProPresenter, Resi, Adobe Creative Cloud, Companion, StreamDeck, Dante, ATEM, LiveU, Blackmagic, Pro Tools, Lightkey and other related systems.

Ability to:

  • Diagnose technical problems and identify root causes.
  • Develop creative, practical, and sustainable solutions.
  • Research and evaluate equipment and technology.
  • Lead technical projects from planning through installation and implementation.
  • Train, supervise, and support technical staff and volunteers.
  • Communicate effectively with technical and non-technical team members.
  • Manage multiple priorities and respond calmly to time-sensitive situations.
  • Work independently while remaining accountable to ministry leadership.
  • Maintain organized systems, documentation, schedules, and equipment.
  • Serve with flexibility, initiative, patience, and a servant-leadership mindset.

Measures of Success

  • Success in this role includes reliable and high-quality worship production, consistent and effective livestream experiences, well-maintained and sustainable technical systems, and healthy, engaged volunteer teams.

EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE

Bachelor's degree in audio engineering, digital media, media communications, technical theater, information technology, or a related field preferred.

Equivalent combination of education, training, and professional experience may be considered.

Demonstrated experience with live audio, video production, livestreaming, church production, or related technical environments is required. Experience supervising staff and managing technical projects is preferred.

At Houston Methodist, the Clinical Pastoral Education (CPE) Student Educator Phase I position is responsible for participating in a multi-year training program towards achievement as a Clinical Pastoral Education Certified Educator by the Association for Clinical Pastoral Education (ACPE). Under supervision of the CPE Certified Educator and/or CPE Director/Manager, this position performs activities towards the fulfillment of certification requirements to include facilitating and teaching CPE courses, participating in curriculum development, and providing individual and group student supervision. The CPE Student Educator Phase I position also performs the job of Chaplain, initially about 50% of the time and lessening as responsibilities associated with the student training increase over time due to receiving candidate status by ACPE. This position assists leadership in carrying out the Houston Methodist mission, vision, and values, participating in activities in these efforts.

FLSA STATUS
Exempt

QUALIFICATIONS

EDUCATION
  • Master’s degree in theological studies from an institution accredited by a member of the Council for Higher Education Accreditation (CHEA), or equivalency approved by the Association of Professional Chaplains (APC), American Association of Pastoral Counselors (AAPC and only if prior to 2017), National Association of Catholic Chaplains (NACC), Neshama: Association of Jewish Chaplains (NAJC), Canadian Association for Spiritual Care (CASC), Association for Clinical Pastoral Education (ACPE), or Spiritual Care Association (SCA)
  • Four units of CPE from Association for Clinical Pastoral Education (ACPE) accredited center

EXPERIENCE
  • Experience as a professional chaplain preferred

SKILLS AND ABILITIES
  • Demonstrates the skills and competencies necessary to safely perform the assigned job, determined through on-going skills, competency assessments, and performance evaluations
  • Sufficient proficiency in speaking, reading, and writing the English language necessary to perform the essential functions of this job, especially with regard to activities impacting patient or employee safety or security
  • Ability to effectively communicate with patients, physicians, family members and co-workers in a manner consistent with a customer service focus and application of positive language principles
  • Endorsed for chaplaincy by a recognized endorsing body
  • Demonstrates knowledge of ACPE Standards and Manuals, ACPE Code of Professional Ethics, and APC Common Code of Ethics for Chaplains, Pastoral Counselors, Pastoral Educators, and Students
  • Possesses basic computer knowledge; operates various computer systems to enter and maintain patient documents
  • Ability to work independently; capable of effectively handling challenging/difficult interactions, patient care situations; demonstrates sound judgment and executes above average communication skills
  • Exhibits strong interpersonal and team player skills with all levels of the healthcare team
  • Demonstrates knowledge of and adherence to attributes of integrity, honesty, personal responsibility, and accountability
  • Demonstrates emotional and spiritual maturity
  • Adapts to multiple ongoing priorities with minimal supervision including organizing workflow and actively participating in problem-solving
  • Very strong organizational skills and detail-oriented nature
  • Professional handling of exposure to confidential/sensitive information
  • Demonstrates ability to utilize educational resources to develop reflectivity
  • Demonstrates awareness of emotional self and the ability to translate awareness into spiritual care action
  • Demonstrates knowledge and awareness of how socio-economic and cultural systems and structures impact well-being of individuals and groups
  • Exhibits the ability to mentor others on pastoral/professional functioning
  • Demonstrates awareness of the need for a theoretical foundation in education and personality development for Certified Educators
  • Demonstrates integration of theory and practice in the provision of spiritual care
  • Demonstrates awareness of multi-faceted roles in chaplaincy or pastoral/spiritual care context
  • Demonstrates basic knowledge of current ACPE Standards and the Common Qualifications and Competencies for Professional Chaplains and how to access the documents


ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS

PEOPLE ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS
  • Promotes a supportive and positive environment for Houston Methodist CPE students, collaborating and communicating in a non-judgmental manner. Articulates the importance of and demonstrates ability to navigate interdisciplinary systems to accomplish shared goals for the benefit of care receivers. Communicates beliefs, thoughts, values, and feelings clearly through congruent verbal, non-verbal, and written skills.
  • After receiving candidate status by ACPE, provides group and individual mentoring of CPE students, including spiritual care support to patients, family members, and employees on assigned clinical units, when on call, participating in patient rounds, discharge planning, support groups, sacred story groups and other interprofessional teams. Upholds ethical behavior and protects the welfare of others within spiritual care practice.
  • Exhibits and demonstrates the ability to learn from peers, recognize relational dynamics, and establishes collaborative and dialogical relationships. Displays self-awareness and reflection in spiritual care practice. Demonstrates basic knowledge of spiritual care assessment tools and human development. Recommends initiatives to improve department scores for employee engagement.

SERVICE ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS
  • Makes pastoral visit, providing spiritual care that is sensitive to individuals' social, religious, and cultural contexts. Uses tools for assessment, plan of care, intervention, and evaluation of outcomes appropriate to the patient care context. Provides spiritual care to meet the spiritual, religious, and emotional needs of patients and their family members of all faiths, during hospitalization and particularly for pre-operative, critically ill and dying patients. Respects physical, emotional, and spiritual boundaries in the practice of spiritual care. Enables others to utilize their own faith as a resource for health and healing.
  • Demonstrates basic knowledge of spiritual care assessment tools and human development. Exhibits ability to provide care as a skillful, empathic, and compassionate spiritual caregiver Empowers others to initiate and receive feedback in a clinical consultation. Understands own need for consultation in clinical context.
  • Articulates a theology/philosophy of spiritual care that is integrated with spiritual care practice. Recognizes situations that challenge adherence to ACPE Standards and Ethics. Proactively identifies when a change in approach or intervention is necessary, taking appropriate action and involving others as needed. Provides crisis intervention for patients and family, visitors, employees, and physicians.
  • Recommends initiatives/activities to meet/exceed department and organization targets for patient satisfaction measures.

QUALITY/SAFETY ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS
  • Under supervision of a CPE Certified Educator and/or CPE Director/Manager, plans and develops CPE curriculum, co-teaches, or independently teaches and facilitates CPE courses/units.
  • Accurately and thoroughly documents patient visits and spiritual care provided in the patient’s record. Ensures the accuracy and thoroughness of documentation performed by students in patient records.
  • Upholds ethical behavior and protects the welfare of others within spiritual care practice. Articulates organizational strengths and weaknesses from current and previous spiritual care contexts. Instructs and facilitates reflection in other learners or professionals.
  • Consults with physicians, clinical management, hospital leadership and staff to assess quality and safety of services provided by CPE students. Identifies opportunities for corrective action and improvement, providing recommendations, contributing to achievement of hospital and department targets for quality and safety.

FINANCE ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS
  • Self-motivated to independently manage time effectively and prioritize daily tasks to achieve maximum results in a timely manner. Utilizes time efficiently, demonstrating responsible financial stewardship, and proactively helps other team members.

GROWTH/INNOVATION ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS
  • Articulates the role of chaplain/spiritual caregiver as a potential change agent. facilitate groups such as staff debriefings and support groups worship services, I CARE values integration, accreditation readiness, bioethics, etc. Displays self-awareness and reflection in spiritual care practice. Incorporates understanding of personal/cultural development, educational and vocational history, religious/spiritual development, and CPE experience into practice of spiritual care.
  • Progressively assumes increasing responsibilities associated with fulfilling the requirements for achieving ACPE certification as Educator CPE. Articulates knowledge of ethical theories appropriate to a spiritual care context. Demonstrates basic research literacy and familiarity with evidence-based practice in spiritual care. Prepares and submits supervisory and theological theory papers, participates in video conferences with other Student Educators peer group.


SUPPLEMENTAL REQUIREMENTS
    WORK ATTIRE
    • Uniform: No
    • Scrubs: No
    • Business professional: Yes
    • Other (department approved): No

    ON-CALL*
    *Note that employees may be required to be on-call during emergencies (ie. Disaster, Severe Weather Events, etc) regardless of selection below.
    • On Call* No

    TRAVEL**
    **Travel specifications may vary by department**
    • May require travel within the Houston Metropolitan area Yes
    • May require travel outside Houston Metropolitan area No

1 - Day (United States of America)



Job Category:

Non-clinical

Houston Methodist is one of the nation’s leading health systems and academic medical centers. The health system consists of eight hospitals: Houston Methodist Hospital, its flagship academic hospital in the Texas Medical Center, seven community hospitals and one long-term acute care hospital throughout the Greater Houston metropolitan area. Houston Methodist also includes a research institute; a comprehensive residency program; international patient services; freestanding comprehensive care clinics, emergency care and imaging centers; and outpatient facilities. Rooted in our Christian faith, Bethany Christian Services works to ensure children are safe, loved, and connected through family. Across 29 states, we strengthen families, support foster care and adoption, and walk alongside refugees with compassion. Here, living out your faith means using your gifts to bring hope and make a lasting impact.

Working at Bethany means joining a team of dedicated professionals with diverse skills, serving communities across the country. Responsive recruiter
The Community Engagement Ministry Associate (CEMA) supports the Pastor of Community Engagement by coordinating the people, projects, events, communication, and systems that help the Community Engagement ministry run effectively. This part-time role focuses on organization, execution, and follow-through, ensuring ministry ideas and initiatives move from planning to completion with excellence. Additionally, this position is responsible for overseeing the onsite needs of the Mercy Ministry Center.

CORE COMPETENCIES
  1. Organization: Effectively manages projects, deadlines, people, and details.
  2. Follow-Through & Ownership: Takes responsibility for assignments and ensures tasks are completed with excellence.
  3. Proactivity: Anticipates needs and next steps without requiring constant direction.
  4. Attention to Detail: Notices important details and maintains accuracy in communication, planning, and execution.
  5. Relational Warmth & Humility: Communicates graciously with partners, volunteers, families, and staff while helping others succeed.
  6. Adaptability & Systems Thinking: Responds well to changing ministry needs while creating processes that improve organization and efficiency.

RESPONSIBILITIES
  1. Ministry Coordination & Follow-Through – Support the day-to-day execution of Community Engagement by turning meetings, ideas, and ministry initiatives into clear next steps and keeping projects moving toward completion.
    1. Maintain project plans, timelines, calendars, task lists, and deadlines.
    2. Track assignments and follow up with staff, volunteers, and ministry partners.
    3. Identify upcoming needs, deadlines, and outstanding action items before they become urgent.
    4. Provide regular updates to the Pastor of Community Engagement and help develop repeatable processes for recurring ministry activities.
    5. Help lead the support team that helps with administrative tasks for community engagement.
  2. Community Partner Support and Coordination – Help maintain strong and organized relationships with Community Engagement ministry partners by coordinating communication, meetings, requests, and follow-up.
    1. Maintain accurate partner records, contacts, requests, and commitments.
    2. Help with coordinating meetings, site visits, serving opportunities, and other partnership logistics.
    3. Send routine follow-up communication and track outstanding decisions or responsibilities.
    4. Capture meeting notes, next steps, and ensure partners experience Mercy Church as responsive, dependable, and organized.
  3. Volunteer Coordination Support –  Support the recruitment, communication, preparation, and organization of Community Engagement volunteers so they are equipped to serve with clarity and confidence.
    1. Create and maintain volunteer opportunities, registrations, rosters, and role information through POINT.
    2. Send confirmations, reminders, instructions, and other volunteer communication through POINT
    3. Track background checks, waivers, training requirements, and other necessary volunteer steps through Church Community Builder. 
    4. Support volunteer leaders with resources and help identify consistent volunteers who may be ready for more leadership
  4. Event & Project Support – Provide logistical and administrative support for Community Engagement events and serving opportunities, helping ensure each initiative is well planned, communicated, and executed.
    1. Develop event timelines, checklists, volunteer assignments, and registration plans.
    2. Coordinate supplies, food, facilities, room arrangements, signage, and printed materials.
    3. Communicate with volunteers, ministry partners, and other stakeholders leading up to the event.
    4. Support event setup, execution, and post-event follow-up.

*Miscellaneous Responsibilities – This job description is not meant to be an all-inclusive statement of every duty and responsibility that will be required of an employee in this position. Therefore, additional duties may be assigned and/or changed without advance notice. 

CONDITIONS OF EMPLOYMENT
*Performance Evaluation – It is understood that the performance for this job will be primarily measured and evaluated by the “responsibilities” and the “general expectations” laid out in this job description.  
  1. Models the biblical standard of personal conduct and lifestyle that is expected of all Mercy Church staff and covenant members
  2. Fully participates in the life of the church as an active covenant member
  3. Supports and adheres to the mission, vision, values, and philosophy of the ministry of Mercy Church
  4. Submits to and supports the leadership of the church elders 
  5. Works well as a team player with the elders, staff, key leaders, and ministry team members at Mercy Church.

General Expectations
  1. Report to the office during Office Hours. You will also be required to attend various extra Church events relevant to your ministry oversight areas and/or as church needs arise.
  2. Should always exhibit professionalism, demonstrated by a well-groomed appearance, conscientious work ethic, teachability, and accountability.
  3. Should be willing and able to adapt quickly to changing circumstances, with composure and flexibility.
  4. Should be ever conscious of the need for confidentiality.
  5. Should always exercise discernment and wise judgment.
  6. Should be a person who gives extreme attention to detail with an eye for excellence.
  7. Should have the willingness to seek new information, training, and resources as needed.
  8. Should be a self-starter and good at multitasking and prioritizing projects.

JOB REQUIREMENTS

Physical Requirements
  1. Ability to frequently stand, sit, and/or walk
  2. Ability to occasionally bend, squat, kneel, climb stairs, and/or lift
  3. Ability to occasionally lift between 10-50 lbs
  4. Ability to continuously communicate with other people
  5. Ability to continuously operate a computer in order to complete necessary office work
  6. Ability to continuously comprehend both physical and digital documents
  7. Ability to continuously prepare/create both physical and digital documents

Work Environment
  1. May occasionally work in temperatures above 95 degrees and below 32 degrees
  2. May occasionally walk on slippery, wet, or uneven surfaces
  3. Noise level in the environment will occasionally be loud
  4. May occasionally work outdoors
  5. May occasionally be required to travel for work
  6. May continuously work indoors in an office space
  7. May continuously work in a shared office space with coworkers

Office Hours and Work Schedule
  1. Work Hours: This is a part-time role but must be available Monday and Wednesday Mornings and flexible for evening or weekend serve events.  
  2. Officeing at the Mercy Ministry Center: Maintain consistent weekly office hours at the Mercy Ministry Center for calls, vendor appointments, mail, and other on-site needs. Specific days and times are negotiable.
  3. Additional Hours: This person will be expected to be at key events/meetings outside of the above office hours. Please see supervisor for details.
  4. Overtime and extra work days: Some overtime will be required. Please consult the Mercy Staff Handbook for the Overtime Policy 
  5. Holidays: All staff-wide Holidays are outlined in the Mercy Staff Handbook
  6. Time Off: Please consult the Mercy Staff Handbook for the time-off policy



MISSION

To make disciples who love God, love each other, and love our world.
Our mission is what we aim to do – the call to action we believe Christ has placed on his church. This mission is the goal of every decision we make and is borne out of two moments in the gospel of Matthew where Jesus summarizes the driving heartbeats of a follower of Christ: The Great Commandment and The Great Commission. The first is found in Matthew 22:36-40, a conversation between Jesus and a lawyer:

“Teacher, which is the great commandment in the Law?” And he said to him, “You shall love the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your mind. This is the great and first commandment. And a second is like it: You shall love your neighbor as yourself. On these two commandments depend all the Law and the Prophets.”
The other is in Matthew 28:19, the final command that Jesus gives his followers just before ascending into heaven:

“Go therefore and make disciples of all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit…”

VISION

To see a gospel awakening in the city of Charlotte that is carried to the ends of the earth.
Our vision is what we aim to see – what we believe God will do as we carry out our mission. This gospel awakening is not just our desire, but what we believe is the natural manifestation and outcome of disciples who make disciples who love God, love each other, and love our world.

A true understanding of the gospel changes everything, and if we strive to help the people of our city understand the good news of Jesus, we expect that God will change lives. The more people who understand that a relationship with God is not based on what we’ve done, but on what has been done for us in Christ; that our lives are not for our own glory, but for the glory of God; that the gospel is not just the front door to the Christian life, but is the house in which the believer dwells – the more people we begin taking their next step in following Jesus and live on mission here and around the world.
