Campus Staff Minister - Michigan Lower Peninsula Region (Undergraduate Ministry)

Work Location:

Michigan

Job Type:

Full time

God has called InterVarsity to plant and to build witnessing communities of students and faculty who follow Jesus on college and university campuses. Through these groups, we believe ever- increasing numbers of students and faculty from all ethnic groups and areas of the campus will be transformed by the Gospel. We expect to see campuses increasingly become places where people, ideas, and structures flourish to the glory of God. We confidently anticipate that our InterVarsity alumni will become change agents across the country and around the world. We pursue this calling by discerning and actively participating in what God is already doing on campus. This is the essence of being a Campus Staff Minister (CSM).

ESSENTIAL COMMITMENTS/RESPONSIBILITIES 

Spiritual Growth 

You pursue maturity as a disciple of Jesus Christ so that your life and work increasingly reflects a growing love for God, God’s Word, God’s people of every ethnicity and culture, and God’s purposes in the world. To do this, you will: 

  • Pursue a vibrant relationship with the triune God through engagement with Scripture, prayer, and worship, both individually and in community 

  • Develop self-leadership (growing in self-awareness, self-management, relational integrity, and resiliency) 

  • Embrace Scriptural standards for behavior and attitudes 

 

Campus Leadership 

You communicate and model InterVarsity’s vision to see students and faculty transformed, campuses renewed and world changers developed 

  • Create a culture of humble dependence on God and bold expectation in God’s intention to start new witnessing communities throughout the campus and on new campuses 

  • Model – in person and through programs – InterVarsity’s vision and Core Values, including a biblically-defined commitment to engage every ethnic and social group on campus 

  • Lead students and faculty – individually and collectively – through Scripture, prayer, teaching, and discipleship experiences, so that they articulate and align their ministry activities around this vision 

  • Set annual goals through prayer, research and reflection with your teams (students, faculty, and staff) for qualitative and quantitative growth, including conversions and leadership development 

 

You create, develop, align and leverage ministry plans, programs, teams, and structures to close the gap between current reality and the aspirational goals. 

  • Build leadership teams who trust and partner well with you and who demonstrate spiritual vitality, relational health, and mission alignment 

  • Develop and execute plans to achieve annual goals, evaluating and modifying the plan as needed throughout the year 

  • Increase momentum for the vision by aligning programs, structures, conferences and teams around the goals 

  • Mobilize students and faculty to engage their relational networks with the gospel and to start new missional communities 

  • Under the direction of the Area Director, may supervise Ministry Interns and Campus Ministry Interns as delegated 

 

You intentionally gather, invite, and develop diverse groups of students and faculty so that they not only encounter and follow Jesus as Savior and Lord but also advance the mission on campus as participants and leaders. 

  • Create ways for faculty and students to encounter and follow Jesus through Scripture, worship, prayer, mission experiences, conferences, etc. 

  • Equip students and faculty so that they think strategically about campus engagement and so that they proclaim – in word, deed, and power – the good news of Jesus, regularly inviting students and faculty to follow him as Savior and Lord 

  • Disciple students and faculty by equipping them to hear the Word, respond actively, and debrief and interpret the experience so that they grow in Christlikeness, reflect our Core Values, and develop ministry skills 

  • Invite, coach, and equip students and faculty to become increasingly effective participants and leaders, including starting new witnessing communities on campuses 

 

Organizational Collaboration 

You work with a network of other local, area, regional, and national InterVarsity staff and volunteers so that our work reflects Biblical standards of excellence, integrity, and partnership. 

  • Partner with and respond positively to the direction and coaching of your supervisors and national leaders 

  • Contribute to collaborative and productive team meetings and relationships 

  • Affiliate chapters under your care and submit Graduating Student Forms in order to increase our partnership with current students and alumni 

  • Use national ministry resources and tools, as requested, including recruiting and/or participating in local, regional, or national conferences as  

  • Complete reporting, planning and review requirements in a timely way so that you and your supervisors can assess and improve your work as a CSM 

  • Comply with all InterVarsity policies and procedures 

 

Ministry Partnership Development 

You will develop a team of partners – churches and individuals (including alumni and community members) – who will resource the ministry financially, in prayer, or volunteer service that advances the mission. 

  • Raise 100% of the financial budget assigned by your supervisor 

  • Communicate regularly with your ministry partners, nurturing the relationship through visits, phone calls, emails and regular prayer letters 

  • Develop on-going, long-lasting partnership with alumni and volunteers 

  • Comply with all Ministry Partnership Policies 

  • Identify and invest in advocates who will build networks of volunteers and donors on InterVarsity’s behalf 

 

Accomplish all other assigned tasks as appropriate 

 

QUALIFICATIONS (common to all levels of CSM) 

  • Annually affirm InterVarsity’s Statement of Agreement (Doctrinal Basis and Purpose Statement). Abide by InterVarsity’s Code of Conduct. Believe and behave consonantly with InterVarsity’s Human Sexuality Theological Paper. Affirm and behave consonantly with InterVarsity’s “Women in Ministry Statement of Affirmation” 

  • Bachelor’s degree for CSMs assigned to a four-year campus. A minimum of an Associate’s degree for CSMs assigned to a two-year campus or a community college 

  • Strong interpersonal skills (including ability to minister to diverse ethnic communities and faculty) 

  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills 

  • Demonstrated problem solving skills 

  • Familiarity with word processing, presentation, email, and spreadsheet software 

 

WORK ENVIRONMENT/PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS 

The CSM position leads ministry in a college campus environment. A designated office space may or may not be available. The CSM is required to travel to on-campus and off- campus sites as appropriate. Off-campus travel includes, but is not limited to: student ministry conferences, Ministry Partnership Development meetings, and InterVarsity- sponsored training sessions, meetings, and conferences. The CSM is regularly required to communicate with others, and routinely uses standard office equipment such as computers, phones, photocopiers, filing cabinets, etc. 

Pay Range: $39,288.00 - $52,392.00 per year

Pay: This position is funded through personal fundraising. Accordingly, compensation will vary based on the ability of the individual to secure a donor team to fund the cost of his/her salary. The anticipated salary range for this position on a full-time basis (40 hours/week) is dependent on a variety of factors, including location and cost of living. The actual salary received, including any geographic adjustment to account for location and cost of living, is subject to the individual’s ability to raise funds necessary to cover the full amount of such salary within the range set forth in the job posting details.

Benefits:

We offer a competitive benefits package, including health care and retirement savings with a match. Eligibility is based on employee type and hours worked.  Benefits include the following:

  • 403(b) Retirement Savings Plan

  • 403(b) matching contributions

  • Dental insurance

  • Employee assistance program

  • Employee discounts

  • Flexible work schedule

  • Flexible spending accounts

  • Health insurance

  • Health savings account

  • Life insurance

  • Paid time off

  • Parental leave

  • Professional development assistance

  • Vision insurance

Equal Employment Opportunity: 

 

InterVarsity Christian Fellowship/USA is both an equal opportunity employer and a faith-based religious organization. We conduct hiring without regard to race, color, ancestry, national origin, citizenship, age, sex, marital status, parental status, membership in any labor organization, political ideology, or disability of an otherwise qualified individual. The status of InterVarsity Christian Fellowship/USA as an equal opportunity employer does not prevent the organization from hiring staff based on their religious beliefs so that all staff share the same religious commitment.  Pursuant to the Civil Rights Act of 1964, Section 702 (42 U.S.C. 2000e 1(a)) InterVarsity Christian Fellowship/USA has the right to, and does, hire only candidates who agree with InterVarsity’s Statement of Agreement: Purpose and Doctrinal Basis because InterVarsity believes that each and every staff plays a vital role in advancing InterVarsity’s mission and purposes.

Purpose within the Organization:

The purpose of this position is to provide all the technical needs for the Grand Canyon University Worship Team. This is to support the Chapel and Gathering events put on by Spiritual Life.

Responsibilities Related to Purpose:

  • Setup Chapel Services (Drums, In-Ear Monitors, Mics, and Cabling).

  • Setup Audio For Gathering Services.

  • Setup Lighting for Gathering Services.

  • Setup Video for Gathering Services.

  • Assist the Worship Team with setting up and tearing down equipment.

  • Prepare Computer for Gathering and Chapel Services.

Qualifications:

  • Must have a high level of technical skill in the areas of audio, video, and lighting.

  • Must be able to work with a band.

  • Know how to set up a sound system and musical equipment.

  • Must have good communication skills.

  • Be willing to work well in a team environment.

  • Must be able to lift heavy equipment. 

Grand Canyon University is committed to a student first policy.
Therefore, all applicants must meet the following eligibility requirements to be considered for student employment:

  • Enrolled at GCU as a full-time student in a Bachelor’s program or Master’s program.

You may be subject to termination if you fall below the minimum requirements.

Description

Position Title: Pastoral Associate for Parish Ministries

 

Position Type

Full Time

 

Description

Our Parish Family:

Through the Partners in the Gospel initiative, the Roman Catholic Archdiocese of Seattle has integrated parishes and resources into groupings of parish families that are now in the process of becoming new canonical parishes. Saint Michael Parish (Olympia) and Saint Edward Parish (Shelton) constitute a dynamic and growth-oriented parish family.  St. Michael Parish and St. Michael Parish School comprises a truly vibrant multicultural Catholic community that serves approximately 2,800 families, representing 7,000 individual mass attendees per weekend and approximately 440 school students enrolled in pre-k through 8th grade. The past decade has witnessed unprecedented growth in parish life engagement, ministry participation, and school enrollment. St Edward Parish is a diverse parish, inclusive of many ethnic cultures including multilingual staff, mass offerings in Spanish and serving approximately 1200 families per weekend.

 

Position Overview:

 

The Pastoral Associate for Parish Ministry serves as a senior staff leader responsible for assisting the pastor in advancing the parish mission: “To place God first in all things:proclaim the Gospel of Jesus Christ; and grow in holiness through prayer, sacraments, and service. We Make Disciples.”

 

Ingrained in an intimate relationship with Jesus and his Church, the Pastoral Associate for Parish Ministries reports directly to the pastor and provides leadership and oversight for the parish's efforts related to faith formation (including ministries for children, youth and adults),  discipleship, catechesis, sacramental preparation (including Christian initiation), liturgy (including sacred music), pastoral care, volunteer catechist development and vocational accompaniment. The position establishes the culture, priorities, and strategic direction of the Office for Parish Ministry and ensures that all parish ministry initiatives contribute to the mission and long-term vitality of the parish. This role is responsible for creating pathways through which parishioners encounter Christ, engage in lifelong faith formation, deepen their discipleship, embrace the teachings of the Church, discern their vocation, and actively participate in the life and mission of the Church.

 

 

The Pastoral Associate for Parish Ministry works closely with the Pastor; Pastoral Associate for Parish Life; Pastoral Associate for Financial Administration, Pastoral Associate for Parish Family Resources; School Principal; parish staff; ministry leaders; catechists; and volunteers to foster a vibrant, mission-driven parish community. The Pastoral Associate for Parish Ministry is a person who has a strong faith, witnesses to the Good News of Jesus Christ, blessed with a deep love of the people of God, and of the Catholic Church. They are knowledgeable about the church’s teachings and committed to its mission. By their lives, their attitudes and their ministry, they enrich the parish even as they are themselves enriched through the gifts of those with whom they minister or to whom they serve.

 

Essential Responsibilities

 

Mission Vision and Leadership
 

  • Promote and advance the parish mission in all parish ministry initiatives.
  • Collaborate with the Pastor and parish leadership in developing and implementing parish vision and strategic priorities including parish mission, vision, priorities, staffing, and ministry development.
  • Work with the Pastoral Associate for Parish Life to align engagement, evangelization, formation, and discipleship efforts.
  • Collaborate with the Pastoral Associate for Parish Family Finances regarding ministry budgets and financial stewardship.
  • Work with the Pastoral Associate for Parish Family Resources regarding facilities, technology, and operational support.
  • Collaborate with the School Principal to strengthen parish-school faith formation and family engagement.
  • Ensure parish values are reflected throughout formation programs, sacramental preparation, liturgical life, and pastoral ministries.
  • Provide leadership that fosters engagement, formation, catechesis, discipleship, and vocational discernment.
  • Develop systems and structures that help parishioners grow from initial engagement to mature Christian discipleship.

 

Faith Formation and Catechesis

  • Ensure consistency in prayer, curriculum, and ministry effectiveness throughout all formation programs.
  • Provide oversight for parish catechetical ministries, ensure fidelity to Catholic doctrine and reflect the mission, vision and values of the parish.
  • Provide leadership and foster collaboration among ministries to create seamless transitions between stages of lifelong formation
  • Recruit, form, and support catechists and volunteer ministry leaders.

Discipleship and Engagement

  • Promote meaningful engagement opportunities that invite parishioners into ongoing formation and parish life.
  • Collaborate with Pastoral Assistant for Faith Formation and support the formation of missionary disciples through small groups, retreats, Bible studies, and ongoing formation opportunities.

Sacramental Life and Vocational Accompaniment

  • Oversee sacramental preparation processes for our parish and parish school and ensure processes follow Archdiocesan norms and reflect sound pastoral practice. (This includes, Marriage, Baptism, First Communion, Confirmation, TNTT and Christian Initiation.)
  • Collaborate with clergy and parish leadership in coordinating sacramental celebrations and preparation.
  • Promote lifelong participation in the sacramental life of the Church.
  • Encourage parishioners to discern their vocation through prayer, formation, and participation in parish life.

Liturgy, Spiritual Formation and Pastoral Care

  • Oversee liturgical ministries and sacred music in collaboration with clergy and ministry leaders.
  • Foster full, conscious, and active participation in the liturgical life of the parish.
  • Support retreats, seasonal formation opportunities, and parish-wide spiritual initiatives.
  • Provide leadership for pastoral care ministries serving parishioners throughout life's milestones.

Administration and Office Leadership

  • Direct the daily operations of the Office for Parish Ministry.
  • Supervise assigned staff and provide coaching, support, evaluation, and professional development.
  • Develop annual goals, objectives, and performance measures for the Office for Parish Ministry.
  • Oversee ministry budgets in collaboration with the Pastoral Associate for Parish Family Finances.
  • Ensure compliance with Archdiocesan policies, Safe Environment requirements, and parish procedures.
  • Maintain effective administrative systems supporting all parish ministry initiatives.

Directly Supervises

  • Pastoral Assistant for Children's Ministry (Catechesis of the Good Shepherd)
  • Pastoral Assistant for Middle School Ministry (Edge)
  • Pastoral Assistant for High School Ministry (Life Teen and Confirmation)
  • Pastoral Assistant for Adult Faith Formation
  • Pastoral Assistant for Christian Initiation (OCIA/OCIC)
  • Pastoral Assistant for Sacramental Preparation (Baptism and Marriage)
  • Pastoral Assistant for Pastoral Care
  • Pastoral Assistant for Liturgy and Sacred Music

 



Qualifications

Qualifications

Essential Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in ministry, theology or related discipline, or equivalent professional experience.
  • Minimum of five years of progressively responsible leadership experience in parish ministry.
  • Demonstrated experience supervising staff and volunteers.
  • Strong pastoral, organizational, leadership, and interpersonal skills.
  • The position requires mature judgment, confidentiality, strong pastoral leadership, and a commitment to fostering lifelong faith formation and missionary discipleship.
  • Evening and weekend work will be required for liturgical celebrations, sacramental preparation, retreats, parish formation opportunities, and seasonal ministry events.
  • Model Christian discipleship through active practice of Catholic faith, practices servant leadership, collaboration, and pastoral charity.

Preferred Attributes

Lakewood Church is seeking caring, dependable, and ministry-minded teachers to serve children in our Spanish Children’s Ministry, Niños con Vida.

As a Ministry Teacher, you’ll help create a positive and engaging classroom environment where children can learn, grow, and experience the love of Jesus. You’ll minister to children through teaching, guidance, encouragement, and care while supporting their physical, emotional, and spiritual needs.

As part of the Niños con Vida team, you’ll help ensure quality ministry takes place in your assigned classroom or role while creating a welcoming experience for children and their families.

Teach & Minister to Children

  • Minister to children through teaching, guiding, comforting, and encouraging them

  • Engage children at their individual developmental stages
  • Care for the physical, emotional, and spiritual needs of children
  • Help ensure quality ministry takes place in the assigned classroom or role

  • Help children transition into and out of classroom environments
  • Respond positively and appropriately when challenging behaviors arise

Serve as Part of the Niños con Vida Team

  • Work collaboratively with Niños con Vida staff, volunteers, coordinators, and ministry leaders
  • Actively look for opportunities to assist with classroom transitions, additional responsibilities, and team needs
  • Encourage and inspire volunteer commitment in others
  • Maintain a cooperative, respectful, and positive team attitude
  • Remain gracious, kind, and loving even in high-pressure situations
  • Be open to correction and responsive to volunteer and staff leadership

Be Prepared & Dependable

  • Arrive in assigned areas on time, prepared, and ready to serve
  • Complete assigned classroom paperwork and classroom clean-up
  • Attend Niños con Vida team meetings, staff meetings, and area trainings
  • Communicate schedule changes in a timely manner with the appropriate coordinator and ministry leaders
  • Maintain flexibility when requested schedule changes are needed
  • Perform other related duties as assigned

Qualifications

Successful candidates will demonstrate:

  • An uncompromised commitment to Lakewood Church’s vision, values, and core beliefs
  • A growing and committed relationship with Christ and a heart to serve and minister to children and their parents
  • Fluency in both English and Spanish
  • The ability to relate positively to children of all ages, parents, volunteers, staff, and leaders
  • Strong interpersonal and communication skills
  • A cooperative and respectful attitude
  • The ability to remain gracious, kind, and loving under pressure
  • Openness to correction and responsiveness to volunteer and staff leadership
  • A demonstrated commitment to excellence in assigned responsibilities
  • The ability to lift 20 pounds or more
  • Willingness to make requested changes to work schedules

Education & Experience:

  • High School Diploma or GED required
  • Minimum six months of volunteering, daycare, or teaching experience
  • One year of volunteering, daycare, or teaching experience preferred

Our Mission

As a member of the Lakewood Church team, you play an important role in helping fulfill our mission of bringing hope through Jesus Christ to people around the world.

Employees serving in this position are expected to support the Church’s mission, maintain a lifestyle consistent with our biblical beliefs, participate in the life of the Church, and serve as part of our faith community. Ministerial responsibilities include regular attendance at church services and classes, serving as a Prayer Partner or ministry volunteer, and participating in community outreach opportunities as needed.

The Worship and Outreach Director is responsible for creating an inviting worshipful environment for the congregation and organizing MBC Prince William to serve the community. 

As a Worship Director, this person will be responsible for overseeing the worship portion of services, including singing, musical selection and arrangement; training and shepherding volunteers and musicians; collaborating with all MBC Location Worship Leaders to ensure consistent quality and theology across all of our Locations. This responsibility will include some commitment to our Tysons Location. 

As an Outreach Director, this person will be responsible for organizing and executing outreach to the community while equipping the church to participate. 


Duties and responsibilities (Essential Functions)

The following items describe some of the ways this individual will accomplish this task:

  • Fulfill the duties required of McLean Bible Church members as outlined in our Mission and Beliefs
  • Philosophical and doctrinal alignment with Scripture/Church Leadership
  • Passionate about the MBC vision
  • Demonstrated musical skill and theological discernment. 
  • Proven track record in ministry and biblical discipleship of others 
  • Proven track record as a leader
  • Possess excellent verbal communication skills and cultural awareness.

 

Worship (MBC Prince William) 

  • Assist the Location Pastor in creating and cultivating the worship singing culture of the Prince William Location
  • Responsible for arranging music, helping musicians grow in their ability to play the arrangements skillfully, leading the band through arrangements during rehearsal and service
  • Collaborate with the Location Pastor to plan weekly worship services, especially as relates to musical selection and arrangements
  • Weekly service planning including song selection and arrangements for weekend and services (including leading vocal and band rehearsal weekly).
  • Oversee leading worship for weekend Location services, as well as weekly Staff/ Directorship meetings
  • Disciple, mentor and develop Worship leaders and teams who can rotate and provide quality worship
  • Recruit, train, organize, and shepherd music and production volunteers serving with bands and production teams.
  • Lead worship for special events (Good Friday, Christmas, weekday events, etc.).
  • Participate in songwriting, arranging, and recording.
  • Serve at other MBC Locations, as needed; Collaborate with staff at those Locations to ensure consistency in messaging and quality.
  • Help plan and lead weekly services with the Location Pastor and other pastoral staff, focusing on musical selections and arrangements 
  • Understand and help thoughtfully arrange the various elements of the worship gathering: songs, prayers, Scriptures, exhortations, commissioning, and ordinances
  • Oversee arrangements and lead rehearsal for services and special events; this could include loading tracks into mainstage prior to rehearsal, etc.
  • Help encourage, equip, and empower new musicians
  • Other Worship responsibilities as requested and approved by Location pastor. 

 

Qualifications

  • Experience with IEMs, talkback mics, and some live audio required
  • Experience with Planning Center, ProPresenter, Multi-tracks, and Mainstage 
  • Skilled vocalist and instrumentalist with ability to deliver a mix of musical genres to satisfy a diverse congregation and to include/accommodate a variety of instruments and vocal styles (contemporary, big band, classical, pop, inspirational, gospel, choral, traditional, etc.)
  • Proven success at multi-tasking, time management, and prioritizing.
  • Views congregational singing as a spiritual function not just a musical one
  • Ability to handle sensitive issues and maintain confidentiality and trust regarding Director and member information.
  • Proven ability to work with and maintain positive, loyal relationships with those inside and outside the church. 
  • Ability to recruit, develop, empower and equip volunteers, direct reports or other stakeholders.
  • Love for Jesus and a desire to see lives and communities changed by the gospel.
  • Mature team player, with a passion for ministry and a dynamic walk with Christ
  • Punctual, attention to detail, team player, musician's ear
  • Experience in multicultural music and ministry
  • Minimum Degree - bachelor’s degree
  • Minimum Experience 3 to 5 years’ experience in leading worship preferred 
  • Commit to MBC Prince William Location as their local church
  • Passion for serving the church.

 

Working conditions

  • The Worship and Outreach Director position requires great flexibility in hours available for work, including evenings, weekends and holidays.
  • This job operates mostly on a musical stage using equipment such as microphones and speakers. 
  • This position requires up to 5% local travel.

 

Physical requirements

Must be able to read, speak, and hear. Must be able to effectively communicate both orally and in writing. While performing the duties of this job, the individual is required to stand or sit for long periods of time while using equipment. 

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job.

Executive Support

Residency Program Outline

VISION: The goal of the residency is to fully equip every individual to be an effective minister of the Gospel, either in a traditional ministry setting or church-planting context.


FOUR OBJECTIVES OF THE PROGRAM

1. Ministry Exposure

Preparation for Gospel work will flourish if those in training can be placed in a local church where they have opportunities to test and grow their gifts. Only by putting into practice what they are learning in the classroom will they grow. Residents need a safe environment to make mistakes and learn from them. They also need the opportunity to develop the right instincts for ministry by participating in a substantial, meaningful way.

2. Personal Development

Formal education offers great content and a logical structure for teaching. However, when it comes to personal and character development, nothing compares with having a mentor. This dynamic is particularly true in Gospel ministry where life and doctrine are so intimately connected.

3. Professional Development

Although pastors are not strictly professionals, there are professional skills that are applied every day. Therefore, residents will be developed in some strategic ways: church administration, public speaking, productivity, leading staff teams, etc.

4. Theological and Spiritual Development

If you are going to teach the Bible well, you will need tools that will help you read, understand, and prepare to teach God's Word. Our goal is to prepare you to share and apply God's Word thoughtfully and faithfully.


The Residency will begin on June 15th, 2027 and end on July 31st, 2029.

Campus Staff Minister - South Carolina (Graduate & Faculty Ministry)

Work Location:

South Carolina

Job Type:

Full time

God has called InterVarsity to plant and to build witnessing communities of students and faculty who follow Jesus on college and university campuses. Through these groups, we believe ever- increasing numbers of students and faculty from all ethnic groups and areas of the campus will be transformed by the Gospel. We expect to see campuses increasingly become places where people, ideas, and structures flourish to the glory of God. We confidently anticipate that our InterVarsity alumni will become change agents across the country and around the world. We pursue this calling by discerning and actively participating in what God is already doing on campus. This is the essence of being a Campus Staff Minister (CSM).

Please submit the GFM Interest Form before completing the full application for a position with Graduate & Faculty Ministries in our online system. We will contact you when we are ready to proceed with the application process.  

This position is open to applicants working less than 40 hours/week. If you are interested in part-time work please apply for this position. 

The pay range listed is for an employee working 40 hours/week at CSM level II. Pay will be prorated for employees who work less than 40 hours/week.

Volunteers are welcome. Volunteer opportunities range from prayer and hospitality to leading a campus fellowship of graduate students and faculty. Those interested in volunteering will go through an application and interview process, however, volunteer openings are not posted online. For more information, complete the GFM Interest Form. 

ESSENTIAL COMMITMENTS/RESPONSIBILITIES 

Spiritual Growth 

As a Campus Staff Minister, you pursue maturity as a disciple of Jesus Christ so that your life and work increasingly reflect a growing love for God, God’s Word, God’s people of every ethnicity and culture, and God’s purposes in the world. To do this, you will: 

  • Pursue a vibrant relationship with the triune God through engagement with Scripture, prayer, and worship, both individually and in community

  • Develop self-leadership (growing in self-awareness, self-management, relational integrity, and resiliency) 

  • Embrace Scriptural standards for behavior and attitudes 

 

Campus Leadership 

As a Campus Staff Minister, you increase the number of witnessing communities, as well as the size, health, spiritual maturity, and campus-wide influence of existing witnessing communities of students and faculty by being a: 

  • Visionary Guide: 

You communicate and model InterVarsity’s vision to see students and faculty transformed, campuses renewed, and world changers developed 

  • Create a culture of humble dependence on God and bold expectation in God’s intention to start new witnessing communities throughout the campus and on new campuses 

  • Model – in person and through programs – InterVarsity’s vision and Core Values, including a biblically-defined commitment to engage every ethnic and social group on campus 

  • Lead students and faculty – individually and collectively – through Scripture, prayer, teaching, and discipleship experiences, so that they articulate and align their ministry activities around this vision 

  • Set annual goals through prayer, research and reflection with your teams (students, faculty, and staff) for qualitative and quantitative growth, including conversions and leadership development 

  • Structural Architect: 

You create, develop, align, and leverage ministry plans, programs, teams, and structures to close the gap between current reality and the aspirational goals. 

  • Build leadership teams who trust and partner well with you and who demonstrate spiritual vitality, relational health, and mission alignment 

  • Develop and execute plans to achieve annual goals, evaluating and modifying the plan as needed throughout the year 

  • Increase momentum for the vision by aligning programs, structures, conferences, and teams around the goals 

  • Mobilize students and faculty to engage their relational networks with the gospel and to start new missional communities 

  • Under the direction of the Area Director, may supervise Ministry Interns and Campus Ministry Interns as delegated 

  • Missional Developer: 

You intentionally gather, invite, and develop diverse groups of students and faculty so that they not only encounter and follow Jesus as Savior and Lord but also advance the mission on campus as participants and leaders. 

  • Create ways for faculty and students to encounter and follow Jesus through Scripture, worship, prayer, mission experiences, conferences, etc. 

  • Equip students and faculty so that they think strategically about campus engagement and so that they proclaim – in word, deed, and power – the good news of Jesus, regularly inviting students and faculty to follow him as Savior and Lord 

  • Disciple students and faculty by equipping them to hear the Word, respond actively, and debrief and interpret the experience so that they grow in Christlikeness, reflect our Core Values, and develop ministry skills 

  • Invite, coach, and equip students and faculty to become increasingly effective participants and leaders, including starting new witnessing communities on campuses 

 

Organizational Collaboration 

As a Campus Staff Minister, you have joined a national mission. Therefore, you work with a network of other local, area, regional, and national InterVarsity staff and volunteers so that our work reflects Biblical standards of excellence, integrity, and partnership. 

  • Partner with and respond positively to the direction and coaching of your supervisors and national leaders 

  • Contribute to collaborative and productive team meetings and relationships 

  • Affiliate chapters under your care and submit Graduating Student Forms in order to increase our partnership with current students and alumni 

  • Use national ministry resources and tools, as requested, including recruiting and/or participating in local, regional, or national conferences as  

  • Complete reporting, planning and review requirements in a timely way so that you and your supervisors can assess and improve your work as a CSM 

  • Comply with all InterVarsity policies and procedures 

 

Ministry Partnership Development 

As a Campus Staff Minister, you will develop a team of partners – churches and individuals (including alumni and community members) – who will resource the ministry financially, in prayer, or volunteer service that advances the mission. 

  • Raise 100% of the financial budget assigned by your supervisor 

  • Communicate regularly with your ministry partners, nurturing the relationship through visits, phone calls, emails and regular prayer letters 

  • Develop on-going, long-lasting partnership with alumni and volunteers 

  • Comply with all Ministry Partnership Policies 

  • Identify and invest in advocates who will build networks of volunteers and donors on InterVarsity’s behalf 

 

Accomplish all other assigned tasks as appropriate 

 

QUALIFICATIONS (common to all levels of CSM) 

  • Annually affirm InterVarsity’s Statement of Agreement (Doctrinal Basis and Purpose Statement). Abide by InterVarsity’s Code of Conduct. Believe and behave consonantly with InterVarsity’s Human Sexuality Theological Paper. Affirm and behave consonantly with InterVarsity’s “Women in Ministry Statement of Affirmation” 

  • Bachelor’s degree for CSMs assigned to a four-year campus. A minimum of an Associate’s degree for CSMs assigned to a two-year campus or a community college 

  • Strong interpersonal skills (including ability to minister to diverse ethnic communities and faculty) 

  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills 

  • Demonstrated problem solving skills 

  • Familiarity with word processing, presentation, email, and spreadsheet software 

 

WORK ENVIRONMENT/PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS 

The CSM position leads ministry in a college campus environment. A designated office space may or may not be available. The CSM is required to travel to on-campus and off- campus sites as appropriate. Off-campus travel includes, but is not limited to: student ministry conferences, Ministry Partnership Development meetings, and InterVarsity- sponsored training sessions, meetings, and conferences. The CSM is regularly required to communicate with others, and routinely uses standard office equipment such as computers, phones, photocopiers, filing cabinets, etc. 

Pay Range: $44,016.00 - $58,680.00 per year

Pay: This position is funded through personal fundraising. Accordingly, compensation will vary based on the ability of the individual to secure a donor team to fund the cost of his/her salary. The anticipated salary range for this position on a full-time basis (40 hours/week) is dependent on a variety of factors, including location and cost of living. The actual salary received, including any geographic adjustment to account for location and cost of living, is subject to the individual’s ability to raise funds necessary to cover the full amount of such salary within the range set forth in the job posting details.

Benefits:

We offer a competitive benefits package, including health care and retirement savings with a match. Eligibility is based on employee type and hours worked.  Benefits include the following:

Description

SUMMARY 

The School of Ministry seeks Adjunct Instructors to teach graduate-level courses in Bible, theology, pastoral ministry, non-profit leadership, chaplaincy, philosophy of religion, intercultural studies philosophy of religion, intercultural studies, or other ministry-related disciplines. The position requires a strong commitment to the Christian faith, as well as excellence in teaching, scholarly research, and service.

Palm Beach Atlantic University is a comprehensive Christian university whose mission is to equip students to grow in wisdom, lead with conviction, and serve God boldly, emphasizing moral, spiritual, and intellectual development.

STATUS

Applications reviewed on a rolling basis until positions are filled.

EDUCATION

Required to hold an earned terminal degree for the specific discipline (Ph.D. or equivalent, D.Min.). Earned 18 graduate credit hours in a biblical, theological, philosophical, or ministry-related discipline, preferred.

QUALIFICATIONS

  • Demonstrated expertise in the discipline.
  • Prior collegiate-level teaching experience, preferred.
  • Commitment to teaching excellence and service to the college, university, and community.

APPLICATION REQUIREMENTS

All applications must be submitted through the university’s career portal at pba.edu. At least three (3) references should be included within the CV.

About Palm Beach Atlantic University

Palm Beach Atlantic University is a private, nondenominational Christian university in West Palm Beach, Florida, known for its faith-guided academics and ocean-side location. It offers a liberal arts curriculum with a focus on developing character and promoting spiritual growth. PBA has a main campus in downtown West Palm Beach and an online program.

The Associate Worship Pastor is primarily responsible for leading and building the worship experience for our campus and church online attenders.
 
At Life.Church, we exist to lead people to become fully devoted followers of Christ. It’s been our mission since 1996 and has guided us every day. Leading people isn’t just an expectation; it’s a necessity.  It’s a cornerstone of our culture. That's why we’re always seeking leaders—leaders like you—to bring your skills to life. We are one church meeting in multiple locations, and we want to help you become the person God made you to be. 
 
The Life.Church Worship Team inspires and moves people towards Christ by creating spiritual experiences through story-telling and biblical truth. Worship is the musical expression of Life.Church. It’s the first part of a service that people experience and often the time they identify as what makes a campus “theirs.” It sets the stage for the message of the day, and it primes people for life change. 
 
The Associate Worship Pastor will provide musical and technical leadership to pursue excellence for worship experiences. Additionally, the Associate Worship Pastor will support the Worship Pastor by leading various ministerial services, such as weddings, baptisms, funerals, and hospital visits. Furthermore, this role will contribute to the planning, organizing, and leading of multiple worship experiences throughout the week.

What You'll Do

  • Plan, organize, and spiritually lead multiple weekly worship services.
  • Recruit, train, and build worship teams.
  • Plan and organize worship services to meet weekly time requirements.
  • Sharpen musical and technical abilities in an ongoing way.
  • Lead contractors and volunteers to sharpen musical abilities.
  • Master Pro-Tools and other experience-based systems.
  • Assist with all campus team technical efforts.
  • Lead volunteer and contractor recruitment and development efforts. 
  • Provide pastoral guidance to Life.Church’s staff members and attenders during hospital visits on a weekly basis.
  • Perform various ministerial services, such as weddings, funerals, baptisms, etc.
  • Administer communions, counseling, and SYMBIS.
  • Manage social media accounts, volunteer applications and reports, AED, First Aid, campus calendars, and pastor on call rotation.

Skills Needed to Succeed

  • Ability to develop an understanding of band dynamics, worship environment production, and ministry teamwork in a worship team setting.
  • Must exemplify a high level of customer focus.
  • Ability to create a vision and execute effectively.
  • Strong interpersonal skills and positive attitude.
  • Ability to self-motivate and make independent decisions.
  • Highly talented vocalist.
  • Experience with keys, guitar, and/or other instruments.
  • Familiar with Pro-Tools.
  • Effective at multi-tasking, time management, and following up.
  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills.
  • Strong spiritual maturity.
  • Comfortable in diplomatic interactions.
  • Exceptional talent vocally to lead a worship experience.
  • Maintain composure during stressful situations.
  • High school diploma or GED.
  • 1-3 years of related work experience.
 
#LI-ONSITE

At Life.Church, we are passionate about reaching more people in more communities. We hire new team members to begin their journey at an existing Life.Church location so they can learn the culture and systems of our church from experienced pastors already on the team. Our hope is, as we continue to launch new locations, we can send pastors who are ready to lead on day one because of what they’ve learned at an existing location in preparation.  
 
Check out the list of current locations and the cities we’re exploring or considering for future locations. We’d love to discuss which locations you are interested in.

Benefits We Offer

  • Paid parental leave, including maternity, paternity, and adoption leave.
  • Generous employer-paid leave for the use of vacation, sick time, and other qualifying reasons. 
  • Innovative and comprehensive Medical, Dental, and Vision insurance that provides team members with useful resources and savings to navigate their holistic health. 
  • Life insurance policy provided for all staff members at 2x annual salary at no cost. Additional life insurance coverage is available to purchase. 
  • Short-Term and Long-Term disability is covered at 100% for full-time qualified staff members.
  • Comprehensive wellness and mental health benefits allow staff to proactively invest in their physical and emotional health.
  • Generous 401(k) retirement plan allowing a team member to have up to 12.5% (including employee contribution, employer match, and employer discretionary contribution) contributed into their account in their first year. It doesn’t stop there—the more years on staff, the greater the investment! 
  • $160 annually in development dollars for team members to invest in their professional growth. 
  • Casual dress and work environment.
  • And much more!
 

Our Beliefs, Culture, and Commitment to Diversity

At Life.Church, every staff member, and intern is a minister and is expected to engage in the church's ministry fully. We consider ministry readiness and an individual’s capacity to represent Life.Church’s beliefs as a minister during the selection process for all staff and intern positions. An essential function within every position held by a staff member or intern at Life.Church is to uphold and represent the beliefs of Life.Church. Learn more about what we believe at Life.Church. 
 
While we unite around our mission, we know unity doesn’t mean uniformity. Our calling is too great, and our mission is too important not to be intentional about strengthening our team through diversity. We know that diverse perspectives in race, ethnicity, background, age, and gender are essential to reaching the world for Christ. To learn more about how we strengthen our team through diversity, visit our careers page.

post_html:
Overview

For over 25 years, G&A Partners has been helping entrepreneurs grow their businesses, take better care of their employees, and enjoy a higher quality of life by providing proven HR solutions and technology. G&A Partners' client is currently seeking an Executive Assistant to the Senior Pastor to join its team in Humble,TX.

 

Summary

The Executive Assistant to the Senior Pastor serves as a highly trusted administrative and strategic partner responsible for maximizing the effectiveness, efficiency, and stewardship of the Office of the Senior Pastor.

 

This position manages executive scheduling, communications, project coordination, meeting preparation, board and community engagement logistics, and confidential administrative matters on behalf of the Senior Pastor. The Executive Assistant helps ensure that priorities are aligned, deadlines are met, relationships are maintained, and the Senior Pastor can focus on vision, preaching, leadership development, and strategic ministry initiatives.

 

The ideal candidate is exceptionally organized, proactive, emotionally intelligent, detail-oriented, and able to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced ministry environment while maintaining the highest level of professionalism and confidentiality.

 

This role serves a critical leadership support function in advancing The Church's mission, vision, and strategic priorities by effectively managing the Senior Pastor's office.

Responsibilities

GENERAL

  • A Christian in complete agreement with The Church's statement of faith, willing and able to serve Christ and His church, spiritually mature.
  • Demonstrate commitment to the mission, vision, and values of The Church.
  • Maintain the highest standards of professionalism, discretion, and confidentiality.
  • Build exemplary relationships with members, staff, volunteers, community partners, and external stakeholders.
  • Represent the Senior Pastor with professionalism, hospitality, and excellence.
  • Perform other duties as assigned by the Senior Pastor.

EXECUTIVE OFFICE MANAGEMENT

 

CALENDAR AND SCHEDULING MANAGEMENT

  • Manage and maintain the Senior Pastor's calendar, appointments, meetings, speaking engagements, travel, and ministry commitments.
  • Coordinate travel arrangements, itineraries, lodging, transportation, and logistics for the Senior Pastor.
  • Prioritize requests and opportunities according to strategic organizational priorities.
  • Coordinate meeting logistics, agendas, briefing materials, and follow-up actions.
  • Anticipate scheduling conflicts and proactively recommend solutions.

CORRESPONDENCE AND COMMUNICATIONS

  • Serve as the primary point of contact for communications to the Office of the Senior Pastor.
  • Draft, edit, and manage correspondence, reports, recommendations, and executive communications, including routine responses for the Senior Pastor's review and approval.
  • Manage and prioritize incoming email and requests on behalf of the Senior Pastor, ensuring timely, professional follow-up.
  • Coordinate communication between the Senior Pastor and church leadership, staff, trustees, board members, ministry leaders, and external partners.

CONFIDENTIAL ADMINISTRATIVE SUPPORT

  • Handle highly confidential information regarding personnel matters, leadership discussions, donor information, church business, and strategic initiatives.
  • Maintain organized records, files, reports, and executive documentation.
  • May occasionally assist with confidential scheduling and logistical matters involving the Senior Pastor's family, while maintaining the highest level of discretion and professionalism.

STRATEGIC PROJECT MANAGEMENT

 

EXECUTIVE PROJECT COORDINATION

  • Assist in coordinating strategic initiatives led by the Senior Pastor.
  • Track key projects, deadlines, deliverables, and follow-up items.
  • Monitor progress on assignments delegated by the Senior Pastor.
  • Capture and track action items resulting from meetings involving the Senior Pastor.
  • Coordinate follow-up with ministry and administrative leaders to ensure commitments, deadlines, and deliverables are completed.
  • Prepare executive summaries, briefing documents, and status reports.

BOARD, GOVERNANCE, AND COMMUNITY ENGAGEMENT SUPPORT

  • Coordinate materials, logistics, and communication related to board, advisory, and community leadership responsibilities.
  • Assist with preparation for educational, civic, and community meetings.
  • Maintain records and action items related to governance and external leadership commitments.

EVENTS AND ENGAGEMENT

 

SENIOR PASTOR EVENTS AND ENGAGEMENTS

  • Coordinate logistics for speaking engagements, conferences, community appearances, and special events involving the Senior Pastor.
  • Assist with the administrative preparation of presentations, teaching materials, and speaking engagements, including research coordination, document preparation, and distribution of materials as requested.Prepare briefing documents and event materials.
  • Serve as administrative liaison for event organizers and external partners.

CONGREGATIONAL CARE AND RELATIONSHIP MANAGEMENT

  • Maintain and strengthen strategic relationships with major donors, community leaders, ministry partners, elected officials, educational institutions, and church members through proactive communication, exceptional hospitality, and consistent follow-up.
  • Ensure appropriate follow-up and hospitality related to executive engagements and meetings.

Qualifications

KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, AND ABILITIES REQUIRED FOR THIS POSITION

  • Bachelor's degree strongly preferred; an equivalent combination of education and progressively responsible executive administrative experience may be considered.
  • Minimum of 5 years of executive-level administrative support experience.
  • Experience supporting senior executives, pastors, CEOs, nonprofit leaders, or elected officials is strongly preferred.
  • Exceptional organizational, planning, and time-management skills.
  • Strong written, verbal, and interpersonal communication skills.
  • Demonstrated ability to interact professionally with executives, board members, elected officials, community leaders, donors, and church members.
  • Demonstrated ability to anticipate needs, exercise sound judgment, solve problems proactively, and manage multiple competing priorities with strong attention to detail in a high-capacity executive environment.
  • Advanced proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite, Google Workspace, and calendar management platforms; Working proficiency with AI productivity tools (such as Microsoft Copilot, ChatGPT, Claude, and similar platforms) to draft correspondence, summarize materials, and increase efficiency.
  • Demonstrated emotional intelligence, professionalism, and servant leadership.
  • Ability to work independently while exercising sound judgment and initiative.

Equal Opportunity Employer Statement

G&A Partners as an Equal Opportunity Employer considers all applicants and prohibits discrimination of any type on the basis of actual or perceived race, color, creed, religion, national origin, ancestry, citizenship status, age, sex or gender (including pregnancy, childbirth and pregnancy-related conditions), gender identity or expression (including transgender status), sexual orientation, marital status, military service and veteran status, physical or mental disability, genetic information, or any other characteristic protected by applicable federal, state or local laws and ordinances. Our management team is dedicated to providing a work environment free of discrimination and harassment based on any of these characteristics. We are committed to this policy and achieving a diverse workforce with respect to recruitment, hiring, placement, promotion, transfer, training, compensation, benefits, employee activities, access to facilities and programs and general treatment during employment.

The Youth Pastor will provide consistent teaching, relational presence and organizational oversight, helping students, families and volunteers stay connected to the life and mission of AHCC. This is a full-time position.

• Oversee all weekly programming for middle school and high school students, ensuring each gathering is welcoming and discipleship focused
• Articulate a clear vision for AHCC students and execute it with organizational follow-through.
• Teach regularly and create environments where students can know, love and follow Jesus
• Ensure a visible leadership presence at Sunday gatherings and actively participate in the broader life of AHCC

• Develop a plan for student care, spiritual growth and leadership development through groups, mentoring and discipleship rhythms

• A vibrant and growing relationship with Jesus Christ

SUMMARY

The Worship Associate works in partnership with the Starkville Campus Lead Worship Pastor to lead the worship and technical teams for Pinelake Starkville’s campus. As a leader, this person will assist in the development, implementation, direction, and promotion of a Worship Ministry that is relevant to both the Pinelake Starkville congregation and to the wider community. The Worship Associate will serve as the primary worship leader for PL College services as well as provide leadership and oversight to worship in our NextGen environments. This person will be responsible for the spiritual health and musical development of the teams within his/her care.

GENERAL RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Learn
    • Pursue a growing relationship with Jesus through consistent time in God’s Word and prayer.
    • Continually grow in your understanding of the Jesus-Centered Life (salvation, identity, life, and authority in Christ).
    • Remain teachable and hungry, seeking feedback, learning from others, and developing both spiritually and professionally.
    • Cultivate awareness of God’s presence in everyday life, listening to the Holy Spirit and responding in obedience.
  • Live
    • Practice and model the rhythms of Be the Church (Grow, Pray, Connect, and Share).
    • Pursue emotional health by engaging in self-awareness, addressing past wounds, and cultivating honest, healthy relationships.
    • Practice healthy rhythms, prioritizing your relationship with Jesus and your family
    • Embody a life of integrity and surrender, allowing your private life with God to shape your work.
  • Lead
    • Take ownership of disciple-making by personally investing in others and helping them move toward a Jesus-Centered Life.
    • Walk others through the Discipleship Pathway (Essentials → JCL → Be the Church), helping them discover and take their next step.
    • Shepherd people, not just programs, by listening for where God is at work in their story and walking with them toward transformation.
    • Equip and release others by developing Servant Leaders and multiplying disciples who Learn from Christ, Live in Christ, and Lead others to Christ.
    • Measure success by life change, spiritual formation, and multiplication—not just attendance or activity.
  • Embrace the Culture
    • Value and embody the staff values, which we call the 7 H’s: Humility, Honor, Honesty, Hunger, Holy Spirit, Health, and Harmony
    • Communicate clearly, honestly, and proactively in a way that builds trust, unity, and momentum.
    • Work in alignment with the church vision and leadership
    • Participate fully in the life of your campus or team, contributing to the unity, health, and shepherding of the faith family.

SPECIFIC LIST OF DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Plans, oversees and evaluates all components of College Worship ministry and NextGen worship.
  • Conducts regular planning meetings with peers and servant leaders.
  • As necessary, assists other pastors and local campus ministries in the successful completion of regular worship events and special events.
  • Assists with the management of the campus worship ministry budget within the parameters established by the One Church Worship team and Starkville Campus Lead Worship Pastor.
  • Establishes goals and objectives for College Worship ministry and initiates strategies to fulfill them.
  • Works closely with Starkville Campus Lead Worship Pastor, College and Student Pastors/Ministers to ensure continuity of worship service programming among areas of the ministries.
  • Plans and promotes activities to support College worship ministry.
  • In keeping with the principles taught in Ephesians 4:11-12, supervises the enlistment, education, and evaluation of all servant leaders in the College Worship Ministry, which may include vocalists, band members, and production support teams.
  • Performs administrative duties such as compiling reports, preparing expense reports and completing purchasing orders as specified by church policy.
  • Attends at least one regular weekly worship service and be present on the church campus during all other regular weekly worship services.
  • Performs other duties as assigned.

SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES

Works with and leads servant leaders.

QUALIFICATIONS

To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily. The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skill and/or ability required. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform essential functions.

EDUCATION AND/OR EXPERIENCE

Bachelor’s degree preferred. Two years of experience minimum for competitive candidates. Applicable experience may substitute for portions of the educational framework.

LANGUAGE SKILLS

The individual must be able to understand written or oral instructions; read, analyze, and interpret documents, instruction manuals, and policies and procedures. Excellent interpersonal skills, ability to work with a diverse group of people, communicate clearly and effectively on the telephone, email and in person, demonstrating tact and diplomacy.

COMPUTER AND MATHEMATICAL SKILLS

The individual must have demonstrated skill in the use of Windows/MacOS to complete tasks, including word processing and spreadsheets and the ability to use the internet for information retrieval. The individual must have basic mathematical skills, knowledge of bookkeeping and basic accounting, and budget and expense monitoring. The individual must have the ability to read financial information and spreadsheets.

The ability to simultaneously conceptualize and plan multiple tasks; project outcomes using different implementation strategies; and apply creative and innovative thinking to problem situations is required. The ability to work effectively and efficiently under stressful conditions to ensure deadlines are met is essential.

PHYSICAL DEMANDS

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to sit, stand, and talk or hear. The employee is required to stand, walk, and reach with hands and arms.

Must be able to lift up to 25 lbs.

WORK ENVIRONMENT

The work environment characteristics described here are representative of those an employee encounters while performing the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

post_html:
*Please note this position would require our Staff to live near the community where they would be doing ministry.

Description:

There are nearly 300,000 teenagers of active-duty U.S. military parents who are stationed all over the world. These teens move an average of seven times during their school-aged years. The questions of identity and belonging that all teens face grow even more challenging to answer amid starting over and meeting new friends at each location.

This is where you can be the difference in a military teen’s life! By being in their world, walking alongside them, and creating a community where they experience the truth of God’s love and purpose for them, our staff provide a safe space where teens can develop friendships and connections to experience laughter, build hope, and generate resiliency.

We are currently providing incarnational ministry at many military installations around the world. You will have the opportunity to lead and oversee the overall Young Life Military program, known as Club Beyond, which is ecumenically focused and outreach oriented.

We are currently looking for both full-time and part-time staff throughout the United States, as well as international locations. Colorado Springs, CO, is the headquarters.

Responsibilities:

  • Actively develop healthy relationships with adults, as well as kids, and build vibrant relationships with the local community, the military installation, and the chapel community.
  • Be a role model (incarnational) and assist with developing community outreach to "unchurched" teens, discipleship to Christian teens, and leading and equipping volunteers to do "hands-on" middle and high school Christian youth programs.
  • Work well in an environment that sees (due to high military operational tempo) a high degree of turnover among teens, families, chaplains and volunteers.
  • Be respectful of and embrace a community that is deeply influenced by a military culture.
  • In this ministry, you will need to live out the Club Beyond Core Value Statement:

Club Beyond is a Christ-centered community of leaders with an exclusively military focus. Our methods are incarnational, and our perspective is ecumenical. We leverage strategic partnerships for the greatest results. We value professionalism from our staff and excellence in our stewardship.

Qualifications:

  • A deep love for Christ and for lost teens.
  • Competent communicator with youths, parents, and senior military leaders.
  • Teachable heart.
  • Willingness to make a three-year commitment.
  • Minimum of three years' youth ministry experience preferred.
  • College degree preferred.
  • Willingness to raise part of the budget through personal support.
  • Committed to a relational ministry approach.
  • Energetic.
  • Small event planning skills.
  • Strong initiative.
  • Note, this position would require our Staff to live near the community where they would be doing ministry.

Salary:

The Base Salary range: $45,000 to $60,000 (Salary is based on education and experience). In addition to salary, a Cost of Living Adjustment, dependent on location, is available. The Annual National Funding provided is $16,667.

Location:

Youth Director - Trinity Evangelical Church

Youth Director (Part-Time)

Trinity Evangelical Church — North Reading, MA
20 hours/week | $25–$30/hour, based on experience | Reports to the Lead Pastor

Trinity is a gospel-centered, non-denominational church north of Boston. For more than 200 years, we have existed to help people become rooted in Jesus, grow together, and serve our community. We typically gather in two Sunday services (one service in the summer) and live-stream as well.

We are seeking a Youth Director who loves Jesus, loves students, and is passionate about helping the next generation grow in their faith. Our Student Ministry currently serves more than 60 active middle and high school students in grades 6–12.

This role is a great fit if one

  • Has a growing relationship with Christ and can affirm Trinity’s Statement of Faith

  • Is passionate about helping middle and high school students follow Jesus

  • Is a strong communicator, relational leader, and team builder

  • Can create engaging, biblically grounded environments for students

  • Enjoy recruiting, developing, and caring for volunteers

  • Value partnering with parents in their children’s spiritual growth

  • Is organized, self-motivated, creative, and collaborative

Core Responsibilities

  • Provide vision and leadership for Student Ministry, grades 6–12

  • Oversee engaging Sunday morning and midweek programming

  • Teach and communicate biblical truth in ways students can understand and apply

  • Build authentic community and a welcoming environment for students

  • Recruit, train, schedule, and support volunteer leaders

  • Partner with parents to encourage students’ spiritual growth

  • Develop opportunities for discipleship, outreach, service, and leadership

  • Collaborate with the Lead Pastor and church staff

What Success Looks Like

Students growing in their relationship with Christ, a welcoming and thriving youth community, strong partnerships with parents, and a healthy team of equipped and cared-for volunteers.

Compensation

$25–$30 per hour for approximately 20 hours per week, depending on experience and qualifications.

How to Apply

Submit the following with the subject line Youth Director and include:

  1. A brief letter of interest

  2. résumé

  3. Contact information for two or three references

Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis until the position is filled.

Trinity Evangelical Church is committed to equal employment opportunity consistent with applicable federal and Massachusetts law. As a religious organization, we may give preference to individuals who support and further Trinity’s vision, mission, Statement of Faith, and bylaws, where permitted by law.

The primary goal of the Director of Worship & Arts is to help people meet and follow Jesus utilizing music, media, and other artistic expression. The DWA will lead all things worship and production at CCC, and will recruit and develop other leaders to share the stage and the ministry.


Apply for This Job 


Why We Love This Opportunity

I love what God is doing at Christ Community Church. A beautiful expression of the heart of Christ in a beautiful community. I’m excited to find CCC’s new Worship Pastor because this is a strong team, excited about a new season of ministry.


A great match for this position would be:

  • Team player
  • Passion to build a healthy worship culture
  • Strong singer and musician
  • Recruiting and building a team 
  • Basic knowledge of AVL systems




About This Organization

Christ Community Church is a growing church in beautiful Rochester, Minnesota. CCC is not so much a community practicing a religion as much as a community learning to trust in Jesus and growing in a relationship with God. CCC is a member of the Christian & Missionary Alliance, a Christian denomination full of believers who long to introduce the love of God to all nations. The church is preparing to celebrate its 60th year of ministry in Rochester. CCC has 3 identical weekend services, one on Saturday and two on Sunday. Small groups also meet throughout the week. The church is known in the community for their outward focus, serving alongside and partnering with several local ministries who serve the marginalized in the city, and for its ministry to families (including an ACSI certified 4-star Parent Award winning pre-school and an outstanding AWANA program that meets on Wednesday nights).


Location

Rochester is a highly liveable city and is consistently ranked as one of the best places in the United States to live and raise a family. We are a smaller town with big amenities. As home to Mayo Clinic, we have the culture, food, and entertainment of a bigger city. We have miles of walking, hiking, and biking trails and an abundance of city and state parks close by. Rochester Public Schools are highly ranked and there are several bedroom communities close by whose schools are also excellent.  


Mission, Vision, and Values

Mission:

  • We introduce people to Jesus and follow Him together.

 

Vision: 

  • To be a church of generous people who honor Jesus, love each other, and serve our neighbors.

https://www.cccrochester.org/about

 

Key Distinctions: 

  • We desire depth in our relationship with Jesus and take the gospel to the darkest places. We believe “deep” expresses itself in “wide”, meaning that you have the heart and mind of Jesus when you care deeply for and think often about people who do not yet know Him. 


Key Responsibilities

  • Champion the mission and vision of Christ Community Church.
  • Be responsible for leading the Worship & Arts Ministry to an ever-increasing level of engagement and excellence.
  • Develop other worship leaders for the stage.
  • Recruit, train, schedule, and coordinate necessary teams and team leaders for all services.
  • Schedule and oversee rehearsals for all teams.
  • Lead worship service planning process.
  • Meet regularly with worship, tech, and arts teams for discipleship, relationship building, planning, and troubleshooting.
  • Provide leadership, mentorship and guidance for kidcity and Impact worship leaders and teams.
  • Assist in additional services held on campus (weddings, funerals, seasonal events – these are pretty minimal).
  • Maintain and upgrade (as needed) sound, music, and video equipment.
  • Create short and long-term plans for maintenance and improvements for all technical equipment.


Key Qualifications

  • An undergraduate degree in worship ministries or other creative fields is preferred.
  • Strategic and creative leader with 3-5 years of relevant leadership experience.
  • Excellent leadership, organizational, and communication skills.
  • Effective team builder with high emotional intelligence.
  • Experience in a larger church is strongly preferred.
  • Proven ability to design effective worship services that are relevant, excellent, intentional, and effective in helping CCC accomplish its mission.
  • Alignment with the Christian & Missionary Alliance and a willingness to pursue licensing.

Description

SUMMARY

In support of the university’s mission and objectives, the Recruiter for the School of Ministry Graduate Programs is responsible for executing recruitment activities for the School of Ministry graduate programs. This position focuses on high-touch outreach, recruitment travel, relationship development, and direct engagement with prospective students, churches, and ministry partners. The Recruiter works collaboratively with academic leadership, admissions, and enrollment marketing to support enrollment growth goals.

Recruitment Activities and Outreach

  • Participates in recruitment events and travel aligned with established enrollment strategy and goals.
  • Coordinates and hosts recruiting events and prospective student visits on campus in collaboration with the Dean, Associate Dean for Graduate Programs, Admissions, and other university departments.
  • Represents the School of Ministry at conferences, graduate fairs, seminary days, church events, and denominational meetings.

Recruitment Engagement and Operations

EXPERIENCE

Position: Worship Leader

Hours: Part-time (10 hours per week)

The part-time Worship Leader is responsible for planning, preparing, and leading the music portion of the weekly worship service. Their primary focus is creating celebrative, Christ-centered environments where all generations are invited into the presence of Jesus through song and praise.

The Worship Leader will work closely with the Campus Pastor to develop worship service orders that effectively proclaim the Gospel and fit well with the sermon.

Requirements:

To continue that mission, Marble seeks a dynamic and inspiring Senior Minister to spiritually lead and build a sustainable future for its congregation while honoring and carrying forward the church’s extraordinary legacy. This is an opportunity for a gifted preacher, pastor, theologian, and leader to help shape the next chapter of this iconic church.

 

The Senior Minister serves as Marble’s primary pastoral, theological, and organizational leader, providing strategic leadership, a compelling vision for the church’s spiritual future, and inspired, biblically grounded preaching. Each week, Marble brings together a diverse in-person congregation and a national and global audience through livestreamed worship and other online offerings. In partnership with ministerial staff, the Marble staff, and the Marble Board, the Senior Minister will strengthen and grow this community, deepening the lives of those in the congregation while finding creative and innovative ways to engage an expanding online audience.

 

The successful candidate will be an approachable, engaged pastoral presence in the church. The Senior Minister will cultivate a welcoming and inclusive culture grounded in compassion, patience, forgiveness, and respect for different perspectives, while creating a compelling vision for Marble’s future that is rooted in its faith, history, and enduring legacy.

 

This is an opportunity to lead the congregation at an important moment in the church’s story and to honor what makes Marble unique, carrying forward the legacy of this iconic church and helping to build an inclusive and long-lasting community for generations to come.

 

Marble Collegiate Church has retained Freeman Philanthropic Services, LLC to assist with this significant recruitment.

Montana
