Description

WORSHIP PASTOR

Colorado Springs, CO 80907

 

Overview

Full-Time | Trace Church | 3,500+ Weekly Attendance

 

Vision & Calling

At Trace Church, we believe worship is more than music — it is spiritual formation, discipleship, and leadership development expressed through song and surrendered lives.

The Worship Pastor is more than a service leader; this pastor is a shepherd of people and a cultivator of culture. This leader will build a thriving worship ministry by developing vocalists and worship leaders in their craft, culture, character, and relationship with Christ.

We believe we are not paid for performance, but for preparation. The Worship Pastor models spiritual health, personal discipline, and relational maturity so that the ministry never outpaces the leader.

 

Worship Pastor Position Overview

The Worship Pastor leads and oversees the entire worship ministry of Trace Church across all services and environments. This role focuses heavily on:

  • Recruiting and developing worship leaders and vocalists. 
  • Shaping and strengthening the worship culture.
  • Shepherding the spiritual lives of team members.
  • Ensuring worship gatherings are spiritually powerful and musically excellent.

This role requires both pastoral depth and musical excellence to lead a growing congregation of 3,500+ people into authentic, Spirit-led worship.

 

Primary Responsibilities

Spiritual & Pastoral Leadership

  • Shepherd the worship ministry as a pastor first and musician second.
  • Provide intentional discipleship for worship leaders, vocalists and musicians. 
  • Develop leaders in character, humility, holiness, and spiritual maturity.
  • Establish rhythms of prayer, devotion, and spiritual growth for the team.
  • Lead through conflict biblically while cultivating a culture of honor and unity.

Recruitment & Team Building

  • Proactively recruit high-capacity vocalists and musicians.
  • Oversee audition processes with excellence and clarity.
  • Build and maintain a sustainable leadership pipeline.
  • Identify potential worship leaders and create intentional growth pathways.
  • Ensure teams are large enough to support growth and multiple services.
  • Develop bench strength for future campuses and expansion.

Worship Leader Development (Craft, Culture, Character, & Christ)

The Worship Pastor is responsible for developing worship leaders holistically in the following areas:

  • Craft
    • Train vocalists in harmony, blend, tone, pitch, and stage awareness.
    • Develop worship leaders in song selection, transitions, and flow.
    • Coach leaders in communication and congregational engagement.
    • Lead rehearsals with musical excellence and intentional feedback.
    • Develop leaders’ proficiency on primary instruments.
  • Culture
    • Shape a team culture marked by humility, unity, honor, and excellence.
    • Establish clear standards for preparation and professionalism.
    • Reinforce that platform ministry flows from private devotion.
    • Create an environment where growth, feedback, and accountability are embraced.
  • Character
    • Model and teach integrity, servanthood, and emotional health.
    • Develop leaders who are spiritually mature before they are platform-ready.
    • Provide consistent pastoral care and mentorship.
  • Relationship with Christ
    • Ensure leaders prioritize personal devotion over performance.
    • Cultivate a culture grounded in prayer and dependence on the Holy Spirit.
    • Develop worship leaders who lead from overflow, not obligation.

Weekend Worship Leadership

  • Lead worship for all weekend services and major church events.
  • Provide strong, engaging vocal leadership for a congregation of 3,500+.
  • Create Christ-centered worship experiences aligned with teaching themes.
  • Design worship sets that flow seamlessly and support the direction of each service.
  • Model authentic worship both on and off stage.

Music Leadership & Production Partnership

  • Champion musical excellence across all services.
  • Lead band arrangements and rehearsals with clarity and direction.
  • Collaborate closely with production, lighting, and media teams.
  • Continuously evaluate and elevate the overall worship environment.

 

Strategic Leadership & Growth

  • Develop scalable systems to support continued growth.
  • Identify, recruit and prepare worship leaders across ministries and possible future campuses.
  • Collaborate with the Executive Pastor of Creative Arts on long-term vision and strategy, with final approval resting with Executive Pastor.  
  • Build a worship culture that can multiply beyond a single leader.


 

 

Qualifications

Spiritual Qualifications

  • Clear calling to pastoral ministry.
  • Evidence of a mature, growing relationship with Jesus Christ.
  • Alignment with Trace Church’s theology, mission, and cultural values.
  • Strong emotional health and relational intelligence.

Leadership Qualifications 

  • Proven experience leading worship in a church of 3,000+.
  • Demonstrated success recruiting and developing volunteer teams.
  • Experience developing and multiplying worship leaders.
  • Strong communication and team-building skills.
  • Ability to lead through growth and change.

Musical & Technical Qualifications

  • Strong, confident vocal leadership.
  • Proficient instrumentalist (guitar preferred).
  • Experience leading full band arrangements.
  • Working knowledge of Ableton Live, Logic Pro, Planning Center Online.
  • Understanding of large-room dynamics and congregational engagement.

 

Staff Expectations 

  • Participate in annual retreats and team gatherings.
  • Engage in a small group and faithfully tithe to Trace Church.
  • Champion and live out Trace’s Cultural Distinctives.
  • Model healthy work rhythms and a consistent Sabbath.


 

 

What Success Looks Like

Within 12–24 months:

  • A deep bench of equipped and developed worship leaders.
  • A thriving and spiritually healthy worship team culture.
  • Strong vocal and musical excellence across services.
  • Clear and effective systems for recruitment and leader development.
  • Worship that leads the congregation into deeper engagement with Christ.

 

Education & Experience

  • Bachelor’s degree in Music, Worship, Theology, or related field (preferred).
  • 5+ years of worship leadership experience in a growing church environment.

 

Employment Details

  • Reports To: Executive Pastor of Creative Arts

Description:

There are nearly 300,000 teenagers of active-duty U.S. military parents who are stationed all over the world. These teens move an average of seven times during their school-aged years. The questions of identity and belonging that all teens face grow even more challenging to answer amid starting over and meeting new friends at each location.

This is where you can be the difference in a military teen’s life! By being in their world, walking alongside them, and creating a community where they experience the truth of God’s love and purpose for them, our staff provide a safe space where teens can develop friendships and connections to experience laughter, build hope, and generate resiliency.

We are currently providing incarnational ministry at many military installations around the world. You will have the opportunity to lead and oversee the overall Young Life Military program, known as Club Beyond, which is ecumenically focused and outreach oriented.

We are currently looking for both full-time and part-time staff throughout the United States, as well as international locations. Colorado Springs, CO, is the headquarters.

Responsibilities:

  • Actively develop healthy relationships with adults, as well as kids, and build vibrant relationships with the local community, the military installation, and the chapel community.
  • Be a role model (incarnational) and assist with developing community outreach to "unchurched" teens, discipleship to Christian teens, and leading and equipping volunteers to do "hands-on" middle and high school Christian youth programs.
  • Work well in an environment that sees (due to high military operational tempo) a high degree of turnover among teens, families, chaplains and volunteers.
  • Be respectful of and embrace a community that is deeply influenced by a military culture.
  • In this ministry, you will need to live out the Club Beyond Core Value Statement:

Club Beyond is a Christ-centered community of leaders with an exclusively military focus. Our methods are incarnational, and our perspective is ecumenical. We leverage strategic partnerships for the greatest results. We value professionalism from our staff and excellence in our stewardship.

Qualifications:

  • A deep love for Christ and for lost teens.
  • Competent communicator with youths, parents, and senior military leaders.
  • Teachable heart.
  • Willingness to make a three-year commitment.
  • Minimum of three years' youth ministry experience preferred.
  • College degree preferred.
  • Willingness to raise part of the budget through personal support.
  • Committed to a relational ministry approach.
  • Energetic.
  • Small event planning skills.
  • Strong initiative.
  • Note, this position would require our Staff to live near the community where they would be doing ministry.

Benefits:

Salary:

The Base Salary range: $45,000 to $60,000 (Salary is based on education and experience). In addition to salary, a Cost of Living Adjustment, dependent on location, is available. The Annual National Funding provided is $16,667.

Location:

Club Beyond works on military installations all over the world. We currently have openings at:

In the USA:

  • Fort Rucker, Alabama

Overview and Purpose

 

Overview:

  • A 9-month pre- or post-seminary residency
  • Typically runs from September 1 through May 31
  • 30 hours per week
  • $20K living stipend

 

Our aim is three-fold:

 

  • Shepherd: To shepherd interns to grow in their affection for God, character, and competency to serve in the church.
  • Guide: To help interns clarify their potential future ministry direction and next steps.
  • Develop: To raise leaders to make disciples and to plant and strengthen churches among our neighbors and the nations.

 

Values and Emphases

 

The residency will be marked by these emphases:

 

  • Gospel Culture: We very intentionally seek to cultivate a church ethos that reflects the gospel. An ethos that humbly welcomes, serves, and honors one another as Christ welcomes, serves, and honors us. We want to shepherd each candidate as Christ would shepherd them, and to train them in how they can create gospel culture in their future ministries.

 

  • Relational: Although we have many “guides” in Christ, we also need spiritual fathers (1 Cor. 4:15). We seek to provide this kind of relational training. Much of what we will teach must be both taught and caught.

 

  • Church-Focused: We complement seminary training by providing a hands-on, relational context to grow in the character and skills needed for healthy church ministry. We will emphasize making disciples, cultivating a gospel culture, encouraging others, personally communing with God, building true friendships, growing in holiness, loving the nations, leading humbly, and ministering in a sustainable way, all within the context of a local church.

 

  • Historically-Enriched: While we need to understand our 21st century context, many ministry trends have not produced fruitful disciples. Some of the best examples of fruit-bearing ministry come from our heritage. Therefore, there will be a substantial amount of reading that will draw from the likes of Augustine, Luther, Calvin, Goodwin, Newton, Edwards, etc.

 

  • Well-Rounded: Ministry leaders need to be trained to grow in both doctrine and character. They also need to be exposed to the whole life of a church–not only to its strengths, but also its weaknesses. Our internship will focus on forming well-rounded, healthy leaders for sustainable ministry.

 

 

Structure and Responsibilities

 

This program divides its time between study and reflection, pastoral mentoring, and ministry exposure and experience.

 

Study and Reflection

Interns will have weekly reading assignments and will write reflection papers which will be discussed with one of the pastors.

 

Pastoral Mentoring

The intern will meet weekly with one of the mentor-pastors as well as with one of the other ministry staff members or ministry leaders.



Ministry Experience and Leadership Development

  • Participate in weekly staff meeting
  • Engage in bi-weekly meetings with various leaders and members: The intern will arrange individual meetings with various ZF leaders to learn about spiritual growth and local church ministry.
  • Various opportunities to teach and disciple.
  • Co-lead a small group and assist in the leadership of a particular ministry.
  • Observe and debrief elders’ meetings each month.
  • Weekly meeting to discuss the principles and practices of Christ-centered biblical exposition.
  • Engage in a number of opportunities by participating or shadowing a leader. For example, Small Group Leadership meetings; funeral and wedding process; Simeon Trust preaching workshop, hospital visitation; meetings for elders, deacons, youth group, etc; membership course; welcome team; men’s ministry.

 

 

Assumptions

 

We assume following of all residents:

 

  1. They will cultivate a daily habit of communing with God through meditating on God’s word and prayer. This is not officially part of the internship, but is a required foundation for the residency to be fruitful.

 

  1. They will be all-in and committed to fulfilling expectations. This includes completing assignments on time, taking initiative in conversations, and seeking to glean from various readings and experiences.

 

  1. They will view themselves as servants and remain open to any kind of task they’re called to fulfill. We seek to follow the example of Jesus, who did not come to be served, but to serve.



Details and FAQs

 

Is office space provided?

Yes, the intern will be provided office space. The intern will ideally use the office for a significant portion of time each week and will set specific office hours. This provides opportunities to get to know staff and members, to participate in the culture of the staff, and to experience daily church-office rhythms.

 

Is housing assistance available?

We are committed to doing what we can to assist with housing. In some cases, and when available, we will be able to secure housing with a family of ZF. In other cases, we may be able to assist with the cost of housing. If we have multiple single interns, we would encourage them to live together as we provide some assistance.

 

What is the church and internships theological perspective?

We are broadly reformed and appreciate the confession statements of The Gospel Coalition and the 1689 London Baptist Confession.

 

Who leads and oversees the internship and residency?

Drew Hunter provides the overall leadership for the internship and residency. Drew is the Teaching Pastor of Zionsville Fellowship, where he provides overall leadership, biblical teaching, and serves as an elder. He graduated from Moody Bible Institute and received MAs from Wheaton College Graduate School in Biblical Exegesis and Systematic & Historical Theology. He and his wife, Christina, have four sons. 

 

Interns and residents will be paired with other pastoral mentors who serve on the staff of Zionsville Fellowship.

The Associate LifeKids Pastor is responsible for building, equipping, and leading a team of volunteer leaders.
 
At Life.Church, we exist to lead people to become fully devoted followers of Christ. It’s been our mission since 1996 and has guided us every day. Leading people isn’t just an expectation; it’s a necessity. It’s a cornerstone of our culture. That's why we’re always seeking leaders—leaders like you—to bring your skills to life. We are one church meeting in multiple locations, and we want to help you become the person God made you to be.
 
Our children's ministry, LifeKids, provides relevant, age-appropriate learning and connection opportunities for kids from birth through 6th grade. LifeKids is dedicated to partnering with parents to help raise children to have a strong relationship with Christ. 
 
The Associate LifeKids Pastor will also work with the LifeKids Pastor to foster an environment conducive to excellence and safety in the LifeKids ministry. Furthermore, this role will oversee recruiting, training, and placing volunteers in roles based on their personal gifts and passions.

What You'll Do

  • ​​Recruit and inspire people to serve in the LifeKids ministry.
  • Make sure ​​leaders are equipped to serve and rooms are set up for families to have an excellent experience.
  • Connect with LifeKids leaders weekly via phone calls, in-person meetings and leading volunteers in group communication.
  • Help ensure the overall operations of the weekend are meeting all expectations.
  • Oversee volunteer onboarding that sets the stage for ongoing care for each volunteer on the team.
  • ​​Maintain a positive LifeKids environment that inspires volunteers and families to engage in the ministry.
  • Communicate daily with the LifeKids Pastor.
  • Balance tasks and relational aspects of the role.
  • ​​Work with LifeKids Pastor to contribute to LifeKids and Campus goals
  • Lead day-to-day operations of the ministry.

Skills Needed to Succeed

  • Must exemplify a high level of passion for sharing the vision of LifeKids with our community.
  • Facilitate ongoing training and coaching for volunteers and next steps for families.
  • Ability to stay organized and can maintain administrative duties.
  • ​​Clear understanding of LifeKids programming, systems, policies and opportunities for attenders to take next steps through the ministries of Life.Church.
  • Effective at conflict management, time management, and coaching skills.
  • Excellent verbal, written, and interpersonal communication skills.
  • Exceptional problem-solving skills.
  • Maintain composure during stressful situations.
  • High school diploma or GED.
  • Up to 12 months of related work experience.

At Life.Church, we are passionate about reaching more people in more communities. We hire new team members to begin their journey at an existing Life.Church location so they can learn the culture and systems of our church from experienced pastors already on the team. Our hope is, as we continue to launch new locations, we can send pastors who are ready to lead on day one because of what they’ve learned at an existing location in preparation.  
 
Check out the list of current locations and the cities we’re exploring or considering for future locations. We’d love to discuss which locations you are interested in.

Benefits We Offer

  • Paid parental leave, including maternity, paternity, and adoption leave.
  • Generous employer-paid leave for the use of vacation, sick time, and other qualifying reasons. 
  • Innovative and comprehensive Medical, Dental, and Vision insurance that provides team members with useful resources and savings to navigate their holistic health. 
  • Life insurance policy provided for all staff members at 2x annual salary at no cost. Additional life insurance coverage is available to purchase. 
  • Short-Term and Long-Term disability is covered at 100% for full-time qualified staff members.
  • Comprehensive wellness and mental health benefits allow staff to proactively invest in their physical and emotional health.
  • Generous 401(k) retirement plan allowing a team member to have up to 12.5% (including employee contribution, employer match, and employer discretionary contribution) contributed into their account in their first year. It doesn’t stop there—the more years on staff, the greater the investment! 
  • $160 annually in development dollars for team members to invest in their professional growth. 
  • Casual dress and work environment.
  • And much more!
 

Our Beliefs, Culture, and Commitment to Diversity

At Life.Church, every staff member, and intern is a minister and is expected to engage in the church's ministry fully. We consider ministry readiness and an individual’s capacity to represent Life.Church’s beliefs as a minister during the selection process for all staff and intern positions. An essential function within every position held by a staff member or intern at Life.Church is to uphold and represent the beliefs of Life.Church. Learn more about what we believe at Life.Church. 
 
While we unite around our mission, we know unity doesn’t mean uniformity. Our calling is too great, and our mission is too important not to be intentional about strengthening our team through diversity. We know that diverse perspectives in race, ethnicity, background, age, and gender are essential to reaching the world for Christ. To learn more about how we strengthen our team through diversity, visit our careers page.

General Summary

The Executive Business Administrator provides strategic leadership and operational leadership for the administrative and operational functions of The Mount Church and serves as the bridge between vision and execution. Working closely with the Senior Pastor and the Executive Leadership team, the Executive Administrator ensures that the church’s mission, vision and ministry goals are effectively supported through strong organizational systems, financial stewardship, staff leadership, and operational excellence.

The Executive Business Administrator will help translate strategy into actionable goals for performance and growth helping to implement organization-wide goal setting, performance management, and annual operating planning. 

Supervisory Responsibilities:

This role supervises the Administration, Operations, and Marketing & Communications. 

Essential Functions

Strategic Leadership:

  • Partner with the Senior Pastor and Executive Leadership to implement the Church’s vision, mission, and strategic initiatives.
  • Support in the Development, implementation, and execution of five-year strategic plan to fulfill Senior Pastor’s vision.
  • Oversee the annual strategic planning sessions for the church. Ownership of strategic plan communication to all levels of the church. 
  • Assist in translating ministry goals into operational plans and measurable outcomes.
  • Lead organizational planning, prioritization, and execution across departments.
  • Monitor performance and operational effectiveness of the church (KPI’s).
  • Develop actionable business strategies and plans that ensure alignment with short-term and long-term objectives developed in tandem with the Senior Pastor.
  • Monitor KPI’s (Key Performance Indicators) with tracking and establish corrective measures as needed, and prepare detailed reports, both current and forecasting.

Marketing & Communications:

  • Provide leadership, guidance, direction and oversight of day-to-day activities of the Marketing & Communication Department to ensure the Marketing & Communications initiatives align with the organization’s strategic goals.
  • Manage the Marketing & Communications Departmental Staff/Contractors/Volunteers, performance metrics, and collaborate across departments to drive brand awareness, member engagement and growth. 

Operations Management:

  • Develop and implement efficient systems, processes, and policies.
  • Ensure smooth coordination between operational and ministry teams.
  • Support planning and logistics for church wide events, services and special initiatives.

Staff Leadership & Development:

  • Develop and implement leadership structures, accountability systems, and support leadership development.
  • Lead leadership team meetings (monthly/quarterly) ensuring alignment, communication and momentum.
  • Foster a healthy staff culture that is aligned with the church’s values and mission.

Ministry Integration &Support:

  • Ensures ministries are resourced with the systems, tools and support needed to succeed.
  • Partner with the Ministry Leader to streamline processes and remove operational barriers and are collaborating and moving in a unified direction.
  • Collaborate with the Ministry Leader to identify gaps, redundancies, or misalignments across ministries and operations and bring resolution.
  • Provide project management support for major ministry initiatives.

Sunday Experience:

  • Ensure ministries are resourced with the systems, tools and support needed to succeed.
  • Partner with the Worship Director to streamline processes and remove operational barriers.
  • Provide project management support for major church wide initiatives.

Finance:

  • Develop and manage the church budget to ensure that it is aligned with the strategic vision of the church.
  • Collaborate with the Finance Team to ensure responsible stewardship of the church finances.
  • Partner with the Finance Team on financial reporting, controls and accountability processes. 
Leadership:

  • Support the work of the Senior Pastor and Executive Leadership through operational insights and reporting.
  • Prepare reports, agendas and materials for board meetings, implement board decisions operationally.
  • Oversee strategic plans and churchwide calendar to ensure alignment with the strategic plan.Provide leadership for innovation and strategic partnerships. 
  • Analyze internal operations and identify areas of process enhancement to support the overall strategy.
  • Maintain and build trusted relationships with key members, clients, partners, and stakeholders.
  • Adhere to church, federal, state, and local business requirements, enforcing compliance when necessary.
  • Manage key leadership meetings to assist in execution of strategy
  • Attend and successfully complete all training as required by The Mount Church.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

Spiritual Qualifications:

  • Demonstrates a strong personal faith and commitment to the mission of The Mount Church.
  • Models Christian character, integrity, and servant leadership.
  • Alignment with the church’s core values and statement of faith.

Education & Experience:

  • This position requires a minimum of a bachelor’s degree in business administration, Christian leadership, nonprofit management or related field.
  •  7-10 years of leadership experience in operations, administration, or executive management.
  • Masters’ degree (MBA, MDIV, or equivalent) strongly preferred.
  • Experience in nonprofit, church, or mission-driven organizations preferred.
  • A solid grasp of data analysis and performance metrics.
 

Skills & Competencies:

Strategic Thinking: Sees the big picture and builds practical plans to get there.                                        Spiritual Maturity: Leads from a place of prayer, humility, and Spirit-dependence.
Execution & Accountability: Gets things done; creates systems and measures results.                           Relational Intelligence: Builds trust, navigates conflict, and leads with emotional maturity.
Communication & Clarity: Communicates vision, expectations, and feedback with clarity.                      Leadership & People Development: Inspires, develops, and holds staff accountable with grace and truth.
 

Key Outcomes:

Success in this role will be measured by:

  • Effective implementation of the church’s vision and strategic initiatives
  • Efficient operational systems and reporting
  • Ministries that are well-supported and able to grow.

Physical Requirements

  • An employee in this position primarily works in a typical office environment and uses office equipment to fulfill the position duties. 
  • An employee in this position is required to walk, hear, speak, and stand to inspect the property and interact with staff, church members, and volunteers. 
  • Work is conducted in a fast-paced, rapidly changing environment. 
  • The ability to manage stress, build professional and collaborative relationships, and reason through complex church business situations is required.
  • A flexible schedule is required since this position requires evening and weekend work. 

Travel Requirements:
A valid Texas drivers’ license and acceptable motor vehicle record is required.

Church Membership:
This position is required to be or become a member of The Mount Church. Employees in this position are expected to sincerely hold the same religious beliefs as expressed by The Mount Church.

 
About Us:
Mount Hebron Missionary Baptist Church is a vibrant and welcoming faith community rooted in the Garland, TX area, committed to spiritual growth, community outreach, and servant leadership. Our congregation is known for its warm fellowship, impactful ministry programs, and dedication to making a difference in the lives of those we serve. We are proud to have a team of passionate staff and volunteers who are united by a shared calling to serve God and community.

We are an equal opportunity employer and all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability status, protected veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law.




About The Mount Church

For generations, Mt. Hebron Missionary Baptist Church, affectionately known as The Mount, has been a beacon of faith on the hill in Garland, Texas. We are a multigenerational church committed to strong Bible-based teaching, vibrant worship, and authentic fellowship. Through every season, we help generations encounter Jesus, grow together, and impact the world for God—building a legacy of faith that will outlast us all.


Our Mission

To build a legacy of faith from generation to generation: Leading people to encounter Jesus, grow together, and impact the world for God.

Our Values

These values are the convictions that bind us together and guide everything we do.


Bible-Based Teaching

Strong, foundational teaching rooted in God's Word that gives hope and light to our community.
2 Timothy 3:16–17 | Hebrews 4:12 | Psalm 119:105


Vibrant Worship

Engaging, passionate worship that creates space for all generations to encounter Jesus.
Psalm 95:1–2 | John 4:23–24 | Psalm 150:1–6


Authentic Fellowship

Welcoming community where people develop genuine relationships and grow together in faith.
Acts 2:42–47 | Hebrews 10:24–25 | 1 John 1:7


Cheerful Generosity

Joyful, sacrificial giving of our resources, time, and talents to advance God's Kingdom.
2 Corinthians 9:7 | Acts 20:35 | Proverbs 11:25
Cheerful Generosity


Dependent Prayer

Complete reliance on God through prayer, seeking His wisdom and power as our first response in all things.
James 5:16 | 1 Thessalonians 5:17 | 2 Chronicles 7:14


Compassionate Impact

Selfless action driven by God's love, meeting needs and transforming lives in our community and beyond.
Matthew 9:36 | Micah 6:8 | James 2:14–17

  • Generous employer-paid leave for the use of vacation, sick time, and other qualifying reasons. 
  • Innovative and comprehensive Medical, Dental, and Vision insurance that provides team members with useful resources and savings to navigate their holistic health. 
  • Life insurance policy provided for all staff members at 2x annual salary at no cost. Additional life insurance coverage is available to purchase. 
  • Short-Term and Long-Term disability is covered at 100% for full-time qualified staff members.
  • Comprehensive wellness and mental health benefits allow staff to proactively invest in their physical and emotional health.
  • Generous 401(k) retirement plan allowing a team member to have up to 12.5% (including employee contribution, employer match, and employer discretionary contribution) contributed into their account in their first year. It doesn’t stop there—the more years on staff, the greater the investment! 
  • $160 annually in development dollars for team members to invest in their professional growth. 
  • Casual dress and work environment.
  • And much more!
 

Our Beliefs, Culture, and Commitment to Diversity

At Life.Church, every staff member, and intern is a minister and is expected to engage in the church's ministry fully. We consider ministry readiness and an individual’s capacity to represent Life.Church’s beliefs as a minister during the selection process for all staff and intern positions. An essential function within every position held by a staff member or intern at Life.Church is to uphold and represent the beliefs of Life.Church. Learn more about what we believe at Life.Church. 
 
While we unite around our mission, we know unity doesn’t mean uniformity. Our calling is too great, and our mission is too important not to be intentional about strengthening our team through diversity. We know that diverse perspectives in race, ethnicity, background, age, and gender are essential to reaching the world for Christ. To learn more about how we strengthen our team through diversity, visit our careers page. 
 
All data collected in our application process, from resume collection to application questions, is used for recruitment purposes only.

Summary of Position:
Provide pastoral ministry at the campus in the areas of the Youth ministry, as well as lead pastorally within the Gateway congregation. This is a generalist role designed to recruit and develop volunteers, coordinate weekly services, preach and teach, partner closely with other Jackson Hole churches and youth ministries, and help youth develop an intimate relationship with God. This role also includes other serving and ministry roles at the campus outside of youth, including pastoral ministry at various levels. The Youth Pastor leads and manages teams to equip the saints for work in ministry. Success in this role includes recruiting and training a healthy leadership team, outreach and discipleship of youth, leadership and presence in Jackson Hole youth ministries outside of Gateway, and a strong pastoral interaction with the congregation.


 

Principal Job Responsibilities:

  • Pastor, oversee, and lead Gateway Youth ministry at the campus and within the larger Jackson Hole community.
  • Recruit, onboard, train, and develop the youth volunteer team.
  • Responsible for preparing sermons and speaking at Wednesday Night services. The Central Youth team will provide content for these messages that this pastor will make their own.
  • Serve at every weekend service at campus (except when on vacation).
    • Every other week the youth pastor will lead the “Mix” room to connect with current and future youth.
    • On alternating weekends, the youth pastor will serve in various weekend ministry roles at the campus alongside the ministry team.
  • Lead or oversee all administrative responsibilities, including Coupa (budget software), Data base processes (in the ROCK system)- including weekly metrics, the volunteer workflow, building reservations, weekly service agenda, etc.)
  • Hold monthly meetings with volunteers to cast vision and set direction for the ministry.
  • Seek to maintain a healthy ratio of volunteers to youth and empower and train volunteers in connecting with students and following up with guests.
  • Communicate regularly and effectively with volunteers and parents.
  • Partner with parents through proactive communication and connection.
  • Plan, manage and execute four Gateway Youth campus events annually (Summer Kickoff, Back-to-School Bash, Friendsgiving and our local version of Youth-Con: “Crossroads”)
  • Plan, manage and execute offsite services as often as needed. (Currently this is an additional Sr. High service that is multi-church led for the purpose of reaching the whole community.)
  • Work with other local youth outreach ministries for influence and impact in the community (i.e. FCA and Young Life)
  • Connect with other youth pastors in Jackson to both strengthen the relationships as well as to strategically align to impact the youth of Jackson Hole.
  • Build and sustain relationships with local junior high/middle schools and high schools to serve the school, build relationships with youth, and facilitate ministry on campus.
  • Serve as pastor on call as necessary.
  • Demonstrates careful attention to detail in planning weekly services and off-site events.
  • Perform biblical counseling for congregants as necessary.
  • Manage youth financial aid requests for both camp and conference.
  • Organize transportation for their youth to camp and conference. (if applicable)
  • Help with serving at the campus in multiple ways outside of youth ministry (as a small campus, everyone wears multiple hats)

General Skills & Qualifications:

  • Proficient written and verbal communication skills.
  • Ability to prepare, develop, and deliver a theologically sound and compelling sermon.
  • Ability to disciple leaders and build a discipleship culture of community and personal growth across the student ministry.
  • Ability to communicate vision as well as lead, correct, and encourage a team of volunteers.
  • Strong time-management skills and multitasking ability.
  • Ability to lead and work well within a team environment.
  • Proficient in Microsoft Office with aptitude to operate standard Gateway Staff applications and learn new software systems as necessary.

General Physical Requirements:
The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of the job. While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to:

  • Sit/stand for long periods of time.
  • Occasionally kneel or crouch.
  • Lift and/or move up to 10 lbs. and occasionally lift and/or move up to 25 lbs.


*This description is not all-inclusive, and other duties may be assigned as necessary.
 
 

Gateway Church does not discriminate in employment opportunities or practices on the basis of race, color, sex, national origin, age, disability, or any other characteristic protected by law as it applies to churches. However, Gateway Church does discriminate on the basis of religion.
 

Employment Requirement: All staff must be a member or become a member of Gateway Church upon employment.

Your Career Starts Here!

  • Must pass a background check and drug screening.
  • Availability to work flexible hours, including nights, weekends, and holidays.
  • Availability to work: Sunday 830am-1230pm

Work Environment:

  • Primary post will be at a gatehouse in Florida, requiring work in both indoor and outdoor environments.
  • Exposure to varying weather conditions.

Why Join PGSUSA?

  • Competitive compensation and benefits.
  • Supportive team environment with opportunities for growth and career advancement.

To apply, please submit your resume, a copy of your valid Florida security licenses (Class "D" and "G")

PGSUSA is an equal opportunity employer. We welcome candidates from diverse backgrounds and experiences to apply.

Campus Staff Minister - West Michigan Area (Undergraduate Ministry)

Work Location:

Michigan

Job Type:

Full time

God has called InterVarsity to plant and to build witnessing communities of students and faculty who follow Jesus on college and university campuses. Through these groups, we believe ever- increasing numbers of students and faculty from all ethnic groups and areas of the campus will be transformed by the Gospel. We expect to see campuses increasingly become places where people, ideas, and structures flourish to the glory of God. We confidently anticipate that our InterVarsity alumni will become change agents across the country and around the world. We pursue this calling by discerning and actively participating in what God is already doing on campus. This is the essence of being a Campus Staff Minister (CSM).

ESSENTIAL COMMITMENTS/RESPONSIBILITIES 

Spiritual Growth 

You pursue maturity as a disciple of Jesus Christ so that your life and work increasingly reflects a growing love for God, God’s Word, God’s people of every ethnicity and culture, and God’s purposes in the world. To do this, you will: 

  • Pursue a vibrant relationship with the triune God through engagement with Scripture, prayer, and worship, both individually and in community 

  • Develop self-leadership (growing in self-awareness, self-management, relational integrity, and resiliency) 

  • Embrace Scriptural standards for behavior and attitudes 

 

Campus Leadership 

You communicate and model InterVarsity’s vision to see students and faculty transformed, campuses renewed and world changers developed 

  • Create a culture of humble dependence on God and bold expectation in God’s intention to start new witnessing communities throughout the campus and on new campuses 

  • Model – in person and through programs – InterVarsity’s vision and Core Values, including a biblically-defined commitment to engage every ethnic and social group on campus 

  • Lead students and faculty – individually and collectively – through Scripture, prayer, teaching, and discipleship experiences, so that they articulate and align their ministry activities around this vision 

  • Set annual goals through prayer, research and reflection with your teams (students, faculty, and staff) for qualitative and quantitative growth, including conversions and leadership development 

 

You create, develop, align and leverage ministry plans, programs, teams, and structures to close the gap between current reality and the aspirational goals. 

  • Build leadership teams who trust and partner well with you and who demonstrate spiritual vitality, relational health, and mission alignment 

  • Develop and execute plans to achieve annual goals, evaluating and modifying the plan as needed throughout the year 

  • Increase momentum for the vision by aligning programs, structures, conferences and teams around the goals 

  • Mobilize students and faculty to engage their relational networks with the gospel and to start new missional communities 

  • Under the direction of the Area Director, may supervise Ministry Interns and Campus Ministry Interns as delegated 

 

You intentionally gather, invite, and develop diverse groups of students and faculty so that they not only encounter and follow Jesus as Savior and Lord but also advance the mission on campus as participants and leaders. 

  • Create ways for faculty and students to encounter and follow Jesus through Scripture, worship, prayer, mission experiences, conferences, etc. 

  • Equip students and faculty so that they think strategically about campus engagement and so that they proclaim – in word, deed, and power – the good news of Jesus, regularly inviting students and faculty to follow him as Savior and Lord 

  • Disciple students and faculty by equipping them to hear the Word, respond actively, and debrief and interpret the experience so that they grow in Christlikeness, reflect our Core Values, and develop ministry skills 

  • Invite, coach, and equip students and faculty to become increasingly effective participants and leaders, including starting new witnessing communities on campuses 

 

Organizational Collaboration 

You work with a network of other local, area, regional, and national InterVarsity staff and volunteers so that our work reflects Biblical standards of excellence, integrity, and partnership. 

  • Partner with and respond positively to the direction and coaching of your supervisors and national leaders 

  • Contribute to collaborative and productive team meetings and relationships 

  • Affiliate chapters under your care and submit Graduating Student Forms in order to increase our partnership with current students and alumni 

  • Use national ministry resources and tools, as requested, including recruiting and/or participating in local, regional, or national conferences as  

  • Complete reporting, planning and review requirements in a timely way so that you and your supervisors can assess and improve your work as a CSM 

  • Comply with all InterVarsity policies and procedures 

 

Ministry Partnership Development 

You will develop a team of partners – churches and individuals (including alumni and community members) – who will resource the ministry financially, in prayer, or volunteer service that advances the mission. 

  • Raise 100% of the financial budget assigned by your supervisor 

  • Communicate regularly with your ministry partners, nurturing the relationship through visits, phone calls, emails and regular prayer letters 

  • Develop on-going, long-lasting partnership with alumni and volunteers 

  • Comply with all Ministry Partnership Policies 

  • Identify and invest in advocates who will build networks of volunteers and donors on InterVarsity’s behalf 

 

Accomplish all other assigned tasks as appropriate 

 

QUALIFICATIONS (common to all levels of CSM) 

  • Annually affirm InterVarsity’s Statement of Agreement (Doctrinal Basis and Purpose Statement). Abide by InterVarsity’s Code of Conduct. Believe and behave consonantly with InterVarsity’s Human Sexuality Theological Paper. Affirm and behave consonantly with InterVarsity’s “Women in Ministry Statement of Affirmation” 

  • Bachelor’s degree for CSMs assigned to a four-year campus. A minimum of an Associate’s degree for CSMs assigned to a two-year campus or a community college 

  • Strong interpersonal skills (including ability to minister to diverse ethnic communities and faculty) 

  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills 

  • Demonstrated problem solving skills 

  • Familiarity with word processing, presentation, email, and spreadsheet software 

 

WORK ENVIRONMENT/PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS 

The CSM position leads ministry in a college campus environment. A designated office space may or may not be available. The CSM is required to travel to on-campus and off- campus sites as appropriate. Off-campus travel includes, but is not limited to: student ministry conferences, Ministry Partnership Development meetings, and InterVarsity- sponsored training sessions, meetings, and conferences. The CSM is regularly required to communicate with others, and routinely uses standard office equipment such as computers, phones, photocopiers, filing cabinets, etc. 

Pay Range: $39,288.00 - $52,392.00 per year

Pay: This position is funded through personal fundraising. Accordingly, compensation will vary based on the ability of the individual to secure a donor team to fund the cost of his/her salary. The anticipated salary range for this position on a full-time basis (40 hours/week) is dependent on a variety of factors, including location and cost of living. The actual salary received, including any geographic adjustment to account for location and cost of living, is subject to the individual’s ability to raise funds necessary to cover the full amount of such salary within the range set forth in the job posting details.

Benefits:

We offer a competitive benefits package, including health care and retirement savings with a match. Eligibility is based on employee type and hours worked.  Benefits include the following:

  • 403(b) Retirement Savings Plan

  • 403(b) matching contributions

  • Dental insurance

  • Employee assistance program

  • Employee discounts

  • Flexible work schedule

  • Flexible spending accounts

  • Health insurance

  • Health savings account

  • Life insurance

  • Paid time off

  • Parental leave

  • Professional development assistance

  • Vision insurance

Equal Employment Opportunity: 

 

InterVarsity Christian Fellowship/USA is both an equal opportunity employer and a faith-based religious organization. We conduct hiring without regard to race, color, ancestry, national origin, citizenship, age, sex, marital status, parental status, membership in any labor organization, political ideology, or disability of an otherwise qualified individual. The status of InterVarsity Christian Fellowship/USA as an equal opportunity employer does not prevent the organization from hiring staff based on their religious beliefs so that all staff share the same religious commitment.  Pursuant to the Civil Rights Act of 1964, Section 702 (42 U.S.C. 2000e 1(a)) InterVarsity Christian Fellowship/USA has the right to, and does, hire only candidates who agree with InterVarsity’s Statement of Agreement: Purpose and Doctrinal Basis because InterVarsity believes that each and every staff plays a vital role in advancing InterVarsity’s mission and purposes.

POSITION: Youth and Family Ministry Manager, Redeemer Presbyterian Church Lincoln Square (LSQ)
DEPARTMENT: LSQ Family Ministries
REPORTS TO: LSQ Director of Family Ministries
START DATE: August 1, 2026
HOURS WORKED: Full-time (must be able to work Sundays and occasional evenings/weekends for events, as required)
BAND: 6
WAGE RANGE: $65,000-$75,000/ year
FLSA: Exempt


WHY THIS ROLE MATTERS
New York City shapes the world, and the youth of New York City will shape what comes next.

At Redeemer LSQ, we believe kids, youth and family ministry is not just about helping students get through school. It’s about forming a generation of young men and women who know Jesus deeply, love His church, and are equipped to live with purpose in one of the most influential cities in the world.

The Youth & Family Manager sits at the intersection of three vital ministry areas: youth, children, and family. This role is both relational and operational, deeply invested in students and families while keeping the day-to-day ministry running with joy and excellence.


JOB SUMMARY
The Youth & Family Manager will take primary ownership of LSQ’s youth discipleship (6th–12th grade), while also contributing meaningfully to children’s ministry and family engagement. This is a mid-level ministry role for a proven practitioner who is ready to lead, not just assist, while continuing to grow under the vision and leadership of Redeemer LSQ. This role is structured around three areas of responsibility:

  • Youth Ministry (6th–12th grade) — 60%
  • Children’s Ministry (Infant–5th grade) — 20%
  • Family Engagement — 20%


JOB DESCRIPTION

YOUTH MINISTRY — 6th–12th Grade (60%)

The Youth & Family Manager will serve as the primary point of contact and lead for LSQ’s youth discipleship ministry, working in close collaboration with the LSQ Director of Family Ministries.


LSQ Youth

  • Plan and facilitate community building events that foster genuine friendship and belonging among LSQ youth
  • Build consistent, trust-based relationships with students outside of formal programming
  • Oversee logistics, curriculum, attendance, and parent communication for all LSQ Sunday Youth gatherings
  • Lead weekly youth gatherings, small groups, and one-on-one discipleship outside of Sundays
  • Develop and deliver gospel-centered, age-appropriate teaching for both large group gatherings and small group settings

Student Discipleship

  • Build genuine, ongoing relationships with middle and high school students—attending games, performances, and key life moments
  • Mentor students individually and in community, walking alongside them through questions of faith, identity, and calling
  • Lead Communicants Class, guiding students toward a deeper understanding of faith and meaningful participation in church membership

Leadership Development

  • Recruit, train, and shepherd volunteer youth leaders from the LSQ congregation
  • Invest in young adult volunteers, equipping them to disciple middle and high school students
  • Conduct regular one-on-ones and community-building gatherings with volunteers
  • Ensure all volunteers are screened, trained, and compliant with LSQ child safety policies

Programming & Events

  • Plan and execute weekly youth programming
  • Coordinate LSQ student participation in retreats, mission trips, service projects, and events
  • Organize and lead opportunities for students to love and serve New York City

Family & Parent Engagement

  • Build trust-based relationships with the parents of youth students
  • Conduct one-on-one meetings with parents and assist in organizing parenting workshops
  • Maintain consistent communication with families regarding youth events, invites, and registrations

City-Wide Youth Coalition

  • Cultivate organic relationships with youth pastors and ministry leaders across New York City
  • Represent LSQ in the broader gospel-centered youth ministry ecosystem of the city
  • Explore and help develop the vision for a city-wide youth coalition, a collaborative network of NYC youth leaders united around the gospel
  • Identify opportunities for shared events, resource-sharing, and mutual encouragement across church communities


CHILDREN’S MINISTRY — Infant–5th Grade (20%)

The Youth & Family Manager will contribute meaningfully to LSQ’s children’s ministry, taking on focused areas of responsibility in support of the broader team led by the Director of Family Formation.


Sunday Coordination

  • Assist with execution of logistics, curriculum, classroom management, attendance, and parent communication for LSQ children’s programming
  • Rotate periodically with children’s ministry staff to take the lead on Sunday morning management and setup
  • Maintain a welcoming and safe environment for children and families
  • Administration support as needed
  • Support database management (Planning Center), including check-ins and attendance tracking
  • Participate in planning and leading VBS


FAMILY & CHURCH-WIDE INTEGRATION (20%)

The Youth & Family Manager will play a key role in building a culture where families across all ministry areas feel welcomed, known, and equipped to grow as disciples—at church and at home.


Community Building

  • Actively work to integrate families into the broader life of the LSQ congregation—building bridges between children’s, youth, and adult ministries so families experience the church as one unified community
  • Assist in planning and executing seasonal programs, family events, and community-building activities across LSQ
  • Help create environments where families experience genuine belonging and are drawn deeper into the life of the church
  • Collaborate with the Family Ministry team on cross-ministry events and initiatives

Parent Discipleship & Resources

  • Provide resources and support for parents in their role as primary disciplers of their children
  • Assist in leading or facilitating parent workshops, small groups, and informational gatherings
  • Build relationships with families, serving as a point of pastoral care and connection

Vision & Strategic Contribution

  • Contribute ideas and creative solutions to support the long-term vision of family ministry at LSQ
  • Participate in weekly family ministry meetings to set goals and refine strategies
  • Collaborate across ministry departments to ensure alignment with LSQ’s broader mission


QUALIFICATIONS

Required

  • Must embrace LSQ’s vision and have a gospel-oriented heart for New York City
  • Must be aligned with the core theological principles and ministry values of LSQ and the Presbyterian Church of America, including the Westminster Confession
  • Must have a deep and growing relationship with Jesus Christ
  • Four-year undergraduate degree in theology, youth ministry, education, psychology, or a related field; or equivalent work experience
  • Minimum 3–5 years of ministry experience (volunteer or paid), with demonstrated leadership in youth ministry
  • Proven ability to teach the Bible, theology, and Christian discipleship to youth in large and small group settings
  • Experience recruiting, training, and managing volunteers
  • Strong organizational, relational, and communication skills

Preferred

  • Graduate work in theology, counseling, or a related field
  • Experience with urban or multicultural ministry contexts
  • Curriculum development experience
  • Previous public speaking and teaching experience in varied group sizes
  • Familiarity with child safety policies and best practices in family ministry

WHO YOU ARE

  • Relational and warm—someone students and families genuinely want to be around
  • Humble and teachable, eager to learn and grow while leading with confidence
  • An initiator who takes ownership without needing to be asked
  • Pastoral and practical—able to provide care and also keep the ministry running well
  • A creative problem-solver with strong follow-through on administrative details
  • Emotionally mature, professional, and resilient in a dynamic urban ministry environment
  • Deeply committed to the local church and its role in the flourishing of New York City

SKILLS

  • Excellent organizational, leadership, pastoral, communication, and interpersonal skills
  • Ability to manage multiple projects and competing priorities with professionalism
  • Comfort navigating a complex organization and a dynamic, fast-paced ministry environment
  • Proficient in Google Workspace, Microsoft Office, Planning Center (or similar database), social media, and Adobe Creative Suite


Full-time members of the Redeemer Lincoln Square team, are offered competitive salaries, paid time off, and benefits, to include:

  • Fully paid Medical Plan Premiums for employee-only coverage and nominal costs for dependent coverage
  • Fully paid Dental insurance premiums, with dental buy-up plan option
  • Fully paid Vision insurance premiums
  • 403b Retirement, plus company match
  • Redeemer-paid short-term disability, long-term disability and basic life insurance
  • Voluntary accident, life, and AD&D policies for employee, spouse, and children
  • Redeemer-funded HSA and HRA with elected high-deductible medical coverage
  • Optional Limited Purpose FSA for dental, vision, and dependent care costs
  • Transit / commuter benefit
  • Counseling benefit


Relocation assistance is not available for this position.


The wage range for this role takes into account the wide range of factors that are considered in making compensation decisions including but not limited to skill set; experience and training; licensure, certifications, and ordination; and other organizational needs.


Use of Hiring Technology
As part of our recruitment process, we may use technology-assisted tools, including artificial intelligence (AI), to help review applications and identify candidates whose qualifications align with the requirements of the role. AI can assist us in evaluating skills, qualifications, experience, or certain keywords. These tools support, but do not replace, human review and decision-making.


While interviewers may record and transcribe interviews using AI tools, we do not utilize AI to evaluate or analyze interview videos. Recording of interviews is done solely for the purpose of note-taking or transcribing the conversation, and human review is conducted of the notes prior to connecting them with an applicant's file. The organization does not utilize Automated Employment Decision Tools to conduct video analysis of any recorded interviews, and is fully compliant with New York City Local Law 144.

Student Intern - Metro MN (Undergraduate Ministry)

Work Location:

Minnesota

Job Type:

Part time

To advance the purpose of InterVarsity, this position is focused on learning the basics of college campus ministry. This position is limited to students who are currently enrolled in a four-year or community college. Second year students and students enrolled at a community college may intern at a two-year/community college. Third year students and higher can work at a four-year or community college. Non-InterVarsity students who attend a Christian college must have third or fourth year standing.

post_html:
Director of Worship Ministry - Cornerstone Church Auburn
 

Cornerstone Church is seeking a Spirit-filled and musically gifted Worship Leader to cultivate a vibrant culture of worship within our congregation and to help create an environment where disciples of Jesus are multiplied. The Worship Leader will oversee all corporate worship experiences, lead and shepherd worship teams, and design services that foster encounters with God. This individual will partner closely with the Lead Pastor to craft cohesive, Spirit-led services that engage a multi-generational congregation averaging 500 worshipers across two Sunday services.

Key Responsibilities

1. Service Design & Leadership

·       Plan and Lead: Design and lead engaging, biblically grounded corporate worship experiences for both Sunday morning services in collaboration with the Lead Pastor.  

·       Flow & Structure: Integrate sacraments (Holy Communion, Baptism), prayer, and musical elements smoothly into the order of worship.

·       Special Services: Plan and lead additional worship experiences, including Holy Week, Christmas Eve, Ash Wednesday, and special church-wide gatherings

2. Team Recruitment, Development & Shepherding

·       Band & Vocal Team: Recruit, audition, train, and mentor worship team members, including vocalists and instrumentalists.

·       Spiritual Care: Shepherd worship team members through regular prayer, spiritual formation, and relational discipleship.

·       Rehearsals: Conduct high-yield weekly rehearsals (music and tech) to ensure excellence and spiritual preparation.

·       Student/Youth Worship: Mentor and empower young musicians, helping build a pipeline for student ministry worship teams.

3. Production & Worship Technology

·       Tech Team Oversight: Recruits, trains, and oversees sound engineers, live-stream operators, and visual presentation technicians (ProPresenter, Planning Center, etc.).

·       Audio/Visual/Lighting (AVL): Ensure sound quality, visual presentation, and online streams are delivered with excellence and consistency.

·       Equipment Maintenance: Oversee the maintenance, repair, and stewardship of church musical instruments, sound gear, and production software.

4. Pastoral & Administrative Duties

·       Staff Team Member: Participate actively in weekly staff meetings, retreats, and general pastoral care as appropriate.

·       Children & Youth Ministries: Support the worship experiences of the youth and children’s ministry as requested and possible.

·       Budgeting: Manage the Worship Arts department budget, ensuring wise stewardship of church resources.

·       Administration: Manage worship planning platforms (e.g., Planning Center Services), song licensing (CCLI), and chord/chart distributions.

·       Community Life: Be an active, visible member of the church community beyond Sunday mornings.

 

Qualifications & Requirements

·       Spiritual Maturity: A deep, personal relationship with Jesus Christ, evidence of the fruit of the Spirit, and alignment with the doctrines of the church as expressed in the Nicene Creed.

·       Musical Proficiency: Strong vocal leadership and proficiency in leading from an instrument (preferably acoustic guitar or piano/keys). Ability to read music/charts and to train others.

·       Leadership Experience: Minimum 2–4 years of experience leading corporate worship in a medium-to-large local church environment.

·       Tech Savvy: Familiarity with worship planning software (Planning Center), presentation tools (ProPresenter), Digital Audio Workstations/Backing Tracks (Multitracks/Ableton), and live-stream setups.

·       Relational & Discipleship Heart: Excellent interpersonal and communication skills; a genuine desire to shepherd people, not just execute events.

God has called InterVarsity to plant and to build witnessing communities of students and faculty who follow Jesus on college and university campuses. Through these groups, we believe ever- increasing numbers of students and faculty from all ethnic groups and areas of the campus will be transformed by the Gospel. We expect to see campuses increasingly become places where people, ideas, and structures flourish to the glory of God. We confidently anticipate that our InterVarsity alumni will become change agents across the country and around the world. We pursue this calling by discerning and actively participating in what God is already doing on campus. This is the essence of being a Campus Staff Minister (CSM).

LOCATION:

We currently have the most need for Campus Staff Ministers for the following locations/foci. Please indicate in your application which you are interested in (if any):

  • Edinburgh, TX
  • San Antonio, TX

If you are interested in working at a location that is not listed, fill out the application and indicate where in the relevant question. You are also welcome to input multiple locations and we will take them into consideration. Note that our region of InterVarsity serves the states of Texas, Oklahoma, Arkansas, and Louisiana. If you would like to serve in one of those states, search for it in the search bar to find the openings. During the interview, there will be a greater discussion around location and also the opportunity to go to other places in need of staff.

ESSENTIAL COMMITMENTS/RESPONSIBILITIES 

Spiritual Growth 

You pursue maturity as a disciple of Jesus Christ so that your life and work increasingly reflects a growing love for God, God’s Word, God’s people of every ethnicity and culture, and God’s purposes in the world. To do this, you will: 

  • Pursue a vibrant relationship with the triune God through engagement with Scripture, prayer, and worship, both individually and in community 

  • Develop self-leadership (growing in self-awareness, self-management, relational integrity, and resiliency) 

  • Embrace Scriptural standards for behavior and attitudes 

 

Campus Leadership 

You communicate and model InterVarsity’s vision to see students and faculty transformed, campuses renewed and world changers developed 

  • Create a culture of humble dependence on God and bold expectation in God’s intention to start new witnessing communities throughout the campus and on new campuses 

  • Model – in person and through programs – InterVarsity’s vision and Core Values, including a biblically-defined commitment to engage every ethnic and social group on campus 

  • Lead students and faculty – individually and collectively – through Scripture, prayer, teaching, and discipleship experiences, so that they articulate and align their ministry activities around this vision 

  • Set annual goals through prayer, research and reflection with your teams (students, faculty, and staff) for qualitative and quantitative growth, including conversions and leadership development 

 

You create, develop, align and leverage ministry plans, programs, teams, and structures to close the gap between current reality and the aspirational goals.

  • Develop and execute plans to achieve annual goals, evaluating and modifying the plan as needed throughout the year 

  • Increase momentum for the vision by aligning programs, structures, conferences and teams around the goals 

  • Mobilize students and faculty to engage their relational networks with the gospel and to start new missional communities 

  • Under the direction of the Area Director, may supervise Ministry Interns and Campus Ministry Interns as delegated 

 

You intentionally gather, invite, and develop diverse groups of students and faculty so that they not only encounter and follow Jesus as Savior and Lord but also advance the mission on campus as participants and leaders.

  • Equip students and faculty so that they think strategically about campus engagement and so that they proclaim – in word, deed, and power – the good news of Jesus, regularly inviting students and faculty to follow him as Savior and Lord 

  • Disciple students and faculty by equipping them to hear the Word, respond actively, and debrief and interpret the experience so that they grow in Christlikeness, reflect our Core Values, and develop ministry skills 

  • Invite, coach, and equip students and faculty to become increasingly effective participants and leaders, including starting new witnessing communities on campuses 

 

Organizational Collaboration 

You work with a network of other local, area, regional, and national InterVarsity staff and volunteers so that our work reflects Biblical standards of excellence, integrity, and partnership. 

  • Partner with and respond positively to the direction and coaching of your supervisors and national leaders 

  • Contribute to collaborative and productive team meetings and relationships 

  • Affiliate chapters under your care and submit Graduating Student Forms in order to increase our partnership with current students and alumni 

  • Use national ministry resources and tools, as requested, including recruiting and/or participating in local, regional, or national conferences as  

  • Complete reporting, planning and review requirements in a timely way so that you and your supervisors can assess and improve your work as a CSM 

  • Comply with all InterVarsity policies and procedures 

 

Ministry Partnership Development 

You will develop a team of partners – churches and individuals (including alumni and community members) – who will resource the ministry financially, in prayer, or volunteer service that advances the mission.

  • Communicate regularly with your ministry partners, nurturing the relationship through visits, phone calls, emails and regular prayer letters 

  • Develop on-going, long-lasting partnership with alumni and volunteers 

  • Comply with all Ministry Partnership Policies 

  • Identify and invest in advocates who will build networks of volunteers and donors on InterVarsity’s behalf 

 

Accomplish all other assigned tasks as appropriate

  • Annually affirm InterVarsity’s Statement of Agreement (Doctrinal Basis and Purpose Statement). Abide by InterVarsity’s Code of Conduct. Believe and behave consonantly with InterVarsity’s Human Sexuality Theological Paper. Affirm and behave consonantly with InterVarsity’s “Women in Ministry Statement of Affirmation”

Off-campus travel includes, but is not limited to: student ministry conferences, Ministry Partnership Development meetings, and InterVarsity- sponsored training sessions, meetings, and conferences.
