Job Title: Youth Pastor

Location: Rochester, Minnesota

Church Size: 350-400


Why This Is a Great Opportunity:

Northbridge Community Church is seeking a Youth Pastor to step into a strategic season of ministry and build a dynamic student ministry from the ground up. Come and invest in the next generation of teenagers.

Northbridge is positioned for growth. The right leader will establish strong biblical foundations, equip parents, and build a volunteer team capable of discipling the next generation in a rapidly shifting culture.


This role is ideal for a spiritually mature leader who loves God’s Word, values theological clarity, and is passionate about helping students stand firm in faith. You will serve alongside a supportive elder-led leadership team, a committed Lead Pastor, and parents eager for intentional spiritual leadership.


﻿About Northbridge Community Church:


Mission: To exalt God, teach believers, and make disciples.


Vision: Transforming lives through the power of God’s Word.

Northbridge is a Bible-centered, elder-led congregation in Rochester, Minnesota, affiliated with the Berean Church Fellowship. The church is committed to: Biblical Veracity, Humility, Prayer, Obedience, Unity, Generosity.

Learn more: https://nbchurch.org/beliefs



Key Responsibilities:

Youth Ministry Leadership

  • Ability to pioneer a new and fresh chapter of youth ministry at Northbridge Community
  • Lead and develop a biblically grounded ministry for grades 6–12.
  • Establish weekly gatherings focused on teaching, discipleship, worship, outreach, serving, prayer, and relationships.
  • Build a clear discipleship pathway rooted in God’s Word.
  • Build, recruit, train, and shepherd volunteer leaders.
  • Equip and encourage parents as primary disciplers. 
  • Communicate consistently to students, volunteers, parents, and staff.


Team Collaboration & Ministry Development

  • Report to the Lead Pastor and church leadership team.
  • Integrate students into the broader life of the church.
  • Strengthen and expand programming beyond Sunday nights.
  • Steward the youth ministry budget and prepare for growth.


Pastoral Leadership

  • Provide pastoral care to students and families.
  • Model Christlike character, humility, and spiritual health.


Qualifications:

  • Spiritually mature, authentic follower of Jesus.
  • Agreement with Northbridge’s theological convictions.
  • A passion for Youth Ministry and for impacting students.
  • Bible or Ministry degree required; Master’s preferred.
  • 1-4 years of student ministry experience is preferred.
  • Strong alignment with collaborative and unified leadership.
  • Organizational strength, communication skill, and leadership development mindset.
  • Reliable, trustworthy, and grace-filled.


What Success Looks Like in Year One:

  • Strong relationships with staff and elders.
  • Trusted and loved by students.
  • Supported by parents.
  • Clear discipleship direction established.
  • The volunteer team strengthened and growing.


Benefits & Compensation:

  • Full-time role
  • Salary: $60,000 - $68,000 annually (based on experience)
  • Possible Benefits Package: Health insurance, life insurance, retirement, paid time off
  • Ministry Coaching through LEAD222


About Rochester, Minnesota:

Rochester is a thriving city of approximately 125,000 residents with a strong medical and professional workforce. The city offers excellent schools, safe neighborhoods, parks, and family-friendly amenities, making it a stable and attractive place for long-term ministry.


﻿The Opportunity:

This is a new position. The foundation is laid. The leadership is supportive. The theology is clear. Northbridge is ready for a shepherd who will love students, teach God’s Word faithfully, build leaders, and prepare the next generation to stand firm in truth.

If you feel called to this kind of spiritual leadership, we would love to connect.

Contract
Description

SUMMARY

The Worship Leader at Black Diamond Camps will help prayerfully plan sets appropriate for staff, campers (based on program) and youth pastors and families from all denominations. Multi-talented with vocal, guitar (acoustic, electric, bass) and percussion (full set and hand drums). They sing on-stage and on-location throughout camp and help with programming and behind-the-scenes to keep camp running smoothly including cleaning, dishwashing and necessary work projects as needed. The person in this position shall, at all times, demonstrate cooperative behavior towards colleagues, guests, supervisors, volunteers and guests. Regular attendance is essential for this position. All team members are expected to maintain an environment of professionalism, safety and fun.


ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

Includes the following; other duties may be assigned:

  1. Have ability to communicate and work with campers age 5-18 and volunteers of high school age, during their various camp activities and provide necessary instruction to campers.
  2. Respond to emergencies in accordance to training and camp policies.
  3. Possess abilities to observe camper and volunteer behavior, assess its appropriateness, enforce applicable safety regulations and emergency procedures and apply effective behavior-management techniques.
  4. Help build excitement for the opening day of camp each week and conduct oneself in such a way as to encourage the transfer of trust onto oneself by the parents and campers.
  5. Work as a team member with the other BDC staff and volunteers toward the overall goals of the camp.
  6. Be a positive roles model to the summer staff in his/her spiritual walk, self-respect, love and consideration of others, enthusiasm and work ethic.
  7. Be able to lead worship effectively and confidently several times a day with or without other members of a worship team.
  8. Be flexible with the needs of each group and program.
  9. Recognize and respond to opportunities for presenting the "Good News" of Jesus Christ.
  10. Be prepared to assist campers during other recreational activities (training and support given).
  11. Perform the duties and tasks of being a counselor in either program as listed below:

Group Camp: Each week co-counselors (mostly working in co-ed teams) will lead 20-30 junior high and high school students through purposeful and pre-planned experiences. Counselors are part of creating flexible schedules that cater to each group's needs; they lead Bible studies, build relationships and facilitate activities/group development that provide opportunities for scripture to come to life. Counselors sleep in nearby dorms with other counselors unless the group requests otherwise.


Day Camp: These counselors work with our youngest campers, starting with campers entering Kindergarten-6th grade (ages 5-12). They begin first thing in the morning at parent drop-off through mid afternoon when parents pick up their campers. These counselors are required to be high energy with a passion and desire for fun! The day camp experience is a Monday-Friday camp, with other supporting camp roles throughout the rest of your work week. Counselors will work in pairs to take care of their cabin groups and work together to make sure their campers are having an incredible summer camp experience. Counselors are in charge of leading their campers in activities, group development, Bible studies, and many other high energy activities. On occasion counselors might be asked to sleep in cabins with same gender campers for overnight camp add ons.


12. Include the following. Other duties may be assigned.


Activities/Adventure Elements:

  • Demonstrate competency to belay/spot elements and activities.
  • Demonstrate proper set up of gear on ground and use of appropriate knots.
  • Competent in ability to instruct and supervise participants on different challenge course elements.
  • Demonstrate proper belay set up and belay method.
  • Demonstrate the ability to see and manage inherent risk to minimize the risk of injury.


Lifeguard (demonstrated upon training):

  • Maintain up-to-date Lifeguard/First Aid & CPR certifications (if you don't already have these certifications, be willing to obtain them).
  • Demonstrate effective patron surveillance of up to 100 swimmers with the aquatic team.
  • Demonstrate competency to recognize and respond to emergency situations.
  • Able to properly open and close up aquatic environments.
  • Able to identify and manage environmental and other hazards related to the activity.
  • Competent in ability to instruct participants in canoe procedures, pool rules and/or basic swim instruction.


SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES

This position has no supervisory responsibilities.


MINISTRY STATEMENT

Warm Beach Camp Ministries exists to share the hope and love of Christ through camping ministries and experiences in the Pacific Northwest.

At Black Diamond Camp, we exist to inspire Christ-like change through outdoor adventure, authentic relationships and biblical truth.


CLASSIFICATION

This is a seasonal, contract position.

Requirements

QUALIFICATIONS

To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duties satisfactorily. The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skill, and/or ability required. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

  1. Must be 18 years of age or older.
  2. Have a sincere love for the Lord and be committed to the Lordship of Christ in every area of their life.
  3. Have a burden and a love for all people and a desire to see them totally committed to the Lordship of Jesus.
  4. Be willing to support the philosophy and goals of Warm Beach Camp Ministries and Black Diamond Camp through attitude, speech and action.
  5. Be willing to accept supervision and guidance.

EDUCATION and/or EXPERIENCE

High school diploma or general education degree (GED); or one to three months related experience and/or training; or equivalent combination of education and experience.


CERTIFICATES, LICENSES, REGISTRATIONS

Current CPR/First Aid Certification or ability to obtain Lifeguard Certification or ability to obtain

Food Handler's Card

Valid Driver's License (for those age 21 or older) to be authorized to drive camp vehicles.


LANGUAGE SKILLS

Ability to read and comprehend simple instructions, short correspondence, and memos. Ability to write simple correspondence. Ability to effectively present information in one-on-one, small group and large group situations.


MATHEMATICAL SKILLS

Ability to add, subtract, multiply and divide in all units of measure, using whole numbers, common fractions and decimals. Ability to compute rate, ratio and percent and to draw and interpret bar graphs.


REASONING ABILITY

Ability to apply common sense understanding to carry out instructions furnished in written, oral or diagram form. Ability to deal with problems involving several concrete variables in standardized situations.


PHYSICAL DEMANDS

While performing the duties of this position, the employee is regularly required to: stand, walk and/or sit for extended periods of time; use hands to handle or feel; reach with hands and arms; climb or balance; stoop, kneel, crouch, or crawl. The employee must frequently assist in the lifting and/or moving up to 75 pounds. Specific vision requirements of the position includes close vision, distance vision, color vision, peripheral vision, depth perception and ability to adjust focus. The employee must regularly talk or hear. The physical demands described here are representative of the minimum physical requirements that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable qualified individuals.

The employee must wear face covering/mask per the guidelines and regulations in place during the time of employment as established by CDC, state and local authorities.


WORK ENVIRONMENT

The work environment characteristics described here are representative of those an employee encounters while performing the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable qualified individuals. While performing the duties of this position, the employee is regularly exposed to high, precarious places and outside weather conditions. The noise level in the work environment is usually moderate.


ON-CAMP HOUSING CONDITION

The employee in this position is required to live on the camp premises in staff housing in order to provide round-the-clock supervision of campers and volunteers and fulfill the program requirements of this position.

Salary Description
$360-$410/wk

Campus Staff Minister - AZ / CO / NM / UT / WY (Graduate & Faculty Ministry)

Work Location:

Colorado

Job Type:

Full time

God has called InterVarsity to plant and to build witnessing communities of students and faculty who follow Jesus on college and university campuses. Through these groups, we believe ever- increasing numbers of students and faculty from all ethnic groups and areas of the campus will be transformed by the Gospel. We expect to see campuses increasingly become places where people, ideas, and structures flourish to the glory of God. We confidently anticipate that our InterVarsity alumni will become change agents across the country and around the world. We pursue this calling by discerning and actively participating in what God is already doing on campus. This is the essence of being a Campus Staff Minister (CSM).

Please submit the GFM Interest Form before completing the full application for a position with Graduate & Faculty Ministries in our online system. We will contact you when we are ready to proceed with the application process.​ 

We are open to part-time applicants working less than 40 hours/week. If you are interested in part-time work please apply for this position.

The pay range listed for this position is for an employee working 40 hours/week. Pay will be prorated for employees who work less than 40 hours/week. Additional pay (as a geographic adjustment) is available in high cost of living areas.

We have positions in the following locations:

  • CU Boulder

  • Colorado State University

ESSENTIAL COMMITMENTS/RESPONSIBILITIES 

Spiritual Growth 

You pursue maturity as a disciple of Jesus Christ so that your life and work increasingly reflects a growing love for God, God’s Word, God’s people of every ethnicity and culture, and God’s purposes in the world. To do this, you will: 

  • Pursue a vibrant relationship with the triune God through engagement with Scripture, prayer, and worship, both individually and in community 

  • Develop self-leadership (growing in self-awareness, self-management, relational integrity, and resiliency) 

  • Embrace Scriptural standards for behavior and attitudes 

 

Campus Leadership 

You communicate and model InterVarsity’s vision to see students and faculty transformed, campuses renewed and world changers developed 

  • Create a culture of humble dependence on God and bold expectation in God’s intention to start new witnessing communities throughout the campus and on new campuses 

  • Model – in person and through programs – InterVarsity’s vision and Core Values, including a biblically-defined commitment to engage every ethnic and social group on campus 

  • Lead students and faculty – individually and collectively – through Scripture, prayer, teaching, and discipleship experiences, so that they articulate and align their ministry activities around this vision 

  • Set annual goals through prayer, research and reflection with your teams (students, faculty, and staff) for qualitative and quantitative growth, including conversions and leadership development 

 

You create, develop, align and leverage ministry plans, programs, teams, and structures to close the gap between current reality and the aspirational goals. 

  • Build leadership teams who trust and partner well with you and who demonstrate spiritual vitality, relational health, and mission alignment 

  • Develop and execute plans to achieve annual goals, evaluating and modifying the plan as needed throughout the year 

  • Increase momentum for the vision by aligning programs, structures, conferences and teams around the goals 

  • Mobilize students and faculty to engage their relational networks with the gospel and to start new missional communities 

  • Under the direction of the Area Director, may supervise Ministry Interns and Campus Ministry Interns as delegated 

 

You intentionally gather, invite, and develop diverse groups of students and faculty so that they not only encounter and follow Jesus as Savior and Lord but also advance the mission on campus as participants and leaders. 

  • Create ways for faculty and students to encounter and follow Jesus through Scripture, worship, prayer, mission experiences, conferences, etc. 

  • Equip students and faculty so that they think strategically about campus engagement and so that they proclaim – in word, deed, and power – the good news of Jesus, regularly inviting students and faculty to follow him as Savior and Lord 

  • Disciple students and faculty by equipping them to hear the Word, respond actively, and debrief and interpret the experience so that they grow in Christlikeness, reflect our Core Values, and develop ministry skills 

  • Invite, coach, and equip students and faculty to become increasingly effective participants and leaders, including starting new witnessing communities on campuses 

 

Organizational Collaboration 

You work with a network of other local, area, regional, and national InterVarsity staff and volunteers so that our work reflects Biblical standards of excellence, integrity, and partnership. 

  • Partner with and respond positively to the direction and coaching of your supervisors and national leaders 

  • Contribute to collaborative and productive team meetings and relationships 

  • Affiliate chapters under your care and submit Graduating Student Forms in order to increase our partnership with current students and alumni 

  • Use national ministry resources and tools, as requested, including recruiting and/or participating in local, regional, or national conferences as  

  • Complete reporting, planning and review requirements in a timely way so that you and your supervisors can assess and improve your work as a CSM 

  • Comply with all InterVarsity policies and procedures 

 

Ministry Partnership Development 

You will develop a team of partners – churches and individuals (including alumni and community members) – who will resource the ministry financially, in prayer, or volunteer service that advances the mission. 

  • Raise 100% of the financial budget assigned by your supervisor 

  • Communicate regularly with your ministry partners, nurturing the relationship through visits, phone calls, emails and regular prayer letters 

  • Develop on-going, long-lasting partnership with alumni and volunteers 

  • Comply with all Ministry Partnership Policies 

  • Identify and invest in advocates who will build networks of volunteers and donors on InterVarsity’s behalf 

 

Accomplish all other assigned tasks as appropriate 

 

QUALIFICATIONS (common to all levels of CSM) 

  • Annually affirm InterVarsity’s Statement of Agreement (Doctrinal Basis and Purpose Statement). Abide by InterVarsity’s Code of Conduct. Believe and behave consonantly with InterVarsity’s Human Sexuality Theological Paper. Affirm and behave consonantly with InterVarsity’s “Women in Ministry Statement of Affirmation” 

  • Bachelor’s degree for CSMs assigned to a four-year campus. A minimum of an Associate’s degree for CSMs assigned to a two-year campus or a community college 

  • Strong interpersonal skills (including ability to minister to diverse ethnic communities and faculty) 

  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills 

  • Demonstrated problem solving skills 

  • Familiarity with word processing, presentation, email, and spreadsheet software 

 

WORK ENVIRONMENT/PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS 

The CSM position leads ministry in a college campus environment. A designated office space may or may not be available. The CSM is required to travel to on-campus and off- campus sites as appropriate. Off-campus travel includes, but is not limited to: student ministry conferences, Ministry Partnership Development meetings, and InterVarsity- sponsored training sessions, meetings, and conferences. The CSM is regularly required to communicate with others, and routinely uses standard office equipment such as computers, phones, photocopiers, filing cabinets, etc. 

Pay Range: $45,324.00 - $60,420.00 per year

The anticipated salary range for this position on a full-time basis (40 hours/week) is dependent on a variety of factors, including location and cost of living. We offer a competitive benefits package, including health care and retirement savings with a match. Eligibility is based on employee type and hours worked.  Benefits include the following:

post_html:
The Director of Youth & College Ministries will provide spiritual and strategic leadership for Eastminster’s ministry to middle school, high school, and college students, helping young people move from participation toward meaningful discipleship and a growing relationship with Jesus Christ. The Director will create a unified vision for student ministry, build relationships with students and families, develop volunteer leaders, and provide biblical teaching and meaningful opportunities for worship, mission, fellowship, and service. This is an opportunity to build upon an established youth ministry while developing Eastminster’s growing ministry to college students. The next Director will join a healthy, multigenerational congregation that values relationships, biblical teaching, missions, and investing in the faith of the next generation.



Why We Love This Opportunity

Eastminster offers the opportunity to lead student ministry in a church that already believes deeply in investing in children, students, and families. I especially love that this role is not simply about running youth programs, but about building relationships with students, walking alongside families, developing leaders, and creating a pathway of discipleship that can continue from middle school through college.

There is also an exciting opportunity to build upon an established youth ministry while helping a budding college ministry take its next significant steps.

A great match for this position would be:

  • A relational and spiritually mature ministry leader who genuinely enjoys being present in the lives of students and families.
  • Someone who is passionate about helping middle school, high school, and college students develop a personal and lasting relationship with Jesus Christ.
  • A gifted biblical teacher who can communicate Scripture in ways that connect with students and help them apply God’s Word to everyday life.
  • A leader who can develop a unified discipleship strategy for youth and college ministry rather than simply maintaining a calendar of programs and events.
  • Someone who enjoys recruiting, developing, and empowering adult volunteers and student leaders rather than attempting to carry the ministry alone.
  • A collaborative teammate who can work effectively with pastors, staff, parents, volunteers, and Eastminster’s Christian Education and Youth Ministry teams.
  • A self motivated and organized leader who can balance relationships, teaching, programming, communication, events, trips, and administrative responsibilities.
  • A candidate who resonates with Eastminster’s Reformed theological identity and can enthusiastically affirm the Essential Tenets and commitments of ECO.


About This Organization

Eastminster Presbyterian Church is a welcoming, multigenerational congregation located in East Cobb, just outside Atlanta. For more than 50 years, Eastminster has sought to follow Jesus faithfully and serve as a beacon of hope to its community, city, and world. The church describes itself as a “Church for the Community,” with strong ministries in worship, Christian education, missions, children, youth, fellowship, and outreach.

Eastminster includes 564 Covenant Partners with an average Sunday worship attendance of approximately 283. The congregation offers both contemporary and traditional worship, an established children’s and youth ministry, a growing college ministry, a Christian preschool serving more than 100 children, and significant participation in Sunday School and small groups. Eastminster is financially healthy, debt free, and supported by a robust staff and active volunteer culture.

Eastminster has been part of ECO: A Covenant Order of Evangelical Presbyterians since 2013 and is rooted in Scripture, the Trinity, and the Reformed tradition. The church is led by a Session of 16 elders and served by 14 deacons, alongside a ministry staff committed to advancing the mission of Jesus through the life of the congregation.


Location

Eastminster is located in East Cobb, Marietta, Georgia, in the northern portion of the greater Atlanta metropolitan area. The community combines the accessibility and opportunities of a major metropolitan region with established suburban neighborhoods, strong schools, convenient shopping, parks, and family oriented communities.

Greater Atlanta provides access to major healthcare systems, professional sports, universities, arts and entertainment, and a wide variety of cultural experiences. East Cobb is also well positioned for enjoying the broader region, from the North Georgia mountains and lakes to destinations such as Savannah and Georgia’s coastal islands.


Mission, Vision, and Values

Mission:

Eastminster’s mission is to make disciples of Jesus Christ by Engaging community, Equipping believers, Empowering servants, and Extending our reach to the world.

Vision:

Eastminster seeks to be a church that faithfully follows Jesus and serves as a beacon of Christ’s hope and grace to East Cobb, the greater Atlanta community, and the world. The church desires to see people introduced to a relationship with Jesus Christ, grow in that relationship, and discover a community in which they can mature as disciples.

Values:

Eastminster values the Lordship of Jesus Christ as the head of the Church, Christ centered worship through Word and Sacrament, prayer and Bible centered teaching, genuine relationships, missions and evangelism, and the importance of family, fellowship, and caring for one another. These convictions are grounded in Scripture and Eastminster’s commitment to the Reformed tradition and the Essential Tenets of ECO.


Key Responsibilities

  • Provide spiritual leadership and overall direction for Eastminster’s ministries to middle school, high school, and college students, helping students progress from participation toward discipleship.
  • Develop and implement a cohesive vision for youth and college ministries with intentional benchmarks for spiritual growth and faith development.
  • Teach, disciple, mentor, counsel, and nurture students while cultivating a biblical worldview and mission minded faith.
  • Build meaningful relationships with students and families, including being present at extracurricular activities and connecting with students beyond scheduled church programming.
  • Recruit, disciple, train, and equip adult volunteers and student leaders to serve effectively within student ministry.
  • Provide leadership for Sunday School, Confirmation, Sunday evening youth gatherings, Wednesday Bible studies, and other regular student ministry environments.
  • Plan and lead retreats, mission experiences, conferences, summer activities, special events, and seasonal gatherings for students and college aged young adults.
  • Develop meaningful opportunities for students to participate in worship and the broader life of the congregation, including Eastminster’s annual Youth Sunday.
  • Maintain consistent year round communication and connection with college students, including students living away from East Cobb while attending school.
  • Partner with parents and families as they disciple their children and navigate the transition from adolescence into young adulthood.
  • Participate as an active member of the Eastminster staff team and collaborate with the Christian Education Team and Youth Ministry Team.
  • Provide guidance and oversight for the annual youth ministry budget and related administrative responsibilities.


Key Qualifications

  • A growing, vibrant, and demonstrable relationship with Jesus Christ.
  • A genuine calling and passion for ministry with middle school, high school, and college aged students and their families.
  • Previous experience leading or serving in student, youth, college, or next generation ministry.
  • Strong biblical teaching skills with the ability to communicate Scripture clearly and help students apply biblical truth to everyday life.
  • Demonstrated ability to build trusted relationships with students, parents, volunteers, and ministry colleagues.
  • Experience recruiting, developing, training, and empowering volunteer leaders.
  • Strong communication, interpersonal, organizational, and administrative skills.
  • Experience planning and leading ministry programs, events, retreats, trips, and other student experiences.
  • A collaborative ministry approach combined with the initiative and self direction necessary to lead a growing ministry.
  • A college degree is expected, with biblical, theological, or ministry training preferred.
  • Alignment with Eastminster’s theological convictions and willingness to embrace the Constitution, Essential Tenets, Polity, and Rules of Discipline of ECO: A Covenant Order of Evangelical Presbyterians.


For more information about this opportunity, please contact Phil Christian, Executive Recruiter, at pchristian@slingshotgroup.org

post_html:
Description

Grace Chapel is seeking a skilled, experienced worship leader ready to take the next step in their ministry career. This role serves as the primary worship leader for the Sunday morning services at our Wilmington Campus and collaborates with worship leaders across our campuses to ensure excellence and alignment in worship. This position works closely with the Central Pastor of Worship to strengthen and develop our worship experiences and partners with the digital team to create online worship content that extends our reach beyond Sunday mornings.  

This Worship Leader will provide creative, and spiritual leadership to worship gatherings at Grace Chapel’s Wilmington location. This role requires more than musical ability—it calls for a leader with broad creative instincts, strong experience in church worship leadership, and working knowledge of AVL (audio, video, and lighting) systems. The ideal candidate is both a skilled musician and a team builder who inspires excellence, disciples volunteers, and curates engaging, Christ-centered worship environments. 

This position is part time, with the opportunity to be full time by taking on additional responsibilities.

Worship Leadership  

  • Plan, lead, and oversee all aspects of the worship services in Wilmington. 

  • Lead congregational worship with excellence and authenticity, primarily as a vocalist and instrumentalist.  

  • Curate song selections that reflect theological depth, cultural relevance, and congregational sing-ability.  

  • In coordination with the Pastor of Worship and digital team, curate online worship experiences that reach unchurched and de-churched people  

  • Contribute to worship experiences, as needed, for weddings and funerals 

  • Participate in special events like Nights of Worship 

  • Help develop NextGen worship  

  • Creative Arts & AVL  

  • Collaborate with production, music, and teaching teams to design cohesive, creative, and Spirit-led worship experiences.  

  • Explore and implement creative worship elements (visuals, lighting, media, stage design) to enhance engagement. 

  • Provide input on AVL systems, working with technical staff and volunteers to ensure seamless execution.  

  • Leadership & Team Development  

  • Provide leadership and team development for the worship and tech team members.  

  • Recruit, disciple, and equip volunteer musicians and vocalists. 

  • Work closely with the Central Pastor of Worship and other campus worship leaders to align services with Grace Chapel’s vision and values.  

  • Partner with creative, communications, and pastoral teams on major events (Advent, Christmas, Easter, and outreach services) and worship recordings for our Online campus. 



Qualifications

Skills and qualifications 
A candidate for this position should have the following prerequisites and qualifications: 

  • Leader: A gifted and energetic team-builder and an inspirational leader who can cast a clear and compelling vision and who will equip people to find, develop, and act on their God-given calling. 

  • Communicator: An individual with the ability to communicate effectively in large and small group settings. 

  • DNA Carrier: An individual who resonates with the long-standing vision and values of Grace Chapel and who is passionate about extending its kingdom impact in the community. 

  • Champion of Diversity: An individual who values the diversity that God has brought to Grace Chapel and will work to increase it. 

Qualifications  

  • A vibrant and growing personal relationship with Jesus Christ, with alignment to Grace Chapel’s statement of faith and values.  

  • Minimum of 2 years of experience leading worship in a church of comparable size or complexity.

JOB DESCRIPTION
KIDS MINISTRY MANAGER

JOB TITLE:    Kids Ministry Manager
REPORTS TO: Director of Family and Women’s Ministries
HOURS/WEEK: 40 hours/week
FLSA DESIGNATION: Full time, Non-exempt
STAFF CATEGORY:  Kids Ministry

ILLUMINATE’S MISSION: We are called to love all people, make disciples, and empower them to be on mission for God.
ILLUMINATE’S VISION: Our vision is to be a “city on a hill” where the broken, hurting, and searching are drawn to the light and love of Jesus.

SUMMARY OF POSITION:
The Kids Ministry Manager provides hands-on leadership and ownership for Illuminate Kids Ministry from birth through 4th grade, creating safe, welcoming, and Christ-centered environments where children are known, loved, and intentionally discipled. This role oversees weekly ministry readiness, developmentally appropriate curriculum for ages 2 through 4th grade, volunteer and lead teacher development, classroom environments, SHINE support, and supervision of the Kids Ministry Assistants. The Kids Ministry Manager leads proactively with organization, encouragement, accountability, adaptability, and excellence with purpose: the intentional stewardship of the people, spaces, resources, and ministry opportunities God has entrusted to us.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES (Specific responsibilities include but are not limited to):

Birth-4th Grade Ministry Leadership: Lead Sunday and applicable midweek programming; ensure each classroom has the staffing, curriculum, supplies, setup, and resources needed for effective ministry; serve as the primary point person for volunteers and lead teachers; maintain effective schedules, records, supply systems, and communication rhythms; and proactively identify, solve, and communicate significant ministry needs.

Curriculum and Teacher Development: Prepare and adapt biblical, Christ-centered, engaging, and developmentally appropriate curriculum for ages 2 through 4th Grade. Provide lesson materials and expectations with sufficient lead time, observe classrooms, and equip teachers through encouragement, coaching, and actionable feedback in child engagement, behavior management, classroom leadership, and age-appropriate discipleship.

Volunteer Leadership: Recruit, onboard, train, schedule, develop, and care for Birth-4th grade and childcare volunteers. Anticipate staffing gaps, identify and develop emerging leaders, delegate effectively, and build a culture in which volunteers feel known, valued, equipped, connected to the mission, and appropriately accountable.

Sunday Ministry Leadership: Arrive by 6:30 AM; confirm that environments, supplies, and staffing are ready before families arrive; lead pre-service huddles for prayer, encouragement, and updates; remain visible and available; oversee ministry flow; troubleshoot classroom, staffing, child, family, and supply needs; step into ministry roles when necessary; and ensure rooms are reset and significant concerns receive follow-up.

SHINE Support and Inclusion: Help ensure the SHINE room is staffed and prepared for the 9:30 and 11:00 AM services. Coordinate with families and volunteers; provide age-appropriate Bible lessons, activities, sensory supports, and materials; pursue inclusion in age-appropriate classrooms when it best supports the child; and maintain SHINE as an intentional smaller-class environment for students needing individualized care.

Classroom Environments and Safety: Maintain the appearance, organization, functionality, cleanliness, safety, and readiness of Birth-Kindergarten and SHINE environments and storage areas. Proactively coordinate needed repairs, replacements, technology, furniture, signage, supplies, and improvements, and know, model, and uphold all safety policies, classroom ratios, incident procedures, and confidentiality expectations.

Childcare Oversight: Directly supervise, support, and develop the Childcare Assistant; recruit and develop a dependable childcare team; and ensure childcare environments meet the same standards of safety, care, organization, and excellence expected during Sunday ministry.

Family Care and Communication: Build trusted relationships with children and families, create a warm experience for new families, communicate appropriately with parents, and partner with them in their children's spiritual growth. Escalate significant pastoral, behavioral, safety, medical, or family concerns to the appropriate leader.

Events and Team Collaboration: Collaborate in planning and executing Easter, Christmas, VBS, family events, and other ministry initiatives. Participate in team planning, setup, execution, cleanup, and evaluation, and step into team-wide needs in support of the greater mission.

PROFESSIONAL COMPETENCIES  
  • Maintains strict confidentiality and sound judgement when handling sensitive information related to church operations, staff, and congregants.
  • Demonstrates strong verbal and written communication skills.
  • Works effectively in a team-oriented environment, collaborating with staff, volunteers, and ministry leaders.
  • Displays initiative, reliability, and strong organizational skills.
  • Able to manage multiple responsibilities while maintaining attention to detail and professionalism.
  • Functions effectively both behind the scenes and in public-facing situations, depending on ministry needs.
  • Demonstrates the ability to lead, encourage, coach, develop, and appropriately hold volunteers or teams accountable.
  • Relates and communicates effectively with adults and children and provides clear feedback with grace.
  • Is highly organized, attentive to detail, and able to manage multiple priorities, schedules, and deadlines.
  • Takes initiative, anticipates needs, develops solutions, delegates effectively, and works without continual direction.
  • Remains calm, adaptable, and effective when plans or ministry needs change and receives feedback with a commitment to continued growth.
  • Possesses experience working with young children; knowledge of early childhood development and previous church or ministry experience are strongly preferred.
SPIRITUAL & CHARACTER QUALIFICATIONS
  • A committed follower of Jesus Christ whose life reflects biblical character and aligns with Illuminate Community Church’s Statement of Faith, Position Statements and Staff Handbook.
  • Demonstrates a high level of personal and professional integrity, striving to live above reproach in both personal life and ministry responsibilities.
  • Supports and promotes a Christ-centered work environment, contributing positively to staff unity and the mission of the church.
  • Serves as a Christlike example to the church body, fellow staff and the broader community through conduct, attitude, and relationships.
  • Demonstrates humility, teachability, and a servant-hearted approach to ministry.
  • Demonstrates a genuine love for Jesus, His Church, children, families, and volunteers through a warm, approachable, dependable, and servant-hearted presence.
  • Is proactive, team-oriented, willing to take ownership, and able to balance high standards with grace when navigating corrective conversations.
  • Is inclusion-minded and committed to helping children of varying abilities experience belonging and meaningful participation.
  • Is committed to excellence with purpose, recognizing excellence as intentional stewardship rather than perfection.
ADDITIONAL EXPECTATIONS
  • Supports and participates in the overall ministry and mission of Illuminate Community Church.
  • Attends required staff meetings and church events (including Easter and Christmas) as requested.
  • Performs other duties as assigned to support the effectiveness of the ministry and staff team.
  • Maintains Sunday attendance and availability as essential functions of the role, including arrival by 6:30 AM.
  • Is available for staff meetings, evening programs, special events, Easter, Christmas, and other significant ministry dates; hours and responsibilities may shift during high-demand ministry seasons.
  • Serves as one team with one mission by noticing needs, taking initiative, supporting others, and stepping in when help is needed.
PHYSICAL DEMANDS:
Constant sitting, standing, moving and viewing of screens. Occasional lifting of 20 pounds or more.

Campus Staff Minister- Longwood University (Undergraduate Ministry)

Work Location:

Virginia

Job Type:

Full time

God has called InterVarsity to plant and to build witnessing communities of students and faculty who follow Jesus on college and university campuses. Through these groups, we believe ever- increasing numbers of students and faculty from all ethnic groups and areas of the campus will be transformed by the Gospel. We expect to see campuses increasingly become places where people, ideas, and structures flourish to the glory of God. We confidently anticipate that our InterVarsity alumni will become change agents across the country and around the world. We pursue this calling by discerning and actively participating in what God is already doing on campus. This is the essence of being a Campus Staff Minister (CSM).

ESSENTIAL COMMITMENTS/RESPONSIBILITIES 

Spiritual Growth 

You pursue maturity as a disciple of Jesus Christ so that your life and work increasingly reflects a growing love for God, God’s Word, God’s people of every ethnicity and culture, and God’s purposes in the world. To do this, you will: 

  • Pursue a vibrant relationship with the triune God through engagement with Scripture, prayer, and worship, both individually and in community 

  • Develop self-leadership (growing in self-awareness, self-management, relational integrity, and resiliency) 

  • Embrace Scriptural standards for behavior and attitudes 

 

Campus Leadership 

You communicate and model InterVarsity’s vision to see students and faculty transformed, campuses renewed and world changers developed 

  • Create a culture of humble dependence on God and bold expectation in God’s intention to start new witnessing communities throughout the campus and on new campuses 

  • Model – in person and through programs – InterVarsity’s vision and Core Values, including a biblically-defined commitment to engage every ethnic and social group on campus 

  • Lead students and faculty – individually and collectively – through Scripture, prayer, teaching, and discipleship experiences, so that they articulate and align their ministry activities around this vision 

  • Set annual goals through prayer, research and reflection with your teams (students, faculty, and staff) for qualitative and quantitative growth, including conversions and leadership development 

 

You create, develop, align and leverage ministry plans, programs, teams, and structures to close the gap between current reality and the aspirational goals. 

  • Build leadership teams who trust and partner well with you and who demonstrate spiritual vitality, relational health, and mission alignment 

  • Develop and execute plans to achieve annual goals, evaluating and modifying the plan as needed throughout the year 

  • Increase momentum for the vision by aligning programs, structures, conferences and teams around the goals 

  • Mobilize students and faculty to engage their relational networks with the gospel and to start new missional communities 

  • Under the direction of the Area Director, may supervise Ministry Interns and Campus Ministry Interns as delegated 

 

You intentionally gather, invite, and develop diverse groups of students and faculty so that they not only encounter and follow Jesus as Savior and Lord but also advance the mission on campus as participants and leaders. 

  • Create ways for faculty and students to encounter and follow Jesus through Scripture, worship, prayer, mission experiences, conferences, etc. 

  • Equip students and faculty so that they think strategically about campus engagement and so that they proclaim – in word, deed, and power – the good news of Jesus, regularly inviting students and faculty to follow him as Savior and Lord 

  • Disciple students and faculty by equipping them to hear the Word, respond actively, and debrief and interpret the experience so that they grow in Christlikeness, reflect our Core Values, and develop ministry skills 

  • Invite, coach, and equip students and faculty to become increasingly effective participants and leaders, including starting new witnessing communities on campuses 

 

Organizational Collaboration 

You work with a network of other local, area, regional, and national InterVarsity staff and volunteers so that our work reflects Biblical standards of excellence, integrity, and partnership. 

  • Partner with and respond positively to the direction and coaching of your supervisors and national leaders 

  • Contribute to collaborative and productive team meetings and relationships 

  • Affiliate chapters under your care and submit Graduating Student Forms in order to increase our partnership with current students and alumni 

  • Use national ministry resources and tools, as requested, including recruiting and/or participating in local, regional, or national conferences as  

  • Complete reporting, planning and review requirements in a timely way so that you and your supervisors can assess and improve your work as a CSM 

  • Comply with all InterVarsity policies and procedures 

 

Ministry Partnership Development 

You will develop a team of partners – churches and individuals (including alumni and community members) – who will resource the ministry financially, in prayer, or volunteer service that advances the mission. 

  • Raise 100% of the financial budget assigned by your supervisor 

  • Communicate regularly with your ministry partners, nurturing the relationship through visits, phone calls, emails and regular prayer letters 

  • Develop on-going, long-lasting partnership with alumni and volunteers 

  • Comply with all Ministry Partnership Policies 

  • Identify and invest in advocates who will build networks of volunteers and donors on InterVarsity’s behalf 

 

Accomplish all other assigned tasks as appropriate 

 

QUALIFICATIONS (common to all levels of CSM) 

  • Annually affirm InterVarsity’s Statement of Agreement (Doctrinal Basis and Purpose Statement). Abide by InterVarsity’s Code of Conduct. Believe and behave consonantly with InterVarsity’s Human Sexuality Theological Paper. Affirm and behave consonantly with InterVarsity’s “Women in Ministry Statement of Affirmation” 

  • Bachelor’s degree for CSMs assigned to a four-year campus. A minimum of an Associate’s degree for CSMs assigned to a two-year campus or a community college 

  • Strong interpersonal skills (including ability to minister to diverse ethnic communities and faculty) 

  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills 

  • Demonstrated problem solving skills 

  • Familiarity with word processing, presentation, email, and spreadsheet software 

 

WORK ENVIRONMENT/PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS 

The CSM position leads ministry in a college campus environment. A designated office space may or may not be available. The CSM is required to travel to on-campus and off- campus sites as appropriate. Off-campus travel includes, but is not limited to: student ministry conferences, Ministry Partnership Development meetings, and InterVarsity- sponsored training sessions, meetings, and conferences. The CSM is regularly required to communicate with others, and routinely uses standard office equipment such as computers, phones, photocopiers, filing cabinets, etc. 

Pay Range: $33,900.00 - $45,204.00 per year

Pay: This position is funded through personal fundraising. Accordingly, compensation will vary based on the ability of the individual to secure a donor team to fund the cost of his/her salary. SUMMARY

Provides administrative support to the Campus Pastor to fulfill the overall goals and objectives of the Starkville Campus and Pinelake Church. Primary responsibilities include providing daily support for the Campus Pastor (including email, schedule, and budget), coordinating campus-wide events, providing campus information to the One Church team, and updating and monitoring church management software.

GENERAL RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Learn
    • Pursue a growing relationship with Jesus through consistent time in God’s Word and prayer.
    • Continually grow in your understanding of the Jesus-Centered Life (salvation, identity, life, and authority in Christ).
    • Remain teachable and hungry, seeking feedback, learning from others, and developing both spiritually and professionally.
    • Cultivate awareness of God’s presence in everyday life, listening to the Holy Spirit and responding in obedience.
  • Live
    • Practice and model the rhythms of Be the Church (Grow, Pray, Connect, and Share).
    • Pursue emotional health by engaging in self-awareness, addressing past wounds, and cultivating honest, healthy relationships.
    • Practice healthy rhythms, prioritizing your relationship with Jesus and your family
    • Embody a life of integrity and surrender, allowing your private life with God to shape your work.
  • Lead
    • Take ownership of disciple-making by supporting and strengthening environments where people can take their next step toward a Jesus-Centered Life.
    • Leverage your role, systems, and responsibilities to remove barriers and create clarity, helping both staff and the church move forward in the Discipleship Pathway (Essentials → JCL → Be the Church).
    • Contribute to life-change by bringing your skills, organization, and follow-through to your work, knowing that what you build and manage helps others lead and shepherd more effectively.
    • Build people through your influence—encouraging, supporting, and serving teammates and Servant Leaders in ways that help them grow and thrive.
    • Measure success not only by task completion, but by how your work contributes to disciples being formed and multiplied across the church.
  • Embrace the Culture
    • Value and embody the staff values, which we call the 7 H’s: Humility, Honor, Honesty, Hunger, Holy Spirit, Health, and Harmony
    • Communicate clearly, honestly, and proactively in a way that builds trust, unity, and momentum.
    • Work in alignment with the church vision and leadership
    • Participate fully in the life of your campus or team, contributing to the unity, health, and shepherding of the faith family.


SPECIFIC LIST OF DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Provide comprehensive administrative support to the Campus Pastor by managing email and phone communications, coordinating meeting requests, and welcoming in-person guests.
  • Maintain and update the Campus Pastor's calendar, communicate schedule changes promptly, and ensure timely access to and distribution of important information and updates.
  • Develop and maintain advanced proficiency in Rock (church management system) to assist in the oversight of facility scheduling, including processing room reservations, updating existing bookings, and resolving scheduling conflicts to ensure the accurate coordination of all campus activities.
  • Provide training and refresher instruction to staff on the effective use of Rock as needed.
  • Utilize established room management processes to ensure accurate event setup by confirming room arrangements, cross-checking events with the campus calendar, and coordinating with the Facilities team to ensure clear communication and proper execution of all room setups.
  • Serve as the primary resource for the One Church and Starkville Campus calendars by ensuring all events are planned and approved through the appropriate ministry, maintaining calendar accuracy, and coordinating Security and MRT support as needed.
  • Review and file Campus Pastor expenses, ensuring that all information is provided in a timely manner and expenses are in the correct accounts.
  • Provide complete administrative support for the campus baptisms (calendaring, Rock information and approvals, scheduling baptism hosts, etc.)
  • Provide project support to the staff as needed and directed by the Campus Pastor.
  • Facilitate database management for new staff hires and exiting staff to ensure compliance with our policies and systems.
  • Develop a strong working knowledge of the Personnel Policy and help ensure the team consistently follows established policies and procedures.
  • Keep track of needed office supplies (including kitchen supplies) and restock when necessary.

Perform other duties as assigned.

SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES
May supervise and coordinate work with servant leaders.

To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily. The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skill and/or ability required. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform essential functions.

EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE REQUIRED
High school diploma or equivalent minimum; college experience preferred. Two to five years of administrative experience.

LANGUAGE SKILLS
The individual must be able to understand written or oral instructions; read, analyze and interpret documents, instructions manuals, and policies and procedures. Excellent interpersonal skills, ability to work with a diverse group of people, communicate clearly and effectively on the telephone, email and in person, demonstrating tact and diplomacy.

COMPUTER AND MATHEMATICAL SKILLS
The individual must have demonstrated skill in the use of Windows/MacOS to complete tasks (including word processing and spreadsheets) and the ability to use the internet for information retrieval. The individual must be able to apply basic mathematical concepts and operations to such tasks as accounting, budget management, and financial expense monitoring.

REASONING ABILITY
The ability to simultaneously conceptualize and plan multiple tasks; project outcomes using different implementation strategies; and apply creative and innovative thinking to problem situations is required. The ability to work effectively and efficiently under stressful conditions to ensure deadlines are met is essential.

PHYSICAL DEMANDS
The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to sit and talk or hear. The employee is required to stand, walk and reach with hands and arms.

Must be able to lift up to 25 lbs.

WORK ENVIRONMENT
The work environment characteristics described here are representative of those an employee encounters while performing the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

The noise level of the work environment is usually moderate.

post_html:
Campus Ministry Intern - Carolinas Region (Undergraduate Ministry)

Work Location:

North Carolina

Job Type:

Full time

To advance the purpose of InterVarsity, this position is focused on learning and preparing for the full responsibilities of a Campus Minister. The associate will be assigned campus work based on strengths and growth areas determined by the application process. This is a 16 month position in which the individual receives intensive training and exercises ministerial functions consistent with a campus minister. The associate is paid a monthly salary. A supervisory decision, with input from the Campus Ministry Associate, is made at the end of the term of service as to whether the individual is suitable for continuing employment with InterVarsity. The Campus Ministry Associate may end employment at any time with notice given.

INTEREST FORM

If you are new to InterVarsity in the Carolinas and have not spoken with one of our Area Directors about the possibility of applying to work with us, please complete this interest form and wait for us to contact you before proceeding with the application.


PLACEMENT

Upon completion of the application to work for InterVarsity's Carolinas Region, you will be contacted about interviewing for a position in our region. Following your interview if an associate offer is made, we will offer you placement at our training site at the University of North Carolina - Chapel Hill. Our internship is typically 16 months long beginning in September and ending 16 months later in December.

 

HIRING TIMELINE

If you are an InterVarsity student, the most typical timeline for hiring takes place in the semester that you are graduating. That provides the opportunity for you to receive training in funding the ministry (3 hours per week) while you are finishing your degree. 

 

Spring Semester Hiring Window:

  • Application and references are due the second week of January.
  • An interview will be scheduled for mid-February, at a location in the Carolinas (typically Raleigh or Charlotte) 
  • Our Offer or Declination to follow within one week of the interview
  • Your acceptance or declination of offer within one week of the offer.
  • Ministry Partnership Development Training begins with a weekend of training in mid to late March

**Specific dates will be provided to you upon request or as soon as you enter the application process

Other Hiring Windows: 

If you are a current student graduating at a different time of year or a candidate considering a move from another field or ministry context, and in need of a different timeline, we will work with you to set up a different hiring timeline.


 

MAJOR RESPONSIBILITIES

Personal:

  • Be a maturing disciple of Jesus Christ: growing in love for God, God's Word, God's people of every ethnicity and culture, and God's purposes in the world
  • Practice daily spiritual disciplines
  • Pursue spiritual relationships and involvement in a worshiping community
  • Continue learning and growth in spiritual understanding, biblical knowledge, ministry experience and skills
  • Experience and live out an ongoing call to ministry service with InterVarsity and its mission.

Ministry Training:

  • Exhibit a learning posture in the context of new ministry assignments and experiences
  • Complete all reading and campus assignments given by Area Director and Campus Trainer

Ministry Leadership: (based on developing skills)

  • Develop a Witnessing Community on Campus
    • Seek opportunities to proclaim and demonstrate the Gospel of Jesus Christ 
    • Learn to guide chapters (or assigned segments of a chapter) in the development of strategic thinking regarding witness to the university 
    • Train students to share their faith on campus
    • Encourage a prayerful lifestyle in students and faculty, especially focusing on those who do not yet follow Jesus as Lord and Savior
  • Learn to model and assist students and faculty in growing in their love for God's people of every ethnicity and culture 
    • Invest in growth and understanding of own ethnicity
    • Help grow multi-ethnic ministry in the InterVarsity community
  • Missional Student Leadership Development
    • Teach students to love, study and apply Scripture to their lives
    • Plan and lead students in discipleship cycles that encourage personal transformation and mission engagement
    • Help students grow into leaders and leaders of leaders
    • Work with student and faculty leadership teams
  • Cast Vision for Ministry on Campus
    • Articulate a compelling vision for reaching the campus
    • Embody the vision on campus
    • Invite students to live out the vision
  • Work with InterVarsity structures:  Lead and guide chapter structures such as Small Groups, Large Groups, Outreach to accomplish mission on campus (as assigned by trainer)
  • Participate in the area ministry team to contribute to the accomplishment of the team’s plans for spiritual growth and transformation in the lives of students
  • Recruit students and faculty to and provide specific leadership for retreats and conferences 
  • Engage positively with the supervision you receive from your staff ministry director and campus trainer

Administration

  • Comply with Risk Management and Legal policies and procedures
  • Follow budgeting and expense guidelines
  • Fulfill area, regional, and national reporting requirements

Ministry Partner Development (MPD) and Public Relations:

  • Develop and contact a list of potential donors
  • Execute plans to secure financial and prayer support among partners as directed by MPD coach
  • Communicate with donors regularly
  • Serve as a representative of InterVarsity to ministry partners, churches, and community connections
  • Maintain expenses within allocated budget


 

QUALIFICATIONS

  • Annually affirm InterVarsity’s Statement of Faith
  • Bachelor’s Degree for work at 4 year institutions; Associate’s Degree for work at 2 year institutions
  • Ministry experience:  (in InterVarsity as a student or another ministry context) teaching spiritual and biblical principles, planning ministry programs, spiritually discipling others. 
  • Growing competence in self-management
  • Effective oral and written communication skills
  • Demonstrated ability and commitment to work in a diverse team environment
  • Willing to regularly travel for team meetings, student/staff retreats & conferences, training events

PAY RANGE

$44,000 annually for this Carolinas Campus Ministry Associate position


Pay: 

This position is funded through personal fundraising. Accordingly, compensation will vary based on the ability of the individual to secure a donor team to fund the cost of individual salary (and additional budget items). The anticipated salary range for this position on a full-time basis (40 hours/week) is dependent on a variety of factors, including location and cost of living. The actual salary received, including any geographic adjustment to account for location and cost of living, is subject to the individual’s ability to raise funds necessary to cover the full amount of such salary within the range set forth in the job posting details.


The InterVarsity Campus Intern Budget, in addition to salary, includes benefits, ministry expenses, training expenses, and overhead.




InterVarsity Christian Fellowship/USA

FRAME OF REFERENCE


All staff members subscribe annually to the Purpose Statement of InterVarsity:


In response to God’s love, grace and truth:

The purpose of InterVarsity Christian Fellowship/USA is

to establish and advance at colleges and universities

witnessing communities of students and faculty

who follow Jesus as Savior and Lord:

growing in love for God,

God’s Word,

God’s people of every ethnicity and culture

and God’s purposes in the world.


This purpose is admittedly more limited than the Great Commission.  As a mission extension of the local church, we have adopted boundaries on our activities based on our call to serve a defined group of God’s people.  Within the context of InterVarsity’s purpose, all of the relationships and tasks that staff members engage in as part of their work for InterVarsity have both eternal and temporal components.  


 

INTERVARSITY CHRISTIAN FELLOWSHIP/USA® Doctrinal Basis

We believe in:

The only true God, the almighty Creator of all things, existing eternally in three persons; Father, Son, and Holy Spirit; full of love and glory.


The unique divine inspiration, entire trustworthiness and authority of the Bible.


The value and dignity of all people: created in God’s image to live in love and holiness, but alienated from God and each other because of our sin and guilt, and justly subject to God's wrath.


Jesus Christ, fully human and fully divine, who lived as a perfect example, who assumed the judgment due sinners by dying in our place, and who was bodily raised from the dead and ascended as Savior and Lord.


Justification by God’s grace to all who repent and put their faith in Jesus Christ alone for salvation.


The indwelling presence and transforming power of the Holy Spirit, who gives to all believers a new life and a new calling to obedient service.


The unity of all believers in Jesus Christ, manifest in worshipping and witnessing churches making disciples throughout the world.


The victorious reign and future personal return of Jesus Christ, who will judge all people with justice and mercy, giving over the unrepentant to eternal condemnation but receiving the redeemed into eternal life.


To God be glory forever.

job_name: Campus Ministries Teacher & Children's Ministry Specialist
post_html:
Overview

The Campus Ministries Teacher and Children's Ministry Specialist (CMS) serves as a Day Care Teacher for school-age children, providing care, guidance, and programmatic engagement in a nurturing environment. This role supports the holistic development of children through structured activities and faith-based learning. In addition to this daycare responsibility, this role also serves as a member of the Campus Ministries pastoral team, with a focus on the spiritual care and ministry leadership of children at the College of Officer Training (CFOT). This includes teaching, mentoring, and leading children in their faith journey through worship, discipleship, and community-building programs. 

This ministry requires a deep commitment to loving and serving children and their families, fostering spiritual growth, and collaborating with other leaders to create a vibrant and supportive environment. 

Responsibilities

Lead Teacher

  • Implement the daily program while following the daily schedule as closely as possible. 
  • Supervise and ensure the safety and well-being of the children at all times, being alert to the needs and/or problems of the children as individuals and as a group.
  • Alert the CM Leadership of potential.
  • When applicable, complete an Incident and Accident form.
  • Plan a developmentally appropriate curriculum to include activities and experiences contributing to each child’s growth and development.
  • Supervise activities and interact with the children.
  • Submit monthly communications to the Director and distribute to parents. 
  • Decorate the classroom with bulletin boards, pictures, children's artwork, and other hangings to enhance the vision and mission of the space.
  • Maintain the organization of classroom materials and equipment. 
  • Maintain classroom supplies and advise the Assistant Director when supplies need replenishing. 
  • Prepare and deliver snacks for the children.
  • Evaluate each child's particular needs and attempt to meet them in concurrence with the Director and Assistant Director. 
  • Greet the parents at arrival and depature times, building a good relationship with clear communication. Encourage and welcome parents to be involved in CM's activities. 
  • Conform to meeting New York State Day Care regulations, including teacher-in-service training. 
  • Attend regular staff planning and evaluation meetings.
  • Lead weekly programmatic activities assigned by leadership in CM.
  • Daily supervision and help with classroom cleanup, vacuuming, and laundering of rest linens as needed.
  • Handle discipline promptly and in accordance with the stated policy on discipline. 
  • Check each child daily for visible signs of illness and report it to CM Leadership. 
  • Maintain Campus Ministries' health policies. 
  • Perform and additional duties centered on the children's care as requested by the Director. 
  • Provide transportation to Campus Ministries' children in Salvation Army vehicles assigned to Campus Ministries, as needed. 
  • Provide support to other classrooms, as needed. 
  • Follow all New York State Day Care and KeepSAfe reporting mandates.
  • Perform all other duties as assigned by the supervisor. 

Spiritual Life

  • Lead small groups and serve as a small group leader to CFOT children. 
  • Assist in providing day-to-day pastoral care to the youth at CFOT.
  • Collaborate with the CM Officer and CM Leadership to develop ideas to present age-appropriate, engaging and creative Biblical education.
  • Support and assist in the creation of a Spiritual Development Plan for CFOT youth in conjunction with the Director and CM Officer.
  • Weekly planning and executing age-appropriate activities for all CM youth (infant to teenage), including workship, retreats, and other activities.
  • Be present in the Day Care area during work hours, building relationships with children. 
  • Plan special activities for youth, including chaperoning teen retreats (i.e., youth councils, Commissioning) in conjunction with the Director and CM Officer. 

 

Qualifications

  • Associate's degree or equivalent from a two-year college or technical school, or equivalent combination of education and work experience. 
  • Valid driver’s license and approval to drive a 12-passenger van.
  • NY State Teaching Certificate 
  • Active Christian in good standing. 
  • Must be available to work on Sundays, as required.

Full Time Church Planter in Residency Position – Movement Church, Port Charlotte, FL

Movement Church is seeking to multiply it’s Kingdom impact by developing and deploying a church planter in residence. Movement is a fast-growing church of more than one thousand people that are inviting others to know Jesus, love others, and live changed. In partnership with the Alliance Southeast, they desire to extend their impact by planting a church that will become a fully mature congregation within the Christian and Missionary Alliance (C&MA).

This residency will last two years as a full-time staff position at Movement Church with the goal of continuing as a full-time staff position as the planting pastor of the resulting church plant. Applicants should have experience leading at an executive level in churches of 200 or more and have a heart for reaching the unchurched and those far from God. Ideal applicants will have solid communication and people skills along with the ability to form and execute a clear ministry strategy.

While previous experience is required, the ideal applicant will desire to be coached and developed into Movement’s ministry model and culture. Additional coaching will be provided by the Alliance Southeast in the areas of disciple making, leadership development, soul care, and fundraising methods. The goal will be for the final six months of this residency to be focused on core team building and launch with access to existing campus facilities being made available for training and soft-launch programs and services.

Candidates must be able to meet licensing and ordination requirements with the C&MA which includes having previously completed at least thirty hours of theological education at an accredited school or through a C&MA approved program. To learn more about the C&MA and the Alliance Southeast visit www.alliancese.org

To be considered for this position, please forward your resume and any accompanying materials to the Alliance Southeast office of the C&MA, attention Michelle Hill, mhill@alliancese.org

Please do not contact the church directly.

At Life.Church, we exist to lead people to become fully devoted followers of Christ. It’s been our mission since 1996 and has guided us every day. Leading people isn’t just an expectation; it’s a necessity.  It’s a cornerstone of our culture. That's why we’re always seeking leaders—leaders like you—to bring your skills to life. We are one church meeting in multiple locations, and we want to help you become the person God made you to be. 
 
The Life.Church Switch ministry is devoted to leading students in 6th-12th grade to become fully devoted followers of Christ. Staff and volunteer leaders develop relationships with students during weekly experiences, small groups, and serving opportunities by teaching truth through God's Word and being culturally relevant.
 
The Associate Youth Pastor (AYP) will be, in part, responsible for the leadership and execution of the vision of student ministry. Success for this role will be people (students and adults alike) in the AYPs sphere of influence taking next steps in their spiritual growth-like beginning a relationship with Jesus, serving, inviting, giving, engaging in God’s word, and leading.  

What You'll Do

  • Consistently inspire people to use their gifts to lead in Switch.
  • Follow protocol to onboard new leaders, including background screening, training, and orientations.
  • Provide ongoing leadership development for the leader team.
  • Connect with and develop the team of coaches who will provide the most direct leadership and relational connection to the larger leader team.
  • Develop coaches to ensure that lobby set up/tear down is executed with excellence and Switch Host Team is prepared and ready to greet and provide hospitality to students and parents.
  • Ensure that a volunteer coach has all video files downloaded and that the program (including lighting and technology) is prepared with excellence.
  • Provide support if challenges arise during an experience.
  • Provide support on the weekend for Loop (5th-6th grade experience).
  • Identify and inspire and train/develop adults to lead students in Loop during the weekend.
  • Occasionally communicate a live message to Loop students with provided notes and video support from Central.
  • Provide Pastoral care to families.
  • Identify and inspire students to serve on the weekend.
  • Communicate to leaders, parents, and students in multiple forms (text, email, social media, lobby) the vision and values of Switch and Life.Church.
  • Lead or co-lead special events like Leader Nights, At the Movies projects, Family Weekend, and Capacity (student leadership conference) prep.
  • Learn the budget process.
  • Learn about and be able to communicate about all other Life Church ministries.

Skills Needed to Succeed

  • Inspire people both verbally and in written communication.
  • Clearly present expectations, processes, and policies in a way that leads to the right outcome.
  • Ability to provide objective solutions to ministry issues/complaints.
  • Ability to self-motivate and make independent decisions.
  • Knowledgeable in all necessary systems that Life.Church uses to manage volunteers, present content on the weekend in Loop and on Wednesdays in the auditorium, and report appropriate information and analytics at the organizational level.
  • Savvy with social media.
  • Skilled in empowering people and growing a team, and leading others to reach a desired outcome.
  • Adept at leading through conflict.
  • Time management skills.
  • High school diploma or GED.

We hire new team members to begin their journey at an existing Life.Church location so they can learn the culture and systems of our church from experienced pastors already on the team. Our Beliefs, Culture, and Commitment to Diversity

At Life.Church, every staff member, and intern is a minister and is expected to engage in the church's ministry fully. We consider ministry readiness and an individual’s capacity to represent Life.Church’s beliefs as a minister during the selection process for all staff and intern positions. An essential function within every position held by a staff member or intern at Life.Church is to uphold and represent the beliefs of Life.Church. Learn more about what we believe at Life.Church. 
 
While we unite around our mission, we know unity doesn’t mean uniformity. Our calling is too great, and our mission is too important not to be intentional about strengthening our team through diversity. We know that diverse perspectives in race, ethnicity, background, age, and gender are essential to reaching the world for Christ. To learn more about how we strengthen our team through diversity, visit our careers page.
