The Family Pastor provides vision, leadership, and pastoral care for all ministries serving children, students, and families (birth–12th grade). This role is responsible for building a unified, scalable discipleship strategy that equips parents, develops leaders, and ensures alignment across Kids and Student Ministries. The Family Pastor leads through staff and leaders—not by executing weekly programming—and is responsible for developing the Kids Ministry Director and overseeing Student Ministry leadership.



Why We Love This Opportunity

I love this opportunity because Ascent is at an inflection point. They are at a place where growth has been happening and with the right new leader, they believe substantial growth is happening. This person will have a chance to lead at a high level at a church with incredible growth and opportunity.


A great match for this position would be:

  • Developer and Manager of Systems and People: Someone who can assess and know systems and the ability to develop systems and people to accomplish the vision of the church.
  • Communicator: Someone who is able to communicate God’s Word to the congregation.
  • Shepherd: someone who has a heart and passion to care for people and families. 
  • Humility with Ideology and Theology: Someone who has a strong biblical theology but is also able to sit in the tension that others may be different and can sit at the table with all individuals and all beliefs.
  • Multiplier of People: Someone who can inspire others and multiply people’s skills and gifts for the vision of the church.



About This Organization

Ascent Church started 13 years ago in an old Sam’s Club that had been left vacant for years in the community. Bill Stephens and Jim Candy founded the church, along with a team of about 40-50 people who helped lead all areas of ministry. The two founding pastors had over 40 combined years of experience in strong college, high school, and middle school ministry, and wanted to establish a church that would reflect the high value they put on relationships and walking closely with anyone who walks through our doors. The church grew to over 1200 people in the first 8 years, then COVID hit. We now have about 750-1000 people that call Ascent home, with roughly 500 in attendance on Sundays.


Using scripture as our guide, and the example Jesus set in all ways of life, we built a church with five distinct pillars; Personal, Inspiring, Generous, Risk Taking, and Accessible. We wanted to be a church that cared so deeply for the community that they would be disappointed if we were to leave. We set out to operate with no strings attached generosity, with great relationships and partnerships with all city entities, especially our local schools. We wanted to present the Gospel with great humility, understanding that it’s imperfect people presenting a perfect God in an imperfect way. We focused much of our efforts on intergenerational ministry, recognizing that the future of the church is dependent on our Vintage folks, our kids, and everyone in between.  

 

We deeply value racial justice, women in any and all areas of leadership in the church, and the ability to sit at the table with people of differing ideologies and theology, and find common ground under the umbrella of Jesus and His love and compassion. We seek to live out the call of Jesus to represent and re-present Him locally, regionally and globally. In this day and age of extreme division in our country and in our churches, we seek to be peacemakers and a church that will draw the unchurched to the love of Jesus, and those in the church to the unity that Jesus prayed for in the days leading up to the cross.


Location

Ascent Church is located in Louisville, Colorado, nestled between Boulder and Denver along the beautiful Front Range of the Rocky Mountains. Our community is known for its exceptional quality of life, excellent schools, family-friendly neighborhoods, extensive trail systems, and easy access to outdoor recreation. Residents enjoy hiking, biking, skiing, and mountain adventures, while also benefiting from the cultural, educational, and professional opportunities found throughout the Boulder-Denver corridor. The area attracts people who are thoughtful, engaged, and passionate about building meaningful lives, families, and communities.

At the same time, our community presents a unique ministry opportunity. Many people in this area are highly educated, spiritually curious, and deeply interested in purpose, relationships, and personal growth, yet many have little connection to a local church or carry skepticism toward organized religion. Ascent seeks to be a church that genuinely loves and serves our city, creating a place where people from all backgrounds can explore faith, encounter Jesus, and experience authentic community. We believe God is at work in our region, and we are excited to participate in what He is doing.


Mission, Vision, and Values

At Ascent, we believe the church exists not simply in a city, but for the good of its city. We love our city and the surrounding communities, and we want to be known as a church that serves, supports, and contributes to the flourishing of the people around us. Rather than approaching our community as a problem to solve, we approach it as neighbors to love. We hope that through our care, generosity, and presence, people experience what Jesus is like: safe, loving, gracious, and life-giving.


We are a congregation made up of people from many different backgrounds, experiences, convictions, and perspectives. What unites us is not agreement on every issue, but a shared commitment to follow Jesus, study the Scriptures, and center our lives on Him. We believe spiritual growth happens in community, and we invite people to remain at the table with one another, even when they disagree, while staying anchored to Christ. Our desire is to present Jesus clearly, help people grow as His disciples, and participate together in bringing His Kingdom to earth as it is in heaven.


Key Responsibilities

Vision & Strategy:

  • Develop and implement a comprehensive family ministry strategy (birth–12th grade)
  • Direct and oversee Kids Ministry, including curriculum selection, establishing year-long program initiatives, developing parental wellness opportunities, and managing ministry budgets. Walk alongside new parents and serve as a pastoral resource for all families.
  • Direct and support Student Ministry, including the school year program plan, mission trips and community service projects, and approving the ministry budget. Pastor families as they navigate raising older children.
  • Ensure alignment between Kids Ministry, Student Ministry, and the broader church vision.
  • Define clear spiritual growth pathways and key milestone moments.

 

Parent Discipleship & Engagement:

  • Equip parents as the primary spiritual leaders of their children
  • Develop and lead:
  • Parenting resources
  • Classes and events
  • Communication rhythms
  • Meet with and pastor families in all stages of their parenting
  • Create meaningful milestone moments (dedications, transitions, etc.)


Key Qualifications

At least 5 years' experience working with the next generation.


For more information about this role, please contact Phil Christian at pchristian@slingshotgroup.org

ABOUT CATALYST CHURCH 

Catalyst Church is a young, growing, and vibrant church located in Artesia in southeastern New Mexico. In June of 2025, our church family celebrated a major milestone as we moved into a brand-new facility, creating space for the continued growth and momentum God has been bringing to our congregation. Just a few months later, in January 2026, we celebrated our 10th anniversary as a church—reflecting on a decade of ministry, life change, and God’s faithfulness in our community.

Catalyst is a church that values both hard work and genuine joy. Our staff culture is built on teamwork, humility, and fun—we truly see ourselves as a family. People at Catalyst care deeply for one another, and that sense of belonging extends to everyone who walks through our doors. We’re passionate about helping people take their next step with Jesus and creating an environment where faith can grow in authentic community.

God has been blessing our church with steady growth. Our current average attendance for the year is over 250, up from 211 last year. Over the past nine months alone, we’ve celebrated 27 baptisms, including 15 students…evidence that God is moving powerfully among the next generation.

Student ministry is an especially exciting area of growth for Catalyst. Our youth ministry averages about 45 students each Wednesday night and continues to build strong momentum. Students are actively involved in the life of the church, not only attending but serving. Many of them participate on the worship team, run media and production, help in kids ministry, and contribute throughout the church. There is a strong foundation already in place and tremendous potential for future impact.

We’re looking for a leader who wants to be fully invested, not just in the church but in the community as well. Artesia is the kind of town where relationships matter, and being present in students’ lives means showing up to games, activities, and community events. The right leader will build on the solid groundwork that has already been laid while helping guide students toward deeper discipleship and leadership in the church.

Catalyst Church is a place where relationships are strong, ministry is growing, and the future is full of possibility. If you’re passionate about discipling students, building meaningful relationships, and serving in a church that feels like family, Catalyst may be exactly where God is calling you to serve.

Learn more about Catalyst Church HERE. 



ABOUT THE IDEAL CANDIDATE
We are seeking a passionate, relational, and mission-minded Youth Pastor who is excited to disciple the next generation and invest deeply in the lives of students in Artesia and the surrounding community.

This is not simply a program-management role.

This is a relational leadership opportunity for a pastor who believes student ministry is about discipleship, spiritual formation, and raising up young leaders who actively participate in the life of the church.

Our student ministry already has a strong foundation. With roughly 45 students gathering weekly and many of them already serving in areas like worship, media, and kids ministry, we’re looking for a leader who will build on that momentum, helping students grow deeper in their faith while empowering them to live it out in the church, their schools, and the community.

THE OPPORTUNITY
The Youth Pastor will lead and shape the student ministry of Catalyst by developing meaningful discipleship environments, equipping volunteers, and building relationships with students and families.

Your leadership will help cultivate:
  • A vibrant weekly student gathering centered on worship, biblical teaching, and authentic community
  • Strong discipleship pathways that help students grow in their relationship with Jesus
  • A team of volunteers who are equipped, encouraged, and empowered to invest in students
  • A culture where students actively serve and engage in the broader life of the church
  • Meaningful relationships with students through presence in their everyday lives—school events, activities, and community moments
This role also provides opportunities to contribute to the life of the broader church through preaching occasionally on Sunday mornings, participating in church-wide initiatives, and serving alongside a unified staff team.

WHO THRIVES HERE
The right candidate for Catalyst will be someone who embraces both relational ministry and intentional leadership.

A Shepherd at Heart 
You genuinely love students and want to walk alongside them through the most formative years of their lives. You are approachable, relational, and invested in helping students follow Jesus.

A Relational Leader
You understand that effective youth ministry happens beyond the church building. You enjoy showing up at games, performances, school events, and community activities where students are already living their lives.

A Builder of Teams 
You recruit, train, and empower volunteers to be part of the mission. You believe great ministry happens through teams, not individuals.

A Biblical Communicator
You can teach Scripture clearly and faithfully in ways that connect with students and help them understand how God’s Word shapes everyday life.

A Team Player 
You enjoy working alongside other staff members, supporting church-wide initiatives, and contributing to the overall health and mission of the church.

A Growing Disciple
 Your leadership flows from a vibrant and growing relationship with Jesus Christ, marked by spiritual maturity, integrity, and humility.

WHAT YOU’LL LEAD
  • The Youth Pastor will oversee the primary rhythms and environments of the student ministry, including:
  • Weekly student worship and Bible study gatherings (Wednesday nights)
  • Student events throughout the year including camps, retreats, trips, and outreach opportunities
  • Volunteer recruitment, development, and leadership
  • Ongoing communication with students and parents through social media, church communications, and regular updates
  • Curriculum development or selection to help students grow in biblical understanding and spiritual maturity
  • Intentional relationship building with students throughout the week
You will also participate in the life of the broader church through occasional preaching, assisting with weekend service preparation as needed, and supporting church events and ministries.

WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR
  • Experience leading or serving in student ministry within a church context
  • A strong and growing personal relationship with Jesus Christ
  • Alignment with the doctrine and statement of faith of Catalyst Church
  • The ability to lead, organize, and communicate effectively
  • A heart for discipleship and developing young leaders
  • Some formal Bible training preferred
This is a full-time pastoral role for a leader who is excited to invest in students, serve the local church, and become part of a church family that works hard, has fun, and is passionate about seeing lives transformed by Jesus.



ABOUT ARTESIA, NM

Artesia is a close-knit, welcoming community in southeastern New Mexico where relationships matter and people genuinely care for one another. With a population of just over 12,000, it offers a safe, family-friendly environment, strong schools, and a steady rhythm of community events that bring people together throughout the year. Life here moves at a relational pace—neighbors know each other, families are deeply connected, and there’s a strong sense of pride in the town and its people.

Often referred to as the “City of Champions,” Artesia is known across the state for its rich athletic tradition and deep-rooted community pride in sports. From youth leagues to championship-level high school programs, athletics are a central part of the culture, creating a shared identity and energy throughout the town. Beyond sports, Artesia reflects a strong set of values—hard work, resilience, and community commitment—that shape everyday life and make it a great place to invest in people and ministry.

Conveniently located between Roswell and Carlsbad—home to the world-famous Carlsbad Caverns National Park—Artesia serves as a central hub for the region. The city is also less than 60 miles from the beautiful Sacramento Mountains and within two hours of Ruidoso, offering easy access to hiking, camping, skiing, and year-round outdoor recreation. Whether you enjoy small-town living or quick getaways to the mountains, Artesia offers a unique blend of simplicity, opportunity, and adventure.

Summary

Serves as a Chaplain Clinical Pastoral Educator (CPE) performing senior-level clinical assignments for the VHA. The incumbent provides comprehensive religious, spiritual, and pastoral care to all persons that are commensurate with the needs, desires, and voluntary consent of the Veteran, caregiver, or staff. The incumbent addresses the spiritual component of health and wellness in every patient care setting to ensure that pastoral care is fully integrated into all aspects of chaplain services.


Duties

Duties Include but are not limited to:

  • Serves as a certified Chaplain (CPE) providing comprehensive, religious ministry
    services and training to Veteran patients and students according to their specific needs.
  • Carries out an education ministry with the CPE Center, which is highly integrated into
    VHA's Chaplain program. Provides thorough guidance and advice to Chaplain Service
    management staff, students, other Chaplains, and stakeholders.
  • Manages the daily operations of the CPE Center and develops and implements
    program policies and procedures. Serves as a certified educator of record for all CPE
    students for an assigned designated area. Provides administrative oversight and
    programmatic resources and monitors educational outcomes.
  • Offers students an opportunity to develop and expand professional caring skills in a
    clinical setting to address a person's spiritual, emotional, and physical needs; and offers
    students experience with hands-on spiritual care for hospitalized patients.
  • Maintains records for all educator evaluations, student records, center portfolio, and
    CPE accreditation requirements, which may include off-site CPE satellite and placement
    contracts.
  • Seeks approval for allied health trainee positions through the Office of Academic
    Affiliations (OAA). Conducts recruitment and interviews and selects students for the
    CPE program.
  • Ensures all documentation is completed for compliance. Develops educational curricula
    that are measurable, outcome-oriented, and evidence-based and designed to meet
    board certification competencies.
  • Develops relationships with key staff related to the CPE program, e.g., clinical
    preceptors, Advisory Group members, and OAA staff.
  • Provides extended and intensive pastoral counseling as an integral part of the treatment
    program with patients facing complex, ethical, moral, and/or spiritual issues.
  • Monitors the CPE Center's program effectiveness and modification of service pattern,
    which includes research and leadership of clinical teams. Develops and implements
    methods to measure the effectiveness of the Chaplain educational program.
  • Uses outcome evaluations to improve educational services and to design education
    system changes. Seeks best practices, primary research, and research literature that
    informs the ministry specialty and one's spiritual care practice.
  • Provides leadership, direction, orientation, coaching, in-service training, staff
    development, and continuing education programs.
  • Serves as a primary senior Chaplain education resource, spiritual advisor, and liaison
    for the spiritual needs of Veterans patients, students, caregivers, and staff.
  • Conducts comprehensive religious services and worship, pastoral ministry, and
    administration of Chaplain services. Addresses the religious, spiritual, moral, and ethical
    problems of patients and staff through educational means.
  • Completes various complex educational projects, task groups, and assignments to
    obtain pertinent high-level information needed for Chaplain Service senior management
    officials.

Work Schedule: Full-time, 07:30am-4:00pm, Rotating days and weekends
Compressed/Flexible: Available

Virtual: This is not a virtual position.

Requirements

Conditions of employment

  • You must be a U.S. Citizen to apply for this job.

As a condition of employment for accepting this position, you will be required to serve a 1 or 2-year trial period during which we will evaluate your fitness and whether your continued employment advances the public interest. In determining if your employment advances the public interest, we may consider:
  • your performance and conduct;
  • the needs and interests of the agency;
  • whether your continued employment would advance organizational goals of the agency or the Government; and
  • whether your continued employment would advance the efficiency of the Federal service.
Upon completion of your trial period, your employment will be terminated unless you receive certification, in writing, that your continued employment advances the public interest.

Qualifications

Complete all application requirements detailed in the "Required Documents" section of this announcement.

Basic Requirements:

  • United States Citizenship: Non-citizens may only be appointed when it is not possible to recruit qualified citizens in accordance with VA Policy.
  • Education. Applicants must possess a Master of Divinity degree or equivalent educational qualifications as evidenced by a graduate-level theological degree from a college, university or theological school accredited by a member of the Council for Higher Education Accreditation (CHEA) or Association of Theological Schools (ATS) and recognized by the U.S. Department of Education. NOTE: For applicants who do not possess a Master of Divinity degree or equivalent educational degree, an approved educational equivalency review from a nationally recognized board certification body for chaplains (see paragraph d) is acceptable.
  • Ecclesiastical Endorsement. In accordance with 38 C.F.R. § 17.655, ecclesiastical endorsement is a condition of employment as a VA chaplain. An individual must possess and maintain a full and active ecclesiastical endorsement to be employed as a VA chaplain. Applicants must have an ecclesiastical endorsement, dated within the past 12 months. Ecclesiastical endorsements must be from the official national endorsing authority of the applicant's/employee's faith group or denomination. Ecclesiastical endorsement is a written official statement, by the official national endorsing body of the faith group or denomination, certifying that the applicant is in good standing with the applicant's faith group or denomination; and stating that the individual is, in the opinion of the endorsing body, qualified to perform the full range of ministry required in the VA pluralistic setting. Loss of endorsement will result in removal from the GS-0060 Chaplain series and may result in termination of employment.
  • Board Certification.
    • Certification. Applicants must be a Board-Certified Chaplain certified by BCCI ® or a U.S. certifying body that has a reciprocity agreement with BCCI ®. Board Certification that requires 4 units of CPE is qualifying. Note: Provisional or Associate or other status as a candidate for board certification does not meet the board certification requirement for the FPL GS-11 or above
Grade Determinations:
  • Chaplain (Clinical Pastoral Educator), GS-12.
    • Experience. One year of creditable experience equivalent to the next lower grade.

CPE Educators must be certified by the same accrediting body as the CPE training program where the position is being filled for the CPE training program to maintain accreditation.
    • Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities (KSAs). In addition to the experience above, the candidate must demonstrate the following KSAs:
      • (a) Ability to independently educate all levels of CPE students and plan, organize, and implement all levels of the CPE program.
      • (b) Skill in adhering to all accreditation standards, processes and practices including, but not limited to, timely and professional submission of all required program reports, center portfolio, fees and dues.
      • (c) Skill in written and verbal communication that are articulate, professional and cohesive.
      • (d) Ability to recruit, interview and select students for the CPE program.
      • (e) Knowledge of professional ethics for certified educators and history of CPE.
      • (f) Ability to apply theoretical understanding for and competence in administering and conducting all levels of CPE programs.
      • (g) Knowledge of emerging trends and research in the area of pastoral education.
      • (h) Knowledge of various conceptual frameworks for developing educational curriculum.

job_name: Director Of Church And Community Partnerships
post_html:
Description

Position Summary

The Director of Church and Community Partnerships builds and stewards missional relationships that resource the youth and families served by Murphy-Harpst Children's Centers. This role carries two complementary responsibilities: cultivating congregational and pastoral partnerships across Georgia, and developing corporate and community partnerships in the Central Savannah River Area (CSRA) — together working to fund Murphy-Harpst's mission and support the Evolve program's continued growth. The ideal candidate brings pastoral credibility, an established network somewhere in the region south and east of Atlanta — Augusta, Athens, or a comparable East Georgia community — and the relational gifts to represent Murphy-Harpst's mission with warmth, conviction, and integrity.

Church & Pastoral Stewardship

• Build and steward missional partnerships with congregations, pastors, and church-affiliated foundations across Georgia, with a primary focus on the CSRA and North Georgia.

• Serve as a trusted, ordained representative of Murphy-Harpst in pulpits, church gatherings, denominational meetings, and pastoral networks, articulating the ministry's mission and needs with theological fluency.

• Develop and execute an annual church engagement strategy, including new partner identification, giving campaigns, and recurring stewardship touchpoints.

• Identify opportunities for congregations to provide volunteer support, in-kind resources, and mission trip or service-day engagement with Murphy-Harpst programs.

• Support cultivation of church-connected funding sources as Murphy-Harpst explores expansion of services to meet critical foster care needs statewide.

Corporate & Community Engagement (CSRA)

• Identify, cultivate, and steward corporate and community partners in the Augusta/CSRA market to provide funding and volunteer resources for the Evolve program.

• Coordinate volunteer engagement for Evolve, including recruiting, scheduling, and stewarding corporate and community volunteer groups.

• Represent Murphy-Harpst at CSRA civic, business, and community events to raise visibility and grow the local donor and partner base.

• Collaborate with the Director of Corporate and Community Engagement (Cedartown/Atlanta market) to maintain clear territory alignment and share best practices.

General Advancement

• Maintain accurate, timely records of partner engagement, moves management, and gift activity in the organization's CRM.

• Partner with the Advancement Services Coordinator to ensure donor communications, acknowledgments, and stewardship touchpoints for church and CSRA partners are executed with excellence.

• Represent the Advancement office in a manner consistent with Murphy-Harpst's mission, values, and centennial vision.

• Perform other duties as assigned by the Vice President of Advancement.

 



Qualifications

Qualifications

 

Ordained minister or equivalent pastoral/ministry credential strongly preferred, with demonstrated credibility among pastors and congregations.

• Established relationships within the Augusta/CSRA and/or broader East Georgia region (e.g., Athens) faith and business community strongly preferred, with the flexibility to serve congregations and partners across the area south and east of Atlanta.

• 3+ years of experience in ministry, nonprofit development, church stewardship, or a related relationship-based field.

• Comfortable and effective as a public speaker in church and community settings.

• Strong relational and written communication skills; ability to represent Murphy-Harpst with theological and professional credibility alike.

• Self-directed and comfortable with regular travel, including evenings and occasional weekends for church and community engagements.

• Familiarity with donor CRM systems (e.g., Bloomerang, Virtuous) a plus.

• Alignment with Murphy-Harpst's Christian mission and its commitment to serving children and families who have experienced trauma.

post_html:
Covenant Review, a division of CreditSights which is a Fitch Solutions company,  is currently seeking a Director, Senior Covenant Analyst based out of our New York City office.  

 

Celebrating its 26th anniversary this year, CreditSights continues to offer award-winning, unbiased research on global credit markets, empowering clients to make informed investment decisions. With offices in New York, London, Singapore, Glasgow, Denver, and Charlotte, we serve a diverse global institutional client base, including banks, investment advisors, mutual funds, and hedge funds. As a leading voice in credit research, our expert insights are featured in top publications such as Bloomberg, The Wall Street Journal, and Financial Times. As a Fitch Solutions Company, CreditSights provides a dynamic environment fostering professional growth and innovation, where you collaborate with seasoned analysts to deliver critical intelligence in complex financial markets.


Working at CreditSights offers the chance to be part of a premier independent credit research firm, renowned for its in-depth analysis and insights. You'll collaborate with a team of seasoned analysts, delivering critical intelligence that helps clients navigate complex financial markets. This dynamic environment encourages professional growth and innovation, enabling you to make a meaningful impact in the field of credit research.

 

About the Team  

Exciting opportunity to be a covenant analyst for our market leading leveraged finance intelligence team at Covenant Review, celebrating its 20th anniversary this year. The role will involve writing research that is consumed by a broad spectrum of leveraged finance market participants including hedge funds, CLOs, law firms, and sell-side financial institutions.

 

A keen eye for detail, issue spotting, transaction structuring (“Can they do it?”), transaction deconstruction (“How did they do that?”), and impeccable writing are necessary skills for this role.  The key skill set, however, is the ability to deconstruct complex issues or contract provisions and summarize them in concise but precise language that is understandable by the most junior research analyst and sophisticated enough for the most senior law firm partner.  We expect that candidates for this role have deep familiarity with the leveraged finance market preferably from the perspective of both the buyside and the sell side. 

 

The compensation for this position is competitive with in-house legal positions of similar seniority, but superior in many ways.  Our covenant analysts work fixed hours, with no late night or weekend work.  In addition, our analysts get all the benefits of working for Fitch Solutions, a leading financial information services company, while at the same time being immersed in Covenant Review’s start-up culture.

 

How You’ll Make an Impact: 

  •  Write research reports on broadly syndicated and private credit leveraged loan covenants.  Our analysts follow a name from cradle (new issuance) to grave (bankruptcy).
  • Assist with preparation of private credit portfolio analyses and data reports.
  • Write event-driven research and reports on special situations as they develop in the market.
  • Write research for our growing library of covenant primers targeted at our less sophisticated subscribers. Write market leading reports that set the conversation on new trends and market developments.
  • Engage with our subscribers as they seek clarification on our research or discuss potential transactions.
  • Work alongside colleagues at CreditSights and LevFin Insights to create powerful cross-disciplinary research.
  • Establish credibility in the market as a subject matter expert on leveraged finance.
  • Meet tight deadlines for publication.

 

You May be a Good Fit if:

  • The ideal candidate is a senior lawyer with extensive experience drafting, negotiating, and reviewing leveraged finance documentation, including credit agreements and indentures.
  • 6 years of Big Law experience in leveraged finance.
  • Deep understanding of the leveraged finance market and how covenants and financial definitions work in leveraged finance documents.
  • Solid business acumen with commercial sensibilities.
  • Experience communicating with business principals on complex leveraged finance issues.
  • Experience working on deadline.

 

EDUCATION

  • Law degree. Member in good standing of the New York Bar.

 

Why Choose Fitch: 

  • Hybrid Work Environment: 2 to 3 days a week in office required based on your line of business and location
  • A Culture of Learning & Mobility: Dedicated trainings, leadership development and mentorship programs designed to ensure that your time at Fitch will be a continuous learning opportunity
  • Investing in Your Future: Retirement planning and tuition reimbursement programs that empower you to achieve your short and long-term goals
  • Promoting Health & Wellbeing: Comprehensive healthcare offerings that enable physical, mental, financial, social, and occupational wellbeing
  • Supportive Parenting Policies: Family-friendly policies, including a generous global parental leave plan, designed to help you balance career and family life effectively
  • Inclusive Work Environment: A collaborative workplace where all voices are valued, with Employee Resource Groups that unite and empower our colleagues around the globe
  • Dedication to Giving Back: Paid volunteer days, matched funding for donations and ample opportunities to volunteer in your community

Fitch is committed to providing global securities markets with objective, timely, independent and forward-looking credit opinions. To protect Fitch’s credibility and reputation, our employees must take every precaution to avoid conflicts of interest or any appearance of a conflict of interest. Should you be successful in the recruitment process at Fitch Ratings you will be asked to declare any securities holdings and other potential conflicts prior to commencing employment. If you, or your immediate family, have any holdings that may conflict with your work responsibilities, you may be asked to divest yourself of them before beginning work.

Fitch is proud to be an Equal Opportunity and Affirmative Action Employer. We evaluate qualified applicants without regard to race, color, national origin, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability, protected veteran status, and other statuses protected by law.  

 

FOR NEW YORK ONLY: Expected base pay rates for the role will be between $225,000 and $275,000 per year. Actual salaries will be determined on an individualized basis and may vary based on factors including but not limited to education, training, experience, past performance, and other job-related factors.  Base pay is one part of Fitch’s total compensation package, which, depending on the position, may also include commission earnings, discretionary bonuses, long-term incentives, and other benefits sponsored by Fitch.

Description

The Executive Administrator to Lead Pastors is a trusted and integral part of the Lead Pastors’ team, helping carry the heart, vision, and mission of Next Level Church through exceptional administrative leadership and relational support. Reporting to Director of Resource Expansion and Lead Pastors Office, the Executive Administrator has the primary responsibility of supporting the Lead Pastors’ office by managing priorities, anticipating needs, coordinating details, and helping to turn decisions into action. This role helps remove distractions, so the Lead Pastors can focus on pastoring and leading Next Level Church and the Next Level Relational Network. This is a part-time role working 20-25hrs a week. 


Essential Functions: 

  • Support the Lead Pastors: Serve as a trusted first point of contact, manage calendars and daily priorities, coordinate meetings and appointments, prepare necessary resources, and ensure timely follow-through on decisions and commitments. 
  • Coordinate and Execute: Organize travel, guest speaker details, meetings, retreats, events, and special projects while providing Sunday and special event support, including sermon slides and presentation materials. 
  • Lead and Collaborate: Build and lead a central administrative serve team, partner with the Lead Pastors’ administrative team, coordinate with Executive Leadership Team administrators, and provide clear direction, encouragement, and relational and spiritual investment. 

Other Duties: 

  • Maintain an organized and efficient Lead Pastors’ office, including files, SharePoint, resources, expenses, and administrative systems. 
  • Anticipate and manage the practical details that keep the Lead Pastors and their office running smoothly. 
  • Attend meetings with the Lead Pastors as needed and capture key notes, decisions, and follow-up items. 
  • Support Executive Leadership Team meetings, off-sites, retreats, and special gatherings.

  • Take on additional responsibilities and projects as needed to support the Lead Pastors and the ongoing needs of Next Level Church. 
Requirements

EXPECTATIONS / SKILLS / PREREQUISITES: 

  • Exceptional interpersonal, verbal, written, and organizational skills. 
  • Professional, confident, and able to thrive in a fast-paced, multi-tasking environment. 
  • Strong judgment and leadership ability, with the confidence to make decisions when necessary. 
  • Highly organized, detail-oriented, resourceful, creative, and committed to excellence. 
  • Ability to maintain confidentiality and handle sensitive information with wisdom and discretion. 
  • Strong editing and proofreading skills with a basic understanding of budgeting and administrative processes. 
  • Ability to build relationships, lead a team, and work collaboratively across multiple departments and projects. 
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office and ability to learn new software and technology as needed. 
  • Positive, steady, people-oriented team player with a strong work ethic and heart to serve. 

TRAITS FOR SUCCESS IN CALLING:

PERFORMANCE MEASURES:

TIME COMMITMENT:

The staff member may perform other related duties requested by their supervisor or Executive Leadership Team to meet the ongoing needs of the ministry of the church.

    Director of Music Ministry


     

    St. Albert the Great Parish, North Royalton Ohio

    "This is an opportunity for a gifted Catholic musician and pastoral leader to shape and lead a substantial parish music ministry and to contribute meaningfully to the spiritual life of a vibrant evangelical Eucharistic Catholic community."

    Fr. Ed Estok, Pastor

    Position Summary

    The Director of Music Ministry provides pastoral and musical leadership for the parish's worship and music ministries, collaborating closely with the pastor, pastoral staff, Assistant Music Director, school leadership, volunteers, and Liturgical Commission.

    Our parish vision, *Called to More 2030*, identifies weekend worship as a primary opportunity for parishioners, visitors, and seekers to encounter Jesus Christ. The Director helps make that encounter possible through excellent, prayerful, and faithful sacred music ï¿½ overseeing musical preparation for weekend Masses, school liturgies, seasonal celebrations, funerals, weddings, and other major parish celebrations.

    The parish music ministry assists at weekend Masses, Friday school Mass (during the school year), and currently includes an Assistant Music Director, a Eucharistic Choir with paid section leaders and accompanist, an eight-voice Schola, a 14-member Bell Choir, a Children's Choir, and additional paid weekend cantors.

    Essential Duties & Responsibilities

    Music Ministry

    * Plan, direct, and oversee music for weekend Masses, Holy Day Masses, and other major parish liturgies, in collaboration with the pastor, staff, and Liturgical Commission.

    * Supervise and collaborate with the Assistant Music Director and accompanist; lead rehearsals and establish effective rehearsal schedules.

    * Secure additional instrumentalists and musicians when appropriate, and maintain sound quality in the worship space.

    * Coordinate musical leadership for approximately 80 funerals and 5ï¿½10 weddings annually, working with families, clergy, funeral coordinators, and couples to select music that conforms to Catholic liturgical norms and parish policy, planning for Advent, Christmas, Lent, Holy Week, the Sacred Triduum, Easter, solemnities, and major parish celebrations.

    * Direct and develop the Eucharistic Choir, Schola, Bell Choir, and Children's Choir, fostering participation and musical growth across ensembles.

    * Provide music leadership for the weekly school Mass and other special school liturgies, collaborating with school faculty and staff.

    * Recruit, train, mentor, and schedule paid and volunteer cantors, section leaders, and other music ministers.

    Liturgy & Formation

    * Serve as a member of the Liturgical Commission, contributing to the planning of parish liturgies.

    * Provide musical, liturgical, and spiritual formation for musicians, cantors, and choir members, fostering a culture of prayer, service, fraternity, excellence, and stewardship.

    * Offer opportunities for spiritual enrichment among music ministers.

    * Assist with music planning for special occasions, including First Communion, Confirmation, weddings, and funerals, in collaboration with clergy and staff.

    * Promote the full, conscious, and active participation of the assembly in the liturgy.

    Leadership & Collaboration

    * Serve as a member of the pastoral staff, contributing to the broader pastoral life of the parish.

    * Ensure liturgical and musical practices align with the General Instruction of the Roman Missal (GIRM) and diocesan guidelines.

    * Communicate effectively with clergy, staff, musicians, volunteers, families, and parishioners; serve as liaison to ensure smooth liturgical celebrations.

    * Develop and manage the annual music ministry budget; monitor expenditures and recommend purchases of music, instruments, and equipment.

    * Maintain music resources, records, schedules, and ministry information; coordinate the music calendar with the parish liturgical calendar and establish seasonal and annual planning timelines.

    Qualifications

    Required

    * Deep knowledge of Catholic liturgy, the Roman Rite, and Eucharistic theology, and a strong understanding of the theology and purpose of sacred music.

    * Demonstrated experience directing a Catholic parish music program or comparable liturgical ministry.

    * Advanced musical ability, with strong conducting, rehearsal, and ensemble leadership skills.

    * Ability to serve effectively as a cantor and/or liturgical musician.

    * Experience working with choirs, cantors, instrumentalists, and volunteers.

    * Strong organizational, administrative, interpersonal, and communication skills, including scheduling, budgeting, and volunteer coordination.

    * Compliance with diocesan ministerial requirements, including Virtus training and a public lifestyle consistent with ministry in the Catholic Church and the Diocese of Cleveland.

    * Ability to work evenings, weekends, Holy Days, and other parish events as required, with increased workload during Advent, Christmas, Lent, Holy Week, Easter, and periods with numerous funerals and weddings.
     

    Preferred

    * Bachelor's or master's degree in music, sacred music, liturgy, music education, or a related field (or equivalent professional experience).

    * Formal study or certification in Catholic liturgy or sacred music.

    * Proficiency in organ, piano, or another appropriate accompanying instrument, and choral direction.

    * Familiarity with Catholic hymnody, chant, polyphony, contemporary sacred music, and the broader Catholic sacred music tradition.

     

    Personal Qualities

    * Genuine love for the Catholic Church, the Eucharist, and the Church's liturgical life.

    * Understands music ministry as pastoral ministry, not simply musical performance, and leads the assembly toward deeper participation in the liturgy.

    * Prayerful, pastoral, and collaborative spirit, with humility, professionalism, dependability, and emotional maturity.

    * Balances musical excellence, liturgical integrity, pastoral sensitivity, and practical parish realities.

    * Passionate about evangelization through beauty, music, and liturgy.

    * Comfortable working with clergy, staff, volunteers, children, families, and parishioners of diverse musical backgrounds.
     

    Additional Remuneration to Salary

    * Stipend for musical services at funeral liturgies (approximately 80 annually).

    * Stipend for musical services at wedding liturgies (approximately 5ï¿½10 annually).

    Salary Range

    $60,000 ï¿½ $70,000, commensurate with qualifications and experience.

     

    St. Albert the Great

    6667 Wallings Rd.

    North Royalton, OH  44133

     

    Contact:  Maureen Holodnak

Description

Orchard NEO is a church planting program located in Northeast Ohio. Orchard NEO works alongside these planters to realize God’s vision for their role in this mission, training them to be as effective as possible. Work Location:

California Northern

Job Type:

Full time

God has called InterVarsity to plant and to build witnessing communities of students and faculty who follow Jesus on college and university campuses. Through these groups, we believe ever- increasing numbers of students and faculty from all ethnic groups and areas of the campus will be transformed by the Gospel. We expect to see campuses increasingly become places where people, ideas, and structures flourish to the glory of God. We confidently anticipate that our InterVarsity alumni will become change agents across the country and around the world. We pursue this calling by discerning and actively participating in what God is already doing on campus. This is the essence of being a Campus Staff Minister (CSM).

ESSENTIAL COMMITMENTS/RESPONSIBILITIES 

Spiritual Growth 

As a Campus Staff Minister, you pursue maturity as a disciple of Jesus Christ so that your life and work increasingly reflect a growing love for God, God’s Word, God’s people of every ethnicity and culture, and God’s purposes in the world. To do this, you will: 

  • Pursue a vibrant relationship with the triune God through engagement with Scripture, prayer, and worship, both individually and in community 

  • Develop self-leadership (growing in self-awareness, self-management, relational integrity, and resiliency)

  • Embrace Scriptural standards for behavior and attitudes 

 

Campus Leadership 

As a Campus Staff Minister, you increase the number of witnessing communities, as well as the size, health, spiritual maturity, and campus-wide influence of existing witnessing communities of students and faculty by being a: 

  • Visionary Guide: 

You communicate and model InterVarsity’s vision to see students and faculty transformed, campuses renewed, and world changers developed 

  • Create a culture of humble dependence on God and bold expectation in God’s intention to start new witnessing communities throughout the campus and on new campuses

  • Model – in person and through programs – InterVarsity’s vision and Core Values, including a biblically-defined commitment to engage every ethnic and social group on campus

  • Lead students and faculty – individually and collectively – through Scripture, prayer, teaching, and discipleship experiences, so that they articulate and align their ministry activities around this vision

  • Set annual goals through prayer, research and reflection with your teams (students, faculty, and staff) for qualitative and quantitative growth, including conversions and leadership development 

  • Structural Architect: 

You create, develop, align, and leverage ministry plans, programs, teams, and structures to close the gap between current reality and the aspirational goals. 

  • Build leadership teams who trust and partner well with you and who demonstrate spiritual vitality, relational health, and mission alignment

  • Develop and execute plans to achieve annual goals, evaluating and modifying the plan as needed throughout the year

  • Increase momentum for the vision by aligning programs, structures, conferences, and teams around the goals

  • Mobilize students and faculty to engage their relational networks with the gospel and to start new missional communities

  • Under the direction of the Area Director, may supervise Ministry Interns and Campus Ministry Interns as delegated 

  • Missional Developer: 

You intentionally gather, invite, and develop diverse groups of students and faculty so that they not only encounter and follow Jesus as Savior and Lord but also advance the mission on campus as participants and leaders. 

  • Create ways for faculty and students to encounter and follow Jesus through Scripture, worship, prayer, mission experiences, conferences, etc.

  • Equip students and faculty so that they think strategically about campus engagement and so that they proclaim – in word, deed, and power – the good news of Jesus, regularly inviting students and faculty to follow him as Savior and Lord

  • Disciple students and faculty by equipping them to hear the Word, respond actively, and debrief and interpret the experience so that they grow in Christlikeness, reflect our Core Values, and develop ministry skills

  • Invite, coach, and equip students and faculty to become increasingly effective participants and leaders, including starting new witnessing communities on campuses 

 

Organizational Collaboration 

As a Campus Staff Minister, you have joined a national mission. Therefore, you work with a network of other local, area, regional, and national InterVarsity staff and volunteers so that our work reflects Biblical standards of excellence, integrity, and partnership. 

  • Partner with and respond positively to the direction and coaching of your supervisors and national leaders

  • Contribute to collaborative and productive team meetings and relationships

  • Affiliate chapters under your care and submit Graduating Student Forms in order to increase our partnership with current students and alumni

  • Use national ministry resources and tools, as requested, including recruiting and/or participating in local, regional, or national conferences as

  • Complete reporting, planning and review requirements in a timely way so that you and your supervisors can assess and improve your work as a CSM

  • Comply with all InterVarsity policies and procedures 

 

Ministry Partnership Development 

As a Campus Staff Minister, you will develop a team of partners – churches and individuals (including alumni and community members) – who will resource the ministry financially, in prayer, or volunteer service that advances the mission. 

  • Raise 100% of the financial budget assigned by your supervisor

  • Communicate regularly with your ministry partners, nurturing the relationship through visits, phone calls, emails and regular prayer letters

  • Develop on-going, long-lasting partnership with alumni and volunteers

  • Comply with all Ministry Partnership Policies

  • Identify and invest in advocates who will build networks of volunteers and donors on InterVarsity’s behalf 

 

Accomplish all other assigned tasks as appropriate 

 

QUALIFICATIONS (common to all levels of CSM) 

  • Annually affirm InterVarsity’s Statement of Agreement (Doctrinal Basis and Purpose Statement). Abide by InterVarsity’s Code of Conduct. Believe and behave consonantly with InterVarsity’s Human Sexuality Theological Paper. Affirm and behave consonantly with InterVarsity’s “Women in Ministry Statement of Affirmation”

  • Bachelor’s degree for CSMs assigned to a four-year campus. A minimum of an Associate’s degree for CSMs assigned to a two-year campus or a community college

  • Strong interpersonal skills (including ability to minister to diverse ethnic communities and faculty)

  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills

  • Demonstrated problem solving skills

  • Familiarity with word processing, presentation, email, and spreadsheet software 

 

WORK ENVIRONMENT/PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS 

The CSM position leads ministry in a college campus environment. A designated office space may or may not be available. The CSM is required to travel to on-campus and off- campus sites as appropriate. Off-campus travel includes, but is not limited to: student ministry conferences, Ministry Partnership Development meetings, and InterVarsity- sponsored training sessions, meetings, and conferences. The CSM is regularly required to communicate with others, and routinely uses standard office equipment such as computers, phones, photocopiers, filing cabinets, etc.

Worship & Connections Pastor

Paradise Alliance Church, Paradise, CA

Full-Time Job Description

We exist to Know Jesus, Grow Together, and Bring Hope

The Worship & Connections Pastor helps foster a Christ-centered Sunday morning environment where people are welcomed, connected, discipled, and led into worship of Jesus Christ. This role provides leadership for worship ministries, volunteer teams, and guest connections while helping cultivate a healthy, authentic, and gospel-centered church culture.

Qualifications

  • Demonstrates a clear testimony of faith in Jesus Christ and ongoing spiritual maturity.
  • Can clearly identify the gifting of the Holy Spirit toward ministry leadership.
  • Lives consistently with the biblical qualifications for church leadership outlined in 1 Timothy 3 and Titus 1.
  • Bachelor of Arts and/or other equivalent training and education.
  • Willing and able to work towards licensing and ordination with the C&MA denomination.
  • We are seeking a leader who is humble, teachable, relational, emotionally healthy, and passionate about building teams that serve with authenticity and excellence.

Responsibilities

  • Be a part of and contribute to a healthy, creative, and Spirit-led Pastoral staff.
  • Works collaboratively with the Lead Pastor, elders, and staff while supporting the vision and direction of Paradise Alliance Church.
  • Able to:
    • Lead our church in Christ-centered worship that aligns with the teaching and mission of PAC.
    • Recruit, equip, and delegate volunteer teams in worship, production, hospitality, and guest connections through an encouraging and servant-hearted style of leadership.
    • Understand the culture of the community and develop effective ways to reach people with the Gospel of Christ, and encourage spiritual growth.
    • Provide oversight and development for worship and production ministries including music, audio, visual, livestream, and service coordination teams.
  • Plan with the Pastoral staff for Holiday services and special events.
  • Help shape a welcoming and Christ-centered Sunday morning culture where every environment, from the parking lot to the auditorium, helps people feel encouraged, connected, and pointed toward Jesus through trained and servant-hearted volunteer teams. This includes hospitality, greeters, lobby environment, worship service coordination, and helping attenders connect into the life and ministries of the church.
  • You are flexible and collaborative with the needs of the church and community by performing other duties as assigned.

We are seeking a leader who values worship, discipleship, teamwork, authenticity, and shepherding people toward deeper faith in Christ.

To be considered for this position, please complete the application to include your testimony, resume and other background information related to the position.

If the district office has reviewed your application and they think you may be a potential match for the position, that the hiring manager will reach out to you for next steps.

This position may require licensing with The Christian & Missionary Alliance. To learn more about The Alliance and requirements for licensing, please visit our website

Please do not contact the church directly.

Area Ministry Director — North Florida (Undergraduate Ministry)

Work Location:

Florida

Job Type:

Full time

An Area Director leads and oversees a ministry team to plant and to grow witnessing communities of students and faculty who follow Jesus on college and university campuses. Through these groups, we believe ever-increasing numbers of students and faculty from all ethnic groups and areas of the campus will be transformed by the gospel. We expect to see campuses increasingly become places where people, ideas, and structures flourish for the common good and to the glory of God. We confidently anticipate that our InterVarsity alumni will be growing disciples and change agents across the country and around the world.

The North Florida Area is currently comprised of campus work in the cities of Tallahassee, Jacksonville, and Gainesville, with two Campus Staff Ministers and three Campus Ministry Interns. With a strong emphasis on prayer and Scripture engagement, the team works together to host events together for students, alums, and ministry partnership development. They have a strong team culture of collaboration and trust, prayer and worship, and student discipleship. For the past several years, the North Florida Area has hosted a summer student internship program which has helped to both guide and prepare prospective staff for the Field.

We are looking for an Area Director who can support and resource the work of the city teams in Tallahassee and Gainesville, while also growing the work in Jacksonville and planting new witnessing communities on multiple rural community college campuses. 

Fall Hiring Window

  • Application is due by 08/30/2026
  • References should be received by 09/08/2026
  • An interview will be scheduled for 09/13/2026, 10am-4pm, location TBA 
  • Offer or Declination to follow within one week of the interview

ESSENTIAL COMMITMENTS/RESPONSIBILITIES

1. Spiritual Growth

The Area Ministry Director models spiritual maturity as a disciple of Jesus Christ so that your life and work increasingly reflects a growing love for God, God’s Word, God’s people of every ethnicity and culture, and God’s purposes in the world.

  • Pursue a vibrant relationship with the triune God through engagement with Scripture, prayer, and worship, both individually and in community
  • Exercise self-leadership (growing in self-awareness, self-management, relational integrity, and resiliency)
  • Embrace and practice Scriptural standards for behavior and attitudes, including those described in the Code of Conduct

​2. Campus Ministry Leadership

As an Area Director, you inspire, coach and develop campus staff ministers (“ministers”), students, faculty, and ministry partners to increase the number of witnessing communities, as well as the size, health, spiritual maturity, and campus-wide influence of existing witnessing communities by being a:

Visionary Guide:

  • Create a culture of dependence on God to gain vision for establishing and advancing witnessing communities that reach every corner of every campus in your area
  • Model InterVarsity’s vision and Core Values for supervisees
  • Lead staff, students, and faculty through Scripture, prayer, teaching and discipleship experiences in a way that motivates and shapes their ministry around vision
  • Set appropriate annual goals through prayer, research and reflection with your teams

Structural Architect:

  • Lead your team to develop and implement plans to achieve ministry goals
  • Adapt the plan as needed through rhythms of action, reflection and evaluation
  • Develop, align and leverage programs and structures to move the mission forward

Missional Developer:

  • Recruit a diversity of qualified minister candidates
  • Develop ministers to spiritually grow in Christ in intimacy, like Christ in character, and with Christ in his mission to current and new campuses
  • Develop ministers professionally so that they are consistently increasing their gifts and skills as ministry leaders
  • Supervise ministers, using appropriate leadership style for the individual and situation, to help them accomplish assigned tasks. This will require coaching, assessing, correcting and affirming job-related behaviors
  • Proactively establish and develop healthy relationships across racial, ethnic, national background, and gender barriers with staff, students, faculty, and ministry partners to build effective and diverse communities
  • Build an effective minister team that collaborates well and accomplishes goals

3. Organizational Collaboration

As an Area Director, you are part of a national organization and work in partnership with local, area, divisional, regional, and national InterVarsity ministers and volunteers.

  • Participate in regional leadership as determined by the Regional Director, to set ministry vision and strategies, contribute to accomplishing plans, and provide regional leadership in specific areas
  • Positively and constructively respond to the direction and coaching of line supervisors
  • Build productive ministry partnerships with regional and national collaborative leaders
  • Establish systems, processes and protocols to fulfill regular operational and administrative tasks in a timely manner (reporting, finances, human resources, etc.)
  • Maintain sound financial status of the area through management of budgeting, expense control and ministry partnership development
  • Become familiar with and comply with all InterVarsity policies and procedures

4. Ministry Partnership Development (MPD)

As an Area Director, you will develop a team of partners who will resource the ministry financially, in prayer, or with volunteer service that advances the mission.

  • Develop and maintain a ministry among partners who will fund InterVarsity
  • Ensure ministry budget is fully funded
  • Supervise each minister’s MPD (collaborating with coaches when applicable) and equip staff to build ministry partners
  • Build resource networks with alumni, volunteers, churches, advocacy councils, and major donors, in particular to fund low-network ministers
  • Communicate regularly with ministry partners

5. Accomplish all other assigned tasks as appropriate

QUALIFICATIONS

post_html:
The NextGen Pastor will lead and develop a comprehensive strategy for discipling the next generation—from kids to students to families—within the life of the church. This role is responsible for building a healthy, growing ministry that reaches unchurched families, strengthens biblical foundations, and creates clear pathways for spiritual growth. The ideal candidate is a visionary leader who can think strategically, execute effectively, and build teams that foster both numerical growth and deep discipleship, all while aligning with the church’s mission, theology, and culture. Provide vision, leadership, and execution for a thriving NextGen ministry (kids, students, families) that drives discipleship, engagement, and measurable growth. Build intentional pathways to reach unchurched students and families, creating environments where they connect, belong, and grow in their faith. Collaborate with pastoral, ministry and staff leaders to align Next Gen strategy with the overall mission of creating disciples and hitting growth goals of the church.



Why We Love This Opportunity

What draws me to this opportunity is the chance to build something that is both deeply rooted and genuinely impactful. I’m energized by the combination of strong biblical conviction, clear structure, and a culture that values real community—because that’s the kind of environment where lasting discipleship actually happens. The vision for reaching kids, students, and families isn’t just about maintaining programs, but about creating intentional pathways for growth and connection, and that aligns closely with how I’m wired as a leader.

I also love the opportunity to serve in a church that has a wide cultural range—where “suits and flip flops” can coexist—and where people are welcomed as they are while being challenged to grow. The stability of a congregational, committee-supported structure combined with a relational, Southern culture creates a unique platform to build something that lasts. Add to that the setting of Fernandina Beach—a place where families are putting down roots and community still matters—and it feels like a place where I could invest deeply, lead strategically, and see long-term fruit in the lives of the next generation.

A great match for this position would be:

A great match for this position is a leader who is both strategic and steady, able to build a thriving NextGen ministry while honoring the church’s convictional and relational culture. They are theologically aligned and culturally comfortable in a traditional Southern Baptist context, leading with clarity and confidence without constantly pushing against established values. They are a builder of people and systems, capable of creating clear discipleship pathways while recruiting, developing, and empowering volunteers. They lead through relational influence, not ego, earning trust with staff, families, and lay leaders over time while keeping the mission front and center.

  • Theologically aligned with Baptist Faith & Message (2000) and complementarian in conviction
  • Comfortable in a traditional, Southern, and politically conservative cultural context
  • Proven ability to build and grow kids, student, and family ministries with measurable impact
  • Strong recruiter and developer of volunteer leaders and teams
  • Strategic thinker who can create clear discipleship pathways, not just run programs
  • Relational leader who builds trust and leads through influence within a structured environment
  • Team player who collaborates well with staff and works within congregational and committee systems
  • Committed to long-term ministry, valuing consistency, stability, and lasting fruit over quick wins



About This Organization

Located along the scenic coastline of Fernandina Beach, Florida, First Baptist Church Fernandina Beach (FBFirst) is a growing, multi-campus church rooted in a long-standing presence in the North Florida community while continuing to expand its reach today. With its Island Campus just minutes from the beach and a second campus in Central Nassau, the church is strategically positioned to serve both coastal residents and surrounding inland communities. 

Grounded in a mission to “glorify God by…making and equipping disciples,” FBFirst blends a rich history of faithful ministry with a forward-looking vision, engaging people of all ages through worship, discipleship, and community outreach. As it continues to grow, the church is focused on reaching families, students, and individuals across the region—locally and beyond—by fostering a culture of connection, spiritual formation, and gospel-centered impact.


Location

Fernandina Beach sits on the northern end of Amelia Island along Florida’s Atlantic coast, blending a laid-back beach lifestyle with the feel of a historic Southern town. The area is known for its 13 miles of beaches, walkable historic downtown, and slower pace of life that attracts both young families and retirees. Demographically, the community leans older, established, and family-oriented, with a strong percentage of homeowners, veterans, and long-term residents. The population is generally affluent and highly educated, with median household incomes near six figures and over half of adults holding a bachelor’s degree or higher. The culture of the area carries a distinct North Florida/South Georgia tone—conservative, community-minded, and relational. Nassau County schools are regarded as strong compared to much of Florida, making the area attractive for families seeking both quality education and a safe coastal environment. While Fernandina Beach offers a high quality of life, the popularity of Amelia Island has driven housing costs upward in recent years, especially near the beach and historic district, though it remains more affordable than many larger coastal markets in Florida. Residents enjoy a unique combination of small-town familiarity, coastal recreation, Southern hospitality, and proximity to Jacksonville, giving the community both charm and accessibility.


Staff Culture

A relational, high-trust, and conviction-driven staff culture that moves with urgency, executes with excellence, and values long-term alignment and faithfulness as much as strong relationships and meaningful collaboration.

 

Key Characteristics:

  • Aligned around clear theological conviction and shared ministry philosophy
  • Collaborative within a structured, committee-informed environment
  • Relational, low-ego team dynamic that values trust and loyalty
  • Emphasis on faithfulness, consistency, and long-term ministry impact
  • Leadership driven by influence, trust-building, and relational credibility
  • Clear ownership of roles with alignment to the overall mission

 

A team member will thrive on staff as someone who:

  • Values team over platform
  • Can navigate structure without frustration
  • Builds trust naturally with both staff and lay leaders
  • Is secure enough not to need constant spotlight
  • Plays the long game in ministry


Key Responsibilities

  • Communication of biblical messages for the purpose of making disciples of Christ in alignment with Baptist Faith and Message.
  • Develop and execute a clear, scalable strategy for Next Gen ministry growth, including attendance, volunteer pipeline, and discipleship pathways. 
  • Create systems that increase student and family engagement, retention, and first-time guest follow-up. 
  • Equip leaders and communicate effectively in large and small group environments, delivering engaging, relevant, and biblically sound teaching. 
  • Coach, train, mentor and empower those in the pastoral calling pipeline.
  • Accountable for tracking clear metrics (attendance, salvations, baptisms, volunteer growth, small group participation). 
  • Cast vision that mobilizes students, parents, and volunteers toward active participation and ownership. 
  • Own the full Next Gen ministry calendar, ensuring high-quality, well-executed weekly services, events, and environments. 
  • Design and lead impactful experiences (camps, retreats, outreach events) that drive spiritual growth and connection while creating more disciples. 
  • Build, train, and multiply a strong volunteer leadership team with clear roles, expectations, and accountability. 
  • Manage ministry budget with a focus on stewardship, impact, and growth initiatives. 
  • Select and implement relevant, engaging curriculum that connects families. 
  • Partner cross-functionally to create dynamic worship tailored to students. 
  • Collaborate across ministries to integrate students into broader church community. 
  • Build strong relationships with students and parents, provide leadership, care, and consistent communication. 
  • Actively contribute to staff culture, leadership alignment, and initiatives. 
  • Drive discipleship, innovation and continuous improvement within the Next Gen ministry. 


Key Qualifications

  • Demonstrates a vital, growing relationship with Jesus Christ and alignment with biblical leadership standards. 
  • Doctrinal, methodological, and philosophical alignment with Baptist Faith & Message, as well as Pastoral leadership.
  • Meets biblical qualifications of Church leadership (1 Timothy 3:1-13). 
  • Passion for reaching and discipling the next generation in a rapidly changing culture. 
  • Commitment to the mission, vision, and worship philosophy of FB First. 
  • Maintain healthy leadership of own family, leading them to engage in the larger ministry of the Church.
  • Proven ability to lead, grow, and scale teams and ministries. 
  • Strong relational intelligence with students, parents, and volunteers across diverse backgrounds. 
  • Ability to engage and lead across multiple generations and demographics. 
  • High ownership mindset with strong execution and follow-through. 
  • Comfortable leveraging technology, social media, and modern tools to reach and engage students. 
  • Strong planning and execution of events, services, and ministry environments.


For more information, please contact Phil Christian, Executive Recruiter, at pchristian@slingshotgroup.org

About 9fin

9fin is the AI platform powering global debt markets — the world’s largest asset class at over $145 trillion.

Debt markets are vast, global, and mission-critical, yet still run on fragmented data, PDFs, and manual workflows. 9fin replaces this broken infrastructure with a single platform that centralises proprietary credit data, deep analysis, and high-value workflows across global markets.

Today, 9fin powers teams at 300+ blue-chip institutions worldwide, including global banks, asset managers, private equity firms, law firms, and advisors. The business is scaling at exceptional speed, with rapid expansion in the US and best-in-class retention driven by deep workflow adoption.

We’re at a defining inflection point. With proven product-market fit and strong, global market pull, 9fin is accelerating toward becoming the category-defining platform for debt markets worldwide.

The Opportunity

9fin is looking for a corporate finance attorney who geeks out about a good credit agreement or indenture and who has broader ambitions to write and be a thought-leader in the industry they love. This role will help our distressed editorial teams understand all the nuances of interesting bond and loan documents that could factor into restructuring and liability management exercises. It is perfect for an experienced finance attorney who is looking to recalibrate their work-life balance to allow for a little more life, but who loves their work. We’re growing our groundbreaking coverage of complex out-of-court restructurings with an emphasis on distressed coverage. The role will report into our New York office with flexibility to work from home / remotely as needed.

This role offers a unique opportunity for a legal professional to use their expertise within a rapidly growing start-up environment, with opportunities to refine an already valuable skillset while learning all of the new skills that comes with working with technologists, credit analysts and journalists.

What you'll work on

Every day is different, but here’s an example of the kind of things you’ll work on:

  • Reviewing leveraged finance and high yield documentation to produce commercially focused and insightful analysis on distressed scenarios and the primary market

  • Writing topical reports on secondary situations, collaborating closely across 9fin’s team of lawyers and credit analysts

  • Answering client questions about the covenant packages of specific borrowers and issuers

  • Using 9fin’s proprietary technology to build and expand our restructuring and LME databases

  • Delivering seminars, teach-ins and podcast segments as a subject matter expert

  • Representing 9fin in the press and at industry conferences and events

About You

This role will be a great fit if you have the following:

  • JD with 5+ years of experience within a capital solutions, leveraged finance, capital markets, restructuring and/or special situations team at a top-tier law firm

  • Experience drafting, reviewing and negotiating high yield bond and/or leveraged loan documents, restructuring support agreements, and Chapter 11 documentation

  • Keen commercial awareness of leveraged finance and restructuring markets

  • Strong technical understanding of how leveraged finance covenants and definitions operate

  • Existing network of relationships within the leveraged finance community

  • Excellent relationship building skills

  • Effective written and verbal communication skills, able to explain complex covenant concepts to non-lawyers concisely

  • Ability to work both independently and collaboratively

 

Our benefits

We’re a scaling start up and we enjoy sharing our success, when the company succeeds, we always reinvest that in our people. We also offer huge amounts of responsibility, an abundance of opportunity for growth and a platform to truly excel.

Financial & Insurance

  • Competitive Salary: $256,000-$340,000

  • Equity Options

  • 401(k) (9fin pay 3%, employee contributions are uncapped)

  • Private Health Insurance, with Dental and Vision

  • Paid sick leave

  • Disability Insurance (New York)

  • Commuter Benefit

Time off

  • 25 vacation days per year

  • Local public holiday

  • Work abroad for up to 3 months a year

  • 1 month paid sabbatical after 5 years of service

  • Enhanced parental leave & flexible working arrangements available

Training & Culture

  • Professional learning and development budget

  • Bi-annual team socials

  • Summer and Winter company social events

Hybrid Policy

9fin is a hybrid company, and the office is a regular part of how we work. From January 2027, all employees will work from their designated 9fin office on Tuesdays and Wednesdays. Some teams may be asked to be in the office more often, where the nature of their work calls for it. For the rest of the week, you may work from wherever works best for you and your team. Your Talent Partner will share hybrid working details for this role.

9fin is an equal opportunities employer

At 9fin we are dedicated to building and promoting a fair and inclusive workplace where everyone can reach their full potential and truly belong. We recognize that building diverse teams enables a more creative and productive environment. If you’re excited about this role but your experience doesn’t perfectly align with the job description, we encourage you to apply anyway. You might just be who we’re looking for — either for this role, or perhaps another.
