Campus Staff Minister - WI - UW Madison (Undergraduate Ministry)

Work Location:

Wisconsin

Job Type:

Part time

God has called InterVarsity to plant and to build witnessing communities of students and faculty who follow Jesus on college and university campuses. Through these groups, we believe ever- increasing numbers of students and faculty from all ethnic groups and areas of the campus will be transformed by the Gospel. We expect to see campuses increasingly become places where people, ideas, and structures flourish to the glory of God. We confidently anticipate that our InterVarsity alumni will become change agents across the country and around the world. We pursue this calling by discerning and actively participating in what God is already doing on campus. This is the essence of being a Campus Staff Minister (CSM).

ESSENTIAL COMMITMENTS/RESPONSIBILITIES 

Spiritual Growth 

You pursue maturity as a disciple of Jesus Christ so that your life and work increasingly reflects a growing love for God, God’s Word, God’s people of every ethnicity and culture, and God’s purposes in the world. To do this, you will: 

  • Pursue a vibrant relationship with the triune God through engagement with Scripture, prayer, and worship, both individually and in community 

  • Develop self-leadership (growing in self-awareness, self-management, relational integrity, and resiliency) 

  • Embrace Scriptural standards for behavior and attitudes 

 

Campus Leadership 

You communicate and model InterVarsity’s vision to see students and faculty transformed, campuses renewed and world changers developed 

  • Create a culture of humble dependence on God and bold expectation in God’s intention to start new witnessing communities throughout the campus and on new campuses 

  • Model – in person and through programs – InterVarsity’s vision and Core Values, including a biblically-defined commitment to engage every ethnic and social group on campus 

  • Lead students and faculty – individually and collectively – through Scripture, prayer, teaching, and discipleship experiences, so that they articulate and align their ministry activities around this vision 

  • Set annual goals through prayer, research and reflection with your teams (students, faculty, and staff) for qualitative and quantitative growth, including conversions and leadership development 

 

You create, develop, align and leverage ministry plans, programs, teams, and structures to close the gap between current reality and the aspirational goals. 

  • Build leadership teams who trust and partner well with you and who demonstrate spiritual vitality, relational health, and mission alignment 

  • Develop and execute plans to achieve annual goals, evaluating and modifying the plan as needed throughout the year 

  • Increase momentum for the vision by aligning programs, structures, conferences and teams around the goals 

  • Mobilize students and faculty to engage their relational networks with the gospel and to start new missional communities 

  • Under the direction of the Area Director, may supervise Ministry Interns and Campus Ministry Interns as delegated 

 

You intentionally gather, invite, and develop diverse groups of students and faculty so that they not only encounter and follow Jesus as Savior and Lord but also advance the mission on campus as participants and leaders. 

  • Create ways for faculty and students to encounter and follow Jesus through Scripture, worship, prayer, mission experiences, conferences, etc. 

  • Equip students and faculty so that they think strategically about campus engagement and so that they proclaim – in word, deed, and power – the good news of Jesus, regularly inviting students and faculty to follow him as Savior and Lord 

  • Disciple students and faculty by equipping them to hear the Word, respond actively, and debrief and interpret the experience so that they grow in Christlikeness, reflect our Core Values, and develop ministry skills 

  • Invite, coach, and equip students and faculty to become increasingly effective participants and leaders, including starting new witnessing communities on campuses 

 

Organizational Collaboration 

You work with a network of other local, area, regional, and national InterVarsity staff and volunteers so that our work reflects Biblical standards of excellence, integrity, and partnership. 

  • Partner with and respond positively to the direction and coaching of your supervisors and national leaders 

  • Contribute to collaborative and productive team meetings and relationships 

  • Affiliate chapters under your care and submit Graduating Student Forms in order to increase our partnership with current students and alumni 

  • Use national ministry resources and tools, as requested, including recruiting and/or participating in local, regional, or national conferences as  

  • Complete reporting, planning and review requirements in a timely way so that you and your supervisors can assess and improve your work as a CSM 

  • Comply with all InterVarsity policies and procedures 

 

Ministry Partnership Development 

You will develop a team of partners – churches and individuals (including alumni and community members) – who will resource the ministry financially, in prayer, or volunteer service that advances the mission. 

  • Raise 100% of the financial budget assigned by your supervisor 

  • Communicate regularly with your ministry partners, nurturing the relationship through visits, phone calls, emails and regular prayer letters 

  • Develop on-going, long-lasting partnership with alumni and volunteers 

  • Comply with all Ministry Partnership Policies 

  • Identify and invest in advocates who will build networks of volunteers and donors on InterVarsity’s behalf 

 

Accomplish all other assigned tasks as appropriate 

 

QUALIFICATIONS (common to all levels of CSM) 

  • Annually affirm InterVarsity’s Statement of Agreement (Doctrinal Basis and Purpose Statement). Abide by InterVarsity’s Code of Conduct. Believe and behave consonantly with InterVarsity’s Human Sexuality Theological Paper. Affirm and behave consonantly with InterVarsity’s “Women in Ministry Statement of Affirmation” 

  • Bachelor’s degree for CSMs assigned to a four-year campus. A minimum of an Associate’s degree for CSMs assigned to a two-year campus or a community college 

  • Strong interpersonal skills (including ability to minister to diverse ethnic communities and faculty) 

  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills 

  • Demonstrated problem solving skills 

  • Familiarity with word processing, presentation, email, and spreadsheet software 

 

WORK ENVIRONMENT/PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS

Job Title: Faculty in Church History/Wesley Studies

Reporting Relationship: Dean of the Faculty

Unit: Wesley Seminary

Department: Ministry & Divinity-Wesley Seminary

Campus Location: NGM Building, Marion, IN

Summary of Position:    Wesley Seminary at Indiana Wesleyan University, a leading evangelical seminary in the Wesleyan-Holiness tradition and the official seminary of The Wesleyan Church, seeks a passionate and innovative faculty member for a full-time position in Church History and Wesley Studies to begin July 1, 2027. We are looking for a dynamic and versatile scholar-practitioner who resonates deeply with our mission to equip Christian leaders for missional ministry locally and globally.

Please prepare a cover letter, a one-page statement summarizing your philosophy of seminary education within the Wesleyan tradition, and a curriculum vitae (including education; relevant teaching, ministry, and volunteer experience; scholarship and publications; and references). All materials should be submitted electronically via Indiana Wesleyan University’s employment portal. Shortlisted candidates may be invited to submit additional written materials before a virtual or on-campus interview. The preliminary application deadline is December 1, 2026; the position will remain open until filled.


Duties and Responsibilities

  • A teaching load of 21 credit hours per 12-month contract period 
  • Oversight of relevant courses within the faculty member’s academic discipline; development of additional course offerings within the discipline and related subject areas 
  • Contribution to program assessment and review processes 
  • Relevant institutional committee work and service and relevant scholarly activity 
  • This position requires relocation to the region and regular presence on IWU’s campus in Marion, Indiana

Qualifications: According to Indiana Wesleyan University employment policy all employees must possess a strong Christian commitment and adhere to the standards outlined in the IWU Community Lifestyle Statement.

Education

  • PhD, ThD, or equivalent terminal degree in a Church History discipline (e.g., Church History, Wesley Studies, Holiness Studies, or Historical Theology) or a closely related field from an accredited institution

Experience

  • Demonstrated ability to teach effectively, especially online, at the graduate level, with a student-centered approach
  • A deep commitment to and heart for the local church and training pastors and Christian leaders for ministry
  • Enthusiastic embrace of the Wesleyan tradition and the ability to function well within a learning community hosted by The Wesleyan Church

Required Skills

  • Excellent interpersonal and communication skills; demonstrated ability to work effectively with colleagues and students from diverse communities and cultures
  • Facility with educational technologies such as the Microsoft Office suite (Outlook, PowerPoint, Word, Excel), online learning management systems, and other supplemental tools (e.g., audio and/or video recording)

IWU Kingdom Diversity Statement

IWU, in covenant with God's reconciling work and in accordance with the Biblical principles of our historic Wesleyan tradition, commits to build a community that reflects Kingdom diversity.  We will foster an intentional environment for living, teaching and learning, which exhibits honor, respect, and dignity.  Acknowledging visible or invisible differences, our community authentically values each member's earthly and eternal worth.  We refute ignorance and isolation and embrace deliberate and courageous engagement that exhibits Christ's commandment to love all humankind.

LIMITATIONS AND DISCLAIMER

As a religious educational institution operating under the auspices of The Wesleyan Church, Indiana Wesleyan University is permitted and reserves the right to prefer employees on the basis of religion (42 U.S.C., Sections 2000e-1 and 2000e-2).

The above job description is meant to describe the general nature and level of work being performed; it is not intended to be construed as an exhaustive list of all responsibilities, duties and skills required for the position. Employees will be required to follow other job-related instructions and to perform other job-related duties requested by their supervisor in compliance with Federal and State Laws.

Full-time
Description

SUMMARY


The Youth Ministry Coordinator is responsible for coordinating and implementing parish youth ministry for junior and senior high school students. This includes fostering faith formation, community building, service opportunities, and leadership development, while engaging youth and their families in parish life. The Coordinator collaborates with the Parish Catechetical Leader, Pastor, and parish staff to ensure alignment with overall faith formation efforts and diocesan standards.


The Diocese of Orlando four core values lay the foundation for the work performed by its employees.

  1. Authenticity: Conviction that God has called us to reflect exteriorly our inner life of faith in our daily living.
  2. Respect: Affirming each person’s God-given dignity and uniqueness.
  3. Courage: Inspired by this gift of the Holy Spirit, we proclaim and live the Word of God fearlessly and devotedly.
  4. Commitment: Individually and collectively, we are steadfast to the team and its purpose.


ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES


The duties and functions outlined herein are representative of the types of tasks performed within this classification. They are not listed in any order of importance. The omission of specific duties or functions does not exclude them from the classification if the work is similar, related, or a logical assignment for this role. Other duties may be required and assigned.


Program Development and Relationships

  • Assists in developing and sustaining a youth ministry advisory group composed of youth and adults. 
  • Assists in the development and implementation of a parish youth ministry plan in collaboration with the Pastor, Parish Catechetical Leader, and parish staff. 
  • Facilitates leadership development opportunities for youth and adult volunteers. 
  • Assists in the preparation of liturgical celebrations for youth, including reconciliation services, confirmation, retreats, and special events. 
  • Provides pastoral presence through listening, advising, and referral as appropriate. 
  • Coordinates retreats and reflection opportunities by developing and supporting retreat teams. 
  • Builds relationships with parents to foster open communication and engagement in youth ministry. 
  • Develops and implements age-appropriate catechetical programming in alignment with diocesan standards. 
  • Provides opportunities for service and justice education, promoting Catholic social teaching. 
  • Supports youth in discerning and utilizing their gifts within parish ministry. 
  • Collaborates with the Parish Catechetical Leader to align youth ministry with broader faith formation efforts. 
  • Develops peer ministry opportunities to support retreats, service projects, and prayer experiences.


Recruitment and Training

  • Recruits, trains, assigns, and supports youth ministry volunteers and leaders. 
  • Coordinates participation in diocesan-sponsored training and formation opportunities. 
  • Provides ongoing guidance, evaluation, and support to volunteer leaders. 
  • Defines roles and responsibilities for adult leaders and advisors. 
  • Ensures compliance with diocesan Safe Environment policies and requirements. 
  • Promotes continuing education and formation opportunities for volunteers through diocesan and external programs. 
  • Encourages participation and support from parents and the broader parish community.


Administration

  • Assesses the needs, interests, and engagement of youth to inform program development. 
  • Plans, organizes, and implements youth ministry programs and experiences. 
  • Assists in the preparation and administration of the ministry budget. 
  • Maintains accurate program records, reports, and documentation. 
  • Coordinates communication and promotion of youth ministry activities. 
  • Provides periodic updates and reports to the Pastor and parish leadership. 
  • Assists in evaluating the effectiveness of youth ministry programs. 


Communication

  • Collaborates with the Parish Catechetical Leader and parish staff in planning and implementing ministry initiatives.
  • Participates in parish staff meetings and keeps leadership informed of youth ministry activities.
  • Communicates youth ministry programs and goals to the parish community.
  • Maintains relationships with diocesan offices, deanery groups, and other parish ministries.
  • Coordinates scheduling of youth ministry events and activities.
  • Encourages parent involvement and maintains regular communication with families.
  • Stays informed on youth ministry trends through ongoing learning and professional engagement.
  • Connects with community resources that support youth and families.
  • Assists in setting and monitoring annual goals for youth ministry programs.


Professional and Personal Development

  • Participates in retreats and engages in ongoing spiritual development. 
  • Actively participates in deanery and diocesan formation opportunities. 
  • Maintains progress in diocesan catechetical certification. 
  • Attends diocesan, regional, and national training opportunities. 
  • Seeks continued professional and ministerial development.
Requirements

QUALIFICATIONS


To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily. The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skill, and/or ability required. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.


CATHOLIC FAITH


Practice of the Catholic faith is required. Church employees must conduct themselves in a manner that is consistent with and supportive of the mission and purpose of the Church. Their public behavior must not violate the faith, morals or laws of the Church or the policies of the diocese.


EDUCATION and/or EXPERIENCE

  • Bachelor’s degree in Theology, Catechetics, Religious Studies, Pastoral Ministry, Youth Ministry, or related field, or equivalent combination of education and experience. 
  • Minimum of three (3) years of experience in parish ministry or related field. 
  • Must have or be in the process of obtaining diocesan catechetical certification.


OTHER SKILLS and ABILITIES

  • Strong communication, organizational, problem-solving, and analytical skills. 
  • Knowledge of Catholic doctrine and beliefs as presented in the documents of the Second Vatican Council, the Catechism of the Catholic Church, and other relevant ecclesial documents and publications. 
  • Ability to work effectively with a diverse range of individuals across all organizational levels. 
  • Ability to effectively engage and minister to adolescents in a faith-based environment. 
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite, including Word, Excel, Outlook, and Publisher. 
  • Valid Florida driver’s license required, with an acceptable driving record.


WORKING ENVIRONMENT:


Work is performed primarily in an office setting. This position may require a flexible schedule, including evenings and weekends, and may involve extended computer use.


PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS


Tasks require the ability to perform light physical work, which may include lifting, carrying, pushing, and/or pulling objects and materials up to 15 pounds. Work may involve extended periods at a computer or workstation.

A review of this position has excluded the marginal functions of the position that are incidental to the performance of fundamental job duties. All duties and responsibilities are essential job functions and requirements are subject to possible modifications to reasonably accommodate individuals with disabilities. To perform this job successfully, the incumbent(s) will possess the abilities and aptitudes to perform each duty proficiently. Requirements are representative of the minimum level of knowledge, skills, and ability.

Description

Mission: 

 

Create environments where middle school and high school students can learn about who God is, explore what life looks like with Him, and become disciple-makers while equipping volunteers to love, teach, and serve those students well. 

 

 

*This role is full-time, 40 hours a week.


 

What will be expected of you:

 

  • Help maintain the mission and vision of Canyon Ridge across the student ministry.
  • Provide collaborative leadership to the student ministry by investing in students and volunteers.
  • Provide a summer camp experience for middle and high school students in partnership with the Student Team and Family Pastor.
  • Manage the middle and high school ministry budget areas with the fellow Student Pastor.
  • Establish decision making roles during events and programming with the fellow Student Pastor.
  • Spearhead the development of a comprehensive communication strategy for the student ministry, overseeing parent outreach, apparel/merchandise, print media, and environmental signage. Collaborate directly with the Student Coordinator to align social media messaging and design graphics.
  • Lead out in creating and executing a disciple-making strategy for students that include but are not limited to baptism and disciple-making classes.
  • Lead out in developing impactful and relevant student services including series themes, teaching schedules, service schedules, programming, hosts, worship, and production. Responsible to build teams that effectively create environments where students encounter Jesus and that equip volunteers to discover, explore, and utilize their gifts.
  • Identify and explore the current needs of students in becoming disciple-makers in partnership with the Student Team.
  • In coordination with the Student Team, develop local service opportunities and at least one mission or service trip per year.
  • In coordination with Family Pastor, set 1-year and 3-year goals for the Student Ministry, paying attention to future needs and culture influences.
  • Participate in regular developmental opportunities that help you to grow as a disciple-maker and a leader.


Qualifications

Description

Organization Profile

The Office of National Mission coordinates and supports domestic ministries that serve congregations and schools through the districts of the Synod (Bylaw 3.8.2.3).

Reporting Relationships

  • Reports and is directly accountable to the ONM Managing Director, Congregations and Districts. Is ultimately accountable to the ONM Executive Director, Chief Mission Officer (CMO) and President of Synod.

Working Relationships

  • Works closely and collaboratively with ONM Managing Directors, Ministry Leaders and all ONM staff to achieve mutually established ONM objectives while executing the strategic vision of School Ministry throughout the LCMS.
  • Interacts with designated representatives from the various entities of the Synod and offices within corporate Synod, especially the mission and ministry units under the supervision of the Chief Mission Officer.

Essential Job Functions

  • Provides leadership and strategically directs the work of LCMS School Ministry.
  • Develop resources and support for the Lutheran School models of early childhood centers, elementary and secondary schools, as well as other forms of Lutheran Education (e.g. classical, micro, home, etc.)
  • Plans, implements and oversees all School Ministry activities and events in line with the goals and mission of the Synod and ONM.
  • Directs and is responsible for all programs related to School Ministry, including but not limited to the National Lutheran School Accreditation program [NLSA], Genesis studies, the Lutheran School Consulting Services [LSCS], the School Leader Development program [SLED], and others.
  • Strives to broaden and strengthen the School Ministry network through networking and presenting at conferences, conventions, workshops, meetings and other functions.
  • Provides leadership (visitation) and resources (conferences, etc.) which support and extend Lutheran schools operated by the Synod’s member congregations.
  • Sets direction and offers guidance in the development of materials to promote Lutheran Schools (web, print, social, television, etc.)
  • Develops the annual School Ministry budget proposal; manages expenditures within approved budget amounts; monitors financial reporting; collaborates with Mission Advancement on grant proposals and funding for School Ministry projects from outside sources.
  • Provides regular reports to ONM and Synod staff and participating districts.
  • Secures, interprets and communicates pertinent school statistics in order to support school related decision making at the national, district, university and local level.
  • Works collaboratively with district Education Executives, RSO’s, and other 3rd parties engaged in the School Ministry sphere, communicating regularly and providing training and leadership.
  • Oversees the ongoing relationship between School Ministry and district staff to ensure that work is aligned and carried out with the support of each district.
  • Other duties as assigned by the Executive Director of ONM, or its Managing Directors.

Education and Experience

  • A commissioned or ordained minister of the Lutheran Church—Missouri Synod, faithful to the Scriptures and the Lutheran Confessions, preferably with a minimum of ten years in school ministry with significant leadership experience.
  • A member in good standing of Lutheran church—Missouri Synod congregation who is supportive of the Synod’s constitution, bylaws and policies and familiar with the structure, policy, organization and procedures of the Synod.
  • Demonstrates understanding of and commitment to the Word and Sacrament ministry of the Church.
  • Understands the structure of the Synod and is supportive of the Synod’s position.
  • Experience in long- and short-range planning techniques and procedures.
  • Experience in writing and public speaking to various groups and organizations.
  • Experience in conducting seminars, conferences, workshops and training events.
  • Authorship of published articles on subjects related to Lutheran education (desirable).
  • An advanced degree in Lutheran education or administration, a terminal degree is preferred.
  • Post-graduate course work in administration, supervision and leadership.

The Armed Church Security Officer plays a critical role in ensuring the safety and security of church premises, congregants, staff, and visitors. This position involves proactively monitoring the environment to prevent and respond to potential threats or emergencies, maintaining a visible security presence to deter unlawful activities. The officer will collaborate closely with church leadership and local law enforcement to develop and implement security protocols tailored to the unique needs of a faith-based community. Additionally, the role requires maintaining confidentiality, exercising sound judgment, and demonstrating respect for the diverse backgrounds and beliefs of all individuals on site. Ultimately, the officer’s efforts contribute to creating a safe, welcoming, and peaceful environment where worship and community activities can flourish without disruption.

Minimum Qualifications:

  • Valid state-issued firearms permit and certification to carry and operate a firearm legally in the United States.
  • Completion of a recognized armed security officer training program.
  • Minimum of two years of experience in armed security, law enforcement, or a related field.
  • Strong knowledge of security protocols, emergency response procedures, and conflict de-escalation techniques.
  • Ability to pass background checks and drug screenings in compliance with federal and state regulations.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Must have Ex-military and/or Ex-police background.

  • Experience working in faith-based or community-oriented security roles.
  • Certification in first aid, CPR, and emergency medical response.
  • Familiarity with local law enforcement agencies and community resources.
  • Training in cultural sensitivity and diversity awareness.

Skills:

US Catholic Bishop's Southeast Regional Office for Hispanic Ministry, also known as SEPI, coordinates and supports Hispanic Ministry in the 30 Catholic dioceses of the Southeast United States (Alabama, Florida, Georgia, Kentucky, Louisiana, Mississippi, North Carolina, South Carolina, and Tennessee). Through its three pillars of Evangelization, Formation and Communion, SEPI strives to facilitate the full participation of Hispanics/Latinos in the mission of the Catholic Church and society as authentic missionary disciples. SEPI was born in 1979 as a response to the need for Hispanic education as recommended by the II National Hispanic Pastoral Meeting. SEPl's mission and values are to form and accompany Catholic leaders and communities in the Southeast by fostering communion, formation, and evangelization, grounded in the lived faith of Hispanic/Latino communities and in service to the Church's mission today.

job_name: Pastor of Intergenerational Life - First Congregational Church of Redlands
post_html:
Pastor of Intergenerational Life - First Congregational Church of Redlands
 

Our Church
First Congregational Church of Redlands is a historic Congregational church in Redlands, California. Our weekly worship service would best be described as ‘traditional,’ centering on our choir and organ, preaching from the Lectionary, and embodying the shared ministry model of historic Congregationalism. Our practices have remained in place for 146 years and will remain the primary way we engage with one another and our community.

Our (Current) Need
The steady growth we’ve experienced over the past three years has exceeded the capacity of our current pastoral staff, especially with children and emerging adults. We are a multi-generational church and have discerned that the standard models of compartmentalizing ministries by age diminish our church’s capacity to minister intergenerationally. Specifically, we are looking for someone to focus on the spiritual life and development of children, youth, young adults, singles, and families while co-developing a unique intergenerational ministry alongside the other pastors and volunteer leaders.

Job Description
In the context of a shared leadership model, the Pastor of Intergenerational Life is responsible for building and nurturing a church culture in which all ages—from toddlers to centenarians—grow and are integrated into the life, worship, and mission of the congregation. This will emerge and develop through a “youth-forward” approach. Meaning, starting with children and youth while integrating all generations into life together.

This is not a youth pastor role with occasional intergenerational activities. It is an intergenerational pastor whose primary leadership focus is on the generational gaps in our congregation. Gaps that currently show up most visibly among children, youth, and families. Through shared understanding, deepened affection for God and one another, a maturing congregational purpose, and embodied participation in the life of the church, this pastor will help FCC Redlands move further into intergenerational shared life and experiences.

Primary Responsibilities

·      As a member of the pastoral staff that operates under a polycentric model of shared leadership, we address the spiritual needs of our congregation together, including visitations, discipleship, preaching, and administrative tasks. We are looking for a candidate with strong pastoral skills and instincts.

·      While most of the direct responsibilities will involve ministry to children, youth, and emerging adults, it will not be isolated. We are looking for a Bridge-Builder who can speak the "language" of a Gen Z student and a Silent Generation retiree with equal ease.

·      Build new ministries that respond to the actual needs of our community. In other words, assessing the current needs and building from there rather than trying to impose programs without curiosity and discernment.

·      As a historic Congregational Church, the candidate will be familiar with our history and church governance. The members of the church are the highest governing body and the primary means of implementing and carrying out the ministries of the Church.

·      Beginning with children, design and support opportunities for people of all ages to engage together in worship, Scripture, prayer, small groups, and Christian service. We do church together, and we believe that apart from the abiding presence of Christ in our community, we have no greater resource than one another.

·      Pastoring and discipleship are embodied practices. While much of the job takes place on Sunday morning and in the office, much of it takes place outside of traditional working hours. This is a full-time salaried position that will not follow a traditional 9-5 structure.

·      Discernment is an essential part of this job, as we are building ministries that are not currently in place and existing models do not address where we believe God to be leading our church in this new season. We are not looking for an administrator but a creative galvanizer to help us create something tailor-made to our needs.

Skills and Experience

·      5+ years of pastoral experience on a church staff.

·      A bachelor’s degree is mandatory, and a seminary degree is strongly preferred.

·      Experience in ministry leadership, preferably across multiple age groups

·      Experience building intergenerational ministry, with demonstrated ability to engage children, youth, and adults together.

·      Demonstrated ability to lead volunteers and develop teams.

·      Comfort in working with technology and an ability to learn new software systems.

·      A natural connector with strong interpersonal skills.

Area Ministry Director - GFM NJ/Eastern PA (Graduate and Faculty Ministry)

Work Location:

New Jersey

Job Type:

Full time

An Area Director leads and oversees a ministry team to plant and to grow witnessing communities of students and faculty who follow Jesus on college and university campuses. Through these groups, we believe ever-increasing numbers of students and faculty from all ethnic groups and areas of the campus will be transformed by the gospel. We expect to see campuses increasingly become places where people, ideas, and structures flourish for the common good and to the glory of God. We confidently anticipate that our InterVarsity alumni will be growing disciples and change agents across the country and around the world.

This position is open to both full-time and part-time applicants living in NJ, PA, or DE. The pay range listed is for an employee working 40 hours/week as an Area Director. Pay will be prorated for employees who work less than 40 hours/week. Increased pay may be available in high cost of living areas (as a geographic adjustment).

Please submit the GFM Interest Form before completing the full application for a position with Graduate & Faculty Ministries in our online system. We will contact you when we are ready to proceed with the application process.

Volunteers are welcome. Volunteer opportunities range from prayer and hospitality to leading a campus fellowship of graduate students and faculty. Those interested in volunteering will go through an application and interview process, however, volunteer openings are not posted online. For more information, complete the GFM Interest Form.

ESSENTIAL COMMITMENTS/RESPONSIBILITIES

1. Spiritual Growth

The Area Ministry Director models spiritual maturity as a disciple of Jesus Christ so that your life and work increasingly reflects a growing love for God, God’s Word, God’s people of every ethnicity and culture, and God’s purposes in the world.

  • Embrace and practice Scriptural standards for behavior and attitudes, including those described in the Code of Conduct

​2. Campus Ministry Leadership

As an Area Director, you inspire, coach and develop campus staff ministers (“ministers”), students, faculty, and ministry partners to increase the number of witnessing communities, as well as the size, health, spiritual maturity, and campus-wide influence of existing witnessing communities by being a:

Visionary Guide:

  • Create a culture of dependence on God to gain vision for establishing and advancing witnessing communities that reach every corner of every campus in your area
  • Model InterVarsity’s vision and Core Values for supervisees
  • Lead staff, students, and faculty through Scripture, prayer, teaching and discipleship experiences in a way that motivates and shapes their ministry around vision
  • Set appropriate annual goals through prayer, research and reflection with your teams

Structural Architect:

  • Lead your team to develop and implement plans to achieve ministry goals
  • Adapt the plan as needed through rhythms of action, reflection and evaluation
  • Develop, align and leverage programs and structures to move the mission forward

Missional Developer:

  • Recruit a diversity of qualified minister candidates
  • Develop ministers to spiritually grow in Christ in intimacy, like Christ in character, and with Christ in his mission to current and new campuses
  • Develop ministers professionally so that they are consistently increasing their gifts and skills as ministry leaders
  • Supervise ministers, using appropriate leadership style for the individual and situation, to help them accomplish assigned tasks. This will require coaching, assessing, correcting and affirming job-related behaviors
  • Proactively establish and develop healthy relationships across racial, ethnic, national background, and gender barriers with staff, students, faculty, and ministry partners to build effective and diverse communities
  • Build an effective minister team that collaborates well and accomplishes goals

3. Organizational Collaboration

As an Area Director, you are part of a national organization and work in partnership with local, area, divisional, regional, and national InterVarsity ministers and volunteers.

  • Participate in regional leadership as determined by the Regional Director, to set ministry vision and strategies, contribute to accomplishing plans, and provide regional leadership in specific areas
  • Positively and constructively respond to the direction and coaching of line supervisors
  • Build productive ministry partnerships with regional and national collaborative leaders
  • Establish systems, processes and protocols to fulfill regular operational and administrative tasks in a timely manner (reporting, finances, human resources, etc.)
  • Maintain sound financial status of the area through management of budgeting, expense control and ministry partnership development
  • Become familiar with and comply with all InterVarsity policies and procedures

4. Ministry Partnership Development (MPD)

As an Area Director, you will develop a team of partners who will resource the ministry financially, in prayer, or with volunteer service that advances the mission.

  • Develop and maintain a ministry among partners who will fund InterVarsity
  • Ensure ministry budget is fully funded
  • Supervise each minister’s MPD (collaborating with coaches when applicable) and equip staff to build ministry partners
  • Build resource networks with alumni, volunteers, churches, advocacy councils, and major donors, in particular to fund low-network ministers
  • Communicate regularly with ministry partners

5. Accomplish all other assigned tasks as appropriate

QUALIFICATIONS

  • Annually affirm InterVarsity’s Statement of Agreement (Doctrinal Basis and Purpose Statement). Abide by InterVarsity’s Code of Conduct
  • Bachelor’s degree required

  • Strong ministry skills (including the ability to communicate spiritual vision, teach spiritual and biblical principles, plan ministry programs, and spiritually disciple, coach and mentor)
  • Proven ability to work well with others and the ability to develop a team of campus ministers.

WORK ENVIRONMENT/PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS

The AD position leads ministry in a college campus environment. A designated office space may or may not be available. The AD is required to travel to on-campus and off-campus sites as appropriate. Off-campus travel includes, but is not limited to student ministry conferences, MPD meetings, and InterVarsity-sponsored training sessions, meetings, and conferences. The AD is regularly required to communicate with others, and routinely uses standard office equipment such as computers, phones, etc.

The Worship Coordinator at our Pickerington Campus is a part-time (15 hours/week) ministry leadership position that plays a key role in helping people encounter God through worship. This person will provide leadership, spiritual guidance, and administrative support for the Pickerington Campus worship ministry, creating environments where people can connect with God, engage in authentic worship, and participate fully in the life of the church.

Working closely with the Lead Pastor for Pickerington Campus and the broader Vineyard Columbus worship team, this Worship Coordinator will lead weekend worship services, develop and care for volunteer musicians and vocalists, coordinate worship planning and rehearsals, and help cultivate a culture of worship that aligns with the mission and values of Vineyard Columbus. This role blends musical leadership with team development and ministry administration, requiring someone who loves worship, enjoys investing in people, and can bring both creativity and organization to ministry environments.

This is an exciting opportunity to help shape the worship life of a growing congregation by creating meaningful worship experiences, developing volunteer leaders, and fostering a culture that encourages people to encounter Jesus and respond to His presence.

About us:

Vineyard Columbus exists to develop multiethnic communities of disciples who experience God, love one another, and partner with Christ to heal the world. 

Our Pickerington Campus is located in a rapidly growing suburban community serving people from Pickerington, Reynoldsburg, Canal Winchester, Lithopolis, Baltimore, and surrounding areas. The congregation reflects the diversity of its community and values worship, discipleship, service, and life together across generations. 

Beyond weekend services at multiple locations across Central Ohio, we serve our neighbors through ministries that address practical needs while creating opportunities to share the love of Jesus in tangible ways. We are committed to cultivating Christlike unity, celebrating diversity, and helping people flourish as they pursue God's calling in their lives. 

Who we're looking for:

We are seeking a spiritually mature, team-oriented leader who is passionate about leading people in worship and helping others use their gifts to serve the church. The ideal candidate enjoys building relationships, developing volunteers, and creating worship environments that are Christ-centered, engaging, and spiritually meaningful.

This person is both creative and organized. They are energized by leading worship, preparing teams, coordinating ministry details, and helping create services that support the spiritual formation of the congregation. They thrive in collaborative settings, communicate clearly, and bring a positive, flexible attitude to the changing rhythms of ministry.

The ideal candidate is also a developer of people who enjoys identifying, recruiting, training, and empowering volunteer musicians and vocalists. They understand that healthy worship ministry is built through healthy teams and are passionate about helping others grow both musically and spiritually.

Most importantly, this individual demonstrates a genuine love for Jesus, a commitment to personal spiritual growth, and a desire to help others respond to God's presence through worship.

Desired qualifications:

  • Passion for leading people into meaningful encounters with God through worship.
  • Demonstrated experience leading worship and coordinating worship teams.
  • Strong vocal and/or instrumental ability.
  • Ability to recruit, train, support, and empower volunteer musicians and vocalists.
  • Strong organizational and administrative skills, with the ability to manage schedules, rehearsals, and service planning.
  • Ability to direct rehearsals and help teams pursue musical excellence.
  • Experience utilizing Planning Center, PRIME Multi-Track, or similar worship planning tools is preferred.
  • Effective verbal and written communication skills.
  • Demonstrated spiritual maturity and a lifestyle that reflects Biblical values.
  • Strong collaboration skills, dependability, and commitment to teamwork
  • Satisfactory background check required for all positions. 

We offer:

Vineyard Columbus values hard work, sustainable rhythms, and the pursuit of healthy and well-balanced lives. Our staff are supported in their ministry by a great team environment and generous benefits. Benefits for this role include: 

  • Paid time off for holidays, sick time, bereavement, and other types of leave. 
  • Equivalent of 13 days off per calendar year for holidays and staff refresh days. 
  • Access to a robust Employee Assistance Program. 
  • Gym membership or equivalent subsidy. 
  • 403(b) Retirement Plan and Ohio’s 529 Plan with College Advantage available.
  • Workers’ Compensation coverage.

Have you often felt like you wanted your work to have meaning? Every day, Resurrection staff members are doing work that matters with people who care. Resurrection’s purpose since its conception in 1990 is to “build a Christian community where non-religious and nominally religious people are becoming deeply committed Christians.” Join our team and see how your contributions move the needle in transforming the World. 

Resurrection has an opening for a Worship Experience Specialist in the Ministries & Programs division! The position is part-time, exempt with Sundays required and is located at the Overland Park campus at 8412 W 95th St, Overland Park, KS 66212. Please see below for a full job description. 

Job Summary  

The Worship Experience Specialist is the church’s location leader responsible for creating a meaningful worship experience that guides guests and existing members on their journey to become deeply committed Christians. As a member of the Worship Team, the Location Worship Experience Specialist will steer all logistics related to weekend worship, ensuring that every person who attends worship has an exceptional experience. Weekend worship responsibilities consist of leading the ministries of Holy Communion and Baptisms as well as the management of Hospitality teams including Greeters and Ushers, Parking teams, Connection Point/Info Desk, Medical Team and others supporting first impressions and the guest experience related to worship. The Location Worship Experience Specialist is also responsible for key administrative aspects of the location such as first-time guest follow up and serves as a collaborative team member at the West location. 

Essential Responsibilities and Expectations: 

Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions. 

Position-Specific 

  • Serve as the on-site Staff leader in Worship Experience for all worship services.
  • Provide holistic leadership, training, and support to all Worship Experience Teams
    • Manage volunteer schedules and ensure adequate coverage for all services.
    • Build effective teams, identifying high-capacity leaders and equipping people for ministry. 
    • Ministry assessment and performance evaluation, goal setting, mentoring, spiritual encouragement, support, and conflict resolution.
    • Prepare for and conduct team meetings, trainings, and celebration/recognition events.
  • Lead logistical planning and implementation of worship elements in weekly worship and special events
    • Includes special worship events and liturgical holidays.   Examples: Communion, Acolytes, Baptism, Anointing, Ash Imposition, processionals, recessionals, remembrance of baptism. 
  • Oversee Communion logistics for Sanctuary
    • Sets up Sanctuary for Communion each month, ensuring altar is set according to Pastor preference. 
    • Lead volunteers as staff person on-site during communion services each month.
  • Manage logistics of special worship-related handouts or sermon series promotional items, i.e, print collateral. Worship giveaways, sermon series items, etc.
  • Collaborate with the Worship Experience Team provide timely oversight of first-time guest follow up practices as well as other member and guest communications relating to the worship experience including location specific online platforms.
  • Maintain a functional and reverent aesthetic in all worship spaces. 
    • Seasonally work with Worship Design Manager and contracted florists/interior designers to support the development and implementation of a décor scheme that enhances the worship experience during holidays and in accordance with the liturgical calendar, i.e., Lent, Maundy Thursday, Easter, Advent, Christmas. 
      • Recruit and provide leadership to volunteer teams or contractors assigned to implement this plan.
  • Coordinate logistics of large-scale worship services such as Candlelight Christmas Eve and Easter as well as recruiting and equipping additional volunteers for these larger special services. 
  • Attend Worship Experience and Location-specific team meetings, All-Staff meetings, etc. 
  • Provide support to location team in the event of large weddings or funerals in the Sanctuary. 
  • Other duties and tasks as assigned.

Churchwide 

  • Follow Jesus and engage in the “five essential practices” of the Christian life: worship, study, serve, give, and share.
  • Support the church’s purpose of “building a Christian community where non-religious and nominally religious people become deeply committed Christians.”
  • Exemplify the church’s values and support its theological direction as a United Methodist Church.

Competencies

  • Activating - proactively takes on new challenges and opportunities with energy and urgency.
  • Developing Others – coaches, encourages and resources individuals and teams to discover their calling and meet career and church goals.
  • Driving Vision and Clarity – ensures people are on the same page and understands the cross-functional role teams play in making the church a success.
  • Innovating – provides new solutions that will elevate the church’s effectiveness. 
  • Improving Systems – configures organizational systems, structures, and processes for greater effectiveness. 
  • Leading Change – promotes, champions and enables changes and helps bring others along in the process. 
  • Motivating – creates a climate where people are inspired to do their best to help the church achieve its purpose.
  • Orchestrating – ensures everyone works together to achieve the same goal of staging seamless, coherent user experiences.
  • Problem Solving – makes good decisions quickly, solves problems effectively to help move the church forward.
  • Resourcing – secures and deploys resources as effectively and efficiently as possible. 
  • Team Building – forms highly effective teams, whether supervised or informal, where individuals with diverse skills achieve ambitious goals.

Qualifications 

  • Positive and professional communication skills with strong acumen for working with a wide variety of people.
  • Proficient computer skills, especially with MS Excel, Outlook, and Word.   
  • Data management expertise through database maintenance and reporting. 
  • Aptitude working with web content management software. 
  • Ability to multi-task and manage competing priorities.
  • Knowledge of the United Methodist Book of Discipline relating to sacraments and worship practices. 
  • Physical Requirements: Must be able to lift, push, or pull 50lbs., stand for long periods of time and walk extensively during worship services.

Inspiring People to Move Closer to Jesus

 

At K-LOVE, every role is ministry.

Here's what we are looking for:

This role serves as the primary shepherding elder and executive leader of the campus, guiding staff, leaders, and the congregation in carrying out Grace Church's mission and vision.

This role calls for someone who takes ownership, leads with initiative, and lives under the authority of Scripture in alignment with the biblical definition of eldership.

post_html:
Area Ministry Director - Florida (Graduate & Faculty Ministry)

Work Location:

Florida

Job Type:

Full time

An Area Director leads and oversees a ministry team to plant and to grow witnessing communities of students and faculty who follow Jesus on college and university campuses. Through these groups, we believe ever-increasing numbers of students and faculty from all ethnic groups and areas of the campus will be transformed by the gospel. We expect to see campuses increasingly become places where people, ideas, and structures flourish for the common good and to the glory of God. We confidently anticipate that our InterVarsity alumni will be growing disciples and change agents across the country and around the world.

Please submit the GFM Interest Form before completing the full application for a position with Graduate & Faculty Ministries in our online system. We will contact you when we are ready to proceed with the application process.  

This position is open to applicants working less than 40 hours/week. If you are interested in part-time work please apply for this position. 

The pay range listed is for an employee working 40 hours/week. Pay will be prorated for employees who work less than 40 hours/week.

ESSENTIAL COMMITMENTS/RESPONSIBILITIES

1. Spiritual Growth

The Area Ministry Director models spiritual maturity as a disciple of Jesus Christ so that your life and work increasingly reflects a growing love for God, God’s Word, God’s people of every ethnicity and culture, and God’s purposes in the world.

  • Pursue a vibrant relationship with the triune God through engagement with Scripture, prayer, and worship, both individually and in community
  • Exercise self-leadership (growing in self-awareness, self-management, relational integrity, and resiliency)
  • Embrace and practice Scriptural standards for behavior and attitudes, including those described in the Code of Conduct

​2. Campus Ministry Leadership

As an Area Director, you inspire, coach and develop campus staff ministers (“ministers”), students, faculty, and ministry partners to increase the number of witnessing communities, as well as the size, health, spiritual maturity, and campus-wide influence of existing witnessing communities by being a:

Visionary Guide:

  • Create a culture of dependence on God to gain vision for establishing and advancing witnessing communities that reach every corner of every campus in your area
  • Model InterVarsity’s vision and Core Values for supervisees
  • Lead staff, students, and faculty through Scripture, prayer, teaching and discipleship experiences in a way that motivates and shapes their ministry around vision
  • Set appropriate annual goals through prayer, research and reflection with your teams

Structural Architect:

  • Lead your team to develop and implement plans to achieve ministry goals
  • Adapt the plan as needed through rhythms of action, reflection and evaluation
  • Develop, align and leverage programs and structures to move the mission forward

Missional Developer:

  • Recruit a diversity of qualified minister candidates
  • Develop ministers to spiritually grow in Christ in intimacy, like Christ in character, and with Christ in his mission to current and new campuses
  • Develop ministers professionally so that they are consistently increasing their gifts and skills as ministry leaders
  • Supervise ministers, using appropriate leadership style for the individual and situation, to help them accomplish assigned tasks. This will require coaching, assessing, correcting and affirming job-related behaviors
  • Proactively establish and develop healthy relationships across racial, ethnic, national background, and gender barriers with staff, students, faculty, and ministry partners to build effective and diverse communities
  • Build an effective minister team that collaborates well and accomplishes goals

3. Organizational Collaboration

As an Area Director, you are part of a national organization and work in partnership with local, area, divisional, regional, and national InterVarsity ministers and volunteers.

  • Participate in regional leadership as determined by the Regional Director, to set ministry vision and strategies, contribute to accomplishing plans, and provide regional leadership in specific areas
  • Positively and constructively respond to the direction and coaching of line supervisors
  • Build productive ministry partnerships with regional and national collaborative leaders
  • Establish systems, processes and protocols to fulfill regular operational and administrative tasks in a timely manner (reporting, finances, human resources, etc.)
  • Maintain sound financial status of the area through management of budgeting, expense control and ministry partnership development
  • Become familiar with and comply with all InterVarsity policies and procedures

4. Ministry Partnership Development (MPD)

As an Area Director, you will develop a team of partners who will resource the ministry financially, in prayer, or with volunteer service that advances the mission.

  • Develop and maintain a ministry among partners who will fund InterVarsity
  • Ensure ministry budget is fully funded
  • Supervise each minister’s MPD (collaborating with coaches when applicable) and equip staff to build ministry partners
  • Build resource networks with alumni, volunteers, churches, advocacy councils, and major donors, in particular to fund low-network ministers
  • Communicate regularly with ministry partners

5. Accomplish all other assigned tasks as appropriate

QUALIFICATIONS

  • Annually affirm InterVarsity’s Statement of Agreement (Doctrinal Basis and Purpose Statement). Abide by InterVarsity’s Code of Conduct
  • Bachelor’s degree required
  • Minimum three years campus ministry or equivalent work experience required
  • Strong ministry skills (including the ability to communicate spiritual vision, teach spiritual and biblical principles, plan ministry programs, and spiritually disciple, coach and mentor)
  • Proven ability to work well with others and the ability to develop a team of campus ministers.
  • Strong interpersonal skills (including ability to minister to diverse ethnic communities and faculty)
  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills
  • Demonstrated problem solving skills
  • Familiarity with word processing, presentation, email, and spreadsheet software

WORK ENVIRONMENT/PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS

The AD position leads ministry in a college campus environment. A designated office space may or may not be available. The AD is required to travel to on-campus and off-campus sites as appropriate. Off-campus travel includes, but is not limited to student ministry conferences, MPD meetings, and InterVarsity-sponsored training sessions, meetings, and conferences. The AD is regularly required to communicate with others, and routinely uses standard office equipment such as computers, phones, etc.

Pay Range: $55,200.00 - $73,608.00 per year

Pay: This position is funded through personal fundraising. Accordingly, compensation will vary based on the ability of the individual to secure a donor team to fund the cost of his/her salary. The anticipated salary range for this position on a full-time basis (40 hours/week) is dependent on a variety of factors, including location and cost of living. The actual salary received, including any geographic adjustment to account for location and cost of living, is subject to the individual’s ability to raise funds necessary to cover the full amount of such salary within the range set forth in the job posting details.

Benefits:

We offer a competitive benefits package, including health care and retirement savings with a match. Eligibility is based on employee type and hours worked.  Benefits include the following:

  • 403(b) Retirement Savings Plan

  • 403(b) matching contributions

  • Dental insurance

  • Employee assistance program

  • Employee discounts

  • Flexible work schedule

  • Flexible spending accounts

  • Health insurance

  • Health savings account

  • Life insurance

  • Paid time off

  • Parental leave

  • Professional development assistance

  • Vision insurance

Equal Employment Opportunity: 

 

InterVarsity Christian Fellowship/USA is both an equal opportunity employer and a faith-based religious organization. We conduct hiring without regard to race, color, ancestry, national origin, citizenship, age, sex, marital status, parental status, membership in any labor organization, political ideology, or disability of an otherwise qualified individual. The status of InterVarsity Christian Fellowship/USA as an equal opportunity employer does not prevent the organization from hiring staff based on their religious beliefs so that all staff share the same religious commitment.  Pursuant to the Civil Rights Act of 1964, Section 702 (42 U.S.C. 2000e 1(a)) InterVarsity Christian Fellowship/USA has the right to, and does, hire only candidates who agree with InterVarsity’s Statement of Agreement: Purpose and Doctrinal Basis because InterVarsity believes that each and every staff plays a vital role in advancing InterVarsity’s mission and purposes.

JOB DESCRIPTION SUMMARY:  

The Interim Director of Kids Ministry leads the Kids Ministry Department within the Family Life Zone. This position oversees all ministries for children from Birth through 5th grade under the guidance of the Associate Pastor (Internal Ministries) and Family Life Zone Director. This person must love kids and have a passion to see children give their hearts and lives to Jesus and grow to be more like Him. This position reports to the Family Life Zone Director. This is a temporary, part-time (25 hours/week), non-exempt (hourly), temporary position without benefits.

Specific Responsibilities:

  • Interim Department Leadership: 
    • Provide leadership and resources for an effective and contagious Christ-centered Kids Ministry in order to accomplish the overall Ministry Plan of Colorado Community Church. 
    • In coordination with the Associate Pastor (Internal Ministries) and Family Life Zone Director, help execute the annual ministry plan for the Kids Ministry Department while operating within the confines of the annual budget.
    • Help onboard and acclimate the new Kids Ministry Director once hired.
  • Kids Ministry Staff Collaboration:
  • Collaborate with Kids Ministry Department staff to ensure weekend programming and core activities are carried out with excellence.
  • Kids Ministry Volunteer Coordination:
    • In coordination with the Family Life Zone Director, Kids Ministry staff and the interim volunteer leadership team, recruit, train, lead and shepherd volunteers (e.g. teachers, storytellers, musicians, etc. composed of adults, youth and 4th or 5th grade kids)
  • Program Development: 
  • With assistance from the Family Life Zone Director, plan, coordinate and oversee Kids Ministry programming with a specific focus on weekend services and key family events.
  • Equip and resource parents in their roles as the primary spiritual leaders of their children.
  • Additional Responsibilities:
  • Provide general care to the kids and families associated with our Kids Ministry.
  • Work Schedule & Meetings: 
    • Schedule: Regularly work weekend services on Saturday/Sunday with other hours to be determined based on availability and department needs.
    • Meetings: To be determined by Associate Pastor (Internal Ministries) and Family Life Zone Director.

Qualifications:

  • Character: 
    • A Christ honoring life marked by personal holiness, prayer, bible study, spiritual and emotional maturity and increasing dependence on the Holy Spirit (Titus 1:6-9, 1 Timothy 3:1-7). 
    • Unquestionable integrity specifically in areas of handling finances, relationships and time management. 
    • A person who understands and models the Christian principle of servant-leadership. Someone who is eager, flexible and has a teachable spirit.
  • Competency: 
    • Pastoral gifting; naturally shepherds with strong gifts in leadership and teaching.
    • Proven experience in team building and training people for ministry with a Missional attitude and focus.
    • Effectively communicates with and relates to people of all ages.
    • Broad knowledge of teenager’s development and needs.
    • Comfortable in interdenominational settings.
    • Takes personal initiative in learning.
    • Seminary degree preferred but equivalent ministry experience is acceptable.
    • Solid computer skills with MS Office programs (Word, Outlook, Excel, PowerPoint etc.).
    • Willing to learn and effectively utilize the church database system.
  • Convictions: 
  • In full agreement with Colorado Community’s “Statement of Faith” and wholeheartedly embraces and champions “Who We Are”.
  • Supportive of the structure and leadership of Colorado Community Church (i.e.: Christ centered, Board governed, Staff led, Congregation Mobilized).
  • Strives for excellence in all work duties and is passionate about seeing others succeed.

Company Description

CCV Stars is a year-round, rapidly growing, multi-site outreach ministry of CCV that exists to connect the community through sports. Stars provides a comprehensive program that not only develops the skills of players, but also comes alongside the parents to help form a foundation that will develop character and integrity, making sports more than a game. CCV Stars is the largest youth sports program of its kind with over 20,000 youth participants each year. We currently offer various levels of flag football and soccer at various times of the year. The Stars Pastor will be responsible for all aspects of their campus’ sports ministry, including oversight over the many volunteers necessary to execute. 

Job Description

Essential Job Functions 

Ministry: 

  • Reinforce the mission of Stars to move people across the parking lot to CCV   
  • Building relationships with Stars families & coaches  
  • Guide coaches and volunteers to grow in their next steps  
  • Ensure More Than A Game elements like huddles, cards, and prayer are taking place  
  • Help integrate the Stars ministry with other CCV ministries   

Programming: 

  • Constantly recruiting and training volunteers for coaches, guest services, and field ops  
  • Implement and execute leagues and camps (make teams, schedules, maps, referees, etc)  
  • Communicate information, updates, and promotions regularly with Stars families  
  • Support volunteer coaches as needed during practices and games  
  • Connect with local community, schools, and city functions to promote Stars to the community 

Operations: 

  • Ensure facility ready for all practices/games (signage, equipment, fields/courts, restrooms, etc)  
  • Manage and steward facility and equipment/inventory 
  • Oversee safety and quality of facility, handling minor repairs and communicating with landscapers 

Miscellaneous: 

  • Ability to multitask and manage time, often working on 2-3 seasons at a time 
  • Variable schedule including ~2 nights a week and Saturdays on the fields during season 
  • Assist and contribute to non-Stars related campus wide events 

Qualifications

Minimum Qualifications 

Character & Chemistry 

Alignment with CCV core values: 

  • Commitment to Excellence-We set ridiculously high expectations and exceed them. 
  • Heart for Evangelism-We will risk it all to win one more. 
  • Relationships-We value people over process. 
  • Integrity-We follow through every time. 
  • Servant Attitude-We pick up trash. 
  • Teamwork-We celebrate teamwork over talent.  

Fully engaged (or willingness to) in CCV Next Steps: 

  • Baptism-by immersion at an age of decision 
  • Worship-regularly attend CCV service with family 
  • Connect-participation in CCV small group 
  • Serve-volunteer somewhere within a CCV ministry 
  • Give-returning at least a full 10% tithe to the local church CCV 

Competency 

  • Interpersonal Skills-connect well relationally with people from all walks of life and various levels of spiritual maturity 
  • Conflict Resolution-able to diffuse upset people and facilitate conversations between parties at odds  
  • Leadership Skills-lead Stars volunteers and families to execute the program and keep focus on mission  
  • Customer Focus-going the extra mile to love people well and prioritize convenience with how we program 
  • Drive for Results-being a self-starter and taking initiative necessary to meet and exceed expectations 
  • Self-Development-constantly growing in skills needed for the job, spiritual and leadership growth, seeks feedback  
  • Strategic Planning Skills-ability to multitask and manage time as often working on 2-3 seasons at once 
  • Administrative Skills-prioritizing details necessary to run organized programs, execute established processes 

Education and Experience 

  • College experience preferred 
  • Previous leadership experience highly desired 
  • Coaching and Stars experience are assets 
  • Proficient in Microsoft Office 

Additional Information

All your information will be kept confidential according to EEO guidelines.

General Information

The above statements are intended to describe the general nature and level of work being performed by individuals assigned to this position. They are not intended to be an exhaustive list of all duties, responsibilities, and skills required of employees. CCV Leadership reserves the right to revise the position, its job functions, minimum qualifications and other aspects of the position in any way at any time.

Overview

The Corps Ministries Coordinator supports the Corps Officer in the ministry and program life of the Old Orchard Beach Corps. The position coordinates ministry and discipleship programs for all ages, supports volunteer leaders and teachers, and provides local support for special events and the Seaside Pavilion. The Coordinator also contributes to the spiritual life of the corps through teaching and direct ministry involvement.

Responsibilities

In a typical week, the Coordinator leads corps ministry programs, supports volunteer leaders and teachers, and coordinates logistics for special events and the Seaside Pavilion.

  • Plan, organize, and coordinate corps ministry and discipleship programs for all ages, including youth, music and arts, and character building
  • Provide support, guidance, and resources to corps ministry leaders, including Sunday school teachers and youth and arts leaders
  • Provide spiritual leadership in corps programs, including teaching classes and leading ministry activities
  • Recruit, prepare, and support volunteer leaders, local officers, and teachers
  • Coordinate special events and local logistics for the Seaside Pavilion, including retreats and contact with vendors and service providers
  • Participate in corps ministry planning with the Corps Officer, and attend Sunday worship to support corps ministries

Qualifications

  • High school diploma or equivalent and five years of related experience required; a degree in a related field is preferred
  • Valid driver's license
  • Demonstrated ability to coordinate multiple programs, events, and the people involved in them at the same time
  • Ability to guide, encourage, and support volunteer leaders and teachers of varied ages and backgrounds
  • Salvationist in good standing, with a working knowledge of the beliefs and ministry of The Salvation Army and the faith and experience to offer sound spiritual guidance to program leaders
  • Proficiency with Microsoft 365 applications and ability to communicate clearly and professionally with staff, volunteers, and vendors

 

What We Offer:

  • Paid time off
  • Paid holidays
  • Sick leave
  • Personal days
  • Bereavement leave
  • Medical, dental and vision benefits
  • Short term and long term disability
  • Retirement plan

Benefits may vary based on position classification and eligibility.

 

About Us:

The Salvation Army, an international movement, is an evangelical part of the universal Christian church. Its message is based on the Bible. Its ministry is motivated by the love of God. Its mission is to preach the gospel of Jesus Christ and to meet human needs in His name without discrimination.

The Northern New England Division serves communities across Maine, New Hampshire and Vermont through local corps and programs, supported by Divisional Headquarters in Portland, Maine.

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, sex, national origin, disability or protected veteran status.

The purpose of this position is to research and qualify organizations recommended to receive charitable grants. This person applies critical data-gathering and analytical skills to qualify charities based on established organizational and IRS standards and is accountable for the accurate and timely processing of those requests. Through the work performed in this research role, the organization is able to fulfill its charitable purpose as a grant-making organization while serving givers in a timely manner and providing excellent customer service.

POSITION TITLE: Campus Ministry Coordinator


POSITION DESCRIPTION:

Campus Ministry Coordinator is a dynamic, faith-filled leader who focuses on connecting our students with the faith, both within and beyond the school. The Campus Ministry Coordinator is responsible for overseeing and programming faith formation needs of the student body. 

Position Status: Part-Time, Exempt 

QUALIFICATIONS:

A Catholic in good standing who embraces and transmits the Catholic Church’s teachings on matters of faith and morals

Possess a Bachelor’s degree or higher in Theology, Pastoral Ministry, Religious Studies or related field

Hold a current Archdiocese of Detroit Catechist Certification, or commitment to achieve this certification as well as ongoing formation.

Experience with youth, young adults and parish ministry or related field


RESPONSIBLE TO:

The Campus Ministry Coordinator reports to the Principal 


PERFORMANCE RESPONSIBILITIES:  

Foster the spiritual growth and faith formation of individual students and the broader Bishop Foley Catholic High School community.

Lead the planning, coordination, and administration of all student retreats and faith-formation experiences.

Oversee the care, organization, and maintenance of the school chapel and ensure it remains a welcoming and reverent space for prayer and worship.

Collaborate with School Administration, Faculty, and Staff to further Bishop Foley Catholic High School’s mission of developing faith-filled servant leaders.

Oversee the student service-hour program, including tracking student requirements, communicating expectations, and coordinating opportunities for service.

Develop and coordinate meaningful service opportunities for both students and staff that reflect Catholic Social Teaching and the mission of the school.

Coordinate speakers, programs, and educational opportunities related to Catholic Social Teaching, service, faith, and social responsibility.

Participate in school committees and initiatives as needed, including the Alignment Board, Catholic Schools Week planning, and other mission-centered programs and events. 



GENERAL RESPONSIBILITIES 


Reports to the school on a schedule agreed upon with the Principal, based on an 11-month contract. 

Attend and actively participate in all required staff meetings, professional and faith formation opportunities, and staff retreats.     

Attend Open Houses and other school events (as needed) to assist with welcoming students and families, and showcasing the Chapel and Faith Life at Bishop Foley Catholic High School.

Interested candidates should submit a cover letter and resume directly to:

Jenna Kokenos
Director of Finance
kokenos@bishopfoley.org
