Children’s Ministry Preschool Teacher (Part-Time) – Kids Life
Kids Life | Non-Exempt

Help Build a Foundation of Faith in the Early Years

If you have a heart for nurturing little ones during their most formative years, this is a role with a profound purpose.

As Kids Life continues to grow, Lakewood Church is expanding our ministry to include midweek Wednesday services, creating more opportunities to pour into children during these early, foundational years.

We are seeking patient, loving, and Christ-centered individuals who enjoy teaching, comforting, and guiding preschool-age children in a safe, joyful, and faith-filled environment.

As a Preschool Teacher, you’ll primarily serve children from age three through five years/Kindergarten, helping introduce them to God’s love through engaging classroom ministry, age-appropriate teaching, encouragement, and care.

Compensation

  • $14 per hour base pay
  • $20 per hour Sunday premium rate

Work Schedule

  • Part-time, 12 to 20 hours per pay period
  • Sunday 7:30 a.m.- 2 p.m. and Wednesday 6:30 p.m.-9:30 p.m.
  • Additional hours may be available for special events as needed

What You’ll Do

Working directly with the Preschool Manager, you’ll help create a safe, welcoming, and engaging ministry environment where preschool-age children can learn, participate, and grow.

Teach & Minister to Children

  • Minister to children through teaching, guiding, comforting, and encouraging them
  • Care for the physical, emotional, and spiritual needs of children
  • Engage children at their individual developmental stages
  • Teach assigned curriculum with enthusiasm
  • Help ensure quality ministry takes place in the assigned classroom or role
  • Primarily serve children from age three through five years/Kindergarten while remaining flexible to assist with children of other ages or in different ministry roles as needed

Create a Safe & Positive Classroom Experience

  • Follow established Child Safety and Emergency protocols in accordance with Lakewood Church policies and applicable requirements
  • Help children transition successfully between activities and classroom environments
  • Respond appropriately and positively to challenging behaviors
  • Model a Christ-like attitude in interactions with children, parents, volunteers, staff, and leaders
  • Help ensure children, parents, Kids Life staff, and volunteers have a positive experience
  • Maintain professionalism, discretion, and a Christ-like attitude when handling sensitive or confidential information

Serve as Part of the Kids Life Team

  • Work cooperatively with Kids Life staff, volunteers, coordinators, and ministry leaders
  • Look for opportunities to assist with classroom transitions, additional duties, and team needs
  • Encourage and inspire volunteer commitment in others
  • Maintain a cooperative and respectful attitude
  • Remain gracious, kind, and loving even in high-pressure situations
  • Be open to correction and responsive to volunteer and staff leadership
  • Maintain flexibility when classroom assignment changes are needed

Be Prepared & Dependable

  • Arrive in assigned areas on time, prepared, and ready to serve
  • Maintain a high level of dependability and reliability for assigned work schedules
  • Communicate schedule changes promptly with the Preschool Manager, Coordinator, Team Lead, and other appropriate staff
  • Complete assigned paperwork and classroom clean-up
  • Attend Kids Life team meetings, staff meetings, and area trainings
  • Maintain availability for regular ministry days, including Sundays and Wednesdays, and for special events as needed
  • Perform other related duties as assigned

Qualifications

Successful candidates will demonstrate:

  • An uncompromised commitment to Lakewood Church’s vision, values, and core beliefs
  • Christ-like character
  • A passion for serving and ministering to children, families, volunteers, and staff
  • The ability to relate positively to children of different ages, parents, volunteers, staff, and leaders
  • Excellent teamwork, leadership, and interpersonal skills
  • An understanding of and commitment to following child safety policies and processes
  • A cooperative and respectful approach to working with others
  • The ability to remain gracious, kind, and loving under pressure
  • Openness to correction and responsiveness to ministry leadership
  • A commitment to excellence in assigned responsibilities
  • Professional appearance and conduct
  • The ability to regularly lift up to 20 pounds
  • The ability to stand and remain mobile for extended periods of time

Education & Experience:

  • High School Diploma or GED required
  • Minimum six months of volunteer, daycare, or teaching experience
  • One year of volunteer, daycare, or teaching experience preferred

Our Mission

As a member of the Lakewood Church team, you play an important role in helping fulfill our mission of bringing hope through Jesus Christ to people around the world.

Employees serving in this position are expected to support the Church’s mission, maintain a lifestyle consistent with our biblical beliefs, participate in the life of the Church, and serve as part of our faith community. Ministerial responsibilities include regular attendance at church services and classes, serving as a Prayer Partner or ministry volunteer, and participating in community outreach opportunities as needed.

If you have a heart for preschool-age children and want to help create a safe, joyful, and faith-filled environment where children can begin building a strong foundation of faith, we encourage you to apply.

POSITION SUMMARY:


The Vicariate Hispanic Ministry Coordinator, under the leadership of the Diocesan Director of Hispanic Ministry, belongs to a Team that shares the mission to oversee and support all areas of Hispanic ministry within the Diocese of Charlotte, while assisting the Pastors and parish communities in developing, coordinating, and administering an effective ministry for the Catholic Hispanic community. The Coordinator is tasked with fostering a greater understanding of the needs of a multi-cultural faith community; and providing leadership formation to members at the local level involved in this ministry with the goal of maintaining and fortifying the Catholic faith. The Hispanic Ministry Coordinator aids the Pastors of the Vicariate in the implementation of the USCCB’s National Hispanic Pastoral Plan.


KEY RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • The primary responsibility of the Vicariate Hispanic Ministry Coordinator is to accompany the Hispanic Faithful in their journey of Faith. The Coordinator serves as a resource for the Pastors of the parishes within the vicariate.
  • The Vicariate Hispanic Ministry Coordinator is expected to be in close communication and dialogue with the Pastors in the parishes. They are professional Pastoral Agents prepared to offer all the diocesan resources available for Formation and Continuing Education to the parish Hispanic catechists, such as Baptism preparation, Pre-Cana, Faith Formation for children and youth, Parish leadership, OCIA, Leaders of Apostolic groups, and Youth Ministry.
  • The Vicariate Hispanic Ministry Coordinator is available to offer preparation for liturgical ministries, workshops for Lectors, Extraordinary ministers of Holy Communion, ushers, etc.
  • The Vicariate Hispanic Ministry Coordinator is prepared to offer training in Family crisis support, ranging from difficulties such as homebound persons, terminal illness situations, grief support ministry (Pastoral de Duelo), matrimony problems support (Acompañantes Matrimoniales), and other culturally specific needs.
  • The Vicariate Hispanic Ministry Coordinator is available to prepare and guide days of reflection and retreats.

About ValleyLight Church

ValleyLight Church exists to make Jesus unignorable on the westside of the Salt Lake Valley. Since launching in September 2023, this young church plant has grown to an average of 140 people on Sunday mornings, with more than 50 baptisms! 

ValleyLight serves one of the most strategic mission fields in the country. West Valley City is Utah's second-largest city and one of its most diverse. ValleyLight is the only English-speaking evangelical church serving a community of roughly 65,000 people, a community that ranks among the least-reached in the United States. It is also a religiously unique and spiritually complex mission field, where many who walk through ValleyLight's doors are meeting the gospel for the first time while others are finding gospel clarity, often for the first time. We experience new guests regularly who found us online because they are spiritually hungry and searching for something more.

ValleyLight is a multicultural, multigenerational, family-oriented congregation. New and longtime believers, honest seekers, families, kids, teenagers, and adults from many different backgrounds worship side by side, and everyone is still growing in faith. People here love being together and they love their church. Beyond that, ValleyLight has built a strong reputation in the community it serves.



The Opportunity and the Reality

The Foundation Is Already Here
ValleyLight is not starting from zero. There is real gospel fruit, real community awareness, and real opportunity already in place. 

  • ValleyLight averages around 140 on Sundays
  • More than 50 baptisms in 3 years
  • Multiple services with 300 to 400 people present
  • Has contact information for more than 1,000 people who have come through the ministry
This opportunity doesn't require the most gifted and experienced leader. It requires a pastor who will love people well and keep showing up in the community. People are already searching, already finding ValleyLight, and already walking through the door.

ValleyLight also has meaningful ministry partners, including several larger churches, and the next pastor will inherit those relationships. 

Still a Church Plant, Still a Mobile Church 
This is not a typical pastorate, ValleyLight is very much a church plant. The church currently meets in a school and operates as a mobile church, with limited resources. The church is still developing the systems, leaders, and ministry structures needed for long-term health. Very little here is permanent, polished, or already built. The right candidate will feel like the missing leadership piece who can help pull the opportunity together. This is a great opportunity for the right leader to shape the future and ministry of the church.

About the Ideal Candidate (Lead Pastor)

ValleyLight is looking for a Lead Pastor who will preach, shepherd, and build, helping the church mature into its next season. We are looking for a missionary-minded pastor with a church planter's heart, who sees ValleyLight as the foundation for something much larger and is willing to build with limited resources. This is a calling for someone who wants to be planted long-term. 

A Shepherd-Builder with a Planter's Heart 
This role calls for a shepherd-builder, not a preacher-maintainer. You need to be resourceful and adaptable, and comfortable leading when everything is not yet permanent, polished, or already built. Prior church-planting experience is a bonus, not a requirement, but you should understand what it means to build something with limited resources. If you've ever wrestled with whether God is calling you to plant a church of your own, this role may be a way to live out that calling by stepping into an existing work that is still in its formative years. 

Seasoned, Not Rigid 
ValleyLight isn't looking for someone brand new to vocational ministry; a minimum of five years of pastoral experience is preferred. That said, a proven track record of fruit and character matters more than a particular resume. While formal education is preferred, it is not required. Experience, especially in discipleship and leadership development, carries more weight than credentials. 

Called to This Specific Place 
West Valley City is not the polished side of the Salt Lake Valley, and Magna keeps its own working-class, small-town identity within it. ValleyLight is looking for someone who wants to live among the people he serves rather than commute in from somewhere else, and who feels genuinely called to this specific, multicultural, lower-income part of the valley as part of an incarnational, missional strategy. 

Partnership Development and Vision Casting 
ValleyLight can currently offer compensation of around $60,000, and that number can grow. The right leader will be willing to steward and develop ministry partnerships, including outside support, and the additional support he raises can increase his total compensation over time. ValleyLight already has meaningful partner relationships, including several larger churches. The next pastor will inherit some of those relationships and will need to strengthen and grow them, and those partners will be looking to him to determine whether and how they continue partnering with ValleyLight. A big part of the role is about partnership development, vision casting, and support raising.

Qualifications at a Glance 
  • Five or more years of vocational ministry experience preferred; church planting experience is a strong plus 
  • No formal education requirement; ministry fruit, character, and experience carry more weight than a degree 
  • Alignment with, or a genuine appreciation for, Southern Baptist Convention doctrine and practice 
  • A track record of discipling people and building teams and leaders, not just running programs 
  • Willingness to raise and steward support: you do not need to arrive as an experienced fundraiser, but you must be willing to learn how to cast vision, build trust with partners, steward relationships, and help raise outside support when needed 
  • A missionary mindset and a church planter's heart, with the creativity and resourcefulness to lead a mobile church without everything already built 
  • Willing and called to live in West Valley City/Magna 

ValleyLight is not simply hiring someone to pastor a 140-person church. We are looking for someone who can see the foundation of a much larger work and help develop the partnerships, systems, and leadership needed to get there. The foundation is here and the community doors are open. What ValleyLight needs is the right long-term leader to pull the pieces together, strengthen systems, develop leaders, grow partnerships, disciple new believers, and help ValleyLight mature without losing its missionary edge. 



About the Community: West Valley City & Magna

West Valley City, Utah's second-largest city, is nestled in the Salt Lake Valley between the Wasatch and Oquirrh mountain ranges. The city's scenic beauty is enhanced by its sense of community and grit. 

More than 137,000 people call West Valley City home, and it's one of the most diverse communities in the state, nearly evenly split between Anglo and Hispanic residents, with meaningful Asian and Pacific Islander populations as well. The city is still writing its own story. ValleyLight sees that as an invitation: the church has a real opportunity to help shape what West Valley City becomes, not just serve a community that already knows who it is. 

Magna, our neighboring community, has an identity all its own. It is an old mining community with a working-class, small-town identity, and it carries its pride and independence today. It's the kind of place where neighbors know each other and are proud to call Magna home. 

That's really the character of the whole area: you can live in a big metro and still feel like you're in a small town. West Valley City sits just 15 to 20 minutes from downtown Salt Lake City, close enough for a Utah Jazz or Utah Mammoth game at the Delta Center, a Real Salt Lake match, or a night out downtown, and just minutes from Salt Lake City International Airport. West Valley is also one of the major concert and event hubs of the Salt Lake Valley, with the Maverik Center and the Utah First Credit Union Amphitheater bringing big concerts and events right into the city. 

Outdoor life here is hard to beat. Six world-class ski resorts, Alta, Snowbird, Brighton, Solitude, Park City, and Deer Valley, are within about 45 minutes, and the Great Salt Lake and Utah's mountain lakes offer boating, fishing, and hiking most of the year. Hogle Zoo is about 30 minutes away, and families have their pick of three major universities in the area, the University of Utah, Utah Valley University, and BYU, for sports, arts, and events. Whether it's a winter weekend on the slopes or a summer afternoon at the lake, there's rarely a reason to leave the valley to find something to do. 

For the right pastor, West Valley City and Magna offer something rare: a genuine, still forming mission field inside one of the fastest-growing metro areas in the country, with big-city amenities a short drive away and small-town relationships right outside the door.

Area Ministry Director for InterMountain Area - Rocky Mountain Region (Undergraduate Ministry)

Work Location:

Utah

Job Type:

Full time

An Area Director leads and oversees a ministry team to plant and to grow witnessing communities of students and faculty who follow Jesus on college and university campuses. Through these groups, we believe ever-increasing numbers of students and faculty from all ethnic groups and areas of the campus will be transformed by the gospel. We expect to see campuses increasingly become places where people, ideas, and structures flourish for the common good and to the glory of God. We confidently anticipate that our InterVarsity alumni will be growing disciples and change agents across the country and around the world.

We will be hiring for both an Area Ministry Director and an Associate Area Ministry Director. Part time to Full time hours will be negotiated upon hire. Start date for both positions are July 1, 2027.

As specified below, this is a support-raised position. Like all of our staff, you will build a team of ministry partners (individuals and churches) whose financial support resources your salary and ministry expenses.

ESSENTIAL COMMITMENTS/RESPONSIBILITIES

1. Spiritual Growth

The Area Ministry Director models spiritual maturity as a disciple of Jesus Christ so that your life and work increasingly reflects a growing love for God, God’s Word, God’s people of every ethnicity and culture, and God’s purposes in the world.

  • Pursue a vibrant relationship with the triune God through engagement with Scripture, prayer, and worship, both individually and in community
  • Exercise self-leadership (growing in self-awareness, self-management, relational integrity, and resiliency)
  • Embrace and practice Scriptural standards for behavior and attitudes, including those described in the Code of Conduct

​2. Campus Ministry Leadership

As an Area Director, you inspire, coach and develop campus staff ministers (“ministers”), students, faculty, and ministry partners to increase the number of witnessing communities, as well as the size, health, spiritual maturity, and campus-wide influence of existing witnessing communities by being a:

Visionary Guide:

  • Create a culture of dependence on God to gain vision for establishing and advancing witnessing communities that reach every corner of every campus in your area
  • Model InterVarsity’s vision and Core Values for supervisees
  • Lead staff, students, and faculty through Scripture, prayer, teaching and discipleship experiences in a way that motivates and shapes their ministry around vision
  • Set appropriate annual goals through prayer, research and reflection with your teams

Structural Architect:

  • Lead your team to develop and implement plans to achieve ministry goals
  • Adapt the plan as needed through rhythms of action, reflection and evaluation
  • Develop, align and leverage programs and structures to move the mission forward

Missional Developer:

  • Recruit a diversity of qualified minister candidates
  • Develop ministers to spiritually grow in Christ in intimacy, like Christ in character, and with Christ in his mission to current and new campuses
  • Develop ministers professionally so that they are consistently increasing their gifts and skills as ministry leaders
  • Supervise ministers, using appropriate leadership style for the individual and situation, to help them accomplish assigned tasks. This will require coaching, assessing, correcting and affirming job-related behaviors
  • Proactively establish and develop healthy relationships across racial, ethnic, national background, and gender barriers with staff, students, faculty, and ministry partners to build effective and diverse communities
  • Build an effective minister team that collaborates well and accomplishes goals

3. Organizational Collaboration

As an Area Director, you are part of a national organization and work in partnership with local, area, divisional, regional, and national InterVarsity ministers and volunteers.

  • Participate in regional leadership as determined by the Regional Director, to set ministry vision and strategies, contribute to accomplishing plans, and provide regional leadership in specific areas
  • Positively and constructively respond to the direction and coaching of line supervisors
  • Build productive ministry partnerships with regional and national collaborative leaders
  • Establish systems, processes and protocols to fulfill regular operational and administrative tasks in a timely manner (reporting, finances, human resources, etc.)
  • Maintain sound financial status of the area through management of budgeting, expense control and ministry partnership development
  • Become familiar with and comply with all InterVarsity policies and procedures

4. Ministry Partnership Development (MPD)

As an Area Director, you will develop a team of partners who will resource the ministry financially, in prayer, or with volunteer service that advances the mission.

  • Develop and maintain a ministry among partners who will fund InterVarsity
  • Ensure ministry budget is fully funded
  • Supervise each minister’s MPD (collaborating with coaches when applicable) and equip staff to build ministry partners
  • Build resource networks with alumni, volunteers, churches, advocacy councils, and major donors, in particular to fund low-network ministers
  • Communicate regularly with ministry partners

5. Accomplish all other assigned tasks as appropriate

QUALIFICATIONS

  • Annually affirm InterVarsity’s Statement of Agreement (Doctrinal Basis and Purpose Statement). Abide by InterVarsity’s Code of Conduct
  • Bachelor’s degree required
  • Minimum three years campus ministry or equivalent work experience required
  • Strong ministry skills (including the ability to communicate spiritual vision, teach spiritual and biblical principles, plan ministry programs, and spiritually disciple, coach and mentor)
  • Proven ability to work well with others and the ability to develop a team of campus ministers.
  • Strong interpersonal skills (including ability to minister to diverse ethnic communities and faculty)
  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills
  • Demonstrated problem solving skills
  • Familiarity with word processing, presentation, email, and spreadsheet software

WORK ENVIRONMENT/PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS

The AD position leads ministry in a college campus environment. A designated office space may or may not be available. The AD is required to travel to on-campus and off-campus sites as appropriate. Off-campus travel includes, but is not limited to student ministry conferences, MPD meetings, and InterVarsity-sponsored training sessions, meetings, and conferences. The AD is regularly required to communicate with others, and routinely uses standard office equipment such as computers, phones, etc.

Pay Range: $56,844.00 - $75,792.00 per year

Pay: This position is funded through personal fundraising. Accordingly, compensation will vary based on the ability of the individual to secure a donor team to fund the cost of his/her salary. The anticipated salary range for this position on a full-time basis (40 hours/week) is dependent on a variety of factors, including location and cost of living. The actual salary received, including any geographic adjustment to account for location and cost of living, is subject to the individual’s ability to raise funds necessary to cover the full amount of such salary within the range set forth in the job posting details.

Benefits:

We offer a competitive benefits package, including health care and retirement savings with a match. Eligibility is based on employee type and hours worked.  Benefits include the following:

  • 403(b) Retirement Savings Plan

  • 403(b) matching contributions

  • Dental insurance

  • Employee assistance program

  • Employee discounts

  • Flexible work schedule

  • Flexible spending accounts

  • Health insurance

  • Health savings account

  • Life insurance

  • Paid time off

  • Parental leave

  • Professional development assistance

  • Vision insurance

Equal Employment Opportunity: 

 

InterVarsity Christian Fellowship/USA is both an equal opportunity employer and a faith-based religious organization. We conduct hiring without regard to race, color, ancestry, national origin, citizenship, age, sex, marital status, parental status, membership in any labor organization, political ideology, or disability of an otherwise qualified individual. The status of InterVarsity Christian Fellowship/USA as an equal opportunity employer does not prevent the organization from hiring staff based on their religious beliefs so that all staff share the same religious commitment.  Pursuant to the Civil Rights Act of 1964, Section 702 (42 U.S.C. 2000e 1(a)) InterVarsity Christian Fellowship/USA has the right to, and does, hire only candidates who agree with InterVarsity’s Statement of Agreement: Purpose and Doctrinal Basis because InterVarsity believes that each and every staff plays a vital role in advancing InterVarsity’s mission and purposes.

Director of Children's and Youth Ministries - Barrington United Methodist Church
 

Summary of Position

The Barrington United Methodist Church Director of Children and Youth Ministries is a servant leader, supporting the mission and vision of the church through the development and implementation of ministries, classes, programs and events that introduce children to their identity as children of God, that bring children, youth, and their families into relationship with one another and as the family of God, and that support the faith development of children from birth through young adult.

This is a part-time, exempt position reporting to the Sr. Pastor - approximately 20-25 hours per week; Sundays and Christian holidays required, as well as some evenings and weekends.

Position Responsibilities

The Director of Children & Youth Ministries works with staff and ministry areas to meet the needs and guide the spiritual growth of children, youth and their families from birth through young adult.

* Understands and supports the vision of church leadership and aligns programming with the BUMC mission, vision, and values.

* Prepares and manages an annual budget, providing documentation and receipts for all expenditures.

* Supervises the Children’s Ministry Assistant and Family Event Coordinator(s).

* Attends staff meetings, church leadership meetings, and other meetings as deemed necessary.

* Works to ensure programming provides a cohesive, cradle to college program.

* Develops, implements and oversees Sunday morning programming for children through high school, which includes planning themes for the year, decorating the room and preparing all crafts and lessons.

* Selects, develops and/or writes curriculum for children / youth that is age appropriate and in alignment with United Methodist theology.

* Incorporates best faith formation practices across the age and program continuum.

* Creates a safe environment for all children and youth who attend any ministry function through Barrington United Methodist Church, and takes appropriate actions to protect them from harm, including but not limited to follow the Safe Sanctuary Policy adopted by Barrington United Methodist Church.

* Supervises, schedules and trains BUMC staff and volunteers that work with children and youth. Provides, updates and maintains Safe Gatherings training and background checks for all Staff and Volunteers.

* Effectively invites, engages and manages volunteers, equipping them to serve in ways that merge their passions, skills, and strengths with the needs of the church.

* Develops and implements a nurturing environment in the nursery for infants and toddlers and their families.

* Develops, implements, and oversees family events; event programming for tweens (3rd – 5th grade); event programming for Youth (6th -12th grade). Plan Group Events and age appropriate activities for all children, youth and young adults. This entails planning, shopping, decorating, setting up, running the event, clean up and tear down.

* Leads the Confirmation program for Barrington United Methodist Church under the direction of the Senior Pastor, and follows the guidelines outlined by the United Methodist Church.

* Implements, creates and oversees annual Vacation Bible School as a faith development, community building and evangelism opportunity for the children and families. This event entails: planning, organizing and decorating areas used throughout the church, preparing all materials, training volunteers, and set up / clean up each day.

* Encourages and supports children and youth to participate in all facets of the community of faith at Barrington United Methodist Church, including but not limited to worship, Sunday School, Bible studies, family and youth activities, service projects, music programs, the acolyte program and ushering, etc.

* Maintains open lines of communication with Pastoral staff to communicate pastoral care concerns and needs of children, youth and families.

* Be an integral part of the worshiping community of Barrington United Methodist Church.

 

Qualifications

Previous experience in education

Able to pass a thorough background check

Safe Sanctuaries certification within 3 months of employment

Computer skills and proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite, Adobe, Canva

Self-motivated, creative, energetic; strong organizational skills

Ability to attract and lead volunteers

Experience planning and leading short-term mission trips strongly desired

Must be Christian and have a growing faith through a personal relationship with Jesus Christ.

Have, or be willing to gain education in Methodist Theology from the United Methodist Church

 

Education

Bachelor’s Degree - preferably in Christian Education, Early Childhood Education or Elementary Education; or extensive related experience

 

About Barrington United Methodist Church:

We are a welcoming, vibrant congregation dedicated to embodying grace and hospitality. We believe we are beloved children of God and exist to experience and share His love.

How to Apply: Please submit a cover letter and resume.  Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis until the position is filled.

An Equal Opportunity Employer

Westwood’s Way of Life:

Be and love like Jesus


Westwood’s Purpose and Mission: 

To know God and share Jesus through loving others here, near, and far


Role:

The Groups and Engagement Pastor provides pastoral and strategic leadership to help adults move from attendance to belonging, from belonging to discipleship, and from discipleship to mission. This role exists to connect people into small groups, discipleship environments, serving opportunities, and relational pathways where they can be known, cared for, challenged, and formed in the way of Jesus.

This is a key pastoral role at Westwood. The Groups and Engagement Pastor champions small groups as a primary environment for adult discipleship, care, and community. This person helps ensure that no one falls through the cracks, that leaders are equipped and supported, and that Westwood continues to become a church where people are known, connected, and invited to be and love like Jesus.


Responsibilities:

     · Serve as a Pastor at-large of Westwood Community Church, participating in staff meetings, retreats, all-church functions, pastoral care and counsel, teaching, officiating church ordinances, weddings, and funerals as assigned, and serving on a pastor-on-call rotation.

     · Lead, develop, and manage Westwood’s Engagement Ministry, with primary emphasis on small groups as a central environment for adult discipleship, care, and belonging.

     · Build and strengthen a small group culture where people are invited into biblical community, spiritual formation, mutual care, and missional living.

     · Recruit, equip, coach, and care for small group leaders, coaches, and other key lay leaders.  

     · Develop systems for launching new groups, strengthening existing groups, identifying new leaders, and multiplying healthy discipleship environments.

     · Provide pastoral oversight and strategic alignment for men’s and women’s ministry, with an emphasis on connecting these ministries to ongoing small group engagement and discipleship.

     · Provide strategic development, implementation, and oversight for Westwood’s adult discipleship pathway.

     · Design and lead large-funnel engagement experiences that help people move from worship attendance or initial connection into deeper community, discipleship, serving, and mission.

     · Partner with campus pastors and ministry leaders to create clear next steps for new attenders, regular attenders, members, and those seeking greater connection.

     · Develop systems that help identify, follow up with, and care for people who are new, disconnected, spiritually seeking, or in need of pastoral connection.

     · Use data, stories, pastoral insight, and ministry feedback to evaluate engagement trends, group health, leader needs, and gaps in connection.

     · Ensure ministry areas are using lay leaders who are trained in Volunteer Development and aligned with Westwood’s Leadership Pathway.

     · Assist in the development of the annual ministry plan through objectives, budgets, and measurable ministry goals.

     · Collaborate with campus pastors as the central voice for groups and engagement ministry.

     · Participate with ministry peers in implementing Westwood’s mission, vision, and strategy.

     · Serve on leadership teams, work groups, and carry out other responsibilities as assigned by the Supervisor or Lead Pastor.

     · Align to and live out the Westwood Staff Values:

        o Head High

        o Heart Soft

        o Arms Linked

        o Feet Forward


Relationships:

     · Reports to the Executive Pastor of Ministries.

     · Supervises and collaborates with ministry area staff, as assigned.

     · Oversees ministry area volunteers and lay leaders.

     · Works closely with campus pastors, adult ministry leaders, care ministry leaders, connections teams, and other pastor/director staff.

     · Interacts regularly with Westwood staff, congregation members, small group leaders, volunteers, new attenders, and ministry participants.

· Someone who lives a life that honors God in heart, actions, and relationships, with the goal of becoming more like Jesus

· Bachelor’s degree required. Seminary degree preferred, in process, or equivalent theological training and ministry experience.

· Demonstrated ability to pastor, shepherd, counsel, and care for people with wisdom, maturity, and grace.

· Ability to teach and preach the Word of God effectively.

· Demonstrated passion for discipleship, biblical community, leadership development, and helping people take next steps in following Jesus.

· Demonstrated results in building, leading, and multiplying small groups or adult discipleship environments.

· Demonstrated ability to design and implement ministry systems, pathways, and scalable engagement strategies.

· Strong relational instincts and excellent interpersonal communication skills with a wide variety of audiences.

· Ability to recruit, develop, supervise, coach, and care for employees, volunteers, and ministry leaders.

· Demonstrated ability to work within a highly interdependent church ministry model.

· Proficient with Microsoft Office tools.

· Ability to handle confidential information in a professional and pastoral manner.

· Endorse and support Westwood’s Statement of Faith and traditional orthodox evangelical theology.

  • Lead Campus Staff -  Pastor, care, and lead the campus staff and equip them to develop leaders and multiply volunteers. Includes leading staff meetings, create feedback/evaluation mechanisms, department goal setting, team accountability, ministry alignment, etc.
  • Leadership Development - Work to build up the leadership pipeline of your campus and continually develop and mobilize volunteer leaders to serve with their gifts. The priority for a CP to mobilize high level leaders over every main ministry area.
  • Shepherd the Echo DNA - Lead your campus in proactively moving toward the Echo.Church visionary goals, embracing Echo values, and prioritizing Echo main strategies.  See Echo’s playbook here.
  • Weekend Readiness - Ensure all weekend services are executed with excellence in all areas (worship, kids, guest experience etc.). Work to remove every obstacle or distraction that could keep the campus from growing.
  • Stage Communication - Prayerfully and adequately prepare how you or those you develop will cast vision during the Welcome and Next Steps Sunday moment, always helping people take practical steps.  Prayerfully get familiar with every Sunday message and be available and ready to occasionally teach. Contribute to team teaching meetings and teach locally when needed.  
  • Echo Group Development - Prioritize the development of Echo Groups and discipleship on your campus by working with the Groups department to recruit, train, and release people to lead. The adult attendance in groups should stay above 70% of weekend adult attendance, with the goal of 80%+.
  • Connection & Follow up - Weekly connect (phone/text/zoom…) with first time guests and those committing to take next steps. Lead the campus connection strategy and process. Volunteer sign-ups, group sign ups, decisions to get baptized…
  • Community Engagement & Evangelism - Build relationships with lost people, city staff, business leaders, church leaders, entrepreneurs, and others in the community surrounding your campus. 
  • Oversee Campus Online Presence and Strategy - the management of your Campus online presence, other advertising/marketing, and all local marketing (signs, billboards, banners, mailers, etc.). This is done in conjunction with our Communications Director.
  • Manage Campus Budget - Set campus budget and ensure that your campus departments are staying within it, tracking reports, and planning expenses effectively. 
  • Other - Benevolence requests, model discipleship, develop marketing and evangelism strategies, plan community outreach events, manage campus facilities, pioneer giving initiatives...

Key Campus Health Indicators

A Campus Pastor should carefully monitor and ensure the integrity of the following data points, which are indicators of health at their campus.

  1. Activate attendance and follow up
  1. Sunday Attendance
  2. Giving Totals and First Time Givers
  3. Groups Sign-ups & Attendance (80%+ signed up per semester, 80% attending average)
  4. First Time Decisions to Follow Jesus
  5. First Time Guests
  6. Second Time Guests
  7. Baptisms (10:1 adult to baptisms annually)
  8. Volunteers Serving (15-20% of adult attendance serving weekly)
  9. Community Engagement 

Weekly / bi-weekly tasks:

  • Follow up with first time guests and those who indicated taking next steps (salvation, baptism, volunteer, life groups).
  • Participate in weekend planning meetings. 
  • Prepare and run campus staff meetings and direct reports with campus staff.
  • Lead staff in making and evaluating quarterly goals in light of overall church goals.
  • Meet with key leaders, donors, and volunteers for development and care.

Click here to learn more about Campus Pastor Rhythms

Echo.Church ministerial duties of all commissioned, licensed and ordained ministers includes:

  • Praying and giving spiritual advice for others
  • Leading others to worship by helping them serve with their gifts
  • Teaching and leading Echo Groups
  • Sharing the Gospel message with clarity
  • Teaching, instructing, or organizing religious initiatives
  • Performing baptisms, serving communion, performing wedding ceremonies and funerals.

Program Outline

The Catalyst Church Residency exists to equip and deploy future church leaders. It is a 1-2 year program during which you will be a full-time member of the Catalyst Church Staff Team. Your assigned areas of ministry will depend on your residency track, giftings, passions, and areas of need within Catalyst Church. While not required, we recommend that you take 2-3 seminary classes each semester and provide you hours during the work week to do some homework!

Residency Tracks

  • College Staff Track: The university campus is a ripe mission field and a potent mission force. Our Catalyst College team functions as a missionary and disciple-making team at CNU. This track is for recent college graduates seeking to give their first 1-2 years to the mission of God on the university campus and who may or may not be called into lifelong vocational ministry. We hope you will join our efforts to see a disciple-making, church-planting movement explode from Newport News.
  • Ministry Staff Track: You will be placed in an area of ministry within the church (ie, Worship, Community Groups, Kids, Serving Teams, etc). You will have meaningful responsibility within the church, incredible learning experiences on a church staff, and the opportunity to gain a theological education. This track is for those with little to no theological education and vocational ministry experience.
  • Pastoral Track: The church in America has a shortage of qualified men to lead and serve as pastors. This track develops men into godly leaders who sense a calling to pastoral ministry, some theological training, and some ministry experience. This track is similar in many ways to the Ministry Staff track, with added elder development, teaching, and preaching opportunities.

Next Steps

Click on "Apply to Position" to show your interest. Following an initial screening, we will send you the rest of the application to move forward.

*This is a support-based position. You will need to be eligible for employment in the US to apply for this position.

Description

The LCMS Mission
"In grateful response to God's grace and empowered by the Holy Spirit through Word and Sacraments, the mission of The Lutheran Church—Missouri Synod is vigorously to make known the love of Christ by word and deed within our churches, communities, and world."

Department Profile

The Office of International Mission, which relates to the Board for International Mission and implements its policies, is 
responsible to the President of the Synod through the Chief Mission Officer for the work of the Synod in foreign countries as stated in the Bylaws.

Reporting Relationships

  • The position reports to the Area Facilitator.
  • Works closely with the LCMS Communication staff to inform and involve LCMS constituents in a meaningful way in the work of the OIM on the field through support-building, newsletter-writing and home-service presentation reporting

Essential Job Functions

  • Commit to an ongoing schedule and strategy for ministry support raising, (Network Support Model) Orientation and initial support building is typically six (6) months.
  • Communicate via monthly newsletter to and maintain a relationship with the sending church that includes Together-In-Mission (TIM) congregations as well as other supporting churches, groups, and individuals. 
  • Complete missionary training and language acquisition plan under the direction of the Regional Director and the Director of Missionary Services.
  • Communicate the OIM mission strategy and work clearly and effectively.
  • Serve as a church planter in cooperation with the church partner.
  • Preach, teach, and administer the Sacraments in the congregations and missions of the country according to the needs of the ministry team.
  • Travel and present/teach at conferences, continuing education modules, or intensive courses within or beyond the assigned church body as requested by the OIM supervisor.
  • Support the development of local-language theological materials.
  • Advocate for the school and students with partners and potential partners of the church.
  • Mentor future pastors in theology and practice.
  • Theological Education:  He will assist in the identifying and training of congregational leadership (pastors and deaconesses) in conjunction with the regional seminary.
  • If authorized for altar and pulpit ministry in the local church, support pastors in providing Word and Sacrament ministry to underserved congregations.
  • Travel and present/teach at conferences, continuing education modules, or intensive courses within or beyond the assigned church body as requested by the OIM supervisor.
  • This position may travel up to 15% of the time.

Education and Experience

  • An ordained and rostered pastor of the Lutheran Church—Missouri Synod.
  • Master of Divinity degree or equivalent required.
  • Pastoral, cross-cultural and Lutheran church planting experience preferred.

Competencies (Knowledge, Skills and Abilities)

  • An active member of the LCMS, an LCMS congregation or a congregation of any of its partner churches and personal faithfulness to the Holy Scriptures and the Lutheran Confessions.
  • Solid comprehension of confessional Lutheran theology and ability to clearly articulate same.
  • Demonstrated adaptability and flexibility to live and work in a second culture.
  • Demonstrated resilience and ability to effectively implement, complete and report on a project.
  • Ability to function effectively in a team setting.
  • Interpersonal relationship skills that will facilitate initiating and maintaining relationships with people both within and outside the church.
  • Ability to initiate and maintain relationships with people of another culture.
  • Good physical, mental, emotional, social and spiritual health with the ability to carry on sustained work in international setting.
  • Demonstrated skill in communication, both oral and written.
  • Ability to utilize standard technology on the field – laptop, smartphone, and basic connectivity troubleshooting.
  • Ability to use the Microsoft Office suite, particularly Microsoft Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and the email functions and calendar functions of Microsoft Outlook. 
  • Demonstrated ILR 2+ proficiency in local Language preferred. If not proficient, a willingness to participate in a language learning program to achieve such proficiency.

Supervisory Responsibility

  • None

The Assistant Teacher supports the classroom team in delivering high-quality, developmentally appropriate, and Christ-centered care and instruction for children. Working under the direction of the Academy Leadership and with the support of Lead Teachers, the Assistant Teacher helps maintain a nurturing, safe, and engaging environment that reflects Lionheart’s mission, values, and commitment to children. This role is ideal for team members who have a heart to serve, a desire to grow professionally, and a passion for early childhood education and ministry.
 

Classroom Support & Instruction

Team Collaboration

  • Partner closely with the Lead Teacher to ensure smooth daily operations and a joyful, unified classroom culture.
  • Communicate proactively with the other staff regarding classroom needs, child updates, and support required.
  • Demonstrate flexibility in assisting other classrooms or academy-wide needs when requested.
  • Participate in staff meetings, required trainings, and academy events.

Family Engagement

  • Greet families warmly and maintain positive, Christ-centered relationships.
  • Provide basic daily communication as requested by the Lead Teacher or Academy Leadership.

Academy and Operational Support

  • At least 18 years of age; high school diploma or GED required.

  • Alignment with Lionheart’s mission and values.
  • Positive peer and family relationships; willingness to grow and receive coaching.

Competencies

  • Teamwork & Collaboration: Works cooperatively with staff and leadership.

Skills

  • Curriculum Support: Helps facilitate classroom activities and routines.

job_name: Director of Worship  Arts - Christ Community Church
post_html:
Christ Community Church in Rochester, Minnesota is seeking a genuine, humble, passionate leader for the worship ministries of our church.

The primary goal of the Director of Worship & Arts (DWA) is to help people meet and follow Jesus utilizing music, media, and other artistic expression. The DWA will lead all things worship and production at CCC, and will recruit and develop other leaders to share the stage and the ministry. The ideal candidate will be very proficient vocally and on at least one instrument and will have demonstrated skills in team-building, conducting rehearsals and collaborative worship service planning. They will need at least a working knowledge of AV tech for trouble-shooting and problem-solving purposes and to have experience with ProPresenter, Ableton, Lightkey, and ProLogic.

Church and Community Overview

Christ Community Church is part of the Christian and Missionary Alliance denomination, and are intentionally living into our vision statement to be a church of generous people who honor Jesus, love each other, and serve our neighbors. We have 3 services with about 1100 people participating each weekend. We would describe our church’s worship culture as sincere and responsive and we enjoy the Lord’s presence together when we are gathered for worship.

Rochester, MN is a community of about 150,000 people, home to Mayo Clinic, and consistently recognized as one of the best places to live in the United States.

Education & Experience

  • An undergraduate degree in worship ministries or other creative field is preferred.
  • Strategic and creative leader with 3-5 years of relevant leadership experience.
  • Excellent leadership, organizational, and communication skills.
  • Effective team builder with high emotional intelligence.
  • Experience in a larger church is strongly preferred.
  • Proven ability to design effective worship services that are relevant, excellent, intentional, and effective in helping CCC accomplish its mission.
  • Alignment with the Christian & Missionary Alliance and a willingness to pursue licensing.

Personal Characteristics, Skill & Knowledge

  • Have a strong, mature, and growing faith in Jesus.
  • Be passionate for and believe in the local church.
  • Be “above reproach” in character and conduct of life.
  • Care deeply about people who do not know Jesus being introduced to Him.
  • Demonstrate humility and curiosity where answers are unknown or uncertain.
  • Be able to lead worship from an instrument.
  • Be able to read music and direct musicians.
  • Have high emotional intelligence.
  • Genuinely love people.
  • Have a sense of humor.
  • Develop processes and systems so that things run smoothly (and so that there is margin for when they don’t).
  • Be a team player.
  • Have a creative eye and be able to develop and strategize new creative initiatives for the well-being of the ministry.
  • Know how to coach others while remaining coachable.
  • Possess strong change-leadership and change-management skills.

Responsibilities Include

  • Champion the mission and vision of Christ Community Church.
  • Be responsible for leading the Worship & Arts Ministry to an ever-increasing level of engagement and excellence.
  • Develop other worship leaders for the stage.
  • Recruit, train, schedule, and coordinate necessary teams and team leaders for all services.
  • Schedule and oversee rehearsals for all teams.
  • Lead worship service planning process.
  • Meet regularly with worship, tech, and arts teams for discipleship, relationship building, planning, and troubleshooting.
  • Provide leadership, mentorship and guidance for kidcity and Impact worship leaders and teams.
  • Assist in additional services held on campus (weddings, funerals, seasonal events – these are pretty minimal).
  • Maintain and upgrade (as needed) sound, music, and video equipment.
  • Create short and long-term plans for maintenance and improvements for all technical equipment.

Staff Relationships

  • The DWA will report to the Lead Pastor and collaborate with the Communications Team and other staff members as needed.
  • The DWA will provide leadership for the Tech Director and Student Impact worship leader.

We will provide you with

  • A helpful on-boarding experience.
  • Clarity on expectations, responsibilities, and authority.
  • A positive working environment and a healthy team atmosphere.
  • A sufficient ministry budget.
  • Personal & professional development opportunities.
  • A competitive salary and benefits package commensurate with your experience.

To Apply

If you would like to begin the conversation about this ministry opportunity, please email your resume and links to videos that demonstrate your vocal and musical proficiency, along with anything else you would want us to know about you at this stage of the process, to worshipsearch@cccrochester.org.

To be considered for this position, please complete the application to include your testimony, resume and other background information related to the position.

If the district office has reviewed your application and they think you may be a potential match for the position, that the hiring manager will reach out to you for next steps.

This position may require licensing with The Christian & Missionary Alliance. To learn more about The Alliance and requirements for licensing, please visit our website

Please do not contact the church directly.

post_html:
Campus Staff Minister - Northern California (Graduate & Faculty Ministry)

Work Location:

California Northern

Job Type:

Full time

God has called InterVarsity to plant and to build witnessing communities of students and faculty who follow Jesus on college and university campuses. Through these groups, we believe ever- increasing numbers of students and faculty from all ethnic groups and areas of the campus will be transformed by the Gospel. We expect to see campuses increasingly become places where people, ideas, and structures flourish to the glory of God. We confidently anticipate that our InterVarsity alumni will become change agents across the country and around the world. We pursue this calling by discerning and actively participating in what God is already doing on campus. This is the essence of being a Campus Staff Minister (CSM).

Please submit the GFM Interest Form before completing the full application for a position with Graduate & Faculty Ministries in our online system. We will contact you when we are ready to proceed with the application process.​ 

This position is open to applicants working less than 40 hours/week. If you are interested in part-time work please apply for this position.  Additional pay (as a geographic adjustment) is available in high cost of living areas.

The pay range listed is for an employee working 40 hours/week at CSM level II. Pay will be prorated for employees who work less than 40 hours/week. 

Volunteer opportunities range from prayer and hospitality to leading a campus fellowship of graduate students and faculty. People who are interested in volunteering will go through an application and interview process, however, volunteer openings are not posted at the job opportunities link above. For more information, talk with a local InterVarsity staff or staff director.

We have positions in the following locations:

  • UC Davis - graduate students

  • UC San Francisco - graduate students

  • UC Santa Cruz - graduate students

ESSENTIAL COMMITMENTS/RESPONSIBILITIES

Spiritual Growth

As a Campus Staff Minister, you pursue maturity as a disciple of Jesus Christ so that your life and work increasingly reflects a growing love for God, God’s Word, God’s people of every ethnicity and culture, and God’s purposes in the world. To do this, you will:

  • Pursue a vibrant relationship with the triune God through engagement with Scripture, prayer, and worship, both individually and in community
  • Develop self-leadership (growing in self-awareness, self-management, relational integrity, and resiliency)
  • Embrace Scriptural standards for behavior and attitudes

2.Campus Leadership

As a Campus Staff Minister, you increase the number of witnessing communities, as well as the size, health, spiritual maturity, and campus-wide influence of existing witnessing communities of students and faculty by being a:

  • Visionary Guide:

You communicate and model InterVarsity’s vision to see students and faculty transformed, campuses renewed and world changers developed

  • Create a culture of humble dependence on God and bold expectation in God’s intention to start new witnessing communities throughout the campus and on new campuses
  • Model – in person and through programs – InterVarsity’s vision and Core Values, including a biblically-defined commitment to engage every ethnic and social group on campus
  • Lead students and faculty – individually and collectively – through Scripture, prayer, teaching, and discipleship experiences, so that they articulate and align their ministry activities around this vision
  • Set annual goals through prayer, research and reflection with your teams (students, faculty, and staff) for qualitative and quantitative growth, including conversions and leadership development
  • Structural Architect:

You create, develop, align and leverage ministry plans, programs, teams, and structures to close the gap between current reality and the aspirational goals.

  • Build leadership teams who trust and partner well with you and who demonstrate spiritual vitality, relational health, and mission alignment
  • Develop and execute plans to achieve annual goals, evaluating and modifying the plan as needed throughout the year
  • Increase momentum for the vision by aligning programs, structures, conferences and teams around the goals
  • Mobilize students and faculty to engage their relational networks with the gospel and to start new missional communities
  • Under the direction of the Area Director, may supervise Ministry Interns and Campus Ministry Interns as delegated
  • Missional Developer:

You intentionally gather, invite, and develop diverse groups of students and faculty so that they not only encounter and follow Jesus as Savior and Lord but also advance the mission on campus as participants and leaders.

  • Create ways for faculty and students to encounter and follow Jesus through Scripture, worship, prayer, mission experiences, conferences, etc.
  • Equip students and faculty so that they think strategically about campus engagement and so that they proclaim – in word, deed, and power – the good news of Jesus, regularly inviting students and faculty to follow him as Savior and Lord
  • Disciple students and faculty by equipping them to hear the Word, respond actively, and debrief and interpret the experience so that they grow in Christlikeness, reflect our Core Values, and develop ministry skills
  • Invite, coach, and equip students and faculty to become increasingly effective participants and leaders, including starting new witnessing communities on campuses

3.Organizational Collaboration

As a Campus Staff Minister, you have joined a national mission. Therefore, you work with a network of other local, area, regional, and national InterVarsity staff and volunteers so that our work reflects Biblical standards of excellence, integrity, and partnership.

  • Partner with and respond positively to the direction and coaching of your supervisors and national leaders
  • Contribute to collaborative and productive team meetings and relationships
  • Affiliate chapters under your care and submit Graduating Student Forms in order to increase our partnership with current students and alumni
  • Use national ministry resources and tools, as requested, including recruiting and/or participating in local, regional, or national conferences as required
  • Complete reporting, planning and review requirements in a timely way so that you and your supervisors can assess and improve your work as a CSM
  • Comply with all InterVarsity policies and procedures

4.Ministry Partnership Development

As a Campus Staff Minister, you will develop a team of partners – churches and individuals (including alumni and community members) – who will resource the ministry financially, in prayer, or volunteer service that advances the mission.

  • Raise 100% of the financial budget assigned by your supervisor
  • Communicate regularly with your ministry partners, nurturing the relationship through visits, phone calls, emails and regular prayer letters
  • Develop on-going, long-lasting partnership with alumni and volunteers
  • Comply with all Ministry Partnership Policies
  • Identify and invest in advocates who will build networks of volunteers and donors on InterVarsity’s behalf

5.Accomplish all other assigned tasks as appropriate

QUALIFICATIONS (common to all levels of CSM)

  • Annually affirm InterVarsity’s Statement of Agreement (Doctrinal Basis and Purpose Statement). Abide by InterVarsity’s Code of Conduct. Believe and behave consonantly with InterVarsity’s Human Sexuality Theological Paper. Affirm and behave consonantly with InterVarsity’s “Women in Ministry Statement of Affirmation”
  • Bachelor’s degree required for CSMs assigned to a four-year campus. A minimum of an Associate’s degree required for CSMs assigned to a two-year campus or a community college
  • Strong interpersonal skills (including ability to minister to diverse ethnic communities and faculty)
  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills
  • Demonstrated problem solving skills
  • Familiarity with word processing, presentation, email, and spreadsheet software

WORK ENVIRONMENT/PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS

The CSM position leads ministry in a college campus environment. A designated office space may or may not be available. The CSM is required to travel to on-campus and off- campus sites as appropriate. Off-campus travel includes, but is not limited to: student ministry conferences, Ministry Partnership Development meetings, and InterVarsity- sponsored training sessions, meetings, and conferences. The CSM is regularly required to communicate with others, and routinely uses standard office equipment such as computers, phones, photocopiers, filing cabinets, etc.

Pay Range: $45,324.00 - $60,420.00 per year

Pay: This position is funded through personal fundraising. Accordingly, compensation will vary based on the ability of the individual to secure a donor team to fund the cost of his/her salary. The anticipated salary range for this position on a full-time basis (40 hours/week) is dependent on a variety of factors, including location and cost of living. The actual salary received, including any geographic adjustment to account for location and cost of living, is subject to the individual’s ability to raise funds necessary to cover the full amount of such salary within the range set forth in the job posting details.

Benefits:

We offer a competitive benefits package, including health care and retirement savings with a match. Eligibility is based on employee type and hours worked.  Benefits include the following:

  • 403(b) Retirement Savings Plan

  • 403(b) matching contributions

  • Dental insurance

  • Employee assistance program

  • Employee discounts

  • Flexible work schedule

  • Flexible spending accounts

  • Health insurance

  • Health savings account

  • Life insurance

  • Paid time off

  • Parental leave

  • Professional development assistance

  • Vision insurance

Equal Employment Opportunity: 

 

InterVarsity Christian Fellowship/USA is both an equal opportunity employer and a faith-based religious organization. We conduct hiring without regard to race, color, ancestry, national origin, citizenship, age, sex, marital status, parental status, membership in any labor organization, political ideology, or disability of an otherwise qualified individual. The status of InterVarsity Christian Fellowship/USA as an equal opportunity employer does not prevent the organization from hiring staff based on their religious beliefs so that all staff share the same religious commitment.  Pursuant to the Civil Rights Act of 1964, Section 702 (42 U.S.C. 2000e 1(a)) InterVarsity Christian Fellowship/USA has the right to, and does, hire only candidates who agree with InterVarsity’s Statement of Agreement: Purpose and Doctrinal Basis because InterVarsity believes that each and every staff plays a vital role in advancing InterVarsity’s mission and purposes.

Peninsula Covenant Church is a growing, dynamic, community-focused church in Redwood City, CA.  The beautiful 16-acre campus serves as host to our worship gatherings, children and adult ministries, community center (including swim and fitness activities), preschool, after-school care, and summer programs and supports numerous partner ministries.  Healthy and successful team members are those who Seek Jesus First, are Humble, Stay Hungry, Extend Grace, and Prioritize Team.  We actively support a culture of collaboration, and kindness across our PCC teams.  Join us in our vision, as we exist to know Jesus deeply, follow Him faithfully, and guide the next generation to do the same.   Come experience what the community of PCC is all about!

VISION OF PCC
To empower generations to passionately follow Jesus one person at a time.

PRINCIPLE OBJECTIVE
The Young Adult Ministry Leader will implement a comprehensive program of Christian life development for the 18 – 32 year old, college, career, single and married adults in our community. It is essential that this person be able to connect with young adults on a social and spiritual level, with the intent of coaching them towards Christ-like maturity. Under the supervision of the Family Ministry Director, this person is the staff point person for PCC’s Young Adult Ministry.

RESPONSIBILITIES
  • In partnership with the Spiritual Formation Pastor develop the missional, spiritual and programmatic direction of Young Adult Ministry.  
  • Assist in recruiting, training and equipping a Young Adult Ministry team.  
  • Give leadership to Young Adult Ministry small groups, events, retreats, and/or mission trips. 
  • Incorporate an externally focused missional approach.
  • Engage in regular prayer and reading to keep heart, soul and passion fresh.  
  • Develop ministry skills and personal leadership under the direction of the Spiritual Formation Pastor and on-going training/education.
  • Provide organizational support to the Ministry including communications, meeting and events coordination, speaker recruitment, etc.
  • Annual budget development and maintenance. 
 COMMITTEE AND MINISTRY TEAM RESPONSIBILITIES
  • Lead volunteer young adult leadership team 
  • Communication, coordination and integration with PCC’s other ministries
SPIRITUAL
  • Profess Jesus Christ as personal Lord and Savior
  • Commitment to God-honoring professionalism, personal spiritual growth, and healthy lifestyle.
  • Model standards and expectations of church leaders within our fellowship, including worship attendance, small group participation, lifestyle of generosity, and serving out of call and giftedness
SKILLS

The Middle School Ministry Coordinator at our Westerville Campus is a full-time position that plays a key role in helping students discover and follow Jesus during one of the most formative seasons of life. This person will provide leadership, organization, and support for Vineyard Columbus' ministry at our Westerville Campus to middle school students, creating environments where students can grow in faith, build meaningful relationships, and experience authentic community. 

Working closely with the VC Students Pastor, the Middle School Ministry Coordinator will lead Sunday morning programming for grades 6–8, support Student Night gatherings on Sunday evenings, develop and care for volunteer leaders, and oversee the administrative systems that help ministry run effectively. This role combines relational ministry with practical leadership, requiring someone who loves students, enjoys developing volunteers, and can bring both creativity and organization to ministry environments. 

This is an exciting opportunity to invest in the next generation by helping students take meaningful steps in their faith while building a safe, engaging, and spiritually formative ministry culture for students and families. 

About us:

Vineyard Columbus exists to develop multiethnic communities of disciples who experience God, love one another, and partner with Christ to heal the world.

As a church, we are committed to being a great friend to our city and to building communities that reflect Christlike unity while celebrating the diversity of our congregation and staff.

Beyond weekend services at multiple locations across Central Ohio, we serve our neighbors through the Vineyard Community Center, which provides free health clinics, food assistance, ESL classes, Value Life resources, a Counseling Center and other practical support—all opportunities to share the love of Jesus in tangible ways.

Who we're looking for:

We are seeking a spiritually mature, team-oriented leader who is passionate about helping middle school students encounter Jesus and grow in their faith. The ideal candidate enjoys building relationships with students, equipping volunteers, and creating environments where young people feel known, valued, and connected. 

This person is equally comfortable building relationships and managing details. They are energized by leading teams, coordinating ministry details, and helping create engaging experiences that are biblically grounded and age appropriate. They thrive in collaborative settings, communicate clearly, and bring a positive, flexible attitude to the changing rhythms of student ministry. They find joy in developing volunteers and empowering others to have a meaningful impact in the lives of students.

Most importantly, this individual demonstrates a genuine love for students, a commitment to personal spiritual growth, and a desire to help the next generation develop a lasting faith in Jesus. 

Desired qualifications:

  • Passion for helping middle school students grow in their relationship with Jesus. 
  • Some experience serving with children, students, or related youth programming.

  • Experience working with diverse students and families from a variety of cultural backgrounds.

  • Demonstrated spiritual maturity and a lifestyle that reflects biblical values. 
  • Strong collaboration skills, dependability, and a commitment to teamwork.
  • Satisfactory background check required for all positions.
