Interested candidates must submit a cover letter and résumé,  for full consideration. Incomplete submissions may not receive the same level of review as complete packets.

 

For any questions or additional information contact Kelly Shumate, HR Generalist/Recruiter at jobs@richmonddiocese.org


The Catholic Diocese of Richmond is seeking an Executive Director of Campus Ministry to serve the Catholic Campus Ministry at James Madison University in Harrisonburg, VA.

 

James Madison University is a public, liberal arts university with an undergraduate population of approximately 20,000 students.  The Director of Campus Ministry is responsible for the development, implementation, and oversight of a comprehensive campus ministry program for the students of the JMU.  Furthermore, these responsibilities include developing student leaders, pastorally responding to student needs, and overseeing student programs and activities. 

 

Additionally, the Director oversees financial accounts, serves as the liaison between the local Catholic parish, furthers development efforts and campaigns, and builds interfaith relationships among the other campus ministries.  The Director also supervises a staff, including a Priest Chaplain, Director of Development, and FOCUS team.


Qualifications:

  • Practicing Catholic in good standing
  • Through knowledge of Church teachings and theology with the ability to relate that knowledge to young adults in a campus ministry setting
  • Familiar with relevant church documents pertaining to ministry and evangelization, specifically:
    • Evangelii Nuntiandi (Evangelization in the Modern World)
    • Redemptoris Missio (Mission of the Redeemer)
    • Catechesi Tradendae (Catechesis in our Times)
    • Evangelii Gaudium (Joy of the Gospel)
    • Disciples Called to Witness
    • Renewing the Vision
    • Sons & Daughters of Light
  • Knowledge of adolescent and young adult development, spiritual development and application
  • Ability to articulate a clear ministry vision and set appropriate milestones to accomplishing the vision
  • Exceptional people skills
  • Exceptional oral communication skills
  • Ability to work well in a multi-faith and multicultural settings
  • Ability to empathize with others
  • Self-motivated, works easily alone or with others
  • Ability to maintain confidentiality
  • Detail-oriented and highly organized
  • Ability to multitask and prioritize tasks in an office setting and at events
  • Ability to interact with faculty and staff at a peer academic level
  • Ability to recognize the unique development needs of University students
  • Ability to work with diverse groups related to student life and health
  • Strong computer and digital communication skills
  • Strong small group facilitation skills

 

Education Required: 

  • A minimum of a bachelor’s degree is required with a master’s degree preferred (in a relevant field). 
  • 3-5 years of prior experience in pastoral work, preferably campus ministry.

 

Working Conditions:

This is a full-time (minimum of 40 hours per week), exempt professional ministry position. Night and weekend work is necessary primarily during the academic year. Regular, weekly schedule will be required. A physical presence on the local campus is required on a weekly basis as well. The position also requires travel to campus ministers’ meetings and other diocesan events, reimbursable through the approved budget. The Director will work regularly with the Diocesan Associate Director of the Office for Evangelization, the Campus Ministry Chaplain, faculty, staff and students of James Madison University as well as other Diocesan Campus Ministers.

Résumé du poste 

Le/la Manager de Pastoralisme Durable est responsable de la conception, de la supervision stratégique et du leadership technique de toutes les activités de WCS liées au pastoralisme, à la gestion des parcours et à la mitigation des conflits pastoraux dans le nord de la RCA. L’objectif est de développer des modèles innovants au sein du nexus conservation et pastoralisme au niveau régional, en assurant la mise en œuvre opérationnelle de notre stratégie de transhumance. En s’appuyant sur l’analyse approfondie des données et les leçons apprises du programme PAIRIAC, il/elle structurera une gestion durable des parcours via des outils technologiques de pointe et une coordination transfrontalière renforcée. 

Relevant du Directeur du paysage pour la gestion quotidienne et sous la supervision technique directe de la Directrice Technique Régionale, le/la Manager mettra en place les meilleures pratiques en matière de santé animale (« Une seule santé ») et de valorisation des filières durables au cœur des actions de terrain. Garant de l’intégrité technique et de la responsabilité sociale, il/elle veillera à ce que l'engagement communautaire repose sur les principes de Consentement Libre, Informé et Préalable (CLIP) et sur une inclusion active du genre dans tous les processus de gouvernance. 


Internal Qualification Requirements
Tâches et responsabilités

Conception Stratégique et Leadership : Développer, affiner et diriger la mise en œuvre de la stratégie du programme en matière de pastoralisme et de résolution des conflits, en s'assurant qu'elle est fondée sur des données probantes et adaptée au contexte local. Cela inclut la synchronisation opérationnelle des calendriers de mouvements et des couloirs de transhumance avec les programmes WCS et les partenaires des pays limitrophes pour une gestion cohérente à l’échelle régionale.

Gestion d'Équipe et Données : Assurer la supervision directe, le mentorat et la formation continue des Assistants Programme Transhumance et des agents de sensibilisation (Tango). Il/elle doit garantir la qualité des données collectées par les équipes Tango pour alimenter une gestion adaptative du paysage, en s'appuyant sur les acquis de PAIRIAC.

Engagement des Parties Prenantes et Négociation : Servir de liaison principale entre WCS, les leaders communautaires, les autorités et les acteurs non étatiques au niveau du paysage et national. Établir un dialogue de haut niveau pour faciliter la gestion concertée des parcours et intégrer les protocoles de Consentement Libre, Informé et Préalable (CLIP) ainsi que l'inclusion des femmes.

Gestion des Conflits et des Parcours : Concevoir des mécanismes de prévention des conflits et mettre en œuvre des plans de gestion durable des parcours. Il/elle doit promouvoir des incitations économiques et des filières durables valorisant le respect des zones de conservation par les pasteurs.

Santé Animale et Expertise Technique : Intégrer les meilleures pratiques « Une seule santé » (One Health) dans les activités de terrain en coordonnant des interventions sanitaires à l’interface entre la faune sauvage et le bétail.

Suivi, Évaluation et Apprentissage (SEA) : Mettre en place un système de SEA robuste pour mesurer l'efficacité des interventions, documenter les leçons apprises (notamment de PAIRIAC) et adapter les stratégies via des outils de suivi spatial.

Sécurité et Coordination Opérationnelle : Travailler en étroite collaboration avec les équipes de gestion du parc et de l'aviation pour intégrer les activités pastorales dans la planification globale. Maintenir une coordination quotidienne avec la salle de contrôle (Control Room) pour assurer la sécurité des équipes de terrain.

Rapports Techniques et Conseil : Rédiger des rapports de haute qualité pour les bailleurs et fournir des conseils stratégiques à la direction de WCS sur les enjeux du nexus conservation/pastoralisme.



Compétences et qualifications requises

Expérience : Au minimum huit (8) ans d'expérience professionnelle pertinente dans le domaine du pastoralisme, des systèmes agropastoraux, de la gestion des parcours ou de la résolution de conflits, de préférence dans la région soudano-sahélienne. Une expérience avérée dans la conception et la mise en œuvre de programmes de terrain est indispensable.

Formation : Diplôme universitaire supérieur (Master / MSc ou équivalent) en développement rural, écologie des parcours, anthropologie, sociologie, sciences de l'environnement, ou un domaine connexe.

Compétences Techniques:

Excellente compréhension des dynamiques socio-culturelles, économiques et écologiques de la transhumance en Afrique centrale.

Solides compétences en négociation, médiation et facilitation de dialogues multipartites.

Capacité avérée à concevoir et mettre en œuvre des stratégies d'engagement communautaire efficaces.

La connaissance des approches de conservation est un atout, mais l'expertise en pastoralisme est primordiale.

Gestion de données et analyse : Capacité avérée à superviser la collecte de données de terrain de haute qualité, à gérer des bases de données complexes et à utiliser ces informations pour orienter une gestion adaptative et documenter les leçons apprises (ex. : via les outils SIG ou l'analyse des acquis de programmes précédents comme PAIRIAC).

Langues :

Maîtrise du Fr

post_html:
Campus Staff Minister - WI NE Area (Undergraduate Ministry)

Work Location:

Wisconsin

Job Type:

Full time

God has called InterVarsity to plant and to build witnessing communities of students and faculty who follow Jesus on college and university campuses. Through these groups, we believe ever- increasing numbers of students and faculty from all ethnic groups and areas of the campus will be transformed by the Gospel. We expect to see campuses increasingly become places where people, ideas, and structures flourish to the glory of God. We confidently anticipate that our InterVarsity alumni will become change agents across the country and around the world. We pursue this calling by discerning and actively participating in what God is already doing on campus. This is the essence of being a Campus Staff Minister (CSM).

ESSENTIAL COMMITMENTS/RESPONSIBILITIES 

Spiritual Growth 

You pursue maturity as a disciple of Jesus Christ so that your life and work increasingly reflects a growing love for God, God’s Word, God’s people of every ethnicity and culture, and God’s purposes in the world. To do this, you will: 

  • Pursue a vibrant relationship with the triune God through engagement with Scripture, prayer, and worship, both individually and in community 

  • Develop self-leadership (growing in self-awareness, self-management, relational integrity, and resiliency) 

  • Embrace Scriptural standards for behavior and attitudes 

 

Campus Leadership 

You communicate and model InterVarsity’s vision to see students and faculty transformed, campuses renewed and world changers developed 

  • Create a culture of humble dependence on God and bold expectation in God’s intention to start new witnessing communities throughout the campus and on new campuses 

  • Model – in person and through programs – InterVarsity’s vision and Core Values, including a biblically-defined commitment to engage every ethnic and social group on campus 

  • Lead students and faculty – individually and collectively – through Scripture, prayer, teaching, and discipleship experiences, so that they articulate and align their ministry activities around this vision 

  • Set annual goals through prayer, research and reflection with your teams (students, faculty, and staff) for qualitative and quantitative growth, including conversions and leadership development 

 

You create, develop, align and leverage ministry plans, programs, teams, and structures to close the gap between current reality and the aspirational goals. 

  • Build leadership teams who trust and partner well with you and who demonstrate spiritual vitality, relational health, and mission alignment 

  • Develop and execute plans to achieve annual goals, evaluating and modifying the plan as needed throughout the year 

  • Increase momentum for the vision by aligning programs, structures, conferences and teams around the goals 

  • Mobilize students and faculty to engage their relational networks with the gospel and to start new missional communities 

  • Under the direction of the Area Director, may supervise Ministry Interns and Campus Ministry Interns as delegated 

 

You intentionally gather, invite, and develop diverse groups of students and faculty so that they not only encounter and follow Jesus as Savior and Lord but also advance the mission on campus as participants and leaders. 

  • Create ways for faculty and students to encounter and follow Jesus through Scripture, worship, prayer, mission experiences, conferences, etc. 

  • Equip students and faculty so that they think strategically about campus engagement and so that they proclaim – in word, deed, and power – the good news of Jesus, regularly inviting students and faculty to follow him as Savior and Lord 

  • Disciple students and faculty by equipping them to hear the Word, respond actively, and debrief and interpret the experience so that they grow in Christlikeness, reflect our Core Values, and develop ministry skills 

  • Invite, coach, and equip students and faculty to become increasingly effective participants and leaders, including starting new witnessing communities on campuses 

 

Organizational Collaboration 

You work with a network of other local, area, regional, and national InterVarsity staff and volunteers so that our work reflects Biblical standards of excellence, integrity, and partnership. 

  • Partner with and respond positively to the direction and coaching of your supervisors and national leaders 

  • Contribute to collaborative and productive team meetings and relationships 

  • Affiliate chapters under your care and submit Graduating Student Forms in order to increase our partnership with current students and alumni 

  • Use national ministry resources and tools, as requested, including recruiting and/or participating in local, regional, or national conferences as  

  • Complete reporting, planning and review requirements in a timely way so that you and your supervisors can assess and improve your work as a CSM 

  • Comply with all InterVarsity policies and procedures 

 

Ministry Partnership Development 

You will develop a team of partners – churches and individuals (including alumni and community members) – who will resource the ministry financially, in prayer, or volunteer service that advances the mission. 

  • Raise 100% of the financial budget assigned by your supervisor 

  • Communicate regularly with your ministry partners, nurturing the relationship through visits, phone calls, emails and regular prayer letters 

  • Develop on-going, long-lasting partnership with alumni and volunteers 

  • Comply with all Ministry Partnership Policies 

  • Identify and invest in advocates who will build networks of volunteers and donors on InterVarsity’s behalf 

 

Accomplish all other assigned tasks as appropriate 

 

QUALIFICATIONS (common to all levels of CSM) 

  • Annually affirm InterVarsity’s Statement of Agreement (Doctrinal Basis and Purpose Statement). Abide by InterVarsity’s Code of Conduct. Believe and behave consonantly with InterVarsity’s Human Sexuality Theological Paper. Affirm and behave consonantly with InterVarsity’s “Women in Ministry Statement of Affirmation” 

  • Bachelor’s degree for CSMs assigned to a four-year campus. A minimum of an Associate’s degree for CSMs assigned to a two-year campus or a community college 

  • Strong interpersonal skills (including ability to minister to diverse ethnic communities and faculty) 

  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills 

  • Demonstrated problem solving skills 

  • Familiarity with word processing, presentation, email, and spreadsheet software 

 

WORK ENVIRONMENT/PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS 

The CSM position leads ministry in a college campus environment. A designated office space may or may not be available. The CSM is required to travel to on-campus and off- campus sites as appropriate. Off-campus travel includes, but is not limited to: student ministry conferences, Ministry Partnership Development meetings, and InterVarsity- sponsored training sessions, meetings, and conferences. The CSM is regularly required to communicate with others, and routinely uses standard office equipment such as computers, phones, photocopiers, filing cabinets, etc. 

Pay Range: $39,288.00 - $52,392.00 per year

Pay: This position is funded through personal fundraising. Accordingly, compensation will vary based on the ability of the individual to secure a donor team to fund the cost of his/her salary. The anticipated salary range for this position on a full-time basis (40 hours/week) is dependent on a variety of factors, including location and cost of living. The actual salary received, including any geographic adjustment to account for location and cost of living, is subject to the individual’s ability to raise funds necessary to cover the full amount of such salary within the range set forth in the job posting details.

Benefits:

We offer a competitive benefits package, including health care and retirement savings with a match. Eligibility is based on employee type and hours worked.  Benefits include the following:

  • 403(b) Retirement Savings Plan

  • 403(b) matching contributions

  • Dental insurance

  • Employee assistance program

  • Flexible work schedule

  • Flexible spending accounts

  • Health insurance

  • Health savings account

  • Life insurance

  • Paid time off

  • Parental leave

  • Professional development assistance

  • Vision insurance

post_html:
Company Description

The mission of Christ’s Church of the Valley is to win people to Jesus Christ, train believers to become disciples, and send disciples to impact the world. The Students Ministry supports the mission of CCV by shaping students to become Christ-centered difference makers. The Students Pastor will assist pastoring Junior and Senior High students through recruiting, training, and retaining youth coaches, as well as implementing Junior and Senior High school programs and events. The Students Pastor will also assist in growing the campus in all areas numerically such as attendance, coaches, and baptisms. 

Job Description

Essential Job Functions 

  • Execute Junior and Senior High events and programs 
  • Cast the overall CCV & Students Ministry vision with parents and volunteers 
  • Provide pastoral care for families and coaches 
  • Recruit, train, and retain volunteers for all weekend areas and events 
  • Develop and maintain school campus involvement 
  • Following up with first time students 
  • Collect and report accurate weekly attendance according to established standards and deadlines 
  • Work with the team to plan and execute various church-wide events. These may include, but are not limited to: 
    • Kick off events 
    • Easter 
    • Christmas Eve 

Qualifications

CHARACTER & CHEMISTRY 

Alignment with our CORE Values & Staff Fundamentals 

  • Commitment to Excellence – We bring our best, every time. Excellence honors God and moves people. 
  • Heart for Evangelism – We will risk it all to reach one more. Jesus’ last command is our priority. 
  • Radical Generosity – We steward all things with open hands. The God who owns it all, gave it all.  
  • Integrity – We commit to zero gap between what we say and do. Jesus modeled integrity in EVERYTHING. 
  • Servant Attitude – We put others before ourselves. If serving is beneath you, leading is beyond you. 
  • Teamwork – We are fiercely committed to the power of teams. Jesus chose to work with a team. So will we.  

Agreement with our CORE Commitments 

  • Must support the vision & mission of CCV. 
  • Must be/become an ACTIVE MEMBER of CCV 
  • Must regularly ATTEND WORSHIP with their family 
  • Must be an active participant in a CCV Group and consistently tithe 
  • Demonstrated maturity as a Christ follower 

Fully engaged (or willingness to) in CCV Next Steps: 

  • Baptism-by immersion at an age of decision 
  • Worship-regularly attend CCV service with family 
  • Connect-participation in CCV small group 
  • Serve-volunteer somewhere within a CCV ministry 
  • Give-returning at least a full 10% tithe to the local church CCV 

Competency 

  • Leadership Skills – is able to trust, coach, and guide people to influence others. Continually communicates overall vision and purpose effectively. 
  • Drive for Results – Steadfastly pushes self and others for results.  Is action-oriented and displays focus, passion & initiative.  Takes appropriate action when something needs to be done. 
  • Customer Focus – is dedicated to meeting the expectations of internal and external customers. 
  • Interpersonal Skills – relates well to all kinds of people and builds effective relationships, communicates effectively both interpersonally and corporately. 
  • Self-Development – Committed to improvement, seeks constructive criticism, understands strengths and weaknesses. 

Education and Experience 

  • 2 years minimum experience leading a ministry of youth and volunteers 
  • Degree in Youth Ministry preferred, however training or proven experience in the field will be considered 
  • Athletic team experience is helpful 
  • Software and technology skills is a bonus 

Additional Information

All your information will be kept confidential according to EEO guidelines.

General Information

The above statements are intended to describe the general nature and level of work being performed by individuals assigned to this position. They are not intended to be an exhaustive list of all duties, responsibilities, and skills required of employees. CCV Leadership reserves the right to revise the position, its job functions, minimum qualifications and other aspects of the position in any way at any time.

post_html:
Campus Staff Minister - Oregon Area (Undergraduate Ministry)

Work Location:

Oregon

Job Type:

Full time

God has called InterVarsity to plant and to build witnessing communities of students and faculty who follow Jesus on college and university campuses. Through these groups, we believe ever- increasing numbers of students and faculty from all ethnic groups and areas of the campus will be transformed by the Gospel. We expect to see campuses increasingly become places where people, ideas, and structures flourish to the glory of God. We confidently anticipate that our InterVarsity alumni will become change agents across the country and around the world. We pursue this calling by discerning and actively participating in what God is already doing on campus. This is the essence of being a Campus Staff Minister (CSM).

ESSENTIAL COMMITMENTS/RESPONSIBILITIES 

Spiritual Growth 

You pursue maturity as a disciple of Jesus Christ so that your life and work increasingly reflects a growing love for God, God’s Word, God’s people of every ethnicity and culture, and God’s purposes in the world. To do this, you will: 

  • Pursue a vibrant relationship with the triune God through engagement with Scripture, prayer, and worship, both individually and in community 

  • Develop self-leadership (growing in self-awareness, self-management, relational integrity, and resiliency) 

  • Embrace Scriptural standards for behavior and attitudes 

 

Campus Leadership 

You communicate and model InterVarsity’s vision to see students and faculty transformed, campuses renewed and world changers developed 

  • Create a culture of humble dependence on God and bold expectation in God’s intention to start new witnessing communities throughout the campus and on new campuses 

  • Model – in person and through programs – InterVarsity’s vision and Core Values, including a biblically-defined commitment to engage every ethnic and social group on campus 

  • Lead students and faculty – individually and collectively – through Scripture, prayer, teaching, and discipleship experiences, so that they articulate and align their ministry activities around this vision 

  • Set annual goals through prayer, research and reflection with your teams (students, faculty, and staff) for qualitative and quantitative growth, including conversions and leadership development 

 

You create, develop, align and leverage ministry plans, programs, teams, and structures to close the gap between current reality and the aspirational goals. 

  • Build leadership teams who trust and partner well with you and who demonstrate spiritual vitality, relational health, and mission alignment 

  • Develop and execute plans to achieve annual goals, evaluating and modifying the plan as needed throughout the year 

  • Increase momentum for the vision by aligning programs, structures, conferences and teams around the goals 

  • Mobilize students and faculty to engage their relational networks with the gospel and to start new missional communities 

  • Under the direction of the Area Director, may supervise Ministry Interns and Campus Ministry Interns as delegated 

 

You intentionally gather, invite, and develop diverse groups of students and faculty so that they not only encounter and follow Jesus as Savior and Lord but also advance the mission on campus as participants and leaders. 

  • Create ways for faculty and students to encounter and follow Jesus through Scripture, worship, prayer, mission experiences, conferences, etc. 

  • Equip students and faculty so that they think strategically about campus engagement and so that they proclaim – in word, deed, and power – the good news of Jesus, regularly inviting students and faculty to follow him as Savior and Lord 

  • Disciple students and faculty by equipping them to hear the Word, respond actively, and debrief and interpret the experience so that they grow in Christlikeness, reflect our Core Values, and develop ministry skills 

  • Invite, coach, and equip students and faculty to become increasingly effective participants and leaders, including starting new witnessing communities on campuses 

 

Organizational Collaboration 

You work with a network of other local, area, regional, and national InterVarsity staff and volunteers so that our work reflects Biblical standards of excellence, integrity, and partnership. 

  • Partner with and respond positively to the direction and coaching of your supervisors and national leaders 

  • Contribute to collaborative and productive team meetings and relationships 

  • Affiliate chapters under your care and submit Graduating Student Forms in order to increase our partnership with current students and alumni 

  • Use national ministry resources and tools, as requested, including recruiting and/or participating in local, regional, or national conferences as  

  • Complete reporting, planning and review requirements in a timely way so that you and your supervisors can assess and improve your work as a CSM 

  • Comply with all InterVarsity policies and procedures 

 

Ministry Partnership Development 

You will develop a team of partners – churches and individuals (including alumni and community members) – who will resource the ministry financially, in prayer, or volunteer service that advances the mission. 

  • Raise 100% of the financial budget assigned by your supervisor 

  • Communicate regularly with your ministry partners, nurturing the relationship through visits, phone calls, emails and regular prayer letters 

  • Develop on-going, long-lasting partnership with alumni and volunteers 

  • Comply with all Ministry Partnership Policies 

  • Identify and invest in advocates who will build networks of volunteers and donors on InterVarsity’s behalf 

 

Accomplish all other assigned tasks as appropriate 

 

QUALIFICATIONS (common to all levels of CSM) 

  • Annually affirm InterVarsity’s Statement of Agreement (Doctrinal Basis and Purpose Statement). Abide by InterVarsity’s Code of Conduct. Believe and behave consonantly with InterVarsity’s Human Sexuality Theological Paper. Affirm and behave consonantly with InterVarsity’s “Women in Ministry Statement of Affirmation” 

  • Bachelor’s degree for CSMs assigned to a four-year campus. A minimum of an Associate’s degree for CSMs assigned to a two-year campus or a community college 

  • Strong interpersonal skills (including ability to minister to diverse ethnic communities and faculty) 

  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills 

  • Demonstrated problem solving skills 

  • Familiarity with word processing, presentation, email, and spreadsheet software 

 

WORK ENVIRONMENT/PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS 

The CSM position leads ministry in a college campus environment. A designated office space may or may not be available. The CSM is required to travel to on-campus and off- campus sites as appropriate. Off-campus travel includes, but is not limited to: student ministry conferences, Ministry Partnership Development meetings, and InterVarsity- sponsored training sessions, meetings, and conferences. The CSM is regularly required to communicate with others, and routinely uses standard office equipment such as computers, phones, photocopiers, filing cabinets, etc. 

Pay Range: $39,288.00 - $52,392.00 per year

Pay: This position is funded through personal fundraising. Accordingly, compensation will vary based on the ability of the individual to secure a donor team to fund the cost of his/her salary. The anticipated salary range for this position on a full-time basis (40 hours/week) is dependent on a variety of factors, including location and cost of living. The actual salary received, including any geographic adjustment to account for location and cost of living, is subject to the individual’s ability to raise funds necessary to cover the full amount of such salary within the range set forth in the job posting details.

Benefits:

We offer a competitive benefits package, including health care and retirement savings with a match. Eligibility is based on employee type and hours worked.  Benefits include the following:

  • 403(b) Retirement Savings Plan

  • 403(b) matching contributions

  • Dental insurance

  • Employee assistance program

  • Employee discounts

  • Flexible work schedule

  • Flexible spending accounts

  • Health insurance

  • Health savings account

  • Life insurance

  • Paid time off

  • Parental leave

  • Professional development assistance

  • Vision insurance

Equal Employment Opportunity: 

 

InterVarsity Christian Fellowship/USA is both an equal opportunity employer and a faith-based religious organization. We conduct hiring without regard to race, color, ancestry, national origin, citizenship, age, sex, marital status, parental status, membership in any labor organization, political ideology, or disability of an otherwise qualified individual. The status of InterVarsity Christian Fellowship/USA as an equal opportunity employer does not prevent the organization from hiring staff based on their religious beliefs so that all staff share the same religious commitment.  Pursuant to the Civil Rights Act of 1964, Section 702 (42 U.S.C. 2000e 1(a)) InterVarsity Christian Fellowship/USA has the right to, and does, hire only candidates who agree with InterVarsity’s Statement of Agreement: Purpose and Doctrinal Basis because InterVarsity believes that each and every staff plays a vital role in advancing InterVarsity’s mission and purposes.

Part-time
Description

  

JOB SUMMARY: The youth minister plays a crucial role in our parish, performing various activities to direct and coordinate a robust faith-filled youth ministry aimed at helping youth grow as disciples of Jesus Christ. The mission of the youth minister will be directed towards youth grades 6-12. This person is to engage in relational ministry with youth and parents, provide for catechesis, and invite youth to serve others and make disciples. To that end, the youth minister is responsible for the development, coordination, supervision, and execution of parish programs designed to engage the parish youth. He or she should develop close communication with and mutual support from families of youth.

We are seeking a unique individual with a deep spirit and heart for ministry, and the ability to organize and run a comprehensive, fun, engaging ministry. Your unique qualities and passion for youth ministry are what we value most.

Requirements

  

Qualifications: Bilingual, basic organizing skills, adequate communication skills in English and Spanish, language and with a college education preferably in Theology or any equivalent training, and knowledge of Microsoft Office (word, excel, and/ or power point).  

APPLICATION SUBMISSION: Application materials should be sent to:

Attn: Fr. Al O. Abainza, SOLT, Pastor

Email: frabainza@mht.org

Most Holy Trinity Catholic Church

8620 N. 7th St. Phoenix AZ 85020

Description

The Campus Minister for Faith & Community Life is a 12-month position that is responsible for developing and overseeing opportunities to deepen and form the faith of our undergraduate students through communal experiences.  The Campus Minister will play a strong role in forming student leaders and overseeing opportunities for students to grow in their faith and in their understanding of our Jesuit tradition.

Under the direction and guidance of the Assistant Director of Undergraduate Campus Ministry, the Campus Minister is responsible for overseeing 2-3 retreats a year. This will involve supporting and supervising student coordinators, working with retreat leaders, creating and leading meaningful prayer experiences, coordinating schedules and transportation, and other tasks related to leading a retreat.  

With the support of the Office of Campus Ministry and the Office of Residential Life, the Campus Minister coordinates the Residence Hall Ministry in our first-year halls, supervising the Peer Ministry Advisors who work in designated halls. The Campus Minister will also serve on the Cortina Advisory Board to support sophomores living in this residential community.

The Campus Minister will also be responsible for working with student leaders to coordinate Agape Latte, a monthly speaker event that invites students to hear from leader on campus and to reflect on their faith.

The Campus Minister will also oversee programs in our office that focus on supporting students from other religious traditions, including a weekly Protestant Christian service and Bible study.  

The Campus Minister will work collaboratively as an integral member of the Campus Ministry team and the Division of Mission and Ministry to assist emerging adults in their faith development including, but not limited to: providing pastoral care to students, offering spiritual companionship, and supporting larger Campus Ministry events throughout the year.

Essential Functions:

  • Coordinates Residence Hall ministry, retreats, and other ministry opportunities
  • Administrative work including budget management, assessment, and promotion of programs. 
  • Collaborates as an integral member of the Campus Ministry Department, the Division of Mission and Ministry, and multiple other campus partners on various projects, programs, and events. 

  • Provides individual pastoral care and spiritual companionship to students.

     

Qualifications:

•    Bachelor’s degree in theology, pastoral studies, ministry or related required; Master’s degree strongly preferred
•    1-3 years of ministerial experience preferred
•    Experience working with diverse populations of students

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities:

•    Strong written and communication skills  
•    Knowledge of and commitment to the Jesuit mission 
•    Highly collaborative work ethic, with a comfort to reach out to University partners and also delegate when appropriate
•    Detail-oriented 
•    Ability to take initiative and be a self-starter

Position Title:

Director, Center for Latine Theology and Ministry

Position Type:

Regular

Hiring Range:

$102,800.00 - $128,560.00; Compensation will be based on education, experience, skills relevant to the role, and internal equity.

Pay Frequency:

Annual

A. POSITION PURPOSE


Under the supervision of the Sr. Assistant Dean / Chief Operating Officer of the Jesuit School of Theology at Santa Clara University (JST-SCU), the Director will provide vision, strategic leadership, and administrative oversight for the Center for Latine Theology and Ministry (CLTM). The director will oversee  the development, implementation, and sustainability of academic programs, ministerial formation, scholarly research, and community outreach initiatives that serve Latine pastoral leaders and communities. 


Towards this end, the Director will contribute to the strategic implementation of SCU’s recent  $10 Million Lilly Endowment Large-Scale Collaboration Grant (see press release). This will be done in coordination with the creation and launch of the Pope Francis Institute for Pastoral Flourishing (PFI), which integrates the work of the Jesuit School of Theology (JST), the Graduate Program in Pastoral Ministries (GPPM), and the Department of Religious Studies.  The Director will play a vital leadership role in establishing Santa Clara University as a primary national hub for Latine theology and ministry. Informed by JST-SCU’s strategic plan, En Camino, and Santa Clara University’s Santa Clara Impact 2030, the Director will guide the Center through its integration into Santa Clara’s Mission campus and foster strategic collaboration across university programs.



B. ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES


1. Strategic Leadership 

  • Lead the implementation of the strategic vision set forth for the Center for Latino Theology and Ministry in the $10M Lilly Endowment Large-Scale Collaboration Grant, positioning Santa Clara University as a primary national hub for Latine theology and ministry.
  • Align the work of the Center for Latine Theology and Ministry with the overall vision of the  Pope Francis Institute for Pastoral Flourishing (PFI). This will entail a year of co-design that aligns and integrates programs and initiatives between the Jesuit School of Theology, the Graduate Program in Pastoral Ministries, and the Department of Religious Studies.  
  • Provide overall vision and strategic direction for the CLTMin alignment with JST-SCU’s mission and strategic goals.
  • Oversee the strategic planning, growth, and continuous quality improvement of non-degree and continuing education programs, including the Instituto Hispano.
  • Collaborate with administrators and faculty across the university leadership, faculty, and academic programs to integrate Latine theological perspectives and ministerial formation into broader academic offerings.

2. Academic Research Support 

  • Promote and support academic research and scholarship focused on U.S. Latine theology, religiosidad popular, intercultural ministry, and contextual pastoral praxis.
  • Work towards establishing the CLTM as a hub for transdisciplinary research, bridging academic theological reflection with practical ministerial formation.
  • Convene symposia, academic lectures, and research initiatives that leverage Santa Clara University’s robust cohort of Latine faculty (in the JST, GPPM, and Department of Religious Studies), who do work in U.S. Latine theology and ministry 
  • Advance key priorities and themes articulated in the National Pastoral Plan for Hispanic/Latino Ministry and the V Encuentro through scholarly output and pastoral partnerships.

3. Network Building & Strategic Partnerships

  • Formalize and manage strategic academic and pastoral partnerships with national organizations, including  the Academy of Catholic Hispanic Theologians of the United States (ACHTUS), to advance scholarly research, mentorship, and leadership formation.
  • Partner with external regional organizations such as RECOSS (Red de Educación Continua del Sur de California) and Iskali to expand young adult leadership initiatives, mentorship, and community-of-practice programs (acompañamiento).
  • Cultivate and sustain strong collaborative relationships with diocesan leaders, pastoral institutes, Catholic organizations, and community partners across the West Coast and nationally.
  • Lead and support advisory bodies, including local and regional pastoral partner councils, to ensure program offerings remain responsive to community needs.
  • Represent SCU and the Center at national conferences, academic symposia, and ministerial gatherings.
  • Develop initiatives to identify future Latine leaders and help them discern a degree in theological or pastoral studies

4. Grant Administration & Resource Development

  • Oversee the administration, execution, and reporting for grants awarded directly to or specifically supporting the CLTM
  • Lilly LSC Integration & Input: Serve as a key contributor and subject-matter expert for the Lilly Endowment Large-Scale Collaboration (LSC) Grant by providing accurate program data, metrics, and progress updates to the dedicated LSC Project Manager, who manages centralized grant reporting.
  • Resource Development & Sustainability: In collaboration with University Development, identify external funding opportunities, assist in cultivating donors, and draft grant proposals to ensure the long-term sustainability and expansion of CLTM initiatives.
  • Budget Oversight: Monitor center-specific budget allocations, program revenue (including Instituto Hispano revenue), and match funding commitments in coordination with the Dean’s Office and JST Finance.

5. Operational & Personnel Management

  • Supervise, mentor, and evaluate CLTM administrative staff, including the Instituto Hispano Program Coordinator, project staff, and graduate student assistants.
  • Direct day-to-day operations of the Center, ensuring efficient administrative processes, event execution, and participant support.
  • Oversee marketing, outreach, and communications strategies to promote Center activities and engage prospective students.

6. Other duties as assigned in support of JST’s mission and operational needs



C. PROVIDES WORK DIRECTION


Directly supervises professional staff (e.g., Instituto Hispano Program Coordinator), grant-funded staff, and graduate assistants.



D. GENERAL GUIDELINES

Recommends initiatives and implements changes to improve quality and services.

Identifies and determines cause of problems; develops and presents recommendations for improvement of established processes and practices.

Maintains contact with partners, community leaders, and students to solicit feedback for improved services.

Maximizes productivity through use of appropriate tools, planned training, and performance initiatives.

Researches and develops resources that create timely and efficient workflow.

Prepares progress reports; informs supervisor of project status and deviation from grant or program goals.

Ensures completeness, accuracy, and timeliness of all operational and grant-related functions.

Prepares and submits grant and institutional reports as requested and required.

Develops and implements guidelines to support the functions of the unit.



E. QUALIFICATIONS


This position requires the ability to establish and maintain effective and cooperative working relationships within a diverse multicultural environment.  Professional qualifications include the following:

1. Scholarly and Professional Expertise 

  • Deep knowledge of Latine theology and ministerial formation, and the ways in which they connect to the  pastoral realities of Latine communities in the United States.
  • Strong understanding of the values, ideals, and mission of the Jesuit School of Theology and Jesuit higher education, more broadly.
  • Knowledge of ATS-accredited graduate theological education and non-degree certificate program structures.

2. Skills

  • Exceptional written and oral communication skills in both English and Spanish (bilingual fluency required).
  • Strong project management and organizational skills with sharp attention to detail.
  • Proven leadership and interpersonal skills in managing staff, building teams, and facilitating advisory groups.
  • Familiarity with grant management processes, grant reporting standards, and budget administration.

3. Abilities

  • Ability to engage, collaborate, and build trust with diverse stakeholders, including bishops, diocesan personnel, grassroots pastoral leaders, and faculty.
  • Ability to manage grant budgets, track metrics, and meet formal reporting deadlines.
  • Ability to navigate organizational transitions and lead strategic program growth.
  • Ability to exercise sound judgment, discretion, and maintain confidentiality.

4. Education


Ph.D., D.Min., or equivalent doctorate preferred; Master’s degree in Theology, Pastoral Ministry, Divinity, or a closely related field required.


5. Years of Experience

  • Four or more years of  progressively responsible administrative, leadership, or educational experience in a university, theological seminary, or pastoral organization. Experience managing grant-funded programs strongly preferred.


F. PHYSICAL DEMANDS


The physical demands described below are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. In accordance with the Americans with Disabilities Act, as amended, the California Fair Employment & Housing Act, and all other applicable laws, SCU provides reasonable accommodations for qualified persons with disabilities.

  • Considerable time is spent at a desk using a computer terminal.
  • Travel between campuses, diocesan locations, and/or partner sites will most likely be required
  • May be required to attend conference and training sessions regionally and nationally.
  • May be required to work some evenings and weekends to accommodate program events and partner meetings.


G. WORK ENVIRONMENT


JST-SCU allows employees to submit requests for Flexible and Remote work schedules as described in Policy 307 of the SCU employee handbook. If a remote schedule is approved, the school’s standard is that all permanent employees work in person at least 60% of the time. Currently, this position is based at the JST-SCU campus in Berkeley, California. Beginning in Fall 2027, the position will be based at the school’s location on Santa Clara University’s main campus in Santa Clara, California.

  • Typical office environment.
  • Mostly indoor office environment with windows.
  • Offices with equipment noise and frequent interruptions.

This is an initial 3-year fixed-term position, with potential for extension dependent on project milestones, performance, and funding allocation.



Telecommute

Santa Clara University is registered to do business in the following states: California, Nevada, Oregon, Washington, Arizona, and Illinois. Employees approved to telecommute are required to perform their work within one of these states.

 

EEO Statement

Equal Opportunity/Notice of Nondiscrimination

All qualified applicants are encouraged to apply and will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, ethnicity, national origin, citizenship, ancestry, religion, age, sex, sexual orientation, gender, gender expression, gender identity, marital status, parental status, veteran or military status, physical or mental disability, medical conditions, pregnancy or related conditions, reproductive health decision making, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state, or local laws.  For a complete copy of Santa Clara University’s equal opportunity and nondiscrimination policies, please visit the Office of Equal Opportunity and Title IX website at  https://www.scu.edu/title-ix/.

Description

Sun River Health provides the highest quality of comprehensive primary, preventative and behavioral health services to all who seek it, regardless of insurance status and ability to pay, especially for the underserved and vulnerable. Sun River Health is a Federally Qualified, Non-Profit Health Center serving communities in New York City, Suffolk, Rockland, Orange, Dutchess, Ulster, Sullivan, Columbia and Westchester. We are currently hiring for a full-time Medical Scribe located in Brooklyn, New York.

Position Summary

Medical Scribes are individuals trained in medical documentation who assist a physician throughout their shift. The primary goal of the Medical Scribe is to increase the efficiency and the productivity of the physician they are working for. Under the supervision of the VP of Practice Management, the medical scribe will be responsible for capturing accurate and detailed documentation of the medical encounter into the Electronic Medical Record (eClinical Works) in a timely manner. He/She will provide excellent customer service to our patients, adhering to established protocols and work processes and successfully managing volume without ever compromising quality.

Job Type: Full-Time

Pay Range: $20.50 - $21.11 per hour

Sign-On Bonus: $1,500 Sign-On Bonus for Eligible External Applicants – Terms and Conditions Apply.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities

  • Procedures and treatments performed by healthcare professionals, including nurses and physician assistants.
  • Communicating with patients, pharmacies, and physicians over the phone under physician guidance
  • Accurately and thoroughly document medical visits and procedures as they are being performed by the physician
  • Ensure that all clinical data, lab or other test results, the interpretation of the results by the physician are recorded accurately in the medical record.
  • Facilitating any necessary diagnostic tests (e.g., CT, MRI, ultrasounds, etc.) and referrals to medical specialists for follow-up care when indicated
  • Patient medical history and physical exam
  • Collect, organize and document data for physician quality reporting system and other quality improvement efforts and format for submission and reporting
  • Being able to manage a minimum of three to four patients per hour on average
  • Assisting the physician with basic patient care and medical indicated procedures set-ups as indicated
  • Communicating with clinical operations staff regarding patient needs and follow-up
  • Proofread and edit all the physician’s medical documents for accuracy, spelling, punctuation, and grammar
  • Physician-dictated diagnoses, prescriptions and instructions for patient or family members for self-care and follow-up
  • Attend trainings on diverse subjects such as information technology, legal, HIPAA and regulatory compliance, billing and coding, proofread and edit all the physician’s medical documents for accuracy, spelling, punctuation, and grammar.
  • Must comply with specific standards that apply to the style of medical records and to the legal and ethical requirements for preparing medical documents and for keeping patient information confidential.

Requirements:

  • Minimum Education Requirement: High school diploma/ GED
  • Minimum Work-Related Experience: 2-4 years

About Sun River Health

Sun River Health has a rich history of providing quality, affordable health care to communities in need. Founded in the early 1970s by four African American women in Peekskill, New York, the organization was established to address the lack of accessible health services in their community. With the help of a small federal grant, the first Sun River Health site opened its doors in 1975. Over the years, Sun River Health has grown into a comprehensive Federally Qualified Health Center (FQHC) system with over 50 locations, serving more than 250,000 patients across the Hudson Valley, New York City and Long Island. Our exceptional primary care practitioners, specialists and support staff are dedicated to delivering high-quality care to all individuals, regardless of their ability to pay. In December 2018, Sun River Health expanded its reach by merging with Brightpoint Health, an FQHC network offering integrated medical, behavioral and social support services in New York City. This merger allowed us to enhance our services and continue our mission under the unified name of Sun River Health.

Our Culture

At Sun River Health, we believe in fostering a culture of wellness, inclusivity and recognition. Our Workforce Wellness Program promotes staff wellness through ongoing challenges and activities, encouraging participation and rewarding engagement. We celebrate our staff's dedication and person-centered spirit through the Planetree Recognition Awards, which honor innovation, leadership and community spirit. We are committed to creating a supportive and collaborative work environment where all team members can thrive. Our values of respect, integrity and excellence guide our interactions with patients and colleagues alike, ensuring that everyone receives the care and support they deserve.

Benefits

At Sun River Health, we are committed to building a personal relationship with our team and supporting you in every way we can. We offer competitive compensation and a comprehensive benefits package for you and your family, including:

  • Medical, Dental and Vision Insurance: Comprehensive health coverage to ensure you and your family stay healthy.
  • Life and Disability Coverage: Financial protection for you and your loved ones in case of unforeseen circumstances.
  • Retirement Savings Plan: Plan for your future with our retirement savings options.
  • Commuter and Transit Benefits: Assistance with your daily commute to make your journey to work easier.
  • Employee Assistance Program (EAP): Access to confidential support and resources for personal and work-related issues.
  • Employee Discount Program: Enjoy discounts on various products and services as a valued member of our team.

Professional Development, Education and Loan Assistance Benefit Programs 

  • Sun River Health is committed in fostering continued growth, education, and professional advancement across its organization. Through a range of development opportunities and loan repayment programs employees are supported at every stage of their careers.
  • Eligible employees may have the opportunity to participate in federal and state loan repayment or loan forgiveness programs, including those administered by the Health Resources and Services Administration (HRSA) and the National Health Service Corps (NHSC) with support provided throughout the application process.
  • In addition, Sun River Health offers a Tuition Reimbursement Program for eligible employees that supports job-related coursework completed through accredited institutions, helping employees continue building their skills and advancing their careers. 

Why Join Sun River Health?

  • Mission-Driven Work: Be part of a proud network of care that offers high-quality health and social support services to communities in need.
  • Professional Growth: We provide opportunities for career advancement and professional development.
  • Supportive Environment: Our culture promotes wellness, inclusivity, and recognition, ensuring a supportive and collaborative work environment.
  • Community Impact: Make a difference in the lives of individuals and families by providing quality, affordable health care.

Join us at Sun River Health and be part of an award-winning network of care that has been serving our communities since 1975. We are always looking for skilled and dedicated professionals to join our team and help us continue our mission of providing quality health care to all.



Responsibilities

Relation to Mission
The mission of Sun River Health is to increase access to comprehensive primary and preventive health care and to improve the health status of our community, especially for the underserved and vulnerable.

Equal Employment Opportunity
Sun River Health provides equal employment opportunities to all qualified individuals without regard to race, creed, color, religion, national origin, age, sex, marital status, sexual preference, or non-disqualifying physical or mental handicap or disability in each aspect of the human resources function.

Americans with Disabilities Act
Applicants as well as employees who are or become disabled must be able to perform the essential job functions either unaided or with reasonable accommodation. The organization shall determine reasonable accommodation on a case-by-case basis in accordance with applicable law.

Job Responsibilities

Sun River Health may change the specific job duties with or without prior notice based on the needs of the organization.

Pastor -  Pathway Baptist Church
 

Pathway Baptist Church, Prudenville, Michigan

Pathway Baptist Church is a warm, loving, and tight-knit congregation of approximately 30 – 50 members located in the beautiful resort community of Prudenville, on Houghton Lake, Michigan. We are firmly rooted in Baptist faith and message, committed to sound biblical teaching, heartfelt worship, and local outreach. We are seeking a relational Lead Pastor who loves the small-church environment and is eager to shepherd our flock while helping us grow deeper in our faith.

The Lead Pastor will serve as the primary spiritual leader, preacher, and undershepherd of our congregation on a full-time basis. In our small church setting, this role requires a “hands-on” leader who thrives on building close personal relationships, visiting members, and handling both the pulpit ministry and everyday church administration.

 Key Responsibilities

Expository Preaching: Deliver weekly, biblically sound, gospel-centered sermons that align with historic Baptist doctrine.

Relational Shepherding: Provide intentional pastoral care through home visits, hospital visitations, and personal prayer with members.

Discipleship & Small Groups: Lead or equip volunteers to run Sunday School, Bible studies, and prayer meetings.

Collaborative Leadership: Work closely with the Deacons and church committees to oversee administrative tasks and budget management.

Ordinances & Services: Administer the scriptural ordinances of Believer’s Baptism and the Lord’s supper, and conduct weddings and funerals.

Qualifications & Requirements

Spiritual Character: Must meet the biblical qualifications outlined in 1Timothy 3:1-7 and Titus 1:5-9

Doctrinal Alignment: Full agreement with the Baptist Faith and Message 2000

Education: A degree in Biblical Studies, Theology, or Ministry from a recognized Baptist seminary or college is preferred, but equivalent ministry experience will be highly valued.

Experience: Previous experience as a pastor, assistant pastor, or interim pastor in a small or mid-sized congregation is preferred.

Heart for Small Church: A visible passion for a small-church dynamic where everyone knows your name.

Compensation, Housing & Benefits

Full-Time Salary: Negotiable

Parsonage Provided: A family-friendly 3-bedroom, 2-bath parsonage is provided. The home features a large yard perfect for outdoor activities and is fully kid and pet friendly.

Utilities: Full utilities are included as part of the housing package.

This person will provide relational, organizational, and administrative support for Vineyard Columbus' young adult ministry, helping create environments where young adults can build authentic relationships, deepen their faith, and engage in the life of the church.

Working closely with the Young Adult Pastor, the Young Adult Ministry Coordinator will help connect new young adults into community, support small group leaders, assist with Young Adult Night gatherings, and oversee many of the administrative systems that help the ministry operate effectively. This role combines relationship-building with practical ministry leadership, requiring someone who is passionate about young adults, enjoys developing leaders, and can bring both warmth and organization to ministry environments.

This is an exciting opportunity to invest in a growing community of young adults by helping people find belonging, develop lasting relationships, and grow as disciples of Jesus.

About us:

Vineyard Columbus exists to develop multiethnic communities of disciples who experience God, love one another, and partner with Christ to heal the world.

As a church, we are committed to being a great friend to our city and to building communities that reflect Christlike unity while celebrating the diversity of our congregation and staff.

Beyond weekend services at multiple locations across Central Ohio, we serve our neighbors through the Vineyard Community Center, which provides free health clinics, food assistance, ESL classes, Value Life resources, a Counseling Center and other practical support—all opportunities to share the love of Jesus in tangible ways.

Who we're looking for:

We are seeking a spiritually mature, relational, and team-oriented leader who is passionate about helping young adults experience authentic Christian community and grow in their faith. The ideal candidate enjoys meeting new people, connecting individuals into meaningful relationships, and creating environments where people feel welcomed, known, and valued.

This person is equally comfortable building relationships and managing details. They are energized by supporting ministry gatherings, coordinating volunteers, communicating with leaders, and helping create pathways for young adults to become actively engaged in community and discipleship. They thrive in collaborative settings, communicate clearly, and bring a positive, flexible attitude to ministry.

The ideal candidate is also a developer of leaders who enjoys supporting, encouraging, and equipping small group leaders and volunteers. They understand that healthy ministry happens through healthy relationships and are passionate about helping others grow in their leadership and influence.

Most importantly, this individual demonstrates a genuine love for Jesus, a commitment to personal spiritual growth, and a desire to help young adults connect more deeply with God, community, and mission.

Campus Staff Minister - Michigan Lower Peninsula Region (Undergraduate Ministry)

Work Location:

Michigan

Job Type:

Full time

God has called InterVarsity to plant and to build witnessing communities of students and faculty who follow Jesus on college and university campuses. Through these groups, we believe ever- increasing numbers of students and faculty from all ethnic groups and areas of the campus will be transformed by the Gospel. We expect to see campuses increasingly become places where people, ideas, and structures flourish to the glory of God. We confidently anticipate that our InterVarsity alumni will become change agents across the country and around the world. We pursue this calling by discerning and actively participating in what God is already doing on campus. This is the essence of being a Campus Staff Minister (CSM).

ESSENTIAL COMMITMENTS/RESPONSIBILITIES 

Spiritual Growth 

You pursue maturity as a disciple of Jesus Christ so that your life and work increasingly reflects a growing love for God, God’s Word, God’s people of every ethnicity and culture, and God’s purposes in the world. To do this, you will: 

  • Pursue a vibrant relationship with the triune God through engagement with Scripture, prayer, and worship, both individually and in community 

  • Develop self-leadership (growing in self-awareness, self-management, relational integrity, and resiliency) 

  • Embrace Scriptural standards for behavior and attitudes 

 

Campus Leadership 

You communicate and model InterVarsity’s vision to see students and faculty transformed, campuses renewed and world changers developed 

  • Create a culture of humble dependence on God and bold expectation in God’s intention to start new witnessing communities throughout the campus and on new campuses 

  • Model – in person and through programs – InterVarsity’s vision and Core Values, including a biblically-defined commitment to engage every ethnic and social group on campus 

  • Lead students and faculty – individually and collectively – through Scripture, prayer, teaching, and discipleship experiences, so that they articulate and align their ministry activities around this vision 

  • Set annual goals through prayer, research and reflection with your teams (students, faculty, and staff) for qualitative and quantitative growth, including conversions and leadership development 

 

You create, develop, align and leverage ministry plans, programs, teams, and structures to close the gap between current reality and the aspirational goals. 

  • Build leadership teams who trust and partner well with you and who demonstrate spiritual vitality, relational health, and mission alignment 

  • Develop and execute plans to achieve annual goals, evaluating and modifying the plan as needed throughout the year 

  • Increase momentum for the vision by aligning programs, structures, conferences and teams around the goals 

  • Mobilize students and faculty to engage their relational networks with the gospel and to start new missional communities 

  • Under the direction of the Area Director, may supervise Ministry Interns and Campus Ministry Interns as delegated 

 

You intentionally gather, invite, and develop diverse groups of students and faculty so that they not only encounter and follow Jesus as Savior and Lord but also advance the mission on campus as participants and leaders. 

  • Create ways for faculty and students to encounter and follow Jesus through Scripture, worship, prayer, mission experiences, conferences, etc. 

  • Equip students and faculty so that they think strategically about campus engagement and so that they proclaim – in word, deed, and power – the good news of Jesus, regularly inviting students and faculty to follow him as Savior and Lord 

  • Disciple students and faculty by equipping them to hear the Word, respond actively, and debrief and interpret the experience so that they grow in Christlikeness, reflect our Core Values, and develop ministry skills 

  • Invite, coach, and equip students and faculty to become increasingly effective participants and leaders, including starting new witnessing communities on campuses 

 

Organizational Collaboration 

You work with a network of other local, area, regional, and national InterVarsity staff and volunteers so that our work reflects Biblical standards of excellence, integrity, and partnership. 

  • Partner with and respond positively to the direction and coaching of your supervisors and national leaders 

  • Contribute to collaborative and productive team meetings and relationships 

  • Affiliate chapters under your care and submit Graduating Student Forms in order to increase our partnership with current students and alumni 

  • Use national ministry resources and tools, as requested, including recruiting and/or participating in local, regional, or national conferences as  

  • Complete reporting, planning and review requirements in a timely way so that you and your supervisors can assess and improve your work as a CSM 

  • Comply with all InterVarsity policies and procedures 

 

Ministry Partnership Development 

You will develop a team of partners – churches and individuals (including alumni and community members) – who will resource the ministry financially, in prayer, or volunteer service that advances the mission. 

  • Raise 100% of the financial budget assigned by your supervisor 

  • Communicate regularly with your ministry partners, nurturing the relationship through visits, phone calls, emails and regular prayer letters 

  • Develop on-going, long-lasting partnership with alumni and volunteers 

  • Comply with all Ministry Partnership Policies 

  • Identify and invest in advocates who will build networks of volunteers and donors on InterVarsity’s behalf 

 

Accomplish all other assigned tasks as appropriate 

 

QUALIFICATIONS (common to all levels of CSM) 

  • Annually affirm InterVarsity’s Statement of Agreement (Doctrinal Basis and Purpose Statement). Abide by InterVarsity’s Code of Conduct. Believe and behave consonantly with InterVarsity’s Human Sexuality Theological Paper. Affirm and behave consonantly with InterVarsity’s “Women in Ministry Statement of Affirmation” 

  • Bachelor’s degree for CSMs assigned to a four-year campus. A minimum of an Associate’s degree for CSMs assigned to a two-year campus or a community college 

  • Strong interpersonal skills (including ability to minister to diverse ethnic communities and faculty) 

  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills 

  • Demonstrated problem solving skills 

  • Familiarity with word processing, presentation, email, and spreadsheet software 

 

WORK ENVIRONMENT/PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS 

The CSM position leads ministry in a college campus environment. A designated office space may or may not be available. The CSM is required to travel to on-campus and off- campus sites as appropriate. Off-campus travel includes, but is not limited to: student ministry conferences, Ministry Partnership Development meetings, and InterVarsity- sponsored training sessions, meetings, and conferences. The CSM is regularly required to communicate with others, and routinely uses standard office equipment such as computers, phones, photocopiers, filing cabinets, etc. 

Pay Range: $39,288.00 - $52,392.00 per year

Senior Pastor

We are seeking a Senior Pastor to provide biblical, spiritual, and organizational leadership to a loving, caring, and Bible-centered congregation as we enter our next season of ministry.

About Our Church

Our church has an average Sunday attendance of approximately 100 and a current membership of 37. We are a warm, generous, and compassionate congregation representing a range of ages, backgrounds, and life experiences. We value biblical truth, unity, service, and genuine care for one another.

Our desire is to grow in our outreach and involvement in the community, strengthen marriages and families, develop disciples and lay leaders, and expand ministry to youth and men.

Position Description

The Senior Pastor will provide spiritual leadership and faithfully communicate God's Word while helping equip the congregation for ministry.

Key areas of ministry include:

  • Biblical preaching and teaching
  • Spiritual leadership and vision
  • Discipleship and development of lay leaders
  • Evangelism and community outreach
  • Pastoral care, visitation, and counseling
  • Ministry to marriages and families
  • Leadership of staff, volunteers, and ministry programs
  • Partnership with church elders and leadership
  • Worship service oversight

  • Biblical conflict management

Qualifications

We are seeking a godly, Spirit-filled pastor who is confident in Christ, disciplined, committed to God's Word, and genuinely loves people.

Compensation will be commensurate with the candidate's training, experience, and ministry effectiveness. Boston College Introduction

Founded in 1863, Boston College is a Jesuit, Catholic university located six miles from downtown Boston with an enrollment of 9,654 full-time undergraduates and 5,072 graduate and professional students. Ranked 37 among national universities, Boston College has 923 full-time and 1,336 FTE faculty, 2,822 non-faculty employees, an operating budget of $1.4 billion, and an endowment in excess of $3.9 billion.



Job Description

The Church in the 21st Century Center (C21) is a catalyst and resource for the renewal of the Catholic Church, engaging critical issues facing the Church and Catholic community through conversation, programming, publications, and other creative initiatives. The Center is part of Boston College’s Division of University Mission & Ministry, which advances the University’s Jesuit, Catholic mission and supports the formation of the Boston College community.

The Associate Director collaborates closely with the Director in implementing the goals and overall direction of the Church in the 21st Century Center. The Associate Director serves as managing editor of the annual C21 Resources magazine, working with guest editors and the editorial board. With strong editing and writing skills and an eye for creative design, the Associate Director serves as the primary liaison with the printer/publishing house in the development and production of each issue.

The Associate Director coordinates strategic marketing initiatives, including working with multiple academic and administrative units throughout the University to plan and implement a wide array of programs; interacting with Boston College students, faculty, administrators, and prominent external scholars and speakers; and managing the Center’s marketing and promotional activity. Creativity is central to this role, and the Associate Director will help conceive and develop engaging new approaches to C21’s programming, publications, communications, and outreach.

The Associate Director also serves on the C21 Advisory Committee and works collaboratively with colleagues across C21 and University Mission & Ministry.

Full-Time Equivalent Hiring Range: $82,100 to $102,650; salary commensurate with relevant experience.

Requirements

At minimum, a bachelor’s degree and at least eight years of work experience in a directly related professional role, including staff management, are required. A communications or theology background is preferred, along with excellent writing, editing, and presentation skills; demonstrated strength in creative design and digital marketing; and a strong understanding of contemporary issues facing the Catholic Church.



Closing Statement

Boston College offers a broad and competitive range of benefits depending on your job classification eligibility:

  • Tuition remission for Employees
  • Tuition remission for Spouses and Children who meet eligibility requirements
  • Generous Medical, Dental, and Vision Insurance
  • Low-Cost Life Insurance
  • Eligibility for both University-Funded 401k and Employer-Sponsored 403b Retirement Plans
  • Paid Holidays Annually
  • Generous Sick and Vacation Pay

Boston College conducts pre-employment background checks as part of the hiring process.

Boston College is an Equal Opportunity Employer and does not discriminate on the basis of any legally protected category, including disability and protected veteran status. Boston College's Notice of Nondiscrimination can be viewed at https://www.bc.edu/nondiscrimination.
