Campus Staff Minister - Mississippi (Graduate & Faculty Ministry)

Work Location:

Mississippi

Job Type:

Full time

God has called InterVarsity to plant and to build witnessing communities of students and faculty who follow Jesus on college and university campuses. Through these groups, we believe ever- increasing numbers of students and faculty from all ethnic groups and areas of the campus will be transformed by the Gospel. We expect to see campuses increasingly become places where people, ideas, and structures flourish to the glory of God. We confidently anticipate that our InterVarsity alumni will become change agents across the country and around the world. We pursue this calling by discerning and actively participating in what God is already doing on campus. This is the essence of being a Campus Staff Minister (CSM).

Please submit the GFM Interest Form before completing the full application for a position with Graduate & Faculty Ministries in our online system. We will contact you when we are ready to proceed with the application process.​ 

This position is open to applicants working less than 40 hours/week. If you are interested in part-time work please apply for this position. 

The pay range listed is for an employee working 40 hours/week at CSM level I. Pay will be prorated for employees who work less than 40 hours/week.

We have positions in the following locations:

  • Mississippi State University
  • University of Mississippi (Ole Miss)
  • University of Southern Mississippi
  • Jackson State University

Volunteers are welcome. Volunteer opportunities range from prayer and hospitality to leading a campus fellowship of graduate students and faculty. Those interested in volunteering will go through an application and interview process. However, volunteer openings are not posted online. For more information, complete the GFM Interest Form. 

ESSENTIAL COMMITMENTS/RESPONSIBILITIES 

Spiritual Growth 

As a Campus Staff Minister, you pursue maturity as a disciple of Jesus Christ so that your life and work increasingly reflect a growing love for God, God’s Word, God’s people of every ethnicity and culture, and God’s purposes in the world. To do this, you will: 

  • Pursue a vibrant relationship with the triune God through engagement with Scripture, prayer, and worship, both individually and in community

  • Develop self-leadership (growing in self-awareness, self-management, relational integrity, and resiliency) 

  • Embrace Scriptural standards for behavior and attitudes 

 

Campus Leadership 

As a Campus Staff Minister, you increase the number of witnessing communities, as well as the size, health, spiritual maturity, and campus-wide influence of existing witnessing communities of students and faculty by being a: 

  • Visionary Guide: 

You communicate and model InterVarsity’s vision to see students and faculty transformed, campuses renewed, and world changers developed 

  • Create a culture of humble dependence on God and bold expectation in God’s intention to start new witnessing communities throughout the campus and on new campuses 

  • Model – in person and through programs – InterVarsity’s vision and Core Values, including a biblically-defined commitment to engage every ethnic and social group on campus 

  • Lead students and faculty – individually and collectively – through Scripture, prayer, teaching, and discipleship experiences, so that they articulate and align their ministry activities around this vision 

  • Set annual goals through prayer, research and reflection with your teams (students, faculty, and staff) for qualitative and quantitative growth, including conversions and leadership development 

  • Structural Architect: 

You create, develop, align, and leverage ministry plans, programs, teams, and structures to close the gap between current reality and the aspirational goals. 

  • Build leadership teams who trust and partner well with you and who demonstrate spiritual vitality, relational health, and mission alignment 

  • Develop and execute plans to achieve annual goals, evaluating and modifying the plan as needed throughout the year 

  • Increase momentum for the vision by aligning programs, structures, conferences, and teams around the goals 

  • Mobilize students and faculty to engage their relational networks with the gospel and to start new missional communities 

  • Under the direction of the Area Director, may supervise Ministry Interns and Campus Ministry Interns as delegated 

  • Missional Developer: 

You intentionally gather, invite, and develop diverse groups of students and faculty so that they not only encounter and follow Jesus as Savior and Lord but also advance the mission on campus as participants and leaders. 

  • Create ways for faculty and students to encounter and follow Jesus through Scripture, worship, prayer, mission experiences, conferences, etc. 

  • Equip students and faculty so that they think strategically about campus engagement and so that they proclaim – in word, deed, and power – the good news of Jesus, regularly inviting students and faculty to follow him as Savior and Lord 

  • Disciple students and faculty by equipping them to hear the Word, respond actively, and debrief and interpret the experience so that they grow in Christlikeness, reflect our Core Values, and develop ministry skills 

  • Invite, coach, and equip students and faculty to become increasingly effective participants and leaders, including starting new witnessing communities on campuses 

 

Organizational Collaboration 

As a Campus Staff Minister, you have joined a national mission. Therefore, you work with a network of other local, area, regional, and national InterVarsity staff and volunteers so that our work reflects Biblical standards of excellence, integrity, and partnership. 

  • Partner with and respond positively to the direction and coaching of your supervisors and national leaders 

  • Contribute to collaborative and productive team meetings and relationships 

  • Affiliate chapters under your care and submit Graduating Student Forms in order to increase our partnership with current students and alumni 

  • Use national ministry resources and tools, as requested, including recruiting and/or participating in local, regional, or national conferences as  

  • Complete reporting, planning and review requirements in a timely way so that you and your supervisors can assess and improve your work as a CSM 

  • Comply with all InterVarsity policies and procedures 

 

Ministry Partnership Development 

As a Campus Staff Minister, you will develop a team of partners – churches and individuals (including alumni and community members) – who will resource the ministry financially, in prayer, or volunteer service that advances the mission. 

  • Raise 100% of the financial budget assigned by your supervisor 

  • Communicate regularly with your ministry partners, nurturing the relationship through visits, phone calls, emails and regular prayer letters 

  • Develop on-going, long-lasting partnership with alumni and volunteers 

  • Comply with all Ministry Partnership Policies 

  • Identify and invest in advocates who will build networks of volunteers and donors on InterVarsity’s behalf 

 

Accomplish all other assigned tasks as appropriate 

 

QUALIFICATIONS (common to all levels of CSM) 

  • Annually affirm InterVarsity’s Statement of Agreement (Doctrinal Basis and Purpose Statement). Abide by InterVarsity’s Code of Conduct. Believe and behave consonantly with InterVarsity’s Human Sexuality Theological Paper. Affirm and behave consonantly with InterVarsity’s “Women in Ministry Statement of Affirmation” 

  • Bachelor’s degree for CSMs assigned to a four-year campus. A minimum of an Associate’s degree for CSMs assigned to a two-year campus or a community college 

  • Strong interpersonal skills (including ability to minister to diverse ethnic communities and faculty) 

  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills 

  • Demonstrated problem solving skills 

  • Familiarity with word processing, presentation, email, and spreadsheet software 

 

WORK ENVIRONMENT/PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS 

The CSM position leads ministry in a college campus environment. A designated office space may or may not be available. The CSM is required to travel to on-campus and off- campus sites as appropriate. Off-campus travel includes, but is not limited to: student ministry conferences, Ministry Partnership Development meetings, and InterVarsity- sponsored training sessions, meetings, and conferences. The CSM is regularly required to communicate with others, and routinely uses standard office equipment such as computers, phones, photocopiers, filing cabinets, etc.

HomeBase provides case management and essential services to at-risk individuals and families to prevent homelessness. Individuals and families receive services that will help overcome problems with public benefits, housing, education, health care and other issues that could impede their ability to maintain stable households. 

Position: Intake Specialist 

Reports To: Assistant Director/Program Manager     

Location: Church Ave, Brooklyn NY

What The Intake Specialist Does:

  • Coordinate the intake process with individuals and families facing housing crises. This includes reviewing eligibility documentation, gathering detailed information about their current situation, housing history, income, expenses, barriers to housing stability, and support systems. 
  • Assess the level of homelessness risk based on established criteria and program guidelines. 
  • Effectively communicate the homelessness prevention program's services, eligibility requirements, and limitations to potential clients. 
  • Schedule appointments, make referrals, and provide all individuals with information on community resources. 
  • Ensure that all client resources are up-to-date and available in the reception area. 
  • Perform periodic outreach activities to publicize the availability of services. 
  • Perform data entry, filing, copying and faxing of documents. 
  • Provide referrals to appropriate internal and external resources, such as emergency shelters, housing assistance programs, legal services, employment services, mental health services, and community-based organizations. 
  • Collaborate effectively with program staff, including Program Supervisors, case managers, case support workers and outreach workers, to ensure coordinated service delivery. 
  • Stay informed about current housing trends, local resources, and relevant guidelines related to homelessness prevention. 
  • Participate in regular team meetings, supervision sessions, and training opportunities to enhance skills and knowledge. 
  • Adhere to agency policies and procedures, ethical guidelines, and professional standards of conduct. 
  • Report to work daily with fully charged cell phone for multifactor authentication.  
  • Conduct home visits and inspections for any open HomeBase case; not limited to assigned cases only. Evaluate living conditions and/or conduct inspections as per DHS/DSS/HRA standards.  
  • Create and maintain client files, both hard copy and electronic.  
  • Assist with reception duties when necessary. 
  • Other duties as assigned.

Education, Licenses and/or Certifications Required: 

  • High school diploma or G.E.D. 

Minimum Experiences and Skills Required:  

  • Four years of relevant experience, preferably in a mid-sized (250+ employees) organization.

  • Strong writing skills, with the ability to draft assessments, service plans, progress notes, weekly reports, and general client-related correspondence.

author: Katie Weeks
post_html:
Job Description

Crisis Assistance Ministry seeks a mission-anchored, people-centered, growth-oriented, and community-minded leader to serve as its next Chief Executive Officer. This is a rare opportunity to lead one of Charlotte-Mecklenburg’s most trusted institutions at a time when its work has never been more necessary. 

Following Carol Hardison’s retirement in 2027 after more than 26 years of leadership, the next CEO will inherit a stable organization, experienced team, strong culture, deep community relationships, and significant credibility. This is not a turnaround assignment, nor is it a caretaker role. The opportunity is to earn trust, understand what makes the organization effective, and guide its continued evolution with fresh perspective, sound judgment, and a clear vision for measurable growth and greater impact.  

Mission: To provide assistance and advocacy for people in financial crisis, helping them move toward self-sufficiency.

Vision: Our ultimate vision is a community where everyone has the resources and stability to thrive without our services.

Reporting Structure: The CEO reports to a 25-member Board of Directors and leads a five-member executive leadership team: the Chief People and Culture Officer, Chief Customer Experience Officer, Chief Advancement Officer, Chief Housing Stability Officer, and Chief Technology and Financial Operations Officer.

Impact and Scale: Crisis Assistance Ministry employs approximately 60 people and operates with an $18.4 million FY2026 budget. In 2025, the organization served nearly 44,000 people, distributed 1.7 million clothing and household items, and provided more than $8 million in emergency housing assistance.

Location and Working Environment: The role is based in Charlotte and requires a visible, consistent presence with staff, customers, donors, public officials, and community partners. This is not a remote leadership position.

Compensation and Benefits: Crisis Assistance Ministry offers competitive compensation and a comprehensive benefits package. The salary range is $215,000-$225,000.  

The Leadership Opportunity 

Honor the foundation. Lead the next chapter. Crisis Assistance Ministry is healthy, and it cannot stand still. The cost of living continues to rise, increasing the demand for services. The organization has the staff and operational ability to serve more people, but available aid funding has not kept pace with demand. The next CEO must expand and diversify resources while working with staff, customers, and community partners to increase housing stability for low-income residents of Mecklenburg County.

Key Responsibilities of the Chief Executive Officer 

Strategic Direction and Measurable Growth 

  • Lead an inclusive planning process that defines the organization’s five-year direction, establishes measurable priorities, and creates accountability. Balance immediate crisis response with prevention, financial empowerment, and systems-level work while remaining grounded in the organization’s core mission. 
  • Use customer experience, program outcomes, community data, and staff expertise to determine what should be preserved, improved, piloted, expanded, or stopped. 
  • Set and achieve ambitious, measurable growth goals for public and private funding so direct customer assistance can keep pace with the community’s growing needs while protecting staff well-being, operational effectiveness, and customer dignity. 

Fundraising and Financial Stewardship 
  • Partner closely with the Chief Advancement Officer while personally leading high-level relationships, visibility, storytelling, and asks that cannot be delegated. Cultivate durable relationships with individual donors, foundations, corporations, faith communities, and public funders. 
  • Drive significant growth in major gifts, planned giving, and private and public revenue strategies to ensure the organization can sustain greater direct assistance to customers.  
  • Ensure disciplined financial management, risk oversight, resource allocation, and transparent reporting to the Board and community. 

Community Leadership, Partnership, and Voice 
  • Expand Crisis Assistance Ministry’s role as a highly visible community leader, trusted convener, educator, and advocate addressing the systemic conditions that drive financial instability. Build strong partnerships across government, philanthropy, business, nonprofits, schools, housing providers, faith communities, and neighborhoods. 
  • Convene partners, collaborate with organizations with similar missions, strengthen referrals, and improve connections to long-term housing solutions.  
  • Center the experiences of customers and people with lived experience in public education, advocacy, service design, and organizational decision-making. 

People, Culture, and Organizational Effectiveness 
  • Preserve a culture where dignity, integrity, respect, empathy, compassion, trust, flexibility, and employee well-being are experienced, not simply stated. 
  • Lead through a strong executive team by setting direction, opening doors, removing barriers, and holding leaders accountable. 
  • Communicate consistently and candidly across departments. 
  • Strengthen staff development, succession planning, training, internal mobility, onboarding, and the thoughtful transfer of institutional knowledge. 


Service, Technology, and Operational Improvement 

  • Prioritize customer support and process efficiency as part of the organization’s continued evolution.  
  • Use technology, automation, data, and responsible AI to make services more accessible and efficient while preserving a personal and humane approach. 

Board Partnership  
  • Build a candid, strategic partnership with the Board by providing timely information and encouraging open dialogue. 
  • Engage directors meaningfully in strategy, fundraising, community relationships, CEO accountability, and stewardship of the leadership transition. 

The Ideal Candidate Profile

There is no single background that guarantees success. Three capabilities will be especially important: demonstrated fundraising and donor development, visible external community leadership and public advocacy, and ambitious vision and innovation. Through progressively responsible leadership experience, the strongest candidates will demonstrate these priorities and the following capabilities: 
  • Authentic commitment to economic justice and to developing deep expertise in poverty, housing instability, and the realities facing households with limited financial resources. 
  • A people-centered leadership style marked by humility, curiosity, emotional intelligence, transparency, calm, flexibility, and the ability to develop and empower strong leaders. 
  • A record of significant, measurable fundraising growth across individual giving, major gifts, foundations, corporations, and public funding, with the confidence and skill to personally cultivate and ask for meaningful gifts and commitments. 
  • Enterprise-level leadership in a complex environment. 
  • A record of visible external leadership, conveying partners and building trust across government, philanthropy, business, community organizations, media, and people with lived experience; Charlotte relationships are valuable but not required if the candidate can build credibility quickly. 
  • An ambitious, innovative, growth-oriented mindset, with the ability to translate bold vision into a focused, measurable strategy while exercising sound financial, operational, and risk-management judgment. 
  • Experience guiding ambitious change, thoughtfully listening before acting, explaining decisions, and moving with appropriate urgency while helping people feel stable and included through transition. 
  • Strong public speaking, storytelling, advocacy, and media skills, paired with the judgment to navigate political complexity. 
  • Meaningful experience partnering with a governing board.  
  • A bachelor’s degree is required; an advanced degree is preferred.   

What Success Could Look Like After Two Years 
  • Staff engagement remains strong, and employees describe the culture as stable, caring, transparent, and open to thoughtful improvement. 
  • The Board, staff, and community understand a focused multi-year strategy, and the organization is measuring progress against it. 
  • Donors, government leaders, and partners experience continuity of mission while recognizing the new CEO’s distinctive leadership. 
  • Public and private fundraising are on a measurable growth trajectory enabling the organization to meet more of the community’s need. 
  • Customers and referral partners experience clearer, more accessible, and more dignified pathways to assistance. 
  • The executive team is empowered, the Board is governing actively, and responsibility for the organization’s success is broadly shared. 


About Crisis Assistance Ministry 

Founded in 1975, Crisis Assistance Ministry is Charlotte-Mecklenburg’s trusted safety net and a leader in housing stability and financial security. The organization provides emergency rent and utility assistance, free clothing and household essentials, financial empowerment coaching, community education, advocacy, and partnership-building — all grounded in dignity, integrity, compassion, and trust.

Want to know more? Visit crisisassistance.org. 

Benefits

The benefits package includes medical, dental, and vision insurance; executive 401(k) match; flexible spending accounts (FSA); life and AD&D insurance; short- and long-term disability coverage; group accident and critical illness insurance; and an Employee Assistance Program (EAP). Paid time off includes vacation, sick time, bereavement, volunteer time, and holidays.  

Equal Opportunity

Crisis Assistance Ministry does not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, national origin, disability, genetic information, marital status, status as a covered veteran, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state, or local laws, in any of its activities or operations. 

How to Apply

This is an opportunity to inherit an organization that Charlotte trusts and help ensure that trust translates into greater stability, dignity, and opportunity for thousands of customers. The next CEO will be asked to lead Crisis Assistance Ministry confidently into its next chapter. 

To apply, scroll to the bottom of this page.  You will see instructions for uploading your compelling cover letter, resume, and salary requirements.

Please provide all requested information to be considered. For technical assistance, contact talent@armstrongmcguire.com. No phone calls, please. Applications will not be accepted by email or directly from third-party posting sites. 

Timing: Applications received by October 2, 2026, will receive priority consideration. The Board anticipates selecting the next CEO in late 2026, with an early 2027 start date. A thoughtful transition process will support the transfer of key relationships and institutional knowledge while giving the new CEO appropriate space to establish their own leadership.

The lead pastor and church planter will lead the church to build a fresh, vibrant expression of Jesus's work in their community to effectively make disciples in Perry County for generations to come. Currently, a transitional pastor is guiding the elders and members to discern the greatest needs in their church so they can best be positioned to impact their community with the Gospel.

Church Location Description: Perry County is in the picturesque hills of rural South Central Pennsylvania, not far from Carlisle and the Western Shore of Harrisburg. Among the 45k+ people that call Perry County home are wide open fields and state game lands. This area is perfect for those who love the country and outdoors, yet still like easy access to metropolitan conveniences.

Compensation: Part-Time Salary, Housing Allowance

Minimum Education Level: If necessary, must be willing to complete the Ministerial Study Program.

Minimum Credential Level: Must be willing to complete the Alliance accreditation process

Minimum Years of Experience: The ideal candidate has proven experience leading change and making disciples.

Qualifications:

  • Skilled in communicating the Gospel and connecting it to every aspect of life

  • Ability to mentor others in their commitment to follow Christ

  • Gives focused attention to disciple well-rounded and effective leaders

  • Ability to shepherd and create paths of opportunities for the congregation to engage with mission communities, outreach, and community events

  • Willing to invest in understanding the local people, history, culture, and traditions

Church Size: Less than 50 Avg. Sunday Attendance

Church Setting: Rural/Small Town

Church Vision: Honor Perry’s legacy by creating a fresh, vibrant expression of Jesus's work in the community that can effectively make disciples in Perry County for generations to come.

Church History: Perry Alliance Church, as it was originally known, was planted in 1989 by a group from a neighboring New Buffalo Alliance Church who desired to reach more of Perry County with the Gospel. The church experienced significant growth in the early 2000s before a series of challenges led to the decision to replant the church in 2024. As it moves toward the future, the church desires a restart that will allow it to continue its original mission.

To be considered for this position, please complete the application to include your testimony, resume and other background information related to the position.

If the district office has reviewed your application and thinks you may be a potential match for the position, the hiring manager will contact you to discuss the next steps.

This position requires licensing with The Christian & Missionary Alliance. To learn more about The Alliance and requirements for licensing, please visit our website

Please do not contact the church directly.

Overview

The Corning Corps of The Salvation Army is seeking a Part-time (15 Hr/Wk) Ministry assistant.

 

Our part-time positions offer generous time off every year including 14 paid holidays, vacation time and sick time

 

SCOPE AND PURPOSE OF POSITION:

Assist the Corps Officers in multiple aspects of ministry at the Corning Corps. The CMA assists in planning and coordinating kids and teen program, VBS, outreach ministry, Sunday School and they will assist with seasonal events such as Kettles and Back to School. They will be expected to share a vision for growing the corps and the Kingdom of God.

Responsibilities

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:

Reasonable accommodation may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

  •  
  • To be fully involved in Sunday activities including attending services, leading Sunday School classes and junior church in rotation with Corps Officers
  • Assist the Corps Officer with the development, planning and implementation of various programs, including but not limited to:
    • Social and evangelistic ministry programs;
    • Seasonal efforts such as Kettles, Angel Tree, Back to School, etc.
    • Corps summer youth ministries, including the recruitment for camps and Bible school programs;
  • Assist the Corps Officer in providing leadership at events including assisting the Corps Officers in the promotion, registration and implementation of events/activities.
  • Assist with transportation for programs, divisional events, Camp Long Point, and seasonal needs (kettles, Angel Tree, etc.)
  • Complete training and licensing requirements for Kid’s Café program to be able to step in as coverage as needed for call offs of Kid’s Café staff
  • Gather and regularly submit program statistics and maintain program records
  • Assist as needed for general, daily Corps support needs and perform special projects as assigned by the Corps Officers.

Qualifications

SPECIAL SKILLS, CERTIFICATES, LICENSES, REGISTRATIONS:

·        High School diploma

·        Effective communication skills

                       ·        Valid driver’s license and approval to drive TSA vehicles

·        Basic computer skills

·        Emotional and spiritual maturity

·        As this position is a ministry position, individuals must support and uphold The      Salvation Army Mission Statement and Salvation Army Doctrines

 

We are an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability or veteran status.

post_html:
Campus Staff Minister I - Greater North Texas Area (Undergraduate Ministry)

Work Location:

Texas

Job Type:

Full time

God has called InterVarsity to plant and to build witnessing communities of students and faculty who follow Jesus on college and university campuses. Through these groups, we believe ever- increasing numbers of students and faculty from all ethnic groups and areas of the campus will be transformed by the Gospel. We expect to see campuses increasingly become places where people, ideas, and structures flourish to the glory of God. We confidently anticipate that our InterVarsity alumni will become change agents across the country and around the world. We pursue this calling by discerning and actively participating in what God is already doing on campus. This is the essence of being a Campus Staff Minister (CSM).

CONTEXT:

Join our Greater North Texas Ministry team! We offer excellent and practical ministry training for each part of your job from discipleship, outreach, evangelism, student empowerment, and missions to professional development and support raising. You will learn how to plant new ministry as well as grow established student chapters alongside a diverse team of students, staff and types of focused ministries. Our team is known for holistic discipleship, hospitality, communal support, and having lots of fun together. This is also a great team for moms in ministry. Come learn and grow with us!

LOCATION:

We currently have the most need for Campus Staff Ministers for the following locations/foci. Please indicate in your application which you are interested in (if any):

  • Baylor University
  • The University of Texas at Arlington

If you are interested in working at a location that is not listed, fill out the application and indicate where in the relevant question. You are also welcome to input multiple locations and we will take them into consideration. Note that our region of InterVarsity serves the states of Texas, Oklahoma, Arkansas, and Louisiana. If you would like to serve in one of those states, search for it in the search bar to find the openings. During the interview, there will be a greater discussion around location and also the opportunity to go to other places in need of staff.

ESSENTIAL COMMITMENTS/RESPONSIBILITIES 

Spiritual Growth 

You pursue maturity as a disciple of Jesus Christ so that your life and work increasingly reflects a growing love for God, God’s Word, God’s people of every ethnicity and culture, and God’s purposes in the world. To do this, you will: 

  • Pursue a vibrant relationship with the triune God through engagement with Scripture, prayer, and worship, both individually and in community 

  • Develop self-leadership (growing in self-awareness, self-management, relational integrity, and resiliency) 

  • Embrace Scriptural standards for behavior and attitudes 

 

Campus Leadership 

You communicate and model InterVarsity’s vision to see students and faculty transformed, campuses renewed and world changers developed 

  • Create a culture of humble dependence on God and bold expectation in God’s intention to start new witnessing communities throughout the campus and on new campuses 

  • Model – in person and through programs – InterVarsity’s vision and Core Values, including a biblically-defined commitment to engage every ethnic and social group on campus 

  • Lead students and faculty – individually and collectively – through Scripture, prayer, teaching, and discipleship experiences, so that they articulate and align their ministry activities around this vision 

  • Set annual goals through prayer, research and reflection with your teams (students, faculty, and staff) for qualitative and quantitative growth, including conversions and leadership development 

 

You create, develop, align and leverage ministry plans, programs, teams, and structures to close the gap between current reality and the aspirational goals. 

  • Build leadership teams who trust and partner well with you and who demonstrate spiritual vitality, relational health, and mission alignment 

  • Develop and execute plans to achieve annual goals, evaluating and modifying the plan as needed throughout the year 

  • Increase momentum for the vision by aligning programs, structures, conferences and teams around the goals 

  • Mobilize students and faculty to engage their relational networks with the gospel and to start new missional communities 

  • Under the direction of the Area Director, may supervise Ministry Interns and Campus Ministry Interns as delegated 

 

You intentionally gather, invite, and develop diverse groups of students and faculty so that they not only encounter and follow Jesus as Savior and Lord but also advance the mission on campus as participants and leaders. 

  • Create ways for faculty and students to encounter and follow Jesus through Scripture, worship, prayer, mission experiences, conferences, etc. 

  • Equip students and faculty so that they think strategically about campus engagement and so that they proclaim – in word, deed, and power – the good news of Jesus, regularly inviting students and faculty to follow him as Savior and Lord 

  • Disciple students and faculty by equipping them to hear the Word, respond actively, and debrief and interpret the experience so that they grow in Christlikeness, reflect our Core Values, and develop ministry skills 

  • Invite, coach, and equip students and faculty to become increasingly effective participants and leaders, including starting new witnessing communities on campuses 

 

Organizational Collaboration 

You work with a network of other local, area, regional, and national InterVarsity staff and volunteers so that our work reflects Biblical standards of excellence, integrity, and partnership. 

  • Partner with and respond positively to the direction and coaching of your supervisors and national leaders 

  • Contribute to collaborative and productive team meetings and relationships 

  • Affiliate chapters under your care and submit Graduating Student Forms in order to increase our partnership with current students and alumni 

  • Use national ministry resources and tools, as requested, including recruiting and/or participating in local, regional, or national conferences as  

  • Complete reporting, planning and review requirements in a timely way so that you and your supervisors can assess and improve your work as a CSM 

  • Comply with all InterVarsity policies and procedures 

 

Ministry Partnership Development 

You will develop a team of partners – churches and individuals (including alumni and community members) – who will resource the ministry financially, in prayer, or volunteer service that advances the mission. 

  • Raise 100% of the financial budget assigned by your supervisor 

  • Communicate regularly with your ministry partners, nurturing the relationship through visits, phone calls, emails and regular prayer letters 

  • Develop on-going, long-lasting partnership with alumni and volunteers 

  • Comply with all Ministry Partnership Policies 

  • Identify and invest in advocates who will build networks of volunteers and donors on InterVarsity’s behalf 

 

Accomplish all other assigned tasks as appropriate 

 

QUALIFICATIONS (common to all levels of CSM) 

  • Annually affirm InterVarsity’s Statement of Agreement (Doctrinal Basis and Purpose Statement). Abide by InterVarsity’s Code of Conduct. Believe and behave consonantly with InterVarsity’s Human Sexuality Theological Paper. Affirm and behave consonantly with InterVarsity’s “Women in Ministry Statement of Affirmation” 

  • Bachelor’s degree for CSMs assigned to a four-year campus. A minimum of an Associate’s degree for CSMs assigned to a two-year campus or a community college 

  • Strong interpersonal skills (including ability to minister to diverse ethnic communities and faculty) 

  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills 

  • Demonstrated problem solving skills 

  • Familiarity with word processing, presentation, email, and spreadsheet software 

 

WORK ENVIRONMENT/PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS 

The CSM position leads ministry in a college campus environment. A designated office space may or may not be available. The CSM is required to travel to on-campus and off- campus sites as appropriate. Off-campus travel includes, but is not limited to: student ministry conferences, Ministry Partnership Development meetings, and InterVarsity- sponsored training sessions, meetings, and conferences. The CSM is regularly required to communicate with others, and routinely uses standard office equipment such as computers, phones, photocopiers, filing cabinets, etc. 

Pay Range: $39,288.00 - $52,392.00 per year

Pay: This position is funded through personal fundraising. Accordingly, compensation will vary based on the ability of the individual to secure a donor team to fund the cost of his/her salary. The anticipated salary range for this position on a full-time basis (40 hours/week) is dependent on a variety of factors, including location and cost of living. The actual salary received, including any geographic adjustment to account for location and cost of living, is subject to the individual’s ability to raise funds necessary to cover the full amount of such salary within the range set forth in the job posting details.

Benefits:

We offer a competitive benefits package, including health care and retirement savings with a match. Eligibility is based on employee type and hours worked.  Benefits include the following:

  • 403(b) Retirement Savings Plan

  • 403(b) matching contributions

  • Dental insurance

  • Employee assistance program

  • Employee discounts

  • Flexible work schedule

  • Flexible spending accounts

  • Health insurance

  • Health savings account

  • Life insurance

  • Paid time off

  • Parental leave

  • Professional development assistance

  • Vision insurance

Equal Employment Opportunity: 

 

InterVarsity Christian Fellowship/USA is both an equal opportunity employer and a faith-based religious organization. We conduct hiring without regard to race, color, ancestry, national origin, citizenship, age, sex, marital status, parental status, membership in any labor organization, political ideology, or disability of an otherwise qualified individual. The status of InterVarsity Christian Fellowship/USA as an equal opportunity employer does not prevent the organization from hiring staff based on their religious beliefs so that all staff share the same religious commitment.  Pursuant to the Civil Rights Act of 1964, Section 702 (42 U.S.C. 2000e 1(a)) InterVarsity Christian Fellowship/USA has the right to, and does, hire only candidates who agree with InterVarsity’s Statement of Agreement: Purpose and Doctrinal Basis because InterVarsity believes that each and every staff plays a vital role in advancing InterVarsity’s mission and purposes.

Summary

This position is located in the Veterans Health Administration (VHA), Southeast Network (VISN 7), VA Augusta Health Care System (VAAHCS) in Augusta, Georgia located in the Chaplain Service Department. The Chaplain provides services within various settings, including Veterans Integrated Service Networks (VISNs), Inpatient Clinics, Outpatient Clinics and domiciliary throughout the United States.


Duties

Duties include but are not limited to:

  • Serves as a certified Chaplain (CPE) providing comprehensive, religious ministry services and training to Veteran patients and students according to their specific needs.
  • Carries out an education ministry with the CPE Center, which is highly integrated into VHA's Chaplain program. Provides thorough guidance and advice to Chaplain Service management staff, students, other Chaplains, and stakeholders.
  • Manages the daily operations of the CPE Center and develops and implements program policies and procedures. Serves as a certified educator of record for all CPE students for an assigned designated area. Provides administrative oversight and programmatic resources and monitors educational outcomes.
  • Offers students an opportunity to develop and expand professional caring skills in a clinical setting to address a person's spiritual, emotional, and physical needs; and offers students experience with hands-on spiritual care for hospitalized patients.
  • Maintains records for all educator evaluations, student records, center portfolio, and CPE accreditation requirements, which may include off-site CPE satellite and placement contracts.
  • Seeks approval for allied health trainee positions through the Office of Academic Affiliations (OAA). Conducts recruitment and interviews and selects students for the CPE program.
  • Ensures all documentation is completed for compliance. Develops educational curricula that are measurable, outcome-oriented, and evidence-based and designed to meet board certification competencies.
  • Develops relationships with key staff related to the CPE program, e.g., clinical preceptors, Advisory Group members, and OAA staff.
  • Provides extended and intensive pastoral counseling as an integral part of the treatment program with patients facing complex, ethical, moral, and/or spiritual issues.
  • Monitors the CPE Center's program effectiveness and modification of service pattern, which includes research and leadership of clinical teams. Develops and implements methods to measure the effectiveness of the Chaplain educational program.
  • Uses outcome evaluations to improve educational services and to design education system changes. Seeks best practices, primary research, and research literature that informs the ministry specialty and one's spiritual care practice.
  • Provides leadership, direction, orientation, coaching, in-service training, staff development, and continuing education programs.
  • Serves as a primary senior Chaplain education resource, spiritual advisor, and liaison for the spiritual needs of Veterans patients, students, caregivers, and staff.
  • Serves as a primary senior Chaplain education resource, spiritual advisor, and liaison for the spiritual needs of Veterans patients, students, caregivers, and staff.
  • Serves as a Chaplain senior representative and a fully recognized member of an interdisciplinary treatment team (IDT). Advises and collaborates with other senior members of the treatment team to provide comprehensive healthcare services to Veterans.
  • Engages in group consultative discussions or conferences with treatment professionals to provide senior-level Chaplain related input. Collaborates with IDT on the evaluation and review of VHA's CPE Center program progress.
  • Coordinates with community organizations to provide spiritual care and educational outreach, e.g., interested community organizations, local clubs, church groups, special agencies, business organizations, and other stakeholders to sustain the necessary links with the outside community.
Work Schedule: 8:00am to 4:30pm, Monday thru Friday
Telework: Not Available
Virtual: This is not a virtual position.
Functional Statement #: 60306F
Relocation/Recruitment Incentives: Not Authorized
Permanent Change of Station (PCS): Not Authorized
PCS Appraised Value Offer (AVO): Not Authorized


Requirements

Conditions of employment

  • You must be a U.S. Citizen to apply for this job.
  • Selective Service Registration is required for males born after 12/31/1959.
  • Must be proficient in written and spoken English.
  • Subject to background/security investigation.
  • Selected applicants will be required to complete an online onboarding process. Acceptable form(s) of identification will be required to complete pre-employment requirements (https://www.uscis.gov/i-9-central/form-i-9-acceptable-documents). Effective May 7, 2025, driver's licenses or state-issued identification cards that are not REAL ID compliant cannot be utilized as an acceptable form of identification for employment.
  • Must pass pre-employment physical evaluation.
  • Participation in the seasonal influenza vaccination program is a requirement for all Department of Veterans Affairs Health Care Personnel (HCP).
  • Complete all application requirements detailed in the "Required Documents" section of this announcement.
As a condition of employment for accepting this position, you will be required to serve a 1 or 2-year trial period during which we will evaluate your fitness and whether your continued employment advances the public interest. In determining if your employment advances the public interest, we may consider:
  • your performance and conduct;
  • the needs and interests of the agency;
  • whether your continued employment would advance organizational goals of the agency or the Government; and
  • whether your continued employment would advance the efficiency of the Federal service.
Upon completion of your trial period, your employment will be terminated unless you receive certification, in writing, that your continued employment advances the public interest.

Qualifications

Applicants pending the completion of educational or certification/licensure requirements may be referred and tentatively selected but may not be hired until all requirements are met.

Basic Requirements:

  • United States Citizenship: Non-citizens may only be appointed when it is not possible to recruit qualified citizens in accordance with VA Policy.
  • English Language Proficiency. Candidates must be proficient in spoken and written English in accordance with 38 U.S.C. § 7403(f).
  • Education. Applicants must possess a Master of Divinity degree or equivalent educational qualifications as evidenced by a graduate-level theological degree from a college, university or theological school accredited by a member of the Council for Higher Education Accreditation (CHEA) or Association of Theological Schools (ATS) and recognized by the U.S. Department of Education.
  • NOTE: For applicants who do not possess a Master of Divinity degree or equivalent educational degree, an approved educational equivalency review from a nationally recognized board certification body for chaplains (see paragraph d) is acceptable.
  • Foreign Education. To be creditable, education completed outside the U.S. must be submitted to a current affiliate agency of the National Association of Credential Evaluation Services (NACES) at https://www.naces.org/members and be deemed at least equivalent to that gained in a conventional U.S. program.
  • CPE Educator. CPE Educators must be certified by an agency whose CPE units of training are recognized by the BCCI ® or a U.S. certifying body that has a reciprocity agreement with BCCI ®. CPE Educators must be certified by the same accrediting body as the CPE training program where the position is being filled for the CPE training program to maintain accreditation.
  • Ecclesiastical Endorsement. In accordance with 38 C.F.R. § 17.655, ecclesiastical endorsement is a condition of employment as a VA chaplain. An individual must possess and maintain a full and active ecclesiastical endorsement to be employed as a VA chaplain. Applicants must have an ecclesiastical endorsement, dated within the past 12 months. Ecclesiastical endorsements must be from the official national endorsing authority of the applicant's/employee's faith group or denomination. Ecclesiastical endorsement is a written official statement, by the official national endorsing body of the faith group or denomination, certifying that the applicant is in good standing with the applicant's faith group or denomination; and stating that the individual is, in the opinion of the endorsing body, qualified to perform the full range of ministry required in the VA pluralistic setting. Loss of endorsement will result in removal from the GS-0060 Chaplain series and may result in termination of employment. The National Chaplain Service maintains a list of approved endorsing organizations that can be found here: National VA Chaplain Service SharePoint.
  • Board Certification. Applicants must be a Board-Certified Chaplain certified by BCCI ® or a U.S. certifying body that has a reciprocity agreement with BCCI ®. Board Certification that requires 4 units of CPE is qualifying. The National Chaplain Service maintains a list of approved certifications found on the National VA Chaplain Service SharePoint.

May qualify based on being covered by the Grandfathering Provision as described in the VA Qualification Standard for this occupation (only applicable to current VHA employees who are in this occupation and meet the criteria).

Grade Determinations: GS-12

Specialized Experience. At the GS-12 level, the candidate must have one year of creditable experience equivalent to the next lower grade level, GS-11, that is directly related to the position to be filled. Specialized experience can be described as but not limited to: Providing advance care planning education, information, and counseling for patients and their families. Providing guidance and/or support for patients to express values through processes such as life review, oral history, and end of life preparation and documentation. Supporting the development of staff resiliency by providing emotional and spiritual support and compassionate presence and develops programs for staff development and wellness. Providing education and equipping other healthcare staff and trainees to screen for spiritual and religious needs, and the importance of appropriate referrals to chaplains for complex spiritual distress.

Certification. CPE Educators must be certified by an agency whose CPE units of training are recognized by the BCCI ® or a U.S. certifying body that has a reciprocity agreement with BCCI ®. CPE Educators must be certified by the same accrediting body as the CPE training program where the position is being filled for the CPE training program to maintain accreditation.

Demonstrated Knowledge, Skills and Abilities. In addition to the experience or education above, the candidate must demonstrate the following KSAs:
  • Ability to independently educate all levels of CPE students and plan, organize, and implement all levels of the CPE program.
  • Skill in adhering to all accreditation standards, processes and practices including, but not limited to, timely and professional submission of all required program reports, center portfolio, fees and dues.
  • Skill in written and verbal communication that are articulate, professional and cohesive.
  • Ability to recruit, interview and select students for the CPE program.
  • Knowledge of professional ethics for certified educators and history of CPE.
  • Ability to apply theoretical understanding for and competence in administering and conducting all levels of CPE programs.
  • Knowledge of emerging trends and research in the area of pastoral education.
  • Knowledge of diverse conceptual frameworks for developing educational curriculum.
Preferred Experience:
  • A certified Clinical Pastoral Educator from VA-approved professional organization and recognized by the Department of Education such as Association of Clinical Pastoral Education (ACPE)
  • Experience in providing educational supervision for Clinical Pastoral Education (CPE) to CPE Level 1 and CPE Level 2 students.
  • Experience in providing educational supervision for students seeking to become CPE Educator.
  • Experience in demonstrating skills in adhering to all CPE accreditation standards, processes and practices including, but not limited to, timely and professional submission of all required program reports, center portfolio, fees and dues.
  • Proficiency in Electronic Health Record (EHR) documentation (particularly Spiritual Assessments/Reassessments) and in teaching Joint Commission documentation standards of timeliness to CPE students.

Reference: For more information on this qualification standard, please visit https://www.va.gov/ohrm/QualificationStandards/.

The full performance level of this vacancy is GS-12. The actual grade at which an applicant may be selected for this vacancy is in the range of GS-12

Physical Requirements: This position requires the Chaplain to meaningfully engage with Veteran patients and family members by walking and moving within the healthcare setting or with the incumbent using an assistive device. The Chaplain is required to speak, hear (hearing aid permitted) and work closely with others.

Education

Note: Only education or degrees recognized by the U.S. Department of Education from accredited colleges, universities, schools, or institutions may be used to qualify for Federal employment. You can verify your education here: http://ope.ed.gov/accreditation/. If you are using foreign education to meet qualification requirements, you must send a Certificate of Foreign Equivalency with your transcript in order to receive credit for that education. For further information, visit: https://sites.ed.gov/international/recognition-of-foreign-qualifications/.

Additional information

Receiving Service Credit for Earning Annual (Vacation) Leave: Federal Employees earn annual leave at a rate (4, 6 or 8 hours per pay period) which is based on the number of years they have served as a Federal employee. Selected applicants may qualify for credit toward annual leave accrual, based on prior work experience or military service experience. This credited service can be used in determining the rate at which they earn annual leave. Such credit must be requested and approved prior to the appointment date and is not guaranteed.

During the application process you may have an option to opt-in to make your resume available to hiring managers in the agency who have similar positions. Opting in does not impact your application for this announcement, nor does it guarantee further consideration for additional positions.

This job opportunity announcement may be used to fill additional vacancies.

This position is in the Excepted Service and does not confer competitive status.

VA encourages persons with disabilities to apply. The health-related positions in VA are covered by Title 38, and are not covered by the Schedule A excepted appointment authority.

If you are unable to apply online or need an alternate method to submit documents, please reach out to the Agency Contact listed in this Job Opportunity Announcement.

Under the Fair Chance to Compete Act, the Department of Veterans Affairs prohibits requesting an applicant's criminal history prior to accepting a tentative job offer. For more information about the Act and the complaint process, visit Human Resources and Administration/Operations, Security, and Preparedness (HRA/OSP) at The Fair Chance Act.

Candidates should be committed to improving the efficiency of the Federal government, passionate about the ideals of our American republic, and committed to upholding the rule of law and the United States Constitution.

post_html:
Campus Staff Minister - Michigan Lower Peninsula Region (Undergraduate Ministry)

Work Location:

Michigan

Job Type:

Full time

God has called InterVarsity to plant and to build witnessing communities of students and faculty who follow Jesus on college and university campuses. Through these groups, we believe ever- increasing numbers of students and faculty from all ethnic groups and areas of the campus will be transformed by the Gospel. We expect to see campuses increasingly become places where people, ideas, and structures flourish to the glory of God. We confidently anticipate that our InterVarsity alumni will become change agents across the country and around the world. We pursue this calling by discerning and actively participating in what God is already doing on campus. This is the essence of being a Campus Staff Minister (CSM).

ESSENTIAL COMMITMENTS/RESPONSIBILITIES 

Spiritual Growth 

You pursue maturity as a disciple of Jesus Christ so that your life and work increasingly reflects a growing love for God, God’s Word, God’s people of every ethnicity and culture, and God’s purposes in the world. To do this, you will: 

  • Pursue a vibrant relationship with the triune God through engagement with Scripture, prayer, and worship, both individually and in community 

  • Develop self-leadership (growing in self-awareness, self-management, relational integrity, and resiliency) 

  • Embrace Scriptural standards for behavior and attitudes 

 

Campus Leadership 

You communicate and model InterVarsity’s vision to see students and faculty transformed, campuses renewed and world changers developed 

  • Create a culture of humble dependence on God and bold expectation in God’s intention to start new witnessing communities throughout the campus and on new campuses 

  • Model – in person and through programs – InterVarsity’s vision and Core Values, including a biblically-defined commitment to engage every ethnic and social group on campus 

  • Lead students and faculty – individually and collectively – through Scripture, prayer, teaching, and discipleship experiences, so that they articulate and align their ministry activities around this vision 

  • Set annual goals through prayer, research and reflection with your teams (students, faculty, and staff) for qualitative and quantitative growth, including conversions and leadership development 

 

You create, develop, align and leverage ministry plans, programs, teams, and structures to close the gap between current reality and the aspirational goals. 

  • Build leadership teams who trust and partner well with you and who demonstrate spiritual vitality, relational health, and mission alignment 

  • Develop and execute plans to achieve annual goals, evaluating and modifying the plan as needed throughout the year 

  • Increase momentum for the vision by aligning programs, structures, conferences and teams around the goals 

  • Mobilize students and faculty to engage their relational networks with the gospel and to start new missional communities 

  • Under the direction of the Area Director, may supervise Ministry Interns and Campus Ministry Interns as delegated 

 

You intentionally gather, invite, and develop diverse groups of students and faculty so that they not only encounter and follow Jesus as Savior and Lord but also advance the mission on campus as participants and leaders. 

  • Create ways for faculty and students to encounter and follow Jesus through Scripture, worship, prayer, mission experiences, conferences, etc. 

  • Equip students and faculty so that they think strategically about campus engagement and so that they proclaim – in word, deed, and power – the good news of Jesus, regularly inviting students and faculty to follow him as Savior and Lord 

  • Disciple students and faculty by equipping them to hear the Word, respond actively, and debrief and interpret the experience so that they grow in Christlikeness, reflect our Core Values, and develop ministry skills 

  • Invite, coach, and equip students and faculty to become increasingly effective participants and leaders, including starting new witnessing communities on campuses 

 

Organizational Collaboration 

You work with a network of other local, area, regional, and national InterVarsity staff and volunteers so that our work reflects Biblical standards of excellence, integrity, and partnership. 

  • Partner with and respond positively to the direction and coaching of your supervisors and national leaders 

  • Contribute to collaborative and productive team meetings and relationships 

  • Affiliate chapters under your care and submit Graduating Student Forms in order to increase our partnership with current students and alumni 

  • Use national ministry resources and tools, as requested, including recruiting and/or participating in local, regional, or national conferences as  

  • Complete reporting, planning and review requirements in a timely way so that you and your supervisors can assess and improve your work as a CSM 

  • Comply with all InterVarsity policies and procedures 

 

Ministry Partnership Development 

You will develop a team of partners – churches and individuals (including alumni and community members) – who will resource the ministry financially, in prayer, or volunteer service that advances the mission. 

  • Raise 100% of the financial budget assigned by your supervisor 

  • Communicate regularly with your ministry partners, nurturing the relationship through visits, phone calls, emails and regular prayer letters 

  • Develop on-going, long-lasting partnership with alumni and volunteers 

  • Comply with all Ministry Partnership Policies 

  • Identify and invest in advocates who will build networks of volunteers and donors on InterVarsity’s behalf 

 

Accomplish all other assigned tasks as appropriate 

 

QUALIFICATIONS (common to all levels of CSM) 

  • Annually affirm InterVarsity’s Statement of Agreement (Doctrinal Basis and Purpose Statement). Abide by InterVarsity’s Code of Conduct. Believe and behave consonantly with InterVarsity’s Human Sexuality Theological Paper. Affirm and behave consonantly with InterVarsity’s “Women in Ministry Statement of Affirmation” 

  • Bachelor’s degree for CSMs assigned to a four-year campus. A minimum of an Associate’s degree for CSMs assigned to a two-year campus or a community college 

  • Strong interpersonal skills (including ability to minister to diverse ethnic communities and faculty) 

  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills 

  • Demonstrated problem solving skills 

  • Familiarity with word processing, presentation, email, and spreadsheet software 

 

WORK ENVIRONMENT/PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS 

The CSM position leads ministry in a college campus environment. A designated office space may or may not be available. The CSM is required to travel to on-campus and off- campus sites as appropriate. Off-campus travel includes, but is not limited to: student ministry conferences, Ministry Partnership Development meetings, and InterVarsity- sponsored training sessions, meetings, and conferences. The CSM is regularly required to communicate with others, and routinely uses standard office equipment such as computers, phones, photocopiers, filing cabinets, etc. 

Pay Range: $39,288.00 - $52,392.00 per year

Pay: This position is funded through personal fundraising. Accordingly, compensation will vary based on the ability of the individual to secure a donor team to fund the cost of his/her salary. The anticipated salary range for this position on a full-time basis (40 hours/week) is dependent on a variety of factors, including location and cost of living. The actual salary received, including any geographic adjustment to account for location and cost of living, is subject to the individual’s ability to raise funds necessary to cover the full amount of such salary within the range set forth in the job posting details.

Benefits:

We offer a competitive benefits package, including health care and retirement savings with a match. Eligibility is based on employee type and hours worked.  Benefits include the following:

  • 403(b) Retirement Savings Plan

  • 403(b) matching contributions

  • Dental insurance

  • Employee assistance program

  • Employee discounts

  • Flexible work schedule

  • Flexible spending accounts

  • Health insurance

  • Health savings account

  • Life insurance

  • Paid time off

  • Parental leave

  • Professional development assistance

  • Vision insurance

Equal Employment Opportunity: 

 

InterVarsity Christian Fellowship/USA is both an equal opportunity employer and a faith-based religious organization. We conduct hiring without regard to race, color, ancestry, national origin, citizenship, age, sex, marital status, parental status, membership in any labor organization, political ideology, or disability of an otherwise qualified individual. The status of InterVarsity Christian Fellowship/USA as an equal opportunity employer does not prevent the organization from hiring staff based on their religious beliefs so that all staff share the same religious commitment.  Pursuant to the Civil Rights Act of 1964, Section 702 (42 U.S.C. 2000e 1(a)) InterVarsity Christian Fellowship/USA has the right to, and does, hire only candidates who agree with InterVarsity’s Statement of Agreement: Purpose and Doctrinal Basis because InterVarsity believes that each and every staff plays a vital role in advancing InterVarsity’s mission and purposes.

Key Responsibilities

  • Lead and direct weekly rehearsals and worship services, including special events (e.g., holidays, memorials, funerals)
  • Provide vocal leadership and guide the congregation in worship
  • Select and arrange music in coordination with the Chaplain
  • Deliver opening remarks and prayers aligned with Protestant traditions
  • Prepare and provide music scores, arrangements, and audio/visual lyrics

Qualifications

Education & Experience

  • Minimum of 4 years of college-level education in music or equivalent experience
  • At least 4 years of experience leading worship teams or bands in a church setting

Skills & Abilities

  • Strong vocal ability and experience leading congregational worship
  • Proficiency in sight-reading, arranging, and performing music
  • Ability to lead a contemporary Protestant praise team
  • Strong organizational and leadership skills
  • Excellent interpersonal and communication skills

Missions and Outreach Pastor/Director

POSITION SUMMARY

The Missions and Outreach Pastor will provide leadership and vision for Eagle Church’s global, regional, and local missions and outreach ministries. This pastor will develop strategies to mobilize the congregation to participate in God’s mission through prayer, giving, serving, evangelism, and meaningful partnerships.

The Missions and Outreach Pastor will cultivate relationships with Christian and Missionary Alliance (C&MA) International Workers (IWs), global and local ministry partners, and community organizations while equipping and mobilizing Eagle Church to reach our immediate neighborhood and surrounding communities with the Gospel.

This is a full time, salaried position.

RESPONSIBILITIES

Leadership

  • Lead the Missions Team in developing, implementing and evaluating Eagle Church’s overall missions’ strategy and policies.
  • Develop and lead a Local Outreach Team that would explore and implement ministry initiatives in our surrounding community.
  • Recruit, equip, and develop volunteers and lay leaders to participate in and lead missions and outreach ministries.
  • Work collaboratively with other staff and ministry leaders to integrate missions, outreach, and evangelism throughout the church.
  • Oversee the mission’s budget and ensure responsible stewardship of missions and outreach resources.
  • Develop effective communication strategies that regularly tell the story of what God is doing through Eagle Church’s missions and outreach partnerships.
  • Evaluate ministry partnerships and initiatives regularly, identifying opportunities for greater engagement and Kingdom impact.
  • Will participate in Staff meetings and planning.

Missions

  • Cultivate and maintain meaningful relationships with C&MA IWs, Alliance ministries, other global partners, and local missions organizations through regular communication, prayer, encouragement, and engagement.
  • Develop opportunities for Eagle Church members to engage in missions through prayer, giving, serving, short-term trips, and ongoing relationships with mission’s partners.
  • Oversee adult short-term missions’ trips and work collaboratively with Eagle Students on student missions opportunities.
  • Equip and prepare individuals and teams for effective cross-cultural ministry and provide meaningful follow-up after trips.
  • Plan and oversee the annual Missions Fest and other opportunities to connect the congregation with IWs and missions partners.
  • Identify and develop strategic missions partnerships that align with Eagle Church’s mission, values, and ministry priorities.

Outreach

  • Develop and implement a strategic local outreach plan focused on Eagle Church’s immediate neighborhood and surrounding communities.
  • Build relationships with local schools, organizations, community leaders, nonprofits, and ministry partners to identify meaningful opportunities for Gospel-centered engagement.
  • Oversee and develop local outreach initiatives such as block parties, Upward Sports, service projects, community events, and other strategic outreach opportunities.
  • Work with the Discipleship Director to equip the congregation in personal evangelism, relational outreach, and sharing the Gospel.
  • Help create a culture in which every believer understands their role in participating in God’s mission through their relationships, workplaces, neighborhoods, schools, and community.
  • Develop sustainable outreach strategies that move beyond individual events toward ongoing relationships and opportunities to share the Gospel.

QUALIFICATIONS

  • Demonstrates a personal relationship with Jesus Christ and a life consistent with a biblical worldview.
  • Full agreement with C&MA Statement of Faith and Global Mission Objectives.
  • Understanding of biblical and missional theology and a passion for the Great Commission.
  • 5+ years of ministry, missions, or related leadership experience preferred.
  • Demonstrates an ability to build healthy relationships and work collaboratively with International Workers, ministry organizations, community partners and church leaders.
  • Demonstrates an ability to recruit, organize, and lead short-term missions trips
  • Demonstrates an ability to recruit, equip, and mobilize volunteers.
  • C&MA background such as church attendance, college, or mission field preferred.
  • Ordination with the C&MA or a willingness to pursue licensing and ordination.

ACCOUNTABILITY

  • The Missions and Outreach Pastor/Director will receive direct supervision from the Associate Pastor.
  • The Missions and Outreach Pastor/Director will be indirectly accountable to the Lead Pastor and Elder Board.

Immanuel Bible Church in Saginaw, MI has an opening for a full-time Senior Pastor.  The Senior Pastor serves with the Elders to shepherd the church of God, modeling Christlike character, conduct, humility, and servant-leadership. He is devoted to praying for and walking alongside the congregation, encouraging and equipping believers to grow in their relationship with Christ. With a heart for the church and the lost, the Senior Pastor fosters a culture of discipleship that calls the church to actively participate in Bible study, prayer, service, hospitality, discipleship, evangelism, and mobilizes the church to live out the mission of the gospel together.


Responsibilities:

Preaching & Teaching

  • Serve as the primary preaching/teaching pastor
  • Preach expository sermons in two services each Sunday
  • Provide biblical teaching in other ministry contexts as needed
  • Spend sufficient time in prayer and the study of God’s Word to faithfully fulfill pastoral responsibilities

Shepherding & Pastoral Care

  • Administer the ordinances of baptism by immersion and the Lord’s Supper
  • Officiate funerals and weddings
  • Provide wise, biblical counsel to individuals, couples, and families, in spiritual matters
  • Participate in the loving, caring “one another” life of the church

Leadership & Vision

  • Serve as the primary leader among the Elders by facilitating meetings, guiding discussion, and helping the Elders move toward clear, unified decisions
  • Provide operational leadership and accountability for the Pastoral and church staff, offering guidance, evaluation, and support to promote effective ministry and alignment with the church’s mission, vision, values, and priorities
  • Lead the church from a long-term, big-picture perspective by identifying ministry needs and opportunities, working with the Elders to develop ministry plans, and overseeing their implementation
  • Work closely with church leadership on calendar planning, strategic planning, and financial planning
  • Work closely with church leadership to develop, communicate, and promote a clear vision for the church's mission and ministry
  • Facilitate quarterly and annual Congregational business meetings

Elder Collaboration & Church Oversight

  • Plan for the preaching of God’s Word
  • Protect the church from false teaching and guard against influences that could lead the congregation astray
  • Engage in conflict resolution and church discipline when necessary
  • Identify, disciple, and develop future ministry leaders within the church, including future Elders


Requirements

Have  a clear calling of God, knowing Christ as his personal savior, and be living an exemplary life in accordance with scriptural guidelines for church leaders (1 Timothy 3:1-7 and Titus 1:5-9).   Be sound in faith and doctrine and qualified to preach and teach the Word of God as led by the Holy Spirit.

Prefer a minimum of a theologically related bachelor’s degree or equivalent, with a strong preference for an advanced theological or seminary degree.

Must have at least five years of pastoral ministry experience, with preference given to Senior/Lead pastoral or previous preaching experience.   Additionally, experience working with a pastoral team is strongly preferred.

Must be a U.S, citizen, green card holder, refugee or Asylee.

Benefits

Base Salary:

The base salary for this position will be determined upon hire, considering related education and experience. Annual compensation reviews and adjustments are made by an independent Personnel Committee that regularly reviews relevant data from similar churches and ministry organizations to establish a competitive and equitable compensation package.   The Senior Pastor is responsible for securing housing and health insurance from their compensation package

Retirement contributions/403b:

The Immanual Bible Church matching contribution toward retirement will be 4% of the annual base salary.

Professional Expenses :

The anticipated professional expenses (meals, mileage, books, education, ministry related expenses, etc.) will be designated from the compensation package

Time Off:

3 weeks of compensated vacation will be given for the first year, prorated to your start date. An additional week will be added to the compensation the following calendar year.

Professional Development:

Four weeks of paid professional development (i.e. conference, education, study leave) are given for each calendar year. The registration fees for one Elder-approved conference will be compensated annually.

Sabbatical:

A minimum 13-week paid sabbatical will be earned every seven years of employment to be taken within or near the year awarded.
