Ada Bible Church is seeking Worship Residents to join the worship ministry and be part of Ada Bible's Residency Program. Working closely with a Campus Worship Leader and campus staff, you will participate in worship leading, program planning and implementation, volunteer coordination and care, and professional development-all essential foundations for ministry in the local church ministry.

Through real-world ministry involvement, intentional leadership development, mentoring, and spiritual formation, Residents grow in clarity of calling, competency in ministry skills, and Christlike character—preparing them for faithful service to Jesus and His Church.

In addition to their worship-specific role, Worship Residents participate in Ada Bible Church's broader Residency Program, which provides weekly leadership development sessions, mentorship, and community with other ministry residents.

About Ada Bible's Residency Program

Ada Bible Church's Residency Program exists to help individuals pursue God’s call to vocational ministry through hands-on ministry experience, intentional leadership development, and a deepening relationship with Jesus. Residents are challenged to grow not only in skill and responsibility, but also as leaders, servants, and faithful followers of Christ.

Position Details

This is a part-time temporary position offered up to 20 hours per week for the August 2026 - May 2027 ministry season with potential for a second ministry season of August 2027-May 2028.

Applicants must have availability during the listed times:

  • Weekends – Sunday mornings, Wednesday evenings, and Sunday evenings (residents won't serve every week at these times, but primary leadership environments occur during this time)
  • Weekdays (Tues/Thurs) – Primary in-office days are Tuesday and Thursday with some flexibility
    • ** Starting in September thru the first week in May, weekly on Tuesdays from 1:30 pm to 3:00 pm, you will meet with other ministry residents at Ada Bible Church for leadership development.

What You Will Do

Ministry Experience

  • Serve regularly on bands and lead worship for a variety of ministry events, including the weekend services, student ministry, and adult ministries of Ada Bible
  • Participate in Worship team meetings to gain insight into collaborative ministry planning 
  • Grow as a leader and musician through mentorship, musical training, and goal-setting conversations
  • Assist in creative programming, set planning, and service execution for the different worship experiences
  • Support the care, development, and training for student musicians
  • Play a key role in all-church serving opportunities such as Easter, Christmas, and other major events 

Leadership Development

  • Attend quarterly meetings with the department Residency Program Coordinator focused on leadership development and growth
  • Participate in Tuesday afternoon Residency Leadership Development Program focused on leadership development and group-based project work
  • Apply what you learn in the Residency Leadership Development Program within the context of your role and responsibility in your assigned ministry area

Mentoring & Formation

  • Engage in regular mentoring relationships with assigned leaders
  • Demonstrate a teachable posture by receiving feedback, coaching, and guidance
  • Actively reflect on calling, character, and competency as part of vocational discernment
 

Who We're Looking For

We’re looking for individuals who are passionate about the worship of God, growing in their leadership, and learning how to lead, build, and develop a thriving worship ministry. To be considered for the position, you should be interested in pursuing vocational ministry as a career. Previous experience or formal education in ministry or worship is preferred but not required.


Beyond that, ideal candidates are:

  •  Actively pursuing a vibrant relationship with Christ, building it on prayer and a Biblical foundation
  • Humble and teachable; willing to receive regular constructive feedback and follow-up on goal-setting processes
  • Comfortable leading worship vocally and from an instrument (or learning to lead from an instrument)
  • Interested in investing in others, building community, and seeing people grow
  • Hungry to grow in leadership abilities, practical skills, and ministry experience
  • Desire to work hard, but also likes to have fun in the process

 **Please note: applicants will be asked to submit any videos, recordings, or portfolio samples to gain an idea of musical skill/experience.**


Ready to apply?

If this all sounds good to you and you would like to join us, we want to learn more about you! To apply, click the “Apply” button at the bottom of this page. Be sure to submit your cover letter and resume along with your employment application.


About Ada Bible Church

Ada Bible Church is a thriving and growing multi-site church serving greater Grand Rapids, Michigan. Each weekend, more than 8,500 people worship with us at our campus locations throughout the community. To learn more about us or to view a weekend service, visit our website at: www.adabible.org.

CUSTODIAN I – SHIFT 2

Church Creek School

 

Performs work required for the routine cleaning, maintenance and upkeep of buildings, grounds, and equipment.

CHURCH PLANTING DIRECTOR

Alliance New England

The Director of Church Planting provides catalytic leadership, strategic oversight, and development for the church planting and multiplication efforts of Alliance New England (ANE). Working through ANE’s established Church Planting Pathway, the Director will identify and develop church planters, mobilize churches toward multiplication, cultivate strategic opportunities and partnerships, and provide leadership, support, and oversight from initial calling and assessment through the development of healthy, accredited Alliance churches.

The Director will champion ANE’s vision for multiplication throughout New England, building upon the strong foundation and systems already in place while bringing the relational leadership, creativity, initiative, and catalytic energy necessary to expand church planting across the region.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Champion and advance ANE’s established Church Planting Pathway, providing catalytic leadership that expands its reach, strengthens its effectiveness, and mobilizes leaders and churches toward multiplication in alignment with the mission and vision of Alliance New England and The Christian & Missionary Alliance (C&MA).
  • Actively identify and recruit potential church planting pastors, helping them discern their calling and guiding qualified candidates into and through ANE’s established Church Planting Pathway, including its assessment process.
  • Develop collective mission and multiplication opportunities throughout New England, fostering collaboration and partnerships among churches, clusters, church planters, and ministry partners.
  • Mobilize ANE churches and leaders toward a culture of multiplication, helping churches identify and engage opportunities to participate in church planting through prayer, people, partnership, and resources.
  • Provide ongoing support and development for church planting pastors and teams, including coaching, training, spiritual formation, leadership development, and practical ministry experience.
  • Establish developmental environments and experiences that identify, equip, and prepare emerging church planters for future ministry opportunities.
  • Guide church plants and developing churches through the phases of ANE’s Church Planting Pathway toward accreditation and healthy, sustainable ministry within The Christian & Missionary Alliance.
  • Cultivate relationships with Alliance churches, denominational leaders, cluster members, ministry partners, and other stakeholders to strengthen collaboration and support for church planting and multiplication.
  • Develop and pursue sustainable funding strategies and multiple funding streams to support church planting and multiplication efforts.
  • Develop and manage budgets related to church planting efforts, ensuring resources are strategically aligned with ANE’s church planting priorities.
  • Stay current with developing methodologies, emerging opportunities, and best practices in church planting, multiplication, evangelism, and outreach, bringing relevant learning and innovation into ANE’s established Church Planting Pathway.
  • Evaluate the health, progress, and viability of church planting efforts and, when necessary, lead appropriate decisions regarding their continuation, redirection, or conclusion.

ADDITIONAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Maintain consistent relational contact with church planting pastors and teams, providing pastoral care, encouragement, development, support, and appropriate accountability.
  • Maintain a visible and relational presence among ANE churches through Sunday speaking engagements, church visits, district gatherings, and other opportunities to inspire and mobilize churches toward multiplication.
  • Represent and advocate for church planting and multiplication within Alliance New England and in appropriate denominational, regional, and ministry settings.
  • Participate as a collaborative member of the Alliance New England team, contributing to the broader mission, vision, and ministry priorities of the district.

EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE

  • Bachelor’s degree in Bible, Theology, Pastoral Ministry, or another ministry-related field.
  • Significant pastoral leadership experience, with a minimum of five years of demonstrated experience in church planting, church revitalization, multiplication ministry, or a closely related ministry context.
  • Licensed as an Official Worker of The Christian & Missionary Alliance preferred; otherwise, must be able and willing to meet C&MA licensing and ordination/consecration requirements.
  • Excellent leadership and communication skills, with the ability to build trusted relationships with pastors, churches, denominational leaders, ministry partners, and a variety of stakeholders.
  • A catalytic and entrepreneurial leadership approach, with a demonstrated ability to identify opportunities, mobilize people and churches, build partnerships, and turn vision into action.

  • Demonstrated ability to identify and develop leaders, coach ministry practitioners, and foster environments in which emerging leaders can discern, develop, and deploy their calling.

LOCATION

Must live within a two-hour drive of South Easton, Massachusetts, or be willing to relocate within that radius.

To be considered for this position, please send cover letter, testimony, resume to holly@alliancenewengland.org

If the district office has reviewed your application and they think you may be a potential match for the position, that the hiring manager will reach out to you for next steps.

This position requires licensing with The Christian & Missionary Alliance. To learn more about The Alliance and requirements for licensing, please visit our website

Please do not contact the church directly.

Children's Pastor - First Baptist Church
 

At First Baptist Church Andrews, we believe children are not just the future of the Church—they are an essential part of what God is doing today. We are seeking a passionate, relational, and Christ-centered Children's Minister who is excited to invest in the next generation and help children discover, grow, and live out a lifelong faith in Jesus Christ.

This is more than a ministry position—it's an opportunity to build something meaningful. As our Children's Minister, thr Children's Pastor will have the freedom to dream, create, and lead a thriving ministry that reaches children from birth through 6th grade while partnering with families to disciple their children at home. One will build lasting relationships, equip incredible volunteers, and connect with our community through local schools, sports, and family events.

First Baptist Church Andrews is a growing, multi-generational congregation with a heart for biblical teaching, authentic relationships, and sharing the hope of the gospel throughout our community.

job_name: Worship Pastor at Grace Christian in Odessa, Texas
post_html:
Grace Christian - Worship Pastor

Odessa, Texas


This position offers a rare rebuild-and-elevate opportunity for a growing church of 550–600, with strong momentum and a clear path toward future expansion. The role calls for a relational, team-first leader who can raise the level of musicianship, tighten production quality, and unify a diverse volunteer base…without blowing up the culture or bulldozing existing voices. You’ll lead Thursday and Sunday services, invest heavily in developing people (not just performing), and bring structure, clarity, and consistency. Beyond the platform, this role carries real influence, shaping student worship, contributing to future kids ministry, and helping stabilize tech systems. This is a leadership role for someone who can build trust, create excellence, and move a good worship culture into a great one without losing its soul.


Why We Love This Opportunity

I love this opportunity because it’s not about stepping into something polished, it’s about building something meaningful. There’s real momentum here, a healthy culture, and the kind of leadership that actually invites collaboration instead of control. It’s the kind of place where if you bring vision, humility, and grit, you can make a lasting impact…not just on a stage, but in people.


Watch a Video from Lead Pastor Ben Ford share about the church and this role!


A great match for this position would be:

  • A relational, team-first leader who knows how to unify diverse personalities without needing to control everything.
  • Strong musical and production instincts…can raise the level of the room without turning it into a performance circus.
  • Organized and forward-thinking, able to plan 6+ weeks out and bring structure. 
  • Confident but not arrogant…can lead from the front while still developing and empowering volunteers behind the scenes.
  • Emotionally intelligent and spiritually grounded, with the maturity to navigate transition, build trust, and play the long game.


About This Organization

Grace Christian is a family-focused church in Odessa, Texas that emphasizes community, connection, and spiritual growth. Grace is a place where people can find hope, discover purpose, and build meaningful relationships in a supportive family. Grace Christian aims to create an authentic, welcoming environment where people can grow together through both the highs and lows of life.


Location

Located in the heart of the Permian Basin, Odessa offers a thriving economy, strong job market, and a welcoming community rooted in resilience and growth. With affordable living, excellent schools, and a family-friendly atmosphere, Odessa provides the perfect balance of opportunity and quality of life. Big enough to have everything you need, yet small enough to feel like family, Odessa is great place to do life and ministry.


“It’s rare to find a workplace that feels like home. Here, we aren’t just coworkers; we’re a community fueled by a shared passion for Jesus. Whether it’s carrying a heavy load or offering a hand before being asked, the support is constant. I’m so grateful to be part of a team that has become family so quickly.”

David Cadena – Adult Ministry Pastor


Mission, Vision, and Values

  • Mission: We make disciples of Jesus Christ by leading people to grow in faith through a personal relationship with Him.
  • Vision: Helping people find hope, discover purpose, and connect with a church family so their lives might be made new in Christ.
  • Values: We help people to experience Grace through – Generosity, Serving, Authenticity, Relationship, Growth, and Truth.


Staff Culture

  • Highly collaborative and low-ego. People jump in to help without territorial nonsense.
  • Relational and supportive. Staff actually like each other and work well together, not just coexist.
  • Led with a healthy balance of friendship and accountability. Clear expectations without micromanagement.
  • Flexible and team-oriented. Everyone contributes beyond their role when needed to move the mission forward.


Key Responsibilities

  • Lead and execute worship for Thursday night and Sunday morning services with consistency and clarity.
  • Recruit, develop, and pastor volunteer musicians and vocalists…building both skill and spiritual maturity.
  • Plan services including song selection, team scheduling, and service flow.
  • Oversee and improve production quality (sound, tracks, ProPresenter, stage setup, and overall environment).
  • Collaborate closely with the Lead Pastor on service direction and church-wide vision.
  • Support and develop worship environments for students, Celebrate Recovery, and future kids ministry.
  • Manage worship and tech systems, including MultiTracks, loops/stems, and team communication.
  • Foster a healthy, unified team culture by building relationships, resolving tension, and setting clear expectations.


Key Qualifications

  • Proven ability to lead worship with both musical excellence and strong stage presence that engages the congregation.
  • Demonstrated experience building, developing, and pastoring volunteer teams .
  • Solid understanding of modern worship production, including tracks, click, ProPresenter, and basic audio systems.
  • Strong organizational skills with the ability to plan services 4–6 weeks in advance and execute with consistency.
  • Relational leadership style is collaborative, emotionally intelligent, and able to navigate team dynamics and tension.
  • Alignment with the church’s theology and culture (grounded, not overly charismatic, team-oriented).
  • Self-starter with a high work ethic who can take ownership without constant oversight.
  • Flexibility to lead across multiple environments (main services, students, recovery ministry, future kids worship).

post_html:
Campus Staff Minister - North Carolina (Graduate & Faculty Ministry)

Work Location:

North Carolina

Job Type:

Full time

God has called InterVarsity to plant and to build witnessing communities of students and faculty who follow Jesus on college and university campuses. Through these groups, we believe ever- increasing numbers of students and faculty from all ethnic groups and areas of the campus will be transformed by the Gospel. We expect to see campuses increasingly become places where people, ideas, and structures flourish to the glory of God. We confidently anticipate that our InterVarsity alumni will become change agents across the country and around the world. We pursue this calling by discerning and actively participating in what God is already doing on campus. This is the essence of being a Campus Staff Minister (CSM).

Please submit the GFM Interest Form before completing the full application for a position with Graduate & Faculty Ministries in our online system. We will contact you when we are ready to proceed with the application process.  

This position is open to applicants working less than 40 hours/week. If you are interested in part-time work please apply for this position. 

The pay range listed is for an employee working 40 hours/week at CSM level II. Pay will be prorated for employees who work less than 40 hours/week.

Volunteers are welcome. Volunteer opportunities range from prayer and hospitality to leading a campus fellowship of graduate students and faculty. Those interested in volunteering will go through an application and interview process, however, volunteer openings are not posted online. For more information, complete the GFM Interest Form. 

ESSENTIAL COMMITMENTS/RESPONSIBILITIES 

Spiritual Growth 

As a Campus Staff Minister, you pursue maturity as a disciple of Jesus Christ so that your life and work increasingly reflect a growing love for God, God’s Word, God’s people of every ethnicity and culture, and God’s purposes in the world. To do this, you will: 

  • Pursue a vibrant relationship with the triune God through engagement with Scripture, prayer, and worship, both individually and in community

  • Develop self-leadership (growing in self-awareness, self-management, relational integrity, and resiliency) 

  • Embrace Scriptural standards for behavior and attitudes 

 

Campus Leadership 

As a Campus Staff Minister, you increase the number of witnessing communities, as well as the size, health, spiritual maturity, and campus-wide influence of existing witnessing communities of students and faculty by being a: 

  • Visionary Guide: 

You communicate and model InterVarsity’s vision to see students and faculty transformed, campuses renewed, and world changers developed 

  • Create a culture of humble dependence on God and bold expectation in God’s intention to start new witnessing communities throughout the campus and on new campuses 

  • Model – in person and through programs – InterVarsity’s vision and Core Values, including a biblically-defined commitment to engage every ethnic and social group on campus 

  • Lead students and faculty – individually and collectively – through Scripture, prayer, teaching, and discipleship experiences, so that they articulate and align their ministry activities around this vision 

  • Set annual goals through prayer, research and reflection with your teams (students, faculty, and staff) for qualitative and quantitative growth, including conversions and leadership development 

  • Structural Architect: 

You create, develop, align, and leverage ministry plans, programs, teams, and structures to close the gap between current reality and the aspirational goals. 

  • Build leadership teams who trust and partner well with you and who demonstrate spiritual vitality, relational health, and mission alignment 

  • Develop and execute plans to achieve annual goals, evaluating and modifying the plan as needed throughout the year 

  • Increase momentum for the vision by aligning programs, structures, conferences, and teams around the goals 

  • Mobilize students and faculty to engage their relational networks with the gospel and to start new missional communities 

  • Under the direction of the Area Director, may supervise Ministry Interns and Campus Ministry Interns as delegated 

  • Missional Developer: 

You intentionally gather, invite, and develop diverse groups of students and faculty so that they not only encounter and follow Jesus as Savior and Lord but also advance the mission on campus as participants and leaders. 

  • Create ways for faculty and students to encounter and follow Jesus through Scripture, worship, prayer, mission experiences, conferences, etc. 

  • Equip students and faculty so that they think strategically about campus engagement and so that they proclaim – in word, deed, and power – the good news of Jesus, regularly inviting students and faculty to follow him as Savior and Lord 

  • Disciple students and faculty by equipping them to hear the Word, respond actively, and debrief and interpret the experience so that they grow in Christlikeness, reflect our Core Values, and develop ministry skills 

  • Invite, coach, and equip students and faculty to become increasingly effective participants and leaders, including starting new witnessing communities on campuses 

 

Organizational Collaboration 

As a Campus Staff Minister, you have joined a national mission. Therefore, you work with a network of other local, area, regional, and national InterVarsity staff and volunteers so that our work reflects Biblical standards of excellence, integrity, and partnership. 

  • Partner with and respond positively to the direction and coaching of your supervisors and national leaders 

  • Contribute to collaborative and productive team meetings and relationships 

  • Affiliate chapters under your care and submit Graduating Student Forms in order to increase our partnership with current students and alumni 

  • Use national ministry resources and tools, as requested, including recruiting and/or participating in local, regional, or national conferences as  

  • Complete reporting, planning and review requirements in a timely way so that you and your supervisors can assess and improve your work as a CSM 

  • Comply with all InterVarsity policies and procedures 

 

Ministry Partnership Development 

As a Campus Staff Minister, you will develop a team of partners – churches and individuals (including alumni and community members) – who will resource the ministry financially, in prayer, or volunteer service that advances the mission. 

  • Raise 100% of the financial budget assigned by your supervisor 

  • Communicate regularly with your ministry partners, nurturing the relationship through visits, phone calls, emails and regular prayer letters 

  • Develop on-going, long-lasting partnership with alumni and volunteers 

  • Comply with all Ministry Partnership Policies 

  • Identify and invest in advocates who will build networks of volunteers and donors on InterVarsity’s behalf 

 

Accomplish all other assigned tasks as appropriate 

 

QUALIFICATIONS (common to all levels of CSM) 

  • Annually affirm InterVarsity’s Statement of Agreement (Doctrinal Basis and Purpose Statement). Abide by InterVarsity’s Code of Conduct. Believe and behave consonantly with InterVarsity’s Human Sexuality Theological Paper. Affirm and behave consonantly with InterVarsity’s “Women in Ministry Statement of Affirmation” 

  • Bachelor’s degree for CSMs assigned to a four-year campus. A minimum of an Associate’s degree for CSMs assigned to a two-year campus or a community college 

  • Strong interpersonal skills (including ability to minister to diverse ethnic communities and faculty) 

  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills 

  • Demonstrated problem solving skills 

  • Familiarity with word processing, presentation, email, and spreadsheet software 

 

WORK ENVIRONMENT/PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS 

The CSM position leads ministry in a college campus environment. A designated office space may or may not be available. The CSM is required to travel to on-campus and off- campus sites as appropriate. Off-campus travel includes, but is not limited to: student ministry conferences, Ministry Partnership Development meetings, and InterVarsity- sponsored training sessions, meetings, and conferences. The CSM is regularly required to communicate with others, and routinely uses standard office equipment such as computers, phones, photocopiers, filing cabinets, etc. 

Pay Range: $44,016.00 - $58,680.00 per year

Pay: This position is funded through personal fundraising. Accordingly, compensation will vary based on the ability of the individual to secure a donor team to fund the cost of his/her salary. The anticipated salary range for this position on a full-time basis (40 hours/week) is dependent on a variety of factors, including location and cost of living. The actual salary received, including any geographic adjustment to account for location and cost of living, is subject to the individual’s ability to raise funds necessary to cover the full amount of such salary within the range set forth in the job posting details.

Benefits:

We offer a competitive benefits package, including health care and retirement savings with a match. Eligibility is based on employee type and hours worked.  Benefits include the following:

  • 403(b) Retirement Savings Plan

  • 403(b) matching contributions

  • Dental insurance

  • Employee assistance program

  • Employee discounts

  • Flexible work schedule

  • Flexible spending accounts

  • Health insurance

  • Health savings account

  • Life insurance

  • Paid time off

  • Parental leave

  • Professional development assistance

  • Vision insurance

Equal Employment Opportunity: 

 

InterVarsity Christian Fellowship/USA is both an equal opportunity employer and a faith-based religious organization. We conduct hiring without regard to race, color, ancestry, national origin, citizenship, age, sex, marital status, parental status, membership in any labor organization, political ideology, or disability of an otherwise qualified individual. The status of InterVarsity Christian Fellowship/USA as an equal opportunity employer does not prevent the organization from hiring staff based on their religious beliefs so that all staff share the same religious commitment.  Pursuant to the Civil Rights Act of 1964, Section 702 (42 U.S.C. 2000e 1(a)) InterVarsity Christian Fellowship/USA has the right to, and does, hire only candidates who agree with InterVarsity’s Statement of Agreement: Purpose and Doctrinal Basis because InterVarsity believes that each and every staff plays a vital role in advancing InterVarsity’s mission and purposes.

Description:

Young Life Military is looking for those with a heart to serve and a desire to grow in their walks with Christ. We are excited for you to consider the possibility of joining us for a long-term internship. Our interns are accepted through Young Life and will work with an experienced Young Life Military/Club Beyond staff person. Interns have the opportunity to serve either in the United States or in Europe. The Club Beyond supervising staff person gives direction and trains the intern as they assist with many aspects of the ministry. Activities include camps, clubs, Bible studies as well as just "hanging out" with kids and modeling a personal example of Jesus Christ. A desire to love and serve kids should be a priority.

This is where you can be the difference in a military teen’s life! By being in their world, walking alongside them, and creating a community where they experience the truth of God’s love and purpose for them, our staff provide a safe space where teens can develop friendships and connections to experience laughter, build hope, and generate resiliency.

We are currently providing incarnational ministry at many military installations around the world. You will have the opportunity to lead and oversee the overall Young Life Military program, known as Club Beyond, which is ecumenically focused and outreach oriented.

We are currently looking for both full-time and part-time staff throughout the United States, as well as international locations. Colorado Springs, CO, is the headquarters.

Responsibilities:

  • Training: Meet weekly with supervising staff using Club Beyond team agenda tools.
  • Direct Ministry: Participate in leadership with a team to conduct Club Beyond club and small group ministry to teens with excellence.
  • Spiritual Development: Develop a 90-day personal growth plan that fosters a vibrant spiritual life including time for solitude, retreat, reflection, prayer, and a sincere commitment to understanding God’s Word. Attend Chapel on installation as often as you are in community.
  • Leadership Development: Attend volunteer leader meetings. Meet weekly with one volunteer to discuss their involvement in Club Beyond. Meet with your supervisor and learn how to recruit and train new leaders and build a leadership team that reflects the diversity of the community.
  • Resource Development: Discuss with your supervisor raising financial support, both the benefits and the challenges. Communicate monthly updates with personal donor partners.
  • Be a role model (incarnational/relational ministry) and assist with developing community outreach to "unchurched" teens, discipleship to believing teens, and leading and equipping volunteers for "hands-on" middle and high school Christian youth ministry.
  • Be respectful of and embrace a community that is deeply influenced by a military culture.
  • In this ministry, you will need to live out the Club Beyond Core Value Statement:

Club Beyond is a Christ-centered community of leaders with an exclusively military focus. Our methods are incarnational, and our perspective is ecumenical. We leverage strategic partnerships for the greatest results. We value professionalism from our staff and excellence in our stewardship.

Qualifications:

  • Graduated high school at least 2 years prior
  • A deep love for Christ and for lost teens.
  • Competent communicator.
  • Teachable heart.
  • Willingness to raise part of the budget through personal support.
  • Committed to a relational ministry approach.
  • Energetic.
  • Small event planning skills.
  • Strong initiative.
  • Note, this position would require our Staff to live near the community where they would be doing ministry.

Financial Commitment:

  • This is a paid internship program. Each applicant is responsible to RAISE the salary needed to participate in the summer internship program, with a minimum of $1160 to a maximum of $4,000 (Depending on the location and number of weeks served).

Location:

Club Beyond works on military installations all over the world; our active locations are listed here: https://clubbeyond.org/locations.

Contact us through:
Robert Raedeke: RecruitingTeam@clubbeyond.org

Want to know more about our mission and culture?

Please check out clubbeyond.org to learn how Club Beyond has been changing the lives of military teens for over 40 years!

Early Childhood Coordinator



POSITION

Crossroads Bible Church is seeking a Kid’s Ministry Early Childhood Coordinator who has a heart and a talent for engaging with families and young children. This position plays an integral role in how young families experience Crossroads Kids on Sunday Mornings and with creating and maintaining midweek programming. Overview

The Campus Ministries Teacher and Children's Ministry Specialist (CMS) serves as a Day Care Teacher for school-age children, providing care, guidance, and programmatic engagement in a nurturing environment. This role supports the holistic development of children through structured activities and faith-based learning. In addition to this daycare responsibility, this role also serves as a member of the Campus Ministries pastoral team, with a focus on the spiritual care and ministry leadership of children at the College of Officer Training (CFOT). This includes teaching, mentoring, and leading children in their faith journey through worship, discipleship, and community-building programs. 

This ministry requires a deep commitment to loving and serving children and their families, fostering spiritual growth, and collaborating with other leaders to create a vibrant and supportive environment. 

Responsibilities

Lead Teacher

  • Implement the daily program while following the daily schedule as closely as possible. 
  • Supervise and ensure the safety and well-being of the children at all times, being alert to the needs and/or problems of the children as individuals and as a group.
  • Alert the CM Leadership of potential.
  • When applicable, complete an Incident and Accident form.
  • Plan a developmentally appropriate curriculum to include activities and experiences contributing to each child’s growth and development.
  • Supervise activities and interact with the children.
  • Submit monthly communications to the Director and distribute to parents. 
  • Decorate the classroom with bulletin boards, pictures, children's artwork, and other hangings to enhance the vision and mission of the space.
  • Maintain the organization of classroom materials and equipment. 
  • Maintain classroom supplies and advise the Assistant Director when supplies need replenishing. 
  • Prepare and deliver snacks for the children.
  • Evaluate each child's particular needs and attempt to meet them in concurrence with the Director and Assistant Director. 
  • Greet the parents at arrival and depature times, building a good relationship with clear communication. Encourage and welcome parents to be involved in CM's activities. 
  • Conform to meeting New York State Day Care regulations, including teacher-in-service training. 
  • Attend regular staff planning and evaluation meetings.
  • Lead weekly programmatic activities assigned by leadership in CM.
  • Daily supervision and help with classroom cleanup, vacuuming, and laundering of rest linens as needed.
  • Handle discipline promptly and in accordance with the stated policy on discipline. 
  • Check each child daily for visible signs of illness and report it to CM Leadership. 
  • Maintain Campus Ministries' health policies. 
  • Perform and additional duties centered on the children's care as requested by the Director. 
  • Provide transportation to Campus Ministries' children in Salvation Army vehicles assigned to Campus Ministries, as needed. 
  • Provide support to other classrooms, as needed. 
  • Follow all New York State Day Care and KeepSAfe reporting mandates.
  • Perform all other duties as assigned by the supervisor. 

Spiritual Life

  • Lead small groups and serve as a small group leader to CFOT children. 
  • Assist in providing day-to-day pastoral care to the youth at CFOT.
  • Collaborate with the CM Officer and CM Leadership to develop ideas to present age-appropriate, engaging and creative Biblical education.
  • Support and assist in the creation of a Spiritual Development Plan for CFOT youth in conjunction with the Director and CM Officer.
  • Weekly planning and executing age-appropriate activities for all CM youth (infant to teenage), including workship, retreats, and other activities.
  • Be present in the Day Care area during work hours, building relationships with children. 
  • Plan special activities for youth, including chaperoning teen retreats (i.e., youth councils, Commissioning) in conjunction with the Director and CM Officer. 

 

Qualifications

  • Associate's degree or equivalent from a two-year college or technical school, or equivalent combination of education and work experience. 
  • Valid driver’s license and approval to drive a 12-passenger van.
  • NY State Teaching Certificate 
  • Active Christian in good standing. 
  • Must be available to work on Sundays, as required.

Required Education and Experience

post_html:
DIRECTOR OF MUSIC AND WORSHIP

MISSION CONTEXT

St. Maria Goretti Parish exists to reveal the presence of Christ in the New Orleans East community and bring the scattered to Him. The Director of Music and Worship serves this mission by ensuring that the Church's public prayer is celebrated with reverence, theological integrity, cultural authenticity, and pastoral sensitivity so that the People of God are drawn into full, conscious, and active participation in the liturgy.

POSITION OVERVIEW

The Director of Music and Worship is responsible for the planning, preparation, and execution of music and liturgical elements for parish worship, with particular attention to the Weekend Experience as the source and summit of parish life. This role collaborates closely with the Pastor and parish leadership to ensure that music and worship are not treated as standalone functions, but are fully integrated into the pastoral vision, preaching themes, liturgical seasons, and broader mission of the parish.

The Director of Music and Worship is not simply a musician, but a liturgical leader who understands the Mass as prayer, proclamation, and encounter, and who forms others to serve within that vision.

PRIMARY RESPONSIBILITIES

Liturgical Planning and Leadership
Plan music and worship in fidelity to the Roman Missal, the liturgical calendar, and the norms of the Church, with particular care for Ordinary Time, Advent, Lent, Easter, and major solemnities.

Collaborate with the Pastor to align music with preaching themes, seasonal movements, and parish wide focuses.

Ensure that music serves the liturgy rather than drawing attention to itself, supporting prayer, proclamation, and communal participation.

Prepare and oversee music for all weekend Masses, holy days of obligation, and major parish liturgies.

Coordinate worship for special liturgies including funerals, weddings, school Masses, sacramental celebrations, and parish wide services.

Music Ministry Development

Recruit, train, and pastorally accompany cantors, choir members, instrumentalists, and other music ministers.

Foster a prayerful and disciplined music ministry culture rooted in service, preparation, and reverence.

Provide ongoing formation for music ministers that deepens their understanding of the Mass, sacred music, and the spiritual nature of their role.

Schedule and oversee rehearsals that are purposeful, well organized, and respectful of volunteers' time.

Musical and Cultural Sensitivity

Select music that is theologically sound, pastorally appropriate, and resonant with the cultural life of the parish, particularly within the Black Catholic tradition.

Balance tradition and accessibility so that the assembly is able to sing, respond, and pray rather than observe.

Ensure musical choices support congregational participation and do not overshadow the spoken and proclaimed Word.

Collaboration and Administration

Work collaboratively with parish staff, especially the Pastor, Director of Parish Life, and Director of Discipleship, to support the overall pastoral plan of the parish.

Prepare worship schedules, music plans, and seasonal outlines in advance.

Manage music ministry resources responsibly, including music library, instruments, and equipment.

Support the formation of liturgical ministers by understanding how music interfaces with lectors, presiders, servers, and hospitality.

QUALIFICATIONS AND FORMATION

A practicing Catholic with a demonstrated love for the Eucharist and the Church's liturgy.

Formal training or significant experience in music, liturgy, or sacred music ministry.

Strong understanding of the structure of the Mass and the purpose of music within it.

Ability to lead others with clarity, patience, and pastoral sensitivity.

Comfort working within a collaborative parish staff environment and receiving direction from the Pastor.

post_html:
Job Title: Student Ministries Pastor


Location: Waukesha County, Wisconsin (Milwaukee Metro Area)


Church Size: 2300


Why This Is a Great Opportunity:

Spring Creek Church is seeking a Student Ministries Pastor. This role offers the opportunity to shepherd a large and thriving student ministry while helping shape the next generation of disciples.


Spring Creek is a healthy, multi-generational church with more than 2,300 people attending weekly and a long legacy of strong biblical teaching. The church is entering a new season of leadership following the transition to a new Lead Pastor after 38 years of faithful leadership. This makes it a strategic moment for a leader who is passionate about discipleship, student ministry, and building strong relationships with families.


With 300–350 students engaged weekly and more than 600 unique students participating over the course of a year, the ministry has both strong weekly consistency and broad relational reach. While sports schedules and activities impact weekly attendance, a large number of students consider Spring Creek their student ministry home.

If you love teaching God’s Word, building leaders, and helping students develop a lifelong faith in Christ, this is a unique opportunity to lead a ministry that is already positioned for impact.


About Spring Creek Church:

Mission

To honor God by producing fully devoted followers of Jesus Christ.


Vision

To boldly proclaim the gospel to every generation, because Jesus changes everything.

Spring Creek Church is a thriving, multi-generational church located in Waukesha County within the greater Milwaukee metro area. The church reflects a wide range of ages, from young families to seniors, and places a strong emphasis on discipleship at every stage of life. The church has 24 full-time staff members and 26 part-time staff members, including eight pastors. The church is independent and non-denominational in structure while holding Baptist doctrine and practice, including baptism by immersion and monthly communion. 


Learn more: https://springcreek.church


Spring Creek has a vibrant and well-established student ministry with strong participation and a reputation for biblical teaching, meaningful worship, and authentic community.


Ministry Structure:

  • Sunday morning environments for both Middle School and High School students, with separate gatherings:
  • Middle School meets during the first service with teaching, worship, and discipleship groups.
  • High School meets during the second service with teaching, worship, and discipleship groups.
  • Wednesday night gatherings alternating between large group teaching and discipleship groups.
  • Monthly Serving Saturdays serving local community partners
  • Fall retreat and spring retreat 
  • Summer mission trips and student experiences


The ministry currently includes 60–65 volunteer leaders and a staff team of three direct reports:

  • Student Ministry Director: Worship & Leadership
  • Student Ministry Director: Engagement & Tech 
  • Associate/Assistant
  • The church also has a vision to continue investing in the growth of student ministry leadership, including future plans to hire a Middle School Pastor as the ministry continues to grow. 


Key Responsibilities:

  • Provide overall vision and leadership for the student ministry (grades 6–12).
  • Deliver clear, biblically grounded, engaging teaching to students.
  • Shepherd students, parents, volunteer leaders, and ministry staff.
  • Strengthen discipleship pathways for students.
  • Evaluate and improve ministry programming while maintaining healthy rhythms.
  • Recruit, train, and care for volunteer leaders.
  • Lead and develop the student ministry staff team.
  • Build strong partnerships with parents as primary disciplers.
  • Collaborate with church leadership and ministries across the church.
  • Help students become integrated into the broader life of the church.
  • Participate in staff meetings and church leadership rhythms.
  • Provide spiritual care for students and families.
  • Model Christlike character, humility, and servant leadership.
  • Maintain a growing personal walk with Jesus.


What Success Looks Like in Year One:

  • Strong relationships built with volunteer leaders and student ministry staff
  • Healthy trust established with students and parents
  • Consistent, clear teaching rhythms developed
  • Alignment and unity strengthened among volunteer leaders
  • Ministry programming evaluated and refined where needed
  • A healthy personal and family transition into the community


Qualifications:

  • A mature and growing follower of Jesus Christ
  • Alignment with Spring Creek Church’s theology and convictions
  • Minimum 5 years of church ministry experience, preferably in student ministry
  • Strong biblical teaching ability
  • Proven leadership and shepherding skills
  • Humility paired with confidence
  • Ability to lead teams and develop leaders
  • Preferred: Master of Divinity (M.Div.) or Th.M.
  • Acceptable:Bible college degree or equivalent theological training


Character Traits:

  • Biblically grounded
  • Passionate about student ministry
  • Humble and teachable
  • Courage
  • Kindness
  • Wisdom


Compensation & Benefits:

Salary Range: $82,000-90,000 depending on education and experience. Plus benefits. 

  • Vacation and personal days
  • Sabbatical policy (8 weeks after every 5 years)
  • Supportive pastoral leadership environment


About the Community:

Spring Creek Church is located in Waukesha County, part of the greater Milwaukee metro area.

  • County population: 400,000+
  • Metro population: 1.5 million

The region offers excellent schools, strong family communities, and access to both urban amenities and outdoor recreation. 


The Opportunity:

Spring Creek Church believes the student ministry is one of the most important ministries in the life of the church. Many families come because of the strength of this ministry, and the church is deeply committed to seeing it thrive. This is an opportunity for a leader who loves students, believes deeply in the authority of Scripture, and wants to invest in the spiritual formation of the next generation. The foundation is strong. The team is supportive. The church is healthy. The right leader will help take this ministry into its next chapter.

Disclaimer:

Vierra Communities provides equal employment opportunities (EEO) to all employees and applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability or genetics. In addition to federal law requirements, Vierra complies with applicable state and local laws governing nondiscrimination in employment in every location in which the company has facilities.

General Information

Name of Church: Somerset Alliance

Church Location: Somerset, in the Laurel Highlands of southwestern Pennsylvania — 70 miles east of Pittsburgh

Type of Community: A borough of roughly 6,000 residents within Somerset County (total county population approximately 74,000)

Online Presence: Church website, Facebook, Instagram, and YouTube

Church Ministries

SERVICE DAYS & TIMES

  • Corporate Worship Service — Sundays at 10:15 AM
  • Youth, Children's Ministries, & Adult Bible Study — Wednesdays at 6:45 PM
  • Young Adult Ministries — Thursdays at 7:00 PM

OTHER KEY MINISTRIES & PROGRAMS

  • Alliance Women
  • Congregational Care
  • Grief Share / Divorce Care
  • Ministry Development
  • Somerset Christian School & Daycare
  • Christian Counseling Associates Partnership
  • Mom's Ministry
  • Men's Ministry

PRESENT WORSHIP FORMS & STYLE

Our primary worship style at SAC is contemporary, reflecting a transition the church made over the last 12 15 years. While contemporary songs make up the majority of our music selections, we intentionally incorporate familiar hymns and choruses into our Sunday gatherings by updating their arrangements to fit a modern sound while still remaining connected to the richness of the Church's traditional heritage. Above all, our worship times are structured to be Jesus-centered and Spirit-led, creating an inviting space for the congregation to participate in deep, meaningful worship. We prioritize authentic encounters with God, posturing an openness to the Holy Spirit.

Church Analysis

KEY GOALS FOR THE NEXT 3 YEARS (IN PRIORITY ORDER)

  • Small Group Community (Spiritual Growth & Missional Community)
  • Lay Leader Development
  • Improve partnership between elder/governing board and staff

KEY ACCOMPLISHMENTS OF THE LAST 3 YEARS (IN ORDER OF IMPORTANCE)

  • “Debt Free by 2023” — the 2008 building-expansion mortgage was paid off
  • Discipleship guidebook “40 Weeks with Jesus” completed, printed, and sold
  • Worked alongside Parkview Alliance to help keep it open, before releasing it to independent ministry in 2025

MOST SIGNIFICANT STRENGTHS & OPPORTUNITIES

  • Sunday morning worship gathering
  • Alliance partnership
  • Personal growth
  • Financial stewardship

MOST SIGNIFICANT WEAKNESSES & THREATS

  • Community outreach
  • Effective organization
  • Missions focus

Facilities

Somerset Alliance Church occupies approximately 56,000 square feet across two connected sections. The original building, constructed in 1979–80, comprises roughly 36,000 square feet and includes a 900-seat sanctuary, gymnasium, offices, a conference room, classrooms, and a dedicated prayer room. In 2009–10, a 24,000-square-foot addition was completed, housing preschool-through-elementary classrooms, adult education spaces, a fellowship hall, and a commercial kitchen.

In 2025, the church began a multi-phase sanctuary remodel. The majority of Phase 1 — which focused on sound, video, and platform upgrades — has been completed. Two additional phases are planned to continue modernizing the sanctuary space.

Other Relevant Information

Somerset Alliance Church serves as a hub for several community-facing ministries and partnerships. The church houses Somerset Christian Day Care and Somerset Christian School, which operate as a ministry of the church with their own separate board and finances. The church also provides dedicated counseling space for CCA (Christian Counseling Associates), whose licensed counselors meet with individuals from both the church and the broader community on-site. Once a month, the church parking lot hosts a mobile food bank distribution. The church has a long-standing culture of generosity with its facilities, regularly opening its doors for community organizations and events.

Pastoral Role Priorities

PASTORAL EXPECTATIONS

High Priority — required and critical; the church will not call a candidate for whom these are not the highest priority.

  • Vision Caster / Keeper
  • Preacher / Teacher
  • Administrator

Moderately High Priority — desired and important; may impact the call.

  • People Developer
  • Prophetic Vision
  • Community Engagement

Moderately Low Priority — helpful, with less impact on the call.

  • Entrepreneurial Leader
  • Mission Mobilizer
  • Counselor / Care

Major Needs of the Church Requiring Attention

  • Improve partnership between elder/governing board and staff
  • ‘Siloed’ ministries
  • Healing of past wounds (repentance / forgiveness)
  • Development of lay leaders
  • Community outreach
  • A balanced approach to internal discipleship that supports both new believers and mature Christians in their ongoing walk with Christ
  • Staff opportunities
  • Lack of volunteers

Personal Strengths Sought (spiritual, emotional, social)

  • A unifier with wisdom and courage to move beyond superficial peace, address issues at the root, and help bridge relational gaps between older and younger generations.
  • A humble shepherd dedicated to prayer, sensitive to God's leading, with the emotional intelligence to connect with people.
  • A man of godly character and genuine authenticity, faithful to the gifts God has placed in him and not artificial or performative.
  • A doctrinally sound leader who is grounded in Scripture and able to lead with biblical clarity and conviction.
  • A relationally mature and diplomatic leader who can foster trust, navigate conflict wisely, and build healthy connections across the church.
  • A clear and compelling vision caster who can help the church move forward in unity and faithfulness to God's calling.
  • Someone actively involved in the community who serves as a visible, respected leader beyond the walls of the church.

Other Significant Considerations for the Call of the Next Pastor

  • The pastor should understand and embrace the culture of our area.
  • The pastor’s family would be expected to reside in the church parsonage.

How a New Pastor Should Expect to Fulfill His Leadership Role

We anticipate a new pastor would fulfill his leadership role by prayerfully discerning God's direction, faithfully teaching His Word, and leading with humility, authenticity, and love. He should recognize and cultivate the strengths God has already placed within our church rather than trying to remake it in the image of a previous ministry, while encouraging healing, unity, and trust among leaders, staff, and the congregation. He should also equip and develop lay leaders, encourage meaningful discipleship across all generations, and lead us outward in compassionate outreach to our community. Above all, we hope he is a unifying, Spirit-led shepherd who helps our church grow in Christlikeness, deeper community, and effective kingdom ministry in Somerset and beyond.

Applications

Candidates for this position must be ordained or qualified for ministry accreditation with the Christian and Missionary Alliance. Interested parties should send their resume to the Western Pennsylvania District of the Christian and Missionary Alliance at ealyp@cmawpa.org .

Church financial statements, compensation and other information will be made available to candidates in the course of the interview process.

To be considered for this position, please complete the application to include your testimony, resume and other background information related to the position.

If the district office has reviewed your application and they think you may be a potential match for the position, that the hiring manager will reach out to you for next steps.

This position requires licensing with The Christian & Missionary Alliance. To learn more about The Alliance and requirements for licensing, please visit our website

post_html:

Description:

There are nearly 300,000 teenagers of active-duty U.S. military parents who are stationed all over the world. These teens move an average of seven times during their school-aged years. The questions of identity and belonging that all teens face grow even more challenging to answer amid starting over and meeting new friends at each location.

This is where you can be the difference in a military teen’s life! By being in their world, walking alongside them, and creating a community where they experience the truth of God’s love and purpose for them, our staff provide a safe space where teens can develop friendships and connections to experience laughter, build hope, and generate resiliency.

We are currently providing incarnational ministry at many military installations around the world. You will have the opportunity to lead and oversee the overall Young Life Military program, known as Club Beyond, which is ecumenically focused and outreach oriented.

We are currently looking for both full-time and part-time staff throughout the United States, as well as international locations. Colorado Springs, CO, is the headquarters.

Responsibilities:

  • Actively develop healthy relationships with adults, as well as kids, and build vibrant relationships with the local community, the military installation, and the chapel community.
  • Be a role model (incarnational) and assist with developing community outreach to "unchurched" teens, discipleship to Christian teens, and leading and equipping volunteers to do "hands-on" middle and high school Christian youth programs.
  • Work well in an environment that sees (due to high military operational tempo) a high degree of turnover among teens, families, chaplains and volunteers.
  • Be respectful of and embrace a community that is deeply influenced by a military culture.
  • In this ministry, you will need to live out the Club Beyond Core Value Statement:

Club Beyond is a Christ-centered community of leaders with an exclusively military focus. Our methods are incarnational, and our perspective is ecumenical. We leverage strategic partnerships for the greatest results. We value professionalism from our staff and excellence in our stewardship.

Qualifications:

  • A deep love for Christ and for lost teens.
  • Competent communicator with youths, parents, and senior military leaders.
  • Teachable heart.
  • Willingness to make a three-year commitment.

  • Willingness to raise part of the budget through personal support.
  • Committed to a relational ministry approach.
  • Energetic.

You are passionate about seeing students know God, find freedom in groups, and discover their calling in serving the local Church. You are adaptable, fun, and have a heart to build teams of volunteers to do ministry with students. Good day or bad day, people feel the love of Jesus when they are around you. The Church

We are a diverse, growing community of around 1200 people in San Antonio ,Tx. who take worship seriously and don't take ourselves too seriously. We're looking for a Worship Arts Pastor to help us keep meeting God together, week after week.


The Role

This is a full-time pastoral role. You'll lead the people, the planning, and the musical and creative vision behind our weekend worship experience. You'll partner closely with our Creative Arts Director, who oversees Sunday production, so the two of you can deliver services that are both musically strong and well produced. It also means being a pastor: caring for people, shaping spiritual formation, and helping a room full of worshipers grow in their journey.


You will partner in true collaboration with the Lead Pastor. You will provide direction and support to the Creative Arts Director on worship and service execution, and you lead the worship team and its volunteers. Your work week runs Sunday through Thursday.


Sundays + weekend worship

  • Serve as our primary worship leader, and lead worship week to week with excellence and authenticity
  • Plan and evaluate weekend services alongside our service leaders so every Sunday is intentional
  • Set the worship and creative vision for each service, and partner with the Creative Arts Director to bring it to life on stage and screen
  • Provide direction and support to the Creative Arts Director, who oversees Sunday production—align on service flow and keep music and production moving together


Volunteer culture (your biggest win)

  • Recruit, train, and coach musicians, vocalists, and worship team leads
  • Build a leadership pipeline so worship doesn't depend on one person
  • Create a culture where volunteers feel known, valued, and developed
  • Run rehearsals that are prepared, prayerful, and worth people's time


Pastoral care + spiritual formation

  • Shepherd your team spiritually, not just musically
  • Share in pastoral care: preaching, weddings, funerals, hospital visits, coaching, and counseling
  • Help worship form people, connecting what happens on Sunday to how people follow Jesus the rest of the week


Ministry administration + budget

  • Own the worship ministry's calendar, volunteer onboarding pipeline, and Worship Arts handbook
  • Build and manage the worship ministry budget (plan, track, adjust)
  • Model fiscal responsibility and stewardship, and approve expenditures within your area
  • Collaborate across teams to align calendars, strategy, and resourcing


What We're Looking For

  • 3+ years of progressively responsible worship or music ministry experience, or a high level of musical competence (band leadership, modulation/transposition, improvisation)
  • Proven ability to recruit, lead, and develop volunteers
  • Strong communication with volunteers, parents, staff, and the congregation
  • Grounded in biblical theology, spiritual formation, and the foundational beliefs of the Christian faith
  • Organized, relational, steady under pressure


Preferred (not required)

  • Licensed and/or ordained minister
  • Bachelor's degree (music, ministry, or related field)
  • Large church experience (750+)
  • Fluency in the full range of worship elements: vocal, instrumental, visual, content, movement
  • Familiarity with Planning Center Online and music software (Finale, Logic, MainStage, Ableton Live)


What success looks like (first 6–12 months)

  • Sundays feel consistent, excellent, and spiritually engaging across every service
  • Worship teams are staffed, trained, and supported—less scrambling
  • A real leadership pipeline exists, so the ministry isn't carried by one person
  • Music and production move together seamlessly through a strong partnership with the Creative Arts Director


What it's like to work here

Outer West is a team-first church. We move fast, communicate directly, and build healthy systems—because people matter more than last-minute chaos. We work hard, we laugh a lot, and we protect what keeps leaders healthy. We're a diverse, growing community that puts God first and is generous with our time, talent, and treasure.


What We Ask of Every Staff Member

  • An active, personal relationship with Jesus Christ.
  • Personal engagement with OWCC's mission, vision, and values.
  • A commitment to our staff values and to our Partnership and Leadership Covenants.
  • A willingness to partner across departments to lead and launch ministry initiatives together.


Mission

Outer West Community Church exists to draw people closer to Jesus Christ and each other


Values

God First  | We seek God in all things through prayer and Scripture

Community | We live in compassionate community where everyone belongs

Diversity | We embrace diversity and unity found within the Body of Christ

Service | We passionately serve our church, San Antonio, and beyond

Generosity | We are generous with our time, talent, and treasure

post_html:
Restoration Church Wausau (www.rcwausau.org)

Position: Pastor of Student and Family Discipleship

Level: Full-time (Compensation to include salary and full benefits)

Ministry Focus

The Pastor of Student and Family Discipleship is responsible for leading and overseeing the disciple-making ministry from birth through 12th grade, providing vision and leadership oversight (not operational management) to the Children’s Ministry through its staffed leadership team, but giving primary focus to the middle school and high school student ministry.

Some of the qualifications and traits for serving as the Pastor of Student and Family Discipleship are:

  • A growing, vibrant walk with Christ.

  • Clear theological alignment with the church’s doctrine and disciple-making mission.

  • Demonstrated ability to teach Scripture faithfully and clearly.

  • A shepherd’s heart with relational warmth and spiritual courage.

  • Proven ability to develop and lead volunteer teams.

General Pastoral Responsibilities

Pastors of Restoration Church are first, pastors to the church as a whole and then second, pastors in their specific ministries. As a member of the pastoral team, the Pastor of Student and Family Discipleship will:

  • Attend weekly staff/pastor meetings.

  • Attend bi-monthly elder meetings.

  • Participate in churchwide events.

  • Provide general pastoral care to members of the body.

  • Supply the pulpit when needed (approximately 4–5 times per year).

Student Ministry (Grades 6–12)

The Pastor will serve as the primary shepherd, teacher, and vision-caster for the Student Ministry with average attendances ranging between 80 and 110 students.

1. Spiritual Leadership & Vision

  • Cast and implement a clear, gospel-centered discipleship vision for grades 6–12.

  • Ensure student ministry aligns with the overall mission and theology of the church.

  • Cultivate a culture of spiritual seriousness, relational warmth, and joyful obedience.

  • Develop a pathway for students to move from conversion to mature disciple-making.

2. Teaching & Theological Formation

  • Regularly oversee the structure and teaching of Wednesday night gatherings.

  • Ensure teaching is biblically faithful, Christ-centered, and missionally focused.

3. Shepherding & Discipleship

  • Personally disciple students through intentional relational investment.

  • Provide shepherding care to students and families.

  • Be available to families navigating spiritual, relational, or cultural challenges.

4. Leader Development

  • Recruit, onboard, and train youth leaders (approximately 25–30 leaders).

  • Provide policy, training, and accountability structures for leaders.

  • Equip leaders to make disciples, not merely supervise events.

  • Send weekly communication to leaders and parents to reinforce alignment and clarity.

5. Ministry Administration & Events

  • Work with the Youth Ministry Assistant to plan and coordinate ministry events.

  • Coordinate Sunday School curriculum and teaching schedules with the Youth Sunday School Lead.

  • Ensure Church Management System updates and event registrations are accurate.

  • Maintain consistent connection with local schools.

Children’s Ministry Oversight (Birth–5th Grade)

The Pastor provides vision and leadership oversight for Children’s Ministry, overseeing part-time children’s ministry staff, ensuring alignment, health, and discipleship clarity.

  • Cast unified discipleship vision for birth through 12th grade, ensuring that the children’s ministry aligns with the church’s theology, philosophy of ministry, and discipleship framework.

  • Oversee and support the Director(s) of Children’s Ministry.

    • Provide spiritual shepherding and accountability.

    • Help clarify priorities and time management.

  • Provide high-level budget oversight.

  • Provide counsel in complex shepherding or discipline situations when necessary.

For more information, or to send a resume, reach out to Pastor Greg Schmidt.

Greg Schmidt

greg@rcwausau.org

715-845-3199

Living Faith Alliance is seeking a new ministry leader to come join us at a critical time in the life of our church. We have been through a season of challenge, loss and also growth and believe God is giving us vision for our little outpost of His kingdom in Cumberland County. We have been learning to work together as a team, making prayer more central to all that we do, and trying to be more sensitive to God’s leading.

We do that by focusing on 4 circles of relationship where we believe Jesus wants to strategically bring his influence: in our lives, in our homes, in our church family, and in our community. If that's you and God is leading you to a new challenge and a new opportunity, get to know us by checking us out online at livingfaithalliance.org and prayerfully consider sending in your resume, with cover letter, references, and answers to preliminary questions to Elders@lfachurch.org.

The Minister of Youth and Pastoral Care is also working to honor the call in 1 Peter 5:1-4 to shepherd the flock entrusted to our care. This is accomplished by syncing up the Pastoral Care Team, the Pastor's Team, with other key leaders to assess, discuss and work in cooperation with one another to implement care. Department: Congregational Care

Position Summary
   The Associate Pastor of Congregational Care and Support (APCC) focuses primarily on supporting and healing Christ’s lost, hurt, or wandering sheep. He works with the Associate Director/Pastor of Discipleship to build up the body of Christ, feed and protect Christ’s sheep and equip the saints for works of service as we make disciples of all nations.


   Thus, the APCC leads the saints in the healing and supporting offices and ministries of the church. These include, pastoral and shepherding ministries, the deaconate, marriage enrichment/support, healing (called: Oaks), and benevolence. This work is done by personal work in the pastoral duties as well as training volunteers to take on effective pastoral ministries.


   This is a meaningful, people-centered role suited for someone who is equally at home sitting with a family in crisis, leading a volunteer team, or developing systems that help our congregation experience genuine, ongoing care. As a large and growing church, we believe that no one should fall through the cracks—and this pastor will play a central role in ensuring that our people are known, shepherded, and supported at every stage of life.


Core Responsibilities

  • Pastoral Counseling
    • Provide pastoral counseling to individuals and families navigating grief, crisis, relational difficulty, and spiritual struggle.
    • Maintain a consistent counseling caseload, offering both short-term support and referrals to licensed professionals when appropriate.
    • Develop and maintain a referral network of Christian therapists and licensed counselors in the community.
    • Respond with pastoral care and presence in moments of congregational crisis, including hospitalizations, deaths, and family emergencies.
  • Marriage Ministry
    • Oversee and develop the church’s marriage ministry, including premarital counseling programs, marriage enrichment events, and the Re|engage ministry.
    • Conduct or coordinate premarital counseling for engaged couples within the congregation.
    • Recruit, train, and support mentor couples who walk alongside newlyweds and struggling marriages.
    • Curate resources that support healthy marriages across all stages of life.
  • Shepherding Team
    • Recruit , train, and pastor the volunteer Shepherding Team—laypeople who provide front-line care and connection within the congregation.
    • Develop structures and rhythms that allow the Shepherding Team to identify needs, make visits, and follow up with members and regular attenders.
    • Hold regular team meetings, provide spiritual formation input, and foster a team culture of joy and compassion.
    • Serve as the primary point of accountability and encouragement for Shepherding Team volunteers.
  • The Oaks Ministry
    • Provide pastoral oversight for Oaks, the church’s ministry to create a gospel-centered, rehabilitative space for people.
  • Benevolence Fund
    • Administer the church’s benevolence fund alongside the Benevolence Team with wisdom, compassion, and sound stewardship practices.
    • Develop and maintain clear policies and procedures for benevolence requests, approvals, and follow-up.
    • Partner with local community organizations to extend care beyond what the church can provide directly.
    • Maintain appropriate confidentiality while keeping leadership informed of trends and needs within the congregation.
  • Deacon Ministry
    • Work closely with the deacon body to align their ministry with the broader congregational care vision.
    • Provide pastoral support, equipping, and direction for deacons serving in areas of practical care and service.
    • Collaborate with deacon leadership on identifying and meeting tangible needs within the congregation.
    • Support the ongoing development and health of the deacon ministry as a whole.


Qualifications

  • Required
    • Genuine, vibrant Christian faith and active membership in a local church community.
    • Masters level knowledge in relevant theological fields: spiritual theology, theology, pastoral duties or spiritual direction. The APCC should be interested in growing in his knowledge of areas of theology and other knowledge relevant to mastery and leadership of his areas of ministry. Master of Divinity (M.Div.) or equivalent theological education strongly preferred; relevant pastoral experience may be considered.
    • Mastery of the Bible and the Gospel- able to call up the relevant Biblical knowledge and truths of the Gospel for ministry in each situation.
    • Minimum of 3–5 years of pastoral ministry experience in the local church, with demonstrated involvement in care-related ministry. (This may be as an elder, or key non-paid position.)
    • Leadership- able to lead groups primarily of volunteers to do the work of ministry. He is able to inspire, equip, deploy, rally and unify people to the works he is overseeing.
    • A heart for people across all ages and life stages—especially those who are hurting, overlooked, or struggling.
    • Strong interpersonal and listening skills; ability to hold confidential information with discretion and care.
    • Experience recruiting, developing, and leading volunteers.
    • Alignment with the church’s statement of faith, values, and vision.
    • A flexible team player, adamant to hold unity and support the ethos of our staff values. Will handle conflict directly, be reasonably flexible, honor the chain of command, forgive real offence, overlook most slights, and be passionate about the integrity of our team dynamic.


Character & Core Competencies

  • Pastoral presence: You bring calm, warmth, and genuine care into difficult and tender moments.
  • Organizational clarity: You can build and sustain systems that help volunteers thrive and needs get met.
  • Collaborative spirit: You work well alongside other staff, deacons, and lay leaders with a non-territorial posture.
  • Emotional resilience: You can enter into others’ pain without losing your own joy or perspective.
  • Theological grounding: Your care is shaped by the gospel, not just sentiment.
  • Cultural awareness: You understand and honor the diversity of experience within a large congregation.
  • Moral Clarity: You are able to speak the truth with candor and integrity while being kind. You know when compromise is productive and mature and when it is a betrayal of God’s will.
