Join Us on a Purpose-Driven Mission to Share the Gospel - Women’s Evangelism and Concierge Ministry Assistant Wanted!

 

Serve with purpose

At the North American Mission Board (NAMB), we are committed to advancing the gospel and helping churches engage people with the hope of Christ. The Women’s Evangelism and Concierge Ministry Assistant supports this mission by providing reliable administrative, communications, and event coordination for the National Director of Women’s Evangelism and the broader ministry.

In this role, you will help coordinate women’s evangelism events and resources, support the Concierge ministry, and communicate with pastors, churches, ministry partners, and NAMB teams. Your organization, initiative, and service will help the ministry operate effectively and serve others well.

 

About the role


The Women’s Evangelism and Concierge Ministry Assistant provides administrative and operational support across a range of ministry activities. Responsibilities include managing calendars and travel, coordinating meetings and events, preparing presentations and communications, supporting resource development, and helping organize communication between pastors and Concierge ministry agents.

The successful candidate is highly organized, comfortable managing competing priorities, and able to communicate with professionalism, warmth, and attention to detail.

 

Ministerial qualifications

All staff positions at NAMB are considered ministerial in nature because of the organization’s purpose and mission.

 

Key responsibilities


  • Support ministry leadership: Provide administrative coordination for the National Director of Women’s Evangelism, including calendar management, speaking requests, meeting scheduling, travel arrangements, and expense reports.
  • Communicate with ministry partners: Represent the National Director professionally in communications with state and associational partners, churches, pastors, SBC leaders, NAMB team members, and other ministry partners.
  • Coordinate events and meetings: Assist with planning and logistics for women’s evangelism conferences, trainings, and other on-site and off-site events, including in-person and virtual meetings.
  • Support event follow-up: Review event surveys and identify insights that can help improve future events and ministry efforts.
  • Prepare presentations and materials: Create clear, polished PowerPoint presentations from provided teaching outlines and support the preparation of ministry materials.
  • Support ministry communications: Coordinate with marketing and events teams and assist with email, newsletter, social media, and other communications for Women’s Evangelism.
  • Assist with resource development: Proofread and edit resource content, and work with the marketing team to support resources through the production process.
  • Support the Concierge ministry: Help organize and communicate with Concierge agents, maintain the list of participating pastors, and coordinate communication between pastors and agents.
  • Provide general team support: Resolve relevant Help Desk tickets, assist with special projects, and take on other duties as needed to support Women’s Evangelism and the Concierge ministry.
  • Protect sensitive information: Handle ministry, personnel, and partner information with appropriate care and discretion.

Qualifications


  • High school diploma or equivalent required.
  • Associate degree or higher in business administration, communications, ministry, or a related field preferred.
  • At least three years of experience in an administrative, executive assistant, or program coordination role required.
  • Experience supporting senior leaders and coordinating events, meetings, travel, or communications preferred.
  • Experience in a church, ministry, or nonprofit setting preferred.
  • Advanced proficiency with Microsoft 365, including Outlook, Teams, Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and OneDrive.
  • Demonstrated ability to manage complex calendars, coordinate meetings, arrange travel, and prepare accurate expense reports.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to communicate professionally with ministry partners, pastors, and internal teams.
  • Ability to create polished presentations from teaching outlines.
  • Experience supporting in-person and virtual events, including logistics, communications, and follow-up.
  • Experience supporting email, newsletter, and social media communications and collaborating with marketing and events teams.
  • Strong proofreading and editing skills, with careful attention to accuracy, tone, and detail.

Work environment and physical requirements


This position is based in Alpharetta, Georgia. The role involves regular computer and phone use, coordination with internal and external partners, and support for in-person and virtual meetings and events. Event-related responsibilities may require occasional lifting or carrying of materials and movement around event spaces.

The physical requirements described are representative of those necessary to perform the essential functions of the position. Reasonable accommodations may be made for individuals with disabilities.

 

Why NAMB?


Join a purpose-driven organization committed to advancing the gospel and serving churches and ministry partners. In this role, you will have the opportunity to:

  • Support women’s evangelism efforts and the Concierge ministry.
  • Help pastors, churches, and ministry partners connect with ministry resources and events.
  • Contribute to a collaborative, faith-based team environment.
  • Support ministry communications, events, and resources that serve NAMB’s mission.
  • Access benefits that may include medical, dental, vision, and life insurance; retirement plans; disability insurance; paid time off; and paid holidays.

Ready to serve?


Apply today to support the Women’s Evangelism and Concierge ministries at NAMB. Bring your administrative strengths, communication skills, and commitment to service to work that helps advance the gospel and support ministry partners.

Campus Staff Minister - Northern MN & NW WI Area (Undergraduate Ministry)

Work Location:

Remote - USA

Job Type:

Full time

God has called InterVarsity to plant and to build witnessing communities of students and faculty who follow Jesus on college and university campuses. Through these groups, we believe ever- increasing numbers of students and faculty from all ethnic groups and areas of the campus will be transformed by the Gospel. We expect to see campuses increasingly become places where people, ideas, and structures flourish to the glory of God. We confidently anticipate that our InterVarsity alumni will become change agents across the country and around the world. We pursue this calling by discerning and actively participating in what God is already doing on campus. This is the essence of being a Campus Staff Minister (CSM).

ESSENTIAL COMMITMENTS/RESPONSIBILITIES 

Spiritual Growth 

As a Campus Staff Minister, you pursue maturity as a disciple of Jesus Christ so that your life and work increasingly reflect a growing love for God, God’s Word, God’s people of every ethnicity and culture, and God’s purposes in the world. To do this, you will: 

  • Pursue a vibrant relationship with the triune God through engagement with Scripture, prayer, and worship, both individually and in community 

  • Develop self-leadership (growing in self-awareness, self-management, relational integrity, and resiliency)

  • Embrace Scriptural standards for behavior and attitudes 

 

Campus Leadership 

As a Campus Staff Minister, you increase the number of witnessing communities, as well as the size, health, spiritual maturity, and campus-wide influence of existing witnessing communities of students and faculty by being a: 

  • Visionary Guide: 

You communicate and model InterVarsity’s vision to see students and faculty transformed, campuses renewed, and world changers developed 

  • Create a culture of humble dependence on God and bold expectation in God’s intention to start new witnessing communities throughout the campus and on new campuses

  • Model – in person and through programs – InterVarsity’s vision and Core Values, including a biblically-defined commitment to engage every ethnic and social group on campus

  • Lead students and faculty – individually and collectively – through Scripture, prayer, teaching, and discipleship experiences, so that they articulate and align their ministry activities around this vision

  • Set annual goals through prayer, research and reflection with your teams (students, faculty, and staff) for qualitative and quantitative growth, including conversions and leadership development 

  • Structural Architect: 

You create, develop, align, and leverage ministry plans, programs, teams, and structures to close the gap between current reality and the aspirational goals. 

  • Build leadership teams who trust and partner well with you and who demonstrate spiritual vitality, relational health, and mission alignment

  • Develop and execute plans to achieve annual goals, evaluating and modifying the plan as needed throughout the year

  • Increase momentum for the vision by aligning programs, structures, conferences, and teams around the goals

  • Mobilize students and faculty to engage their relational networks with the gospel and to start new missional communities

  • Under the direction of the Area Director, may supervise Ministry Interns and Campus Ministry Interns as delegated 

  • Missional Developer: 

You intentionally gather, invite, and develop diverse groups of students and faculty so that they not only encounter and follow Jesus as Savior and Lord but also advance the mission on campus as participants and leaders. 

  • Create ways for faculty and students to encounter and follow Jesus through Scripture, worship, prayer, mission experiences, conferences, etc.

  • Equip students and faculty so that they think strategically about campus engagement and so that they proclaim – in word, deed, and power – the good news of Jesus, regularly inviting students and faculty to follow him as Savior and Lord

  • Disciple students and faculty by equipping them to hear the Word, respond actively, and debrief and interpret the experience so that they grow in Christlikeness, reflect our Core Values, and develop ministry skills

  • Invite, coach, and equip students and faculty to become increasingly effective participants and leaders, including starting new witnessing communities on campuses 

 

Organizational Collaboration 

As a Campus Staff Minister, you have joined a national mission. Therefore, you work with a network of other local, area, regional, and national InterVarsity staff and volunteers so that our work reflects Biblical standards of excellence, integrity, and partnership. 

  • Partner with and respond positively to the direction and coaching of your supervisors and national leaders

  • Contribute to collaborative and productive team meetings and relationships

  • Affiliate chapters under your care and submit Graduating Student Forms in order to increase our partnership with current students and alumni

  • Use national ministry resources and tools, as requested, including recruiting and/or participating in local, regional, or national conferences as

  • Complete reporting, planning and review requirements in a timely way so that you and your supervisors can assess and improve your work as a CSM

  • Comply with all InterVarsity policies and procedures 

 

Ministry Partnership Development 

As a Campus Staff Minister, you will develop a team of partners – churches and individuals (including alumni and community members) – who will resource the ministry financially, in prayer, or volunteer service that advances the mission. 

  • Raise 100% of the financial budget assigned by your supervisor

  • Communicate regularly with your ministry partners, nurturing the relationship through visits, phone calls, emails and regular prayer letters

  • Develop on-going, long-lasting partnership with alumni and volunteers

  • Comply with all Ministry Partnership Policies

  • Identify and invest in advocates who will build networks of volunteers and donors on InterVarsity’s behalf 

 

Accomplish all other assigned tasks as appropriate 

 

QUALIFICATIONS (common to all levels of CSM) 

  • Annually affirm InterVarsity’s Statement of Agreement (Doctrinal Basis and Purpose Statement). Abide by InterVarsity’s Code of Conduct. Believe and behave consonantly with InterVarsity’s Human Sexuality Theological Paper. Affirm and behave consonantly with InterVarsity’s “Women in Ministry Statement of Affirmation”

  • Bachelor’s degree for CSMs assigned to a four-year campus. A minimum of an Associate’s degree for CSMs assigned to a two-year campus or a community college

  • Strong interpersonal skills (including ability to minister to diverse ethnic communities and faculty)

  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills

  • Demonstrated problem solving skills

  • Familiarity with word processing, presentation, email, and spreadsheet software 

 

WORK ENVIRONMENT/PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS 

The CSM position leads ministry in a college campus environment. A designated office space may or may not be available. The CSM is required to travel to on-campus and off- campus sites as appropriate. Off-campus travel includes, but is not limited to: student ministry conferences, Ministry Partnership Development meetings, and InterVarsity- sponsored training sessions, meetings, and conferences. The CSM is regularly required to communicate with others, and routinely uses standard office equipment such as computers, phones, photocopiers, filing cabinets, etc. 

Pay Range: $39,288.00 - $52,392.00 per year

Pay: This position is funded through personal fundraising. Accordingly, compensation will vary based on the ability of the individual to secure a donor team to fund the cost of his/her salary. The anticipated salary range for this position on a full-time basis (40 hours/week) is dependent on a variety of factors, including location and cost of living. The actual salary received, including any geographic adjustment to account for location and cost of living, is subject to the individual’s ability to raise funds necessary to cover the full amount of such salary within the range set forth in the job posting details.

Benefits:

The International Mission Board is seeking a Church Engagement Strategist to strengthen and expand partnerships with key Southern Baptist churches. In this highly relational role, you will help churches deepen their impact on global missions by cultivating meaningful partnerships that increase prayer, generosity, and missionary sending among the nations.


Location: Remote in the Midwest

Compensation: $74,489-$87,634 annually*


The Church Engagement Strategist combines strategic account management, ministry partnership development, and mobilization leadership. You'll provide concierge-level service to church leaders, helping them identify meaningful opportunities to engage with the International Mission Board's mission and strategic initiatives worldwide.


Responsibilities:

  • Develop deep, trust-based relationships with senior pastors, missions leaders, and key church influencers. Serve as the primary point of contact between assigned churches and the IMB.
  • Create customized engagement strategies tailored to each church's unique vision, culture, and capacity. Research church and denominational trends to identify opportunities for increased missions engagement.
  • Inspire churches to expand their involvement in global missions through prayer, missionary sending, and financial support.
  • Connect churches with missionaries, field initiatives, and strategic mission opportunities.
  • Identify and cultivate new pathways for partnership and engagement.
  • Manage communications, travel planning, CRM records, and engagement tracking.
  • Serve as a bridge between church partners and missionaries serving around the world. Share stories of impact that demonstrate how church partnerships advance the gospel globally.
  • Collaborate with internal teams to ensure churches receive timely resources, updates, and opportunities.
  • Partner with fellow engagement strategists and ministry teams to share best practices and innovative ideas. Contribute to national engagement strategies and organizational initiatives.
  • Maintain accurate records of partnership activity and engagement outcomes.
  • Assist in cross-functional collaboration to strengthen overall ministry effectiveness.

Qualifications:

  • Bachelor's degree and seminary training (MDiv or MRE) or equivalent missionary experience
  • At least 5 years of relevant ministry, missions, church engagement, fundraising, business development, or relationship management experience.
  • Active membership in a Southern Baptist Convention (SBC) church.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities

Job Summary: 

The NextGen Worship Lead (Support) role facilitates worship in Kids, Youth, and Young Adult environments at an assigned campus in partnership with the Campus Worship Pastor. This part-time permanent role cares for campus Next Gen worship teams, trains worship leaders and musicians, plans and schedules worship-related events, and leads worship. With support from the Regional Next Gen Associate Worship Pastor, the Team Lead carries the churchwide Next Gen worship standards into each campus environment. 


Principal Job Responsibilities: 

  • Builds and stewards the NextGen worship Serve Team at the campus: recruiting, training, scheduling, retention, and appreciation 
  • Executes the set lists, Ableton/Playback sessions, and service plans provided by Next Gen Worship rather than creating a separate standard 
  • Develops young worship leaders and musicians at the campus, and mentors students on the team 
  • Runs rehearsals and pre-service preparation for NextGen environments at the campus 
  • Partners with the Campus Worship Pastor and campus NextGen leadership on platform, scheduling, and shared needs 
  • Raises local realities and needs to the Regional NextGen Associate Worship Pastor rather than absorbing them 
  • Supports campus NextGen events, camps, and team nights 
  • Is present and serving at weekend services and churchwide events as the ministry calendar requires 
  • Performs other duties as assigned. 

 

As a member of the Gateway Church team, this position is expected to support, recruit, and develop Serve Team members, and to serve alongside the broader team as ministry and organizational needs arise. 


General Skills & Qualifications: 

  • A clear passion for Jesus and a strong biblical foundation 
  • A heart for students and kids, with the ability to lead worship in their environments 
  • Musical craft and talent, with proficiency as a worship leader on voice and at least one instrument 
  • Demonstrated ability to recruit, train, and retain volunteers 
  • Able to take direction on standards from Central while owning execution locally 
  • Consistently growing in craft, character, and leadership capacity 
  • Professional in punctuality, communication, and appearance 
  • Demonstrated emotional and relational intelligence 
  • Strong time-management skills and the ability to hold several priorities at once 
  • Proficient in Microsoft Office and able to learn and function within new software and systems 

Education/Certification(s): 

  • High school diploma or equivalent, and one or more years of worship leading experience — required 
  • Experience leading kids or student worship — preferred 
  • Prior experience in a multisite church environment — preferred 

General Physical Requirements: 

The physical demands described here represent those that an employee must meet to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. While performing the duties of this position, the employee is regularly required to: 

  • Sit or stand for extended periods of time 
  • Occasionally kneel or crouch 
  • Frequently lift and/or move up to 10 lbs. 
  • Occasionally lift and/or move up to 25 lbs. 
  • Able to lift and move instruments and equipment up to 40 lbs, and available to work weekends and evenings as the ministry calendar requires 

*This description is not all inclusive, and other duties may be assigned as necessary. 

 
Gateway Church does not discriminate in employment opportunities or practices on the basis of race, color, sex, national origin, age, disability, or any other characteristic protected by law as it applies to churches. However, Gateway Church does discriminate on the basis of religion. 

 
Employment Requirement: Must be a member or become a member of Gateway Church upon employment.

post_html:
Campus Staff Minister I - Central Texas Area (Undergraduate Ministry)

Work Location:

Texas

Job Type:

Part time

God has called InterVarsity to plant and to build witnessing communities of students and faculty who follow Jesus on college and university campuses. Through these groups, we believe ever- increasing numbers of students and faculty from all ethnic groups and areas of the campus will be transformed by the Gospel. We expect to see campuses increasingly become places where people, ideas, and structures flourish to the glory of God. We confidently anticipate that our InterVarsity alumni will become change agents across the country and around the world. We pursue this calling by discerning and actively participating in what God is already doing on campus. This is the essence of being a Campus Staff Minister (CSM).

CONTEXT:
With over 70 years of collective ministry experience, InterVarsity's Central Texas area ministry has a rich history of reaching every corner of the University of Texas campus. Beyond UT we also have established work at St. Edward's University and are looking to replant work at Austin Community College and Texas State as well as other Universities in Austin and surrounding areas.

We are a diverse movement of witnessing communities, sent to make disciples of Jesus in Austin and beyond. Our area vision is to communally partner with the work that God is doing on campus’ in Central Texas and empower students to walk in spiritual authority and use the gifts God has given them.

Our multi-ethnic team is a mix of full time staff and volunteers who enjoy collaboration, hospitality and fun.

LOCATION & HOURS:

We currently have the most need for Campus Staff Ministers for the following locations/foci. Please indicate in your application which you are interested in (if any):

  • University of Texas - Asian American Ministries
  • University of Texas - General
  • Concordia University - General
  • Austin Community College - General

If you are interested in working at a location that is not listed, fill out the application and indicate where in the relevant question. You are also welcome to input multiple locations and we will take them into consideration. Note that our region of InterVarsity serves the states of Texas, Oklahoma, Arkansas, and Louisiana. If you would like to serve in one of those states, search for it in the search bar to find the openings.

Part-time employees can work anywhere between 10-29 hours per week.

ESSENTIAL COMMITMENTS/RESPONSIBILITIES 

Spiritual Growth 

You pursue maturity as a disciple of Jesus Christ so that your life and work increasingly reflects a growing love for God, God’s Word, God’s people of every ethnicity and culture, and God’s purposes in the world. To do this, you will: 

  • Pursue a vibrant relationship with the triune God through engagement with Scripture, prayer, and worship, both individually and in community 

  • Develop self-leadership (growing in self-awareness, self-management, relational integrity, and resiliency) 

  • Embrace Scriptural standards for behavior and attitudes 

 

Campus Leadership 

You communicate and model InterVarsity’s vision to see students and faculty transformed, campuses renewed and world changers developed 

  • Create a culture of humble dependence on God and bold expectation in God’s intention to start new witnessing communities throughout the campus and on new campuses 

  • Model – in person and through programs – InterVarsity’s vision and Core Values, including a biblically-defined commitment to engage every ethnic and social group on campus 

  • Lead students and faculty – individually and collectively – through Scripture, prayer, teaching, and discipleship experiences, so that they articulate and align their ministry activities around this vision 

  • Set annual goals through prayer, research and reflection with your teams (students, faculty, and staff) for qualitative and quantitative growth, including conversions and leadership development 

 

You create, develop, align and leverage ministry plans, programs, teams, and structures to close the gap between current reality and the aspirational goals. 

  • Build leadership teams who trust and partner well with you and who demonstrate spiritual vitality, relational health, and mission alignment 

  • Develop and execute plans to achieve annual goals, evaluating and modifying the plan as needed throughout the year 

  • Increase momentum for the vision by aligning programs, structures, conferences and teams around the goals 

  • Mobilize students and faculty to engage their relational networks with the gospel and to start new missional communities 

  • Under the direction of the Area Director, may supervise Ministry Interns and Campus Ministry Interns as delegated 

 

You intentionally gather, invite, and develop diverse groups of students and faculty so that they not only encounter and follow Jesus as Savior and Lord but also advance the mission on campus as participants and leaders. 

  • Create ways for faculty and students to encounter and follow Jesus through Scripture, worship, prayer, mission experiences, conferences, etc. 

  • Equip students and faculty so that they think strategically about campus engagement and so that they proclaim – in word, deed, and power – the good news of Jesus, regularly inviting students and faculty to follow him as Savior and Lord 

  • Disciple students and faculty by equipping them to hear the Word, respond actively, and debrief and interpret the experience so that they grow in Christlikeness, reflect our Core Values, and develop ministry skills 

  • Invite, coach, and equip students and faculty to become increasingly effective participants and leaders, including starting new witnessing communities on campuses 

 

Organizational Collaboration 

You work with a network of other local, area, regional, and national InterVarsity staff and volunteers so that our work reflects Biblical standards of excellence, integrity, and partnership. 

  • Partner with and respond positively to the direction and coaching of your supervisors and national leaders 

  • Contribute to collaborative and productive team meetings and relationships 

  • Affiliate chapters under your care and submit Graduating Student Forms in order to increase our partnership with current students and alumni 

  • Use national ministry resources and tools, as requested, including recruiting and/or participating in local, regional, or national conferences as  

  • Complete reporting, planning and review requirements in a timely way so that you and your supervisors can assess and improve your work as a CSM 

  • Comply with all InterVarsity policies and procedures 

 

Ministry Partnership Development 

You will develop a team of partners – churches and individuals (including alumni and community members) – who will resource the ministry financially, in prayer, or volunteer service that advances the mission. 

  • Raise 100% of the financial budget assigned by your supervisor 

  • Communicate regularly with your ministry partners, nurturing the relationship through visits, phone calls, emails and regular prayer letters 

  • Develop on-going, long-lasting partnership with alumni and volunteers 

  • Comply with all Ministry Partnership Policies 

  • Identify and invest in advocates who will build networks of volunteers and donors on InterVarsity’s behalf 

 

Accomplish all other assigned tasks as appropriate 

 

QUALIFICATIONS (common to all levels of CSM) 

  • Annually affirm InterVarsity’s Statement of Agreement (Doctrinal Basis and Purpose Statement). Abide by InterVarsity’s Code of Conduct. Believe and behave consonantly with InterVarsity’s Human Sexuality Theological Paper. Affirm and behave consonantly with InterVarsity’s “Women in Ministry Statement of Affirmation” 

  • Bachelor’s degree for CSMs assigned to a four-year campus. A minimum of an Associate’s degree for CSMs assigned to a two-year campus or a community college 

  • Strong interpersonal skills (including ability to minister to diverse ethnic communities and faculty) 

  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills 

  • Demonstrated problem solving skills 

  • Familiarity with word processing, presentation, email, and spreadsheet software 

 

WORK ENVIRONMENT/PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS 

The CSM position leads ministry in a college campus environment. A designated office space may or may not be available. The CSM is required to travel to on-campus and off- campus sites as appropriate. Off-campus travel includes, but is not limited to: student ministry conferences, Ministry Partnership Development meetings, and InterVarsity- sponsored training sessions, meetings, and conferences. The CSM is regularly required to communicate with others, and routinely uses standard office equipment such as computers, phones, photocopiers, filing cabinets, etc. 

Pay Range: $33,900.00 - $45,204.00 per year

Pay: This position is funded through personal fundraising. Accordingly, compensation will vary based on the ability of the individual to secure a donor team to fund the cost of his/her salary. The anticipated salary range for this position on a full-time basis (40 hours/week) is dependent on a variety of factors, including location and cost of living. The actual salary received, including any geographic adjustment to account for location and cost of living, is subject to the individual’s ability to raise funds necessary to cover the full amount of such salary within the range set forth in the job posting details.

Benefits:

We offer a competitive benefits package, including health care and retirement savings with a match. Eligibility is based on employee type and hours worked.  Benefits include the following:

  • 403(b) Retirement Savings Plan

  • 403(b) matching contributions

  • Dental insurance

  • Employee assistance program

  • Employee discounts

  • Flexible work schedule

  • Flexible spending accounts

  • Health insurance

  • Health savings account

  • Life insurance

  • Paid time off

  • Parental leave

  • Professional development assistance

  • Vision insurance

Equal Employment Opportunity: 

 

InterVarsity Christian Fellowship/USA is both an equal opportunity employer and a faith-based religious organization. We conduct hiring without regard to race, color, ancestry, national origin, citizenship, age, sex, marital status, parental status, membership in any labor organization, political ideology, or disability of an otherwise qualified individual. The status of InterVarsity Christian Fellowship/USA as an equal opportunity employer does not prevent the organization from hiring staff based on their religious beliefs so that all staff share the same religious commitment.  Pursuant to the Civil Rights Act of 1964, Section 702 (42 U.S.C. 2000e 1(a)) InterVarsity Christian Fellowship/USA has the right to, and does, hire only candidates who agree with InterVarsity’s Statement of Agreement: Purpose and Doctrinal Basis because InterVarsity believes that each and every staff plays a vital role in advancing InterVarsity’s mission and purposes.

JOB SUMMARY:

The Christ Fellowship Kids Ministry Assistant provides support and care for every aspect of the Children’s Ministry area. 

JOB DUTIES:

  • Involved in selecting and equipping a volunteer team so they can thrive in their assigned roles on the Christ Fellowship Kids team.
  • Ensure weekend resources are prepared and distributed in preparation for the weekend experience.
  • Supporting weekend and midweek programming as directed.
  • Contributing to Central Team initiative development and implementation as directed by and in cooperation with Central Kids Directors and team.
  • Attending weekly staff meetings and Department meetings as directed.
  • Serve as a PHASE expert.

EDUCATION:

  • Degree in progress; a focus in education/ministry is a plus.
  • Experienced with 1 year in a kids’ ministry environment, either as staff or volunteer.

JOB SPECS: 

Classification: Part-time (25 hours) Hourly (non - exempt) position including weekends and some week nights.
Reporting to: Kids Coordinator

Company Description

The mission of Christ’s Church of the Valley is to win people to Jesus Christ, train believers to become disciples, and send disciples to impact the world. The Students Ministry supports the mission of CCV by shaping students to become Christ-centered difference makers. The Students Pastor will assist pastoring Junior and Senior High students through recruiting, training, and retaining youth coaches, as well as implementing Junior and Senior High school programs and events. The Students Pastor will also assist in growing the campus in all areas numerically such as attendance, coaches, and baptisms. 

Job Description

Essential Job Functions 

  • Execute Junior and Senior High events and programs 
  • Cast the overall CCV & Students Ministry vision with parents and volunteers 
  • Provide pastoral care for families and coaches 
  • Recruit, train, and retain volunteers for all weekend areas and events 
  • Develop and maintain school campus involvement 
  • Following up with first time students 
  • Collect and report accurate weekly attendance according to established standards and deadlines 
  • Work with the team to plan and execute various church-wide events. These may include, but are not limited to: 
    • Kick off events 
    • Easter 
    • Christmas Eve 

 

Qualifications

CHARACTER & CHEMISTRY 

Alignment with our CORE Values & Staff Fundamentals 

  • Commitment to Excellence – We bring our best, every time. Excellence honors God and moves people. 
  • Heart for Evangelism – We will risk it all to reach one more. Jesus’ last command is our priority. 
  • Radical Generosity – We steward all things with open hands. The God who owns it all, gave it all.  
  • Integrity – We commit to zero gap between what we say and do. Jesus modeled integrity in EVERYTHING. 
  • Servant Attitude – We put others before ourselves. If serving is beneath you, leading is beyond you. 
  • Teamwork – We are fiercely committed to the power of teams. Jesus chose to work with a team. So will we.  

Agreement with our CORE Commitments 

  • Must support the vision & mission of CCV. 
  • Must be/become an ACTIVE MEMBER of CCV 
  • Must regularly ATTEND WORSHIP with their family 
  • Must be an active participant in a CCV Group and consistently tithe 
  • Demonstrated maturity as a Christ follower 

Fully engaged (or willingness to) in CCV Next Steps: 

  • Baptism-by immersion at an age of decision 
  • Worship-regularly attend CCV service with family 
  • Connect-participation in CCV small group 
  • Serve-volunteer somewhere within a CCV ministry 
  • Give-returning at least a full 10% tithe to the local church CCV 

Competency 

  • Leadership Skills – is able to trust, coach, and guide people to influence others. Continually communicates overall vision and purpose effectively. 
  • Drive for Results – Steadfastly pushes self and others for results.  Is action-oriented and displays focus, passion & initiative.  Takes appropriate action when something needs to be done. 
  • Customer Focus – is dedicated to meeting the expectations of internal and external customers. 
  • Interpersonal Skills – relates well to all kinds of people and builds effective relationships, communicates effectively both interpersonally and corporately. 
  • Self-Development – Committed to improvement, seeks constructive criticism, understands strengths and weaknesses. 

Education and Experience 

  • 2 years minimum experience leading a ministry of youth and volunteers 
  • Degree in Youth Ministry preferred, however training or proven experience in the field will be considered 
  • Athletic team experience is helpful 
  • Software and technology skills is a bonus 

  

Additional Information

General Information

The above statements are intended to describe the general nature and level of work being performed by individuals assigned to this position. They are not intended to be an exhaustive list of all duties, responsibilities, and skills required of employees. CCV Leadership reserves the right to revise the position, its job functions, minimum qualifications and other aspects of the position in any way at any time.

Title of Position: Lead Pastor (Full-Time)

Church Name: Immanuel Church

Job Description: Immanuel Church is seeking a Lead Pastor who will lead the congregation in growing a transforming relationship with Jesus, connecting in community with one another, and sharing Jesus with the world. The ideal candidate will shepherd a multi-staff team, champion a culture of worship and prayer, equip believers to serve in their spiritual gifts, and continue Immanuel's strong commitment in discipleship, small groups, and sending their people out to share Christ locally, regionally, and globally. MINISTRY SUMMARY
The Pastor of Adult Ministries provides leadership and direction for the spiritual formation and growth of HOPE Church. Rooted in our mission to Let God love You, Love Him in return, and Love Others in Jesus name, this role equips attenders to become fully devoted followers of Jesus who live out their faith in everyday life. Through developing environments, relationships, and pathways for growth, including but not limited to small groups, the Pastor of Adult Ministries helps people move from initial connection to active participation in worship, service, and witness—so that the church increasingly reflects the transforming power of Christ in our community and beyond.
 
MINISTRY DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES
The following duties are normal for this position.  These are not to be construed as exclusive or all-inclusive.  Other duties may be required and assigned.
  • Develop and implement – in collaboration with the Lead Pastor and Strategy Team, and in alignment with HOPE Church’s mission, vision, and culture—a comprehensive adult discipleship strategy that includes small groups, study classes, mentoring, and service opportunities.
  • Recruit, equip, and empower volunteers to actively lead and participate in discipleship ministries. As a “leader of leaders,” the Pastor of Adult Ministries will cultivate a multiplying culture of spiritual growth in which discipleship becomes the shared work of the whole church, not solely church staff.
  • Teach and preach as part of the adult discipleship ministry and, when invited, in Sunday worship gatherings (approximately 3–4 times per year).
QUALIFICATIONS
  • A minimum of a bachelor’s degree in Bible, ministry, or a related field required; a Master of Divinity or some seminary education is preferred.
TRAINING & DEVELOPMENT
The Pastor of Adult Ministries will receive guidance, instruction, and support from the Lead Pastor.
It is expected that the Pastor of Adult Ministries to take part in recommended training and development activities, as suggested by the Lead Pastor.  It is assumed that training and learning will be an ongoing part of this leadership position.
 
TIME COMMITMENT
  • 45-50 hours/week as required
WORKING RELATIONSHIPS
Responsible for:
  • Developing and implementing a comprehensive strategy for the spiritual growth of all who attend HOPE Church, with the goal of nurturing “fully devoted followers of Jesus.” This includes fostering regular participation in worship, relational connection with others, active engagement in service, and intentional involvement in sharing the gospel with others.
Responsible to:
  • Lead Pastor
Works closely with:
  • Lead Team, Strategy Team, Lead Pastor, Executive Pastor
LENGTH OF SERVICE
The length of service will be for an indefinite period. 
 
HOPE STAFF TEAM EXPECTATIONS
  • Be devoted to Jesus — Maintain a sincere, growing walk with Christ, His Church, and pursue excellence in His service.
  • Be aligned with HOPE’s beliefs — Support and uphold the doctrine, mission, vision, and values of HOPE Church and the Evangelical Covenant denomination.
  • Live with integrity and ethics — Practice Christ-honoring character, honesty, and self-control in every area of life.
  • Engage in worship rhythm — Participate weekly in worship services and be available for occasional evening gatherings.
  • Be present in meetings — Attend staff and ministry meetings as needed.
  • Work as one team — Build relationships, communicate concerns biblically and promptly, and contribute to a collaborative staff culture.
  • Honor confidentiality — Protect sensitive information and foster trust, integrity, and respect.
  • Model generosity — We anticipate our staff are tithing faithfully to HOPE Church or taking steps to move in that direction as a witness of Kingdom investment (Matthew 6:19–20).
  • Develop leaders and volunteers — Equip and empower volunteers within ministry areas.
  • Communicate and coordinate well — Keep staff and leadership informed so ministry efforts move in unity.
  • Demonstrate professionalism — Maintain a neat appearance, an organized workspace, and communicate clearly with Senior Leadership.
  • Serve beyond your lane — Offer assistance to other ministry areas when appropriate.

Summary and Purpose

The Senior Pastor serves as the primary spiritual leader, teacher, and visionary of Deeper Life in Christ Church. Pastor is responsible for preaching and teaching God’s Word, shepherding the congregation, equipping believers for ministry, leading staff and ministry leaders, and guiding the overall mission, vision, and values in alignment with the Christian & Missionary Alliance (C&MA). This role requires a shepherd’s heart, strong communication skills, and Spirit-led leadership grounded in biblical truth and the Great Commission, both locally and globally.

About Our Church

At Deeper Life in Christ Church, we seek to live the deeper life in Christ by:

  • Following Jesus in obedience (Colossians 2:6–7; Mark 8:34)
  • Growing in grace (2 Peter 3:18a)
  • Fostering a genuine faith family (Acts 3:32)
  • Serving others with gladness (Psalm 100:2)
  • Boldly proclaiming the gospel (Ephesians 6:15; 2 Cor. 4:15; Matthew 28:18–20)

Our vision is summarized in the C&MA theme: “All of Jesus for All the World.”

Our Core Commitments (Non-Negotiables)

  • Biblical preaching and teaching.
  • Continued emphasis on discipleship.
  • Worship focused on God, not man.

Qualifications

Education & Experience

  • Credentialed and licensed by the Christian & Missionary Alliance or willing to pursue licensing.
  • Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in ministry or theology preferred.
  • Minimum of 5 years pastoral leadership experience or related experience.
  • Demonstrated experience in preaching, team leadership, and pastoral care.
  • Demonstrated ability to lead and cultivate multi-generational ministry, engaging diverse age groups in unified discipleship and mission.

Spiritual & Personal

  • Evidences a mature, growing relationship with Jesus Christ.
  • Meets biblical qualifications for an elder (1 Tim. 3:1–7; Titus 1:6–9).
  • Genuine love for God’s people; approachable and available.
  • Man of prayer, Spirit-led, and committed to discipleship.
  • Models healthy rhythms of work, rest, and family life.
  • Emotionally healthy and relationally mature.
  • Servant-leader with humility and integrity

Family

  • If married, Senior Pastor’s wife is willing to participate in church life in a volunteer capacity.

Knowledge, Skills & Abilities

  • In-depth knowledge of the Bible and C&MA doctrine.
  • Strong biblical communicator with clarity and relevance.
  • Ability to interact with a variety of individuals in a caring, professional, and tactful manner.
  • Visionary yet collaborative; able to lead through change with grace and wisdom.
  • Demonstrated commitment to the spiritual growth and health of a local church.
  • Ability to handle sensitive and confidential information.
  • Ability to operate within and uphold church by-laws and denominational guidelines.
  • Ability to pass background checks and maintain a valid driver’s license and reliable transportation.

Workload & Compensation

  • Part-time (approximately 20 hours/week) exempt pastoral position with potential to grow into full time.
  • Compensation aligned with education and experience.

Key Responsibilities

1. Preaching & Teaching (35–45%)

  • Prepare and deliver weekly biblically based preaching and teaching that is doctrinally sound and truth-telling.
  • Provide oversight for all ministries to ensure theological alignment with C&MA doctrine.
  • Equip the church through classes, Bible studies, and discipleship pathways.

2. Vision & Strategic Leadership (15–20%)

  • Seek the Lord’s direction for the church and clearly articulate a Spirit-led vision.
  • Collaborate with the Elders to establish ministry priorities and long-term direction.
  • Encourage a “mindshift” toward immediate kingdom work, helping the church transition from talking to doing.
  • Ensure ministry alignment with the mission and values of the C&MA (Our Faith and Mission).
  • Lead the church with a multi-generational focus, fostering ministry that engages children, youth, adults, and seniors together in discipleship, worship, and mission.

3. Shepherding & Pastoral Care (15–20%)

  • Provide pastoral care through prayer, visitation, counseling, and crisis support.
  • Lead or oversee weddings, funerals, dedications, baptisms, and other pastoral functions.
  • Equip and mobilize leaders and volunteers to participate in pastoral care.
  • Demonstrate relational warmth, empathy, and approachability.
  • Serve in a way that strengthens unity and discipleship.

4. Leadership of Ministry Teams (10–20%)

  • Oversee ministry team leadership; provide clarity, encouragement, accountability, and support.
  • Intentionally develop leaders through coaching, mentoring, and team development.
  • Foster a healthy, unified, collaborative ministry culture.
  • Serve as a leadership developer with ministry leaders reporting to the Senior Pastor.

5. Administration & Governance (10–15%)

  • Chair the Elder Board, setting spiritual and strategic vision.

  • Partner with the Elder Board to ensure strong governance, financial oversite and effective ministry operations.
  • Oversee ministry planning, goal setting, and implementation.
  • Demonstrate progress toward or completion of C&MA licensing requirements, if licensing if needed.
  • Ensure compliance with church by-laws, policies and procedures, modeling integrity and accountability in governance.

6. Community & Global Mission (5–10%)

  • Promote active engagement in local outreach, evangelism, and compassion ministries.
  • Help the church engage in 1–2 focused community outreach ministries on a regular basis.
  • Champion the Great Commission Fund and C&MA global mission efforts.
  • Support and encourage cross-cultural ministry and sending workers.
  • Foster partnerships with other Alliance churches in the area and other local churches.

post_html:
General Summary of the Position 

The Campus Worship & Development Director at Grace Community Church – GE Campus serves in a dual capacity to advance both the worship culture and strategic growth of the Grace Español community.

 

As Worship Director, this leader champions our core value of worship—cultivating both corporate gatherings and personal devotion that reflect a Romans 12:1 lifestyle: offering our whole selves as a living sacrifice in response to the love of God. This includes shepherding teams, fostering Christ-centered environments of praise, and guiding our church family into authentic, Spirit-led worship.

 

As Campus Development Director, this role supports the growth and health of the Grace Español Campus by nurturing people, strengthening ministry teams, and stewarding resources. In close partnership with the Campus Pastor, this leader helps build systems, care for volunteers, oversee membership integration, and prepare the campus for future growth—all while embodying the mission and culture of Grace.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities for WORSHIP: (accountabilities included but not limited to)

  • Work with Grace Español Campus Pastor, GE staff, Senior Worship Pastor, and Grace global worship staff to program, organize, and execute weekly worship services.

  • Lead the music portion of the services and run weekly rehearsals.

  • Work with the Worship Department Coordinator to prepare slides for Sunday morning worship services.

  • Lead, recruit, and develop an all-volunteer worship team for the GE Campus.

  • Work with the Audio/Visual department on sound/lighting/projection/stage design.

  • Collaborate with Grace staff, both GE and global, beyond what is required.

  • Facilitate “extra” worship services as needed. (e.g. Christmas Eve, Good Friday...etc.)

  • Communicate well and be timely and organized with weekly responsibilities.

  • Align with the theological doctrine and core beliefs of Grace Community Church. 

 

Worship Skills and Abilities:

  • Sing in-tune and with appropriate style.

  • Fluent in both Spanish and English.

  • Play guitar or piano with proficiency.

  • Program, read and arrange music.

  • Lead rehearsals of instrumentalists and vocalists.

  • Train musicianship into band members as needed.

  • Be willing to learn new musical styles.

  • Be willing to write original material in a collaborative environment.

 

Essential Duties and Responsibilities for CAMPUS DEVELOPMENT: (accountabilities included but not limited to)

  • Know, love, serve, and pray for the GE Campus community.

  • Work with Campus Pastor to care for and nurture a young church plant, while adhering to Grace's mission and culture.

  • Work with Campus Pastor on design and execution of regular Campus team meetings.

  • Take initiative to identify and address needs as the GE Campus grows.

  • Develop structure and support for the Campus volunteer ministry leaders (small groups, guest services, women’s & men’s ministries, GSM, etc.).

  • Oversee the Discover: Membership class (3x per year) and follow-up tasks to provide members care and integration within the GE family (serving, baptism, community).

  • Steward and maintain the appropriate budgets that this role would oversee (General Admin, Campus Development, General Ministries, etc.).

  • Execute weekly Campus duties that the Campus Pastor assigns.

  • Serve as liaison between GE Campus, Operations Team, and GCS to troubleshoot problems and manage common resources.

  • Work with Campus Pastor on special ministry projects and future-oriented plans.

  • Attend and participate in weekly/monthly staff and campus-specific meetings.

  • Provide administrative support for the Grace Español Campus by coordinating room reservations and ensuring spaces are properly scheduled, prepared, and aligned with ministry needs. 

  • Assist in organizing and tracking campus-related logistics, calendars, and communication to support smooth weekly operations. 

  • Engage in and help coordinate local mission activities, fostering opportunities for the Español Campus to serve the surrounding community. 

  • Support general campus administration by maintaining organization of resources, assisting with event planning, and collaborating with staff to ensure effective stewardship of facilities and ministry efforts.

 

Education, Training, Experience:

  • Must be Bilingual (Spanish-English)

  • College degree

  • 3 years of experience in leading worship

  • Familiar with Planning Center Online, Google Drive…etc.

  • Applicants must be authorized to work in the United States without company sponsorship, as we are unable to sponsor or take over employment visas at this time.

 

Work or Ministry Team Context: 

This position is attached to the Sr. Worship Pastor for Worship and Grace Español Campus Pastor for Campus Development. It is based primarily out of the Tyler Offices of Grace Community Church and expected on-site at the Grace Español Campus on Sunday mornings.

We’re seeking assistance with pastoral roles to include building and expanding a new house church movement. Many people today are longing for something deeper—authentic community, real discipleship, and spaces where their faith can be lived out, not just observed. We believe house churches meet that need, and we’re committed to helping people find and flourish in these environments. This role will support identifying individuals and partner churches who are open to helping pilot and shape this model from the ground up.


You will work directly alongside the T.E.A.M. Church House Church Leader to help establish and grow this network. This includes supporting communication with emerging small group leaders, assisting potential hosts as they step into this role, and helping build relationships with new partners. This is a hands-on opportunity to help lay the foundation for a growing ministry and create spaces where people are seen, discipled, and connected. Administrative tasks will be performed as needed. If you feel called to be part of establishing something that centers people in real relationship with Christ and one another, we’d love to connect with you.

Summary of Primary Purpose 

Harvest desires to prepare pastors and ministry leaders for the work of ministry through the church for the world. The purpose of Harvest Apprenticeship Program is to receive proper ministry exposure and practice while Apprentices concurrently mature in the faith: Knowledge, Character, and Ministry Skill.

 

This program takes the Apprentice through (1) practical ministry responsibilities connected to their Ministry areas of responsibility at Harvest Bible Chapel; (2) Biblical and Theological study to mature in the Faith and to prepare for a lifetime of growth. To support holistic discipleship.

 

Scope of role: 

In keeping with the objective of ministry exposure and practice within the Harvest community, the ministry placement will vary depending on (1) the Apprentice’s capacity and interests, and (2) the Church’s needs. We strive to provide ministry opportunities that align well with one’s experience as well as ministry opportunities that will stretch and strengthen an Apprentice’s ministry capacity and skills.

 

Essential Roles & Responsibilities, included but not limited to:

  • Serve effectively and purposefully within the specific Ministry area(s). The ministry context will vary from Apprentice to Apprentice. It may include a Campus Focus or a Ministry Focus.
  • Maintain consistent academic progress in the accredited classes required and included.
  • Prepare for and participate in the required Cohort classes / seminars on theology and ministry.
  • Meet regularly, not less than monthly, with Leadership Development for ongoing encouragement in academic, ministry and Spiritual progress.

 

Ministry Duties/Expectations:

  • Desire to grow in discipleship, serving, equipping, learning, and leading
  • Personal and growing relationship with Jesus and a humility to testify to it
  • Ability to explain “What Harvest Bible Chapel Believes”
  • Ability to pray with other employees, guests, and attenders of the church
  • Be an active, engaged, and accountable in the congregational life at Harvest Bible Chapel

 

Skills/Knowledge Required: 

  • Basic ability to communicate clearly and concisely (verbal and written)
  • Strong doctrinal agreement with church leadership on primary level beliefs
  • Is known to have a lifestyle that honors and uplifts the name of Christ
  • Teachable self-starter with adequate ministry experience to serve HBC well
  • Intermediate ability to lead and a strong ability to follow direction
  • Intermediate decision-making capability based upon Church doctrine and policy/procedure
  • Strong love for God, His Church, and His world with a passion to grow in knowledge, character, and skill

 

Education and Experience: 

  • High school graduate or completed GED.
  • Ability to enroll in a Post-secondary education / Bachelor’s level program.
  • Volunteer experience in a ministry context is preferred.

 

Salary Information

$17.50 per hour.  Approx. 20 -22 hrs/week

Area Ministry Director -- Georgia (Undergraduate Ministry)

Work Location:

Remote - USA

Job Type:

Full time

An Area Director leads and oversees a ministry team to plant and to grow witnessing communities of students and faculty who follow Jesus on college and university campuses. Through these groups, we believe ever-increasing numbers of students and faculty from all ethnic groups and areas of the campus will be transformed by the gospel. We expect to see campuses increasingly become places where people, ideas, and structures flourish for the common good and to the glory of God. We confidently anticipate that our InterVarsity alumni will be growing disciples and change agents across the country and around the world.

What we are looking for:

We are looking for a highly motivated self-starter who loves Jesus and is equipped to navigate the nuances of college campus life with God’s compassion, grace, and truth. The ideal candidate knows how to balance individual effort with delegation and dependence, rest with hard work, and professional development with ministry care. While being based in Atlanta is preferred — we have a strong contingent of staff and alumni in the area and would love a leader who can grow that network and our presence throughout Georgia — it is not a requirement.

ESSENTIAL COMMITMENTS/RESPONSIBILITIES

1. Spiritual Growth

The Area Ministry Director models spiritual maturity as a disciple of Jesus Christ so that your life and work increasingly reflects a growing love for God, God’s Word, God’s people of every ethnicity and culture, and God’s purposes in the world.

  • Pursue a vibrant relationship with the triune God through engagement with Scripture, prayer, and worship, both individually and in community
  • Exercise self-leadership (growing in self-awareness, self-management, relational integrity, and resiliency)
  • Embrace and practice Scriptural standards for behavior and attitudes, including those described in the Code of Conduct

​

2. Campus Ministry Leadership

As an Area Director, you inspire, coach and develop campus staff ministers (“ministers”), students, faculty, and ministry partners to increase the number of witnessing communities, as well as the size, health, spiritual maturity, and campus-wide influence of existing witnessing communities by being a:

Visionary Guide:

  • Create a culture of dependence on God to gain vision for establishing and advancing witnessing communities that reach every corner of every campus in your area
  • Model InterVarsity’s vision and Core Values for supervisees
  • Lead staff, students, and faculty through Scripture, prayer, teaching and discipleship experiences in a way that motivates and shapes their ministry around vision
  • Set appropriate annual goals through prayer, research and reflection with your teams

Structural Architect:

  • Lead your team to develop and implement plans to achieve ministry goals
  • Adapt the plan as needed through rhythms of action, reflection and evaluation
  • Develop, align and leverage programs and structures to move the mission forward

Missional Developer:

  • Recruit a diversity of qualified minister candidates
  • Develop ministers to spiritually grow in Christ in intimacy, like Christ in character, and with Christ in his mission to current and new campuses
  • Develop ministers professionally so that they are consistently increasing their gifts and skills as ministry leaders
  • Supervise ministers, using appropriate leadership style for the individual and situation, to help them accomplish assigned tasks. This will require coaching, assessing, correcting and affirming job-related behaviors
  • Proactively establish and develop healthy relationships across racial, ethnic, national background, and gender barriers with staff, students, faculty, and ministry partners to build effective and diverse communities
  • Build an effective minister team that collaborates well and accomplishes goals

3. Organizational Collaboration

As an Area Director, you are part of a national organization and work in partnership with local, area, divisional, regional, and national InterVarsity ministers and volunteers.

  • Participate in regional leadership as determined by the Regional Director, to set ministry vision and strategies, contribute to accomplishing plans, and provide regional leadership in specific areas
  • Positively and constructively respond to the direction and coaching of line supervisors
  • Build productive ministry partnerships with regional and national collaborative leaders
  • Establish systems, processes and protocols to fulfill regular operational and administrative tasks in a timely manner (reporting, finances, human resources, etc.)
  • Maintain sound financial status of the area through management of budgeting, expense control and ministry partnership development
  • Become familiar with and comply with all InterVarsity policies and procedures

4. Ministry Partnership Development (MPD)

As an Area Director, you will develop a team of partners who will resource the ministry financially, in prayer, or with volunteer service that advances the mission.

  • Develop and maintain a ministry among partners who will fund InterVarsity
  • Ensure ministry budget is fully funded
  • Supervise each minister’s MPD (collaborating with coaches when applicable) and equip staff to build ministry partners
  • Build resource networks with alumni, volunteers, churches, advocacy councils, and major donors, in particular to fund low-network ministers
  • Communicate regularly with ministry partners

5. Georgia Specific Commitments/Responsibilities
 

As the Area Director of Georgia, you will be responsible for growing the student and staff work throughout Georgia. This will include, but not be limited to:
 

  • Pastorally and professionally care for the current team of field staff and volunteer staff
  • Manage and nurture existing partnerships and establish new ones to support the ministry
  • Develop a staff recruitment strategy to grow the team
  • Provide staff with vision and direction for growth
  • Participate in a diverse Regional Leadership Team that sets vision and strategy for the whole region
  • Develop a strategy for reaching unreached campuses in partnership with national initiatives and partners
  • Strengthen partnerships with Historically Black Colleges and Universities (HBCUs), Hispanic-Serving Institutions (HSIs), and Asian American communities
  • Continue building a communal funding model that supports the financial health of all staff

6. Accomplish all other assigned tasks as appropriate

QUALIFICATIONS

  • Annually affirm InterVarsity’s Statement of Agreement (Doctrinal Basis and Purpose Statement). Abide by InterVarsity’s Code of Conduct
  • Bachelor’s degree required
  • Minimum three years campus ministry or equivalent work experience required
  • Strong ministry skills (including the ability to communicate spiritual vision, teach spiritual and biblical principles, plan ministry programs, and spiritually disciple, coach and mentor)
  • Proven ability to work well with others and the ability to develop a team of campus ministers.
  • Strong interpersonal skills (including ability to minister to diverse ethnic communities and faculty)
  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills
  • Demonstrated problem solving skills
  • Familiarity with word processing, presentation, email, and spreadsheet software

WORK ENVIRONMENT/PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS

The AD position leads ministry in a college campus environment. A designated office space may or may not be available. The AD is required to travel to on-campus and off-campus sites as appropriate. Off-campus travel includes, but is not limited to student ministry conferences, MPD meetings, and InterVarsity-sponsored training sessions, meetings, and conferences. The AD is regularly required to communicate with others, and routinely uses standard office equipment such as computers, phones, etc.

Pay Range: $56,844.00 - $75,792.00 per year

Pay: This position is funded through personal fundraising. Accordingly, compensation will vary based on the ability of the individual to secure a donor team to fund the cost of his/her salary. The anticipated salary range for this position on a full-time basis (40 hours/week) is dependent on a variety of factors, including location and cost of living. The actual salary received, including any geographic adjustment to account for location and cost of living, is subject to the individual’s ability to raise funds necessary to cover the full amount of such salary within the range set forth in the job posting details.

Benefits:

We offer a competitive benefits package, including health care and retirement savings with a match. Eligibility is based on employee type and hours worked.  Benefits include the following:

  • 403(b) Retirement Savings Plan

  • 403(b) matching contributions

  • Dental insurance

  • Employee assistance program

  • Employee discounts

  • Flexible work schedule

  • Flexible spending accounts

  • Health insurance

  • Health savings account

  • Life insurance

  • Paid time off

  • Parental leave

  • Professional development assistance

  • Vision insurance

Equal Employment Opportunity: 

 

InterVarsity Christian Fellowship/USA is both an equal opportunity employer and a faith-based religious organization. We conduct hiring without regard to race, color, ancestry, national origin, citizenship, age, sex, marital status, parental status, membership in any labor organization, political ideology, or disability of an otherwise qualified individual. The status of InterVarsity Christian Fellowship/USA as an equal opportunity employer does not prevent the organization from hiring staff based on their religious beliefs so that all staff share the same religious commitment.  Pursuant to the Civil Rights Act of 1964, Section 702 (42 U.S.C. 2000e 1(a)) InterVarsity Christian Fellowship/USA has the right to, and does, hire only candidates who agree with InterVarsity’s Statement of Agreement: Purpose and Doctrinal Basis because InterVarsity believes that each and every staff plays a vital role in advancing InterVarsity’s mission and purposes.

Associate Pastor

Church Profile

Lakeview Community Church, part of the Christian & Missionary Alliance, has faithfully served the Putnam County, NY area for the past 23 years under the leadership of our founding pastor. Located about an hour north of NYC, we are a welcoming, multi-cultural/ generational church that over 250 people call home, many of whom are young families.

The mission of LCC is to make the invisible Christ visible… in Putnam County and around the world.

We strive to do that by helping people make relational connections…

  • to God,

  • to an authentic church community,

  • and to the world around us, making Jesus’ presence visible through words and actions, both locally and globally.

Position Description

The Associate Pastor will use his unique giftings, experiences, and passions, in partnership with our Lead Pastor, to equip and empower our church body to make a multiplied Kingdom impact. This role offers potential opportunity for growth in responsibility and leadership.

Qualifications

  • Clear call to ministry & passion for the greater Putnam region

  • Education: Masters of Divinity (or comparable degree/ in process)

  • Experience: At least three years of pastoral ministry experience.

  • Licensing/ Ordination: With the C&MA (or sustaining accreditation)

Primary Responsibilities

Pastoral Ministry

  • Preach at a regular interval as a part of the preaching team.
  • Collaborate with Lead Pastor to provide compassionate pastoral care to individuals as needed.

Life Groups/ Disciple Making

  • Lead Life Group ministry.
  • Lead local community outreach strategy.
  • Collaborate with ministries to create appropriate discipleship pathways for different stages of spiritual maturity.
  • Track discipleship effectiveness and implement improvements with staff team.

Leadership & Ministry Development

  • Resource ministry leaders, providing practical tools, guidance and encouragement
  • Identify and develop leaders.

Skills and Strengths

Character & Integrity

Your life models a mature love for God, demonstrating integrity, humility, empathy, and authenticity, aligned with the qualities described in 1 Timothy 3 and Titus 1.

Biblical Conviction

You are committed to communicating scripture in a clear, engaging, exegetically sound manner. You align with the doctrinal convictions of LCC and the C&MA.

Team-Building & Leadership Development

You are skilled at identifying, developing and encouraging new leaders. You naturally invest in others, building effective teams and creating environments where people can thrive in life and ministry.

Relational Focus & Communication

You comfortably model clear communication and healthy conflict resolution along with an approachable, compassionate demeanor in pastoral care settings.

Adaptability & Flexibility

You have a willingness to adapt to new opportunities and ministry needs, being flexible and responsive to effectively serve and lead in a changing environment.

Compensation

Total compensation package: $85,000 - $100,000 including benefits and housing
allowance

How to Apply

Interested candidates are invited to submit a resume and cover letter highlighting
pastoral experience, personal ministry philosophy, and alignment with LCC’s vision to
search team at dmcinty@gmail.com

To be considered for this position, please complete the application to include your testimony, resume and other background information related to the position.

If the district office has reviewed your application and they think you may be a potential match for the position, that the hiring manager will reach out to you for next steps.

This position requires licensing with The Christian & Missionary Alliance. To learn more about The Alliance and requirements for licensing, please visit our website

job_name: Next Gen Ministry Coordinator – Pickerington Campus
post_html:
The Next Gen Ministry Coordinator at our Pickerington Campus is a part-time (32 hours/week) ministry leadership role that plays a key role in helping students discover and follow Jesus during some of the most formative years of their lives. This person will provide leadership, discipleship, and support for students in grades 6–12 at our Pickerington Campus, creating environments where students can grow in faith, build meaningful relationships, and experience authentic community. 

Working closely with the Lead Pastor for our Pickerington Campus and the broader VC Students Team, the Next Ministry Coordinator will lead weekly student programming, support discipleship initiatives, develop and care for volunteer leaders, and help connect students to larger church-wide events and experiences. This role blends relational ministry with practical leadership, requiring someone who loves students, enjoys building teams, and can bring both creativity and organization to ministry environments. 

This is an exciting opportunity to invest in the next generation by helping students take meaningful steps in their faith while building a safe, engaging, and spiritually formative ministry culture for students and families. 

About us:

Vineyard Columbus exists to develop multiethnic communities of disciples who experience God, love one another, and partner with Christ to heal the world. 

Our Pickerington Campus is located in a rapidly growing suburban community serving people from Pickerington, Reynoldsburg, Canal Winchester, Lithopolis, Baltimore, and surrounding areas. The congregation reflects the diversity of its community and values worship, discipleship, service, and life together across generations. 

Beyond weekend services at multiple locations across Central Ohio, we serve our neighbors through ministries that address practical needs while creating opportunities to share the love of Jesus in tangible ways. We are committed to cultivating Christlike unity, celebrating diversity, and helping people flourish as they pursue God's calling in their lives. 

Who we're looking for:

We are seeking a spiritually mature, team-oriented leader who is passionate about helping students encounter Jesus and develop a lasting faith. The ideal candidate enjoys building relationships with students, equipping volunteers, and creating environments where young people feel known, valued, challenged, and connected. 

This person is equally comfortable building relationships and managing details. They are energized by leading teams, coordinating ministry details, and helping create engaging experiences that encourage discipleship, outreach, and spiritual growth. They thrive in collaborative settings, communicate clearly, and bring a positive, flexible attitude to the changing rhythms of student ministry. 

The ideal candidate is also a developer of leaders who enjoys recruiting, training, and empowering volunteers to make a meaningful impact in the lives of students. They understand that healthy ministry is built through healthy teams and are passionate about helping others discover and use their gifts. 

Most importantly, this individual demonstrates a genuine love for students, a commitment to personal spiritual growth, and a desire to help the next generation become lifelong disciples of Jesus. 

Desired qualifications:

  • Passion for helping middle and high school students grow in their relationship with Jesus. 
  • Demonstrated experience in student ministry, church leadership, or related youth programming. 
  • Ability to recruit, train, support, and empower volunteer leaders. 
  • Strong organizational and administrative skills, with the ability to manage multiple projects and priorities. 
  • Effective verbal and written communication skills. 
  • Ability to build meaningful relationships with students, families, volunteers, and church leaders. 
  • Experience working in diverse and multicultural environments. 
  • Comfortable learning and utilizing Planning Center or similar ministry management tools. 
  • Demonstrated spiritual maturity and a lifestyle that reflects biblical values. 
  • Strong collaboration skills, dependability, and a commitment to teamwork. 
  • Satisfactory background check required for all positions. 

We offer:

Vineyard Columbus values hard work, sustainable rhythms, and the pursuit of healthy and well-balanced lives. Our staff are supported in their ministry by a great team environment and generous benefits. Benefits for this role include: 

  • Low-cost medical, dental, vision and insurance available, including an HSA plan with employer contributions. 
  • Paid time off for personal, sick, and parental leave. 
  • Equivalent of 13 days off per calendar year for holidays and staff refresh days. 
  • Access to a robust Employee Assistance Program. 
  • Gym membership or equivalent subsidy. 
  • Tuition reimbursement and professional development benefits. 
  • Employer-paid life insurance, and short-term and long-term disability coverage. 
  • 403(b) Retirement Plan with immediate eligibility for employer match.
