Full-time
Description

   

Job Title: Director of Religious Education and Youth and Young Adult Ministries (For Holy Spirit Parish)

  • Primary duty: Pray, lead, love, and teach.
  • Status: Full-Time (Exempt, 40 hours/week)
  • Schedule: Flexible hours, including evenings and weekends.
  • Reports to: Pastor

Position Summary

The Director brings love, compassion, and faith in God to the young people of the parish, providing vision and leadership for all catechetical, youth, and young adult evangelization efforts at Holy Spirit Parish in Creston, Iowa. This unified role manages Religious Education (Pre-K–10th Grade as applicable), Sacramental Preparation, and comprehensive ministries for pre-K to middle school, high school, and young adults. Following the USCCB framework, Renewing the Vision, and the Des Moines Diocese guidelines, the Director recruits volunteers, builds the faith community, and inspires families to actively participate in the sacramental life of the Church and in their children’s faith development.

Qualifications

  • Faith: Practicing Catholic in good standing, or actively enrolled in OCIA with entry into the Church within one year of hire.
  • Experience & Education: Background in theology, education, or youth ministry preferred. Proven experience planning programs and leading groups or classes.

Essential Duties & Responsibilities

1. Religious Education & Sacramental Prep

  • Directs the Wednesday evening Religious Education (RE) for Holy Spirit Parish (Grades 1–10) from September to May.
  • Coordinates sacramental preparation, parent/sponsor meetings, logistics, and dates for First Reconciliation, First Holy Communion, and Confirmation.
  • Selects curriculum resources in consultation with the Pastor and the school principal; teaches RE lessons as needed.
  • Lead the transition of the parish’s religious education to align with the new diocesan Confirmation plan.

2. Youth & Young Adult Evangelization

  • Plans and executes comprehensive ministry programs, social events, and outreach for children (Pre-K–5th Grade), youth (Grades 6–12), and young professionals.
  • Forms & Runs the Youth Leadership Team.
  • Integrates youth into parish life through liturgy, devotions, hospitality, service projects, and altar server training and scheduling.
  • Organizes youth retreats and Confirmation service opportunities in collaboration with parish staff.

3. Leadership & Safe Environment

  • Recruits, trains, mentors, and evaluates volunteer catechists and adult youth mentors.
  • Manages safe environment compliance by ensuring all volunteers complete background screenings and VIRTUS training on time.

4. Administration & Communication

  • Manages the RE and Youth Ministry budgets, submits receipts, and tracks registration fees.
  • Maintains accurate database records (family rosters, attendance, sacramental registries) using ParishSOFT and any approved database.
  • Communicates program updates via email, text, phone, website, and social media.
  • Attends staff meetings and presents half-yearly updates to the Pastoral Council.
  • Complies with all Diocese of Des Moines policies and participates in diocesan leadership training and workshops.

Skills & Requirements

  • Strong interpersonal, communication, and conflict-resolution skills, leading with gentleness and perseverance.
  • Proficient with Microsoft Office, Google Workspace, Website, Facebook, and ParishSOFT.
  • Physical ability to operate standard office equipment, lift up to 45 pounds, and travel for retreats, conferences, or diocesan events.
  • Ongoing Spiritual & Professional Development: Actively pursue personal, spiritual, and professional growth through regular prayer, Scripture study, theological reading, workshops, and holistic self-care.

Benefits

  • Optional health, dental, and vision insurance.
  • Parish-provided long-term disability and $25,000 group term life insurance.
  • 403(b) retirement program with a parish match of 50% up to 8% of employee contribution.
Requirements

Practicing Catholic in good standing with the Church or enrolled in OCIA and preparing to become Catholic within one year of acceptance of the position


Prior experience planning and developing programs for large and small groups of people desired.

Background in education and training preferred.

Previous experience as religious education instructor is helpful.

Physical ability to operate standard office equipment, lift up to 45 lbs, and travel for retreats, conferences, diocesan events.

Has a valid driver's license.

Campus Staff Minister-Purdue University/West Lafayette (Greek Ministry)

Work Location:

Indiana

Job Type:

Full time

God has called InterVarsity to plant and to build witnessing communities of students and faculty who follow Jesus on college and university campuses. Through these groups, we believe ever- increasing numbers of students and faculty from all ethnic groups and areas of the campus will be transformed by the Gospel. We expect to see campuses increasingly become places where people, ideas, and structures flourish to the glory of God. We confidently anticipate that our InterVarsity alumni will become change agents across the country and around the world. We pursue this calling by discerning and actively participating in what God is already doing on campus. This is the essence of being a Campus Staff Minister (CSM).

ESSENTIAL COMMITMENTS/RESPONSIBILITIES 

Spiritual Growth 

You pursue maturity as a disciple of Jesus Christ so that your life and work increasingly reflects a growing love for God, God’s Word, God’s people of every ethnicity and culture, and God’s purposes in the world. To do this, you will: 

  • Pursue a vibrant relationship with the triune God through engagement with Scripture, prayer, and worship, both individually and in community 

  • Develop self-leadership (growing in self-awareness, self-management, relational integrity, and resiliency) 

  • Embrace Scriptural standards for behavior and attitudes 

 

Campus Leadership 

You communicate and model InterVarsity’s vision to see students and faculty transformed, campuses renewed and world changers developed 

  • Create a culture of humble dependence on God and bold expectation in God’s intention to start new witnessing communities throughout the campus and on new campuses 

  • Model – in person and through programs – InterVarsity’s vision and Core Values, including a biblically-defined commitment to engage every ethnic and social group on campus 

  • Lead students and faculty – individually and collectively – through Scripture, prayer, teaching, and discipleship experiences, so that they articulate and align their ministry activities around this vision 

  • Set annual goals through prayer, research and reflection with your teams (students, faculty, and staff) for qualitative and quantitative growth, including conversions and leadership development 

 

You create, develop, align and leverage ministry plans, programs, teams, and structures to close the gap between current reality and the aspirational goals. 

  • Build leadership teams who trust and partner well with you and who demonstrate spiritual vitality, relational health, and mission alignment 

  • Develop and execute plans to achieve annual goals, evaluating and modifying the plan as needed throughout the year 

  • Increase momentum for the vision by aligning programs, structures, conferences and teams around the goals 

  • Mobilize students and faculty to engage their relational networks with the gospel and to start new missional communities 

  • Under the direction of the Area Director, may supervise Ministry Interns and Campus Ministry Interns as delegated 

 

You intentionally gather, invite, and develop diverse groups of students and faculty so that they not only encounter and follow Jesus as Savior and Lord but also advance the mission on campus as participants and leaders. 

  • Create ways for faculty and students to encounter and follow Jesus through Scripture, worship, prayer, mission experiences, conferences, etc. 

  • Equip students and faculty so that they think strategically about campus engagement and so that they proclaim – in word, deed, and power – the good news of Jesus, regularly inviting students and faculty to follow him as Savior and Lord 

  • Disciple students and faculty by equipping them to hear the Word, respond actively, and debrief and interpret the experience so that they grow in Christlikeness, reflect our Core Values, and develop ministry skills 

  • Invite, coach, and equip students and faculty to become increasingly effective participants and leaders, including starting new witnessing communities on campuses 

 

Organizational Collaboration 

You work with a network of other local, area, regional, and national InterVarsity staff and volunteers so that our work reflects Biblical standards of excellence, integrity, and partnership. 

  • Partner with and respond positively to the direction and coaching of your supervisors and national leaders 

  • Contribute to collaborative and productive team meetings and relationships 

  • Affiliate chapters under your care and submit Graduating Student Forms in order to increase our partnership with current students and alumni 

  • Use national ministry resources and tools, as requested, including recruiting and/or participating in local, regional, or national conferences as  

  • Complete reporting, planning and review requirements in a timely way so that you and your supervisors can assess and improve your work as a CSM 

  • Comply with all InterVarsity policies and procedures 

 

Ministry Partnership Development 

You will develop a team of partners – churches and individuals (including alumni and community members) – who will resource the ministry financially, in prayer, or volunteer service that advances the mission. 

  • Raise 100% of the financial budget assigned by your supervisor 

  • Communicate regularly with your ministry partners, nurturing the relationship through visits, phone calls, emails and regular prayer letters 

  • Develop on-going, long-lasting partnership with alumni and volunteers 

  • Comply with all Ministry Partnership Policies 

  • Identify and invest in advocates who will build networks of volunteers and donors on InterVarsity’s behalf 

 

Accomplish all other assigned tasks as appropriate 

 

QUALIFICATIONS (common to all levels of CSM) 

  • Annually affirm InterVarsity’s Statement of Agreement (Doctrinal Basis and Purpose Statement). Abide by InterVarsity’s Code of Conduct. Believe and behave consonantly with InterVarsity’s Human Sexuality Theological Paper. Affirm and behave consonantly with InterVarsity’s “Women in Ministry Statement of Affirmation” 

  • Bachelor’s degree for CSMs assigned to a four-year campus. A minimum of an Associate’s degree for CSMs assigned to a two-year campus or a community college 

  • Strong interpersonal skills (including ability to minister to diverse ethnic communities and faculty) 

  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills 

  • Demonstrated problem solving skills 

  • Familiarity with word processing, presentation, email, and spreadsheet software 

 

WORK ENVIRONMENT/PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS 

The CSM position leads ministry in a college campus environment. A designated office space may or may not be available. The CSM is required to travel to on-campus and off- campus sites as appropriate. Off-campus travel includes, but is not limited to: student ministry conferences, Ministry Partnership Development meetings, and InterVarsity- sponsored training sessions, meetings, and conferences. The CSM is regularly required to communicate with others, and routinely uses standard office equipment such as computers, phones, photocopiers, filing cabinets, etc. 

Pay Range: $40,476.00 - $53,952.00 per year

Pay: This position is funded through personal fundraising. Accordingly, compensation will vary based on the ability of the individual to secure a donor team to fund the cost of his/her salary. The anticipated salary range for this position on a full-time basis (40 hours/week) is dependent on a variety of factors, including location and cost of living. The actual salary received, including any geographic adjustment to account for location and cost of living, is subject to the individual’s ability to raise funds necessary to cover the full amount of such salary within the range set forth in the job posting details.

Benefits:

We offer a competitive benefits package, including health care and retirement savings with a match. Eligibility is based on employee type and hours worked.  Benefits include the following:

  • 403(b) Retirement Savings Plan

  • 403(b) matching contributions

  • Dental insurance

  • Employee assistance program

  • Employee discounts

  • Flexible work schedule

  • Flexible spending accounts

  • Health insurance

  • Health savings account

  • Life insurance

  • Paid time off

  • Parental leave

  • Professional development assistance

  • Vision insurance

Equal Employment Opportunity: 

 

InterVarsity Christian Fellowship/USA is both an equal opportunity employer and a faith-based religious organization. We conduct hiring without regard to race, color, ancestry, national origin, citizenship, age, sex, marital status, parental status, membership in any labor organization, political ideology, or disability of an otherwise qualified individual. The status of InterVarsity Christian Fellowship/USA as an equal opportunity employer does not prevent the organization from hiring staff based on their religious beliefs so that all staff share the same religious commitment.  Pursuant to the Civil Rights Act of 1964, Section 702 (42 U.S.C. 2000e 1(a)) InterVarsity Christian Fellowship/USA has the right to, and does, hire only candidates who agree with InterVarsity’s Statement of Agreement: Purpose and Doctrinal Basis because InterVarsity believes that each and every staff plays a vital role in advancing InterVarsity’s mission and purposes.

About the Worship Pastor: 

The Worship Pastor is responsible for leading and developing the worship ministry at Bayou City Fellowship’s Tomball Campus. This role provides pastoral, musical, and organizational leadership to create worship environments that are Christ-centered, biblically grounded, culturally relevant, and meaningful.

The Worship Pastor will recruit, develop, disciple, and lead worship staff and volunteers while overseeing the planning and execution of weekly worship services and other campus events. This role partners closely with the Lead Campus Pastor and campus staff to support the mission and vision of Bayou City Fellowship.

The Worship Pastor is expected to model a growing relationship with Jesus, a life of prayer and integrity, biblical faithfulness, humility, and dependence on the Holy Spirit.

Ministry Philosophy

The Worship Pastor is committed to helping Bayou City Fellowship become a people who treasure Jesus above all else. Worship ministry should point people to the gospel, faithfully communicate the truth of Scripture, cultivate prayer and discipleship, and create space for people to respond to God in authentic worship.

The Worship Pastor should lead from a posture of dependence on the Holy Spirit, recognizing that worship ministry is ultimately about making much of Jesus—not building a platform, pursuing trends, or elevating talent.

Guiding Scripture: 2 Timothy 1–4

Key Responsibilities

Worship Leadership

  • Plan and lead weekly worship services, including song selection, service flow, musical arrangements, and worship elements.

  • Lead and oversee weekly rehearsals for worship teams and musicians.

  • Ensure worship is biblically faithful, gospel-centered, and aligned with the vision and culture of Bayou City Fellowship.

  • Lead worship for campus-wide and other ministry events as needed.

  • Partner with the Lead Campus Pastor to develop and implement the campus worship vision.

Team Development & Discipleship

  • Recruit, audition, equip, disciple, and develop worship volunteers and leaders.

  • Identify and develop emerging worship leaders, musicians, and vocalists.

  • Provide pastoral care, encouragement, accountability, and spiritual development for worship staff and volunteers.

  • Establish a healthy culture marked by humility, excellence, teamwork, prayer, and spiritual growth.

  • Help develop a sustainable worship development pathway for the Tomball Campus.

  • Encourage worship team members to actively participate in the broader discipleship life of Bayou City Fellowship.

Production & Operations

  • Provide oversight and direction for the Audio/Visual and production teams supporting worship services.

  • Ensure effective coordination between worship, production, communications, and other ministry teams.

  • Maintain appropriate systems, schedules, resources, and processes for weekly worship ministry.

  • Manage the worship ministry budget and related expenses.

  • Utilize Planning Center, ProPresenter, and other ministry technologies effectively.

Campus & Church-Wide Collaboration

  • Participate in weekly staff meetings, leadership meetings, and church-wide initiatives.

  • Collaborate with other ministry leaders to support worship needs for Kids, Students, Women’s Ministry, Community Groups, and other events.

  • Contribute to the overall life and ministry of the Cypress Campus beyond the worship ministry.

  • Participate in staff development and performance management processes.

  • Perform other duties as assigned by the Lead Campus Pastor.

Personal & Spiritual Qualifications

The ideal candidate will:

  • Demonstrate a clear profession of faith in Jesus Christ and a growing personal relationship with Him.

  • Model spiritual maturity, integrity, humility, and moral character.

  • Demonstrate a commitment to prayer, Scripture, discipleship, and the local church.

  • Be committed to the mission, vision, values, and worship philosophy of Bayou City Fellowship.

  • Lead with a shepherd’s heart and a genuine desire to serve and develop others.

  • Be teachable, collaborative, relational, and emotionally healthy.

  • Demonstrate initiative, strong organizational skills, and attention to detail.

  • Balance musical excellence with authentic, Spirit-dependent worship.

  • Desire to see musicians, artists, and volunteers grow both spiritually and musically.

Education & Experience

  • Demonstrated musical and vocal proficiency with experience leading congregational worship.

  • Strong understanding of biblical theology and the ability to evaluate worship songs and service elements through a gospel-centered, biblical lens.

  • Strong communication, leadership, and interpersonal skills.

  • Ability to lead and develop teams of staff and volunteers.

  • Working knowledge of worship technology and production systems, including Planning Center and ProPresenter.

  • Ability to manage multiple priorities, schedules, and ministry details effectively.

  • Bachelor’s degree in Music, Worship Ministry, Theology, or a related field preferred; equivalent ministry experience will be considered.

  • Master’s degree preferred.

  • Minimum of 4 years of worship ministry/leadership experience or equivalent.

As a Campus Staff Minister, you pursue maturity as a disciple of Jesus Christ so that your life and work increasingly reflect a growing love for God, God’s Word, God’s people of every ethnicity and culture, and God’s purposes in the world. To do this, you will: 

  • Pursue a vibrant relationship with the triune God through engagement with Scripture, prayer, and worship, both individually and in community
  • Develop self-leadership (growing in self-awareness, self-management, relational integrity, and resiliency) 
  • Embrace Scriptural standards for behavior and attitudes 

 

Campus Leadership 

As a Campus Staff Minister, you increase the number of witnessing communities, as well as the size, health, spiritual maturity, and campus-wide influence of existing witnessing communities of students and faculty by being a: 

  • Visionary Guide: 

You communicate and model InterVarsity’s vision to see students and faculty transformed, campuses renewed, and world changers developed 

  • Create a culture of humble dependence on God and bold expectation in God’s intention to start new witnessing communities throughout the campus and on new campuses 
  • Model – in person and through programs – InterVarsity’s vision and Core Values, including a biblically-defined commitment to engage every ethnic and social group on campus 
  • Lead students and faculty – individually and collectively – through Scripture, prayer, teaching, and discipleship experiences, so that they articulate and align their ministry activities around this vision 
  • Set annual goals through prayer, research and reflection with your teams (students, faculty, and staff) for qualitative and quantitative growth, including conversions and leadership development 
  • Structural Architect: 

You create, develop, align, and leverage ministry plans, programs, teams, and structures to close the gap between current reality and the aspirational goals. 

  • Build leadership teams who trust and partner well with you and who demonstrate spiritual vitality, relational health, and mission alignment 
  • Develop and execute plans to achieve annual goals, evaluating and modifying the plan as needed throughout the year 
  • Increase momentum for the vision by aligning programs, structures, conferences, and teams around the goals 
  • Mobilize students and faculty to engage their relational networks with the gospel and to start new missional communities 
  • Under the direction of the Area Director, may supervise Ministry Interns and Campus Ministry Interns as delegated 
  • Missional Developer: 

You intentionally gather, invite, and develop diverse groups of students and faculty so that they not only encounter and follow Jesus as Savior and Lord but also advance the mission on campus as participants and leaders. 

  • Create ways for faculty and students to encounter and follow Jesus through Scripture, worship, prayer, mission experiences, conferences, etc. 
  • Equip students and faculty so that they think strategically about campus engagement and so that they proclaim – in word, deed, and power – the good news of Jesus, regularly inviting students and faculty to follow him as Savior and Lord 
  • Disciple students and faculty by equipping them to hear the Word, respond actively, and debrief and interpret the experience so that they grow in Christlikeness, reflect our Core Values, and develop ministry skills 
  • Invite, coach, and equip students and faculty to become increasingly effective participants and leaders, including starting new witnessing communities on campuses 

 

Organizational Collaboration 

As a Campus Staff Minister, you have joined a national mission. Therefore, you work with a network of other local, area, regional, and national InterVarsity staff and volunteers so that our work reflects Biblical standards of excellence, integrity, and partnership. 

  • Partner with and respond positively to the direction and coaching of your supervisors and national leaders 
  • Contribute to collaborative and productive team meetings and relationships 
  • Affiliate chapters under your care and submit Graduating Student Forms in order to increase our partnership with current students and alumni 
  • Use national ministry resources and tools, as requested, including recruiting and/or participating in local, regional, or national conferences as required 
  • Complete reporting, planning and review requirements in a timely way so that you and your supervisors can assess and improve your work as a CSM 
  • Comply with all InterVarsity policies and procedures 

 

Ministry Partnership Development 

As a Campus Staff Minister, you will develop a team of partners – churches and individuals (including alumni and community members) – who will resource the ministry financially, in prayer, or volunteer service that advances the mission. 

  • Raise 100% of the financial budget assigned by your supervisor 
  • Communicate regularly with your ministry partners, nurturing the relationship through visits, phone calls, emails and regular prayer letters 
  • Develop on-going, long-lasting partnership with alumni and volunteers 
  • Comply with all Ministry Partnership Policies 
  • Identify and invest in advocates who will build networks of volunteers and donors on InterVarsity’s behalf 

 

Accomplish all other assigned tasks as appropriate 

 

QUALIFICATIONS (common to all levels of CSM) 

  • Annually affirm InterVarsity’s Statement of Agreement (Doctrinal Basis and Purpose Statement). Abide by InterVarsity’s Code of Conduct. Believe and behave consonantly with InterVarsity’s Human Sexuality Theological Paper. Affirm and behave consonantly with InterVarsity’s “Women in Ministry Statement of Affirmation” 
  • Bachelor’s degree required for CSMs assigned to a four-year campus. A minimum of an Associate’s degree required for CSMs assigned to a two-year campus or a community college 
  • Strong interpersonal skills (including ability to minister to diverse ethnic communities and faculty) 
  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills 
  • Demonstrated problem solving skills 
  • Familiarity with word processing, presentation, email, and spreadsheet software 

 

WORK ENVIRONMENT/PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS 

The CSM position leads ministry in a college campus environment. A designated office space may or may not be available. The CSM is required to travel to on-campus and off- campus sites as appropriate. Off-campus travel includes, but is not limited to: student ministry conferences, Ministry Partnership Development meetings, and InterVarsity- sponsored training sessions, meetings, and conferences. The CSM is regularly required to communicate with others, and routinely uses standard office equipment such as computers, phones, photocopiers, filing cabinets, etc.

Summary of Primary Purpose:

Harvest desires to prepare pastors and ministry leaders for the work of ministry in the church. The purpose of the Ministry Resident is to receive proper ministry preparation and practice with the support of the academy (Grace Seminary) or a similar program through an intentional 2-to-4-year program (depending on one’s degree).  

 

This training takes the Resident through (1) significant ministry responsibilities connected to their Ministry areas of responsibility at Harvest Bible Chapel; (2) rigorous academic study and projects in order to develop and demonstrate the outcomes for Grace Seminary’s Deploy Program or a similar program.

Essential Roles & Responsibilities, included but not limited to:

Ministry Duties/Expectations:

company_description: About Us Welcome to Harvest Christian Fellowship, a vibrant, non-denominational church founded in 1973 by Pastor Greg Laurie in Riverside, California. For over five decades, our mission has been simple yet profound: Knowing God and Making Him Known. We are a community of believers dedicated to fostering a deep relationship with Jesus Christ and sharing His love with the world. Our Story Harvest began humbly as a Bible study led by a young Greg Laurie during the Jesus People movement of the late 1960s. What started in a small gathering has grown into a multi-campus ministry with locations in Riverside, Orange County, and Maui. Today, with a weekly attendance of over 9,000 people, Harvest remains committed to biblical teaching, authentic worship, and meaningful fellowship. In 1990, Pastor Greg launched the Harvest Crusades, a large-scale evangelistic event that has reached millions with the Gospel. What We Believe At Harvest, we believe in the transformative power of the Bible as God’s Word. Our core values center on: Worship: Engaging in heartfelt, Christ-centered worship. Teaching: Providing sound biblical teaching to equip believers for life and faith. Community: Building authentic relationships through small groups, ministries, and outreach. Service: Serving others locally and globally, reflecting Christ’s love in action. Our Community With campuses in Southern California and Hawaii, Harvest is a place where everyone is welcome. Whether you’re exploring faith for the first time or seeking a deeper connection with God, you’ll find a home here. Our services feature dynamic worship, relevant messages, and opportunities to connect through ministries like Harvest Kids, Youth, Young Adults, Men’s (Valor), Women’s (Virtue), and Harvest Groups.

Youth Pastor - The Compass Church

South Naperville Campus | The Compass Church

Naperville, Illinois | Full-Time (40+ hours/week) | Salaried, Exempt | $50,000-$80,000

HELP THE NEXT GENERATION FIND & FOLLOW GOD

The Compass Church is seeking a relational, biblically grounded, and strategic Youth Pastor / Director of Student Ministries to provide vision and leadership for Junior High Ministry (JHM) and High School Ministry (HSM) at our South Naperville Campus.

This is an opportunity to lead a meaningful student ministry without building alone. You will shape local ministry while benefiting from the resources, relationships, support, and collaboration of a multi-site church serving more than 4,000 people each week. The successful candidate will help students grow in their faith, develop leaders, partner with parents, and create environments where young people experience authentic disciple-making relationships.

Depending on the successful candidate's education, ministry experience, and qualifications, the position may carry either the Pastor of Student Ministries or Director of Student Ministries title.

ABOUT THE COMPASS CHURCH

The Compass Church is a multi-site church in the Chicagoland area and a member of the Evangelical Free Church of America (EFCA). Founded in 1952, the church serves more than 4,000 people each week across locations in Bolingbrook, Hinsdale, Naperville, South Naperville, Plainfield, and Wheaton, as well as through CompassOnline and Compass Español.

United by its mission, Helping People Find & Follow God, The Compass Church emphasizes biblical teaching, discipleship, outreach, and healthy, collaborative ministry leadership.

The South Naperville Campus describes itself with one word: family. The campus places a high priority on the next generation and seeks to create a welcoming church environment where people can belong, grow, serve, and live out their faith.

POSITION SUMMARY

The Youth Pastor / Director of Student Ministries will provide vision and direction for the faith development and spiritual growth of students in Grades 6-12. This leader will work alongside a strong team of adult and student leaders to create disciple-making environments focused on three primary groups: students, their parents, and lay leaders.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Lead the overall growth, health, and spiritual direction of Junior High Ministry (Grades 6-8) and High School Ministry (Grades 9-12).
  • Recruit, onboard, train, equip, shepherd, and empower adult and student leaders.
  • Oversee Junior High Ministry gatherings on Sunday mornings and Thursday evenings.
  • Oversee High School Ministry gatherings on Sunday evenings and Wednesday evenings.
  • Develop and implement strategies that help students engage in The Compass Church's four priorities: Pursue Him Daily, Connect in Groups, Serve in Teams, and Reach Your Neighbor.
  • Encourage students to take meaningful spiritual next steps, including baptism and sharing their faith journey.
  • Plan and lead student ministry events, conferences, mission trips, and other short-term ministry initiatives.
  • Partner intentionally with parents as important spiritual influencers in their students' lives.
  • Maintain accurate records of students, participants, and ministry leaders in the church database.
  • Collaborate across locations to share ideas, resources, and best practices and to strengthen church-wide Student Ministries.
  • Oversee and steward the Student Ministries budget responsibly.

COLLABORATION & CHURCH-WIDE LEADERSHIP

  • Maintain strong communication and partnership with the South Naperville Campus Pastor and campus staff.
  • Collaborate with CompassKids to create a smooth transition into Student Ministries for incoming sixth-grade students.
  • Establish and pursue quarterly ministry objectives under the guidance of the South Naperville Campus Pastor.
  • Collaborate with Student Ministries pastors and directors across The Compass Church.
  • Contribute to a healthy, team-oriented staff culture and assist with other ministry responsibilities as needed.

QUALIFICATIONS & REQUIREMENTS

  • Bachelor's degree in ministry, theology, education, or a related field, OR at least five years of relevant ministry experience.
  • Three to five years of leadership experience in a church of 300+ members or a comparable ministry setting.
  • Proven ability to recruit, train, equip, develop, and empower volunteers.
  • Strong relational and team-building skills, with the ability to build trust and work effectively with students, parents, volunteers, staff, and people from diverse church demographics and generations.
  • Excellent public speaking, biblical teaching, and interpersonal communication skills.
  • Ability to organize and successfully manage multiple ministries, events, projects, and priorities.
  • Self-starter who demonstrates initiative, creativity, sound judgment, and effective problem-solving skills.
  • Strong team player with the ability to collaborate effectively across ministries and locations.
  • Full affirmation of The Compass Church Statement of Faith and theological alignment with the Evangelical Free Church of America (EFCA).
  • Must be, or become, a member of The Compass Church within 12 months of employment.

ADDITIONAL POSITION EXPECTATIONS

  • Attend weekly campus and/or ministry staff meetings and monthly All-Staff meetings.
  • Regularly attend The Compass Church weekend worship services.
  • Maintain basic proficiency with Microsoft Office and use technology effectively for ministry planning, communication, and administration.
  • Demonstrate flexibility and a team-first attitude, including a willingness to assist with other ministry responsibilities as needed.

POSITION DETAILS

Position: Youth Pastor / Director of Student Ministries, South Naperville Campus

Reports to: South Naperville Campus Pastor

Schedule: Full-time, 40+ hours per week

Employment status: Salaried, exempt

Classification: Director/Pastor

Salary range: $50,000-$80,000 annually

COMPENSATION & BENEFITS

Salary range: $50,000-$80,000 annually, based on qualifications and experience.

Full-time benefits include medical, dental, and vision insurance (80% paid), a Health Savings Account (HSA), life and disability insurance (100% paid), vacation, paid holidays, a 403(b) retirement plan match, event discounts, and access to an Employee Assistance Program (EAP).

WHY CONSIDER THIS OPPORTUNITY?

This role offers a compelling combination of local ministry ownership and church-wide support. The Youth Pastor / Director of Student Ministries will have the opportunity to develop students and leaders, partner with families, strengthen JHM and HSM, and help shape the future of Student Ministries at the South Naperville Campus while serving as part of a larger multi-site ministry team.

If you love Jesus, love students, develop leaders, communicate Scripture effectively, and want to help the next generation Find & Follow God, The Compass Church would welcome the opportunity to hear from you.

TO APPLY

Please submit a resume and cover letter.

Peninsula Covenant Church is a growing, dynamic, community-focused church in Redwood City, CA.  The beautiful 16-acre campus serves as host to our worship gatherings, children and adult ministries, community center (including swim and fitness activities), preschool, after-school care, and summer programs and supports numerous partner ministries.  Healthy and successful team members are those who Seek Jesus First, are Humble, Stay Hungry, Extend Grace, and Prioritize Team.  We actively support a culture of collaboration, and kindness across our PCC teams.  Join us in our vision, as we exist to know Jesus deeply, follow Him faithfully, and guide the next generation to do the same.   Come experience what the community of PCC is all about!

VISION OF PCC
To empower generations to passionately follow Jesus one person at a time.

PRINCIPLE OBJECTIVE
The Young Adult Ministry Leader will implement a comprehensive program of Christian life development for the 18 – 32 year old, college, career, single and married adults in our community. It is essential that this person be able to connect with young adults on a social and spiritual level, with the intent of coaching them towards Christ-like maturity. Under the supervision of the Family Ministry Director, this person is the staff point person for PCC’s Young Adult Ministry.

RESPONSIBILITIES
  • In partnership with the Spiritual Formation Pastor develop the missional, spiritual and programmatic direction of Young Adult Ministry.  
  • Assist in recruiting, training and equipping a Young Adult Ministry team.  
  • Give leadership to Young Adult Ministry small groups, events, retreats, and/or mission trips. 
  • Incorporate an externally focused missional approach.
  • Engage in regular prayer and reading to keep heart, soul and passion fresh.

MUST-HAVES

NICE-TO-HAVES

Elevation Church exists so that people far from God will be raised to life in Christ. Founded and led by Pastor Steven Furtick in Charlotte, NC, Elevation Church has multiple physical locations throughout the U.S. and Canada, as well as a thriving online community. We are a church fueled by great faith, and we've seen God do things that only He can do - thousands of lives changed, marriages restored, families healed, and spirits renewed.

3. We honor one another to glorify God.

It’s about: Valuing People.

4. We are contributors, not consumers.

It’s about: Taking Action.

5. We think inside the box.

It’s about: Embracing Limitation.

6. We can do more by doing less.

It’s about: Focused Excellence.

It’s about: Ongoing Growth.

It’s about: Teachable Attitudes.

9. We want to be known for what we are for.

It’s about: Promoting Unity.

10. We will not take this for granted.

It’s about: Expressing Gratitude.

Work Location:

Minnesota

Job Type:

Full time

God has called InterVarsity to plant and to build witnessing communities of students and faculty who follow Jesus on college and university campuses. Through these groups, we believe ever- increasing numbers of students and faculty from all ethnic groups and areas of the campus will be transformed by the Gospel. We expect to see campuses increasingly become places where people, ideas, and structures flourish to the glory of God. We confidently anticipate that our InterVarsity alumni will become change agents across the country and around the world. We pursue this calling by discerning and actively participating in what God is already doing on campus. This is the essence of being a Campus Staff Minister (CSM).

ESSENTIAL COMMITMENTS/RESPONSIBILITIES 

Spiritual Growth 

You pursue maturity as a disciple of Jesus Christ so that your life and work increasingly reflects a growing love for God, God’s Word, God’s people of every ethnicity and culture, and God’s purposes in the world. To do this, you will: 

  • Pursue a vibrant relationship with the triune God through engagement with Scripture, prayer, and worship, both individually and in community 

  • Develop self-leadership (growing in self-awareness, self-management, relational integrity, and resiliency) 

  • Embrace Scriptural standards for behavior and attitudes 

 

Campus Leadership 

You communicate and model InterVarsity’s vision to see students and faculty transformed, campuses renewed and world changers developed 

  • Create a culture of humble dependence on God and bold expectation in God’s intention to start new witnessing communities throughout the campus and on new campuses 

  • Model – in person and through programs – InterVarsity’s vision and Core Values, including a biblically-defined commitment to engage every ethnic and social group on campus 

  • Lead students and faculty – individually and collectively – through Scripture, prayer, teaching, and discipleship experiences, so that they articulate and align their ministry activities around this vision 

  • Set annual goals through prayer, research and reflection with your teams (students, faculty, and staff) for qualitative and quantitative growth, including conversions and leadership development 

 

You create, develop, align and leverage ministry plans, programs, teams, and structures to close the gap between current reality and the aspirational goals. 

  • Build leadership teams who trust and partner well with you and who demonstrate spiritual vitality, relational health, and mission alignment 

  • Develop and execute plans to achieve annual goals, evaluating and modifying the plan as needed throughout the year 

  • Increase momentum for the vision by aligning programs, structures, conferences and teams around the goals 

  • Mobilize students and faculty to engage their relational networks with the gospel and to start new missional communities 

  • Under the direction of the Area Director, may supervise Ministry Interns and Campus Ministry Interns as delegated 

 

You intentionally gather, invite, and develop diverse groups of students and faculty so that they not only encounter and follow Jesus as Savior and Lord but also advance the mission on campus as participants and leaders. 

  • Create ways for faculty and students to encounter and follow Jesus through Scripture, worship, prayer, mission experiences, conferences, etc. 

  • Equip students and faculty so that they think strategically about campus engagement and so that they proclaim – in word, deed, and power – the good news of Jesus, regularly inviting students and faculty to follow him as Savior and Lord 

  • Disciple students and faculty by equipping them to hear the Word, respond actively, and debrief and interpret the experience so that they grow in Christlikeness, reflect our Core Values, and develop ministry skills 

  • Invite, coach, and equip students and faculty to become increasingly effective participants and leaders, including starting new witnessing communities on campuses 

 

Organizational Collaboration 

You work with a network of other local, area, regional, and national InterVarsity staff and volunteers so that our work reflects Biblical standards of excellence, integrity, and partnership. 

  • Partner with and respond positively to the direction and coaching of your supervisors and national leaders 

  • Contribute to collaborative and productive team meetings and relationships 

  • Affiliate chapters under your care and submit Graduating Student Forms in order to increase our partnership with current students and alumni 

  • Use national ministry resources and tools, as requested, including recruiting and/or participating in local, regional, or national conferences as  

  • Complete reporting, planning and review requirements in a timely way so that you and your supervisors can assess and improve your work as a CSM 

  • Comply with all InterVarsity policies and procedures 

 

Ministry Partnership Development 

You will develop a team of partners – churches and individuals (including alumni and community members) – who will resource the ministry financially, in prayer, or volunteer service that advances the mission. 

  • Raise 100% of the financial budget assigned by your supervisor 

  • Communicate regularly with your ministry partners, nurturing the relationship through visits, phone calls, emails and regular prayer letters 

  • Develop on-going, long-lasting partnership with alumni and volunteers 

  • Comply with all Ministry Partnership Policies 

  • Identify and invest in advocates who will build networks of volunteers and donors on InterVarsity’s behalf 

 

Accomplish all other assigned tasks as appropriate 

 

QUALIFICATIONS (common to all levels of CSM) 

  • Annually affirm InterVarsity’s Statement of Agreement (Doctrinal Basis and Purpose Statement). Abide by InterVarsity’s Code of Conduct. Believe and behave consonantly with InterVarsity’s Human Sexuality Theological Paper. Affirm and behave consonantly with InterVarsity’s “Women in Ministry Statement of Affirmation”

  • Strong interpersonal skills (including ability to minister to diverse ethnic communities and faculty) 

  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills 

  • Demonstrated problem solving skills 

  • Familiarity with word processing, presentation, email, and spreadsheet software 

 

WORK ENVIRONMENT/PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS 

The CSM position leads ministry in a college campus environment. A designated office space may or may not be available. The CSM is required to travel to on-campus and off- campus sites as appropriate. Off-campus travel includes, but is not limited to: student ministry conferences, Ministry Partnership Development meetings, and InterVarsity- sponsored training sessions, meetings, and conferences. The CSM is regularly required to communicate with others, and routinely uses standard office equipment such as computers, phones, photocopiers, filing cabinets, etc.

Description:
There are nearly 300,000 teenagers of active-duty U.S. military parents who are stationed all over the world. These teens move an average of seven times during their school-aged years. The questions of identity and belonging that all teens face grow even more challenging to answer amid starting over and meeting new friends at each location.
This is where you can be the difference in a military teen’s life! By being in their world, walking alongside them, and creating a community where they experience the truth of God’s love and purpose for them, our staff provide a safe space where teens can develop friendships and connections to experience laughter, build hope, and generate resiliency.
We are currently providing incarnational ministry at many military installations around the world. You will have the opportunity to lead and oversee the overall Young Life Military program, known as Club Beyond, which is ecumenically focused and outreach oriented.
Responsibilities:
  • Actively develop healthy relationships with adults, as well as kids, and build vibrant relationships with the local community, the military installation, and the chapel community.
  • Be a role model (incarnational) and assist with developing community outreach to "unchurched" teens, discipleship to Christian teens, and leading and equipping volunteers to do "hands-on" middle and high school Christian youth programs.
  • Work well in an environment that sees (due to high military operational tempo) a high degree of turnover among teens, families, chaplains and volunteers.
  • Be respectful of and embrace a community that is deeply influenced by a military culture.
  • In this ministry, you will need to live out the Club Beyond Core Value Statement:
Club Beyond is a Christ-centered community of leaders with an exclusively military focus. Our methods are incarnational, and our perspective is ecumenical. We leverage strategic partnerships for the greatest results. We value professionalism from our staff and excellence in our stewardship.
Qualifications:

  • Note, this position would require our Staff to live near the community where they would be doing ministry.

Summary

This position is part of Department of War. The incumbent will be responsible for serving as the principal Subject Matter Expert (SME) to the Minister/Chief of Defense (MoD/CHOD) and the Commander, Military and Security Authority (MISA) on all aspects of national-level Security operations. Oversees and approves contractor military security SMEs work concerning development of security infrastructure and Mil. security officer training within the MISA, partners Armed Forces, and Mil. installations.


Duties

This position is located in the Defense Security Cooperation Agency (DSCA), Defense Security Cooperation Service (DSCS).
As a Ministry of Defense Advisor you will be responsible for the following duties:

  • Ability to select and apply appropriate evaluation and measurement techniques to determine partner nation's progress, measure Institutional Capacity Building (ICB) accomplishments, and align outcomes with Combatant Command (CCMD) theater campaign goals and DoW policy direction.
  • Mastery Knowledge of interpersonal relations, diplomatic tact, and political-military acumen required to establish credibility and exert peer-to-peer influence within complex, multi-national environments.
  • Possess expert knowledge of ICB core processes (strategy and policy, force management, human resources management, acquisition and logistics, resource management, and defense governance) and the focus areas supporting security cooperation.
  • The ability to work independently, with a high degree of initiative and resourcefulness, to develop solutions to complex and sensitive problems that are not subject to treatment by commonly used methods.
  • The incumbent is recognized as an expert in developing and interpreting guidance on Security program planning and evaluation.
  • The incumbent must be highly original and use sound judgment to formulate, evaluate, and ensure implementation of programs and policies pertaining to Ministry of Defense Advisor (MoDA)/ICB issues.


Requirements

Conditions of employment

  • Must be a US citizen
  • Selective Service Requirement: Males born after 12-31-59 must be registered for Selective Service, For more information please visit https://www.sss.gov
  • Resume and supporting documents (See: How to Apply)
  • Suitable for Federal employment determined by background investigation
  • May be required to successfully complete a probationary period
  • Subject to the 5 year foreign area limitation DODI 1400.25-V1230 72612
  • WORK SCHEDULE: Full Time
  • OVERTIME: Occasionally
  • TOUR OF DUTY: May be Authorized 36 Months
  • RECRUITMENT INCENTIVES: May be Authorized
  • FINANCIAL DISCLOSURE: Not Required
  • TELEWORK ELIGIBILITY: This position is telework eligible
  • Must posses a valid driver's license
  • Must attain DoD SCW Certification IAW with the NDAA 2017, Title 10 USC, Section 384 and Security Cooperation Certification Program 2.0. requirements.
  • Employee will be subject to pre-employment medical requirements and must meet Foreign Service Medical Clearance requirements
  • This position is designated as a Testing Designated Position (TDP) under the civilian Drug-Testing Program.
  • Employee is required to obtain an Official passport and Visa as specified in the Department of Defense Foreign Clearance Guide for Qatar.
  • Employee must successfully complete Foreign Affairs Counter Threat (FACT) Training in accordance with Department of State, 13 FAM 301.4-2.
  • Employee must obtain and maintain a Special Sensitive/Top Secret/SCI Security Clearance.

Qualifications

Group Coverage Qualification Standard for Administrative and Management Positions for positions https://www.opm.gov/policy-data-oversight/classification-qualifications/general-schedule-qualification-standards/0300/miscellaneous-administration-and-program-series-0301/ for OPM qualification standards, competencies and specialized experience needed to perform the duties of the position as described in the MAJOR DUTIES and QUALIFICATIONS sections of this announcement by 10/15/2026

You must have one year Specialized Experience equivalent to the GS-14 level in the Federal service (experience may have been gained in the private/military sector) giving the particular knowledge, skills and abilities to perform successfully the duties of the position, and that is typically in or related to the work of the position. Experience must be reflected in your resume.

Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community, student, social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge, and skills and can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience.

Specialized experience required for this position is:

  • Serves as the principal subject matter expert to the Minister/Chief of Defense (MoD/CHOD) and the Commander, Military and Security Authority (MISA) on all aspects of national-level Security operations.
  • Advise the Minister/Chief of Defense and MISA Commander on national security strategy, threat landscape, and security level postures.
  • Collaborates enterprise-wide security program change management efforts across the national security enterprise to achieve mission assurance.
  • Facilitates planning and readiness for the partners security enterprise, crisis response efforts, incident management, and joint exercises.
  • Coordinates with U.S. federal agencies, DoW to include the military departments, and other U.S. private organizations to implement the partners Military Security Officer training program.
  • Analyzes and evaluates issues regarding development in terms of impact to broader U.S. SC and security assistance goals and objectives. Provides ICB input into long-term DoW ICB planning.
  • Prepares written assessments and reports, coordinating ICB visits and representing DoW as a primary Security point of contact for ICB efforts with MoD counterparts.

* For additional information on the Ministry of Defense Advisor (MoDA) Program, copy pastelink https://dscu.edu/icbd

Specifically you will be evaluated on the following competencies:
  • Attention to Detail
  • Customer Service
  • Decision Making
  • Flexibility
  • Influencing/Negotiating
  • Integrity/Honesty
  • Interpersonal Skills
  • Learning
  • Reasoning
  • Self-Management
  • Stress Tolerance
  • Teamwork

Requirements for Proficiency Level 3 -At least 1 year of successful SC work experience with a performance appraisal rating of 3 or better. IAW the National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA) 2017, Title 10 United States Code, Section 384 and Security Cooperation Certification Program 2.0 requirements. Description

Blessed Sacrament Parish seeks a dynamic and faith-filled Catholic leader to serve as Director of Religious Education & Youth Ministry.  This position provides leadership for parish faith formation programs for children, youth, and families while developing and growing a vibrant youth ministry program for middle school and high school students.

Requirements

1. Parish Religious Education Program:

  • The primary responsibility of the Director of Religious Education is to administer  (design, develop, direct, communicate and evaluate) the Parish Religious Education  Program for the parish children and parents who attend the program.  
  • Oversees the development of the Parish Religious Education Program from Grade Level  K through Grade 12, in conformity with the guidelines of the Religious Education Office  of Rockford Diocese.   
  • Schedules faith formation opportunities for children and parents within the Religious  Education Program calendar  ? Provides access and inclusion for children with special learning needs  
  • Ensures that the Safe Environment requirements, policies, and mandates for Parish  Religious Education volunteers are in compliance with Rockford Diocese  
  • Obtains approval and support from the pastor for the general direction of the religious  education of the parish  
  • Meets with pastor routinely to discuss matters relating to the parish religious education  and sacramental preparation   
  • Ensures that the Religious Education Program’s schedule of classes and activities are  submitted to the pastor for his approval.    
  • Updates and distributes the Parish Religious Education Program handbook for catechists  and the Parish Religious Education handbook for parents/guardians on an annual basis  
  • Recruits, orients and provides ongoing professional training and spiritual development  for the Parish Religious Education catechists 
  • Participates in Diocesan sponsored events such as the Catechetical Leaders  Convocations, Fall and Spring Professional Days and Retreats 
  • Attends the monthly Directors and Coordinators of Religious Education meetings  sponsored by Aurora Deanery 

2.  Sacramental Program

  • The Director of Religious Education oversees the coordination and sacramental  preparation of parish school-age candidates who attend the Parish Religious Education  Program, Catholic school or private Catholic academies. 
  • Schedules at the pastor’s directives dates for First Penance and First Holy Communion 
  • Schedules, coordinates and prepares retreat days for parents and students preparing for  First Penance, First Communion and Confirmation  
  • Prepares the liturgy (with the pastor) for First Penance, First Holy Communion and  Confirmation  
  • Creates and oversees catechetical plans for older baptized Catholic children or teens who  seek the reception of First Penance, First Holy Communion and/or Confirmation.   

3. Youth Ministry

  • Establish and develop a comprehensive youth ministry program for the parish. 
  • Plan youth gatherings, retreats, service projects, leadership opportunities, and diocesan  events. 
  • Develops a parish youth ministry core team. 
  • Build relationships with youth and their families.  
  • Recruit and mentor adult youth ministry volunteers.  

4.  Additional Responsibilities Include:

  • Coordinate Youth and Young Adults Ministry and Youth and Young Adult Ministry  Leaders  
  • Liturgy of the Word for Children – coordinate teams for Sunday Liturgy  
  • Vacation Bible School/Camp  
  • Make sure books used for the program are on the conformity list per Rockford Diocese  policy.   
  • Work evenings and weekends (Sunday morning Religious Education Program mornings)   

5.  Skills and Qualifications

  • Bachelors/Masters degree in related field and/or extensive experience in Faith Formation  
  • If no bachelors/masters, Ministry Formation is required. It takes 2 years to complete.  
  • Computer literate and able to learn Parish Data System program; know Microsoft Office,  work with Flocknote, and PDS, know or familiar with social media platforms so to  communicate with parishioners  
  • Excellent language and communication skills required 
  • Must pass current Diocesan clearances 
  • Manage repetitive tasks with little or no supervision 
  • Strong Public speaking skills  
  • Dress appropriately for office and public speaking  


Salary Description:  

$20.90-$26.00 per hour (commensurate with experience)  

Summary of Benefits

  • Submit a cover letter, resume, and three professional references to:  

Blessed Sacrament Parish  Attn: Father Downing- Parochial Administator  801 Oak Street  North Aurora, IL 60542  Email: adowning@rockforddiocese.org  Phone: 630-897-1029

At Elevation Church, we look to link arms in ministry with those who are passionate about stepping into their God-given calling. While we’re a staff from all different backgrounds and walks of life, our mission is the same - to reach people with the Gospel. We’re grounded in scripture and guided by our values, so check out our website (www.elevationchurch.org) to be sure you’re aligned before you step into the application process with us, particularly paying attention to our Beliefs and our Code.

RESPONSIBILITIES

  • You’ll participate in designing albums and single artwork for artists on Elevation Worship Records.
  • You’ll participate in designing auxiliary marketing content and promotional graphics.
  • You’ll participate in designing and/or updating branding for Elevation Worship and Elevation RHYTHM tours.
  • You’ll reformat existing assets to work for promotional ads and social media.
  • You’ll collaborate with a team in designing merchandise for artists on the Label and for various tours.
  • You’ll collaborate with the creative team in ideating for various video and/or photo-related projects.

MUST-HAVES

  • Active participation in a church (we look for a lifestyle of inviting people to church, volunteering, generosity, and prioritizing community)
  • College degree or 2+ years of relevant experience in Graphic Design
  • Proficiency in Illustrator, Photoshop, and InDesign
  • Portfolio illustrating a wide variety of design solutions
  • Good communication skills
  • Sense of calling to use your creative skill set in ministry
  • Collaborative, flexible, goal-driven personality
  • Grit and resilience; strong, proactive work ethic

NICE-TO-HAVES

  • Experience designing with AI tools such as Midjourney, DALL-E, etc.

DAY-TO-DAY

  • We’re a Sunday-Thursday work environment. Monday-Thursday, we’re in the office (8:30AM - 5PM); on Sunday, we’re supporting the weekend worship experience either directly in our roles or by choosing a weekly serving opportunity at one of our Elevation Church campuses.
  • There’s a lot to accomplish each week, so we’re pretty fast-paced. We’re also not afraid to pivot a strategy or project quickly to meet the needs of the weekend - adaptability is a key competence for us.
  • Yes, we work hard. But we’re good at playing hard, too. We’re a creative staff, so there’s no shortage of activities around our offices to have some fun!

  • Bring your full self to every project, conversation, and initiative at hand.

BENEFITS

  • Elevation Church pays 100% of every employee’s medical benefits for full-time staff
  • 403b with 4% match
  • Dental & Vision benefits
  • Paid time off for life, vacations, and rest
  • Elevation Church subsidized 6 sessions of counseling annually
  • Basic Life Insurance for employee, spouse, and child(ren)

The Deaf Teen Ministry Intern will assist in building Christ-centered relationships with Deaf and Hard of Hearing teens through consistent engagement, ministry programming, mentorship, and outreach efforts. This role supports the mission of Central Ohio Youth for Christ by helping young people develop authentic relationships with Jesus and their community.

Key Responsibilities

Relational Ministry & Student Engagement

  • Build Christ-centered relationships with Deaf and Hard of Hearing teens
  • Engage students through consistent encouragement, mentorship, and support
  • Assist in leading weekly ministry programs, outreach activities, and events
  • Support student participation and engagement opportunities

Ministry Support & Leadership Development

  • Assist in recruiting students, volunteers, and ministry leaders
  • Help facilitate team meetings, ministry activities, and special events
  • Support ministry organization through attendance tracking, communication, and data entry
  • Participate in staff meetings, ministry trainings, and fundraising events

Spiritual Growth & Ministry Formation

  • Grow as a minister of the Gospel through prayer, devotion, and sharing your faith
  • Support the mission, values, and ministry philosophy of Youth for Christ
  • Participate in mentorship and leadership development opportunities

Qualifications

  • A committed follower of Jesus Christ with a desire to live out and share the Gospel
  • Passion for serving Deaf and Hard of Hearing youth
  • Knowledge of American Sign Language (ASL)
  • Teachable, dependable, and willing to grow in ministry and leadership skills
  • Strong interpersonal and communication abilities
  • Ability to work collaboratively within a team environment
  • Previous youth ministry or volunteer experience is a plus, but not required

What You’ll Gain

  • Hands-on ministry experience with Deaf and Hard of Hearing teens
  • Mentorship from experienced ministry leaders
  • Training in Youth for Christ ministry models, leadership, and community development
  • Opportunities for spiritual growth and ministry development
  • Practical experience in nonprofit and youth ministry operations

About Central Ohio Youth for Christ

Central Ohio Youth for Christ reaches young people everywhere, working together with the local church and other like-minded partners to raise up lifelong followers of Jesus who lead by their godliness in lifestyle, devotion to the Word of God and prayer, passion for sharing the love of Christ, and commitment to social involvement.

Overview

In this remote role, you will develop training programs, build networks of ministry leaders, oversee content creation, and collaborate cross-functionally with the Lifeway Women's team to deliver resources that strengthen local churches across the country. If you have deep church ministry experience, a passion for developing other leaders, and a gift for speaking, writing, and building relationships, this is a rare opportunity to shape women's ministry on a national scale.

 

Why Lifeway? 

 

Lifeway is a place where you can bring your faith and work experience to join in the most important mission in the world: making disciples of Jesus Christ. Whether you’re a creator or storyteller, data guru or problem-solver, or anywhere in between, if you’re passionate about serving the church, we have a place for you. Lifeway has a strong Work from Anywhere (WFA) culture that is deeply focused on our mission and values. While headquartered in Nashville, TN, many of our positions are remote-eligible and have autonomy and flexibility with work hours. We provide equipment and resources to ensure team members have access to a productive and ergonomic workspace. We believe building relationships and community is essential to how we work together, so Lifeway hosts all-team meetings several times per year and provides travel for key team gatherings for remote-based team members. Full-time employees are eligible for enrollment in our comprehensive benefits plans including healthcare, vacation and sick time, holiday pay, care days, 401(k) plan, maternity and paternity leave, adoption assistance, mission trip time, and more. If this sounds like a place where you would be excited to serve the kingdom of God, we would love for you to join our team.

 

Learn more about our culture at team.lifeway.com/culture-code 

 

This is a remote position in the U.S. with occasional travel to Nashville for in-person team gatherings. #LI-Remote 

 

Responsibilities

Skills, Knowledge, & Experiences, required

  • 5 or more years of event planning and content development experience
  • Expert-level relationship management and network-building skills

Member / actively involved in an evangelical Christian church
