The Administrative Assistant in the Campus Ministry Office of Father Ryan High School provides clerical support for faith formation programs, student retreats, and Campus Ministry events, as well as administrative support for day-to-day operations of the office. 


  Primary Roles

  • Support the Campus Ministry team and the school's mission to be an experience of the living Gospel while challenging students to reach their spiritual, academic, and personal potential. 
  • Act as a liaison between the Campus Ministry office and students, parents, staff, and local parish and Diocesan leaders.
  • Provide relational ministry with students who choose to spend time in the Campus Ministry office.      
  • Manage day-to-day office tasks to keep department programs running smoothly. 

Key Responsibilities

  • Event & Liturgy Coordination: Help set up school Masses, prayer services, Penance services, service days, retreats.
  • Student Service Events: Work with Coordinator of Service Learning on Relay for Life Event, Christmas Eve Room in the Inn   overnight dinner event, assist with Service Fair and other on-campus service events.
  • Penance Service Coordination: Work with priests of the Diocese in scheduling school wide Advent and Lenten Penance Services for students.
  • Supplies & Finances: Procure Campus ministry and Chapel supplies, manage inventory, and approve invoices.
  • Scheduling: Maintain chapel calendar for spiritual events and Mass intentions. 
  • Senior Event Coordination: Help with planning and logistics for spring Almost Alumni Day and Senior Class Baccalaureate      Mass. 
  • Diocese Youth Group Events: Coordinate with local Catholic church youth group directors to plan student luncheons on campus. 
  • Catholic Schools Week Events: Work with Director of Campus Ministry and Director of Houses to celebrate Catholic Schools Week
  • Extracurricular Events: Assistance required at select student ball games, tailgates and some extracurricular events. 
  • Faith and Service Trip Management: Book lodging and travel, create itineraries, coordinate with 3rd parties, communication with stakeholders, procure supplies and food. 
Requirements

  

Qualifications

  • Faith and Values: Practicing Catholic in good standing who supports the teachings and mission of the Church.
  • Education: High school diploma required; an associate or bachelor's degree is preferred.
  • Experience: Prior administrative or secretarial experience, ideally in a school or parish setting. Experience working with children/teens is preferable. 
  • Skills: Strong computer literacy, including Microsoft Office (Word, Excel) plus great communication and organizational skills. We are looking for a self-motivated, flexible, friendly individual who can work in a fast-paced and energetic environment. 
  • Willingness to learn new systems, such as BlackBaud, Brightly event management software, Monday workflow management software, and other work-related systems. 

Other

· This position is a student-services role. Duties apply when students are in school and on-campus. 

· Compensation is based on an hourly rate. Typical school hours are 7:30am-3:30pm, but some work outside of these hours is required. 

· Benefits are included in this role, i.e. health insurance, disability insurance, 403(b) retirement accounts, etc.

· This position will also serve as a staff Mentor through our House System. 

· Other duties as assigned:

o Attend Faculty Meetings (monthly)

o Other staff duties as assigned

o Campus Ministry does assist with some special Masses on the weekends, such as the Kevin Paul Davis Scholarship Mass and the Golden Grad Mass. The Administrative Assistant does attend these weekend events.

job_name: Next Gen Pastor - Sanctuary Family Worship Center
post_html:
Next Gen Pastor - Sanctuary Family Worship Center

Sanctuary is seeking a full-time Next Gen Pastor (Family Pastor) to lead multiple teams of volunteers and oversee the discipleship of kids and students, 0-18 years.

Church Environment
Sanctuary is: 

  • An interdenominational kingdom-focused community of diverse believers.
  • A contemporary Spirit-filled church with deep Bible-based teaching, a team approach to ministry, and a growth track for discipleship. 
  • A church with a high level of networking in the local community.
  • A church that uses modern resources to engage the next generation and the lost. 
  • A supportive, family-oriented church built on honest relationships.
  • A welcoming, come as you are people, offering grace and love to the broken.

Position Overview
The Next Gen Pastor will provide ministry vision, implement a cohesive curriculum, and serve as a pastoral presence to both children and youth. Will help Sanctuary to effectively reach students in the community and equip parents at home. Train, resource and schedule volunteer leaders in kids ministry. The Next Gen Pastor will rotate teaching and preaching with teams of volunteers, while being the primary teacher in Sanctuary Kids. As an associate pastor, will supervise a team of 12+ kids team members, a part-time youth director, and 6+ youth team members.

Key Responsibilities

  • Spiritual Formation: Ensure a strong Spirit-filled and Bible based discipleship of Sanctuary's kids and youth.  
  • Program Development: Cast vision and lead volunteers to implement age-appropriate ministry programs, events, and retreats to reach and disciple students.
  • Teach & Preach: Rotate with volunteers as one of the primary teachers in Sunday Kids Church. Assist in Wednesday youth ministry monthly to ensure a cohesive Next Gen ministry. 
  • Volunteer Coordination: Recruit, train, and schedule volunteers in the Next Generation departments.
  • Pastoral Care: Provide counseling, guidance, and support for kids and youth and visit schools weekly.
  • Collaboration: Work with the church leadership team and Lead Pastor to ensure Next Gen ministries are integrated into the overall church's vision and mission. Serve in unity with Sanctuary's part-time Youth Director and Youth Team for a cohesive Next Gen department. 
  • Administration: Oversee the kids ministry calendar, communicate with parents, utilize weekly social media for communication and outreach, download and print curriculum for teams and ensure volunteers are trained and background checked.  
  • Community: They will visit local schools weekly as an official campus chaplain. 


Qualifications 

  • Credentialed with the Assemblies of God and provide positive ministry references that demonstrate: 
    • A divine calling in Next Gen Ministries 
    • A personable and engaging personality to reach students 
    • A humble and mature Christian character
    • Strong communication skills for volunteer and parent engagement.
    • Gifts in administration for planning events, organizing calendars and scheduling volunteers
    • Gifts in leadership for training and inspiring teams of volunteers. 

Cultural Environment:
Jena, Louisiana is a rural conserviative town in LaSalle Parish, Louisiana with a regional reach of 15,000 people. The people of LaSalle Parish are 85% Southern Baptist, primarily middle to lower class, and work primarily in the oil industry, health care industry, correctional industry, or school system. It is a very safe, hospitable and tight community, with a great school system. Passtimes for many include hunting, fishing, baseball, and football. Overall, Jena is a great place to raise a family.

tag_categories: [API Management]
post_html:
How to Apply
Applications accepted through the Diocese of Fort Wayne South Bend hiring site or you may send a cover letter, resume, and three references (at least one a pastor or ministry supervisor) to ryan@kreagerconsulting.com, or start at johnboscocommission.org/ym-position.

Applications are reviewed as they arrive; the position is open until filled.


The Role

The Youth Minister leads the shared youth ministry of four Mishawaka parishes: St. Joseph, St. Monica, St. Bavo, and Queen of Peace. This person runs Antioch, our high school ministry, and Emmaus, our middle school ministry. The work is discipleship: building a community where teens are known by name, encounter the Lord in the sacraments and in real friendship, and grow into leaders who bring their peers with them.

This is a part-time contract position for the coming year, funded in full by the four parishes. The parishes are building the financial support to make this a full-time Director of Youth Ministry and Young Adult Ministry, and the person who leads this year well is the natural first candidate for that role. 

What You Will Do

Antioch (high school)
• Lead the weekly Thursday night gathering at St. Monica: nights of worship, catechesis, small groups, service, and fun, planned and run with the adult core team.
• Plan and lead two retreats a year on the Antioch model, each with ten weeks of preparation: forming the teen team, recruiting core and host homes, organizing meals, and preparing talks and prayer.

Emmaus (middle school)

• Oversee and grow Emmaus, and recruit Antioch teens sixteen and older to serve there as ministers, so our high schoolers learn to lead by leading.


Core team and leaders
• Recruit and form adult core members, including young adults at least two years out of high school, through discipleship, education, prayer, and a ministry leadership retreat.
• Help teens discern their gifts and call them to their baptismal role in ministry: on the teen team, at Emmaus, and among their peers.

Presence and promotion
• Be a consistent, visible advocate and pastoral presence for the ministry: at Masses, in bulletins, and in person at Mishawaka Catholic School, Queen of Peace Catholic School, St. Thomas More Catholic Academy, Marian High School, and St. Joseph High School.
• Communicate regularly with parents and students.
• Recruit prayer partners for the ministry, and stay connected with local young adult groups and Newman Centers as a bridge for graduating seniors.


Qualifications

• A practicing Catholic in good standing.
• Experience in youth ministry, campus ministry, or a Catholic missionary apostolate (FOCUS, NET, Damascus, Encounter, or similar).
• A track record of building trust with teens, parents, and volunteers.
• Comfort out front: teaching, leading prayer, and running a room.
• Enough organization to prepare and run a retreat.
• Availability on evenings and weekends, Thursday nights above all. A diocesan background check and Safe Environment compliance are required before any ministry with young people.

Preferred
• A degree in theology, pastoral ministry, or a related field, or equivalent ministry experience.

• Preferably worshiping at one of the Mishawaka parishes.

• Familiarity with retreat-based models (Antioch, Life Teen, Steubenville) and experience leading praise and worship or small groups.

About Crossroads

Crossroads Church is a growing multi-site, interdenominational church. Our sites are currently located in Ohio and Kentucky, with plans to expand to additional cities. We also have an online presence that serves thousands of people who aren’t located near one of our physical sites.

We believe the story of Jesus' redemption is the greatest story ever told, and that's why we embrace creativity, adventure, authenticity, and tenacity to share this story with the world.

Our desire is to model our staff and church community after the church in Revelation, where people of all nations, tribes, and tongues are worshiping and working together. We’re not there yet, but it’s what we’re working toward with every hire and every person who walks through our doors. 

Job Summary

The Students Worship Leader leads the overall music and worship experience for a site at Crossroads Students. This person is an exceptional vocalist, has a commanding, authentic presence on stage and exhibits an infectious excitement in worship. They also have technical musical skills and the ability to arrange music, create charts, tracks, samples and plays multiple instruments. Most importantly this person has an authentic relationship with Jesus that they are willing to share with those they are leading in worship.

Principal Duties and Responsibilities 

  • Serve as one of our primary worship leaders, instrumentalists and provide pastoral moments to Crossroads Students on the weekends.

  • Collaborate with the site team and production volunteers to produce a high quality, authentic worship experience each week

  • Recruit and shepherd volunteers to assist in weekend service execution

  • Network with site support and other campus counterparts in the production and creation of worship experiences

Education Requirements

  • High School Diploma or equivalent work experience.

Experience/Skills Requirements

  • Minimum 2 years experience creating and leading worship services for large congregations

  • Gifts and skills in leadership, exhortation, creative arts, collaboration and people development

  • Proven ability to manage multiple duties and priorities in deadline-intensive situations

  • Able to flourish in a creative team environment as well as operate independently

  • Experience building volunteer teams and leading them to excellent execution

  • Excellent interpersonal skills, both in technical and non-technical environments

  • Background in designing services and managing the details

  • Proficient in Planning Center Online and Multitracks

  • Performs effectively under pressure and against strict time constraints

Physical Requirements

  • Must be able to walk up to 3 miles

  • Able to lift 25 lbs.

Scheduling/Travel Requirements

  • Available to work evenings, weekends, and long hours

Crossroads Staff Qualities

Qualities all staff teammates should exhibit:

  • Mission Oriented: Committed to the Crossroads mission and expectations in the staff “I Promise” document, including using the Bible as the ultimate standard of truth, practicing spiritual disciplines, tithing, and pursuing personal purity.

  • Availability: Expected to work outside of “normal” schedule for All Hands on Deck high-impact events (Holy Week/Easter, Super Bowl, Christmas, others as needed), participate in all-staff meetings, day of solitude, offsites, etc.

  • Authenticity: Communicates clearly, directly, and honestly, even under stress, and does so with a sustained positive attitude and demeanor.

  • Personal Leadership: Envisions, energizes, and enables others to operate at full potential.

  • Collaborative Self-starter: Thrives as an individual contributor and works well on a team.

  • Proactive Problem Solver: Takes initiative to understand departmental objectives, adapts to changing and fluid environments, and proactively solves problems.

  • Humility: Puts others above self and takes ownership of mistakes. 

  • Learner: Desires growth and learning from others.

  • Flexibility: Able to quickly shift between projects as organizational direction and needs change, able to successfully balance competing priorities.

Crossroads Church is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees.

Our church... is a non-denominational multi-site church with four St. Louis-area campuses where we gather each weekend to study this ancient story found in Scripture that is still transforming lives today. We believe church should be a place where believers in Jesus and skeptics can stand side-by-side to study truth and ask tough questions. We blend teaching and worship with art and technology to create a service where you can experience the message of Jesus in practical and life-changing ways.

Pastor/Care Ministries.....This full-time position involves managing Care Resourcing, which includes counseling and referrals, as well as leading and assisting in pastoral care development and training of care classes/events. It also requires staying updated on best practices, teaching, providing pastoral care, participating in various events, and overseeing specific responsibilities at the Fenton campus.

This individual must have a passion for Jesus Christ, the vision of The Crossing, and a heart for those seeking and walking with Jesus in our community. This individual will work closely with senior leadership team, the pastoral teaching team, counselors, and with various departments within the church.

ESSENTIAL JOB RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Manage Care Resourcing which includes the counseling and organization referral process.
  • Lead and direct development and implementation of growth strategies for classes as directed by the Director of Care Ministries.
  • Assist with development of pastoral care response and training across campuses, including but not limited to funerals, hospital visits, and crises situations.
  • Assist with pastoral and leadership responsibilities in various environments and care classes/events as needed and determined by Care Pastor and Director of Care.
  • Create curriculum and implement training opportunities for pastors, staff and key volunteers who will be leading care conversations.

Overview and Purpose

 

Overview:

  • A 1-Year Internship for M.Div students (renewable up to three years).
  • For men concurrently pursuing a M.Div
  • 20 hours/week
  • $20K / year - includes living stipend and educational expenses. Assumes the student will be attending Indianapolis Theological Seminary and the church obtains the BIOS grant.



Purpose: We believe that a combination of seminary and training in the context of the local church is the best combination for developing pastors. Our aim is three-fold:

 

  • Shepherd: To shepherd interns to grow in their affection for God, character, and competency to serve in the church.
  • Guide: To help interns clarify their potential future ministry direction and next steps.
  • Develop: To raise leaders who make disciples, and therefore build the greater Church through planting and strengthening churches among our neighbors and the nations.

 

Values and Emphases

 

The internship will be marked by these emphases:

 

  • Gospel Culture: We very intentionally seek to cultivate a church ethos that reflects the gospel. An ethos that humbly welcomes, serves, and honors one another as Christ welcomes, serves, and honors us. We want to shepherd each candidate as Christ would shepherd them, and to train them in how they can create that ethos in their future ministries.

 

  • Relational: Although we have many “guides” in Christ, we also need spiritual fathers (1 Cor. 4:15). We seek to provide this kind of relational training. Much of what we will teach must be both taught and caught.

 

  • Church-Focused: We complement seminary training by providing a hands-on, relational context to grow in the character and skills needed for healthy church ministry. We will emphasize making disciples, cultivating a gospel culture, encouraging others, personally communing with God, building true friendships, growing in holiness, loving the nations, leading humbly, and ministering in a sustainable way, all within the context of a local church.

 

  • Historically-Enriched: While we need to understand our 21st century context, many ministry trends have not produced fruitful disciples. Some of the best examples of fruit-bearing ministry come from our heritage. Therefore, there will be a substantial amount of reading that will draw from the likes of Augustine, Luther, Calvin, Goodwin, Newton, Edwards, etc.

 

  • Well-Rounded: Ministry leaders need to be trained to grow in both doctrine and character. They also need to be exposed to the whole life of a church–not only to its strengths, but also its weaknesses. Our internship will focus on forming well-rounded, healthy leaders for sustainable ministry.

  

Structure and Responsibilities

 

This program divides its time between study and reflection, pastoral mentoring, and ministry exposure and experience.

 

Study and Reflection

Interns will have weekly reading assignments and will write reflection papers which will be discussed with one of the pastors.

 

Pastoral Mentoring

The intern will meet weekly with one of the mentor-pastors. The intern will also meet weekly with one of the other ministry staff members or ministry leaders.



Ministry Experience and Leadership Development 

  • Participate in weekly staff meeting
  • Engage in bi-weekly meetings with various leaders and members: The intern will arrange individual meetings with various ZF leaders to learn about spiritual growth and local church ministry.
  • Various opportunities to teach and disciple.
  • Co-lead a small group and assist in the leadership of a particular ministry.
  • Observe and debrief elders’ meetings each month.
  • Weekly meeting to discuss the principles and practices of Christ-centered biblical exposition.
  • Engage in a number of opportunities by participating or shadowing a leader: For example, Small Group Leadership meetings; funeral and wedding process; Simeon Trust preaching workshop, hospital visitation; meetings for elders, deacons, youth group, etc; membership course; welcome team; men’s ministry.

  

Assumptions

 

We assume the following for all interns:

 

  1. They will cultivate a daily habit of communing with God through meditating on God’s word and prayer. This is not officially part of the internship, but is a required foundation for the residency to be fruitful.

 

  1. They will be all-in and committed to fulfilling expectations. This includes completing assignments on time, taking initiative in conversations, and seeking to glean from various readings and experiences.

 

  1. They will view themselves as servants and remain open to any kind of task they’re called to fulfill. We seek to follow the example of Jesus, who did not come to be served, but to serve.


Details and FAQs

 

Is office space provided?

Yes, the intern will be provided office space. The intern will ideally use the office for a significant portion of time each week and will set specific office hours. This provides opportunities to get to know staff and members, to participate in the culture of the staff, and to experience daily church-office rhythms.

 

Is housing assistance available?

In some cases, we may be able to assist interns in finding affordable housing or a place in the one the church member’s homes. If we have several single interns, we would encourage them to live together.

 

What is the church and internships theological perspective?

We are broadly reformed and appreciate the confession statements of The Gospel Coalition and the 1689 London Baptist Confession.

 

Who leads and oversees the internship and residency?

Drew Hunter provides the overall leadership for the internship and residency. Drew is the Teaching Pastor of Zionsville Fellowship, where he provides overall leadership, biblical teaching, and serves as an elder. He graduated from Moody Bible Institute and received MAs from Wheaton College Graduate School in Biblical Exegesis and Systematic & Historical Theology. He and his wife, Christina, have four sons.

Position Title: Children's Ministry Pastor/Director

Reports To: BJ Forguson - Executive Pastor


Kids Pastor

Job Summary

The Pastor/Director of Children's Ministry (AOKids) oversees all programs for children from birth through 5th grade, prioritizing proclaiming the gospel, promoting spiritual growth, and providing parental support. The role is responsible for creating engaging environments that foster genuine relationships with Christ.


Guiding Scriptures for Ministry

Matthew 22:37-39, Matthew 28:19-20, and Deuteronomy 6:5-9


Primary Responsibilities:

  • Cultivate an environment where every child can meet, know, and follow Jesus.
  • Develop and oversee all AOKids programs and activities to ensure alignment with ministry goals.
  • Facilitate connections between children, families, and volunteers to foster community and discipleship.
  • Supervise AOKids staff, providing training and support for effective ministry.
  • Recruit, screen, and train volunteers to serve in various capacities within AOKids.
  • Ensure the safety and security of all children in all environments.
  • Equip parents with resources and support for spiritual leadership in the home.
  • Collaborate with other ministries to provide holistic support for families.
  • Strategically engage new children and families in the life of Austin Oasks Church
  • Provide pastoral care and support to children and families as needed.
  • Organize and execute ministry events to build community and reach out to young families.
  • Manage the Children's Ministry budget effectively.


Organizational Relationships

  • Maintain accountability through regular reporting and meetings with supervisor.
  • Foster positive and supportive relationships with staff, lat leaders, parents, and children.
  • Communicate effectively with all stakeholders to address suggestions and concerns.


Qualifications: The ideal candidate:

  • Demonstrates a passionate commitment to Jesus Christ and the mission of Austin Oaks Church.
  • Holds a degree in church ministry, children's/youth ministry, education, or a related field (preferred)
  • Brings a minimum of 3 years of experience in Children's Ministry or a related field (preferred)
  • Possess strong leadership skills and a love for working with children and families.
  • Exhibits a positive attitude, willingness to collaborate, and teachable spirit.
  • Demonstrates effective multi-tasking and organizational ability


Physical Requirements:

  • Ability to stand and speak for extended periods.
  • Capability to occasionally lift up to 25 pounds.




LOCATION & DEMOGRAPHICS

Located in South Austin, Austin Oaks Church sits in one of the city’s most vibrant and diverse areas. Austin is consistently ranked as one of the top cities for lifestyle, culture, and business, and the South Austin community reflects this energy with its unique blend of Texas charm, creative arts, thriving local businesses, and access to Austin’s renowned title as the live music capital of the world.

South Austin is not only a cultural hotspot but also an excellent place to raise a family. The area offers a welcoming community, an abundance of parks and green spaces, and proximity to top-rated schools. While Austin’s cost of living has increased in recent years, South Austin neighborhoods like Sunset Valley and Manchaca provide more accessible options for families looking to settle down and connect with the city’s vibrant life. Austin Oaks Church is proud to be part of this thriving community, serving as a hub for faith, connection, and growth.



AOKids

Austin Oaks Kids is the vibrant children’s ministry of Austin Oaks Church, welcoming over 110 kids each weekend. The ministry is designed to help kids discover and develop a relationship with Jesus, connect with their peers, and grow alongside caring leaders. Through engaging worship, Bible teaching, small groups, and fun activities, children are invited into an exciting journey of faith.

The program is divided into three age-targeted groups: Nursery/PreK, Elementary, and 4th/5th Grade, each with spaces designed to meet the unique needs of these age groups. The Kid’s Director provides oversight for all programming from birth through 5th grade, ensuring a safe, fun, and meaningful experience for every child.

​

​SNAPSHOT:

  • Sundays - 110-120 kids
  • Wednesdays - 20 kids - Club 45 only
  • Volunteers - 160

Kids Ministry Staff:

  • Kids director
  • Assistant Kids Director
  • Hospitality
  • Administrative assistant

Curriculum - Austin Oaks uses the Orange Curriculum. Most of the teaching is delivered live by their talented volunteer team, with some support from video resources for worship and story time.


Check-in and Database - Church Community Builder (CCB)




SUNDAYS


PRESCHOOL (Birth - Kindergarten)

The Austin Oaks Kids team is dedicated to creating a safe, engaging, and fun environment where children can discover and explore key biblical truths from God’s Word. Their staff and volunteers ensure a secure check-in/check-out process, exciting activities, and thoughtfully designed indoor and outdoor spaces tailored to each age group.

They aim to make Austin Oaks Kids a place where children are excited to return each week, building a foundation of faith in a setting that parents can trust and kids will love! This is so much more than childcare or babysitting, this is ministry.


ELEMENTARY (1st - 3rd Grades)

At Austin Oaks Kids, they strive to make Sunday the best time of the week for every child! Through engaging large and small group settings, children have a blast learning about Jesus while connecting with friends and leaders.

They believe that what happens at home is even more important than what happens at church. That’s why they partner with parents to help guide their children on their spiritual journey. To support families, they provide simple, weekly take-home resources that build on the lessons taught on Sunday mornings, making it easy to continue faith conversations throughout the week.


CLUB 45 (4th - 5th Grades)

The 4th and 5th-grade students have a dedicated space designed just for them. Each Sunday begins in their room, where they check in with their leaders, greet friends, and prepare for an exciting day ahead.

Afterward, they join the larger group of elementary kids for worship and the main teaching. Following the lesson, they often head upstairs to the gym for group games before returning to their room for small group time. These small groups provide an opportunity for deeper discussions, connection, and prayer.


​WEDNESDAYS


Club45

Club 45 is a vibrant group for 4th and 5th graders, designed to help students build friendships with each other, their leaders, and, most importantly, Jesus. Led by a passionate team of committed leaders, including the enthusiastic Mr. Ted, Club 45 meets on Wednesday evenings from 7:00 to 8:30 PM. The evening kicks off with Hang Out Time from 7:00 to 7:30, featuring games like foosball, billiards, and ping pong. From 7:30 to 8:00, the Large Group gathers for exciting group games, worship, and a brief lesson or video teaching. The night wraps up with Small Group time from 8:00 to 8:30, including a Bible lesson activity, discussion, prayer, and Check-Out.



CHALLENGE & OPPORTUNITY


MULTICULTURAL

Austin Oaks has a thriving Spanish ministry. Leading a kids ministry that involves both the English and Spanish congregations is both a tremendous opportunity and a unique challenge. Language barriers can create hurdles, especially for children and parents who do not speak English fluently. The new leader must possess cultural sensitivity and a heart for diversity, creating a space where all families feel welcomed and connected. They should work to bridge language gaps through creative programming, resources, and intentional relationships. This role calls for someone who understands how to celebrate cultural diversity while fostering unity, ensuring that every child and family feels seen, valued, and included in the ministry’s mission.


MULTIGENERATIONAL

Austin Oaks is uniquely positioned as a church where every generation has a voice and a place. From young families to retirees, the congregation is beautifully balanced, creating a rich tapestry of wisdom, energy, and perspective. The new leader will need to excel at engaging with people of all ages, adapting their communication and leadership style to connect with everyone—from the youngest child to the most seasoned elder. They will need to design programs that gives opportunities for kids, youth, and seniors the opportunity to serve and grow together.


FRESH WIND

The ministry is at a pivotal moment, ready to embrace fresh vision, strategy, and heart. While the team has worked hard to keep things running smoothly, they are eager for a leader to provide clear direction and inspiring leadership. This leader must bring innovative ideas and a contagious enthusiasm to breathe new life into the ministry. Their role will include casting a vision that unites the team, developing strategies that align with the church’s mission, and fostering a renewed sense of purpose among volunteers. Central to this effort is helping volunteers see their work as ministry—not just child care. With the right guidance, this team can create a transformative impact on the lives of kids and families.

​

STRENGTHING THE TEAM

The elementary ministry team (upstairs) is a well-oiled machine, filled with dedicated, trained, and experienced volunteers. In contrast, the preschool ministry team (downstairs) is newer and still finding its footing. The new leader will need to provide tailored support to each group, affirming and encouraging the established elementary team while offering intentional training and development for the preschool team. This role requires someone skilled in team building and leadership development, with a keen ability to identify and empower the unique strengths of each volunteer.

​

START WITH THE END IN MIND

To design a ministry that reaches families and is prepared for growth, this leader must begin with the future in mind. They need to envision what a thriving ministry looks like years down the road and work backward to create a strategic plan that leads to that goal. This involves designing programs and structures that are scalable, sustainable, and family-focused. The leader must also prioritize innovation and adaptability, ensuring the ministry evolves alongside the needs of the community. By building on the church’s existing strengths and integrating fresh ideas, this leader will lay a foundation for a ministry that not only serves families today but continues to grow and flourish in the years to come.

​

Full time

An Area Director leads and oversees a ministry team to plant and to grow witnessing communities of students and faculty who follow Jesus on college and university campuses. Through these groups, we believe ever-increasing numbers of students and faculty from all ethnic groups and areas of the campus will be transformed by the gospel. We expect to see campuses increasingly become places where people, ideas, and structures flourish for the common good and to the glory of God. Please submit the GFM Interest Form before completing the full application for a position with Graduate & Faculty Ministries in our online system. We will contact you when we are ready to proceed with the application process.​

Candidates may live in:

  • Ohio, Pittsburgh (western Pennsylvania) or West Virginia.

This job is for those who are not an Area Ministry Director with InterVarsity. If you already serve as an Area Ministry Director, please apply for the other Area Ministry Director - Midwest (Graduate and Faculty Ministry) position in the Jobs Hub.


We have positions in the following locations:

ESSENTIAL COMMITMENTS/RESPONSIBILITIES

1. Spiritual Growth

The Area Ministry Director models spiritual maturity as a disciple of Jesus Christ so that your life and work increasingly reflects a growing love for God, God’s Word, God’s people of every ethnicity and culture, and God’s purposes in the world.

  • Pursue a vibrant relationship with the triune God through engagement with Scripture, prayer, and worship, both individually and in community
  • Exercise self-leadership (growing in self-awareness, self-management, relational integrity, and resiliency)

​2. Campus Ministry Leadership

As an Area Director, you inspire, coach and develop campus staff ministers (“ministers”), students, faculty, and ministry partners to increase the number of witnessing communities, as well as the size, health, spiritual maturity, and campus-wide influence of existing witnessing communities by being a:

Visionary Guide:

  • Create a culture of dependence on God to gain vision for establishing and advancing witnessing communities that reach every corner of every campus in your area
  • Model InterVarsity’s vision and Core Values for supervisees
  • Lead staff, students, and faculty through Scripture, prayer, teaching and discipleship experiences in a way that motivates and shapes their ministry around vision

Structural Architect:

  • Lead your team to develop and implement plans to achieve ministry goals
  • Adapt the plan as needed through rhythms of action, reflection and evaluation

Missional Developer:

  • Recruit a diversity of qualified minister candidates

  • Proactively establish and develop healthy relationships across racial, ethnic, national background, and gender barriers with staff, students, faculty, and ministry partners to build effective and diverse communities
  • Build an effective minister team that collaborates well and accomplishes goals

3. Organizational Collaboration

As an Area Director, you are part of a national organization and work in partnership with local, area, divisional, regional, and national InterVarsity ministers and volunteers.

  • Participate in regional leadership as determined by the Regional Director, to set ministry vision and strategies, contribute to accomplishing plans, and provide regional leadership in specific areas
  • Positively and constructively respond to the direction and coaching of line supervisors
  • Build productive ministry partnerships with regional and national collaborative leaders
  • Establish systems, processes and protocols to fulfill regular operational and administrative tasks in a timely manner (reporting, finances, human resources, etc.)
  • Maintain sound financial status of the area through management of budgeting, expense control and ministry partnership development
  • Become familiar with and comply with all InterVarsity policies and procedures

As an Area Director, you will develop a team of partners who will resource the ministry financially, in prayer, or with volunteer service that advances the mission.

  • Develop and maintain a ministry among partners who will fund InterVarsity

  • Build resource networks with alumni, volunteers, churches, advocacy councils, and major donors, in particular to fund low-network ministers

post_html:
Music Ministry Director - Fort Myers Community Church
 

The Role

Fort Myers Community Church is looking for a Music Ministry Director to lead our people in worship that is rich in truth and full of God. We want a person who sings, a leader who builds, and a worshiper who points every eye to Jesus.

The Music Ministry Director oversees two areas: Music Ministry and Environments. Both serve one aim. When our church gathers, we want people to leave more amazed by God than by anything happening on the stage.


Music Ministry
The Director builds and leads the music ministry of FMCC and multiplies themself in others.

• Building and Leading: Plan, rehearse, and lead worship for Sunday mornings, Wednesday nights, and Thursday nights. Recruit and shepherd musicians and vocalists so each gathering is served with excellence and care.
• Raising Up Worship Leaders: Identify, train, and release worship leaders for every environment, from youth to kids to community gatherings. Success is not one strong leader on Sunday. Success is a bench of faithful leaders across the whole church.

Environments
The Director shapes environments of worship and prayer across every ministry of FMCC. What we sing teaches what we believe, so song selection is a theological task.


• Worship and Prayer Across All Ministries: Create rhythms of sung worship and prayer in Sunday gatherings, midweek services, youth, kids, and ministry events.
• Modern Contemporary Hymns: Lead songs that pair modern sound with timeless truth, both new hymns and the great hymns of the church.
• Godward Focused Worship: Choose songs that magnify the character and works of God and the finished work of Jesus.

Job Description: Senior Pastor

Community Church Big Bear is seeking an individual to serve as the Senior Pastor for our church. This is a full-time salaried ministry position, with a generous benefits package. Applicants: please send a resume, your written testimony, references, and video links (preaching examples).

Background Information

Our church is pastor led. We are searching for a pastor to fulfill that role. This includes leading our Elder Board, our paid staff, our ministry volunteers, and every age group and category of individuals. Big Bear is a small tourist community in the SoCal mountains. We enjoy four seasons and beautiful natural environment. Winters can be difficult for some people. We have a full-time staff of three people, and four part-time, with two Sunday Services and a Wednesday mid-week program. Our weekly worship attendance is between 400-475.

Responsibilities include:

  • Develop vision and values for the church to follow in the coming years, in accordance with the scriptures and the teachings of Jesus.
  • Foster a Christian community culture that embraces and engages newcomers in the life of the church. Providing an active role for as many people as possible.

  • Continue to develop a global outreach ethos that demonstrates God’s heart for the nations.
  • Develop and maintain relationships with community leaders. Be engaged in the community, both by hosting non-church groups on campus, and outside the church events that show a heart for the community.

Education/Experience:

Pastor/leader should have significant experience in leadership, pastoring, counseling, preaching, and team building.

A Master’s level education in Christian Studies/Theology is preferred.

The Most Holy Name of Jesus Catholic Church

Position Title: Youth and Young Adult Minister
Position Status: Non-Exempt, Full-time
Immediate Supervisor: Pastor
Work Schedule: Attendance at all staff meetings; Weekend activities; summer activities

Position Summary: The youth and young adult minister (YM) has two main areas of responsibility:
1) Coordinates the evangelization, catechesis, formation, and mission to students, grades 8-12,
including summer activities, as well as administering the confirmation program for 11th grade; and
2) Facilitates weekly ministry activities for young adults, ages 21-35. The duties will include
leading weekly or bi- weekly gatherings, monthly activities, yearly retreats, and sacramental
preparation. Salary negotiable based on experience and education.

Duties and Responsibilities

Youth Ministry

Coordinate the evangelization and ministry to all 8 – 12 graders in the parish, based on the
2024 USCCB document, Listen, Teach, Send: A National Pastoral Framework for Ministries with Youth
and with Young Adults.
Develop curriculum for a comprehensive youth ministry program for grades 8-12.
Serve as a member of the parish staff. Attend all staff meetings, retreats, faith formation.
Recruit, train, and support adult volunteers for the Youth Leadership Core Team, which
assists in planning, implementing and evaluating a comprehensive youth ministry program.
Provide appropriate training for the adults and young people in leadership positions.
Administer and lead the parish's Confirmation program, including sacramental registration.
Organize confession for youth, twice per year.
Coordinate youth participation in parish liturgies as well as Exposition and Adoration of the
Blessed Sacrament.
Communicate regularly and effectively to the parish, the staff, and the parish council about
youth ministry activities.
Spend time in relational ministry with youth. Besides the scheduled ministry events of our
program, this should include things like attending high schools' special events, such as Masses,
sporting, cultural, and social events, when possible.
Engage in ongoing personal education, faith formation, and youth ministry training.
Connect and coordinate with other youth ministry groups, offices, and committees in the
diocese and in appropriate professional associations.
Work evenings and weekends as needed.
Work collaboratively with the Director of Religious Education (DRE).
Ensure compliance with all Archdiocesan policies and procedures including Safe Environment
protocols.
Organize and develop fundraising for youth events, trips, and projects.

Young Adult Ministry

Coordinate a young adult ministry group at Holy Name of Jesus Church, including planning and
promoting regularly scheduled events during the year focused on the young adults of the region.
Develop new opportunities to engage young adults in deepening their spirituality, expanding
their knowledge of Church teaching, forming a peer community, or participating in service projects.
Communicate to the young adult community in the region through regular emails, updating
relevant websites, and appropriate use of social media.
Support those ministering with young adults at the parish level. Provide networking

SUMMARY

The Worship Pastor provides spiritual, pastoral, and strategic leadership for the Worship Ministry at Pinelake’s Madison campus. This leader is responsible for cultivating a healthy worship culture by making disciples, developing staff and servant leaders, and equipping teams to lead others toward Jesus through Christ-centered worship.

GENERAL RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Learn
    • Pursue a growing relationship with Jesus through consistent time in God’s Word and prayer.
    • Continually grow in your understanding of the Jesus-Centered Life (salvation, identity, life, and authority in Christ).
    • Remain teachable and hungry, seeking feedback, learning from others, and developing both spiritually and professionally.
    • Cultivate awareness of God’s presence in everyday life, listening to the Holy Spirit and responding in obedience.
  • Live
    • Practice and model the rhythms of Be the Church (Grow, Pray, Connect, and Share).
    • Pursue emotional health by engaging in self-awareness, addressing past wounds, and cultivating honest, healthy relationships.
    • Practice healthy rhythms, prioritizing your relationship with Jesus and your family
    • Embody a life of integrity and surrender, allowing your private life with God to shape your work.
  • Lead
    • Take ownership of disciple-making by personally investing in others and helping them move toward a Jesus-Centered Life.
    • Walk others through the Discipleship Pathway (Essentials → JCL → Be the Church), helping them discover and take their next step.
    • Shepherd people, not just programs, by listening for where God is at work in their story and walking with them toward transformation.
    • Equip and release others by developing Servant Leaders and multiplying disciples who Learn from Christ, Live in Christ, and Lead others to Christ.
    • Measure success by life change, spiritual formation, and multiplication—not just attendance or activity.
  • Embrace the Culture
    • Value and embody the staff values, which we call the 7 H’s: Humility, Honor, Honesty, Hunger, Holy Spirit, Health, and Harmony
    • Communicate clearly, honestly, and proactively in a way that builds trust, unity, and momentum.
    • Work in alignment with the church vision and leadership
    • Participate fully in the life of your campus or team, contributing to the unity, health, and shepherding of the faith family.

SPECIFIC LIST OF DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Provide leadership and oversight for all worship and production ministries and environments at the Madison Campus.
  • Recruit, equip, schedule, and develop staff and servant leaders.
  • Embody a Jesus-Centered Life and build a culture of discipleship in the Worship Ministry.
  • Supervise, coach, and develop the Worship Associate, Next Gen Worship Associate, and Production Director.
  • Partner with the Lead Pastor of Worship and the Pinelake Worship One Church Team to implement worship strategy, programming, and resources.
  • Contribute to the planning of weekend worship services and special events as led by One Church Team.
  • Build healthy ministry systems for planning, communication, scheduling, execution, and evaluation.
  • Establish ministry goals, evaluate effectiveness, and lead continuous improvement.
  • Steward ministry budgets, gear and resources with wisdom and accountability.
  • Work collaboratively with campus and One Church ministry leaders to support the overall mission of the church.
  • Complete administrative responsibilities and other duties as assigned.

SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES
Lead/supervise the Worship Associate, Next Gen Worship Pastor and Production Director.
Supervises and coordinates work with servant leaders.

QUALIFICATIONS
To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily. The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skill and/or ability required. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform essential functions.

EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE REQUIRED
Bachelor’s degree as a minimum. A four to six years of applicable experience leading worship as well as parallel leadership of staff as well as servant leaders. Must also exhibit proficiency in leading worship from a primary instrument.

LANGUAGE SKILLS
The individual must have excellent interpersonal skills, ability to work with a diverse group of people, communicate clearly and effectively on the telephone, e-mail and in person, demonstrating tact and diplomacy. Exceptional interpersonal skills are required to develop and maintain strong working relationships with volunteers, co-workers, the public and church members and regular attendees. The individual must have the ability to understand written or oral instructions; read, analyze and interpret complex documents, instructions manuals, policies and procedures is essential.

COMPUTER AND MATHEMATICAL SKILLS
The individual must have demonstrated skill in the use of Windows/MacOS to complete tasks, including word processing and spreadsheets and the ability to use the internet for information retrieval. The individual must have basic mathematical skills, knowledge of bookkeeping and basic accounting, and budget and expense monitoring. The individual must have the ability to read financial information and spreadsheets.

REASONING ABILITY
The individual must be able to define problems, collect data, establish facts, and draw valid conclusions; respond effectively to the most sensitive inquiries; simultaneous conceptualization and planning of multiple tasks, ability to project outcomes using different implementation strategies and ability to apply creative and innovative thinking to problem situations; and solve practical problems. The ability to work effectively and efficiently under stressful conditions to ensure deadlines are met is essential.

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to sit and talk or hear. The employee is required to stand, walk, and reach with hands and arms.

Must be able to lift up to 25 lbs.

The work environment characteristics described here are representative of those an employee encounters while performing the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

post_html:
Campus Staff Minister - Chicago (Graduate and Faculty Ministry)

Work Location:

Illinois

Job Type:

Full time

God has called InterVarsity to plant and to build witnessing communities of students and faculty who follow Jesus on college and university campuses. Through these groups, we believe ever- increasing numbers of students and faculty from all ethnic groups and areas of the campus will be transformed by the Gospel. We expect to see campuses increasingly become places where people, ideas, and structures flourish to the glory of God. We confidently anticipate that our InterVarsity alumni will become change agents across the country and around the world. We pursue this calling by discerning and actively participating in what God is already doing on campus. This is the essence of being a Campus Staff Minister (CSM).

Please submit the GFM Interest Form before completing the full application for a position with Graduate & Faculty Ministries in our online system. We will contact you when we are ready to proceed with the application process.​ 

We are open to part-time applicants working less than 40 hours/week. If you are interested in part-time work please apply for this position.

The pay range listed for this position is for an employee working 40 hours/week. Pay will be prorated for employees who work less than 40 hours/week. Additional pay (as a geographic adjustment) is available in high cost of living areas.

ESSENTIAL COMMITMENTS/RESPONSIBILITIES 

Spiritual Growth 

You pursue maturity as a disciple of Jesus Christ so that your life and work increasingly reflects a growing love for God, God’s Word, God’s people of every ethnicity and culture, and God’s purposes in the world. To do this, you will: 

  • Pursue a vibrant relationship with the triune God through engagement with Scripture, prayer, and worship, both individually and in community 

  • Develop self-leadership (growing in self-awareness, self-management, relational integrity, and resiliency) 

  • Embrace Scriptural standards for behavior and attitudes 

 

Campus Leadership 

You communicate and model InterVarsity’s vision to see students and faculty transformed, campuses renewed and world changers developed 

  • Create a culture of humble dependence on God and bold expectation in God’s intention to start new witnessing communities throughout the campus and on new campuses 

  • Model – in person and through programs – InterVarsity’s vision and Core Values, including a biblically-defined commitment to engage every ethnic and social group on campus 

  • Lead students and faculty – individually and collectively – through Scripture, prayer, teaching, and discipleship experiences, so that they articulate and align their ministry activities around this vision 

  • Set annual goals through prayer, research and reflection with your teams (students, faculty, and staff) for qualitative and quantitative growth, including conversions and leadership development 

 

You create, develop, align and leverage ministry plans, programs, teams, and structures to close the gap between current reality and the aspirational goals. 

  • Build leadership teams who trust and partner well with you and who demonstrate spiritual vitality, relational health, and mission alignment 

  • Develop and execute plans to achieve annual goals, evaluating and modifying the plan as needed throughout the year 

  • Increase momentum for the vision by aligning programs, structures, conferences and teams around the goals 

  • Mobilize students and faculty to engage their relational networks with the gospel and to start new missional communities 

  • Under the direction of the Area Director, may supervise Ministry Interns and Campus Ministry Interns as delegated 

 

You intentionally gather, invite, and develop diverse groups of students and faculty so that they not only encounter and follow Jesus as Savior and Lord but also advance the mission on campus as participants and leaders. 

  • Create ways for faculty and students to encounter and follow Jesus through Scripture, worship, prayer, mission experiences, conferences, etc. 

  • Equip students and faculty so that they think strategically about campus engagement and so that they proclaim – in word, deed, and power – the good news of Jesus, regularly inviting students and faculty to follow him as Savior and Lord 

  • Disciple students and faculty by equipping them to hear the Word, respond actively, and debrief and interpret the experience so that they grow in Christlikeness, reflect our Core Values, and develop ministry skills 

  • Invite, coach, and equip students and faculty to become increasingly effective participants and leaders, including starting new witnessing communities on campuses 

 

Organizational Collaboration 

You work with a network of other local, area, regional, and national InterVarsity staff and volunteers so that our work reflects Biblical standards of excellence, integrity, and partnership. 

  • Partner with and respond positively to the direction and coaching of your supervisors and national leaders 

  • Contribute to collaborative and productive team meetings and relationships 

  • Affiliate chapters under your care and submit Graduating Student Forms in order to increase our partnership with current students and alumni 

  • Use national ministry resources and tools, as requested, including recruiting and/or participating in local, regional, or national conferences as  

  • Complete reporting, planning and review requirements in a timely way so that you and your supervisors can assess and improve your work as a CSM 

  • Comply with all InterVarsity policies and procedures 

 

Ministry Partnership Development 

You will develop a team of partners – churches and individuals (including alumni and community members) – who will resource the ministry financially, in prayer, or volunteer service that advances the mission. 

  • Raise 100% of the financial budget assigned by your supervisor 

  • Communicate regularly with your ministry partners, nurturing the relationship through visits, phone calls, emails and regular prayer letters 

  • Develop on-going, long-lasting partnership with alumni and volunteers 

  • Comply with all Ministry Partnership Policies 

  • Identify and invest in advocates who will build networks of volunteers and donors on InterVarsity’s behalf 

 

Accomplish all other assigned tasks as appropriate 

 

QUALIFICATIONS (common to all levels of CSM) 

  • Annually affirm InterVarsity’s Statement of Agreement (Doctrinal Basis and Purpose Statement). Abide by InterVarsity’s Code of Conduct. Believe and behave consonantly with InterVarsity’s Human Sexuality Theological Paper. Affirm and behave consonantly with InterVarsity’s “Women in Ministry Statement of Affirmation” 

  • Bachelor’s degree for CSMs assigned to a four-year campus. A minimum of an Associate’s degree for CSMs assigned to a two-year campus or a community college 

  • Strong interpersonal skills (including ability to minister to diverse ethnic communities and faculty) 

  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills 

  • Demonstrated problem solving skills 

  • Familiarity with word processing, presentation, email, and spreadsheet software 

 

WORK ENVIRONMENT/PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS 

The CSM position leads ministry in a college campus environment. A designated office space may or may not be available. The CSM is required to travel to on-campus and off- campus sites as appropriate. Off-campus travel includes, but is not limited to: student ministry conferences, Ministry Partnership Development meetings, and InterVarsity- sponsored training sessions, meetings, and conferences. The CSM is regularly required to communicate with others, and routinely uses standard office equipment such as computers, phones, photocopiers, filing cabinets, etc. 

Pay Range: $44,016.00 - $58,680.00 per year

Pay: This position is funded through personal fundraising. Accordingly, compensation will vary based on the ability of the individual to secure a donor team to fund the cost of his/her salary. The anticipated salary range for this position on a full-time basis (40 hours/week) is dependent on a variety of factors, including location and cost of living. The actual salary received, including any geographic adjustment to account for location and cost of living, is subject to the individual’s ability to raise funds necessary to cover the full amount of such salary within the range set forth in the job posting details.

Benefits:

We offer a competitive benefits package, including health care and retirement savings with a match. Eligibility is based on employee type and hours worked.  Benefits include the following:

  • 403(b) Retirement Savings Plan

  • 403(b) matching contributions

  • Dental insurance

  • Employee assistance program

  • Employee discounts

  • Flexible work schedule

  • Flexible spending accounts

  • Health insurance

  • Health savings account

  • Life insurance

  • Paid time off

  • Parental leave

  • Professional development assistance

  • Vision insurance

Equal Employment Opportunity: 

 

InterVarsity Christian Fellowship/USA is both an equal opportunity employer and a faith-based religious organization. We conduct hiring without regard to race, color, ancestry, national origin, citizenship, age, sex, marital status, parental status, membership in any labor organization, political ideology, or disability of an otherwise qualified individual. The status of InterVarsity Christian Fellowship/USA as an equal opportunity employer does not prevent the organization from hiring staff based on their religious beliefs so that all staff share the same religious commitment.  Pursuant to the Civil Rights Act of 1964, Section 702 (42 U.S.C. 2000e 1(a)) InterVarsity Christian Fellowship/USA has the right to, and does, hire only candidates who agree with InterVarsity’s Statement of Agreement: Purpose and Doctrinal Basis because InterVarsity believes that each and every staff plays a vital role in advancing InterVarsity’s mission and purposes.

ABOUT WOODDALE CHURCH

Wooddale Church is a multigenerational, Bible-teaching church in Minnesota with campuses in Eden Prairie, Edina, and the University of Minnesota. With a mission to honor God by making more disciples for Jesus Christ, Wooddale has a rich history and a future of sharing the gospel locally and globally by planting churches, supporting global partners, and serving its local community.

OVERVIEW

The Children’s Ministry Program Director leads a thriving Woods Kids ministry at the Edina campus by building teams, developing leaders, and equipping volunteers to help children know and follow Jesus. Serving children ages six weeks through fourth grade and their families, this leader creates safe, welcoming, gospel-centered environments where children experience God’s love, families find belonging, and volunteers serve with confidence and joy. We’re looking for a relational, proactive leader with the initiative to grow ministry and the discipline to follow through. Leading with joy and generosity, this person sees potential in people, invites them into meaningful ministry, and provides them the training, encouragement, and ownership they need to lead well. They bring both a heart for people and an appreciation for clear systems, strengthening established practices and helping develop better ones where needed. As an active member of both the Edina campus staff and Wooddale’s broader Children’s Ministry team, the director contributes to shared planning, learning, and ministry alignment. The director implements shared curriculum, ministry strategy, and safety standards while adapting delivery to the Edina campus. 

RESPONSIBILITIES

Build teams and develop leaders

  • Recruit, onboard, equip, and retain volunteers for nursery, preschool, elementary, and ministry support teams.
  • Identify and develop team captains and other volunteer leaders who can lead people, own ministry responsibilities, and equip others.
  • Delegate meaningful responsibility with clear expectations, appropriate decision-making authority, resources, and regular coaching.
  • Establish consistent rhythms of training, prayer, encouragement, feedback, and appreciation that strengthen volunteers’ faith and effectiveness.
  • Develop team depth and dependable coverage so ministry runs well across services, seasons, and leadership absences.

Lead an excellent children’s ministry

  • Oversee Sunday morning and Wednesday evening Woods Kids programming, ensuring age-appropriate biblical teaching, meaningful relationships, and engaging experiences.
  • Equip teams to prepare and lead every part of the ministry experience, including check-in, classrooms, teaching, worship, activities, and transitions.
  • Maintain a visible, relational presence with children, families, and volunteers; model excellent ministry and coach others through hands-on involvement.
  • Plan and lead campus children’s and family ministry events, including VBS and outreach opportunities, in partnership with campus and Children’s Ministry staff.

Partner with parents and welcome families

  • Build trusting relationships with parents and caregivers, equipping them with practical resources and encouragement to nurture faith at home.
  • Create a welcoming experience for new families, with clear next steps and timely, personal follow-up.
  • Communicate proactively with families and volunteers about ministry plans, schedules, expectations, and opportunities.
  • Respond thoughtfully to family needs and concerns, coordinating additional care and support with appropriate staff.

Strengthen systems and steward resources

  • Maintain clear, dependable processes for volunteer onboarding and scheduling, classroom preparation, attendance, communication, and guest follow-up.
  • Implement Wooddale’s child safety policies and procedures, including volunteer screening, check-in and release, supervision, and incident reporting; ensure teams understand and follow them.
  • Use established church tools and shared processes consistently. Identify gaps, recommend improvements, and help document and implement approved changes.
  • Plan ahead for staffing, space, supplies, and ministry growth; steward assigned resources and spending within approved budgets.
  • Review participation, volunteer engagement, family feedback, and ministry effectiveness with the Campus Pastor, translating observations into practical improvements.

Collaborate and move ministry forward

  • Translate campus vision and shared Children’s Ministry direction into clear goals, plans, and team responsibilities.
  • Participate actively in campus, Children’s Ministry, and churchwide staff rhythms, contributing ideas and following through on commitments.
  • Work constructively across teams, communicate capacity and priorities early, and address differences with humility, clarity, and respect.
  • Pursue opportunities to reach new families and expand ministry capacity while sustaining healthy teams and dependable execution.

QUALIFICATIONS

  • Spiritual maturity: A growing relationship with Jesus, a heart for children and families, and a life marked by integrity, prayer, humility, and service.
  • Proven team leadership: Demonstrated success recruiting, developing, and retaining volunteers or leading comparable teams, with evidence of equipping others to own responsibilities.
  • Relational strength: Warmth, emotional maturity, sound judgment, and the ability to build trust with children, parents, volunteers, and colleagues from varied backgrounds.
  • Initiative and execution: A self-directed approach, healthy ambition for ministry growth, and the ability to turn ideas into realistic plans and completed work.
  • Organizational ability: Strong planning, communication, delegation, and follow-through; comfort using ministry technology and maintaining clear, repeatable processes.
  • Collaborative leadership: Ability to contribute to multiple teams, receive feedback, navigate shared expectations, and remain accountable to campus leadership.
  • Ministry understanding: Experience in children’s ministry or a related setting, with an understanding of age-appropriate discipleship, child development, and safe ministry practices.
  • Church commitment: Affirm Wooddale’s Statement of Faith and Covenant; support its mission, vision, values, and leadership; participate regularly in worship and become or remain a member in good standing.

RELATIONSHIPS
• Reports to the Edina Campus Pastor
• Works collaboratively with Edina Staff & Eden Prairie Children’s Ministry Staff

SCHEDULE & WORKING EXPECTATIONS
This full-time role includes weekday responsibilities, Sunday mornings, Wednesday evenings, and occasional additional evening or weekend events. The primary work location is the Edina campus, with occasional travel to other campuses for meetings, training, and shared ministry activities. The Campus Pastor establishes the regular schedule and on-site expectations. The director participates in regular supervisor meetings, campus and Children’s Ministry meetings, full-staff gatherings, and staff development. 

BENEFITS & COMPENSATION
Wooddale Church offers a comprehensive benefits package for all 40+ hour full-time employees, which includes opportunities to elect Medical (30+ hour full-time), Dental, Life/AD&D, HSA, Flex, LTD, optional Vision, optional Life/AD&D, and a 403(b) retirement plan with company match and immediate vesting. Projected salary is $55,00 - $65,000 depending upon experience and qualifications.

OTHER DUTIES
This description outlines the role’s primary responsibilities and is not an exhaustive list. Duties and responsibilities may change as ministry needs develop.

WORK ENVIRONMENT/PHYSICAL DEMANDS

The Children’s Ministry role requires the ability to be physically present and actively engaged in a dynamic ministry environment involving children, families, volunteers, classrooms, worship spaces, and ministry events. 
 • Ability to remain on one’s feet for extended periods, including standing, walking, and moving throughout classrooms, hallways, worship spaces, and event areas.

• Ability to frequently walk, bend, stoop, kneel, reach, and move between different ministry environments as needed.

• Ability to safely interact with and supervise children in a variety of settings and activities.

• Ability to lift, carry, push, or move ministry supplies, equipment, boxes, tables, chairs, and other materials as needed.

• Ability to assist with setup, teardown, room preparation, activities, transitions, and special events such as Camp Woods Kids (VBS) and family outreach events.

• Ability to work in an active environment that may include varying noise levels, frequent movement, and interaction with groups of children and adults.

• Visual requirements: Ability to read printed and electronic materials, schedules, signage, attendance information, safety procedures, communication materials, and computer screens; ability to visually observe children, volunteers, activities, room conditions, and safety concerns. 

• Hearing requirements: Ability to hear and respond to verbal communication from children, parents, volunteers, staff members, and ministry leaders in individual and group settings; ability to hear announcements, instructions, alarms, and other safety-related sounds. 

• Ability to communicate effectively in person and through electronic and other standard workplace communication methods.

• Ability to safely perform the essential physical functions of the position, with or without reasonable accommodation.

• Physical demands may vary based on ministry programming, special events, seasonal activities, and campus needs.

Reasonable accommodations may be provided to enable qualified individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions of the position.

Other Duties

Please note this job description is not designed to cover or contain a comprehensive listing of activities, duties or responsibilities that are required of the employee for this job. Duties, responsibilities and activities may change at any time with or without notice.

JOB DESCRIPTION:
The University of Vermont Medical Center (UVMMC) seeks a Clinical Pastoral Education (CPE) Partner who is an ACPE (Association for Clinical Pastoral Education) Certified Educator. The CPE Partner is responsible for creating, implementing, and overseeing the organization’s Clinical Pastoral Education Program. This role provides leadership for all aspects of CPE, including program administration, curriculum design, student recruitment and supervision, accreditation management, educational quality, and strategic program development. The CPE Partner serves as the organization’s subject matter expert in clinical pastoral education and collaborates with spiritual care, clinical, academic, and organizational leaders to integrate experiential spiritual care education throughout the health system. The CPE Partner cultivates a learning environment grounded in respect, curiosity, cultural humility, and openness to diverse beliefs, perspectives, identities, and lived experiences. The successful candidate demonstrates a commitment to fostering belonging, compassionate dialogue, and equitable learning experiences for students, colleagues, patients, families, and community partners.

The CPE Partner develops and maintains educational programs that meet ACPE standards and competencies, ensuring ongoing compliance with accreditation requirements, policies, reporting obligations, and continuous quality improvement expectations. The CPE program cohort size and frequency may vary based on learner demand, accreditation requirements, educator assessment, and program maturity. Typical program offerings may include multiple educational units annually, often including fall, winter, and summer intensive internship experiences, with approximately 4 to 8 students participating in each unit. The position is responsible for recruiting, mentoring, supervising, and evaluating CPE students and, as the program evolves, residents and other pastoral learners. The CPE Partner administers the operational and educational components necessary to sustain a high-quality accredited program, including program planning, learner assessment, documentation, and outcomes evaluation.

Through strategic leadership, the CPE Partner advances the growth, innovation, and long-term sustainability of Clinical Pastoral Education at UVMMC and across UVM Health. This includes developing partnerships with clinical and academic stakeholders within the Medical Group, identifying innovative learning opportunities at UVMMC and partner sites, expanding clinical training experiences beyond our academic medical center and into home health and hospice, community-based hospital partners, and more rural settings. The CPE Partner will lead efforts toward the development of CPE residency programs and a comprehensive pastoral education pathway that supports the mission, values, workforce needs, and strategic priorities of the organization.

EDUCATION:
Certification as an Associate, or fully certified Supervisor of Clinical Pastoral Education by the Association of Clinical Pastoral Education, Inc.


EXPERIENCE:

Minimum of 3–5 years of progressively responsible experience in hospital chaplaincy, including demonstrated experience in Clinical Pastoral Education, educational supervision, teaching, mentoring, and program leadership. Prior experience serving as an ACPE Certified Educator or Associate Certified
Educator strongly preferred.

St. Patrick Catholic Church, Laurie, MO, the National Shrine of Mary, Mother of the Church and the mission parish, St Philip Benizi Church in Versailles, MO, are seeking a Director of Liturgy and Music. This pastoral leader will build, strengthen, and take to the next level our current teams to model and renew all things in the liturgy & music ministry of the parish community and the Shrine. It builds and equips teams of engaged volunteers to implement the Shrine and parish's mission and vision into the liturgical life.

A practicing Catholic in good standing with Church who:
-acts as a role model within and outside the parish community;
-shares the treasures and truths of the Catholic faith with others;
-works collaboratively to enhance the life of the Shrine & parish community;
-strives to be a good steward of the blessings of the community;
-positively engages with others for the sake of the Shrine and parish.

SUMMARY

The Connections Minister is responsible for casting the vision, strategically planning and daily implementing the activities and atmosphere of the Connections ministry at Pinelake’s Madison Campus. The role is also responsible for developing, implementing and sustaining processes and systems for continued connecting, developing and multiplying of leaders and teams as well as implementing the One Church vision of connecting the Madison community to their next step. This person lives out their gifting of hospitality and helps guides members and guests from first impression to next steps, including hosting Essentials.

GENERAL RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Learn
    • Pursue a growing relationship with Jesus through consistent time in God’s Word and prayer.
    • Continually grow in your understanding of the Jesus-Centered Life (salvation, identity, life, and authority in Christ).
    • Remain teachable and hungry, seeking feedback, learning from others, and developing both spiritually and professionally.
    • Cultivate awareness of God’s presence in everyday life, listening to the Holy Spirit and responding in obedience.
  • Live
    • Practice and model the rhythms of Be the Church (Grow, Pray, Connect, and Share).
    • Pursue emotional health by engaging in self-awareness, addressing past wounds, and cultivating honest, healthy relationships.
    • Practice healthy rhythms, prioritizing your relationship with Jesus and your family
    • Embody a life of integrity and surrender, allowing your private life with God to shape your work.
  • Lead
    • Take ownership of disciple-making by personally investing in others and helping them move toward a Jesus-Centered Life.
    • Walk others through the Discipleship Pathway (Essentials → JCL → Be the Church), helping them discover and take their next step.
    • Shepherd people, not just programs, by listening for where God is at work in their story and walking with them toward transformation.
    • Equip and release others by developing Servant Leaders and multiplying disciples who Learn from Christ, Live in Christ, and Lead others to Christ.
    • Measure success by life change, spiritual formation, and multiplication—not just attendance or activity.
  • Embrace the Culture
    • Value and embody the staff values, which we call the 7 H’s: Humility, Honor, Honesty, Hunger, Holy Spirit, Health, and Harmony
    • Communicate clearly, honestly, and proactively in a way that builds trust, unity, and momentum.
    • Work in alignment with the church vision and leadership
    • Participate fully in the life of your campus or team, contributing to the unity, health, and shepherding of the faith family.

  • Develop plan for creating and implementing welcoming environment for all attendees of Pinelake’s Madison Campus.
  • Develop an effective leader recruitment strategy that is reproducible and sufficient for meeting the goals of the ministry.
  • Build and lead a team that consists of servant leaders who champion the vision and mission of Pinelake Church.
  • Cast Pinelake’s Vision and Mission for the discipleship pathway amongst our Connections Teams regularly.
  • Utilize ROCK (church management system) as the main communication among leaders, members, and pastors. Equip the entire ministry in the same way.
