Senior Pastor - Fellowship Alliance Chapel 
 

Fellowship Alliance Chapel (FAC) is seeking its next Senior Pastor who, with God’s direction, will lead us into the next season of ministry in southern New Jersey. God has moved through FAC for over 40 years in Medford, NJ. The role of Senior Pastor at FAC is accountable to a plurality of elders and helps give leadership to over 20 staff.

Our church is a member of the Christian and Missionary Alliance, elder governed, and staff led with a mix of ages, represented across all levels of our ministry. The average weekend attendance is about 1,200 people. FAC has an annual operating budget of ~$4M with stewardship of multiple buildings on campus as well as a lake/summer day camp. Our current ministry program includes family support ministries, extensive programs for adults, children and youth, as well as care ministries, and missions. Trinity Preparatory Christian School also partners with FAC in leasing our facilities for their operational use.

Our theological tradition is evangelical. While our church is solidly committed to the Christian and Missionary Alliance as our denominational family, we would consider candidates with theological beliefs compatible with our Alliance heritage but have served in other independent or evangelical fellowships. The Senior Pastor is required to complete licensing and ordination (or sustain prior ordination) with the Christian and Missionary Alliance.

Our church building is in Medford, New Jersey. Located 45 minutes from Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, and 60 minutes from the Jersey shore, Medford serves as a hub for professionals and families in this region. There are five high schools within a 20-minute drive from the church, demonstrating the church’s central location to the surrounding townships. Members of the congregation live in these communities as well as many other townships beyond a 20-minute commute. There is great variety in neighborhoods when choosing where to live, with amenities that appeal to families. The public schools report strong graduation rates and college admission.

FAC is a single-site, multigenerational congregation committed to a mission that more and more people would live a Jesus-centered and missionally engaged life. Within the last ten years the church completed a campus building project, located on the same property with its original building in Medford, NJ. FAC has been the recipient of generous land donations where the Senior Pastor will need to partner with the elder board and financial committee to navigate future debt reduction and giving campaigns.

 Required Qualifications:
    Seminary education or equivalent ministry preparation
    Minimum 5-10 years senior pastoral experience
    Strong expository preaching and teaching abilities
    Demonstrated leadership in staff management and organizational development
    Experience with financial stewardship and capital campaigns preferred
    Christian & Missionary Alliance ordination required (or willingness to obtain)
    Theological alignment with evangelical and C&MA beliefs
    Must be a US Citizen

FAC offers a generous compensation package including salary, benefits, retirement plan contributions, and parsonage housing available to the Senior Pastor.

post_html:
Mission & Grace Español Pastor

Grace Community Church & Grace Español | Roswell, New Mexico Full-Time

About Grace Community Church

Since 1998, Grace Community Church has been on a singular mission: helping Roswell find and fulfill God's purpose for their lives. What began with 90 people gathered in a living room has grown into a thriving congregation. Two years ago, Grace was averaging 750 people each weekend. Today, with the addition of Grace Español, they are running over 950 a weekend. That is roughly 27% growth in two years, and the momentum is still building. Grace is an interdenominational, purpose-driven community church, built not on denominational tradition but on God's clear purposes that meet the deepest needs of people.

The staff team is unified, deeply relational, and marked by humor, grace, and genuine care for one another. When one person on the team struggles, everyone shows up. In 2025, under Senior Pastor Nate's leadership, Grace celebrated 63 baptisms and 100 new members. The church's vision is captured in the G.R.A.C.E. framework, Grow, Reach, Adore, Connect, Equip, and every ministry, budget, and calendar event flows from these five purposes. The goal is always the same: help people move from the edges of the community into a life fully surrendered to Christ and sent on mission.

Grace's primary global mission partnership is with New Vision Latin America Missions, supporting church planting and discipleship development across Venezuela, Panama, Brazil, and Spain. The heart of this church has always been turned toward the Spanish-speaking world.

About Grace Español

Grace Español is a growing Spanish-language congregation, one church with two languages, united in mission, vision, and leadership. Now in its third year, Grace Español gathers 60–75 adults each week. It is still in a season of formation, and that is not a weakness. It is an invitation. The right leader will find real freedom here to pray, build, and shape a congregation that reflects the beauty and depth of the community it serves. The groundwork has been laid by faithful people. What is needed now is a pastor who carries both the shepherd's heart and the builder's hands to take it forward.

You can find more information about Grace Community Church HERE. 



About the Role

This is not a translator's role or a satellite ministry. This is a full pastoral calling for a bilingual leader who can stand in two worlds with equal confidence and bring them together around one gospel.

As Lead Pastor of Grace Español, you will provide primary spiritual leadership, preaching weekly in Spanish, developing leaders from within the congregation, shepherding families through the joys and hardships of life, and casting vision for what Grace Español is becoming.

As Missions Pastor for Grace Community Church, you will champion local outreach, particularly within Roswell's large and underserved Spanish-speaking community, while coordinating the church's international mission partnerships, including 1–2 international trips per year.

This role reports directly to the Senior Pastor and serves as a full and equal member of the pastoral team.

The Opportunity

You may already know this world.

You may have grown up in a home where Spanish was the first language spoken in the morning. You may have watched your parents or grandparents work hard, build community, and hold their faith quietly but deeply. You may know what it feels like to belong to two cultures at once, and you may have spent years wondering how God would use that.

This is how.

Roswell is a city where more than 60% of the population, roughly 29,000 people, identify as Hispanic or Latino. More than a third of residents speak a language other than English at home. Chaves County is one of New Mexico's most productive agricultural regions, with more than two dozen dairy farms, expansive cattle ranches, and large-scale farming operations across the Pecos Valley. These industries are sustained in large part by Spanish-speaking workers, including families who have been here for generations alongside seasonal and migrant laborers who come to work the land. Many find themselves far from community, far from belonging, and far from a church that can speak to their lives in the language of their heart.

These are your neighbors. And many of them have never heard the gospel from someone who sounds like home. 

Who Thrives Here

A Bilingual Shepherd. You preach, counsel, pray, and lead with equal confidence in Spanish and English. You move between worlds naturally because you have lived in both.

A Builder with Vision. Grace Español is still taking shape. You are not looking for a finished ministry to manage. You are looking for open ground to cultivate, and you know how to build something that lasts.

A Missional Heart. You feel the weight of a community that is largely unreached. You build trust slowly and relationships deeply, and you know that the most important ministry often happens outside the church building, at the soccer field, at the school, at the kitchen table.

A Team Player. You thrive in a high-trust environment where people say what they mean and have each other's backs. You value the wisdom of shared leadership and you bring your full self to the team.

A Faithful Administrator. You follow through. You communicate well. You work within systems without losing your pastoral instincts, and you steward what you have been given with care and accountability.

Qualifications

  • Fluent in Spanish and English; the ability to preach and pastor in Spanish is essential
  • A clear calling to pastoral ministry, demonstrated through fruit, not just credentials
  • Strong preaching and teaching ability in both languages
  • A bachelor's degree in Biblical Studies or Ministry is preferred. Formal theological training through an accredited ministry certificate program will also be considered.
  • 3–5 years of vocational ministry experience
  • Experience leading or serving in a Spanish-speaking congregation preferred
  • Experience in community outreach or local missions preferred
  • Married candidates preferred; family participation in ministry is valued
  • Alignment with Grace Community Church's doctrine, mission, and values
Compensation: $55,000–$65,000+ commensurate with experience. Benefits include full family medical, life insurance, disability, cell phone reimbursement, retirement, and a ministry budget.





About Roswell, New Mexico

Roswell is a city where you will not feel like an outsider. More than 60% of residents identify as Hispanic or Latino, Spanish is woven into the fabric of everyday life, and the culture of the Pecos Valley reflects generations of families who built something meaningful here in the high desert of southeastern New Mexico.

The city is a regional hub anchored by agriculture, oil and gas, healthcare, and education. The cost of living is well below national averages, housing is affordable, and the pace of life allows for the kind of deep, unhurried relationships that make ministry possible. Chaves County leads New Mexico in dairy production and is home to significant ranching and farming operations that draw workers and families from across the Spanish-speaking world.

For those who love the outdoors, Roswell delivers. The city maintains nearly 700 acres of parks and 11 miles of trails. Bottomless Lakes State Park, Bitter Lake National Wildlife Refuge, and the Pecos River are minutes away. Carlsbad Caverns, White Sands National Park, and the mountain resort town of Ruidoso are all within two hours. The Roswell Museum and Art Center, the Anderson Museum of Contemporary Art, and a lively calendar of community events, including the annual Roswell Jazz Festival, round out a city that has far more texture and life than most people expect.

This is a place where you can raise your family, know your neighbors, and do ministry that matters for a long time.

The Invitation

Grace is a family. They are large enough to make a real impact and close enough to feel it personally. They are a people of grace and forgiveness, and they are ready to welcome the right person not just onto their staff, but into their life.

Grace Español is young. It is still becoming. And it needs someone who has been shaped by both worlds to help it find its voice, its depth, and its reach.

If you grew up navigating two languages and two cultures and have spent your life wondering how God would use all of that, the answer might be Roswell. Come meet this family. Come see this city. Come be part of something that is still being written.

post_html:
Mary, Queen of Peace Catholic Church is looking for a Director of Youth and Young Adult
Ministry. This is a full-time position.

As the Director of Youth and Young Adult Ministry, the individual is responsible for the leadership
and direction of Middle School (5-6), Jr. High (7-8), and High School (8-12) Youth Ministry
Programs - all under the umbrella of PAX Youth - as well as Young Adult (ages 18-35) Initiatives.

This individual will support and collaborate with the current PAX Youth team members who oversee
praise, worship, Bible studies, and community nights. In addition, this pastoral team member will
develop a dynamic middle school program and offer a fresh, innovative, and sustainable approach to
forming our youth into intentional disciples of Christ.

The Director of Youth and Young Adult Ministry will also implement a comprehensive program of
Christian life development for the 18– to 35-year-old, college, career, single, and married adults
in our community. It is essential that this person be able to connect with young adults on a social
and spiritual level, with the intent of coaching them toward Christ-like maturity. The Director of
Youth and Young Adult Ministry collaborates with other Pastoral Team members in developing and
implementing an engaging and life- giving youth faith formation model as well as ensuring
continuity with the Order of Christian Initiation process.

As Director of Youth and Young Adult Ministry, the individual's behavior is required to be
consistent with culture and cores values of Mary, Queen of Peace Catholic Church:

Fundamentally Relational: As fundamentally relational beings, made in the image of our
relational God, we engage in relationships by being attentive and present to those we serve and
serve alongside.
Mission Driven: We put the Lamb of God at the forefront of all that we do, aligning ourselves
to the collective mission of fostering life-changing encounters with Jesus.
Innovatively Excellent: Ensuring quality and excellence, we transcend expectations by thinking
beyond the norm to meet the needs of today.
Radically Hospitable: We are committed to radical hospitality, to be a place for doubters and
disciples, for people with deep questions and deep convictions; all have a home here with us.

Ministerial Character

The Pastor is the visible principle and foundation of unity in Mary, Queen of Peace Catholic Church
which the Archbishop has entrusted to him. He makes Christ's mission present and enduring in the
parish. In order to fulfill his mission, the Pastor employs suitable, chosen collaborators
(clerics, religious, or laypeople). He shares with them his mission and entrusts various
responsibilities to them.

Positions employed at Mary, Queen of Peace Catholic Church help to extend the ministry of the
Pastor in particular ways as outlined in the job description. Therefore, the employee in this
position is closely connected to and assists the Pastor in the performance of his ministry and
thereby engages in ministry for the Church.

Job Summary
As the Director of Youth and Young Adult Ministry, the individual will be responsible for
continuing and enhancing the current PAX Youth program, which has embraced the Ablaze model of
youth ministry, empowering volunteers to form, lead, and transform youth into intentional disciples
of Jesus Christ. The Director of Youth and Young Adult Ministry oversees the development and
implementation of the Confirmation Program, including the formation, retreat, liturgical
celebration, and other requirements as deemed by the pastor and Archdiocese. This team member
provides vision, formation, and collaboration for a team of adult and youth volunteers who
currently oversee high school youth ministry; this pastoral team member is also tasked with
building middleschool and junior high programs as well as young adult ministry to expand our mission field. A
comprehensive ministry plan would involve regular gatherings, ministry nights, seasonal events,
retreats, service opportunities, and mission trips for youth, college students, and young adults.

The position reports to the Pastor, collaborates with the clergy, pastoral and administrative
staff, and operates with latitude for the use of independent judgment and initiative. The Director
of Youth and Young Adult Ministry must understand the nature and purpose of religious education,
youth formation, and pastoral ministry, while working with the pastor and parish staff, the youth
ministry volunteers, parents, and parishioners. This individual will be expected to demonstrate
good public relations skills, as well as teaching skills.

Essential Duties: (Overarching)
Support and uphold the teachings of the Catholic Church and the mission of the parish in both
your professional and personal life.
Act as a witness to Gospel values by modeling the teachings of the Roman Catholic Church.
Continuously grow in your ministry by participating in ongoing professional and personal faith
formation.
Ensure compliance with all Archdiocese of New Orleans policies and procedures including Safe
Environment protocols.
Participate in parish staff and diocesan meetings and trainings.
Maintain a work schedule that maximizes availability and accessibility.

Essential Duties: (Director of Youth and Young Adult Ministry)
Enhance and build upon the current model of high school (8-12 grade) ministry, with formation,
community building, and leadership formation.
Work collaboratively with the Director of Children's Formation and our Catholic School on
creating a vibrant middle school (5-6) and junior high (7-
8) youth program.
Collaborate with our Catholic School and the Dean of Christian Formation in the development of
the 5th, 6th, and 7th grade school retreats and other initiatives to enhance parish and school
relationship.

Oversee a comprehensive preparation program for the sacrament of Confirmation as well as all
necessary coordination for the liturgical celebration of Confirmation.
Provide appropriate training for the adults and young people in leadership positions.
Foster the involvement of young people in the life of the parish, including serving in various
ministerial roles, serving on various parish committees, and being involved in parish activities.
Coordinate the outreach to and evangelization of all young people in the parish.
Recruit, train, and provide support for Youth Ministry volunteers.
Collaborate with the Director of Evangelization, Engagement, and Adult Formation on enhancing
our Young Adult Ministry.

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities
Knowledge of the structure and basic teachings of the Roman Catholic Church.
Knowledge of ministry of catechesis
Skill in communicating with diverse audiences both oral and written.
Ability to operate various word-processing software, spreadsheets, and database
programs.
Ability to excel in professional relationships and work effectively with staff, clergy, and
laity.
Ability to organize, prioritize, carry out multiple tasks, meet deadlines and utilize
effective time management techniques.
Ability to maintain confidentiality at all times.
Ability to follow instructions furnished in verbal or written format.

Minimum Qualifications
Bachelor's degree from an accredited college or university with coursework in theology,
religious education, pastoral ministry, or a related field is preferred.
Experience in pastoral ministry is preferred.
Must be a practicing Roman Catholic in good standing with the Church.

Interested applicants should send a cover letter, resume, and at least three references to
kbaker@maryqueenofpeace.org. For questions or additional information, please contact our Director
of Parish Operations and Stewardship, Karen Baker, at (985) 202- 0232.

Part-Time, Hourly, Non-Exempt. Availability on Sunday mornings (4-5 hours), plus Approximately 12-15 hours During the Week, and Occasional Special Events.

Benefits:  Paid Time Off for Sick and Jury Duty

 

REQUIRED:    Resume and completed St. Andrew’s Employment Application.                 

 

SUMMARY

The Kids Ministry Curriculum and Resource Coordinator at St. Andrew’s Presbyterian supports the mission and vision of Children’s Ministries by providing organizational support and structure to events and programming. The role focuses on preparing and managing curriculum, maintaining ministry resources, and equipping volunteers with the tools they need to succeed.  This coordinator is well organized and delights in details in the support of discipleship excellence.

 

ESSENTIAL ROLE & RESPONSIBILITIES

 

Curriculum and Teaching Support

  • Prepare, organize and distribute curriculum materials for all Children’s Ministry programs and classrooms.
  • Ensure curriculum is printed, assembled, and distributed in advance for weekly ministry use (preparing monthly).
  • Organize and maintain curriculum, resource systems, archives, and teaching materials for easy access.
  • Serve as a resource for volunteers who need to supplement their lesson plans.
  • Available to teach and/or lead programming with children as needed.

 

Resource and Supply Management

  • Organize, maintain, and improve children’s ministry resource rooms, supply closets and storage spaces.
  • Create systems that keep materials labeled, stocked, and easily accessible.
  • Monitor inventory and order supplies, craft items, and ministry resources as needed, for both Sunday morning programs and special events, such as VBS.
  • Plan and coordinate regular workdays to organize, clean and maintain ministry spaces.

 

Events and Ministry Support

  • Assist with planning and preparation for special events, such as VBS, Fall Fest, and other outreach and family events.
  • Provide a welcoming and loving environment for children, parents and volunteers when serving in a Children’s Ministry classroom.
  • Help coordinate materials, logistics and volunteer support for ministry events.
  • Participate in Children’s Ministry team meetings and training opportunities.  


Qualifications

QUALIFICATIONS & EXPECTATIONS

  • Agreement with and support of the mission, vision, and values of St. Andrews Presbyterian.
  • Bachelor’s degree with at least 2 years experience working with children.

  • Experience with ProPresenter and Planning Center preferred.

High School Student Pastor

Christian Life Center is an Assemblies of God church in the Dayton area with a passion for Spirit-led worship, genuine community, and reaching the next generation. We believe that students are not the future of the Church — they are the Church right now. Our NextGen ministry exists to call students into a real, lasting relationship with Jesus and to equip them to live it out loud. We are looking for someone who shares that conviction and is ready to build something that lasts.
 
The Role
 
The High School Student Pastor leads our 9th–12th grade student ministry with vision, relational depth, and organizational excellence. This is not a program manager position — it is a shepherd role. You will teach God's Word with clarity and conviction, build a volunteer culture that multiplies your impact, partner with parents as the primary spiritual leaders of their students, and create an environment where students encounter Jesus and grow into who He has called them to be.
 
This role requires someone who can lead from both the front and the side — a communicator who moves a room and a pastor who knows students by name.

Lead and Teach
  • Deliver relevant, biblically sound weekly and midweek teaching to High School students
  • Lead small groups that create real accountability, discipleship, and spiritual growth
  • Speak into students' everyday lives — not just on Sunday
Build and Develop
  • Recruit, train, and invest in a healthy team of adult volunteer leaders
  • Identify and develop student leaders within the ministry
  • Partner with parents, equipping and communicating with them as the front line of spiritual formation
Create and Execute
  • Oversee worship and creative arts within the High School ministry, drawing primarily from student talent
  • Plan and execute events that connect students relationally — and open doors for their unchurched friends
  • Develop and steward a ministry budget with integrity and attention to detail
Collaborate and Serve
  • Work closely with the NextGen Team and broader CLC staff to advance a unified ministry vision
  • Participate in district Assemblies of God student ministry events and activities
  • Fulfill general pastoral responsibilities at CLC — weddings, funerals, congregational care — as needed
What You’ll Bring
  • Bachelor's degree required; Ministry, Theology, or Christian Education preferred
  • Ordained or licensed with the Assemblies of God — or willing and eligible to pursue credentialing
  • 3+ years of experience leading in student ministry
  • A genuine shepherd's heart and the organizational capacity to back it up
  • Strong communicator — equally comfortable in front of 200 students or around a small group table
  • A team builder who leads with humility, vision, and accountability
  • Models a healthy personal, marriage, and family life consistent with biblical leadership
  • Active, growing faith and full alignment with CLC's mission, values, and Assemblies of God doctrine
  • Must successfully complete a background check prior to employment

  • Employer paid Disability Coverage (Short-Term and Long-Term)
  • 13 Paid Holidays
  • Generous Paid Time Off Schedule

Why Join CLC?

Description

Leads a team effort to support spiritual vitality throughout Landis Homes. Is alert to gifts of the residents and encourages their use in the spiritual life of the community.

  • Gives leadership to the Pastoral Services team, supervises chaplains and coordinator.
  • Responsible for Pastoral Care of residents residing in Residential Living. Assists with visits in Personal Care and Healthcare.
  • Visits new residents in Residential Living.
  • Attends Residential Living interdisciplinary meetings and consults with interdisciplinary team as needed.
  • Plans with chaplains for hospital visitation while a resident is hospitalized.
  • Participates in department on-call rotation.
  • Organizes and resources volunteer chaplains to provide resident visits in coordination with other chaplains.
  • Preaches or leads worship/songs in Sunday morning services as needed.
  • In collaboration with the Pastoral Services team, plans special services such as Communion, Good Friday, and Service of Remembrance.
  • Provides end of life support, coordinates Walk of Honor, and assists families, pastors, and funeral directors in planning memorial services as needed.
  • Assists Director of Organizational Communications & Church Relations with planning the annual clergy breakfast and by attending church conferences.
  • Actively participates in the Operations team.
  • Represents Landis Homes and aging services, along with other Pastoral Services team members, through availability to speak and preach as requested by congregations and others. Also refers speaker requests to appropriate individuals on the Speakers Resource list.
  • Listens to interests and needs of congregations as they seek to meet the needs of aging members and families/caregivers, and represents these interests to Landis Homes as we consider new ways to serve and partner with congregations.
  • Provides, or arranges for, educational seminars/articles on the spirituality of aging adults and pastoral concerns for residents, staff, family members and other interested people.
  • Develops and reviews strategic plan annually and identifies action plans to achieve those objectives.
  • Develops an annual budget within the framework of the organization's financial objectives. Monitors monthly expenses and is able to justify variances.
  • Understands and models the Honoring Lives principles in leadership, relationships and customer service.
  • Supervises, motivates, trains, and defines the organization's standards and communicates effectively with staff using team leadership concepts.
  • Provides and supports growth and development opportunities for team members.
  • Completes One 2 One Conversations with team members in a timely fashion.
  • Communicates calmly and gently with residents, family members and staff, exhibiting patience, compassion, understanding and sensitivity.
  • Participates in training and development opportunities as offered.
  • Demonstrates dependability, competence, accuracy and is observant.
  • Adheres to compliance policies regarding confidentiality, HIPAA regulations, and resident and client rights.
  • Complies with regulatory agency standards and applicable policies and procedures.
  • Complies with safety and infection control protocols in all aspects of the job.
  • Demonstrates understanding of the Code of Conduct and abides by its guidelines in all aspects of the job.
  • Additional duties and responsibilities as assigned.


Qualifications
  • Master's degree in pastoral related ministry required.
  • Minimum of one unit of Clinical Pastoral Education required and working towards four units.
  • Congregational affirmation of gifts for ministry. Ordination or licensing required.
  • Minimum 3 years’ experience in related role preferred.
  • Gifted for pastoral care and preaching.
  • Demonstrates meaningful personal experience with Jesus Christ.
  • Proficient in use of computer and related technology required for the role.
  • Good verbal, non-verbal and written communication skills required.
  • Demonstrates leadership, management skills, dependability and a positive demeanor.
  • Demonstrates an understanding of and respect for the values and mission of the organization and its Mennonite/Anabaptist connections.

SUMMARY:

The Associate Worship Minister exists to help Storyline proclaim the good news of the gospel by serving alongside the Director of Worship in cultivating gatherings that are theologically serious, aesthetically excellent, and congregationally formative. This role helps lead worship across the life of the church, develops future worship leaders, contributes creatively through songwriting and musical arrangement, and strengthens a culture of worship that forms disciples and serves the mission of Storyline Church.


VISION & RESPONSIBILITIES:

The Sunday Gathering

The Sunday Gathering is one of the primary ways Storyline rehearses the good news of the gospel together. The Associate Worship Minister partners with the Director of Worship to help create worship gatherings where Scripture, song, prayer, and liturgy encourage the church to know Jesus and love all people.

  • Assist in planning and leading weekly worship gatherings.
  • Lead worship regularly, helping cultivate joyful congregational participation.
  • Provide leadership, care, and development for the Storyline Worship Choir.
  • Support rehearsals, musical preparation, and worship planning.
  • Help maintain a culture of excellence that serves the congregation rather than performance.


Partner with Storyline Ministries

Worship at Storyline extends beyond Sunday mornings. Every ministry environment is an opportunity to form disciples through gospel-centered worship.

  • Partner with ministry leaders to lead worship within The Salt Company, Students, Kids, and other ministry environments.
  • Recruit, train, and shepherd volunteers serving in these ministries.
  • Cultivate a consistent worship culture across the life of Storyline Church.
  • Encourage and equip emerging worship leaders to serve in a variety of ministry contexts.


Develop Future Leaders

Healthy worship ministries multiply leaders. The Associate Worship Minister plays an important role in identifying, investing in, and developing musicians and worship leaders who will faithfully serve the local church.

  • Disciple developing worship leaders through coaching, encouragement, and ministry opportunities.
  • Invest in volunteers by helping them grow spiritually, musically, and as servant leaders.
  • Support the Worship Residency by mentoring residents and modeling faithful ministry.
  • Help prepare future worship leaders to serve Storyline, church plants, and the broader Church.


Songs for the Church

Storyline desires to write songs that grow out of the life of our church and help our people sing the truths of the gospel. The Associate Worship Minister contributes creatively by helping develop music that serves the local church and future generations.

  • Write and develop original songs rooted in Scripture and the life of Storyline Church.
  • Create musical arrangements that strengthen congregational singing.
  • Help oversee the creative process for recordings and worship resources.
  • Contribute to a growing catalog of music that serves Storyline and the broader Church.


    RELATIONSHIP WITH THE STORYLINE TEAM:

    • I report to: Director of Worship, other ministry Directors
    • I work with: Worship team and Storyline staff
    • I lead: Worship Volunteers

     

    QUALIFICATIONS:

    • A daily pursuit of Christian Maturity
    • Agree with & live in alignment with Storyline Mission, Values, and Statement of Faith
    • 2+ years of experience in worship ministry preferred
    • Strong vocal and instrumental proficiency with the ability to lead confidently from the platform
    • Demonstrated gifting in arranging music and cultivating engaging congregational worship
    • Ability to coach and equip musicians and technical artists
    • Proficiency in Planning Center, ProPresenter, Google Suite
    • Ability to create a positive and intentional leadership culture 
    • Proficiency in G Suite, ProPresenter, and Planning Center

      Disclosure:
      We are committed to providing a safe and secure environment for our children and adults in our ministry programs. We have preventative measures in place to safeguard each child, as well as those who serve them. These preventative measures include awareness training, skillful screening processes, policies and procedures, background checks, and monitoring and oversight to help us maintain compliance and accountability. Furthermore, we report all suspicions and allegations of abuse because we believe this policy best protects children in our care.

Position Purpose:
Reporting to the Vice President, Field Ministry, you are responsible to deepen existing Capernaum ministries and to grow new Capernaum clubs in each Region.
Teenagers with disabilities will hear the Gospel in terms they can understand from someone who cares for them personally so as to accomplish Young Life’s mission to “glorify God by sharing Jesus Christ with the entire next generation.” You build relationships with teenagers, local adults, committee, and area staff, helping to present the Gospel of Jesus Christ incarnationally, always trying to bridge the gap between teenagers and Jesus.
As a member of the Religious Order of Young Life of Canada, the Director agrees with the Order’s Statement of Faith and abides by its Codes of Conduct (i.e. Faith and Conduct, Sexual Conduct, and Protecting Teenagers, Volunteers and Staff policies).

Key Responsibilities:
Grow and Deepen the Work 20%
? Expand the number of clubs and staff in both unique Capernaum and inclusive clubs in partnership with Regional and Ministry Directors.
? Ensure existing work is well supported and resourced.
? Innovate new and creative expressions of Capernaum ministry across the country
? Partner with like-minded organisations across Canada to expand and support Capernaum
? Provide start-up areas with initial ministry resources, training, and financial support as needed.


Leadership Development of Capernaum Staff and Volunteers 20%
? Partner with the Vice President of Field Ministry to lead Capernaum nationally and align ministry strategy with organizational goals.
? Collaborate with Regional Directors, Ministry Directors and Area Directors to develop strategic and sustainable Capernaum ministry plans, including the launch and support of new ministry areas. December 2025 Ministry Director - Capernaum Page 1 of 6
? Provide regular communication, coaching, and support to Capernaum staff (including the Capernaum Core Leadership Team - CCLT) and volunteer team leaders, offering guidance in problem-solving, planning, vision, and goal-setting.
? Offer disability expertise to staff and volunteers and create meaningful opportunities for disability-related learning and development.
? Maintain regular communication with their supervisors for effective onboarding and ongoing development.
? Develop and oversee leadership pipelines for staff and volunteers, including pathways for individuals with and without disabilities.
? Serve on Field Leadership Team to help develop and implement vision, goals, training, camping, resource development, and communications initiatives.


Resource Development 20%
? Raise personal financial support as required for the role.
? Cultivate and steward donor relationships to grow and sustain Capernaum ministry across Canada.
? Develop, support, and collaborate with the National Capernaum Committee to advance fundraising, awareness, practical support, and prayer for the ministry.
? Clearly communicate the mission, vision, and impact of Capernaum to potential donors, churches, and community partners.
? Adhere to Taking Donors Seriously (TDS) practices and systems.
? Maintain financial accountability by ensuring expenses remain within the approved budget.

Direct Ministry Leadership 15%
? Oversee all aspects of Capernaum camping ministries, including Capernaum Family Camp (CFC*), Capernaum participation in Branch, Regional Camps, and Day Camps.
? Ensure branch and camp environments are equipped, trained, and structured to fully include individuals with disabilities.
? Create and ensure opportunities for Capernaum youth to grow in their faith through Capernaum programming, Leadership Experience, Work Crew and Summer Staff pathways.


Capernaum Family Camp Leadership 15%
? Provide overall leadership for the vision, planning, and execution of Capernaum Family Camp.
? Invite families and support regional and area staff as they engage families in their communities.
? Lead the long-term vision for the growth and impact of CFC in supporting families affected by disability.
? Collaborate with the committee to raise annual scholarships and funding for CFC.

Ministry Support and Administration 5%
? Maintain accurate ministry statistics and reporting through Engage Spaces.
? Provide clear, timely, professional communication to staff, families, volunteers, and stakeholders across the mission.
? Develop annual ministry goals and strategic plans and review progress regularly with the Capernaum Committee.
? Support the creation and distribution of resources that strengthen ministry effectiveness and accessibility.

Training and Professional Development 5%
? Participate in ongoing professional development, continuing education, and disability-related training to enhance effectiveness and stay current with best practices.

Guiding Principles and General Responsibilities

Spiritual Leadership
? Model Christ in word, deed and actions.
? Model and promote Young Life’s mission and values. Represent Young Life positively and professionally within the community.
? Provide spiritual leadership to direct reports and volunteers, if applicable.
? Pray for kids, Young Life volunteers, and fellow Young Life staff.
? Pursue personal spiritual growth and involvement in a local church.

General Responsibilities
? Cultivate new funding within the region to grow Capernaum in new areas. Cast a fundraising vision to the Capernaum committee and work with them using the Taking Donors Seriously philosophy, to raise funds and promote, grow and sustain emerging Capernaum clubs
? Establish and manage an annual Capernaum budget per the timeline set by Young Life’s fiscal policies. In partnership with the Committee Chairperson, ensure adequate financial support is raised to fund expenses.
? Support the regional director to determine how best to financially integrate the flagship club with the local area ministry.
? Establish financial sustainability for Capernaum through a combination of donor cultivation and seeking out grants to fund the work.
? Adhere to all Young Life financial policies and procedures.
? Raise personal support as outlined in the area budget.

Team Duties and Responsibilities
? Model open communication and work collaboratively within the Young Life staff family, and in particular, the regional team, for the good of the organization, in support of Young Life’s mission, core values and strategic plan.
? Engage with and foster healthy relationships with the regional staff team.
? Attend staff meetings, staff conferences, and prayer days locally.
? Accept national and/or regional responsibilities as agreed upon by the individual, the Regional Director and committee.
? Nourish a truthful, accountable, forgiving, joyful, and healthy work culture.

Personal and Professional Development
? Pursue spiritual growth.
? Continue to develop professionally as an expert regarding kids with disabilities. Seek out opportunities to learn about kids with disabilities.
? Build and sustain a healthy relationship with YL Capernaum USA.
? Continue to hone your leadership skills. Partner with regional directors and senior area directors to learn more about their role as it relates to building a leadership pipeline, growing the new and next, etc.
? Own the challenges and solve the problems. Grow in professionalism and leadership so you are an influencer, teaching people to have vision for and ownership of Capernaum.
? Pursue opportunities to learn through books, courses, on-line resources, etc. Qualifications:
Spiritual
? Personal knowledge and experience of the saving work of Jesus Christ.
? Agreement with Young Life’s Statement of Faith.

Education and Experience
? Bachelor’s degree or equivalent.
? Completed Young Life of Canada’s staff training program.
? 1-3 years’ experience mentoring and discipling young people in a relational ministry setting in a church, community organization, or ministry.
? Past or current involvement in local or regional Capernaum ministry.

General Qualifications
? Intermediate to expert knowledge of how to effectively work with and support kids with physical or mental challenges is required.
? A natural initiator with an entrepreneurial drive.
? Engaging personality. Laughs readily. Positive outlook.
? Team builder with demonstrated leadership ability.
? Excellent verbal communication and interpersonal skills.
? Able to communicate with teenagers. Willingness to enter their world.
? Flexible with a positive attitude toward serving, learning and training. December 2025 Ministry Director - Capernaum Page 4 of 6
? Understand the unique issues faced by teens with disabilities and their families.
? Proven relational skills with both adolescents and adults.
? Ability to maintain confidentiality.
? Proven strategic planning skills.
? Ability to implement new strategies.
? Ability to work independently as well as with a group.
? Self-motivated and goal oriented.

Training and Certification
? Legally entitled to work in Canada.
? Valid Class 5 driver’s license and clean Driver’s Abstract or equivalent.
? Clean criminal record check, including vulnerable sector search, required as a condition of employment. Work Conditions

Work Location:
• Work is performed in a variety of settings, including office, school, private homes, camps, and restaurants. It requires frequent travel by car or bus. Some travel by car, bus or airplane to other cities within Canada will be required several times per year.

Physical Requirements:
• The work is generally sedentary in nature but may require standing or walking up to 30% of the time, and more strenuous physical activity such as running or hiking up to 10% of the time. Employee will occasionally be required to sleep on church floors or on a bus.
Work Environment:
• Work environment is generally favourable. The work may be outdoors 10% of the time. The position is required to work with teenagers in middle and high school. Job requires employee to transport teenagers by car or van.

Hours of Work:
• This position is required to work evenings and weekends on a regular basis to accommodate the out-of-school / off-work availability of teenagers and volunteers.

Hazards:
• Hazards are considered minor and controllable. Employee is required to hear information about teenagers’ lives which may be troubling or upsetting, and may cause emotional issues including vicarious trauma.

Other:
• Due to the nature of the job, and our commitment to a safe environment for teenagers and volunteers, the individual is subject to a criminal record check, including a vulnerable sector search, and must submit a current driver’s abstract or provincial equivalent.
The above statements are intended to describe the general nature and level of work performed by people in this position. They are not intended to be an exhaustive list of all responsibilities, duties and skills

The Lead Teacher is a role model and mentor within the classroom, responsible for delivering high-quality, developmentally appropriate, and Christ-centered programs for children. In addition to all Teacher responsibilities, the Lead Teacher supports the onboarding, observation, and mentorship of new teachers within their age group, helping to verify skills and foster a culture of excellence and spiritual growth. This position is designed for experienced educators who demonstrate spiritual leadership, strong communication, and a heart for serving others.
 

Classroom & Instructional Leadership

  • Plan and deliver daily activities that support spiritual, social, emotional, and academic development, integrating Bible stories, prayer, and Christian values in age-appropriate ways.
  • Maintain a safe, clean, and age-appropriate learning environment; follow all licensing, NAC, and CACFP requirements.
  • Use varied instructional strategies to meet diverse learning needs.
  • Track attendance, developmental milestones, and classroom routines consistently.

Mentorship & Onboarding

  • Serve as a mentor for new teachers within the assigned age group, providing classroom observation, feedback, and support during onboarding.
  • Assist with skills verification and practical training for new hires, using Lionheart’s New Employee Orientation tools and checklists.
  • Model best practices in classroom management, curriculum implementation, and spiritual integration.
  • Support the development of a positive, collaborative team culture.

Leadership & Professional Development

  • Participate in Lead Teacher orientation/training and ongoing leadership development.
  • Take initiative in identifying and addressing classroom or team needs.
  • Assist Academy Directors and Assistant Directors with special projects, pilot programs, or process improvements as needed.
  • Demonstrate flexibility and a willingness to serve across age groups or support academy-wide initiatives.

Family Engagement

  • Build strong partnerships with families through daily communication, milestone sharing, and spiritual updates.
  • Respond promptly and professionally to family concerns.

Team & Academy Responsibilities

  • Collaborate with co-teachers, floaters, and leadership to ensure smooth classroom operations.
  • Participate in staff meetings, training sessions, and academy events.
  • Assist with housekeeping, laundry, and restocking supplies as needed.

 

  • At least 18 years of age; high school diploma or GED required.
  • Meets all state minimum standards and qualifications for an Early Childhood Lead Teacher; CDA, AA, or BA in Early Childhood Education preferred.
  • Minimum 1 year of experience in a licensed child care facility.
  • Demonstrated spiritual leadership and alignment with Lionheart’s mission and values.
  • Positive peer and family relationships; strong communication skills.
  • Criminal background check.

Competencies

  • Spiritual Alignment: Models a Christ-centered life and integrates faith into daily work.
  • Mentorship & Leadership: Guides, encourages, and supports peers and new hires.
  • Intentional Relationships: Builds trust and collaboration with children, families, and staff.
  • Heart to Serve: Joyfully serves with humility and strength.
  • Tenacity & Adaptability: Perseveres through challenges and responds creatively to change.
  • Effective Communication: Clearly conveys updates, feedback, and biblical principles.

Skills

  • Safety & Compliance: Maintains sight-and-sound supervision, adheres to licensing, NAC, and CACFP requirements, and ensures a safe and clean classroom.
  • Curriculum Implementation: Plans and delivers developmentally appropriate spiritual and academic activities tailored to children’s needs.
  • Family Engagement: Builds trust through daily communication, milestone sharing, and proactive partnership with families.
  • Observation & Documentation: Accurately records attendance, care routines, developmental progress, and CACFP point-of-service counts.
  • Effective Communication: Clearly conveys updates to families, collaborates with co-teachers, and models biblical principles.

Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)

  • Successful onboarding and retention of new teachers.
  • Positive feedback from mentees, families, and team members.
  • Compliance with all state licensing, NAC, CACFP, and safety standards.
  • Accurate and timely completion of documentation.
  • Demonstrated teamwork and alignment with Lionheart’s mission and values.

Woodside Bible Church is seeking a spiritually mature, relational, and passionate Family Ministry Director to lead Kids and Student Ministry at our White Lake Campus. Working closely with campus leadership and Central Ministry teams, the Family Ministry Director helps build a unified approach to family discipleship that supports Woodside's mission of helping people Belong to Christ, Grow in Christ, and Reach the World for Christ.

This is a full-time, salaried, exempt position. Membership and active participation at Woodside Bible Church's White Lake Campus are required.

What You'll Do

  • Provide leadership and oversight for Kids and Student Ministry, including weekend and midweek programming.

  • Recruit, train, disciple, and develop healthy volunteer teams.

  • Partner with parents to equip and encourage them as the primary spiritual influencers in their children's lives.

  • Plan and oversee ministry events, retreats, camps, and family milestones.

  • Collaborate with Central Kids and Student Ministry teams to ensure alignment with Woodside's ministry vision and curriculum.

  • Oversee ministry budgets, scheduling, communication, and Child Protection Program (CPP) compliance.

  • Develop and implement strategies that strengthen family discipleship and foster spiritual growth.

What We're Looking For

  • A spiritually mature follower of Jesus with a passion for reaching and discipling the next generation.

  • Strong leadership, biblical teaching, and communication skills.

  • Experience recruiting, developing, and shepherding staff and volunteer teams.

  • 3–5 years of children's, student, or family ministry leadership experience preferred.

  • Strong organizational and relational skills with the ability to engage children, students, parents, and volunteers.

  • Bachelor's degree required; ministry or Christian education preferred.

  • Alignment with Woodside's mission, values, Statement of Faith, and ministry philosophy.

If you're passionate about investing in the next generation, equipping families, and developing leaders who make a lasting spiritual impact, we'd love to hear from you!

Metro-Phoenix Chinese Alliance Church - Tempe, AZ

Senior Pastor

We are seeking a Senior Pastor who will provide spiritual leadership and help guide our congregation through an important season of transition and growth.

About Our Church

Our church officially launched in November 1982 and has served the Cantonese-speaking immigrant community from Hong Kong for more than 40 years.

Our congregation averages approximately 50 people in Sunday worship, with 35 current members. About 90% of our congregation came from Hong Kong and speaks Cantonese, while approximately half can understand and converse in Mandarin and English.

We are a close-knit congregation with longstanding relationships. Many members have known one another for more than 30 years.

Our current ministries include family small groups, a sister group, a mothers' group, an elderly fellowship, a gentlemen's coffee gathering, prayer meetings and Bible studies, as well as developing evangelistic Bible studies and discipleship opportunities.

We maintain close relationships with other churches and pastors in the area and participate in evangelistic events, Vacation Bible School, outreach activities, and community service alongside other churches.

Looking ahead, we desire to develop an English-speaking congregation, with a particular focus on reaching second-generation Chinese families and beginning ministry with pre-teens. We are investing in youth ministry training and seeking a pastor with the passion and gifts to help lead the church into this next stage. We are also working toward establishing an Elder Board to provide long-term leadership and planning.

Position Description

The Senior Pastor will be expected to:

  • Provide leadership and vision for the church's future.
  • Communicate the Word of God through preaching, teaching, instruction, exhortation, and correction.
  • Recruit, develop, and mentor lay leaders.
  • Model and mobilize one-on-one discipleship.
  • Mobilize the congregation toward evangelistic outreach and greater engagement with the surrounding community.
  • Provide pastoral care, including visitation and counseling.
  • Minister to families and help develop ministry to children, pre-teens, youth, and the next generation.
  • Help develop an English-speaking ministry, with particular attention to second-generation Chinese families.
  • Oversee and participate in worship ministry.
  • Oversee ministry programs and projects.
  • Work with church leadership as the church establishes its Elder Board and clarifies ministry responsibilities.
  • Facilitate healthy collaboration among church leaders and ministries.
  • Participate in community events and relationships with other churches and local ministry organizations.
  • Encourage greater awareness, commitment, and participation in missions, including prayer, giving, sending, and going.
  • Manage conflict biblically and promote unity within the congregation.

The pastor will join a congregation that values strong relationships while seeking to become more outward-focused and engaged with the surrounding community.

Qualifications

The ideal candidate will:

  • Demonstrate a strong Christian faith, godly character, spiritual discipline, and evidence of a Spirit-filled life.
  • Be qualified for pastoral ministry within The Christian and Missionary Alliance and meet its requirements for pastoral service.
  • Possess strong biblical preaching and teaching abilities.
  • Have demonstrated pastoral ministry experience.
  • Have the ability and desire to develop and mentor lay leaders.
  • Have a passion for evangelism, discipleship, missions, and community engagement.
  • Have a heart for children, pre-teens, youth, and second-generation Chinese families.
  • Be able to provide leadership and vision while working collaboratively with church leadership.
  • Be able to minister effectively within a Cantonese-speaking congregation while helping the church move toward expanded English-language ministry.
  • Be comfortable working with a congregation composed primarily of Cantonese-speaking immigrants from Hong Kong and their families.
  • Demonstrate the ability to build relationships across generations and cultures.
  • Be committed to biblical conflict resolution and maintaining unity within the church.

A Master of Divinity or equivalent theological education is among the educational levels being considered for the position.

Compensation

The church intends to provide a compensation package appropriate to the pastor's training, experience, and ministry responsibilities.

The terms of call are expected to address:

  • Annual salary
  • Housing allowance
  • Health insurance
  • Travel and ministry-related expense account
  • Annual vacation
  • Study leave
  • Illness leave
  • Retirement provision
  • Agreed-upon moving expenses

Specific compensation amounts and benefit details will be determined as part of the call process.

If the district office has reviewed your application and they think you may be a potential match for the position, that the hiring manager will reach out to you for next steps.

This position requires licensing with The Christian & Missionary Alliance. To learn more about The Alliance and requirements for licensing, please visit our website

They are seeking a Kids Pastor to rebuild and revitalize a ministry that disciples the next generation from Birth through 5th grade. This is an incredible opportunity to bring fresh vision, recruit and empower volunteer teams, and partner with parents in a diverse, multi-generational community.


Church In The Son Snapshot:

  • Theology - Charismatic/Pentecostal theological alignment
  • You will have freedom to cast vision and design a ministry approach to reach kids
  • Serving in a non-performative, steady staff culture
  • Great facilities with a dedicated kids' auditorium.
  • Strong up-front stage presence and teaching ability.
  • Focused on discipleship and Bible engagement



About This Organization

Church In The Son began on Palm Sunday, 1990, with its very first service held at the Orlando Museum of Art. To our amazement, over 250 people attended that first Sunday. Our founder and Lead Pastor, Alex Clattenburg, had a vision to create a church where the Holy Spirit would be free to work in the lives of people, where worship could be experienced freely, and where people could move beyond traditional formality. With no backing from any organization, but fueled by prayer and obedience, we stepped out in faith, believing for God to do something great—and He did!

From the beginning, we’ve been passionate about reaching those far from God and sharing the love of Jesus. Through our ministries, we continue to see people from all backgrounds experience the power of the Holy Spirit and their lives transformed.On December 15th, 2024, Pastor Alex anointed Pastor Jonathan and Jackie D’Angelo as our new lead pastors, marking an exciting new chapter for Church in the Son.

We are so grateful to God for what he has done in and through our church family. The story of Church In The Son is still being written, and we can’t wait to see what God has in store for the future!


Location

Orlando, FL is one of the fastest growing and most popular areas in the country right now. Beautiful weather, loads of sunshine, and a seemingly endless array of things to do make this an incredible place to live and raise a family. Disney and Universal Studios are right in town, beautiful beaches are just an hour away, and there is no shortage of opportunities for shopping and entertainment across the city. Schools are very strong, the average home price is $350K, and family-friendly culture make Orlando a terrific place to raise kids.


Key Responsibilities

  • Oversee all programming and ministry for children ages Birth to 5th grade, including Sunday services, mid-week services, summer programming, and special events
  • Regularly select and develop curriculum for a children’s Christian education for each age group encouraging spiritual formation and growth
  • Implement children’s registration, classroom management, and security polices/practices in alignment with church guidelines and legal requirements
  • Direct the recruitment, training, and development of volunteers as needed to staff children’s ministry classrooms and special events
  • Lead and motivate staff in the operation of a children’s ministry by casting vision and providing leadership guidance
  • Maintain a strategy for reaching and assimilating new children and families to be engaged in church, oversee the follow up for new Pre-K families, oversee events like parents’ night out, movie nights, help with outreaches offsite
  • Oversee Family Experience, Host Team
  • Assist in managing annual budget for Kids ministry
  • Developing Community with the families of the children
  • Function as a member of the church’s Pastoral staff providing pastoral care and oversight for children and parents as needed


Mission, Vision, and Values

Vision:

  • Love God. Love People. Affect the World. We loving God by experiencing a daily personal relationship with the Lord through living a life of obedience. We love people by being connected in meaningful relationships and serving together in ministry. We affect the world by giving to, praying for, and participating in community projects and world missions.

Core Values: 

  • We believe: 
  • Creation didn’t “just happen.” God made it all. 
  • The Bible is God’s perfect, life-changing message of truth for living. 
  • Jesus Christ is the Son of God, the leader of the Church, and the source of eternal life. Jesus died and rose again so that we can experience forgiveness and freedom through faith and repentance. 
  • As Christ followers, we live a holy life that is fully surrendered to Him. 
  • Prayer is open conversation with God. He loves to talk to us and help us. 
  • The Baptism of the Holy Spirit is given to empower us to be a witness for Jesus daily. 
  • Spiritual gifts have been given to the Church to help others. Healing is provided for every Christ follower through the power of the cross. 
  • Building healthy, God-honoring relationships and serving others is the heart of God. 

Mission:

  • To help people who are far from God find a new life. We are called to make disciples of all nations. Jesus is coming again, and will ultimately establish His Kingdom on the earth.

Campus Staff Minister - Central South New Jersey

Work Location:

New Jersey

Job Type:

Full time

God has called InterVarsity to plant and to build witnessing communities of students and faculty who follow Jesus on college and university campuses. Through these groups, we believe ever- increasing numbers of students and faculty from all ethnic groups and areas of the campus will be transformed by the Gospel. We expect to see campuses increasingly become places where people, ideas, and structures flourish to the glory of God. We confidently anticipate that our InterVarsity alumni will become change agents across the country and around the world. We pursue this calling by discerning and actively participating in what God is already doing on campus. This is the essence of being a Campus Staff Minister (CSM).

ESSENTIAL COMMITMENTS/RESPONSIBILITIES 

Spiritual Growth 

As a Campus Staff Minister, you pursue maturity as a disciple of Jesus Christ so that your life and work increasingly reflect a growing love for God, God’s Word, God’s people of every ethnicity and culture, and God’s purposes in the world. To do this, you will: 

  • Pursue a vibrant relationship with the triune God through engagement with Scripture, prayer, and worship, both individually and in community 

  • Develop self-leadership (growing in self-awareness, self-management, relational integrity, and resiliency)

  • Embrace Scriptural standards for behavior and attitudes 

 

Campus Leadership 

As a Campus Staff Minister, you increase the number of witnessing communities, as well as the size, health, spiritual maturity, and campus-wide influence of existing witnessing communities of students and faculty by being a: 

  • Visionary Guide: 

You communicate and model InterVarsity’s vision to see students and faculty transformed, campuses renewed, and world changers developed 

  • Create a culture of humble dependence on God and bold expectation in God’s intention to start new witnessing communities throughout the campus and on new campuses

  • Model – in person and through programs – InterVarsity’s vision and Core Values, including a biblically-defined commitment to engage every ethnic and social group on campus

  • Lead students and faculty – individually and collectively – through Scripture, prayer, teaching, and discipleship experiences, so that they articulate and align their ministry activities around this vision

  • Set annual goals through prayer, research and reflection with your teams (students, faculty, and staff) for qualitative and quantitative growth, including conversions and leadership development 

  • Structural Architect: 

You create, develop, align, and leverage ministry plans, programs, teams, and structures to close the gap between current reality and the aspirational goals. 

  • Build leadership teams who trust and partner well with you and who demonstrate spiritual vitality, relational health, and mission alignment

  • Develop and execute plans to achieve annual goals, evaluating and modifying the plan as needed throughout the year

  • Increase momentum for the vision by aligning programs, structures, conferences, and teams around the goals

  • Mobilize students and faculty to engage their relational networks with the gospel and to start new missional communities

  • Under the direction of the Area Director, may supervise Ministry Interns and Campus Ministry Interns as delegated 

  • Missional Developer: 

You intentionally gather, invite, and develop diverse groups of students and faculty so that they not only encounter and follow Jesus as Savior and Lord but also advance the mission on campus as participants and leaders. 

  • Create ways for faculty and students to encounter and follow Jesus through Scripture, worship, prayer, mission experiences, conferences, etc.

  • Equip students and faculty so that they think strategically about campus engagement and so that they proclaim – in word, deed, and power – the good news of Jesus, regularly inviting students and faculty to follow him as Savior and Lord

  • Disciple students and faculty by equipping them to hear the Word, respond actively, and debrief and interpret the experience so that they grow in Christlikeness, reflect our Core Values, and develop ministry skills

  • Invite, coach, and equip students and faculty to become increasingly effective participants and leaders, including starting new witnessing communities on campuses 

 

Organizational Collaboration 

As a Campus Staff Minister, you have joined a national mission. Therefore, you work with a network of other local, area, regional, and national InterVarsity staff and volunteers so that our work reflects Biblical standards of excellence, integrity, and partnership. 

  • Partner with and respond positively to the direction and coaching of your supervisors and national leaders

  • Contribute to collaborative and productive team meetings and relationships

  • Affiliate chapters under your care and submit Graduating Student Forms in order to increase our partnership with current students and alumni

  • Use national ministry resources and tools, as requested, including recruiting and/or participating in local, regional, or national conferences as

  • Complete reporting, planning and review requirements in a timely way so that you and your supervisors can assess and improve your work as a CSM

  • Comply with all InterVarsity policies and procedures 

 

Ministry Partnership Development 

As a Campus Staff Minister, you will develop a team of partners – churches and individuals (including alumni and community members) – who will resource the ministry financially, in prayer, or volunteer service that advances the mission. 

  • Raise 100% of the financial budget assigned by your supervisor

  • Communicate regularly with your ministry partners, nurturing the relationship through visits, phone calls, emails and regular prayer letters

  • Develop on-going, long-lasting partnership with alumni and volunteers

  • Comply with all Ministry Partnership Policies

  • Identify and invest in advocates who will build networks of volunteers and donors on InterVarsity’s behalf 

 

Accomplish all other assigned tasks as appropriate 

 

QUALIFICATIONS (common to all levels of CSM) 

  • Annually affirm InterVarsity’s Statement of Agreement (Doctrinal Basis and Purpose Statement). Abide by InterVarsity’s Code of Conduct. Believe and behave consonantly with InterVarsity’s Human Sexuality Theological Paper. Affirm and behave consonantly with InterVarsity’s “Women in Ministry Statement of Affirmation”

  • Bachelor’s degree for CSMs assigned to a four-year campus. A minimum of an Associate’s degree for CSMs assigned to a two-year campus or a community college

  • Strong interpersonal skills (including ability to minister to diverse ethnic communities and faculty)

  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills

  • Demonstrated problem solving skills

  • Familiarity with word processing, presentation, email, and spreadsheet software 

 

WORK ENVIRONMENT/PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS 

The CSM position leads ministry in a college campus environment. A designated office space may or may not be available. The CSM is required to travel to on-campus and off- campus sites as appropriate. Off-campus travel includes, but is not limited to: student ministry conferences, Ministry Partnership Development meetings, and InterVarsity- sponsored training sessions, meetings, and conferences. The CSM is regularly required to communicate with others, and routinely uses standard office equipment such as computers, phones, photocopiers, filing cabinets, etc.

post_html:
Program Outline

Residency Program Philosophy

VISION: The goal of the residency is to fully equip every individual to be an effective minister of the Gospel, either in a traditional ministry setting or church-planting context.

FOUR OBJECTIVES OF THE PROGRAM

Ministry Exposure

Preparation for Gospel work will flourish if those in training can be placed in a local church where they have opportunities to test and grow their gifts. Only by putting into practice what they are learning in the classroom will they grow. Residents need a safe environment to make mistakes and learn from them. They also need the opportunity to develop the right instincts for ministry by participating in a substantial, meaningful way.

Personal Development

Formal education offers great content and a logical structure for teaching. However, when it comes to personal and character development, nothing compares with having a mentor. This dynamic is particularly true in Gospel ministry where life and doctrine are so intimately connected.

Professional Development

Although pastors are not strictly professionals, there are professional skills that are applied every day. Therefore, residents will be developed in some strategic ways: church administration, public speaking, productivity, leading staff teams, etc.

Theological and Spiritual Development

If you are going to teach the Bible well, you will need tools that will help you read, understand, and prepare to teach God's Word. Our goal is to prepare you to share and apply God's Word thoughtfully and faithfully.

Job Description

The Redeemer Residency Program is a total of two years. This gives the resident time to not only observe but also do meaningful ministry.

Requirements for the Redeemer Church Resident:

  • A desire to pursue full-time ministry
  • Evidence of love for Christ
  • Evidence of love for His Word
  • Evidence of love for His people and an ability to work well with others
  • Evidence of personal holiness
  • General agreement with Redeemer’s doctrinal statement and Elder Statement
  • A bachelor’s degree or above
  • Attend Redeemer’s doctrine class or taken an equivalent course.
  • General base of Systematic Theology — If not, must take Redeemer’s Doctrine Class

Weekly Time Commitments:

The average time spent per week for Redeemer residents will be 40 hours. We want to ensure that residents are taking two days off to rest each week.

  • Character and Personal Development: 2-5 hours per week
  • Theological Development: 5-7 hours per week
  • Staff Meetings and Staff Trainings: 2-3 hours per week
  • Professional Development: 1-2 hours per week
  • Specialized Track: 15-20 hours per week
  • Administration & Support Raising: 1-2 hours per week
  • Sunday Services: 7 hours per week (available to serve different ministries)

Next Steps

Click on "Apply to Position" to show your interest. Following an initial screening, we will send you the rest of the application to move forward.

*This is a support-based position. You will need to be eligible for employment in the US to apply for this position.
