post_html:
Campus Ministry Associate - Arkansas Area (Undergraduate Ministry)

Work Location:

Arkansas

Job Type:

Part time

To advance the mission and purpose of InterVarsity, this position will focus on learning and preparing for the full responsibilities of a Campus Staff Minister. The Campus Ministry Associate will be assigned work based on skills determined by the application process. This is a one or two-year position in which the individual receives intensive training and exercises ministerial functions consistent with a Campus Staff Minister.

Personal Spiritual Duties 

  • Be a maturing disciple of Jesus Christ: growing in love for God, God's Word, God's people of every ethnicity and culture, and God’s purposes in the world 

  • Practice daily spiritual disciplines  

  • Pursue spiritual relationships and involvement in a worshipping community  

  • Continue learning and growth in spiritual understanding, biblical knowledge, ministry experience and skills 

  • Experience and live out an ongoing call to ministry service with InterVarsity and its mission 

 

Ministry Leadership 

  • Participate and be fully engaged in the ministry team to cast spiritual vision and direction, to contribute to the accomplishment of the team’s plans for spiritual growth and transformation, and to provide area leadership in specific areas 

  • Teach students to love, study and apply Scripture to their lives  

  • Learn about and assist in leading in ministry to students and faculty on campus 

  • Promote and press forward the Mission on campus Seek opportunities to proclaim and demonstrate the Gospel of Jesus Christ  

  • Learn to guide chapters (or assigned segments of a chapter) in the development of strategic thinking regarding witness to the university  

  • Learn to model and assist students and faculty in growing in their love for God's people of every ethnicity and culture  

  • Help to develop student and/or faculty ministry leadership teams, based on developing skills  

  • Encourage a prayerful lifestyle in students and faculty, especially focusing on those who do not yet follow Jesus as Lord and Savior  

  • Engage positively with the supervision you receive from your staff ministry director 

 

Pastoral Care and Support (assist as assigned and based on skill level) 

  • Provide pastoral care and support for student and/or leadership teams and individual students and faculty 

  • Provide training, resources and opportunities for students and faculty for their spiritual development 

  • Recruit students and/or faculty and providing specific leadership for conferences and projects  

 

 

Administration  

  • Perform the necessary administrative tasks to fulfill the purpose of InterVarsity and to comply with InterVarsity’s policies and procedures 

  • Comply with Risk Management policies  

  • Follow the budgeting and expense reporting guidelines  

  • Lead students in filing annual chapter affiliation, in coordination with assigned Campus Staff Minister 

  • Fulfill area and regional reporting requirements  

  • Fulfill national reporting requirements  

 

Ministry Partner Development and Public Relations 

  • Serve as an ambassador of InterVarsity to individual ministry partners and churches, through prayer, discussion of ministry efforts, mission, and accomplishments. 

  • Carry out the tasks required for effective fund development and to develop strong public relations for the ministry of InterVarsity  

  • Maintain expenses within allocated budgets  

  • Secure personal financial, prayer support and maintain a ministry among partners who will fund InterVarsity 

  • Develop and implement an annual 30-day plan for raising personal budget  

  • Communicate with ministry partners at least four times a year  

  • Cultivate and maintain supportive relationships with alumni  

 

QUALIFICATIONS 

  • Annually affirm InterVarsity’s Statement of Agreement (Doctrinal Basis and Purpose Statement); abide by InterVarsity’s Code of Conduct; believe and behave consonantly with InterVarsity’s Human Sexuality Theological Paper. Affirm and behave consonantly with InterVarsity’s “Women in Ministry Statement of Affirmation” 

  • Exploring calling to InterVarsity and its mission  

  • Bachelor's degree for non-enrolled candidates assigned to four-year campuses; Associate's degree for non-enrolled candidates assigned to two-year campuses 

  • Prior experience with InterVarsity or other campus ministry preferred (including as a student) 

  • Willing to receive training to become a Campus Staff Minister 

  • Ability to contribute to an open and supportive relationship with ministry team members  

  • Ministry skills: Prior experience teaching spiritual and biblical principles, planning ministry programs, and spiritually discipling others 

  • Excellent oral and written communication skills  

  • Demonstrated problem-solving skills  

  • A supervisory decision, with input from the Campus Ministry Associate, is made at the end of the term of service as to whether the individual is suitable for continuing employment with InterVarsity.

Pay Range: $35,088.00 - $46,776.00 per year

Pay: This position is funded through personal fundraising. Accordingly, compensation will vary based on the ability of the individual to secure a donor team to fund the cost of his/her salary. The anticipated salary range for this position on a full-time basis (40 hours/week) is dependent on a variety of factors, including location and cost of living. The actual salary received, including any geographic adjustment to account for location and cost of living, is subject to the individual’s ability to raise funds necessary to cover the full amount of such salary within the range set forth in the job posting details.

Benefits:

We offer a competitive benefits package, including health care and retirement savings with a match. Eligibility is based on employee type and hours worked.  Benefits include the following:

  • 403(b) Retirement Savings Plan

  • 403(b) matching contributions

  • Dental insurance

  • Employee assistance program

  • Employee discounts

  • Flexible work schedule

  • Flexible spending accounts

  • Health insurance

  • Health savings account

  • Life insurance

  • Paid time off

  • Parental leave

  • Professional development assistance

  • Vision insurance

Equal Employment Opportunity: 

 

InterVarsity Christian Fellowship/USA is both an equal opportunity employer and a faith-based religious organization. We conduct hiring without regard to race, color, ancestry, national origin, citizenship, age, sex, marital status, parental status, membership in any labor organization, political ideology, or disability of an otherwise qualified individual. The status of InterVarsity Christian Fellowship/USA as an equal opportunity employer does not prevent the organization from hiring staff based on their religious beliefs so that all staff share the same religious commitment.  Pursuant to the Civil Rights Act of 1964, Section 702 (42 U.S.C. 2000e 1(a)) InterVarsity Christian Fellowship/USA has the right to, and does, hire only candidates who agree with InterVarsity’s Statement of Agreement: Purpose and Doctrinal Basis because InterVarsity believes that each and every staff plays a vital role in advancing InterVarsity’s mission and purposes.

Job Summary:

The Youth Pastor leads youth ministry at one campus for middle school and high school students. They own how that ministry runs locally — its plan inside the campus operating plan, the budget, and the Serve Team and Team Members who deliver it — while holding the church-wide standard for Youth. This role exists to build a thriving student environment that fosters discipleship, leadership development, and genuine community.


Principal Job Responsibilities:

  • Leads youth ministry at one campus, owning its plan within the campus operating plan
  • Delivers the church-wide standard for youth ministry locally, adapting the expression without changing the standard
  • Recruits, hires, leads, trains, develops, and provides accountability for Youth Team
  • Builds and stewards the Serve Team for the ministry: recruiting, training, retention, and appreciation
  • Owns the ministry budget for the area and spends within the approved threshold
  • Pastors the people the ministry reaches, through care, prayer, and presence
  • Participates in the cross-campus meeting for the ministry, led by the Area Leader Pastor
  • Reviews the measures for the ministry and makes decisions accordingly
  • Leads the campus's youth environments and services for middle school and high school students
  • Develops and delivers message content for youth services, and plans and schedules services with Youth Central
  • Builds healthy community through youth small groups and challenges students to grow as leaders
  • Builds a student lead team that involves students and empowers them as leaders
  • Owns the safety, security, check-in, and screening standards for youth environments
  • Engages parents and guardians of students and responds to their questions and concerns in a timely manner
  • Plans and leads camps, retreats, and youth events at the campus
  • Holds a ministerial license to minister, preach the gospel, and fulfill the work of serving God's kingdom, valid for the duration of pastoral ministry at Gateway Church, and carries spiritual authority within the church
  • Serves the congregation by officiating weddings, funerals, baby dedications, communion, and other ministry services
  • Is present and serving at weekend services and churchwide events as the ministry calendar requires, and is available to the congregation for pastoral care as needs arise
  • Teaches through biblical principles and by lifestyle example
  • Performs other duties as assigned.

 

As a member of the Gateway Church team, this position is expected to support, recruit, and develop Serve Team members, and to serve alongside the broader team as ministry and organizational needs arise.


General Skills & Qualifications:

  • A clear passion for Jesus and a strong biblical foundation
  • Clear and effective communicator with both large and small groups
  • Demonstrated ability to gather, develop, and deploy staff and volunteers
  • Strong critical thinking, and the ability to manage ambiguity and lead others through change
  • A heart for students and families, with the ability to connect with middle school and high school students
  • Able to develop and deliver message content for a student audience
  • Able to hold a high standard for safety, security, and screening without losing warmth
  • Comfortable holding others accountable with clarity and care
  • Demonstrated emotional and relational intelligence
  • Willingness and ability to engage in courageous conversations
  • Strong time-management skills and the ability to hold several priorities at once
  • Proficient in Microsoft Office and able to learn and function within new software and systems


Education/Certification(s):

  • Four or more years of student or youth ministry experience — required
  • Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience — required
  • Licensed as a minister, or eligible to be licensed upon employment — required
  • Prior experience in a multisite church environment — preferred


General Physical Requirements:

The physical demands described here represent those that an employee must meet to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. While performing the duties of this position, the employee is regularly required to:

  • Sit or stand for extended periods of time
  • Occasionally kneel or crouch
  • Frequently lift and/or move up to 10 lbs.
  • Occasionally lift and/or move up to 25 lbs.
  • Able to help set up and lead events, camps, and retreats, and available to work weekends and evenings

*This description is not all inclusive, and other duties may be assigned as necessary.


Gateway Church does not discriminate in employment opportunities or practices on the basis of race, color, sex, national origin, age, disability, or any other characteristic protected by law as it applies to churches. However, Gateway Church does discriminate on the basis of religion.


Employment Requirement: Must be a member or become a member of Gateway Church upon employment.

Student Minister

The student minister will be assigned to a specific campus and work on a team of Student ministers to lead and guide our church's middle and high school students. The student minister will support the Family Team in equipping parents to build stronger families and disciple students to be fully devoted followers of Jesus Christ, and shepherd teams of servant leaders for ministry excellence.

·      Communicate regularly and creatively with servant leaders, parents, and staff-at-large all pertinent information regarding the student ministry.

·      A clear call to serve families in the context of the local church  
·      A follower of Jesus and have demonstrated faith through full immersion baptism

·      Demonstrate a proven record of exhibiting the following skills and competencies:
o   Ability to develop, empower, and lead high functioning servant leader teams

Church Description

The Boston Chinese Evangelical Church (BCEC) is an established non-denominational evangelical church located in Boston's Chinatown, with an additional campus in Newton, Massachusetts. We are a multi-generational, multilingual Chinese heritage church consisting of six congregations: two English-speaking, two Mandarin-speaking, and two Cantonese-speaking.

The Position

The Ministry Assistant plays a vital support role at BCEC’s Chinatown Campus, working closely with Chinese-speaking pastoral staff to ensure the smooth and effective functioning of church ministries.

This highly visible, relationship-oriented position supports Sunday worship services, ministry programs, and church-wide administrative operations. The ideal candidate is organized, detail-oriented, culturally aware, and committed to serving God and His people with excellence.

The Ministry Assistant reports to the Office Manager and collaborates with Chinese pastoral staff as well as administrative and ministry team members.

Key Responsibilities

Chinese Ministry Support

  1. Provide administrative support to Chinese-speaking pastors and ministry teams

  2. Coordinate logistics for Sunday services and church events (e.g., worship teams, A/V, room setup)

  3. Prepare weekly and special event bulletins (print and digital)

  4. Translate and edit materials such as flyers, reports, and announcements (English ↔ Chinese)

  5. Design and produce promotional and ministry materials using tools like Canva

  6. Manage digital platforms, including YouTube, social media, and the Chinese-language website (via CMS)

  7. Assist with visitor follow-up and outreach coordination

  8. Maintain ministry records (e.g., membership, visitors, attendance, event participation)

General Administration & Office Support

  1. Serve as receptionist at the Chinatown Campus

  2. Manage office supplies, incoming mail, bulletin boards, and literature displays

  3. Coordinate room reservations and facility usage

  4. Support communication across staff, volunteers, and congregants across campuses

  5. Collaborate with administrative and ministry teams as needed

  6. Perform other duties as assigned

Qualifications

  • Fluency in Cantonese, Mandarin, and English (spoken and written)

  • Proficiency in Chinese word processing

  • Strong administrative, organizational, and time management skills

  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook)

  • Comfortable with technology and a quick learner with new systems and tools

  • Experience using content management systems (CMS), or ability to quickly learn CMS platforms

  • Detail-oriented, adaptable, collaborative, and professional

  • Culturally sensitive, with awareness of Asian American and bicultural church dynamics

Preferred

  • College degree or equivalent work experience

  • Experience in a church or nonprofit environment

  • Familiarity with tools such as ProPresenter and Canva

  • Basic skills in media, graphic design, or website publishing

Personal Attributes

  • A growing Christian faith and alignment with BCEC’s mission and values

  • Servant-hearted, trustworthy, and maintains confidentiality

  • Friendly, approachable, and strong interpersonal communication skills

Application Process

Please include the names and contacts of two references with your application. Upon review of your resume, we will request a submission of two letters of reference.

Please send a cover letter and résumé by email to:

Personnel Deacon

Boston Chinese Evangelical Church

Email address: [email protected]

For Further Information: Visit our website at www.bcec.net/jobs

  • Health, Vision, & Dental Insurance

Campus Staff Minister (United States Naval Academy)

Work Location:

Maryland

Job Type:

Full time

God has called InterVarsity to plant and to build witnessing communities of students and faculty who follow Jesus on college and university campuses. Through these groups, we believe ever- increasing numbers of students and faculty from all ethnic groups and areas of the campus will be transformed by the Gospel. We expect to see campuses increasingly become places where people, ideas, and structures flourish to the glory of God. We confidently anticipate that our InterVarsity alumni will become change agents across the country and around the world. We pursue this calling by discerning and actively participating in what God is already doing on campus. This is the essence of being a Campus Staff Minister (CSM).

ESSENTIAL COMMITMENTS/RESPONSIBILITIES 

Spiritual Growth 

You pursue maturity as a disciple of Jesus Christ so that your life and work increasingly reflects a growing love for God, God’s Word, God’s people of every ethnicity and culture, and God’s purposes in the world. To do this, you will: 

  • Pursue a vibrant relationship with the triune God through engagement with Scripture, prayer, and worship, both individually and in community 

  • Develop self-leadership (growing in self-awareness, self-management, relational integrity, and resiliency) 

  • Embrace Scriptural standards for behavior and attitudes 

 

Campus Leadership

You communicate and model InterVarsity’s vision to see students and faculty transformed, campuses renewed and world changers developed 

  • Create a culture of humble dependence on God and bold expectation in God’s intention to start new witnessing communities throughout the campus and on new campuses.

  • Model – in person and through programs – InterVarsity’s vision and Core Values, including a biblically-defined commitment to engage every ethnic and social group on campus 

  • Lead students and faculty – individually and collectively – through Scripture, prayer, teaching, and discipleship experiences, so that they articulate and align their ministry activities around this vision 

  • Set annual goals through prayer, research and reflection with your teams (students, faculty, and staff) for qualitative and quantitative growth, including conversions and leadership development 

 

You create, develop, align and leverage ministry plans, programs, teams, and structures to close the gap between current reality and the aspirational goals. 

  • Build leadership teams who trust and partner well with you and who demonstrate spiritual vitality, relational health, and mission alignment 

  • Develop and execute plans to achieve annual goals, evaluating and modifying the plan as needed throughout the year 

  • Increase momentum for the vision by aligning programs, structures, conferences and teams around the goals 

  • Mobilize students and faculty to engage their relational networks with the gospel and to start new missional communities 

  • Under the direction of the Area Director, may supervise Ministry Interns and Campus Ministry Interns as delegated 

 

You intentionally gather, invite, and develop diverse groups of students and faculty so that they not only encounter and follow Jesus as Savior and Lord but also advance the mission on campus as participants and leaders. 

  • Create ways for faculty and students to encounter and follow Jesus through Scripture, worship, prayer, mission experiences, conferences, etc. 

  • Equip students and faculty so that they think strategically about campus engagement and so that they proclaim – in word, deed, and power – the good news of Jesus, regularly inviting students and faculty to follow him as Savior and Lord 

  • Disciple students and faculty by equipping them to hear the Word, respond actively, and debrief and interpret the experience so that they grow in Christlikeness, reflect our Core Values, and develop ministry skills 

  • Invite, coach, and equip students and faculty to become increasingly effective participants and leaders, including starting new witnessing communities on campuses 

 

Organizational Collaboration 

You work with a network of other local, area, regional, and national InterVarsity staff and volunteers so that our work reflects Biblical standards of excellence, integrity, and partnership. 

  • Partner with and respond positively to the direction and coaching of your supervisors and national leaders 

  • Contribute to collaborative and productive team meetings and relationships 

  • Affiliate chapters under your care and submit Graduating Student Forms in order to increase our partnership with current students and alumni 

  • Use national ministry resources and tools, as requested, including recruiting and/or participating in local, regional, or national conferences as  

  • Complete reporting, planning and review requirements in a timely way so that you and your supervisors can assess and improve your work as a CSM 

  • Comply with all InterVarsity policies and procedures 

 

Ministry Partnership Development 

You will develop a team of partners – churches and individuals (including alumni and community members) – who will resource the ministry financially, in prayer, or volunteer service that advances the mission. 

  • Raise 100% of the financial budget assigned by your supervisor 

  • Communicate regularly with your ministry partners, nurturing the relationship through visits, phone calls, emails and regular prayer letters 

  • Develop on-going, long-lasting partnership with alumni and volunteers 

  • Comply with all Ministry Partnership Policies 

  • Identify and invest in advocates who will build networks of volunteers and donors on InterVarsity’s behalf 

 

Accomplish all other assigned tasks as appropriate 

 

QUALIFICATIONS (common to all levels of CSM) 

  • Annually affirm InterVarsity’s Statement of Agreement (Doctrinal Basis and Purpose Statement). Abide by InterVarsity’s Code of Conduct. Believe and behave consonantly with InterVarsity’s Human Sexuality Theological Paper. Affirm and behave consonantly with InterVarsity’s “Women in Ministry Statement of Affirmation” 

  • Bachelor’s degree for CSMs assigned to a four-year campus. A minimum of an Associate’s degree for CSMs assigned to a two-year campus or a community college 

  • Strong interpersonal skills (including ability to minister to diverse ethnic communities and faculty) 

  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills 

  • Demonstrated problem solving skills 

  • Familiarity with word processing, presentation, email, and spreadsheet software 

 

WORK ENVIRONMENT/PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS 

The CSM position leads ministry in a college campus environment. A designated office space may or may not be available. The CSM is required to travel to on-campus and off- campus sites as appropriate. Off-campus travel includes, but is not limited to: student ministry conferences, Ministry Partnership Development meetings, and InterVarsity- sponsored training sessions, meetings, and conferences. The CSM is regularly required to communicate with others, and routinely uses standard office equipment such as computers, phones, photocopiers, filing cabinets, etc.

Emmanuel Lutheran Church is a Christ-centered community of believers that seeks to encourage, strengthen and equip people to share the love of Jesus and help people to follow Him. We are part of the Lutheran Congregations in Mission for Christ.

Campus Staff Minister - Ohio (Graduate and Faculty Ministry)

Work Location:

Ohio

Job Type:

Full time

God has called InterVarsity to plant and to build witnessing communities of students and faculty who follow Jesus on college and university campuses. Through these groups, we believe ever- increasing numbers of students and faculty from all ethnic groups and areas of the campus will be transformed by the Gospel. We expect to see campuses increasingly become places where people, ideas, and structures flourish to the glory of God. We confidently anticipate that our InterVarsity alumni will become change agents across the country and around the world. We pursue this calling by discerning and actively participating in what God is already doing on campus. This is the essence of being a Campus Staff Minister (CSM).

Please submit the GFM Interest Form before completing the full application for a position with Graduate & Faculty Ministries in our online system. We will contact you when we are ready to proceed with the application process.​ 

This position is open to applicants working less than 40 hours/week. If you are interested in part-time work please apply for this position.  Additional pay (as a geographic adjustment) is available in high cost of living areas.

The pay range listed below is for an employee working 40 hours/week at CSM level II. Pay will be prorated for employees who work less than 40 hours/week. 

Volunteer opportunities range from prayer and hospitality to leading a campus fellowship of graduate students and faculty. People who are interested in volunteering will go through an application and interview process, however, volunteer openings are not posted at the job opportunities link above. For more information, talk with a local InterVarsity staff or staff director.

We have positions throughout the state of Ohio in addition to the specific locations below:
 

Case Western Reserve University - Graduate Students and Faculty

Cleveland State University - Graduate Students, Faculty, International Student Ministry

Miami University - Graduate Students and Faculty

Ohio University (Athens) - Graduate Students and Faculty

The Ohio State University - Graduate Students and Faculty, Black Scholars and Professionals

University of Cincinnati - Graduate Students and Faculty

ESSENTIAL COMMITMENTS/RESPONSIBILITIES 

Spiritual Growth 

You pursue maturity as a disciple of Jesus Christ so that your life and work increasingly reflects a growing love for God, God’s Word, God’s people of every ethnicity and culture, and God’s purposes in the world. To do this, you will: 

  • Pursue a vibrant relationship with the triune God through engagement with Scripture, prayer, and worship, both individually and in community 

  • Develop self-leadership (growing in self-awareness, self-management, relational integrity, and resiliency) 

  • Embrace Scriptural standards for behavior and attitudes 

 

Campus Leadership 

You communicate and model InterVarsity’s vision to see students and faculty transformed, campuses renewed and world changers developed 

  • Create a culture of humble dependence on God and bold expectation in God’s intention to start new witnessing communities throughout the campus and on new campuses 

  • Model – in person and through programs – InterVarsity’s vision and Core Values, including a biblically-defined commitment to engage every ethnic and social group on campus 

  • Lead students and faculty – individually and collectively – through Scripture, prayer, teaching, and discipleship experiences, so that they articulate and align their ministry activities around this vision 

  • Set annual goals through prayer, research and reflection with your teams (students, faculty, and staff) for qualitative and quantitative growth, including conversions and leadership development 

 

You create, develop, align and leverage ministry plans, programs, teams, and structures to close the gap between current reality and the aspirational goals. 

  • Build leadership teams who trust and partner well with you and who demonstrate spiritual vitality, relational health, and mission alignment 

  • Develop and execute plans to achieve annual goals, evaluating and modifying the plan as needed throughout the year 

  • Increase momentum for the vision by aligning programs, structures, conferences and teams around the goals 

  • Mobilize students and faculty to engage their relational networks with the gospel and to start new missional communities 

  • Under the direction of the Area Director, may supervise Ministry Interns and Campus Ministry Interns as delegated 

 

You intentionally gather, invite, and develop diverse groups of students and faculty so that they not only encounter and follow Jesus as Savior and Lord but also advance the mission on campus as participants and leaders. 

  • Create ways for faculty and students to encounter and follow Jesus through Scripture, worship, prayer, mission experiences, conferences, etc. 

  • Equip students and faculty so that they think strategically about campus engagement and so that they proclaim – in word, deed, and power – the good news of Jesus, regularly inviting students and faculty to follow him as Savior and Lord 

  • Disciple students and faculty by equipping them to hear the Word, respond actively, and debrief and interpret the experience so that they grow in Christlikeness, reflect our Core Values, and develop ministry skills 

  • Invite, coach, and equip students and faculty to become increasingly effective participants and leaders, including starting new witnessing communities on campuses 

 

Organizational Collaboration 

You work with a network of other local, area, regional, and national InterVarsity staff and volunteers so that our work reflects Biblical standards of excellence, integrity, and partnership. 

  • Partner with and respond positively to the direction and coaching of your supervisors and national leaders 

  • Contribute to collaborative and productive team meetings and relationships 

  • Affiliate chapters under your care and submit Graduating Student Forms in order to increase our partnership with current students and alumni 

  • Use national ministry resources and tools, as requested, including recruiting and/or participating in local, regional, or national conferences as  

  • Complete reporting, planning and review requirements in a timely way so that you and your supervisors can assess and improve your work as a CSM 

  • Comply with all InterVarsity policies and procedures 

 

Ministry Partnership Development 

You will develop a team of partners – churches and individuals (including alumni and community members) – who will resource the ministry financially, in prayer, or volunteer service that advances the mission. 

  • Raise 100% of the financial budget assigned by your supervisor 

  • Communicate regularly with your ministry partners, nurturing the relationship through visits, phone calls, emails and regular prayer letters 

  • Develop on-going, long-lasting partnership with alumni and volunteers 

  • Comply with all Ministry Partnership Policies 

  • Identify and invest in advocates who will build networks of volunteers and donors on InterVarsity’s behalf 

 

Accomplish all other assigned tasks as appropriate 

 

QUALIFICATIONS (common to all levels of CSM) 

  • Annually affirm InterVarsity’s Statement of Agreement (Doctrinal Basis and Purpose Statement). Abide by InterVarsity’s Code of Conduct. Believe and behave consonantly with InterVarsity’s Human Sexuality Theological Paper. Affirm and behave consonantly with InterVarsity’s “Women in Ministry Statement of Affirmation” 

  • Bachelor’s degree for CSMs assigned to a four-year campus. A minimum of an Associate’s degree for CSMs assigned to a two-year campus or a community college 

  • Strong interpersonal skills (including ability to minister to diverse ethnic communities and faculty) 

  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills 

  • Demonstrated problem solving skills 

  • Familiarity with word processing, presentation, email, and spreadsheet software 

 

WORK ENVIRONMENT/PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS 

The CSM position leads ministry in a college campus environment. A designated office space may or may not be available. The CSM is required to travel to on-campus and off- campus sites as appropriate. Off-campus travel includes, but is not limited to: student ministry conferences, Ministry Partnership Development meetings, and InterVarsity- sponsored training sessions, meetings, and conferences. The CSM is regularly required to communicate with others, and routinely uses standard office equipment such as computers, phones, photocopiers, filing cabinets, etc. 

Pay Range: $44,016.00 - $58,680.00 per year

Pay: This position is funded through personal fundraising. Accordingly, compensation will vary based on the ability of the individual to secure a donor team to fund the cost of his/her salary. The anticipated salary range for this position on a full-time basis (40 hours/week) is dependent on a variety of factors, including location and cost of living. The actual salary received, including any geographic adjustment to account for location and cost of living, is subject to the individual’s ability to raise funds necessary to cover the full amount of such salary within the range set forth in the job posting details.

Benefits:

We offer a competitive benefits package, including health care and retirement savings with a match. Eligibility is based on employee type and hours worked.  Benefits include the following:

  • 403(b) Retirement Savings Plan

  • 403(b) matching contributions

  • Dental insurance

  • Employee assistance program

  • Employee discounts

  • Flexible work schedule

  • Flexible spending accounts

  • Health insurance

  • Health savings account

  • Life insurance

  • Paid time off

  • Parental leave

  • Professional development assistance

  • Vision insurance

Equal Employment Opportunity: 

 

InterVarsity Christian Fellowship/USA is both an equal opportunity employer and a faith-based religious organization. We conduct hiring without regard to race, color, ancestry, national origin, citizenship, age, sex, marital status, parental status, membership in any labor organization, political ideology, or disability of an otherwise qualified individual. The status of InterVarsity Christian Fellowship/USA as an equal opportunity employer does not prevent the organization from hiring staff based on their religious beliefs so that all staff share the same religious commitment.  Pursuant to the Civil Rights Act of 1964, Section 702 (42 U.S.C. 2000e 1(a)) InterVarsity Christian Fellowship/USA has the right to, and does, hire only candidates who agree with InterVarsity’s Statement of Agreement: Purpose and Doctrinal Basis because InterVarsity believes that each and every staff plays a vital role in advancing InterVarsity’s mission and purposes.

*This is a support-based position. You will need to be eligible for employment in the US to apply for this position.

Program Outline

A Season of Development for a Lifetime of Ministry

The Center Church Residency is a purposeful, two-year leadership development program for 22–25-year-olds who are exploring vocational ministry and desire a season of intentional development and service to the local church.

Each resident will serve within a ministry track based on their gifts, experience, and the needs of the church. Ministry tracks may include Connections, Operations, Discipleship & Groups, Missions, Prayer, Students, Kids, Worship & Production, Creative Communications, and Salt Company (College Ministry).

Our vision is to build an outpost of the Kingdom of God that changes the spiritual climate of our city, and that starts with leaders who lead the way. Over the course of two years, residents will be developed holistically in theology, character, leadership, and ministry skill, preparing them to faithfully serve wherever God sends them.

Invested in Your Development

We believe deeply in investing in the next generation of ministry leaders. As part of the residency, Center Church provides funding to help residents pursue theological education or professional development.

Residents may use this funding toward a seminary degree from Southeastern Baptist Theological Seminary (SEBTS), with support available for up to two classes during the fall and spring semesters, or they may use those funds toward other professional development opportunities that align with their growth and ministry goals.

Our hope is to help each resident develop in ways that are both theologically grounded and practically equipped, connecting what they are learning to the realities of ministry and their unique calling.

Real Responsibility and Kingdom Impact

At Center Church, residents don't just observe ministry—they lead, serve, build, and take ownership.

Residents will be given meaningful responsibility within their ministry track, leading teams, shepherding people, managing projects, and contributing to the life and mission of the church. You will have opportunities to develop the practical skills and leadership instincts necessary for long-term ministry while being consistently shepherded and challenged by experienced leaders.

Throughout the residency, you will also gain a deeper understanding of what it means to make, mature, and multiply disciples and to live out the Great Commission in the local church and beyond.

We are looking for men and women who are hungry to grow, eager to be shepherded, committed to the local church, and passionate about the Great Commission. Our hope is that residents leave Center with greater clarity about how God has uniquely gifted and called them, along with the character, theological foundation, and leadership experience to faithfully steward those gifts for the sake of the Kingdom.

Job Description

The average time commitment for the residency is approximately 40 hours per week. We prioritize healthy rhythms of work and rest and want residents to have two days off each week.

A typical week will include:

  • Staff Meetings & Leadership Development: 2–3 hours per week
  • Ministry Track: 20–25 hours per week
  • Administration & Support Raising: 1 hour per week
  • Sunday Services & Ministry: 8-12 hours per week
  • Seminary (optional): 3-6 hours per week

The specific rhythm and responsibilities will vary based on each resident's ministry track and season of development.

Next Steps

Click 'Apply to Position' to express your interest in the Center Church Residency. After an initial screening, we will send you the full application and next steps in the process.

We'd love to get to know you, hear more about how God has been working in your life, and explore whether the Center Residency could be the next step in your ministry journey.

Campus Staff Minister - Tennessee (Graduate & Faculty Ministry)

Work Location:

Tennessee

Job Type:

Full time

God has called InterVarsity to plant and to build witnessing communities of students and faculty who follow Jesus on college and university campuses. Through these groups, we believe ever- increasing numbers of students and faculty from all ethnic groups and areas of the campus will be transformed by the Gospel. We expect to see campuses increasingly become places where people, ideas, and structures flourish to the glory of God. We confidently anticipate that our InterVarsity alumni will become change agents across the country and around the world. We pursue this calling by discerning and actively participating in what God is already doing on campus. This is the essence of being a Campus Staff Minister (CSM).

Please submit the GFM Interest Form before completing the full application for a position with Graduate & Faculty Ministries in our online system. We will contact you when we are ready to proceed with the application process.  

This position is open to applicants working less than 40 hours/week. If you are interested in part-time work please apply for this position. 

The pay range listed is for an employee working 40 hours/week at CSM level II. Pay will be prorated for employees who work less than 40 hours/week.

Volunteers are welcome. Volunteer opportunities range from prayer and hospitality to leading a campus fellowship of graduate students and faculty. Those interested in volunteering will go through an application and interview process, however, volunteer openings are not posted online. For more information, complete the GFM Interest Form. 

ESSENTIAL COMMITMENTS/RESPONSIBILITIES 

Spiritual Growth 

As a Campus Staff Minister, you pursue maturity as a disciple of Jesus Christ so that your life and work increasingly reflect a growing love for God, God’s Word, God’s people of every ethnicity and culture, and God’s purposes in the world. To do this, you will: 

  • Pursue a vibrant relationship with the triune God through engagement with Scripture, prayer, and worship, both individually and in community

  • Develop self-leadership (growing in self-awareness, self-management, relational integrity, and resiliency) 

  • Embrace Scriptural standards for behavior and attitudes 

 

Campus Leadership 

As a Campus Staff Minister, you increase the number of witnessing communities, as well as the size, health, spiritual maturity, and campus-wide influence of existing witnessing communities of students and faculty by being a: 

  • Visionary Guide: 

You communicate and model InterVarsity’s vision to see students and faculty transformed, campuses renewed, and world changers developed 

  • Create a culture of humble dependence on God and bold expectation in God’s intention to start new witnessing communities throughout the campus and on new campuses 

  • Model – in person and through programs – InterVarsity’s vision and Core Values, including a biblically-defined commitment to engage every ethnic and social group on campus 

  • Lead students and faculty – individually and collectively – through Scripture, prayer, teaching, and discipleship experiences, so that they articulate and align their ministry activities around this vision 

  • Set annual goals through prayer, research and reflection with your teams (students, faculty, and staff) for qualitative and quantitative growth, including conversions and leadership development 

  • Structural Architect: 

You create, develop, align, and leverage ministry plans, programs, teams, and structures to close the gap between current reality and the aspirational goals. 

  • Build leadership teams who trust and partner well with you and who demonstrate spiritual vitality, relational health, and mission alignment 

  • Develop and execute plans to achieve annual goals, evaluating and modifying the plan as needed throughout the year 

  • Increase momentum for the vision by aligning programs, structures, conferences, and teams around the goals 

  • Mobilize students and faculty to engage their relational networks with the gospel and to start new missional communities 

  • Under the direction of the Area Director, may supervise Ministry Interns and Campus Ministry Interns as delegated 

  • Missional Developer: 

You intentionally gather, invite, and develop diverse groups of students and faculty so that they not only encounter and follow Jesus as Savior and Lord but also advance the mission on campus as participants and leaders. 

  • Create ways for faculty and students to encounter and follow Jesus through Scripture, worship, prayer, mission experiences, conferences, etc. 

  • Equip students and faculty so that they think strategically about campus engagement and so that they proclaim – in word, deed, and power – the good news of Jesus, regularly inviting students and faculty to follow him as Savior and Lord 

  • Disciple students and faculty by equipping them to hear the Word, respond actively, and debrief and interpret the experience so that they grow in Christlikeness, reflect our Core Values, and develop ministry skills 

  • Invite, coach, and equip students and faculty to become increasingly effective participants and leaders, including starting new witnessing communities on campuses 

 

Organizational Collaboration 

As a Campus Staff Minister, you have joined a national mission. Therefore, you work with a network of other local, area, regional, and national InterVarsity staff and volunteers so that our work reflects Biblical standards of excellence, integrity, and partnership. 

  • Partner with and respond positively to the direction and coaching of your supervisors and national leaders 

  • Contribute to collaborative and productive team meetings and relationships 

  • Affiliate chapters under your care and submit Graduating Student Forms in order to increase our partnership with current students and alumni 

  • Use national ministry resources and tools, as requested, including recruiting and/or participating in local, regional, or national conferences as  

  • Complete reporting, planning and review requirements in a timely way so that you and your supervisors can assess and improve your work as a CSM 

  • Comply with all InterVarsity policies and procedures 

 

Ministry Partnership Development 

As a Campus Staff Minister, you will develop a team of partners – churches and individuals (including alumni and community members) – who will resource the ministry financially, in prayer, or volunteer service that advances the mission. 

  • Raise 100% of the financial budget assigned by your supervisor 

  • Communicate regularly with your ministry partners, nurturing the relationship through visits, phone calls, emails and regular prayer letters 

  • Develop on-going, long-lasting partnership with alumni and volunteers 

  • Comply with all Ministry Partnership Policies 

  • Identify and invest in advocates who will build networks of volunteers and donors on InterVarsity’s behalf 

 

Accomplish all other assigned tasks as appropriate 

 

QUALIFICATIONS (common to all levels of CSM) 

  • Annually affirm InterVarsity’s Statement of Agreement (Doctrinal Basis and Purpose Statement). Abide by InterVarsity’s Code of Conduct. Believe and behave consonantly with InterVarsity’s Human Sexuality Theological Paper. Affirm and behave consonantly with InterVarsity’s “Women in Ministry Statement of Affirmation” 

  • Bachelor’s degree for CSMs assigned to a four-year campus. A minimum of an Associate’s degree for CSMs assigned to a two-year campus or a community college 

  • Strong interpersonal skills (including ability to minister to diverse ethnic communities and faculty) 

  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills 

  • Demonstrated problem solving skills 

  • Familiarity with word processing, presentation, email, and spreadsheet software 

 

WORK ENVIRONMENT/PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS 

The CSM position leads ministry in a college campus environment. A designated office space may or may not be available. The CSM is required to travel to on-campus and off- campus sites as appropriate. Off-campus travel includes, but is not limited to: student ministry conferences, Ministry Partnership Development meetings, and InterVarsity- sponsored training sessions, meetings, and conferences. The CSM is regularly required to communicate with others, and routinely uses standard office equipment such as computers, phones, photocopiers, filing cabinets, etc. 

Pay Range: $44,016.00 - $58,680.00 per year

Pay: This position is funded through personal fundraising. Accordingly, compensation will vary based on the ability of the individual to secure a donor team to fund the cost of his/her salary. The anticipated salary range for this position on a full-time basis (40 hours/week) is dependent on a variety of factors, including location and cost of living. The actual salary received, including any geographic adjustment to account for location and cost of living, is subject to the individual’s ability to raise funds necessary to cover the full amount of such salary within the range set forth in the job posting details.

Benefits:

We offer a competitive benefits package, including health care and retirement savings with a match. Eligibility is based on employee type and hours worked.  Benefits include the following:

  • 403(b) Retirement Savings Plan

  • 403(b) matching contributions

  • Dental insurance

  • Employee assistance program

  • Employee discounts

  • Flexible work schedule

  • Flexible spending accounts

  • Health insurance

  • Health savings account

  • Life insurance

  • Paid time off

  • Parental leave

  • Professional development assistance

  • Vision insurance

Equal Employment Opportunity: 

 

InterVarsity Christian Fellowship/USA is both an equal opportunity employer and a faith-based religious organization. We conduct hiring without regard to race, color, ancestry, national origin, citizenship, age, sex, marital status, parental status, membership in any labor organization, political ideology, or disability of an otherwise qualified individual. The status of InterVarsity Christian Fellowship/USA as an equal opportunity employer does not prevent the organization from hiring staff based on their religious beliefs so that all staff share the same religious commitment.  Pursuant to the Civil Rights Act of 1964, Section 702 (42 U.S.C. 2000e 1(a)) InterVarsity Christian Fellowship/USA has the right to, and does, hire only candidates who agree with InterVarsity’s Statement of Agreement: Purpose and Doctrinal Basis because InterVarsity believes that each and every staff plays a vital role in advancing InterVarsity’s mission and purposes.

About This Role

The Preschool Minister shepherds our preschool ministry (birth through pre-K) at Severns Valley Baptist Church. This role exists to help young children and their families pursue God, grow in faith, and connect with our church family—fulfilling their role in God's story.
 
This is relational, hands-on work. You'll create a safe, joyful, gospel-centered environment where young children can begin to know and love Jesus. You'll invest deeply in volunteer leaders, walk alongside parents as they disciple their children, and lead with warmth and presence. You're not managing programs; you're shepherding people.
 
Whether you're new to ministry leadership or transitioning into kids ministry, you'll join a great team of SV Kids staff and volunteers. You won't figure this out alone. You'll be supported through a six-month partnership with Shepherd Staff, which provides weekly coaching, volunteer development training, and the systems and rhythms that make sustainable ministry possible.
 
You'll serve under the Lead Pastor and work closely with the SV Kids Team, other ministry leaders, and the families God has entrusted to our care.
 

What You'll Do

 
Our values are pursue, equip, and connect. You'll see those three running through everything in this role.
Pursue — Shepherd children and families toward Jesus
 
  • Lead by example in discipleship and pastoral care
  • Build relationships with children through consistent presence and genuine care
  • Walk alongside parents as the primary disciple-makers in their children's lives—equipping them, not replacing them
  • Lead and teach regularly in preschool environments on Sunday mornings and Wednesday evenings
  • Develop ministry pathways that welcome every child and create belonging for those with special needs
 
Equip — Build and develop a thriving volunteer ecosystem
  • Identify, recruit, and develop a strong team of volunteer leaders who share the vision
  •  Train and empower volunteers in their spiritual growth and leadership
  •  Build a culture where volunteers feel equipped, valued, and called to something bigger than programming
  •  Oversee classroom setup, curriculum preparation, seasonal environments, and overall ministry space management
  •  Select or develop age-appropriate curriculum for Sunday morning, midweek, and topical studies
 
Connect — Build bridges between children, families, and our church family
  • Plan and execute family programming, outreach events, and seasonal activities
  • Help lead VBS and preschool-related missions and service opportunities
  • Partner with the SV staff team to maintain a consistent discipleship pathway from birth through senior adulthood
  • Be present at key church events and gatherings to foster connection and strengthen community
  • Work closely with the SV Kids Team to align vision and values across all children's ministry environments

Who We're Looking For

We're seeking someone relational, teachable, and spiritually grounded. Someone passionate about helping preschool children and families step into a vibrant faith. You may be early in your ministry leadership journey, but you demonstrate strong character, real potential, and a genuine heart for young children and families.
 
Essential Qualities
  • A committed follower of Jesus whose life reflects the gospel—anchored in Scripture and evangelical, Reformed theology within the SBC tradition
  • Genuine passion for discipling children and partnering with families
  • Relational leadership style—you connect well with volunteers, parents, and staff
  • Teachable and humble—open to coaching, feedback, and growth
  • Organized and self-motivated—able to plan, execute, and steward a calendar and team
  • Able to communicate clearly and lead with warmth, energy, and presence
  • Emotionally intelligent and relationally skilled—able to read a room and adapt
  • Comfortable with Google Workspace and basic digital tools
  • Aligned with SVBC's theology, mission, and values—willing to become a member
 
Ideal Background & Experience
  • Background in preschool education (local school teacher preferred) or experience serving in children's ministry, education, camps, VBS, or related environments
  •  Some volunteer or leadership experience; full-time ministry experience is not required
  •  Demonstrated ability to recruit, develop, and empower volunteers
  •  Proven gifts in teaching and one-on-one pastoral care
  •  A degree or ministry training is helpful but not required; we're looking for teachability and character above all

How We'll Support You

You won't figure this out alone. The selected candidate will participate in the six-month Kids Ministry Leadership Development (KMLD) Program through our partnership with Shepherd Staff. Weekly coaching, practical training, and ongoing support will equip you to thrive.
 
What the KMLD Program Provides:
  • Weekly coaching and leadership development
  • Child safety and ministry systems training
  • Volunteer recruitment and leadership strategies
  • Parent partnership and discipleship coaching
  • Curriculum planning and teaching support
  • Sustainable ministry rhythms and healthy leadership practices
  • Ongoing encouragement, accountability, and practical tools
We're not looking for someone to run programs. We're investing in a leader with real potential—someone who can grow into a healthy, sustainable, and impactful preschool ministry through coaching, support, and partnership.
 

What Success Looks Like

 
We want you to thrive in this role, not just survive it. Here's what your first 12–18 months look like:
 
  • First 90 Days: Learn & Connect
  • Build genuine relationships with volunteers, childcare staff, and families. Know their names, their stories, what keeps them serving.
  • Observe the rhythms, systems, and culture of preschool ministry before making changes
  • Meet with the SV Kids Team and key volunteer leaders; understand how preschool ministry connects to the broader church
  • Identify volunteer capacity—who's thriving, who's stretched, where the gaps are
Months 4–9: Build & Strengthen
  • Establish a sustainable volunteer recruitment and development pipeline. Build a growing team of equipped leaders, not one person carrying the load.
  • Establish clear communication rhythms with volunteers and families so people feel informed, valued, and connected
  • Refine classroom environments, curriculum, and systems to reflect both excellence and warmth
  • Identify and invest in potential team leaders who can own specific areas of ministry
Months 10–18: Multiply & Flourish
  •  Volunteer leaders are taking real ownership of key areas—rooms, events, training—not just filling slots
  •  Families are engaged and connected—not dropping kids off, but growing in their role as the primary disciplers of their children
  •  The ministry can sustain a Sunday absence from you because your team is equipped and empowered
  • The gospel-centered vision for preschool ministry is understood and carried by your volunteer team, not just you

 Compensation & Benefits

 We believe in caring well for those who shepherd our flock. We offer:
  •  Competitive Salary: $45,000–$50,000 depending on experience and background
  •  Health Insurance: Comprehensive health, dental, vision, and life insurance
  •  Disability Coverage: Short and long-term disability insurance
  •  Retirement Plan: 403(b) with church contribution
  •  Professional Development: Encouraged and funded by the church (conferences, training, resources)
  •  Moving/Relocation Assistance: Available to help with transition
  •  Vacation: 2–5 weeks annually depending on ministry experience
  •  Sabbath: We believe in rest. You'll be encouraged to actually take your days off.

Next Steps

 
If the Lord is stirring something as you read this, we'd be honored to start a conversation.
 
Interested candidates are invited to submit their application at:
 
https://tss.chat/242412_OP

About Severns Valley

 
Severns Valley Baptist Church is a multi-generational church family in Elizabethtown, Kentucky. We gather Sundays at 9:00 a.m. and 10:45 a.m. at 1100 Ring Road. Our purpose is simple:
 
Love God. Love people. Make disciples.
We pursue that purpose through three environments:

Program Overview

Praying Pelican Missions (PPM) exists to equip, encourage, and support local churches in reaching their communities for Christ.  The Ministry Leader program is designed to develop, equip, and support Christian leaders in ministry through investing in genuine partnerships. Serving as a vital bridge between local churches and mission teams, Ministry Leaders facilitate both the logistical and relational dimensions of PPM short-term trips. Participants engage in a comprehensive training model that combines interactive video conferences, digital learning modules, and immersive on-the-field experience to prepare them for impactful service. 

The Ministry Leader position is seasonal, beginning January 4th and ending August 13th, 2027. The Ministry Leader will act as vital support to their assigned location, assisting with trip setup, team consulting as assigned, and trip leading. 

Key Responsibilities

  • Professional Conduct: Promote a positive image of PPM, build trust across staff, and maintain healthy, God-honoring team relationships.
  • Trip Preparation: From January through May, commit 10 hours weekly to leadership development, trip setup-related tasks, and group consulting. Assist group leaders with spiritual and logistical prep, ensuring all capstone calls and pre-trip requirements are completed before departure. 
  • Ministry Operations: Partner with the location leader to source ministry opportunities and finalize team itineraries. Lead daily operations on the ground—managing schedules, logistics, and supplies while actively serving alongside teams in community outreach and service projects.
  • Leadership Support: Support Location Leadership in executing team delegations through joining L10 location meetings or, if unavailable, report directly to your Operations Leader.
  • Spring Field Training: Complete at least one PPM training mission trip experience in the assigned location between January and April. The Location Manager will coordinate this trip to familiarize the Ministry Leader with location logistics, host partners, and ministry operations. This requirement must be completed by late April unless an exception is approved by the Program Manager.
  • Summer Trip Leading: Complete all required preparations to serve as an effective Trip Leader during the busy summer season, leading 8-10 mission trips based on scheduling needs.
  • Offboarding Commitment: Complete program wrap-up requirements including finishing expense reports, completing all trip leader surveys, having an end-of-summer exit interview with the program manager, return of all PPM equipment if applicable, and fulfillment of all scheduled trip assignments.

Requirements

  • Faith & Alignment: You are a devoted Christ-follower who is actively engaged in your local church. You are in alignment with PPM’s Statement of Faith (a core requirement for all staff): It is as follows:
    • The Bible is God’s complete and perfect Word and our ultimate authority as followers of Christ. (2 Timothy 3)
    • We are all lost, fallen short of the glory of God, and in need of a Savior. (Romans 3)
    • Jesus came to earth for the purpose of seeking and saving the lost. (Luke 19:10)
    • Jesus died on the cross. Three days later, He rose from the grave, paying the ultimate sacrifice and conquering death for all who believe in Him. (1 Peter 3:18, 1 John 2:2, Romans 5:8, Romans 10:9)
    • As a result of God’s grace alone, through faith in Christ alone, we are saved. (Ephesians 2, John 14)
    • Jesus, God, and the Holy Spirit are One. (John 1)
    • Jesus Himself commissioned His followers (the Church) to go into the world and make disciples. (Matthew 28) 
  • Character: Those who know you consider you humble, dependable, and see no task as too big or too small. You’re excited to work with people from diverse cultural, geographical, and denominational backgrounds each week, knowing you’re good at uniting people and able to focus on common ground rather than differences. You are a problem-solver who is adaptable, not easily thrown off by changes to schedules or environments. You get excited about close community living and working, and have a commitment to servant leadership.
  • Leadership Experience: You must have proven leadership experience, preferably in missions and/ or a previous PPM leadership mission setting.  
  • Age & Availability:
    Open to candidates 18 and older, with a strong preference for applicants 21 or older. Position requires a commitment of 10 hours/week from Jan–May, followed by a flexible summer schedule leading 6 to 10 weeks of trips from late May–Aug, based on operational need.
  • Licensed Driver: Must possess a valid driver’s license and be prepared to safely transport others during the trip week to and from sites.
  • Mandatory Training:
    Attendance at meetings and trips on the following dates is required:
    • Program Orientation via video conference the week of January 4th, 2027.
    • Weekly training sessions as assigned by the program manager via video conference 
      • If a session cannot be joined due to an approved absence (class or work conflict), ML will work with the program manager to make up training. Proof of attendance will be required.
    • Commit to completing Pelican University online training by the assigned deadline. 
    • Attend an on-site training trip in the assigned location between January and April. 
    • In-person attendance at the PPM Spring Conference in Black Mountain, North Carolina, from April 23-25, 2027 is required.

Benefits and Compensation

Travel Benefits

  • Air travel, lodging, and meal expenses are covered by PPM for applicable weeks of service as well as the Spring Conference.
    • Mileage reimbursement may be available for those who live within driving distance of their assigned location. Must be pre-approved by the location manager.

Please note: All travel and lodging will be managed by PPM Operations Staff. Meals will be allotted within budgeting parameters.

Compensation 

  • PPM considers you a seasonal employee and, therefore, ineligible for the benefit plans available to regular year-round employees, unless stated otherwise. 
  • PPM classifies this position as exempt from minimum wage and overtime pay through the ministerial exception to the Fair Labor Standards Act.
  • PPM will apply deductions for standard payroll taxes related to earnings and taxable benefits.
  • January through August: in recognition of ML training, consulting, trip planning, and spring mission trip experience
    • New Ministry Leader pay rate is $700 per month ($350 per pay period)
    • Returning Ministry Leader pay rate is $770 per month ($385 per pay period)
    • Payment is twice monthly on the 15th and last business day of each month, with the first pay date to occur on January 29th, 2027.

Bonus Eligibility and Payout: MLs are eligible for bonuses for each trip worked. These will be paid out the month after completing the trip (ex- March trip paid on April 30). Bonuses are calculated as follows:

  • $450/week that the ML served as a Trip Leader
  • $250/week that the ML served as an Assistant Trip Leader

job_name: Senior Pastor at Corry Alliance Church
post_html:
THE POSITION

TITLE: Senior Pastor

ORGANIZATION: Corry Christian & Missionary Alliance Church

LOCATION: 721 Hatch Street, Corry, PA 16407

WEBSITE: www.corryalliance.org

MISSION: A Christ-centered church with a family-oriented ministry. Love God, love others, and make disciples

Core Values:

  • Solid Biblical Preaching – 2 Timothy 4:2
  • Persistent Prayer – 1 Thessalonians 5:16-28
  • God-Centered Worship – John 4:24
  • Global Witness – Matthew 28:19-20

A CHURCH PROFILE - 2026 INTRODUCTION AND HISTORY

The Corry Alliance Church is located in the rural community of Corry, Pennsylvania. The City of Corry (pop. 6,210) is centrally located approximately 2 hours from Pittsburgh, Buffalo, and Cleveland. The church is located on Route 6 on the western side of the state, approximately one-hour south-east of Lake Erie.

Many residents in Corry enjoy the four seasons each year that are beautiful and allow many opportunities for outdoor activities. Corry was originally founded as a Climax locomotive manufacturing city and still is home to many other manufacturing businesses. The church is twenty minutes from a great ski & golf resort and only one hour from the beaches on Lake Erie. Corry is known for being a safe place to raise children and has a great school system. The average graduating class is approximately 150 students.

Corry Alliance Church was founded as part of the Christian and Missionary Alliance in 1893 by a handful of members who first met in homes and tents before moving to the first church building in 1895. The members met faithfully at this location until the property was purchased at the corner of Route 6 and Hatch Street in 1975. As the church grew in the early 2000’s, we built a two-story addition with conference room, handicap elevator, and rooms for starting a daycare. The daycare later expanded into the Corry Alliance Academy for schooling kindergarten and first grade. A second addition was built in 2010 for the Academy, which now houses 68 students from kindergarten through sixth grade.

WORSHIP & MUSIC

We currently have two worship services each Sunday morning – an 8am and 10:45am service. The first service typically ends around 9:10am and Sunday School begins at 9:30am with the second service to follow. Musically, the Corry Alliance has transitioned from strictly traditional music to a mixture of current worship choruses and hymns with doctrinally sound lyrics. The worship music is the same in both services. Selected weekly music is led by a contemporary style worship team.

SUNDAY SCHOOL

Currently, we offer a variety of classes for all ages on Sunday mornings. There are five adult classes to choose from as well as classes for toddlers, school-age children and teens. Classes are held from 9:30am-10:30am. Each class has its own curriculum.

CHILDREN’S MINISTRY

The Corry Alliance is blessed to offer many options for kids of all ages. Sunday ministries for children include nursery and toddler care, Sunday School and Children’s Church for ages four through grade one. Midweek from September through April, the church offers an AWANA program for pre-k through grade six. The church holds its annual Vacation Bible School the first full week of summer vacation. Our VBS is a summer highlight that has a large community impact.

YOUTH MINISTRY

The church employs a full-time Assistant Pastor of Youth who manages the ministries for students in grades 6 through 12. The youth pastor runs the youth Sunday School, Sunday night Refuge youth ministry, and a chapter of Impact Campus Fellowship in the local public junior/senior high school. Refuge youth ministries purposes to provide a refuge for youth to hear the soul-saving news of the gospel, fellowship, have fun, and know and share Psalm 46:1 – “God is our refuge and strength, a very present help in trouble.” The church has contact with over one hundred youth through the church and school ministries.

ADULT / FAMILY

The Corry Alliance Church offers Sunday evening services, a mid-week prayer meeting, a men’s Bible study, etc. Also offered are many other small group studies, gatherings, etc.

OUTREACH

The Corry Alliance Church strives to introduce people to Christ through a variety of outreach opportunities including:

  • Alliance Daycare / childcare (Newborn – Elementary)
  • Corry Alliance Academy (K - Grade 6)
  • Vacation Bible School (June)
  • AWANA (age three – grade six)(September – March)
  • Annual Game Dinner – (January)
  • Impact Campus Fellowship outreach into the Corry public Jr./Sr. High School
  • CMA Cross Country team – (pre-k – grade six)
  • Friends Group ? Hallelujah Party
  • Women’s prayer meeting / Bible Studies
  • Life Resource Center
  • As opportunities arise in the community (Community Service Projects, parades, etc.)
  • Summer mornings with moms (playground events)

MISSIONS

We understand the importance of the Great Commission Fund to assist in reaching the lost with the gospel. We offer short-term ministry opportunities for church members as well as support many domestic mission teams. Our teens and children also participate in the Operation Christmas Child shoebox program. Our missions weekend includes a different missionary each year and a dinner or tea time to dig deeper into their ministries from around the world.

PHYSICAL FACILITY

Our building sits on an 18-acre lot which includes a softball field and several playgrounds. The church parsonage sits on the back of the property but faces Hillcrest Drive. You can walk the cross-country trail or drive approximately 2 miles to access the parsonage. The church sanctuary comfortably holds approximately 400 people. The fellowship hall/gymnasium serves multiple purposes and contains a commercial kitchen. The Academy and Daycare are located within the main building.

EDINBORO CAMP AND RETREAT CENTER

Edinboro Camp is located approximately 45 minutes away. The Corry Alliance Church is partnered and committed physically and financially to the mission and ministry of Edinboro Camp. Among other things, we provide camp scholarships to AWANA students who complete their studies and help older youth fundraise for camp. Annually, we support approximately 40 students financially and prayerfully to attend camp.

LEADERSHIP STRUCTURE

Our church leadership structure consists of an Elder board and a Governing Board who oversee the spiritual and financial aspects of the church and its ministries. A deaconess committee holds a critical role in support of the needs of the church.

The Academy has a school board as well as a full-time principal and the day care has a full-time director overseeing the daily tasks while reporting to the Elder and Governing boards.

STAFF & ADMINISTRATION

  • Senior Pastor
  • Assistant Pastor of Youth
  • Church Administrative Assistant
  • Academy Administrator
    • Academy Employees
  • Daycare Director
    • Daycare Workers
  • Custodians

FINANCES AND BUDGET

The Corry Alliance is a financially healthy church that prioritizes wise stewardship of the resources that God has given us.

POSITION SUMMARY

The Senior Pastor of Corry Alliance Church will be an advocate for, support, and bring life to the vision of loving God, loving others, and making disciples. This is done under the authority of the elders and shared leadership with the staff. The Senior Pastor is ultimately responsible to Christ, who is the true head of Corry Alliance Church. The Senior Pastor is a member of the church and operates under its bylaws.

REPORTING RELATIONSHIPS - The Senior Pastor reports to the Elder Board.

SENIOR PASTOR RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Preaching/Teaching o Serve as the primary preacher/teacher, leading in the proclamation of the whole Word, sound doctrine, and worship.
    • Present the gospel so that the unsaved will be given regular opportunity to hear and to respond to the truth.
    • Lead the efforts to love God, love others, and make disciples.
    • Devote adequate time to personal prayer and Bible study.
    • Lead effort to create pathways for Discipleship. Build a culture of disciples, who are making future disciples.
  • Strategy/Vision/Direction
    • In conjunction with the Elders, develop and oversee the mission, vision, and strategy of the church, ensuring alignment with the clear teaching of Scripture. Serve as the primary communicator and leader of church mission, vision and strategy.
    • Actively encourage the church staff towards fulfillment of the church’s vision to Love God, Love Others, and Make Disciples.
    • Serving on the Elder Board with a team of elders to guide and lead the church family with skill and integrity.
    • Global Mission Minded – Great commission (Matthew 28:19-20)
  • Biblical Counseling & Pastoral Care
    • Be a leader of Biblical Counseling and support the church family where needed.
    • Oversee, in conjunction with our current staff, official church functions such as weddings, funerals, and other events.
    • Visit the sick, dying and hurting in conjunction with our lay leaders, prioritizing the needs.

WHAT YOU BRING

  • Education and Experience o Formal Seminary Education preferred.
    • Experience as a senior pastor preferred.
    • Ordained or willing to be ordained by the Christian and Missionary Alliance required.
    • Biblical Counseling background is preferred.
  • Character
    • The Senior Pastor must meet the qualifications for an elder listed in 1 Timothy 3:1-13, Titus 1:6 9 and 1 Peter 5:2-3.
    • The Senior Pastor must agree with the church bylaws, doctrinal statement, and overall mission, vision, and strategy.
    • Maintains a healthy, vibrant, and growing relationship with Jesus.
    • Relationship with wife / family is thriving.
    • Man of humility, grace, prayer, and love.
    • Demonstrates authenticity, steadiness, integrity, transparency, and Christ-centered confidence.
    • Continually growing, both personally and in ministry, regularly seeking to learn.
    • His identity is not found in the success of the ministry nor in those he serves, rather in Christ alone.
    • He seeks the glory of Jesus first in all things.
  • Personal Characteristics
  • Skills/Knowledge – Excellent oral and written communication skills, strong interpersonal skills, gifted communicator of God’s Word, high relational bent with an emphasis on caring for staff and leaders and church attendees.
  • Leadership – Leads with humility and team mentality as we lead and create disciples together (Ephesians 4:1-7)
  • Heart of love – He must have a love for God, his family, God’s people, the church, the lost and the ministry. He must be a pastor with a caring, shepherding spirit.
  • Man of faith – He must realize that without wisdom from God it is not possible to do the work of the ministry or even live a fruitful Christian life. Must model a life of faith and prayer.
  • Doctrinal Position – Willing to take a scriptural stance on worldly issues (i.e. LGBTQ, abortion, etc.) and an advocate of literal interpretation of scripture

AUTHORITY & STRUCTURE

Corry Alliance Church operates with a shared leadership model – Elders, Senior Pastor, and Assistant / Youth Pastor, working together to accomplish the vision of the church. The Senior Pastor serves as an Elder and has a voice into the vision and direction of the church. He is the primary communicator of the church vision and is responsible for the spiritual development of the staff to ensure a thriving team.

To be considered for this position, please complete the application to include your testimony, resume and other background information related to the position.

If the district office has reviewed your application and they think you may be a potential match for the position, that the hiring manager will reach out to you for next steps.
