First Alliance Church, a vibrant, multigenerational church located in suburban Lexington, Kentucky is prayerfully seeking its next Lead Pastor - a spiritually mature, visionary shepherd who can lead its next season of ministry and local and global impact for the Gospel.

First Alliance Church was founded in 1956 as a local church in the Christian & Missionary Alliance denomination. Following a recent leadership transition, FAC is prayerfully seeking its next Lead Pastor. FAC has experienced meaningful growth in attendance, engagement, and giving. Sunday morning attendance is averaging over 1700 people. We are seeking a visionary leader who will lead the church forward in its mission to be a loving community of disciple-makers who passionately pursue God, extend life-changing hope, and disciple people to be Spirit-empowered followers of Jesus. The Lead Pastor will honor FAC’s history while helping the church move forward with clarity, unity, and renewed outward focus.

Duties and Responsibilities
The Lead Pastor serves the body of Christ at FAC by providing spiritual, pastoral, and strategic leadership for First Alliance Church, giving general oversight to the church’s ministry, staff, and mission.

Preaching and Teaching
Serve as the primary preacher and teacher, handling the Word of God with biblical depth, clarity, and practical application.
Teach in a way that forms mature disciples, calls people to faithful obedience, and shapes the theological direction and spiritual tone of worship.
Work with appropriate staff to plan worship services that are biblically grounded and spiritually formative.

Spiritual Leadership and Shepherding
Shepherd the congregation with humility, warmth, approachability, and spiritual maturity.
Give strategic oversight to congregational care while empowering staff and lay leaders to provide direct care.
Lead in a way that reflects a deep, visible, and contagious walk with Jesus, helping the church build trust, heal from transition, and move forward with unity.

Vision and Strategic Direction
Work with the Leadership Board and staff to clarify and advance the church's next season of ministry, casting vision clearly and consistently.
Help move vision from discussion to action through clear plans, priorities, and follow-through.
Lead with prayerful discernment, wise decisiveness, and a willingness to evaluate and refine ministry goals as needed.

Staff Health and Organizational Leadership
Build, empower, and release a healthy leadership team by delegating leadership, not only tasks, to qualified staff and ministry leaders.
Clarify staff roles, reporting relationships, expectations, and accountability rhythms.
Develop and mentor key staff and leaders, helping establish healthy systems for goals, feedback, evaluation, and growth.

Churchwide Discipleship and Leadership Development
Strengthen a culture of discipleship throughout the church by identifying and developing emerging staff, lay leaders, and volunteers.
Equip leaders to disciple, develop, and empower others through healthy leadership pipelines.
Help connect spiritual formation, ministry service, and leadership development into a unified culture of growth.

Outreach, Evangelism, and Mission
Champion local outreach, global missions, and evangelism as central to the life of the church.
Support and empower the Pastor of Outreach and Missions, encouraging pathways for people to share their faith and serve their neighbors.
Keep the church focused on reaching neighbors, the nations, and the next generation, welcoming new believers into community and discipleship.

Board Partnership and Governance
Report regularly to the Leadership Board, working together to establish long-term goals, priorities, and measures of success.
Support healthy communication and alignment between the Board, staff, and congregation.
Receive feedback with humility, participate in regular accountability, and help the Board identify major ministry opportunities, challenges, and staffing needs.

Personal Health and Accountability
Maintain a growing personal relationship with Jesus Christ, pursuing healthy accountability with trusted people inside and outside the church.
Demonstrate humility, self-awareness, teachability, and integrity in all areas of life.
Protect personal, family, spiritual, and emotional health, leading from maturity, humility, and integrity.


Qualifications and Expectations
Spiritual and Theological
Meets the biblical qualifications for elder/pastor.
Fully aligned with the doctrine, mission, and polity of the Christian & Missionary Alliance.
Ordained or willing and able to pursue ordination with the Christian & Missionary Alliance.
Demonstrates a life marked by prayer, humility, integrity, and dependence on the Holy Spirit.

Educational
Graduate-level theological education preferred, such as an M.Div., M.A. in Theology/Ministry, or equivalent.
Demonstrated ability to preach, teach, and apply Scripture with depth and clarity.
Commitment to ongoing theological, pastoral, and leadership development.

Ministry Experience
Significant pastoral leadership experience in a local church.
Experience preaching and teaching in a congregational setting.
Experience leading staff, ministry teams, or key leaders.
Experience in a growing, multi-generational church preferred.
Experience working with boards, elders, or governing leadership teams preferred.

Reporting Structure
Ongoing direction and performance evaluation are provided by the FAC Leadership Board.
Accountability for pastoral licensing and church polity comes from the Ohio Valley District of the Christian & Missionary Alliance.

To be considered for this position, please complete the application to include your testimony, resume and other background information related to the position.

If the district office has reviewed your application and they think you may be a potential match for the position, that the hiring manager will reach out to you for next steps.

This position requires licensing with The Christian & Missionary Alliance. To learn more about The Alliance and requirements for licensing, please visit our website

post_html:
WORSHIP DIRECTOR

POSITION OVERVIEW

At the Washington Alliance Church, the Lord has been growing us in many ways, and we see His impact within our church and in our community expanding (Acts 2:47). Presently, we find ourselves following His direction to find a Worship Director who can be an integral member of our leadership team. This is a full-time support position to build and develop our ministry groups responsible for the music and media elements of our worship services. The Worship Director will work closely with our lead pastor and other support staff in cultivating services and developing teams that lead our congregation in true and intimate worship of our Savior (John 4:23).

It is our desire that the Worship Director bring their God-given gifts of creativity, musical skill, Biblical foundations, and heart for shepherding and “presence-ministry” to our team. Our church body has a desire to truly worship, and we believe the Holy Spirit will continue to lead us and teach us. We sing the best of old and the best of new songs to Jesus, but we also recognize that true worship is so much more than music (Romans 12:1).

Finding our Worship Director, whom we believe God has been preparing, is a priority for our church. To the best of our understanding, we are seeking an individual who is called and gifted by God to join our teams and lead in the following areas:

RESPONSIBILITIES FOR WORSHIP (MUSIC)

The primary current need and critical responsibility for the Worship Director is oversight and leadership of the worship music ministry at our church.

  • Develop worship services that encourage and welcome people to encounter the presence of God and connect with Him
  • Lead the congregation and the members of the music ministry and media teams to grow in their hunger and relationship with God through worship
  • Modeling and leading passionate and heartfelt worship in an invitational style that draws people into the throne room, encourages participation, and points people to Jesus
  • Create and teach a worship culture, and effectively communicate vision for worship
  • Capable of selecting songs prayerfully that will resonate with the congregation and align with the overall worship vision
  • Serve as the music director, leading and shepherding the current and expanding worship teams, mentor volunteer worship leaders, and giving leadership opportunities to others as appropriate
  • Utilize a mix of new, current, and traditional songs and styles, understanding the mixed demographics of our congregation

RESPONSIBILITIES FOR WORSHIP (MEDIA & OTHER MINISTRIES)

In addition to music, the Worship Director will be critically involved in leadership and development of the media team as well as opportunities to partner with other ministries of the church in regard to worshipping the Lord.

  • Provide vision and oversight for our technical ministries — including sound, video, lighting, ProPresenter, and Planning Center — working alongside an existing team of dedicated volunteers to continue developing these areas.
  • Partner with Children and Student Ministries to enhance their ministry and develop future worship volunteers/leaders
  • Teach scripture, pray, and incorporate other elements into creative worship elements
  • Utilize other giftings to bless the church and further the Gospel
  • Manage various day-to-day responsibilities associated with ministry
  • Serve in other areas as directed by the Lead Pastor and shared staff
  • Attend Staff meetings regularly. Attend Board of Ministries and Elders meetings as necessary.
  • Recognize God’s unique anointing and giftedness upon you, discover what new and possibly yet unspoken opportunities exist to glorify and worship Him together with us

QUALIFICATIONS

The Worship Director has great responsibility to alignment with the Word of God, in a growing and personal relationship in the Lord, in protecting truth in worship, and in bringing our very best to Jesus.

Required:

  • A clear testimony of faith in Jesus Christ, a vital and growing relationship with Him, and a solid commitment to the Lordship of Christ
  • Experience in leading a band and worship teams
  • Musical proficiency and vocal skills
  • Ability to exemplify the church’s values and uphold staff policies
  • Must be personable and work well with people, have a good rapport with congregation and healthy relationships with people
  • Committed to developing leaders
  • Must have a teachable spirit and a willingness to learn and grow in their craft
  • Must have a heart for lost people and a vision for reaching them
  • A sincere desire to be actively involved in ministering to people

Preferred:

  • Bachelors (or Masters) degree from an accredited college/university with a concentration in a field of Pastoral, Worship, or Music is preferred but not required
  • Demonstrated proven ministry experience relevant to the position will be helpful for us to understand the calling God has placed on your heart
  • Musical proficiency is desirable in instrument(s) of your choice
  • A desire to pursue additional training, personal development, and/or licensing in ministry will be supported and encouraged by the Church

REPORTING STRUCTURE

The Worship Director serves as a member of the ministry staff under the direct supervision of the Lead Pastor and is accountable to the Board of Elders.

COMPENSATION

Washington Alliance Church offers compensation commensurate with education, experience, and qualifications, with an anticipated salary range of $45,000 – $55,000 annually. A housing allowance and additional benefits are available. Final package is determined by the Board of Ministries and Finance Committee.

Resumes can be sent to ealyp@cmawpa.org. For more information, contact the Western PA District of the C&MA at (814) 938–6920.

To be considered for this position, please complete the application to include your testimony, resume and other background information related to the position.

If the district office has reviewed your application and they think you may be a potential match for the position, that the hiring manager will reach out to you for next steps.

To learn more about The Alliance and requirements for licensing, please visit our website

Mary, Queen of Peace Catholic Church is looking for a Digital Missionary. This is a
parttime position.

Position Type: Part-Time | Not Benefits Eligible (15-20 hours/week, flexible schedule including
some weekends/events, mostly working remotely) | Paid Hourly

Reports To: Director of Communications and Media / Pastor

Position Overview

Mary, Queen of Peace Catholic Church is seeking a creative, mission-driven Digital Missionary to
extend our parish presence into the digital continent. Rather than managing routine marketing, this
role approaches social media, digital content, and online engagement as an instrument of
evangelization, relational ministry, and radical hospitality.

The Digital Missionary will create compelling digital content, facilitate authentic online
community interaction, and help bridge the gap between digital engagement and active parish life in
Mandeville.

As a Digital Missionary, the individual's behavior is required to be consistent with culture and
cores values of Mary, Queen of Peace Catholic Church:

● Fundamentally Relational: As fundamentally relational beings, made in the image of our
relational God, we engage in relationships by being attentive and present
to those we serve and serve alongside.

● Mission Driven: We put the Lamb of God at the forefront of all that we do, aligning ourselves
to the collective mission of fostering life-changing encounters with Jesus.
● Innovatively Excellent: Ensuring quality and excellence, we transcend expectations by thinking
beyond the norm to meet the needs of today.
● Radically Hospitable: We are committed to radical hospitality, to be a place for doubters and
disciples, for people with deep questions and deep convictions; all have a home here with us.

Ministerial Character

The Pastor is the visible principle and foundation of unity in Mary, Queen of Peace Catholic Church
which the Archbishop has entrusted to him. He makes Christ's mission present and enduring in the
parish. In order to fulfill his mission, the Pastor employs suitable, chosen collaborators
(clerics, religious, or laypeople). He shares with them his mission and entrusts various
responsibilities to them.

Positions employed at Mary, Queen of Peace Catholic Church help to extend the ministry of the
Pastor in particular ways as outlined in the job description. Therefore, the employee in this
position is closely connected to and assists the Pastor in the performance of his ministry and
thereby engages in ministry for the Church.

Key Responsibilities

1. Evangelization & Content Creation (40%)

● Design visually engaging graphics, video clips, reels, and stories for parish social media
channels (Facebook, Instagram, YouTube, etc.).
● Translate Sunday homilies, parish events, and Catholic traditions into shareable, uplifting
digital content that inspires faith and connection.
● Capture high-quality photography and short video footage during parish events, Sacramental
celebrations, and ministry activities.
● Maintain a consistent parish brand identity rooted in warmth, beauty, and authentic Catholic
theology.

2. Community Engagement & Online Hospitality (35%)

● Actively monitor social media channels, responding to comments, direct messages, and inquiries
with radical hospitality and pastoral warmth.
● Foster an encouraging online environment where parishioners, seekers, and visitors feel seen,
welcomed, and prayerfully supported.

SUMMARY

The Lead Pastor of Missions, in cooperation with the Lead Pastor of Discipleship, provides visionary leadership, strategic direction, and pastoral oversight for all personal, local, national, and global outreach efforts. This role is responsible for cultivating a culture of missional living across Pinelake Church, mobilizing people into impactful groups and service opportunities, while stewarding partnerships that advance Pinelake's mission both locally and globally and strengthen its discipleship pathway.

GENERAL RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Learn
    • Pursue a growing relationship with Jesus through consistent time in God’s Word and prayer
    • Continually grow in your understanding of the Jesus-Centered Life (salvation, identity, life, and authority in Christ).
    • Remain teachable and hungry, seeking feedback, learning from others, and developing both spiritually and professionally.
    • Cultivate awareness of God’s presence in everyday life, listening to the Holy Spirit and responding in obedience.
  • Live
    • Practice and model the rhythms of Be the Church (Grow, Pray, Connect, and Share).
    • Pursue emotional health by engaging in self-awareness, addressing past wounds, and cultivating honest, healthy relationships.
    • Practice healthy rhythms, prioritizing your relationship with Jesus and your family
    • Embody a life of integrity and surrender, allowing your private life with God to shape your work.
  • Lead
    • Take ownership of disciple-making by personally investing in others and helping them move toward a Jesus-Centered Life.
    • Walk others through the Discipleship Pathway (Essentials → JCL → Be the Church), helping them discover and take their next step.
    • Shepherd people, not just programs, by listening for where God is at work in their story and walking with them toward transformation.
    • Equip and release others by developing Servant Leaders and multiplying disciples who Learn from Christ, Live in Christ, and Lead others to Christ.
    • Measure success by life change, spiritual formation, and multiplication—not just attendance or activity.
  • Embrace the Culture
    • Value and embody the staff values, which we call the 7 H’s: Humility, Honor, Honesty, Hunger, Holy Spirit, Health, and Harmony
    • Communicate clearly, honestly, and proactively in a way that builds trust, unity, and momentum.
    • Work in alignment with the church vision and leadership
    • Participate fully in the life of your campus or team, contributing to the unity, health, and shepherding of the faith family.

SPECIFIC LIST OF DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

Vision & Strategy

Campus Ministry Intern

OUR MISSION

Our mission is transforming college students to transform the world. We call college students to serve Jesus Christ with their entire lives by:

  1. Sharing the Gospel with students and developing passionate disciples of Jesus Christ.

  2. Serving together with the church and inviting students into the lives of local congregations. 

  3. Giving students a vision for serving Jesus Christ in their studies, jobs, communities, and families.


OUR VISION

Our vision is to see a generation of college students transformed by the power of Jesus Christ and His Gospel, in partnership with the local church, reaching the world for the glory of God.


OUR VALUES

1. All things belong to God.

2. Jesus changes people’s lives.

3. We love college students.

4. We embrace God’s multiethnic kingdom.

      5. Faithfulness is pursued together.

6. We celebrate life. 


PURPOSE OF POSITION

To provide the opportunity to catalyze Kingdom transformation on campus by sharing the Gospel and inviting students

into the life of the local church. Develop deep relationships with students that promote strong biblical discipleship, life long commitment to the Church, and the flourishing of Christ’s kingdom in their local context and all areas of life.


RESPONSIBILITIES

Organizational Responsibilities 

  • Attend National and Regional CCO Gatherings. (i.e. Summer Conference, Cultivate, Fall Retreat, and Jubilee) 

    • CMSI Program Launch (virtual): July 1 + 2, 2027

    • CCO Summer Conference: Third week in July, 2027

  • Participate in the monthly national CMSI Training Call via Zoom.

  • Complete ministry strategy assignments and training artifacts that partner with on-campus ministry experience.

  • Meet weekly with campus intern supervisor, or Campus Staff Mentor. 

  • Diligently perform fundraising behaviors in support of meeting 100% of campus goals and initiatives. 

  • Assist in administrative duties as assigned.


Campus Responsibilities

Engage

  • Be knowledgeable of and collaborative in the execution of the campus ministry plan in line with the 5E’s Campus Ministry Strategy.

  • Make contact with students, following up with them and inviting students into ministry opportunities.

  • Assist in the planning and execution of student events that create environments for connection. 

Evangelize

  • Commit to praying for not-yet Christians on campus and in the community.  

  • Assist in the creation of events/environments where students will hear the gospel.

  • Lead and/or participate in evangelism conversations with students inviting them to know and follow Jesus. 

Establish

  • Assist in the facilitation of gatherings of students on campus throughout the week that include prayer, teaching,

evangelism, leadership development, and applying Scripture to life in college and beyond.

  • Regularly invite students into the life of the local church.

Equip

  • Invite students to become student leaders within the CCO.

  • Assist in the facilitation of student leadership development on campus.

Embody

  • Invite students regularly to CCO’s Jubilee conference and other transformative opportunities.

  • Assist in the facilitation of events that model the Jubilee Vision for campus and beyond.


REQUIREMENTS

Education

  • Currently enrolled as a college student.

  • Must have completed 1 year of college at the start of internship

Experience

  • Served as a student leader on campus in some capacity in an organization or club.

Skill Set 

  • Able to organize and prioritize time properly. 

  • Collaborates with teams.

  • Manages competing priorities and tasks in a timely manner.

  • Displays initiative and can work independently.

  • Ability to engage a wide range of audiences.

  • Desire to learn, grow, and mentor others.

Spiritual Health

  • Values worship in a local church, prayer, Scripture study, and other spiritual disciplines.

Personal Conduct

  • Displays personal conduct consistent with CCO Statement of Faith, Core Values and the CCO employee handbook.

Professional Growth

  • Be open to professional development opportunities approved by the internship supervisor, schedule permitting.

Work Value

  • Demonstrates a passion for the Gospel, the church, and college students.

  • Proactive in preparation and timely in response. 

  • Encourages the growth and development of others.

  • Values excellence.



We will ensure that individuals with disabilities are provided reasonable accommodation to participate in the job application or interview process, to perform essential job functions, and to receive other benefits and privileges of employment. Please contact us to request accommodation.

Wisconsin

Part time

To advance the purpose of InterVarsity, this position is focused on learning the basics of college campus ministry. This position is limited to students who are currently enrolled in a four-year or community college. Second year students and students enrolled at a community college may intern at a two-year/community college. Third year students and higher can work at a four-year or community college. Non-InterVarsity students who attend a Christian college must have third or fourth year standing.

MAJOR RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Participate and engage fully with the campus ministry team to cast spiritual vision and direction
  • Contribute to the accomplishment of the campus ministry team’s plans for spiritual growth and transformation
  • Teach students to love, study, and apply Scripture to their lives
  • Promote the Mission on campus (to advance witnessing communities that are bolder, broader, and more ethnically diverse):
    • Seek opportunities to proclaim and demonstrate the Gospel of Jesus Christ

QUALIFICATIONS

Description:
There are nearly 300,000 teenagers of active-duty U.S. military parents who are stationed all over the world. These teens move an average of seven times during their school-aged years. The questions of identity and belonging that all teens face grow even more challenging to answer amid starting over and meeting new friends at each location.
This is where you can be the difference in a military teen’s life! By being in their world, walking alongside them, and creating a community where they experience the truth of God’s love and purpose for them, our staff provide a safe space where teens can develop friendships and connections to experience laughter, build hope, and generate resiliency.
We are currently providing incarnational ministry at many military installations around the world. You will have the opportunity to lead and oversee the overall Young Life Military program, known as Club Beyond, which is ecumenically focused and outreach oriented.
Responsibilities:
  • Actively develop healthy relationships with adults, as well as kids, and build vibrant relationships with the local community, the military installation, and the chapel community.
  • Be a role model (incarnational) and assist with developing community outreach to "unchurched" teens, discipleship to Christian teens, and leading and equipping volunteers to do "hands-on" middle and high school Christian youth programs.
  • Work well in an environment that sees (due to high military operational tempo) a high degree of turnover among teens, families, chaplains and volunteers.
  • Be respectful of and embrace a community that is deeply influenced by a military culture.
  • In this ministry, you will need to live out the Club Beyond Core Value Statement:
Club Beyond is a Christ-centered community of leaders with an exclusively military focus. Our methods are incarnational, and our perspective is ecumenical. We leverage strategic partnerships for the greatest results. We value professionalism from our staff and excellence in our stewardship.
Qualifications:
  • A deep love for Christ and for lost teens.
  • Competent communicator with youths, parents, and senior military leaders.
  • Teachable heart.
  • Willingness to make a three-year commitment.
  • Minimum of three years' youth ministry experience preferred.
  • College degree preferred.
  • Willingness to raise part of the budget through personal support.
  • Committed to a relational ministry approach.
  • Energetic.
  • Small event planning skills.
  • Strong initiative.
  • Note, this position would require our Staff to live near the community where they would be doing ministry.
Benefits:
  • Full-time salary: Based on experience, responsibility, and fundraising levels.
  • Benefits: Full health coverage (including dental, vision and life insurance).
  • Expense reimbursement (mileage [office and ministry related]).
  • Training and career development is built into the job.
Salary:
The Base Salary range: $45,000 to $60,000 (Salary is based on education and experience). In addition to salary, a Cost of Living Adjustment, dependent on location, is available. The Annual National Funding provided is $16,667.
Location:
Club Beyond works on military installations all over the world. We currently have openings at:
In the USA:
  • Fort Rucker, Alabama
  • Joint Base Elmendorf-Richardson (JBER), Alaska
  • Fort Irwin, California
  • Camp Pendleton, California
  • Travis Air Force Base, California
  • Joint Base Anacostia-Bolling (JBAB), Washington, D.C.
  • Eglin Air Force Base, Florida
  • Fort Benning, Georgia
  • Fort Stewart, Georgia
  • Fort Riley, Kansas
  • Fort Bragg, North Carolina
  • Fort Sill, Oklahoma
  • Fort Jackson, South Carolina
  • Fort Belvoir, Virginia
  • Joint Base Lewis-McChord (JBLM), Washington

Overseas:
  • Geilenkirchen, Germany and various other locations in Germany
  • Naval Base Guam
  • Aviano Air Base, Italy
  • Vicenza, Italy
  • Camp Zama, Japan
  • Yokosuka, Japan
Want to know more about our mission and culture?
Please check out clubbeyond.org to learn how Club Beyond has been changing the lives of military teens for over 40 years!

Position Summary

The Ministry Assistant (MA) provides essential administrative and program execution support to Congregational Care and Faith Formation ministries. Providing logistical organization, a keen attention to detail, and professional discretion, the Ministry Assistant supports the pastoral and program staff offer care ministries and spiritual formation engagements reflecting the generous welcome of the church’s mission.

· Provide general administrative support to Congregational Care and Faith Formation ministries and program staff leaders, including preparations for meetings (Deacons, Formation Formation), gathering information, supply materials, coordinating schedules.

· Manage communications and on-call assignments for the pastoral care team, ensuring that someone is assigned to respond to all pastoral care needs.

· Work alongside the Pastor for Care + Belonging to maintain the church’s weekly prayer list.

· Provide administrative support for memorial service planning and care of the church columbarium.

· Assist with curriculum orders and distribution to leaders and class members.

· Assist with processing background checks for adults working with minors and vulnerable adults; report updates needed for training and forms.

· Coordinate event registrations and sign-ups, as requested.

Qualifications

· Committed to embodying the mission and values of FPC Dallas.

· Demonstrated experience working successfully with teams reflecting diverse backgrounds.

· Digital proficiency, including facility with Microsoft Office Suite and readiness to navigate various data management platforms.

· Successful completion of a criminal background check and child protection training (required of all employees).

job_name: Youth Ministry Director at Fort Benning, Georgia
post_html:
*Please note this position would require our Staff to live near the community where they would be doing ministry.

Description:

There are nearly 300,000 teenagers of active-duty U.S. military parents who are stationed all over the world. These teens move an average of seven times during their school-aged years. The questions of identity and belonging that all teens face grow even more challenging to answer amid starting over and meeting new friends at each location.

This is where you can be the difference in a military teen’s life! By being in their world, walking alongside them, and creating a community where they experience the truth of God’s love and purpose for them, our staff provide a safe space where teens can develop friendships and connections to experience laughter, build hope, and generate resiliency.

We are currently providing incarnational ministry at many military installations around the world. You will have the opportunity to lead and oversee the overall Young Life Military program, known as Club Beyond, which is ecumenically focused and outreach oriented.

We are currently looking for both full-time and part-time staff throughout the United States, as well as international locations. Colorado Springs, CO, is the headquarters.

Responsibilities:

  • Actively develop healthy relationships with adults, as well as kids, and build vibrant relationships with the local community, the military installation, and the chapel community.
  • Be a role model (incarnational) and assist with developing community outreach to "unchurched" teens, discipleship to Christian teens, and leading and equipping volunteers to do "hands-on" middle and high school Christian youth programs.
  • Work well in an environment that sees (due to high military operational tempo) a high degree of turnover among teens, families, chaplains and volunteers.
  • Be respectful of and embrace a community that is deeply influenced by a military culture.
  • In this ministry, you will need to live out the Club Beyond Core Value Statement:

Club Beyond is a Christ-centered community of leaders with an exclusively military focus. Our methods are incarnational, and our perspective is ecumenical. We leverage strategic partnerships for the greatest results. We value professionalism from our staff and excellence in our stewardship.

Qualifications:

  • A deep love for Christ and for lost teens.
  • Competent communicator with youths, parents, and senior military leaders.
  • Teachable heart.
  • Willingness to make a three-year commitment.
  • Minimum of three years' youth ministry experience preferred.
  • College degree preferred.
  • Willingness to raise part of the budget through personal support.
  • Committed to a relational ministry approach.
  • Energetic.
  • Small event planning skills.
  • Strong initiative.
  • Note, this position would require our Staff to live near the community where they would be doing ministry.

Benefits:

  • Full-time salary: Based on experience, responsibility, and fundraising levels.
  • Benefits: Full health coverage (including dental, vision and life insurance).
  • Expense reimbursement (mileage [office and ministry related]).
  • Training and career development is built into the job.

The Base Salary range: $45,000 to $60,000 (Salary is based on education and experience). In addition to salary, a Cost of Living Adjustment, dependent on location, is available. The Annual National Funding provided is $16,667.

Title of Position: Lead Pastor (Full-Time) - Updated details 7.21.26

Church Name: Sandhills Alliance Church

Church Location: Pinehurst, NC

Description of Position: The church is seeking a lead pastor who is motivated to growing a church in a rapidly growing community, plus disciple and shepherd the congregation to be outward focused.

Description of Church's Location: The Village of Pinehurst, which is in Moore County, NC, is famous for its Golf course resort. It is also located approximately 21/2 hours from the mountains of NC and the NC shore. Approximately 40% of the community are retirees but it and the surrounding towns have a large presence of military families. There are younger families moving into the community near the church building.

Essential Characteristics, Skills and Strengths Required

  • Characterized by values of humility, integrity, and accountability
  • A good listener and effective communicator
  • Strong preaching and teaching the Word of God skill from the pulpit as well as in small groups and one-to-one conversations
  • A visionary leader who cultivates enthusiasm within the congregation, delegating effectively and motivating others to ministry and service
  • Proficient in relating to a multigenerational congregation of believers as well as those at various stages of spiritual growth.
  • Called to minister and grow a congregation.
  • A leader with a heart for CMA missions.
  • Proven ability to develop local outreach programs.
  • Willingness to mentor, encourage, and support the church’s ministry leaders.

Minimum Education Level: Bachelor’s degree minimum, Masters preferred.

Minimum Credential Level: Must be eligible for C&MA license and willing to begin the Alliance ordination process

Minimum Years of Experience: The ideal candidate has five to ten years of experience in pastoral ministry.

Church Size: Sunday attendance averages around 50-60 congregants.

Church Setting: Suburban

Church History: Sandhills Alliance Church is approximately 42 years old, planted in 1984. The congregation is friendly and welcoming. The current pastor is ready for retirement, and he has guided the search committee to begin their process to seek out their next pastor.

To be considered for this position, please complete the application to include your testimony, resume and other background information related to the position.

If the district office has reviewed your application and they think you may be a potential match for the position, that the hiring manager will reach out to you for next steps.

This position requires licensing with The Christian & Missionary Alliance. To learn more about The Alliance and requirements for licensing, please visit our website

Please do not contact the church directly.

author: Whitworth University
post_html:
Whitworth University is a residential campus shaped by learning, curiosity, and community life. This role is based on campus and requires consistent, in-person engagement.

Position Summary

As a Program Coordinator at Whitworth University, you will provide essential administrative and logistical support to the Office of Church Engagement (OCE) and the Weyerhaeuser Center for Faith and Learning (WEY). Working closely with the Directors and staff of both departments, you will help ensure that programs, events, meetings, and day-to-day operations are organized and carried out effectively.

This position is a key support role for two active departments. The Program Coordinator manages calendars and scheduling, assists with event and program logistics, coordinates routine office operations, supports departmental communications, and provides administrative assistance with purchasing, expenses, and grant-related documentation.

This is a highly collaborative role suited to someone who is organized with a high attention to detail and knack for hospitality.

Core Responsibilities

Program & Event Coordination | 35%

  • Provide administrative and logistical support for OCE and WEY programs, events, lectures, retreats, conferences, and other departmental activities, including coordinating room reservations, catering, equipment, materials, and other university support.
  • Coordinate arrangements for speakers, guests, and ministry partners, including travel, lodging, itineraries, and other logistics.
  • Create and process contracts and other documentation associated with events and programs.
  • Maintain event calendars, timelines, and logistical information.
  • Provide on-site hospitality and support for departmental events as needed.
  • Assist Directors and staff with the implementation of programs and activities.
Administrative & Office Support | 35%
  • Serve as the primary point of contact for OCE and WEY, welcoming visitors, answering phone calls and general inquiries, and directing questions and requests to the appropriate staff member.
  • Monitor and respond to general departmental email and other inquiries, handling routine questions and referring more complex requests.
  • Provide day-to-day administrative support to OCE and WEY Directors and staff, including preparing documents, reports, and meeting materials.
  • Schedule meetings and appointments and maintain departmental and Directors' calendars.
  • Maintain accurate files, records, and archives in university systems and databases.
  • Coordinate routine departmental needs with university offices including needs related to facilities, technology, equipment, and office supplies.
  • Provide general technological and administrative support using Microsoft 365 and other university systems.
  • Assist with the supervision and coordination of student employees as assigned.
  • Develop and maintain relationships with key contacts across campus to efficiently coordinate departmental needs.
  • Provide administrative and logistical support for OCE and WEY communications as needed.
Finance Support | 25%
  • Assist with routine tracking and documentation of departmental and program expenses and budgets.
  • Process checks, payment requests, purchasing card documentation, and other financial transactions.
  • Provide administrative support for grant-related recordkeeping and reporting in collaboration with the OCE Finance Coordinator.
Other | 10%
  • Other duties as assigned.
  • Participate in department events and special projects.

Qualifications and Core Competencies

  • Whitworth considers candidates with a wide range of educational backgrounds. We value the skills and knowledge candidates bring to Whitworth, regardless of the paths they have taken to acquire them.
  • 1-2 years of experience providing administrative support in a professional setting, including tasks such as managing calendars, scheduling appointments, handling correspondence, assisting with budgets, and organizing documents.
  • A personal commitment to the Christian faith and to the integration of faith and learning.
  • A commitment to the educational mission of Whitworth University as a comprehensive Christian liberal arts university affiliated with the Presbyterian church
Core Competencies 
  • Knowledge of current academic, business, and administrative practices and procedures.
  • Effective organizational, analytical, verbal, and written (grammar, punctuation, proofreading) communication and interpersonal skills.
  • Demonstrated ability to work collaboratively with a wide array of constituents.
  • The ability to multi-task and perform a wide variety of tasks with minimal supervision and multiple interruptions.
  • Ability to supervise student employees. 
  • Ability to work with confidential information.
  • Willingness and ability to learn new tasks.
  • Ability to plan and schedule events.
  • Demonstrated proficiency with Microsoft 365.
Preferred Qualifications
  • University experience.
  • 3 or more years of related work experience.

Other Details

Schedule
10 months | 30 hours per week | .63 FTE (considered full time for benefits)

Whitworth University is a Christian liberal arts university. Our shared mission is to provide our diverse students with an education of mind and heart, equipping them to honor God, follow Christ, and serve humanity. We seek candidates who are willing to engage with the university’s mission and integrate their Christian faith into their work.
 
Interested candidates should submit a cover letter, resume, faith statement, and contact information for at least three professional references. A background check and sexual misconduct check will be required of the successful candidate.

Applicants must be legally authorized to work in the United States at the time of hire and maintain valid work authorization throughout the duration of employment, including those on OPT. Whitworth University does not offer visa sponsorship for this position.

You are on this webpage because a position at Whitworth sparked your curiosity. If you find yourself questioning hitting the apply button because you might not meet 100% of the qualifications, we think you should do it! When you click apply and submit an application,  your application is reviewed by a committee of real, living, and breathing human beings who want to understand your background, experience and skills to find ways you relate to the key competencies needed for success in the position. 

Looking for resources to help with writing a faith statement? Check out our faith statement resource page for more information.

post_html:
Who We Are

We are a community living out our God-given calling as we follow Jesus and make disciples every day and empower others to do the same. Rooted in our faith and centered on Christ, we seek to reflect His heart in all we do—serve others, grow together, and advance His mission with purpose and passion.

Jesus leads our way. We look to Him as our ultimate example, guide, and authority. His life and teachings shape our decisions, our culture, and our direction.

Unity protects our purpose. We believe we are stronger together. By honoring one another, communicating openly, and working collaboratively, we safeguard the mission entrusted to us.

Faithfulness builds our future. We are committed to stewarding our responsibilities with integrity and consistency, trusting that daily obedience produces lasting impact.

Rest restores our soul. We value rhythms of Sabbath and renewal, recognizing that abiding in Christ fuels sustainable, healthy ministry.

Joy sets our tone. We approach our work with gratitude and hope, confident in God’s goodness and expectant for what He will do through us.

Working at Long Hollow is more than a job. It’s a calling to contribute to a larger purpose. Together, we are a team on mission—following Jesus, making disciples, and faithfully living out our calling every day.


What We Believe

Long Hollow is a cooperating member of the Southern Baptist Convention. An overview of our core beliefs along with the scriptures that inform them can be found here .


Character Traits

  • Is a Christ-follower with a personal commitment to Jesus Christ as their Lord and Savior
  • Demonstrates integrity and professional conduct in all interactions
  • Shows flexibility and adaptability in a ministry environment
  • Exhibits patience, care, and respect when working with other staff and church members
  • Maintains a positive, engaging attitude that creates a welcoming environment
Requirements

  

Role Summary 

The School of Ministry Director leads the day-to-day life of Long Hollow’s School of Ministry (SOM), carrying its mission, direction, and values into every class, cohort, and partnership. This role owns the quality, growth, and reach of the SOM—recruiting and developing teachers, growing the student body across Long Hollow, the community, and virtual learners, and connecting training across ministries so that the SOM becomes a true equipping hub for the church and a leadership pipeline for future Long Hollow staff.  


What You’ll Do

  

   Mission & Quality 

  • Implement the mission, direction, and values of the School of Ministry, ensuring consistent content, feel, and DNA across all classes 
  • Evaluate classes and teachers regularly through observation, student feedback, and outcomes, and make improvements as needed 

   Teaching & Curriculum 

  • Recruit, train, and coach qualified teachers who reflect Long Hollow’s beliefs, values, and teaching standards 
  • Fill in teaching opportunities as needed, serving as a primary back-up instructor across SOM courses 
  • Identify and prepare additional course studies, and keep existing curriculum biblically sound, practical, and consistent with Long Hollow’s DNA 

   Students & Reach 

  • Oversee recruitment of students from Long Hollow, the surrounding community, and virtual learning opportunities 
  • Manage SOM calendars, enrollment, and completion tracking, and report regularly to leadership on enrollment, outcomes, and pipeline health 

   Equipping Hub & Leadership Pipeline 

  • Connect training opportunities across ministries and staff to create a true equipping hub at Long Hollow 
  • Shape and lead a cohort among key certificate students, providing deeper discipleship, mentoring, and leadership development 
  • Ensure a leadership pipeline for future Long Hollow staff by identifying and developing emerging leaders in partnership with ministry leaders and HR • Partner with seminaries and other institutions to create pathways for further study 

Skills Needed to Succeed

  

  • Master of Divinity (M.Div.) required 
  • 5+ years’ experience in local church ministry, with demonstrated teaching experience in adult learning environments 
  • Strong biblical and theological foundation consistent with Long Hollow’s beliefs and the Baptist Faith & Message 
  • Gifted communicator and teacher able to engage a wide range of learners
  • Experience recruiting, training, and developing teachers or volunteer leaders 
  • Curriculum design and development experience 
  • Ability to disciple, mentor, and develop emerging leaders 
  • Program management and organizational skills, including enrollment and records oversight 
  • Relational skills to build partnerships across ministries, staff teams, and seminaries
  • Familiarity with virtual and hybrid learning platforms 

Benefits

  • Paid vacation (starts at 3 weeks) 
  • Paid Holidays (12+ days)
  • 401K Match
  • Paid Medical & Dental Insurance w/HSA Contribution
  • Vision Insurance available 
  • Access to free counseling & legal services
  • Paid time off to serve in other ministry areas
  • Paid Time off to attend Conferences

Description

United Methodist Endorsing Agency

After endorsement by the United Methodist Endorsing Agency (UMEA), part of the General Board of Higher Education and Ministry (GBHEM), bishops appoint clergy to specialized ministries that reach far beyond the local church. More than 500 United Methodist clergy endorsed by UMEA are answering God’s call in diverse and meaningful ways. These chaplains, pastoral counselors, life coaches and spiritual care providers serve in places where the church’s presence is deeply needed — military bases, hospitals, prisons, counseling centers, truck stops and more.

About the Role

The United Methodist Endorsing Agency (UMEA) seeks an experienced consultant to advise and support the agency's efforts to strengthen the spiritual, emotional, and professional well-being of endorsed clergy serving in specialized ministry settings. Working collaboratively with the UMEA Director, the consultant will assess current care initiatives, develop scalable support strategies, provide training and educational resources, and recommend best practices for sustaining healthy and effective ministry.

Scope of Services:

  • Strategic Wellness Consultation
    • Assess current UMEA clergy wellness by being in regular direct contact with endorsed clergy. Build support programs and recommend and enhancements to strengthen clergy resilience, engagement, and vocational sustainability.
    • Provide one-on-one pastoral care as needed to individuals in the endorsed community when warranted and in consultation with the Director of UMEA.
    • Design and recommend frameworks for clergy wellness outreach, including tools, protocols, and assessment methodologies for identifying clergy support needs.
  • Program Resource Development & Facilitation
    • Develop and facilitate virtual and in person support groups, workshops, and cohort-based learning opportunities focused on clergy wellness, resilience, and vocational longevity.
    • Assist in planning retreats, conferences, and continuing education offerings that promote spiritual renewal and personal well-being.
  • Organizational Advisement & Agency Support
    • Serve as a subject matter expert to the UMEA Director on clergy wellness, pastoral care practices, and organizational support strategies.
    • Provide periodic reports summarizing findings, trends, recommendations, and opportunities for future program development.
  • Evaluation & Continuous Improvement
    • Review aggregate clergy feedback, annual reports, and wellness indicators to identify emerging needs and opportunities for intervention.


Qualifications
  • Advanced degree in theology, pastoral care, counseling, social work, psychology, organizational leadership, or related field.
  • Experience in chaplaincy, specialized ministry, clergy care, military ministry, healthcare ministry, or institutional settings.
  • Demonstrated expertise in clergy wellness, burnout prevention, trauma-informed care, and moral injury.
  • Experience designing and facilitating educational programs, support groups, retreats, and leadership development initiatives.
  • Strong consulting, assessment, and strategic planning skills.
  • Familiarity and experience with The United Methodist Church structure and endorsement processes preferred.
  • Exceptional written communication, facilitation, and relationship-building abilities.

 

 

Deliverables:

  • The consultant will provide:
    • Strategic assessment of existing clergy care programs.
    • Written recommendations and implementation roadmap.
    • Resource library and training materials.
    • Facilitated workshops and/or cohort sessions.
    • Periodic progress and trend reports.
    • Final report summarizing outcomes, recommendations, and future opportunities.

 

How to Apply:

    • 1) A cover letter

    • 5)Three references [2 supervisory and 1 professional]

Campus Staff Minister (Georgetown University)

Work Location:

Maryland

Job Type:

Full time

God has called InterVarsity to plant and to build witnessing communities of students and faculty who follow Jesus on college and university campuses. Through these groups, we believe ever- increasing numbers of students and faculty from all ethnic groups and areas of the campus will be transformed by the Gospel. We expect to see campuses increasingly become places where people, ideas, and structures flourish to the glory of God. We confidently anticipate that our InterVarsity alumni will become change agents across the country and around the world. We pursue this calling by discerning and actively participating in what God is already doing on campus. This is the essence of being a Campus Staff Minister (CSM).

ESSENTIAL COMMITMENTS/RESPONSIBILITIES 

Spiritual Growth 

You pursue maturity as a disciple of Jesus Christ so that your life and work increasingly reflects a growing love for God, God’s Word, God’s people of every ethnicity and culture, and God’s purposes in the world. To do this, you will: 

  • Pursue a vibrant relationship with the triune God through engagement with Scripture, prayer, and worship, both individually and in community 

  • Develop self-leadership (growing in self-awareness, self-management, relational integrity, and resiliency) 

  • Embrace Scriptural standards for behavior and attitudes 

 

Campus Leadership

You communicate and model InterVarsity’s vision to see students and faculty transformed, campuses renewed and world changers developed 

  • Create a culture of humble dependence on God and bold expectation in God’s intention to start new witnessing communities throughout the campus and on new campuses.

  • Model – in person and through programs – InterVarsity’s vision and Core Values, including a biblically-defined commitment to engage every ethnic and social group on campus 

  • Lead students and faculty – individually and collectively – through Scripture, prayer, teaching, and discipleship experiences, so that they articulate and align their ministry activities around this vision 

  • Set annual goals through prayer, research and reflection with your teams (students, faculty, and staff) for qualitative and quantitative growth, including conversions and leadership development 

 

You create, develop, align and leverage ministry plans, programs, teams, and structures to close the gap between current reality and the aspirational goals. 

  • Build leadership teams who trust and partner well with you and who demonstrate spiritual vitality, relational health, and mission alignment 

  • Develop and execute plans to achieve annual goals, evaluating and modifying the plan as needed throughout the year 

  • Increase momentum for the vision by aligning programs, structures, conferences and teams around the goals 

  • Mobilize students and faculty to engage their relational networks with the gospel and to start new missional communities 

  • Under the direction of the Area Director, may supervise Ministry Interns and Campus Ministry Interns as delegated 

 

You intentionally gather, invite, and develop diverse groups of students and faculty so that they not only encounter and follow Jesus as Savior and Lord but also advance the mission on campus as participants and leaders. 

  • Create ways for faculty and students to encounter and follow Jesus through Scripture, worship, prayer, mission experiences, conferences, etc. 

  • Equip students and faculty so that they think strategically about campus engagement and so that they proclaim – in word, deed, and power – the good news of Jesus, regularly inviting students and faculty to follow him as Savior and Lord 

  • Disciple students and faculty by equipping them to hear the Word, respond actively, and debrief and interpret the experience so that they grow in Christlikeness, reflect our Core Values, and develop ministry skills 

  • Invite, coach, and equip students and faculty to become increasingly effective participants and leaders, including starting new witnessing communities on campuses 

 

Organizational Collaboration 

You work with a network of other local, area, regional, and national InterVarsity staff and volunteers so that our work reflects Biblical standards of excellence, integrity, and partnership. 

  • Partner with and respond positively to the direction and coaching of your supervisors and national leaders 

  • Contribute to collaborative and productive team meetings and relationships 

  • Affiliate chapters under your care and submit Graduating Student Forms in order to increase our partnership with current students and alumni 

  • Use national ministry resources and tools, as requested, including recruiting and/or participating in local, regional, or national conferences as  

  • Complete reporting, planning and review requirements in a timely way so that you and your supervisors can assess and improve your work as a CSM 

  • Comply with all InterVarsity policies and procedures 

 

Ministry Partnership Development 

You will develop a team of partners – churches and individuals (including alumni and community members) – who will resource the ministry financially, in prayer, or volunteer service that advances the mission. 

  • Raise 100% of the financial budget assigned by your supervisor 

  • Communicate regularly with your ministry partners, nurturing the relationship through visits, phone calls, emails and regular prayer letters 

  • Develop on-going, long-lasting partnership with alumni and volunteers 

  • Comply with all Ministry Partnership Policies 

  • Identify and invest in advocates who will build networks of volunteers and donors on InterVarsity’s behalf 

 

Accomplish all other assigned tasks as appropriate 

 

QUALIFICATIONS (common to all levels of CSM) 

  • Annually affirm InterVarsity’s Statement of Agreement (Doctrinal Basis and Purpose Statement). Abide by InterVarsity’s Code of Conduct. Believe and behave consonantly with InterVarsity’s Human Sexuality Theological Paper. Affirm and behave consonantly with InterVarsity’s “Women in Ministry Statement of Affirmation” 

  • Bachelor’s degree for CSMs assigned to a four-year campus. A minimum of an Associate’s degree for CSMs assigned to a two-year campus or a community college 

  • Strong interpersonal skills (including ability to minister to diverse ethnic communities and faculty) 

  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills 

  • Demonstrated problem solving skills 

  • Familiarity with word processing, presentation, email, and spreadsheet software 

 

WORK ENVIRONMENT/PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS 

The CSM position leads ministry in a college campus environment. A designated office space may or may not be available. The CSM is required to travel to on-campus and off- campus sites as appropriate. Off-campus travel includes, but is not limited to: student ministry conferences, Ministry Partnership Development meetings, and InterVarsity- sponsored training sessions, meetings, and conferences. The CSM is regularly required to communicate with others, and routinely uses standard office equipment such as computers, phones, photocopiers, filing cabinets, etc. 

Pay Range: $39,288.00 - $52,392.00 per year

Pay: This position is funded through personal fundraising. Accordingly, compensation will vary based on the ability of the individual to secure a donor team to fund the cost of his/her salary. The anticipated salary range for this position on a full-time basis (40 hours/week) is dependent on a variety of factors, including location and cost of living. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

Overview

With hope and expectation, New Life Church in Aitkin, MN is seeking a new Senior Pastor, one who is energized by the prospect of shaping vision, building momentum and leading a church that is ready to move forward together. United around a clear mission of helping each person take their next step of faith in Christ, New Life Church is poised and ready to welcome a pastor who will love them and lead them into a new ministry season.

The Big Idea

For the pastor who enjoys maximizing potential, developing people and activating the church on mission, New Life Church presents an exciting opportunity! This congregation is eager to begin writing their next chapter. This includes shepherding and further developing people who are energized, generous and invested in the mission. It also includes guiding the church to complete the journey they began several years ago to build and relocate to a larger new facility. Land has been purchased and prepped, and they have significant funds in the bank, but leadership is needed to discern how best to proceed. Ministries to the next generation are very important to New Life, and the incoming pastor will have the opportunity to call a youth or family pastor to shape a ministry strategy to make New Life an even stronger spiritual home for children, youth and families.

The Church

Affiliation: Christian and Missionary Alliance (C&MA)
Attendance: A vibrant, missional, multi-generational congregation of 110 people
About: Offering two services at 10:15 a.m. and 6 p.m., the morning service blends traditional hymns with gentle contemporary music while the evening service is more relaxed, with modern worship. Attenders value preaching that is grounded in the biblical text, relevant and applicable.

The Candidate

New Life would love to welcome a relationally warm and approachable pastor who embodies an authentic and evident care for people. He will be energized by time with people; remembering names and taking time to get to know others personally and spiritually. He will be a gifted communicator of Scripture, teaching the Bible with clarity, relevance and conviction. While remaining grounded in the biblical text, he will be authentic and transparent, sharing stories that help people know and trust their pastor. He will lead with a servant’s heart, demonstrating integrity, emotional intelligence and a collaborative spirit. Rather than arriving at the church with a predetermined agenda, he will listen carefully, build trust and work alongside the Leadership Team and Elders to shape a compelling, shared vision for the future. Passionate about equipping others, he will invest in developing leaders, mobilizing volunteers and helping individuals discover and use their spiritual gifts for meaningful Kingdom impact.

The Location

Aitkin offers an great quality of life for those who love the outdoors and value the simplicity of small town living. Nestled in the heart of Minnesota’s lake country, Aitkin is known for its natural beauty, quality schools and strong sense of community. Year-round recreational opportunities abound including hunting, fishing, boating, biking and snowmobiling. The town is home to the county government center, a regional hospital and a strong school system. For a pastor who values meaningful relationships and engagement in the local community, Aitkin provides a deeply rewarding place to live, lead and build a lasting ministry.

The Qualifications

Be in agreement with the C&MA Statement of Faith. Be ordained, or willing to be ordained in the C&MA. Agree with New Life Church’s values and beliefs. Theological or Bible degree preferred. Previous experience understanding or exposure to life in rural America. Five to ten years of associate or senior pastor experience in growing ministry. Be an experienced biblical communicator. Preach 40 - 44 weeks per year and regularly invite people to take their next step of faith. To see the full list of candidate qualifications, please click on link below.

About Praxis

Praxis began in 2011 with a desire to support and equip Christian entrepreneurs and has grown steadily into a 30+ person, NY-centric team advancing the redemptive imagination and action of founders, funders, and innovators motivated by their faith to address the major issues of our time. As a $15M+/year nonprofit with ambitious growth plans, we're expanding our venture-building work globally, organizing around the major issues of our time, and building media and more to activate the redemptive potential of Christians around the world. We see our team as the first carriers of the mission, building an organization that is great to work at, excellent in its craft, and redemptive in its finances as well as its programs.

The Role

Praxis is hiring a Director of Church Engagement to lead its work with local churches and universities. This person helps churches use the Praxis Course and related resources well, builds trusted friendships with senior pastors, and makes sure churches feel served and equipped rather than sold to. They lead a growing team and are responsible for whether churches move from first interest, to actively hosting, to a lasting habit of forming their people in the Redemptive Way. The posture is one of service to the church and its pastors, in the spirit of helping the church do what only the church can do.

This role exists to serve, equip, and enable the local church and its senior pastor. The Director of Church Engagement is the person who carries Praxis’s relationship with churches: understanding what pastors are trying to build, removing friction, and helping each church use Praxis resources in a way that fits its own community and calling. The aim is not to grow Praxis. The aim is to help churches activate people, and to help pastors lead congregations that practice generosity, courage, and care for their neighbors over the long haul.

While Praxis is known and respected amongst local church leadership, it is a newer entrant (with new offerings) to church-facing work, so unlike organizations with an established church presence, this role includes a healthy, servant-hearted invitation in the early years: helping churches discover the Course (and other formational experiences) and decide to host it. That invitation is always offered in the posture of service, never as a sales pitch.

What Success Looks Like

If this role is working, Praxis, through the Course and additional resources, is deployed as the vocational version of Alpha. We will see more people formed, through more churches, more often. 

We will track our progress by asking a few simple questions:

  • How many churches are actively engaged with Praxis resources?
  • What share of each congregation is taking part?
  • How often do churches run the Course again after their first time?
  • How is the fruit and faithful action of those encountering Praxis ideas, stories and resources changing over time?

Leading indicators we will watch include:

  • Churches where the senior pastor is personally engaged.
  • Churches where a staff member owns the work day to day.
  • The rate at which churches return to host again.
  • Churches that clearly understand what Praxis offers and why.
  • Stories and case studies that show formation taking root.

Key Areas of Responsibility

Church Engagement Strategy

  • Develop the vision and strategy for how we will engage and reach local church leaders, networks and denominations. Igniting a global community activating redemptive potential of their local congregations.
  • Approach the role with an entrepreneurial and innovative mindset. Develop creative approaches to strategy, engagement, community, reach and fellowship.

Pastor & Church Relationships

  • Build and steward trusted relationships with senior pastors and church teams, helping them move from interest, to hosting, to building a lasting culture of redemptive formation.

Church Activation & Formation

  • Help churches host the Praxis Course well, and guide them in weaving it into the rhythms of congregational life.
  • Lead the development and ongoing improvement of the Church Activation Toolkit, gathering feedback from churches, naming the friction points, and turning what works into resources others can use.

Pastor Cohort & Activate

  • Cast vision and help run the Pastor Cohort, the program that walks deeply with a small number of pioneering senior pastors and churches each year.
  • Contribute to Activate, our in development annual gathering for pastors, lay leaders, and culture-makers.

Team Leadership

  • Lead a growing church engagement team, including the Sr. Manager Praxis Course Product & Engagement and TBC roles pending growth

Who You Are

  • You love the local church and have spent meaningful time inside it, ideally on staff as Senior Pastor or in close partnership with pastors.
  • You are trusted by senior leaders, and you carry yourself with humility, warmth, and discretion.
  • You can hold theological depth and practical excellence at the same time, and you are comfortable serving churches across a range of traditions.
  • You are an entrepreneurial builder who is happy to do the early, unglamorous work of standing something up, and a leader who can grow a team as the work grows.
  • You are organized, follow through, and turn what you learn into resources that help the next church.
  • You share Praxis’s conviction that Christians are called to be redemptive culture-makers, and you want to help the church live that out.
  • You practice what we preach. We have to be redemptive exemplars on our team, in how we work, and how we treat others in our community.

Additional Details

Location: New York City preferred. Remote will be considered for a highly experienced candidate.
Travel: 

  • Quarterly team meetings (typically held at Praxis HQ in New York City)
  • Annual Praxis Summit
  • Additional travel as needed for in-person Design Sprints, film and production meetings, and major events such as our Regional Gatherings and Activate
  • All travel expenses covered by Praxis

Reports to: Managing Partner, Media, Brand and Product

  • Range: $120K to $155K based on experience and location
  • Comprehensive benefits including fully paid health insurance for families
  • 5% matching 401k
  • Flexible vacation policy

For all Praxis roles, we are open to candidates who are "outside of range." Growth-minded applicants at an earlier stage of career and compensation, and candidates with experience above the top of the range, are welcome and encouraged to apply.

Cultural Alignment
Praxis finds its theological identity most clearly stated in the Lausanne Covenant (1974) and the Cape Town Commitment (2010). All Praxis staff and program participants are asked to affirm The Apostles’ Creed as a statement of their own beliefs. The ideal candidate will demonstrate alignment with the above, as well as our mission to advance redemptive entrepreneurship. We're seeking a leader who combines operational excellence with a spirit of humility and service, contributing to our vision of building an organization that embodies redemptive principles in all aspects of its work and culture, which includes shared rhythms such as daily team prayer and a company-wide weekly Sabbath, as detailed in our Rule of Life for Redemptive Entrepreneurs (rule.praxislabs.org).
